### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this training/attendance record, e.g. CTR-YYYY-0001. |
| Training Title | Enter the official name of the training course, briefing, awareness session, induction, or competence activity delivered. |
| Training Type | Enter the category of training using allowed values: Information Security Awareness, Role-Based Security Training, Secure Development, Incident Response, Privacy/Data Protection, Physical Security, Supplier Security, Induction, Refresher, Other. |
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Reference | Enter the relevant clause or control reference, typically Cl. 7.2 and/or A.6.3; include any other applicable internal ISMS control reference if relevant. |
| Competence Requirement / Learning Objective | State the specific competence, awareness outcome, or skill the attendee is expected to gain, linked to their role or information security responsibilities. |
| Audience / Role Required | Enter the target audience or role group required to complete the training, e.g. All Employees, Developers, Service Desk, Privileged Users, ISMS Internal Auditors, Senior Management. |
| Mandatory Training | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the training is mandatory for the attendee’s role. |
| Training Provider | Enter the internal team, individual, external supplier, or learning platform that provided the training. |
| Delivery Method | Enter one allowed value: Classroom, Virtual Live, E-Learning, Toolbox Talk, Workshop, On-the-Job Training, Simulation/Exercise, Other. |
| Training Date | Enter the date the training was delivered or assigned in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Training Duration Hours | Enter the duration of the training in hours as a number, e.g. 1, 1.5, 2. |
| Attendee Name | Enter the full name of the person who attended or was assigned the training. |
| Attendee Unique ID | Enter the employee ID, contractor ID, learner ID, or other unique workforce identifier. |
| Job Title / Role | Enter the attendee’s current job title or functional role at the time of training. |
| Department / Team | Enter the attendee’s department, business unit, or team. |
| Employment Type | Enter one allowed value: Employee, Contractor, Temporary Worker, Supplier, Intern, Other. |
| Manager / Approver | Enter the attendee’s line manager or responsible approver for competence and training requirements. |
| Attendance Status | Enter one allowed value: Attended, Completed Online, Assigned Not Started, In Progress, Absent, Cancelled, Exempted. |
| Completion Date | Enter the date the attendee completed the training in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if not completed. |
| Assessment Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether a test, quiz, observation, exercise evaluation, or other assessment was required. |
| Assessment Method | Enter the method used to assess competence, e.g. Quiz, Practical Exercise, Manager Observation, Simulation, Interview, Attendance Only, Not Applicable. |
| Score / Result | Enter the score or outcome achieved, including units where applicable, e.g. 85%, 18/20, Satisfactory, Completed; use Not Applicable if no assessment was required. |
| Pass Mark | Enter the required pass threshold or acceptance criterion, e.g. 80%, 16/20, Satisfactory; use Not Applicable if no assessment was required. |
| Pass / Fail Status | Enter one allowed value: Pass, Fail, Not Applicable, Pending. |
| Competence Achieved | Enter Yes, No, or Pending to indicate whether the required competence has been demonstrated based on completion and assessment results. |
| Retraining Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether further training is required due to failure, absence, role change, expired competence, or management decision. |
| Retraining Due Date | Enter the required retraining deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if retraining is not required. |
| Certificate / Evidence Reference | Enter the certificate number, LMS completion ID, attendance sheet reference, assessment record ID, or other evidence identifier. |
| Record Location / Link | Enter the file path, SharePoint/Teams link, LMS URL, HRIS reference, or document repository location where supporting evidence is stored. |
| Trainer / Assessor Name | Enter the name of the trainer, facilitator, assessor, or system that delivered or assessed the training. |
| Trainer / Assessor Competence Evidence | Enter a brief reference confirming the trainer/assessor is competent, e.g. qualification, certification, role experience, approved trainer list reference, or Not Applicable for automated LMS content. |
| Notes / Exceptions | Enter any relevant exception, exemption reason, late completion note, accessibility adjustment, or management decision; leave blank if none. |
| Record Created Date | Enter the date this record was first created in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record Last Updated Date | Enter the date this record was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record Owner | Enter the role accountable for maintaining this record, e.g. HR Learning Manager, ISMS Manager, Security Awareness Lead. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the HR Learning Manager with oversight from the ISMS Manager or Security Awareness Lead. Update after each training event or LMS completion import, review at least monthly, and draw source data from the LMS, HRIS, attendance sheets, assessment results, certificates, and the ISMS competence/training matrix.

ISO27-030.title: Awareness Programme Materials
ISO27-030.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Document ID] | 1.0 | [Information Security / GRC Owner] | [Effective Date] | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | Annex A.6.3 — Information Security Awareness, Education and Training | Internal |

## Purpose

This template is used to plan, document, approve, deliver, and retain evidence of information security awareness programme materials supporting ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.6.3.

Annex A.6.3 requires personnel and relevant interested parties to receive appropriate information security awareness, education, and training, including updates to organisational policies, topic-specific guidance, and responsibilities relevant to their roles. This template provides a consistent format for creating and evidencing awareness materials such as:

- Slide decks and training modules
- Posters, intranet content, email campaigns, and newsletters
- Phishing simulation notices, test scenarios, and learning materials
- Role-based awareness content for privileged users, managers, developers, contractors, and other relevant groups
- Refresher communications following incidents, audit findings, risk assessments, or policy changes

The completed form supports audit evidence by showing that awareness content is planned, relevant, approved, delivered, measured, and retained.

## Instructions

1. Complete this template for each awareness material, campaign, training module, poster set, phishing simulation, or awareness communication package.
2. Use one form per distinct awareness item or campaign. For example:
 - One form for the annual mandatory security awareness training deck.
 - One form for a phishing simulation campaign.
 - One form for a poster campaign on reporting suspicious emails.
3. Ensure the material aligns to applicable information security policies, acceptable use rules, incident reporting expectations, data protection requirements, and role-specific security responsibilities.
4. Identify the intended audience clearly, including whether the material applies to:
 - All personnel
 - Employees only
 - Contractors or temporary workers
 - Privileged users
 - Developers or technical teams
 - Managers
 - Third-party users with access to organisational information or systems
5. Include measurable learning or awareness objectives where practical.
6. Obtain approval before publication, delivery, or launch, especially for phishing simulations and organisation-wide communications.
7. Ensure phishing tests are ethically designed, lawful, proportionate, and approved by relevant stakeholders before execution.
8. Attach or reference the actual awareness materials, such as slide decks, posters, emails, landing pages, LMS modules, intranet articles, screenshots, or phishing templates.
9. After delivery, update the completion and effectiveness fields with evidence such as attendance, completion rates, quiz results, phishing click rates, reporting rates, feedback, and remediation actions.
10. Retain the completed form and supporting evidence in the approved records repository.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Awareness Material ID | Text | Yes | Unique identifier for the material or campaign, such as `AW-2025-001`. |
| Material / Campaign Title | Text | Yes | Name of the awareness item, such as “Annual Security Awareness Training”, “Recognising Phishing Emails”, or “Secure Remote Working Poster Campaign”. |
| Material Type | Select | Yes | Select one or more: Slide Deck, LMS Module, Poster, Email Campaign, Newsletter, Intranet Article, Phishing Simulation, Workshop, Video, Quick Reference Guide, Role-Based Training, Other. |
| Description / Summary | Long text | Yes | Briefly describe the content, purpose, and expected outcome of the material. |
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Control Mapping | Text | Yes | Default: Annex A.6.3 — Information Security Awareness, Education and Training. Include additional relevant controls where applicable, such as A.5.10, A.5.12, A.5.14, A.5.15, A.5.16, A.5.24, A.5.26, A.8.7, A.8.12, or A.8.24. |
| Related Policy / Standard / Procedure | Text / Links | Yes | Reference applicable internal documents, such as Information Security Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, Access Control Policy, Incident Management Procedure, Data Classification Standard, Remote Working Standard, Secure Development Standard, or Privacy Policy. |
| Awareness Objective(s) | Long text | Yes | State what the audience should understand or do after receiving the material. Objectives should be specific and action-oriented. Example: “Personnel can identify common phishing indicators and report suspicious emails using [reporting mechanism].” |
| Target Audience | Multi-select / Text | Yes | Define audience groups. Examples: All Personnel, New Joiners, Contractors, Privileged Users, Developers, Service Desk, Finance Team, HR Team, Executives, Third Parties. |
| Audience Size / Population | Number / Text | No | State the estimated or actual number of recipients, learners, or test subjects. |
| Delivery Method | Select / Text | Yes | Select or describe delivery channel: LMS, classroom, virtual session, intranet, email, collaboration platform, posters in office, screensavers, phishing simulation platform, team briefing, onboarding workflow. |
| Delivery Frequency | Select | Yes | Select: One-Time, Onboarding, Annual, Quarterly, Monthly, Event-Driven, Policy-Change-Driven, Incident-Driven, Risk-Driven, Other. |
| Planned Delivery Date / Period | Date / Date range | Yes | Planned date or campaign period for delivery, publication, or simulation launch. |
| Actual Delivery Date / Period | Date / Date range | No | Complete after delivery. Record actual delivery, publication, or launch date. |
| Campaign Owner | Name / Role | Yes | Person accountable for preparation and delivery of the material. Usually Information Security, GRC, HR Learning & Development, or Communications. |
| Content Author | Name / Role | Yes | Person or team responsible for drafting the material. |
| Subject Matter Reviewer | Name / Role | Yes | Reviewer responsible for technical and policy accuracy. |
| Legal / Privacy Reviewer | Name / Role | Conditional | Required where material involves personal data, monitoring, phishing simulation, disciplinary implications, external communications, or regulated topics. |
| HR / Learning Reviewer | Name / Role | Conditional | Required for mandatory training, onboarding, learning management system content, or people-management implications. |
| Communications Reviewer | Name / Role | Conditional | Required for broad communications, posters, branded campaigns, intranet publication, or executive messaging. |
| Approval Authority | Name / Role | Yes | Person authorised to approve release, such as CISO, Information Security Manager, Head of GRC, HR Learning Lead, or designated control owner. |
| Content Version | Text | Yes | Version of the awareness material, such as `v1.0`. Update when content is materially changed. |
| Content Location / Link | URL / Repository path | Yes | Link to the approved slide deck, poster files, LMS module, email copy, phishing template, landing page, screenshots, or campaign package. |
| Classification of Material | Select | Yes | Select: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. Most internal awareness material should be Internal unless it includes sensitive details such as phishing test design or incident specifics. |
| Sensitive Content Included | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether the material includes sensitive examples, internal system names, simulated attacks, incident details, personal data, or restricted operational information. |
| Accessibility and Inclusion Check Completed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm content is reasonably accessible, legible, understandable, and appropriate for the audience. Consider language, readability, alternative text, captions, and colour contrast where applicable. |
| Localisation / Language Requirements | Text | No | Identify translations or regional adaptations required for the target audience. |
| Mandatory Completion Required | Yes/No | Yes | State whether completion is mandatory. Mandatory training should have defined due dates and escalation rules. |
| Completion Due Date | Date | Conditional | Required if mandatory completion is required. |
| Completion Tracking Method | Select / Text | Conditional | Required for mandatory or measurable campaigns. Examples: LMS report, attendance register, HR system, email analytics, phishing platform report, acknowledgement form. |
| Assessment Method | Select / Text | No | Examples: Quiz, knowledge check, phishing simulation metrics, acknowledgement, manager confirmation, attendance, practical exercise, no assessment. |
| Pass Mark / Success Criteria | Text | Conditional | Required where an assessment is used. Example: “80% quiz score” or “Phishing reporting rate greater than click rate.” |
| Reinforcement / Remediation Approach | Long text | No | Describe follow-up for non-completion, failed assessments, repeat phishing clickers, or low-awareness teams. Include coaching, reminder communications, refresher training, or manager escalation. |
| Key Messages | Long text | Yes | Summarise the primary messages. Example: “Report suspicious emails immediately; do not reuse passwords; protect confidential information; follow clear desk and screen locking requirements.” |
| Behaviour Expected from Audience | Long text | Yes | State the required actions or behaviours. Example: “Use [reporting mechanism] to report suspected phishing; classify documents before sharing; complete mandatory training by the due date.” |
| Incident Reporting Instructions Included | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm the material tells personnel how and where to report suspected information security events or weaknesses. |
| Policy Responsibilities Included | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm the material references personnel responsibilities under applicable information security policies and acceptable use requirements. |
| Role-Based Content Included | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether the material includes tailored content based on job function or access level. |
| Trigger for Material | Select / Text | Yes | Select or describe trigger: Annual Programme, New Joiner Onboarding, Policy Update, New Risk, Security Incident, Audit Finding, Regulatory Requirement, Seasonal Threat, Phishing Trend, Technology Change, Other. |
| Threat / Risk Topic Covered | Multi-select / Text | Yes | Examples: phishing, social engineering, malware, ransomware, password security, MFA, data handling, clean desk, remote working, mobile device security, cloud usage, secure development, supplier security, incident reporting, privacy, physical security. |
| Supporting Evidence Required | Checklist / Text | Yes | Identify evidence to retain, such as approved deck, poster PDF, email copy, LMS report, attendance register, phishing report, screenshots, quiz results, approval record, communications plan. |
| Delivery Status | Select | Yes | Select: Draft, Under Review, Approved, Scheduled, Delivered, Cancelled, Superseded. |
| Effectiveness Metrics | Long text | No | Complete after delivery. Include measurable results such as completion rate, average quiz score, phishing click rate, phishing report rate, attendance rate, acknowledgement rate, user feedback score, or incident trend impact. |
| Lessons Learned / Improvement Actions | Long text | No | Record improvements for future awareness activities, such as simplifying content, targeting high-risk groups, improving reporting instructions, or changing delivery frequency. |
| Exceptions / Deviations | Long text | No | Record any deviations from planned delivery, audience, approval, or tracking, including justification and compensating actions. |
| Next Review Date | Date | Yes | Date the content must be reviewed for accuracy and continued relevance. At minimum, review annually or after major policy, threat, legal, organisational, or technology changes. |
| Superseded By | Text / Link | No | Complete when the material is replaced by a newer version or campaign. |
| Record Owner | Name / Role | Yes | Person accountable for maintaining this completed form and associated evidence. |

### Awareness Material Planning Checklist

| Checklist Item | Yes/No/NA | Evidence / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Material addresses information security responsibilities relevant to the target audience. | | |
| Material aligns with current approved information security policies and procedures. | | |
| Material includes clear instructions for reporting suspected information security events or weaknesses. | | |
| Material is appropriate to the audience’s role, access level, and risk exposure. | | |
| Mandatory completion requirements, due dates, and escalation paths are defined where applicable. | | |
| Content has been reviewed for technical accuracy. | | |
| Content has been reviewed for legal, privacy, or HR considerations where applicable. | | |
| Content has been approved before release. | | |
| Evidence of delivery and completion will be captured. | | |
| Effectiveness metrics have been defined. | | |
| Accessibility, readability, and language needs have been considered. | | |
| Review date and record owner have been assigned. | | |

### Example Awareness Content Register

| Material ID | Title | Type | Audience | Frequency | Owner | Status | Evidence Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AW-2025-001 | Annual Information Security Awareness Training | LMS Module / Slide Deck | All Personnel | Annual | Information Security | Approved | [Repository link] |
| AW-2025-002 | Report Phishing Fast | Poster / Email Campaign | All Personnel | Quarterly | Security Awareness Lead | Scheduled | [Repository link] |
| AW-2025-003 | Privileged Access Responsibilities | Role-Based Training | Administrators / Privileged Users | Annual | IAM Owner | Draft | [Repository link] |
| AW-2025-004 | Secure Coding Refresher | Workshop / Slide Deck | Developers | Semi-Annual | Application Security Lead | Delivered | [Repository link] |
| AW-2025-005 | Phishing Simulation Q2 | Phishing Simulation | Selected Personnel | Quarterly | Security Operations | Under Review | [Repository link] |

### Phishing Simulation-Specific Fields

Complete this section where the material or campaign includes a phishing test, simulation, or social engineering exercise.

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Simulation ID | Text | Yes | Unique identifier for the phishing simulation, such as `PHISH-2025-Q2`. |
| Simulation Objective | Long text | Yes | Define the learning and measurement objective. Example: “Assess recognition and reporting of credential-harvesting phishing emails.” |
| Target Group Selection Method | Long text | Yes | Describe how participants are selected. Ensure selection is risk-based, fair, proportionate, and approved. |
| Number of Recipients | Number | Yes | Planned number of recipients in scope. |
| Scenario Theme | Text | Yes | Describe the scenario theme without including unnecessary sensitive detail. Example: “Fake document share notification” or “Benefits update”. |
| Risk Level of Simulation | Select | Yes | Select: Low, Medium, High. High-risk simulations require additional approval and privacy/HR review. |
| Use of Credentials / Data Capture | Select | Yes | Select: No Capture, Username Only, Simulated Entry Only, Other. Avoid collecting real passwords or unnecessary personal data. |
| Landing Page Message | Text / Link | Yes | Link to or describe the educational landing page shown after interaction. It should provide immediate, constructive learning. |
| Reporting Mechanism Tested | Text | Yes | Identify reporting route tested, such as phishing report button, service desk ticket, security mailbox, or hotline. |
| Pre-Notification Approach | Text | No | Describe whether general awareness or campaign notice is provided, without compromising test validity. |
| Success Metrics | Long text | Yes | Examples: delivery rate, open rate, click rate, credential submission rate, report rate, time to report, repeat click rate. |
| Remediation Plan | Long text | Yes | Describe follow-up training, coaching, or communications for individuals or groups needing improvement. |
| Privacy Impact Considered | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm that personal data processing, monitoring, reporting, and retention have been considered. |
| HR / Employee Relations Review Completed | Yes/No/NA | Yes | Required where individual-level results may be used for follow-up, escalation, or performance-related actions. |
| Executive / Senior Approval Obtained | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm senior approval before launch. |
| Simulation Launch Window | Date range | Yes | Planned launch window. Avoid critical business periods unless explicitly approved. |
| Actual Simulation Completion Date | Date | No | Complete after simulation. |
| Results Report Location | URL / Repository path | No | Link to final simulation report and lessons learned. |

### Delivery and Effectiveness Log

| Date | Activity | Audience / Group | Delivery Channel | Evidence Captured | Result / Metric | Follow-Up Required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Date] | [Training delivered / poster published / phishing launched] | [Audience] | [Channel] | [Evidence] | [Metric] | [Yes/No and action] |

## Approval / Routing

The completed template and associated awareness materials must be routed for review and approval before publication, training delivery, or campaign launch.

| Stage | Reviewer / Approver | Required When | Approval Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Content Author Review | Content Author | All materials | Draft version and author confirmation |
| Information Security Review | Information Security Manager / Control Owner | All materials mapped to A.6.3 | Review comments, approval workflow, or signed approval |
| Policy / GRC Review | GRC Owner or Policy Owner | Materials referencing policies, audit requirements, or ISO/IEC 27001 obligations | Review record or approval ticket |
| Technical SME Review | Relevant SME | Technical, role-based, secure development, cloud, access control, or incident response content | Review comments or approval |
| HR / Learning & Development Review | HR / L&D Representative | Mandatory training, onboarding, personnel records, non-completion escalation, employee communications | LMS approval, HR sign-off, or workflow approval |
| Legal / Privacy Review | Legal / Privacy Representative | Phishing simulations, monitoring, personal data, regulated content, or sensitive investigations | Legal/privacy approval or DPIA reference where applicable |
| Communications / Brand Review | Communications Representative | Posters, intranet content, executive messages, broad campaigns | Communications approval |
| Senior Management Approval | CISO / Security Steering Committee / Executive Sponsor | Organisation-wide campaigns, phishing simulations, high-risk awareness activities, or campaigns with business impact | Approval minutes, workflow approval, or signed authorisation |

Approval record:

| Approval Role | Name | Decision | Date | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Content Author | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Information Security Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required | [Date] | [Comments] |
| GRC / Policy Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required | [Date] | [Comments] |
| HR / L&D Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required / Not Applicable | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Legal / Privacy Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required / Not Applicable | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Communications Reviewer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required / Not Applicable | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Final Approver | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Changes Required | [Date] | [Comments] |

## Records & Retention

Completed awareness programme material forms and associated evidence must be retained as controlled information security management system records.

Records should demonstrate that information security awareness, education, and training were planned, approved, delivered, and evaluated in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.6.3.

| Record Type | Examples | Retention Requirement | Record Location | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completed Awareness Programme Materials Form | This completed template, approval records, routing history | Minimum 3 years or longer if required by legal, regulatory, contractual, or audit obligations | [Records repository / GRC system] | [Record Owner] |
| Approved Awareness Content | Slide decks, LMS modules, posters, email copy, newsletters, intranet screenshots, videos, quick reference guides | Retain current version plus prior versions for minimum 3 years | [Content repository / LMS / intranet archive] | [Information Security / L&D Owner] |
| Training Delivery Evidence | Attendance registers, LMS completion reports, acknowledgements, webinar logs, onboarding completion records | Minimum 3 years | [LMS / HR system / records repository] | [HR / L&D Owner] |
| Assessment Evidence | Quiz results, pass/fail records, knowledge check summaries, completion certificates | Minimum 3 years | [LMS / records repository] | [HR / L&D Owner] |
| Phishing Simulation Evidence | Approved simulation plan, email templates, landing page screenshots, campaign metrics, results report, remediation records | Minimum 3 years, subject to privacy and employment law requirements | [Phishing platform / records repository] | [Security Operations / Awareness Owner] |
| Effectiveness and Improvement Records | Metrics dashboards, lessons learned, improvement actions, management reporting | Minimum 3 years | [GRC system / records repository] | [GRC Owner] |
| Review and Supersession Records | Review notes, version history, superseded materials, change approvals | Minimum 3 years after supersession | [Document management system] | [Document Owner] |

Retention and handling requirements:

- Store records in an approved repository with access restricted to authorised roles.
- Protect individual-level training, assessment, and phishing simulation results as confidential personnel-related information.
- Do not retain real passwords, unnecessary personal data, or excessive behavioural monitoring data.
- Ensure records are available for internal audit, external audit, management review, and certification assessment.
- Dispose of records securely after the approved retention period, subject to legal hold, investigation, regulatory, contractual, or audit requirements.
- Review awareness materials at least annually and whenever significant changes occur to threats, policies, technology, legal obligations, organisational context, or incident trends.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Review ID | Enter a unique identifier for this access review cycle or review record, e.g. AR-YYYY-Q#-SYSTEM or AR-YYYY-MM-###. |
| Review Period | Enter the period covered by the review in YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the access review was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| System / Application / Repository | Enter the exact name of the system, application, database, cloud platform, file share, code repository, or other access-controlled asset being reviewed. |
| System Owner | Enter the accountable business or technical owner of the system, using full name and/or role title. |
| Access Reviewer | Enter the person performing the review, normally the system owner, data owner, application owner, or delegated manager; use full name and role. |
| User Full Name | Enter the full legal or HR-recorded name of the individual whose access is being reviewed. |
| User ID / Account Name | Enter the unique account identifier as shown in the source system, directory, IAM platform, or application. |
| User Email | Enter the user's corporate email address, or N/A for non-person accounts. |
| Department / Business Unit | Enter the user's current department, team, or business unit according to HR or identity records. |
| Line Manager | Enter the user's current line manager according to HR records; use full name. |
| Employment Status | Enter one allowed value: Active, Leaver, Suspended, Contractor Active, Contractor Ended, Transferred, Unknown. |
| Account Type | Enter one allowed value: Named User, Privileged Admin, Service Account, Shared Account, Break-glass, Third-party, System Account. |
| Access Role / Group / Permission | Enter the specific role, group, permission set, profile, entitlement, access level, or membership being reviewed exactly as named in the source system. |
| Privilege Level | Enter one allowed value: Standard, Elevated, Privileged, Administrative, Read-only, Service, Unknown. |
| Access Purpose / Business Justification | Enter the business reason the access is required, tied to job role, responsibility, support need, or approved service operation. |
| Access Source | Enter where the access record was obtained from, e.g. Active Directory, Entra ID, Okta, SAP, AWS IAM, GitHub, application export, database query. |
| Last Login Date | Enter the most recent successful login or use date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Never if no login is recorded, or Unknown if the source does not provide it. |
| Access Granted Date | Enter the date the access was originally granted in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Unknown if not available. |
| Previous Review Decision | Enter the outcome from the prior review for this same access, if available; allowed values: Retain, Remove, Modify, Exception, Not Previously Reviewed, Unknown. |
| Reviewer Decision | Enter the review decision using one allowed value: Retain, Remove, Modify, Suspend, Investigate, Exception Required. |
| Decision Rationale | Enter a concise explanation supporting the reviewer decision, including why access remains appropriate or why change/removal is required. |
| Remediation Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether any access change, removal, suspension, or investigation is required. |
| Remediation Action | If remediation is required, enter the specific action to be taken, e.g. remove group membership, downgrade role, disable account, confirm with manager; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the person or team responsible for completing the remediation action, e.g. IAM Team, Service Desk, System Administrator, Application Owner. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target completion date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Completion Date | Enter the actual date remediation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required or Pending if not yet complete. |
| Remediation Ticket / Change Reference | Enter the ticket, change, request, or workflow reference used to evidence the remediation; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Post-Remediation Status | Enter one allowed value: Not Required, Pending, Completed, Overdue, Failed, Risk Accepted. |
| Exception Approved | Enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether an exception to normal access policy was formally approved. |
| Exception Reference | If an exception exists, enter the risk acceptance, exception, or approval reference; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the controlled location or link where evidence is stored, such as review export, signed approval, ticket, screenshot, IAM report, or GRC record. |
| Reviewer Sign-off Date | Enter the date the reviewer completed and signed off the review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Approver | Enter the person providing final approval or oversight of the access review, if required by procedure; use full name and role, or N/A. |
| Approver Sign-off Date | Enter the final approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not required. |
| Comments | Enter any additional relevant notes, constraints, anomalies, or follow-up information; do not include unnecessary personal data. |

### Maintenance

This template is owned by the Information Security Manager or IAM/GRC process owner, with review input from system owners and business data owners. It is updated at least annually and whenever access review procedures, systems, roles, or IAM sources change; records should be drawn from authoritative IAM directories, HR records, application entitlement exports, privileged access management tools, and service desk/change management systems.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Change Ticket ID | Enter the unique identifier from the change management system, e.g. CHG-000123; must be unique and traceable. |
| Change Title | Enter a short descriptive title of the proposed change. |
| Change Description | Describe exactly what is being changed, including scope, components, configuration, software, infrastructure, process, or access changes. |
| Change Type | Select one allowed value: Standard, Normal, Emergency. |
| Change Category | Select the most relevant category, e.g. Application, Infrastructure, Network, Security, Cloud, Database, Endpoint, Identity and Access, Process, Supplier. |
| Change Priority | Select one allowed value: Low, Medium, High, Critical, based on business urgency and impact. |
| Requestor | Enter the full name and job title or user ID of the person requesting the change. |
| Requesting Department/Team | Enter the department, function, or team requesting the change. |
| Date Requested | Enter the date the change was requested in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Business Justification | Enter the business reason for the change, including problem, requirement, regulatory driver, risk treatment, or improvement objective. |
| Affected Information Assets/Systems | List all affected systems, services, applications, databases, networks, information assets, or configuration items; use asset IDs where available. |
| Affected Data Classification | Select the highest classification of information affected by the change, e.g. Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, or the organisation's approved classification labels. |
| Affected Locations/Environments | Identify affected environments or locations, e.g. Production, UAT, Development, DR, Cloud Region, Data Centre, Office Location. |
| Security Impact Assessment Completed | Select Yes, No, or Not Required; Yes means the security implications of the change have been assessed before approval. |
| Security Impact Summary | Summarise identified security implications, including impact on confidentiality, integrity, availability, logging, monitoring, access control, vulnerabilities, resilience, or compliance. |
| Risk Assessment Reference | Enter the linked risk assessment ID, security assessment ID, or risk register reference; enter Not Required only if formally exempted. |
| Risk Rating Before Change | Enter the assessed pre-change risk rating using the organisation's scale, e.g. Low, Medium, High, Critical. |
| Required Security Controls/Conditions | Record any controls, conditions, or prerequisites required before implementation, such as MFA enabled, backup verified, vulnerability scan passed, firewall rule reviewed, segregation of duties confirmed, or logging enabled. |
| Testing Plan Reference | Enter the test plan, validation checklist, deployment verification, or release test reference; include a link if maintained electronically. |
| Testing Completed | Select Yes, No, Partially, or Not Required; record whether testing was completed before approval or implementation as applicable. |
| Test Results Summary | Summarise the outcome of testing, including pass/fail status, defects, security test results, and any accepted residual issues. |
| Rollback/Backout Plan Reference | Enter the rollback plan reference or link; if not applicable, enter Not Applicable and state why in the linked change record. |
| Implementation Plan Reference | Enter the implementation plan, runbook, deployment plan, or release reference used to perform the change. |
| Planned Implementation Start | Enter planned start date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format, including time zone if relevant. |
| Planned Implementation End | Enter planned end date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format, including time zone if relevant. |
| Expected Service Impact | Describe expected downtime, degradation, customer/user impact, security impact, or state No Impact if none is expected. |
| User/Stakeholder Communication Required | Select Yes or No; if Yes, ensure the communication evidence or reference is included in Evidence/Attachment Links. |
| Approver Name | Enter the full name of the authorised approver or change advisory board chair who made the decision. |
| Approver Role | Enter the approver's role, e.g. Change Manager, Service Owner, System Owner, Information Security Manager, CAB Chair. |
| Approval Decision | Select one allowed value: Approved, Rejected, Approved with Conditions, Deferred, Cancelled. |
| Approval/Rejection Date | Enter the date the approval decision was made in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Approval/Rejection Rationale | Record the reason for the approval, conditional approval, rejection, deferral, or cancellation, including key risk, testing, business, or security considerations. |
| Emergency Change | Select Yes or No; Yes means the change followed the emergency change process due to urgent business, operational, or security need. |
| Emergency Approval Details | For emergency changes, record who authorised the emergency change, when, and why; enter Not Applicable for non-emergency changes. |
| Implemented By | Enter the full name, team, or supplier responsible for implementing the change. |
| Actual Implementation Start | Enter the actual start date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format, including time zone if relevant; leave blank until implemented. |
| Actual Implementation End | Enter the actual end date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format, including time zone if relevant; leave blank until implemented. |
| Implementation Status | Select one allowed value: Not Started, In Progress, Implemented Successfully, Implemented with Issues, Rolled Back, Failed, Cancelled. |
| Post-Implementation Review Completed | Select Yes, No, or Not Required; Yes confirms the implemented change was reviewed for success, issues, and unintended security impact. |
| Post-Implementation Review Date | Enter the date the post-implementation review was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until completed. |
| Post-Implementation Review Outcome | Summarise whether objectives were met, whether there were incidents or deviations, whether rollback was needed, and whether further actions are required. |
| Incidents/Issues Linked | Enter linked incident, problem, defect, vulnerability, or issue IDs related to the change; enter None if no related issues. |
| Change Closure Date | Enter the date the ticket was formally closed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until closed. |
| Record Owner | Enter the role or named person accountable for maintaining the accuracy of this change record. |
| Evidence/Attachment Links | Provide links or references to supporting evidence, such as approvals, CAB minutes, test results, security assessment, risk assessment, implementation plan, rollback plan, communications, and post-implementation review. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Change Manager or Service Management Lead, with Information Security oversight; updated for every submitted change ticket and reviewed at least monthly for completeness and audit readiness. The authoritative source should be the organisation's ITSM/change management system, with supporting evidence drawn from CAB records, risk assessments, testing repositories, deployment tools, and security review records.

ISO27-033.title: Backup Records & Test Results
ISO27-033.content:
## Backup Records & Test Results (XLSX/PDF template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Record ID | Control Reference | Backup Policy / Procedure Reference | Business Service / System | Data Set / Asset Name | Asset Owner | Backup Type | Backup Scope | Backup Frequency | Scheduled Backup Date/Time | Actual Backup Start Date/Time | Actual Backup End Date/Time | Backup Status | Backup Job ID | Backup Tool / Platform | Backup Storage Location | Storage Media / Repository | Retention Period | Encryption Applied | Encryption Method / Key Reference | Integrity Verification Performed | Integrity Verification Result | Backup Size | Backup Operator / Automation Account | Exception / Failure Description | Corrective Action Taken | Corrective Action Owner | Corrective Action Due Date | Corrective Action Status | Restore Test Required | Restore Test Date | Restore Test Scope | Restore Test Environment | Restore Test Performed By | Recovery Point Objective (RPO) | Recovery Time Objective (RTO) | Actual Recovery Point Achieved | Actual Restore Duration | Restore Test Result | Restored Data Validation Performed | Restored Data Validation Result | Issues Identified During Restore Test | Lessons Learned / Improvement Actions | Evidence Reference / Link | Reviewed By | Review Date | Review Outcome | Comments |

| [EXAMPLE: BAK-2025-001] | [EXAMPLE: A.8.13] | [EXAMPLE: Backup and Restore Procedure v1.2] | [EXAMPLE: Finance ERP] | [EXAMPLE: ERP production database] | [EXAMPLE: Head of Finance Systems] | [EXAMPLE: Full] | [EXAMPLE: Full production database including transaction and configuration tables] | [EXAMPLE: Daily] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-03 22:00 UTC] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-03 22:01 UTC] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-03 22:48 UTC] | [EXAMPLE: Successful] | [EXAMPLE: JOB-784512] | [EXAMPLE: Enterprise Backup Platform] | [EXAMPLE: Cloud backup vault - UK region] | [EXAMPLE: Immutable Storage] | [EXAMPLE: 90 days] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: AES-256 using KMS key alias backup-prod] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Passed] | [EXAMPLE: 185 GB] | [EXAMPLE: svc-backup-prod] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not Required] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-10] | [EXAMPLE: Database restored to test environment and sample records validated] | [EXAMPLE: Isolated DR test environment] | [EXAMPLE: Infrastructure Operations Team] | [EXAMPLE: 24 hours] | [EXAMPLE: 4 hours] | [EXAMPLE: 22 hours] | [EXAMPLE: 1h 20m] | [EXAMPLE: Passed] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Passed] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: Evidence repository link REF-2025-BAK-001] | [EXAMPLE: IT Operations Manager] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-11] | [EXAMPLE: Accepted] | [EXAMPLE: None] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this backup or restore-test record, using a consistent format such as BAK-YYYY-NNN or REST-YYYY-NNN. |
| Backup Policy / Procedure Reference | Enter the approved internal backup policy, standard, runbook, or procedure reference that this record follows, including document ID and version where available. |
| Business Service / System | Enter the name of the business service, application, server, database, SaaS platform, or infrastructure component being backed up or tested. |
| Data Set / Asset Name | Enter the specific data set, database, file share, VM, container volume, configuration set, or information asset covered by the backup. |
| Asset Owner | Enter the accountable business or technical owner of the system or data, using name and role or team mailbox. |
| Backup Type | Enter one allowed value: Full, Incremental, Differential, Snapshot, Image, Replication, Configuration Export, SaaS Export, Other. |
| Backup Scope | Describe exactly what is included and excluded in the backup, such as full database, selected tables, VM image, user files, application configuration, or tenant export. |
| Backup Frequency | Enter the scheduled frequency using an allowed value such as Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, On Change, Continuous, Ad hoc, Other. |
| Scheduled Backup Date/Time | Enter the planned backup execution date and time in ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, including time zone where relevant. |
| Actual Backup Start Date/Time | Enter the actual backup start date and time in ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, including time zone where relevant. |
| Actual Backup End Date/Time | Enter the actual backup completion date and time in ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, including time zone where relevant. |
| Backup Status | Enter one allowed value: Successful, Successful with Warnings, Failed, Missed, Cancelled, In Progress, Not Applicable. |
| Backup Job ID | Enter the unique job, task, run, or transaction ID generated by the backup platform or script. |
| Backup Tool / Platform | Enter the name of the backup software, cloud service, script, native platform feature, or managed service used to perform the backup. |
| Backup Storage Location | Enter the logical or physical backup destination, such as cloud region, data centre, backup vault, object storage bucket, offsite location, or repository name; do not include secrets. |
| Storage Media / Repository | Enter the media or repository type, such as Disk, Tape, Immutable Storage, Object Storage, Snapshot Repository, Cloud Backup Vault, SaaS Backup Repository. |
| Retention Period | Enter the required retention period for the backup, using a clear duration such as 30 days, 90 days, 7 years, or Until contract termination. |
| Encryption Applied | Enter Yes or No to confirm whether backup data is encrypted at rest and/or in transit as required. |
| Encryption Method / Key Reference | Enter the encryption method and non-sensitive key reference, such as AES-256, KMS key alias, HSM-backed key ID, or backup platform managed encryption; do not record key material. |
| Integrity Verification Performed | Enter Yes or No to confirm whether backup integrity verification was performed, such as checksum, catalogue verification, automated validation, or test mount. |
| Integrity Verification Result | Enter one allowed value: Passed, Failed, Warning, Not Performed, Not Applicable. |
| Backup Size | Enter the backup size with unit, such as MB, GB, or TB, using a numeric value plus unit. |
| Backup Operator / Automation Account | Enter the person, team, service account, automation job, or managed service responsible for executing the backup. |
| Exception / Failure Description | If the backup status is not fully successful, describe the exception, warning, missed job, or failure cause; enter None if not applicable. |
| Corrective Action Taken | Describe the remediation action taken for any backup failure, warning, missed job, or restore issue; enter None if not applicable. |
| Corrective Action Owner | Enter the person or team responsible for completing corrective action; enter Not Applicable if no action is required. |
| Corrective Action Due Date | Enter the due date for corrective action in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Applicable if no action is required. |
| Corrective Action Status | Enter one allowed value: Not Required, Open, In Progress, Completed, Overdue, Risk Accepted. |
| Restore Test Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether this backup is subject to restore testing under the backup policy or test schedule. |
| Restore Test Date | Enter the date the restore test was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Performed if no restore test was performed for this record. |
| Restore Test Scope | Describe what was restored during the test, such as full system, selected files, database restore, table-level restore, configuration restore, or sample transaction data. |
| Restore Test Environment | Enter where the restore was tested, such as DR environment, test environment, isolated sandbox, staging tenant, or production-approved restore location. |
| Restore Test Performed By | Enter the person, team, service provider, or automation account that performed the restore test. |
| Recovery Point Objective (RPO) | Enter the approved maximum tolerable data loss for the service or data set, using a duration such as 15 minutes, 4 hours, 24 hours, or Not Defined. |
| Recovery Time Objective (RTO) | Enter the approved maximum tolerable restoration time for the service or data set, using a duration such as 1 hour, 8 hours, 24 hours, or Not Defined. |
| Actual Recovery Point Achieved | Enter the actual age of the restored data relative to the failure scenario, using a duration such as 10 minutes, 2 hours, or 1 day. |
| Actual Restore Duration | Enter the elapsed time to complete the restore test, using a duration such as 00:45, 2h 15m, or 1 business day. |
| Restore Test Result | Enter one allowed value: Passed, Passed with Issues, Failed, Not Performed, Not Applicable. |
| Restored Data Validation Performed | Enter Yes or No to confirm whether restored data was validated for usability, completeness, and readability. |
| Restored Data Validation Result | Enter one allowed value: Passed, Failed, Partial, Not Performed, Not Applicable. |
| Issues Identified During Restore Test | Describe any restore failure, missing data, corruption, access issue, excessive duration, configuration gap, or dependency issue; enter None if no issues were identified. |
| Lessons Learned / Improvement Actions | Record any improvement actions arising from the backup or restore test, such as procedure updates, scheduling changes, capacity changes, or monitoring enhancements; enter None if not applicable. |
| Evidence Reference / Link | Enter the location or reference for supporting evidence, such as backup job report, monitoring alert, ticket number, restore test screenshot, checksum report, or audit evidence repository link. |
| Reviewed By | Enter the name and role of the person who reviewed the backup record or restore test result. |
| Review Date | Enter the date of review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Outcome | Enter one allowed value: Accepted, Accepted with Actions, Rejected, Further Investigation Required. |
| Comments | Enter any additional relevant notes that support the backup record or restore test result; enter None if not applicable. |

### Maintenance

The IT Operations Manager or Backup Service Owner owns this template and ensures entries are updated after each scheduled backup, backup exception, and restore test, with formal review at least monthly. Source data should be drawn from the backup platform, monitoring tools, service desk tickets, restore test reports, asset inventory, and approved backup/restore procedures.

field_guidance.Backup Type: Enter one allowed value: Full, Incremental, Differential, Snapshot, Image, Replication, Configuration Export, SaaS Export, Other.
field_guidance.Backup Scope: Describe exactly what is included and excluded in the backup, such as full database, selected tables, VM image, user files, application configuration, or tenant export.
field_guidance.Backup Frequency: Enter the scheduled frequency using an allowed value such as Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, On Change, Continuous, Ad hoc, Other.
field_guidance.Scheduled Backup Date/Time: Enter the planned backup execution date and time in ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, including time zone where relevant.
field_guidance.Actual Backup Start Date/Time: Enter the actual backup start date and time in ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, including time zone where relevant.
field_guidance.Actual Backup End Date/Time: Enter the actual backup completion date and time in ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, including time zone where relevant.
field_guidance.Backup Status: Enter one allowed value: Successful, Successful with Warnings, Failed, Missed, Cancelled, In Progress, Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Backup Job ID: Enter the unique job, task, run, or transaction ID generated by the backup platform or script.
field_guidance.Backup Tool / Platform: Enter the name of the backup software, cloud service, script, native platform feature, or managed service used to perform the backup.
field_guidance.Backup Storage Location: Enter the logical or physical backup destination, such as cloud region, data centre, backup vault, object storage bucket, offsite location, or repository name; do not include secrets.
field_guidance.Storage Media / Repository: Enter the media or repository type, such as Disk, Tape, Immutable Storage, Object Storage, Snapshot Repository, Cloud Backup Vault, SaaS Backup Repository.
field_guidance.Retention Period: Enter the required retention period for the backup, using a clear duration such as 30 days, 90 days, 7 years, or Until contract termination.
field_guidance.Encryption Applied: Enter Yes or No to confirm whether backup data is encrypted at rest and/or in transit as required.
field_guidance.Encryption Method / Key Reference: Enter the encryption method and non-sensitive key reference, such as AES-256, KMS key alias, HSM-backed key ID, or backup platform managed encryption; do not record key material.
field_guidance.Integrity Verification Performed: Enter Yes or No to confirm whether backup integrity verification was performed, such as checksum, catalogue verification, automated validation, or test mount.
field_guidance.Integrity Verification Result: Enter one allowed value: Passed, Failed, Warning, Not Performed, Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Backup Size: Enter the backup size with unit, such as MB, GB, or TB, using a numeric value plus unit.
field_guidance.Backup Operator / Automation Account: Enter the person, team, service account, automation job, or managed service responsible for executing the backup.
field_guidance.Exception / Failure Description: If the backup status is not fully successful, describe the exception, warning, missed job, or failure cause; enter None if not applicable.
field_guidance.Corrective Action Taken: Describe the remediation action taken for any backup failure, warning, missed job, or restore issue; enter None if not applicable.
field_guidance.Corrective Action Owner: Enter the person or team responsible for completing corrective action; enter Not Applicable if no action is required.
field_guidance.Corrective Action Due Date: Enter the due date for corrective action in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Applicable if no action is required.
field_guidance.Corrective Action Status: Enter one allowed value: Not Required, Open, In Progress, Completed, Overdue, Risk Accepted.
field_guidance.Restore Test Required: Enter Yes or No to indicate whether this backup is subject to restore testing under the backup policy or test schedule.
field_guidance.Restore Test Date: Enter the date the restore test was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Performed if no restore test was performed for this record.
field_guidance.Restore Test Scope: Describe what was restored during the test, such as full system, selected files, database restore, table-level restore, configuration restore, or sample transaction data.
field_guidance.Restore Test Environment: Enter where the restore was tested, such as DR environment, test environment, isolated sandbox, staging tenant, or production-approved restore location.
field_guidance.Restore Test Performed By: Enter the person, team, service provider, or automation account that performed the restore test.
field_guidance.Recovery Point Objective (RPO): Enter the approved maximum tolerable data loss for the service or data set, using a duration such as 15 minutes, 4 hours, 24 hours, or Not Defined.
field_guidance.Recovery Time Objective (RTO): Enter the approved maximum tolerable restoration time for the service or data set, using a duration such as 1 hour, 8 hours, 24 hours, or Not Defined.
field_guidance.Actual Recovery Point Achieved: Enter the actual age of the restored data relative to the failure scenario, using a duration such as 10 minutes, 2 hours, or 1 day.
field_guidance.Actual Restore Duration: Enter the elapsed time to complete the restore test, using a duration such as 00:45, 2h 15m, or 1 business day.
field_guidance.Restore Test Result: Enter one allowed value: Passed, Passed with Issues, Failed, Not Performed, Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Restored Data Validation Performed: Enter Yes or No to confirm whether restored data was validated for usability, completeness, and readability.
field_guidance.Restored Data Validation Result: Enter one allowed value: Passed, Failed, Partial, Not Performed, Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Issues Identified During Restore Test: Describe any restore failure, missing data, corruption, access issue, excessive duration, configuration gap, or dependency issue; enter None if no issues were identified.
field_guidance.Lessons Learned / Improvement Actions: Record any improvement actions arising from the backup or restore test, such as procedure updates, scheduling changes, capacity changes, or monitoring enhancements; enter None if not applicable.
field_guidance.Evidence Reference / Link: Enter the location or reference for supporting evidence, such as backup job report, monitoring alert, ticket number, restore test screenshot, checksum report, or audit evidence repository link.
field_guidance.Reviewed By: Enter the name and role of the person who reviewed the backup record or restore test result.
field_guidance.Review Date: Enter the date of review in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Review Outcome: Enter one allowed value: Accepted, Accepted with Actions, Rejected, Further Investigation Required.
field_guidance.Comments: Enter any additional relevant notes that support the backup record or restore test result; enter None if not applicable.

example_rows: [EXAMPLE: Full production database including transaction and configuration tables]
[EXAMPLE: AES-256 using KMS key alias backup-prod]
[EXAMPLE: Database restored to test environment and sample records validated]
table.maintenance: The IT Operations Manager or Backup Service Owner owns this template and ensures entries are updated after each scheduled backup, backup exception, and restore test, with formal review at least monthly. Source data should be drawn from the backup platform, monitoring tools, service desk tickets, restore test reports, asset inventory, and approved backup/restore procedures.

ISO27-034.title: Vulnerability Management Records
ISO27-034.content:
## Vulnerability Management Records (XLSX/PDF template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Record ID | Detection Date | Source Type | Source Reference | Scan/Assessment Name | Asset ID | Asset Name | Asset Type | Business Service | Asset Owner | IP Address/Hostname/URL | Environment | Vulnerability ID | Vulnerability Title | Vulnerability Description | CVE/CWE Reference | Affected Product/Component | Affected Version/Configuration | Severity Rating | CVSS Score | CVSS Vector | Exploitability Status | Threat Intelligence Reference | Business Impact | Risk Rating | Priority | Required Remediation Action | Patch/Fix Reference | Compensating Controls | Remediation Owner | Remediation SLA Due Date | Current Status | Status Update Date | Remediation Completion Date | Change/Release Reference | Verification Method | Verification Date | Verified By | Residual Risk | Exception/Deferral Approved | Exception/Deferral Reference | Exception Expiry Date | Closure Date | Closure Evidence Location | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [EXAMPLE: VULN-2025-0001] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-03] | [EXAMPLE: Automated Scan] | [EXAMPLE: Nessus Scan ID 84521] | [EXAMPLE: Monthly Internal Infrastructure Scan] | [EXAMPLE: AST-000123] | [EXAMPLE: FIN-APP-SRV-01] | [EXAMPLE: Server] | [EXAMPLE: Finance Application] | [EXAMPLE: Finance Systems Owner] | [EXAMPLE: 10.10.4.25] | [EXAMPLE: Production] | [EXAMPLE: CVE-2024-12345] | [EXAMPLE: Unsupported OpenSSL Version Detected] | [EXAMPLE: The host is running an outdated OpenSSL package with known security vulnerabilities.] | [EXAMPLE: CVE-2024-12345] | [EXAMPLE: OpenSSL] | [EXAMPLE: 1.1.1x] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: 8.1] | [EXAMPLE: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:L] | [EXAMPLE: Public Exploit Available] | [EXAMPLE: Vendor advisory VA-2025-014] | [EXAMPLE: Potential compromise of encrypted communications and service disruption.] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: P2] | [EXAMPLE: Upgrade OpenSSL to the vendor-supported fixed version.] | [EXAMPLE: Vendor patch openssl-1.1.1z-4] | [EXAMPLE: Restricted inbound access to approved management subnet until patching completes.] | [EXAMPLE: Infrastructure Operations Team] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-17] | [EXAMPLE: In Remediation] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-02-10] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: CHG-2025-00294] | [EXAMPLE: Rescan] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: Not Assessed] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: Awaiting approved maintenance window.] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this vulnerability record, using a consistent format such as VULN-YYYY-NNNN. |
| Detection Date | Enter the date the vulnerability was first identified, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Source Type | Enter the source of identification; allowed values: Automated Scan, Penetration Test, Threat Intelligence, Vendor Advisory, Internal Review, External Report, Other. |
| Source Reference | Enter the report ID, ticket number, advisory reference, scanner finding ID, or URL that evidences the detection. |
| Scan/Assessment Name | Enter the name of the vulnerability scan, assessment, test, or review that produced the finding. |
| Asset ID | Enter the unique asset identifier from the asset inventory or CMDB. |
| Asset Name | Enter the system, server, application, endpoint, network device, cloud resource, or database name. |
| Asset Type | Enter the type of asset affected; allowed values: Server, Endpoint, Network Device, Application, Database, Cloud Resource, Container, SaaS, Other. |
| Business Service | Enter the business process, application service, or operational service supported by the affected asset. |
| Asset Owner | Enter the named individual or role accountable for the affected asset. |
| IP Address/Hostname/URL | Enter the relevant IP address, fully qualified domain name, hostname, or URL where the vulnerability was detected. |
| Environment | Enter the environment affected; allowed values: Production, Pre-Production, Test, Development, Disaster Recovery, Corporate, Cloud, Other. |
| Vulnerability ID | Enter the scanner plugin ID, advisory ID, CVE ID, internal finding ID, or other unique vulnerability identifier. |
| Vulnerability Title | Enter a concise title of the vulnerability as reported by the source system or assessor. |
| Vulnerability Description | Enter a clear description of the vulnerability, including the weakness, exposure, or misconfiguration identified. |
| CVE/CWE Reference | Enter applicable CVE or CWE identifiers, or enter Not Applicable if none exists. |
| Affected Product/Component | Enter the software, hardware, operating system, library, package, protocol, service, or configuration item affected. |
| Affected Version/Configuration | Enter the affected version number, build, package release, firmware version, or insecure configuration setting. |
| Severity Rating | Enter the severity assigned by the organisation or approved vulnerability management process; allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational. |
| CVSS Score | Enter the CVSS base score as a number from 0.0 to 10.0, where available; otherwise enter Not Available. |
| CVSS Vector | Enter the full CVSS vector string, where available; otherwise enter Not Available. |
| Exploitability Status | Enter the known exploit status; allowed values: Known Exploited, Public Exploit Available, Proof of Concept Available, No Known Exploit, Unknown. |
| Threat Intelligence Reference | Enter the source of exploit or threat intelligence used to support prioritisation, such as CISA KEV, vendor advisory, ISAC alert, scanner intelligence feed, or enter Not Applicable. |
| Business Impact | Enter the expected business impact if exploited, such as data disclosure, service disruption, privilege escalation, malware infection, regulatory impact, or operational impact. |
| Risk Rating | Enter the risk rating after considering severity, exploitability, exposure, and business criticality; allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low. |
| Priority | Enter the remediation priority; allowed values: P1, P2, P3, P4, where P1 is highest priority. |
| Required Remediation Action | Enter the required action, such as apply patch, upgrade version, change configuration, disable service, remove software, restrict access, or implement compensating control. |
| Patch/Fix Reference | Enter the patch ID, vendor bulletin, package version, configuration standard, knowledge base article, or fix release reference to be applied. |
| Compensating Controls | Enter any temporary or permanent compensating controls used to reduce risk, such as WAF rule, firewall restriction, EDR monitoring, network segmentation, or enter None. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the named individual, team, or supplier responsible for remediation. |
| Remediation SLA Due Date | Enter the required remediation deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on the organisation’s approved vulnerability remediation SLA. |
| Current Status | Enter the current lifecycle status; allowed values: New, Triaged, Assigned, In Remediation, Awaiting Change, Deferred, Risk Accepted, Remediated, Verified Closed, False Positive. |
| Status Update Date | Enter the date this record was last updated, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Remediation Completion Date | Enter the date remediation was completed, in YYYY-MM-DD format, or leave blank until completed. |
| Change/Release Reference | Enter the approved change ticket, release record, deployment ID, or patch management reference used to implement the fix. |
| Verification Method | Enter how remediation was validated; allowed values: Rescan, Manual Test, Configuration Review, Patch Inventory Check, Supplier Attestation, Other. |
| Verification Date | Enter the date remediation was verified, in YYYY-MM-DD format, or leave blank until verified. |
| Verified By | Enter the name or role of the person, team, or tool that verified remediation. |
| Residual Risk | Enter the remaining risk after remediation or compensating controls; allowed values: None, Low, Medium, High, Critical, Not Assessed. |
| Exception/Deferral Approved | Enter whether remediation has been formally deferred or risk accepted; allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Exception/Deferral Reference | Enter the approved exception, risk acceptance, or deferral record reference; enter Not Applicable if no exception exists. |
| Exception Expiry Date | Enter the expiry or review date for an approved exception in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Applicable if no exception exists. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the record was formally closed, in YYYY-MM-DD format, or leave blank until closed. |
| Closure Evidence Location | Enter the file path, ticket link, GRC record, scanner report link, screenshot repository, or evidence reference demonstrating closure. |
| Notes | Enter any additional audit-relevant context, decisions, dependencies, or constraints; do not use this field as a substitute for required fields. |

### Maintenance

The Vulnerability Manager or Security Operations Manager owns this template and ensures records are updated at each triage, remediation, verification, exception, and closure event, with formal review at least weekly for open Critical/High items and monthly for all open items. Source data should be drawn from approved vulnerability scanners, penetration test reports, vendor advisories, threat intelligence feeds, patch management tools, CMDB/asset inventory, ITSM/change records, and GRC risk acceptance records.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Incident ID | Enter the unique incident reference assigned by the organisation, using the defined format such as INC-YYYY-0001. |
| Linked Event ID(s) | Enter any related security event, alert, SIEM, EDR, helpdesk, or monitoring IDs; use comma-separated values if more than one, or 'N/A'. |
| Date/Time Detected | Enter the date and time the event or incident was first detected in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, including timezone if used. |
| Date/Time Reported | Enter the date and time the event or incident was reported to the security/incident response function in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM. |
| Reported By | Enter the name, role, team, supplier, customer, or automated system that reported the event or incident. |
| Reporting Channel | Enter the channel used to report the incident, such as SIEM Alert, EDR Alert, Helpdesk Ticket, Email, Phone, User Report, Supplier Notification, Customer Notification, or Other. |
| Incident Title | Enter a short descriptive title that clearly identifies the incident, such as 'Phishing email with credential harvesting link'. |
| Event/Incident Description | Enter a factual summary of what happened, including observed indicators, timeline known so far, and how the issue was identified. |
| Affected Information Asset(s) | Enter the information asset name or asset register ID affected, such as database, document repository, endpoint asset ID, application, or data set. |
| Affected System(s)/Service(s) | Enter the system, application, infrastructure component, cloud service, network segment, or business service affected. |
| Affected Business Process | Enter the business process impacted, such as payroll, customer onboarding, order fulfilment, finance reporting, or 'N/A'. |
| Location/Environment | Enter the physical or logical environment affected, such as Production, Test, Development, Corporate Network, Cloud, Data Centre, Remote User, or Office Location. |
| Incident Category | Select the best-fit category: Malware, Phishing, Unauthorized Access, Data Loss/Leakage, Denial of Service, Vulnerability Exploitation, Misconfiguration, Insider Threat, Physical Security, Third-Party Incident, Policy Violation, or Other. |
| Suspected Root Cause | Enter the suspected cause at the time of assessment, such as compromised credentials, unpatched vulnerability, user error, malicious email, misconfiguration, supplier failure, unknown, or 'To be determined'. |
| Threat Actor Type | Enter the suspected actor type: External, Internal, Third Party/Supplier, Automated/Bot, Nation State, Criminal, Hacktivist, Unknown, or N/A. |
| Confidentiality Impact | Enter the assessed impact to confidentiality: None, Low, Medium, High, or Unknown. |
| Integrity Impact | Enter the assessed impact to integrity: None, Low, Medium, High, or Unknown. |
| Availability Impact | Enter the assessed impact to availability: None, Low, Medium, High, or Unknown. |
| Personal Data Involved | Enter Yes, No, or Unknown; if Yes, include type of personal data and approximate number of data subjects in the description or communication fields. |
| Sensitive/Regulated Data Involved | Enter Yes, No, or Unknown; if Yes, specify the data type such as financial, health, payment card, credentials, confidential business data, export-controlled, or regulated records. |
| Initial Severity | Enter the initial severity rating using the organisation's incident classification scheme, such as Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Informational. |

It is updated in real time during incident handling and reviewed at least monthly, drawing from the incident management platform, SIEM/SOAR, EDR, service desk, evidence repository, and post-incident review records.

ISO27-036.title: Supplier Due Diligence File
ISO27-036.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [GRC-EVD-SUP-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [Procurement / Vendor Risk Owner] |
| Effective Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Framework | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |
| Classification | Confidential |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Supplier Due Diligence File is to provide auditable evidence that [Organisation Name] has assessed, approved, and documented information security risks associated with each supplier relationship in accordance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.5.19.

This evidence file demonstrates that supplier-related information security requirements are identified and addressed before engagement, during onboarding, and throughout the supplier lifecycle, based on the supplier’s access to information assets, systems, facilities, services, or business processes.

This document is intended to be maintained as a per-supplier evidence record and used to support internal governance, supplier risk management, management review, internal audit, external certification audit, and regulatory or customer assurance activities.

## What This Evidence Demonstrates

This evidence demonstrates that [Organisation Name] has performed appropriate supplier information security due diligence before entering into or materially changing a supplier relationship.

For each supplier, the evidence file demonstrates that:

| Evidence Objective | Demonstrated By | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| The supplier relationship has been identified and recorded | Supplier profile, business owner, service description, contract reference, onboarding date | Confirms the organisation understands the supplier relationship and its context |
| Information security risks associated with the supplier have been assessed | Supplier risk assessment, inherent risk rating, data classification, access profile, criticality assessment | Supports identification and treatment of supplier-related risks |
| Information security requirements have been defined for the supplier | Contractual clauses, security schedules, data protection terms, service-level requirements | Supports establishment of security requirements in supplier relationships |
| Due diligence has been performed proportionate to supplier risk | Security questionnaire, certifications, audit reports, penetration test summaries, policies, compliance attestations | Demonstrates risk-based validation of supplier security posture |
| Supplier access to information and systems has been reviewed | Access scope, privileged access status, connectivity details, authentication requirements | Supports protection of organisational assets accessible to suppliers |
| Legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations have been considered | Data processing agreement, confidentiality terms, regulatory applicability assessment | Demonstrates supplier obligations are aligned with organisational requirements |
| Risks, exceptions, and remediation actions have been recorded | Risk treatment plan, exceptions register, compensating controls, remediation due dates | Demonstrates governance and control over supplier-related security gaps |
| Supplier approval was formally obtained | Approval record from business owner, information security, legal, procurement, and privacy where applicable | Confirms accountable decision-making before supplier engagement |
| Ongoing monitoring requirements have been defined | Review frequency, assurance refresh cycle, performance/security monitoring criteria | Supports continued management of supplier security risks |
| Evidence is retained and access-controlled | Evidence repository record, retention period, access permissions | Supports integrity, confidentiality, and auditability of due diligence records |

This evidence supports the conclusion that supplier relationships are subject to appropriate information security governance and that risks arising from supplier access to [Organisation Name] information assets are managed through defined requirements, assessment, approval, and monitoring.

## Scope

This Supplier Due Diligence File applies to each external supplier, vendor, service provider, contractor organisation, outsourcing provider, professional services provider, cloud service provider, managed service provider, software-as-a-service provider, data processor, hosting provider, facilities provider, or other third party that may:

- Access, process, store, transmit, or manage [Organisation Name] information;
- Access [Organisation Name] information systems, networks, applications, premises, or operational environments;
- Provide technology, infrastructure, security, business process, or operational services;
- Support critical or important business activities;
- Process personal data, confidential information, regulated information, intellectual property, authentication credentials, logs, telemetry, or customer information;
- Have privileged, remote, administrative, integration, or API-based access;
- Provide services that affect the confidentiality, integrity, availability, privacy, or resilience of [Organisation Name] information or services.

This evidence file shall be completed for each supplier where information security risk exists. The level of due diligence shall be proportionate to the supplier risk classification.

### Supplier Risk Classification

| Risk Tier | Typical Supplier Characteristics | Minimum Due Diligence Expected | Review Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | Supports critical business service; stores or processes highly confidential or regulated data; has privileged or persistent access; provides core infrastructure, cloud, managed security, identity, or production services | Full security questionnaire, independent assurance report where available, contractual security schedule, data protection review, business continuity review, risk approval, executive or delegated risk owner approval | At least annually |
| High | Processes confidential or personal data; integrates with internal systems; supports important business process; has remote or API access | Security questionnaire, evidence of security controls, contractual security requirements, privacy/legal review where applicable, risk owner approval | At least annually or every 18 months |
