This report is intended for internal use by authorised personnel only. Distribution should be limited to stakeholders with a legitimate governance, risk management, compliance, technology, audit, legal, procurement, or operational resilience role.

Approved distribution list:

| Recipient / Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Board Risk Committee | Oversight and challenge |
| Executive Committee | Sponsorship and prioritisation |
| Chief Executive Officer | Accountability and strategic oversight |
| Chief Risk Officer | Risk governance and remediation oversight |
| Chief Information Security Officer | ICT and security remediation ownership |
| Chief Information Officer / Chief Technology Officer | Technology control implementation |
| Chief Operating Officer | Operational resilience alignment |
| Compliance | Regulatory readiness and reporting |
| Legal | Contract remediation and notification obligations |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | ICT third-party risk remediation |
| Internal Audit | Assurance planning |
| Business Service Owners | Dependency mapping and resilience validation |
| Programme Management Office | Remediation tracking |

External distribution, including to regulators, auditors, consultants, service providers, or legal advisers, requires approval from [Authorised Role] and should be managed in accordance with confidentiality, legal privilege, contractual, and regulatory considerations.

### Confidentiality

This report is classified as Internal Confidential. It contains sensitive information about ICT risks, control gaps, operational resilience capabilities, third-party dependencies, and potential remediation priorities.

Handling requirements:

- Store only in approved secure repositories.
- Do not forward outside approved distribution without written authorisation.
- Do not upload to unauthorised collaboration platforms or public AI tools.
- Redact sensitive technical, supplier, incident, and security details before broader circulation.
- Apply need-to-know access.
- Retain in accordance with [Organisation Name] records management requirements.
- Report unauthorised disclosure immediately to [Information Security / Legal / Compliance Contact].

### Version and Approval Record

| Version | Date | Author | Reviewer | Approver | Summary of Changes |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | [Date] | [Author] | [Reviewer] | [Approver] | Initial draft |
| 1.0 | [Date] | [Author] | [Reviewer] | [Approver] | Approved version |

### Next Review

This report should be reviewed and updated:

- After completion of Phase 1 mobilisation activities.
- Following material remediation milestones.
- After any major ICT incident or significant third-party disruption.
- Following major changes to critical services, systems, providers, or operating model.
- At least annually as part of the digital operational resilience assurance cycle.

DORA-005.title: ICT Risk Mgmt Framework Document
DORA-005.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | Chief Information Security Officer | [Effective Date] | Digital Operational Resilience | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes the organisation’s mandatory requirements for maintaining a sound, comprehensive and well-documented Information and Communication Technology Risk Management Framework ("ICT RMF").

The ICT RMF provides the governance, processes, roles, controls, records and reporting needed to identify, assess, manage, monitor and remediate ICT risks that may affect the confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, continuity or resilience of the organisation’s services, information assets and supporting technology.

The purpose of this Policy is to ensure that ICT risk management is embedded into business decision-making, technology lifecycle management, third-party oversight, operational resilience, incident management, change delivery and executive governance.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All business units, functions, subsidiaries, branches and locations operated by the organisation.
- All employees, contractors, temporary staff, consultants, interns and other personnel who access, manage, operate or support the organisation’s information or ICT assets.
- All ICT assets, including applications, infrastructure, cloud services, networks, end-user devices, data repositories, security tools, operational technology where applicable, and supporting platforms.
- All information assets processed, stored, transmitted or managed by the organisation, regardless of format or location.
- ICT services provided by third parties, including cloud service providers, managed service providers, software vendors, data processors, outsourcing partners and other technology service providers.
- All phases of the ICT lifecycle, including strategy, architecture, procurement, design, development, testing, deployment, operation, monitoring, maintenance, change, decommissioning and disposal.
- ICT risks arising from cyber threats, technology failures, data loss, unauthorised access, operational disruption, inadequate resilience, supplier failure, human error, misconfiguration, poor change control, legacy technology, concentration risk and other relevant sources.

This Policy does not replace detailed procedures, standards, technical baselines or operational playbooks. Those documents must align with this Policy and provide the implementation detail needed to meet its requirements.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall establish, maintain and operate an ICT Risk Management Framework that is approved by senior management and appropriate to the organisation’s size, complexity, risk profile, services, operating model and reliance on ICT.

2. The ICT RMF shall be documented, communicated, implemented and kept current so that stakeholders understand their responsibilities for managing ICT risk.

3. The ICT RMF shall cover the full ICT risk lifecycle, including risk identification, analysis, evaluation, treatment, acceptance, monitoring, reporting and review.

4. The organisation shall define and maintain an ICT risk appetite that sets clear expectations for acceptable levels of ICT risk, including resilience, security, availability, data protection, third-party dependency and recovery objectives.

5. ICT risk appetite statements shall be approved by senior management and reviewed at least annually, and whenever material changes occur to the organisation, its technology environment, threat landscape or regulatory obligations.

6. The organisation shall maintain a documented inventory of ICT assets, information assets and supporting dependencies that is accurate enough to support risk assessment, incident response, continuity planning, vulnerability management, access control and third-party oversight.

7. The ICT asset inventory shall identify asset ownership, business criticality, data classification, location, technology owner, service dependency, supplier dependency, lifecycle status and any material resilience requirements.

8. The organisation shall classify ICT-supported business services by criticality, considering customer impact, financial impact, regulatory impact, operational impact, reputational impact and substitutability.

9. The organisation shall maintain documented mappings between critical business services, ICT assets, data, processes, people, locations, third parties and recovery arrangements.

10. The organisation shall perform ICT risk assessments on new, changed and existing ICT assets, services, projects, third-party arrangements and material business processes.

11. ICT risk assessments shall consider threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact, existing controls, control effectiveness, residual risk, risk ownership and required treatment actions.

12. ICT risk assessments shall be performed before production deployment of new or materially changed ICT services, and periodically thereafter based on criticality and risk exposure.

13. The organisation shall maintain a central ICT risk register that records identified ICT risks, ratings, owners, treatment plans, target dates, status, residual risk decisions and evidence of management review.

14. Each ICT risk shall have an accountable business or technology owner with authority and responsibility to manage the risk within approved appetite.

15. ICT risks that exceed approved appetite shall be escalated promptly to the appropriate governance forum and shall have documented remediation or risk acceptance decisions.

16. The organisation shall define a consistent ICT risk assessment methodology that uses agreed impact and likelihood criteria, risk rating scales and escalation thresholds.

17. The ICT risk methodology shall be applied consistently across business units and technology teams to support reliable comparison, prioritisation and reporting.

18. The organisation shall implement and maintain ICT controls that are proportionate to the risk, criticality and sensitivity of the relevant asset, service or process.

19. ICT controls shall address, at a minimum, identity and access management, network security, endpoint security, secure configuration, vulnerability management, logging and monitoring, data protection, encryption, backup, resilience, change management, incident response, physical security where relevant, supplier oversight and secure disposal.

20. The organisation shall establish and maintain policies, standards and procedures that support the ICT RMF and define the minimum control requirements for personnel, processes and technology.

21. The organisation shall ensure that ICT risk management is integrated into strategic planning, budgeting, procurement, architecture, solution design, project delivery, change approval, operational management and supplier management.

22. Material ICT decisions shall include documented risk consideration, including the impact on resilience, security, data protection, service continuity, third-party dependency and operational capacity.

23. The organisation shall ensure that ICT projects and changes are subject to appropriate governance, risk assessment, testing, approval, segregation of duties and post-implementation review.

24. Emergency changes shall be controlled, documented, reviewed after implementation and assessed for residual risk.

25. The organisation shall implement a vulnerability and patch management process that identifies, assesses, prioritises, remediates and tracks vulnerabilities in line with asset criticality and risk exposure.

26. Vulnerabilities affecting critical or internet-facing assets shall be prioritised for remediation according to defined risk-based service levels.

27. The organisation shall maintain secure configuration baselines for relevant technology platforms and shall monitor for unauthorised or insecure configuration changes.

28. The organisation shall implement identity and access management controls that ensure access is authorised, appropriate, reviewed, monitored and removed when no longer required.

29. Privileged access shall be restricted, approved, logged, monitored and reviewed at a frequency appropriate to the risk of the role and system.

30. The organisation shall protect ICT systems and information against unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, loss, destruction and disruption through preventive, detective and corrective controls.

31. The organisation shall maintain logging, monitoring and alerting capabilities that enable timely detection, investigation and response to ICT incidents and anomalous activity.

32. Security and operational logs for critical systems shall be protected against unauthorised alteration and retained for a period that supports investigation, compliance and business needs.

33. The organisation shall establish and maintain an ICT incident management process that enables timely identification, classification, escalation, containment, eradication, recovery, communication and lessons learned.

34. ICT incidents shall be assessed for business impact, service disruption, data impact, customer impact, regulatory implications and need for escalation.

35. The organisation shall maintain business continuity, disaster recovery and ICT continuity arrangements for critical services and supporting technology.

36. Recovery arrangements shall be aligned to approved business impact analysis results, recovery time objectives, recovery point objectives and maximum tolerable disruption thresholds.

37. Backups and recovery capabilities shall be tested periodically to confirm they are usable, protected and sufficient to support recovery requirements.

38. The organisation shall conduct resilience testing appropriate to the criticality and risk profile of ICT services, including technical recovery testing, scenario testing, failover testing, tabletop exercises and lessons learned reviews.

39. Testing results shall be documented, reported and tracked to closure where weaknesses are identified.

40. The organisation shall manage ICT third-party risk through due diligence, contractual safeguards, ongoing monitoring, performance management, security requirements, resilience expectations and exit planning.

41. ICT third-party arrangements supporting critical or important functions shall be subject to enhanced risk assessment and oversight.

42. Contracts for material ICT services shall include appropriate requirements for security, resilience, incident notification, access to information, audit cooperation, data protection, subcontracting, service levels, business continuity and termination assistance.

43. The organisation shall identify and manage ICT concentration risk arising from reliance on a limited number of providers, technologies, locations, platforms or critical skills.

44. The organisation shall maintain exit and transition plans for material ICT third-party services where service disruption or provider failure could materially affect operations.

45. The organisation shall ensure that data processed by ICT systems is protected according to its sensitivity, business value and legal requirements.

46. The organisation shall maintain processes for data retention, secure deletion, encryption, backup, restoration, transfer protection and access restriction.

47. The organisation shall ensure that ICT personnel and relevant business users receive appropriate training and awareness on ICT risk responsibilities, cyber hygiene, incident reporting, data protection, secure use of technology and resilience obligations.

48. Personnel with privileged or specialist ICT responsibilities shall receive role-specific training appropriate to their access, duties and risk exposure.

49. The organisation shall establish governance forums to oversee ICT risk, review material issues, approve risk decisions, monitor remediation and escalate concerns to senior management.

50. ICT risk reporting shall be provided to management on a periodic basis and shall include risk posture, key risk indicators, material incidents, control weaknesses, overdue remediation, risk acceptances, resilience testing results, third-party risk, audit findings and emerging threats.

51. The organisation shall maintain key risk indicators and key control indicators that provide timely insight into ICT risk exposure and control effectiveness.

52. ICT risk metrics shall be reviewed periodically for relevance, accuracy and usefulness in supporting management decisions.

53. The organisation shall maintain records sufficient to demonstrate the design, operation and effectiveness of the ICT RMF.

54. Records shall be accurate, protected, retained and retrievable for management review, audit, regulatory request, incident investigation and lessons learned activity.

55. The organisation shall require ICT risk remediation actions to be assigned to accountable owners, tracked to completion and verified where appropriate.

56. Overdue or repeatedly deferred ICT risk actions shall be escalated according to their severity and business impact.

57. Risk acceptance shall be permitted only where the residual risk is understood, documented, time-bound where appropriate and approved by an authorised decision-maker.

58. Risks outside approved appetite shall not be accepted without senior management approval and a documented rationale.

59. The organisation shall ensure that independent assurance activities periodically evaluate the effectiveness of the ICT RMF, including governance, controls, documentation, implementation and reporting.

60. Findings from audit, assurance, incident reviews, testing, regulatory feedback and control assessments shall be tracked, prioritised and remediated according to risk.

61. The ICT RMF shall be reviewed and updated following material ICT incidents, significant organisational change, major technology change, material third-party changes, changes in threat environment, audit findings or changes in legal or regulatory expectations.

62. The organisation shall maintain alignment between the ICT RMF and related governance documents, including information security policies, business continuity plans, incident response plans, outsourcing policies, data protection policies, change management procedures and enterprise risk management processes.

63. The organisation shall ensure that ICT risk management responsibilities are clearly allocated and that no critical ICT risk management activity is left without accountable ownership.

64. The organisation shall apply segregation of duties where necessary to prevent conflicts of interest in ICT risk assessment, control implementation, approval, testing and assurance.

65. The organisation shall ensure that the ICT RMF supports timely decision-making during normal operations, incidents, crises, technology changes and supplier disruptions.

66. The organisation shall ensure that ICT risk management activities are proportionate, repeatable, evidence-based and capable of being demonstrated to internal and external stakeholders.

The following minimum ICT risk management activities shall be performed:

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Owner | Required Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| ICT risk appetite review | At least annually | Chief Risk Officer and Chief Information Security Officer | Approved risk appetite statement and meeting record |
| ICT asset inventory validation | At least quarterly for critical assets; at least annually for all assets | Chief Information Officer | Updated asset inventory and reconciliation record |
| Critical service and dependency mapping review | At least annually and after material change | Business Service Owners | Updated service maps and dependency records |
| ICT risk assessment for critical services | At least annually and before material change | Risk Owner | Completed risk assessment and risk register update |
| ICT risk register review | At least monthly for high risks; at least quarterly for all open risks | ICT Risk Manager | Risk register extract and governance minutes |
| Vulnerability review for critical assets | At least monthly or more frequently based on exposure | Security Operations Lead | Vulnerability dashboard and remediation status |
| Privileged access review | At least quarterly | System Owner | Access review sign-off and remediation evidence |
| Backup restoration test for critical systems | At least annually, or more frequently where required by business impact | Infrastructure Owner | Test results and issue log |
| ICT continuity and recovery testing | At least annually for critical services | Business Continuity Manager | Test plan, results and improvement actions |
| Material ICT third-party risk review | At least annually and before renewal | Third-Party Risk Manager | Due diligence record and risk assessment |
| ICT incident lessons learned review | After major incidents | Incident Manager | Post-incident report and action tracker |
| ICT RMF effectiveness review | At least annually | Chief Information Security Officer | Review report and improvement plan |

## Roles & Responsibilities

The organisation shall assign and maintain the following responsibilities for the ICT RMF.

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board or Governing Body | Approves the overall approach to ICT risk oversight; ensures ICT risk is considered in business strategy; challenges management on resilience and risk exposure; receives reporting on material ICT risks and incidents. |
| Executive Management | Ensures the ICT RMF is implemented, resourced and embedded across the organisation; approves material risk decisions within authority; ensures remediation of significant ICT control weaknesses. |
| Chief Information Security Officer | Owns this Policy; leads the design and maintenance of the ICT RMF; defines security control expectations; oversees cyber risk management, security monitoring, vulnerability management and security incident response. |
| Chief Information Officer | Ensures ICT services, infrastructure, applications and operations are managed in line with this Policy; ensures asset inventories, lifecycle controls, change management and technical resilience arrangements are maintained. |
| Chief Risk Officer | Ensures ICT risk is integrated into the enterprise risk management approach; maintains risk appetite governance; provides independent challenge on material ICT risks and risk acceptance decisions. |
| Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead | Advises on ICT risks affecting personal data; supports assessment of data protection implications; ensures privacy obligations are considered in ICT risk management activities. |
| Business Service Owners | Define criticality, impact tolerances and recovery requirements for services; identify business impacts of ICT disruption; own risks affecting business service delivery. |
| System Owners | Maintain risk and control accountability for assigned systems; ensure access, configuration, patching, monitoring, backup and lifecycle activities are performed; support audits and risk assessments. |
| ICT Risk Manager | Maintains the ICT risk register; coordinates ICT risk assessments; tracks remediation actions; prepares risk reporting; supports governance forums. |
| Security Operations Team | Monitors threats, alerts and security events; supports vulnerability management, incident detection, incident response and security reporting. |
| Infrastructure and Operations Teams | Operate and maintain ICT infrastructure; implement technical controls; manage backup, recovery, availability, capacity, patching and operational resilience. |
| Application Owners and Development Teams | Ensure applications are developed, configured, tested, changed and maintained securely; remediate application risks and vulnerabilities; maintain application documentation. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Coordinates business impact analysis, continuity planning, recovery testing and resilience exercises with business and ICT stakeholders. |
| Third-Party Risk Manager | Coordinates risk assessment, due diligence, contract control requirements and ongoing monitoring of ICT third-party providers. |
| Procurement and Legal Teams | Ensure ICT contracts include appropriate security, resilience, audit, notification, data protection, subcontracting, exit and service continuity provisions. |
| Internal Audit or Independent Assurance Function | Provides independent assessment of the ICT RMF, control effectiveness, governance and compliance with internal requirements. |
| Employees, Contractors and Users | Follow ICT policies and standards; protect information and systems; report incidents, weaknesses and suspicious activity; complete required training. |

The following RACI model applies to core ICT RMF activities:

| Activity | Board / Governing Body | Executive Management | CISO | CIO | CRO | Business Owners | System Owners | Internal Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Approve ICT risk appetite | A | R | C | C | R | C | I | I |
| Maintain ICT RMF documentation | I | A | R | C | C | C | C | I |
| Maintain ICT asset inventory | I | A | C | R | I | C | R | I |
| Conduct ICT risk assessments | I | A | R | R | C | R | R | I |
| Maintain ICT risk register | I | A | R | C | C | C | C | I |
| Approve material risk acceptance | I | A | C | C | R | R | C | I |
| Oversee ICT incident response | I | A | R | R | C | C | C | I |
| Conduct resilience testing | I | A | C | R | C | R | R | I |
| Monitor ICT third-party risk | I | A | C | C | C | R | C | I |
| Provide independent assurance | I | I | C | C | C | I | I | R |

Legend: R = Responsible, A = Accountable, C = Consulted, I = Informed.

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through governance reporting, control testing, risk reviews, assurance activities, audits, incident analysis, third-party reviews, vulnerability reporting and management oversight.

The following compliance and monitoring activities shall be maintained:

| Monitoring Area | Method | Frequency | Responsible Function | Escalation Trigger |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| ICT risk register completeness | Review of open risks, ownership, ratings and treatment plans | Monthly | ICT Risk Management | Unowned risks, missing treatment plans or overdue high-risk actions |
| Risk appetite adherence | Comparison of current risk exposure against approved appetite | Quarterly | Risk Management | Any material breach or sustained adverse trend |
| Critical asset control coverage | Review of required controls for critical systems | Quarterly | Information Security and ICT Operations | Missing key controls or unsupported assets |
| Vulnerability remediation | Dashboard review of open vulnerabilities and ageing | Monthly | Security Operations | Overdue critical or high-risk vulnerabilities |
| Access control compliance | Review of privileged access, leavers and excessive permissions | Quarterly | System Owners and Identity Management | Unauthorised privileged access or failed recertification |
| Incident management performance | Review of incident handling, escalation, recovery and lessons learned | Quarterly | Information Security | Major incident, delayed escalation or repeat root cause |
| Resilience and recovery readiness | Review of testing results, backup success and recovery gaps | Semi-annually | Business Continuity and ICT Operations | Failed recovery test or unmet recovery objective |
| Third-party ICT risk | Review of material providers, issues and service performance | Quarterly | Third-Party Risk Management | Provider control weakness, service failure or unresolved audit issue |
| Policy compliance | Control self-assessment and assurance review | Annually | Compliance, Risk or Assurance | Material non-compliance or repeat exceptions |
| Training completion | Review of mandatory ICT risk and security training completion | Quarterly | Human Resources and Information Security | Missed training deadlines by high-risk user groups |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in one or more of the following actions:

- Formal escalation to the relevant manager, risk owner, executive sponsor or governance forum.
- Requirement to develop and complete a remediation plan.
- Restriction, suspension or removal of system access.
- Delay or rejection of technology changes, projects, procurements or go-live approvals.
- Increased monitoring, assurance review or independent assessment.
- Contractual remedies or supplier management action for third-party non-compliance.
- Disciplinary action in line with the organisation’s HR policies.
- Notification to legal, compliance, regulators, customers or other stakeholders where required.

Managers shall ensure that personnel under their supervision comply with this Policy and complete assigned remediation actions within agreed timelines.

Control failures, material weaknesses, significant risks and repeated non-compliance shall be reported to senior management and tracked until resolved or formally accepted.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy are permitted only where there is a documented business need and the associated ICT risk is understood, assessed and approved by an authorised decision-maker.

All exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception title | Clear summary of the requested deviation |
| Requestor | Name, role and business unit of the person requesting the exception |
| Affected asset, service or process | Systems, data, suppliers, users or processes impacted |
| Policy requirement affected | Description of the requirement that cannot be met |
| Business justification | Reason the exception is necessary |
| Risk assessment | Likelihood, impact, affected controls and residual risk |
| Compensating controls | Alternative measures to reduce risk |
| Duration | Requested start date and end date |
| Remediation plan | Actions required to return to compliance |
| Approval authority | Role required to approve the exception |
| Review frequency | How often the exception will be reassessed |
| Evidence | Supporting documents, diagrams, risk assessments or approvals |

Exceptions shall be:

- Recorded in an exception register.
- Risk assessed before approval.
- Time-bound unless explicitly approved as a long-term risk acceptance.
- Subject to compensating controls where practical.
- Reviewed before expiry.
- Escalated where the residual risk exceeds approved appetite.
- Closed when the organisation returns to compliance or the affected asset, service or process is retired.

The following approval thresholds shall apply unless a stricter internal authority matrix is defined:

| Exception Risk Level | Minimum Approval Authority | Maximum Initial Duration |
|---|---|---:|
| Low | System Owner and ICT Risk Manager | 12 months |
| Medium | Business Owner and Chief Information Security Officer | 6 months |
| High | Relevant Executive and Chief Risk Officer | 3 months |
| Critical or outside risk appetite | Executive Management or Board-delegated forum | As specifically approved |

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless formally renewed before expiry.

Permanent exceptions are not permitted where they would leave the organisation operating outside approved ICT risk appetite without explicit senior management approval and documented ongoing monitoring.

## Review & Maintenance

The Chief Information Security Officer owns this Policy and is responsible for ensuring it remains accurate, current and aligned with the organisation’s ICT risk profile, operating model and resilience objectives.

This Policy shall be reviewed:

- At least annually.
- Following a material ICT incident or near miss.
- Following a significant change to the organisation’s technology environment, business model, critical services or outsourcing arrangements.
- Following a material change in the threat landscape.
- Following significant audit findings, assurance findings or control failures.
- Following relevant legal, regulatory or supervisory developments.
- When risk appetite, governance structures or organisational responsibilities materially change.

The Policy review shall consider:

| Review Area | Review Consideration |
|---|---|
| Scope | Whether all relevant entities, assets, services, users and third parties remain covered |
| Governance | Whether roles, responsibilities and reporting lines remain accurate |
| Risk appetite | Whether ICT risk appetite remains suitable and measurable |
| Control requirements | Whether mandatory requirements remain appropriate to current risks |
| Operational effectiveness | Whether the ICT RMF is operating as intended |
| Incident and testing lessons | Whether lessons learned require Policy updates |
| Third-party dependency | Whether material supplier or concentration risks require stronger requirements |
| Assurance findings | Whether audit or control assessment results indicate gaps |
| Metrics and reporting | Whether indicators support timely management decisions |
| Documentation alignment | Whether related standards, procedures and plans remain consistent |

Material changes to this Policy shall be approved by [Approving Authority]. Minor administrative changes, such as formatting, role title updates or clarification that does not alter policy intent, may be approved by the Policy Owner.

The current approved version of this Policy shall be stored in [Document Repository]. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.

Related documents shall be reviewed for alignment whenever this Policy is materially updated, including:

- Information Security Policy.
- Enterprise Risk Management Policy.
- ICT Incident Management Procedure.
- Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy.
- ICT Change Management Procedure.
- Access Control Standard.
- Vulnerability and Patch Management Standard.
- Secure Configuration Standard.
- Third-Party Risk Management Policy.
- Data Protection and Privacy Policy.
- Logging and Monitoring Standard.
- Backup and Recovery Standard.
- ICT Asset Management Standard.

DORA-006.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |

| [Document ID] | 1.0 | Chief Information Security Officer | [Effective Date] | Digital Operational Resilience Act | Confidential - Internal Use |

# Annual ICT RMF Review Report

## Purpose

This report documents the annual review of the organisation’s ICT Risk Management Framework (ICT RMF) and provides a consolidated assessment of its design, implementation, effectiveness, maturity and improvement priorities.

The report is intended to support senior management oversight, evidence regulatory accountability and provide a structured record that can be submitted to the competent authority on request. It may also be used following a major ICT-related incident, material business change, significant outsourcing event or major control failure where an extraordinary review of the ICT RMF is required.

The report evaluates whether the ICT RMF remains appropriate for the organisation’s business model, ICT risk profile, operational resilience objectives, threat environment, dependency on third-party service providers and tolerance for disruption.

This report specifically addresses:

- Governance and accountability for ICT risk management.
- Identification, classification and documentation of ICT-supported business functions, information assets and dependencies.
- Protection, detection, response and recovery capabilities.
- Management of ICT-related incidents and cyber threats.
- ICT business continuity, disaster recovery and operational resilience testing.
- ICT third-party risk management and oversight.
- Security awareness, training and ICT risk culture.
- Issues, exceptions, remediation activities and management actions.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Review period | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Review type | Annual ICT RMF review |
| Report preparation date | [Report Date] |
| Review owner | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Executive accountable body | Management Body / Board |
| Primary contributors | Risk Management, Information Security, ICT Operations, Business Continuity, Procurement, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, Data Protection, Business Owners |
| Trigger for review | Scheduled annual review |
| Extraordinary review trigger, if applicable | [Major Incident / Material Change / Not Applicable] |

### Organisational Scope

This review covers the ICT risk management arrangements supporting the organisation’s regulated financial services activities, critical or important functions and material business operations.

Included in scope:

- ICT governance, policies, standards and operating procedures.
- ICT risk identification, assessment, treatment and reporting.
- ICT asset inventory and information classification practices.
- Identity and access management controls.
- Network, endpoint, application, cloud and data protection controls.
- Security monitoring, logging, vulnerability management and threat detection.
- ICT incident detection, escalation, classification, response and reporting.
- Backup, restoration, disaster recovery and ICT continuity arrangements.
- Testing programmes for resilience, recovery and cyber scenarios.
- ICT change management, configuration management and secure development practices.
- ICT third-party service provider governance, including outsourced and cloud services.
- Awareness and training relevant to ICT risk and digital operational resilience.
- Risk acceptance, exceptions and overdue remediation actions.

Excluded from scope:

| Exclusion | Rationale | Compensating Oversight |
|---|---|---|
| [Excluded Entity / System / Process] | [Reason] | [Oversight Mechanism] |

### Systems, Services and Functions Reviewed

| Category | In-Scope Items |
|---|---|
| Critical or important business functions | [Function 1], [Function 2], [Function 3] |
| Core ICT systems | [System 1], [System 2], [System 3] |
| Infrastructure platforms | [Data Centre / Cloud Platform / Network / Endpoint Estate] |
| Security platforms | [SIEM / EDR / IAM / Vulnerability Scanner / DLP / Email Security] |
| Key third-party ICT providers | [Provider 1], [Provider 2], [Provider 3] |
| Business continuity and recovery capabilities | [BCP Platform / Backup Platform / DR Site / Crisis Management Tool] |
| Major projects or changes reviewed | [Project / Migration / Transformation Initiative] |

### Review Criteria

The review assessed whether the ICT RMF:

- Is approved, owned and overseen at an appropriate senior level.
- Is integrated into enterprise risk management and business planning.
- Reflects the organisation’s actual ICT environment and operational dependencies.
- Provides clear responsibilities for managing ICT risk across all lines of defence.
- Enables timely identification, assessment, monitoring and reporting of ICT risk.
- Supports effective prevention, detection, response, recovery and learning.
- Covers ICT third-party and supply chain dependencies.
- Produces reliable management information for decision-making.
- Is tested, improved and updated in response to threats, incidents, control failures and business changes.

## Executive Summary

### Overall Conclusion

The ICT Risk Management Framework is assessed as **[Effective / Partially Effective / Requires Significant Improvement]** for the reporting period.

The framework provides a defined governance structure for ICT risk management and includes core components expected for a regulated financial entity, including ICT risk assessment, asset management, security monitoring, incident response, resilience testing, business continuity and third-party ICT risk oversight.

However, the review identified areas requiring improvement to strengthen operational resilience, improve consistency of evidence, reduce dependency risk and enhance management reporting. The most significant themes are:

- Inconsistent documentation of end-to-end dependencies for critical or important functions.
- Gaps in timely closure of ICT risk remediation actions.
- Variable quality of third-party exit plans and resilience evidence.
- Need for more integrated testing between cyber incident response, crisis management, business continuity and disaster recovery.
- Opportunities to improve risk appetite metrics and board-level reporting.

### Overall Rating

| Review Area | Rating | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| ICT governance and accountability | [Effective / Partially Effective / Ineffective] | Governance forums are established, but reporting can be further aligned to risk appetite and resilience outcomes. |
| ICT risk identification and assessment | [Effective / Partially Effective / Ineffective] | Risk assessment process exists; dependency mapping requires greater consistency. |
| Asset and information management | [Effective / Partially Effective / Ineffective] | Inventories are maintained, though completeness and reconciliation need improvement for some platforms. |

## Methodology

### Review Approach

The annual review was conducted using a risk-based assessment approach. The review combined document examination, stakeholder interviews, evidence sampling, control walkthroughs, management information analysis and assessment of remediation progress.

The review considered both the design of the ICT RMF and evidence of operating effectiveness during the reporting period.

### Review Activities

| Activity | Description | Evidence Reviewed |
|---|---|---|
| Policy and framework review | Assessed whether ICT RMF documentation remains current, approved and aligned to business operations. | ICT RMF, ICT policies, standards, procedures, governance terms of reference. |
| Governance assessment | Reviewed decision-making forums, reporting packs, meeting minutes and escalation records. | Committee packs, board reports, risk dashboards, minutes, action logs. |
| ICT risk assessment review | Examined ICT risk register entries, risk ratings, treatment plans and accepted risks. | Risk registers, treatment plans, risk acceptance records, KRIs. |
| Asset and dependency review | Tested the completeness and consistency of asset, service and dependency records. | CMDB, application register, service catalogue, data flow records, dependency maps. |
| Control evidence sampling | Sampled preventive, detective and recovery controls across selected systems and services. | Access reviews, vulnerability scans, patch reports, backup logs, monitoring alerts. |
| Incident management review | Reviewed incident records, escalation, classification, root cause analysis and closure evidence. | Incident tickets, post-incident reviews, communications, lessons learned. |
| Continuity and recovery review | Assessed business continuity, disaster recovery and restoration testing evidence. | Test plans, exercise reports, recovery metrics, backup restoration results. |
| Resilience testing review | Reviewed cyber, operational resilience and scenario testing performed during the period. | Exercise schedules, tabletop reports, technical test reports, remediation logs. |
| Third-party risk review | Assessed governance over material ICT third-party providers. | Due diligence records, contract summaries, service reports, assurance reports, exit plans. |
| Stakeholder interviews | Conducted interviews with accountable business, ICT, security, risk and compliance stakeholders. | Interview notes, management confirmations, follow-up evidence. |

### Rating Method

Findings were rated using the following severity definitions:

| Severity | Definition | Expected Management Response |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | A material weakness that could cause severe disruption to critical or important functions, major regulatory concern or significant harm to clients or the market. | Immediate executive attention, formal remediation plan and frequent progress reporting. |
| High | A significant control gap or framework weakness that increases the likelihood or impact of ICT disruption, security compromise or resilience failure. | Time-bound remediation with accountable owner and senior management oversight. |
| Medium | A control weakness, inconsistency or process deficiency that should be corrected to improve reliability and maturity. | Planned remediation through standard governance channels. |
| Low | Minor improvement opportunity with limited immediate risk impact. | Address through continuous improvement or routine process enhancement. |

Framework effectiveness ratings were applied as follows:

| Rating | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Effective | Controls and governance are appropriately designed, implemented and evidenced, with only minor improvement opportunities. |
| Partially Effective | Core arrangements are in place, but design or operating weaknesses require management action. |
| Ineffective | Significant weaknesses exist that materially impair the organisation’s ability to manage ICT risk. |
| Not Assessed | Area was not assessed due to scope limitation or insufficient evidence. |

### Limitations

The review was based on evidence available at the time of assessment and on sampling of selected systems, incidents, controls, third-party providers and business functions. It did not constitute a full technical audit, penetration test or independent assurance engagement unless explicitly stated.

## Analysis

### Overall ICT Risk Management Maturity

The ICT RMF demonstrates a functioning and improving approach to ICT risk management. The organisation has established governance, policies, operational processes and technical controls that support digital operational resilience. The framework is embedded in several key management routines, including risk reporting, incident management, testing and third-party oversight.

The most mature areas are:

- Policy ownership and governance cadence.
- Core incident management process.
- Backup monitoring and restoration testing.
- Endpoint protection and vulnerability scanning.
- Mandatory user awareness training.

Areas requiring further maturity are:

- End-to-end dependency mapping for critical or important functions.
- Consolidated view of ICT risk, resilience testing and remediation.
- Third-party exit planning and concentration risk reporting.
- Integrated testing across cyber, technology, business continuity and crisis management.
- Forward-looking board-level risk indicators.

### Trend Analysis

| Area | Prior Period Position | Current Period Position | Trend | Commentary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ICT governance | [Rating] | [Rating] | Improving | Governance cadence strengthened; reporting quality still maturing. |
| Risk assessment | [Rating] | [Rating] | Stable | Process is established; aggregation and accepted risk review require improvement. |
| Asset management | [Rating] | [Rating] | Stable | Inventories exist; reconciliation remains a recurring issue. |
| Security monitoring | [Rating] | [Rating] | Improving | Additional monitoring coverage added during the period. |
| Incident management | [Rating] | [Rating] | Improving | Process tested through real incidents; action tracking remains fragmented. |
| Recovery capability | [Rating] | [Rating] | Stable | Technical tests completed; business service recovery evidence should improve. |
| Resilience testing | [Rating] | [Rating] | Improving | Programme expanded; mapping to critical functions is needed. |
| Third-party risk | [Rating] | [Rating] | Stable | Oversight exists; exit and subcontractor visibility remain key gaps. |
| Training and awareness | [Rating] | [Rating] | Improving | Completion rates strong; role-based training should expand. |

### Risk Appetite Position

The review assessed the ICT RMF against management-approved risk appetite statements and related operational indicators.

| Risk Appetite Area | Current Position | Status | Commentary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Availability of critical or important functions | [Within / Near / Outside Appetite] | [Green / Amber / Red] | [Commentary] |
| Timely remediation of high-risk ICT issues | [Within / Near / Outside Appetite] | [Green / Amber / Red] | Overdue actions indicate pressure against appetite. |
| Critical vulnerability remediation | [Within / Near / Outside Appetite] | [Green / Amber / Red] | [Commentary] |
| Major ICT incident frequency | [Within / Near / Outside Appetite] | [Green / Amber / Red] | [Commentary] |
| Third-party service performance | [Within / Near / Outside Appetite] | [Green / Amber / Red] | [Commentary] |
| Recovery testing success | [Within / Near / Outside Appetite] | [Green / Amber / Red] | [Commentary] |
| Security awareness completion | [Within / Near / Outside Appetite] | [Green / Amber / Red] | [Commentary] |

### Root Cause Themes

The findings indicate the following cross-cutting root cause themes:

1. **Fragmented evidence and action tracking** 
 Multiple teams maintain separate action logs, test records and issue trackers. This limits the organisation’s ability to present a single consolidated view of ICT RMF effectiveness.

2. **Business service mapping still maturing** 
 Some ICT processes are mature at the technology layer but are not fully mapped to business service outcomes, dependencies and recovery priorities.

3. **Third-party resilience assurance requires deeper validation** 
 Supplier oversight relies on due diligence and assurance artefacts, but more work is needed to confirm that third-party recovery capabilities meet the organisation’s own operational resilience needs.

4. **Reporting is operationally strong but strategically incomplete** 
 Senior reporting includes useful metrics, but should better highlight emerging trends, residual risk, risk appetite breaches, dependency concentration and remediation velocity.

5. **Testing is broad but not yet fully integrated** 
 Individual tests are performed, but complex scenarios involving cyber response, ICT recovery, business continuity, crisis decision-making and third-party coordination need expansion.

### Regulatory Readiness Assessment

The organisation is able to evidence key elements of an ICT RMF, including governance, risk assessment, protection, detection, incident management, continuity, testing and third-party oversight. The framework is suitable for submission to the competent authority on request, subject to appropriate management approval and confirmation that report data is current at the time of submission.

To strengthen regulatory readiness, the organisation should prioritise:

- Maintaining a clear, current inventory of critical or important functions and their ICT dependencies.
- Demonstrating timely escalation and closure of ICT risk remediation.
- Evidencing end-to-end resilience testing outcomes.
- Maintaining complete incident timelines, decisions and communications.
- Demonstrating management oversight of material ICT third-party providers.
- Linking risk appetite, testing, incidents and remediation into a coherent management view.

## Recommendations & Actions

### Management Action Plan

| Ref | Recommendation | Priority | Action Owner | Target Date | Status |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| R-01 | Complete and validate end-to-end dependency mapping for all critical or important functions, including applications, infrastructure, data, people, premises, third parties, subcontractors and manual workarounds. | High | Head of Operational Resilience | [Date] | Open |
| R-02 | Implement enhanced escalation for overdue high-risk ICT remediation actions, including executive review where target dates are missed or revised. | High | Chief Information Officer | [Date] | Open |
| R-03 | Update material ICT third-party exit plans to include operational transition steps, data migration considerations, alternative provider options, internal responsibilities, trigger events and test approach. | High | Head of Procurement / Third-Party Risk | [Date] | Open |
| R-04 | Establish an integrated resilience exercise programme combining cyber incident response, disaster recovery, business continuity, crisis management, communications and third-party coordination. | Medium | Head of Business Continuity | [Date] | Open |
| R-05 | Enhance board and executive ICT risk reporting to include trend analysis, risk appetite position, emerging threats, concentration risks, test coverage, remediation ageing and residual risk decisions. | Medium | Chief Risk Officer | [Date] | Open |
| R-06 | Implement periodic reconciliation between application inventory, infrastructure inventory, security tooling and monitoring coverage, with exceptions tracked to closure. | Medium | Head of ICT Operations | [Date] | Open |
| R-07 | Create a single consolidated action log for ICT RMF findings arising from incidents, tests, audits, risk reviews and third-party assessments. | Medium | CISO | [Date] | Open |
| R-08 | Standardise evidence packs for significant ICT incidents, including timeline, classification rationale, decision log, stakeholder communications, root cause analysis, impact assessment and lessons learned. | Medium | Head of Service Management | [Date] | Open |
| R-09 | Define a structured role-based training programme for incident response, crisis management, business continuity coordinators, application owners and third-party relationship managers. | Low | Head of Learning and Development | [Date] | Open |
| R-10 | Define minimum closure evidence requirements for ICT RMF remediation actions and require independent validation for high-risk items. | Medium | Chief Risk Officer | [Date] | Open |

### Immediate Priorities

The following actions should be prioritised within the next [30 / 60 / 90] days:

| Priority | Action | Expected Outcome |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm accountable owners for all high-severity findings and agree remediation milestones. | Clear ownership and delivery timeline for material weaknesses. |
| 2 | Identify all overdue high-risk ICT remediation actions and agree revised dates or escalation. | Reduced unmanaged exposure and improved governance discipline. |
| 3 | Complete dependency mapping plan for critical or important functions. | Defined path to reliable service dependency evidence. |
| 4 | Select material ICT providers for exit plan enhancement and testing. | Improved readiness for provider failure, termination or transition. |
| 5 | Update board reporting template to include forward-looking risk and resilience indicators. | Better senior oversight and decision-making. |

### Target State

By the next annual ICT RMF review, the organisation should be able to demonstrate:

- Complete and validated mapping of critical or important functions to ICT assets, third parties, data and recovery dependencies.
- A consolidated ICT risk and resilience dashboard aligned to risk appetite.
- Timely closure or formal escalation of high-risk remediation actions.
- Tested and practical exit plans for material ICT third-party providers.
- Integrated exercises demonstrating coordinated response and recovery from severe but plausible ICT disruption.
- Clear evidence linking technical recovery capabilities to business recovery requirements.
- Standardised evidence for significant incidents, resilience tests and remediation closure.
- Improved visibility of subcontractor, concentration and substitutability risks.
- Role-based training for staff with ICT risk, incident, resilience and supplier oversight responsibilities.

### Management Approval

| Role | Name | Decision | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chief Information Security Officer | [Name] | [Approved / Approved with Comments / Not Approved] | [Date] |
| Chief Information Officer | [Name] | [Approved / Approved with Comments / Not Approved] | [Date] |
| Chief Risk Officer | [Name] | [Approved / Approved with Comments / Not Approved] | [Date] |
| Chief Operating Officer | [Name] | [Approved / Approved with Comments / Not Approved] | [Date] |
| Management Body / Board Representative | [Name] | [Approved / Approved with Comments / Not Approved] | [Date] |

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Classification

This report is classified as **Confidential - Internal Use**. It contains sensitive information regarding the organisation’s ICT risk posture, control effectiveness, vulnerabilities, incidents, third-party dependencies, remediation activities and operational resilience capabilities.

The report must be handled in accordance with the organisation’s information classification, document handling and records management requirements.

### Authorised Distribution

| Recipient / Group | Purpose | Distribution Method |
|---|---|---|
| Management Body / Board | Oversight and approval | Secure board portal |
| Executive Committee | Management accountability and action tracking | Secure document repository |
| Risk Committee | Risk oversight and challenge | Secure document repository |
| Audit Committee | Assurance oversight | Secure document repository |
| Chief Information Security Officer | Framework ownership and remediation | Secure document repository |
| Chief Information Officer | ICT remediation and operational ownership | Secure document repository |
| Chief Risk Officer | Risk oversight and reporting | Secure document repository |
| Chief Operating Officer | Operational resilience oversight | Secure document repository |
| Compliance Function | Regulatory readiness and coordination | Secure document repository |
| Internal Audit | Independent assurance planning | Secure document repository |
| Competent Authority | Submission on request | Approved regulatory communication channel |

### Restrictions

This report must not be:

- Shared externally without approval from Legal, Compliance and the accountable executive owner.
- Distributed to third-party providers except where specifically approved and limited to relevant extracts.
- Stored in unauthorised locations or personal drives.
- Modified after approval without version control and documented approval.
- Used as a public representation of the organisation’s security or resilience posture.

### Submission to Competent Authority

If requested by the competent authority, the Compliance Function will coordinate submission of this report. Prior to submission:

1. The report must be reviewed for accuracy, completeness and current status.
2. Any draft content, incomplete placeholders or unresolved factual discrepancies must be addressed.
3. Legal and Compliance must confirm the appropriate submission channel and accompanying communication.
4. Senior management approval must be obtained or confirmed.
5. A record of submission must be retained.

### Retention

|---|---|---|

| Supporting evidence pack | [Retention Period] | [Repository] |
| Management approvals | [Retention Period] | [Repository] |
| Competent authority submission record, if applicable | [Retention Period] | [Repository] |
| Action tracking records | Until closure plus [Retention Period] | [Repository] |

### Version and Change Control

Any changes to this report after approval must be recorded in the document history and approved by the report owner.

| Version | Date | Author | Summary of Change | Approval |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Inventory Record ID | Enter a unique stable identifier for this register entry, using format ICTBF-###, e.g. ICTBF-001. Do not reuse IDs after retirement. |
| Business Function Name | Enter the formal name of the business function supported by ICT, e.g. Payments Processing, Claims Management, Trade Execution. |
| Business Function Description | Describe what the function does and its purpose in clear business terms; include scope boundaries and main outputs. |
| Legal Entity / Business Unit | Enter the legal entity, branch, department, or business unit accountable for the function. |
| Function Owner | Enter the accountable senior business owner by role/title and name where available, e.g. Head of Retail Banking. |
| Process Owner | Enter the operational process owner responsible for day-to-day execution and process documentation. |
| ICT Owner | Enter the accountable ICT/application/platform owner responsible for the ICT assets supporting the function. |
| Function Criticality Classification | Classify the function using the organisation’s approved criticality scale, e.g. Critical, High, Medium, Low. |
| Critical or Important Function Flag | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the function is classified as critical or important for DORA purposes. |
| Criticality Rationale | Provide the reason for the criticality classification, referencing impact on financial services, clients, market integrity, regulatory obligations, or operational continuity. |
| Business Service / Product Supported | List the business service, financial service, customer journey, or product supported by the function. |
| Key Activities Supported by ICT | List the main operational activities performed using ICT, separated by semicolons. |
| Information Assets Used or Processed | List the key information assets used, stored, transmitted, or processed by the function, e.g. customer records, transaction data, risk models. |
| Information Asset Classification | Enter the highest applicable classification for information assets, using the organisation’s scheme, e.g. Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. |
| Personal Data Processed | Enter Yes or No; if Yes, indicate whether special category or sensitive personal data is included. |
| Regulated / Sensitive Data Types | List applicable data categories such as payment data, client assets data, trading data, AML/KYC data, personal data, confidential supervisory data, or N/A. |
| Primary ICT Assets Supporting Function | List the main ICT asset IDs/names from the CMDB or asset inventory that directly support the function. |
| Supporting Applications | List application names and IDs used to perform or enable the function, separated by semicolons. |
| Supporting Infrastructure / Platforms | List servers, cloud platforms, network components, middleware, operating environments, or platform services supporting the function. |
| Supporting Databases / Data Stores | List databases, data warehouses, data lakes, file stores, or repositories used by the function. |
| Supporting End-User Computing / Tools | List spreadsheets, macros, robotic process automation bots, reporting tools, or other EUC tools material to the function, or enter N/A. |
| ICT Third-Party Service Providers | List ICT third-party providers supporting the function, including provider name and service supplied; enter N/A if none. |
| Internal Dependencies | List internal teams, functions, systems, shared services, or upstream/downstream processes that this function depends on. |
| External Dependencies | List external dependencies other than ICT third-party providers, such as market infrastructures, payment schemes, data providers, utilities, telecoms, or N/A. |
| Recovery Time Objective (RTO) | Enter the maximum targeted time to restore the function after disruption, using format number plus unit, e.g. 4 hours, 1 day. |
| Recovery Point Objective (RPO) | Enter the maximum tolerable data loss period, using format number plus unit, e.g. 15 minutes, 1 hour, 0 for no data loss. |
| Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) | Enter the maximum time the function can be unavailable before intolerable impact occurs, using format number plus unit. |
| Operational Impact if Unavailable | Describe operational consequences if the function or its ICT support is unavailable, including affected processes and volumes where known. |
| Financial Impact if Unavailable | Describe potential financial loss, liquidity impact, revenue impact, compensation exposure, or enter qualitative rating if quantitative data is unavailable. |
| Customer / Market Impact if Unavailable | Describe impact on clients, counterparties, market participants, service availability, transaction completion, or market confidence. |
| Regulatory / Legal Impact if Unavailable | Describe possible regulatory breach, reporting failure, contractual breach, legal obligation impact, or enter N/A if none identified. |
| ICT Risk Assessment Reference | Enter the reference ID or link to the latest ICT risk assessment covering the function or supporting assets. |
| Business Impact Assessment Reference | Enter the reference ID or link to the BIA record used to support criticality, RTO, RPO, and MTD values. |
| Data Location / Hosting Region | Enter the country or region where data is stored or hosted, including cloud region where applicable. |
| Primary Processing Location | Enter the primary location where processing takes place, such as data centre, cloud region, office location, or outsourced processing site. |
| Backup / Resilience Arrangements | Summarise backup, replication, failover, alternate site, manual workaround, or resilience arrangements supporting the function. |
| Access / Privileged Access Owner | Enter the role/team responsible for approving and reviewing access and privileged access to the supporting ICT assets. |
| Linked Policies / Procedures | List relevant policy, procedure, runbook, or operating manual references governing the function and supporting ICT use. |
| Linked Controls | List control IDs mapped to this function and supporting ICT assets, e.g. access control, backup, logging, incident response, change management. |
| Last Review Date | Enter the date this register entry was last reviewed and validated, using YYYY-MM-DD. |
| Next Review Due Date | Enter the next scheduled review date, no later than 12 months after the last review, using YYYY-MM-DD. |
| Review Trigger | Enter the reason for the current review using allowed values: Annual Review, New Function, Material ICT Change, Third-Party Change, Incident Follow-Up, Regulatory Change, Organisational Change. |
| Review Status | Enter current validation status using allowed values: Draft, Pending Owner Review, Approved, Requires Update, Retired. |
| Material Change Since Last Review | Enter Yes or No; if Yes, briefly state the change, e.g. new application, new provider, hosting migration, changed criticality. |
| Approver | Enter the accountable person or governance forum approving the register entry and classification. |
| Approval Date | Enter the date of approval using YYYY-MM-DD; leave blank until approved. |
| Comments / Open Actions | Record any clarification, data quality issue, remediation action, owner, and target date; enter N/A if none. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the ICT Risk Management function with accountable input from business function owners, ICT asset owners, enterprise architecture, third-party risk management, data governance, and business continuity. Updated at least annually and whenever there is a new function, material ICT change, outsourcing/provider change, incident-driven update, or organisational change, drawing from the CMDB/ICT asset inventory, application portfolio, information asset register, BIA records, ICT risk assessments, third-party register, and data governance catalogue.

DORA-008.title: ICT Asset Inventory
DORA-008.content:
## ICT Asset Inventory (XLSX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Asset ID | Asset Name | Asset Type | Asset Description | ICT Asset Category | Business Function Supported | Business Function Criticality | Information Asset / Data Set Processed | Data Classification | Personal Data Processed | Regulated / Sensitive Data Type | Asset Owner | Technical Owner | Business Owner | Legal Entity / Business Unit | Location / Hosting Model | Environment | Supplier / Third-Party Provider | Third-Party Arrangement Reference | ICT Service Supported | Dependency Type | Upstream Dependencies | Downstream Dependencies | Critical Dependency Indicator | Asset Criticality Rating | Availability Requirement | Integrity Requirement | Confidentiality Requirement | Recovery Time Objective (RTO) | Recovery Point Objective (RPO) | Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) | Operational Status | Lifecycle Stage | Version / Model | Patch / Firmware Level | End-of-Life Date | End-of-Support Date | Primary Control Baseline | Key Security Controls Implemented | Backup Required | Backup Frequency | Monitoring Required | Logging Required | Resilience / DR Arrangement | Last Major Change Date | Major Change Reference | Last Review Date | Next Review Date | Inventory Update Trigger | Record Status | Comments / Exceptions |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Asset ID | Enter the unique inventory identifier for the ICT asset, using the organisation's standard naming convention; this must be stable and not reused, e.g. ICT-APP-000123. |
| Asset Name | Enter the official name of the ICT asset as used in the CMDB, asset register, architecture repository, or supplier documentation. |
| Asset Type | Select the asset type from an approved list such as Application, Infrastructure, Server, Database, Network Device, Cloud Service, SaaS, Endpoint, Middleware, API, Information Asset, Security Tool, Facility Technology, or Other. |
| Asset Description | Briefly describe what the ICT asset is and what it is used for, sufficient for an independent reviewer to understand its purpose. |
| ICT Asset Category | Classify the asset into a controlled category, for example Hardware, Software, Data, Network, Cloud, Outsourced ICT Service, Information System, or Supporting Facility. |
| Business Function Supported | Enter the business function, process, or service that depends on this asset; if multiple functions are supported, list each separated by semicolons. |
| Business Function Criticality | Classify the supported business function using the organisation's approved scale, e.g. Critical, Important, Standard, or Low, aligned to business impact analysis criteria. |
| Information Asset / Data Set Processed | Enter the name of the information asset, data set, or records processed, stored, or transmitted by this ICT asset; use 'None' only where no business data is processed. |
| Data Classification | Select the highest classification of data handled by the asset, e.g. Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, Secret, or organisation-specific equivalent. |
| Personal Data Processed | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the asset processes personal data under applicable data protection laws. |
| Regulated / Sensitive Data Type | Identify any regulated or sensitive data processed, such as Personal Data, Special Category Data, Payment Data, Client Assets Data, Trading Data, Authentication Data, Financial Reporting Data, or None. |
| Asset Owner | Enter the accountable owner for the asset, normally a named role or individual responsible for the asset's governance, classification, and risk acceptance. |
| Technical Owner | Enter the technical role or team responsible for operating, maintaining, patching, and technically managing the asset. |
| Business Owner | Enter the business role or team accountable for the business service or process supported by the asset. |
| Legal Entity / Business Unit | Enter the legal entity, branch, subsidiary, or business unit that owns or primarily uses the asset. |
| Location / Hosting Model | Enter where and how the asset is hosted, using values such as On-Premises, Private Cloud, Public Cloud, Hybrid Cloud, SaaS, Colocation, End-User Device, or Third-Party Hosted; include country or region where relevant. |
| Environment | Select the environment in which the asset operates, e.g. Production, Disaster Recovery, Test, Development, UAT, Staging, Sandbox, or Archive. |
| Supplier / Third-Party Provider | Enter the supplier, cloud provider, managed service provider, or third party involved in providing, hosting, operating, or supporting the asset; enter 'Internal' if fully internally provided. |
| Third-Party Arrangement Reference | Enter the contract, outsourcing register, third-party risk record, or service agreement reference ID linked to this asset; use 'N/A' if not third-party supported. |
| ICT Service Supported | Enter the ICT service or technology service this asset contributes to, using the organisation's ICT service catalogue name. |
| Dependency Type | Describe the nature of the dependency, selecting one or more values such as Business Process, Application, Database, Infrastructure, Network, Identity, Security, Cloud Platform, Supplier, Data Feed, API, Facility, or Other. |
| Upstream Dependencies | List assets, suppliers, services, data feeds, infrastructure, or processes that this asset depends on; use Asset IDs or service references where available, separated by semicolons. |
| Downstream Dependencies | List assets, systems, business functions, services, or third parties that depend on this asset; use Asset IDs or service references where available, separated by semicolons. |
| Critical Dependency Indicator | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether failure or degradation of this dependency could materially disrupt a critical or important function. |
| Asset Criticality Rating | Classify the asset's criticality using the organisation's approved scale, e.g. Critical, High, Medium, Low, based on impact to business functions, data, customers, financial stability, regulatory obligations, and operational resilience. |
| Availability Requirement | Select the required availability level, e.g. Very High, High, Medium, Low, or specify an agreed percentage such as 99.9%. |
| Integrity Requirement | Select the required integrity level for the asset and data, e.g. Very High, High, Medium, Low, based on tolerance for unauthorised or erroneous modification. |
| Confidentiality Requirement | Select the required confidentiality level, e.g. Very High, High, Medium, Low, based on the sensitivity of data and access restrictions. |
| Recovery Time Objective (RTO) | Enter the maximum acceptable time to restore the asset after disruption, in hours or minutes, e.g. 4h or 30m; align to business impact analysis and continuity requirements. |
| Recovery Point Objective (RPO) | Enter the maximum acceptable data loss period, in hours or minutes, e.g. 1h or 15m; use 'N/A' only where the asset does not store or process recoverable data. |
| Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) | Enter the maximum duration the asset can be unavailable before causing unacceptable business impact, in hours or days, e.g. 8h or 2d. |
| Operational Status | Select the current status from Planned, Active, In Maintenance, Suspended, Retiring, Retired, or Decommissioned. |
| Lifecycle Stage | Select the lifecycle stage from Design, Build, Test, Production, Maintenance, Legacy, End-of-Life, Decommissioning, or Decommissioned. |
| Version / Model | Enter the software version, hardware model, platform release, or service version where applicable; use 'N/A' only if not versioned. |
| Patch / Firmware Level | Enter the current patch level, firmware version, build number, or last applied security update reference; use the format provided by the vendor or internal patch tool. |
| End-of-Life Date | Enter the vendor or internal end-of-life date in YYYY-MM-DD format; use 'Unknown' only where formally under investigation. |
| End-of-Support Date | Enter the vendor or support end date in YYYY-MM-DD format; use 'N/A' where the asset is internally developed and not subject to vendor support. |
| Primary Control Baseline | Enter the applicable security and resilience control baseline or standard, e.g. CIS Level 1, Internal Critical System Baseline, Cloud Security Baseline, or DORA Critical Asset Baseline. |
| Key Security Controls Implemented | List the principal controls applied to the asset, such as MFA, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, privileged access management, vulnerability scanning, EDR, network segmentation, backup, monitoring, or logging. |
| Backup Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether backup or equivalent recoverability is required for this asset. |
| Backup Frequency | Enter the approved backup frequency, e.g. Real-time replication, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or N/A if Backup Required is No. |
| Monitoring Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the asset must be monitored for availability, performance, security events, and capacity. |
| Logging Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether security, operational, or audit logs must be collected and retained for this asset. |
| Resilience / DR Arrangement | Describe the resilience or disaster recovery arrangement, e.g. Active-Active, Active-Passive, Hot Standby, Warm Standby, Cold Restore, Backup Restore, Manual Workaround, or None Approved. |
| Last Major Change Date | Enter the date of the last major change affecting the asset, its classification, ownership, dependencies, supplier, hosting model, or criticality, using YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Major Change Reference | Enter the change ticket, release ID, project ID, architecture decision record, or transformation reference that triggered the latest inventory update. |
| Last Review Date | Enter the date the inventory record was last reviewed and confirmed by the accountable owner, using YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date using YYYY-MM-DD format, based on the asset criticality and inventory review policy. |
| Inventory Update Trigger | Select the reason the record was created or updated, e.g. New Asset, Major Change, Supplier Change, Criticality Change, Dependency Change, Data Classification Change, Ownership Change, Lifecycle Change, Periodic Review, or Decommissioning. |
| Record Status | Select the inventory record status from Draft, Pending Owner Validation, Approved, Requires Update, Archived, or Superseded. |
| Comments / Exceptions | Enter any relevant notes, unresolved data quality issues, temporary exceptions, assumptions, or remediation actions; include exception reference IDs where applicable. |

### Maintenance

The ICT Asset Inventory should be owned by the CIO or Head of ICT Asset Management, with accountable validation by asset owners and oversight by ICT Risk/Operational Resilience. It should be updated immediately for every major change and reviewed at least quarterly for critical or important assets, drawing from the CMDB, ICT service catalogue, architecture repository, change management system, third-party register, vulnerability/patch tools, and business impact analysis records.
