69. Where backup media or storage devices are transported, stored externally, or handled by third parties, they shall be protected against loss, theft, tampering, unauthorised access, and environmental damage.

70. Physical backup media shall be tracked through inventory records, chain-of-custody records where appropriate, secure storage, and authorised destruction processes.

71. The organisation shall define and test emergency access procedures for backup and restoration activities, including controls to prevent misuse and requirements for post-event review.

72. The organisation shall maintain a documented communication and escalation process for restoration activities during major ICT incidents, including engagement with business owners, ICT teams, security teams, crisis management, third parties, and senior management.

73. The organisation shall ensure that backup and restoration arrangements remain effective during periods of elevated threat, major incident response, system migration, merger or acquisition activity, and technology transformation.

74. The organisation shall not rely solely on manual backup processes for systems supporting critical or important functions unless automated backup is not technically feasible and compensating controls are approved.

75. Any manual backup or restoration activity shall be documented, authorised, verified, and retained as evidence.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board / Governing Body | Provides oversight of ICT resilience expectations and ensures that backup and restoration capabilities are adequately governed, resourced, and challenged. |
| Senior Management | Ensures that backup and restoration requirements are implemented across business areas, prioritises remediation of material deficiencies, and accepts residual risks where appropriate. |
| Chief Information Security Officer / Security Lead | Defines security requirements for backup protection, encryption, access control, logging, ransomware resilience, compromise assessment, and secure restoration. |
| Head of ICT / Technology Lead | Owns the operational implementation of this Policy and ensures that ICT teams maintain effective backup and restoration capabilities. |
| Business Owners | Define business recovery priorities, approve recovery objectives, validate restored services, and confirm that recovery outcomes meet business needs. |
| System Owners | Ensure that assigned systems are included in backup schedules, restoration procedures are current, dependencies are documented, and restoration tests are completed. |
| Data Owners | Define data retention, sensitivity, legal hold, and recovery requirements for data sets under their ownership. |
| ICT Operations Team | Operates backup platforms, monitors backup jobs, investigates failures, performs restorations, maintains technical documentation, and records operational evidence. |
| Infrastructure and Cloud Teams | Configure backup storage, snapshots, replication, recovery environments, system images, infrastructure recovery processes, and cloud recovery services. |
| Application Teams | Ensure applications can be restored consistently, support application-level validation, maintain deployment and configuration recovery documentation, and assist with testing. |
| Database Administrators | Configure and monitor database backups, transaction log backups, consistency checks, point-in-time recovery, and database restoration testing. |
| Incident Response Team | Coordinates backup-related actions during cyber incidents, including contamination checks, evidence preservation, and recovery sequencing. |
| Business Continuity / Operational Resilience Lead | Ensures backup and restoration arrangements align with continuity plans, impact tolerances, resilience testing, and business service recovery priorities. |
| Risk Management Function | Reviews backup and restoration risks, monitors remediation of material gaps, and supports risk acceptance decisions. |
| Compliance / Legal | Advises on regulatory, contractual, legal hold, data retention, evidence preservation, and notification requirements. |
| Procurement / Third-Party Risk Management | Ensures supplier contracts and oversight processes include appropriate backup, restoration, assurance, notification, and exit requirements. |
| Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance over the design and operating effectiveness of backup and restoration controls. |
| Third-Party ICT Service Providers | Perform backup and restoration obligations in accordance with contractual requirements, provide evidence on request, support testing, and notify the organisation of relevant issues. |
| All Users | Store organisational data only in approved locations so that it is protected by managed backup and recovery arrangements. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy shall be monitored through operational reporting, control testing, restoration exercises, risk assessments, third-party assurance, management review, and audit activity.

The organisation shall maintain a backup and restoration control dashboard or equivalent reporting mechanism that includes, at minimum:

| Metric | Minimum Reporting Frequency | Audience |
|---|---:|---|
| Backup success rate for systems supporting critical or important functions | Monthly | ICT Management, Security, Operational Resilience |
| Failed backup jobs by severity and age | Weekly or monthly based on criticality | ICT Operations and System Owners |
| Systems without current backup coverage | Monthly | ICT Management and Risk Management |
| Restoration tests completed versus plan | Monthly or quarterly | ICT Management, Business Owners, Risk Management |
| Restoration tests failed or completed with issues | Monthly or quarterly | ICT Management, Security, Operational Resilience |
| Recovery objectives not met during testing | Quarterly | Senior Management and relevant governance forum |
| Backup storage capacity and growth trends | Monthly | ICT Operations |
| Privileged access reviews for backup platforms | Quarterly | ICT Management and Security |
| Third-party backup assurance status | At least annually | Third-Party Risk, Risk Management, ICT Management |
| Open remediation actions relating to backup or restoration | Monthly | ICT Management, Risk Management, Internal Control Owners |

The following minimum evidence shall be retained and made available for audit, assurance, regulatory engagement, and management review where required:

| Evidence Type | Required Content |
|---|---|
| Backup Register | Systems, owners, backup method, frequency, retention, recovery objectives, storage location, encryption, testing status |
| Backup Job Logs | Success, failure, warnings, skipped items, start and end times, affected systems |
| Failure Remediation Records | Incident or ticket number, cause, impact, remediation, closure approval |
| Restoration Test Records | Scope, method, restore point, duration, validation, defects, lessons learned, approvals |
| Recovery Runbooks | Restoration sequence, dependencies, access requirements, validation steps, escalation contacts |
| Access Review Evidence | Backup platform users, privileged accounts, approvals, removals, exceptions |
| Third-Party Assurance | Supplier attestations, test results, service reports, contractual confirmations, remediation actions |
| Risk Acceptances | Approved deviations, compensating controls, expiry date, accountable owner |
| Management Reporting | Metrics, issues, decisions, remediation tracking, escalation records |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in one or more of the following actions:

- Formal risk assessment and remediation plan.
- Escalation to ICT management, security management, operational resilience governance, senior management, or the governing body.
- Suspension of system go-live, change approval, migration, or service onboarding until backup and restoration requirements are met.
- Increased monitoring, independent assurance, or audit review.
- Contractual remedies or supplier remediation action where third-party obligations are not met.
- Disciplinary action for employees or contractors where non-compliance is deliberate, negligent, or repeated.
- Reporting through incident, risk, compliance, or regulatory processes where required.

Material backup or restoration failures affecting systems supporting critical or important functions shall be escalated promptly and managed through the organisation’s incident management, operational resilience, and risk management processes.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business, technical, legal, or operational justification and where the associated risk has been assessed and approved by the appropriate authority.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Individual and business area requesting the exception |
| System or Data Scope | Systems, data sets, services, or suppliers affected |
| Policy Requirement | Specific requirement that cannot be met |
| Justification | Business or technical reason for the exception |
| Risk Assessment | Confidentiality, integrity, availability, operational, customer, regulatory, and contractual impact |
| Compensating Controls | Alternative measures to reduce risk |
| Duration | Start date and expiry date |
| Remediation Plan | Actions required to achieve compliance, with target dates |
| Approval | Required approval based on risk and system criticality |
| Review Frequency | Frequency for reassessing the exception |

Exceptions affecting systems supporting critical or important functions shall require approval from the relevant Business Owner, System Owner, ICT Owner, Security Lead, and Risk Management function.

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed [maximum exception period, e.g., 12 months] without reapproval. Permanent exceptions shall not be permitted unless formally approved as an accepted residual risk by senior management.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed, closed, or replaced by an approved remediation plan.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever a material change occurs that may affect backup or restoration requirements.

A review shall also be triggered by:

- A major ICT incident, cyber incident, ransomware event, data corruption event, or failed restoration.
- A significant change to business services, critical or important functions, recovery objectives, or impact tolerances.
- Introduction of new ICT systems, cloud services, outsourcing arrangements, or material third-party dependencies.
- Significant technology changes, including migration, decommissioning, platform replacement, architecture redesign, or backup tooling changes.
- Audit findings, regulatory feedback, risk assessment outcomes, or control testing results.
- Material changes to legal, regulatory, contractual, or data retention requirements.
- Lessons learned from continuity exercises, crisis simulations, restoration tests, or operational resilience testing.

The Policy Owner shall ensure that this Policy remains current, approved, communicated, and aligned with related governance documents, including:

- ICT Risk Management Policy.
- Information Security Policy.
- Business Continuity Management Policy.
- ICT Incident Response Policy.
- Disaster Recovery Plan.
- Data Retention and Disposal Policy.
- Access Control Policy.
- Cryptography and Key Management Policy.
- Third-Party ICT Risk Management Policy.
- Change Management Policy.
- Asset Management Policy.
- Logging and Monitoring Policy.

Changes to this Policy shall be reviewed by relevant stakeholders, approved through the organisation’s policy governance process, and communicated to personnel and third parties with backup or restoration responsibilities.

DORA-016.title: Crisis Communication Plan
DORA-016.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DORA-PLAN-CCP-001] | 1.0 | [Head of Corporate Communications / ICT Risk Owner] | [DD MMM YYYY] | Digital Operational Resilience Act | Internal |

## Purpose & Objectives

This Crisis Communication Plan defines how [Organisation Name] will communicate during major ICT-related incidents that may affect clients, counterparties, regulators, employees, service providers, market participants, or the organisation’s operational resilience and reputation.

The plan supports timely, accurate, coordinated, and controlled communications during disruptive ICT events, including cyber-attacks, technology outages, data integrity issues, third-party ICT service failures, payment or trading service disruption, and other incidents that may materially affect business services.

The objectives of this plan are to:

- Ensure crisis communications are activated promptly when a major ICT-related incident occurs or is suspected.
- Provide clear responsibilities for internal and external communications during an ICT crisis.
- Support rapid, factual, and consistent messaging to stakeholders.
- Avoid inaccurate, premature, misleading, or unauthorised communications.
- Enable coordinated communication with incident response, business continuity, legal, compliance, risk, senior management, and third-party providers.
- Preserve customer trust, market confidence, and regulatory credibility.
- Ensure communication records are retained for post-incident review, audit, and evidence purposes.
- Support notification and communication obligations without exposing sensitive security information.
- Provide practical templates, channels, approval routes, and escalation thresholds for crisis communication.

This plan is not an incident response procedure, business continuity plan, regulatory reporting procedure, or media policy. It works alongside those documents and focuses specifically on communication management during major ICT-related incidents.

## Scope

This plan applies to all major ICT-related incidents affecting, or reasonably likely to affect, [Organisation Name], including incidents involving outsourced or third-party ICT services.

The plan covers communication activities for:

- Internal stakeholders, including employees, executive management, board members, business service owners, ICT teams, risk, compliance, legal, operations, and customer-facing teams.
- External stakeholders, including clients, customers, counterparties, regulators, competent authorities, law enforcement where appropriate, media, investors, suppliers, and critical third-party service providers.
- Public-facing communications, including website notices, social media posts, press statements, client notifications, and market statements.
- Communication support for incident detection, containment, recovery, restoration, and post-incident review.
- Communication during both confirmed incidents and high-impact suspected incidents where proactive coordination is required.

This plan applies to ICT-related incidents that may involve one or more of the following:

- Material disruption to important or critical business services.
- Loss of availability, integrity, authenticity, or confidentiality of ICT systems or data.
- Cyber-attack, ransomware, malware, distributed denial-of-service attack, account compromise, unauthorised access, data leakage, or system manipulation.
- Failure of core infrastructure, applications, networks, cloud services, data centres, or telecommunications.
- ICT third-party or outsourced service disruption affecting regulated activities.
- Incident affecting customer access, transaction processing, trading, payments, reporting, records, or client communications.
- Incident with actual or potential media, customer, market, regulator, or board-level interest.
- Incident requiring regulatory notification, client notification, public statement, or coordinated communications with third parties.

Out of scope:

- Routine IT service communications for minor incidents handled through standard service desk processes.
- General marketing, public relations, or non-crisis corporate communications.
- Detailed technical incident containment steps, which are addressed in the ICT Incident Response Plan.
- Regulatory notification content and submission procedures, which are addressed in the Regulatory Incident Notification Procedure.
- Disaster recovery execution steps, which are addressed in ICT Disaster Recovery Plans.
- Full business continuity response arrangements, which are addressed in the Business Continuity Plan.

Where uncertainty exists about whether this plan should be activated, the incident should be escalated to the Crisis Communication Lead and Incident Commander for assessment.

## Assumptions & Dependencies

This plan is based on the following assumptions:

- [Organisation Name] maintains an approved ICT Incident Response Plan, Business Continuity Plan, Crisis Management Plan, and Regulatory Incident Notification Procedure.
- Major ICT-related incidents are classified and escalated through established incident management channels.
- A Crisis Management Team or equivalent senior decision-making group is available for significant incidents.
- Contact lists for internal teams, executives, regulators, third-party providers, legal counsel, and communication channels are maintained and accessible during an incident.
- Communication channels may be impaired during an ICT crisis; alternative channels must therefore be available.
- Not all facts will be known at the start of an incident; communications must be appropriately caveated and updated as verified information becomes available.
- Public statements may require review by Legal, Compliance, Communications, Executive Management, and, where necessary, external counsel.
- Technical details must be limited to what is necessary for stakeholder understanding, regulatory engagement, and customer protection.
- Communications must not compromise investigation, containment, recovery, law enforcement activity, litigation strategy, or security posture.
- Communications with regulators and authorities must be consistent with the organisation’s formal incident notifications and updates.
- Staff must not speak to the media, customers, regulators, or third parties about the incident unless authorised to do so.

The effectiveness of this plan depends on:

| Dependency | Required Condition | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Incident classification process | Major ICT-related incidents are identified and escalated promptly | Head of ICT Operations / CISO |
| Crisis Management Team | Senior decision-makers are available or have nominated deputies | COO / Crisis Management Chair |
| Approved communication templates | Draft statements and holding messages are maintained and tested | Corporate Communications |
| Contact directory | Contact details are current, accessible offline, and tested | Corporate Communications / Business Continuity Manager |
| Alternative communication tools | Backup communication channels are available if primary tools fail | ICT Operations |
| Regulatory notification process | Compliance and Legal can confirm notification requirements and timing | Chief Compliance Officer / General Counsel |
| Customer communication channels | Customer notification methods are available and can be prioritised | Head of Customer Operations |
| Third-party coordination | Critical ICT service providers provide timely incident updates | Third-Party Risk Manager |
| Evidence retention | Communication decisions, approvals, and issued messages are logged | Crisis Communication Lead |
| Training and exercises | Relevant teams understand their roles and escalation routes | Business Continuity Manager |

Key constraints:

- Speed must not override accuracy where facts are unverified.
- No individual may issue unauthorised public, customer, regulatory, or media statements.
- Communications must remain aligned across incident response, legal, compliance, executive leadership, and customer operations.
- Confidential or sensitive security information must be shared only on a need-to-know basis.
- Personal data breach communications, where relevant, must be coordinated with the Data Protection Officer or privacy lead.

## Approach / Phases

The crisis communication approach follows a structured lifecycle aligned with the organisation’s incident response and crisis management arrangements.

### Phase 1 - Preparation and Readiness

The objective of this phase is to ensure the organisation is ready to communicate effectively before a major ICT-related incident occurs.

Key activities:

- Maintain this plan and associated communication templates.
- Maintain current contact lists for crisis communication stakeholders.
- Identify authorised spokespersons and deputies.
- Define approval workflows for different communication types.
- Maintain offline copies of key documents and contact details.
- Prepare holding statements for common ICT crisis scenarios.
- Ensure communication channels can operate during ICT disruption.
- Train relevant personnel on escalation, approvals, and messaging discipline.
- Conduct periodic crisis communication exercises with ICT incident scenarios.
- Review lessons learned from incidents, exercises, industry events, and regulatory feedback.

Prepared communication scenarios should include:

| Scenario | Prepared Communication Materials |
|---|---|
| Cyber-attack affecting service availability | Holding statement, customer service script, regulator update summary, website notice |
| Ransomware or malware event | Internal staff advisory, customer holding statement, media Q&A, executive briefing |
| Major outage of customer-facing platform | Customer notification, status page update, call centre script, social media holding line |
| Third-party cloud or technology provider failure | Client update, provider coordination brief, executive update, regulator briefing summary |
| Data confidentiality or integrity concern | Internal escalation message, customer notification draft, legal review checklist |
| Payment, trading, or transaction processing disruption | Market participant update, client statement, regulator briefing note, operations script |
| Loss of corporate communication systems | Alternative communication activation message and leadership contact protocol |

### Phase 2 - Activation and Initial Assessment

This phase begins when a major ICT-related incident is declared or when a suspected ICT incident could materially affect operations, customers, regulatory commitments, market confidence, or reputation.

Activation criteria include:

- Incident has been classified as major by the Incident Commander or equivalent authority.
- Incident affects or may affect important business services.
- Incident is likely to require regulatory notification.
- Customer, client, market, or media impact is likely.
- Sensitive data may have been compromised.
- A critical third-party ICT service provider is involved.
- Executive or board-level oversight is required.
- The incident could create reputational, legal, financial, or operational harm.

Activation steps:

| Step | Action | Responsible Role | Target Timing |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Incident Commander notifies Crisis Communication Lead of potential communication need | Incident Commander | Immediately after major incident assessment |
| 2 | Crisis Communication Lead joins incident response or crisis management bridge | Crisis Communication Lead | Within [15 minutes] |
| 3 | Confirm known facts, unknowns, affected services, stakeholder impacts, and restrictions | Crisis Communication Lead / Incident Commander | Within [30 minutes] |
| 4 | Determine communication classification and stakeholder communication needs | Crisis Communication Lead / Legal / Compliance | Within [45 minutes] |
| 5 | Prepare initial internal holding message and executive brief | Corporate Communications | Within [60 minutes] |
| 6 | Obtain approval for first communications | Crisis Management Chair / Legal / Compliance | Before release |
| 7 | Issue approved communications through agreed channels | Communications Team / Stakeholder Owners | As authorised |
| 8 | Start communication log and decision record | Communications Scribe | From activation |

Initial communication classification:

| Communication Level | Description | Typical Audience | Approval Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level 1 - Internal Awareness | Incident may affect internal teams, but external communication is not yet required | ICT, operations, customer service, executives | Crisis Communication Lead |
| Level 2 - Controlled Stakeholder Update | Incident has limited external impact or selected stakeholders require information | Affected clients, suppliers, regulators, service owners | Crisis Communication Lead, Legal, Compliance |
| Level 3 - Public or Market-Sensitive Communication | Incident may attract media, market, customer, or broad regulatory attention | Public, media, market participants, broad customer base | Crisis Management Chair, Legal, Compliance, Executive Spokesperson |
| Level 4 - Severe Crisis Communication | Incident has material operational, customer, regulatory, market, or reputational impact | Board, regulators, public, customers, media, authorities | CEO or delegated executive, Legal, Compliance, Crisis Management Chair |

### Phase 3 - Message Development and Approval

The objective of this phase is to produce accurate, consistent, and approved communications.

All crisis communications must be based on verified facts and must clearly distinguish between confirmed information and ongoing assessment.

Standard message structure:

- What happened, in plain language, without unnecessary technical detail.
- Which services, customers, operations, or locations are affected, if known.
- What the organisation is doing to contain, investigate, and recover.
- What stakeholders should do, if any action is required.
- What is not yet known, where appropriate.
- When the next update will be provided.
- Where stakeholders can obtain further information.
- Contact point for questions or urgent concerns.

Message principles:

- Be factual, concise, calm, and transparent.
- Avoid speculation, blame, technical jargon, and unsupported assurances.
- Avoid stating that an incident is “contained”, “resolved”, or “not a breach” unless confirmed by authorised leads.
- Avoid disclosing security weaknesses, attack methods, defensive measures, or sensitive investigation details.
- Maintain consistency between internal, customer, regulator, media, and third-party communications.
- Ensure customer-facing messages are understandable and actionable.
- Ensure staff-facing messages explain what employees must and must not do.
- Consider accessibility, language, jurisdiction, and customer vulnerability needs.
- Include time and date stamps on updates where appropriate.

Approval workflow:

| Communication Type | Drafted By | Reviewed By | Approved By | Release Channel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Internal all-staff message | Corporate Communications | Incident Commander, HR, Legal | Crisis Communication Lead / Crisis Management Chair | Email, intranet, emergency messaging |
| Executive or board update | Crisis Communication Lead | Incident Commander, Risk, Legal, Compliance | Crisis Management Chair / CEO | Secure email, board portal, crisis bridge |
| Customer notification | Customer Operations / Communications | Legal, Compliance, Data Protection Officer where relevant | Responsible Executive / Crisis Management Chair | Email, portal, website, contact centre |
| Regulator communication support | Compliance | Legal, Incident Commander, Risk | Chief Compliance Officer / General Counsel | Regulatory reporting channel |
| Media statement | Corporate Communications | Legal, Compliance, CEO Office | Authorised Spokesperson / CEO | Press office, media release |
| Social media post | Corporate Communications | Legal, Crisis Communication Lead | Authorised Spokesperson | Approved corporate social channels |
| Third-party provider communication | Third-Party Risk / Procurement | Legal, Incident Commander | Third-Party Risk Owner / Crisis Management Chair | Supplier management channel |
| Law enforcement communication support | Legal / Security | CISO, Compliance | General Counsel | Approved authority channel |

Minimum approval standards:

- No public or external communication may be issued without Legal and Compliance review unless an emergency delegation has been invoked.
- Any communication involving personal data, confidential information, or customer harm must include review by the Data Protection Officer or privacy lead.
- Market-sensitive or investor-relevant communication must include review by Legal and the relevant executive owner.
- Regulatory communication must be coordinated by Compliance, supported by Incident Response and Legal.
- Emergency communications may be issued under pre-approved templates where delay would increase harm, but must be logged and reviewed as soon as practicable.

### Phase 4 - Internal Communication

Internal communication ensures that employees, leaders, and affected teams receive accurate instructions and do not create confusion or risk.

Internal communication audiences include:

- Executive management.
- Board or board committee members.
- Crisis Management Team.
- ICT incident response team.
- Business service owners.
- Customer service and complaint handling teams.
- Operations teams.
- Relationship managers and client-facing teams.
- Risk, compliance, legal, data protection, and internal audit.
- Human resources and facilities teams where relevant.
- All employees, where general awareness or behavioural instructions are required.

Internal communication priorities:

| Priority | Communication Need | Example Content |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate control | Prevent unauthorised statements and unsafe behaviours | “Do not discuss this incident externally. Refer all enquiries to [contact].” |
| Operational alignment | Ensure affected teams know what is happening and what actions to take | Service impact, workaround instructions, escalation route |
| Executive oversight | Enable leadership decisions | Incident summary, impact, risks, next decision points |
| Customer handling | Ensure consistent responses to customer enquiries | Approved script, FAQs, escalation path |
| Staff protection | Reduce phishing, social engineering, or misinformation risk | Security advisory, password guidance, reporting instructions |
| Recovery support | Support restoration and business continuity | Expected timelines, manual processes, service prioritisation |

Standard internal holding message:

> [Organisation Name] is currently responding to an ICT-related incident affecting [service/system/business area]. Investigation and recovery activities are underway. At this stage, confirmed information is limited to [confirmed facts]. Employees must not comment externally, post about the incident, or respond to media or customer enquiries unless authorised. Please direct enquiries to [contact/team]. Further updates will be provided by [time/date].

Internal updates should continue at a frequency appropriate to the incident severity. For severe incidents, updates should normally be issued at least every [60-120 minutes] during the active crisis period, even if there is no major change, to prevent uncertainty and rumour.

### Phase 5 - External Communication

External communication must be coordinated, authorised, and aligned with legal, regulatory, operational, and customer obligations.

External audiences may include:

- Retail customers.
- Corporate clients.
- Counterparties.
- Business partners.
- Regulators and competent authorities.
- Critical ICT third-party service providers.
- Industry bodies and financial market infrastructure operators.
- Law enforcement or national cyber authorities where appropriate.
- Media.
- Investors or shareholders.
- Public users of affected services.

External communication triggers include:

| Trigger | Potential Communication Response |
|---|---|
| Customers cannot access services | Customer notice, status page update, contact centre script |
| Transactions are delayed, rejected, duplicated, or uncertain | Targeted customer and counterparty communication |
| Data confidentiality or integrity may be affected | Legal-reviewed customer and regulator communication |
| Incident has public visibility | Holding statement and media Q&A |
| Third-party provider outage affects services | Customer update coordinated with provider information |
| Regulator requests information | Compliance-led response supported by incident facts |
| Service restoration is materially delayed | Update on workarounds, expected next update, customer support routes |
| Misinformation is circulating | Corrective statement through approved channels |
| Incident creates customer protection risk | Direct customer instructions and fraud prevention guidance |

Customer communication must be clear about:

- Affected services.
- Whether the customer needs to take action.
- Known workarounds.
- Expected update timing.
- Support channels.
- Any security precautions customers should take.
- Complaint or escalation routes, where appropriate.

Customer communications must not:

- Include unverified root cause statements.
- Promise restoration times unless approved by the Incident Commander.
- Disclose sensitive security details.
- Minimise customer impact without evidence.
- Shift blame to a third-party provider without Legal approval.
- Contradict regulatory notifications or public statements.

Sample customer holding message:

> We are currently experiencing an ICT-related issue affecting [service/channel]. Our teams are working urgently to investigate and restore normal service. At this time, [confirmed impact]. If you need assistance, please contact [support channel]. We will provide the next update by [time/date] or sooner if there is a material development. We apologise for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

Sample media holding statement:

> [Organisation Name] is aware of an ICT-related incident affecting [general service area]. We have activated our incident response and crisis management arrangements and are working to restore services safely. We are assessing the impact and will provide further information when confirmed. Protecting our customers and maintaining service integrity remain our priorities.

Sample third-party provider coordination message:

> [Organisation Name] is managing a major ICT-related incident affecting [service/process]. Your service may be involved or impacted. Please provide an immediate status update covering service availability, known incidents, affected components, estimated restoration times, incident reference numbers, and escalation contacts. All information shared must be treated as confidential and coordinated through [contact/team].

### Phase 6 - Communication During Containment and Recovery

During containment and recovery, communications must support stakeholder confidence while avoiding premature statements.

Ongoing communication activities include:

- Maintain a single source of truth for approved incident facts.
- Issue regular status updates according to incident severity and stakeholder impact.
- Update FAQs, contact centre scripts, and customer service guidance.
- Monitor internal and external stakeholder sentiment.
- Correct misinformation or inconsistent messaging.
- Coordinate public messaging with restoration milestones.
- Confirm when services are restored and whether any limitations remain.
- Clarify customer actions after restoration.
- Maintain records of issued messages, approval decisions, timing, and distribution lists.

Status updates should include:

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Incident reference | Internal incident identifier |
| Current status | Investigating, containing, recovering, restored, monitoring |
| Confirmed impact | Services, customer groups, geographies, channels, or operations affected |
| Actions underway | High-level recovery and protection actions |
| Stakeholder action required | Any customer, employee, or partner action |
| Next update | Time and channel for further update |
| Contact point | Approved contact route |

Recovery communication must be carefully worded. A service should not be described as fully restored unless the Incident Commander and relevant service owner have confirmed stable operation. If monitoring continues, this should be stated.

Sample restoration update:

> Services for [service/channel] have been restored and are currently being monitored. Customers may experience [residual issue, if any]. We continue to investigate the cause of the incident and will provide further updates if required. If you continue to experience issues, please contact [support channel].

### Phase 7 - De-escalation and Closure

Communications may be de-escalated when:

- The Incident Commander confirms the incident is contained or resolved.
- Critical services have been restored to an agreed operational level.
- Required regulatory notifications and updates have been submitted or scheduled.
- Customer and external stakeholder updates have been issued, where required.
- Media and public interest has reduced or is manageable through normal channels.
- No further urgent crisis communication decisions are required.

Closure activities:

- Issue final stakeholder updates where appropriate.
- Confirm transition to normal communication processes.
- Archive all communication records.
- Capture lessons learned.
- Identify required changes to templates, channels, approvals, or training.
- Support the post-incident review with a communication timeline and evidence pack.

Closure communication evidence should include:

| Evidence Item | Required Content |
|---|---|
| Communication log | Time, date, audience, channel, owner, approval status |
| Approved messages | Final version of each issued message |
| Drafts and approvals | Key drafts, comments, approval records |
| Stakeholder list | Recipients and distribution groups used |
| Media records | Enquiries, responses, published statements |
| Customer communication evidence | Notices, emails, scripts, FAQs, website updates |
| Regulator communication support | Material provided to Compliance and Legal |
| Decision record | Rationale for issuing or not issuing major communications |
| Lessons learned | Issues, improvements, owners, due dates |

### Phase 8 - Post-Incident Review and Improvement

After a major ICT-related incident, crisis communication performance must be reviewed as part of the broader post-incident review.

The review should assess:

- Whether the plan was activated at the right time.
- Whether roles and approval routes were clear.
- Whether communication was timely and accurate.
- Whether internal and external messages were consistent.
- Whether customers and affected stakeholders received appropriate information.
- Whether regulatory communication support was effective.
- Whether media and social media activity was monitored and managed.
- Whether any unauthorised communication occurred.
- Whether alternative communication channels worked as expected.
- Whether communication evidence was complete and accessible.
- Whether templates and contact lists were fit for purpose.

Improvement actions must be assigned owners, due dates, and tracked to completion.

## Milestones & Timeline

The following timeline sets out the implementation plan for establishing and maintaining this Crisis Communication Plan.

| Milestone | Key Activities | Owner | Target Date | Deliverable / Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Confirm governance and ownership | Appoint Crisis Communication Lead, deputies, approvers, spokespersons, and document owner | COO / Head of Communications | [DD MMM YYYY] | Approved role assignments |
| Map stakeholder groups | Identify internal and external stakeholders for major ICT incident communications | Corporate Communications / Compliance / Business Owners | [DD MMM YYYY] | Stakeholder communication matrix |
| Define activation thresholds | Align communication activation criteria with ICT incident severity levels | CISO / Incident Response Lead / Communications | [DD MMM YYYY] | Activation and escalation criteria |
| Develop communication templates | Create holding statements, customer notices, staff advisories, media lines, FAQs, and executive update templates | Corporate Communications | [DD MMM YYYY] | Approved template pack |
| Establish approval workflow | Define standard and emergency approval routes for all communication types | Legal / Compliance / Communications | [DD MMM YYYY] | Approval workflow and delegation record |
| Validate communication channels | Test email, intranet, emergency messaging, status page, website, contact centre, and backup channels | ICT Operations / Business Continuity | [DD MMM YYYY] | Channel test results |
| Compile and verify contact lists | Confirm contact details for crisis team, executives, regulators, providers, media contacts, and deputies | Communications / Business Continuity | [DD MMM YYYY] | Current contact directory |
| Train crisis communication participants | Deliver role-based training to communications, customer operations, ICT, legal, compliance, and executives | Business Continuity Manager | [DD MMM YYYY] | Training attendance records |
| Run tabletop exercise | Exercise a major ICT incident scenario involving customer, regulator, media, and third-party communications | Crisis Management Chair / CISO | [DD MMM YYYY] | Exercise report and action plan |
| Address improvement actions | Remediate gaps identified through testing and training | Action Owners | [DD MMM YYYY] | Completed action tracker |
| Obtain plan approval | Submit plan for approval by accountable executive or governance forum | Document Owner | [DD MMM YYYY] | Approval record |
| Move into steady-state maintenance | Schedule periodic reviews, contact list tests, training, and exercises | Document Owner / Business Continuity | [DD MMM YYYY] | Maintenance calendar |

During an active major ICT-related incident, the following operational communication timeline should be used unless the Crisis Management Team approves an alternative cadence.

| Incident Timeframe | Communication Activity | Responsible Role | Expected Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-15 minutes after major incident declaration | Notify Crisis Communication Lead and join incident bridge | Incident Commander | Communications function activated |
| 15-30 minutes | Confirm known facts, potential impact, communication restrictions, and stakeholder exposure | Crisis Communication Lead | Initial communication assessment |
| 30-60 minutes | Draft internal holding message and executive brief | Corporate Communications | Draft messages for approval |
| Within 60 minutes, where practicable | Issue approved internal instructions to relevant teams | Crisis Communication Lead | Staff and operational awareness |
| Within 90 minutes, where required | Prepare external holding message or customer statement | Corporate Communications / Customer Operations | Approved external draft |
| Ongoing every [60-120 minutes] for severe incidents | Issue internal and external updates as appropriate | Crisis Communication Lead | Status updates and refreshed FAQs |
| At material change | Update stakeholders when impact, cause, recovery status, customer action, or risk changes materially | Stakeholder Owners | Targeted updates |
| After service restoration | Issue restoration or monitoring update | Corporate Communications / Service Owner | Recovery communication |
| Within [5 business days] after closure | Provide communication evidence and lessons learned to post-incident review | Crisis Communication Lead | Communication review pack |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board / Board Committee | Provides oversight of major crisis communication capability; receives updates on severe ICT incidents and post-incident lessons; ensures senior accountability for operational resilience and stakeholder communication. |
| Chief Executive Officer | Acts as ultimate executive authority for severe public or market-sensitive communications; may serve as spokesperson for the most material incidents; approves strategic messaging where required. |
| Crisis Management Chair | Leads the senior crisis response forum; approves communication strategy and priorities; resolves conflicts between speed, accuracy, legal exposure, customer needs, and reputational considerations. |
| Crisis Communication Lead | Owns activation and execution of this plan during an ICT crisis; coordinates message development, approvals, stakeholder communication, communication cadence, logs, and post-incident communication review. |
| Corporate Communications Team | Drafts and issues approved communications; manages media lines, website notices, social media, FAQs, staff messages, and communication templates; monitors media and public sentiment. |
| Incident Commander | Leads technical and operational incident response; provides confirmed facts, impact assessment, recovery status, and technical constraints to support accurate communications. |
| CISO / Security Lead | Provides security risk assessment, threat context, sensitivity restrictions, and guidance on information that must not be disclosed. |
| ICT Operations Lead | Provides status of affected systems, infrastructure, recovery activities, service restoration, and alternative channels. |
| Business Service Owner | Confirms business impact, customer consequences, service priorities, operational workarounds, and recovery acceptance criteria. |
| Chief Compliance Officer | Leads regulatory communication coordination; confirms regulatory communication obligations; ensures consistency between communications and formal notifications. |
| General Counsel / Legal Team | Reviews external, public, contractual, customer, media, and regulator-related communications; advises on liability, privilege, litigation, law enforcement, and disclosure risk. |
| Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | Advises on communication requirements where personal data may be affected; reviews customer, employee, and regulator communications involving personal data. |
| Customer Operations Lead | Provides customer impact insight; issues approved scripts to contact centres and relationship teams; monitors customer enquiries, complaints, and vulnerable customer issues. |
| Relationship Managers / Client-Facing Teams | Communicate with clients only using approved messages; escalate client concerns; do not speculate or provide unauthorised commitments. |
| Third-Party Risk Manager | Coordinates communication with critical ICT service providers; obtains provider status updates; ensures provider communications are integrated into incident communications. |
| Human Resources | Supports employee communications, workforce instructions, staff welfare messaging, and disciplinary escalation for unauthorised disclosures where required. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Ensures alignment with crisis management and business continuity arrangements; supports exercises, contact list maintenance, and lessons learned. |
| Communications Scribe / Log Keeper | Maintains the communication log, approval records, message versions, stakeholder lists, decisions, and evidence pack. |
| Authorised Spokesperson | Delivers approved media, public, customer, or market statements; does not deviate from approved messaging without authorisation. |
| All Employees | Follow internal instructions; report suspicious activity or misinformation; do not comment externally or on social media; direct enquiries to approved contacts. |

RACI summary:

| Activity | Crisis Communication Lead | Incident Commander | Legal | Compliance | Corporate Communications | Business Owner | Executive / Crisis Chair |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Activate crisis communication response | A/R | C | C | C | C | C | I |
| Confirm incident facts for messaging | C | A/R | C | C | I | C | I |
| Draft internal communication | A | C | C | C | R | C | I |
| Draft customer communication | A | C | C | C | R | C | I |
| Approve public or media statement | C | C | R | R | R | C | A |
| Coordinate regulatory communication support | C | C | C | A/R | I | C | I |
| Issue approved communications | A | I | I | I | R | R where applicable | I |
| Maintain communication log | A | I | I | I | R | I | I |
| Conduct post-incident communication review | A/R | C | C | C | R | C | I |

Legend: A = Accountable, R = Responsible, C = Consulted, I = Informed.

## Resources

The following resources are required to implement, operate, and maintain this plan.

### People and Expertise

| Resource | Purpose | Minimum Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Crisis Communication Lead and deputies | Lead communication response during major ICT incidents | Named primary and at least two alternates |
| Corporate Communications specialists | Draft, coordinate, issue, and monitor communications | Availability during crisis response, including out-of-hours arrangements |
| Legal counsel | Review external and sensitive communications | Access to internal or external counsel during severe incidents |
| Compliance lead | Coordinate regulatory communication alignment | Availability for incidents with potential regulatory impact |
| Data protection / privacy specialist | Review communications involving personal data | Available for suspected data compromise scenarios |
| ICT incident response experts | Provide accurate technical and operational facts | Integrated with communication response |
| Customer operations representatives | Translate incident facts into customer scripts and support actions | Named representatives for key service lines |
| Third-party risk representatives | Coordinate with ICT suppliers and outsourced service providers | Access to supplier escalation channels |
| Executive spokespersons | Deliver public, media, or market-sensitive statements | Trained and authorised spokesperson pool |
| Communications scribe | Maintain evidence records | Assigned for each activated crisis communication response |

### Tools and Channels

| Tool / Channel | Use | Resilience Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Emergency notification platform | Rapid alerts to crisis team and staff | Accessible outside primary corporate network |
| Email distribution lists | Internal and targeted stakeholder updates | Maintained and periodically tested |
| Secure collaboration platform | Crisis coordination and document review | Alternative available if unavailable |
| Conference bridge / virtual meeting platform | Crisis meetings and approval discussions | Backup bridge and dial-in details maintained |
| Corporate website / service status page | Public and customer service updates | Access controlled; emergency publishing route tested |
| Customer relationship management system | Targeted customer communications | Backup customer contact export available |
| Contact centre scripting platform | Approved customer service responses | Manual fallback scripts available |
| Social media management tool | Approved public updates and monitoring | Admin access restricted and recoverable |
| Media monitoring service | Track press and public commentary | Alternative manual monitoring process defined |
| Secure document repository | Store approved templates and logs | Offline copy of critical documents maintained |
| Communication log template | Record messages, approvals, and decisions | Available in online and offline formats |

### Core Documents

This plan should be maintained alongside the following documents:

- ICT Incident Response Plan.
- Crisis Management Plan.
- Business Continuity Plan.
- ICT Disaster Recovery Plans.
- Major ICT Incident Classification Standard.
- Regulatory Incident Notification Procedure.
- Data Breach Response Procedure.
- Media Relations Policy.
- Social Media Policy.
- Customer Communication Standards.
- Third-Party ICT Risk Management Procedure.
- Supplier Incident Notification Requirements.
- Contact Directory and Escalation Matrix.
- Crisis Communication Template Pack.
- Post-Incident Review Template.

### Communication Template Pack

The template pack should include, at minimum:

| Template | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Initial internal holding message | Rapid staff awareness and instruction |
| Executive briefing note | Senior leadership decision support |
| Board incident update | Board-level situational awareness |
| Customer holding statement | Early external customer communication |
| Customer detailed update | Follow-up communication with service impact and actions |
| Contact centre script | Consistent customer handling |
| Relationship manager client note | Controlled client-facing messaging |
| Website service notice | Public service status update |
| Social media holding line | Short public acknowledgement |
| Media holding statement | Press enquiry response |
| Media Q&A | Approved answers for anticipated media questions |
| Third-party provider escalation request | Supplier incident information request |
| Regulator briefing support note | Factual incident summary for Compliance |
| Restoration message | Service recovery notification |
| Final closure message | Incident closure communication |
| Lessons learned communication summary | Post-incident evidence and improvement input |

### Budget and Capacity

The document owner must ensure that adequate budget and capacity are available for:

- Training and exercises.
- Out-of-hours communication support.
- Emergency notification and status page tooling.
- Media monitoring.
- External legal or communication advisory support, where required.
- Translation and accessibility support for customer communications.
- Secure and resilient communication infrastructure.
- Maintenance of contact lists, templates, and evidence repositories.

## Success Metrics

The effectiveness of this plan will be measured using quantitative and qualitative indicators.

| Metric | Target / Threshold | Evidence Source | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Time from major incident declaration to communication lead activation | Within [15 minutes] | Incident log / communication log | Incident Commander |
| Time to first internal holding message for severe incidents | Within [60 minutes], where practicable | Communication log | Crisis Communication Lead |
| Availability of named communication deputies | 100% of critical roles have deputies | Role assignment record | Document Owner |
| Contact list accuracy | At least [95%] accuracy during tests | Contact list test results | Business Continuity Manager |
| Communication templates current and approved | 100% reviewed within required cycle | Template repository | Corporate Communications |
| External communications legally reviewed before release | 100%, except approved emergency delegation cases | Approval records | Legal |
| Regulatory communications aligned with public/customer messaging | No material inconsistencies | Post-incident review | Compliance |
| Unauthorised external communications | Zero confirmed incidents | HR / Legal / Communications reports | Crisis Communication Lead |
| Communication log completeness | 100% of issued communications logged | Communication evidence pack | Communications Scribe |
| Crisis communication exercise completion | At least annually, or more frequently if risk profile requires | Exercise records | Business Continuity Manager |
| Post-incident communication review completion | Within [30 calendar days] of incident closure | Review report | Crisis Communication Lead |
| Improvement action closure | [90%] closed by due date | Action tracker | Action Owners |
| Customer-facing message clarity | No material avoidable confusion identified in review | Complaints, call logs, customer feedback | Customer Operations |
| Channel resilience test success | Critical channels and backups tested successfully | Channel test report | ICT Operations |
| Media response consistency | 100% of media responses use approved lines | Media log | Corporate Communications |

Additional qualitative success indicators:

- Leadership had sufficient information to make timely communication decisions.
- Customer-facing teams received clear instructions before or alongside external communications.
- Messages were appropriately transparent without disclosing sensitive security details.
- Stakeholders received updates at a reasonable cadence.
- Communications reduced uncertainty and supported confidence in the response.
- Lessons learned led to demonstrable improvements in plan, templates, training, or tooling.

## Review & Update Triggers

This plan must be reviewed at least annually and whenever a material trigger occurs.

Scheduled reviews:

| Review Activity | Frequency | Owner | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full plan review | At least annually | Document Owner | Approved updated plan or review record |
| Contact list verification | At least quarterly | Business Continuity Manager | Contact test results |
| Template review | At least annually and after major incidents | Corporate Communications | Approved template versions |
| Channel resilience test | At least annually | ICT Operations | Test results |
| Role and deputy confirmation | At least semi-annually | Document Owner | Role confirmation record |
| Crisis communication exercise | At least annually | Business Continuity Manager / Crisis Management Chair | Exercise report |
| Lessons learned review | After each major ICT-related incident or exercise | Crisis Communication Lead | Action tracker |

Update triggers include:

- Major ICT-related incident affecting [Organisation Name].
- Crisis communication exercise identifying gaps or improvement opportunities.
- Material change to business services, customer base, operating model, or legal entity structure.
- Material change to ICT architecture, cloud services, outsourcing arrangements, or critical third-party providers.
- Change in crisis management, incident response, business continuity, regulatory notification, or media handling processes.
- Change in communication channels, emergency notification tools, status page arrangements, or customer contact methods.
- Change in executive leadership, authorised spokespersons, crisis roles, or deputies.
- Regulatory feedback, supervisory engagement, enforcement action, audit findings, or independent assurance findings.
- Significant industry incident that highlights relevant communication risks or good practice.
- Material change in customer vulnerability considerations, accessibility requirements, language needs, or jurisdictional footprint.
- New or changed legal, privacy, contractual, market disclosure, or customer notification obligations.
- Post-incident review identifying delays, inconsistencies, unauthorised communications, unclear approvals, or incomplete records.
- Failure of a communication channel, contact list test, or out-of-hours activation test.

All updates must be version-controlled, approved by the document owner or designated governance forum, and communicated to relevant stakeholders. Superseded versions must be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.

DORA-017.title: Awareness & Training Programme
DORA-017.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [DORA-PLAN-AWARENESS-TRAINING] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | Digital Operational Resilience Act |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose & Objectives

This plan defines how [Organisation Name] will design, deliver, evidence, and continuously improve its ICT security awareness and digital operational resilience training programme.

The programme is intended to ensure that personnel understand their role in protecting information assets, maintaining secure and resilient ICT operations, identifying and reporting threats, and supporting the organisation’s response to ICT-related incidents and disruption.

The objectives of this plan are to:

- Establish a structured, risk-based awareness and training programme covering ICT security, cyber hygiene, operational resilience, incident reporting, and safe use of digital services.
- Ensure all relevant personnel receive appropriate training based on their role, access level, responsibilities, and exposure to ICT risk.
- Provide targeted training for management, ICT staff, control functions, business continuity teams, incident response teams, third-party relationship owners, and other key roles.
- Reinforce a culture of timely reporting, secure behaviour, resilience awareness, and accountability.
- Ensure training content remains current with the organisation’s threat landscape, ICT risk profile, lessons learned, regulatory expectations, and changes to systems, processes, or suppliers.
- Maintain sufficient records to evidence completion, effectiveness, follow-up actions, and ongoing improvement.
- Support the organisation’s broader ICT risk management, business continuity, incident management, third-party risk management, and operational resilience arrangements.

The programme will be delivered through a combination of mandatory e-learning, live briefings, role-based workshops, tabletop exercises, phishing simulations, communications campaigns, induction training, and periodic refresher activities.

## Scope

This plan applies to all personnel who access, manage, support, process, or influence the security and resilience of [Organisation Name]’s ICT environment, including:

- Employees, including permanent, temporary, part-time, and fixed-term staff.
- Executive management and members of governing bodies.
- Contractors, consultants, secondees, interns, and agency workers.
- Privileged users, system administrators, developers, architects, security staff, and ICT operations personnel.
- Business owners, process owners, data owners, application owners, and service owners.
- Incident management, crisis management, business continuity, disaster recovery, and communications teams.
- Procurement, legal, compliance, risk, audit, and third-party relationship management teams.
- Personnel responsible for overseeing critical or important outsourced ICT services.
- Third-party personnel where contractually required, especially those with access to [Organisation Name] systems, data, premises, or critical ICT processes.

The programme covers awareness and training relating to:

- ICT security principles and expected user behaviour.
- Digital operational resilience and the organisation’s resilience responsibilities.
- Safe use of email, collaboration tools, mobile devices, removable media, cloud services, and remote access.
- Password, passphrase, multi-factor authentication, and credential protection practices.
- Phishing, social engineering, business email compromise, malware, ransomware, and fraud-related cyber threats.
- Data handling, confidentiality, integrity, availability, and secure sharing.
- Incident identification, escalation, reporting channels, and time-critical reporting expectations.
- Business continuity, disaster recovery, crisis response, and continuity of critical business services.
- Third-party ICT risk awareness, including the responsibilities of staff who manage outsourced ICT services.
- Secure development, change management, vulnerability management, and operational controls for technical teams.
- Lessons learned from internal incidents, near misses, tests, exercises, audits, regulatory feedback, and sector threat intelligence.

Out of scope:

- Detailed technical certification training not directly required by this plan, unless separately approved as part of role-based capability development.
- General non-ICT training, except where it supports resilience, security behaviour, incident response, or continuity objectives.
- Supplier internal training programmes, unless contractually mandated or necessary to protect [Organisation Name]’s ICT environment.

## Assumptions & Dependencies

The successful delivery of this plan depends on the following assumptions and dependencies.

| Area | Assumption / Dependency | Impact if Not Met | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Senior sponsorship | Executive management visibly supports mandatory training and participation in exercises | Low completion rates, weak culture, limited accountability | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Accurate population data | HR and identity records accurately identify personnel, joiners, movers, leavers, roles, locations, and contractor status | Training may not reach all required participants or may be assigned incorrectly | Human Resources |
| Role mapping | Critical roles and privileged access groups are clearly identified | Role-based training may be incomplete or misdirected | ICT Operations / Information Security |
| Learning platform | A learning management system or equivalent tracking mechanism is available | Inadequate completion evidence and weak audit trail | Learning & Development |
| Content ownership | Subject matter experts are available to review and update training content | Training may become outdated or misaligned to current risks | Information Security |
| Incident and testing feedback | Lessons from incidents, exercises, tests, and risk assessments are provided to the training owner | Programme may fail to reflect real threats and control weaknesses | Operational Resilience Lead |
| Communications support | Internal communications channels are available for campaigns and reminders | Reduced engagement and lower retention of key messages | Corporate Communications |
| Management enforcement | Line managers act on overdue training and repeated non-compliance | Persistent gaps may remain unresolved | Business Unit Heads |
| Supplier access control | Third-party access records identify external users requiring training | External users may create unmanaged ICT risk | Third-Party Risk Management |
| Budget | Funding is available for content development, platform licensing, simulations, and specialist training | Delays, limited coverage, or reduced quality | Finance / Chief Information Security Officer |

Key planning assumptions:

- Mandatory baseline training will be assigned to all in-scope personnel at onboarding and refreshed at least annually.
- Additional role-based training will be assigned according to job function, privileged access, criticality of responsibilities, and exposure to ICT risk.
- Personnel working on critical or important functions will receive enhanced resilience awareness relevant to their responsibilities.
- Training completion will be tracked centrally and reported to management.
- Failure to complete mandatory training within required deadlines will be escalated through line management.
- The programme will align with, and not duplicate unnecessarily, existing compliance, privacy, business continuity, and information security training activities.
- Training materials will be made accessible for personnel with disabilities and available in appropriate languages where required by the workforce profile.

## Approach / Phases

The awareness and training programme will be implemented through a structured lifecycle consisting of eight phases.

### Phase 1 - Programme Initiation and Governance

The objective of this phase is to establish ownership, governance, decision rights, and delivery controls.

Key activities:

- Confirm the programme owner, delivery lead, and supporting stakeholders.
- Approve the annual training calendar and delivery model.
- Confirm reporting cadence to relevant governance forums.
- Define mandatory completion periods, escalation paths, exception handling, and evidence requirements.
- Confirm alignment with ICT risk management, operational resilience, business continuity, incident management, third-party risk management, and HR onboarding processes.
- Establish a central repository for programme documents, completion records, content approvals, communications, metrics, and review evidence.

Expected outputs:

- Approved programme plan.
- Stakeholder register.
- Annual training calendar.
- Programme evidence repository.
- Defined escalation and exception process.

### Phase 2 - Audience Identification and Training Needs Analysis

The objective of this phase is to identify who requires training and determine the appropriate level and type of training.

Audience groups will include, at minimum:

| Audience Group | Training Need |
|---|---|
| All personnel | Baseline ICT security awareness, digital resilience responsibilities, incident reporting, secure working practices |
| New joiners | Initial onboarding training before or shortly after access to systems is granted |
| Executive management and governing body members | ICT risk oversight, resilience responsibilities, decision-making during disruption, regulatory and reputational implications |
| Line managers | Reinforcement of expected behaviours, managing overdue training, supporting incident escalation |
| Privileged users and administrators | Secure administration, credential protection, logging, vulnerability response, change discipline, incident escalation |
| ICT operations teams | Resilient operations, monitoring, incident response, backup and recovery, change and configuration practices |
| Security operations and incident response teams | Threat detection, triage, containment, escalation, evidence handling, communications, lessons learned |
| Developers and engineering teams | Secure design, secure coding, testing, secrets management, vulnerability remediation, resilience by design |
| Business continuity and crisis teams | Scenario response, continuity procedures, communications, decision-making under disruption |
| Third-party relationship owners | ICT supplier risk awareness, contractual obligations, concentration risk, exit readiness, supplier incident escalation |
| Procurement, legal, risk, compliance, and audit teams | ICT third-party oversight, resilience requirements, evidence expectations, control assurance |
| High-risk business functions | Fraud-enabled cyber threats, secure customer and transaction handling, resilience of critical processes |
| External users with system access | Security obligations, acceptable use, incident reporting, access protection, confidentiality expectations |

Training needs will be determined using:

- Role and access information from HR and identity management records.
- ICT risk assessments.
- Business impact analysis results.
- Critical or important function mapping.
- Privileged access reviews.
- Incident and near-miss trends.
- Phishing simulation outcomes.
- Audit findings and assurance results.
- Technology change and transformation plans.
- Third-party risk assessments.
- Management input and lessons learned.

Expected outputs:

- Training audience matrix.
- Role-based training assignment rules.
- List of high-risk groups requiring enhanced content.
- Exceptions and special handling requirements.

### Phase 3 - Content Design and Development

The objective of this phase is to develop practical, relevant, and current training content.

Baseline content for all personnel will include:

- Why ICT security and digital operational resilience matter to [Organisation Name].
- Individual responsibilities for secure and resilient working.
- Recognising and reporting suspicious activity, phishing, social engineering, malware, ransomware indicators, and fraud attempts.
- Correct use of passwords, passphrases, authentication methods, and password managers where applicable.
- Safe use of email, messaging, collaboration platforms, file sharing, cloud services, mobile devices, remote access, and public networks.
- Protecting confidential, personal, regulated, customer, and business-critical information.
- Physical security considerations affecting ICT assets and information.
- Acceptable use of systems, devices, networks, and corporate data.
- How to report ICT incidents, security concerns, data concerns, and service disruption.
- What to do during system outages, suspected compromise, or continuity events.
- Consequences of failing to follow required security and resilience practices.

Role-based content will include:

| Role-Based Module | Key Content |
|---|---|
| Executive and board-level awareness | Oversight responsibilities, risk appetite, resilience investment, crisis decision-making, incident communications, accountability |
| Privileged user security | Secure administration, access segregation, privileged session handling, credential vaulting, emergency access, logging expectations |
| Secure development and engineering | Secure design, code review, dependency management, vulnerability handling, environment segregation, resilience testing |
| ICT operations resilience | Monitoring, alerting, backup, restore, capacity, availability, patching, change control, operational handover |
| Incident response | Classification, escalation, containment, evidence preservation, communications, coordination with business teams |
| Business continuity and recovery | Continuity plans, workarounds, recovery priorities, manual processing, communications, return to normal operations |
| Third-party ICT risk | Due diligence, contract expectations, supplier monitoring, supplier incident escalation, exit and substitution planning |
| High-risk business function awareness | Threat scenarios relevant to the business process, secure transaction handling, customer impact, disruption workarounds |

Content design principles:

- Use plain language and role-relevant examples.
- Include realistic scenarios based on the organisation’s environment and threat profile.
- Prioritise practical behaviours over abstract compliance messaging.
- Clearly identify required actions and reporting channels.
- Include knowledge checks for mandatory modules.
- Support accessibility needs and workforce language requirements.
- Avoid unnecessary disclosure of sensitive security architecture or detailed defensive configurations.
- Include version control, content owner approval, and periodic review dates.

Expected outputs:

- Baseline training module.
- Role-based modules.
- Executive briefing pack.
- Awareness campaign materials.
- Phishing simulation templates.
- Knowledge checks and assessment questions.
- Training content approval records.

### Phase 4 - Delivery and Deployment

The objective of this phase is to deliver training through appropriate channels and ensure completion by the intended audience.

Delivery methods may include:

| Delivery Method | Use Case | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| E-learning | Mandatory baseline and refresher training | Completion records, scores, timestamps |
| Live virtual sessions | Role-based briefings and interactive Q&A | Attendance logs, materials, recordings where appropriate |
| In-person workshops | Executive, crisis, continuity, incident response, and technical training | Attendance records, agendas, action logs |
| Tabletop exercises | Incident, disruption, supplier failure, ransomware, and crisis scenarios | Exercise report, participant list, lessons learned |
| Phishing simulations | Testing susceptibility and reinforcing reporting behaviours | Campaign results, reporting rates, follow-up actions |
| Awareness campaigns | Monthly or quarterly reinforcement of key behaviours | Communications records, engagement metrics |
| Posters and intranet content | Ongoing reminders and quick-reference guidance | Published materials, update records |
| Manager toolkits | Team-level reinforcement and discussion prompts | Distribution evidence, manager attestations where used |
| Onboarding briefings | New joiners and contractors | Induction completion records |

Minimum delivery expectations:

- New joiners must complete baseline training within [Number] days of joining or before privileged/system access where required by risk.
- All personnel must complete annual refresher training within the assigned completion window.
- Privileged users must complete enhanced security training before privileged access is granted, unless a documented exception is approved.
- Personnel assigned to incident, crisis, business continuity, or recovery roles must participate in relevant exercises or workshops at planned intervals.
- Executives and governing body members must receive periodic briefings on ICT risk and digital operational resilience.
- Third-party users must receive relevant training or confirm equivalent training where contractually allowed and risk-assessed as acceptable.

Expected outputs:

- Training assignments.
- Training communications.
- Completion evidence.
- Attendance logs.
- Exercise participation records.
- Exception and escalation records.

### Phase 5 - Reinforcement and Behavioural Testing

The objective of this phase is to reinforce learning and assess whether training leads to improved behaviour.

Reinforcement activities will include:

- Periodic phishing simulations with varied difficulty and realistic scenarios.
- Targeted reminders following phishing simulation results.
- Short awareness messages aligned to current threats.
- Campaigns linked to events such as remote working, travel, year-end fraud risk, supplier incidents, or major technology changes.
- Scenario-based team discussions for high-risk functions.
- Refresher communications following internal incidents or near misses.
- Recognition of positive reporting behaviours, where appropriate.

Behavioural testing will assess:

- Susceptibility to phishing and social engineering.
- Promptness and accuracy of suspicious email reporting.
- Awareness of incident reporting channels.
- Understanding of business continuity roles.
- Compliance with mandatory training deadlines.
- Effectiveness of targeted training for high-risk groups.
- Improvements in repeat-failure groups following intervention.

Expected outputs:

- Campaign plan.
- Simulation results.
- Behavioural trend analysis.
- Targeted follow-up actions.
- Lessons learned incorporated into training updates.

### Phase 6 - Monitoring, Reporting and Escalation

The objective of this phase is to provide management with reliable visibility of programme execution, completion, gaps, and effectiveness.

Monitoring will include:

- Training assignment status.
- Completion rates by business unit, role, location, and audience group.
- Overdue training.
- Assessment pass rates.
- Reassignment and retake rates.
- Phishing simulation performance.
- Incident reporting trends.
- Participation in exercises and role-based sessions.
- Exceptions and non-compliance.
- Content review status.
- Open improvement actions.

Reporting will be provided to:

| Reporting Audience | Frequency | Content |
|---|---:|---|
| Chief Information Security Officer | Monthly | Completion status, overdue training, high-risk gaps, campaign results, issues |
| Operational Resilience Forum | Quarterly | Resilience training coverage, exercise participation, lessons learned, improvement actions |
| Risk Committee or equivalent | Quarterly | Programme effectiveness, material gaps, risk acceptance, trends |
| Executive management | At least annually and as needed | Overall maturity, key risks, investment needs, significant non-compliance |
| Internal Audit / Assurance | Upon request | Evidence of plan execution, completion records, content approvals, metrics, exceptions |

Escalation approach:

| Trigger | Escalation Path | Expected Action |
|---|---|---|
| Individual overdue training beyond [Number] days | Line manager | Reminder and completion follow-up |
