ISO41-008.title: Facility Management Manual
ISO41-008.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [FM-POL-001] | 1.0 | Facility Management System Manager | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO 41001:2018 | — Documented Information | Internal |

## Purpose

This Facility Management Manual establishes the mandatory policy requirements for creating, controlling, maintaining, retaining, and improving documented information required by the organisation’s Facility Management System (FMS) in accordance with ISO 41001:2018,.

The purpose of this Policy is to ensure that FMS documented information is:

- available and suitable for use where and when needed;
- adequately protected from loss of confidentiality, improper use, loss of integrity, or unintended modification;
- appropriately created, reviewed, approved, distributed, updated, stored, retained, and disposed of;
- identifiable, traceable, and controlled throughout its lifecycle;
- sufficient to demonstrate conformity with ISO 41001:2018 and effective operation of the FMS;
- aligned with organisational objectives, facility management requirements, statutory and regulatory obligations, and stakeholder needs.

This Manual serves as the top-level documented information policy for the FMS and defines the governance framework for all FMS policies, procedures, plans, records, registers, reports, specifications, service requirements, contractual facility management information, and other controlled information necessary to support effective facility management performance.

## Scope

This Policy applies to all documented information required for the establishment, implementation, maintenance, evaluation, and continual improvement of the FMS.

The scope includes documented information:

- required by ISO 41001:2018;
- determined by the organisation as necessary for the effectiveness of the FMS;
- required to demonstrate planning, operation, performance evaluation, and improvement of facility management activities;
- required by legal, regulatory, contractual, occupational health and safety, environmental, security, asset management, quality, business continuity, and other applicable obligations;
- created or maintained by internal personnel, outsourced service providers, contractors, consultants, and other relevant parties acting on behalf of the organisation.

This Policy applies to documented information in any format or medium, including but not limited to:

- electronic documents and records;
- physical hard-copy documents;
- drawings, floor plans, schematics, asset registers, and building information models;
- service specifications and service level agreements;
- maintenance schedules and inspection records;
- statutory compliance certificates;
- risk assessments and method statements;
- emergency and continuity plans;
- performance reports and audit records;
- meeting minutes, approvals, action logs, and management review outputs;
- contractor and supplier documentation;
- FMS policies, objectives, processes, procedures, work instructions, templates, and forms.

This Policy applies to all locations, facilities, services, departments, functions, and persons within the defined scope of the FMS, including outsourced or externally provided facility management activities where the organisation retains accountability for conformity.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall establish, implement, maintain, and continually improve documented information necessary to support the effective operation of the Facility Management System in accordance with ISO 41001:2018,.

2. The organisation shall determine the documented information required by ISO 41001:2018 and the documented information determined by the organisation as necessary for the effectiveness of the FMS.

3. The organisation shall maintain this Facility Management Manual as the top-level FMS documented information policy that defines mandatory requirements for document and record control across the FMS.

4. The organisation shall ensure that all FMS documented information is appropriate to the organisation’s purpose, context, facility management objectives, stakeholder requirements, legal and regulatory obligations, and the scope of the FMS.

5. The organisation shall ensure that documented information supports the planning, delivery, monitoring, evaluation, audit, management review, and improvement of facility management services.

6. The organisation shall ensure that documented information is created and updated in a controlled manner.

7. Each FMS document shall have a clearly identifiable title, document identifier, owner, version number, approval authority, effective date, classification, and review period.

8. Each FMS record shall be identifiable, legible, retrievable, protected, retained for the required period, and disposed of in accordance with approved retention and disposal requirements.

9. The organisation shall ensure that documented information is reviewed and approved for suitability and adequacy prior to issue.

10. Only authorised personnel shall approve FMS documented information prior to release, use, or publication.

11. The organisation shall ensure that changes to documented information are reviewed, approved, version-controlled, communicated, and traceable.

12. The organisation shall prevent unintended use of obsolete FMS documented information.

13. Obsolete documented information retained for legal, knowledge preservation, contractual, historical, or audit purposes shall be clearly identified as obsolete, superseded, archived, or withdrawn.

14. The organisation shall ensure that current versions of applicable FMS documented information are available at the point of use.

15. Documented information shall be stored in approved repositories that support appropriate access control, retention, backup, recovery, traceability, and integrity.

16. FMS documented information shall be protected from unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, deletion, damage, deterioration, or loss.

17. Access to FMS documented information shall be granted based on business need, role requirements, legal obligations, confidentiality classification, and information security requirements.

18. The organisation shall maintain a controlled FMS document register identifying approved FMS documents, owners, versions, approval dates, review dates, status, classification, and storage locations.

19. The organisation shall maintain an FMS records register or retention schedule identifying required records, retention periods, responsible owners, storage locations, and disposal requirements.

20. The organisation shall define mandatory document control requirements for FMS documented information, including identification, description, format, media, review, approval, distribution, access, retrieval, storage, preservation, change control, retention, and disposal.

21. The organisation shall ensure that externally originated documented information determined as necessary for the planning and operation of the FMS is identified and controlled.

22. Externally originated documented information shall include, where applicable, legislation, regulations, standards, codes of practice, landlord requirements, manufacturer manuals, contractor documents, supplier certificates, warranties, permits, statutory inspection reports, and client requirements.

23. The organisation shall ensure that externally provided facility management service providers comply with applicable FMS documented information control requirements.

24. Contractors, suppliers, consultants, and outsourced service providers shall submit required FMS records in the required format, within required timelines, and through approved channels.

25. The organisation shall ensure that facility management service specifications, service level agreements, maintenance requirements, inspection schedules, compliance records, operational plans, and performance evidence are maintained as controlled documented information.

26. The organisation shall ensure that FMS documented information is sufficient to provide evidence of conformity with applicable facility management requirements and the effective operation of the FMS.

27. The organisation shall ensure that documented information required for statutory, regulatory, health and safety, environmental, security, asset, and operational compliance is retained for no less than the minimum period required by law, contract, or organisational requirement, whichever is longer.

28. The organisation shall maintain documented information to support facility management objectives, including measurement criteria, performance indicators, monitoring results, analysis, improvement actions, and evidence of achievement.

29. The organisation shall maintain documented information needed to support operational planning and control of facility management services.

30. The organisation shall maintain documented information required to demonstrate competence, awareness, communication, procurement control, supplier performance, emergency preparedness, audit, nonconformity management, corrective action, and management review within the FMS.

31. The organisation shall ensure that FMS documented information is written in a clear, consistent, and usable manner appropriate to the intended audience and operational context.

32. The organisation shall ensure that document formats, templates, naming conventions, metadata, and approval workflows are standardised where practical to enable consistency, retrieval, and auditability.

33. FMS documented information shall be classified according to its sensitivity, criticality, legal status, and operational importance.

34. The organisation shall ensure that confidential, security-sensitive, commercially sensitive, or personally identifiable information within FMS documents and records is protected in accordance with applicable information security, privacy, and data protection requirements.

35. FMS records shall not be destroyed, altered, concealed, falsified, or removed except in accordance with authorised retention and disposal requirements.

36. Any suspected loss, unauthorised disclosure, unauthorised modification, or destruction of FMS documented information shall be reported and managed as an incident in accordance with applicable organisational incident management requirements.

37. Documented information relevant to emergency response, life safety, statutory compliance, critical assets, business continuity, and essential facility services shall be readily accessible to authorised personnel when required.

38. The organisation shall ensure that personnel are made aware of applicable FMS documented information and their responsibilities for using, maintaining, and protecting it.

39. The organisation shall ensure that documented information is available to internal auditors, external auditors, regulators, clients, certification bodies, and other authorised interested parties when required, subject to applicable confidentiality and access requirements.

40. The organisation shall monitor the effectiveness of FMS documented information controls through audits, management review, compliance checks, document reviews, record sampling, corrective actions, and performance monitoring.

41. The organisation shall ensure that nonconformities relating to FMS documented information are recorded, investigated, corrected, and subject to corrective action where required.

42. The organisation shall continually improve the adequacy, suitability, accessibility, integrity, and effectiveness of FMS documented information controls.

The following minimum FMS documented information set shall be maintained unless formally justified as not applicable within the FMS scope:

| Documented Information Category | Minimum Requirement | Typical Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| FMS scope and context | The boundaries, applicability, internal and external issues, and interested party requirements relevant to the FMS shall be documented and maintained. | FMS scope statement, context analysis, interested parties register |
| Facility management policy and objectives | Approved FM policy, objectives, measures, and plans to achieve objectives shall be maintained. | FM policy, objectives register, KPI dashboard |
| Roles, responsibilities, and authorities | Responsibilities and authorities for FMS operation and governance shall be documented. | Organisation chart, RACI matrix, job descriptions |
| Operational planning and control | Documented requirements for delivering FM services shall be maintained. | Service plans, work instructions, maintenance plans, inspection schedules |
| Asset and facility information | Key facility, asset, space, and infrastructure information shall be controlled. | Asset register, space register, drawings, BIM data, equipment manuals |
| Compliance evidence | Records demonstrating statutory, regulatory, contractual, and other compliance obligations shall be retained. | Permits, certificates, inspection records, compliance register |
| Supplier and contractor information | Documented information required to control outsourced FM services shall be maintained. | Contracts, SLAs, method statements, RAMS, contractor performance reports |
| Performance evaluation | Records of monitoring, measurement, analysis, evaluation, audit, and management review shall be maintained. | KPI reports, audit reports, management review minutes |
| Nonconformity and improvement | Nonconformities, corrective actions, lessons learned, and improvement records shall be maintained. | Corrective action register, improvement log, incident records |
| Document and record control | Document registers, retention schedules, approval evidence, and version histories shall be maintained. | Controlled document register, records retention schedule, approval workflow logs |

The following document control metadata shall be applied to controlled FMS documents:

| Metadata Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Document title | Shall clearly describe the document purpose or subject. |
| Document identifier | Shall be unique and traceable within the FMS document register. |
| Version number | Shall identify the current approved version and support change history. |
| Owner | Shall identify the accountable role or function responsible for the document. |
| Approver | Shall identify the authorised role approving the document for use. |
| Effective date | Shall identify when the document becomes applicable. |
| Review date | Shall identify the next planned review date. |
| Status | Shall identify whether the document is draft, approved, superseded, obsolete, archived, or withdrawn. |
| Classification | Shall identify the information classification and handling requirements. |
| Storage location | Shall identify the approved repository or physical location. |
| Change history | Shall summarise material changes between versions. |

The organisation shall apply the following minimum retention requirements unless superseded by stricter legal, regulatory, contractual, insurance, or organisational requirements:

| Record Type | Minimum Retention Period | Responsible Owner |
|---|---:|---|
| Approved FMS policies, manuals, and procedures | Current version plus 7 years | FMS Manager |
| FMS scope, context, and interested party records | Current version plus 7 years | FMS Manager |
| FM objectives, plans, and performance records | 7 years | FMS Manager |
| Statutory inspection and compliance certificates | As legally required, or 7 years minimum | Compliance Manager / Facilities Manager |
| Asset maintenance records | Life of asset plus 7 years | Facilities Manager |
| Critical asset maintenance and inspection records | Life of asset plus 7 years | Facilities Manager |
| Contractor compliance records | Contract term plus 7 years | Procurement Manager / Facilities Manager |
| Supplier and contractor performance records | 7 years | Procurement Manager / Facilities Manager |
| Internal audit records | 7 years | Internal Audit Lead |
| Management review records | 7 years | Top Management / FMS Manager |
| Nonconformity and corrective action records | 7 years after closure | FMS Manager |
| Training, competence, and awareness records | Employment or engagement term plus 7 years | Human Resources / FMS Manager |
| Emergency preparedness and response records | 7 years | Facilities Manager / Business Continuity Manager |
| Incident reports affecting facilities or FMS performance | 7 years, or longer where legally required | Facilities Manager / Risk Manager |
| Obsolete controlled documents retained for reference | As defined by document owner and retention schedule | Document Owner |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Top Management | Shall ensure that adequate resources, governance, accountability, and authority are provided for effective control of FMS documented information. Shall demonstrate leadership and commitment by requiring conformity with this Policy and reviewing FMS documented information effectiveness during management review. |
| Facility Management System Manager | Shall own this Policy, maintain the FMS documentation framework, ensure documented information required by ISO 41001:2018 is established and controlled, maintain the controlled document register, coordinate document reviews, and report document control performance to management. |
| Facilities Manager | Shall ensure that operational facility management documentation and records are created, maintained, accessible, accurate, and retained, including maintenance records, inspection schedules, asset information, service delivery evidence, statutory records, and contractor submissions. |
| Document Owners | Shall create, update, review, and maintain assigned documents; ensure technical accuracy and suitability; initiate revisions when requirements change; approve or obtain approval for changes; and ensure obsolete content is withdrawn from use. |
| Document Approvers | Shall review and approve documented information for adequacy, suitability, compliance, and alignment with FMS requirements before release. |
| Records Owners | Shall ensure records under their control are complete, accurate, legible, protected, retrievable, retained, and disposed of in accordance with approved requirements. |
| Compliance Manager | Shall identify legal, regulatory, statutory, contractual, and other compliance obligations affecting FMS documented information and verify that required evidence is maintained. |
| Quality / Management Systems Function | Shall support document control governance, audit readiness, corrective action tracking, and continual improvement of the FMS documented information framework. |
| Internal Audit Lead | Shall audit conformity with ISO 41001:2018 and this Policy, report findings, and verify closure of corrective actions relating to documented information. |
| Information Security / IT Function | Shall ensure approved electronic repositories provide appropriate access control, backup, recovery, availability, integrity, monitoring, and protection for FMS documented information. |
| Procurement / Contract Management Function | Shall ensure supplier and contractor documentation requirements are defined in procurement and contract documents and that required records are obtained, reviewed, controlled, and retained. |
| Human Resources / Training Function | Shall retain competence, awareness, training, and qualification records required to support FMS effectiveness. |
| Contractors, Suppliers, and Outsourced Service Providers | Shall comply with applicable FMS document and record requirements, submit accurate and timely documented information, protect organisational information, and use only current approved documents when providing facility management services. |
| All Personnel | Shall use current approved FMS documented information, comply with this Policy, protect FMS documents and records, report inaccuracies or obsolete information, and create records that are accurate, timely, complete, and truthful. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all personnel and relevant external parties within the scope of the FMS.

The organisation shall monitor conformity with this Policy through planned and risk-based activities, including:

- internal audits against ISO 41001:2018 requirements;
- document register reviews;
- record sampling and retention checks;
- operational compliance inspections;
- contractor documentation checks;
- statutory compliance evidence reviews;
- access control and repository reviews;
- management system performance monitoring;
- nonconformity and corrective action trend analysis;
- management review.

The following minimum monitoring activities shall be performed:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of controlled FMS document register | Quarterly | FMS Manager | Updated register, review notes |
| Review of overdue document reviews | Monthly | FMS Manager | Overdue review report, action log |
| Sampling of FMS records for completeness and retrievability | Quarterly | FMS Manager / Records Owners | Sampling results, corrective actions |
| Statutory compliance documentation review | Monthly or as required by obligation | Compliance Manager / Facilities Manager | Compliance register, certificates, inspection reports |
| Contractor documentation compliance check | At onboarding, renewal, and at defined contract intervals | Procurement Manager / Facilities Manager | Contractor document checklist, approval evidence |
| Internal audit of controls | At least annually | Internal Audit Lead | Internal audit report |
| Repository access review for FMS documentation | At least annually | Information Security / IT Function | Access review record |
| Management review of documented information effectiveness | At least annually | Top Management / FMS Manager | Management review minutes |

Policy violations may include, but are not limited to:

- use of obsolete or uncontrolled FMS documents;
- failure to create or retain required FMS records;
- unauthorised alteration, deletion, removal, or destruction of documented information;
- failure to protect confidential or sensitive FMS information;
- failure to provide required contractor or supplier documentation;
- failure to approve documents before release;
- failure to maintain statutory or regulatory compliance evidence;
- falsification or intentional misrepresentation of FMS records;
- failure to correct identified document control nonconformities.

Where nonconformity is identified, the organisation shall take appropriate action, which may include:

- immediate correction or containment;
- withdrawal or replacement of uncontrolled or obsolete documents;
- recovery or reconstruction of missing records where possible;
- root cause analysis;
- corrective action;
- additional training or awareness;
- supplier or contractor performance action;
- disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policy;
- escalation to legal, compliance, risk, or executive management where required;
- notification to regulators, clients, insurers, or other authorities where legally or contractually required.

Failure to comply with this Policy may result in disciplinary action, contract remedies, supplier corrective action, termination of access, termination of contract, or other enforcement action appropriate to the nature and severity of the violation.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business, legal, technical, operational, or emergency justification and where the exception does not compromise the effectiveness of the FMS, legal or regulatory compliance, life safety, statutory obligations, information security, or ISO 41001:2018 conformity.

All exceptions shall be formally documented, risk assessed, approved, time-bound, and reviewed.

Exception requests shall include, at minimum:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Exception identifier | Unique reference number assigned to the exception request. |
| Requestor | Name, role, and function of the person requesting the exception. |
| Requirement affected | Specific policy statement, document control requirement, or record requirement affected. |
| Business justification | Explanation of why the exception is necessary. |
| Risk assessment | Assessment of risks to FMS effectiveness, compliance, operations, safety, confidentiality, integrity, and availability. |
| Compensating controls | Measures implemented to reduce risk during the exception period. |
| Duration | Start date, expiry date, and review date. |
| Approval | Approval by the FMS Manager and any additional required authority based on risk. |
| Closure criteria | Conditions required to end the exception and return to normal compliance. |

Exceptions shall not be used to avoid statutory, regulatory, contractual, health and safety, or certification requirements.

Emergency exceptions may be verbally authorised by an appropriate senior manager where immediate action is necessary to protect life, safety, assets, operations, or the environment. Emergency exceptions shall be documented retrospectively within [number] business days and shall be subject to formal review and approval.

The FMS Manager shall maintain an exceptions register and report active and overdue exceptions to Top Management as part of FMS governance and management review.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect the FMS documented information framework, including:

- changes to ISO 41001:2018 requirements or certification expectations;
- changes to the FMS scope, facilities, services, processes, or organisational structure;
- changes in legal, regulatory, statutory, contractual, or stakeholder requirements;
- changes to outsourced facility management arrangements;
- significant audit findings, nonconformities, incidents, or compliance failures;
- changes to document repositories, systems, information security controls, or record retention requirements;
- management review decisions requiring policy update;
- evidence that documented information controls are ineffective or unsuitable.

The FMS Manager shall coordinate the review and maintenance of this Policy. Updates shall be reviewed and approved by authorised management prior to release.

All revisions shall be recorded in a document change history. Superseded versions shall be withdrawn from general use and retained only in accordance with approved retention requirements.

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Author | Approver |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Initial issue | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |

ISO41-009.title: FM Policy
ISO41-009.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [FM-POL-001] | 1.0 | [Facilities Management Executive / Head of Facilities Management] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO 41001:2018 — Facility Management Management Systems | — Policy | Internal |

## Purpose

This FM Policy establishes the organisation’s leadership-approved commitment to a facility management management system aligned with ISO 41001:2018. It defines mandatory policy requirements for facility management (“FM”) that are appropriate to the organisation’s purpose, context and strategic direction, and that support the achievement of intended FM outcomes.

This Policy provides the basis for setting FM objectives, meeting applicable requirements, managing risks and opportunities, delivering effective facility services, supporting demand organisation needs, and continually improving the FM management system.

## Scope

This Policy applies to all facility management activities, services, assets, locations, workplaces, infrastructure, contracted services and supporting processes within the boundaries of the organisation’s FM management system.

Unless otherwise stated in the FM management system scope, this Policy applies to:

- all owned, leased, occupied or managed facilities under the organisation’s control;
- all internal personnel involved in planning, procuring, delivering, monitoring or improving FM services;
- outsourced FM providers, contractors, consultants and suppliers acting on behalf of the organisation;
- FM services supporting the demand organisation, including workplace, property, maintenance, utilities, cleaning, catering, security, space management, environmental services, health and safety interfaces, business continuity support and related support services, where applicable;
- FM-related decisions that affect people, places, assets, operational performance, service continuity, sustainability, legal compliance or stakeholder satisfaction.

This Policy does not replace statutory, regulatory, contractual, health and safety, environmental, security or financial requirements. Where such requirements impose a higher standard, the higher standard shall apply.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall establish, implement, maintain and continually improve a facility management management system consistent with ISO 41001:2018 and aligned with the organisation’s purpose, context, values and strategic direction.

2. Top management shall approve, communicate and support this FM Policy as the formal statement of the organisation’s commitment to effective facility management.

3. The FM Policy shall be appropriate to the organisation’s nature, scale, facilities, services, stakeholder needs, operational context, risks and opportunities.

4. The FM Policy shall provide a framework for establishing, reviewing and updating FM objectives that are measurable where practicable and aligned with organisational priorities.

5. FM objectives shall support the needs of the demand organisation, users, customers, service recipients and other relevant interested parties.

6. The organisation shall ensure that FM services support the achievement of intended outcomes, including safe, functional, compliant, effective, efficient and sustainable facilities and workplaces.

7. The organisation shall identify and fulfil applicable legal, regulatory, statutory, contractual, financial, health, safety, environmental, security, accessibility and other compliance obligations relevant to FM activities and services.

8. FM activities shall be planned and delivered using a risk-based approach, including consideration of operational continuity, asset condition, service criticality, user needs, safety, environmental impact, supplier dependency and business priorities.

9. The organisation shall ensure that FM planning, service delivery and performance evaluation consider the requirements of relevant interested parties, including employees, occupants, visitors, customers, regulators, landlords, tenants, service providers, emergency responders, insurers and local communities, where applicable.

10. The organisation shall define, document and maintain FM requirements, service levels and performance expectations for relevant FM services.

11. The organisation shall ensure that FM services are delivered by competent persons with appropriate skills, qualifications, training, supervision and awareness of applicable FM requirements.

12. The organisation shall ensure that outsourced FM services are controlled to achieve required outcomes and remain consistent with this Policy, ISO 41001:2018 requirements and applicable contractual obligations.

13. The organisation shall allocate appropriate resources for the establishment, implementation, maintenance and continual improvement of the FM management system, including people, infrastructure, technology, information, financial resources and external support where required.

14. The organisation shall integrate FM requirements into relevant organisational planning, procurement, change management, asset management, business continuity, health and safety, environmental management, security and financial management processes.

15. The organisation shall ensure that FM decision-making considers lifecycle value, operational performance, cost effectiveness, service quality, resilience, user experience, compliance obligations and sustainability impacts.

16. The organisation shall promote effective communication, consultation and coordination between FM, the demand organisation, service users, internal functions and external providers.

17. The organisation shall maintain documented information necessary to support effective FM planning, service delivery, performance monitoring, compliance demonstration and continual improvement.

18. The organisation shall monitor, measure, analyse and evaluate FM performance against defined objectives, service levels, compliance obligations, stakeholder requirements and management system criteria.

19. The organisation shall address nonconformities, service failures, incidents, complaints and performance deviations through appropriate corrective action and improvement processes.

20. The organisation shall promote continual improvement of the FM management system, FM services and facility outcomes through performance review, audit results, stakeholder feedback, lessons learned, innovation and management review.

21. The organisation shall ensure that this FM Policy is available as documented information, communicated within the organisation, and made available to relevant interested parties as appropriate.

22. All personnel and service providers within scope shall comply with this Policy and shall perform FM-related activities in accordance with approved FM processes, service requirements, controls and delegated authorities.

23. The organisation shall ensure that FM policy commitments are reflected in relevant contracts, service specifications, supplier performance requirements and internal procedures where applicable.

24. The organisation shall not knowingly accept FM practices that create unmanaged risks to legal compliance, user safety, service continuity, asset integrity, environmental performance, security or organisational reputation.

25. Top management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment by ensuring accountability for FM effectiveness, promoting the intended outcomes of the FM management system and supporting continual improvement.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Top Management | Approves and visibly supports this Policy; ensures alignment with organisational strategy; provides resources; assigns responsibilities and authorities; promotes continual improvement; reviews FM performance through management review. |
| FM Executive / Head of Facilities Management | Owns this Policy; establishes and maintains the FM management system; ensures FM objectives are set; oversees service delivery, compliance, performance monitoring and improvement; reports FM performance to top management. |
| FM Management System Representative / FM Compliance Lead | Coordinates ISO 41001:2018 alignment; maintains documented information; supports internal audits, compliance reviews, corrective actions and management review inputs. |
| Department Heads / Business Unit Leaders | Communicate FM needs and demand requirements; support implementation of FM controls within their areas; cooperate with FM planning, workplace changes, service performance reviews and improvement activities. |
| FM Service Managers | Implement FM processes and service requirements; manage operational risks; monitor service levels; control contractors; maintain records; escalate issues and nonconformities. |
| Procurement / Commercial Management | Ensures FM supplier procurement and contracts include applicable policy, service, compliance, competence, reporting and performance requirements. |
| Health, Safety, Environment and Security Functions | Provide specialist requirements and assurance for FM-related safety, environmental, emergency, physical security and regulatory obligations. |
| Finance | Supports FM budgeting, cost control, lifecycle planning and financial governance for FM services and assets. |
| Employees, Occupants and Users | Use facilities responsibly; follow applicable FM instructions; report hazards, defects, incidents, service issues and improvement opportunities. |
| Contractors, Suppliers and Outsourced FM Providers | Comply with this Policy, contractual requirements, site rules, legal obligations and FM management system requirements; provide required records and performance information. |
| Internal Audit / Assurance Function | Performs independent assurance activities, where assigned, to assess conformity with this Policy, ISO 41001:2018 requirements and related controls. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all personnel, contractors, suppliers and service providers within scope.

The organisation shall monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of this Policy and the FM management system through planned and risk-based assurance activities, including performance measurement, compliance checks, supplier reviews, internal audits and management review.

Minimum monitoring requirements are defined below.

| Monitoring Activity | Minimum Frequency | Accountable Role | Evidence / Records |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of FM objectives and progress against targets | Quarterly | FM Executive / Head of Facilities Management | FM performance dashboard, objective tracker, meeting minutes |
| Service level and KPI performance review | Monthly or as contractually defined | FM Service Managers | KPI reports, service review records, corrective action logs |
| Compliance obligation review for FM activities | At least annually and upon significant change | FM Compliance Lead with relevant specialists | Compliance register, legal update records, action plans |
| Supplier and outsourced service provider performance review | Quarterly or as risk-rated | FM Service Managers / Procurement | Supplier scorecards, review minutes, nonconformance records |
| Internal audit of FM management system requirements | At least annually according to audit programme | Internal Audit / FM Compliance Lead | Audit plan, audit reports, findings, corrective actions |
| FM management review input and reporting | At least annually | FM Executive / Top Management | Management review pack, decisions, actions |
| Policy awareness and communication confirmation | At onboarding and upon material update | FM Executive / HR / Line Managers | Training records, acknowledgements, communication logs |
| Corrective action status review | Monthly until closure | FM Compliance Lead / Action Owners | Corrective action register, closure evidence |

Noncompliance with this Policy shall be recorded, assessed and addressed in accordance with the organisation’s corrective action and disciplinary processes, contractual remedies or supplier management procedures, as applicable.

Enforcement actions may include:

- requirement to complete remedial training or awareness activities;
- formal corrective action and root cause analysis;
- escalation to senior management;
- suspension of unsafe or noncompliant work;
- withholding of acceptance or payment for nonconforming services, where contractually permitted;
- supplier performance improvement plans;
- contract remedies, including termination where justified;
- employee disciplinary action in accordance with [HR disciplinary procedure].

Serious or repeated breaches that may affect legal compliance, health and safety, environmental obligations, service continuity, security, asset integrity or organisational reputation shall be escalated promptly to top management and relevant assurance or specialist functions.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy are permitted only where compliance is not feasible, would create a greater risk, or is temporarily impracticable due to documented operational, legal, contractual, emergency or business continuity constraints.

All exceptions shall:

1. be documented using the approved exception process;
2. include the reason for the exception and the specific policy requirement affected;
3. include a risk assessment and any required compensating controls;
4. identify an accountable owner;
5. specify an expiry date or review date;
6. be approved by the FM Executive / Head of Facilities Management and, where material, by top management or another delegated authority;
7. be reviewed periodically until closure;
8. not waive applicable legal, regulatory or statutory requirements.

Emergency deviations may be approved verbally by an authorised leader where immediate action is required to protect life, safety, security, critical services or assets. Such deviations shall be documented retrospectively within [5 business days].

| Exception Attribute | Required Information |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | [EXC-YYYY-###] |
| Policy requirement affected | Clause number from this Policy |
| Facility / service affected | [Facility, site, service or contract] |
| Justification | Business, operational, legal or emergency rationale |
| Risk assessment | Impact, likelihood, affected interested parties and risk rating |
| Compensating controls | Temporary controls to reduce risk |
| Owner | Named accountable person |
| Approval authority | FM Executive / Top Management / delegated authority |
| Expiry or review date | Defined date not exceeding [12 months] unless reapproved |
| Closure evidence | Evidence that normal compliance has resumed or permanent control is approved |

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at planned intervals and when significant changes occur to ensure it remains suitable, adequate and effective.

At a minimum, the Policy shall be reviewed annually by the FM Executive / Head of Facilities Management and approved by top management.

The review shall consider:

- changes to organisational strategy, context, facilities, occupancy, services or operating model;
- changes to applicable legal, regulatory, statutory, contractual or other obligations;
- changes in the needs and expectations of relevant interested parties;
- FM performance results and progress against FM objectives;
- audit findings, nonconformities and corrective actions;
- supplier performance and outsourced service outcomes;
- incidents, disruptions, complaints and lessons learned;
- risks and opportunities affecting the FM management system;
- management review outputs;
- changes to ISO 41001:2018 or related management system requirements.

| Review Trigger | Required Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduled annual review | Assess continued suitability and recommend approval or updates | FM Executive / Head of Facilities Management |
| Significant organisational or facility change | Review impact on FM commitments, scope and objectives | FM Executive / FM Compliance Lead |
| Significant legal, regulatory or contractual change | Update policy or related controls as needed | FM Compliance Lead / Legal / Procurement |
| Major FM incident, nonconformity or audit finding | Assess whether policy changes are required | FM Executive / Corrective Action Owner |
| Management review decision | Implement approved policy updates | FM Executive / Document Control |

Approved changes shall be version-controlled, communicated to relevant personnel and interested parties as appropriate, and retained as documented information.

The current approved version of this Policy shall be maintained in [document management system / repository], and superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document retention requirements.

ISO41-010.title: FM Objectives & Targets
ISO41-010.content:
| Metadata | Details |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [FM-POL-006-002] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [Head of Facilities Management] |
| Effective Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Framework | ISO 41001:2018 — Facility Management Management Systems |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes mandatory requirements for defining, approving, communicating, monitoring, reviewing and updating Facility Management (FM) objectives and targets in alignment with ISO 41001:2018.

The purpose of this Policy is to ensure that FM objectives are measurable, consistent with the FM policy, aligned with organisational needs, and supported by plans that identify what will be done, required resources, responsibilities, completion timeframes and evaluation methods.

## Scope

This Policy applies to all FM activities, services, processes, locations, assets, service providers and personnel within the scope of the organisation’s ISO 41001:2018 Facility Management Management System.

This includes, but is not limited to:

- Buildings, workplaces, sites, campuses and facilities under the organisation’s control.
- Hard FM services, including maintenance, utilities, building systems, technical services, asset management and statutory compliance activities.
- Soft FM services, including cleaning, security, reception, mailroom, catering, waste management, grounds maintenance and workplace support services.
- Internal FM teams, contracted service providers, consultants and other parties performing FM activities on behalf of the organisation.
- FM objectives established at strategic, tactical and operational levels.
- Objectives related to service quality, user experience, compliance, health and safety, sustainability, business continuity, cost management, asset performance, space utilisation and supplier performance.

This Policy applies to all personnel who define, approve, deliver, monitor, report on or influence FM objectives and targets.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall establish FM objectives at relevant functions, levels and processes within the Facility Management Management System.

2. FM objectives shall be consistent with the organisation’s FM policy and shall support the intended outcomes of the Facility Management Management System.

3. FM objectives shall be aligned with applicable organisational objectives, business requirements, stakeholder needs, service-level commitments, statutory and regulatory obligations, and relevant operational risks and opportunities.

4. FM objectives shall be measurable, or capable of performance evaluation through defined qualitative or quantitative criteria.

5. Each FM objective shall have one or more defined targets or performance indicators that allow progress and achievement to be assessed objectively.

6. FM objectives shall be documented and maintained as controlled information.

7. FM objectives shall be communicated to relevant personnel, service providers and interested parties whose activities affect achievement of the objectives.

8. FM objectives shall be established using a structured planning process that defines, at a minimum:
 - What will be done.
 - The resources required.
 - Who is responsible.
 - When actions will be completed.
 - How results will be evaluated.

9. FM objectives shall be reviewed for relevance and effectiveness at planned intervals and whenever significant changes occur to organisational priorities, facilities, service delivery models, legal requirements, operational risks or stakeholder expectations.

10. FM objectives shall be updated as appropriate to ensure continued alignment with the FM policy, organisational context, stakeholder requirements and performance results.

11. FM objectives shall be suitable to the nature, scale and complexity of the organisation’s facilities and FM services.

12. FM objectives shall address, where applicable, both planned service performance and improvement of the FM Management System.

13. FM objectives shall include both leading and lagging indicators where appropriate, to support proactive management and continual improvement.

14. FM objectives shall be risk-informed and shall consider identified FM risks and opportunities, including operational disruption, asset failure, health and safety exposure, environmental impact, supplier underperformance, compliance failure and user dissatisfaction.

15. FM objectives shall be realistic and achievable within approved resources, budgets and operational constraints.

16. FM objectives shall include defined baselines where required to demonstrate improvement or performance against an established reference point.

17. Targets shall be time-bound and shall specify the period, deadline or review cycle for achievement.

18. FM objectives shall be prioritised based on organisational impact, criticality, risk, stakeholder value, compliance obligations and available resources.

19. FM objectives shall not conflict with statutory, regulatory, health and safety, environmental, security, accessibility or business continuity obligations.

20. FM objectives shall be integrated, where appropriate, into FM plans, service specifications, supplier contracts, service level agreements, preventive maintenance plans, asset management plans, sustainability plans and business continuity arrangements.

21. The organisation shall maintain an FM Objectives Register or equivalent controlled record to document approved FM objectives and targets.

22. The FM Objectives Register shall include, at a minimum, the following information:

| Required Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Objective ID | Unique reference for each FM objective. |
| Objective Statement | Clear description of the intended result. |
| Alignment | Link to FM policy commitment, organisational priority, stakeholder need, risk, opportunity or compliance obligation. |
| Target / KPI | Measurable target or performance indicator. |
| Baseline | Current or prior performance level, where applicable. |
| Owner | Accountable person or role responsible for delivery. |
| Supporting Actions | Key actions required to achieve the objective. |
| Resources Required | Budget, personnel, systems, equipment, data or supplier support required. |
| Due Date / Review Date | Completion date or scheduled review date. |
| Evaluation Method | Method for measuring achievement and verifying results. |
| Status | Current status, such as Not Started, In Progress, At Risk, Achieved or Not Achieved. |
| Evidence Location | Location of supporting records and evidence. |

23. FM objectives shall be approved by authorised management before implementation.

24. Changes to approved FM objectives, targets, due dates or evaluation methods shall be documented, justified and approved by the relevant authority.

25. FM objective achievement shall be monitored at planned intervals using reliable data sources, including FM systems, service reports, audits, inspections, surveys, financial data, supplier performance data and compliance records.

26. The organisation shall define review frequencies for FM objectives based on risk, criticality and performance impact.

| Objective Category | Minimum Review Frequency | Typical Review Forum |
|---|---:|---|
| Statutory compliance and life safety objectives | Monthly | FM compliance meeting or risk review |
| Critical asset and service availability objectives | Monthly | Operational performance review |
| Supplier service level objectives | Monthly or quarterly | Supplier performance review |
| User satisfaction and workplace experience objectives | Quarterly | FM performance review |
| Energy, environmental and sustainability objectives | Quarterly | Sustainability or FM management review |
| Cost, budget and efficiency objectives | Monthly or quarterly | Finance and FM performance review |
| Strategic FM improvement objectives | Quarterly or semi-annually | FM management review |
| ISO 41001 management system objectives | At least annually | Management review |

27. Performance against FM objectives shall be reported to relevant management and governance forums at planned intervals.

28. Where an FM objective is not being achieved, or is forecast not to be achieved, corrective action shall be identified, assigned, tracked and reviewed.

29. Corrective actions related to underperforming FM objectives shall include root cause consideration proportionate to the impact and risk of the non-achievement.

30. The organisation shall retain documented information as evidence of FM objective planning, approval, communication, monitoring, review, updates and achievement.

31. FM objectives shall be considered during management review of the Facility Management Management System.

32. Management review outputs shall include decisions or actions related to new, revised, retired or continued FM objectives as appropriate.

33. FM objectives shall support continual improvement of FM service delivery, workplace effectiveness, asset performance, compliance performance and stakeholder satisfaction.

34. Objectives assigned to contractors or outsourced service providers shall be included in relevant contracts, service specifications, performance schedules, statements of work or service level agreements where applicable.

35. Service providers shall be required to supply performance information necessary to monitor FM objectives assigned to or dependent upon them.

36. FM objectives shall be communicated in a manner appropriate to the audience, including through FM plans, dashboards, team briefings, supplier meetings, performance reports, intranet pages, management reviews or other approved communication channels.

37. Personnel responsible for achieving FM objectives shall be provided with appropriate information, authority, resources and competence to fulfil their assigned responsibilities.

38. FM objectives shall be retained as documented information in accordance with the organisation’s document control and records retention requirements.

39. FM objectives shall be traceable to relevant planning outputs, including identified risks and opportunities, stakeholder requirements, FM strategy, service requirements, compliance obligations and management review decisions.

40. The organisation shall not rely solely on informal or undocumented targets to demonstrate conformance with ISO 41001:2018.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Top Management | Shall ensure that FM objectives are established at relevant functions and levels; shall ensure alignment with the FM policy and organisational direction; shall provide resources required to achieve objectives; shall review FM objective performance through management review. |
| [Head of Facilities Management] | Shall own this Policy; shall coordinate the FM objective-setting process; shall ensure objectives are documented, approved, communicated, monitored and reviewed; shall escalate significant risks to objective achievement. |
| FM Management Team | Shall propose objectives and targets for their areas of responsibility; shall ensure objectives are measurable and achievable; shall monitor performance; shall implement corrective actions where performance is below target. |
| FM Objective Owners | Shall be accountable for assigned objectives; shall define supporting actions, resources, timelines and evidence; shall report performance status; shall maintain records demonstrating progress and completion. |
| FM Compliance / Management System Lead | Shall verify that FM objectives meet ISO 41001:2018 requirements; shall maintain or oversee controlled documented information; shall support audit readiness and evidence collection. |
| Service Managers | Shall translate approved FM objectives into operational plans, service requirements, work orders, inspections, maintenance plans and team activities as applicable. |
| Procurement / Contract Management | Shall ensure applicable FM objectives and targets are reflected in supplier contracts, service level agreements and performance review mechanisms. |
| Finance / Budget Owner | Shall support resource planning for FM objectives; shall review financial feasibility; shall monitor budget-related FM targets where applicable. |
| Health, Safety, Environment and Sustainability Functions | Shall provide input to FM objectives related to safety, statutory compliance, environmental performance, sustainability, energy, waste and workplace wellbeing. |
| Service Providers and Contractors | Shall comply with FM objectives and targets assigned through contracts or instructions; shall provide required performance data; shall participate in reviews and corrective actions where required. |
| Employees, Occupants and Facility Users | Shall provide feedback where requested and shall follow relevant FM arrangements that support achievement of objectives. |
| Internal Audit / Assurance Function | Shall assess whether FM objectives are established, planned, monitored and maintained in accordance with this Policy and ISO 41001:2018. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all in-scope FM activities and personnel.

The organisation shall monitor compliance with this Policy through one or more of the following mechanisms:

- Review of the FM Objectives Register or equivalent documented record.
- Periodic FM performance reviews.
- ISO 41001 internal audits.
- Management reviews.
- Supplier performance reviews.
- Compliance inspections and statutory assurance reviews.
- Review of service level performance reports.
- Corrective action and nonconformity tracking.
- Review of evidence supporting objective achievement.
- Stakeholder satisfaction surveys and feedback analysis.

The following evidence shall be retained, as applicable, to demonstrate compliance with this Policy:

| Evidence Type | Minimum Content | Typical Owner |
|---|---|---|
| FM Objectives Register | Approved objectives, targets, owners, dates, resources and evaluation methods | [Head of Facilities Management] |
| Objective Approval Records | Management approval, version history and change rationale | FM Management System Lead |
| FM Performance Reports | KPI results, trend analysis, status and issues | FM Objective Owners |
| Management Review Minutes | Review of objective performance and related decisions | Top Management / FM Management System Lead |
| Corrective Action Records | Actions, owners, due dates, root cause where applicable and closure evidence | FM Objective Owners |
| Supplier Performance Reports | Contracted FM target performance and service levels | Contract Manager |
| Communication Records | Evidence that objectives were communicated to relevant parties | FM Management Team |
| Audit Records | Internal or external audit findings related to | Internal Audit / Assurance Function |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in:

- Requirement to revise or reissue FM objectives.
- Escalation to FM management or top management.
- Corrective action or preventive action.
- Supplier performance management action.
- Contractual remedies where service providers fail to meet assigned obligations.
- Management review escalation.
- Disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policies where deliberate or negligent non-compliance occurs.

FM objectives that are overdue, materially underperforming or no longer suitable shall be escalated in accordance with the following minimum requirements:

| Condition | Required Action | Escalation Level |
|---|---|---|
| Objective not defined or not measurable | Revise objective and target criteria | FM Management Team |
| Objective missing owner, resources or evaluation method | Complete objective planning details | [Head of Facilities Management] |
| Objective at risk of non-achievement | Identify mitigation or corrective action | FM Objective Owner |
| Objective missed by agreed deadline | Conduct performance review and assign corrective action | FM Management Team |
| Repeated failure or high-risk objective not achieved | Escalate for management review decision | Top Management |
| Supplier-related objective failure | Initiate supplier performance review and remedial action | Contract Manager / Procurement |

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented and approved justification.

An exception shall not remove the requirement to comply with applicable statutory, regulatory, health and safety, environmental, contractual or ISO 41001 management system obligations.

Requests for exceptions shall include, at a minimum:

- Objective, requirement or policy clause for which the exception is requested.
- Business justification for the exception.
- Risk assessment and impact on FM performance, compliance and stakeholders.
- Compensating controls or alternative monitoring arrangements.
- Proposed duration of the exception.
- Responsible owner.
- Approval by [Head of Facilities Management] or delegated authority.
- Additional approval by top management where the exception affects a strategic, statutory, high-risk or ISO 41001 certification-related objective.

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall be reviewed before expiry. Permanent exceptions shall not be permitted unless the relevant objective, target or policy requirement is formally revised and approved through the established governance process.

All approved exceptions shall be recorded in an Exceptions Register or equivalent controlled record.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and additionally when any of the following occur:

- Significant change to the organisation’s FM policy, strategy, scope or operating model.
- Significant change to facilities, assets, occupancy, workplace arrangements or service delivery requirements.
- Change in applicable legal, regulatory, statutory, contractual or ISO 41001 requirements.
- Significant FM incident, service failure, audit finding or management review decision.
- Repeated non-achievement of FM objectives.
- Significant change in stakeholder expectations or organisational priorities.
- Change in outsourced FM service provider arrangements.
- Significant change to FM risks and opportunities.

The [Head of Facilities Management] shall be responsible for ensuring this Policy remains current, approved, communicated and aligned with ISO 41001:2018.

Policy changes shall be controlled in accordance with the organisation’s document control requirements. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with records retention requirements.

The effectiveness of this Policy shall be assessed through audit results, management review outputs, objective performance trends, corrective action records, stakeholder feedback and evidence of continual improvement in FM performance.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Matrix ID | Enter a unique identifier for the matrix line item, using a consistent format such as FM-RACI-001. |
| FM Activity / Decision | Enter the specific FM activity, responsibility, or decision being assigned, such as maintenance planning, contractor approval, space allocation, emergency response, or service performance review. |
| FM Process / Service Area | Enter the relevant FM process or service area, such as Asset Maintenance, Cleaning, Security, Catering, Space Management, Utilities, HSE, Procurement, Helpdesk, or Business Continuity. |
| ISO 41001:2018 Reference | Enter the relevant ISO 41001:2018 clause reference, normally Cl. 5.3; add related clauses where applicable, such as 6.1, 7.2, 7.5, 8.1, 9.1, or 10.2. |
| Activity Objective / Expected Output | Describe the intended outcome or deliverable of the activity in concise terms, such as approved maintenance plan, completed service review, authorised work order, or communicated FM responsibility. |
| Responsible Role(s) - R | Enter the role title(s) that perform or coordinate the work; use role titles, not personal names, and separate multiple roles with semicolons. |
| Accountable Role - A | Enter the single role title with ultimate accountability for ensuring the activity is completed and effective; only one Accountable role should be listed per row. |
| Consulted Role(s) - C | Enter role title(s) whose input must be obtained before or during the activity; use 'None' if not applicable and separate multiple roles with semicolons. |
| Informed Role(s) - I | Enter role title(s) that must be kept informed of status, outcome, or decisions; use 'None' if not applicable and separate multiple roles with semicolons. |
| Authority Granted | Describe the authority assigned to the Accountable or Responsible role, such as approve service schedules, assign FM resources, stop unsafe work, approve contractor access, or escalate nonconformities. |
| Decision / Approval Limit | Enter any financial, operational, risk, or scope limit for the authority, using measurable thresholds where applicable, such as up to USD 10,000, routine changes only, high-risk work excluded, or no financial authority. |
| Interfaces / Dependencies | Enter internal or external functions, suppliers, systems, or processes that interact with this activity, such as Procurement, HR, IT, Finance, HSE, outsourced FM provider, CAFM, CMMS, or landlord. |
| Required Competence or Qualification | Enter the required competence, training, licence, experience, or certification for the role performing the activity; use 'Defined in competence matrix' if controlled elsewhere. |
| Key Documented Information / Record | Enter the policy, procedure, form, system record, report, or evidence generated or used by the activity, such as work order, SLA report, contractor permit, asset register, inspection checklist, or meeting minutes. |
| Escalation Route | Enter the role or governance forum to which issues, conflicts, risks, or authority exceedances are escalated, such as Head of FM, FM Steering Committee, HSE Manager, Top Management, or Client Representative. |
| Frequency / Trigger | Enter when the activity occurs, using values such as Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, Per Work Order, Per Incident, Per Contract Renewal, On Change, or As Required. |
| Effective Date | Enter the date this RACI assignment becomes valid, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date for this assignment, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Matrix Owner | Enter the role responsible for maintaining this matrix, typically Head of Facilities Management, FM Director, or FM Governance Manager. |
| Approval Status | Enter one allowed value: Draft, Under Review, Approved, Superseded, or Retired. |
| Approved By | Enter the role title or governance body that approved the assignment; use 'Pending approval' if not yet approved. |
| Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank only where Approval Status is Draft or Under Review. |
| Change Notes | Briefly describe what changed since the previous version or enter 'Initial issue' for a new assignment. |

### Maintenance

This template is owned by the Head of Facilities Management or FM Governance Manager and is reviewed at least annually, and whenever there are organisational, contractual, service scope, process, or authority changes. It draws from the organisation chart, FM policy, job descriptions, competence matrix, FM procedures, service contracts, CAFM/CMMS, helpdesk system, and approval authority register.
