Corrective action tracking example:

| Source | Finding / Issue | Risk | Corrective Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evacuation drill | Assembly point congestion at main entrance | Delayed accounting and emergency access obstruction | Relocate secondary assembly point and update maps | Facilities | [Due Date] | Open |
| Power outage tabletop | Generator fuel supplier contact outdated | Extended outage response delay | Update supplier contract and emergency contact list | Procurement / Facilities | [Due Date] | Open |
| Escape route inspection | Stored materials blocking secondary exit corridor | Evacuation route compromised | Remove materials and brief area manager | Facilities / Area Manager | [Due Date] | Closed |
| Fire alarm maintenance | Detector fault recurring in plant room | Delayed detection risk | Contractor root cause analysis and replacement plan | Facilities | [Due Date] | In Progress |

## Milestones & Timeline

The following timeline provides a practical implementation schedule. Dates should be confirmed during project initiation and adjusted according to facility complexity, regulatory requirements, and operational constraints.

| Milestone | Key Deliverables | Responsible Role | Target Date | Completion Criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Plan approved and initiated | Approved Emergency Preparedness & Response Plan; assigned owner; confirmed scope | Head of Facilities / HSE Lead | [Date] | Plan approved, communicated, and recorded in document control |
| 2. Emergency governance established | Working group, reporting lines, decision authorities, meeting cadence | Facilities Management | [Date] | Governance terms documented and stakeholders confirmed |
| 3. Legal and compliance requirements reviewed | Updated compliance obligations for fire, evacuation, utilities, emergency systems | Compliance / HSE / Facilities | [Date] | Applicable obligations identified and assigned |
| 4. Facility emergency scenario assessment completed | Scenario register, impact assessment, prioritised risk list | Facilities / HSE / Security | [Date] | Assessment reviewed and approved by plan owner |
| 5. Gap analysis completed | Gap register with corrective actions, owners, and due dates | Facilities Management | [Date] | Actions entered into corrective action tracker |
| 6. Emergency response strategy defined | Response levels, activation criteria, escalation triggers, closure and re-entry criteria | Facilities / HSE / Security | [Date] | Strategy approved by relevant stakeholders |
| 7. Site emergency documentation updated | Procedures, maps, contact lists, utility isolation diagrams, emergency services pack | Facilities Management | [Date] | Controlled documents issued and accessible |
| 8. Emergency resources verified | Equipment registers, inspection records, communication tests, contractor callout checks | Facilities / Maintenance / Security | [Date] | Readiness checklist completed and exceptions logged |
| 9. Role appointments completed | Fire wardens, incident coordinators, facilities responders, deputies | HSE / Facilities / Site Leadership | [Date] | Role coverage documented for operating hours |
| 10. Training and awareness delivered | Training records for workers, wardens, security, contractors, facilities team | HSE / Facilities | [Date] | Required personnel trained and evidence retained |
| 11. Evacuation drill completed | Drill plan, attendance/muster records, evaluation report, action log | HSE / Facilities / Security | [Date] | Drill completed and findings recorded |
| 12. Utility outage tabletop completed | Exercise scenario, decisions log, lessons learned, corrective actions | Facilities / Business Continuity / IT / Security | [Date] | Exercise report approved and actions assigned |
| 13. Corrective actions implemented | Closed action items with evidence | Action Owners | [Date] | High-priority actions closed or risk-accepted |
| 14. Management review completed | Performance metrics, incidents, drill outcomes, open risks, resource needs | Head of Facilities | [Date] | Management review minutes include emergency preparedness status |
| 15. Annual review scheduled | Review calendar, next drill programme, update triggers confirmed | Plan Owner | [Date] | Next review and exercise cycle entered into planning calendar |

## Roles & Responsibilities

The following roles are responsible for implementing, maintaining, and improving emergency preparedness and response arrangements.

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Senior Management | Provide leadership, resources, and authority for emergency preparedness; review significant risks, incidents, and performance; approve major changes requiring investment or operational decisions. |
| Head of Facilities | Own facility management operational control for emergency preparedness; ensure this plan is implemented; ensure resources, maintenance, contractors, and facility controls are adequate; report performance to management. |
| Emergency Preparedness Plan Owner | Maintain this plan; coordinate implementation activities; track milestones; ensure documented information is current; coordinate reviews, exercises, and improvement actions. |
| Health, Safety & Environment Lead | Advise on life safety, evacuation, regulatory duties, incident reporting, and training; support risk assessments and drill evaluation; ensure alignment with health and safety requirements. |
| Fire Safety Responsible Person / Fire Safety Manager | Ensure fire safety arrangements, fire risk assessments, fire system maintenance, evacuation controls, and fire-related compliance obligations are addressed. |
| Facilities Operations Team | Maintain emergency systems, utilities, escape routes, plant access, emergency equipment, and site information; support incident response, isolation, contractor coordination, and recovery. |
| Security Team | Monitor alarms where applicable; support emergency escalation, emergency services access, evacuation flow, visitor information, re-entry control, and incident logging. |
| Reception / Front-of-House Team | Provide visitor information, support visitor evacuation, maintain visitor records where used for emergency accounting, and escalate emergency notifications. |
| Fire Wardens / Evacuation Marshals | Assist evacuation in assigned areas, report status to assembly coordinators, identify blocked routes or persons needing assistance, and participate in drills and training. |
| Incident Coordinator / Site Emergency Lead | Coordinate site-level emergency response until relieved by emergency services or senior incident management; maintain decision logs; authorise re-entry where appropriate and safe. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Coordinate continuity impacts from facility disruption; define critical business service requirements; support decisions on relocation, remote working, or prolonged closure. |
| IT / Telecommunications Lead | Support emergency communication systems, network dependencies, alarm monitoring links, and technology recovery after utility or facility disruptions. |
| Procurement / Supplier Manager | Ensure emergency service levels, contractor competence, callout arrangements, and supplier obligations are included in relevant contracts. |
| Maintenance Contractors | Respond within agreed service levels; maintain emergency and utility systems; provide service reports; notify Facilities of impairments, defects, or unsafe conditions. |
| Utility Providers | Provide outage information, emergency response, restoration estimates, and safety instructions through agreed external contact routes. |
| Tenants / Shared Occupants | Comply with site emergency arrangements; nominate contacts where required; participate in drills; communicate changes affecting occupancy or emergency risk. |
| Employees and Workers | Follow emergency instructions, evacuate promptly when required, report hazards or impairments, and participate in training and drills. |
| Visitors | Follow host, warden, security, and emergency instructions; evacuate or shelter as directed. |
| Contractors | Complete site induction, follow emergency rules, maintain work area safety, report impairments or incidents immediately, and comply with permit and isolation controls. |

RACI summary:

| Activity | Senior Management | Head of Facilities | Plan Owner | HSE Lead | Security | Contractors | Business Continuity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Approve plan | A | R | C | C | C | I | C |
| Maintain plan | I | A | R | C | C | I | C |
| Conduct risk assessment | I | A | R | R | C | C | C |
| Maintain emergency systems | I | A | R | C | C | R | I |
| Deliver training | I | A | C | R | C | I | I |
| Conduct evacuation drills | I | A | R | R | R | I | C |
| Conduct utility outage exercises | I | A | R | C | C | C | R |
| Manage emergency incident response | C | A | R | C | R | C | C |
| Track corrective actions | I | A | R | C | C | C | C |
| Management review reporting | A | R | C | C | C | I | C |

Legend: R = Responsible, A = Accountable, C = Consulted, I = Informed.

## Resources

The following resources are required to implement and maintain this plan effectively.

### People Resources

| Resource | Purpose | Minimum Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Facilities response personnel | Coordinate facility systems, utilities, isolation, contractor response, and recovery | Coverage during operating hours and emergency callout arrangements outside hours |
| Fire wardens / evacuation marshals | Support safe evacuation and area status reporting | Adequate coverage by floor, zone, shift, and occupancy pattern |
| Incident coordinators | Coordinate site emergency response and escalation | Primary and deputy roles assigned and trained |
| Security personnel | Alarm monitoring, access control, emergency services support, re-entry management | Coverage aligned with operating hours and risk profile |
| HSE support | Life safety advice, drill evaluation, regulatory reporting support | Available for planning, exercises, and incident review |
| Contractor specialists | Fire systems, electrical, mechanical, gas, water, lift, BMS, security systems | Emergency callout arrangements with defined response expectations |
| Communications support | Internal and external communications during facility incidents | Pre-approved templates and escalation contacts |
| Business continuity support | Operational impact assessment and continuity activation | Integrated with utility outage and building closure decisions |

### Equipment and Systems

| Resource | Purpose | Readiness Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Fire alarm and detection system | Detect fire and alert occupants | Maintained, tested, monitored where applicable, defects tracked |
| Fire suppression and extinguishing equipment | Control or suppress fire where safe and appropriate | Inspected, accessible, suitable for hazard class |
| Emergency lighting | Support evacuation during power failure | Tested for function and duration |
| Exit signage and evacuation maps | Direct occupants to safe routes and assembly points | Current, visible, and aligned with building layout |
| Public address or alarm voice system | Communicate emergency instructions | Tested and backed by fallback method where required |
| Radios or resilient communications | Support response team coordination | Charged, tested, coverage verified |
| Emergency contact lists | Enable rapid escalation | Current and accessible during outage conditions |
| First aid equipment | Support immediate casualty response | Inspected and stocked |
| Spill kits or environmental response equipment | Support control of minor facility-related releases where applicable | Available and inspected according to risk |
| Generator and fuel supply, where applicable | Maintain critical services during power outage | Tested, maintained, fuel contracts verified |
| UPS systems, where applicable | Maintain short-term power for critical systems | Tested and runtime known |
| Utility isolation points | Enable safe isolation of gas, water, electrical, and mechanical systems | Labelled, accessible, included in site plans |
| Emergency services information pack | Provide critical information to responders | Current, accessible, and version controlled |
| Building Management System | Monitor and control critical building services | Monitored with manual fallback arrangements |
| Access control override mechanisms | Permit emergency egress and responder access | Tested and understood by authorised personnel |

### Financial and Contractual Resources

Budget and procurement arrangements shall be sufficient to support:

1. Statutory inspection, testing, and maintenance of emergency systems.
2. Corrective actions arising from risk assessments, inspections, drills, incidents, and audits.
3. Training for emergency roles.
4. Emergency signage, maps, communications tools, and equipment.
5. Contractor emergency callout retainers or service-level agreements.
6. Generator fuel, temporary welfare facilities, temporary lighting, temporary communications, and other contingency resources where required.
7. Specialist assessments, such as fire engineering, evacuation modelling, accessibility assessments, or utility resilience reviews, where warranted by risk.
8. Post-incident recovery, cleaning, repair, and reinstatement of facility services.

### Information Resources

The following information must be maintained, controlled, and accessible:

| Information Resource | Required Availability |
|---|---|
| Emergency procedures | Available to relevant personnel during normal and emergency operations |
| Evacuation maps | Posted in relevant locations and available digitally where appropriate |
| Emergency contact lists | Available offline to Facilities, Security, and Incident Coordinators |
| Site plans and isolation diagrams | Available to Facilities and emergency services |
| Fire risk assessment or equivalent | Available to authorised stakeholders and auditors |
| Maintenance and inspection records | Retained according to legal and management system requirements |
| Training records | Retained for assigned emergency roles and general awareness |
| Drill and exercise reports | Retained with corrective action evidence |
| Incident reports and decision logs | Retained for investigation, legal, insurance, and improvement purposes |
| Contractor competence and callout records | Retained as evidence of outsourced process control |

## Success Metrics

The following metrics will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of this plan and the associated emergency preparedness programme.

| Metric | Target / Threshold | Measurement Method | Reporting Frequency |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Emergency plan review completion | 100% by due date | Document control review log | Annually |
| Site emergency procedures current | 100% of in-scope facilities | Document register | Quarterly |
| Emergency contact list validation | 100% completed each quarter | Contact list attestation | Quarterly |
| Fire alarm and emergency lighting statutory tests completed | 100% by required due dates | Maintenance records | Monthly / Quarterly |
| Critical emergency system defects overdue | 0 high-risk overdue defects | Defect register | Monthly |
| Escape route inspection completion | ≥ 95% on schedule | Inspection checklist | Monthly |
| Evacuation drill completion | 100% of required drills completed | Drill schedule and reports | Annually |
| Evacuation drill corrective actions closed | ≥ 90% by due date; 100% high-risk actions closed or risk-accepted | Corrective action register | Quarterly |
| Fire warden / marshal coverage | ≥ defined site coverage level for operating hours | Role roster and attendance data | Quarterly |
| Emergency role training completion | ≥ 95% current; 100% for critical roles | Training records | Quarterly |
| Contractor emergency callout verification | 100% of critical contractors tested per schedule | Callout test log | Semi-annually |
| Emergency communication test success | ≥ 95% successful tests; failures remediated | Communications test record | Quarterly |
| Utility outage tabletop exercise completion | At least one relevant exercise annually | Exercise records | Annually |
| Incident reporting timeliness | Emergency incidents logged within [X] hours | Incident management system | Quarterly |
| Post-incident review completion | 100% for significant incidents | Incident review records | After each incident |
| Management review reporting | Emergency preparedness included in 100% of relevant FM management reviews | Management review minutes | At planned review intervals |

Qualitative success criteria include:

1. Occupants understand how to respond to alarms and evacuation instructions.
2. Emergency roles are clearly assigned and deputies are available.
3. Facility systems supporting life safety are maintained and defects are controlled.
4. Utility outage decisions are made using predefined life safety and operational criteria.
5. Emergency communications have tested fallback methods.
6. Contractors understand and meet emergency callout expectations.
7. Emergency exercises produce actionable lessons learned.
8. Planned facility changes include emergency preparedness impact assessment.
9. Documented information is accurate, accessible, and audit-ready.
10. Corrective actions are tracked to completion and verified for effectiveness.

## Review & Update Triggers

This plan shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes or events could affect emergency preparedness and response capability.

Mandatory review and update triggers include:

| Trigger | Required Review Activity | Responsible Role |
|---|---|---|
| Annual scheduled review | Confirm plan accuracy, scope, roles, resources, metrics, and alignment with ISO 41001 | Plan Owner |
| Facility layout change | Review evacuation routes, maps, signage, assembly points, fire systems, and emergency service access | Facilities Management |
| Change in occupancy or operating hours | Review warden coverage, evacuation assumptions, visitor controls, and emergency communications | Facilities / HSE / Security |
| New facility, relocation, closure, or lease change | Reassess scope, responsibilities, legal duties, landlord interfaces, and emergency procedures | Head of Facilities |
| Fire system modification or impairment | Review temporary controls, notification requirements, response arrangements, and revalidation testing | Fire Safety Responsible Person |
| Utility infrastructure change | Review outage scenarios, isolation points, contractor contacts, restoration assumptions, and continuity dependencies | Facilities Management |
| Significant emergency incident | Conduct post-incident review and update plan, procedures, training, or resources as needed | Incident Coordinator / Plan Owner |
| Evacuation drill or exercise finding | Update arrangements based on lessons learned and corrective actions | HSE / Facilities |
| Audit finding or nonconformity | Update controls, documented information, responsibilities, or evidence retention practices | Plan Owner |
| Change in legal or regulatory requirements | Update compliance obligations and operational controls | Compliance / HSE / Facilities |
| Change in critical contractors or suppliers | Update callout lists, service levels, competence records, and escalation routes | Procurement / Facilities |
| Change in emergency services guidance | Update site information packs, access arrangements, and response coordination | Facilities / Security |
| Introduction of new hazards | Reassess emergency scenarios, controls, training, and equipment needs | HSE / Facilities |
| Significant organisational change | Review decision authorities, escalation paths, role assignments, and communication channels | Senior Management / Head of Facilities |
| Repeated defects in emergency systems | Review maintenance strategy, contractor performance, contingency controls, and resource allocation | Facilities Management |
| Business continuity impact change | Review utility outage tolerances, building closure criteria, and recovery interfaces | Business Continuity Manager |

Review outputs shall include:

1. Updated plan version where changes are required.
2. Updated emergency procedures, maps, contact lists, and registers where applicable.
3. Updated risk assessment and action plan where risk profile has changed.
4. Communication of relevant changes to affected workers, contractors, tenants, visitors, and response roles.
5. Evidence of review approval retained in the document control system.
6. Updated training or exercise requirements where changes affect response expectations.

ISO41-016.title: Communication Plan
ISO41-016.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [FM-PLAN-COMM-001] | 1.0 | Facilities Management Director / FM System Owner | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO 41001:2018 Facility Management Management System | — Communication | Internal |

## Purpose & Objectives

The purpose of this Communication Plan is to define the planned communications necessary to support the effective operation, maintenance, improvement, and assurance of the organisation’s Facility Management System (FMS) in accordance with ISO 41001:2018.

This Plan establishes what facility management communications are required, when they occur, with whom they are conducted, how they are delivered, and who is responsible for communicating. It ensures that relevant internal and external stakeholders receive timely, accurate, consistent, and appropriate information relating to facility management services, performance, changes, risks, incidents, responsibilities, and continual improvement.

The objectives of this Plan are to:

- Ensure facility management communications are planned, controlled, and aligned with organisational objectives and stakeholder needs.
- Support effective delivery of FM services, including both in-house and outsourced activities.
- Enable users, clients, service providers, contractors, leadership, and other interested parties to understand relevant FM requirements, service expectations, responsibilities, and changes.
- Provide communication arrangements for normal operations, planned changes, emergency or disruptive events, service performance, compliance obligations, and management review inputs.
- Ensure communications are clear, timely, accessible, authorised, and retained where required as documented information.
- Support evidence-based assurance of ISO 41001:2018 during internal audits, certification audits, and management reviews.
- Promote engagement, awareness, coordination, and feedback across all parties involved in or affected by the FMS.

## Scope

This Communication Plan applies to all communications necessary for the effective implementation, operation, performance evaluation, and improvement of the FMS.

The scope includes communications related to:

- FM policy, objectives, roles, responsibilities, and authority.
- FM service delivery, service levels, operational updates, planned works, maintenance activities, and service disruptions.
- Applicable legal, regulatory, statutory, contractual, health, safety, environmental, security, accessibility, and business continuity requirements affecting FM services.
- Communication with internal users, client functions, senior management, employees, site occupants, visitors, contractors, outsourced service providers, landlords, tenants, regulators, emergency responders, and other relevant interested parties.
- Performance monitoring, service review, customer satisfaction, complaints, corrective actions, risks, opportunities, and continual improvement.
- Emergency, incident, crisis, and business disruption communications where these relate to facilities or FM services.
- Communication channels used for FM notifications, including meetings, email, intranet, service portals, helpdesk systems, signage, dashboards, contract governance forums, mobile alerts, and formal reports.
- Retention of FM communication records where evidence is required for service assurance, compliance, audit, contractual governance, or incident investigation.

This Plan applies to:

- All facilities, buildings, sites, workspaces, assets, and services included within the defined FMS scope.
- All FM personnel, whether permanent, temporary, contractor, consultant, or outsourced provider.
- All parties communicating on behalf of the FMS.

This Plan does not replace detailed incident response, emergency management, health and safety, business continuity, change management, or contractor management procedures. Where such procedures define specific communication steps, this Plan aligns with and references them as supporting arrangements.

## Assumptions & Dependencies

The effectiveness of this Communication Plan depends on the following assumptions and dependencies.

| Category | Assumption / Dependency | Impact if Not Met | Responsible Party |
|---|---|---|---|
| FMS scope | The scope of the FMS, including covered sites, services, interfaces, and outsourced arrangements, is defined and approved. | Communications may omit relevant locations, stakeholders, or services. | FM System Owner |
| Stakeholder identification | Relevant interested parties and their FM information needs are identified and maintained. | Communications may not meet stakeholder expectations or compliance obligations. | FM Governance Lead |
| Roles and authorities | FM communication responsibilities and approval authorities are assigned and understood. | Delayed, inconsistent, or unauthorised communications may occur. | Facilities Management Director |
| Communication channels | Approved channels such as email, intranet, helpdesk, signage, dashboards, and emergency notification tools are available and maintained. | Communications may not reach intended recipients reliably. | FM Operations Manager / IT Service Owner |
| Contact data | Current contact lists exist for employees, occupants, contractors, suppliers, emergency contacts, regulators, landlords, and client representatives as applicable. | Urgent or mandatory communications may fail or be delayed. | Site FM Managers / Procurement / HR |
| Contract governance | FM contracts include communication, escalation, reporting, and notification requirements. | Outsourced providers may not report service performance, incidents, or changes consistently. | Procurement Lead / Contract Manager |
| Legal and compliance input | Applicable legal, regulatory, statutory, and contractual communication obligations are identified. | Mandatory notifications may be missed or inadequately documented. | Compliance Lead / Legal Counsel |
| Emergency arrangements | Emergency and crisis communication protocols exist and are tested. | Disruption communications may be ineffective during time-sensitive events. | HSE Lead / Business Continuity Manager |
| Documented information | Communication records can be retained, retrieved, and protected in line with document control requirements. | Audit evidence and traceability may be insufficient. | Document Control Manager |
| Language and accessibility | Communication formats can be adapted for audience language, accessibility, literacy, and operational needs. | Stakeholders may not understand or act on FM communications. | FM Communications Coordinator |

## Approach / Phases

The organisation will implement and maintain FM communications through the following planned approach.

### Phase 1 — Define Communication Requirements

The FM System Owner, supported by FM governance, site management, compliance, and service delivery leads, shall identify communication requirements necessary to operate and improve the FMS.

Activities include:

- Review ISO 41001:2018 requirements and related FMS processes.
- Identify internal and external interested parties relevant to FM services.
- Determine the information each interested party needs to receive or provide.
- Identify communication obligations arising from:
 - FM policy and objectives.
 - Service level agreements and contracts.
 - Legal, regulatory, statutory, and compliance requirements.
 - Health, safety, environmental, security, accessibility, and business continuity requirements.
 - Incident, emergency, change, and maintenance processes.
 - Management review, audit, risk, corrective action, and continual improvement processes.
- Define mandatory communication attributes:
 - What will be communicated.
 - When communication will occur.
 - With whom communication will take place.
 - How communication will be delivered.
 - Who is responsible for communication.
 - What records will be retained.

### Phase 2 — Map Stakeholders, Channels, and Communication Content

The organisation shall maintain a structured FM Communication Matrix to ensure communications are consistent, planned, and auditable.

| Communication Topic | Purpose / Content | Audience | Frequency / Timing | Channel / Method | Responsible Role | Record / Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FM policy and objectives | Communicate FM commitments, objectives, and alignment with organisational needs. | FM team, service providers, relevant employees, client representatives | On approval, annual refresh, and when materially changed | Intranet, briefing sessions, onboarding pack, contractor induction | FM System Owner | Published policy, briefing attendance records, induction records |
| FMS scope and service model | Explain covered facilities, services, responsibilities, interfaces, and outsourced arrangements. | Senior management, FM team, service providers, site leads, client functions | On FMS implementation and when scope changes | FMS manual, service catalogue, governance meetings | FM Governance Lead | Approved FMS scope, service catalogue, meeting minutes |
| Planned maintenance and works | Notify affected users of scheduled maintenance, access restrictions, service impacts, safety controls, and expected completion. | Site occupants, affected departments, security, reception, contractors | At least [X] business days before planned work; reminders as needed | Email, intranet notice, signage, helpdesk notice, tenant portal | Site FM Manager | Maintenance notices, work orders, distribution logs |
| Unplanned service disruption | Provide timely updates on outages affecting utilities, access, cleaning, catering, security, building systems, or workspace availability. | Affected users, site leadership, service desk, contractors, client representatives | As soon as practicable after identification; updates at agreed intervals until resolved | Email alert, SMS/app alert where available, helpdesk banner, site notice | FM Operations Manager | Incident ticket, notification log, closure communication |
| Emergency facilities communication | Communicate urgent safety, evacuation, shelter-in-place, building closure, access restriction, or critical infrastructure information. | Site occupants, visitors, emergency response team, security, senior management, emergency services as applicable | Immediate upon activation of emergency protocol | Emergency notification system, public address, SMS/app alert, wardens, signage | Incident Controller / Site FM Manager | Incident log, emergency communication record, post-incident report |
| Contractor induction and site rules | Communicate site access, safety, security, environmental, conduct, permit-to-work, and reporting requirements. | Contractors, subcontractors, visiting engineers, outsourced providers | Before site access and periodically per contract or risk level | Induction platform, toolbox talks, permit system, site briefing | Contractor Manager / Site FM Manager | Induction records, permits, attendance sheets |
| Service performance reporting | Communicate KPI performance, SLA results, service trends, complaints, risks, and improvement actions. | FM leadership, client representatives, contract managers, service providers | Monthly operational review; quarterly governance review | Performance dashboard, formal report, review meeting | FM Performance Manager | KPI report, dashboard export, meeting minutes, action log |
| Management review inputs | Provide information on FMS performance, communication effectiveness, stakeholder feedback, risks, nonconformities, audit results, and improvement opportunities. | Top management, FM System Owner, process owners | At least annually and prior to management review | Management review pack, meeting presentation | FM Governance Lead | Management review pack, minutes, decisions, actions |
| Audit and compliance communications | Communicate audit schedules, evidence requests, findings, corrective actions, and closure status. | FM process owners, internal auditors, service providers, compliance team | Per annual audit programme and as findings arise | Audit system, email, audit meetings, corrective action tracker | Internal Audit Lead / FM Governance Lead | Audit plan, evidence logs, nonconformity records, action tracker |
| FM change communications | Communicate changes to FM services, suppliers, systems, operating hours, building use, service levels, or responsibilities. | Affected users, service providers, site leads, support functions, client representatives | Before implementation based on change risk; post-change confirmation where required | Change advisory meeting, email, intranet, service desk notice | FM Change Owner | Change record, approval, communications log |
| Customer satisfaction and feedback | Request and communicate feedback on FM services, complaints, trends, and response actions. | Employees, occupants, client representatives, tenants, visitors where applicable | Continuous via helpdesk; periodic surveys at least annually | Helpdesk survey, pulse survey, tenant forum, focus group | FM Customer Experience Lead | Survey results, complaint logs, improvement actions |
| Legal or regulatory notifications | Communicate required information to authorities or affected parties relating to statutory inspections, incidents, permits, environmental events, or building compliance. | Regulators, authorities, landlords, insurers, internal compliance/legal, affected parties | As required by law, permit, contract, or incident protocol | Formal letter, regulatory portal, email, incident notification process | Compliance Lead / Legal Counsel / FM System Owner | Submitted notification, acknowledgement, compliance record |
| Supplier and contract communications | Communicate expectations, contract obligations, reporting needs, performance issues, corrective actions, and governance decisions. | Outsourced FM providers, suppliers, procurement, contract managers | Contract mobilisation; monthly/quarterly reviews; as issues arise | Contract meetings, supplier portal, formal correspondence | Contract Manager | Meeting minutes, correspondence, supplier performance records |
| Awareness and training communications | Communicate FM-related awareness such as waste management, energy conservation, security procedures, reporting faults, workplace etiquette, and accessibility arrangements. | Site users, employees, contractors, visitors as applicable | During onboarding; campaigns as planned; when requirements change | Intranet, posters, digital signage, toolbox talks, training modules | FM Communications Coordinator | Campaign materials, training records, acknowledgement logs |

### Phase 3 — Establish Communication Governance

To ensure consistency and control, the following governance principles apply:

- FM communications shall be proportionate to the risk, urgency, complexity, and stakeholder impact of the matter being communicated.
- Communications affecting safety, security, compliance, building access, service availability, contractual obligations, or reputation shall be authorised by the designated responsible role before release, except where immediate emergency communication is required.
- Messages shall be accurate, clear, concise, audience-appropriate, and action-oriented.
- Communications shall identify:
 - The issue or topic.
 - Who is affected.
 - Required action by recipients, if any.
 - Effective date, time, and duration.
 - Point of contact or escalation route.
 - Next update timing where ongoing.
- Communications shall be accessible to intended recipients, considering:
 - Physical location and work pattern.
 - Language needs.
 - Disability and accessibility needs.
 - Digital access limitations.
 - Contractor and visitor access to communication channels.
- Where FM services are outsourced, communication requirements shall be included in contracts, service level agreements, mobilisation plans, and governance meetings.
- Records of significant FM communications shall be retained as documented information where required for compliance, audit, incident investigation, service assurance, contract management, or management review.

### Phase 4 — Implement Communication Channels

Approved FM communication channels shall be selected based on audience, urgency, confidentiality, and recordkeeping needs.

| Channel | Primary Use | Appropriate For | Limitations / Controls | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Email distribution lists | Formal notices and updates | Planned works, service changes, policy updates, management reports | Distribution lists must be current; avoid overuse for urgent safety alerts where faster tools exist | FM Communications Coordinator |
| FM helpdesk / service portal | Operational requests, status updates, service disruption notices | Work orders, user requests, ticket updates, trend reporting | Requires user access and monitoring; standard categories must be maintained | FM Service Desk Manager |
| Intranet / FM portal | Persistent reference information | FM policy, service catalogue, guidance, FAQs, awareness campaigns | Content must be version-controlled and reviewed periodically | FM Governance Lead |
| Digital signage / physical notices | Site-specific visibility | Planned works, access restrictions, temporary closures, safety reminders | Must be removed when obsolete; accessible placement required | Site FM Manager |
| Emergency notification system | Time-critical alerts | Evacuation, building closure, critical safety or security events | Contact data and templates must be tested and maintained | Business Continuity Manager |
| Governance meetings | Two-way decision-making and assurance | Service reviews, supplier performance, risks, audit actions, improvement planning | Minutes and action logs required | FM Performance Manager / Contract Manager |
| Toolbox talks / briefings | Task-level communication | Contractor safety, maintenance teams, operational changes | Attendance records required for controlled topics | Contractor Manager / Maintenance Lead |
| Dashboards and reports | Performance transparency | KPIs, SLA performance, complaints, risks, energy, maintenance backlog | Data sources must be accurate and controlled | FM Performance Manager |
| Tenant / occupant forums | Engagement and feedback | Service quality, planned changes, improvement priorities | Feedback and actions must be tracked | FM Customer Experience Lead |
| Formal correspondence | Official external communication | Regulatory notifications, contractual notices, legal matters | Requires authorised signatory and record retention | Legal Counsel / Contract Manager |

### Phase 5 — Control Escalation and Approval

Communication escalation shall ensure that high-impact or time-sensitive matters are communicated promptly to the correct decision-makers and affected parties.

| Scenario | Escalation Threshold | Initial Communication Owner | Approval Required | Target Initial Notification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Life safety or emergency event | Immediate threat to health, safety, life, or building occupancy | Incident Controller / Site FM Manager | Emergency authority per incident protocol; retrospective approval acceptable if urgent | Immediate |
| Critical utility failure | Loss of power, water, HVAC, lifts, access control, fire systems, or critical building services affecting operations | FM Operations Manager | Facilities Management Director / Site Leadership depending impact | Within [X] minutes of confirmation |
| Major service disruption | FM service failure affecting multiple departments, customers, tenants, or business-critical activity | FM Operations Manager | Facilities Management Director | Within [X] hour(s) |
| Regulatory or statutory issue | Reportable incident, statutory inspection failure, permit breach, or regulator request | Compliance Lead / FM System Owner | Legal Counsel and responsible executive where required | As required by regulation; internally within [X] hour(s) |
| High-risk planned works | Works affecting safety systems, security, access, critical infrastructure, or business continuity | Site FM Manager / Project Manager | FM Change Owner / HSE Lead / Security Lead as applicable | At least [X] business days prior |
| Supplier performance issue | Repeated SLA failure, serious nonconformity, contract breach, or unresolved corrective action | Contract Manager | Procurement Lead / Facilities Management Director | At next governance meeting or sooner if severe |
| Adverse stakeholder feedback | Significant complaint trend, executive complaint, tenant escalation, or reputational concern | FM Customer Experience Lead | FM System Owner / Communications Lead where applicable | Within [X] business days |
| Audit nonconformity | Major nonconformity or overdue corrective action affecting FMS conformity | FM Governance Lead | FM System Owner | Within [X] business days of issue |

### Phase 6 — Monitor Effectiveness and Improve

The organisation shall monitor the effectiveness of FM communications and take corrective or improvement actions where communications are late, inaccurate, inaccessible, incomplete, unauthorised, or ineffective.

Monitoring activities include:

- Review of communication-related complaints, feedback, and satisfaction survey results.
- Review of incident post-event reports for communication effectiveness.
- Review of helpdesk response data and notification timeliness.
- Review of contractor and supplier governance records.
- Internal audits against ISO 41001:2018 and related FMS processes.
- Review of communication performance during management review.
- Periodic testing of emergency and urgent notification channels.
- Verification that communication records are retained and retrievable.

Improvement actions may include:

- Updating the FM Communication Matrix.
- Revising communication templates.
- Updating distribution lists and contact data.
- Changing communication channels or frequency.
- Providing training or briefings to responsible communicators.
- Updating supplier contracts or service level requirements.
- Enhancing dashboards, portals, or notification systems.
- Introducing additional accessibility or language support.

## Milestones & Timeline

The following timeline applies to initial implementation of this Communication Plan. Dates should be aligned with the organisation’s ISO 41001:2018 implementation programme.

| Milestone | Description | Responsible Role | Target Date | Deliverable / Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Confirm FMS communication scope | Confirm sites, services, stakeholders, and outsourced arrangements covered by the Plan. | FM System Owner | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Approved scope confirmation | Planned |
| Identify interested parties and communication needs | Document internal and external parties, information needs, obligations, and expectations. | FM Governance Lead | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Interested parties register / stakeholder analysis | Planned |
| Develop FM Communication Matrix | Define what, when, with whom, how, by whom, and recordkeeping requirements. | FM Communications Coordinator | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Approved FM Communication Matrix | Planned |
| Validate legal, regulatory, and contractual communication obligations | Confirm mandatory notification requirements and supplier reporting obligations. | Compliance Lead / Contract Manager | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Compliance and contract communication requirements log | Planned |
| Approve communication channels and escalation routes | Confirm approved communication channels, owners, escalation thresholds, and approval authorities. | Facilities Management Director | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Approved escalation and channel model | Planned |
| Update distribution lists and contact registers | Validate contact details for employees, occupants, contractors, suppliers, emergency contacts, and governance participants. | Site FM Managers | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Current contact lists / access group records | Planned |
| Develop templates and standard messages | Create standard templates for planned works, disruptions, emergency notices, supplier reports, and service updates. | FM Communications Coordinator | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Approved templates | Planned |
| Communicate Plan to responsible roles | Brief FM personnel, site managers, service desk, contractors, and process owners on communication responsibilities. | FM System Owner | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Briefing materials and attendance records | Planned |
| Implement routine reporting cadence | Start planned operational, performance, supplier, and management reporting communications. | FM Performance Manager | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Reports, dashboards, meeting minutes | Planned |
| Test urgent and emergency communication channels | Conduct controlled test of emergency notification and critical disruption communication paths. | Business Continuity Manager / Site FM Manager | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Test report and improvement actions | Planned |
| Conduct initial effectiveness review | Review implementation, stakeholder feedback, audit readiness, and gaps. | FM Governance Lead | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Effectiveness review report / action log | Planned |
| Present to management review | Include communication performance and improvement actions in FMS management review. | FM System Owner | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Management review input and minutes | Planned |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Top Management | Ensure the importance of effective FM communication is understood; provide direction and support; review communication effectiveness through management review; make decisions where significant FM communication risks affect organisational objectives. |
| Facilities Management Director | Own overall FM communication governance; approve this Plan; ensure adequate resources, authorities, and channels exist; resolve escalated communication issues. |
| FM System Owner | Ensure the Communication Plan supports ISO 41001:2018; coordinate integration with the FMS; ensure communication requirements are maintained as documented information; report communication performance to management review. |
| FM Governance Lead | Maintain the communication framework, matrix, records, audit evidence, and review cycle; coordinate internal audit responses and improvement actions related to communication. |
| FM Communications Coordinator | Prepare, coordinate, and issue routine FM communications; maintain templates, distribution lists, and communications calendar; ensure messages are clear, timely, accessible, and aligned with this Plan. |
| FM Operations Manager | Communicate operational service status, disruptions, maintenance impacts, resource constraints, and service restoration updates; coordinate with site FM teams and service providers. |
| Site FM Manager | Communicate site-specific works, risks, access restrictions, local service changes, emergency information, and occupant updates; maintain local contacts and notice channels. |
| FM Service Desk Manager | Ensure the helpdesk/service portal communicates ticket status, service interruptions, user guidance, and escalation information; maintain communication records in service management tools. |
| FM Performance Manager | Prepare and communicate KPI, SLA, trend, complaint, backlog, corrective action, and service improvement reports; facilitate performance review meetings. |
| Contract Manager | Ensure outsourced service providers understand and meet contractual communication, reporting, escalation, and notification obligations; retain supplier communication records. |
| Procurement Lead | Ensure communication requirements are included in procurement documents, contracts, service specifications, and supplier governance arrangements. |
| Compliance Lead | Identify legal, regulatory, statutory, and compliance-related communication obligations; coordinate mandatory notifications and evidence retention. |
| Legal Counsel | Review communications involving legal liability, regulatory notification, contractual disputes, enforcement action, or sensitive external disclosures. |
| HSE Lead | Define and support communication requirements for health, safety, environmental, statutory inspection, incident, and risk control matters. |
| Security Lead | Define and support communications relating to access control, physical security incidents, security procedures, restricted areas, and visitor management. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Ensure FM communications align with crisis, emergency, and continuity arrangements; support testing of urgent notification channels. |
| IT Service Owner | Maintain availability and access to digital communication channels used by FM, including email groups, portals, notification tools, dashboards, and service management systems. |
| Document Control Manager | Ensure relevant FM communications and communication records are controlled, retained, retrievable, and protected in accordance with documented information requirements. |
| Service Providers / Contractors | Provide required reports, notifications, escalation alerts, incident information, risk updates, and completion confirmations; participate in required briefings and governance meetings. |
| Employees, Occupants, and Facility Users | Read and act on relevant FM communications; report faults, incidents, hazards, complaints, and feedback through approved channels. |
| Internal Audit | Assess whether FM communications meet ISO 41001:2018 and internal FMS requirements; report findings and verify corrective actions. |

## Resources

The following resources are required to implement and maintain this Communication Plan.

| Resource Type | Required Resource | Purpose | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| People | FM Communications Coordinator | Coordinate routine FM messaging, templates, communications calendar, and records. | Facilities Management Director |
| People | Site FM Managers | Deliver local communications and maintain site-specific stakeholder contact data. | FM Operations Manager |
| People | FM Governance Lead | Maintain alignment with ISO 41001:2018 requirements and audit evidence. | FM System Owner |
| People | Service Desk Personnel | Provide first-line communication for FM requests, incidents, and status updates. | FM Service Desk Manager |
| People | Contract and Supplier Managers | Manage communication obligations with outsourced providers and contractors. | Contract Manager |
| Technology | FM helpdesk / computer-aided facility management system | Manage requests, ticket communications, work order updates, records, and reporting. | FM Service Desk Manager |
| Technology | Email and distribution list management | Issue formal notices and routine updates to defined audiences. | IT Service Owner |
| Technology | Intranet / FM portal | Publish persistent FM guidance, policies, service catalogue, FAQs, and announcements. | FM Governance Lead |
| Technology | Emergency notification system | Send urgent alerts for facility emergencies, closures, and critical disruptions. | Business Continuity Manager |
| Technology | Digital signage and noticeboards | Communicate site-specific operational notices and awareness messages. | Site FM Manager |
| Technology | Performance dashboards | Communicate KPIs, SLAs, trends, and service performance information. | FM Performance Manager |
| Documented Information | FM Communication Matrix | Record planned communications required by ISO 41001. | FM Communications Coordinator |
| Documented Information | Communication templates | Standardise planned works, disruption, emergency, supplier, and performance messages. | FM Communications Coordinator |
| Documented Information | Contact registers and distribution lists | Ensure communications reach correct recipients. | Site FM Managers / IT Service Owner |
| Documented Information | Meeting minutes and action logs | Evidence governance, decisions, escalations, and follow-up actions. | Meeting Chair |
| Documented Information | Reports and dashboards | Evidence performance communication and management review inputs. | FM Performance Manager |
| Financial | Communications platform licensing and maintenance | Maintain tools needed for reliable communication. | Facilities Management Director / IT Service Owner |
| Financial | Translation, accessibility, and alternative-format support | Ensure communications are accessible to relevant audiences. | FM System Owner |
| Financial | Training and awareness budget | Support communicator training, stakeholder briefings, and awareness campaigns. | Facilities Management Director |

## Success Metrics

The effectiveness of this Communication Plan shall be measured using qualitative and quantitative indicators aligned with ISO 41001:2018 and FMS performance needs.

| Metric | Definition | Target / Threshold | Measurement Method | Frequency | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Communication Matrix completeness | Percentage of required FM communication topics documented with what, when, with whom, how, responsible role, and record requirements. | 100% for in-scope FMS processes | Matrix review | Quarterly | FM Governance Lead |
| Planned works notification timeliness | Percentage of planned works notices issued within defined notification period. | ≥ [X]% | Work order and notice log review | Monthly | Site FM Manager |
| Critical disruption notification timeliness | Percentage of critical disruption communications issued within defined escalation timeframe. | ≥ [X]% | Incident ticket and notification timestamp review | Monthly / per incident | FM Operations Manager |
| Emergency notification test success | Percentage of intended recipients reached during emergency communication tests. | ≥ [X]% | Emergency notification test report | Semi-annually | Business Continuity Manager |
| Distribution list accuracy | Percentage of sampled distribution lists/contact registers confirmed current. | ≥ [X]% | Contact data review and sampling | Quarterly | FM Communications Coordinator |
| Stakeholder satisfaction with FM communication | Stakeholder rating of timeliness, clarity, usefulness, and accessibility of FM communications. | ≥ [X]/5 average | Survey or feedback form | At least annually | FM Customer Experience Lead |
| Repeat complaints due to poor communication | Number of repeat complaints where inadequate communication is identified as a contributing factor. | Downward trend; no unresolved systemic issue | Complaint trend analysis | Monthly / Quarterly | FM Performance Manager |
| Supplier reporting compliance | Percentage of required supplier reports submitted complete and on time. | ≥ [X]% | Supplier governance review | Monthly / Quarterly | Contract Manager |
| Audit findings related to communication | Number and severity of internal or external audit findings against ISO 41001. | Zero major findings; corrective actions closed on time | Audit reports and action tracker | Per audit cycle | FM Governance Lead |
| Communication record retrievability | Percentage of sampled significant communications retrievable within required timeframe. | ≥ [X]% within [X] business days | Documented information sampling | Quarterly | Document Control Manager |
| Management review coverage | Inclusion of communication effectiveness, feedback, incidents, risks, and improvements in FMS management review. | 100% of scheduled management reviews | Management review pack review | Annually | FM System Owner |
| Corrective action closure | Percentage of communication-related corrective or improvement actions closed by due date. | ≥ [X]% | Action tracker | Monthly | FM Governance Lead |

## Review & Update Triggers

This Communication Plan shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that could affect the communication requirements of the FMS.

Review and update triggers include:

- Changes to ISO 41001:2018 implementation scope, FM services, facilities, sites, building use, or service delivery model.
- Changes to organisational structure, FM roles, accountabilities, authorities, or governance forums.
- Introduction, termination, or significant change of outsourced FM service providers, contracts, service level agreements, or supplier reporting requirements.
- Changes to legal, regulatory, statutory, contractual, health, safety, environmental, security, accessibility, or business continuity communication obligations.
- Significant planned changes affecting facility users, including relocations, refurbishments, closures, new systems, changes to operating hours, or service model changes.
- Facility incidents, emergencies, disruptions, near misses, or crisis events where post-incident review identifies communication gaps.
- Internal audit findings, external audit findings, certification audit observations, nonconformities, or corrective actions relating to ISO 41001:2018.
- Management review decisions requiring changes to communication methods, frequency, content, responsibilities, or resources.
- Stakeholder complaints, satisfaction survey results, tenant feedback, or service review outcomes indicating communication is ineffective or insufficient.
- Changes to approved communication tools, helpdesk systems, intranet platforms, emergency notification systems, dashboards, or document management systems.
- Evidence that contact lists, distribution groups, escalation paths, or templates are inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated.
- New or revised risks and opportunities affecting FMS communications.
- Lessons learned from emergency drills, business continuity exercises, supplier performance reviews, or major maintenance activities.
- Changes to classification, confidentiality, privacy, or information handling requirements affecting FM communications.
- Any other material change that could affect what is communicated, when it is communicated, with whom communication takes place, how communication occurs, or who is responsible.

Updates to this Plan shall be approved by the Facilities Management Director or delegated FM System Owner. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with documented information control requirements.

ISO41-017.title: FM Document Control Procedure
ISO41-017.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [FM-PROC-DC-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Facilities Management System Manager |
| Effective Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Framework | ISO 41001:2018 — Facility Management Management Systems |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

This procedure defines how documented information required by the Facility Management Management System (FMMS) is created, approved, controlled, maintained, distributed, accessed, changed, retained and disposed of in accordance with ISO 41001:2018.

The purpose of this procedure is to ensure that FMMS documented information is:

- Available and suitable for use where and when it is needed.
- Adequately protected against loss of confidentiality, improper use, loss of integrity, or unintended changes.
- Properly identified, described, reviewed, approved and version controlled.
- Maintained as evidence of FMMS conformity, performance and continual improvement.
- Controlled throughout its lifecycle, including external documented information determined to be necessary for FMMS planning and operation.

This procedure supports consistent control of FM-related documentation including policies, procedures, work instructions, service specifications, plans, records, registers, forms, drawings, compliance evidence and supplier/service provider documentation.

## Scope

This procedure applies to all documented information required for the planning, operation, monitoring, evaluation and improvement of the FMMS, including documented information required by ISO 41001:2018 and documented information determined by the organisation to be necessary for effective facility management.

This procedure applies to:

- FMMS policies, procedures, manuals, process maps and work instructions.
- Facility management plans, asset-related documents, service delivery plans and maintenance schedules.
- Records evidencing FM performance, compliance, inspections, incidents, audits, service reviews and corrective actions.
- FM-related legal, regulatory, statutory and contractual documentation.
- Service provider, contractor and supplier documents that are necessary for FM operations or compliance.
- Drawings, specifications, permits, certifications, risk assessments and method statements where used to control or evidence FM activities.
- Electronic and hard copy documented information.
- Documented information held in approved repositories, including [Document Management System], [Facilities Management Information System/CAFM/IWMS], shared drives, controlled registers and approved hard copy locations.

This procedure does not apply to:

- General business correspondence unless retained as FMMS evidence.
- Informal notes, draft working papers or transitory communications not used as FMMS records.
- Human Resources, Finance, IT or Legal records unless they are required to support FMMS processes, compliance obligations or facility management service delivery.

Where documented information is governed by another approved organisational procedure, such as information security, privacy, contract management or records retention, this procedure shall be applied in conjunction with that procedure. Where conflicts arise, the stricter control requirement shall apply unless otherwise approved by the Facilities Management System Manager and relevant process owner.

## Prerequisites & Inputs

The following prerequisites shall be in place before this procedure is operated:

| Prerequisite | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Approved document repository | An approved location for controlled FMMS documents, such as [Document Management System], with appropriate access control and backup arrangements. |
| Document control responsibilities | Assigned document owners, reviewers, approvers and administrators for FMMS documented information. |
| Naming and identification rules | Standard document identification, versioning, classification and metadata conventions. |
| Access control model | Defined permissions based on role, operational need, confidentiality and legal/regulatory requirements. |
| Retention requirements | Approved FMMS records retention schedule aligned to statutory, regulatory, contractual and business requirements. |
| Approval workflow | Defined review and approval process before controlled documents are issued or amended. |
| Change control mechanism | Method for requesting, assessing, approving and recording document changes. |
| Obsolete document control | Method for withdrawal, archival, retention or disposal of superseded documents. |
| External document register | Register or equivalent mechanism to identify and control external documented information necessary for the FMMS. |

Inputs to this procedure may include:

- ISO 41001:2018 requirements, specifically.
- FMMS scope, policy, objectives and process requirements.
- Applicable legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.
- Customer, end-user, interested party and organisational requirements.
- FM service specifications and service level agreements.
- Asset information, maintenance requirements, manufacturer instructions and technical manuals.
- Inspection, audit, monitoring and performance evidence.
- Risk assessments, business continuity requirements and operational controls.
- Supplier, contractor and service provider documents.
- Records retention schedule.
- Information classification and handling requirements.
- Corrective action, improvement or management review outputs requiring document updates.

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

1. **Determine the need for documented information**

 1.1. The relevant FM process owner shall determine whether documented information is required to support effective operation, control, monitoring, compliance or improvement of an FMMS process.

 1.2. Documented information shall be created or retained where required by:

 - ISO 41001:2018.
 - Applicable legal, statutory, regulatory or contractual obligations.
 - Organisational FMMS requirements.
 - Customer or end-user requirements.
 - Operational control needs.
 - Risk management or business continuity needs.
 - Evidence of service delivery, compliance, performance, audit or corrective action.
 - Management review or continual improvement actions.

 1.3. The process owner shall confirm the type of documented information required, such as policy, procedure, plan, form, record, register, specification, drawing, checklist or report.

 1.4. The Facilities Management System Manager shall ensure required FMMS documented information is reflected in the FMMS Document Register or approved equivalent.

2. **Classify the document or record**

 2.1. The document owner shall classify the documented information based on its purpose, sensitivity, operational criticality and retention requirement.

 2.2. The classification shall be recorded in the document metadata or register.

 2.3. The following classifications shall be used unless the organisation has an approved alternative classification scheme:

 | Classification | Description | Typical FMMS Examples | Handling Requirement |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Public | Approved for public release. | Published FM service commitments, public access information. | May be shared externally once approved. |
 | Internal | For internal organisational use. | FM procedures, maintenance plans, internal registers. | Access limited to authorised personnel. |
 | Confidential | Sensitive business, contractual, security or personal information. | Security layouts, supplier pricing, incident reports, restricted asset information. | Access restricted to defined roles; sharing requires owner approval. |
 | Restricted | Highly sensitive information requiring strict control. | Critical infrastructure layouts, emergency access codes, high-risk vulnerability information. | Access by explicit authorisation only; enhanced protection required. |

 2.4. Where documented information contains personal data, security-sensitive information, legal privilege, commercially sensitive information or regulated information, the document owner shall consult the relevant function, such as Legal, Information Security, Privacy or Procurement, before approval or distribution.

3. **Create or update the documented information**

 3.1. The document owner shall create or update the document using the approved template where one exists.

 3.2. Controlled FMMS documents shall include, as appropriate:

 - Document title.
 - Document ID or unique identifier.
 - Version number.
 - Owner.
 - Approver.
 - Effective date.
 - Review date or review frequency.
 - Classification.
 - Scope or applicability.
 - Revision history.
 - Related documents or records.
 - Required approvals.
 - Retention requirements where applicable.

 3.3. The document owner shall ensure the documented information is:

 - Fit for its intended purpose.
 - Accurate, current and complete.
 - Consistent with FMMS policy, objectives and operational controls.
 - Aligned with ISO 41001:2018 requirements where applicable.
 - Clear enough to be understood by intended users.
 - Compatible with relevant legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements.
 - Consistent with other controlled FMMS documentation.
 - Suitable for the medium in which it will be used, including mobile, digital or hard copy use where required for FM operations.

 3.4. Where documents are prepared to control operational activities, the document owner shall consult relevant users, including FM operations, service providers, asset managers, health and safety representatives or contract managers, as appropriate.

 3.5. Where a document replaces or significantly changes existing instructions, the document owner shall identify affected documents, records, systems, contracts, training materials and operational controls.

4. **Apply document identification and version control**

 4.1. Each controlled FMMS document shall be assigned a unique identifier before approval.

 4.2. The standard document identification format shall be:

 | Element | Format | Example |
 |---|---|---|
 | Function prefix | FM | FM |
 | Document type | POL, PROC, WI, PLAN, FORM, REG, SPEC, REC | PROC |
 | Short descriptor | 2–5 meaningful letters or numbers | DC |
 | Sequence number | Three digits | 001 |
 | Full ID | Function-Type-Descriptor-Number | FM-PROC-DC-001 |

 4.3. Version numbering shall be applied as follows:

 | Version Type | Use | Example |
 |---|---|---|
 | Draft version | Working draft not approved for use. | 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 |
 | First approved issue | Initial approved controlled version. | 1.0 |
 | Minor update | Administrative or non-substantive change. | 1.1, 1.2 |
 | Major update | Material change to requirements, process, responsibility, control or scope. | 2.0 |

 4.4. Draft documents shall be clearly marked as “Draft” and shall not be used to perform controlled FMMS activities unless specifically authorised by the document owner for pilot or validation purposes.

 4.5. Once approved, the document controller or assigned administrator shall update the FMMS Document Register.

5. **Review and approve documented information before issue**

 5.1. All new or materially revised controlled FMMS documents shall be reviewed and approved before issue.

 5.2. The review shall verify that the documented information is:

 - Adequate for its intended use.
 - Complete and technically accurate.
 - Compatible with FMMS objectives and processes.
 - Consistent with ISO 41001:2018 requirements.
 - Consistent with legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.
 - Clear regarding roles, responsibilities and required records.
 - Appropriately classified and access-controlled.
 - Assigned to an accountable owner and review cycle.

 5.3. Minimum approval requirements are:

 | Document Type | Prepared By | Reviewed By | Approved By |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | FMMS policy | Facilities Management System Manager | Senior FM Leadership, Compliance/Legal as required | Top Management or delegated executive |
 | FMMS procedure | Process Owner | Facilities Management System Manager, affected functions | FM Director or authorised delegate |
 | Work instruction | Supervisor or technical owner | Process Owner, affected users | Process Owner |
 | FM plan or programme | Process Owner or Planner | FM Operations, relevant stakeholders | FM Director or authorised delegate |
 | Form or template | Document Owner | Process Owner | Facilities Management System Manager or delegate |
 | Register | Register Owner | Facilities Management System Manager | Process Owner |
 | Record format | Process Owner | Record users as required | Process Owner |
 | External document acceptance | Document Owner | Technical SME, Contract Manager as applicable | Process Owner |

 5.4. Approval evidence shall be retained through system workflow, electronic signature, email approval, approval log or signed approval page.

 5.5. Approved documents shall not be altered outside the approved change process.

6. **Issue and publish controlled documents**

 6.1. The document controller or authorised administrator shall publish only the approved version of controlled FMMS documents in the approved repository.

 6.2. Published controlled documents shall be made available to users at the point of need, including operational locations, digital systems, contractor portals or mobile platforms where appropriate.

 6.3. For each controlled document, the document controller shall confirm that:

 - The approved version is uploaded to the authorised repository.
 - Metadata is complete and accurate.
 - Access permissions are applied.
 - Previous versions are removed from active use or clearly marked as obsolete.
 - The document is included in the FMMS Document Register.
 - Required communication or training actions are initiated.

 6.4. Hard copy controlled documents may be used only where operationally required, such as plant rooms, reception desks, emergency control points, workshops or field maintenance locations.

 6.5. Controlled hard copies shall include:

 - Document ID.
 - Version number.
 - Issue date.
 - Controlled copy number, where applicable.
 - Location of use.
 - Statement indicating that printed copies are uncontrolled unless specifically marked as controlled.

 6.6. Uncontrolled copies may be used for reference only and shall not be relied upon to perform controlled FMMS activities unless verified against the current approved version.

7. **Maintain document availability and access control**

 7.1. The Facilities Management System Manager shall ensure that documented information required by the FMMS is available and suitable for use where and when needed.

 7.2. The document controller shall maintain access to controlled documents based on user roles, operational need and classification.

 7.3. Access shall be managed using approved mechanisms such as:

 - Role-based access permissions.
 - Read-only publishing folders.
 - Workflow-based editing permissions.
 - Controlled contractor or supplier access.
 - Physical security for hard copy files.
 - Backup and recovery controls for electronic repositories.

 7.4. The document owner shall periodically confirm that intended users can access required documented information.

 7.5. Documents required for emergency response, statutory compliance, critical asset operation or service continuity shall be accessible within timeframes appropriate to their use.

 | Document Category | Availability Requirement | Access Consideration |
 |---|---|---|
 | Emergency and incident response documents | Immediate access during operating hours and emergencies | Accessible to authorised response personnel; offline copy where required |
 | Critical asset information | Available when planning or performing maintenance/repair | Restricted where security-sensitive |
 | Statutory compliance records | Available for inspection, audit or regulatory review | Protected from alteration or loss |
 | Operational work instructions | Available at point of work | Current version only |
 | Contractor documents | Available before and during service delivery | Access aligned to contract and site requirements |
 | FMMS audit records | Available for internal and external audit | Protected from unauthorised modification |

8. **Protect documented information**

 8.1. FMMS documented information shall be protected from:

 - Unauthorised access.
 - Improper use.
 - Loss of integrity.
 - Accidental or unauthorised change.
 - Loss, damage or destruction.
 - Unintended disclosure.
 - Use of obsolete or superseded information.

 8.2. Electronic documented information shall be protected through approved organisational controls, including as applicable:

 - Access authentication.
 - Authorisation based on role and need.
 - Read-only access for approved published documents.
 - Backup and recovery arrangements.
 - Audit logging or change history.
 - Malware protection.
 - Secure storage and transmission.
 - Retention and legal hold controls.

 8.3. Physical documented information shall be protected through appropriate physical controls, including as applicable:

 - Locked cabinets or secure rooms.
 - Controlled access areas.
 - Sign-out logs for sensitive documents.
 - Environmental protection from fire, water or deterioration.
 - Secure disposal bins or shredding.
 - Regular checks of controlled copy locations.

 8.4. Security-sensitive FM documentation, including building layouts, access control information, critical infrastructure information, emergency plans and asset vulnerability information, shall be shared only with authorised personnel and service providers with a legitimate need.

9. **Control changes to documented information**

 9.1. Any user may request a change to FMMS documented information where the document is inaccurate, unclear, obsolete, incomplete or no longer aligned with operational, statutory, contractual or FMMS requirements.

 9.2. Change requests shall be submitted through the approved change method, such as [Document Change Request Form], [Document Management System workflow] or email to the document owner.

 9.3. The change request shall include:

 | Field | Required Information |
 |---|---|
 | Document ID and title | Controlled document affected |
 | Current version | Version requiring change |
 | Requested by | Name, role and department |
 | Date requested | Date of submission |
 | Reason for change | Error, improvement, audit finding, regulatory change, incident, process change, contract change, etc. |
 | Description of proposed change | Specific update requested |
 | Urgency | Routine, time-sensitive, urgent |
 | Affected users/processes | Operational areas impacted |
 | Required effective date | Date by which change is needed |
 | Supporting evidence | Audit finding, incident report, legal requirement, user feedback, etc. |

 9.4. The document owner shall assess the change request and determine whether the change is:

 - Administrative, such as formatting, spelling, contact details or minor clarification.
 - Minor, such as non-material process clarification or update to references.
 - Major, such as changes to requirements, responsibilities, approval authority, operational controls, statutory compliance, service levels or risk controls.

 9.5. Administrative changes may be approved by the document owner or document controller where they do not alter meaning or requirements.

 9.6. Minor and major changes shall follow review and approval requirements defined in this procedure.

 9.7. The document owner shall assess whether the change requires:

 - Updates to related documents.
 - Communication to affected users.
 - Training or competency updates.
 - Contract or supplier notification.
 - System configuration changes.
 - Risk assessment update.
 - Legal, regulatory or customer notification.
 - Management review input.

 9.8. The document controller shall update the revision history for approved changes.

 9.9. Superseded versions shall be withdrawn from active use immediately upon publication of the new approved version, unless a defined transition period is approved.

10. **Control obsolete and superseded documented information**

 10.1. Obsolete documents shall be removed from points of use or clearly identified to prevent unintended use.

 10.2. Electronic obsolete documents shall be moved to an archive location with restricted access or marked as obsolete in the document management system.

 10.3. Hard copy obsolete documents shall be collected, destroyed or stamped “Obsolete” where retention is required.

 10.4. Obsolete versions retained for knowledge preservation, legal, contractual, audit or historical purposes shall be protected from unintended use.

 10.5. The document controller shall record withdrawal or archival activity in the FMMS Document Register.

11. **Control external documented information**
