## Analysis

### Alignment with ISO 41001:2018

ISO 41001:2018 requires the organisation to determine what needs to be monitored and measured, the methods for monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation, when monitoring and measuring shall be performed, and when results shall be analysed and evaluated. This occupant satisfaction survey forms part of the organisation’s FMS performance evaluation process and provides evidence of user-focused monitoring.

The survey supports by:

- Measuring occupant satisfaction with facility management service delivery.
- Evaluating whether facilities support organisational needs and user requirements.
- Providing data for trend analysis and management review.
- Identifying service gaps and improvement opportunities.
- Supporting evidence-based decisions for corrective actions, supplier oversight, resource allocation and workplace planning.
- Maintaining documented information as evidence of monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation.

### Performance Against Objectives

| Facility Management Objective | Related Survey Measure | Result | Objective Status | Commentary |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Maintain occupant satisfaction at or above target | Overall satisfaction | [Score]% | [Met / Not Met] | [Commentary] |
| Provide safe, secure and compliant facilities | Safety and security satisfaction | [Score]% | [Met / Not Met] | Strong perception of safety; awareness gaps require attention |
| Deliver responsive maintenance services | Maintenance responsiveness | [Score]% | [Met / Not Met] | Response and closure communication below expectation |
| Maintain comfortable and productive workplaces | Building comfort and workspace functionality | [Score]% | [Met / Not Met] | Thermal comfort and quiet space availability are key issues |
| Improve engagement with building users | Communication and feedback satisfaction | [Score]% | [Met / Not Met] | Communication requires structured improvement |
| Support sustainability outcomes | Sustainability service satisfaction | [Score]% | [Met / Not Met] | Recycling improvements recognised; guidance still needed |

### Trend Analysis

The current-period results indicate the following trends:

- Overall satisfaction has **[increased / decreased / remained stable]** compared with the previous reporting period.
- Cleanliness and hygiene performance has **[improved / remained stable]**, likely influenced by [cleaning contract review / revised inspection regime / increased cleaning frequency].
- Building comfort satisfaction has **[declined / remained below target]**, indicating persistent HVAC zoning or workplace density issues.
- Maintenance satisfaction has **[declined / improved]** in relation to response timeliness but remains affected by communication during extended repairs.
- Safety and security satisfaction remains consistently high, although emergency procedure awareness should be reinforced.
- Communication satisfaction has **[declined]**, suggesting that operational changes and planned works are not being communicated consistently or early enough.

### Root Cause Considerations

The following likely contributing factors were identified based on survey comments and supporting operational data:

| Issue | Likely Contributing Factors | Additional Verification Required |
|---|---|---|
| Thermal discomfort | HVAC zoning limitations, setpoint controls, occupancy variation, seasonal changes, local equipment heat loads | Review BMS logs, maintenance records and zone temperature readings |
| Maintenance dissatisfaction | SLA delays, lack of automated updates, insufficient closure confirmation, contractor dependency | Review helpdesk workflow and ticket ageing data |
| Poor communication of works | Decentralised communication ownership, inconsistent notice templates, insufficient lead time | Review planned works communication process |
| Meeting room availability | Peak-day occupancy, block bookings, limited room release discipline, hybrid meeting demand | Review booking data and utilisation patterns |
| Quiet space shortage | Increased collaborative activity, open-plan density, limited acoustic separation | Conduct workspace utilisation and acoustic assessment |
| Accessibility concerns | Local layout constraints, equipment availability, limited awareness of adjustment process | Conduct accessibility review with relevant stakeholders |

### Risk and Impact Assessment

| Risk Area | Impact on Facility Management Outcomes | Current Risk Level | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Occupant wellbeing and productivity | Discomfort and noise may reduce productivity and workplace satisfaction | Medium | Repeated comfort and quiet space feedback |
| Service performance perception | Poor updates may reduce trust even where work is progressing | Medium | Maintenance communication below target |
| Safety readiness | Emergency procedure awareness gaps may affect response effectiveness | Medium | Lower awareness among some occupant groups |
| Compliance and accessibility | Unresolved accessibility issues may create legal, reputational or wellbeing impacts | Medium / High depending on issue | Requires further assessment |
| Sustainability engagement | Confusing waste arrangements may reduce recycling effectiveness | Low / Medium | Improvement opportunity rather than immediate nonconformity |

### Evaluation of Data Adequacy

The survey response rate of **[Response Rate]%** is assessed as **[sufficient / partially sufficient / insufficient]** to support evaluation of occupant satisfaction for the reporting period. Results are most reliable for facilities and occupant groups where minimum response thresholds were met. Where response rates were below target, findings should be treated as indicative and supplemented with helpdesk, inspection and occupancy data.

The combination of quantitative scores, qualitative comments and operational metrics provides a reasonable evidence base for management review and improvement planning, subject to further verification of safety, accessibility and comfort-related issues.

## Recommendations & Actions

### Recommended Management Actions

The following actions are recommended to address survey findings and support continual improvement of the Facility Management System.

| Action ID | Recommendation / Action | Priority | Responsible Owner | Due Date | Success Measure | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FM-ACT-[001] | Review HVAC performance in low-scoring zones, including BMS data, setpoints, air balancing and recent maintenance records | High | Facilities Manager / Engineering Lead | [Due Date] | Temperature complaints reduced by [Target]% and comfort score improves to ≥ [Target]% | Open |
| FM-ACT-[002] | Implement standard communication template and minimum notice period for planned works and service disruptions | High | Facilities Management Manager | [Due Date] | Communication satisfaction improves by [Target] pp; ≥ [Target]% planned works issued within required notice | Open |
| FM-ACT-[003] | Configure maintenance helpdesk status updates for acknowledged, in-progress, delayed and closed tickets | High | FM Helpdesk Lead / System Owner | [Due Date] | Maintenance communication score improves to ≥ [Target]%; reduced reopened tickets | Open |
| FM-ACT-[004] | Conduct inspection of reported emergency route obstruction and reinforce emergency route housekeeping controls | Immediate | Site Facilities Coordinator / HSE Lead | [Due Date] | Inspection completed; no blocked routes identified in follow-up checks | Open |
| FM-ACT-[005] | Publish occupant feedback response summary using “you said, we did / we are doing” format | Medium | FM Communications Lead | [Due Date] | Published update; improved perception that FM considers feedback | Open |
| FM-ACT-[006] | Review meeting room and quiet space utilisation data and propose optimisation measures | Medium | Workplace Planning Lead | [Due Date] | Utilisation report completed; action plan approved | Open |
| FM-ACT-[007] | Review accessibility-related comments and complete targeted accessibility assessment for identified areas | High | Facilities Manager / HR / HSE | [Due Date] | Assessment completed; required adjustments tracked to closure | Open |
| FM-ACT-[008] | Update occupant guidance for waste segregation and recycling points | Low / Medium | Sustainability Lead / FM | [Due Date] | Reduced waste confusion comments; improved sustainability score | Open |
| FM-ACT-[009] | Reinforce emergency procedure awareness for new and existing occupants | Medium | HSE Lead / FM | [Due Date] | Emergency awareness score improves to ≥ [Target]% | Open |
| FM-ACT-[010] | Review cleaning schedule and user etiquette controls for kitchen and break areas in low-scoring locations | Medium | Cleaning Contract Manager | [Due Date] | Kitchen cleanliness score improves to ≥ [Target]% | Open |

### Corrective Action Requirements

Where findings indicate failure to meet defined service requirements, legal requirements, internal FM standards or FMS objectives, the responsible owner shall determine whether a corrective action record is required under the organisation’s nonconformity and corrective action process.

Corrective action shall be considered mandatory where:

- A safety or emergency readiness issue is confirmed.
- A service level failure has occurred repeatedly or materially affected occupants.
- A legal, accessibility, health or compliance requirement may not have been met.
- A defined FM objective or KPI has not been achieved and root cause analysis is required.
- Survey results indicate persistent dissatisfaction across multiple reporting periods.

### Follow-Up Monitoring

Progress against actions will be monitored through the following mechanisms:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Owner | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Action tracker review | Monthly until closure | Facilities Management Manager | Updated action log |
| Maintenance SLA reporting | Monthly | FM Helpdesk Lead | Helpdesk performance report |
| HVAC comfort issue review | Monthly during affected season | Engineering Lead | BMS data, complaint trends, maintenance records |
| Safety and emergency route inspection | [Frequency] | HSE / Site FM | Inspection checklist |
| Planned works communication compliance review | Quarterly | FM Communications Lead | Communication records |
| Occupant pulse survey on targeted issues | [Frequency] | FM Manager | Survey summary |
| Management review input | At scheduled FMS management review | FMS Owner | Management review pack |

### Expected Improvement Outcomes

Successful implementation of the recommended actions is expected to:

- Improve occupant satisfaction with building comfort, maintenance and communication.
- Reduce recurring complaints and improve perceived responsiveness.
- Improve evidence-based decision-making for workplace planning.
- Strengthen compliance with ISO 41001 monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation requirements.
- Improve user confidence that facility management listens to and acts on feedback.
- Support continual improvement of the Facility Management System.

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution

This report shall be distributed to roles with responsibility for facility management performance, governance, risk, compliance, service delivery and continual improvement.

| Recipient / Role | Purpose of Distribution |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor for Facility Management | Oversight of user satisfaction and resource implications |
| Facilities Management Manager | Accountability for action planning and service improvement |
| Site Facilities Coordinators | Site-level review and action implementation |
| HSE Manager | Review of safety, emergency and wellbeing-related findings |
| Security Lead | Review of security and access-control feedback |
| Cleaning Contract Manager | Review of cleaning and hygiene findings |
| Maintenance / Engineering Lead | Review of maintenance and comfort-related findings |
| Workplace Planning Lead | Review of space utilisation and functionality findings |
| Sustainability Lead | Review of waste and environmental service feedback |
| ISO 41001 Management System Representative | Evidence for and management review |
| Internal Audit / Compliance Function | Assurance and audit evidence |
| Relevant Service Providers | Limited extracts relevant to contracted services, subject to confidentiality controls |

### Confidentiality

This report is classified as **Internal Confidential**. It contains aggregated occupant feedback, facility performance information and improvement actions. It shall be handled in accordance with the organisation’s information classification, privacy and records management requirements.

The following confidentiality requirements apply:

- Individual respondent identities shall not be disclosed.
- Open-text comments shall be anonymised before broader distribution where there is any risk of identifying individuals.
- Site-level results may be shared with responsible managers for improvement purposes.
- Extracts shared with service providers shall be limited to information necessary for service improvement and contract management.
- The report shall not be distributed externally without approval from the Facilities Management Manager and other required organisational authorities.
- Survey data and supporting analysis shall be retained for the period defined in the FMS documented information retention schedule.
- Any personal data collected during the survey shall be processed in accordance with applicable privacy requirements and the organisation’s data protection policies.

### Documented Information and Audit Evidence

The following records shall be retained with this report as supporting documented information:

| Record | Retention Location | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Final survey questionnaire | [Document Repository / System] | Facilities Management Manager |
| Survey response dataset, anonymised | [Survey Tool / Repository] | FM Survey Owner |
| Survey distribution communications | [Email Archive / Repository] | FM Communications Lead |
| Data analysis workbook / dashboard | [Repository / BI System] | FM Analyst |
| Action tracker | [Action Management System] | Facilities Management Manager |
| Supporting operational metrics | [Helpdesk / CAFM / BMS System] | Relevant System Owner |
| Management review submission | [FMS Repository] | ISO 41001 Management System Representative |

This report and associated records provide evidence that occupant satisfaction has been monitored, measured, analysed and evaluated as part of the organisation’s ISO 41001:2018 Facility Management System performance evaluation process.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Audit Programme Year | Enter the calendar or financial year covered by this audit programme; format YYYY or YYYY/YYYY. |
| Audit ID | Enter a unique identifier for the planned audit; use a controlled format such as IA-FMS-YYYY-###. |
| Audit Title | Enter a short descriptive title for the audit, e.g. Facilities Maintenance Process Audit. |
| FMS Process / Area to be Audited | Enter the specific facilities management system process, function, service, contract, or operational area to be audited. |
| Facility / Site / Location | Enter the physical site, building, region, campus, or location covered by the audit; use 'Organisation-wide' if applicable. |
| ISO 41001:2018 Clause(s) | Enter the applicable ISO 41001:2018 clause references to be audited, e.g. 4.1, 6.1, 8.1, 9.1, 9.2; separate multiple clauses with commas. |
| Organisation FMS Requirement(s) / Procedure Ref(s) | Enter the internal FMS policy, procedure, contract, SLA, process map, work instruction, or documented requirement reference used as audit criteria. |
| Audit Criteria | Enter the requirements against which evidence will be assessed, including ISO 41001 clauses, internal procedures, legal/contractual requirements, SLAs, and customer/user requirements where applicable. |
| Audit Scope | Define the boundaries of the audit, including included processes, activities, services, locations, departments, time period, and any exclusions. |
| Audit Objective | State what the audit is intended to determine, such as conformity to ISO 41001 and internal FMS requirements, effective implementation, or effectiveness of specific controls. |
| Reason for Inclusion / Priority Basis | Enter why this audit is scheduled, considering process importance, FMS risks/opportunities, service criticality, legal/contractual importance, recent changes, incidents, performance issues, or previous audit results. |
| Risk / Importance Rating | Select one value: High, Medium, Low; base the rating on process criticality, risk to facilities services, compliance exposure, customer/user impact, or prior performance. |
| Changes Since Last Audit Considered | Record relevant changes considered when planning the audit, such as organisational change, new suppliers, changed service scope, new systems, incidents, revised procedures, or write 'None identified'. |
| Previous Audit Result Considered | Summarise the relevant previous audit outcome considered for programme planning, e.g. No findings, Minor NCs, Major NC, repeat issue, overdue actions, or Not previously audited. |
| Planned Audit Frequency | Enter the planned recurrence for this audit, e.g. Annual, Semi-annual, Quarterly, Biennial, One-off, or Risk-based. |
| Planned Audit Start Date | Enter the planned audit start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Planned Audit End Date | Enter the planned audit end date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Audit Method | Select one or more methods: On-site, Remote, Hybrid, Document review, Interview, Observation, Sampling, System walkthrough. |
| Lead Auditor | Enter the name or role of the assigned lead auditor responsible for planning, conducting, and reporting the audit. |
| Audit Team Members | Enter names or roles of other assigned auditors or technical experts; enter 'None' if not applicable. |
| Independence / Impartiality Confirmation | Confirm that assigned auditor(s) are independent of the activity being audited; select Yes, No, or Mitigation required, and add brief mitigation if independence risk exists. |
| Auditee Process Owner | Enter the name or role of the manager responsible for the process or area being audited. |
| Relevant Management to Receive Report | Enter the management role(s), committee, or leadership forum that will receive the audit results. |
| Planned Report Issue Date | Enter the planned date for issuing the internal audit report in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Audit Status | Select one value: Planned, Scheduled, In progress, Completed, Deferred, Cancelled. |
| Audit Report / Record Reference | Enter the controlled reference or hyperlink to the audit report or retained documented information once completed; leave blank until available. |
| Linked Corrective Action Reference | Enter the corrective action, nonconformity, or improvement action reference(s) raised from the audit; leave blank until available or enter 'None' after completion if no actions are raised. |
| Programme Approval | Select one value: Draft, Submitted, Approved, Revision required. |
| Programme Approved By | Enter the name and role of the person approving the internal FMS audit programme. |
| Programme Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until approved. |
| Notes / Constraints | Enter any planning constraints, dependencies, blackout periods, access limitations, sampling considerations, or coordination requirements. |

### Maintenance

The FMS Compliance Manager or Internal Audit Programme Owner owns this template and updates it at least annually, and whenever significant FMS changes, risks, incidents, or previous audit results require programme revision. Source inputs should be drawn from the FMS process register, risk and opportunity register, previous internal audit reports, corrective action log, management review outputs, CAFM/service management system, legal/compliance register, and approved FMS procedures.

ISO41-026.title: Internal FMS Audit Report
ISO41-026.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [FMS-IA-REP-001] | 1.0 | [Head of Facilities Management / FMS Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO 41001:2018 Facility Management Systems | — Internal Audit | Confidential — Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This Internal Facility Management System Audit Report documents the results, findings, conclusions, and recommended actions arising from the internal audit of the organisation’s Facility Management System (FMS) conducted in accordance with ISO 41001:2018.

The purpose of this report is to provide objective evidence on whether the FMS:

- Conforms to the organisation’s own requirements for its Facility Management System;
- Conforms to the requirements of ISO 41001:2018;
- Is effectively implemented and maintained;
- Supports the intended outcomes of the FMS, including effective facility service delivery, alignment with demand organisation needs, statutory and regulatory compliance, risk-based planning, performance improvement, and user satisfaction;
- Provides suitable inputs for management review under ISO 41001:2018.

This report is intended for use by senior management, the FMS process owners, internal auditors, and other authorised stakeholders responsible for governance, assurance, corrective action, and continual improvement of the FMS.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

This report covers the internal audit performed during the following period:

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Audit period | [YYYY-MM-DD] to [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Reporting period reviewed | [YYYY-MM-DD] to [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Audit plan reference | [FMS-IA-PLAN-001] |
| Audit programme reference | [FMS-IA-PROG-001] |
| Audit report date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Lead auditor | [Name / Role] |
| Audit team members | [Names / Roles] |
| Auditee representative | [Name / Role] |

### Audit Scope

The audit assessed selected FMS processes, locations, documented information, personnel, outsourced service arrangements, and operational controls relevant to ISO 41001:2018 and associated clauses necessary to determine FMS conformity and effectiveness.

The audit scope included:

- FMS governance, leadership, and accountability;
- Facility management policy and objectives;
- Understanding organisational context and interested party requirements;
- Demand organisation requirements and service level expectations;
- Planning of FMS risks, opportunities, objectives, and changes;
- Support processes, including competence, awareness, communication, and documented information;
- Operational planning and control of facility services;
- Outsourced and supplier-managed facility services;
- Performance evaluation, monitoring, measurement, analysis, and evaluation;
- Previous audit findings, corrective actions, and continual improvement activities.

### Locations / Functions Audited

| Area / Location / Function | Included in Scope | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| [Head Office / Main Facility] | Yes | Review of FMS governance, service delivery, compliance evidence, and records |
| [Site / Region / Facility 1] | Yes | Sample-based review of operational controls and service performance |
| [Site / Region / Facility 2] | [Yes/No] | [Reason if excluded or partially covered] |
| Facilities Helpdesk / CAFM Function | Yes | Work order management, response times, service request data |
| Hard FM Services | Yes | Maintenance, statutory inspections, asset-related controls |
| Soft FM Services | Yes | Cleaning, security, waste, reception, and user-facing services |
| Procurement / Supplier Management | Yes | Contract controls, outsourced FM service monitoring |
| Health, Safety, Environment and Compliance Interface | Yes | Relevant statutory and regulatory facility obligations |

### ISO 41001:2018 Clauses Sampled

While the audit was conducted under the internal audit requirements of, evidence was sampled across the following ISO 41001:2018 clauses to determine conformity and effectiveness:

| ISO 41001 Clause | Area Reviewed | Audit Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | Context of the organisation | Internal and external issues affecting FMS |
| 4.2 | Needs and expectations of interested parties | Interested party requirements and service expectations |
| 4.3 | Scope of the FMS | Defined boundaries and applicability |
| 4.4 | FMS and its processes | Process interactions and maintenance of the FMS |
| 5.1 | Leadership and commitment | Management accountability and support |
| 5.2 | Policy | Facility management policy communication and suitability |
| 5.3 | Roles, responsibilities and authorities | FMS accountability and delegated authority |
| 6.1 | Actions to address risks and opportunities | Risk-based planning for FMS outcomes |
| 6.2 | FMS objectives and planning | Measurable objectives and plans to achieve them |
| 7.2 | Competence | Competence evidence for FM roles and outsourced services |
| 7.3 | Awareness | Awareness of FMS policy, objectives, and responsibilities |
| 7.4 | Communication | Internal and external FMS communications |
| 7.5 | Documented information | Control of FMS records and documents |
| 8.1 | Operational planning and control | Facility service controls and planned activities |
| 8.2 | Coordination with interested parties | Interface with demand organisation and users |
| 8.3 | Integration of services | Coordination of facility services and delivery partners |
| 9.1 | Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation | KPI reporting, compliance monitoring, performance data |
| 9.2 | Internal audit | Audit programme, audit criteria, impartiality, reporting, records |
| 9.3 | Management review | Inputs from audit and FMS performance |
| 10.1 | Nonconformity and corrective action | Corrective action management |
| 10.2 | Continual improvement | Improvement tracking and evidence |

### Exclusions and Limitations

The following limitations apply to this report:

- The audit was conducted on a sampling basis and does not provide absolute assurance that all nonconformities have been identified.
- Evidence was limited to records, personnel, locations, systems, suppliers, and time periods available during the audit.
- Where outsourced facility services were reviewed, supplier records were assessed only to the extent made available by the organisation and relevant contracted providers.
- Technical verification of asset condition, engineering calculations, or specialist statutory compliance testing was not performed unless specifically stated in the findings.
- Financial audit testing of facility management expenditure was outside the scope except where linked to FMS planning, contractual service delivery, or performance evaluation.

## Executive Summary

The internal audit found that the organisation has established and implemented core elements of a Facility Management System aligned with ISO 41001:2018. The FMS demonstrates defined service delivery responsibilities, an operating model for facility services, documented procedures for key activities, routine performance monitoring, and evidence of management oversight.

However, the audit identified gaps in the maturity and consistency of the internal audit programme itself, particularly in relation to audit criteria, risk-based scheduling, independence of auditors, documentation of objective evidence, and timely closure of corrective actions. These issues are directly relevant to ISO 41001:2018, which requires the organisation to conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the FMS conforms to both organisational and ISO 41001 requirements and is effectively implemented and maintained.

### Overall Audit Conclusion

Based on the evidence sampled, the FMS is **partially conforming and operationally implemented**, with improvement required to strengthen assurance under and to ensure audit outputs consistently support management review, corrective action, and continual improvement.

The FMS appears capable of supporting facility management outcomes; however, the internal audit process requires formalisation and more rigorous execution to provide reliable assurance to top management and interested parties.

### Summary of Findings

| Finding Category | Count | Summary |
|---|---:|---|
| Major Nonconformities | 1 | Internal audit programme does not consistently demonstrate risk-based planning, defined audit criteria, and impartial assignment across the full FMS scope. |
| Minor Nonconformities | 4 | Gaps identified in audit evidence retention, audit report consistency, corrective action follow-up, and coverage of outsourced FM services. |
| Opportunities for Improvement | 5 | Enhancements recommended for auditor competence records, audit checklists, trend analysis, audit dashboarding, and integration with management review. |
| Positive Observations | 4 | Evidence of management support, established KPI monitoring, active facilities helpdesk data review, and documented service delivery procedures. |

### High-Level Risk Implications

The findings may affect the organisation’s ability to:

- Demonstrate complete conformity with ISO 41001:2018;
- Provide reliable assurance that the FMS is effectively implemented and maintained;
- Detect recurring facility service failures, compliance weaknesses, or supplier performance issues in a timely manner;
- Ensure audit outputs are sufficiently robust to support management review and continual improvement;
- Maintain audit readiness for external certification or surveillance audits.

### Audit Opinion

| Rating Area | Audit Opinion |
|---|---|
| FMS implementation | Generally implemented with selected gaps |
| FMS effectiveness | Partially effective; evidence of performance monitoring exists but audit assurance requires strengthening |
| conformity | Partially conforming |
| Corrective action discipline | Needs improvement |
| Management visibility | Adequate, but audit reporting should be more structured and risk-based |
| Certification readiness impact | Moderate risk unless findings are addressed before external audit |

## Methodology

### Audit Approach

The audit was conducted using a risk-based, sample-based approach consistent with ISO 41001:2018 requirements and internal audit good practice. The audit assessed whether the FMS audit process is planned, implemented, documented, reported, and maintained in a manner that provides reliable assurance on FMS conformity and effectiveness.

Audit activities included:

- Review of the FMS audit programme and audit schedule;
- Review of audit plans, audit criteria, scope statements, and previous audit reports;
- Interviews with process owners, facility managers, service coordinators, helpdesk personnel, and contract managers;
- Sampling of documented information, including procedures, records, work orders, KPI reports, supplier performance reports, and corrective action logs;
- Review of evidence related to outsourced facility services;
- Testing of corrective action follow-up and closure evidence;
- Walkthroughs of selected FMS processes and facility service delivery controls;
- Evaluation of alignment between internal audit outputs, management review inputs, and continual improvement activities.

### Audit Criteria

The audit criteria included:

- ISO 41001:2018 requirements, with emphasis on;
- Organisation’s FMS policy, objectives, procedures, and process descriptions;
- FMS audit programme and audit planning documents;
- Service level agreements, facility service specifications, contracts, and key performance indicators;
- Applicable statutory, regulatory, and compliance obligations relevant to facility management;
- Internal requirements for document control, corrective action, risk management, and performance reporting.

### Sampling Performed

| Evidence Category | Sample Size / Coverage | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Internal audit reports reviewed | [Number] reports | Included previous FMS audits and related operational audits |
| Corrective actions sampled | [Number] actions | Reviewed closure evidence and timeliness |
| Facility service KPIs reviewed | [Number] months | Included response times, planned maintenance completion, user satisfaction, and supplier KPIs |
| Work orders / service requests sampled | [Number] records | Reviewed from [CAFM / helpdesk system name] |
| Supplier performance records reviewed | [Number] suppliers | Focus on critical outsourced FM providers |
| FMS documents reviewed | [Number] documents | Procedures, plans, registers, and controlled records |
| Interviews conducted | [Number] personnel | Across FM management, operations, support, and suppliers |
| Locations reviewed | [Number] locations | Includes physical or remote evidence review |

### Finding Classification

Findings were classified using the following criteria:

| Classification | Definition |
|---|---|
| Major Nonconformity | Absence of, or significant failure to implement, a required FMS process; a systemic breakdown; or a condition that creates significant risk to FMS conformity, effectiveness, service continuity, statutory compliance, or certification readiness. |
| Minor Nonconformity | Isolated or limited failure to meet a requirement where the FMS process is generally established but not consistently implemented or documented. |
| Opportunity for Improvement | A recommendation to improve effectiveness, efficiency, maturity, integration, or evidence quality, where no formal nonconformity is established. |
| Positive Observation | Evidence of effective practice, good control design, strong implementation, or beneficial behaviour supporting FMS objectives. |

### Audit Independence and Objectivity

The audit team confirmed that assigned auditors did not audit their own work where practicable. Where specialist knowledge was required from operational personnel, those personnel provided technical input only and did not make final audit conclusions for their own area of responsibility.

Any potential conflicts of interest identified during the audit were documented and managed through independent review by the lead auditor or an alternate competent reviewer.

### FMS-IA-2024-01 — Internal Audit Programme Not Fully Risk-Based or Complete Across FMS Scope

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding type | Major Nonconformity |
| ISO 41001 reference | |
| Related clauses | 4.3, 4.4, 6.1, 8.1, 8.3, 9.1 |
| Risk rating | High |
| Process / area | FMS internal audit programme |
| Owner | [FMS Manager] |
| Status | Open |

#### Requirement

ISO 41001:2018 requires the organisation to conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the FMS conforms to the organisation’s own requirements and to ISO 41001, and whether it is effectively implemented and maintained. The organisation must plan, establish, implement and maintain an audit programme, including frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning requirements and reporting, taking into consideration the importance of the processes concerned, changes affecting the organisation, and results of previous audits.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- FMS internal audit programme for [year];
- Internal audit schedule for [year];
- FMS scope statement;
- FMS process map;
- Previous audit reports dated [YYYY-MM-DD], [YYYY-MM-DD];
- FMS risk register;
- Management review minutes dated [YYYY-MM-DD];
- Corrective action register.

#### Finding

The internal audit programme does not consistently demonstrate that audit frequency, scope, and prioritisation are based on the importance of FMS processes, risk, change, outsourced service criticality, or previous audit results. The current audit schedule lists audit activities by calendar month, but it does not show how the programme covers the full FMS scope or why certain high-risk facility services were prioritised or deferred.

Specific gaps identified include:

- No documented mapping between the FMS scope and planned internal audits;
- Critical outsourced services such as [security / cleaning / maintenance / statutory inspection provider] not clearly included in the audit cycle;
- No evidence that previous nonconformities influenced the current audit schedule;
- No documented consideration of major changes affecting the FMS, such as [new site, contract transition, CAFM implementation, organisational restructuring];
- Some FMS processes listed in the process map have not been audited within the stated cycle.

#### Objective Evidence

| Evidence | Observation |
|---|---|
| Audit programme [year] | Contains audit dates and titles but does not include risk rationale, process importance, or previous audit result inputs |
| FMS risk register | Identifies high-risk areas including statutory maintenance and contractor control, but these are not clearly reflected in audit prioritisation |
| Previous audit report [reference] | Raised supplier performance issues, but no follow-up audit activity was scheduled |
| FMS scope statement | Includes all sites and outsourced services, but audit programme coverage is incomplete |

#### Risk / Impact

This creates a risk that significant FMS processes, outsourced services, statutory obligations, and known weak areas may not be independently assessed at planned intervals. It may also reduce the reliability of internal audit outputs used for management review and certification readiness.

#### Conclusion

The absence of a demonstrably risk-based and complete internal audit programme represents a systemic weakness in the implementation of ISO 41001:2018.

#### Required Correction / Corrective Action

- Revise the FMS internal audit programme to include the full FMS scope, processes, locations, outsourced services, and interfaces.
- Define audit frequency based on process importance, risk, changes, supplier criticality, compliance obligations, and previous audit results.
- Document the rationale for audit scheduling and prioritisation.
- Obtain approval from appropriate FMS leadership.
- Retain the revised audit programme as controlled documented information.

---

### FMS-IA-2024-02 — Audit Criteria and Scope Not Consistently Defined in Audit Plans

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding type | Minor Nonconformity |
| ISO 41001 reference | |
| Related clauses | 7.5 |
| Risk rating | Medium |
| Process / area | Audit planning |
| Owner | [Internal Audit Coordinator] |
| Status | Open |

#### Requirement

ISO 41001:2018 requires internal audits to be planned and conducted in accordance with defined audit criteria and scope.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- Audit plans for [audit references];
- Audit reports for [audit references];
- ISO 41001 clause mapping checklist;
- FMS documented procedure [Internal Audit Procedure].

#### Finding

Several audit plans did not clearly define the audit criteria, scope boundaries, locations, functions, or processes to be audited. In some cases, the audit reports referenced ISO 41001 generally but did not specify which clauses, internal procedures, service requirements, or contractual obligations formed the audit criteria.

#### Objective Evidence

| Audit Record | Observation |
|---|---|
| Audit plan [reference] | Scope stated as “FM operations” without defining locations, functions, or service lines |
| Audit report [reference] | Finding raised against “policy non-compliance” without linking to ISO 41001 clause or internal requirement |
| Audit checklist [reference] | Included general questions but did not identify audit criteria |
| Internal Audit Procedure | Requires audit criteria to be documented but template field was left blank in sampled records |

#### Risk / Impact

Incomplete audit planning may lead to inconsistent audit execution, unclear findings, weak traceability, and difficulty demonstrating conformity to during external assessment.

#### Conclusion

The audit planning process is established but not consistently implemented.

#### Required Correction / Corrective Action

- Update audit plan templates to require explicit audit criteria, scope, locations, processes, and exclusions.
- Train auditors on defining audit criteria using ISO 41001 clauses, internal FMS requirements, legal obligations, and service requirements.
- Retrospectively update current-year audit plans where feasible.

### FMS-IA-2024-03 — Incomplete Retention of Audit Evidence and Objective Records

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding type | Minor Nonconformity |
| ISO 41001 reference | |
| Risk rating | Medium |
| Process / area | Documented information and audit records |
| Owner | [Document Control Owner] |
| Status | Open |

#### Requirement

ISO 41001:2018 requires the organisation to retain documented information as evidence of implementation of the audit programme and audit results. requires documented information required by the FMS and ISO 41001 to be controlled.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- Audit reports;
- Auditor notes;
- Interview records;
- Corrective action records;
- Documented information register;
- Shared drive / document repository [system name].

#### Finding

The organisation retains final audit reports but does not consistently retain supporting evidence such as audit checklists, interview notes, sample lists, screenshots, document references, and evidence reviewed. For [number] sampled audits, objective evidence supporting conclusions was incomplete or not retrievable.

#### Objective Evidence

| Evidence Area | Observation |
|---|---|
| Audit [reference] | Final report retained; checklist and sample evidence not found |
| Audit [reference] | Corrective actions recorded, but original nonconformity evidence unavailable |
| Document repository | Audit evidence stored in inconsistent folders and naming conventions |
| Document retention rules | No defined retention period for internal audit working papers |

#### Risk / Impact

Insufficient evidence retention reduces the organisation’s ability to demonstrate that audits were conducted objectively and that conclusions were evidence-based. It may also impair trend analysis, corrective action verification, and external audit readiness.

#### Conclusion

Audit results are retained, but supporting documented information is not consistently controlled.

#### Required Correction / Corrective Action

- Define mandatory audit records and retention requirements.
- Standardise audit evidence storage, naming conventions, and access controls.
- Include audit checklists, sample lists, interview records, and evidence references in the audit record set.
- Perform a retrospective evidence completeness review for current-year audits.

---

### FMS-IA-2024-04 — Corrective Action Follow-Up Not Consistently Evidenced

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding type | Minor Nonconformity |
| ISO 41001 reference | |
| Risk rating | Medium |
| Process / area | Corrective action management |
| Owner | [Corrective Action Owner] |
| Status | Open |

#### Requirement

ISO 41001:2018 requires audit results to be reported to relevant management. requires the organisation to react to nonconformities, evaluate the need for action to eliminate causes, implement required actions, review effectiveness, and retain documented information.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- Corrective action register;
- Previous internal audit reports;
- Root cause analyses;
- Action closure evidence;
- Management review minutes.

#### Finding

Corrective actions from previous internal audits are logged, but follow-up and effectiveness verification are not consistently documented. Several actions were marked as closed based on completion of tasks rather than evidence that the underlying cause had been addressed.

#### Objective Evidence

| Corrective Action | Observation |
|---|---|
| CA-[reference] | Closed after procedure update; no evidence of implementation or effectiveness review |
| CA-[reference] | Target date exceeded by [number] days with no escalation record |
| CA-[reference] | Root cause field incomplete |
| CA-[reference] | Closure approved by same individual responsible for action implementation |

#### Risk / Impact

Without effective follow-up, recurring audit findings may persist, reducing FMS effectiveness and undermining continual improvement.

#### Conclusion

Corrective action tracking exists but requires stronger verification and escalation controls.

#### Required Correction / Corrective Action

- Require documented root cause analysis for all nonconformities.
- Define closure criteria and effectiveness review requirements.
- Assign independent verification where practicable.
- Escalate overdue actions to FMS leadership.
- Report corrective action status in management review.

---

### FMS-IA-2024-05 — Limited Audit Coverage of Outsourced Facility Services

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding type | Minor Nonconformity |
| ISO 41001 reference | |
| Risk rating | Medium |
| Process / area | Outsourced FM services and supplier assurance |
| Owner | [Contract Manager] |
| Status | Open |

#### Requirement

ISO 41001:2018 requires the organisation to ensure that outsourced processes affecting the FMS are controlled. requires audits to assess whether the FMS conforms to requirements and is effectively implemented and maintained, including relevant outsourced facility service arrangements within the FMS scope.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- Supplier contracts and service specifications;
- Supplier KPI reports;
- Meeting minutes with service providers;
- Internal audit programme;
- Supplier performance reviews;
- Helpdesk performance data.

#### Finding

The internal audit programme does not provide sufficient coverage of outsourced facility services that materially affect FMS outcomes. Supplier performance is monitored through contract meetings and KPI reports, but this monitoring is not equivalent to internal audit assurance against FMS requirements, service controls, risk controls, and ISO 41001 expectations.

#### Objective Evidence

| Supplier / Service | Observation |
|---|---|
| [Maintenance provider] | KPI reports reviewed monthly, but no internal audit of statutory maintenance control records in current cycle |
| [Cleaning provider] | Service inspections performed, but not linked to FMS audit criteria or user satisfaction outcomes |
| [Security provider] | Incident logs reviewed, but no audit of competence, escalation, or emergency interface requirements |
| Supplier review meetings | Minutes retained but do not include audit conclusions against FMS requirements |

#### Risk / Impact

Inadequate audit coverage of outsourced services may prevent the organisation from identifying weaknesses in service delivery, compliance, user experience, and supplier controls.

#### Conclusion

Supplier performance monitoring is established, but internal audit coverage of outsourced FMS processes requires improvement.

#### Required Correction / Corrective Action

- Include critical outsourced services in the FMS audit programme.
- Define supplier audit criteria aligned to ISO 41001, contractual obligations, statutory requirements, and service outcomes.
- Conduct sample-based audits of supplier-controlled records for high-risk services.
- Integrate supplier audit findings into corrective action and management review processes.

### Opportunities for Improvement

| ID | Opportunity | ISO 41001 Reference | Suggested Enhancement | Benefit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FMS-IA-2024-06 | Auditor competence matrix could be strengthened | 7.2, 9.2 | Maintain a matrix showing auditor training, ISO 41001 knowledge, FM process knowledge, audit experience, and independence constraints | Improves confidence in audit quality and impartiality |
| FMS-IA-2024-07 | Audit outputs should be better integrated into management review | 9.2, 9.3 | Include audit trend summary, overdue actions, recurring findings, and audit programme completion in management review packs | Enhances leadership oversight and decision-making |
| FMS-IA-2024-08 | Trend analysis of recurring audit findings should be introduced | 9.1, 9.2 | Categorise findings by process, clause, supplier, site, severity, and root cause | Supports continual improvement and risk prioritisation |
| FMS-IA-2024-09 | Standard audit checklist templates should be aligned to ISO 41001 clauses | 9.2 | Develop modular checklists for governance, operations, supplier management, performance evaluation, and corrective action | Improves consistency and evidence traceability |
| FMS-IA-2024-10 | Audit reporting dashboard would improve visibility of assurance status | 9.2, 7.4 | Create dashboard for audit schedule completion, findings status, overdue actions, and risk ratings | Improves management communication and accountability |

### Positive Observations

| ID | Observation | Evidence | Value to FMS |
|---|---|---|---|
| PO-01 | Facility service KPIs are regularly monitored | Monthly FMS performance reports | Supports monitoring and evaluation under |
| PO-02 | Facilities helpdesk data is actively used to identify service issues | [CAFM / helpdesk system] reports and service request trends | Supports responsiveness to users and demand organisation needs |
| PO-03 | Management demonstrates visible support for FMS implementation | Management review records and FMS steering meetings | Supports leadership expectations under |
| PO-04 | Core operational procedures exist for key facility services | Maintenance, cleaning, security, and service request procedures | Supports operational planning and control under |

## Analysis

### Conformity Analysis Against

ISO 41001:2018 establishes specific expectations for internal audits. The table below summarises the audit team’s assessment against these expectations.

| Requirement | Assessment | Evidence / Basis | Conclusion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conduct internal audits at planned intervals | Partially met | Audit schedule exists, but coverage and risk rationale are incomplete | Improvement required |
| Provide information on conformity to organisational FMS requirements | Partially met | Audits review selected internal procedures, but criteria are inconsistently defined | Improvement required |
| Provide information on conformity to ISO 41001 | Partially met | ISO 41001 is referenced, but clause-level mapping is inconsistent | Improvement required |
| Determine whether FMS is effectively implemented and maintained | Partially met | Some effectiveness evidence reviewed, but audit depth varies by process | Improvement required |
| Plan, establish, implement and maintain an audit programme | Partially met | Programme exists but does not fully address process importance, change, or previous results | Major gap identified |
| Define frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning requirements and reporting | Partially met | Responsibilities and reporting exist; methods and planning criteria need strengthening | Improvement required |
| Consider importance of processes, changes, and previous audit results | Not consistently met | No documented rationale linking these inputs to the audit programme | Major nonconformity |
| Define audit criteria and scope | Partially met | Inconsistent in sampled audit plans | Minor nonconformity |
| Select auditors and conduct audits objectively and impartially | Mostly met | Independence considered informally; competence and conflict records need improvement | OFI |
| Ensure results are reported to relevant management | Mostly met | Reports are issued, but escalation and management review integration could improve | OFI |
| Retain documented information as evidence of audit programme and results | Partially met | Final reports retained; working evidence incomplete | Minor nonconformity |

### Root Cause Themes

The findings indicate several common root cause themes:

| Theme | Description | Related Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Incomplete formalisation of audit programme design | Audit planning is schedule-based rather than risk-based and scope-based | FMS-IA-2024-01, FMS-IA-2024-05 |
| Template and documentation weaknesses | Audit planning and reporting templates do not require all elements | FMS-IA-2024-02, FMS-IA-2024-03 |
| Limited assurance integration | Audit results are not fully integrated with management review, risk management, and supplier governance | FMS-IA-2024-04, FMS-IA-2024-07 |
| Inconsistent evidence discipline | Supporting audit records are not consistently retained or traceable | FMS-IA-2024-03 |
| Maturing corrective action process | Closure practices focus on task completion rather than verified effectiveness | FMS-IA-2024-04 |

### Risk Assessment

| Risk Area | Current Exposure | Potential Consequence | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Certification readiness | Moderate to High | External auditor may raise nonconformity against | High |
| FMS effectiveness assurance | Moderate | Management may lack reliable information on FMS implementation and maintenance | High |
| Outsourced service control | Moderate | Supplier failures may not be detected through audit mechanisms | Medium |
| Statutory and regulatory compliance assurance | Moderate | Compliance-related FM controls may not be independently assessed | Medium |
| Continual improvement | Moderate | Recurring issues may persist due to weak corrective action verification | Medium |
| Documented information control | Moderate | Audit evidence may be insufficient to demonstrate conformity | Medium |

### Overall Maturity Assessment

| Area | Maturity Level | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Audit programme governance | Developing | Programme exists but lacks full risk-based and scope-based design |
| Audit planning | Developing | Audit plans are used but criteria and scope are inconsistent |
| Audit execution | Established | Interviews and evidence reviews occur; depth varies by process |
| Evidence retention | Developing | Final outputs retained; working papers inconsistent |
| Reporting | Established | Reports are issued to management, but trend and risk reporting can improve |
| Corrective action follow-up | Developing | Actions are tracked, but effectiveness verification is inconsistent |
| Integration with management review | Developing | Audit outputs are available but not consistently analysed for strategic decision-making |

### Implications for Management Review

The following matters should be included in the next FMS management review:

- Status and effectiveness of the internal audit programme;
- Major and minor nonconformities identified in this report;
- Progress against corrective actions and overdue actions;
- Recurring themes and root causes;
- Adequacy of resources for audit execution and corrective action;
- Assurance over outsourced facility services;
- Changes affecting the FMS audit programme;
- Risks to achieving FMS objectives;
- Opportunities for continual improvement.

## Recommendations & Actions

### Corrective Action Plan

| Finding ID | Required Action | Responsible Owner | Due Date | Evidence Required | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FMS-IA-2024-01 | Redesign the FMS internal audit programme to cover all FMS processes, locations, outsourced services, and ISO 41001 requirements using a documented risk-based methodology | [FMS Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Approved audit programme, scope mapping, risk rationale, leadership approval | High |
| FMS-IA-2024-01 | Map the audit programme to the FMS scope, process map, risk register, previous audit results, and significant changes | [Internal Audit Coordinator] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Audit programme mapping matrix | High |
| FMS-IA-2024-02 | Update audit plan and report templates to require audit criteria, scope, locations, functions, clauses, exclusions, and evidence references | [Internal Audit Coordinator] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Revised templates and controlled document approval | Medium |
| FMS-IA-2024-02 | Provide refresher briefing to auditors on ISO 41001 audit planning and clause-based criteria definition | [Lead Auditor] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Attendance records, training material, competence update | Medium |
| FMS-IA-2024-03 | Establish audit record retention requirements, including working papers and objective evidence | [Document Control Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Document retention schedule, repository structure, access controls | Medium |
| FMS-IA-2024-03 | Conduct evidence completeness review for all current-year FMS audits | [Internal Audit Coordinator] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Evidence completeness checklist and remediation log | Medium |
| FMS-IA-2024-04 | Update corrective action procedure to require root cause analysis, closure criteria, effectiveness verification, and escalation of overdue actions | [Corrective Action Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Revised procedure, approval record, communication record | Medium |
| FMS-IA-2024-04 | Reassess open and recently closed audit corrective actions for adequate closure evidence | [FMS Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Corrective action review record and updated closure status | Medium |
| FMS-IA-2024-05 | Add critical outsourced services to the internal audit programme | [Contract Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Supplier audit schedule and criteria | Medium |
| FMS-IA-2024-05 | Perform sample-based audits of high-risk outsourced FM services | [Lead Auditor / Contract Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Supplier audit reports, findings, corrective actions | Medium |

### Recommended Audit Programme Enhancements

The following structure is recommended for the revised FMS internal audit programme:

| Audit Area | Suggested Frequency | Risk Basis | Example Criteria |
|---|---:|---|---|
| FMS governance and leadership | Annual | Strategic importance and management accountability | ISO 41001 |
| Facility service operations | Annual | Direct impact on service delivery and users | ISO 41001, service procedures, SLAs |
| Statutory maintenance and compliance controls | Annual or semi-annual | High compliance and safety significance | Legal register, maintenance schedules, inspection records |
| Outsourced hard FM services | Annual | Supplier dependency and asset reliability | Contracts, SLAs, ISO 41001 |
| Outsourced soft FM services | Annual | User satisfaction and service quality | Service specifications, inspection records, KPI reports |
| Helpdesk / CAFM process | Annual | Central process for service requests and performance data | Work order procedure, KPI definitions, response targets |
| FMS risks and opportunities | Annual | Required for FMS planning and improvement | ISO 41001, risk register |
| FMS objectives and KPIs | Annual | Performance evaluation and management review input | ISO 41001 |
| Documented information | Annual | Evidence control and audit readiness | ISO 41001 |
| Corrective action and improvement | Annual | Recurrence prevention and continual improvement | ISO 41001 |

### Recommended Audit Report Minimum Content

Each future internal FMS audit report should include, at minimum:

- Audit objective;
- Audit criteria;
- Audit scope, including locations, functions, processes, and exclusions;
- Audit dates and audit team;
- Auditee representatives;
- Methodology and sampling statement;
- Evidence reviewed;
- Findings classified by severity;
- Clear linkage to ISO 41001 clauses and internal requirements;
- Positive observations;
- Conclusion on conformity and effectiveness;
- Required corrective actions;
- Responsible owners and due dates;
- Distribution list;
- Retained evidence references.

### Management Action Tracking

| Action Status | Definition | Required Management Response |
|---|---|---|
| Open | Action assigned but not yet completed | Owner to provide progress update by agreed date |
| In Progress | Work has started and evidence is emerging | Owner to provide interim evidence and revised risk assessment if delayed |
| Awaiting Verification | Owner states action is complete; independent verification pending | Verifier to assess adequacy and effectiveness |
| Closed | Action completed and effectiveness verified | Retain closure evidence and update trend analysis |
| Overdue | Target date missed without approved extension | Escalate to FMS leadership / management review |

### Follow-Up Requirements

Follow-up audit activity shall be conducted to verify:

- Completion of corrective actions;
- Adequacy of root cause analysis;
- Effectiveness of implemented actions;
- Updating of FMS documented information;
- Integration of revised audit programme into management review;
- Evidence that outsourced service assurance has been incorporated into audit planning;
- No recurrence of similar findings in subsequent audits.

A follow-up review should be completed by [YYYY-MM-DD] and formally reported to [FMS Steering Committee / Top Management / Management Review Chair].

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution

This report shall be distributed to authorised personnel with responsibility for FMS governance, implementation, audit, corrective action, and management review.

| Recipient / Role | Purpose of Distribution |
|---|---|
| [Chief Operating Officer / Executive Sponsor] | Oversight of FMS performance and assurance |
| [Head of Facilities Management] | Accountability for FMS implementation and corrective action |
| [FMS Manager] | Action ownership and programme improvement |
| [Internal Audit Coordinator] | Audit programme and methodology improvement |
| [Facilities Operations Managers] | Implementation of process-level corrective actions |
| [Contract / Supplier Manager] | Supplier assurance and outsourced service actions |
| [Document Control Owner] | Control of audit records and documented information |
| [Management Review Chair] | Inclusion in ISO 41001 management review inputs |
| [External Certification Body, if applicable] | Available upon authorised request only |

### Confidentiality Requirements

This report is classified as **Confidential — Internal Use Only**.

The report may contain sensitive information relating to facility operations, supplier performance, statutory compliance, security arrangements, service deficiencies, and internal governance. It shall be handled in accordance with the organisation’s information classification and document control requirements.

Mandatory handling requirements:

- Do not distribute outside authorised recipients without approval from [FMS Manager / Document Owner].
- Do not share supplier-specific findings externally unless approved by [Contract Manager / Legal / Procurement].
- Store the report only in approved repositories such as [document management system].
- Retain the report and supporting audit evidence for the period defined in the FMS documented information retention schedule.
- Redact sensitive operational, security, or commercially confidential details before external disclosure where required.
- Ensure superseded versions are controlled and not used as current audit evidence.

### Record Retention

| Audit working papers and evidence references | [Retention period] | [Restricted audit folder] | [Lead Auditor] |
| Corrective action records | Until closure plus [retention period] | [Corrective action system / register] | [Corrective Action Owner] |
| Management review records referencing this report | [Retention period] | [Management review repository] | [Management Review Chair] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| NC ID | Enter a unique identifier for the nonconformity, using a consistent format such as NC-FM-YYYY-###. |
| Date Identified | Enter the date the nonconformity was first identified in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Identified By | Enter the name and role of the person who identified or reported the nonconformity. |
| Source of Nonconformity | Select or enter the source, such as Internal Audit, External Audit, Management Review, Client Complaint, Service Failure, KPI Monitoring, Supplier Issue, Incident, Inspection, Employee Report, or Other. |
| ISO 41001 Clause / FMS Requirement | Enter the applicable ISO 41001:2018 clause, contractual requirement, internal procedure, SLA, policy, or FM requirement that was not met. |
| FM Process / Service Area | Enter the affected facilities management process or service area, such as maintenance, cleaning, security, catering, utilities, space management, helpdesk, contractor management, asset management, or H&S interface. |
| Location / Site | Enter the site, building, floor, asset location, client location, or operational area affected by the nonconformity. |
| Nonconformity Description | Describe clearly what failed to conform, including what happened, where, when, and the requirement not met; do not include root cause unless already verified. |
| Objective Evidence | Enter the evidence supporting the nonconformity, such as audit finding, work order number, inspection record, photo reference, complaint ID, KPI report, log entry, or document reference. |
| Immediate Correction / Containment Taken | Record immediate action taken to control, correct, contain, or mitigate the nonconformity and its consequences, including date if applicable. |
| Consequences / Impact | Describe the actual or potential impact on FM service delivery, users, client obligations, safety, compliance, assets, business continuity, environment, cost, or reputation. |
| Severity | Enter the assessed severity using agreed values such as Low, Medium, High, or Critical, based on organisational criteria. |
| Responsible Owner | Enter the manager accountable for ensuring the nonconformity is investigated and resolved. |
| Root Cause Analysis Method | Enter the method used to determine cause, such as 5 Whys, Fishbone, Fault Tree, Pareto, Incident Investigation, Process Review, or Not Required with justification. |
| Root Cause | Enter the verified underlying cause or causes of the nonconformity; avoid restating the symptom. |
| Similar or Potential Nonconformities Assessed | Record whether similar nonconformities exist or could occur elsewhere, including areas checked; use Yes, No, or Not Applicable with brief explanation. |
| Corrective Action Required | Enter Yes or No; use Yes where action is needed to eliminate the root cause and prevent recurrence or occurrence elsewhere. |
| Corrective Action Plan | Describe the planned corrective action(s) to eliminate the root cause, including enough detail to verify implementation. |
| Action Owner | Enter the person or role responsible for completing the corrective action. |
| Target Completion Date | Enter the planned completion date for the corrective action in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Actual Completion Date | Enter the date the corrective action was fully implemented in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until complete. |
| Implementation Status | Enter the current status using Not Started, In Progress, Implemented Pending Effectiveness Review, Closed, Overdue, or Cancelled. |
| Effectiveness Review Method | Describe how effectiveness will be verified, such as repeat audit, KPI trend review, inspection, sample check, customer feedback, work order review, or observation. |
| Effectiveness Review Date | Enter the date the effectiveness review was or will be performed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Effectiveness Review Result | Enter the outcome of the effectiveness review using Effective, Not Effective, Partially Effective, or Pending, with a brief rationale. |
| Further Action Required | Enter any additional corrective action required if the original action was not effective, or enter None. |
| Risks / Opportunities Updated | Enter Yes, No, or Not Applicable and reference the risk/opportunity register entry updated where relevant. |
| FMS Documentation / Process Changes Required | Enter any required updates to FMS documents, procedures, work instructions, training, contracts, SLAs, process maps, or controls; enter None if no change is required. |
| Evidence Reference / Link | Enter document IDs, system links, folder paths, work order references, audit report numbers, photos, approvals, or other records proving actions and results. |
| Closure Approval By | Enter the name and role of the authorised person approving closure, independent of the action owner where practicable. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the nonconformity and corrective action were formally closed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record Status | Enter Open, Closed, Reopened, or Archived. |

### Maintenance

The FMS Manager or designated Quality/FM Compliance Manager owns this register and updates it whenever a nonconformity is identified, with formal review at least monthly and before management review. Source data is drawn from audits, inspections, FM helpdesk/CMMS, complaints, KPI reports, incident records, supplier performance records, and management review outputs.

| Attendees_and_Roles | List all attendees and their roles, including top management, FM leadership, process owners, and invited specialists; use 'Name - Role' format separated by semicolons. |
| Scope_of_Review | State the FMS scope reviewed, including sites, services, functions, contracts, or organisational boundaries covered. |
| Review_Period_Covered | Enter the period reviewed using YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Previous_Review_Action_Status | Summarise the status of actions from the previous management review, including overdue items and effectiveness of completed actions; reference action IDs where applicable. |
| Changes_in_Internal_and_External_Issues | Record significant internal or external changes affecting the FMS, such as organisational changes, legal/regulatory changes, market conditions, technology, assets, operating model, or strategic priorities. |
| Changes_in_Interested_Party_Needs_and_Requirements | Record changes in needs, expectations, or requirements of relevant interested parties such as customers, users, regulators, employees, landlords, service providers, or community stakeholders. |
| FMS_Objectives_Performance | Record performance against approved FM objectives, including objective reference, target, actual result, variance, and RAG status using Green/Amber/Red. |
| FM_Process_Performance_and_Service_Conformity | Summarise whether key FM processes and services met planned requirements, SLAs, specifications, statutory obligations, and operational controls. |
| Monitoring_and_Measurement_Results | Record key results from monitoring, measurement, analysis, and evaluation activities, including KPIs, inspections, compliance checks, asset performance, energy or space metrics where applicable. |
| Internal_Audit_Results | Summarise relevant FMS audit outcomes, including audit dates, audit references, major/minor findings, observations, and positive findings. |
| Nonconformities_and_Corrective_Actions | Record FMS nonconformities, incidents, complaints, audit findings, corrective action trends, closure status, and effectiveness results. |
| Customer_User_Satisfaction_and_Feedback | Summarise satisfaction data and feedback from customers, users, occupants, or client representatives, including survey results, complaints, compliments, or service desk trends. |
| Provider_Supplier_Performance | Summarise performance of outsourced FM providers, contractors, suppliers, and partners against contract, SLA, compliance, safety, quality, and delivery expectations. |
| Risks_and_Opportunities_Status | Summarise current FM risks and opportunities, changes in risk ratings, effectiveness of controls, emerging risks, and any escalations required. |
| Adequacy_of_Resources | Record management's assessment of whether people, budget, infrastructure, technology, information, competence, and supplier resources are adequate for the FMS. |
| Opportunities_for_Continual_Improvement | Record identified improvement opportunities relating to FMS effectiveness, service delivery, user experience, costs, sustainability, safety, compliance, or process efficiency. |
| Management_Review_Decisions | Record decisions made by top management during the review, including approvals, rejections, priorities, strategic direction, or escalation decisions. |
| Actions_Arising | Record each agreed action clearly, starting with a verb, and include enough detail for completion to be objectively verified. |
| Action_Owner | Enter the role or named individual accountable for completing the action; use 'Name - Role' format. |
| Action_Due_Date | Enter the agreed completion date for the action in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Action_Status | Enter the current action status using one of: Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Overdue, Deferred, Cancelled. |
| Required_Changes_to_FMS | Record any approved changes needed to the FMS, such as policy, objectives, processes, procedures, controls, scope, governance, documented information, or service delivery model. |
| Required_Resource_Changes | Record any approved resource decisions or needs, such as additional budget, headcount, competence, tools, systems, assets, contractors, or training. |
| Approval_Name_and_Role | Enter the name and role of the person approving the minutes, normally the chair or authorised top management representative. |
| Approval_Date | Enter the date the minutes were approved in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record_Location | Enter the controlled repository path, document management link, or record system reference where the approved minutes and supporting evidence are stored. |

### Maintenance

The Head of Facilities or FMS Manager owns this template and updates it after each scheduled or extraordinary management review, at least annually. Inputs are drawn from the CAFM/helpdesk system, KPI dashboards, audit programme, corrective action log, risk register, supplier performance reviews, customer/user feedback records, and controlled FMS document repository.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Reporting Period | Enter the period covered by the KPI result in format YYYY-MM or YYYY-Q#; for annual reporting use YYYY. |
| Report Issue Date | Enter the date this report version is issued in format YYYY-MM-DD. |
| FM Objective Reference | Enter the unique reference of the related facilities management objective, e.g. FM-OBJ-001; must align to the organisation's FM objectives register. |
| KPI ID | Enter a unique KPI identifier, e.g. FM-KPI-001; use one row per KPI per reporting period. |
| KPI Name | Enter the short name of the performance indicator being monitored, e.g. Planned Maintenance Completion Rate. |
| FM Service / Process Area | Enter the FM service, process, asset group, contract, site, or function being measured, e.g. Maintenance, Cleaning, Security, Utilities, Helpdesk, Space Management. |
| ISO 41001 Clause Reference | Enter the applicable ISO 41001:2018 reference; for this report use Cl. 9.1 unless the KPI also supports another clause. |
| Interested Party / Requirement Monitored | Enter the stakeholder need, statutory requirement, SLA, contract obligation, policy commitment, or user requirement being monitored. |
| KPI Definition | Define exactly what is being measured, including numerator and denominator where applicable, so the calculation is repeatable. |
| Measurement Method | Describe how the result is calculated or assessed, including formula, sampling method, inspection method, or system report used. |
| Unit of Measure | Enter the measurement unit, e.g. %, number, hours, days, kWh, m2, cost, score, incidents/month. |
| Measurement Frequency | Enter how often the KPI is measured; allowed values: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, Per Event, Other. |
| Data Source / System | Enter the authoritative source of data, e.g. CAFM, CMMS, BMS, IWMS, finance system, energy platform, contractor report, audit checklist. |
| Data Owner | Enter the role or team accountable for the accuracy and completeness of the source data, e.g. CAFM Administrator, Energy Manager, Contractor Manager. |
| KPI Owner | Enter the role accountable for KPI performance and evaluation, e.g. Facilities Manager, Head of FM, Maintenance Manager. |
| Target / Acceptance Criteria | Enter the required target, limit, SLA, threshold, or acceptance criterion, including unit and direction of performance, e.g. >=95%, <=4 hours, zero statutory overdue tasks. |
| Threshold - Green | Enter the result range that represents acceptable performance, including unit and comparator, e.g. >=95%. |
| Threshold - Amber | Enter the result range that represents warning or marginal performance, including unit and comparator, e.g. 90% to <95%. |
| Threshold - Red | Enter the result range that represents unacceptable performance requiring action, including unit and comparator, e.g. <90%. |
| Actual Result | Enter the measured result for the reporting period using the unit stated in Unit of Measure. |
| Variance from Target | Enter the difference between actual result and target, including unit or percentage points; use + or - to show direction. |
| RAG Status | Enter the performance status based on the defined thresholds; allowed values: Green, Amber, Red, Not Rated. |
| Trend vs Previous Period | Enter the direction of performance compared with the previous period; allowed values: Improved, Deteriorated, No Change, New KPI, Not Available. |
| Previous Period Result | Enter the prior reporting period's actual result using the same unit of measure, or N/A if not available. |
| Analysis / Evaluation Summary | Enter the management evaluation of the result, including cause of variance, patterns, risks, constraints, and whether the KPI remains suitable. |
| Performance Impact | Enter the impact of the result on FM objectives, service delivery, compliance, users, assets, costs, safety, environment, or business continuity. |
| Nonconformity Raised | Enter Yes or No; select Yes where the result indicates failure to meet a requirement requiring nonconformity control. |
| Corrective / Improvement Action Reference | Enter the linked action, corrective action, risk treatment, or improvement reference, e.g. CA-2025-014; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Action Owner | Enter the role or named accountable person responsible for the linked action; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Action Due Date | Enter the due date for the linked action in format YYYY-MM-DD; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Evidence / Record Location | Enter the file path, system report name, dashboard link, audit record, or document reference proving the KPI result and analysis. |
| Prepared By | Enter the name and role of the person compiling the KPI report. |
| Reviewed By | Enter the name and role of the person reviewing the KPI report for accuracy, completeness, and suitability. |
| Approval Status | Enter the report approval state; allowed values: Draft, Under Review, Approved, Rejected, Superseded. |
| Approved By | Enter the name and role of the approving manager; leave blank until approved. |
| Approval Date | Enter the approval date in format YYYY-MM-DD; leave blank until approved. |

### Maintenance

The Facilities Management Performance Manager or Head of FM owns this template and updates it at the defined KPI reporting cadence, typically monthly with quarterly management review consolidation. Data should be drawn from approved source systems such as CAFM/CMMS/IWMS, BMS or energy platforms, helpdesk logs, contractor SLA reports, finance systems, audit records, and statutory compliance registers.
