ISO41-030.title: Stage 1 Audit Evidence Pack (FM)
ISO41-030.content:
## What This Evidences

The **Stage 1 Audit Evidence Pack (FM)** evidences that the organisation has planned, maintained, and retained appropriate documented information to support an ISO 41001:2018 Stage 1 audit, with specific relevance to ** Internal Audit**.

It demonstrates that the Facility Management System (FMS) has audit arrangements in place, including audit planning, scope, criteria, records, findings, and follow-up status. This pack is **collected from operational systems and repositories**; it is **not authored as a standalone document** and must not be fabricated.

The intent is to provide a structured ZIP file or secure shared-drive folder containing existing FMS documentation and records for auditor review.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect evidence from the organisation’s live FM and governance systems, typically including:

- Document management system: [DMS / SharePoint / Google Drive / Confluence]
- Internal audit management tool: [Audit Tool / GRC Platform]
- Facilities management platform / CAFM system: [CAFM / IWMS / CMMS]
- Corrective action or ticketing system: [ITSM / Action Tracker / Jira / ServiceNow]
- Meeting records repository: [Teams / SharePoint / Board Portal]
- Risk and compliance register: [Risk Register / GRC Tool]
- Training or competency system, if audit competence is in scope: [LMS / HRIS]

## How To Collect

1. Confirm the Stage 1 audit scope, sites, FM services, and audit period with the FMS owner or management representative.
2. Create a controlled collection folder named: `ISO41001_Stage1_EvidencePack_FM_[YYYY-MM-DD]`.
3. Export or download current approved FMS documented information from [DMS], including policy, scope, objectives, process descriptions, and audit procedure.
4. From [Audit Tool / GRC Platform], export the internal audit programme, latest internal audit plan, completed audit reports, findings, nonconformities, and follow-up status.
5. From [CAFM / IWMS / CMMS], export relevant FM operational records that support audited processes, such as maintenance schedules, work order samples, service performance dashboards, and statutory compliance logs.
6. From [Risk Register / GRC Tool], export FM risks, opportunities, controls, treatment actions, and review dates.
7. From [ITSM / Action Tracker], export corrective actions linked to internal audit findings, including owners, due dates, status, and closure evidence.
8. Include relevant management review inputs or outputs showing consideration of audit results.
9. Save exports in PDF, XLSX, CSV, or screenshot format, preserving system-generated metadata where available.
10. Compress the folder into a ZIP file or store it in a read-only shared-drive location.
11. Record a simple index listing each evidence item, source system, extraction date, and collector.

## What To Capture

The pack should include, where applicable:

- FMS scope and boundaries
- FM policy and objectives
- Internal audit programme covering ISO 41001 requirements
- Internal audit plan showing scope, criteria, auditor, date, and area audited
- Completed internal audit reports
- Audit findings, nonconformities, observations, and opportunities for improvement
- Corrective action records with owner, due date, status, and closure evidence
- Evidence of auditor competence or independence
- Management review records referencing audit results
- FM process evidence from [CAFM / IWMS / CMMS], such as work orders, maintenance compliance, service requests, and KPI reports
- Risk register extracts relevant to FM operations
- Document approval status, version, owner, and review date
- System timestamps and export dates

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Before each Stage 1 audit, surveillance audit, recertification audit, or material FMS scope change.
- **Primary Owner:** [FMS Manager / Facilities Director]
- **Supporting Owners:** [Internal Audit Manager], [Compliance Manager], [Document Controller], [CAFM Administrator]
- **Collector:** [Assigned Evidence Coordinator]

## Retention & Storage

Store the ZIP or drive folder in [Controlled Evidence Repository] with read-only access for auditors and authorised personnel.

Minimum retention should align with the organisation’s documented information retention schedule, typically:

- Audit evidence packs: [3–6 years]
- Internal audit records: [3–6 years]
- Corrective action records: until closure plus [3 years]
- Statutory FM compliance records: as required by applicable legal and contractual obligations

Apply access control, version control, and deletion restrictions. Do not overwrite prior audit packs.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence pack where it:

- Is clearly sourced from live organisational systems, not recreated manually
- Covers the defined FMS scope and audit period
- Demonstrates an internal audit programme and completed audit activity in line with ISO 41001:2018
- Includes audit criteria, scope, auditors, dates, results, and follow-up actions
- Shows corrective actions are tracked to closure or actively managed
- Contains approved and current FMS documentation
- Includes sufficient operational FM records to support the documented system
- Preserves source metadata such as export date, system name, record owner, and version
- Is indexed, complete, readable, and access-controlled
- Does not contain unexplained gaps, unverifiable screenshots, or manually fabricated records

ISO41-031.title: Stage 2 Audit Evidence Pack (FM)
ISO41-031.content:
## What This Evidences

This evidence pack supports **ISO 41001:2018 — Internal Audit** by demonstrating that the organisation has planned, conducted, recorded, and followed up internal audits of the Facilities Management System (FMS).

This artifact is **collected operational evidence**, not an authored document. Do not create or recreate audit evidence manually. Export and compile actual records from the organisation’s audit, document management, workflow, ticketing, and facilities management systems into a ZIP or shared drive folder.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect evidence from the systems used to manage internal audits and FM improvement actions, typically:

- Internal audit management tool: `[Audit Management System]`
- Document management system / QMS repository: `[Document Repository]`
- Facilities management platform / CAFM / IWMS: `[FM System]`
- Corrective action or issue tracking tool: `[ITSM / CAPA / Ticketing System]`
- Calendar or planning tool: `[Calendar / Planning System]`
- Meeting records repository: `[SharePoint / Teams / Google Drive]`
- Email archive, where approvals or notifications are retained: `[Email System]`

## How To Collect

1. Identify the audit period in scope, e.g. `[YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD]`.
2. Export the approved internal audit programme or schedule covering the period.
3. Export audit plans for each relevant FMS audit, including scope, criteria, dates, auditors, and audited areas.
4. Export completed internal audit reports from `[Audit Management System]` or `[Document Repository]`.
5. Export evidence of auditor competence and independence, such as auditor assignment records, training records, or conflict-of-interest declarations.
6. Export nonconformity, observation, and opportunity-for-improvement records raised from internal audits.
7. Export corrective action records from `[CAPA / ITSM / Ticketing System]`, including owners, due dates, status, root cause analysis, actions taken, and closure evidence.
8. Export evidence that audit results were communicated to relevant management, such as meeting minutes, email notifications, or management review inputs.
9. Export follow-up verification records showing whether corrective actions were implemented and effective.
10. Save all files into a structured ZIP or drive folder using clear naming, e.g. `Stage_2_Audit_Evidence_Pack_FM_[period]`.

## What To Capture

The evidence pack should include sufficient records to prove the internal audit process operated effectively:

- Internal audit programme / schedule for the FMS
- Audit scope, criteria, methods, and dates
- Assigned auditor names and departments
- Evidence of auditor competence and impartiality
- Completed audit checklists or working papers, where retained
- Final internal audit reports
- Audit findings, including conformities, nonconformities, risks, and improvement opportunities
- Corrective action records linked to audit findings
- Root cause analysis and action plans
- Status, due dates, responsible owners, and completion dates
- Evidence of closure and effectiveness review
- Communication of audit results to relevant FM leadership
- Management review inputs or minutes referencing audit outcomes
- Version history or system metadata showing records are genuine exports

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** At minimum before Stage 2 certification audit, then after each internal audit cycle and management review cycle.
- **Primary Owner:** `[FM System Manager / Facilities Compliance Manager]`
- **Supporting Owners:** `[Internal Audit Lead]`, `[Quality Manager]`, `[Process Owners]`, `[CAPA Owner]`

## Retention & Storage

Store the evidence pack in `[Secure Document Repository / Compliance Drive]` with access restricted to authorised FM, audit, and compliance personnel.

Recommended retention:

- Keep Stage 2 evidence for at least the certification cycle, typically **3 years**, or longer if required by contract, regulation, or organisational policy.
- Preserve original exports where possible.
- Do not overwrite prior evidence packs.
- Use read-only or access-controlled storage.
- Maintain a clear folder structure and index file identifying source systems, export dates, and responsible collector.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence pack if it shows that:

- Internal audits were planned for the FMS and completed within the defined period.
- Audit scope and criteria align with ISO 41001:2018 and the organisation’s FMS requirements.
- Auditors were competent and sufficiently independent of the areas audited.
- Audit reports are complete, dated, and traceable to actual audit activities.
- Findings are recorded and linked to corrective actions where applicable.
- Corrective actions have owners, due dates, implementation evidence, and closure status.
- Follow-up or effectiveness checks are present for closed findings.
- Audit results were communicated to relevant management and considered in FMS oversight.
- Records are exported from live organisational systems and contain timestamps, metadata, IDs, or approvals demonstrating authenticity.

ISO41-032.title: ISO 41001 Certificate
ISO41-032.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Control Reference | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-FM-ATT-001] | 1.0 | [Facilities Management / Integrated Management System Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO 41001:2018 Facility Management — Management Systems | — | [Internal / Public] |

## Purpose

This Attestation confirms that [Organisation Name] has been certified by an accredited certification body as operating a Facility Management Management System that conforms to the requirements of **ISO 41001:2018 — Facility management — Management systems — Requirements with guidance for use**.

The purpose of this document is to provide a controlled, audit-ready record of the ISO 41001 certificate and the associated certification details, including scope, certification authority, evidence relied upon, validity period, and retention requirements.

This Attestation is intended for use by internal stakeholders, auditors, regulators, customers, suppliers, and other authorised interested parties requiring confirmation of [Organisation Name]’s ISO 41001:2018 certification status.

## Scope

This Attestation applies to the certified Facility Management Management System maintained by [Organisation Name] for the facilities, services, locations, and organisational activities defined in the certificate issued by the accredited certification body.

The certification scope is limited to the boundaries formally assessed and certified by the issuing certification body. It does not imply certification of activities, locations, services, subsidiaries, contractors, or outsourced processes outside the certified scope unless explicitly included in the certificate.

| Scope Element | Certified Details |
|---|---|
| Certified Organisation | [Organisation Name] |
| Certified Management System | Facility Management Management System |
| Applicable Standard | ISO 41001:2018 |
| Certified Scope Statement | [Exact certificate scope statement] |
| Certified Sites / Locations | [Certified site addresses or “See certificate annex”] |
| Included Facility Management Services | [e.g., workplace management, maintenance coordination, space management, service partner oversight, utilities coordination, helpdesk/service request management] |
| Exclusions / Limitations | [Any exclusions, limitations, or “None stated on certificate”] |
| Certificate Number | [Certificate Number] |
| Initial Certification Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Current Issue Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Expiry Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Certification Cycle | [e.g., 3-year certification cycle with annual surveillance audits] |

## Attestation Statement

[Organisation Name] attests that it holds a valid ISO 41001:2018 certificate issued by [Certification Body Name], an accredited certification body, confirming that the Facility Management Management System within the certified scope has been assessed and found to conform to the requirements of ISO 41001:2018.

Based on the certificate issued by [Certification Body Name], [Organisation Name]’s Facility Management Management System has been independently assessed against ISO 41001:2018 requirements, including the establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of a management system for effective and efficient facility management.

The certified Facility Management Management System addresses the ISO 41001:2018 requirements relevant to:

- Understanding the organisational context and the needs and expectations of interested parties for facility management.
- Defining the scope of the Facility Management Management System.
- Leadership commitment, facility management policy, roles, responsibilities, and authorities.
- Planning for risks, opportunities, objectives, and actions necessary to achieve facility management outcomes.
- Support processes including resources, competence, awareness, communication, and documented information.
- Operational planning and control of facility management services within the certified scope.
- Performance evaluation, including monitoring, measurement, analysis, evaluation, internal audit, and management review.
- Continual improvement, including corrective action and improvement of the Facility Management Management System.

This Attestation is based on the current certificate and supporting certification records available as of the Effective Date stated above. Continued certification is subject to ongoing conformance with ISO 41001:2018, completion of required surveillance audits, closure of any certification body findings within required timeframes, and successful recertification before certificate expiry.

This Attestation does not replace the official certificate issued by [Certification Body Name]. In the event of any discrepancy between this Attestation and the official certificate, the official certificate and certification body records take precedence.

## Signatory & Authority

This Attestation is authorised by the accountable management representative responsible for maintaining the Facility Management Management System and associated certification records for [Organisation Name].

| Role | Name | Authority / Responsibility | Signature | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Accountable Executive | [Name] | Executive accountability for the certified Facility Management Management System and organisational commitment to ISO 41001:2018 conformance. | [Signature] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Management System Owner | [Name] | Operational ownership of ISO 41001:2018 certification records, certificate maintenance, audit coordination, and management system governance. | [Signature] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Document Owner | [Name] | Preparation, review, version control, and retention of this Attestation and referenced evidence. | [Signature] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

The signatories confirm that, to the best of their knowledge and based on available records:

- The certificate referenced in this Attestation has been issued by the certification body identified herein.
- The certificate applies to the scope stated in the official certificate.
- The certificate has not been knowingly suspended, withdrawn, expired, or materially restricted as of the Effective Date of this Attestation.
- Any material changes affecting the certified scope, facilities, services, organisational structure, or management system will be evaluated for certification impact and communicated to the certification body where required.

## Evidence Referenced

The following evidence supports this Attestation and shall be maintained as controlled records.

| Evidence ID | Evidence Description | Source / Custodian | Reference / Location | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EV-FM-001 | Official ISO 41001:2018 certificate issued to [Organisation Name] | [Certification Body Name] / [Document Custodian] | [Repository path / Certificate file name] | [Current / Superseded] |
| EV-FM-002 | Certificate schedule or annex listing certified locations, services, or scope details, where applicable | [Certification Body Name] / [Document Custodian] | [Repository path] | [Current / Not applicable] |
| EV-FM-003 | Accreditation confirmation for [Certification Body Name] issued by [Accreditation Body Name] | [Accreditation Body Name] / [Document Custodian] | [URL / repository path] | [Verified on YYYY-MM-DD] |
| EV-FM-004 | Stage 1 audit report or readiness assessment report | [Certification Body Name] / [Management System Owner] | [Repository path] | [Current certification cycle] |
| EV-FM-005 | Stage 2 certification audit report confirming conformity assessment outcome | [Certification Body Name] / [Management System Owner] | [Repository path] | [Current certification cycle] |
| EV-FM-006 | Surveillance audit report(s) for current certification cycle | [Certification Body Name] / [Management System Owner] | [Repository path] | [Completed / Scheduled] |
| EV-FM-007 | Corrective action plan and closure evidence for any certification body nonconformities | [Management System Owner] | [Repository path / CAPA system reference] | [Closed / In progress / Not applicable] |
| EV-FM-008 | Management review minutes addressing ISO 41001:2018 performance and certification status | [Management System Owner] | [Repository path] | [Current] |
| EV-FM-009 | Internal audit programme and completed internal audit reports for the Facility Management Management System | [Internal Audit / Management System Owner] | [Repository path] | [Current] |
| EV-FM-010 | ISO 41001:2018 scope statement and documented Facility Management Management System information | [Management System Owner] | [Repository path] | [Current] |

Evidence shall be retained in a manner that preserves authenticity, integrity, accessibility, and traceability. The official certificate shall be protected from unauthorised modification and shall only be distributed in accordance with the classification stated in this document and any certification body rules governing use of certification marks, logos, and claims.

## Frequency

This Attestation shall be reviewed and, where necessary, reissued according to the following schedule.

| Trigger / Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Required Action |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Routine attestation review | At least annually | Management System Owner | Confirm certificate validity, scope, expiry date, accreditation status, and evidence currency. |
| Surveillance audit completion | After each surveillance audit | Management System Owner | Update referenced evidence and confirm whether certification remains active. |
| Recertification | Before certificate expiry and upon new certificate issue | Accountable Executive / Management System Owner | Replace superseded certificate references and reissue this Attestation. |
| Scope change | As required | Management System Owner | Confirm whether the certification scope has changed and update this Attestation if the official certificate is amended. |
| Organisational or facility change affecting certification | As required | Accountable Executive / Management System Owner | Assess certification impact and notify the certification body where required. |
| Certificate suspension, withdrawal, expiry, or restriction | Immediately upon awareness | Accountable Executive / Management System Owner | Withdraw or revise this Attestation and notify affected stakeholders where applicable. |
| Certification body or accreditation status change | Upon awareness | Management System Owner | Verify continuing validity and update evidence references. |

This Attestation remains valid only while the referenced ISO 41001:2018 certificate remains valid, active, and applicable to the stated scope.

## Records & Retention

This Attestation and all referenced evidence shall be managed as controlled records under [Organisation Name]’s documented information and records management requirements.

| Record Type | Retention Period | Record Owner | Storage Location | Disposal Method |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Current ISO 41001:2018 Attestation | While current plus [X] years | [Management System Owner] | [Document repository / GRC system] | Controlled deletion or archival in accordance with records policy |
| Superseded Attestations | [X] years from supersession | [Document Owner] | [Document repository / archive] | Controlled deletion after retention expiry |
| Official ISO 41001:2018 Certificate and Annexes | Certificate validity period plus [X] years | [Management System Owner] | [Document repository / certification records folder] | Controlled deletion or archival |
| Certification Audit Reports | Current certification cycle plus [X] years | [Management System Owner] | [Audit records repository] | Controlled deletion after retention expiry |
| Corrective Action and Closure Records | Current certification cycle plus [X] years | [Management System Owner] | [CAPA system / audit records repository] | Controlled deletion after retention expiry |
| Management Review and Internal Audit Records | [X] years | [Management System Owner] | [Management system repository] | Controlled deletion after retention expiry |
| Accreditation Verification Evidence | Duration of reliance plus [X] years | [Document Custodian] | [Document repository] | Controlled deletion after retention expiry |

Records shall be retained in accordance with applicable contractual, legal, regulatory, accreditation, and management system requirements. Where requirements conflict, the longest applicable retention period shall apply.

Access to this Attestation and supporting evidence shall be limited to authorised personnel and approved external recipients. Public distribution of the ISO 41001:2018 certificate, certification claims, certification marks, or accreditation marks shall comply with the rules issued by [Certification Body Name] and [Accreditation Body Name].

ISO41-033.title: Surveillance Audit Evidence Pack (FM)
ISO41-033.content:
## What This Evidences

The **Surveillance Audit Evidence Pack (FM)** supports ISO 41001:2018 ** — Internal Audit** by providing objective evidence that the organisation’s Facilities Management System (FMS) has been audited at planned intervals and that audit results were recorded, reported, and followed up.

This artifact is **collected, not authored**. It must be assembled from the organisation’s own operational systems, audit records, document repositories, issue/action tracking tools, and management review materials. Do **not** create or rewrite evidence for the audit pack; export or capture existing records that prove the surveillance audit cycle occurred.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect evidence from the systems normally used to operate and govern the FMS, such as:

- **Audit management system**: [Audit Tool / GRC Platform]
- **Document management system**: [SharePoint / Google Drive / DMS]
- **Facilities management platform / CAFM / CMMS**: [FM System Name]
- **Corrective action or issue tracker**: [ITSM / Jira / ServiceNow / Action Tracker]
- **Meeting records repository**: [Board Portal / Teams / SharePoint]
- **Training/competence records system**: [LMS / HR System]
- **Supplier / contractor management system**: [Supplier Portal / Procurement Tool]
- **Previous external surveillance audit portal**, if applicable: [Certification Body Portal]

## How To Collect

1. Identify the surveillance audit period: [start date] to [end date].
2. Locate the approved **internal audit programme/schedule** covering the period.
3. Export the completed internal audit reports relevant to ISO 41001 and FM processes.
4. Collect auditor assignment records showing independence, competence, and audit scope.
5. Export audit checklists, sampling notes, interview notes, or completed audit working papers.
6. Export all nonconformities, observations, improvement actions, and corrective actions raised from the audit.
7. Collect evidence of action ownership, due dates, status, verification, and closure.
8. Capture records showing audit results were reported to relevant management.
9. Include management review inputs/outputs that reference audit results, trends, risks, or improvement actions.
10. Export supporting operational evidence sampled during the audit, such as work orders, maintenance records, supplier performance reviews, service level reports, risk registers, or compliance checks.
11. Package the files into a dated ZIP or controlled Drive folder named: 
 **[YYYY-MM-DD] ISO41001 Surveillance Audit Evidence Pack - FM**
12. Create an index file listing each item, source system, export date, and owner.

## What To Capture

The pack should include sufficient records to show audit planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up:

- Internal audit programme/schedule, including audit dates and FM scope
- Audit plan showing criteria, scope, locations, processes, and assigned auditors
- Auditor competence and independence evidence
- Completed audit reports for ISO 41001 / FMS processes
- Audit checklists, sampling records, interview notes, and reviewed evidence lists
- Register of findings: conformities, nonconformities, observations, and opportunities for improvement
- Corrective action records with root cause, action plan, owner, target date, status, and verification of effectiveness
- Management reporting evidence: meeting minutes, dashboards, packs, or emails
- Management review records referencing audit outputs and improvement decisions
- Evidence from FM operations sampled during the audit, including:
 - maintenance records
 - service requests/work orders
 - statutory/compliance inspections
 - supplier performance records
 - asset or occupancy records
 - customer/user satisfaction or complaint records
 - risk and opportunity registers
- Screenshots or exports showing system timestamps, record IDs, and approval status

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Annually, aligned to the ISO 41001 surveillance audit cycle and internal audit programme.
- **Primary Owner:** [FMS Manager / Head of Facilities]
- **Supporting Owners:** [Internal Audit Lead], [Quality/Compliance Manager], [FM Operations Manager], [Supplier Manager], [Document Controller]

## Retention & Storage

Store the evidence pack in [Controlled DMS / SharePoint / GRC Repository] with restricted access and version control.

Recommended retention:

- Keep for at least **one full certification cycle plus the current cycle**, or
- Follow the organisation’s records retention schedule, if longer.

The storage location should preserve:

- Original exported files where possible
- Export timestamps
- Folder/index structure
- Access permissions
- Evidence integrity
- Audit trail of changes

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will typically accept the pack as sufficient when it:

- Clearly covers the surveillance audit period and ISO 41001 FMS scope
- Shows internal audits were planned and performed in line with
- Includes objective records from source systems, not recreated summaries
- Demonstrates auditor competence and impartiality
- Contains audit findings and evidence of communication to management
- Shows corrective actions were tracked, owned, and verified for effectiveness
- Links findings to relevant FM processes, locations, services, or suppliers
- Includes enough sampled operational records to support audit conclusions
- Is organised, indexed, dated, and traceable to source systems
- Can be independently followed by the auditor without relying on verbal explanation

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Improvement ID | Enter a unique identifier for the improvement initiative, using a controlled format such as CI-YYYY-###. |
| Date Raised | Enter the date the improvement opportunity was formally logged, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Raised By | Enter the name and role or function of the person who identified or submitted the improvement opportunity. |
| Improvement Source | Select the origin of the improvement from allowed values: Internal Audit, External Audit, Management Review, KPI Trend, Customer Feedback, Complaint, Risk Assessment, Incident, Nonconformity, Supplier Review, Staff Suggestion, Benchmarking, Regulatory Change, Technology / Innovation, Other. |
| Source Reference | Enter the reference number, report name, meeting minute ID, audit finding ID, KPI dashboard link, ticket number, or other traceable source reference. |
| ISO 41001 Clause / FM Process | Enter the relevant ISO 41001 clause where applicable and/or the FM process affected, for example Cl. 8.1 Operations, Cl. 9.1 Performance Evaluation, Maintenance, Cleaning, Space Management, Helpdesk, Security, Energy Management. |
| Facility / Site / Service Area | Enter the specific facility, site, building, region, department, asset group, or FM service area to which the improvement applies. |
| Interested Party / Customer Affected | Enter the customer, client, occupier group, internal department, regulator, supplier, user group, or other interested party affected by the improvement. |
| Current Issue or Opportunity Statement | Describe the current condition, gap, inefficiency, trend, risk, or opportunity in clear factual terms; avoid describing the solution only. |
| Improvement Category | Select the primary intent from allowed values: Improve FM Service, Improve FMS Effectiveness, Enhance Customer Satisfaction, Reduce Undesired Effect, Prevent Undesired Effect, Correct Undesired Effect, Improve Efficiency, Improve Compliance, Improve Sustainability, Other. |
| Intended Improvement Objective | State what the initiative is intended to achieve, written as a measurable improvement objective where possible. |
| Alignment to FM Policy / FM Objectives | Identify the relevant FM policy commitment, FM objective, performance target, customer requirement, or strategic business aim supported by the improvement. |
| Baseline Performance / Current State | Record the starting performance level or current state before action, including metric name, value, unit, and measurement period where applicable. |
| Target Outcome / Success Measure | Define the expected result and acceptance criteria, including KPI, target value, unit, threshold, or qualitative success condition. |
| Risk or Opportunity Rating | Enter the assessed significance using the organisation's risk method, for example Low, Medium, High, Critical, or a numeric score such as Likelihood x Impact. |
| Priority | Select the implementation priority from allowed values: Low, Medium, High, Urgent. |
| Proposed Improvement Action | Describe the planned action or initiative to implement the improvement, including key deliverables or change activities. |
| Action Owner | Enter the named person and role accountable for coordinating and delivering the improvement action. |
| Approver / Sponsor | Enter the manager, process owner, contract lead, FM director, or governance body approving resources and priority for the initiative. |
| Resources or Budget Required | Record required resources such as budget, labour, contractor support, tools, technology, training, or capital expenditure; include amount and currency where known. |
| Planned Start Date | Enter the planned commencement date for the improvement action, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Target Completion Date | Enter the planned completion date for the improvement action, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Status | Select the current lifecycle status from allowed values: Proposed, Approved, Not Started, In Progress, On Hold, Completed, Effectiveness Review Pending, Closed, Cancelled. |
| Progress / Update Notes | Enter dated progress notes, decisions, blockers, escalations, or changes to scope; each update should include date, author, and summary. |
| Related Corrective Action ID | Enter any linked corrective action, nonconformity, incident, risk treatment, audit finding, or CAPA reference; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Evidence / Record Location | Enter the controlled document repository path, system link, ticket URL, project folder, report reference, or other evidence location proving implementation. |
| Actual Completion Date | Enter the date the improvement action was completed, in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until completed. |
| Effectiveness Review Required | Select Yes or No to indicate whether post-implementation effectiveness must be verified. |
| Effectiveness Review Date | Enter the planned or actual date for checking whether the improvement achieved its intended outcome, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Effectiveness Review Result | Record the result of the effectiveness check using allowed values: Effective, Partially Effective, Not Effective, Too Early to Confirm, Not Required; include brief rationale if needed. |
| Benefit Realised | Record the actual benefit achieved, including measured KPI change, cost saving, risk reduction, service improvement, customer satisfaction result, compliance improvement, or qualitative benefit. |
| Lessons Learned / Standardisation Action | Record any lessons learned and whether changes were embedded into procedures, training, specifications, contracts, checklists, asset plans, or monitoring arrangements. |
| Closure Approval | Enter the name, role, and approval decision of the person authorised to close the initiative after completion and effectiveness review. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the improvement initiative was formally closed, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |

### Maintenance

The FM Management System Manager owns this template, with updates made at least monthly and reviewed during management review for trends, overdue actions, and effectiveness of improvements. The register draws from the GRC/CAPA system, FM helpdesk or CAFM system, audit reports, KPI dashboards, customer feedback records, risk registers, and management review outputs.

field_guidance.Date Raised: Enter the date the improvement opportunity was formally logged, in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Raised By: Enter the name and role or function of the person who identified or submitted the improvement opportunity.
field_guidance.Improvement Source: Select the origin of the improvement from allowed values: Internal Audit, External Audit, Management Review, KPI Trend, Customer Feedback, Complaint, Risk Assessment, Incident, Nonconformity, Supplier Review, Staff Suggestion, Benchmarking, Regulatory Change, Technology / Innovation, Other.
field_guidance.Source Reference: Enter the reference number, report name, meeting minute ID, audit finding ID, KPI dashboard link, ticket number, or other traceable source reference.
field_guidance.ISO 41001 Clause / FM Process: Enter the relevant ISO 41001 clause where applicable and/or the FM process affected, for example Cl. 8.1 Operations, Cl. 9.1 Performance Evaluation, Maintenance, Cleaning, Space Management, Helpdesk, Security, Energy Management.
field_guidance.Facility / Site / Service Area: Enter the specific facility, site, building, region, department, asset group, or FM service area to which the improvement applies.
field_guidance.Interested Party / Customer Affected: Enter the customer, client, occupier group, internal department, regulator, supplier, user group, or other interested party affected by the improvement.
field_guidance.Current Issue or Opportunity Statement: Describe the current condition, gap, inefficiency, trend, risk, or opportunity in clear factual terms; avoid describing the solution only.
field_guidance.Improvement Category: Select the primary intent from allowed values: Improve FM Service, Improve FMS Effectiveness, Enhance Customer Satisfaction, Reduce Undesired Effect, Prevent Undesired Effect, Correct Undesired Effect, Improve Efficiency, Improve Compliance, Improve Sustainability, Other.
field_guidance.Intended Improvement Objective: State what the initiative is intended to achieve, written as a measurable improvement objective where possible.
field_guidance.Alignment to FM Policy / FM Objectives: Identify the relevant FM policy commitment, FM objective, performance target, customer requirement, or strategic business aim supported by the improvement.
field_guidance.Baseline Performance / Current State: Record the starting performance level or current state before action, including metric name, value, unit, and measurement period where applicable.
field_guidance.Target Outcome / Success Measure: Define the expected result and acceptance criteria, including KPI, target value, unit, threshold, or qualitative success condition.
field_guidance.Risk or Opportunity Rating: Enter the assessed significance using the organisation's risk method, for example Low, Medium, High, Critical, or a numeric score such as Likelihood x Impact.
field_guidance.Priority: Select the implementation priority from allowed values: Low, Medium, High, Urgent.
field_guidance.Proposed Improvement Action: Describe the planned action or initiative to implement the improvement, including key deliverables or change activities.
field_guidance.Action Owner: Enter the named person and role accountable for coordinating and delivering the improvement action.
field_guidance.Approver / Sponsor: Enter the manager, process owner, contract lead, FM director, or governance body approving resources and priority for the initiative.
field_guidance.Resources or Budget Required: Record required resources such as budget, labour, contractor support, tools, technology, training, or capital expenditure; include amount and currency where known.
field_guidance.Planned Start Date: Enter the planned commencement date for the improvement action, in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Target Completion Date: Enter the planned completion date for the improvement action, in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Status: Select the current lifecycle status from allowed values: Proposed, Approved, Not Started, In Progress, On Hold, Completed, Effectiveness Review Pending, Closed, Cancelled.
field_guidance.Progress / Update Notes: Enter dated progress notes, decisions, blockers, escalations, or changes to scope; each update should include date, author, and summary.
field_guidance.Related Corrective Action ID: Enter any linked corrective action, nonconformity, incident, risk treatment, audit finding, or CAPA reference; enter N/A if not applicable.
field_guidance.Evidence / Record Location: Enter the controlled document repository path, system link, ticket URL, project folder, report reference, or other evidence location proving implementation.
field_guidance.Actual Completion Date: Enter the date the improvement action was completed, in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until completed.
field_guidance.Effectiveness Review Required: Select Yes or No to indicate whether post-implementation effectiveness must be verified.
field_guidance.Effectiveness Review Date: Enter the planned or actual date for checking whether the improvement achieved its intended outcome, in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Effectiveness Review Result: Record the result of the effectiveness check using allowed values: Effective, Partially Effective, Not Effective, Too Early to Confirm, Not Required; include brief rationale if needed.
field_guidance.Benefit Realised: Record the actual benefit achieved, including measured KPI change, cost saving, risk reduction, service improvement, customer satisfaction result, compliance improvement, or qualitative benefit.
field_guidance.Lessons Learned / Standardisation Action: Record any lessons learned and whether changes were embedded into procedures, training, specifications, contracts, checklists, asset plans, or monitoring arrangements.
field_guidance.Closure Approval: Enter the name, role, and approval decision of the person authorised to close the initiative after completion and effectiveness review.
field_guidance.Closure Date: Enter the date the improvement initiative was formally closed, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

PCI-001.title: PCI Project Charter & Scope
PCI-001.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | PCI-PLAN-001 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | PCI Compliance Manager |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | PCI DSS v4.0.1 |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose & Objectives

This PCI Project Charter & Scope Plan establishes the authorised business justification, compliance scope, governance approach, and implementation plan for the organisation’s PCI DSS v4.0.1 compliance programme.

The purpose of this plan is to support PCI DSS Requirement 12.5.1 by ensuring that the organisation maintains a documented, current, and business-aligned understanding of its PCI DSS scope and related compliance responsibilities. This includes confirming the applicable merchant level, Self-Assessment Questionnaire type or assessment method, cardholder data environment boundaries, payment channels, in-scope people, processes, technologies, and third-party service provider dependencies.

This document serves as the formal charter for the PCI DSS v4.0.1 compliance project and provides the basis for planning, resourcing, executing, validating, and maintaining compliance activities.

The objectives of this plan are to:

1. Define the business justification for PCI DSS compliance based on the organisation’s acceptance, processing, storage, or transmission of account data.
2. Confirm the applicable PCI DSS assessment approach, including merchant level and SAQ type or Report on Compliance pathway.
3. Establish the scope of the Cardholder Data Environment, including systems, networks, applications, processes, facilities, people, and third-party service providers that may impact cardholder data security.
4. Support executive sponsorship and organisational accountability for PCI DSS v4.0.1 implementation and ongoing compliance.
5. Identify key assumptions, dependencies, resources, roles, milestones, and success criteria for the PCI DSS programme.
6. Provide a baseline scope statement to support PCI DSS gap assessment, remediation planning, control implementation, evidence collection, and assessment activities.
7. Ensure scope is reviewed and updated when business, technical, payment, or third-party changes may affect PCI DSS applicability.

This plan is intended for use by executive management, the PCI Compliance Manager, Information Security, IT Operations, Application Owners, Payment Operations, Legal, Procurement, Risk Management, Internal Audit, and relevant third-party service provider relationship owners.

## Scope

The scope of this PCI DSS v4.0.1 programme includes all organisational components that store, process, or transmit account data, or that could impact the security of the Cardholder Data Environment.

For this plan, “account data” includes cardholder data and sensitive authentication data as defined by PCI DSS v4.0.1. Cardholder data includes the Primary Account Number and, where present with the PAN, any of the following: cardholder name, expiration date, or service code. Sensitive authentication data includes full track data, card verification codes/values, PINs/PIN blocks, and related authentication data, and must not be stored after authorisation unless explicitly permitted by PCI DSS.

The organisation’s PCI DSS scope is determined using the following assessment factors:

| Scope Factor | Current Determination |
|---|---|
| Organisation type | Merchant |
| Business justification | The organisation accepts payment cards as a method of payment for goods and/or services through approved payment channels. PCI DSS compliance is required to protect account data, meet acquiring bank and payment brand obligations, reduce fraud and breach risk, and maintain the ability to process card payments. |
| Merchant level | [Merchant Level] |
| Annual transaction volume basis | [Annual Transaction Volume / Source] |
| Assessment method | [SAQ Type / ROC] |
| Acquiring bank or payment processor | [Acquirer / Processor Name] |
| Payment brands accepted | [Visa / Mastercard / American Express / Discover / JCB / Other] |
| PCI DSS version | PCI DSS v4.0.1 |
| Compliance validation period | [Assessment Year / Period] |
| Executive sponsor | [Executive Sponsor Name / Role] |
| Target validation date | [Target Validation Date] |

The PCI DSS scope includes, at minimum, the following payment channels and business processes:

| Payment Channel / Process | In Scope? | Description | PCI DSS Relevance |
|---|---:|---|---|
| E-commerce payments | [Yes/No] | Online payment acceptance through [website/platform] using [payment integration model] | May involve redirect, iframe, hosted payment page, API integration, JavaScript payment page scripts, or other mechanisms that can affect account data security. |
| Card-present retail payments | [Yes/No] | Face-to-face payments through payment terminals at [locations] | Includes payment terminals, point-of-sale connectivity, store networks, supporting applications, and terminal management processes. |
| Mail order / telephone order payments | [Yes/No] | Payments accepted through call centre, email, forms, or back-office processing | Includes personnel, call recording, CRM systems, payment entry portals, and procedures for handling account data. |
| Recurring / subscription billing | [Yes/No] | Stored token or recurring billing arrangements managed through [provider/system] | Includes token management, billing processes, and service provider dependencies. |
| Refunds and chargebacks | [Yes/No] | Handling of refunds, reversals, and disputes | Includes access to payment platforms, truncated PAN visibility, and operational workflows. |
| Settlement and reconciliation | [Yes/No] | Batch settlement, financial reconciliation, and reporting | Includes finance systems, reports, access controls, and data retention practices. |

The current scope includes the following categories of in-scope components:

| Scope Category | Included Components |
|---|---|
| Cardholder Data Environment | Systems, networks, applications, databases, endpoints, payment devices, and processes that store, process, or transmit account data. |
| Connected-to systems | Systems and network segments connected to or with direct access into the Cardholder Data Environment. |
| Security-impacting systems | Systems that can affect the security of the Cardholder Data Environment, including identity platforms, logging, vulnerability management, endpoint protection, configuration management, backup, monitoring, and administrative access systems. |
| Payment applications and integrations | Applications, payment pages, scripts, APIs, hosted payment integrations, payment gateways, point-of-sale applications, and middleware involved in payment acceptance. |
| People and roles | Employees, contractors, administrators, support staff, developers, finance users, payment operations staff, and third-party personnel with responsibilities affecting account data security. |
| Facilities | Locations where payment acceptance, support, administration, storage, or access to in-scope systems or account data occurs. |
| Service providers | Third parties that store, process, transmit, or could impact the security of account data on behalf of the organisation. |

The following are currently identified as in-scope systems and environments, subject to confirmation during scoping validation:

| System / Service | Type | Environment | PCI DSS Scope Rationale | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Payment Website / Application] | Application | Production | Used to initiate or facilitate payment transactions. | [Owner] |
| [Payment Gateway] | Third-party service | Production | Processes or transmits payment card transactions on behalf of the organisation. | [Owner] |
| [E-commerce Platform] | Application / SaaS | Production | Hosts payment journey or payment-related scripts and integrations. | [Owner] |
| [POS Terminals] | Payment devices | Production | Capture card-present payment data. | [Owner] |
| [Store / Branch Network] | Network | Production | Supports payment terminal connectivity. | [Owner] |
| [Call Centre Platform] | Application / SaaS | Production | May support telephone payment workflows or payment entry. | [Owner] |
| [Identity Provider] | Security-impacting system | Production | Provides authentication or administrative access to in-scope systems. | [Owner] |
| [Logging / SIEM Platform] | Security-impacting system | Production | Collects security logs from in-scope systems. | [Owner] |
| [Vulnerability Scanner] | Security-impacting system | Production | Performs vulnerability scanning of in-scope assets. | [Owner] |
| [Change Management Platform] | Governance system | Production | Supports approval and tracking of changes affecting PCI DSS scope. | [Owner] |

The following data-handling principles apply to the PCI DSS scope:

1. The organisation will not store sensitive authentication data after authorisation.
2. Storage of PAN will be avoided unless there is a documented business need approved by the PCI Compliance Manager and Information Security.
3. Where PAN is stored, displayed, or transmitted, PCI DSS requirements for protection, masking, rendering unreadable, and secure transmission will apply.
4. Tokenisation, hosted payment pages, redirect methods, and validated third-party service providers will be preferred to reduce scope where feasible.
5. Network segmentation, payment integration design, and process controls will be used to minimise systems and personnel in scope.
6. Scope reduction methods will be validated and documented; they will not be assumed effective without evidence.

The following items are considered out of scope only if validated through documented scoping analysis, network diagrams, data-flow diagrams, access reviews, and segmentation testing where applicable:

| Potentially Out-of-Scope Area | Basis for Exclusion | Validation Required |
|---|---|---|
| Corporate user network | No storage, processing, transmission, or connectivity impacting the CDE | Network segmentation evidence, firewall rules, access path review, segmentation testing where applicable. |
| General finance systems | No PAN storage or access to unmasked account data | Data discovery, report review, access review, and reconciliation workflow assessment. |
| Non-payment customer systems | No payment functionality or account data | Application review, data-flow confirmation, and integration review. |
| Development and test environments | No production account data and no connectivity affecting production CDE | Data sanitisation controls, environment separation, access review, and configuration review. |
| General office facilities | No payment acceptance or support of in-scope administration | Process walkthrough and facilities review. |

Any change to payment channels, payment processors, integrations, cardholder data storage, network connectivity, third-party providers, or administrative access paths may affect scope and must be assessed through the organisation’s change and PCI impact assessment processes.

## Assumptions & Dependencies

The following assumptions apply to this PCI DSS v4.0.1 implementation plan:

| Assumption | Impact if Invalid | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| The organisation is classified as a merchant for PCI DSS validation purposes. | Assessment approach and validation obligations may need revision. | PCI Compliance Manager |
| The merchant level and SAQ type or ROC pathway will be confirmed with the acquiring bank or payment brand requirements before formal validation. | Incorrect assessment method may result in rejected attestation. | Finance / Payment Operations |
| The organisation does not intentionally store sensitive authentication data after authorisation. | High-risk compliance gap requiring immediate remediation. | Information Security |
| Existing payment integrations can be documented through current data-flow diagrams and architecture records. | Additional discovery and workshops will be required. | IT Architecture |
| Third-party service providers will provide current PCI DSS Attestations of Compliance and responsibility matrices. | Service provider risk may delay compliance validation. | Procurement / Vendor Management |
| Required stakeholders will be available for scoping workshops, evidence collection, control implementation, and assessment interviews. | Timeline and assessment readiness may be affected. | Executive Sponsor |
| Network segmentation or scope reduction controls, where relied upon, can be technically validated. | Additional systems may be considered in scope. | Network Operations |
| No material payment channel or architecture change will occur during the validation period without PCI impact assessment. | Scope may require reassessment and evidence updates. | Change Advisory Board |

The PCI DSS programme depends on the following internal and external inputs:

| Dependency | Description | Required By | Responsible Party |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acquirer confirmation | Confirmation of merchant level, validation requirements, and required submission format. | Scope confirmation phase | Finance / Payment Operations |
| Transaction volume data | Annual transaction volumes by payment brand and channel. | Scope confirmation phase | Finance |
| Payment channel inventory | Complete list of payment acceptance methods and locations. | Scope confirmation phase | Payment Operations |
| Cardholder data-flow diagrams | Diagrams showing where account data is captured, transmitted, processed, stored, or redirected. | Scoping and assessment | IT Architecture / Application Owners |
| Network diagrams | Current diagrams showing CDE, connected systems, segmentation boundaries, wireless networks, and security controls. | Scoping and control validation | Network Operations |
| Asset inventory | Inventory of in-scope systems, applications, databases, endpoints, payment devices, and cloud services. | Control implementation | IT Operations |
| Service provider documentation | AOCs, contracts, responsibility matrices, and service descriptions for PCI-relevant third parties. | Third-party control validation | Vendor Management |
| Security control evidence | Evidence for access control, logging, vulnerability management, secure configuration, change management, incident response, and policy requirements. | Assessment readiness | Control Owners |
| Qualified assessor support | QSA, ISA, or internal PCI subject matter expertise, depending on assessment method and risk profile. | Gap assessment and validation | PCI Compliance Manager |
| Remediation capacity | Technical and process resources to address identified gaps. | Remediation phase | Executive Sponsor / IT Leadership |

Key dependencies must be tracked through the PCI project plan. Material blockers must be escalated to the Executive Sponsor when they threaten the target validation date or create unresolved compliance risk.

## Approach / Phases

The PCI DSS v4.0.1 implementation programme will be executed through structured phases. Each phase will produce defined outputs and decision points to ensure the scope remains accurate and the selected assessment method remains appropriate.

### Phase 1: Initiation and Charter Approval

The initiation phase establishes formal sponsorship, confirms the business justification, and authorises the PCI DSS project.

Key activities:

1. Appoint the Executive Sponsor, PCI Compliance Manager, project team, and control owners.
2. Confirm the organisation’s obligation to comply with PCI DSS due to payment card acceptance.
3. Obtain current transaction volume and payment brand/acquirer requirements.
4. Confirm merchant level and expected SAQ type or ROC pathway.
5. Approve this PCI Project Charter & Scope Plan.
6. Establish governance cadence, escalation paths, and reporting expectations.

Expected outputs:

- Approved PCI Project Charter & Scope Plan.
- Confirmed project governance structure.
- Initial merchant level and assessment method determination.
- Initial stakeholder and responsibility assignment.

### Phase 2: Scope Discovery and Validation

The scope discovery phase identifies all payment channels, data flows, systems, locations, personnel, and third parties that may be in scope for PCI DSS.

Key activities:

1. Conduct payment process walkthroughs with business owners.
2. Document cardholder data flows for each payment channel.
3. Identify whether account data is stored, processed, transmitted, displayed, logged, or reported.
4. Validate whether sensitive authentication data is present in any system or process after authorisation.
5. Identify all systems connected to or security-impacting the CDE.
6. Review network segmentation and scope reduction mechanisms.
7. Identify service providers that store, process, transmit, or could impact account data security.
8. Confirm payment page and script responsibilities for e-commerce environments, where applicable.
9. Validate whether the selected SAQ type remains appropriate based on actual scope.

Expected outputs:

- Approved PCI scope statement.
- Cardholder data-flow diagrams.
- Network diagrams showing CDE and segmentation boundaries.
- In-scope asset inventory.
- Payment channel inventory.
- Third-party service provider inventory.
- Confirmed assessment method.

### Phase 3: Gap Assessment

The gap assessment phase evaluates current controls against applicable PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirements for the confirmed scope and assessment method.

Key activities:

1. Map applicable PCI DSS requirements to control owners.
2. Review current policies, standards, procedures, configurations, and technical controls.
3. Conduct interviews and evidence reviews with control owners.
4. Assess security controls for in-scope systems and service provider dependencies.
5. Validate whether compensating controls or customised approaches are being used, if applicable.
6. Document gaps, risks, owners, remediation actions, and target dates.
7. Prioritise gaps that affect cardholder data protection, scope validity, and assessment readiness.

Expected outputs:

- PCI DSS v4.0.1 gap assessment results.
- Remediation action plan.
- Updated risk register entries.
- Evidence collection plan.
- Updated project timeline if required.

### Phase 4: Remediation and Control Implementation

The remediation phase addresses identified gaps and implements or improves PCI DSS controls.

Key activities:

1. Implement technical and process remediation actions.
2. Update policies, standards, procedures, and operating records.
3. Confirm secure configurations, access controls, logging, vulnerability management, change management, and incident response capabilities.
4. Obtain and review PCI DSS AOCs and responsibility matrices from service providers.
5. Validate that any scope reduction controls remain effective after remediation.
6. Track remediation progress through governance meetings.
7. Escalate overdue or high-risk remediation items.

Expected outputs:

- Completed remediation actions.
- Updated documentation and control evidence.
- Service provider compliance evidence.
- Updated scope artefacts, where remediation affected architecture or processes.
- Residual risk decisions, where applicable.

### Phase 5: Readiness Review and Evidence Collection

The readiness phase confirms that applicable PCI DSS requirements are operating effectively and that evidence is complete and current.

Key activities:

1. Perform internal readiness review against applicable SAQ or ROC requirements.
2. Confirm evidence completeness, currency, and traceability to control requirements.
3. Validate asset inventories, data-flow diagrams, and network diagrams.
4. Verify that in-scope personnel understand their PCI DSS responsibilities.
5. Confirm that service provider documentation is current and supports reliance on outsourced controls.
6. Conduct management review of open issues, residual risks, and assessment readiness.
7. Obtain approval to proceed to formal validation.

Expected outputs:

- Assessment readiness sign-off.
- Complete evidence repository.
- Updated control owner attestations.
- Management approval to proceed.
- Finalised scope package for assessor or SAQ signatory.

### Phase 6: Formal Validation and Attestation

The validation phase completes the required PCI DSS assessment and submission process.

Key activities:

1. Complete the applicable SAQ, Attestation of Compliance, or Report on Compliance process.
2. Support QSA or ISA assessment activities where applicable.
3. Resolve assessment questions or evidence gaps.
4. Obtain executive review and sign-off on attestation documents.
5. Submit required validation documentation to the acquiring bank, payment brand, or requesting entity.
6. Record assessment outcomes and any required remediation commitments.

Expected outputs:

- Completed SAQ and AOC or ROC and AOC, as applicable.
- Assessment evidence archive.
- Submission confirmation.
- Management sign-off.
- Lessons learned and continuous compliance backlog.

### Phase 7: Continuous Compliance and Scope Maintenance

The continuous compliance phase maintains PCI DSS scope and control effectiveness after formal validation.

Key activities:

1. Monitor changes that may affect PCI DSS scope.
2. Perform periodic scope reviews and update scope documentation.
3. Maintain asset inventories, data-flow diagrams, network diagrams, and service provider records.
4. Track recurring PCI DSS activities, including vulnerability scanning, access reviews, log reviews, awareness, risk assessment, and incident response testing.
5. Confirm that business-as-usual processes include PCI DSS control ownership and evidence retention.
6. Prepare for the next validation cycle.

Expected outputs:

- Updated scope documentation.
- Continuous compliance calendar.
- Periodic control evidence.
- Scope change assessments.
- Updated service provider compliance records.
- Annual reassessment plan.

## Milestones & Timeline

The following timeline is the baseline plan for implementing and validating PCI DSS v4.0.1 compliance. Dates must be adjusted based on the effective date of this plan, confirmed assessment method, remediation complexity, and acquiring bank requirements.

| Milestone | Key Deliverables | Target Date | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Project initiation approved | Executive sponsor confirmed; project team assigned; charter approved. | [Date] | Executive Sponsor | Not Started |
| Merchant level and assessment method confirmed | Transaction volumes reviewed; acquirer confirmation obtained; SAQ type or ROC pathway confirmed. | [Date] | Finance / PCI Compliance Manager | Not Started |
| Payment channel inventory completed | All payment acceptance channels and locations documented. | [Date] | Payment Operations | Not Started |
| Scope discovery workshops completed | Business and technical walkthroughs completed for all payment channels. | [Date] | PCI Compliance Manager | Not Started |
| Cardholder data-flow diagrams completed | Data flows documented and approved for each payment channel. | [Date] | IT Architecture | Not Started |
| Network and segmentation diagrams completed | CDE boundaries, connected systems, segmentation controls, and security-impacting systems documented. | [Date] | Network Operations | Not Started |
| In-scope asset inventory baselined | Systems, applications, payment devices, databases, services, and administrative platforms identified. | [Date] | IT Operations | Not Started |
| Third-party PCI inventory completed | Service providers identified; AOCs and responsibility matrices requested. | [Date] | Vendor Management | Not Started |
| Scope statement approved | PCI DSS scope confirmed and signed off by PCI Compliance Manager and Executive Sponsor. | [Date] | PCI Compliance Manager | Not Started |
| PCI DSS gap assessment completed | Applicable requirements assessed; gaps documented and prioritised. | [Date] | Information Security | Not Started |
| Remediation plan approved | Remediation actions, owners, dates, and escalation criteria approved. | [Date] | Executive Sponsor | Not Started |
| High-risk remediation completed | Critical gaps affecting account data security, scope validity, or assessment readiness resolved. | [Date] | Control Owners | Not Started |
| Service provider evidence completed | Current AOCs, responsibility matrices, and contractual responsibilities obtained and reviewed. | [Date] | Vendor Management | Not Started |
| Internal readiness review completed | Evidence reviewed; open issues dispositioned; readiness sign-off obtained. | [Date] | PCI Compliance Manager | Not Started |
| Formal assessment completed | SAQ/AOC or ROC/AOC completed with required evidence and approvals. | [Date] | PCI Compliance Manager / Assessor | Not Started |
| Submission completed | Required validation documents submitted to acquirer or requesting entity. | [Date] | Finance / PCI Compliance Manager | Not Started |
| Continuous compliance plan activated | Recurring control activities scheduled; scope review triggers integrated into change processes. | [Date] | PCI Compliance Manager | Not Started |

Project status will be reported at least monthly to the Executive Sponsor and relevant governance forum until formal validation is complete. High-risk issues or scope changes must be escalated within five business days of identification.

## Roles & Responsibilities

PCI DSS compliance requires cross-functional ownership. The following roles are accountable for successful implementation, validation, and maintenance of the PCI DSS v4.0.1 programme.

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | Approves the PCI charter, scope, budget, priorities, and remediation decisions; resolves escalated blockers; accepts residual business risk where permitted by organisational risk governance. |
| PCI Compliance Manager | Owns the PCI DSS compliance programme; coordinates scoping, gap assessment, remediation tracking, evidence collection, assessment activities, and scope maintenance; ensures alignment with PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.5.1. |
| Information Security | Provides security control expertise; supports risk assessment, vulnerability management, logging, incident response, security monitoring, policy development, and control validation. |
| Payment Operations | Owns payment acceptance processes; maintains inventory of payment channels and operational workflows; confirms business use of payment platforms and cardholder data handling practices. |
| Finance | Provides transaction volume data; liaises with acquirer or payment processor; supports validation submission and reconciliation process scoping. |
| IT Operations | Maintains in-scope infrastructure, endpoints, servers, databases, backups, and operational controls; supports evidence collection and remediation. |
| Network Operations | Maintains network diagrams, segmentation controls, firewall rules, wireless controls, and connectivity documentation affecting the CDE. |
| Application Owners | Own payment applications, e-commerce platforms, integrations, APIs, and supporting applications; support secure development, change management, access control, and evidence collection. |
| IT Architecture | Documents current-state and target-state payment architectures; maintains data-flow diagrams and validates scope boundaries. |
| Identity and Access Management | Supports user access provisioning, authentication controls, privileged access management, periodic access reviews, and access evidence. |
| Vendor Management / Procurement | Identifies PCI-relevant service providers; obtains AOCs, responsibility matrices, contractual assurances, and monitors ongoing third-party compliance. |
| Legal / Privacy | Supports contract review, regulatory alignment, breach notification considerations, and data retention obligations. |
| Internal Audit / Risk Management | Provides independent challenge, risk oversight, and assurance coordination where applicable. |
| Change Advisory Board | Ensures changes affecting payment systems, CDE connectivity, service providers, or account data flows include PCI DSS impact assessment before implementation. |
| Control Owners | Implement and operate assigned PCI DSS controls; maintain evidence; remediate gaps; attest to control operation when requested. |
| Qualified Security Assessor / Internal Security Assessor | Provides PCI DSS assessment guidance or performs formal assessment activities where required by the validation approach. |
| Service Provider Relationship Owners | Ensure service provider responsibilities are documented, current compliance evidence is obtained, and shared control gaps are escalated. |

The following RACI matrix applies to core PCI DSS project activities:

| Activity | Executive Sponsor | PCI Compliance Manager | Information Security | IT / App Owners | Payment Operations | Finance | Vendor Management |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Approve PCI charter and scope | A | R | C | C | C | C | C |
| Confirm merchant level and assessment method | C | R | C | I | C | A/R | I |
| Document payment channels | I | C | C | C | A/R | C | I |
| Document cardholder data flows | I | A/R | C | R | C | I | C |
| Maintain in-scope asset inventory | I | A | C | R | C | I | C |
| Validate third-party service provider scope | I | A | C | C | C | I | R |
| Perform PCI DSS gap assessment | I | A/R | R | C | C | I | C |
| Execute remediation plan | A | C | C | R | R | C | C |
| Collect assessment evidence | I | A/R | R | R | R | C | R |
| Complete SAQ/AOC or support ROC | A | R | C | C | C | C | C |
| Submit validation documentation | I | C | I | I | C | A/R | I |
| Maintain continuous compliance | A | R | R | R | R | C | R |

RACI definitions:

- **R** = Responsible for performing the activity.
- **A** = Accountable for final decision or outcome.
- **C** = Consulted before or during the activity.
- **I** = Informed of progress or outcome.

## Resources

The organisation will allocate appropriate personnel, tools, budget, and supporting services to complete PCI DSS v4.0.1 implementation and validation.

### Personnel Resources

| Resource | Estimated Commitment | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Executive Sponsor | 1–2 hours per month, plus escalation support | Governance, prioritisation, and approval. |
| PCI Compliance Manager | 0.4–1.0 FTE during implementation | Programme coordination, scoping, evidence management, and assessment readiness. |
| Information Security Lead | 0.2–0.5 FTE during assessment and remediation | Security control review, risk assessment, and remediation support. |
| IT Operations Representatives | As required by system scope | Infrastructure evidence, configuration remediation, logging, vulnerability management, and backup controls. |
| Network Engineer | As required during scoping and segmentation validation | Network diagrams, firewall review, segmentation evidence, and remediation. |
| Application Owners / Developers | As required by payment application scope | Application security, secure development, change evidence, and integration reviews. |
| Payment Operations SME | As required during payment workflow review | Payment process documentation and operational evidence. |
| Vendor Management Specialist | As required during third-party review | Service provider AOCs, responsibility matrices, contract evidence, and follow-up. |
| Finance Representative | As required during validation | Transaction volume confirmation, acquirer coordination, and submission support. |
| QSA / ISA Support | As needed based on assessment method | Assessment advice, readiness review, and formal validation support where required. |

### Tooling and Technical Resources

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Asset inventory / CMDB | Identification and tracking of in-scope systems and ownership. |
| Network discovery and diagramming tools | Validation of connectivity, segmentation boundaries, and CDE architecture. |
| Vulnerability scanning platform | Internal and external vulnerability scanning of in-scope assets. |
| Approved Scanning Vendor service | External vulnerability scanning where applicable. |
| Configuration management tools | Secure configuration evidence and baseline compliance. |
| Logging / SIEM platform | Centralised security monitoring and log retention evidence. |
| Identity and access management tools | Access control, privileged access, authentication, and periodic review evidence. |
| Change management system | Evidence of approved changes and PCI impact assessment. |
| Ticketing / project management tool | Remediation tracking and accountability. |
| Document repository | Controlled storage of PCI DSS evidence, diagrams, policies, and assessment artefacts. |
| Data discovery tools | Identification of account data storage, logs, reports, and unintended PAN exposure. |
| Vendor risk management platform | Tracking of PCI-relevant service provider obligations and compliance status. |

### Budget Considerations

The following cost categories must be considered and approved as required:

| Budget Item | Description | Approval Owner |
|---|---|---|
| QSA / advisory services | External assessment, readiness review, or specialist PCI DSS support. | Executive Sponsor |
| Remediation engineering | Security tooling, configuration, network segmentation, application changes, or infrastructure improvements. | IT Leadership |
| Scanning and testing | ASV scans, penetration testing, segmentation testing, and application security testing. | Information Security |
| Training and awareness | PCI DSS role-based training for in-scope personnel. | PCI Compliance Manager |
| Payment architecture changes | Scope reduction initiatives, hosted payment integration changes, tokenisation, or service provider changes. | Executive Sponsor |
| Documentation and evidence management | Tools or services required to maintain audit-ready evidence. | PCI Compliance Manager |
| Third-party compliance reviews | Vendor assurance, legal review, or contract updates for PCI-relevant service providers. | Vendor Management / Legal |

Resources must be sufficient to ensure the organisation can complete scope validation, remediate compliance gaps, and maintain ongoing PCI DSS controls without relying solely on annual assessment activity.

## Success Metrics

The PCI DSS v4.0.1 implementation will be measured using outcome-based and control-readiness metrics. These metrics support management oversight and demonstrate whether PCI DSS scope is understood, documented, and maintained in accordance with Requirement 12.5.1.

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Reporting Frequency |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Merchant level and assessment method confirmed | 100% complete before gap assessment | Acquirer confirmation or documented validation basis | Once per assessment cycle |
| Payment channels documented | 100% of active payment channels | Approved payment channel inventory | Monthly during project; quarterly thereafter |
| Cardholder data-flow diagrams completed | 100% of in-scope payment channels | Approved diagrams reviewed by business and technical owners | Monthly during project; after material change |
| In-scope asset inventory completeness | 100% of identified CDE, connected-to, and security-impacting systems | Reconciliation against network diagrams, CMDB, and discovery outputs | Monthly during project; quarterly thereafter |
| Service provider PCI evidence obtained | 100% of PCI-relevant service providers | Current AOC and responsibility matrix on file | Monthly during project; at least annually thereafter |
| Scope approval completed | Formal approval before assessment validation | Signed scope statement or governance record | Once per assessment cycle; after scope change |
| High-risk PCI gaps remediated | 100% before formal validation or formally risk-managed where permitted | Remediation tracker and evidence review | Weekly or biweekly during remediation |
| Assessment evidence readiness | 100% of applicable requirements have current evidence | Evidence repository review against SAQ/ROC checklist | Prior to formal validation |
| Open critical scope issues | 0 at validation | Scope issue log and management review | Weekly during assessment readiness |
| PCI impact assessments for relevant changes | 100% of payment, CDE, or service provider changes | Change records with PCI impact field completed | Monthly |
| Validation submitted by target date | Completed by [Target Validation Date] | Submission confirmation from acquirer or requesting entity | Once per assessment cycle |
| Continuous compliance activities scheduled | 100% of recurring PCI tasks assigned and calendared | Compliance calendar and task tracker | Quarterly |

A successful outcome for this plan is achieved when:

1. The organisation has formally confirmed and documented its PCI DSS scope.
2. The merchant level and assessment method are approved and defensible.
3. All payment channels and account data flows are documented.
4. In-scope systems, people, processes, facilities, and service providers are identified.
5. Control ownership and remediation accountability are assigned.
6. Required PCI DSS validation documentation is completed and submitted by the agreed deadline.
7. Business-as-usual processes are established to maintain scope and compliance after validation.

## Review & Update Triggers

This PCI Project Charter & Scope Plan must be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change that could affect PCI DSS scope, assessment method, business justification, merchant level, payment architecture, account data flows, or control responsibilities.

The PCI Compliance Manager is responsible for coordinating reviews and ensuring updates are approved by the appropriate governance authority.

The following events require review and, where applicable, update of this plan:

| Trigger | Required Action | Review Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Annual PCI DSS validation cycle begins | Confirm merchant level, assessment method, scope, roles, timeline, and resources. | PCI Compliance Manager |
| Change in transaction volume | Reassess merchant level and validation requirements. | Finance / PCI Compliance Manager |
| New payment channel introduced | Perform PCI impact assessment; update payment inventory, data flows, systems, and assessment method if needed. | Payment Operations |
