| [EXAMPLE: VULN-INT-2026-Q1-001] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-Q1] | [EXAMPLE: Authenticated Internal Vulnerability Scan] | [EXAMPLE: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 11.3.1 and 11.3.1.2] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-10] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-11] | [EXAMPLE: Compliant] | [EXAMPLE: Quarterly Scheduled] | [EXAMPLE: Full CDE Coverage] | [EXAMPLE: 10.10.0.0/16; 10.20.5.0/24; prod-vpc-cde] | [EXAMPLE: CMDB group CDE-Servers; DB-PROD-01; FW-CDE-01; APP-PAY-*] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: Tenable.sc 6.4.0 / Nessus Engine 10.8.3] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-09] | [EXAMPLE: PCI Internal Authenticated Scan Policy v4] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: SSH; Windows domain credential; SNMPv3] | [EXAMPLE: 248/250 assets authenticated] | [EXAMPLE: APP-PAY-07 host offline; DB-TEST-02 credential expired] | [EXAMPLE: Security Vulnerability Management Team] | [EXAMPLE: Internal vulnerability analyst trained on scanner operation; training record SEC-TRN-2026-014] | [EXAMPLE: Completed with Errors] | [EXAMPLE: CVSS v3.1 plus asset criticality per Vulnerability Risk Ranking Standard] | [EXAMPLE: 1] | [EXAMPLE: 4] | [EXAMPLE: 18] | [EXAMPLE: 37] | [EXAMPLE: 12] | [EXAMPLE: CVE-2026-12345 on 3 Linux servers; TLS weak cipher plugin 98765 on 5 web servers] | [EXAMPLE: Infrastructure Operations Team] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-10] | [EXAMPLE: Remediated Pending Rescan] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-12] | [EXAMPLE: Passed] | [EXAMPLE: 0] | [EXAMPLE: 0] | [EXAMPLE: GRC/Vulnerability/2026/Q1/InternalScan/VULN-INT-2026-Q1-001] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-13] | [EXAMPLE: Security Compliance Manager] | [EXAMPLE: Approved] | [EXAMPLE: Head of Information Security] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-14] | [EXAMPLE: None] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Report ID | Enter the unique identifier for this quarterly internal vulnerability scan report/log entry; use a consistent format such as VULN-INT-YYYY-Q#-###. |
| Reporting Quarter | Enter the quarter covered by the scan in format YYYY-Q1, YYYY-Q2, YYYY-Q3, or YYYY-Q4. |
| Scan Type | Enter the type of scan performed; allowed value for this template is Authenticated Internal Vulnerability Scan. |
| PCI DSS Requirement Reference | Enter the applicable PCI DSS control reference; expected value is PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 11.3.1, and include 11.3.1.2 if this row records authenticated scan evidence. |
| Scan Start Date | Enter the date the internal vulnerability scan began in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Scan End Date | Enter the date the internal vulnerability scan completed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Scan Frequency Compliance | Enter whether the scan met the quarterly requirement; allowed values are Compliant, Late, Missed, or Not Assessed. |
| Scan Trigger | Enter why the scan was performed; allowed values are Quarterly Scheduled, Post-Significant Change, Remediation Rescan, or Other. |
| CDE Scope Covered | State whether the scan covered all in-scope cardholder data environment systems and applicable connected internal systems; allowed values are Full CDE Coverage, Partial CDE Coverage, or Not Confirmed. |
| In-Scope Internal Network Ranges | List the internal IP ranges, subnets, VLANs, cloud VPC/VNet ranges, or asset groups scanned; use CIDR notation where possible, separated by semicolons. |
| In-Scope System Components | List or reference the in-scope servers, databases, applications, containers, network devices, endpoints, and security systems included in the scan; asset IDs or CMDB group names are acceptable. |
| Excluded Assets | List any internal assets, ranges, or components excluded from the scan; enter None if there were no exclusions. |
| Exclusion Justification | For each excluded asset, document the approved reason for exclusion and approval reference; enter N/A if Excluded Assets is None. |
| Scanner Tool Name and Version | Enter the vulnerability scanning tool/platform name and version used, including sensor/engine version where applicable. |
| Scanner Signature/Plugin Feed Date | Enter the vulnerability plugin, feed, or signature update date used for the scan in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Scan Profile/Policy Name | Enter the exact scan policy, template, or profile name used, confirming it is appropriate for internal authenticated vulnerability scanning. |
| Authenticated Scan Performed | Record whether credentials were used for authenticated scanning; allowed values are Yes, No, or Partially. |
| Authentication Method | Enter the authentication mechanism used, such as SSH, Windows domain credential, local admin, sudo, WinRM, SNMPv3, database credential, API credential, agent-based authenticated scan, or N/A. |
| Authentication Coverage | Enter the percentage or count of successfully authenticated assets, such as 98% or 245/250 assets authenticated. |
| Authentication Failures | List assets where authenticated scanning failed and the reason, such as invalid credential, firewall blocked, host offline, insufficient privilege, or enter None. |
| Scan Operator | Enter the name or user ID of the person/team that executed or scheduled the scan. |
| Operator Qualification | Enter evidence that the scan was performed by qualified personnel, such as internal security role, training record, certification, or approved managed service provider reference. |
| Scan Completion Status | Enter the scan result status; allowed values are Completed Successfully, Completed with Errors, Failed, Cancelled, or Incomplete. |
| Vulnerability Severity Rating Method | Enter the severity basis used to rank vulnerabilities in accordance with the entity’s vulnerability risk ranking process under PCI DSS Req 6.3.1, such as CVSS v3.1 plus asset criticality, vendor criticality, scanner severity, or internal risk model. |
| Critical Vulnerabilities Identified | Enter the number of unique critical vulnerabilities identified during the scan; numeric value only. |
| High Vulnerabilities Identified | Enter the number of unique high vulnerabilities identified during the scan; numeric value only. |
| Medium Vulnerabilities Identified | Enter the number of unique medium vulnerabilities identified during the scan; numeric value only. |
| Low Vulnerabilities Identified | Enter the number of unique low vulnerabilities identified during the scan; numeric value only. |
| Informational Findings Identified | Enter the number of informational findings identified during the scan; numeric value only. |
| Critical/High Findings Summary | Summarize critical and high vulnerabilities found, including vulnerability IDs/CVEs/plugin IDs, affected asset count, and business impact; enter None if no critical or high findings were identified. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the individual, team, or service owner responsible for remediating critical and high vulnerabilities; use role or group mailbox if ownership is shared. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target remediation completion date for critical/high findings in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on the organisation’s vulnerability remediation SLA. |
| Remediation Status | Enter the current remediation state; allowed values are Not Started, In Progress, Remediated Pending Rescan, Rescan Passed, Risk Accepted, Deferred with Approval, or N/A. |
| Rescan Required | Enter whether a rescan is required to verify remediation of critical/high vulnerabilities; allowed values are Yes, No, or N/A. |
| Rescan Date | Enter the date the verification rescan was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no rescan is required. |
| Rescan Result | Enter the outcome of the rescan; allowed values are Passed, Failed, Partially Passed, Pending, or N/A. |
| Residual Critical Vulnerabilities | Enter the number of critical vulnerabilities remaining after remediation/rescan; numeric value only, or N/A if rescan not yet performed. |
| Residual High Vulnerabilities | Enter the number of high vulnerabilities remaining after remediation/rescan; numeric value only, or N/A if rescan not yet performed. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the repository path, ticket link, scanner report ID, GRC record URL, or document management reference where the full scan report, raw results, authentication proof, remediation evidence, and rescan evidence are stored. |
| Report Review Date | Enter the date the report/log entry was reviewed by security or compliance personnel in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Reviewed By | Enter the name, role, or user ID of the person who reviewed the scan results for completeness, scope coverage, authentication success, and remediation tracking. |
| Approval Status | Enter the approval state of this quarterly scan report; allowed values are Draft, Reviewed, Approved, Rejected, or Requires Update. |
| Approver | Enter the name, role, or user ID of the authorised manager or control owner approving the quarterly scan report. |
| Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not yet approved. |
| Comments/Exceptions | Enter any additional notes, approved exceptions, compensating circumstances, late-scan explanation, scope limitations, or references to risk acceptance records; enter None if not applicable. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Vulnerability Management or Security Operations control owner, with Compliance/GRC review. Updated at least quarterly after each internal authenticated vulnerability scan and after any required remediation rescans, using evidence from the vulnerability scanner, CMDB/asset inventory, ticketing system, and GRC evidence repository.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Reporting Year | Enter the calendar or PCI reporting year to which the scan belongs, in YYYY format. |
| Quarter | Enter the applicable quarter for the required external ASV scan: Q1, Q2, Q3, or Q4. |
| Scan Trigger | Enter the reason the ASV scan was performed; allowed values: Quarterly Scheduled Scan, Post-Significant Change Scan. |
| PCI DSS Requirement | Enter the control reference covered by this record; use PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 11.3.2. |
| ASV Company Name | Enter the full legal or trading name of the PCI Approved Scanning Vendor that performed the external vulnerability scan. |
| ASV Approval/Listing Reference | Enter the ASV identifier, listing reference, or confirmation reference from the PCI SSC ASV listing, if available; otherwise enter the ASV listing URL or N/A if not provided. |
| ASV Scan Report ID | Enter the unique report number, scan ID, or reference assigned by the ASV platform/report. |
| ASV Scan Report Date | Enter the date shown on the ASV scan report in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Initial Scan Start Date | Enter the date the initial external ASV scan started in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Initial Scan Completion Date | Enter the date the initial external ASV scan completed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| External Scan Scope Covered | Enter the external-facing systems included in the scan, such as internet-facing IP ranges, individual IP addresses, FQDNs, domains, cloud endpoints, or hosted payment pages that are in scope for PCI DSS. |
| Number of In-Scope External IPs/FQDNs Scanned | Enter the total count of unique in-scope external IP addresses and FQDNs included in the ASV scan, as a whole number. |
| Scan Scope Validation Performed | Record whether the scan scope was validated against the current PCI external attack surface before accepting the report; allowed values: Yes, No. If No, explain in Notes/Exceptions. |
| Significant Change Reference | For post-significant-change scans, enter the approved change ticket/reference that triggered the scan; for quarterly scheduled scans enter N/A. |
| Initial ASV Scan Result | Enter the result of the initial ASV scan exactly as concluded by the ASV report; allowed values: Pass, Fail, Not Determined. |
| Highest Vulnerability Severity Reported | Enter the highest severity level found in the initial ASV scan using the ASV report rating; allowed values: None, Low, Medium, High, Critical, Other-ASV-Rated. |
| Failed Vulnerabilities Summary | If the initial result was Fail, summarize the ASV-reported failing vulnerabilities, including CVE/plugin IDs where available; if no failing vulnerabilities, enter None. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the role/team responsible for remediating failed ASV findings, such as Infrastructure Team, Network Team, Cloud Operations, Application Owner, or Managed Service Provider; if not applicable enter N/A. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target date for completing remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; if not applicable enter N/A. |
| Remediation Completion Date | Enter the actual date remediation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; if not applicable enter N/A. |
| Rescan Required | Enter whether a rescan was required to achieve a passing ASV result; allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Rescan Date | Enter the date of the ASV rescan that confirmed remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; if no rescan was required enter N/A. |
| Final ASV Scan Result | Enter the final ASV outcome after remediation and any rescans; allowed values: Pass, Fail, Pending. |
| Passing Scan Achieved Date | Enter the date a passing ASV scan was achieved in YYYY-MM-DD format; if not yet achieved enter Pending. |
| ASV Attestation/Executive Summary Included | Record whether the retained evidence includes the ASV attestation, executive summary, or official passing scan report page required to demonstrate the result; allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Evidence Repository Location | Enter the controlled repository path, document management link, GRC record ID, or ticket attachment location where the ASV report and supporting evidence are retained. |
| Reviewed By | Enter the name and role of the person who reviewed the ASV report for completeness, scope accuracy, and pass/fail status. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the ASV report was reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Management Sign-Off | Enter the name and role of the accountable manager who accepted the quarterly ASV scan record, or enter Pending if not yet signed off. |
| Notes/Exceptions | Enter any relevant clarification, such as scope exclusions, IP ownership changes, ASV disputes, false positive determinations accepted by the ASV, pending remediation, or reasons for late completion; enter None if there are no notes. |

### Maintenance

This template is owned by the PCI Compliance Manager or GRC owner, with input from Infrastructure, Network Security, Cloud Operations, and the ASV account owner. It is updated after every quarterly external ASV scan and after any significant change scan, using the official ASV scan report, ASV portal, vulnerability management platform, change management system, and controlled evidence repository as source systems.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this penetration test log entry, using format PT-YYYY-NNN, for example PT-2026-001. |
| PCI DSS Requirement Reference | Enter the applicable PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement reference(s), using values such as 11.4.1, 11.4.2, 11.4.3, 11.4.4, and where applicable 11.4.5. |
| Test Type | Select the type of test performed: External Network Penetration Test, Internal Network Penetration Test, Application Penetration Test, Segmentation Penetration Test, Combined Network/Application Penetration Test, or Retest. |
| Test Scope | Describe the scope category covered by the report, for example CDE, connected-to systems, security-impacting systems, public-facing systems, segmentation boundary, or specific application estate. |
| CDE / Segmentation Relevance | State how the test relates to the cardholder data environment, using one of: CDE In Scope, Connected-to CDE, Could Impact CDE Security, Segmentation Boundary, Out-of-Scope Validation. |
| Test Trigger | Select why the test was performed: Annual Scheduled Test, Significant Change, Segmentation Validation, Remediation Retest, Service Provider Six-Month Segmentation Test, or Other. |
| Required Test Frequency | Enter the applicable frequency requirement, for example Annually, After Significant Change, At Least Every 12 Months for Segmentation, or Every 6 Months for Service Provider Segmentation where applicable. |
| Testing Period Start Date | Enter the first date testing activity occurred, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Testing Period End Date | Enter the final date testing activity occurred, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Report Issue Date | Enter the date the final penetration test report was issued, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Test Due Date | Enter the latest date by which the next required penetration test must be completed, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Significant Change Reference | If the test was triggered by a significant change, enter the change ticket or project reference; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Penetration Testing Methodology Used | Enter the methodology or standard followed, for example PCI DSS penetration testing methodology, NIST SP 800-115, PTES, OWASP Testing Guide, OSSTMM, or internal approved methodology reference. |
| Methodology Covers PCI DSS 11.4.1 Elements | Confirm whether the methodology addresses the PCI DSS-required elements, including industry-accepted approaches, CDE perimeter and critical systems, testing from inside and outside the network, application and network-layer testing, segmentation validation where used, and retention of results; use Yes, No, or Partially with explanation in Notes. |
| Tester Organisation | Enter the legal name of the external testing company or internal team that performed the test. |
| Tester Type | Select External Third Party, Internal Independent Tester, or Internal Security Team; internal testers must be organizationally independent from the systems being tested. |
| Tester Independence / Qualification Evidence | Record the evidence proving tester competence and independence, such as contract/SOW reference, certifications, CV reference, assessor approval, internal independence attestation, or procurement record. |
| Lead Tester Name | Enter the full name of the lead penetration tester responsible for the report. |
| Report Title / Reference | Enter the exact title, version, and reference number of the penetration test report. |
| Report Storage Location | Enter the controlled repository path, GRC record link, document management URL, or evidence vault reference where the final report and supporting evidence are stored. |
| In-Scope Systems / Applications / Networks | List the specific IP ranges, hostnames, URLs, APIs, applications, cloud accounts, VLANs, network zones, or system groups tested; use a controlled attachment if the list is long. |
| Out-of-Scope Exclusions and Rationale | List any exclusions from testing and the business or technical rationale; enter None if there were no exclusions. |
| Segmentation Boundaries Tested | Where segmentation is used to reduce PCI DSS scope, identify the specific firewalls, VLANs, ACLs, cloud security groups, routing boundaries, zero-trust controls, or other segmentation mechanisms tested; enter N/A if segmentation is not used. |
| Testing Included External Perimeter | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether testing included externally exposed systems and services. |
| Testing Included Internal Network | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether testing included internal network testing from inside the environment. |
| Testing Included Application Layer | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether testing included application-layer attacks such as authentication, session management, input validation, authorization, API, and business logic testing. |
| Testing Included Network Layer | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether testing included network-layer testing such as port/service enumeration, vulnerability exploitation, lateral movement attempts, and protocol/service weakness testing. |
| Testing Included CDE Access Paths | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether testing assessed paths into the CDE from external, internal, connected, or less-trusted networks. |
| Testing Included Cardholder Data Discovery / Validation | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether testing validated whether cardholder data could be accessed, discovered, or exfiltrated through the tested paths, without recording sensitive authentication data or live PAN unnecessarily. |
| Testing Included Exploitation Attempt | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the test attempted controlled exploitation of identified vulnerabilities, consistent with the approved rules of engagement. |
| Critical Findings Count | Enter the number of critical-severity findings in the final report as a non-negative integer. |
| High Findings Count | Enter the number of high-severity findings in the final report as a non-negative integer. |
| Medium Findings Count | Enter the number of medium-severity findings in the final report as a non-negative integer. |
| Low Findings Count | Enter the number of low-severity findings in the final report as a non-negative integer. |
| Informational Findings Count | Enter the number of informational findings in the final report as a non-negative integer. |
| Exploitable Vulnerabilities Identified | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the test identified vulnerabilities that were exploitable or could result in unauthorized access to the CDE, cardholder data, or security-impacting systems. |
| Segmentation Control Failures Identified | Enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether segmentation testing found a way to bypass segmentation or access the CDE from an untrusted or out-of-scope network. |
| Overall Test Result | Select Pass, Pass with Findings, Fail, or Retest Pending based on whether exploitable vulnerabilities and segmentation failures were resolved and validated. |
| Remediation Plan Reference | Enter the remediation plan, risk treatment plan, vulnerability ticket, or project reference used to track correction of findings; enter N/A if no findings required remediation. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the role or named owner accountable for remediation, for example Network Engineering Manager, Application Owner, Cloud Platform Owner, or Vulnerability Management Lead. |
| Target Remediation Completion Date | Enter the planned completion date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Actual Remediation Completion Date | Enter the actual date all required remediation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not yet complete or not required. |
| Retest Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether retesting is required to verify remediation of exploitable vulnerabilities or segmentation failures. |
| Retest Completion Date | Enter the date remediation retesting was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if retesting is not required or not yet completed. |
| Retest Report Reference | Enter the retest report title, version, ticket, or evidence reference confirming retest results; enter N/A if no retest is required. |
| Retest Result | Select Passed, Failed, Partially Passed, Not Performed, or N/A. |
| Residual Risk / Exception Reference | If any finding remains unresolved or risk is accepted, enter the approved risk acceptance or exception reference; enter N/A if there is no residual accepted risk. |
| Management Acceptance Date | Enter the date management approved closure, residual risk, or exception in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Evidence Package Complete | Enter Yes or No to confirm the evidence package contains the final report, scope, rules of engagement, methodology, tester qualification/independence evidence, findings, remediation evidence, and retest evidence where applicable. |
| Reviewer / Approver | Enter the name and role of the person who reviewed and approved the log entry and evidence package. |
| Approval Date | Enter the date the record was reviewed and approved in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record Status | Select Draft, In Progress, Awaiting Remediation, Awaiting Retest, Complete, Exception Approved, or Archived. |
| Notes | Enter concise additional context needed for audit understanding, such as methodology limitations, compensating context, links to attachments, or explanation of Partially/No responses. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the PCI Compliance Manager with operational input from Vulnerability Management, Application Security, Network Security, and system/application owners. Update this log after each penetration test, segmentation test, significant change-triggered test, remediation action, and retest; source data comes from final penetration test reports, rules of engagement, GRC evidence repository, vulnerability management platform, change management system, and remediation ticketing system.

PCI-030.title: Application-Layer Vuln Detection (WAF)
PCI-030.content:
## What This Evidences

This record evidences that an automated technical solution, such as a web application firewall or equivalent application-layer protection tool, is deployed and actively detecting application-layer attacks against public-facing web applications, supporting PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 6.4.2.

This evidence is collected from operational systems and must not be authored manually. The required artifact is the actual log export, report, dashboard snapshot, or PDF generated from the organisation’s own WAF, SIEM, log management platform, or security monitoring tool.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect the evidence from the authoritative system that records application-layer attack detection events, typically one of the following:

- WAF management console: `[WAF platform name]`
- Cloud WAF portal: `[cloud provider/security service name]`
- SIEM or log store: `[SIEM/log platform name]`
- Security analytics dashboard: `[security monitoring platform name]`
- Managed security provider portal: `[MSSP portal name]`

Use the system that receives and retains the live WAF detection logs for the in-scope public-facing web applications handling or protecting cardholder data.

## How To Collect

1. Log in to `[WAF/SIEM/log platform name]` using an account with read-only reporting or security monitoring access.
2. Select the environment or tenant covering PCI in-scope public-facing applications: `[application names / URLs / zones]`.
3. Set the reporting period to the required evidence window, such as `[start date]` to `[end date]`.
4. Filter logs for application-layer detection or blocking events, such as:
 - SQL injection
 - Cross-site scripting
 - Remote file inclusion
 - Local file inclusion
 - Command injection
 - Path traversal
 - Protocol or HTTP anomaly detection
 - Known malicious payload signatures
5. Confirm the records show the WAF or automated solution was active during the period.
6. Export the results in PDF, CSV, JSON, or native report format, depending on auditor request. For this artifact, retain the Logs/PDF output where available.
7. If using a dashboard, export the dashboard/report directly rather than creating a manual summary.
8. Save the file using a clear name, for example: `WAF_AppLayer_Detection_[system]_[YYYY-MM-DD_to_YYYY-MM-DD].pdf`.
9. Record the evidence collection details in `[evidence tracker / GRC platform / audit workspace]`.

## What To Capture

The evidence should include enough detail to prove automated application-layer detection is operating. Capture:

- WAF or automated security tool name
- Protected application, hostname, URL, or zone
- Event timestamp and time zone
- Detection rule, signature, managed rule set, or policy name
- Attack or threat category
- Action taken, such as detected, challenged, blocked, logged, or alerted
- Source IP address or anonymised source identifier, if required by policy
- Destination host, application, or service
- HTTP method and request path, where available
- Severity, confidence, or risk rating
- Event count or individual event records
- Policy status showing enabled/enforcing mode
- Reporting period covered
- Export timestamp or report generation date
- Name of dashboard/report or query used

Where sensitive payload data is present, redact only the minimum required while preserving proof of detection and action.

## Frequency & Owner

- Frequency: Collect at least quarterly, and additionally before PCI DSS assessment activities or after major WAF policy changes.
- Owner: `[Security Operations team / Application Security team / Network Security team]`
- Evidence custodian: `[GRC/audit owner name or role]`
- Technical approver: `[WAF service owner / Security Engineering lead]`

## Retention & Storage

Store the exported evidence in `[GRC repository / audit evidence vault / secure document repository]` with access restricted to authorised security, compliance, and audit personnel.

Retain evidence in line with the organisation’s PCI evidence retention period, typically at least one year unless a longer internal or contractual requirement applies. Preserve the original exported file and avoid editing it. If redaction is necessary, retain both the original restricted-access export and the redacted audit copy where permitted.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence when it shows:

- It was exported from an authoritative WAF, SIEM, log store, or managed security portal
- The reporting period is clearly visible
- The protected public-facing application or environment is identifiable
- Application-layer attack categories are detected by an automated technical solution
- The WAF or equivalent control is enabled for relevant in-scope applications
- Events include timestamps, rule or attack type, affected application, and action taken
- The evidence is system-generated, not manually written
- The export is complete, readable, and traceable to `[WAF/SIEM/log platform name]`
- The evidence date aligns with the assessment period
- Any redactions do not remove the information needed to confirm automated detection is operating

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique inventory identifier for this script record, e.g. PSI-0001; one row per script per payment page/environment where the script is loaded. |
| Payment Page Identifier | Enter the internal name or ID of the payment page where the script executes, e.g. Checkout Payment Form, Hosted Payment iFrame Wrapper, Card Capture Page. |
| Payment Page URL or Route | Enter the exact production or non-production URL, route, or application path where the script is present; mask sensitive query strings if necessary. |
| Environment | Enter one allowed value: Production, Staging, Test, Development, DR. |
| Script Name | Enter the human-readable script name or filename, e.g. payment-widget.js, analytics-loader.js, fraud-check.js. |
| Script Type | Enter one allowed value: Inline, Local Hosted, Third-Party Hosted, Tag Manager Injected, Framework Bundle, Other. |
| Script Source | Enter how the script is introduced to the page, e.g. HTML template, React build, tag manager container, CMS plugin, third-party checkout integration. |
| Script URL or Path | Enter the full external URL or internal path from which the script is loaded; for inline scripts enter Inline and identify the template/component name. |
| Script Host Domain | Enter the domain hosting the script, e.g. static.example.com or cdn.provider.com; for inline scripts enter Internal Inline. |
| First-Party or Third-Party | Enter one allowed value: First-Party, Third-Party. |
| Third-Party Provider | If third-party, enter the provider/vendor legal or service name; if first-party enter N/A. |
| Business Justification | Enter the specific business or technical reason the script is necessary on the payment page, sufficient to support PCI DSS 6.4.3 justification requirements. |
| Data Access or Function on Payment Page | Describe what the script can do or access on the payment page, e.g. renders payment fields, fraud scoring, address lookup, analytics only, no access to cardholder data fields. |
| Script Owner | Enter the accountable internal owner role or team responsible for the script, e.g. Payments Engineering, Digital Marketing, Fraud Operations. |
| Approving Business Owner | Enter the name or role of the business approver who authorized the script to be present on the payment page. |
| Approving Security Owner | Enter the name or role of the security approver who reviewed the script for payment page use. |
| Authorization Status | Enter one allowed value: Authorized, Pending Authorization, Not Authorized, Retired. |
| Authorization Reference | Enter the change ticket, risk review, CAB approval, vendor onboarding record, or other approval reference proving authorization. |
| Authorization Date | Enter the date the script was authorized for use on the payment page in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Expected Script Version | Enter the approved script version, build number, release tag, or vendor version expected to be loaded; enter N/A only where the provider does not expose versions and document this in Comments. |
| Expected Cryptographic Hash | Enter the approved cryptographic hash of the script content used for integrity validation; use lowercase hex or base64 as produced by the monitoring tool. |
| Hash Algorithm | Enter the algorithm used for the expected hash, e.g. SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512. |
| Subresource Integrity Implemented | Enter one allowed value: Yes, No, Not Applicable; use Not Applicable only where SRI cannot technically apply, such as inline scripts or dynamically generated scripts. |
| Expected SRI Value | Enter the expected SRI attribute value, e.g. sha384-..., or N/A if SRI is not implemented or not applicable. |
| Content Security Policy Coverage | Enter one allowed value: Covered, Partially Covered, Not Covered, Not Applicable to indicate whether CSP restricts this script source on the payment page. |
| Allowed CSP Directive | Enter the applicable CSP directive and allowed source expression, e.g. script-src 'self' https://cdn.provider.com; enter N/A if not covered. |
| Change Detection Coverage | Enter one allowed value: Monitored, Not Monitored, Excluded; any Excluded entry must have documented justification in Comments and risk acceptance if applicable. |
| Integrity Monitoring Tool | Enter the tool, service, or process used to detect unauthorized changes to script content, script location, payment page HTTP headers, or payment page content, e.g. file integrity monitoring, CSP monitoring, synthetic browser monitor, payment page change detection tool. |
| Monitoring Frequency | Enter the frequency of integrity/change checks, e.g. Continuous, Daily, Weekly; ensure it meets PCI DSS 11.6.1 timing expectations and the entity-defined targeted risk analysis where applicable. |
| Last Integrity Check Date | Enter the most recent date this script or payment page was checked by the monitoring process in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Integrity Check Result | Enter one allowed value: Pass, Fail, Warning, Not Yet Checked. |
| Last Detected Change Date | Enter the date an actual script, header, or payment page content change was last detected in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if none detected. |
| Change Authorized | Enter one allowed value for the last detected change: Yes, No, Under Review, N/A. |
| Change Ticket or Approval Reference | Enter the change ticket, deployment record, CAB approval, vendor notice, or incident record associated with the last detected change; enter N/A if no change. |
| Alert Generated | Enter one allowed value: Yes, No, N/A to indicate whether monitoring generated an alert for the last detected change or integrity failure. |
| Alert Reference | Enter the SIEM alert ID, monitoring alert ID, incident ticket, or notification reference; enter N/A if no alert. |
| Investigation Status | Enter one allowed value: Not Started, In Progress, Authorized Change Confirmed, Unauthorized Change Confirmed, False Positive, Closed, N/A. |
| Remediation Action | Enter the action taken or planned for failed integrity checks or unauthorized/unexpected changes, e.g. removed script, reverted version, updated approved hash, blocked domain in CSP; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target remediation date in YYYY-MM-DD format for open issues; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Completion Date | Enter the actual completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not completed or not applicable. |
| Residual Risk Accepted | Enter one allowed value: Yes, No, N/A to show whether any remaining risk related to the script or monitoring exception has been formally accepted. |
| Risk Acceptance Reference | Enter the formal risk acceptance ID, approver, and expiry reference where residual risk is accepted; enter N/A otherwise. |
| PCI DSS Requirement Mapping | Enter the applicable PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement references, normally 6.4.3 and/or 11.6.1; include both where the row supports script authorization/inventory and integrity monitoring. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the repository path, GRC record link, monitoring dashboard link, change ticket link, or evidence folder where supporting evidence is stored. |
| Last Reviewed Date | Enter the date this inventory record was last reviewed for accuracy in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Due Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format based on the organisation's review cadence. |
| Record Status | Enter one allowed value: Active, Pending, Retired, Exception. |
| Comments | Enter any additional context needed for auditability, such as technical limitations, vendor constraints, dynamic script behaviour, tag manager notes, or reasons for N/A values. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Payments Application Owner with review and approval by Application Security/GRC. Update whenever payment page scripts, tag manager configurations, CSP rules, script hashes, vendors, or monitoring results change, and formally review at least monthly using sources such as code repositories, CI/CD deployment records, tag manager exports, CSP configuration, payment page integrity monitoring tools, SIEM alerts, and change management tickets.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Inventory ID | Enter a unique identifier for this inventory item, using a consistent format such as TKI-0001. |
| In PCI DSS Scope | Enter Yes or No to confirm whether this key/certificate protects or supports transmission of PAN or is otherwise in scope for PCI DSS Req 4.2.1.1. |
| Environment | Enter the environment where the key/certificate is used; allowed values: Production, Pre-Production, Test, Development, DR, Other. |
| System/Application Name | Enter the name of the system, application, appliance, service, API gateway, load balancer, payment platform, or other component using this key/certificate. |
| Business Service | Enter the business service supported, such as e-commerce checkout, payment gateway, call-centre payments, issuer connection, acquirer connection, or tokenisation service. |
| Data Flow / Connection Name | Enter the name or description of the PAN-bearing transmission path protected by this key/certificate, matching the organisation’s PCI data-flow diagrams where possible. |
| PAN Transmission Channel | Enter the channel over which PAN is transmitted; examples include Internet, private WAN, VPN, API, batch file transfer, payment processor link, internal service-to-service connection. |
| Protocol / Service | Enter the protocol or service using the key/certificate, such as TLS HTTPS, mTLS API, SFTP, FTPS, IPsec VPN, TLS SMTP, MQ TLS, database TLS. |
| Endpoint / Hostname / FQDN | Enter the fully qualified domain name, hostname, virtual service name, or endpoint where the certificate/key is presented or trusted. |
| IP Address / Port | Enter the IP address and port in the format x.x.x.x:port or hostname:port; list multiple values separated by semicolons. |
| Key or Certificate Type | Enter the type; allowed values: Server Certificate, Client Certificate, Mutual TLS Certificate, Intermediate CA Certificate, Root CA Certificate, SSH Host Key, SSH User Key, IPsec/IKE Certificate, Other. |
| Certificate Common Name (CN) | Enter the certificate Subject Common Name exactly as shown in the certificate; enter N/A for non-certificate keys. |
| Subject Alternative Names (SANs) | Enter all SAN DNS names/IPs exactly as shown in the certificate, separated by semicolons; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Issuer / Certificate Authority | Enter the issuing CA name exactly as shown in the certificate, or the authority/source that issued or generated the trusted key. |
| CA Trust Type | Enter the trust model; allowed values: Public CA, Internal Enterprise CA, Partner CA, Self-Signed, Vendor-Managed, Other. |
| Certificate Serial Number | Enter the certificate serial number exactly as shown by the certificate management tool; enter N/A for non-certificate keys. |
| Certificate Fingerprint | Enter the SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate or trusted key in colon-separated hexadecimal format where available; do not use MD5/SHA-1 fingerprints as the primary identifier. |
| Key Algorithm | Enter the algorithm used; examples: RSA, ECDSA, Ed25519, DSA, DH, ECDH. Flag deprecated algorithms in the weak cryptography column. |
| Key Length / Curve | Enter the key size or curve, such as 2048-bit, 3072-bit, 4096-bit, P-256, P-384, Ed25519. |
| Signature Algorithm | Enter the signature algorithm exactly as shown, such as SHA256withRSA, SHA384withECDSA; identify SHA-1 or weaker as deprecated. |
| TLS / Cryptographic Protocol Version | Enter the enabled protocol version(s) used for this connection, such as TLS 1.2, TLS 1.3, SSH-2, IPsec/IKEv2; do not simply enter SSL/TLS. |
| Use / Purpose | Enter the precise purpose, such as encrypts PAN in transit to processor, authenticates client system using mTLS, validates partner server certificate, or protects SFTP batch PAN files. |
| Protects PAN in Transit | Enter Yes only if the key/certificate is used to protect, authenticate, or establish encryption for PAN transmitted over open, public, or internal networks; otherwise enter No and justify in Notes. |
| Certificate Valid From | Enter the certificate validity start date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A for non-certificate keys. |
| Certificate Expiry Date | Enter the certificate expiry date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A only for non-expiring keys and justify in Notes. |
| Expiry RAG Status | Enter Green, Amber, Red, or N/A. Suggested criteria: Green = more than 60 days to expiry, Amber = 30-60 days, Red = less than 30 days or expired, N/A = no expiry date. |
| Private Key Location | Enter where the private key is stored, such as HSM name, KMS vault, certificate manager, appliance keystore, server path, cloud secret store; do not record private key material. |
| Private Key Protection Method | Enter how the private key is protected, such as HSM non-exportable, KMS access policy, encrypted keystore, TPM, passphrase-protected file, restricted OS permissions. |
| Key Custodian / Technical Owner | Enter the named team or role responsible for technical custody, renewal, secure storage, and configuration of the key/certificate. |
| Business Owner | Enter the business owner accountable for the service or data flow protected by this key/certificate. |
| Certificate Lifecycle Status | Enter the current status; allowed values: Planned, Active, Pending Renewal, Renewed Pending Deployment, Retired, Revoked, Expired, Unknown. |
| Approved by Security | Enter Yes, No, or Pending to indicate whether Security/InfoSec has approved the cryptographic configuration and trust relationship. |
| Weak / Deprecated Cryptography Present | Enter Yes or No based on whether SSL, early TLS where not permitted, weak ciphers, SHA-1, RSA below approved organisational minimums, self-signed unapproved certs, expired certs, or other insecure configurations are present. |
| Compensating or Remediation Reference | Enter the ticket, risk acceptance, compensating control, or remediation plan reference if weak/deprecated cryptography or non-compliance exists; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Rotation / Renewal Frequency | Enter the planned renewal or rotation interval, such as annually, every 398 days, every 90 days, every 2 years, on compromise, or per CA policy. |
| Last Reviewed Date | Enter the date this inventory item was last reviewed for accuracy and compliance in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Vulnerability / Configuration Validation Date | Enter the most recent date the endpoint or key/certificate configuration was validated by scan, certificate management tool, manual inspection, or configuration review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Validation Method | Enter how the details were validated, such as certificate management export, TLS scanner, vulnerability scan, CMDB reconciliation, cloud certificate inventory, HSM/KMS report, manual OpenSSL check. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the repository path, GRC record, ticket, scan report link, certificate management record, or other location of evidence supporting the entry. |
| Notes | Enter any relevant context, exceptions, dependencies, migration details, or explanation for N/A values; do not store secrets, passphrases, or private key material. |

Source systems should include the certificate management platform, CMDB, cloud certificate/KMS inventories, HSM/KMS reports, vulnerability/TLS scan results, firewall/load-balancer inventories, managed file transfer platforms, and PCI data-flow diagrams.

## Access Review Records (XLSX template)

| [EXAMPLE: AR-2026-Q1-DB01] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-01] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-31] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-06] | [EXAMPLE: 7.2.5.1] | [EXAMPLE: Cardholder Database DB01] | [EXAMPLE: Raj Patel, Database Owner] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Service Account] | [EXAMPLE: svc_payapp_db] | [EXAMPLE: Payment App Database Service Account] | [EXAMPLE: Raj Patel] | [EXAMPLE: Platform Engineering] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable for System Account] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: db_datareader, db_datawriter] | [EXAMPLE: Allows payment application to read and write required transaction records] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-31] | [EXAMPLE: Required for application-to-database connectivity for payment processing] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Elena Garcia] | [EXAMPLE: System Owner] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Retain] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: DB-ACCESS-REVIEW-Q1-2026] | [EXAMPLE: Service account ownership and purpose validated] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Review Cycle ID | Enter a unique identifier for this access review cycle, e.g. AR-YYYY-QN-SYSTEM or AR-YYYY-MM-SYSTEM. |
| Review Period Start Date | Enter the first date covered by the review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Period End Date | Enter the last date covered by the review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the reviewer performed the access review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| PCI DSS Requirement Reference | Enter the applicable PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement reference; allowed values: 7.2.4, 7.2.5.1, or 7.2.4 / 7.2.5.1. |
| System/Application/Repository Name | Enter the exact name of the system, application, database, directory, cloud platform, security tool, or repository where the account/access exists. |
| System Owner | Enter the named business or technical owner accountable for the system/application. |
| In PCI DSS Scope | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the system or account is in scope for the cardholder data environment or can affect its security. |
| Account Type | Enter one of: Human User, Administrator, Shared/Generic, Service Account, Application Account, System Account, API Account, Database Account, Emergency/Break-Glass. |
| Account/User ID | Enter the unique account identifier exactly as shown in the source system, such as username, account ID, service account name, or API principal. |
| Account Display Name or Service Name | Enter the person's full name for human accounts or the service/application name for non-human accounts. |
| Account Owner | Enter the responsible person for the account; for human accounts this is the user or manager, and for system/service accounts this is the named technical owner. |
| Department/Team | Enter the department, function, or team responsible for the account, e.g. Finance, IT Operations, DevOps, Security Operations. |
| Employment or Account Status | Enter one of: Active, Terminated, Transferred, Contractor Active, Contractor Ended, Dormant, Disabled, Unknown, Not Applicable for System Account. |
| Privileged Access | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the account has elevated, administrative, root, security administration, database administrator, or other high-risk privileges. |
| Current Role/Profile/Group Memberships | List the roles, profiles, AD groups, IAM groups, database roles, application roles, or permission sets currently assigned to the account. |
| Current Access Privileges Description | Describe what the assigned access allows the account to do, focusing on CDE/security-impacting functions such as view cardholder data, modify configurations, administer users, deploy code, access logs, or process transactions. |
| Access Last Used Date | Enter the most recent date the account or privilege was used, if available, in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Available if the source system does not provide this. |
| Business Need / Justification | Enter the current business, operational, or technical reason why the access is required; for system accounts include the application/process dependency. |
| Least Privilege Appropriate | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the current access is limited to only what is required for the user's job function or the system account's purpose. |
| Reviewer Name | Enter the full name of the person who reviewed and approved/rejected the access. |
| Reviewer Role | Enter the reviewer's role, such as Line Manager, System Owner, Application Owner, Data Owner, IAM Owner, or Security Manager. |
| Reviewer Independent of Account Owner | Enter Yes or No to confirm whether the reviewer is different from the account owner/user and has sufficient authority to validate the access. |
| Review Decision | Enter one of: Retain, Modify, Remove, Disable, Investigate, Exception Approved. |
| Required Remediation Action | If the decision is Modify, Remove, Disable, or Investigate, describe the exact action required; enter None if the decision is Retain. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the person or team responsible for completing the remediation action; enter Not Applicable if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target completion date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Applicable if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Completion Date | Enter the actual completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format once completed; leave blank until completed or enter Not Applicable if no remediation is required. |
| Post-Remediation Status | Enter one of: Open, Completed, Overdue, Risk Accepted, Not Applicable. |
| Evidence Reference | Enter the ticket number, workflow ID, screenshot filename, report name, access review campaign ID, or repository link proving review and/or remediation completion. |
| Comments / Exceptions | Enter any relevant notes, exception rationale, compensating controls, unresolved issues, or management-approved deviations. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the IAM/Access Governance owner with review input from system owners, application owners, and data owners; updated for each periodic access review cycle and whenever scoped systems or account types change. Source data should be exported from authoritative IAM, directory services, privileged access management, application, database, cloud IAM, ticketing, and access review workflow systems.

PCI-035.title: Daily Log Review Evidence
PCI-035.content:
## What This Evidences

Daily Log Review Evidence demonstrates that the organisation reviews audit logs every day to identify suspicious activity, anomalies, security events, and potential compromise affecting the cardholder data environment (CDE) and connected systems. This supports PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 10.4.1, which expects audit logs for relevant system components to be reviewed at least daily.

This evidence is **collected, not authored**. Do not create a manual narrative claiming the review occurred. Collect the actual report, dashboard export, SIEM search result, alert queue, ticket, or workflow record from the organisation’s logging, monitoring, or service management systems.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect the evidence from the system used to perform and record daily log reviews, such as:

- SIEM or central log management platform: `[SIEM/log platform name]`
- Security operations platform or alert console: `[SOC tool name]`
- ITSM or ticketing system used to track daily reviews: `[ITSM/ticketing tool name]`
- Managed security provider portal: `[MSSP portal name]`
- Cloud security/logging console: `[cloud logging tool name]`
- Database, firewall, endpoint, identity, or payment application monitoring dashboard: `[tool/system name]`

The preferred source is the central SIEM or log management system covering all in-scope CDE systems and connected security components.

## How To Collect

1. Log in to `[SIEM/log platform name]` or `[review tracking system name]` using an account assigned to the log review role.
2. Navigate to the saved daily review dashboard, report, or query: `[daily log review dashboard/report name]`.
3. Set the date range to the required review day, for example `[YYYY-MM-DD 00:00 to 23:59, timezone]`.
4. Filter scope to in-scope CDE systems and security components, such as:
 - Payment applications
 - Databases storing or processing cardholder data
 - Domain controllers and identity systems
 - Firewalls, IDS/IPS, WAF, VPN, and network security devices
 - Endpoint protection and EDR systems
 - Cloud platforms supporting the CDE
5. Run or open the daily review report.
6. Confirm that events were reviewed, including authentication activity, privileged activity, failed access attempts, account changes, security alerts, and system errors relevant to the CDE.
7. Export the report as PDF, CSV, or native platform export where possible.
8. If the review is tracked in tickets, export or save the corresponding ticket showing reviewer action, timestamp, status, and outcome.
9. Save screenshots only where export is unavailable. Ensure the screenshot includes the tool name, date range, filters, reviewer/action status, and timestamp.
10. Store the collected evidence in `[evidence repository name/path]` using the naming format: `Daily_Log_Review_[YYYY-MM-DD]_[System/Scope]`.

## What To Capture

Evidence should include:

- Review date and time period covered
- Date and time the review was completed
- Reviewer name or user ID
- Source system name, such as `[SIEM/log platform name]`
- CDE scope or asset group reviewed
- Event categories reviewed, including:
 - Failed login attempts
 - Privileged user activity
 - Administrative changes
 - Security alerts
 - Malware or EDR alerts
 - Firewall, IDS/IPS, WAF, or VPN events
 - Changes to accounts, permissions, or logging settings
- Exceptions, alerts, or anomalies identified
- Investigation or escalation outcome
- Linked incident or ticket numbers, where applicable
- Evidence that no material alerts were found, if applicable
- Timestamped approval, closure, or review completion record

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Daily, including weekends and holidays, unless covered by a documented managed service arrangement.
- **Primary owner:** `[SOC team / Security Operations / Information Security team]`
- **Backup owner:** `[on-call analyst / IT Operations / MSSP]`
- **Escalation owner:** `[Security Manager / Incident Response Lead]`

## Retention & Storage

Store collected evidence in `[GRC/evidence repository name]` or `[secure shared evidence location]`.

Retention should meet the organisation’s PCI DSS evidence retention requirements and internal log retention policy. At minimum, retain evidence long enough to support current assessment activities and demonstrate consistent daily operation over the required testing period.

Access to stored evidence should be restricted to authorised security, compliance, and audit personnel. Do not alter exported logs or reports after collection.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will typically accept the evidence if it shows:

- The review was performed daily for the selected sample dates
- The review covered in-scope CDE systems and relevant security components
- The evidence came from an operational system, not a manually created assertion
- The date range reviewed is clear and complete
- The reviewer or responsible team is identifiable
- The review completion timestamp is visible
- Exceptions or alerts were investigated, escalated, or closed with documented outcomes
- Evidence is retained in a controlled repository and can be traced back to the source system
- Sampling across multiple days shows the process is consistently performed, not only prepared for audit purposes

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| POI Device Inventory ID | Enter the organisation-assigned unique identifier for this POI device record; use a stable ID that does not change when the device is moved, for example POI-000123. |
| Device Type | Enter the type of payment device; allowed values: Countertop Terminal, Mobile Terminal, PIN Pad, Unattended Payment Terminal, Kiosk Payment Device, Integrated POS Payment Device, Other. |
| Manufacturer | Enter the device manufacturer exactly as shown on procurement records or the device label, for example Ingenico, Verifone, PAX. |
| Model | Enter the exact manufacturer model name or number as shown on the device label or approved device list. |
| Serial Number | Enter the manufacturer serial number exactly as printed on the device; this must be unique for each physical device. |
| Organisation Asset Tag | Enter the internal asset tag or barcode assigned by the organisation; enter N/A only if no internal asset tagging is used. |
| Acquirer or Processor Terminal ID | Enter the terminal ID assigned by the acquirer, processor, or payment service provider; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Merchant ID | Enter the merchant ID associated with the device or site; enter N/A if not applicable or if managed centrally. |
| Physical Location | Enter the full site or premises where the device is deployed, including site name, address, city, and country. |
| Location Detail | Enter the precise placement of the device within the site, such as Store 012 / Lane 03 / Front Counter Left; must be specific enough for an inspector to locate the device. |
| Business Unit or Site Owner | Enter the business unit, department, store, branch, or site accountable for the device. |
| Device Custodian | Enter the named person or role responsible for day-to-day physical oversight of the device, for example Store Manager or Front Desk Supervisor. |
| Inventory Status | Enter the current lifecycle status; allowed values: In Service, In Storage, In Transit, Under Repair, Retired, Lost, Stolen, Disposed. |
| Date Added to Inventory | Enter the date the device was first recorded in the POI inventory in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Date Removed from Inventory | Enter the date the device was removed from active inventory in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank while the device remains active or in storage. |
| Removal or Replacement Reference | Enter the change record, disposal certificate, RMA, incident, or replacement ticket reference if the device was removed, replaced, lost, stolen, or disposed; leave blank if not applicable. |
| Approved Device Baseline Reference | Enter the reference to the approved baseline used for inspection, such as photo set, seal number record, approved configuration record, or device acceptance record. |
| Inspection Frequency | Enter the required inspection interval for this device; allowed values: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Before Each Use, After Relocation, Other - Specify. |
| Inspection Due Date | Enter the next scheduled inspection due date in YYYY-MM-DD format, calculated according to the defined inspection frequency and risk profile. |
| Inspection Date | Enter the actual date the physical tamper/substitution inspection was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Inspector Name | Enter the full name of the person who performed the inspection. |
| Inspector Role or Team | Enter the inspector's role, team, or function, for example Store Manager, Facilities, IT Support, Security Operations. |
| Device Present at Expected Location | Record whether the device was physically present at the inventory location; allowed values: Yes, No, N/A. |
| Serial Number Verified | Record whether the serial number on the device matched the inventory record; allowed values: Yes, No, N/A. |
| Asset Tag Verified | Record whether the organisation asset tag matched the inventory record and was intact; allowed values: Yes, No, N/A. |
| Device Appearance Matches Baseline | Record whether the device visually matched the approved baseline, including colour, shape, labels, logos, and visible components; allowed values: Yes, No, N/A. |
| Tamper-Evident Seal Status | Record the status of seals or security labels; allowed values: Intact, Broken, Missing, Not Used, N/A. |
| Casing and Keypad Condition | Record whether the casing, screws, seams, display, and keypad showed no signs of damage or tampering; allowed values: OK, Concern, N/A. |
| Card Reader or Contactless Interface Condition | Record whether card slot, chip reader, magstripe reader, and contactless area showed no overlays, skimmers, blockers, damage, or misalignment; allowed values: OK, Concern, N/A. |
| Cables and Connections Condition | Record whether cables, ports, power supplies, network connections, and connected peripherals were expected and undisturbed; allowed values: OK, Concern, N/A. |
| Unexpected Attachments or Overlays Present | Record whether any unapproved attachment, overlay, camera, skimmer, extra cable, or foreign object was found; allowed values: No, Yes, N/A. |
| Device Behaviour Check Result | Record whether device operation appeared normal, including startup, display, prompts, transaction readiness, and error messages; allowed values: Normal, Abnormal, Not Tested, N/A. |
| Inspection Result | Enter the overall inspection outcome; allowed values: Pass, Fail, Not Inspected. |
| Tamper or Substitution Indicators Observed | Describe any suspected tampering, substitution, missing device, serial mismatch, broken seal, overlay, unexpected cable, abnormal behaviour, or other concern; enter None if no indicators were observed. |
| Incident or Ticket Reference | Enter the security incident, service desk, investigation, or change ticket reference raised for any failed inspection or anomaly; enter N/A if no issue was identified. |
| Immediate Action Taken | Enter the immediate action performed when an issue was identified, such as Device removed from service, Payment processing stopped, Security notified, Replacement requested; enter None if no action was required. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the named person, role, or team responsible for resolving any failed inspection finding; enter N/A if the inspection passed. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target date for resolving the finding in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Remediation Closure Date | Enter the date the finding was verified as remediated in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until closure or enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Evidence Reference | Enter the file path, GRC record ID, ticket attachment ID, inspection photo reference, signed checklist reference, or other evidence location supporting the inventory or inspection entry. |
| Record Last Updated | Enter the date this row was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Updated By | Enter the full name or user ID of the person who last updated this row. |

### Maintenance

The POI Device Inventory & Inspection Log is owned by the Payment Operations or Retail Operations control owner, with oversight from Information Security/GRC. It is updated whenever a POI device is added, moved, replaced, inspected, repaired, retired, lost, or disposed, and at least at each required inspection interval using source data from asset management, acquirer/processor terminal records, site registers, service desk tickets, and physical inspection evidence.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| TPSP ID | Enter a unique internal identifier for the third-party service provider, using a consistent format such as TPSP-001. |
| TPSP Legal Name | Enter the full legal entity name of the third-party service provider as shown in the signed agreement. |
| Trading Name / Service Name | Enter the trading name, product name, platform name, or service name used by the organisation, if different from the legal name. |
| TPSP Type | Select the provider category, such as Payment Gateway, Acquirer, Processor, Hosting Provider, Managed Service Provider, Cloud Service Provider, Call Centre, Software Provider, Support Provider, Tokenisation Provider, Storage Provider, or Other. |
| Service Description | Briefly describe the service provided and how it relates to payment processing, account data, or the cardholder data environment. |
| PCI Relevance | Select one: Stores Account Data, Processes Account Data, Transmits Account Data, Can Impact CDE Security, Could Affect PCI DSS Compliance, or Not PCI-Relevant. |
| Account Data Involvement | Select all that apply: Stores, Processes, Transmits, Can Access, No Access, Unknown; account data includes cardholder data and sensitive authentication data. |
| CDE Impact | Select one: Direct CDE Access, Indirect CDE Impact, Security Service for CDE, Connected to CDE, No CDE Impact, Unknown. |
| Primary Business Owner | Enter the internal business owner accountable for the relationship, using name and role or team mailbox. |
| Contract Owner | Enter the internal owner responsible for the contract or agreement, typically Procurement, Legal, or Vendor Management contact. |
| Information Security Owner | Enter the internal security, PCI, or GRC owner responsible for PCI DSS oversight of this TPSP. |
| Engagement Status | Select one: Proposed, Due Diligence, Active, Suspended, Terminating, Terminated, Archived. |
| Service Start Date | Enter the date the service started or is planned to start in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Service End Date | Enter the actual or planned service end date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or enter N/A if ongoing. |
| Agreement / Contract Reference | Enter the contract, MSA, SOW, order form, or agreement reference number or title that governs the service. |
| Agreement Signed | Select Yes, No, Pending, or N/A; for active PCI-relevant TPSPs this should normally be Yes. |
| Agreement Signed Date | Enter the date the relevant agreement was fully executed in YYYY-MM-DD format, or N/A if not signed. |
| Agreement Expiry / Renewal Date | Enter the contract expiry, renewal, or review date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or N/A if not applicable. |
| Agreement Storage Location | Enter the controlled repository path, system record link, or document ID where the signed agreement is stored. |
| PCI Responsibility Acknowledgement Included | Select Yes, No, Pending, or N/A to indicate whether the written agreement includes the TPSP acknowledgement of responsibility for security of account data or the security-impacting services they provide, as applicable to PCI DSS Requirement 12.8.2. |
| PCI Responsibility Acknowledgement Location | Enter the agreement clause number, schedule name, page number, or document reference where the TPSP responsibility acknowledgement is located. |
| TPSP PCI Compliance Evidence Required | Select Yes, No, or To Be Determined; use Yes where the TPSP stores, processes, transmits, can affect the security of account data, or can impact the CDE. |
| Evidence Type | Select the evidence used or expected: PCI DSS AOC, ROC Executive Summary, SAQ, Attestation Letter, Contractual Attestation, Responsibility Matrix Only, Other, or N/A. |
| AOC / Compliance Evidence Received | Select Yes, No, Pending, Not Required, or Expired. |
| AOC / Evidence Date | Enter the date shown on the AOC or compliance evidence in YYYY-MM-DD format, or N/A if not received or not required. |
| AOC / Evidence Expiry Date | Enter the expiry date or one year after the AOC/evidence date in YYYY-MM-DD format, unless the document specifies a different validity period. |
| AOC Assessor / Issuer | Enter the QSA company, assessor, or issuing organisation named on the AOC or compliance evidence, or N/A. |
| AOC Scope Covers Service Used | Select Yes, No, Partially, Unknown, or N/A based on whether the AOC or evidence scope includes the specific service used by the organisation. |
| AOC Scope Notes | Summarise any relevant scope details, exclusions, service names, locations, PCI DSS version, or limitations identified in the AOC or evidence. |
| TPSP PCI DSS Compliance Status | Select Compliant, Non-Compliant, Expired Evidence, Not Yet Validated, Not Required, Unknown, or Under Review. |
| Compliance Status Last Reviewed Date | Enter the date the organisation last reviewed the TPSP PCI DSS compliance status in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Compliance Review Due Date | Enter the next required review date in YYYY-MM-DD format; for PCI-relevant active TPSPs this must be at least annually. |
| TPSP Responsibility Matrix Available | Select Yes, No, Pending, or N/A to indicate whether documented allocation of PCI DSS responsibilities between the organisation and TPSP is available. |
| Responsibility Matrix Location | Enter the document link, repository path, contract schedule, portal location, or internal record containing the responsibility matrix. |
| PCI DSS Requirements Managed by TPSP | List PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement numbers or sub-requirements managed by the TPSP, separated by commas; enter N/A if none. |
| PCI DSS Requirements Shared with TPSP | List PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement numbers or sub-requirements jointly managed by the organisation and TPSP, separated by commas; enter N/A if none. |
| PCI DSS Requirements Retained by Organisation | List key PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement numbers or sub-requirements retained by the organisation for this service, separated by commas; enter N/A if not assessed at this level. |
| Due Diligence Completed Before Engagement | Select Yes, No, Pending, Retrospective, or N/A to indicate whether risk and PCI-related due diligence was completed before engaging the TPSP, supporting PCI DSS Requirement 12.8.3. |
| Due Diligence Completion Date | Enter the date due diligence was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format, or N/A if not applicable. |
| Due Diligence Evidence Location | Enter the repository path, vendor risk assessment record, ticket, questionnaire, approval, or system link evidencing due diligence. |
| Open Issues / Gaps | Record any missing agreement, missing acknowledgement, missing or expired AOC, scope mismatch, unclear responsibility, or other unresolved PCI DSS issue; enter None if there are no open issues. |
| Risk Treatment / Exception Reference | Enter the approved risk acceptance, remediation plan, exception ID, or issue reference for unresolved gaps; enter N/A if no exception is required. |
| Last Updated Date | Enter the date this register row was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Updated By | Enter the name, role, or team mailbox of the person who last updated this register row. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the PCI Compliance Manager or GRC/Vendor Risk owner, with updates when any TPSP is proposed, onboarded, changed, renewed, terminated, or when new compliance evidence is received, and formally reviewed at least annually. Source data should be drawn from the contract lifecycle management system, vendor risk management platform, PCI evidence repository, TPSP AOCs, signed agreements, and approved PCI responsibility matrices.
