PCI-038.title: Incident Response Test Records
PCI-038.content:
## Incident Response Test Records (DOCX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Test Record ID | Test Date | Test Type | Incident Response Plan Version Tested | Scenario Tested | Scenario Description | PCI DSS Scope Covered | Systems, Locations, or Processes Included | Test Objectives | Incident Response Procedures Tested | Participants and Roles | Facilitator | Start Time | End Time | Test Method | Detection and Escalation Tested | Internal and External Communications Tested | Payment Brand or Acquirer Notification Tested | Evidence Preservation Tested | Containment, Eradication, and Recovery Tested | Lessons Learned Captured | Overall Test Result | Key Observations | Issues or Gaps Identified | Corrective Action Required | Corrective Action Owner | Corrective Action Due Date | Corrective Action Status | Retest Required | Retest Date | Evidence Reference | Management Review Date | Approver Name and Role | Approval Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [EXAMPLE: IR-TEST-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-15] | [EXAMPLE: Tabletop] | [EXAMPLE: Incident Response Plan v4.1] | [EXAMPLE: Cardholder Data Breach] | [EXAMPLE: Simulated compromise of an e-commerce payment application with potential exposure of cardholder data logs.] | [EXAMPLE: CDE] | [EXAMPLE: Web payment application, SIEM, SOC escalation process, Legal and Communications teams] | [EXAMPLE: Validate escalation, incident command roles, evidence preservation, acquirer notification decision process, and containment decision-making.] | [EXAMPLE: IRP Sections 4.2, 5.1, 5.3, 6.1; Data Breach Playbook v2.0] | [EXAMPLE: SOC Analyst, Incident Commander, IT Operations Lead, Legal Counsel, Compliance Manager, Communications Lead] | [EXAMPLE: Security Operations Manager] | [EXAMPLE: 09:00 UTC] | [EXAMPLE: 11:30 UTC] | [EXAMPLE: Facilitated conference tabletop using scripted injects] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Partially - customer communications were discussed but not fully drafted] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Partially] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Pass with Findings] | [EXAMPLE: Escalation to incident command was timely; contact list required one update; evidence preservation steps were understood.] | [EXAMPLE: External communications approval path was unclear; one acquirer contact was outdated.] | [EXAMPLE: Update communications approval workflow and acquirer contact list in IRP appendix.] | [EXAMPLE: Compliance Manager] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-15] | [EXAMPLE: In Progress] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-30] | [EXAMPLE: GRC-12345; SharePoint/PCI/IR Tests/2026/IR-TEST-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-20] | [EXAMPLE: Chief Information Security Officer] | [EXAMPLE: Approved] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Test Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this incident response test record, using a consistent format such as IR-TEST-YYYY-###. |
| Test Date | Enter the date the incident response plan test was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Test Type | Enter the type of test performed; allowed values: Tabletop, Simulation, Technical Exercise, Walkthrough, Other. |
| Incident Response Plan Version Tested | Enter the title and version number or document ID of the incident response plan used during the test, for example IRP v3.2. |
| Scenario Tested | Enter a short name for the incident scenario tested, for example Cardholder Data Breach, Ransomware, Web Application Compromise, Lost Media, Insider Threat. |
| Scenario Description | Enter a concise description of the simulated incident, including the assumed trigger, affected asset type, and relevance to the cardholder data environment. |
| PCI DSS Scope Covered | State whether the test covered the cardholder data environment and related response processes; allowed values: CDE, Connected-to-CDE, Security-Impacting Systems, Out-of-Scope Process Validation, Mixed Scope. |
| Systems, Locations, or Processes Included | List the specific systems, applications, network segments, locations, third parties, or business processes included in the test; use asset names or approved identifiers where available. |
| Test Objectives | Enter the specific objectives of the test, such as validating escalation, confirming roles and responsibilities, testing evidence preservation, confirming notification paths, or validating containment decision-making. |
| Incident Response Procedures Tested | List the specific incident response plan procedures or playbooks tested, including section numbers where available. |
| Participants and Roles | List all participants by name or role, department, and incident response role, for example Incident Commander, Security Analyst, Legal, Communications, IT Operations, Compliance. |
| Facilitator | Enter the name and role of the person who led or facilitated the test. |
| Start Time | Enter the test start time in 24-hour HH:MM format, including time zone if participants are in multiple regions. |
| End Time | Enter the test end time in 24-hour HH:MM format, including time zone if participants are in multiple regions. |
| Test Method | Describe how the test was conducted, for example conference tabletop, live simulation in test environment, ticket-driven exercise, or facilitated workshop. |
| Detection and Escalation Tested | Record whether detection and escalation steps were tested; allowed values: Yes, No, Partially, Not Applicable, and include a brief note if not fully tested. |
| Internal and External Communications Tested | Record whether internal and external communication procedures were tested; allowed values: Yes, No, Partially, Not Applicable, and include a brief note if not fully tested. |
| Payment Brand or Acquirer Notification Tested | Record whether procedures for notifying payment brands, acquirers, or other required entities were tested; allowed values: Yes, No, Partially, Not Applicable, and include a brief note if not fully tested. |
| Evidence Preservation Tested | Record whether procedures for preserving logs, forensic evidence, chain of custody, and affected system state were tested; allowed values: Yes, No, Partially, Not Applicable. |
| Containment, Eradication, and Recovery Tested | Record whether containment, eradication, and recovery decision points or actions were tested; allowed values: Yes, No, Partially, Not Applicable. |
| Lessons Learned Captured | Record whether lessons learned were documented during or after the test; allowed values: Yes, No, Partially. |
| Overall Test Result | Enter the overall outcome of the test; allowed values: Pass, Pass with Findings, Fail, Incomplete. |
| Key Observations | Enter concise observations on what worked well, response strengths, timing, coordination, decision-making, and any notable evidence of effective execution. |
| Issues or Gaps Identified | Enter each issue, gap, weakness, delay, missing step, unclear responsibility, missing contact, or documentation deficiency identified during the test; enter None if no issues were identified. |
| Corrective Action Required | Describe the corrective action required to address each issue or gap; enter None if no corrective action is required. |
| Corrective Action Owner | Enter the named role or individual accountable for completing the corrective action; enter Not Applicable if no action is required. |
| Corrective Action Due Date | Enter the target completion date for the corrective action in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Applicable if no action is required. |
| Corrective Action Status | Enter the current status of the corrective action; allowed values: Not Started, In Progress, Complete, Overdue, Deferred, Not Applicable. |
| Retest Required | Indicate whether a follow-up test or validation is required after corrective action; allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Retest Date | Enter the completed or planned retest date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Applicable if no retest is required. |
| Evidence Reference | Enter document links, ticket IDs, meeting minutes, attendance records, screenshots, exercise scripts, after-action reports, or repository paths that evidence the test and its results. |
| Management Review Date | Enter the date the test results and any corrective actions were reviewed by accountable management in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Approver Name and Role | Enter the name and job role of the manager or governance owner who reviewed and approved the test record. |
| Approval Status | Enter the approval state of the record; allowed values: Draft, Submitted, Approved, Rejected, Requires Update. |

### Maintenance

The Incident Response Manager or CISO-owned security operations governance function owns this template and updates it after each incident response test and at least annually to evidence PCI DSS Req 12.10.2. Source records should be drawn from the approved incident response plan, test scripts, meeting attendance, after-action reports, SIEM or ticketing records, GRC issues, and evidence repository links.

PCI-039.title: Internal PCI Compliance Review
PCI-039.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |

## Purpose

This report documents the results of the quarterly internal PCI compliance review for [Organisation Name] as a service provider. The review evaluates whether security controls protecting payment account data and the cardholder data environment are operating effectively, whether compliance responsibilities remain assigned and understood, and whether open risks, exceptions, and remediation activities are being managed appropriately.

The purpose of this report is to provide senior management, control owners, and relevant governance stakeholders with:

- A clear view of current PCI compliance status for the reporting period.
- Evidence that management has reviewed the effectiveness of security controls supporting PCI compliance.
- Identification of control gaps, operational issues, and areas requiring remediation.
- Tracked actions with accountable owners and target completion dates.
- Assurance that the organisation is maintaining PCI compliance as part of ongoing business-as-usual operations, rather than only during annual assessment activity.

This report is intended for internal governance, audit readiness, service provider oversight, and management accountability.

## Reporting Period & Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Reporting period | [Quarter, e.g., Q2 FY2026] |
| Review dates | [YYYY-MM-DD] to [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Report date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Review owner | [Name / Role] |
| Executive sponsor | [Name / Role] |
| Business entity reviewed | [Organisation Name] |
| Service provider status | [Service Provider Level / Description] |
| Primary locations in scope | [Data centres, cloud regions, offices, support locations] |
| External assessor involvement | [None / QSA consulted / QSA validation scheduled] |
| Prior report reference | [Previous report ID or date] |

The review covered systems, services, personnel, processes, and third-party dependencies that store, process, transmit, secure, monitor, administer, or could otherwise impact payment account data handled by [Organisation Name] in its role as a service provider.

In-scope areas included:

- Cardholder data environment and connected systems.
- Cloud platforms and hosting environments supporting payment services.
- Network security controls and segmentation boundaries.
- Identity and access management for privileged and non-privileged users.
- Vulnerability management, patching, and secure configuration activities.
- Logging, monitoring, alerting, and incident response readiness.
- Change management for payment-impacting systems.
- Secure software development and application security activities, where applicable.
- Third-party service providers that could affect PCI compliance.
- Security awareness and role-based training for relevant personnel.
- Evidence of ongoing compliance monitoring and management review.

Out-of-scope areas for this review were limited to systems and services that have been formally documented as not storing, processing, transmitting, or impacting payment account data and that remain appropriately segmented from the cardholder data environment. Any out-of-scope determination is dependent on the continued effectiveness of segmentation controls and documented data flow analysis.

|---|---:|---|
| Payment processing applications | Yes | [Application names] |
| Databases containing account data | Yes | [Database names / platforms] |
| Tokenisation or encryption services | Yes | [Service names] |
| Administrative access platforms | Yes | Includes privileged access paths |
| Security monitoring tooling | Yes | SIEM, alerting, endpoint, vulnerability management |
| Corporate user network | Limited | Reviewed only where connectivity or administrative access may affect in-scope systems |
| Public cloud environment | Yes | [Cloud provider / accounts / subscriptions] |
| Third-party hosted services | Yes | Reviewed through contracts, attestations, responsibilities, and service evidence |
| Physical office facilities | Limited | Reviewed where relevant to administration, support, or media handling |
| Non-payment business applications | No | Excluded where no impact pathway exists and segmentation is documented |

## Executive Summary

The quarterly review found that [Organisation Name] has maintained a generally effective PCI compliance operating model during the reporting period. Core governance activities, access reviews, vulnerability management, logging, change management, and third-party oversight activities were performed, with supporting evidence available for most reviewed areas.

The review identified [number] findings:

| Severity | Count | Summary |
|---|---:|---|
| Critical | [0] | [No critical findings identified / Summary] |
| High | [0] | [No high findings identified / Summary] |
| Medium | [X] | [Summary of medium-risk issues] |
| Low | [X] | [Summary of low-risk issues] |
| Observation | [X] | Process improvement opportunities without immediate compliance impact |

Overall review outcome: **[Compliant with remediation required / Partially compliant / At risk / Compliant with no material exceptions]**

Key positive observations:

- Quarterly management review of PCI compliance was performed and documented.
- Ownership of most PCI compliance activities remains assigned to named control owners.
- Vulnerability scanning and remediation processes are operating on a recurring basis.
- Access review evidence was available for key systems within the cardholder data environment.
- Security monitoring coverage remains in place for critical payment infrastructure.
- Third-party compliance documentation was requested and reviewed for major service providers.
- No evidence was identified of unauthorised storage of sensitive authentication data after authorisation during the reporting period.

Key concerns:

- Some evidence repositories contained incomplete or inconsistently named artefacts, increasing audit preparation effort.
- A small number of user access review exceptions were not closed within the expected internal timeframe.
- Third-party compliance evidence was not received from all providers before the end of the review period.
- Remediation tracking for lower-priority vulnerabilities requires improved ageing visibility.
- Documentation of service provider responsibility boundaries requires refresh for [specific service / platform], due to recent architecture or contractual changes.

Management attention is required to ensure overdue remediation actions are completed, evidence quality is improved, and third-party dependencies continue to be actively monitored.

## Methodology

The review was conducted as an internal governance and compliance assessment using a risk-based sampling approach. The objective was to verify that PCI-related controls remained operational during the quarter and that management had adequate visibility over compliance obligations, issues, and remediation status.

Review activities included:

1. **Document review**
 - Reviewed policies, standards, operating procedures, control matrices, system inventories, data flow diagrams, network diagrams, and responsibility assignments.
 - Confirmed whether documentation remained current and reflected the implemented environment.

2. **Evidence inspection**
 - Reviewed tickets, system exports, access review records, vulnerability scan results, change approvals, monitoring records, training records, third-party attestations, and incident logs.
 - Validated whether evidence was complete, dated, attributable, and relevant to the reporting period.

3. **Control owner interviews**
 - Interviewed selected control owners across Information Security, Infrastructure, Cloud Operations, Engineering, Compliance, Risk, Service Management, and Vendor Management.
 - Confirmed understanding of ongoing PCI responsibilities and escalation paths.

4. **Sample testing**
 - Selected representative samples for access provisioning, access removal, privileged access review, change management, vulnerability remediation, logging, alert review, and third-party monitoring.
 - Sampling was designed to identify whether controls are operating consistently and whether exceptions are detected and managed.

5. **Issue and action review**
 - Reviewed open PCI-related issues, prior findings, remediation actions, accepted risks, compensating measures, and management exceptions.
 - Confirmed status, ownership, due dates, and evidence of closure where applicable.

6. **Management review**
 - Discussed results with relevant management stakeholders.
 - Confirmed proposed remediation actions, accountable owners, and target completion dates.

The review did not constitute a full external assessment or certification activity. It was designed to support internal governance, compliance maintenance, and audit readiness.

### PCI-QTR-[001] - Incomplete Closure Evidence for Access Review Exceptions

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Status | Open |
| Control area | Identity and access management |
| Owner | [IAM Owner] |
| Target completion date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Affected systems | [System names] |

**Condition**

Quarterly access reviews were completed for the sampled in-scope systems; however, [number] access review exceptions did not have complete closure evidence at the time of review. In the sampled cases, reviewers identified accounts requiring removal, role adjustment, or manager confirmation, but the supporting ticket records did not consistently show completion, validation, and final reviewer sign-off.

**Risk**

Incomplete closure evidence may prevent management from demonstrating that inappropriate access was removed in a timely manner. This increases the risk of excessive or unauthorised access to systems that support payment processing or security administration.

**Evidence reviewed**

- Access review sign-off records for [systems].
- User access export dated [YYYY-MM-DD].
- Remediation tickets [ticket references].
- Privileged access group membership export dated [YYYY-MM-DD].

**Root cause**

The access review process identifies exceptions effectively, but closure tracking is split across review spreadsheets and service desk tickets. There is no mandatory field requiring final validation that corrective action was completed and confirmed by the reviewer.

**Management response**

[Management response, e.g., IAM team agrees with the finding and will update the access review workflow to require closure evidence and reviewer confirmation before exceptions are marked complete.]

**Required remediation**

- Update the access review workflow to require linked remediation tickets for all exceptions.
- Require evidence of removal, modification, or business approval for retained access.
- Require final validation by the system owner or delegated reviewer.
- Report overdue access review exceptions to the PCI compliance forum until closure.

---

### PCI-QTR-[002] - Delayed Receipt of Third-Party Compliance Evidence

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Status | Open |
| Control area | Third-party service provider management |
| Owner | [Vendor Management Owner] |
| Target completion date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Affected third parties | [Vendor names] |

**Condition**

Compliance evidence was requested from all identified third-party service providers that could affect payment security. Evidence was received and reviewed for [number] of [number] providers. For [vendor names], current compliance evidence was not received before the close of the reporting period.

**Risk**

Delayed or missing third-party compliance evidence may reduce management’s ability to confirm that outsourced services supporting payment operations are adequately secured. It may also affect the organisation’s ability to respond to customer due diligence requests and external assessment activities.

**Evidence reviewed**

- Vendor inventory dated [YYYY-MM-DD].
- Evidence request emails and portal records.
- Supplier attestations received during the quarter.
- Third-party responsibility matrix.
- Vendor risk register.

**Root cause**

Vendor compliance evidence collection is performed quarterly, but escalation timelines are not sufficiently aligned with supplier response times. Some contracts do not explicitly require evidence delivery within the organisation’s quarterly review window.

**Management response**

[Management response, e.g., Vendor Management will implement earlier evidence requests and contractual tracking for evidence delivery commitments.]

**Required remediation**

- Send evidence requests at the start of each quarter for all in-scope providers.
- Establish escalation points for delayed responses.
- Track evidence expiry dates centrally.
- Update contract renewal checklists to include timely compliance evidence obligations.
- Escalate missing evidence to the PCI governance forum and vendor owner.

### PCI-QTR-[003] - Vulnerability Remediation Ageing Not Consistently Reported

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Severity | Low |
| Status | Open |
| Control area | Vulnerability and patch management |
| Owner | [Security Operations Owner] |
| Target completion date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Affected systems | [Asset groups / platforms] |

**Condition**

Vulnerability scanning was performed during the reporting period and remediation tickets were created for confirmed findings. High-priority items were tracked actively. However, reporting for lower-priority vulnerabilities did not consistently show ageing by asset owner, due date, environment, and business service.

**Risk**

Without consistent ageing reports, lower-priority vulnerabilities may accumulate over time and increase the attack surface of systems connected to, supporting, or adjacent to the cardholder data environment.

**Evidence reviewed**

- Vulnerability scan reports dated [YYYY-MM-DD].
- Remediation tickets [ticket references].
- Vulnerability dashboards.
- Patch deployment records.
- Exception records.

**Root cause**

Existing vulnerability dashboards prioritise critical and high-severity vulnerabilities but do not provide sufficient operational visibility into ageing trends for all open items.

**Management response**

[Management response, e.g., Security Operations will enhance dashboard reporting and distribute ageing reports to asset owners monthly.]

**Required remediation**

- Add ageing buckets for all open vulnerabilities.
- Include asset owner, environment, service name, and remediation due date in reporting.
- Escalate overdue items according to risk and age.
- Include trend reporting in the quarterly PCI review pack.

**Condition**

Evidence supporting quarterly PCI control operation was available, but naming conventions, folder structure, and retention labelling were inconsistent across control areas. Some artefacts required follow-up with control owners to confirm the period covered and system relevance.

**Risk**

Inconsistent evidence management increases audit preparation effort and may delay response to customer assurance requests, external assessor requests, or incident-related investigations.

**Evidence reviewed**

- Quarterly evidence folders.
- GRC evidence records.
- Control owner submissions.
- Prior review evidence packages.

**Root cause**

The evidence repository has grown over time without a single enforced naming standard or metadata requirement for quarterly submissions.

**Management response**

[Management response, e.g., Compliance team will publish an evidence naming standard and perform quality checks before each quarterly review meeting.]

**Required remediation**

- Establish a standard naming convention for all PCI evidence.
- Require each artefact to identify control area, system, owner, period covered, and extraction date.
- Implement quarterly evidence quality checks.
- Maintain a central evidence index for each reporting period.

**Condition**

The organisation’s responsibility matrix documents internal and third-party responsibilities for key payment services. However, recent changes to [cloud service / managed service / platform architecture] were not fully reflected in the current version. Specifically, responsibilities for [logging, key management, patching, vulnerability remediation, access administration, incident notification, or configuration monitoring] require clarification.

**Risk**

Unclear responsibility boundaries may result in control gaps, duplicated effort, or missed operational activities. This is particularly important where payment services rely on cloud platforms, managed services, or outsourced operational support.

**Evidence reviewed**

- Current responsibility matrix.
- Architecture change records.
- Cloud service configuration documents.
- Vendor contract and service description.
- Control owner interview notes.

**Root cause**

Architecture and service changes were approved through change management, but the compliance responsibility matrix was not included as a required update artefact.

**Management response**

[Management response, e.g., Cloud Platform team will update the responsibility matrix and add compliance artefact review to the change checklist for PCI-impacting services.]

**Required remediation**

- Update the responsibility matrix to reflect the current operating model.
- Validate responsibilities with Legal, Vendor Management, Security Operations, Cloud Operations, and Compliance.
- Confirm that evidence sources exist for each assigned responsibility.
- Add responsibility matrix review to change management for PCI-impacting service changes.

Security events reviewed were handled through normal operational processes, and no evidence was identified indicating unauthorised disclosure of payment account data.

## Analysis

The quarterly review indicates that [Organisation Name] continues to operate a mature PCI compliance management process, with recurring control activities embedded across security, infrastructure, engineering, vendor management, and compliance functions. The most important compliance activities are being performed, and there is evidence of management oversight.

The organisation’s strongest areas are:

- **Recurring governance cadence** - The quarterly review process provides a formal checkpoint for management visibility and accountability.
- **Security operations coverage** - Vulnerability scanning, logging, alerting, and incident tracking are operating as routine security activities.
- **Access governance** - Access reviews are being performed, and exceptions are being identified.
- **Change control discipline** - Sampled changes affecting in-scope systems showed evidence of review, approval, and implementation control.
- **Third-party awareness** - The organisation maintains a list of relevant service providers and actively requests compliance evidence.

Areas requiring management focus are primarily related to operational discipline and evidence maturity rather than widespread control absence. The findings show that several processes are functioning but require stronger closure tracking, consistency, and escalation.

The following themes were identified:

### 1. Evidence Quality Needs Standardisation

Evidence exists for most reviewed control areas, but inconsistent labelling and repository structure make it harder to demonstrate compliance efficiently. For an organisation operating as a service provider, evidence quality is especially important because customers, auditors, assessors, and internal stakeholders may request assurance at different points throughout the year.

Improving evidence metadata, naming conventions, and retention structure will reduce assessment effort and support faster responses to due diligence requests.

### 2. Exception Closure Must Be More Explicit

Access review exceptions and remediation activities must not only be identified; they must also be demonstrably resolved. The review found that some closure steps were not consistently evidenced. This creates avoidable uncertainty and may weaken management’s ability to prove that access risks were corrected promptly.

A single workflow with required closure evidence and final reviewer confirmation will strengthen this area.

### 3. Third-Party Dependencies Require Earlier Escalation

Service provider compliance depends partly on other service providers that host, transmit, secure, manage, or support payment-impacting systems. Missing or delayed third-party evidence can create assurance gaps even where internal controls are operating effectively.

Evidence collection should begin earlier in the quarter, with defined escalation points and contractually supported expectations.

### 4. Change Management Should Trigger Compliance Artefact Updates

Architecture, cloud platform, and managed service changes can alter control ownership and evidence sources. The responsibility matrix must remain current and should be treated as a required artefact for any material change affecting payment services.

Adding compliance documentation checks to the change process will reduce the likelihood of outdated responsibility assignments.

### 5. Current Risk Level

The overall PCI compliance risk for the reporting period is assessed as **[Low / Medium / High]**.

| Risk Area | Current Assessment | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Compliance governance | Medium | Review cadence exists; responsibility matrix update required |
| Technical security controls | Low | Core scanning, monitoring, and configuration controls operating |
| Access control | Medium | Reviews performed; exception closure evidence incomplete |
| Third-party reliance | Medium | Some evidence outstanding at quarter close |
| Audit readiness | Medium | Evidence exists but requires improved organisation and metadata |
| Incident exposure | Low | No confirmed payment data incident identified during the reporting period |

The identified findings do not currently indicate systemic failure of the PCI compliance program. However, if not remediated, they may increase audit effort, weaken assurance, and raise the risk of compliance gaps in future reporting periods.

## Recommendations & Actions

Management should approve and track the following remediation actions through the PCI compliance governance process. Action status should be reviewed at least monthly until completion and formally reported in the next quarterly review.

| Action ID | Recommendation / Action | Priority | Owner | Target Date | Success Criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACT-[001] | Implement mandatory closure evidence and reviewer confirmation for all access review exceptions | High | [IAM Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | All exceptions have linked tickets, action evidence, and final sign-off |
| ACT-[002] | Update third-party evidence collection calendar and escalation process | High | [Vendor Management Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Evidence requested at quarter start; overdue suppliers escalated before quarter end |
| ACT-[003] | Enhance vulnerability dashboards to include ageing, owner, service, and overdue status | Medium | [Security Operations Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Monthly report available and reviewed by asset owners |
| ACT-[004] | Publish and enforce PCI evidence naming and metadata standard | Medium | [Compliance Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Evidence index complete for the quarter; artefacts consistently named |
| ACT-[005] | Refresh responsibility matrix for changed cloud and managed service operating model | High | [Cloud Platform Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Updated matrix approved by Security, Cloud, Compliance, and Vendor Management |
| ACT-[006] | Add compliance artefact review to PCI-impacting change checklist | Medium | [Change Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Change templates require confirmation of scope, diagrams, responsibility matrix, and evidence impacts |
| ACT-[007] | Review all open exceptions and confirm expiry dates, owners, and compensating measures | Medium | [Risk Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Exception register contains no expired or ownerless records |
| ACT-[008] | Prepare next quarter evidence request pack for all control owners | Low | [PCI Compliance Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Evidence calendar issued and acknowledged by control owners |

|---|---|---|---|
| Approve remediation plan and owners | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Executive Sponsor] | Required to maintain accountability |
| Confirm risk rating for current quarter | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Risk Committee / CISO] | Recommended rating: [Low / Medium / High] |
| Escalate overdue third-party evidence | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Vendor Management Lead] | Applies to [vendor names] |
| Approve responsibility matrix update priority | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Cloud / Technology Leadership] | Required due to changed operating model |

### Target Timeline

| Milestone | Target Date | Responsible Party |
|---|---|---|
| Report reviewed by PCI Compliance Owner | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [PCI Compliance Owner] |
| Management review meeting completed | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Executive Sponsor] |
| Remediation owners confirm action plans | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Action owners |
| High-priority actions completed or formally risk accepted | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Action owners |
| Evidence repository standard implemented | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Compliance Owner] |
| Next quarterly review preparation begins | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [PCI Compliance Owner] |
| Next quarterly review report issued | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [PCI Compliance Owner] |

### Acceptance Criteria for Closure

A finding may be closed only when:

- The assigned owner has completed the agreed remediation.
- Evidence is available, dated, and stored in the approved repository.
- The PCI Compliance Owner or delegated reviewer has validated the evidence.
- Any residual risk has been documented and approved by the appropriate risk authority.
- The closure decision is recorded in the remediation tracker.

### Ongoing Monitoring

The following items should be monitored between quarterly reviews:

- Open PCI findings and overdue remediation actions.
- Access review completion and exception closure.
- Vulnerability remediation status and overdue items.
- Changes affecting PCI scope, data flows, segmentation, or responsibilities.
- Third-party compliance evidence status and expiry dates.
- Security incidents and significant alerts involving in-scope systems.
- Exceptions, risk acceptances, and compensating measures.
- Evidence collection completeness and quality.

## Distribution & Confidentiality

This report contains confidential information about [Organisation Name]’s payment security controls, compliance posture, third-party dependencies, vulnerabilities, remediation activities, and internal governance processes. It must be handled as confidential internal information.

Approved distribution is limited to:

| Recipient / Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Executive Sponsor] | Governance oversight and risk acceptance |
| [Chief Information Security Officer] | Security accountability and remediation oversight |
| [PCI Compliance Owner] | Compliance management and evidence coordination |
| [Risk and Compliance Team] | Issue tracking and reporting |
| [Security Operations Team] | Technical remediation and monitoring |
| [Infrastructure / Cloud Operations] | Platform and environment remediation |
| [Engineering / Application Owners] | Application and change-related remediation |
| [Vendor Management] | Third-party evidence and contractual follow-up |
| [Internal Audit] | Independent assurance and audit planning |
| [Legal / Privacy, if applicable] | Contractual, regulatory, and notification considerations |

This report must not be shared externally without approval from [Authorising Role], and where applicable, Legal, Compliance, and Information Security. External sharing may require redaction of sensitive technical information, customer information, vendor information, vulnerability details, network details, system names, and internal remediation plans.

Minimum handling requirements:

- Store only in approved repositories with access restricted to authorised personnel.
- Do not email to unauthorised recipients or personal accounts.
- Do not upload to external portals unless approved and required for due diligence or assessment.
- Redact sensitive system, vulnerability, and security architecture details before external release.
- Retain according to the organisation’s compliance evidence retention schedule.
- Dispose of obsolete copies securely when no longer required.

| Information Security Lead | [Name] | [Approved / Pending] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Executive Sponsor | [Name] | [Approved / Pending] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Risk Owner | [Name] | [Approved / Pending] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

PCI-040.title: Nonconformity & Remediation Tracker
PCI-040.content:
## Nonconformity & Remediation Tracker (XLSX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Finding ID | Date Logged | Logged By | Source of Finding | Source Reference | PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement Reference | Affected Incident Response Plan Section | Finding Title | Finding Description | Nonconformity Type | Incident Response Capability Area | Affected Scope | Impact on Cardholder Data Environment | Severity | Risk Rating | Root Cause | Required Remediation Action | Interim Compensating or Containment Action | Action Owner | Business Owner | Target Remediation Date | Due Date Basis | Current Status | Percent Complete | Date Last Updated | Evidence Required for Closure | Evidence Location or Link | Validation Method | Validated By | Validation Date | Closure Decision | Closure Date | Residual Risk Accepted | Risk Acceptance Reference | Escalation Required | Escalation Date | Escalated To | Lessons Learned Captured | Incident Response Plan Updated | Training or Awareness Updated | Retest Required | Retest Date | Retest Result | Comments |

| [EXAMPLE: NCR-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-15] | [EXAMPLE: PCI Compliance Analyst] | [EXAMPLE: Incident Response Tabletop Exercise] | [EXAMPLE: IR-TTX-2026-Q1] | [EXAMPLE: 12.10.2] | [EXAMPLE: Section 4.3 Escalation and Contact List] | [EXAMPLE: Outdated acquirer escalation contact in incident response plan] | [EXAMPLE: The tabletop exercise identified that the acquirer contact listed in the incident response plan was no longer valid, which may delay required notification during a suspected cardholder data compromise.] | [EXAMPLE: Outdated Procedure] | [EXAMPLE: Payment Brand or Acquirer Notification] | [EXAMPLE: Incident response governance process for CDE-related incidents] | [EXAMPLE: Indirect CDE Impact] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: Contact list maintenance procedure not performed after vendor relationship change] | [EXAMPLE: Update acquirer and payment brand contact details in the incident response plan and implement quarterly owner review of emergency contacts.] | [EXAMPLE: Security operations team to use current acquirer contact from vendor management records until the plan is updated.] | [EXAMPLE: Incident Response Manager] | [EXAMPLE: Head of Information Security] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-01] | [EXAMPLE: Severity SLA] | [EXAMPLE: In Progress] | [EXAMPLE: 50] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-20] | [EXAMPLE: Approved updated incident response plan and evidence of quarterly contact review control] | [EXAMPLE: GRC-12345 / Evidence Vault / PCI / Req12.10 / NCR-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: Document review] | [EXAMPLE: PCI Compliance Manager] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-03] | [EXAMPLE: Accepted for Closure] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-03] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Closure pending final document approval.] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Finding ID | Enter a unique identifier for the finding using a consistent format, e.g., NCR-YYYY-###. |
| Date Logged | Enter the date the finding was recorded in the tracker in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Logged By | Enter the name or role of the person who logged the finding. |
| Source of Finding | Select or enter the origin of the finding, such as Incident Response Test, Tabletop Exercise, Security Incident, Internal Audit, External Audit, PCI Gap Assessment, Post-Incident Review, Monitoring Alert Review, or Management Review. |
| Source Reference | Enter the reference to the originating record, such as test report ID, audit issue ID, incident ticket number, assessment report section, or meeting minutes reference. |
| PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement Reference | Enter the applicable PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement reference, e.g., 12.10, 12.10.1, 12.10.2, 12.10.3, 12.10.4, 12.10.5, 12.10.6, or 12.10.7. |
| Affected Incident Response Plan Section | Enter the section, procedure, playbook, escalation path, contact list, communications process, evidence handling process, or testing process affected by the finding. |
| Finding Title | Enter a short, specific title summarising the nonconformity or remediation item. |
| Finding Description | Describe the finding factually, including what was observed, what was expected, and why it does not meet the PCI DSS requirement or internal incident response procedure. |
| Nonconformity Type | Select one value: Missing Control, Ineffective Control, Outdated Procedure, Unassigned Responsibility, Untested Process, Evidence Gap, Training Gap, Communication Gap, Escalation Gap, Tooling Gap, Documentation Gap, Other. |
| Incident Response Capability Area | Select one value: Detection, Triage, Escalation, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, Forensics Evidence Preservation, Legal or Regulatory Notification, Payment Brand or Acquirer Notification, Communications, Lessons Learned, Annual Testing, Training, Contact List Maintenance, Other. |
| Affected Scope | Describe the affected environment, system, process, team, location, service provider, or business function; specify whether it relates to the CDE, connected-to systems, security monitoring, or incident response governance. |
| Impact on Cardholder Data Environment | Select one value: Direct CDE Impact, Indirect CDE Impact, No CDE Impact, To Be Determined; add brief context if needed. |
| Severity | Select one value: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational, based on impact to timely detection, response, containment, recovery, notification, or PCI DSS compliance. |
| Risk Rating | Select one value: Very High, High, Medium, Low, Very Low, based on likelihood and impact after considering current controls. |
| Root Cause | Enter the underlying cause of the finding, such as process not defined, ownership unclear, procedure not maintained, resource constraint, technology limitation, training not completed, vendor dependency, or unknown pending analysis. |
| Required Remediation Action | Enter the specific corrective action required to resolve the finding, written as an actionable task with a clear expected outcome. |
| Interim Compensating or Containment Action | Enter any temporary measure used to reduce risk until full remediation is complete; enter Not Applicable if none is required. |
| Action Owner | Enter the individual role or named owner responsible for completing the remediation action. |
| Business Owner | Enter the accountable business, security, IT, compliance, or process owner who accepts responsibility for the remediation outcome. |
| Target Remediation Date | Enter the planned completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Due Date Basis | State how the due date was determined, such as severity SLA, audit commitment, incident response plan update cycle, management decision, regulatory deadline, or PCI assessment deadline. |
| Current Status | Select one value: New, Assigned, In Progress, Blocked, Pending Validation, Remediated, Closed, Deferred, Risk Accepted, Cancelled. |
| Percent Complete | Enter the completion percentage as a whole number from 0 to 100. |
| Date Last Updated | Enter the most recent date this record was updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Evidence Required for Closure | Describe the evidence needed to prove remediation, such as updated incident response plan, approved playbook, completed test results, training records, contact list update, ticket closure, screenshots, meeting minutes, or validation report. |
| Evidence Location or Link | Enter the repository path, GRC record link, ticket link, document ID, SharePoint path, or evidence vault reference where closure evidence is stored. |
| Validation Method | Select or describe how closure will be verified, such as document review, walkthrough, tabletop retest, technical test, sample inspection, interview, ticket review, or management approval. |
| Validated By | Enter the independent reviewer, control owner, compliance analyst, internal auditor, or manager who validated remediation; leave blank until validation occurs. |
| Validation Date | Enter the date validation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until validation occurs. |
| Closure Decision | Select one value: Not Ready, Accepted for Closure, Rejected, Risk Accepted, No Longer Applicable; leave blank until reviewed. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the finding was formally closed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until closed. |
| Residual Risk Accepted | Select Yes, No, or Not Applicable to indicate whether any remaining risk was formally accepted. |
| Risk Acceptance Reference | If residual risk is accepted, enter the risk acceptance ID, approval record, approver, and expiry date reference; enter Not Applicable if no residual risk is accepted. |
| Escalation Required | Select Yes or No to indicate whether the finding requires escalation due to overdue status, high severity, blocked remediation, or material PCI DSS impact. |
| Escalation Date | Enter the date of escalation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Applicable if escalation is not required. |
| Escalated To | Enter the role, committee, manager, or governance forum receiving the escalation; enter Not Applicable if escalation is not required. |
| Lessons Learned Captured | Select Yes, No, or Not Applicable to indicate whether lessons learned were documented, especially where the finding originated from an incident or incident response test. |
| Incident Response Plan Updated | Select Yes, No, or Not Applicable to indicate whether the incident response plan, playbook, contact list, or related procedure was updated as part of remediation. |
| Training or Awareness Updated | Select Yes, No, or Not Applicable to indicate whether relevant staff training, awareness, or role-specific incident response instruction was updated or delivered. |
| Retest Required | Select Yes or No to indicate whether remediation must be retested before closure. |
| Retest Date | Enter the retest date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Applicable if no retest is required. |
| Retest Result | Select one value: Pass, Fail, Partially Pass, Not Performed, Not Applicable. |
| Comments | Enter concise notes on progress, blockers, management decisions, dependencies, or audit-relevant context. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Incident Response Manager with oversight from the PCI Compliance or GRC function. Update the register whenever a finding is raised or status changes, review at least weekly while open findings exist, and source entries from incident tickets, incident response tests, post-incident reviews, audit reports, PCI gap assessments, GRC issues, and remediation tickets.

PCI-041.title: Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ)
PCI-041.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | [PCI Compliance Owner] | [Effective Date] | PCI DSS v4.0.1 | Confidential |

## Purpose

This Self-Assessment Questionnaire Attestation documents management’s formal representation that [Organisation Name] has completed the applicable PCI DSS self-assessment process for the cardholder data environment and in-scope payment channels.

The purpose of this Attestation is to confirm that:

- The correct Self-Assessment Questionnaire type has been selected based on how [Organisation Name] stores, processes, transmits, or could impact the security of cardholder data.
- The self-assessment was completed using accurate, current, and complete information.
- The responses in the Self-Assessment Questionnaire are supported by evidence.
- Any identified gaps have been documented, risk-assessed, and assigned remediation ownership.
- Management accepts responsibility for the accuracy of the submission and for maintaining PCI DSS compliance after the assessment date.

This document is intended for use by internal stakeholders, acquiring banks, payment brands, service providers, auditors, assessors, and other authorised parties requiring evidence of PCI DSS self-assessment completion.

## Scope

This Attestation applies to the PCI DSS self-assessment performed by [Organisation Name] for the assessment period ending [Assessment End Date].

The assessed environment includes all people, processes, technologies, locations, payment channels, third parties, and network segments that store, process, transmit, or could affect the security of cardholder data.

### Applicable SAQ Type

| Item | Attested Response |
|---|---|
| Applicable SAQ Type | [SAQ A / SAQ A-EP / SAQ B / SAQ B-IP / SAQ C / SAQ C-VT / SAQ P2PE / SAQ D Merchant / SAQ D Service Provider] |
| Reason for SAQ Selection | [Brief description of payment channels and processing model supporting SAQ type selection] |
| Merchant or Service Provider Role | [Merchant / Service Provider / Both] |
| Merchant Level or Service Provider Category | [Applicable level/category, if known] |
| Acquiring Bank or Payment Brand Requesting Attestation | [Name] |
| Assessment Period Covered | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Assessment Completion Date | [Completion Date] |

### In-Scope Payment Channels

| Payment Channel | Included in Assessment | Description | Primary Technology or Provider |
|---|---:|---|---|
| E-commerce | [Yes/No] | [Hosted payment page, redirect, iframe, direct post, API, or other model] | [Platform / Provider] |
| Mail order / telephone order | [Yes/No] | [Call centre, virtual terminal, paper forms, or other model] | [Platform / Provider] |
| Card-present retail | [Yes/No] | [Point-of-sale terminals, attended/unattended devices, or mobile POS] | [Platform / Provider] |
| Recurring payments | [Yes/No] | [Tokenised billing, customer vaulting, subscription platform, or other model] | [Platform / Provider] |
| Back-office payment handling | [Yes/No] | [Refunds, chargebacks, reconciliation, support processes] | [Platform / Provider] |

### In-Scope Locations

| Location | Function | In Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| [Head Office] | [Administration / finance / support] | [Yes/No] | [Notes] |
| [Retail Site / Branch / Facility] | [Payment acceptance / operations] | [Yes/No] | [Notes] |
| [Data Centre / Cloud Region] | [Hosting / processing / storage] | [Yes/No] | [Notes] |
| [Remote Workforce] | [Support / administration / payment handling] | [Yes/No] | [Notes] |

### In-Scope Systems and Services

The following systems, applications, networks, and services were considered for the self-assessment:

| System or Service | Function | In-Scope Rationale | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Payment Application / Platform] | [Payment capture, processing, tokenisation, reporting] | [Stores/processes/transmits cardholder data or affects security] | [System Owner] |
| [E-commerce Website] | [Customer payment journey] | [Can impact payment page security or redirect integrity] | [System Owner] |
| [Virtual Terminal] | [Manual payment entry] | [Used by staff to process card payments] | [Business Owner] |
| [POS Terminals] | [Card-present payment acceptance] | [Used to accept payment cards] | [Operations Owner] |
| [Network Segment] | [Connectivity/security boundary] | [Supports in-scope systems or administrative access] | [Infrastructure Owner] |
| [Cloud Hosting Service] | [Hosting/payment support services] | [Hosts or supports in-scope components] | [Cloud Owner] |
| [Logging/SIEM Platform] | [Security monitoring] | [Collects logs from in-scope systems] | [Security Owner] |

### Out-of-Scope Items

Systems, services, or locations are considered out of scope only where [Organisation Name] has confirmed that they do not store, process, transmit, or affect the security of cardholder data and are appropriately separated from the in-scope environment.

| Item | Reason Excluded | Validation Performed |
|---|---|---|
| [System / Location / Process] | [No cardholder data interaction and no security impact on in-scope environment] | [Network review / data-flow validation / process walkthrough / provider confirmation] |
| [System / Location / Process] | [Handled entirely by validated third party with no organisational access to cardholder data] | [Contract review / responsibility matrix / attestation review] |

### Third-Party Service Providers

The following third-party service providers were considered because they store, process, transmit, or could affect the security of cardholder data on behalf of [Organisation Name]:

| Provider | Service Provided | PCI Responsibility Impact | Evidence Reviewed |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Payment Processor] | [Authorisation, settlement, tokenisation] | [Processes cardholder data] | [Attestation of compliance / responsibility matrix / contract] |
| [Payment Gateway] | [Hosted payment page, API gateway, transaction routing] | [Processes or transmits payment data] | [Attestation of compliance / service description] |
| [Cloud Provider] | [Infrastructure, platform, hosting] | [Hosts or supports in-scope environment] | [Compliance report / shared responsibility documentation] |
| [Managed Service Provider] | [Administration, monitoring, support] | [May affect security of in-scope systems] | [Contract, access records, security commitments] |

## Attestation Statement

Management of [Organisation Name] attests that, to the best of its knowledge and based on the evidence reviewed, the applicable PCI DSS Self-Assessment Questionnaire has been completed for the assessed environment described in this document.

By signing this Attestation, [Organisation Name] confirms that:

1. The SAQ type identified in this document is appropriate for the organisation’s payment acceptance channels, processing methods, technical architecture, and use of third-party service providers.
2. The scope of the assessment was defined using current payment flows, network diagrams, system inventories, third-party service listings, access paths, and business process information.
3. All known locations, applications, systems, networks, people, and service providers that store, process, transmit, or could affect the security of cardholder data were considered.
4. Cardholder data flows were reviewed and are understood by the business, technology, and security owners responsible for the assessed environment.
5. The responses recorded in the completed SAQ are accurate as of [Assessment Completion Date].
6. Evidence supporting the SAQ responses was reviewed and retained in accordance with this document.
7. Where a requirement was marked as in place, [Organisation Name] has evidence showing that the relevant security practice, control, configuration, process, or monitoring activity was operating at the time of assessment.
8. Where a requirement was marked as not applicable, the rationale was documented and is supported by the assessed environment design or business process.
9. Where a requirement was not fully in place, the gap was documented, assigned to an accountable owner, and included in a remediation plan.
10. [Organisation Name] has not intentionally omitted any known cardholder data environment component, payment process, third-party dependency, or relevant security weakness from the self-assessment.
11. [Organisation Name] understands that PCI DSS compliance is not a one-time activity and must be maintained through ongoing security operations, change control, monitoring, vulnerability management, access management, incident response readiness, and supplier oversight.
12. [Organisation Name] will notify relevant stakeholders where significant changes occur that may affect SAQ eligibility, assessment scope, or PCI DSS compliance status.

### Assessment Outcome

| Assessment Item | Status |
|---|---|
| SAQ completed | [Yes/No] |
| All applicable responses supported by evidence | [Yes/No] |
| All not applicable responses justified | [Yes/No] |
| Remediation plan required | [Yes/No] |
| Compensating controls used | [Yes/No] |
| Significant scope changes identified during assessment | [Yes/No] |

### Significant Change Triggers

- Introduction of a new payment channel, payment page, virtual terminal, POS solution, payment application, gateway, or processor.
- Change from hosted or outsourced payment processing to direct handling of cardholder data, or any other change affecting SAQ eligibility.
- Modification to e-commerce payment flows, scripts, redirects, integrations, or customer payment experience.
- Deployment of new systems, cloud services, network segments, administrative access methods, or security technologies affecting the assessed environment.
- Change to segmentation controls, firewall rules, remote access paths, identity providers, logging coverage, encryption methods, or vulnerability management processes.
- Outsourcing, insourcing, replacement, or material change of a service provider that stores, processes, transmits, or could affect cardholder data security.
- Discovery of previously unknown cardholder data storage, transmission, logging, backup, or reporting.
- Security incident, suspected compromise, major vulnerability, or control failure affecting the in-scope environment.
- Merger, acquisition, divestiture, restructuring, or major business process change affecting payment operations.

## Purpose

This Report on Compliance documents the results of the independent assessment of [Organisation Name] against the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard version 4.0.1.

The report is intended to provide acquiring banks, payment brands, executive management, and other authorised stakeholders with a clear, evidence-based view of whether [Organisation Name] has implemented and maintained the security controls required to protect account data within the assessed cardholder data environment.

This report covers:

- The assessed payment channels, business processes, systems, facilities, personnel, service providers, and technologies that store, process, transmit, or can impact the security of cardholder data.
- The validation approach used by the Qualified Security Assessor.
- The assessment results, including areas found to be in place, not in place, not applicable, or subject to compensating controls.
- Management actions required to address identified gaps.
- The overall compliance conclusion for the reporting period.

This report is not a penetration test report, vulnerability assessment report, audit opinion on financial statements, or general-purpose cybersecurity maturity assessment. Its purpose is specifically to document compliance with PCI DSS v4.0.1 for the defined scope and reporting period.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

### Scope Statement

The assessment scope includes all people, processes, technologies, facilities, and third-party services that store, process, or transmit cardholder data, or that can affect the security of the cardholder data environment.

The assessed environment includes the systems and business processes supporting the following payment activities:

| Payment Channel / Process | Description | Included in Scope |
|---|---|---:|
| E-commerce payments | Customer payments submitted through [website / application name] and routed to [payment gateway / processor] | Yes |
| Card-present payments | Payments accepted through [retail locations / terminals / point-of-sale estate] | Yes |
| Mail order / telephone order | Card details received by [call centre / back-office team] for payment processing | [Yes / No] |
| Recurring billing | Stored payment credentials used for repeat transactions | [Yes / No] |
| Refunds and adjustments | Refund processing through [payment platform / acquirer portal] | Yes |
| Administrative access | Management access to payment applications, infrastructure, and security tools | Yes |
| Settlement and reconciliation | Transaction reconciliation using [finance system / acquirer portal] | Yes |

The cardholder data environment consists of the components that directly handle account data and the supporting security infrastructure that protects those components.

| Payment applications | [Payment Application Name], [E-commerce Platform], [POS Application], [Gateway Integration] |
| Databases and storage | Transaction databases, token vaults, file storage locations, backup repositories |
| End-user systems | Administrator workstations, call centre systems, jump hosts, support desktops with access to in-scope systems |
| Cloud services | [Cloud Provider], [Cloud Account / Subscription], hosted payment services, managed security services |
| Facilities | [Data Centre], [Head Office], [Retail Locations], [Call Centre], [Cloud Hosting Region] |
| Third-party services | Payment processors, payment gateways, managed service providers, hosting providers, support vendors, scanning vendors |

### Account Data Flows

The following table summarises the assessed cardholder data flows. Detailed data flow diagrams were reviewed during the assessment and are maintained by [Organisation Name] in [repository / GRC system / architecture library].

| DF-02 | [E-commerce Platform] | API over TLS | [Payment Gateway] | [PAN / Token / Authorisation data] | Encrypted API connection, authentication, restricted endpoints |
| DF-03 | POS terminal | Encrypted payment channel | [Processor / Acquirer] | Encrypted card data | Point-to-point encryption, terminal controls |

| DF-06 | [In-scope Systems] | Backup transfer | [Backup Repository] | [Encrypted backups containing account data] | Encryption, access control, retention controls |

| [Public Website Content Platform] | Does not accept or redirect payment data except through approved integration | Architecture review, payment flow validation |

### Scope Assumptions and Limitations

The assessment conclusions are based on the scope, evidence, interviews, observations, and technical testing performed during the assessment period. Any material changes to payment channels, system architecture, third-party services, cardholder data flows, or segmentation after the assessment period may affect the conclusions in this report.

The following assumptions were applied:

- Management provided complete and accurate information regarding payment processes, systems, data flows, and third-party relationships.
- Evidence supplied during the assessment period was representative of normal operating practices.
- Systems identified as out of scope remain segmented from the cardholder data environment.
- Service provider compliance information reviewed was current and applicable to the services used by [Organisation Name].
- Temporary compensating or remediation measures, where relied upon, remain in operation until permanent corrective action is completed.

## Executive Summary

### Overall Assessment Conclusion

Based on the evidence reviewed, interviews conducted, observations performed, and technical validation completed during the assessment period, [Organisation Name] was assessed as:

**Overall Status:** [Compliant / Compliant with Compensating Controls / Not Compliant Pending Remediation]

| Result Category | Count | Summary |
|---|---:|---|
| In place | [Number] | Controls were implemented, operating, and supported by evidence |
| Not in place | [Number] | Controls were missing, incomplete, ineffective, or not sufficiently evidenced |
| Not applicable | [Number] | Requirements did not apply to the assessed environment based on documented rationale |
| Compensating controls | [Number] | Alternative controls were used where the stated control could not be met directly |
| Targeted risk analysis used | [Number] | Risk-based frequencies or approaches were supported by documented analysis |

### Key Strengths

The assessment identified the following areas of strength:

- [Organisation Name] maintains documented cardholder data flows and network diagrams that align to the assessed payment processes.
- External-facing payment services use encrypted communication channels and are subject to regular vulnerability scanning.
- Access to in-scope administrative systems is restricted to approved personnel and protected using multi-factor authentication.
- Security logging is centralised for key in-scope systems and reviewed by [Security Operations Team / Managed Security Provider].
- Service provider relationships are tracked, and compliance attestations are collected for critical payment service providers.
- Cardholder data storage is limited to approved systems, with masking, truncation, encryption, or tokenisation used where appropriate.
- Incident response responsibilities for payment-related security events are documented and tested.

## Methodology

### Assessment Approach

The assessment was performed by [QSA Company Name] using a risk-based, evidence-led approach appropriate for a full PCI DSS v4.0.1 Report on Compliance.

The methodology included:

1. Planning and scope confirmation.
2. Review of payment channels and account data flows.
3. Identification of systems, people, processes, facilities, and service providers in scope.
4. Review of segmentation and scoping controls.
5. Collection and evaluation of policies, procedures, standards, inventories, diagrams, logs, tickets, reports, and system records.
6. Interviews with personnel responsible for governance, operations, development, security, infrastructure, and payment processing.
7. Observation of control operation where applicable.
8. Sampling of systems, users, events, changes, vulnerabilities, access reviews, and service provider records.
9. Technical validation of selected configurations and security controls.
10. Review of remediation evidence for findings identified during the assessment.
11. Preparation of this Report on Compliance and supporting assessment workpapers.

### Evidence Sources

Evidence reviewed included, but was not limited to:

| Evidence Type | Examples Reviewed |
|---|---|
| Governance documentation | Security policies, standards, procedures, risk assessments, management approvals |
| Scope documentation | Network diagrams, data flow diagrams, asset inventories, payment process descriptions |
| Technical configurations | Firewall rules, system hardening settings, encryption settings, authentication settings |
| Identity and access records | User lists, administrator accounts, access approvals, access review evidence |
| Vulnerability records | Internal scans, external scans, remediation tickets, retest results, penetration test reports |
| Logging and monitoring records | SIEM logs, alert records, incident tickets, daily monitoring evidence |
| Change records | Change approvals, implementation records, testing evidence, emergency change records |
| Development records | Secure coding standards, code review evidence, application testing results |
| Service provider records | Contracts, compliance attestations, responsibility matrices, due diligence records |
| Training records | Security awareness completion, role-based training, developer training |
| Incident response records | Incident response plan, test results, lessons learned, contact lists |
| Backup and recovery records | Backup schedules, restore tests, retention settings, encryption settings |

| PCI Program Manager | Scope, evidence coordination, remediation tracking, reporting |
| Network Engineering | Segmentation, firewall rules, network architecture, remote access |
| Infrastructure Operations | Server configuration, patching, backups, administrative access |
| Cloud Operations | Cloud account structure, identity, logging, network security, shared responsibility |
| Application Development | Secure development, code review, testing, deployment process |
| Database Administration | Data storage, encryption, access control, backup handling |
| Security Operations | Logging, alerting, vulnerability management, incident triage |
| Service Desk / Identity Administration | User provisioning, deprovisioning, access changes |
| Finance / Reconciliation | Settlement, refunds, reporting, acquirer portal access |
| Contact Centre / Retail Operations | Payment handling procedures, terminal controls, staff training |
| Vendor Management / Procurement | Service provider due diligence, contracts, compliance evidence |

### Sampling Method

Sampling was applied where populations were large and where a representative set of evidence was appropriate to validate control design and operating effectiveness.

Sampling considered:

- System criticality.
- Payment data exposure.
- Technology type.
- Location.
- Administrative access level.
- Time coverage across the reporting period.
- Recent changes or incidents.
- Prior assessment findings.
- Service provider dependency.
- Risk indicators from vulnerability or monitoring data.

Sample selections were documented in assessment workpapers. Where a sample exception indicated a possible systemic issue, additional evidence was requested and reviewed.

### Technical Validation Performed

Technical validation included the following activities where applicable:

| Validation Area | Activity |
|---|---|
| Network segmentation | Review of segmentation design, firewall rules, routing, and segmentation test results |
| External exposure | Review of internet-facing assets, external scan results, and remediation records |
| System configuration | Review of selected server, network, database, endpoint, and cloud configurations |
| Encryption | Review of encryption methods for transmission and storage of account data |
| Authentication | Review of password settings, multi-factor authentication, session controls, and privileged access |
| Logging | Review of log sources, alerting rules, retention settings, and monitoring records |
| Vulnerability management | Review of scan schedules, results, remediation actions, and retest evidence |
| Application security | Review of development practices, code review, testing records, and deployment controls |
| Physical security | Review of access restrictions and visitor controls at relevant facilities |
| Data discovery | Review of processes and tools used to identify stored account data |

### Assessment Result Definitions

| Result | Definition |
|---|---|
| In place | The control was implemented, operating as intended, and supported by sufficient evidence |
| Not in place | The control was absent, incomplete, ineffective, or not supported by sufficient evidence |
| Not applicable | The control did not apply to the assessed environment, and the rationale was validated |
| In place with compensating control | The stated control could not be met directly, but an alternative set of controls sufficiently addressed the risk |
| Not tested | The item was not tested because it was outside the validated scope or not applicable to the organisation |

**Condition**

In particular, review records did not consistently show reviewer identity, date of review, rule justification, disposition of obsolete rules, or approval of retained exceptions.

**Risk**

Without complete rule review evidence, unnecessary access may remain permitted into or within the cardholder data environment. This increases the risk of unauthorised access, lateral movement, and exposure of account data.

[Management response]

- Implement a standard rule review template.
- Require documented business justification for each retained rule.
- Track obsolete or excessive rules through change management until removed.
- Retain completed reviews in [GRC tool / ticketing system / repository].
- Perform management review of overdue remediation actions.

[Management response]
