PCI-047.title: Annual Re-Assessment & Updated AOC
PCI-047.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | [Compliance Owner / CISO] | [Effective Date] | PCI DSS v4.0.1 | Confidential |

## Purpose

This attestation confirms that [Organisation Name] has completed its annual PCI DSS re-assessment and has prepared an updated Attestation of Compliance for the current assessment period.

The purpose of this document is to provide management, acquiring banks, payment brands, customers, auditors, and other authorised stakeholders with a formal statement that:

- The cardholder data environment has been re-validated for the assessment year.
- The current scope of PCI DSS applicability has been reviewed and confirmed.
- Required assessment activities have been completed using the appropriate PCI DSS v4.0.1 validation method.
- Supporting evidence has been collected, reviewed, and retained.
- The updated Attestation of Compliance accurately reflects the organisation’s compliance status as of the assessment date.
- Any identified gaps, compensating controls, remediation actions, or residual risks have been documented and approved through the organisation’s governance process.

This attestation is intended to support the annual compliance cycle and does not replace the formal Attestation of Compliance, Self-Assessment Questionnaire, Report on Compliance, or any other validation artefact required by acquiring banks, payment brands, or contractual obligations.

## Scope

This attestation applies to the annual re-assessment of [Organisation Name]’s PCI DSS environment for the assessment period covering [Assessment Start Date] to [Assessment End Date].

The scope includes all people, processes, technologies, facilities, service providers, and network segments that store, process, transmit, or can impact the security of cardholder data or sensitive authentication data.

The following scope elements were reviewed as part of the annual re-assessment:

| Scope Area | Included in Re-Assessment | Description / Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Cardholder data environment | Yes | Systems, applications, databases, network components, and security services involved in cardholder data processing. |
| Connected-to and security-impacting systems | Yes | Systems that could affect the security of the cardholder data environment, including identity services, logging, monitoring, vulnerability management, and administrative access platforms. |
| Payment channels | Yes | [E-commerce / mail order / telephone order / in-person / recurring billing / other applicable channels]. |
| Payment applications | Yes | [Payment application names or descriptions]. |
| Network segmentation controls | Yes | Firewalls, access control lists, segmentation testing, routing controls, and supporting documentation. |
| Cloud and hosted environments | [Yes / No / Not Applicable] | [Cloud providers, hosting locations, managed platforms, or shared responsibility boundaries]. |
| Third-party service providers | Yes | Service providers that store, process, transmit, or can affect the security of account data. |
| Physical locations | [Yes / No / Not Applicable] | [Data centres, offices, call centres, retail sites, storage locations, or other relevant facilities]. |
| Policies, standards, and procedures | Yes | Governance documents supporting the PCI DSS control environment. |
| Security operations processes | Yes | Monitoring, logging, incident response, vulnerability management, change management, access management, and secure configuration processes. |
| Personnel with PCI DSS responsibilities | Yes | Employees, contractors, administrators, developers, support teams, service owners, and compliance stakeholders. |

The following environments, systems, or services were excluded from the assessment scope based on documented scoping analysis:

| Excluded Item | Reason for Exclusion | Validation Performed |
|---|---|---|
| [System / environment / location] | [No storage, processing, transmission, or security impact on account data] | [Segmentation review / data flow review / architecture review / management confirmation] |
| [System / environment / location] | [Reason] | [Validation activity] |

The annual scope review considered:

- Current cardholder data flows.
- Network diagrams and system inventories.
- Payment processing methods and channels.
- Data storage locations and retention practices.
- Administrative access paths.
- Remote access methods.
- Security monitoring and logging coverage.
- Encryption and key management practices.
- Vulnerability management and penetration testing results.
- Changes to systems, applications, service providers, architecture, or business processes since the prior assessment.
- Applicability of any compensating or alternative controls.
- Service provider responsibilities and current compliance status.

## Attestation Statement

On behalf of [Organisation Name], the undersigned attests that an annual re-assessment of the organisation’s PCI DSS environment has been completed for the assessment period ending [Assessment End Date].

Based on the assessment activities performed, evidence reviewed, and management representations obtained, [Organisation Name] attests that:

1. The scope of the cardholder data environment has been reviewed, validated, and documented.
2. Cardholder data flows have been reviewed and confirmed as current.
3. System inventories, network diagrams, and security architecture documentation have been reviewed and updated where necessary.
4. The applicable PCI DSS v4.0.1 validation method has been completed for the organisation’s merchant, service provider, and payment environment profile.
5. The updated Attestation of Compliance has been prepared and reviewed for accuracy.
6. All in-scope systems, processes, and control owners were included in the assessment activities applicable to their responsibilities.
7. Third-party service provider reliance has been reviewed, and current compliance evidence has been obtained or formally risk-assessed where evidence was unavailable or incomplete.
8. Evidence supporting the assessment has been retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.
9. Any control gaps or remediation items identified during the assessment have been documented, assigned to accountable owners, and tracked through governance oversight.
10. Where compensating or alternative controls are used, they have been documented, justified, approved, and supported by evidence demonstrating that the intended security outcome is achieved.
11. No known material misstatement has been included in the updated Attestation of Compliance.
12. No known cardholder data environment component has been intentionally omitted from the assessment scope.
13. Management has reviewed the results of the annual re-assessment and accepts responsibility for maintaining PCI DSS compliance throughout the year.

The annual re-assessment outcome is recorded as follows:

| Assessment Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Assessment period | [Assessment Start Date] to [Assessment End Date] |
| Assessment completion date | [Completion Date] |
| Validation type | [SAQ / ROC / Other validation method] |
| Assessment performed by | [Internal Assessor / Qualified Security Assessor / Internal Security Assessor / Other] |
| Compliance status | [Compliant / Compliant with documented remediation plan / Not compliant pending remediation] |
| Updated AOC prepared | [Yes / No] |
| Updated AOC approved | [Yes / No / Pending] |
| Updated AOC submission required | [Yes / No] |
| Submission recipient | [Acquirer / Payment Brand / Customer / Other] |
| Submission due date | [Due Date] |
| Material scope changes since prior assessment | [Yes / No] |
| Open remediation items | [Number] |
| Approved compensating or alternative controls | [Number / None] |
| Management acceptance obtained | [Yes / No] |

Where the assessment status is not fully compliant, this attestation confirms that the organisation has documented the outstanding items and is managing remediation through an approved corrective action plan.

| Remediation Item | Risk Rating | Owner | Target Completion Date | Current Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Issue or gap summary] | [High / Medium / Low] | [Owner] | [Date] | [Open / In Progress / Completed / Risk Accepted] |
| [Issue or gap summary] | [High / Medium / Low] | [Owner] | [Date] | [Open / In Progress / Completed / Risk Accepted] |

This attestation remains valid only for the assessment state represented by the evidence reviewed as of [Assessment Completion Date]. Significant changes to the cardholder data environment, payment processes, service provider arrangements, security architecture, or control operation may require re-validation before the next scheduled annual assessment.

## Signatory & Authority

The individuals below have authority to approve this attestation and confirm the accuracy of the annual re-assessment statements within their areas of responsibility.

| Role | Name | Responsibility | Signature | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | [Name] | Confirms executive accountability for PCI DSS compliance and approves submission of the updated AOC where required. | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Chief Information Security Officer / Security Lead | [Name] | Confirms security control oversight, assessment coordination, and remediation governance. | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Compliance Owner | [Name] | Confirms assessment evidence, compliance documentation, and AOC preparation have been completed. | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Payment Operations Owner | [Name] | Confirms payment processes, channels, and operational responsibilities are accurately represented. | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Technology Owner | [Name] | Confirms in-scope systems, infrastructure, architecture, and technical control evidence are accurate. | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Assessor, where applicable | [Name / Firm] | Confirms assessment activities were performed and results recorded in the relevant validation artefacts. | [Signature] | [Date] |

By signing this attestation, each signatory confirms that, to the best of their knowledge:

- Information provided for the annual re-assessment is complete and accurate.
- Relevant changes during the assessment period have been disclosed.
- Known gaps, exceptions, and remediation actions have not been concealed.
- Supporting evidence has been made available for review.
- The updated Attestation of Compliance reflects the current compliance status of the organisation.
- Ongoing compliance responsibilities will continue to be performed after the annual assessment date.

Delegated approval may be accepted only where formally authorised by [Organisation Name]’s governance process. Delegated signatories must have sufficient knowledge of the relevant PCI DSS responsibilities and the authority to approve the attestation on behalf of the accountable role.

## Evidence Referenced

The annual re-assessment and updated Attestation of Compliance were supported by the following evidence categories.

| Evidence Category | Evidence Reviewed | Evidence Owner | Repository / Location | Review Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current Attestation of Compliance | Updated AOC for the assessment period | [Compliance Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Assessment workbook or questionnaire | Completed validation responses and assessor notes | [Compliance Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Cardholder data flow diagrams | Current diagrams showing storage, processing, and transmission of account data | [Architecture Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Network diagrams | Current network and segmentation diagrams for in-scope environments | [Network Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Asset inventory | In-scope systems, applications, databases, network devices, and security tools | [Technology Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Data inventory | Locations and retention periods for account data | [Data Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Segmentation validation | Segmentation test results and firewall rule reviews | [Network Security Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Vulnerability management evidence | Internal and external vulnerability scans, remediation records, and scan attestations | [Security Operations Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Penetration testing evidence | Penetration test reports, scope statements, remediation evidence, and retest results | [Security Testing Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Secure configuration evidence | Configuration standards, baseline reviews, hardening evidence, and exception records | [Infrastructure Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Access management evidence | User access reviews, privileged access records, authentication settings, and joiner-mover-leaver samples | [Identity Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Logging and monitoring evidence | Log source inventory, alerting procedures, monitoring samples, and retention evidence | [Security Operations Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Incident response evidence | Incident response plan, testing records, contact lists, and post-incident review records | [Incident Response Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Change management evidence | Change records for in-scope systems and security-impacting changes | [Change Manager] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Cryptography and key management evidence | Encryption design, certificate records, key management procedures, and key rotation evidence | [Cryptography Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Secure development evidence | Secure coding standards, code review records, application testing, and release approvals | [Application Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Service provider evidence | Current AOCs, responsibility matrices, contracts, and monitoring records | [Third-Party Risk Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Policy and procedure evidence | Approved PCI DSS-related policies, standards, and operational procedures | [Policy Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Training and awareness evidence | Security awareness records and role-based training completion evidence | [Training Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Risk and exception records | Approved exceptions, compensating controls, alternative control documentation, and residual risk approvals | [Risk Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Management review records | Meeting minutes, approval records, dashboards, and remediation tracking reports | [Compliance Owner] | [Repository / path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |

Evidence must be sufficient to demonstrate that controls were in place and operating as represented during the assessment period. Evidence should be traceable to the relevant system, process, owner, date, and assessment activity.

The following evidence quality expectations apply:

- Evidence must be current for the assessment period.
- Evidence must be complete and unaltered.
- Screenshots must show relevant system names, timestamps, settings, and user context where appropriate.
- Reports must identify the assessed scope, date performed, methodology, results, and remediation status.
- Sampling must be documented where not every item is reviewed.
- Assessor requests, management responses, and evidence submissions must be retained.
- Evidence supporting exclusions from scope must be clear and defensible.
- Service provider evidence must be current and aligned to the services relied upon by [Organisation Name].
- Remediation evidence must show both correction and validation of effectiveness.
- Exceptions must include business justification, risk assessment, expiry date, and approval.

## Frequency

The annual PCI DSS re-assessment and updated Attestation of Compliance must be completed at least once every twelve months, or more frequently where required by acquiring banks, payment brands, customer contracts, material business change, or significant change to the cardholder data environment.

The annual cycle is managed according to the following indicative timeline:

| Activity | Target Timing | Accountable Owner | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Confirm assessment approach and required validation type | 120 days before due date | [Compliance Owner] | Assessment plan and stakeholder list |
| Refresh scope and cardholder data flows | 100 days before due date | [Architecture Owner] | Updated scope record and data flow diagrams |
| Confirm in-scope systems and service providers | 90 days before due date | [Technology Owner / Third-Party Risk Owner] | Updated inventory and service provider register |
| Collect preliminary control evidence | 75 days before due date | [Control Owners] | Evidence package |
| Complete technical testing and remediation checks | 60 days before due date | [Security Operations Owner] | Scan, test, and remediation records |
| Perform assessor review or internal validation | 45 days before due date | [Assessor / Compliance Owner] | Assessment findings and evidence requests |
| Resolve evidence gaps and control issues | 30 days before due date | [Control Owners] | Remediation evidence and updated tracking |
| Prepare updated AOC and related validation artefacts | 20 days before due date | [Compliance Owner] | Draft AOC and assessment package |
| Management review and approval | 10 days before due date | [Executive Sponsor] | Signed attestation and approval record |
| Submit updated AOC where required | By due date | [Compliance Owner] | Submission confirmation |
| Conduct post-assessment lessons learned | Within 30 days after submission | [Compliance Owner] | Improvement actions for next cycle |

A re-assessment, partial reassessment, or management review must be triggered before the next annual cycle if any of the following occur:

- A new payment channel is introduced.
- Cardholder data storage, processing, or transmission changes materially.
- A major system, application, hosting platform, or network architecture change is implemented.
- Network segmentation controls are redesigned or materially changed.
- A new third-party service provider is engaged for payment or security-impacting services.
- A service provider’s compliance status changes materially.
- A significant security incident affects or may affect the cardholder data environment.
- A material vulnerability or control failure is identified.
- A merger, acquisition, outsourcing arrangement, or divestment affects the cardholder data environment.
- An acquiring bank, payment brand, customer, or regulator requests updated validation.

Ownership for ongoing compliance between annual assessments remains with the accountable control owners. Annual re-assessment is not a substitute for continuous control operation, monitoring, vulnerability management, change governance, or risk management.

## Records & Retention

[Organisation Name] must retain records supporting the annual re-assessment and updated Attestation of Compliance in a secure, access-controlled repository.

The following records must be retained:

| Record Type | Minimum Retention Period | Record Owner | Storage Location | Access Restrictions |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Signed attestation document | [Retention Period] | [Compliance Owner] | [Repository / path] | Compliance, Security, Audit, Executive Management |
| Updated Attestation of Compliance | [Retention Period] | [Compliance Owner] | [Repository / path] | Compliance, Security, Audit, Executive Management |
| Completed assessment questionnaire or report | [Retention Period] | [Compliance Owner] | [Repository / path] | Compliance, Security, Audit, Assessor |
| Evidence package | [Retention Period] | [Compliance Owner] | [Repository / path] | Authorised assessment stakeholders only |
| Scope documentation | [Retention Period] | [Architecture Owner] | [Repository / path] | Compliance, Security, Architecture |
| Data flow diagrams and network diagrams | [Retention Period] | [Architecture Owner] | [Repository / path] | Compliance, Security, Architecture, Network Teams |
| Service provider compliance evidence | [Retention Period] | [Third-Party Risk Owner] | [Repository / path] | Compliance, Legal, Security, Third-Party Risk |
| Remediation and exception records | [Retention Period] | [Risk Owner] | [Repository / path] | Compliance, Security, Risk Owners |
| Management approval records | [Retention Period] | [Compliance Owner] | [Repository / path] | Compliance, Audit, Executive Management |
| AOC submission confirmations | [Retention Period] | [Compliance Owner] | [Repository / path] | Compliance, Legal, Executive Management |

Records must be protected against unauthorised access, alteration, deletion, and disclosure. Because PCI DSS evidence may include sensitive system configuration details, vulnerability information, network diagrams, security procedures, and payment environment details, access must be limited to personnel with a legitimate business need.

Records must be managed according to the following requirements:

- Store final approved records separately from working drafts.
- Maintain evidence integrity, including original file names, timestamps, and source information where practical.
- Retain assessor communications and evidence request logs where they support assessment conclusions.
- Retain approvals for scope decisions, exclusions, compensating controls, alternative controls, and exceptions.
- Retain remediation evidence and closure approvals for issues identified during the assessment.
- Retain submission confirmations where the AOC is provided to an acquiring bank, payment brand, customer, or other authorised party.
- Do not store sensitive authentication data as part of assessment evidence.
- Redact account data from evidence unless explicitly required and approved for assessment purposes.
- Encrypt repositories containing sensitive assessment evidence where supported by the storage platform.
- Review access to the evidence repository at least annually and upon personnel role changes.
- Dispose of expired records securely in accordance with [Organisation Name]’s information retention and disposal requirements.

The Compliance Owner is responsible for confirming that the final signed attestation, updated AOC, and supporting assessment records are complete, approved, securely stored, and available for authorised audit or stakeholder review.

PCI-048.title: BAU Evidence Repository (continuous)
PCI-048.content:
## What This Evidences

The BAU Evidence Repository demonstrates that PCI DSS v4.0.1 business-as-usual security activities are operating continuously throughout the year, not only at assessment time. It supports the control intent of maintaining ongoing logs, vulnerability scans, security reviews, monitoring outputs, remediation evidence, and operational records for systems and processes in scope for the cardholder data environment.

This artifact is collected evidence, not an authored document. Do not create or simulate records. Evidence must be exported or captured from the organisation’s live operational systems, tools, dashboards, repositories, and ticketing workflows.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect evidence from the systems that generate and manage security operations records in your environment, such as:

- SIEM or log management platform: [SIEM/log platform name]
- Vulnerability scanning tool: [scanner name]
- File integrity monitoring or endpoint security platform: [tool name]
- IT service management or ticketing system: [ITSM/ticketing tool name]
- Change management platform: [change tool name]
- Access review or identity governance tool: [IAM/IGA tool name]
- Configuration management or asset inventory system: [CMDB/asset system name]
- Security awareness or training portal: [training platform name]
- Compliance evidence repository or GRC platform: [GRC/evidence repository name]
- Cloud security, network security, or firewall management consoles: [tool names]

## How To Collect

1. Confirm the current PCI DSS scope, including relevant systems, networks, applications, service providers, and processes.
2. Identify the evidence categories required for year-round BAU operation, including logs, scan results, review records, incidents, changes, remediation tickets, and access reviews.
3. In each source system, filter records to the assessment period: [start date] to [end date].
4. Apply scope filters where available, such as asset tags, network segments, application names, environment labels, system owner, or PCI scope indicator.
5. Export reports in native or audit-friendly format, such as PDF, CSV, JSON, or system-generated report package.
6. Capture screenshots only where exports are not available, ensuring the screenshot shows the system name, date/time, filters, and relevant record details.
7. Save each evidence item using a consistent naming convention, such as `[PCI]_[Evidence Type]_[System]_[Period]_[Export Date]`.
8. Record the evidence source, collection date, collector, system owner, and any filters used in [evidence index/register].
9. Store the collected evidence in [GRC platform/evidence repository/secure SharePoint location].
10. Link evidence items to relevant BAU activities, tickets, reviews, or remediation records.

## What To Capture

Capture enough detail to prove the activity occurred, was reviewed, and was followed up where needed:

- Evidence source system name and report/export timestamp
- Assessment period or date range covered
- Scope filters used, such as PCI asset tag, segment, application, or environment
- Log review records, alert queues, escalations, and closure status
- Vulnerability scan schedules, completed scan results, severity ratings, affected assets, and remediation status
- Authenticated scan status where applicable
- Change tickets showing approval, testing, implementation, and closure
- Access review records showing reviewer, population reviewed, decisions, exceptions, and completion date
- Incident/security event tickets showing triage, investigation, containment, resolution, and lessons learned
- Configuration, asset, or inventory extracts showing in-scope systems
- Evidence of recurring review meetings or operational dashboards where used
- Exception records, risk acceptances, compensating actions, and target remediation dates

## Frequency & Owner

- Collection frequency: Monthly at minimum, and additionally before each formal assessment milestone.
- High-risk evidence, such as critical vulnerability remediation, security alerts, and incident records, should be collected as events occur.
- Evidence owner: [PCI Compliance Manager/GRC Lead].
- Source system owners: [SOC Manager], [IT Operations Manager], [Network Manager], [Application Owner], [IAM Owner], and [Vulnerability Management Owner].
- Collection operator: [assigned evidence coordinator or control owner].

## Retention & Storage

Store evidence in [approved evidence repository] with access restricted to authorised compliance, security, audit, and control owner personnel. Retain evidence for at least [retention period], or longer where required by contractual, legal, or assessment needs.

Maintain integrity by preserving original exports where possible, avoiding manual alteration, and retaining metadata such as export date, collector, and source system. Use version control or immutable storage where available. Do not store unnecessary cardholder data, sensitive authentication data, secrets, or excessive personal data in the repository.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the BAU Evidence Repository as sufficient when:

- Evidence is system-generated or directly exported from authoritative operational tools.
- The collection covers the full assessment period, not only a point-in-time sample.
- Records are clearly linked to in-scope PCI systems, applications, networks, or processes.
- Evidence shows recurring operation of logs, scans, reviews, monitoring, remediation, and governance activities.
- Exceptions and failures are tracked through documented tickets or remediation records.
- Each evidence item includes source, date range, collection date, and responsible owner.
- Evidence is complete, readable, tamper-resistant, and stored in an access-controlled repository.
- The repository index allows an assessor to trace each BAU activity to supporting records quickly.

SWF-001.title: Swift Architecture Type Determination
SWF-001.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-SWIFT-ARCH-001] | 1.0 | [CISO / SWIFT Security Officer] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework | Internal |

## Purpose

This policy establishes the mandatory requirements for determining, documenting, approving, and maintaining the organisation’s SWIFT architecture type. Correct architecture type determination is required to ensure that all SWIFT-related systems, interfaces, networks, users, service providers, and security controls are identified and managed appropriately.

The organisation shall determine and document whether each SWIFT environment is classified as architecture type A1, A2, A3, A4, or B, based on the technical design and operational use of SWIFT messaging services. The determination shall be sufficiently evidenced to support internal governance, external assurance, independent assessment, and ongoing control implementation.

## Scope

This policy applies to all environments, platforms, services, systems, infrastructure, applications, users, processes, and third parties that support, connect to, host, administer, or exchange messages through SWIFT services on behalf of the organisation.

This policy applies to:

- SWIFT messaging interfaces and connectivity components.
- SWIFT-related application servers, middleware, databases, gateways, operator workstations, and administrative workstations.
- Systems that create, modify, approve, transmit, receive, store, or process SWIFT messages or related payment instructions.
- Manual, semi-automated, and fully automated SWIFT message workflows.
- On-premises, hosted, outsourced, cloud, and service bureau arrangements.
- Production, disaster recovery, backup, test, development, and support environments where SWIFT-related connectivity or data is present.
- Third parties that provide SWIFT connectivity, operations, hosting, maintenance, administration, monitoring, security, or support services.
- Changes to architecture, connectivity, message flows, hosting, administration, or outsourcing that may affect the applicable architecture type.

This policy does not replace detailed SWIFT security standards, technical build standards, operational procedures, or third-party risk management requirements. Those documents shall align with the architecture type determined under this policy.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain a documented SWIFT architecture type determination for each SWIFT environment, including production, disaster recovery, and any non-production environment that connects to SWIFT services or handles SWIFT message data.

2. The organisation shall classify each SWIFT environment as one of the following architecture types: A1, A2, A3, A4, or B.

3. The organisation shall determine the architecture type based on the actual implemented architecture, not solely on contractual descriptions, vendor product names, historical classifications, or management assumptions.

4. The organisation shall use the following criteria when determining the applicable architecture type:

| Architecture Type | Mandatory Determination Criteria |
|---|---|
| A1 | The organisation uses its own SWIFT interface or messaging application within its own operating environment, and SWIFT message creation, processing, approval, or transmission capabilities are hosted or operated by the organisation or under its direct technical control. |
| A2 | The organisation uses a SWIFT interface or messaging application where some components or operating responsibilities are provided by a third party, but the organisation retains direct access to SWIFT messaging functionality or infrastructure requiring protection within its environment. |
| A3 | The organisation uses a connector, middleware, or application integration arrangement where SWIFT messaging is initiated or processed through locally managed components, while some SWIFT connectivity or messaging services may be provided externally. |
| A4 | The organisation uses an externally hosted or outsourced SWIFT interface or messaging service, but retains local infrastructure, applications, user access, credentials, message initiation, message approval, or administrative activities relevant to SWIFT operations. |
| B | The organisation does not host or operate a SWIFT interface or connectivity infrastructure within its environment and uses a third-party service provider to perform SWIFT connectivity or messaging services, while the organisation may still initiate, approve, or provide instructions to the provider through agreed channels. |

5. The organisation shall document the rationale for the selected architecture type, including the systems, data flows, user activities, administration points, connectivity model, hosting model, and third-party dependencies considered in the determination.

6. The organisation shall not select a lower-risk architecture type for convenience, control reduction, audit simplification, or because a third party performs some SWIFT-related activities.

7. Where uncertainty exists between two or more architecture types, the organisation shall apply the more conservative classification until the SWIFT Security Officer, Technology Owner, and independent assurance function agree on the appropriate determination.

8. The organisation shall maintain an approved SWIFT architecture record containing, at minimum:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Environment name | Name of the SWIFT environment, such as production, disaster recovery, test, or support. |
| Architecture type | Selected type: A1, A2, A3, A4, or B. |
| Business purpose | Business function supported by the environment. |
| SWIFT services used | SWIFT messaging or connectivity services used by the organisation. |
| Hosting model | On-premises, hosted, outsourced, cloud, service bureau, or hybrid model. |
| Key components | SWIFT interfaces, gateways, middleware, databases, operator workstations, administrative systems, security tools, and supporting infrastructure. |
| Message flows | How SWIFT messages are created, approved, transmitted, received, stored, and reconciled. |
| User groups | Business users, operators, approvers, administrators, support teams, and third-party users with SWIFT-related access. |
| Privileged access points | Administrative consoles, service accounts, remote access methods, privileged workstations, and third-party support access. |
| Third-party dependencies | Service bureaus, hosting providers, managed service providers, vendors, cloud providers, and support organisations involved in SWIFT operations. |
| Network boundaries | Segmentation zones, connectivity paths, remote access paths, and interfaces with enterprise systems. |
| Data locations | Locations where SWIFT messages, message files, logs, credentials, configuration files, and backups are stored or processed. |
| Determination rationale | Explanation supporting the selected architecture type. |
| Evidence references | Diagrams, contracts, configuration extracts, asset inventories, workflow documents, and assessment records supporting the determination. |
| Approval records | Names, roles, approval dates, and review outcomes. |

9. The organisation shall maintain current architecture diagrams for each SWIFT environment that show the components and relationships necessary to support architecture type determination.

10. SWIFT architecture diagrams shall include, as applicable:

 - SWIFT interfaces and messaging applications.
 - Connectivity gateways and communication components.
 - Middleware, file transfer, queueing, and integration platforms.
 - Core banking, treasury, payments, sanctions screening, fraud monitoring, reconciliation, and back-office systems connected to SWIFT workflows.
 - Operator and administrator workstations.
 - Authentication and identity infrastructure.
 - Logging, monitoring, and security tooling.
 - Firewalls, network zones, jump hosts, remote access paths, and management networks.
 - Service bureau, hosting provider, managed service provider, vendor, or cloud connectivity.
 - Disaster recovery and backup components.
 - Data stores containing SWIFT messages, logs, credentials, or configuration data.

11. The organisation shall maintain documented data flow and process flow information showing how SWIFT messages or instructions are created, validated, approved, transmitted, received, repaired, cancelled, investigated, reconciled, archived, and deleted.

12. The organisation shall identify and document the boundary of the SWIFT-related environment for each architecture type determination.

13. The SWIFT-related environment boundary shall include any component that can affect the confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, authorisation, transmission, or processing of SWIFT messages or SWIFT-related credentials.

14. The organisation shall identify all third parties involved in SWIFT operations and shall document their role in relation to architecture type determination.

15. The organisation shall not rely solely on a third-party attestation, contract, or service description to determine the organisation’s architecture type; the organisation shall validate how the service is actually used and integrated into its environment.

16. The organisation shall document whether the third party performs any of the following SWIFT-related activities:

 - Hosting SWIFT interfaces or connectivity components.
 - Operating SWIFT messaging services.
 - Providing service bureau functionality.
 - Providing remote administration or technical support.
 - Managing security configurations, certificates, keys, or credentials.
 - Managing infrastructure, operating systems, databases, middleware, or network components.
 - Performing transaction processing, message repair, approval, release, reconciliation, or monitoring.
 - Storing SWIFT messages, message data, logs, configuration files, backups, or authentication material.

17. The organisation shall maintain an asset inventory aligned to the SWIFT architecture type determination.

18. The SWIFT asset inventory shall identify whether each asset is in scope, supporting, connected, third-party managed, or out of scope, and shall include the justification for that classification.

19. The organisation shall ensure that all control scoping activities for SWIFT security are based on the approved architecture type and documented SWIFT environment boundary.

20. The organisation shall review the architecture type determination before implementing any material change to SWIFT-related systems, connectivity, hosting, administration, service providers, message flows, or business processes.

21. The organisation shall require formal approval before any architecture change that may alter the SWIFT architecture type or SWIFT environment boundary is implemented in production.

22. Material changes requiring review shall include, at minimum:

| Change Type | Examples |
|---|---|
| Connectivity change | New SWIFT connectivity method, service bureau connection, network path, remote access method, or external interface. |
| Hosting change | Migration to cloud, outsourced hosting, managed infrastructure, new data centre, or service provider environment. |
| Application change | New payments platform, treasury platform, sanctions screening system, file transfer solution, middleware, or SWIFT interface. |
| Operational change | Outsourcing SWIFT operations, introducing managed services, changing approval workflows, or modifying message release responsibilities. |
| Access change | New privileged access route, vendor support model, administrative workstation, service account model, or authentication mechanism. |
| Data flow change | New message source, message destination, storage location, backup method, logging destination, or reporting interface. |
| Resilience change | New disaster recovery architecture, failover process, backup service, or recovery site. |
| Third-party change | New service bureau, hosting provider, managed service provider, software vendor, support provider, or subcontractor. |

23. The organisation shall integrate SWIFT architecture type determination into change management, technology risk assessment, third-party risk management, security architecture review, and internal assurance planning.

24. The organisation shall retain evidence supporting architecture type determination for the current assessment period and for at least [retention period] thereafter.

25. The organisation shall ensure that personnel involved in SWIFT governance, operations, architecture, security, compliance, audit, and third-party management understand the approved architecture type and its implications for security control scope.

26. The organisation shall maintain traceability between the architecture type determination, SWIFT asset inventory, network diagrams, data flow diagrams, access model, third-party register, risk assessments, and control implementation records.

27. The organisation shall revalidate the architecture type when SWIFT guidance, services, operating models, or the organisation’s SWIFT usage materially changes.

28. The organisation shall ensure that architecture type determination is approved before submitting any SWIFT security attestation or equivalent assurance statement.

29. The organisation shall prohibit unsupported, undocumented, or informally agreed SWIFT connectivity arrangements.

30. The organisation shall escalate any discrepancy between documented architecture and observed implementation to the SWIFT Security Officer and Technology Owner for investigation and remediation.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board or Executive Risk Committee | Provides oversight of SWIFT-related risk and ensures adequate governance, accountability, and resourcing for secure SWIFT operations. |
| Chief Information Security Officer | Owns enterprise security governance for SWIFT, ensures this policy is implemented, and approves significant risk decisions related to architecture type determination. |
| SWIFT Security Officer | Maintains the SWIFT architecture type determination, coordinates reviews, validates supporting evidence, and ensures alignment between architecture classification and security control scope. |
| SWIFT Business Owner | Confirms business processes, message flows, user activities, approval workflows, and third-party operational dependencies relevant to the architecture type. |
| Technology Owner | Provides technical information on SWIFT infrastructure, applications, integrations, connectivity, hosting, disaster recovery, and operational support arrangements. |
| Enterprise Architect / Security Architect | Reviews architecture diagrams, environment boundaries, network flows, data flows, and integration patterns to support accurate classification. |
| Infrastructure and Network Teams | Maintain accurate information on servers, network zones, firewalls, connectivity paths, remote access, monitoring, backup, and resilience components. |
| Application Owners | Identify applications that create, process, approve, transmit, receive, store, or interact with SWIFT messages or instructions. |
| Identity and Access Management Team | Provides information on user access, privileged access, service accounts, authentication, authorisation, and third-party access relevant to SWIFT operations. |
| Third-Party Risk Management Team | Maintains records of SWIFT-related service providers, validates contractual and operational dependencies, and supports review of outsourced or hosted services. |
| Change Advisory Board | Ensures SWIFT-related changes are assessed for architecture type impact before approval and implementation. |
| Compliance / GRC Function | Maintains governance records, monitors adherence to this policy, supports assurance readiness, and coordinates evidence retention. |
| Internal Audit | Performs independent review of architecture type determination, evidence quality, governance effectiveness, and alignment between documented scope and actual implementation. |
| Service Providers | Provide accurate and timely information required to validate architecture type, including service descriptions, roles and responsibilities, data handling, access methods, hosting arrangements, and support models. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy is mandatory for all personnel, contractors, and third parties involved in SWIFT-related services or environments.

The SWIFT Security Officer, supported by the Compliance / GRC function, shall monitor compliance through scheduled reviews, evidence validation, change assessments, and periodic control assurance activities.

The following monitoring activities shall be performed:

| Activity | Frequency | Owner | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Formal review of SWIFT architecture type determination | At least annually | SWIFT Security Officer | Approved architecture determination record |
| Review of SWIFT architecture diagrams | At least annually and after material change | Technology Owner | Current diagrams with approval record |
| Review of SWIFT data flows and process flows | At least annually and after material change | SWIFT Business Owner | Data flow diagrams and process documentation |
| Reconciliation of SWIFT asset inventory to architecture scope | At least quarterly | Technology Owner | Asset inventory review record |
| Review of third-party SWIFT dependencies | At least annually and upon provider change | Third-Party Risk Management Team | Supplier register, contracts, service descriptions |
| Change impact review for SWIFT architecture type | For every material change | Change Advisory Board | Change record and architecture impact assessment |
| Validation before SWIFT assurance submission | Prior to submission | CISO / SWIFT Security Officer | Evidence pack and approval record |
| Independent assurance review | As scheduled in the audit plan | Internal Audit | Audit report or review memo |

Non-compliance shall be recorded, risk assessed, assigned an owner, and tracked to remediation. Where non-compliance could affect the accuracy of SWIFT security scoping or external assurance, the issue shall be escalated to the CISO and relevant executive risk forum.

Examples of non-compliance include:

- No documented architecture type determination exists.
- Architecture type is undocumented, outdated, or unsupported by evidence.
- Architecture diagrams do not reflect the implemented environment.
- Third-party SWIFT dependencies are omitted or inaccurately described.
- Material architecture changes are implemented without classification review.
- SWIFT-connected systems are excluded from scope without documented justification.
- The selected architecture type is inconsistent with actual hosting, connectivity, access, or operational arrangements.
- Control implementation or assurance activity is based on an incorrect architecture type.

Enforcement actions may include mandatory remediation, suspension of unapproved connectivity, restriction of privileged or third-party access, change rollback, additional assurance review, risk acceptance escalation, contractual action with service providers, or disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policies.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy are permitted only where there is a documented business need, a defined compensating control, and formal risk acceptance.

An exception shall not be used to avoid determining the correct SWIFT architecture type. The architecture type shall be documented even where supporting evidence is incomplete, disputed, or pending validation.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception title | Short description of the requested exception. |
| Requestor | Individual and business area requesting the exception. |
| Affected environment | SWIFT environment, system, process, or provider affected. |
| Policy requirement impacted | Specific policy requirement for which exception is requested. |
| Business justification | Reason compliance cannot be achieved within the required timeframe. |
| Risk assessment | Security, operational, compliance, assurance, and financial crime risk implications. |
| Compensating controls | Controls that reduce risk while the exception remains active. |
| Remediation plan | Actions required to achieve compliance. |
| Target remediation date | Date by which the exception will be closed. |
| Approval | Required approval from the CISO or delegated risk authority. |

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed [maximum exception period] without reapproval. Exceptions affecting SWIFT assurance, architecture classification, environment boundary, or external reporting shall require approval from the CISO and notification to the relevant executive risk forum.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as policy non-compliance unless renewed through the formal exception process before expiry.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to SWIFT services, architecture, connectivity, hosting, operations, third-party arrangements, security expectations, or organisational risk appetite.

The SWIFT Security Officer shall coordinate review and maintenance of this policy with input from the CISO, Technology Owner, SWIFT Business Owner, Enterprise Architecture, Compliance / GRC, Third-Party Risk Management, and Internal Audit.

The review shall confirm that:

- Architecture type criteria remain current and practical for the organisation’s SWIFT operating model.
- Roles and responsibilities remain accurate.
- Monitoring activities remain appropriate and effective.
- Required evidence supports assurance and audit needs.
- The policy aligns with related governance documents, including change management, asset management, access control, third-party risk management, network security, incident management, business continuity, and information security risk management policies.
- Lessons learned from incidents, audits, assessments, control testing, and material changes are incorporated.

Policy changes shall be approved by the CISO or designated policy approval authority. Approved versions shall be published in the organisation’s controlled policy repository. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.

SWF-002.title: Swift Secure Zone Scope Document
SWF-002.content:
# Swift Secure Zone Scope Document

| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [POL-SWIFT-SSZ-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [Head of Information Security] |
| Effective Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Framework | SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework |
| Classification | Internal Confidential |

## Purpose

This Policy defines the mandatory scope of the Swift Secure Zone within [Organisation Name]. It establishes which systems, infrastructure, operators, service accounts, administrative functions, connectivity paths, and supporting processes are included in the protected environment used to access, operate, administer, monitor, or support SWIFT services.

The purpose of this Policy is to ensure that all components and personnel capable of influencing the confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, message processing, or operational security of SWIFT-related activities are correctly identified, documented, controlled, monitored, and maintained within an approved security boundary.

This Policy supports consistent implementation of secure architecture, access control, change management, vulnerability management, logging, incident response, supplier oversight, and compliance activities for the organisation’s SWIFT environment.

## Scope

This Policy applies to all business units, employees, contractors, third parties, systems, networks, applications, devices, accounts, facilities, processes, and services that are part of, connected to, support, administer, monitor, or otherwise affect the Swift Secure Zone.

The Swift Secure Zone includes, but is not limited to, the following:

| Scope Area | Included Examples |
|---|---|
| SWIFT messaging components | SWIFT interfaces, messaging applications, communication software, middleware, message queues, transaction processing platforms, and associated databases |
| SWIFT connectivity components | Network devices, firewalls, routers, switches, secure gateways, leased lines, VPNs, service bureau links, jump hosts, and remote access services used for SWIFT connectivity |
| Security infrastructure | Identity platforms, privileged access tools, multi-factor authentication services, endpoint protection, malware protection, encryption services, key management systems, certificate stores, security monitoring tools, and log management platforms supporting the SWIFT environment |
| Administrative systems | Bastion hosts, management workstations, secure administrator workstations, configuration management systems, deployment tools, backup administration systems, and patch management tools used to manage SWIFT components |
| Supporting infrastructure | Virtualisation hosts, storage platforms, backup platforms, directory services, DNS, time synchronisation, database servers, and operating system platforms that support SWIFT services |
| Physical locations | Data centres, operations rooms, secure equipment rooms, network rooms, backup media storage locations, and disaster recovery facilities where SWIFT systems or supporting components are hosted or administered |
| Personnel and accounts | Operators, approvers, administrators, developers, support personnel, security analysts, service desk staff, third-party support users, privileged accounts, service accounts, application accounts, and emergency access accounts with access to or influence over the SWIFT environment |
| Operational processes | User access management, message approval, transaction monitoring, system administration, change management, backup and restoration, vulnerability management, incident response, log review, configuration management, and disaster recovery activities for SWIFT services |
| External parties | Service bureaus, managed service providers, cloud providers, network providers, vendors, consultants, outsourcing partners, and support organisations that access, operate, host, monitor, or maintain any component of the Swift Secure Zone |

The following are outside the Swift Secure Zone unless they connect to, administer, authenticate users for, monitor, store data from, or otherwise influence SWIFT systems:

- General corporate end-user devices.
- Standard office productivity systems.
- Public websites and unrelated business applications.
- Corporate networks with no permitted communication path to SWIFT systems.
- Non-SWIFT payment platforms with no shared infrastructure, identity dependency, data flow, administrative access, or operational dependency.

Where a system, user, service, network, supplier, or process has an unclear relationship to SWIFT services, it shall be treated as in-scope until a formal assessment confirms otherwise.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain a formally approved Swift Secure Zone boundary that identifies all systems, networks, personnel, accounts, services, suppliers, data flows, administration paths, and physical locations included in scope.

2. The Swift Secure Zone shall include all components that create, process, transmit, store, approve, monitor, administer, secure, back up, or recover SWIFT messages, credentials, security logs, configuration data, cryptographic material, or related operational data.

3. The Swift Secure Zone shall include any component that provides authentication, authorisation, privileged access, security monitoring, malware protection, vulnerability management, backup, restoration, time synchronisation, name resolution, network routing, or administrative control for SWIFT systems.

4. The Swift Secure Zone shall include all operator workstations, administrator workstations, jump hosts, privileged access platforms, and remote access solutions used to access or manage SWIFT systems.

5. The Swift Secure Zone shall include all personnel who can operate, approve, release, support, configure, monitor, troubleshoot, or administer SWIFT services, whether they are employees, contractors, temporary staff, consultants, vendor support personnel, or managed service provider personnel.

6. The Swift Secure Zone shall include all privileged accounts, named user accounts, shared accounts where formally approved, service accounts, application accounts, break-glass accounts, and supplier accounts that provide access to SWIFT systems or supporting infrastructure.

7. The organisation shall maintain an approved Swift Secure Zone inventory containing, at minimum, the following information:

 | Inventory Field | Mandatory Content |
 |---|---|
 | Asset or component name | Authorised hostname, application name, service name, device name, or account name |
 | Asset type | Application, server, database, network device, security tool, endpoint, account, facility, supplier service, or process |
 | Business owner | Accountable business role or function |
 | Technical owner | Accountable technical support team or named role |
 | Location | Data centre, site, cloud region, third-party location, or logical hosting location |
 | Environment | Production, disaster recovery, test, development, management, monitoring, or support |
 | Connectivity | Approved inbound and outbound connections relevant to SWIFT operations |
 | Access groups | Authorised user groups, administrative groups, service accounts, or supplier access groups |
 | Criticality | Business and security impact rating |
 | Security classification | Classification of data processed, stored, or transmitted |
 | Status | Active, pending implementation, retired, decommissioned, or under review |
 | Last validation date | Date of most recent scope confirmation |

8. The Swift Secure Zone boundary shall be documented using current architecture diagrams, network diagrams, data flow diagrams, access path diagrams, and dependency maps.

9. Diagrams of the Swift Secure Zone shall clearly identify trusted zones, management zones, user access paths, administrative access paths, external connections, monitoring points, security controls, and interfaces with third parties.

10. The Swift Secure Zone shall be logically segregated from general corporate networks and unrelated systems through approved network controls, access controls, monitoring controls, and administrative restrictions.

11. Only approved and documented communication paths shall be permitted into, out of, or within the Swift Secure Zone.

12. All communication paths involving the Swift Secure Zone shall have a documented business justification, identified owner, approved source, approved destination, approved protocol, approved port, security control requirements, and review frequency.

13. Direct access from general corporate user networks to SWIFT production systems shall be prohibited unless explicitly approved through the exception process and protected by compensating controls.

14. Internet-originated access to SWIFT production systems shall be prohibited unless explicitly required for an approved SWIFT service, vendor support arrangement, or managed service model and protected by strong authentication, encryption, monitoring, and restricted access controls.

15. Remote access to the Swift Secure Zone shall be restricted to authorised users, approved access methods, strong authentication, monitored sessions, and time-bound access where operationally feasible.

16. Privileged access to the Swift Secure Zone shall be granted only to authorised personnel with a defined operational need, management approval, security approval, and appropriate segregation of duties.

17. Operators responsible for creating, modifying, approving, releasing, or monitoring SWIFT messages shall be identified in the scope register and assigned role-based access according to their approved duties.

18. The organisation shall maintain a current list of all SWIFT operators, approvers, administrators, support personnel, and third-party users with access to the Swift Secure Zone.

19. Access rights for personnel within the Swift Secure Zone shall be reviewed at a defined frequency and whenever personnel change role, transfer department, leave the organisation, change supplier assignment, or no longer require access.

20. The organisation shall define and enforce segregation between SWIFT message creation, approval, release, system administration, security administration, and audit or monitoring functions.

21. Shared accounts shall not be used within the Swift Secure Zone unless there is a documented technical constraint, formal approval, compensating monitoring controls, and named accountability for each use.

22. Service accounts used within the Swift Secure Zone shall have a documented owner, business purpose, technical purpose, permitted systems, required permissions, password or key management requirements, and monitoring requirements.

23. The Swift Secure Zone shall include all environments that can affect SWIFT production security, including development, test, staging, training, disaster recovery, and backup environments where they share credentials, configurations, infrastructure, administrative access, code, data, connectivity, or operational dependencies with production.

24. Non-production environments connected to or derived from SWIFT production systems shall be included in scope unless they are demonstrably isolated, do not contain sensitive SWIFT data, do not share privileged access paths, and cannot affect production operations.

25. Backup systems, backup repositories, backup media, restoration platforms, and recovery procedures for SWIFT systems shall be included in the Swift Secure Zone scope.

26. Disaster recovery systems and alternate processing sites for SWIFT services shall be included in the Swift Secure Zone scope and protected to a level consistent with production requirements.

27. Security logging, monitoring, alerting, investigation, and incident response tools that collect or process Swift Secure Zone data shall be included in scope where they can affect confidentiality, integrity, availability, or investigation capability.

28. The organisation shall classify Swift Secure Zone logs, configurations, cryptographic material, authentication data, transaction-related data, and security records according to their sensitivity and protect them from unauthorised access, alteration, deletion, or disclosure.

29. Any third-party service that hosts, manages, accesses, monitors, supports, secures, transmits, or stores data for the Swift Secure Zone shall be included in scope and subject to supplier security oversight.

30. Contracts or service agreements for third parties supporting the Swift Secure Zone shall define security responsibilities, access restrictions, monitoring rights, incident notification obligations, confidentiality obligations, service continuity requirements, and evidence requirements.

31. Any proposed change to systems, connectivity, accounts, suppliers, tools, locations, or operational processes that may affect the Swift Secure Zone shall include a scope impact assessment before implementation.

32. New components shall not be connected to, integrated with, or used to administer the Swift Secure Zone until they have been assessed, approved, inventoried, secured, and documented.

33. Decommissioned components shall be removed from Swift Secure Zone diagrams, inventories, access lists, firewall rules, monitoring rules, backup schedules, and operational documentation after secure retirement has been confirmed.

34. The organisation shall maintain evidence supporting the Swift Secure Zone scope, including inventories, diagrams, access lists, firewall rule reviews, supplier records, change records, risk assessments, monitoring records, and management approvals.

35. The Swift Secure Zone scope shall be validated at least annually and following significant changes to architecture, connectivity, SWIFT services, operating model, outsourcing arrangements, data centre locations, identity services, or security tooling.

36. The organisation shall resolve identified scope inaccuracies, undocumented dependencies, unauthorised connections, orphaned accounts, unsupported systems, or missing ownership records within agreed remediation timelines.

37. The Swift Secure Zone shall be considered a high-security environment, and any ambiguity regarding inclusion shall be resolved using a risk-based approach that favours inclusion until exclusion is formally approved.

38. This Policy shall be communicated to all personnel responsible for designing, operating, securing, auditing, or supporting SWIFT services.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board or Executive Management | Provide oversight for the security of SWIFT operations and ensure adequate resources are available to maintain the Swift Secure Zone. |
| Chief Information Security Officer or equivalent | Own the security requirements for the Swift Secure Zone, approve scope criteria, oversee compliance, and report material risks to management. |
| Swift Business Owner | Confirm the business services, processes, operators, approval roles, and third-party arrangements that must be included in scope. |
| Swift Technical Owner | Maintain technical ownership of SWIFT platforms, infrastructure dependencies, connectivity, operational documentation, and scope accuracy. |
| Information Security Team | Define security controls, review scope assessments, monitor compliance, validate security boundaries, and support audits and assurance activities. |
| Network Team | Maintain approved network segmentation, firewall rules, routing controls, connectivity diagrams, and network access reviews for the Swift Secure Zone. |
| Infrastructure Team | Maintain servers, operating systems, virtualisation, storage, backup, recovery, and supporting infrastructure within scope. |
| Identity and Access Management Team | Maintain authorised access records, privileged access controls, account lifecycle processes, access reviews, and authentication controls for in-scope users and accounts. |
| SWIFT Operators and Approvers | Use only approved systems and access methods, follow assigned duties, protect credentials, and report suspected unauthorised access or processing anomalies. |
| Security Operations Team | Monitor Swift Secure Zone security events, investigate alerts, preserve logs, and escalate incidents according to the incident response process. |
| Change Management Team | Ensure all changes affecting the Swift Secure Zone include scope impact assessment, approval, testing, and implementation evidence. |
| Third-Party Management or Procurement | Ensure suppliers supporting the Swift Secure Zone are assessed, contractually bound to security obligations, and periodically reviewed. |
| Internal Audit or Independent Assurance Function | Provide independent review of scope completeness, control operation, evidence quality, and compliance with this Policy. |
| Asset Owners | Ensure assets under their responsibility are accurately recorded, classified, reviewed, and protected according to this Policy. |
| All Personnel with Swift Secure Zone Access | Comply with access restrictions, operational procedures, acceptable use requirements, reporting obligations, and security training requirements. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all in-scope personnel, systems, services, and third parties.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through the following activities:

| Monitoring Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Expected Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Swift Secure Zone inventory review | Quarterly | Swift Technical Owner | Updated inventory, review sign-off, remediation actions |
| Network connectivity and firewall rule review | Quarterly | Network Team | Firewall rule export, approval records, exception list, remediation evidence |
| User and privileged access review | Quarterly | Identity and Access Management Team | Access review results, approvals, removals, role changes |
| Third-party access review | Quarterly | Third-Party Management and Information Security | Supplier access list, business justification, approval status |
| Architecture and data flow diagram validation | Semi-annually | Swift Technical Owner and Information Security | Current diagrams, validation record, change references |
| Service account review | Semi-annually | Application and Infrastructure Owners | Service account inventory, ownership confirmation, permissions review |
| Backup and disaster recovery scope review | Semi-annually | Infrastructure Team | Backup coverage records, recovery dependency review |
| Scope validation against change records | Quarterly | Change Management Team | Change samples, scope impact assessments, approvals |
| Independent scope assurance review | Annually | Internal Audit or Independent Assurance Function | Assurance report, management response, action plan |
| Policy compliance attestation | Annually | Control Owners | Signed attestation, supporting evidence |

Non-compliance shall be recorded, risk assessed, assigned an owner, and remediated within agreed timelines based on severity.

| Severity | Example Conditions | Target Remediation |
|---|---|---:|
| Critical | Unauthorised external access path, unknown privileged account, unsupported system directly connected to SWIFT production, unapproved supplier access | Immediate containment and remediation plan within [24 hours] |
| High | Missing scope record for an in-use component, excessive privileged access, undocumented administrative path, incomplete monitoring coverage | Remediation plan within [5 business days] |
| Medium | Outdated diagram, incomplete owner information, delayed access review evidence, minor inventory discrepancy | Remediation within [30 calendar days] |
| Low | Formatting issue, non-material documentation inconsistency, minor evidence naming issue | Remediation within [60 calendar days] |

Enforcement actions may include access suspension, removal of unauthorised connections, rejection of changes, supplier escalation, management notification, disciplinary action, contractual remedies, or formal risk acceptance where appropriate.

Any suspected unauthorised access, unauthorised connectivity, unexpected data flow, unsupported component, or unapproved operator activity affecting the Swift Secure Zone shall be reported immediately to the Information Security Team and handled through the security incident response process.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business need, no practical compliant alternative, and an approved risk treatment plan.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception title | Short description of the requested exception |
| Requestor | Name, role, department, and contact details |
| Affected component or process | System, account, supplier, connection, location, or activity affected |
| Policy requirement affected | Specific requirement from this Policy that cannot be met |
| Business justification | Reason the exception is necessary |
| Risk assessment | Security, operational, compliance, and business impact analysis |
| Compensating controls | Additional controls used to reduce risk |
| Duration | Requested start and end date |
| Remediation plan | Steps to return to compliance |
| Owner | Person accountable for managing the exception |
| Approvals | Business owner, technical owner, Information Security, and risk owner approvals |

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed [90 days] unless renewed through formal review and approval.

Standing exceptions for the Swift Secure Zone shall not be permitted without executive risk acceptance and documented compensating controls.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed or remediated before expiry.

The Information Security Team shall maintain an exception register for the Swift Secure Zone and review open exceptions at least monthly.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur to the SWIFT operating environment, technology architecture, network connectivity, outsourcing model, threat landscape, business processes, regulatory expectations, or security control requirements.

The Policy Owner shall coordinate review with relevant stakeholders, including the Swift Business Owner, Swift Technical Owner, Information Security, Network Team, Infrastructure Team, Identity and Access Management, Security Operations, Third-Party Management, Change Management, and Internal Audit where appropriate.

The review shall confirm that:

- The Swift Secure Zone scope criteria remain accurate and complete.
- The inventory fields remain sufficient for governance and audit needs.
- Diagrams and supporting documentation reflect the current environment.
- Roles and responsibilities remain assigned to current organisational functions.
- Monitoring activities and frequencies remain appropriate.
- Exception handling remains effective and time-bound.
- Lessons learned from incidents, audits, assessments, and operational changes are incorporated.
- Third-party and supplier dependencies remain accurately represented.
- Changes to SWIFT architecture, services, connectivity, or operational processes are reflected.

All updates to this Policy shall be version controlled, approved by the Policy Owner, and communicated to affected stakeholders before or upon the effective date.
