RACI key:

| Letter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| R | Responsible for performing the activity |
| A | Accountable for the outcome and decision |
| C | Consulted before or during the activity |
| I | Informed of outcome or status |

## Records & Outputs

The following records must be created or maintained when this procedure is performed.

| Record / Output | Description | Owner | Retention | Storage Location |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Cyber Threat Intelligence Register | Master log of Swift ISAC items received, assessed, actioned, and closed. | Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst | [Retention Period] | [System/Repository] |
| Original Swift ISAC Communication | Original alert, advisory, bulletin, or report received from Swift. | Swift Security Officer | [Retention Period] | Restricted security repository |
| Triage Record | Initial assessment of severity, relevance, and required next steps. | Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst | [Retention Period] | Case management system |
| Relevance Assessment | Documented determination of applicability to the organisation’s Swift environment. | Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst | [Retention Period] | Case record |
| Indicator Search Log | Evidence of indicator searches, data sources reviewed, and results. | Security Operations Centre Lead | [Retention Period] | SIEM, EDR, or case record |
| Threat Hunt Record | Documentation of hypothesis-driven searches and outcomes. | Security Operations Centre Lead | [Retention Period] | Threat hunting repository |
| Action Plan | List of required defensive, operational, fraud, or remediation actions. | Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst | [Retention Period] | Case management system |
| Change Records | Approved changes resulting from Swift ISAC intelligence. | Relevant Change Owner | [Retention Period] | Change management system |
| Detection Rule Records | New or updated rules created from intelligence. | Security Operations Centre Lead | [Retention Period] | Detection engineering repository |
| Vulnerability or Patch Evidence | Evidence of exposure validation and remediation. | Vulnerability Management Lead | [Retention Period] | Vulnerability management platform |
| Payment or Fraud Review Evidence | Evidence of transaction monitoring, fraud scenario review, or operational checks. | Payment Operations Manager / Fraud Monitoring Lead | [Retention Period] | Payment operations or fraud case system |
| Third-Party Assurance Responses | Vendor confirmations, evidence, or remediation updates. | Vendor Risk Manager | [Retention Period] | Vendor risk repository |
| Incident Record | Incident ticket or report where suspected compromise is identified. | Incident Response Manager | [Retention Period] | Incident management system |
| Risk Acceptance Record | Approved decision to defer or accept residual risk. | Risk and Compliance Manager | [Retention Period] | Risk management system |
| Closure Record | Final disposition and approval of case closure. | Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst | [Retention Period] | Case management system |
| Periodic Intelligence Summary | Management report on Swift-related intelligence trends and actions. | Cyber Security Operations Manager | [Retention Period] | Security reporting repository |

Records must be:

- Accurate, complete, and traceable to the source intelligence.
- Stored only in approved repositories.
- Protected from unauthorised access or disclosure.
- Available for internal review, assurance activities, and audit.
- Linked to related incidents, changes, risks, vulnerabilities, or vendor records where applicable.

## Exceptions & Escalation

### Exceptions

An exception occurs when this procedure cannot be followed as written. Examples include:

- Swift ISAC access is unavailable.
- Required logs are not available for the recommended search period.
- Indicators cannot be searched due to tool limitations.
- Required technical actions cannot be implemented within target timeframes.
- A third party cannot provide timely confirmation of exposure or remediation.
- Business operations prevent immediate implementation of a recommended defensive action.
- Sensitive source restrictions prevent normal internal distribution.
- The relevance of intelligence cannot be determined due to incomplete asset or architecture information.

Exceptions must be documented in the case record and include:

| Field | Required Entry |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | [ID] |
| Related intelligence ID | [ID] |
| Description | [Exception details] |
| Reason | [Business, technical, legal, operational, or third-party constraint] |
| Risk impact | [Impact summary] |
| Compensating controls | [Controls in place] |
| Requested by | [Name/Role] |
| Approval required from | [Role] |
| Review date | [Date] |
| Final disposition | Approved / Rejected / Expired / Superseded |

Exception approvals are required as follows:

| Exception Type | Minimum Approver |
|---|---|
| Low or Medium severity procedural delay with no material risk increase | Security Operations Centre Lead |
| High severity delay, incomplete assessment, or deferred remediation | Cyber Security Operations Manager |
| Critical severity delay or material risk acceptance | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Action affecting payment processing availability or integrity | Chief Information Security Officer and Payment Operations Manager |
| Third-party assurance gap affecting Swift services | Cyber Security Operations Manager and Vendor Risk Manager |
| Legal, confidentiality, or external communication issue | Legal Counsel or Compliance Lead |

Approved exceptions must have an expiry or review date. Permanent exceptions are not permitted under this procedure; long-term deviations must be converted into a formal risk treatment plan.

### Escalation

The following escalation paths apply.

| Trigger | Escalate To | Target Timeframe |
|---|---|---:|
| Critical Swift ISAC intelligence received | SOC Lead and Cyber Security Operations Manager | 1 hour |
| Evidence of compromise or indicator match | Incident Response Manager and Cyber Security Operations Manager | Immediate |
| Suspicious or unauthorised payment activity | Payment Operations Manager, Fraud Monitoring Lead, and Incident Response Manager | Immediate |
| Required urgent production change | Change Manager and relevant system owner | Immediate |
| Potential business disruption to Swift messaging | Swift Operations Manager and CISO | Immediate |
| Third party unable to provide assurance for Critical or High item | Vendor Risk Manager and Cyber Security Operations Manager | Same business day |
| Overdue Critical action | Cyber Security Operations Manager and CISO | Same business day |
| Overdue High action | Cyber Security Operations Manager | Within 1 business day |
| Disagreement on severity, relevance, or required action | Cyber Security Operations Manager | Within 1 business day |
| Potential breach of Swift ISAC handling restrictions | Information Security Manager and Compliance Lead | Same business day |
| Media, customer, regulator, or law enforcement implications | CISO, Legal Counsel, Compliance Lead, and Communications Lead | Immediate |

Where escalation results in an incident declaration, the Cyber Security Incident Response Procedure governs containment, eradication, recovery, communications, and post-incident review. This procedure continues to govern the intelligence records and evidence trail related to the original Swift ISAC item.

## Review

This procedure must be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that affect Swift-related threat intelligence handling.

Review triggers include:

- Changes to the Swift environment, architecture, connectivity, or operating model.
- Changes to Swift ISAC access arrangements or approved communication channels.
- Significant cyber threat events affecting Swift users or the financial sector.
- Lessons learned from incidents, simulations, threat hunts, or fraud investigations.
- Audit findings or control assurance observations.
- Material changes to security monitoring, logging, or threat intelligence tooling.
- Changes to third-party providers supporting Swift systems.
- Changes to payment operations processes or fraud monitoring capabilities.
- Repeated exceptions, delays, or evidence gaps identified during procedure execution.

The review must confirm that:

- Named Swift ISAC recipients remain current.
- Access to Swift ISAC and internal repositories is restricted to authorised personnel.
- Severity and relevance criteria remain appropriate.
- Response targets are achievable and aligned with operational risk.
- Required logs and monitoring tools support indicator searches and threat hunting.
- Swift asset inventories and architecture information are accurate.
- Internal distribution lists remain appropriate.
- Records are complete, retained, and retrievable.
- Escalation paths and contact details are current.
- Lessons learned have been incorporated into the procedure and related playbooks.

Review outcomes must be documented.

| Review Item | Required Entry |
|---|---|
| Review date | [Date] |
| Reviewer | [Name/Role] |
| Participants | [Names/Roles] |
| Summary of changes | [Summary] |
| Issues identified | [Issues] |
| Actions raised | [Actions] |
| Approval | [Approver] |
| Next review date | [Date] |

SWF-018.title: Swift Server Hardening Evidence
SWF-018.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | EVD-SWIFT-HARDENING-001 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [SWIFT Infrastructure Owner] |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework |
| Classification | Confidential |

## Purpose

This evidence document records and describes the configuration baseline evidence used to demonstrate that SWIFT-related servers are hardened, consistently configured, and protected against unauthorised or insecure changes.

The purpose of this evidence is to show that servers supporting SWIFT messaging, connectivity, security, monitoring, administration, and supporting infrastructure are configured according to approved hardening standards before use and remain aligned with those standards during operation.

This document is intended to support internal control assurance, independent review, audit activity, and SWIFT security attestation by providing a clear, traceable evidence set for server hardening configuration baselines.

## What This Evidence Demonstrates

This evidence demonstrates that the organisation has applied, validated, and retained configuration baselines for in-scope SWIFT servers. Specifically, it demonstrates that:

- A formally approved hardening baseline exists for each relevant server operating system and server role.
- SWIFT-related servers are built from approved secure configuration standards.
- Unnecessary services, ports, protocols, software, accounts, and administrative tools are disabled or removed.
- Security settings are configured to reduce the risk of unauthorised access, malware execution, privilege misuse, insecure network exposure, and configuration drift.
- Administrative access is restricted, monitored, and aligned with the principle of least privilege.
- Logging, time synchronisation, authentication, session management, and endpoint protection settings are enabled and configured appropriately.
- Configuration baselines are periodically reviewed and updated in response to technology changes, threat intelligence, vendor guidance, and operational requirements.
- Deviations from the approved baseline are documented, risk-assessed, approved, time-bound where applicable, and subject to periodic review.
- Evidence has been collected from authoritative sources such as configuration management platforms, endpoint management tools, server build records, security scanning tools, and manual validation records.
- The evidence is complete, current, traceable to specific systems, and protected against unauthorised modification.

This evidence should allow a reviewer to confirm that hardening is not merely defined as a requirement, but has been implemented on the servers that support the SWIFT environment.

## Scope

This evidence applies to all servers that host, support, secure, monitor, administer, or provide infrastructure services to the organisation’s SWIFT environment.

In-scope systems include, where applicable:

| System Category | Examples of In-Scope Systems | Evidence Expected |
|---|---|---|
| SWIFT messaging servers | SWIFT interface servers, messaging application servers, communication components | Baseline build record, hardening checklist, configuration scan, access control evidence |
| SWIFT connectivity servers | VPN, connectivity, proxy, secure gateway, or communication relay servers supporting SWIFT traffic | Network service hardening evidence, port and protocol validation, secure configuration records |
| Security infrastructure servers | Authentication, privileged access, endpoint protection, vulnerability scanning, logging, monitoring, certificate, and key management servers supporting SWIFT | Security configuration exports, administrative access review, logging and alerting evidence |
| Administration servers | Jump servers, bastion hosts, management servers, deployment servers used for SWIFT administration | Secure build evidence, restricted access configuration, session logging evidence |
| Supporting infrastructure servers | Directory services, DNS, NTP, backup, patch management, configuration management, and monitoring servers used by the SWIFT environment | Baseline compliance records, role-based configuration evidence, service hardening evidence |
| Virtualisation or hosting platforms | Hypervisors, management appliances, dedicated hosting nodes, or cloud-hosted instances supporting SWIFT servers | Host hardening evidence, management access control, platform security configuration evidence |

Out of scope:

- End-user workstations not used for SWIFT administration.
- General corporate servers with no connectivity, administrative, monitoring, authentication, or dependency relationship to the SWIFT environment.
- Network device hardening evidence, unless the device is operating as a server-based SWIFT support component.
- Application-specific configuration evidence that is not part of the underlying server operating system or platform hardening baseline.

Where there is uncertainty about whether a server is in scope, the system owner must document the rationale and obtain confirmation from the [SWIFT Security Officer] or equivalent accountable role.

## Required Contents

The evidence package must contain sufficient detail to allow an independent reviewer to determine what baseline was required, which systems it applied to, how implementation was validated, when validation occurred, who approved any deviations, and whether the evidence remains current.

The following evidence items are required.

| Evidence Item | Description | Minimum Required Details | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Approved server hardening baseline | Current approved baseline for each operating system and server role used in the SWIFT environment | Baseline name, version, owner, approval date, applicable server roles, review date | Configuration standard repository or GRC document library |
| Server inventory extract | Current list of in-scope SWIFT servers | Hostname, asset ID, IP address, environment, server role, operating system, owner, location, criticality | CMDB, asset register, SWIFT architecture inventory |
| Baseline applicability matrix | Mapping of each in-scope server to the applicable hardening baseline | Server name, baseline name, baseline version, exception status, validation date | Configuration management records |
| Build or rebuild records | Evidence that servers were built from approved images or configuration templates | Build date, image or template version, installer, change ticket, approval reference | Change management system, build platform |
| Configuration scan results | Automated evidence showing compliance against the approved baseline | Scan date, tool used, policy profile, pass/fail status, failed checks, remediation status | Security configuration assessment tool |
| Manual hardening checklist | Manual validation where automated testing does not cover all settings | Control area, required setting, observed setting, validator, date, outcome | Infrastructure operations records |
| Service and port review | Evidence that only required services, listening ports, and protocols are enabled | Hostname, listening ports, business justification, owner approval, scan date | Vulnerability scanner, endpoint tool, network scanner |
| Local account and privilege review | Evidence that privileged and local accounts are controlled | Account list, privileged group membership, disabled accounts, service accounts, review outcome | Operating system export, privileged access tool |
| Authentication and session settings | Evidence of secure authentication and administrative session controls | Password or key settings, lockout settings, session timeout, remote access restrictions | Group policy, local security policy, identity platform |
| Logging and time synchronisation settings | Evidence that audit logs are enabled and timestamps are reliable | Audit policy settings, log forwarding destination, time source, time sync status | SIEM, endpoint agent, server configuration export |
| Endpoint protection configuration | Evidence that malware protection, host firewall, application control, or equivalent controls are active | Agent status, policy name, last update, last check-in, firewall profile | Endpoint security console |
| Patch and vulnerability status | Evidence that the server is maintained at an approved security patch level | Patch status, last update, outstanding vulnerabilities, remediation plan | Patch management and vulnerability management tools |
| Baseline deviation register | Record of approved exceptions or deviations from standard hardening settings | Deviation description, affected servers, risk rationale, compensating controls, approval, expiry date | Risk register, exception register |
| Remediation evidence | Evidence that failed baseline checks have been corrected or formally accepted | Finding, corrective action, implementation date, re-test result, closure approval | Ticketing system, scan comparison |
| Periodic review record | Evidence that baselines and system compliance are reviewed on a defined cycle | Review date, participants, conclusions, actions, approval | Security governance records |

The evidence package must include the following minimum data fields for each in-scope server:

| Field | Required Value |
|---|---|
| Hostname | [Hostname] |
| Asset ID | [Asset ID] |
| Environment | Production / Disaster Recovery / Test / Management |
| Server Role | [Server Role] |
| Operating System | [Operating System and Version] |
| Applicable Baseline | [Baseline Name and Version] |
| System Owner | [System Owner] |
| Technical Owner | [Technical Owner] |
| Last Baseline Validation Date | [Validation Date] |
| Validation Method | Automated scan / Manual checklist / Configuration export / Combined |
| Compliance Status | Compliant / Non-compliant / Exception approved / Remediation in progress |
| Open Deviations | Yes / No |
| Evidence Location | [Repository Path or Evidence Link] |

The hardening baseline evidence should cover, at minimum, the following configuration areas:

| Configuration Area | Evidence Expectation |
|---|---|
| Operating system installation | Minimal installation, approved image or template, removal of unnecessary packages |
| System services | Only required services enabled; unused services disabled or removed |
| Network exposure | Only authorised ports and protocols listening; insecure protocols disabled |
| Remote administration | Administrative access restricted to approved management paths and authorised administrators |
| Authentication | Secure account lockout, password, key, and session controls configured |
| Privilege management | Local administrator and privileged groups restricted and reviewed |
| Default accounts | Default, guest, unused, or vendor accounts disabled, renamed, removed, or controlled |
| Service accounts | Service accounts documented, non-interactive where possible, and least-privileged |
| Host firewall | Host firewall enabled with approved inbound and outbound rules |
| Malware protection | Endpoint protection enabled, updated, and centrally monitored |
| Application control | Unauthorised executables, scripts, and tools restricted where supported |
| Logging | Security, system, authentication, privilege, and administrative events logged |
| Log forwarding | Logs forwarded to approved monitoring or SIEM platform |
| Time synchronisation | Servers synchronised to approved time sources |
| File system permissions | Sensitive directories, configuration files, logs, and keys restricted |
| Cryptographic settings | Weak protocols, weak ciphers, and insecure legacy settings disabled where supported |
| Patch configuration | Security updates managed through approved patching process |
| Backup agent configuration | Backup configuration present where required and protected from misuse |
| Monitoring agent configuration | Security and operational monitoring agents installed and active |
| Banner and warning messages | Approved legal or administrative warning banners configured where applicable |
| Configuration drift control | Ongoing monitoring or periodic validation used to detect unauthorised changes |

The evidence must distinguish clearly between:

- The baseline requirement.
- The observed system configuration.
- The validation method.
- The validation result.
- Any remediation or approved deviation.

Example evidence index:

| Evidence Ref | Evidence Name | System or Scope | Date Collected | Collected By | Validation Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EVD-SH-001 | Windows Server Hardening Baseline v[Version] | Windows SWIFT servers | [Date] | [Name/Role] | Approved baseline |
| EVD-SH-002 | Linux Server Hardening Baseline v[Version] | Linux SWIFT servers | [Date] | [Name/Role] | Approved baseline |
| EVD-SH-003 | SWIFT Server Inventory Extract | All in-scope servers | [Date] | [Name/Role] | Complete |
| EVD-SH-004 | Baseline Compliance Scan Report | Production SWIFT servers | [Date] | [Name/Role] | Reviewed |
| EVD-SH-005 | Manual Hardening Validation Checklist | SWIFT communication servers | [Date] | [Name/Role] | Reviewed |
| EVD-SH-006 | Open Hardening Deviations Register | Servers with approved deviations | [Date] | [Name/Role] | Approved where applicable |
| EVD-SH-007 | Remediation Closure Tickets | Previously failed baseline checks | [Date] | [Name/Role] | Closed or tracked |

## Collection & Validation

Evidence must be collected from authoritative systems and reviewed for completeness, accuracy, and currency before it is relied upon for audit or attestation purposes.

Evidence collection must be performed by personnel with appropriate technical knowledge of the SWIFT environment, but validation should include independent review by a person who did not implement the original configuration wherever practicable.

Recommended collection frequency:

| Evidence Type | Minimum Frequency | Trigger-Based Collection |
|---|---:|---|
| Approved hardening baseline | At least annually | Baseline update, new operating system, new server role, material threat or vendor change |
| Server inventory extract | Quarterly | New server, decommissioned server, environment change |
| Configuration compliance scan | Quarterly for production and disaster recovery; before go-live for new servers | Build, rebuild, major patching, configuration change, incident, audit request |
| Manual checklist | At go-live and annually where automated coverage is incomplete | Tool limitation, exception request, high-risk change |
| Service and port review | Quarterly | New application component, network change, unexpected scan result |
| Privileged account review | Quarterly | Joiner, mover, leaver event; privilege change; incident |
| Deviation register review | Monthly for open deviations | Deviation expiry, compensating control change, risk reassessment |
| Remediation evidence | As remediation is completed | Closure of failed scan item or audit finding |

The evidence collection process must include the following steps:

1. Confirm the list of in-scope SWIFT servers against the current asset inventory, architecture diagrams, and service ownership records.
2. Confirm the applicable hardening baseline for each server based on operating system, role, environment, and technology platform.
3. Export or capture the approved baseline documentation from the controlled document repository.
4. Run automated configuration compliance scans using the approved toolset where available.
5. Collect manual configuration evidence for settings not covered by automated tooling.
6. Export supporting evidence from endpoint protection, logging, monitoring, vulnerability management, patch management, and privileged access platforms.
7. Identify failed checks, missing evidence, undocumented services, excessive privileges, or unexpected configuration differences.
8. Link each exception, deviation, or failed check to an approved risk acceptance, remediation ticket, or compensating control.
9. Re-test remediated items and retain the before-and-after evidence.
10. Review the final evidence package for completeness and sign off the validation result.

Validation must confirm:

| Validation Check | Expected Outcome |
|---|---|
| Completeness | Every in-scope server has a corresponding baseline, validation result, and evidence reference |
| Currency | Evidence was collected within the required review period or after the most recent material configuration change |
| Integrity | Evidence comes from approved sources and has not been manually altered outside the evidence repository |
| Traceability | Evidence can be traced to specific servers, dates, tools, reviewers, tickets, and approvals |
| Consistency | Baseline names and versions align across inventory, scan reports, and deviation records |
| Deviation control | All non-standard settings are documented, approved, risk-assessed, and assigned an owner |
| Remediation tracking | Failed checks are either remediated, scheduled for remediation, or formally accepted |
| Operational alignment | Hardened settings do not conflict with documented SWIFT operational requirements without approved justification |

Evidence must not be considered valid if:

- The server is missing from the asset inventory or baseline applicability matrix.
- The scan report does not identify the system, scan date, policy profile, or result.
- The baseline version used for validation is obsolete and no approved rationale exists.
- Failed checks are present with no remediation ticket, exception, or risk acceptance.
- Manual screenshots or exports are not dated or cannot be tied to a specific server.
- Configuration results have been edited without a clear chain of custody.
- The evidence covers test systems only while production systems are in scope.
- The evidence is older than the required collection period and no revalidation has occurred.

Validation sign-off must be recorded as follows:

| Role | Responsibility | Sign-Off Required |
|---|---|---|
| Technical Owner | Confirms configuration settings and remediation actions | Yes |
| SWIFT Infrastructure Owner | Confirms server scope and operational applicability | Yes |
| Security Operations Representative | Confirms security tooling, monitoring, and endpoint protection evidence | Yes |
| Risk or Compliance Representative | Confirms evidence completeness and exception governance | Yes |
| Independent Reviewer | Confirms evidence is suitable for assurance or audit use | Where required |

Sign-off record:

| Role | Name | Date | Outcome | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Technical Owner | [Name] | [Date] | Approved / Rework required | [Comments] |
| SWIFT Infrastructure Owner | [Name] | [Date] | Approved / Rework required | [Comments] |
| Security Operations Representative | [Name] | [Date] | Approved / Rework required | [Comments] |
| Risk or Compliance Representative | [Name] | [Date] | Approved / Rework required | [Comments] |
| Independent Reviewer | [Name] | [Date] | Approved / Rework required | [Comments] |

## Retention & Access

Server hardening evidence must be retained in a controlled repository that protects confidentiality, integrity, and availability. The repository must support access control, version history, audit logging, and recovery in the event of accidental deletion or corruption.

Evidence must be retained for at least [Retention Period] or longer where required by legal, regulatory, contractual, audit, incident response, or internal governance obligations.

Retention requirements:

| Evidence Category | Minimum Retention Expectation | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Approved hardening baselines | Current version plus prior versions for [Retention Period] | Required to prove what baseline applied at a point in time |
| Server inventory extracts | [Retention Period] | Retain periodic snapshots and year-end evidence packs |
| Baseline compliance scan reports | [Retention Period] | Retain original exports and reviewed summaries |
| Manual validation checklists | [Retention Period] | Retain signed or workflow-approved records |
| Deviation and exception approvals | Life of deviation plus [Retention Period] | Retain risk rationale, compensating controls, and expiry decisions |
| Remediation tickets and re-test evidence | [Retention Period] | Retain evidence of closure and validation |
| Sign-off records | [Retention Period] | Retain with the evidence package used for assurance or attestation |
| Audit submissions | [Retention Period] | Retain exactly as submitted, including supporting files |

Access to the evidence repository must be restricted to authorised personnel with a business need. Access should be granted based on role and reviewed periodically.

Recommended access model:

| Role or Group | Access Level | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SWIFT Infrastructure Team | Read/write to technical evidence; read to approved baselines | Evidence collection and remediation |
| Security Operations Team | Read/write to security tool exports and validation comments | Security validation and monitoring evidence |
| Risk and Compliance Team | Read to all evidence; write to review and sign-off records | Assurance, control review, audit support |
| Internal Audit | Read-only, time-bound access | Independent review |
| External Assessor or Auditor | Read-only, time-bound access subject to approval | Assessment or attestation support |
| General IT Users | No access | Not required |

The following handling requirements apply:

- Evidence containing server names, IP addresses, security configurations, vulnerabilities, privileged account details, or security tool outputs must be treated as confidential.
- Evidence must not be emailed externally unless approved by [Information Security Approver] and protected using approved secure transfer methods.
- Screenshots must include sufficient context to show system identity, date, and configuration setting, but should avoid exposing secrets, passwords, private keys, tokens, or unnecessary personal data.
- Exported configuration files must be stored in their original format where possible to preserve integrity.
- If evidence is transformed into a summary, the original export must also be retained.
- Access to evidence must be reviewed at least quarterly and removed promptly when no longer required.
- Any unauthorised access, alteration, deletion, or disclosure of evidence must be reported through the organisation’s security incident process.
- Superseded evidence must be archived, not overwritten, where it is needed to demonstrate historical compliance.
- Evidence used for audit or attestation must be frozen or versioned to preserve the exact evidence set reviewed.

Evidence repository details:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Primary Repository | [Evidence Repository Name or Path] |
| Backup Location | [Backup Location] |
| Repository Owner | [Repository Owner] |
| Access Approver | [Access Approver] |
| Review Frequency | Quarterly |
| Retention Period | [Retention Period] |
| Secure Transfer Method | [Approved Secure Transfer Method] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Report ID | Enter the unique identifier for this vulnerability scan report/log entry; use a consistent format such as VSR-SWIFT-YYYY-NNN. |
| Scan Period | Enter the period covered by the scan in YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Scan Date | Enter the date the vulnerability scan was executed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| SWIFT Environment | Enter the environment scanned; allowed values: Production, Disaster Recovery, Test, Development, Other. |
| SWIFT Zone Scope | Describe the SWIFT zone or secure zone segment covered by the scan, including whether it includes SWIFT infrastructure, operator PCs, jump servers, middleware, network/security devices, or supporting systems. |
| Component / Asset Name | Enter the name of the scanned SWIFT-related component or asset exactly as recorded in the approved asset inventory or CMDB. |
| Asset Type | Enter the asset category; allowed values: SWIFT Interface, SWIFT Gateway, Application Server, Database Server, Operator Workstation, Jump Server, Network Device, Security Device, Virtualisation Host, Supporting Server, Other. |
| Asset Identifier | Enter the unique asset ID, CMDB ID, hostname ID, or inventory reference for the component. |
| IP Address / Hostname | Enter the IP address and/or fully qualified hostname of the scanned asset; use IPv4/IPv6 or FQDN format. |
| System Owner | Enter the accountable business or technical owner for the scanned asset, including role or team name. |
| Scan Type | Enter the type of vulnerability scan performed; allowed values: Internal Network Scan, External Network Scan, Host Scan, Web/Application Scan, Configuration Scan, Credentialed Infrastructure Scan, Other. |
| Authenticated Scan Performed | State whether the scan used authenticated/credentialed access; allowed values: Yes, No, Partially. If No or Partially, explain in Comments / Follow-up Actions. |
| Scanner Tool and Version | Enter the vulnerability scanning tool name and version used, such as Tenable.sc version, Nessus version, Qualys VMDR version, Rapid7 InsightVM version, or equivalent. |
| Scan Policy / Profile Used | Enter the scan template, policy, benchmark, or profile used, including whether it is the approved SWIFT zone vulnerability scan policy. |
| Scanner Signature / Plugin Version | Enter the vulnerability feed, plugin, signature, or detection version current at the time of scan, where available. |
| Scan Coverage Status | Enter the completeness of the scan; allowed values: Complete, Partial, Failed, Not Scanned. Partial, Failed, or Not Scanned entries must be justified in Scan Exceptions / Exclusions. |
| Scan Exceptions / Exclusions | Record any excluded assets, ports, services, credentials, scan limitations, unavailable systems, or approved exclusions; enter None if no exclusions applied. |
| Total Vulnerabilities Identified | Enter the total number of vulnerabilities/findings identified for the asset or scan scope as a non-negative integer. |
| Critical Vulnerabilities | Enter the number of Critical severity vulnerabilities as a non-negative integer, using the scanner's severity rating or approved organisational severity mapping. |
| High Vulnerabilities | Enter the number of High severity vulnerabilities as a non-negative integer. |
| Medium Vulnerabilities | Enter the number of Medium severity vulnerabilities as a non-negative integer. |
| Low Vulnerabilities | Enter the number of Low severity vulnerabilities as a non-negative integer. |
| Informational Findings | Enter the number of Informational findings as a non-negative integer. |
| Highest Severity Rating | Enter the highest severity identified for this entry; allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational, None. |
| Key Vulnerability References | List the most significant vulnerability identifiers relevant to the asset or scan, such as CVE IDs, scanner plugin IDs, advisory IDs, or configuration finding IDs; separate multiple values with semicolons. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the team or individual responsible for remediation of the identified vulnerabilities. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target remediation date in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on the organisation's vulnerability remediation SLA and severity. |
| Remediation Status | Enter the current remediation state; allowed values: Open, In Progress, Remediated, Risk Accepted, False Positive, Deferred, Closed. |
| Risk Acceptance / Exception Reference | Enter the approved risk acceptance, exception, or false-positive reference number if applicable; enter N/A where not applicable. |
| Rescan Required | State whether validation rescan is required; allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Rescan Date | Enter the date the validation rescan was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not yet performed or not required. |
| Rescan Result | Enter the validation outcome; allowed values: Passed, Failed, Partially Passed, Not Performed, N/A. |
| Report Evidence Location | Enter the repository path, ticket link, GRC evidence ID, or document management location where the full scan report and supporting evidence are stored. |
| Reviewed By | Enter the name and role of the person who reviewed the scan results for completeness, severity, and required remediation actions. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the scan report/log entry was reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Approval Status | Enter the approval status of the scan report/log entry; allowed values: Draft, Reviewed, Approved, Rejected. |
| Comments / Follow-up Actions | Record concise notes on material findings, failed scans, incomplete coverage, remediation blockers, escalation actions, or next steps. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Vulnerability Management Lead with review by the SWIFT Security Officer or SWIFT Infrastructure Owner. Update after each scheduled SWIFT zone vulnerability scan and after any validation rescan, drawing evidence from the approved vulnerability scanner, CMDB/asset inventory, ticketing system, and GRC evidence repository.

SWF-020.content:

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this patch record, using a consistent format such as PATCH-SWIFT-YYYY-NNN. |
| SWIFT Environment | Enter the SWIFT-related environment affected by the patch. Allowed values: Production, DR, UAT, Test, Development, Management, Supporting Infrastructure. |
| SWIFT Zone Component Type | Enter the type of asset within or supporting the SWIFT Secure Zone. Allowed values: SWIFT Application Server, SWIFT Interface, Database, HSM, Jump Server, Firewall, Network Device, Hypervisor, Storage, Endpoint, Monitoring Server, Backup Server, Directory Service, Other. |
| Asset ID / CMDB CI | Enter the unique CMDB configuration item ID or asset inventory ID for the patched system. |
| Hostname / Device Name | Enter the hostname, device name, or logical system name exactly as recorded in CMDB or the patch management tool. |
| IP Address | Enter the primary management or service IP address of the asset, using IPv4 or IPv6 format. |
| Business Service / SWIFT Application | Enter the SWIFT service or application supported by the asset, such as Alliance Access, Alliance Gateway, SWIFTNet Link, HSM service, screening interface, or supporting infrastructure service. |
| Patch / Update Identifier | Enter the vendor patch ID, KB number, package name, firmware version, hotfix ID, or update bundle identifier. |
| Vendor / Source | Enter the vendor or trusted source that issued the patch, such as Microsoft, Red Hat, Oracle, Cisco, SWIFT, Thales, VMware, or internal approved repository. |
| Patch Type | Enter the patch category. Allowed values: Security Update, Critical Update, Firmware, OS Patch, Application Patch, Database Patch, Network Device Patch, Hypervisor Patch, Configuration Update, Other. |
| Security Advisory / CVE Reference | Enter the related security advisory ID, CVE number, vendor bulletin, or write N/A if the update is not linked to a specific advisory. |
| Severity / Priority | Enter the assigned patch severity or internal priority. Allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational. |
| Patch Description | Enter a concise description of what the patch fixes, including the vulnerability or security issue addressed where known. |
| Patch Release Date | Enter the date the patch was released by the vendor or made available in the approved repository, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Applicability Confirmed | State whether the patch is applicable to the asset. Allowed values: Yes, No, Under Review. |
| Applicability Assessment Date | Enter the date applicability was assessed, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment Reference | Enter the reference to the risk assessment, impact assessment, vulnerability ticket, or change assessment used before deployment. |
| Change Request ID | Enter the approved change ticket or emergency change reference authorising deployment. |
| Change Approval Date | Enter the date the change was approved, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Maintenance Window | Enter the approved implementation window using format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM-HH:MM TZ. |
| Tested Before Deployment | State whether the patch was tested before production deployment. Allowed values: Yes, No, Not Required, Emergency Deployment. |
| Test Evidence Reference | Enter the location or reference for test results, pilot deployment evidence, UAT record, or write N/A if not required. |
| Deployment Method | Enter how the patch was deployed, such as SCCM, WSUS, Ansible, Red Hat Satellite, manual install, vendor console, firmware utility, or network management platform. |
| Deployment Status | Enter the current implementation status. Allowed values: Planned, In Progress, Deployed, Failed, Rolled Back, Deferred, Not Applicable. |
| Deployment Start Date/Time | Enter the actual deployment start timestamp in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ format. |
| Deployment End Date/Time | Enter the actual deployment completion timestamp in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ format. |
| Installed By | Enter the name, team, or service provider role that performed the deployment; use an individual name where required by internal policy. |
| Privileged Account / Tool Used | Enter the privileged account, PAM session ID, automation job ID, or approved tool account used to perform the deployment. |
| Reboot Required | State whether a reboot or service restart was required. Allowed values: Yes, No, Unknown. |
| Reboot Completed | State whether the required reboot or service restart was completed. Allowed values: Yes, No, Not Required. |
| Post-Deployment Verification Performed | State whether post-deployment checks were completed. Allowed values: Yes, No, Not Required. |
| Verification Date | Enter the date post-deployment verification was completed, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Verification Evidence Reference | Enter the evidence reference proving the update was applied, such as patch scan result, command output, screenshot, EDR record, vulnerability scan ID, or configuration compliance report. |
| Patch Validation Result | Enter the outcome of validation. Allowed values: Passed, Failed, Partially Passed, Pending, Not Applicable. |
| Failure / Rollback Details | If deployment failed or was rolled back, describe the issue, rollback action, and related incident/problem ticket; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Exception / Deferral Required | State whether the patch was deferred or excepted from normal implementation. Allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Exception Reference | If an exception or deferral exists, enter the approved exception/risk acceptance reference; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Exception Expiry Date | If an exception exists, enter the expiry or review date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Compensating Controls | If patching is deferred, describe compensating controls such as isolation, firewall rule, IPS signature, EDR monitoring, disabled service, or access restriction; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Residual Risk Owner | If residual risk remains, enter the accountable risk owner role/name; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the patch record was closed after successful verification or approved exception, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Comments | Enter any additional audit-relevant notes, dependencies, anomalies, or cross-references not captured elsewhere. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the SWIFT Infrastructure or Patch Management Lead with oversight from Information Security/GRC. Updated for every applicable security update cycle and emergency patch event, using CMDB, vulnerability scanning, vendor advisories, change management, patch management, PAM, and verification evidence repositories as source systems.

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this training record, e.g. TRN-SWIFT-YYYY-0001. |
| Training Year | Enter the calendar year to which the annual SWIFT operator training requirement applies, in YYYY format. |
| SWIFT CSCF Version | Enter the SWIFT CSCF version applicable to the training cycle, e.g. CSCF 2024 or CSCF 2025. |
| Operator Full Name | Enter the full legal or HR-recorded name of the operator who is required to complete SWIFT security training. |
| Operator User ID | Enter the organisation user ID, HR ID, IAM ID, or LMS ID used to uniquely identify the operator. |
| Operator Email | Enter the operator’s corporate email address. |
| Team / Department | Enter the operator’s organisational team or department, e.g. Payments Operations, Treasury Operations, SWIFT Support. |
| Role / Job Title | Enter the operator’s business job title as recorded in HR or the access management system. |
| SWIFT Operational Role | Enter the SWIFT-related operational role, e.g. SWIFT Operator, SWIFT Approver, SWIFT Administrator, Security Officer, Application Support, Technical Operator. |
| SWIFT Environment Access | Enter the SWIFT environment or systems the person can access, e.g. Production, Test, Alliance Access, Alliance Lite2, SWIFTNet, HSM, None. |
| BIC(s) / Service(s) Supported | Enter the BIC(s), SWIFT service(s), or messaging services supported by the operator, or N/A if not applicable. |
| Training Requirement Applies | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether annual SWIFT operator security training is required for this person; if No, explain why in Comments. |
| Training Course / Module Name | Enter the exact name of the annual training course or module assigned for SWIFT operator security awareness and responsibilities. |
| Training Content Covered | Summarise the key topics covered, such as SWIFT CSCF responsibilities, secure operating procedures, credential protection, phishing/social engineering, incident escalation, acceptable use, and cyber hygiene. |
| Delivery Method | Enter one allowed value: LMS, Instructor-led, Webinar, Classroom, Self-study, External training, Other. |
| Training Provider | Enter the internal team, LMS provider, SWIFT, or external vendor that delivered or hosted the training. |
| Assigned Date | Enter the date the training was assigned to the operator in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Due Date | Enter the required completion deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format; this should support annual completion monitoring. |
| Completion Date | Enter the actual date the operator completed the training in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until completed. |
| Completion Status | Enter one allowed value: Not Assigned, Assigned, In Progress, Completed, Overdue, Deferred, Not Applicable. |
| Assessment Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the training includes a quiz, test, knowledge check, or other assessment. |
| Assessment Score | Enter the score achieved as a percentage, e.g. 85%, or N/A if no assessment is required. |
| Pass Mark | Enter the minimum required score as a percentage, e.g. 80%, or N/A if no assessment is required. |
| Assessment Result | Enter one allowed value: Pass, Fail, Not Required, Pending. |
| Operator Attestation Completed | Enter Yes or No to confirm whether the operator acknowledged completion and understanding of SWIFT security responsibilities. |
| Evidence Reference / Link | Enter the LMS completion record ID, certificate ID, file path, ticket number, SharePoint link, or GRC evidence reference proving completion. |
| Evidence Type | Enter one allowed value: LMS report, Completion certificate, Attendance record, Signed attestation, Email confirmation, GRC record, Other. |
| Reviewed By | Enter the name or user ID of the person who reviewed the training record for completeness and accuracy. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the record was reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Manager / Control Owner Approval | Enter one allowed value: Approved, Rejected, Pending, Not Required. |
| Exception / Deferral Reference | Enter the approved exception, risk acceptance, or deferral reference if training was not completed by the due date; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Remediation Action | Enter the action required for overdue, failed, incomplete, or deferred training, e.g. reassign course, retake assessment, suspend SWIFT access pending completion; enter N/A if none. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target date for completing remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format, or N/A if not applicable. |
| Comments | Enter any additional audit-relevant context, such as reason for non-applicability, role change, leave of absence, joiner/leaver status, or evidence limitations. |

Updated at least annually for the SWIFT CSCF training cycle and whenever operators join, leave, change SWIFT roles, or complete training; source data should come from the LMS, HR system, IAM/SWIFT access review records, and GRC evidence repository.

SWF-023.title: Logging & Monitoring Evidence (Swift)
SWF-023.content:
## What This Evidences

This evidence supports SWIFT CSCF control 6.4 by demonstrating that security-relevant events for the SWIFT environment are captured, retained, monitored, and alerted on in a timely manner.

This artifact is **collected operational evidence**, not an authored document. Do not create sample logs or manually reconstruct events. Collect the evidence directly from the organisation’s logging, monitoring, SIEM, ticketing, or alerting platforms that receive events from SWIFT-related systems.

The evidence should show that logs are generated, centrally collected, protected from unauthorised alteration, retained for the required period, and reviewed or acted upon through alerting and incident handling processes.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect the evidence from the organisation’s logging and monitoring sources used for the SWIFT environment, typically including:

- SIEM or log management platform: [SIEM / log store name]
- Security monitoring dashboard: [SOC monitoring tool]
- SWIFT infrastructure logs from:
 - SWIFT Alliance Access / Entry: [system name]
 - SWIFT Connector / Gateway: [system name]
 - Operating systems hosting SWIFT components: [server names]
 - Database, middleware, and application logs: [platform names]
- Identity and access management logs: [IAM / AD / PAM system]
- Network and perimeter security tools:
 - Firewalls: [firewall platform]
 - IDS/IPS: [IDS/IPS tool]
 - Endpoint security / EDR: [EDR tool]
- Alert and incident records:
 - ITSM platform: [ITSM tool]
 - SOC case management: [case tool]
 - Email or paging platform: [alerting tool]

## How To Collect

1. Define the evidence period, for example [start date] to [end date].
2. Log in to [SIEM / log store name] using an authorised account.
3. Filter logs for the SWIFT environment using hostnames, IP addresses, application identifiers, or log source groups such as [SWIFT log source group].
4. Export log ingestion evidence showing that SWIFT-related sources are actively sending logs.
5. Run searches for key event types, including authentication events, privileged access, configuration changes, application errors, connectivity events, security alerts, and failed access attempts.
6. Export search results in the native report format or CSV/PDF, preserving timestamps and source details.
7. Capture the monitoring dashboard showing active log sources, last event received, parsing status, and alert status.
8. Retrieve alert rules or correlation rules relevant to SWIFT activity from [SIEM / monitoring tool].
9. Export examples of alerts generated during the period, including related SOC or ITSM tickets.
10. Capture retention configuration from [SIEM / log store name] showing the retention period for SWIFT logs.
11. Store all exports and screenshots in the approved evidence repository with a clear filename and date.

## What To Capture

Capture sufficient evidence to show log capture, retention, and alerting, including:

- Log source inventory for all SWIFT-related systems
- Hostname, IP address, application name, and log source type
- Last event received timestamp for each source
- Log ingestion status and parsing status
- Sample raw and parsed log records
- Event timestamp, source, user ID, action, result, severity, and destination where applicable
- Authentication successes and failures
- Privileged or administrative actions
- Changes to configuration, access rights, or security settings
- SWIFT application and transaction processing events where available
- Security alerts involving SWIFT systems
- Alert rule names, trigger conditions, severity, and notification targets
- SOC or ITSM tickets linked to alerts, including status and resolution notes
- Retention settings for SWIFT log data
- Evidence of time synchronisation where visible, such as consistent timestamps across sources

## Frequency & Owner

- Collection frequency: [monthly / quarterly / before audit / after control testing]
- Operational monitoring frequency: continuous
- Primary owner: [SOC Manager / Security Operations Lead]
- Supporting owners:
 - [SWIFT Operations Manager]
 - [Infrastructure Lead]
 - [IAM/PAM Owner]
 - [ITSM Process Owner]

Evidence should be reviewed by [control owner] before submission to confirm completeness and relevance.

## Retention & Storage

Store collected evidence in [evidence repository / GRC tool / secure document store].

Retention should meet the organisation’s SWIFT, security monitoring, legal, and audit requirements, typically at least [retention period] for security logs and related alert records.

Evidence storage must:

- Restrict access to authorised personnel only
- Preserve original exports where possible
- Prevent unauthorised modification or deletion
- Maintain collection date, collector name, source system, and evidence period
- Use consistent naming, for example: `SWIFT_CSCF_6.4_LoggingMonitoring_[period]_[source]`

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence when it shows that:

- SWIFT-related systems are included in central logging and monitoring
- Logs are being actively received from all in-scope systems
- Events include enough detail to support investigation and accountability
- Security-relevant activities are monitored and alert rules exist
- Alerts are routed to an appropriate SOC, operations team, or ticketing process
- Example alerts or tickets show review, triage, escalation, and closure
- Log retention settings meet the organisation’s stated retention requirement
- Evidence is exported directly from operational systems, not manually created
- The evidence period, source systems, collector, and collection date are clear
- No unexplained gaps exist for critical SWIFT systems or event types

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Evidence Period | Enter the reporting period covered by this record in format YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD. |
| SWIFT CSCF Control Reference | Enter the applicable SWIFT CSCF control reference; normally enter 'CSCF 6.1 - Malware Protection'. |
| Asset ID | Enter the unique asset identifier from the CMDB, endpoint management platform, or SWIFT secure zone asset inventory. |
| Hostname | Enter the device hostname exactly as shown in the anti-malware or endpoint management console. |
| Asset Type | Enter the type of asset using allowed values: Server, Workstation, Jump Server, HSM Management Host, Network Management Host, Virtual Machine, Other. |
| Environment / Zone | Enter the network or operational zone where the asset resides, for example SWIFT Secure Zone, Back Office, DMZ, Management Zone, or Corporate LAN. |
| SWIFT Scope | Enter whether the asset is in scope for SWIFT CSCF using allowed values: In Scope, Supporting System, Out of Scope; include only justified out-of-scope entries where relevant to evidence completeness. |
| Operating System | Enter the operating system name and version, for example Windows Server 2022, Windows 11, RHEL 9, AIX 7.3. |
| IP Address | Enter the primary IP address of the asset in IPv4 or IPv6 format, or enter 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Anti-Malware Product | Enter the vendor and product name of the installed anti-malware solution, for example Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike Falcon, Trellix ENS, Symantec Endpoint Security. |
| Anti-Malware Agent Version | Enter the installed anti-malware agent or sensor version exactly as reported by the management console. |
| Anti-Malware Status | Enter the deployment/health status using allowed values: Installed, Not Installed, Disabled, Unmanaged, Error. |
| Real-Time Protection Status | Enter the status of real-time/on-access protection using allowed values: Enabled, Disabled, Not Supported, Unknown. |
| Malware Definition / Signature Version | Enter the current malware definition, signature, engine, or intelligence version exactly as reported by the anti-malware console. |
| Last Successful Definition Update Date/Time | Enter the last successful definition/signature/intelligence update timestamp in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ. |
| Definition Currency Status | Enter whether definitions are current against policy using allowed values: Current, Outdated, Unknown; define Current according to the organisation's approved anti-malware update policy. |
| Last Successful Full Scan Date/Time | Enter the most recent completed full system scan timestamp in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ, or 'N/A' if full scans are not required by approved policy. |
| Last Successful Quick Scan Date/Time | Enter the most recent completed quick/scheduled scan timestamp in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ, or 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Last Scan Result | Enter the result of the latest completed scan using allowed values: Clean, Threats Found, Failed, Cancelled, Not Run, Unknown. |
| Malware Detected | Enter whether malware was detected during the evidence period using allowed values: Yes, No, Unknown. |
| Malware Detection Count | Enter the number of malware detections for the asset during the evidence period as a whole number; enter 0 if none. |
| Remediation Status | Enter the remediation status using allowed values: Not Required, Quarantined, Removed, Remediated, Pending, Failed, Accepted Risk. |
| Quarantine / Removal Evidence Reference | Enter the ticket ID, alert ID, incident ID, or console evidence reference proving quarantine/removal; enter 'N/A' where no malware was detected. |
| Update Source | Enter the source used for anti-malware updates using allowed values or equivalent: Vendor Cloud, Internal Update Server, EDR Console, WSUS/SCCM, Offline Manual Update, Other. |
| Management Console Policy Name | Enter the anti-malware policy/profile/group assigned to the asset exactly as shown in the management console. |
| Policy Compliance Status | Enter whether the asset complies with the approved anti-malware policy using allowed values: Compliant, Non-Compliant, Not Assessed. |
| Exclusion Configured | Enter whether anti-malware exclusions are configured on the asset using allowed values: Yes, No, Unknown. |
| Exclusion Details / Approval Reference | If exclusions exist, enter a concise description and the approved change/risk acceptance reference; enter 'N/A' if no exclusions exist. |
| Exception Required | Enter whether an exception is required for any non-compliance using allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Exception Reference | Enter the approved exception/risk acceptance/ticket reference for any deviation; enter 'N/A' if no exception is required. |
| Exception Expiry Date | Enter the expiry date of the approved exception in format YYYY-MM-DD, or 'N/A' if no exception applies. |
| Evidence Source | Enter the source of evidence, for example anti-malware management console export, EDR report, endpoint screenshot, SIEM query, vulnerability/asset tool export. |
| Evidence Capture Date/Time | Enter the date and time the evidence was extracted or captured in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ. |
| Reviewed By | Enter the name or role of the person who reviewed the evidence for completeness and compliance. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the evidence was reviewed in format YYYY-MM-DD. |
| Reviewer Conclusion | Enter the review outcome using allowed values: Pass, Pass with Exception, Fail, Follow-Up Required. |
| Follow-Up Action Reference | Enter the remediation ticket, incident, problem, or action reference for any issue identified; enter 'N/A' if no follow-up is required. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Security Operations or Endpoint Security Manager, with review by the SWIFT Control Owner. Updated at least monthly and after any malware event, endpoint onboarding/decommissioning, policy change, or SWIFT secure zone asset change, using exports from the anti-malware/EDR management console, CMDB/asset inventory, SIEM alerts, and remediation ticketing system.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this backup or restore evidence record, using a consistent format such as BAK-YYYY-NNNN. |
| SWIFT CSCF Control Reference | Enter the applicable SWIFT CSCF control reference(s) this record supports, for example the relevant backup, recovery, resilience, or Cross-CSCF evidence reference used by the organisation. |
| Backup Policy / Procedure Reference | Enter the approved backup and restore policy, standard, or procedure document ID and version that defines the requirement followed. |
| Business Service / SWIFT Component | Enter the business service, SWIFT infrastructure component, application, database, server, interface, or supporting service being backed up. |
| Asset / System Name | Enter the exact hostname, application name, database name, virtual machine name, storage volume, or system name as recorded in the CMDB or inventory. |
| Asset ID / CMDB Reference | Enter the authoritative asset identifier from the CMDB, inventory, or asset register. |
| Environment | Enter one allowed value: Production, Disaster Recovery, UAT, Test, Development, Management, Security Tooling, Other. |
| Backup Scope | Describe precisely what is included in the backup, such as full server image, database, configuration files, SWIFT application data, HSM configuration export, logs, or specific filesystem paths. |
| Data Classification | Enter the classification of the backed-up data using the organisation's approved classification scheme, for example Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, or Highly Confidential. |
| Backup Type | Enter one allowed value: Full, Incremental, Differential, Snapshot, Image, Database Dump, Configuration Export, Log Backup, Other. |
| Backup Frequency | Enter the scheduled frequency, for example Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Hourly, Every 4 Hours, On Change, Ad Hoc. |
| Backup Job / Schedule Name | Enter the exact backup job name, schedule name, policy name, or automation identifier from the backup platform. |
| Backup Start Date/Time UTC | Enter the backup start timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. |
| Backup End Date/Time UTC | Enter the backup completion timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. |
| Backup Status | Enter one allowed value: Successful, Successful with Warning, Failed, Cancelled, Missed, In Progress. |
| Failure / Exception Details | If the status is not Successful, enter the error message, exception code, failed object, or missed schedule reason; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Remediation Action Taken | For failed, missed, or warning backups, enter the corrective action taken, such as rerun job, resolved storage capacity, corrected credentials, or escalated incident; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Remediation Completion Date | Enter the date remediation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format, or Not Applicable if no remediation was required. |
| Backup Location / Repository | Enter the primary repository, media, storage bucket, backup appliance, vault, or data centre location where the backup is stored. |
| Offsite / Segregated Copy Location | Enter the offsite, logically segregated, cloud vault, DR site, or secondary location where a copy is held; enter Not Applicable if not required by policy. |
| Encryption Applied | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the backup data is encrypted at rest and/or in transit according to policy. |
| Encryption Method / Key Reference | Enter the encryption method and key reference, such as AES-256, KMS key alias, HSM-backed key ID, or backup platform key policy; do not enter secret key values. |
| Integrity Verification Performed | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether checksum, backup verification, media verification, or platform integrity validation was performed. |
| Integrity Verification Result | Enter one allowed value: Passed, Failed, Not Performed, Not Applicable. |
| Retention Period | Enter the required retention period for this backup, including unit, for example 30 days, 90 days, 1 year, 7 years. |
| Retention Expiry Date | Enter the date the backup is eligible for deletion or archival expiry in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on the retention rule. |
| Immutable / Tamper-Protected Copy | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the backup is protected by immutability, WORM, object lock, vault lock, or equivalent tamper protection. |
| Backup Operator / System Account | Enter the user ID, service account, automation account, or backup platform account that executed the backup. |
| Backup Evidence Reference | Enter the evidence location or reference, such as ticket ID, backup report ID, log extract path, screenshot reference, SIEM event ID, or backup console report URL. |
| Restore Test Required | Enter Yes or No based on whether this backup is selected for restore testing under the approved restore test schedule or sampling plan. |
| Restore Test Date | Enter the date the restore test was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format, or Not Applicable if restore testing was not required for this record. |
| Restore Test Type | Enter one allowed value: File-Level Restore, Database Restore, Full System Restore, Application Restore, Configuration Restore, DR Restore, Tabletop Only, Not Applicable. |
| Restore Test Target Environment | Enter the environment or isolated location where the restore was tested, such as DR, Test, Sandbox, Isolated Recovery Network, or Not Applicable. |
| Restore Test Result | Enter one allowed value: Passed, Passed with Issues, Failed, Not Tested, Not Applicable. |
| Restore Start Date/Time UTC | Enter the restore test start timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, or Not Applicable. |
| Restore End Date/Time UTC | Enter the restore test completion timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, or Not Applicable. |
| RTO Target | Enter the approved Recovery Time Objective for the system, including unit, for example 4 hours, 24 hours, 2 business days. |
| Actual Restore Duration | Enter the actual elapsed restore duration, including unit, for example 2 hours 15 minutes, or Not Applicable if not tested. |
| RPO Target | Enter the approved Recovery Point Objective for the system, including unit, for example 15 minutes, 4 hours, 24 hours. |
| Actual Data Loss / Recovery Point | Enter the actual recovery point achieved or data loss window, including timestamp or duration, for example recovered to YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or 30 minutes; enter Not Applicable if not tested. |
| Restore Validation Performed By | Enter the name, role, or team of the person who validated that restored data, application, configuration, or service was usable. |
| Restore Validation Evidence Reference | Enter the evidence reference proving restore validation, such as test script ID, signed validation checklist, ticket ID, screenshot reference, database query output, or application health check report. |
| Issues Identified During Restore Test | Enter any issues, defects, missing data, integrity concerns, access problems, or performance concerns identified during restore testing; enter None if no issues were identified. |
| Corrective Action Reference | Enter the incident, problem, change, risk acceptance, or corrective action tracking reference for any identified issue; enter Not Applicable if no issue was identified. |
| Record Reviewed By | Enter the name or role of the person who reviewed this record for completeness and accuracy. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the record was reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record Approval Status | Enter one allowed value: Draft, Pending Review, Approved, Rejected, Superseded. |
| Comments | Enter any additional relevant context that supports audit understanding; do not use this field for required data captured elsewhere. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Backup and Recovery Manager with review by the SWIFT Service Owner and Information Security/GRC team. Update after each scheduled backup exception and each restore test, with at least monthly completeness review; source data comes from the backup platform reports, CMDB, ticketing/change system, restore test evidence repository, and approved backup/restore policy.

field_guidance.Record ID: Enter a unique identifier for this backup or restore evidence record, using a consistent format such as BAK-YYYY-NNNN.
field_guidance.SWIFT CSCF Control Reference: Enter the applicable SWIFT CSCF control reference(s) this record supports, for example the relevant backup, recovery, resilience, or Cross-CSCF evidence reference used by the organisation.
field_guidance.Backup Policy / Procedure Reference: Enter the approved backup and restore policy, standard, or procedure document ID and version that defines the requirement followed.
field_guidance.Business Service / SWIFT Component: Enter the business service, SWIFT infrastructure component, application, database, server, interface, or supporting service being backed up.
field_guidance.Asset / System Name: Enter the exact hostname, application name, database name, virtual machine name, storage volume, or system name as recorded in the CMDB or inventory.
field_guidance.Asset ID / CMDB Reference: Enter the authoritative asset identifier from the CMDB, inventory, or asset register.
field_guidance.Environment: Enter one allowed value: Production, Disaster Recovery, UAT, Test, Development, Management, Security Tooling, Other.
field_guidance.Backup Scope: Describe precisely what is included in the backup, such as full server image, database, configuration files, SWIFT application data, HSM configuration export, logs, or specific filesystem paths.
field_guidance.Data Classification: Enter the classification of the backed-up data using the organisation's approved classification scheme, for example Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, or Highly Confidential.
field_guidance.Backup Type: Enter one allowed value: Full, Incremental, Differential, Snapshot, Image, Database Dump, Configuration Export, Log Backup, Other.
field_guidance.Backup Frequency: Enter the scheduled frequency, for example Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Hourly, Every 4 Hours, On Change, Ad Hoc.
field_guidance.Backup Job / Schedule Name: Enter the exact backup job name, schedule name, policy name, or automation identifier from the backup platform.
field_guidance.Backup Start Date/Time UTC: Enter the backup start timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.
field_guidance.Backup End Date/Time UTC: Enter the backup completion timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.
field_guidance.Backup Status: Enter one allowed value: Successful, Successful with Warning, Failed, Cancelled, Missed, In Progress.
field_guidance.Failure / Exception Details: If the status is not Successful, enter the error message, exception code, failed object, or missed schedule reason; otherwise enter Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Remediation Action Taken: For failed, missed, or warning backups, enter the corrective action taken, such as rerun job, resolved storage capacity, corrected credentials, or escalated incident; otherwise enter Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Remediation Completion Date: Enter the date remediation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format, or Not Applicable if no remediation was required.
field_guidance.Backup Location / Repository: Enter the primary repository, media, storage bucket, backup appliance, vault, or data centre location where the backup is stored.
field_guidance.Offsite / Segregated Copy Location: Enter the offsite, logically segregated, cloud vault, DR site, or secondary location where a copy is held; enter Not Applicable if not required by policy.
field_guidance.Encryption Applied: Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the backup data is encrypted at rest and/or in transit according to policy.
field_guidance.Encryption Method / Key Reference: Enter the encryption method and key reference, such as AES-256, KMS key alias, HSM-backed key ID, or backup platform key policy; do not enter secret key values.
field_guidance.Integrity Verification Performed: Enter Yes or No to indicate whether checksum, backup verification, media verification, or platform integrity validation was performed.
field_guidance.Integrity Verification Result: Enter one allowed value: Passed, Failed, Not Performed, Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Retention Period: Enter the required retention period for this backup, including unit, for example 30 days, 90 days, 1 year, 7 years.
field_guidance.Retention Expiry Date: Enter the date the backup is eligible for deletion or archival expiry in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on the retention rule.
field_guidance.Immutable / Tamper-Protected Copy: Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the backup is protected by immutability, WORM, object lock, vault lock, or equivalent tamper protection.
field_guidance.Backup Operator / System Account: Enter the user ID, service account, automation account, or backup platform account that executed the backup.
field_guidance.Backup Evidence Reference: Enter the evidence location or reference, such as ticket ID, backup report ID, log extract path, screenshot reference, SIEM event ID, or backup console report URL.
field_guidance.Restore Test Required: Enter Yes or No based on whether this backup is selected for restore testing under the approved restore test schedule or sampling plan.
field_guidance.Restore Test Date: Enter the date the restore test was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format, or Not Applicable if restore testing was not required for this record.
field_guidance.Restore Test Type: Enter one allowed value: File-Level Restore, Database Restore, Full System Restore, Application Restore, Configuration Restore, DR Restore, Tabletop Only, Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Restore Test Target Environment: Enter the environment or isolated location where the restore was tested, such as DR, Test, Sandbox, Isolated Recovery Network, or Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Restore Test Result: Enter one allowed value: Passed, Passed with Issues, Failed, Not Tested, Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Restore Start Date/Time UTC: Enter the restore test start timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, or Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Restore End Date/Time UTC: Enter the restore test completion timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, or Not Applicable.
field_guidance.RTO Target: Enter the approved Recovery Time Objective for the system, including unit, for example 4 hours, 24 hours, 2 business days.
field_guidance.Actual Restore Duration: Enter the actual elapsed restore duration, including unit, for example 2 hours 15 minutes, or Not Applicable if not tested.
field_guidance.RPO Target: Enter the approved Recovery Point Objective for the system, including unit, for example 15 minutes, 4 hours, 24 hours.
field_guidance.Actual Data Loss / Recovery Point: Enter the actual recovery point achieved or data loss window, including timestamp or duration, for example recovered to YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or 30 minutes; enter Not Applicable if not tested.
field_guidance.Restore Validation Performed By: Enter the name, role, or team of the person who validated that restored data, application, configuration, or service was usable.
field_guidance.Restore Validation Evidence Reference: Enter the evidence reference proving restore validation, such as test script ID, signed validation checklist, ticket ID, screenshot reference, database query output, or application health check report.
field_guidance.Issues Identified During Restore Test: Enter any issues, defects, missing data, integrity concerns, access problems, or performance concerns identified during restore testing; enter None if no issues were identified.
field_guidance.Corrective Action Reference: Enter the incident, problem, change, risk acceptance, or corrective action tracking reference for any identified issue; enter Not Applicable if no issue was identified.
field_guidance.Record Reviewed By: Enter the name or role of the person who reviewed this record for completeness and accuracy.
field_guidance.Review Date: Enter the date the record was reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Record Approval Status: Enter one allowed value: Draft, Pending Review, Approved, Rejected, Superseded.
field_guidance.Comments: Enter any additional relevant context that supports audit understanding; do not use this field for required data captured elsewhere.
