SWF-026.title: Physical Security Evidence (Swift)
SWF-026.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | Physical Security Manager | [Effective Date] | SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework | Confidential |

## Purpose

This evidence document defines the records, artefacts, validation activities, and retention requirements used to demonstrate that physical access to the organisation’s Swift zone is restricted, authorised, monitored, and periodically reviewed.

The purpose of this evidence is to show that only approved personnel can physically access locations where Swift-related systems, workstations, network equipment, authentication devices, printed materials, backup media, or supporting infrastructure are located. It also demonstrates that visitor access, emergency access, and access changes are controlled and traceable.

This document is intended for use by internal control owners, compliance teams, internal audit, external assessors, and authorised Swift assurance reviewers.

## What This Evidence Demonstrates

This evidence demonstrates that the organisation has implemented effective physical security controls for the Swift zone, including:

- Defined physical boundaries for areas supporting Swift operations.
- Controlled entry to Swift-related rooms, cabinets, racks, safes, and restricted work areas.
- Approval-based access for personnel with a business need to enter the Swift zone.
- Removal or modification of access when personnel change role, leave the organisation, or no longer require access.
- Logging of physical entry and exit activity through badge systems, access control systems, guards, visitor registers, or equivalent mechanisms.
- Supervision and registration of visitors, contractors, vendors, and maintenance personnel.
- Protection of Swift components against unauthorised viewing, tampering, theft, loss, or environmental exposure.
- Periodic review and reconciliation of physical access rights against current business need.
- Investigation and remediation of unauthorised, unusual, or failed access attempts.
- Retention of sufficient records to support management review, audit, and assurance activities.

The evidence should be capable of answering the following audit questions:

| Audit Question | Expected Evidence |
|---|---|
| Where is the Swift zone physically located and how is it separated from general office areas? | Swift zone floor plan, data centre cage or room designation, rack location, restricted area definition, photographs where permitted |
| Who is authorised to access the Swift zone? | Approved access list, role-based access matrix, management approvals |
| How is access granted? | Access request records, approval workflow, identity verification, badge or key assignment records |
| How is access removed? | Leaver records, role-change records, access revocation logs, key return records |
| How is entry monitored? | Badge logs, guard logs, door access reports, visitor registers, CCTV review records where applicable |
| Are visitors controlled? | Visitor sign-in logs, escort records, temporary badge records, maintenance tickets |
| Are access rights reviewed? | Periodic access review reports, reviewer sign-off, remediation evidence |
| Are exceptions investigated? | Incident records, failed access reports, exception approvals, corrective actions |
| Are physical assets protected from unauthorised handling? | Rack lock records, cabinet access logs, safe register, media handling records |

## Scope

This evidence applies to all physical locations and assets that support or protect the organisation’s Swift environment.

In scope areas include, where applicable:

- Swift operating room or dedicated Swift workspace.
- Data centre rooms, cages, racks, cabinets, or hosting areas containing Swift infrastructure.
- Secure network rooms containing Swift connectivity components.
- Secure storage areas for Swift-related tokens, certificates, backup media, printed instructions, sealed envelopes, or recovery materials.
- Locations where Swift operator workstations, jump stations, terminals, printers, or related peripherals are located.
- Disaster recovery or alternate processing sites used for Swift operations.
- Any third-party facility where Swift-related infrastructure is hosted, managed, or physically accessible.

In scope personnel include:

- Swift operators.
- Swift administrators.
- Infrastructure administrators supporting Swift systems.
- Network and security administrators supporting Swift connectivity.
- Facilities and data centre personnel with physical access to Swift areas.
- Security guards and reception staff involved in access control.
- Approved third-party support personnel.
- Auditors and assessors requiring supervised access.

Out of scope:

- General office access controls that do not affect the Swift zone.
- Logical access controls to Swift applications or infrastructure, except where linked to physical access evidence.
- General workplace health and safety records unless they relate directly to access to the Swift zone.
- Public areas, reception areas, and shared building spaces not used to protect Swift assets.

The Swift zone for this evidence is defined as:

| Swift Zone Component | Location | Physical Boundary | Primary Access Control | Evidence Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Swift operator workstation area | [Location] | Restricted office / secured room | Badge access and authorised access list | Badge access system report |
| Swift infrastructure rack | [Data Centre / Room / Rack ID] | Locked rack in restricted data centre area | Data centre access control and rack key control | Data centre access log and rack key register |
| Network connectivity equipment | [Network Room / Rack ID] | Restricted communications room | Badge access and facilities approval | Access control report |
| Secure storage for tokens or media | [Secure Storage Location] | Locked safe or secure cabinet | Key control / dual custody where applicable | Safe access register |
| Disaster recovery Swift area | [DR Location] | Restricted room or cage | Badge access and site access approval | DR site access report |

## Required Contents

The evidence pack must contain sufficient records to demonstrate the design and operating effectiveness of physical access controls for the Swift zone.

### 1. Swift Zone Definition and Layout

The evidence pack must include a clear description of the Swift zone and the physical locations where Swift assets are processed, administered, connected, or stored.

Required evidence includes:

| Evidence Item | Minimum Content Required | Owner | Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Swift zone physical boundary definition | Description of restricted areas, rooms, racks, cabinets, and storage points | Physical Security Manager | At implementation and when changed |
| Floor plan or location map | Location of restricted Swift areas, access doors, secured racks, and visitor entry points | Facilities Manager | At implementation and when changed |
| Asset-to-location mapping | Swift assets mapped to room, rack, cabinet, safe, or workstation area | Swift Infrastructure Owner | Quarterly or when changed |
| Photographic evidence where permitted | Photos of restricted doors, badge readers, locked racks, safes, or cabinets without exposing sensitive details | Physical Security Manager | Annually or when changed |
| Third-party site description | Confirmation of physical location and segregation controls at hosted or managed facilities | Third-Party Service Owner | Annually or on contract change |

### 2. Authorised Physical Access List

The evidence pack must include a current list of individuals authorised to physically access the Swift zone.

The authorised access list must include:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Full name | Legal or HR-recorded name of the individual |
| Unique identifier | Employee ID, contractor ID, or third-party reference |
| Organisation / department | Employing organisation and business unit |
| Role | Business role requiring access |
| Access area | Specific Swift-related physical area authorised |
| Access level | Normal access, escorted access, emergency access, maintenance access, or read-only visitor access |
| Business justification | Reason access is required |
| Approving manager | Manager or control owner who approved access |
| Approval date | Date access was approved |
| Access expiry date | Required for contractors, temporary staff, and vendors |
| Last review date | Most recent access recertification date |
| Status | Active, suspended, expired, or revoked |

Example format:

| Name | ID | Department / Organisation | Role | Access Area | Access Level | Approved By | Approval Date | Expiry Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Name] | [ID] | Treasury Operations | Swift Operator | Swift operating room | Normal access | [Approver] | [Date] | N/A | Active |
| [Name] | [ID] | Infrastructure Services | Server Administrator | Data centre rack [Rack ID] | Normal access | [Approver] | [Date] | N/A | Active |
| [Name] | [ID] | [Vendor] | Hardware Maintenance Engineer | Data centre rack [Rack ID] | Escorted access | [Approver] | [Date] | [Date] | Active |

### 3. Access Request and Approval Records

For each individual granted access to the Swift zone, the evidence pack must include a corresponding request and approval record.

Each request must show:

- Requestor name and identifier.
- Role and organisation.
- Area requested.
- Reason for access.
- Access duration.
- Whether access is permanent, temporary, emergency, or visitor-based.
- Confirmation that identity has been verified.
- Approval by the appropriate Swift business owner, physical security owner, data centre owner, or facilities owner.
- Date access was provisioned.
- Badge, key, biometric, or access profile issued.
- Expiry date for temporary or third-party access.

Access must not be granted based solely on informal requests, verbal approval, shared team membership, or convenience.

### 4. Access Removal and Change Records

The evidence pack must include records showing timely removal or modification of physical access when it is no longer required.

Events requiring access removal or modification include:

- Employment termination.
- Contractor end date.
- Vendor engagement end date.
- Role change.
- Department transfer.
- Leave of absence where required by risk.
- Suspension due to investigation.
- Completion of maintenance activity.
- Expiry of temporary access.
- Closure of emergency access event.

Required evidence includes:

| Evidence Item | Minimum Content Required |
|---|---|
| Leaver report | Individual, termination date, access removal date, confirmation of badge or key return |
| Role-change report | Previous role, new role, access reassessment, access modification date |
| Contractor expiry report | Contractor name, expiry date, sponsoring manager, access status |
| Revocation log | Access profile removed, key returned, safe combination changed where applicable |
| Exception record | Any delay in removal, risk acceptance, compensating controls, remediation date |

### 5. Physical Access Logs

The evidence pack must include physical access logs for all controlled Swift zone entry points.

Access logs may be obtained from:

- Badge access systems.
- Data centre access management systems.
- Guard desk registers.
- Visitor management systems.
- Key issue registers.
- Safe access logs.
- Rack or cage access logs.
- Maintenance access logs.
- CCTV access review logs where used to validate entry events.

Minimum log content:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Date and time | Entry and exit time where available |
| Individual name or badge ID | Person accessing the area |
| Access point | Door, room, cage, rack, safe, cabinet, or visitor checkpoint |
| Access result | Granted, denied, forced door, tailgating alert, expired badge, or manual override |
| Access method | Badge, key, guard release, visitor pass, safe code, biometric, or emergency override |
| Escort name | Required for visitors and escorted third parties |
| Reason for access | Required for visitors, maintenance, emergency access, or out-of-hours access |
| Related ticket or approval | Change ticket, maintenance ticket, incident ticket, or visitor request reference |
| Reviewer | Person who reviewed the log |
| Review outcome | Accepted, investigated, escalated, or remediated |

### 6. Visitor and Contractor Access Records

The evidence pack must include records showing that visitors and contractors do not receive uncontrolled access to the Swift zone.

Visitor and contractor access records must show:

- Visitor full name.
- Organisation represented.
- Host or escort name.
- Purpose of visit.
- Entry and exit date and time.
- Area visited.
- Badge or pass number.
- Confirmation that temporary credentials were returned.
- Escort confirmation for restricted Swift areas.
- Maintenance or change ticket reference where applicable.
- Approval by an authorised Swift, facilities, or data centre owner.
- Confirmation that the visitor did not access unauthorised areas.

Example visitor log:

| Date | Visitor Name | Organisation | Purpose | Area Visited | Host / Escort | Time In | Time Out | Badge Returned | Ticket / Approval |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| [Date] | [Name] | [Company] | UPS maintenance | Data centre room [Room ID] | [Escort] | [Time] | [Time] | Yes | [Ticket ID] |
| [Date] | [Name] | [Company] | External audit walkthrough | Swift operating room | [Escort] | [Time] | [Time] | Yes | [Approval ID] |

### 7. Key, Badge, Safe, and Rack Access Control Records

The evidence pack must include records for physical credentials and physical security mechanisms used to protect the Swift zone.

Required records include:

| Control Area | Evidence Required |
|---|---|
| Badge profiles | Badge ID, assigned holder, access profile, activation date, expiry date, revocation date |
| Physical keys | Key number, lock or area, assigned holder, issue date, return date, approval |
| Rack or cabinet locks | Rack ID, authorised key holders, access date, access reason |
| Safe or secure cabinet | Authorised users, access register, combination change record where applicable |
| Emergency keys or break-glass access | Storage location, authorised custodians, use record, post-use review |
| Lost credentials | Incident record, disablement date, replacement record, investigation outcome |

Shared keys, shared badges, untracked access cards, or uncontrolled safe combinations must not be used for Swift zone access.

### 8. Periodic Access Review Evidence

Physical access to the Swift zone must be reviewed periodically to confirm that access remains appropriate.

The evidence pack must include:

- Review population from the access control system.
- Current authorised access list.
- HR active employee and contractor listing.
- Role or department information.
- Confirmation from managers or system owners that access remains required.
- Identification of inappropriate, expired, duplicate, or excessive access.
- Evidence that removals or modifications were completed.
- Reviewer sign-off and date.

Example review record:

| Review Period | Population Reviewed | Reviewer | Exceptions Identified | Remediation Completed | Approval Date |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| [Quarter / Year] | Swift room, data centre rack, safe access | [Reviewer] | [Number] | [Date / N/A] | [Date] |

Example exception tracker:

| Exception ID | Individual | Issue Identified | Risk | Action Required | Owner | Due Date | Completion Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [EX-001] | [Name] | Contractor access active after end date | Unauthorised physical access to Swift rack | Remove access and confirm badge disabled | [Owner] | [Date] | [Date] | Closed |
| [EX-002] | [Name] | Access to Swift room no longer required after role change | Excessive access | Remove Swift room profile | [Owner] | [Date] | [Date] | Closed |

### 9. Monitoring and Exception Evidence

The evidence pack must include evidence that unusual or unauthorised physical access events are monitored, investigated, and resolved.

Events requiring review include:

- Denied access attempts to the Swift zone.
- Access attempts by inactive, expired, or unknown badges.
- Out-of-hours access.
- Access by personnel without a related business reason.
- Forced door or door-held-open alarms.
- Tailgating alerts.
- Emergency override use.
- Use of visitor or temporary badges for sensitive areas.
- Access by terminated or transferred personnel.
- Unplanned maintenance access.
- Missing, lost, or unreturned keys or badges.
- Safe or secure cabinet access outside approved procedures.

The monitoring evidence must show:

| Evidence Item | Minimum Content Required |
|---|---|
| Exception report | Date, individual, access point, event type, access outcome |
| Investigation record | Assigned investigator, review steps, related logs, interview notes where applicable |
| Business validation | Confirmation whether the access was authorised and justified |
| Corrective action | Badge disabled, access removed, alarm repaired, process updated, training completed |
| Closure evidence | Owner sign-off, closure date, residual risk assessment where applicable |

### 10. Environmental and Facility Security Supporting Evidence

Where the Swift zone depends on controlled facility conditions, the evidence pack should include relevant supporting records.

Supporting evidence may include:

| Area | Evidence Examples |
|---|---|
| Door and lock maintenance | Maintenance logs, repair tickets, inspection reports |
| CCTV coverage | Camera location list, retention setting, review records, access to CCTV system |
| Alarm systems | Door alarm test records, incident logs, alarm response procedures |
| Data centre controls | Site access reports, cage access reports, rack lock records, facility attestation |
| Fire and environmental protection | Inspection records, environmental monitoring alerts, response evidence |
| Clean desk / clear screen in Swift room | Spot-check records, exception logs, remediation evidence |
| Secure disposal | Shredding certificates, media destruction records, secure bin collection records |

### 11. Third-Party or Hosted Facility Evidence

If any part of the Swift zone is hosted, operated, or physically protected by a third party, the evidence pack must include assurance that the third party applies suitable physical access controls.

Required evidence includes:

- Current contract or service description identifying physical security responsibilities.
- Description of the hosted Swift-related areas or racks.
- List of third-party personnel with physical access to Swift assets, where contractually available.
- Data centre or facility access reports for relevant Swift assets.
- Visitor and maintenance access logs for relevant periods.
- Evidence of access review for third-party personnel.
- Confirmation that customer access to the hosted facility is approved and logged.
- Facility assurance report, certificate, or independent assessment summary, where available.
- Records of any physical security incidents affecting the hosted environment.
- Evidence that issues raised by the third party or facility provider are tracked to closure.

## Collection & Validation

Evidence must be collected from authoritative sources and validated before submission to compliance, internal audit, external audit, or Swift assurance reviewers.

### Evidence Collection Sources

| Evidence Source | System / Repository | Evidence Owner | Collection Frequency | Output Format |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Badge access system | [Access Control System] | Physical Security Manager | Monthly and on request | PDF / CSV export |
| Data centre access system | [Data Centre Portal] | Data Centre Manager | Monthly and on request | PDF / CSV export |
| Visitor management system | [Visitor System] | Reception / Security Lead | Monthly and on request | PDF / CSV export |
| HR system | [HR System] | HR Operations | Quarterly and on request | CSV / report |
| Contractor register | [Contractor System] | Vendor Management | Quarterly and on request | CSV / report |
| Key register | [Repository / Logbook] | Facilities Manager | Quarterly and on request | Scanned register / spreadsheet |
| Safe access register | [Repository / Logbook] | Swift Operations Manager | Monthly and on request | Scanned register / spreadsheet |
| Physical access review | [GRC Platform] | Compliance Manager | Quarterly | Review report |
| Security incident system | [Incident System] | Security Operations Manager | Monthly and on request | Incident export |
| CCTV review records | [CCTV System / Security Log] | Physical Security Manager | As required | Review note / extract reference |

### Validation Activities

The evidence owner must perform the following validation activities before evidence is accepted:

| Validation Activity | Description | Performer | Minimum Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Completeness check | Confirm all required locations, access points, user groups, and Swift assets are included | Compliance Manager | Quarterly |
| Source verification | Confirm reports were exported from authoritative systems and not manually recreated | Evidence Owner | Each collection |
| Date range verification | Confirm logs cover the required audit period without unexplained gaps | Evidence Owner | Each collection |
| Access list reconciliation | Compare authorised access list against actual badge and key records | Physical Security Manager | Quarterly |
| HR reconciliation | Confirm active physical access holders are current employees, contractors, or approved third parties | HR Operations / Compliance | Quarterly |
| Leaver testing | Sample recent leavers and verify physical access was removed promptly | Compliance Manager | Quarterly |
| Visitor testing | Sample visitor entries and confirm escort, purpose, approval, and badge return | Physical Security Manager | Quarterly |
| Exception review | Confirm denied access, forced doors, emergency use, and out-of-hours access events were investigated | Security Operations Manager | Monthly |
| Remediation verification | Confirm identified issues were corrected and evidence retained | Compliance Manager | Quarterly |
| Management sign-off | Confirm control owner review and acceptance of the evidence pack | Physical Security Manager | Quarterly |

### Sampling Guidance

Where full population review is not practical, sampling must be risk-based and documented.

Minimum sampling expectations:

| Evidence Population | Minimum Sample |
|---|---|
| Active Swift zone access holders | All users where population is 25 or fewer; otherwise at least 25 users or 20%, whichever is greater |
| Access granted during review period | All grants where population is 15 or fewer; otherwise at least 15 grants or 20%, whichever is greater |
| Access removed during review period | All removals where population is 15 or fewer; otherwise at least 15 removals or 20%, whichever is greater |
| Visitor entries to Swift areas | At least 10 entries or 20%, whichever is greater |
| Out-of-hours access events | All events |
| Denied or failed access attempts | All events related to Swift areas |
| Emergency access events | All events |
| Lost badge or key events | All events |
| Third-party maintenance visits | All visits affecting Swift areas |

### Evidence Quality Criteria

Evidence must meet the following quality criteria:

- Complete: includes all relevant Swift physical locations and access methods.
- Current: reflects the applicable audit or assessment period.
- Authoritative: obtained directly from approved systems, registers, or accountable owners.
- Traceable: links access activity to individuals, approvals, tickets, or business reasons.
- Tamper-evident: stored in controlled repositories with restricted edit access.
- Reviewable: sufficiently clear for an independent reviewer to understand the control operation.
- Consistent: user names, identifiers, dates, and locations align across HR, access control, and asset records.
- Actionable: exceptions include owners, due dates, actions, and closure evidence.

### Evidence Pack Index

Each evidence pack must include an index to support reviewer navigation.

| Evidence ID | Evidence Name | Period Covered | Source | Owner | Validation Status | Repository Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PHYS-SWIFT-001 | Swift zone boundary definition | [Period] | Facilities records | Physical Security Manager | Validated | [Link] |
| PHYS-SWIFT-002 | Authorised physical access list | [Period] | Access control system | Physical Security Manager | Validated | [Link] |
| PHYS-SWIFT-003 | Physical access approval records | [Period] | Access request system | Facilities Manager | Validated | [Link] |
| PHYS-SWIFT-004 | Badge access logs | [Period] | Badge access system | Security Operations | Validated | [Link] |
| PHYS-SWIFT-005 | Visitor logs | [Period] | Visitor management system | Reception / Security Lead | Validated | [Link] |
| PHYS-SWIFT-006 | Key and safe access register | [Period] | Facilities register | Facilities Manager | Validated | [Link] |
| PHYS-SWIFT-007 | Quarterly physical access review | [Period] | GRC platform | Compliance Manager | Validated | [Link] |
| PHYS-SWIFT-008 | Physical access exceptions and remediation | [Period] | Incident system | Security Operations Manager | Validated | [Link] |
| PHYS-SWIFT-009 | Third-party facility physical security evidence | [Period] | Third-party portal | Third-Party Service Owner | Validated | [Link] |

### Approval and Sign-Off

The completed evidence pack must be reviewed and approved before submission.

| Role | Responsibility | Name | Date | Approval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Physical Security Manager | Confirms physical access controls and records are complete and accurate | [Name] | [Date] | [Approved / Rejected] |
| Swift Operations Manager | Confirms Swift zone locations and access needs are accurately represented | [Name] | [Date] | [Approved / Rejected] |
| Compliance Manager | Confirms evidence meets assessment and audit requirements | [Name] | [Date] | [Approved / Rejected] |
| Security Operations Manager | Confirms monitoring and exception evidence is complete | [Name] | [Date] | [Approved / Rejected] |

## Retention & Access

Physical security evidence for the Swift zone must be retained in a controlled repository and protected against unauthorised disclosure or alteration.

### Retention Requirements

| Evidence Type | Minimum Retention Period | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Swift zone definition and layout | Current version plus 7 years | Retain superseded layouts where they applied during an assessment period |
| Authorised access lists | 7 years | Retain each periodic snapshot used for access reviews |
| Access request and approval records | 7 years after access removal | Includes permanent, temporary, contractor, and emergency access |
| Access removal records | 7 years | Includes leaver, role-change, expiry, and revocation records |
| Badge and door access logs | 18 months minimum, or longer where required by internal policy | Longer retention is recommended for Swift-related restricted areas |
| Visitor logs | 7 years | Includes visitor purpose, escort, time in, time out, and badge return |
| Key and safe access registers | 7 years | Includes emergency key use and combination change records |
| Physical access review records | 7 years | Includes reviewer sign-off and remediation evidence |
| Exception and investigation records | 7 years after closure | Retain incident evidence, root cause, and corrective actions |
| CCTV footage | As defined by legal and privacy requirements | Retain longer only when linked to an investigation, incident, or audit request |
| Third-party facility evidence | 7 years or contract term plus required retention period | Retain assurance reports and relevant access records |

### Access Restrictions

Access to this evidence must be limited to personnel with a legitimate business need, including:

- Physical Security Manager.
- Facilities Manager.
- Swift Operations Manager.
- Swift Infrastructure Owner.
- Security Operations Manager.
- Compliance and risk personnel.
- Internal audit personnel.
- Authorised external auditors and Swift assurance reviewers.
- Legal, privacy, or investigation personnel where required.
- Approved third-party assessors under confidentiality obligations.

The following restrictions apply:

- Evidence containing floor plans, rack locations, access points, safe locations, CCTV details, badge identifiers, or guard procedures must be treated as sensitive security information.
- Evidence containing employee, contractor, visitor, or badgeholder information must be handled in accordance with privacy and data protection requirements.
- Evidence must not be distributed by email unless encrypted and approved by the evidence owner.
- Screenshots, exports, and scanned registers must be stored in approved repositories only.
- Edit permissions must be restricted to evidence owners and designated compliance administrators.
- Read access must be logged where supported by the repository.
- External sharing must be time-bound, watermarked where practicable, and approved by the Compliance Manager or evidence owner.
- Redaction must be applied where full disclosure is not necessary, provided the evidence remains sufficient for audit validation.

### Repository Requirements

The repository used to store this evidence must provide:

- Role-based access control.
- Version history.
- Audit logging.
- Protection against unauthorised deletion or modification.
- Ability to preserve evidence for the required retention period.
- Searchable indexing by evidence ID, period, owner, and location.
- Secure sharing capability for authorised reviewers.
- Backup and recovery protection.

### Chain of Custody

Where evidence is extracted for audit, investigation, or external assurance, the extraction and transfer must be recorded.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Evidence ID | Unique evidence identifier |
| Extracted by | Person who exported or copied the evidence |
| Extraction date and time | Date and time of extraction |
| Source system | Authoritative system or repository |
| Period covered | Date range represented by the evidence |
| File name or reference | Export file name, report name, or repository link |
| Hash or integrity check | File hash or other integrity measure where required |
| Recipient | Person or organisation receiving the evidence |
| Transfer method | Secure portal, encrypted file transfer, controlled repository access |
| Approval | Evidence owner approval for release |
| Return or destruction confirmation | Required for external copies where applicable |

### Review and Maintenance

This evidence specification must be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to:

- Swift zone location or physical layout.
- Swift infrastructure hosting model.
- Data centre, facilities, or visitor management process.
- Badge, key, safe, rack, or access control technology.
- Third-party provider responsibilities.
- Physical security incident trends.
- Audit or assurance expectations.
- Legal, privacy, or retention requirements.

Review outcome must be documented, approved by the Physical Security Manager and Compliance Manager, and retained with the evidence pack.

| Assessment Cycle | Enter the independent assessment cycle or year, e.g. 2026 Independent Assessment or FY2026. |
| SWIFT CSCF Version | Enter the SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework version applicable to the assessment, e.g. CSCF v2025. |

| Confidentiality Classification | Select the information classification applicable to the evidence, e.g. Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, or Highly Restricted, aligned to the organisation’s data classification policy. |
| Data Handling Restrictions | Record any handling requirements, e.g. no email, masked personal data required, read-only access only, screenshots redacted, no local download, encryption required. |
| Status | Select Not Requested, Requested, In Progress, Submitted, Under Review, Accepted, Rejected, Overdue, or Withdrawn. |

| Auditor / Assessor Reviewer | Enter the name or role of the independent assessor responsible for reviewing the evidence. |

| Final Acceptance Date | Enter the date the independent assessor accepted the evidence in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until accepted. |
| Comments / Notes | Enter any relevant notes, assumptions, scoping comments, exceptions, linkage to prior requests, or reasons for rejection. |

Owned by the SWIFT Compliance Officer or GRC Manager, with input from the independent assessor and SWIFT control owners; updated at assessment planning, weekly during fieldwork, and whenever requests are added, changed, submitted, reviewed, or closed. Source data should be drawn from the GRC tool, audit evidence repository, SWIFT CSCF control mapping, ticketing/workflow system, IAM records, security tooling, and document management repositories.
