### Dependency Analysis

Some improvements should be treated as foundational because they enable multiple other outcomes.

| Foundational Improvement | Enables |
|---|---|
| Defined governance framework and decision rights | Faster decisions, clearer accountability, improved escalation, stronger board reporting |
| Integrated performance dashboard | Better oversight of value, risk, service quality, suppliers and remediation |
| Technology risk appetite translation | Consistent prioritisation of security, resilience, architecture and supplier risks |
| Control register and ownership model | Compliance evidence, assurance planning, audit readiness and control monitoring |
| Data ownership model | Reliable reporting, better analytics, compliance evidence and accountability |
| Supplier risk tiering | Proportionate due diligence, monitoring, contract control and exit planning |
| Benefits realisation model | Improved investment decisions and portfolio value management |

### Impact on COBIT Implementation Readiness

The organisation is ready to proceed with COBIT implementation, provided that management treats the implementation as a governance improvement programme rather than a documentation exercise.

To achieve the target state, the organisation should:

- Assign accountable owners for each governance and management objective.
- Establish a practical capability improvement roadmap.
- Integrate improvement actions into existing governance forums and performance reporting.
- Create standard evidence expectations for key processes.
- Align technology governance reporting with executive decision needs.
- Use capability reassessment to track measurable improvement over time.

### Likely Barriers to Improvement

| Barrier | Potential Effect | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Competing transformation priorities | Improvement actions may be delayed or under-resourced. | Integrate actions into portfolio governance and assign executive sponsorship. |
| Lack of clear ownership | Actions may remain open without progress. | Assign named owners and due dates for each action. |
| Reporting fatigue | Stakeholders may resist new metrics or governance packs. | Rationalise existing reporting and focus on decision-useful measures. |
| Tool fragmentation | Evidence and metrics may remain manual. | Define minimum data requirements before tool enhancement. |
| Cultural preference for informal decisions | Governance discipline may be inconsistently applied. | Clarify decision rights and require documented decisions for material matters. |
| Limited assurance capacity | Control monitoring may not mature quickly. | Prioritise high-risk controls and use management self-assessment where appropriate. |

## Recommendations & Actions

### Improvement Roadmap

The recommended improvement roadmap is divided into three phases:

| Phase | Timeframe | Objective |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 - Stabilise and define | 0 to 3 months | Establish ownership, governance structure, priority remediation and minimum evidence expectations. |
| Phase 2 - Embed and measure | 3 to 9 months | Implement consistent processes, dashboards, risk-based monitoring and management reporting. |
| Phase 3 - Optimise and assure | 9 to 18 months | Strengthen automation, assurance integration, trend analysis and continuous improvement. |

### Priority Action Plan

| Action ID | Improvement Action | Related Objective(s) | Priority | Owner | Target Date | Success Measure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GAP-001 | Document the information and technology governance framework, including committees, decision rights, escalation thresholds, delegated authorities and reporting expectations. | Governance Framework Setting and Maintenance | High | [CIO / Governance Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Approved governance framework and committee map published. |
| GAP-002 | Assign accountable owners for each assessed governance and management objective and confirm responsibilities in role descriptions or accountability matrices. | All objectives | High | [Executive Sponsor] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Objective owner register approved and maintained. |
| GAP-003 | Define technology risk appetite statements and translate them into practical thresholds for security, resilience, supplier, change and project decisions. | Risk Optimisation, Security, Continuity, Suppliers | Critical | [Chief Risk Officer / CISO] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Risk appetite thresholds approved and used in governance reporting. |
| GAP-004 | Implement an integrated technology risk and treatment dashboard showing risk status, owner, treatment progress, residual exposure, overdue actions and escalation items. | Risk Optimisation, Security, Compliance | Critical | [Risk Lead / Technology Risk Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Dashboard reviewed monthly by executive governance forum. |
| GAP-005 | Establish a benefits realisation process requiring measurable benefits, baseline data, benefit owners, review dates and post-implementation validation for material initiatives. | Benefits Delivery, Portfolio, Programmes and Projects | High | [Portfolio Director] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Benefits register implemented and reviewed quarterly. |
| GAP-006 | Refresh portfolio governance to include strategic alignment, risk, capacity, dependencies, benefits, cost-to-complete and delivery confidence. | Managed Portfolio, Strategy, Resource Optimisation | High | [Portfolio Director / CIO] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Portfolio dashboard supports prioritisation and trade-off decisions. |
| GAP-007 | Establish a technology control register covering key controls, owners, frequency, evidence requirements, related risks and testing approach. | Internal Control, Compliance, Assurance | High | [GRC Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Approved control register covering priority technology processes. |
| GAP-008 | Implement risk-based control self-assessment and management testing for high-risk technology controls. | Internal Control Monitoring, Assurance | High | [GRC Lead / Control Owners] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Testing completed for priority controls and findings tracked. |
| GAP-009 | Strengthen continuity governance by validating recovery objectives with business owners, completing dependency mapping and expanding recovery testing coverage. | Managed Continuity | Critical | [Head of Resilience / IT Operations Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Recovery test plan completed and results reported to governance forum. |
| GAP-010 | Define minimum security governance metrics covering vulnerability remediation, privileged access, security incidents, control exceptions, awareness and treatment progress. | Managed Security, Risk Optimisation | Critical | [CISO] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Security dashboard approved and reviewed monthly. |
| GAP-011 | Implement a formal security exception process with risk owner approval, expiry dates, compensating controls and periodic review. | Managed Security, Risk Optimisation, Internal Control | High | [CISO / Risk Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | All active exceptions recorded and reviewed. |
| GAP-012 | Establish data ownership for critical data domains and define data quality rules, issue escalation and reporting responsibilities. | Managed Data, Performance Monitoring, Compliance | High | [Chief Data Officer / Data Governance Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Critical data owner register and data quality scorecard approved. |
| GAP-013 | Develop supplier risk tiering and apply enhanced due diligence, performance monitoring and exit planning to critical and high-risk suppliers. | Managed Suppliers, Continuity, Security, Compliance | High | [Procurement Lead / Supplier Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Supplier tiering completed and critical supplier reviews scheduled. |
| GAP-014 | Create a standard supplier review pack covering service levels, incidents, security, resilience, compliance, financial exposure, risks and improvement actions. | Managed Suppliers | High | [Supplier Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Standard pack used for all critical supplier reviews. |
| GAP-015 | Define architecture review triggers, mandatory design standards and exception management for material technology changes. | Enterprise Architecture, Solutions Build, Change | Medium | [Enterprise Architect] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Architecture review process applied to material initiatives. |
| GAP-016 | Strengthen change management reporting to include failed changes, emergency changes, change-related incidents, unauthorised changes and trend analysis. | Managed Change, Operations, Internal Control | High | [Change Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Monthly change performance report reviewed by service governance forum. |
| GAP-017 | Improve problem management by defining triggers for problem records, root cause quality criteria, known error management and action closure evidence. | Managed Problems, Incidents, Operations | Medium | [Service Management Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Recurring incident reduction and problem closure metrics reported. |
| GAP-018 | Standardise non-functional requirements for security, resilience, privacy, data, reporting, support and compliance across project initiation and design. | Requirements, Solutions Build, Security, Continuity | Medium | [PMO Lead / Architecture Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Updated templates used for new material initiatives. |
| GAP-019 | Implement an integrated performance dashboard covering value, risk, service, supplier, compliance, controls and improvement actions. | Performance Monitoring, Governance, Portfolio | High | [CIO Office / GRC Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Dashboard reviewed at executive governance forum with action tracking. |
| GAP-020 | Coordinate assurance planning across internal audit, compliance, risk and management testing to reduce duplication and focus on high-risk technology areas. | Managed Assurance, Internal Control Monitoring, Compliance | Medium | [Head of Internal Audit / GRC Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Integrated assurance map approved and updated quarterly. |
| GAP-021 | Establish an innovation intake and evaluation process for technology ideas, including risk screening, success criteria and transition-to-production requirements. | Managed Innovation, Strategy, Architecture | Medium | [Innovation Lead / CIO Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Innovation pipeline and evaluation criteria approved. |
| GAP-022 | Define resource and skills reporting for technology operations and change delivery, including key person risk, contractor dependency and capacity constraints. | Resource Optimisation, Portfolio, Operations | Medium | [Technology Operations Lead / HR Partner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Quarterly capacity and skills report reviewed by leadership. |

### Critical Actions Requiring Immediate Executive Attention

| Action | Reason for Immediate Attention | Required Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Define and approve technology risk appetite thresholds. | Current risk decisions may be inconsistent and insufficiently aligned with business tolerance. | Approve risk appetite translation and escalation criteria. |
| Strengthen continuity testing for critical services. | Recovery capability is not fully validated for all critical dependencies. | Approve test schedule, business participation and remediation funding. |
| Improve security governance metrics and exception management. | Security exposure cannot be consistently measured or challenged. | Approve minimum security dashboard and exception process. |
| Assign owners for governance and management objectives. | Improvement actions require clear accountability to progress. | Confirm executive and operational owners. |

### Suggested Implementation Timeline

| Month | Key Milestones |
|---|---|
| Month 1 | Confirm executive sponsor, approve report, assign objective owners, agree remediation governance. |
| Month 2 | Approve governance framework outline, risk appetite thresholds, action plan and reporting cadence. |
| Month 3 | Launch integrated risk dashboard, security exception process, continuity test planning and control register design. |
| Month 4 | Implement benefits realisation process, supplier tiering and portfolio dashboard enhancements. |
| Month 5 | Complete critical supplier reviews and define data owner register for priority data domains. |
| Month 6 | Perform first management control testing cycle for priority controls. |
| Month 7 | Complete expanded recovery testing for selected critical services. |
| Month 8 | Implement integrated technology performance dashboard. |
| Month 9 | Conduct first capability reassessment for critical and high-priority objectives. |
| Months 10-12 | Address reassessment findings, refine metrics, expand data governance and assurance coverage. |
| Months 13-18 | Optimise reporting, automate evidence collection where feasible and mature continuous improvement practices. |

### Remediation Governance

Management should govern remediation through a formal improvement programme with the following characteristics:

- Executive sponsor accountable for overall delivery.
- Named owner for each action.
- Defined due date, milestone and success measure for each action.
- Monthly progress reporting to the designated technology governance forum.
- Risk-based escalation for overdue or blocked actions.
- Evidence requirements defined before action closure.
- Independent or management validation for critical and high-priority action closure.
- Quarterly reporting to the relevant executive or board-level oversight forum.

### Recommended Key Performance Indicators

| KPI | Purpose | Suggested Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| Percentage of objectives with assigned accountable owners | Confirms governance accountability coverage. | Monthly until complete, then quarterly |
| Percentage of high-priority actions on track | Monitors remediation delivery. | Monthly |
| Number of overdue critical and high-priority actions | Identifies execution risk. | Monthly |
| Percentage of material initiatives with measurable benefits and owners | Measures benefits governance adoption. | Quarterly |
| Percentage of critical services with tested recovery plans | Measures continuity readiness. | Quarterly |
| Percentage of critical suppliers with completed risk reviews | Measures supplier governance coverage. | Quarterly |
| Percentage of priority controls tested as scheduled | Measures control monitoring discipline. | Quarterly |
| Percentage of high-risk vulnerabilities remediated within agreed timelines | Measures security risk treatment performance. | Monthly |
| Number of expired or overdue security exceptions | Measures exception governance. | Monthly |
| Percentage of critical data domains with assigned owners | Measures data governance maturity. | Quarterly |
| Change failure rate and emergency change rate | Measures change stability. | Monthly |
| Percentage of recurring incidents linked to problem records | Measures problem management effectiveness. | Monthly |

### Reassessment Plan

A formal reassessment should be performed after the initial remediation period to confirm capability improvement and update priorities.

| Reassessment Activity | Timing | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Interim progress review | 3 months after report approval | Critical and high-priority actions |
| Targeted capability reassessment | 6 months after report approval | Critical and high-priority objectives |
| Full capability reassessment | 12 months after report approval | All assessed objectives |
| Annual improvement planning | Annually thereafter | Target capability refresh and roadmap update |

### Acceptance of Residual Gaps

Where management elects not to remediate a gap to the target capability level, the decision should be formally documented and approved by the appropriate accountable authority. The record should include:

- Gap description.
- Business rationale for acceptance.
- Risk impact.
- Compensating controls.
- Review date.
- Accountable risk owner.
- Approval evidence.

Residual gap acceptance should not be used to defer critical actions without clear risk ownership and executive approval.

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution List

This report is intended for controlled internal distribution only.

| Recipient / Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Chief Executive Officer] | Executive oversight and business accountability |
| [Chief Information Officer] | Technology governance ownership and remediation delivery |
| [Chief Information Security Officer] | Security and cyber risk remediation |
| [Chief Risk Officer] | Enterprise risk alignment and risk acceptance oversight |
| [Chief Financial Officer] | Investment, benefits and resource governance |
| [Chief Operating Officer] | Operational resilience and service impact oversight |
| [Head of Internal Audit] | Assurance planning and independent review alignment |
| [General Counsel / Compliance Lead] | Regulatory and contractual obligation oversight |
| [Data Governance Lead] | Data ownership and quality remediation |
| [Procurement / Supplier Management Lead] | Supplier governance improvement |
| [Board Risk Committee / Technology Committee] | Oversight of critical findings and remediation progress |

### Confidentiality Classification

This report is classified as **Internal Confidential**. It contains sensitive information about governance capability, control weaknesses, security exposure, supplier management, resilience and internal improvement priorities.

The report must be handled in accordance with the organisation’s information handling requirements for confidential internal governance and risk documentation.

### Handling Requirements

Recipients must:

- Use the report only for authorised governance, risk, compliance, audit and improvement purposes.
- Not distribute the report outside the approved recipient list without permission from the report owner.
- Store the report only in approved document repositories or systems.
- Avoid copying report content into unsecured communications or external collaboration platforms.
- Ensure any extracts are clearly marked with the same classification.
- Notify the report owner if unauthorised disclosure is suspected.
- Return or securely delete copies when no longer required, subject to applicable records retention requirements.

### External Sharing

External sharing is not permitted unless approved by [Report Owner] and [Legal / Compliance Function]. Where external sharing is approved, the report should be redacted as appropriate to remove sensitive operational, security, supplier or internal risk details.

Potential external recipients may include:

- External auditors.
- Regulators.
- Approved assurance providers.
- Contractually authorised customers or partners.
- Specialist advisors under confidentiality agreement.

### Records Retention

| Record | Retention Requirement |
|---|---|
| Final approved report | Retain for [X years] |
| Supporting evidence | Retain for [X years] or in line with audit evidence requirements |
| Management responses | Retain with the final report |
| Remediation progress records | Retain until closure plus [X years] |
| Reassessment reports | Retain for [X years] |

### Approval and Version Control

| Role | Name | Approval Status | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Report Owner | [Name] | Pending / Approved | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Executive Sponsor | [Name] | Pending / Approved | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Chief Information Officer | [Name] | Pending / Approved | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Chief Risk Officer | [Name] | Pending / Approved | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Internal Audit Representative | [Name] | Noted / Reviewed | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Risk ID | Enter a unique identifier for the risk using the organisation's naming convention, e.g. IT-RISK-0001. Do not reuse IDs. |
| Risk Title | Enter a short, specific title describing the risk scenario in business terms. |
| Risk Description | Describe the risk clearly as a cause-event-impact statement, explaining what could happen and why it matters. |
| Risk Category | Select the primary risk category. Allowed values: Cybersecurity, Data Protection, Technology Resilience, Third Party, Cloud, Application, Infrastructure, Identity and Access, Change, Compliance, Project / Transformation, Operational IT, Other. |
| COBIT 2019 APO12 Practice Mapping | Enter the applicable COBIT 2019 APO12 management practice reference(s). Allowed values include APO12.01, APO12.02, APO12.03, APO12.04, APO12.05, APO12.06; enter multiple values separated by semicolons if needed. |
| Business Process / Service Affected | Enter the business process, IT service, product, or capability affected by the risk. |
| Information Asset / Technology Asset | Enter the key information asset, application, infrastructure component, platform, data set, or technology environment affected. |
| Asset Owner | Enter the accountable owner of the affected asset, using role or named individual according to organisational practice. |
| Risk Owner | Enter the accountable person or role responsible for managing the risk and ensuring treatment progress. |
| Risk Source / Trigger | Enter how the risk was identified or what triggered it, e.g. risk assessment, incident, audit finding, regulatory change, project review, supplier assessment, vulnerability assessment. |
| Threat / Event Scenario | Describe the threat, event, or scenario that could exploit the condition, such as ransomware attack, privileged access misuse, supplier outage, data leakage, or failed change. |
| Vulnerability / Condition | Describe the weakness, exposure, control gap, or condition that makes the risk possible. |
| Potential Business Impact | Describe the realistic business consequence if the risk materialises, including operational, financial, regulatory, customer, safety, reputational, or strategic impact. |
| Impact Type | Select all applicable impact types. Allowed values: Financial, Operational, Regulatory / Legal, Reputational, Customer, Safety, Data Confidentiality, Data Integrity, Data Availability, Strategic; separate multiple values with semicolons. |
| Inherent Likelihood | Enter the likelihood before considering existing controls. Use the organisation's approved scale, e.g. 1-5 where 1 = Rare and 5 = Almost Certain. |
| Inherent Impact | Enter the impact before considering existing controls. Use the organisation's approved scale, e.g. 1-5 where 1 = Insignificant and 5 = Severe. |
| Inherent Risk Rating | Enter the inherent risk score or rating calculated using the organisation's risk matrix, e.g. Likelihood x Impact score and/or Low, Medium, High, Critical. |
| Existing Controls | List the current controls that reduce the risk, including preventive, detective, and corrective controls. Reference control IDs where available. |
| Control Effectiveness | Assess how well existing controls operate. Allowed values: Effective, Partially Effective, Ineffective, Not Tested, Unknown. |
| Residual Likelihood | Enter the likelihood after considering existing controls. Use the organisation's approved scale, e.g. 1-5. |
| Residual Impact | Enter the impact after considering existing controls. Use the organisation's approved scale, e.g. 1-5. |
| Residual Risk Rating | Enter the residual risk score or rating calculated using the organisation's risk matrix, e.g. Likelihood x Impact score and/or Low, Medium, High, Critical. |
| Risk Appetite / Tolerance Threshold | Enter the relevant approved appetite or tolerance threshold for this risk type, such as maximum acceptable residual rating, downtime limit, loss threshold, or compliance tolerance. |
| Risk Appetite Status | State whether residual risk is within tolerance. Allowed values: Within Appetite, Outside Appetite, Not Defined. |
| Risk Treatment Option | Select the approved treatment decision. Allowed values: Accept, Mitigate, Transfer / Share, Avoid, Monitor. |
| Treatment Plan / Required Actions | For risks not simply accepted, describe the specific action(s), control improvements, remediation activities, or projects required to reach the target risk level. |
| Treatment Owner | Enter the person or role accountable for delivering the treatment actions. |
| Target Completion Date | Enter the planned completion date for treatment actions in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Treatment Status | Enter the current implementation status. Allowed values: Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Deferred, Overdue, Cancelled. |
| Residual Risk Acceptance Required | State whether formal acceptance is required because residual risk remains outside appetite or exceeds approval thresholds. Allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Risk Acceptance Approver | If acceptance is required, enter the authorised approver role or name in line with the risk acceptance authority matrix; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Risk Acceptance Date | If accepted, enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Acceptance Expiry / Review Date | If accepted, enter the date by which the acceptance must be reviewed or renewed in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Key Risk Indicator | Enter the measurable indicator used to monitor this risk, e.g. number of critical vulnerabilities older than SLA, phishing failure rate, failed backup percentage. |
| KRI Threshold | Enter the agreed threshold or trigger level for escalation, including unit of measure, e.g. >10 critical vulnerabilities older than 30 days. |
| Current KRI Value | Enter the latest measured KRI value and measurement date, e.g. 7 as of YYYY-MM-DD. |
| Linked Incident / Issue / Audit Finding | Enter references to related incidents, problems, issues, audit findings, compliance findings, or vulnerability records; enter N/A if none. |
| Related Policies / Standards | Enter applicable internal policies, standards, or procedures relevant to this risk, such as Information Security Policy or Backup Standard. |
| Related Control References | Enter relevant control references from internal control libraries, COBIT objectives, ISO 27001, NIST, CIS, or other frameworks used by the organisation. |
| Dependencies / Assumptions | Record key dependencies or assumptions affecting the risk assessment or treatment, such as supplier delivery, budget approval, architecture change, or resource availability. |
| Last Reviewed Date | Enter the date this risk entry was last formally reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on risk rating and organisational review frequency. |
| Risk Status | Enter the lifecycle status of the risk. Allowed values: Open, Under Treatment, Accepted, Monitored, Closed, Escalated. |
| Comments / Review Notes | Enter concise notes from the latest review, including decisions, changes in rating, escalation outcomes, or reasons for closure. |

### Maintenance

The IT Risk Register template is owned by the IT Risk Manager or equivalent technology risk function, with risk entries maintained by assigned risk owners and reviewed at least monthly for high and critical risks and quarterly for all other risks. Source data should be drawn from the enterprise GRC platform or risk management system, supported by inputs from CMDB/asset inventory, vulnerability management tools, incident management, audit issue tracking, supplier risk assessments, and project governance records.

field_guidance.Risk Appetite Status: State whether residual risk is within tolerance. Allowed values: Within Appetite, Outside Appetite, Not Defined.
field_guidance.Risk Treatment Option: Select the approved treatment decision. Allowed values: Accept, Mitigate, Transfer / Share, Avoid, Monitor.
field_guidance.Treatment Plan / Required Actions: For risks not simply accepted, describe the specific action(s), control improvements, remediation activities, or projects required to reach the target risk level.
field_guidance.Treatment Owner: Enter the person or role accountable for delivering the treatment actions.
field_guidance.Target Completion Date: Enter the planned completion date for treatment actions in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Treatment Status: Enter the current implementation status. Allowed values: Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Deferred, Overdue, Cancelled.
field_guidance.Residual Risk Acceptance Required: State whether formal acceptance is required because residual risk remains outside appetite or exceeds approval thresholds. Allowed values: Yes, No.
field_guidance.Risk Acceptance Approver: If acceptance is required, enter the authorised approver role or name in line with the risk acceptance authority matrix; otherwise enter N/A.
field_guidance.Risk Acceptance Date: If accepted, enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A.
field_guidance.Acceptance Expiry / Review Date: If accepted, enter the date by which the acceptance must be reviewed or renewed in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A.
field_guidance.Key Risk Indicator: Enter the measurable indicator used to monitor this risk, e.g. number of critical vulnerabilities older than SLA, phishing failure rate, failed backup percentage.
field_guidance.KRI Threshold: Enter the agreed threshold or trigger level for escalation, including unit of measure, e.g. >10 critical vulnerabilities older than 30 days.
field_guidance.Current KRI Value: Enter the latest measured KRI value and measurement date, e.g. 7 as of YYYY-MM-DD.
field_guidance.Linked Incident / Issue / Audit Finding: Enter references to related incidents, problems, issues, audit findings, compliance findings, or vulnerability records; enter N/A if none.
field_guidance.Related Policies / Standards: Enter applicable internal policies, standards, or procedures relevant to this risk, such as Information Security Policy or Backup Standard.
field_guidance.Related Control References: Enter relevant control references from internal control libraries, COBIT objectives, ISO 27001, NIST, CIS, or other frameworks used by the organisation.
field_guidance.Dependencies / Assumptions: Record key dependencies or assumptions affecting the risk assessment or treatment, such as supplier delivery, budget approval, architecture change, or resource availability.
field_guidance.Last Reviewed Date: Enter the date this risk entry was last formally reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Next Review Date: Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on risk rating and organisational review frequency.
field_guidance.Risk Status: Enter the lifecycle status of the risk. Allowed values: Open, Under Treatment, Accepted, Monitored, Closed, Escalated.
field_guidance.Comments / Review Notes: Enter concise notes from the latest review, including decisions, changes in rating, escalation outcomes, or reasons for closure.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Architecture Asset ID | Enter a unique, persistent identifier for the repository item, using the organisation's naming convention; recommended format EA-REP-0001. |
| Architecture Domain | Select the primary architecture domain covered by the item; allowed values: Business, Information, Data, Application, Technology. |
| Architecture Viewpoint | Enter the stakeholder or analytical viewpoint represented, such as Capability Map, Process Model, Information Flow, Data Model, Application Portfolio, Integration View, Infrastructure View, Technology Standard, or Roadmap. |
| Architecture Asset Name | Enter the formal name of the architecture artefact, component, model, standard, or repository record. |
| Architecture Asset Description | Provide a concise description of what the item represents, its scope, and intended use. |
| Architecture Asset Type | Select the type of repository item; allowed values: Model, Diagram, Catalogue, Matrix, Standard, Principle, Pattern, Building Block, Roadmap, Decision Record, Reference Architecture. |
| Architecture State | Select whether the item describes the current, future, or interim architecture; allowed values: Baseline, Target, Transition. |
| Version | Enter the controlled version number of the artefact or record, using format vMajor.Minor, for example v1.0. |
| Business Capability or Process Supported | Enter the business capability, value stream, service, or process supported; use the approved capability/process taxonomy name where available. |
| Related Enterprise Goal or Strategy | Enter the enterprise goal, strategic objective, transformation theme, or COBIT goal supported by this architecture item. |
| Information or Data Subject Area | Enter the information asset, data domain, data entity, or subject area covered, if applicable; enter Not Applicable where the item does not relate to information or data. |
| Application or Service Reference | Enter the application, digital service, product, or system reference linked to the architecture item, using the approved application/service catalogue ID where available; enter Not Applicable if not relevant. |
| Technology Platform or Component Reference | Enter the technology platform, infrastructure component, cloud service, middleware, network component, or technical building block reference; enter Not Applicable if not relevant. |
| Owning Business Unit | Enter the accountable business unit or function that owns the capability, process, data, application, or technology represented. |
| Architecture Owner | Enter the role or named person accountable for maintaining and approving the architecture item, such as Enterprise Architect, Domain Architect, Data Architect, Application Architect, or Technology Architect. |
| Technical or Data Steward | Enter the operational steward, system owner, data steward, or technical custodian responsible for day-to-day accuracy of the item; enter Not Applicable if none. |
| Lifecycle Status | Select the lifecycle status of the architecture item or component; allowed values: Proposed, In Design, Approved, Active, Under Review, Deprecated, Retired. |
| Business Criticality | Select the business criticality of the item or supported capability/component; allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low. |
| Information Classification | Select the highest classification of information represented or processed; allowed values: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, Not Applicable. |
| Hosting or Deployment Location | Enter where the architecture component or artefact applies, such as On-premises, Private Cloud, Public Cloud, Hybrid, SaaS, Region/Country, Data Centre, or Not Applicable. |
| Key Dependencies | List material dependencies on other capabilities, data domains, applications, technologies, vendors, programmes, or architecture decisions; separate multiple entries with semicolons. |
| Key Interfaces or Integrations | List major interfaces, integrations, data flows, APIs, or interoperability points relevant to the item; separate multiple entries with semicolons or enter Not Applicable. |
| Applicable Architecture Principles | Enter the approved enterprise architecture principles that apply to this item, using principle IDs or names from the architecture principles register. |
| Applicable Standards or Reference Models | Enter relevant internal or external standards, reference architectures, patterns, frameworks, or technology standards that this item must follow. |
| Architecture Decision Reference | Enter the architecture decision record, design authority decision, or governance forum reference associated with the item; use the approved decision ID or enter Pending. |
| Risk or Constraint Summary | Summarise material risks, issues, assumptions, limitations, compliance constraints, technology constraints, or business constraints affecting the item. |
| Compliance Status | Select the degree to which the item conforms to approved architecture principles, standards, and target architecture; allowed values: Compliant, Partially Compliant, Non-Compliant, Exception Approved, Not Assessed. |
| Approved Exception Reference | Enter the approved waiver or exception ID where non-compliance has been formally accepted; enter Not Applicable if no exception exists. |
| Roadmap or Initiative Reference | Enter the transformation initiative, programme, project, epic, or roadmap item that will create, change, migrate, or retire this architecture item; enter Not Applicable if none. |
| Baseline Effective Date | Enter the date from which the baseline architecture item became effective, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Target Effective Date | Enter the planned date by which the target or transition architecture is expected to be effective, in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Applicable for baseline-only records. |
| Last Review Date | Enter the most recent date the record or artefact was reviewed by the architecture owner, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Due Date | Enter the next scheduled review date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on the organisation's architecture governance cadence. |
| Approval Status | Select the governance approval status; allowed values: Draft, Submitted, Approved, Rejected, Withdrawn, Superseded. |
| Approved By | Enter the approving authority, role, forum, or named approver, such as Architecture Review Board or Enterprise Architecture Lead; enter Not Approved if approval has not occurred. |
| Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not Approved if approval has not occurred. |
| Repository Link | Enter the URL or document management link to the authoritative artefact, model, diagram, catalogue entry, decision record, or repository object. |
| Source System | Enter the authoritative system or repository from which the record is maintained, such as EA tool, CMDB, application portfolio management tool, data catalogue, document repository, or service management platform. |
| Last Updated By | Enter the name or role of the person who last modified the register entry. |
| Last Updated Date | Enter the date the register entry was last updated, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |

### Maintenance

The Enterprise Architecture Repository Register is owned by the Head of Enterprise Architecture, with domain architects and data/application/technology owners responsible for maintaining their assigned records. It should be updated whenever architecture artefacts, decisions, standards, roadmaps, or lifecycle states change and formally reviewed at least quarterly, drawing from the enterprise architecture tool, application portfolio repository, CMDB, data catalogue, architecture decision log, and approved architecture governance records.
