Before solution design is developed, the project team confirms the business, functional, non-functional, operational and compliance requirements that will shape the solution. Activities include:

- Identifying business process impacts and affected user groups.
- Confirming data types, information flows, reporting needs and retention expectations.
- Defining availability, performance, resilience, scalability and support needs.
- Confirming access control, identity, security monitoring and audit logging expectations.
- Identifying privacy, legal, regulatory and contractual considerations.
- Confirming integration points with existing systems and external parties.
- Validating constraints such as budget, timeline, technology standards and supplier limitations.
- Recording requirements traceability to design components and delivery activities.

Unresolved requirements must be recorded as open items and cannot be ignored in the design approval process.

### Phase 3 - High-Level Solution Design

The high-level solution design defines the proposed solution in sufficient detail to support architecture, risk, delivery and funding decisions. It must describe:

- Solution overview and business capability supported.
- Target-state process and technology context.
- Major application, infrastructure, integration and data components.
- Hosting model and environment strategy.
- User roles, access model and identity approach.
- Information classification, data ownership and data flow overview.
- Security and privacy design considerations.
- Resilience, backup, recovery and continuity expectations.
- Reporting, monitoring and logging approach.
- Supplier, licence and service dependencies.
- Alignment with approved technology standards and architecture principles.
- Options considered and rationale for the preferred option.
- Key design risks, constraints and assumptions.
- Estimated implementation complexity and operational impact.

The high-level design must be reviewed by relevant governance stakeholders before detailed design, procurement commitment or build activity proceeds.

### Phase 4 - Detailed Solution Design

The detailed solution design provides the delivery team with the agreed design baseline for configuration, development, integration, testing and deployment. The level of detail must be proportionate to project risk and complexity. The document should include:

- Detailed component architecture.
- Data model, data mapping or data migration approach where applicable.
- Interface specifications and integration patterns.
- Environment, network and infrastructure design.
- Security controls, access provisioning and privileged access considerations.
- Encryption, key management and secrets handling where relevant.
- Logging, monitoring, alerting and audit evidence requirements.
- Error handling, exception management and service recovery design.
- Performance, capacity and scalability assumptions.
- Configuration standards and build parameters.
- Testability considerations and acceptance criteria alignment.
- Operational support model and handover requirements.
- Deployment, rollback and transition considerations.
- Known design exceptions and compensating controls.
- Traceability to approved requirements and design decisions.

Detailed design approval confirms that the solution is ready to move into build, configuration or implementation, subject to any conditions recorded by reviewers.

### Phase 5 - Governance Review and Approval

Formal reviews are conducted at defined points in the project lifecycle. Reviews must be risk-based and involve the stakeholders needed to confirm that the project and solution remain justified, controlled and fit for implementation.

Minimum review expectations include:

| Review Point | Primary Purpose | Minimum Participants |
|---|---|---|
| Charter Review | Confirm project justification, sponsorship, scope, funding approach and governance model. | Sponsor, Project Manager, PMO, Finance, relevant Business Owner |
| Architecture Review | Confirm design alignment with target architecture, standards and integration principles. | Enterprise Architecture, Technical Lead, Application Owner |
| Security and Privacy Review | Confirm security, identity, privacy, logging and data protection considerations. | Information Security, Privacy Office, Data Owner |
| Operational Readiness Review | Confirm support, monitoring, service ownership, documentation and transition readiness. | Service Owner, Operations, Service Desk, Change Manager |
| Implementation Readiness Review | Confirm readiness to deploy, release, migrate or cut over. | Project Manager, Change Manager, Test Lead, Operations, Business Owner |

Review comments must be tracked to closure. Approval conditions, exceptions and deferred actions must have named owners and due dates.

### Phase 6 - Baseline Control and Change Management

Once approved, the project charter and solution design documents become controlled baselines. Changes that affect scope, cost, timeline, benefits, risk, architecture, data flows, security posture, operational support or stakeholder commitments must be assessed and approved before implementation.

The project manager must ensure that:

- Document versions are controlled and approval history is retained.
- Material changes are assessed for impact before acceptance.
- Changes are reflected consistently across project plans, risk registers, requirements, design documents, test plans and operational readiness materials.
- Stakeholders are informed of approved changes that affect their responsibilities or expected outcomes.
- Exceptions are time-bound, risk-assessed and approved by the appropriate authority.

### Phase 7 - Handover, Closure and Lessons Learned

At project closure or transition to operations, the project manager must confirm that final versions of the charter, design documents and related review records are complete and stored in the approved repository.

Closure activities include:

- Confirming that approved design has been implemented or approved deviations are recorded.
- Ensuring operational teams have received final design, support and configuration documentation.
- Confirming ownership of systems, data, risks, controls and service obligations.
- Recording lessons learned relating to charter quality, design accuracy, review effectiveness and governance efficiency.
- Archiving artefacts according to retention requirements.
- Confirming whether any open design actions remain and transferring ownership where necessary.

## Milestones & Timeline

| Milestone | Description | Target Timing | Owner | Key Deliverable / Evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Plan Approved | Approval of this plan and agreement on implementation responsibilities. | Week 1 | PMO Lead | Approved plan and stakeholder communication |
| Templates Finalised | Standard charter, solution design, decision log and review record templates completed. | Week 2 | PMO / Enterprise Architecture | Approved template pack |
| Governance Review Model Confirmed | Review points, approval forums, approvers and escalation paths agreed. | Week 3 | PMO Lead | Governance workflow and approval matrix |
| Repository Configured | Document repository established with version control, permissions and retention settings. | Week 3 | Records Management / IT | Controlled document library |
| Stakeholder Briefings Completed | Sponsors, project managers, architects and review teams briefed on expectations. | Week 4 | PMO | Attendance records and briefing materials |
| Pilot Projects Selected | Representative projects chosen to validate the artefact approach. | Week 4 | PMO / Portfolio Manager | Pilot project list and pilot scope |
| Pilot Charters Completed | Project charters prepared and reviewed for selected pilot projects. | Weeks 5-6 | Project Managers | Approved pilot charters |
| Pilot Designs Completed | High-level solution designs prepared and submitted for review. | Weeks 6-8 | Solution Architects | Approved or conditionally approved designs |
| Lessons Learned Applied | Feedback from pilot projects incorporated into templates and guidance. | Week 9 | PMO / Enterprise Architecture | Updated templates and guidance notes |
| Full Rollout Starts | Standard artefact requirements applied to all applicable new projects. | Week 10 | PMO Lead | PMO communication and updated project intake checklist |
| Compliance Checkpoint | Sample review of live projects to confirm adoption and artefact quality. | Week 14 | PMO Assurance | Quality review results and action log |
| First Management Review | Implementation effectiveness reviewed and improvement actions agreed. | Week 16 | Governance Committee | Review minutes and agreed actions |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Project Sponsor | Owns the business justification, approves the charter, secures funding, resolves senior-level issues and remains accountable for benefits realisation. |
| Project Manager | Leads preparation and maintenance of the charter, coordinates design artefact completion, manages review cycles, tracks actions and ensures approvals are retained. |
| Business Owner | Defines business objectives, process impacts, requirements, acceptance expectations and business readiness needs. |
| Product Owner | Prioritises requirements, confirms solution value, manages backlog alignment and validates that design choices support intended outcomes. |
| Solution Architect | Leads solution design development, documents design decisions, confirms alignment with architecture standards and addresses design review feedback. |
| Enterprise Architect | Reviews alignment with target architecture, technology standards, integration principles and strategic roadmap. |
| Information Security Lead | Reviews security design, access model, logging, monitoring, resilience considerations and risk treatment expectations. |
| Privacy Officer | Reviews personal information processing, privacy obligations, consent, minimisation, retention and data subject considerations where applicable. |
| Data Owner | Confirms data classification, permitted use, quality expectations, access needs, retention requirements and data flow accuracy. |
| Application Owner | Confirms application lifecycle implications, support expectations, technical constraints and compatibility with existing services. |
| Infrastructure / Cloud Lead | Reviews hosting, environment, network, capacity, backup, monitoring and platform requirements. |
| Integration Lead | Reviews interface design, data exchange patterns, error handling, service dependencies and integration support requirements. |
| Service Owner | Confirms operational ownership, service levels, support model, maintenance requirements and ongoing cost impacts. |
| Change Manager | Confirms implementation readiness, release planning, rollback arrangements, change approvals and communications. |
| Procurement Lead | Supports supplier engagement, sourcing approach, contract review and third-party risk coordination. |
| Finance Representative | Validates budget assumptions, cost estimates, funding source and financial approval requirements. |
| Risk and Compliance Representative | Reviews governance risks, compliance obligations, control expectations, exceptions and residual risk acceptance. |
| PMO | Maintains templates, monitors compliance, supports project managers, performs quality checks and reports adoption status to governance bodies. |
| Governance Committee | Approves significant projects, resolves escalations, accepts material risks and monitors overall implementation effectiveness. |

Responsibility assignment for key activities:

| Activity | Sponsor | Project Manager | Solution Architect | PMO | Security / Privacy | Enterprise Architecture | Service Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prepare project charter | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted |
| Approve project charter | Accountable | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted |
| Define solution design | Consulted | Responsible | Accountable | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted |
| Conduct architecture review | Informed | Responsible | Responsible | Informed | Consulted | Accountable | Consulted |
| Conduct security and privacy review | Informed | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | Accountable | Consulted | Consulted |
| Confirm operational readiness | Informed | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | Consulted | Consulted | Accountable |
| Maintain artefact repository | Informed | Responsible | Responsible | Accountable | Informed | Informed | Informed |
| Track review actions | Informed | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Responsible for assigned actions | Responsible for assigned actions | Responsible for assigned actions |
| Report adoption and quality | Informed | Consulted | Informed | Accountable | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted |

## Resources

The following resources are required to implement and sustain this plan.

### People

| Resource | Purpose | Estimated Commitment |
|---|---|---:|
| PMO Lead | Owns implementation of the plan, template governance and adoption monitoring. | 0.2 FTE for rollout, then 0.1 FTE ongoing |
| Project Managers | Prepare and maintain project charters and coordinate review activity. | Project-specific |
| Solution Architects | Prepare solution designs and design decision records. | Project-specific |
| Enterprise Architects | Review architecture alignment and approve design direction. | As needed per review cycle |
| Security and Privacy Specialists | Review controls, data protection, identity, monitoring and compliance considerations. | As needed per project risk |
| Service Management Representatives | Validate operational readiness, support and transition requirements. | As needed per project |
| Records Management / Repository Administrator | Maintains repository permissions, retention and document control features. | 0.1 FTE during setup, then as needed |
| PMO Assurance Analyst | Performs periodic quality sampling and adoption reporting. | 0.1 FTE ongoing |

### Templates and Tools

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Project Charter Template | Standardises project initiation information and approval evidence. |
| High-Level Solution Design Template | Captures proposed solution, architecture fit, key risks and design rationale. |
| Detailed Solution Design Template | Provides build-ready design detail for complex or higher-risk solutions. |
| Design Decision Log | Records material design decisions, alternatives considered and approvals. |
| Review Action Log | Tracks reviewer comments, required actions, owners and closure status. |
| Approval Matrix | Defines required approvers by project type, risk level and change impact. |
| Project Repository | Stores approved artefacts, review records and version history. |
| Workflow / Collaboration Tool | Routes documents for review, approval and comment resolution. |
| Portfolio Management Tool | Links project artefacts to funding, milestones, dependencies and governance reporting. |

### Guidance and Standards

The following internal guidance must be available to project teams:

- Project intake and prioritisation guidance.
- Project classification and risk-rating criteria.
- Architecture principles and approved technology standards.
- Security and privacy design guidance.
- Data classification and handling rules.
- Third-party and cloud service assessment guidance.
- Service transition and operational readiness checklist.
- Change and release management requirements.
- Document control and retention guidance.

### Minimum Artefact Quality Criteria

Each project charter and solution design document must meet the following quality expectations before approval:

| Criterion | Expectation |
|---|---|
| Completeness | Mandatory sections are completed or marked not applicable with rationale. |
| Accuracy | Content reflects current approved requirements, constraints and decisions. |
| Traceability | Business objectives, requirements, design elements and delivery activities are linked where practical. |
| Reviewability | The document is clear enough for reviewers to assess impact, risk and feasibility. |
| Accountability | Owners, approvers, action owners and decision makers are clearly identified. |
| Risk Visibility | Key risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies and exceptions are documented. |
| Alignment | The document aligns with organisational strategy, architecture, security, privacy and operational expectations. |
| Version Control | Version history, approval status and change summary are maintained. |
| Evidence Retention | Review comments, approvals and conditions are retained in the approved repository. |

## Success Metrics

The effectiveness of this plan will be measured using a combination of adoption, quality, timeliness and outcome indicators.

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Reporting Frequency |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Applicable projects with approved charter before mobilisation | 95% or higher | PMO sample review and project intake records | Monthly |
| Applicable projects with approved high-level design before build or procurement commitment | 90% or higher | Governance gate review records | Monthly |
| High-risk projects with completed security and privacy review before implementation | 100% | Security review log and project records | Monthly |
| Design review actions closed by agreed due date | 90% or higher | Review action log | Monthly |
| Projects using approved templates without material omissions | 90% or higher | PMO quality assessment | Quarterly |
| Material design changes documented and approved before implementation | 95% or higher | Change records and design version history | Quarterly |
| Projects with operational readiness evidence before go-live | 95% or higher | Release and service transition records | Monthly |
| Projects with final artefacts archived at closure | 95% or higher | Repository and closure checklist review | Quarterly |
| Repeat review findings caused by incomplete artefacts | Decreasing trend | Governance review issue analysis | Quarterly |
| Stakeholder satisfaction with clarity and usefulness of artefacts | 80% favourable or higher | Survey or structured feedback | Semi-annually |

Qualitative indicators will also be reviewed, including:

- Whether governance forums receive sufficient information to make informed decisions.
- Whether solution designs identify operational and security considerations early enough to avoid rework.
- Whether project teams understand the difference between initiation approval, design approval and implementation approval.
- Whether design decisions remain traceable through delivery and handover.
- Whether lessons learned result in improved templates, guidance and review efficiency.

Where metrics fall below target, the PMO will agree corrective actions with the relevant owners. Corrective actions may include template updates, targeted training, additional review checkpoints, escalation to governance forums or increased assurance sampling.

## Review & Update Triggers

This plan must be reviewed at least annually by the Project Management Office in consultation with enterprise architecture, information security, privacy, service management, finance, procurement and risk stakeholders.

The plan must also be reviewed and updated when any of the following triggers occur:

- Significant changes to the organisation’s project governance, portfolio management or investment approval model.
- Introduction of a new delivery methodology, such as a major shift to agile, product-based or platform-based delivery.
- Material changes to architecture governance, technology standards or approved solution patterns.
- Significant changes to security, privacy, data, resilience, cloud or third-party management expectations.
- Audit, assurance or management review findings indicating that project charters or solution designs are incomplete, inconsistent or ineffective.
- Repeated project delivery issues caused by unclear scope, weak design, unresolved dependencies or poor stakeholder alignment.
- Implementation of a new project management, workflow or document management tool.
- Organisational restructuring that changes project approval rights, service ownership or design accountability.
- Lessons learned from major projects, incidents, failed implementations or post-implementation reviews.
- Changes to document retention, evidence management or classification requirements.

Updates to this plan must be version-controlled, reviewed by affected stakeholders and approved by the document owner or delegated governance authority. Superseded versions must be retained in accordance with organisational record retention requirements.

COB-023.title: Service Catalogue & SLAs
COB-023.content:

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Service ID | Enter the unique identifier for the service in the service catalogue, using the organisation's standard naming convention, e.g. SVC-001. |
| Service Name | Enter the formal catalogue name of the service as users and stakeholders recognise it. |
| Service Description | Enter a concise description of what the service provides, including its purpose and main outcomes. |
| Service Category | Enter the service category, using agreed catalogue values such as Business Application, Infrastructure, End-User Computing, Security, Network, Data/Analytics, or Other. |
| Service Status | Enter the current lifecycle status of the service. Allowed values: Planned, In Design, Live, Suspended, Retiring, Retired. |
| Business Process Supported | Enter the primary business process, function, or capability supported by the service. |
| Business Service Owner | Enter the accountable business owner role/name for the service and SLA outcomes. |
| IT Service Owner | Enter the accountable IT owner role/name responsible for service delivery and performance management. |
| Service Provider | Enter the internal team, shared service, managed service provider, or supplier responsible for delivering the service. |
| Customer/User Group | Enter the business unit, department, customer group, or user population covered by the service and SLA. |
| Business Criticality | Enter the agreed criticality rating based on business impact. Allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low. |
| Service Hours | Enter the hours during which the service is expected to be available, e.g. 24x7, Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 local time, excluding public holidays. |
| Support Hours | Enter the hours during which support is available for incidents, requests, and enquiries, e.g. 24x7 or Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 local time. |
| Service Availability Target (%) | Enter the agreed availability percentage target for the service as a numeric percentage, e.g. 99.5%, measured over the defined window. |
| Availability Measurement Window | Enter the period over which availability is measured, e.g. Monthly, Quarterly, Business Hours Monthly, 24x7 Monthly. |
| Incident Response Target | Enter the agreed maximum time to acknowledge/respond to incidents by priority, e.g. P1 15 min; P2 1 hour; P3 4 hours. |
| Incident Resolution/Restore Target | Enter the agreed maximum time to restore service or resolve incidents by priority, e.g. P1 4 hours; P2 1 business day; P3 5 business days. |
| Service Request Fulfilment Target | Enter the agreed fulfilment target for standard service requests, e.g. access request within 2 business days, standard request within 5 business days. |
| Performance/Capacity Target | Enter measurable service performance or capacity targets, e.g. response time <2 seconds for 95% of transactions, capacity utilisation below 80%. |
| Continuity Requirement - RTO | Enter the maximum tolerable time to restore the service after disruption, using hours or days, e.g. 4 hours, 1 day; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Continuity Requirement - RPO | Enter the maximum tolerable data loss period for the service, using minutes, hours, or days, e.g. 15 minutes, 4 hours; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Security/Compliance Requirements | Enter key security, privacy, regulatory, or compliance obligations relevant to the service, e.g. MFA required, PCI DSS, GDPR, encryption at rest. |
| SLA ID/Reference | Enter the unique identifier or document/link reference for the approved SLA covering this service, e.g. SLA-CRM-001. |
| SLA Version | Enter the current SLA version number in controlled-document format, e.g. v1.0, v2.3. |
| SLA Effective Date | Enter the date the SLA became effective in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| SLA Expiry/Renewal Date | Enter the SLA expiry, renewal, or scheduled re-approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| SLA Approval Status | Enter the approval state of the SLA. Allowed values: Draft, Under Review, Approved, Expired, Retired. |
| OLA/Supporting Agreement Reference | Enter references to internal operational level agreements that support the SLA, e.g. OLA-NET-001, OLA-SD-002; enter N/A if none. |
| Third-Party Contract/UC Reference | Enter references to supplier contracts or underpinning contracts supporting the SLA, e.g. UC-AWS-001, MSA-2025-004; enter N/A if none. |
| Service Dependencies | Enter key dependent services, platforms, suppliers, systems, teams, or infrastructure required to deliver the service. |
| Service Reporting Frequency | Enter how often SLA/service performance is reported. Allowed values: Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, On Request. |
| SLA Performance RAG | Enter the latest overall performance status against SLA targets. Allowed values: Red, Amber, Green, Not Yet Measured. |
| Last SLA Review Date | Enter the most recent date the service and SLA were reviewed with stakeholders in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next SLA Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date for the service and SLA in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Service Improvement Actions Reference | Enter reference IDs or links to improvement actions, CSI items, problem records, or risk treatments related to SLA performance; enter N/A if none. |
| Comments/Exceptions | Enter any approved exceptions, assumptions, limitations, exclusions, or explanatory notes relevant to the service catalogue entry or SLA. |

### Maintenance

The Service Catalogue Manager or IT Service Management Owner owns this register, with input from business service owners, IT service owners, supplier managers, and the service desk. It should be updated whenever a service or SLA changes and formally reviewed at least quarterly, drawing from the ITSM/service catalogue platform, SLA documents, monitoring reports, supplier contracts, CMDB, and service performance reports.

COB-024.title: Operations Procedures
COB-024.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [OPS-PROC-001] | 1.0 | Head of IT Operations | [YYYY-MM-DD] | COBIT 2019 | Internal |

## Purpose

This procedure defines how daily IT operations are planned, executed, monitored, recorded and escalated to ensure reliable delivery of technology services. It provides a consistent operational runbook for IT operations staff, service desk teams, infrastructure teams, application support teams and relevant service providers.

The procedure is intended to ensure that:

- Production services are operated in a controlled, repeatable and auditable manner.
- Scheduled operational tasks are completed on time and to the required standard.
- Events, alerts, failures and exceptions are detected, triaged and resolved promptly.
- Operational records are maintained as evidence of service performance, control execution and issue handling.
- Dependencies between infrastructure, applications, networks, security services, backups, batch processing and third-party services are actively managed.
- Escalations are clear, timely and aligned to business impact.

## Scope

This procedure applies to all live production IT services, supporting infrastructure and operational activities managed by [Organisation Name], including:

- Data centre, cloud, network, endpoint, storage and platform operations.
- Business application operations and routine application support tasks.
- Job scheduling, batch processing and interface monitoring.
- System availability, capacity, performance and health monitoring.
- Backup monitoring and operational recovery checks.
- Operational security monitoring activities performed by IT operations teams.
- Routine service requests assigned to IT operations.
- Daily, weekly and monthly operational checks.
- Supplier-operated services where [Organisation Name] retains accountability for operational oversight.
- Handover activities between shifts, regions, outsourced providers or support tiers.
- Operational evidence required for internal review, management reporting and audit.

This procedure does not replace:

- Incident management procedures.
- Change enablement procedures.
- Problem management procedures.
- Information security incident response procedures.
- Disaster recovery and business continuity procedures.
- Supplier management procedures.
- System-specific technical build documents.

Where another approved procedure governs an activity, this procedure defines the operational trigger, handoff, logging and evidence requirements.

## Prerequisites & Inputs

Before executing daily operations, the responsible team must confirm that the following prerequisites and inputs are available.

### Required Access

| Access Requirement | Purpose | Minimum Role/Group | Approval Required From |
|---|---|---|---|
| IT service management tool access | Record tasks, incidents, requests and escalations | Operations Analyst, Service Desk Analyst, Operations Lead | Service Management Owner |
| Monitoring platform access | Review events, alerts, dashboards and service health | Operations Analyst, Infrastructure Support | Monitoring Platform Owner |
| Job scheduler access | Monitor and manage approved production jobs | Batch Operations Analyst | Application or Platform Owner |
| Backup console access | Verify backup status and initiate approved re-runs | Backup Operator | Infrastructure Owner |
| Cloud management portal access | Review service status, capacity and operational events | Cloud Operations Analyst | Cloud Platform Owner |
| Privileged access management access | Obtain controlled elevated access where authorised | Approved Support Personnel | Privileged Access Owner |
| Knowledge base/runbook repository access | Retrieve approved runbooks and troubleshooting steps | All Operations Personnel | Knowledge Manager |

Access must be role-based, approved, periodically reviewed and removed when no longer required.

### Required Inputs

| Input | Source | Required Frequency | Used For |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Daily operations schedule | IT operations calendar or service management tool | Daily | Confirm planned activities and staffing |
| Shift handover notes | Previous shift or outsourced provider | Each shift | Identify open issues, risks and pending actions |
| Monitoring dashboards | Monitoring and observability platforms | Continuous/Daily | Confirm service health and identify events |
| Open incident queue | Service management tool | Daily and ongoing | Prioritise operational response |
| Open service request queue | Service management tool | Daily | Assign and complete operational requests |
| Approved change schedule | Change calendar | Daily | Identify operational impacts and post-change checks |
| Backup status report | Backup platform | Daily | Verify successful completion of scheduled backups |
| Batch processing status | Job scheduler | Daily | Validate completion of critical jobs |
| Capacity and performance dashboards | Monitoring and analytics tools | Daily/Weekly | Identify threshold breaches and trends |
| Supplier service status | Supplier portal, service report or notification feed | Daily/Ongoing | Confirm third-party service availability |
| Configuration and asset information | Configuration management repository | As needed | Validate ownership, dependencies and support groups |

### Operational Readiness Criteria

Daily operations must not begin without confirmation that:

- Minimum staffing levels for the shift are met.
- On-call contacts are current and reachable.
- Monitoring tools and service management tools are available.
- Escalation paths are available for critical services.
- Any planned maintenance or high-risk business activity for the day has been reviewed.
- Previous shift handover notes have been read and acknowledged.
- Critical unresolved incidents and major risks have assigned owners.
- Applicable production runbooks are current and accessible.

If any readiness criterion is not met, the Operations Lead must record the issue and initiate escalation before proceeding with affected activities.

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

### 1. Start of Shift Preparation

1.1. Log in to the approved IT service management tool, monitoring tools, communication channels and operational dashboards.

1.2. Confirm that personal access is functioning and limited to authorised operational duties.

1.3. Review the shift roster and confirm assigned responsibilities for:

- Monitoring.
- Incident queue oversight.
- Service request fulfilment.
- Backup verification.
- Batch and interface monitoring.
- Supplier status checks.
- Change support.
- Communications and escalation.

1.4. Review the previous shift handover notes and confirm understanding of:

- Open incidents and major incidents.
- Ongoing service degradation.
- Failed or delayed batch jobs.
- Failed backups or backup re-runs.
- Pending escalations.
- Supplier issues.
- Planned maintenance or changes.
- Known risks requiring monitoring.

1.5. Acknowledge shift acceptance in the agreed handover channel or operations log.

1.6. If handover information is missing, incomplete or unclear, contact the previous shift lead or Operations Lead immediately.

### 2. Review the Daily Operations Schedule

2.1. Open the daily operations schedule from the approved calendar, service management tool or operations board.

2.2. Confirm all scheduled operational activities for the day, including:

- Routine infrastructure checks.
- Cloud platform checks.
- Application health checks.
- Backup verification.
- Batch processing reviews.
- File transfer and interface checks.
- Security operations support tasks.
- User provisioning or operational service requests.
- Planned changes requiring operations support.
- Supplier maintenance windows.
- End-of-day or end-of-month processing.

2.3. Identify any conflicts between scheduled operational work and planned changes, business-critical periods or resource constraints.

2.4. Assign each operational activity to a named owner.

2.5. Update the operations board with task status as one of:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Not Started | Task is scheduled but work has not begun |
| In Progress | Task is actively being performed |
| Waiting | Task is blocked by dependency, supplier or approval |
| Completed | Task has been completed and evidence recorded |
| Failed | Task did not complete successfully and requires action |
| Escalated | Task requires management, technical or supplier escalation |
| Deferred | Task is postponed with approval and reason recorded |

2.6. Where a task cannot be completed during the scheduled window, record the reason, impact, owner and next action.

### 3. Perform Production Service Health Checks

3.1. Review service health dashboards for all critical and high-priority services.

3.2. Confirm availability status for:

- Core business applications.
- Identity and access services.
- Network connectivity.
- Internet and remote access services.
- Cloud platforms.
- Database services.
- Middleware and integration services.
- Storage and backup platforms.
- Security monitoring and protection tools.
- End-user productivity platforms.
- Customer-facing digital services.

3.3. Validate service health using approved indicators, which may include:

- Availability status.
- Error rates.
- Transaction success rates.
- Login success rates.
- Response time.
- Queue length.
- CPU, memory, disk and network utilisation.
- Database replication status.
- Certificate validity.
- Interface processing status.
- Synthetic transaction checks.

3.4. Investigate any dashboard item that is red, amber, degraded, unknown, stale or outside threshold.

3.5. For each abnormal condition:

- Check whether an incident already exists.
- If no incident exists, create one immediately.
- Assign the incident to the correct support group.
- Record observed symptoms, affected service, timestamps and evidence.
- Link related alerts, dashboards, logs and configuration items where available.

3.6. Do not clear, suppress, disable or alter monitoring thresholds unless an approved change or authorised temporary exception exists.

### 4. Monitor and Respond to Events and Alerts

4.1. Continuously monitor operational event queues during the shift.

4.2. Classify events using the approved categories:

| Event Category | Description | Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| Informational | No current impact; indicates status or completion | Review and close if expected |
| Warning | Potential issue or threshold approaching | Investigate and monitor |
| Exception | A process, job or service did not behave as expected | Create or update incident |
| Performance | Service degradation or capacity concern | Investigate and escalate if thresholds are breached |
| Availability | Service, component or dependency unavailable | Create incident and escalate based on impact |
| Security-related | Event may indicate unauthorised activity or control failure | Escalate to security process immediately |
| Supplier-related | Event relates to third-party service failure or degradation | Log, contact supplier and track response |

4.3. Correlate repeated or related alerts to avoid duplicate handling while ensuring service impact is not missed.

4.4. Record alert handling in the service management tool or monitoring platform, including:

- Alert name or identifier.
- Affected service or component.
- Time detected.
- Initial assessment.
- Action taken.
- Incident or request reference.
- Escalation status.
- Closure reason.

4.5. If an alert is known to be false-positive, record the reason and notify the Monitoring Platform Owner for tuning review.

4.6. If repeated alerts indicate an underlying defect, raise or link to a problem record in accordance with the problem management process.

### 5. Manage the Operations Incident Queue

5.1. Review all open incidents assigned to IT operations at the start of the shift and at regular intervals.

5.2. Prioritise incidents based on:

- Business impact.
- Number of users affected.
- Criticality of the service.
- Customer or regulatory impact.
- Duration of outage or degradation.
- Availability of workaround.
- Security or data protection implications.
- Executive or business escalation.

5.3. Ensure each incident has:

- Clear description.
- Affected service or configuration item.
- Impact and urgency.
- Priority.
- Assigned owner.
- Current status.
- Latest action note.
- Next action and target time.
- Linked alerts, changes or known errors where applicable.

5.4. For incidents requiring technical support beyond first-line operations:

- Assign to the correct resolver group.
- Provide relevant diagnostics and evidence.
- Notify the resolver group through the agreed channel if priority is high.
- Track progress until ownership is accepted.

5.5. For major or potentially major incidents, immediately follow the major incident process and notify the Operations Lead.

5.6. Do not close an incident until:

- Service restoration is confirmed.
- Monitoring has returned to normal or an approved workaround is in place.
- The user, service owner or resolver group has provided confirmation where required.
- Resolution notes are complete.
- Related operational tasks are updated.

### 6. Execute Routine Operational Tasks

6.1. Perform assigned routine tasks using approved runbooks only.

6.2. Before performing each task, confirm:

- Task is scheduled or authorised.
- Correct system, environment and service are identified.
- Required access is available.
- Expected outcome is understood.
- Backout or escalation step is known.
- The task does not conflict with a freeze period or planned change.

6.3. Routine tasks may include:

| Task Type | Typical Activities | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure checks | Server status, storage utilisation, cluster status, service restarts where approved | Screenshot, dashboard export or operations log entry |
| Network checks | Link status, VPN health, firewall service availability, DNS status | Monitoring event record or health report |
| Cloud checks | Platform health, resource status, quota use, failed deployments | Cloud dashboard extract or ticket note |
| Application checks | Application process status, transaction tests, interface status | Runbook checklist or application health report |
| Database checks | Replication status, job completion, space utilisation, backup status | Monitoring output or DBA confirmation |
| Endpoint operations | Deployment status, patch job status, endpoint management console checks | Console report or task record |
| Security support tasks | Antivirus health, endpoint protection status, logging agent status | Security tool report or escalation record |
| User operations | Approved account actions, group updates, access removals | Service request record |

6.4. Record completion of each task in the operations log or service management tool.

6.5. If a task fails, stop where appropriate, preserve evidence and follow the escalation steps in the runbook.

6.6. Never improvise production changes, scripts, restarts, configuration edits or data corrections outside approved runbooks and change procedures.

### 7. Monitor Backups and Recovery Readiness

7.1. Review the backup platform for all scheduled backups completed during the previous operational period.

7.2. Confirm backup status for:

- Critical servers.
- Databases.
- Cloud workloads.
- File repositories.
- Application data stores.
- Configuration repositories.
- Security platforms where applicable.

7.3. Record backup results as:

| Backup Status | Required Action |
|---|---|
| Successful | Record evidence and no further action required |
| Successful with warning | Review warning, assess risk and record action |
| Failed | Create incident and initiate approved re-run or escalation |
| Missed | Investigate schedule, agent, storage or connectivity issue |
| Running long | Monitor and escalate if business or recovery objectives may be affected |
| Not reporting | Create incident and verify monitoring or agent health |

7.4. For failed or missed backups:

- Create or update an incident.
- Identify affected system and data set.
- Confirm criticality and recovery requirement.
- Attempt approved re-run if permitted by the runbook.
- Escalate to the Backup Owner or Infrastructure Owner if re-run fails.
- Notify the Service Owner where recovery exposure may exceed tolerance.
- Record final status and evidence.

7.5. Do not mark a failed backup as accepted without approval from the accountable Service Owner and Operations Lead.

7.6. Report repeated backup failures to problem management.

### 8. Monitor Batch Processing, Interfaces and Scheduled Jobs

8.1. Review the job scheduler and integration monitoring dashboard at the required times.

8.2. Validate that critical jobs, file transfers and interfaces have completed successfully.

8.3. For each critical job, confirm:

- Scheduled start and end time.
- Actual start and end time.
- Completion status.
- Upstream and downstream dependencies.
- Output file, report, transaction or interface result.
- Business confirmation where required.

8.4. Record daily batch status using the approved operations log.

| Job/Interface | Expected Completion | Actual Completion | Status | Action Taken | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| [Critical Job Name] | [HH:MM] | [HH:MM] | Successful/Failed/Delayed | [Action] | [Role/Team] |
| [Interface Name] | [HH:MM] | [HH:MM] | Successful/Failed/Delayed | [Action] | [Role/Team] |

8.5. For failed or delayed jobs:

- Confirm whether retry is automatic or manual.
- Check runbook for approved re-run conditions.
- Notify the Application Owner or Business Process Owner where processing impact is possible.
- Raise an incident if one does not exist.
- Preserve logs and error output.
- Escalate if downstream processing or business deadlines are at risk.

8.6. Manual job re-runs must only be performed where authorised by the runbook, job owner or approved change.

8.7. Any data correction, file manipulation, job parameter change or production schedule alteration must follow the change procedure unless specifically pre-approved in the runbook.

### 9. Support Approved Changes and Maintenance Activities

9.1. Review the approved change schedule at the start of the shift and before any maintenance window.

9.2. Identify changes requiring operations support, monitoring, communications or validation.

9.3. Before supporting a change, confirm:

- Change is approved.
- Implementation window is current.
- Responsible implementer is identified.
- Backout plan is documented.
- Communication plan is available where required.
- Monitoring criteria are agreed.
- Post-change validation steps are defined.

9.4. During the change window:

- Monitor affected services.
- Record operational observations.
- Support only the approved activities.
- Escalate deviations to the Change Manager or Operations Lead.
- Do not approve scope expansion informally.

9.5. After implementation:

- Perform agreed health checks.
- Confirm alerts have normalised.
- Record post-change validation results.
- Link any incidents to the change record.
- Report failed or backed-out changes through the change process.

### 10. Fulfil Assigned Operational Service Requests

10.1. Review service requests assigned to IT operations.

10.2. Confirm that each request is:

- Logged in the approved service management tool.
- Categorised correctly.
- Approved where approval is required.
- Within the authority of IT operations.
- Supported by an approved fulfilment procedure.

10.3. Execute the request according to the relevant runbook.

10.4. For access-related requests, verify approval, identity and segregation requirements before making changes.

10.5. Record the action taken, outcome, time completed and any evidence required.

10.6. Reassign or escalate requests that are incomplete, unauthorised, unclear or outside operational authority.

10.7. Do not process requests received only by informal channels unless they are subsequently logged and approved in the service management tool.

### 11. Perform Supplier and Third-Party Service Checks

11.1. Review supplier portals, notifications and status feeds for services supporting production operations.

11.2. Confirm the status of critical third-party dependencies, including:

- Cloud service providers.
- Telecommunications providers.
- Managed service providers.
- Payment, identity, messaging or integration providers.
- Software-as-a-service platforms.
- Security service providers.

11.3. Where a supplier incident or maintenance event may affect [Organisation Name]:

- Create or update an internal incident.
- Record the supplier reference number.
- Assess business impact.
- Notify affected Service Owners.
- Track supplier updates at agreed intervals.
- Record restoration confirmation.

11.4. Escalate supplier performance issues where response or resolution does not meet agreed service expectations.

### 12. Maintain Operational Communications

12.1. Use approved communication channels for operational coordination.

12.2. For high-priority incidents or service degradation, provide updates at the agreed frequency to:

- Operations Lead.
- Service Desk.
- Service Owner.
- Incident Manager.
- Business Relationship Manager where required.
- Supplier contact where applicable.

12.3. Operational updates must include:

- Current service status.
- Business impact.
- Actions completed.
- Actions in progress.
- Next update time.
- Escalations required.
- Workaround availability.

12.4. Avoid speculative root cause statements until validated by the responsible technical team.

12.5. Do not share sensitive operational, security or customer information outside approved channels.

### 13. Complete Operational Evidence and Logs

13.1. Ensure every operational task has an auditable record.

13.2. Records must be complete, accurate, timely and attributable to the person or team performing the activity.

13.3. At minimum, operations logs must include:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Date and time | When the activity was performed |
| Operator | Person or team completing the activity |
| Service/system | Affected service, platform or component |
| Activity | Task, check, event or action performed |
| Result | Successful, failed, warning, deferred or escalated |
| Evidence | Screenshot, report, ticket reference, dashboard export or log extract |
| Follow-up | Required action, owner and due time |
| Approval reference | Change, request or exception reference where applicable |

13.4. Store evidence in the approved repository or attach it to the relevant ticket.

13.5. Evidence must be sufficient for another competent person to understand what was checked, what was found and what action was taken.

13.6. Do not edit historical logs to obscure failures or delays. Corrections must be made as additional dated entries.

### 14. Conduct End-of-Shift Handover

14.1. Before the shift ends, review all assigned operational tasks, incidents, alerts, service requests and escalations.

14.2. Update each record with current status, latest action and next step.

14.3. Prepare handover notes covering:

- Critical service status.
- Open incidents and priorities.
- Failed, delayed or at-risk tasks.
- Backup issues.
- Batch processing status.
- Supplier issues.
- Changes in progress or awaiting validation.
- Escalations pending.
- Risks requiring monitoring.
- Unusual activity or lessons learned.

14.4. Conduct verbal handover for high-priority or sensitive matters where required.

14.5. Confirm that the receiving shift or on-call contact has acknowledged the handover.

14.6. If no receiving shift is available, escalate to the Operations Lead before leaving unresolved critical work unattended.

### 15. Daily Operations Review

15.1. The Operations Lead must review daily operational outcomes for completeness and exceptions.

15.2. The review must include:

- Uncompleted scheduled tasks.
- Failed operational activities.
- Major or recurring incidents.
- Backup failures.
- Batch failures or delays.
- Supplier issues.
- Breached or at-risk service levels.
- Monitoring gaps.
- Change-related issues.
- Evidence completeness.

15.3. Assign follow-up actions with owners and due dates.

15.4. Report significant operational issues to IT management and Service Owners as appropriate.

15.5. Identify recurring issues for problem management and continual improvement.

## Roles & RACI

The following RACI matrix defines responsibilities for this procedure.

| Activity | Operations Analyst | Operations Lead | Service Desk | Infrastructure/Application Support | Service Owner | Change Manager | Security Operations | Supplier Manager |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Start-of-shift checks | R | A | C | C | I | I | I | I |
| Daily operations schedule review | R | A | C | C | I | C | I | I |
| Service health monitoring | R | A | C | C | I | I | C | I |
| Event and alert triage | R | A | C | C | I | I | C | I |
| Incident queue management | R | A | R | C | I | I | C | I |
| Routine operational tasks | R | A | C | R | I | I | C | I |
| Backup verification | R | A | I | R | I | I | I | I |
| Batch and interface monitoring | R | A | I | R | C | I | I | I |
| Change support and post-change checks | R | A | I | R | C | A/R | C | I |
| Service request fulfilment | R | A | R | C | I | I | C | I |
| Supplier service checks | R | A | I | C | I | I | I | R |
| Escalation of major service issues | C | A/R | R | R | I | C | C | C |
| Operational evidence maintenance | R | A | C | C | I | I | I | I |
| End-of-shift handover | R | A | C | C | I | I | I | I |
| Daily operations review | C | A/R | C | C | I | C | C | C |

RACI definitions:

| RACI | Definition |
|---|---|
| R | Responsible for performing the activity |
| A | Accountable for ensuring the activity is completed correctly |
| C | Consulted for input, technical support or decision-making |
| I | Informed of status, outcome or impact |

## Records & Outputs

The following records must be created, updated or retained as evidence of operational control.

| Record/Output | Description | Owner | Retention Location | Minimum Retention |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Daily operations log | Record of completed checks, tasks, exceptions and actions | Operations Lead | Service management tool or operations repository | [Retention Period] |
| Shift handover record | Summary of open issues, risks and pending actions | Operations Lead | Handover tool or operations repository | [Retention Period] |
| Monitoring event records | Event status, investigation notes and closure rationale | Monitoring Platform Owner | Monitoring platform | [Retention Period] |
| Incident records | Logged incidents, impact, actions, resolution and closure notes | Incident Manager | Service management tool | [Retention Period] |
| Service request records | Fulfilment details, approvals and completion evidence | Service Request Owner | Service management tool | [Retention Period] |
| Backup status report | Daily backup outcomes and exceptions | Backup Owner | Backup platform or evidence repository | [Retention Period] |
| Batch processing report | Job and interface completion status | Application Operations Owner | Job scheduler or operations repository | [Retention Period] |
| Change support notes | Operational validation and post-change checks | Change Manager | Change record | [Retention Period] |
| Supplier issue log | Supplier incidents, references, updates and resolution | Supplier Manager | Supplier management repository | [Retention Period] |
| Exception approvals | Approved deviations from normal operations procedure | Operations Lead | Risk, exception or service management repository | [Retention Period] |
| Daily operations review notes | Management review of issues, risks and follow-up actions | Head of IT Operations | Operations repository | [Retention Period] |
| Problem candidates | Recurring issues proposed for problem investigation | Problem Manager | Service management tool | [Retention Period] |

All records must be:

- Accurate and created as close as possible to the time of activity.
- Traceable to the person or team performing the work.
- Protected from unauthorised alteration or deletion.
- Stored only in approved systems or repositories.
- Available for management review, assurance activities and audit when requested.
- Handled in accordance with information classification and retention requirements.

## Exceptions & Escalation

### Exceptions

An exception occurs when an operational activity cannot be performed as defined by this procedure or an approved runbook.

Examples include:

- Required tool is unavailable.
- Monitoring data is missing or unreliable.
- Required access is unavailable.
- Scheduled task cannot be completed on time.
- Approved runbook is missing, outdated or incorrect.
- Backup, batch job or interface failure cannot be resolved within the expected window.
- Supplier service status is unavailable or disputed.
- Minimum staffing levels are not met.
- Operational evidence cannot be captured.
- A production action is needed urgently but is not covered by an approved runbook.

Exceptions must be recorded with:

| Field | Required Information |
|---|---|
| Exception date/time | When the exception was identified |
| Reported by | Person or team identifying the exception |
| Affected service/system | Service, process or asset impacted |
| Description | What could not be completed or followed |
| Reason | Cause or constraint |
| Business impact | Actual or potential effect |
| Interim action | Temporary action taken |
| Risk accepted by | Role approving temporary acceptance, where applicable |
| Target resolution | Expected date/time for normal control restoration |
| Follow-up owner | Person or team responsible for closure |

Temporary workarounds must be approved by the Operations Lead and, where business risk is material, by the relevant Service Owner. Workarounds that alter production configuration, data, access, security settings or service behaviour must follow the change process unless emergency handling is formally invoked.

### Escalation Triggers

Escalation is required when any of the following occur:

- Critical service is unavailable or severely degraded.
- Business-critical batch job fails or will miss deadline.
- Backup failure affects a system with significant recovery requirements.
- Monitoring indicates security-related activity or suspected compromise.
- Incident priority requires management visibility.
- Supplier outage affects or may affect production services.
- Repeated alerts indicate systemic failure.
- Required operational task cannot be completed within its agreed window.
- Staff do not have access or authority to resolve the issue.
- A runbook is incorrect, missing or unsafe to follow.
- Service levels are breached or likely to be breached.
- Customer, regulatory, financial or reputational impact is possible.

### Escalation Path

| Escalation Level | Trigger | Notify | Expected Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level 1 - Operational | Task delay, warning alert, minor failure | Operations Lead | Assign owner, monitor and resolve |
| Level 2 - Technical | Resolver expertise required or repeat failure | Infrastructure/Application Support Lead | Investigate, remediate and update record |
| Level 3 - Service Impact | Service degradation, failed critical process, high business risk | Service Owner and Incident Manager | Assess impact, coordinate communications and prioritise recovery |
| Level 4 - Major Incident | Critical outage, widespread impact or executive concern | Major Incident Manager and IT Leadership | Activate major incident coordination |
| Level 5 - Security | Suspected cyber event, unauthorised access or security control failure | Security Operations Lead | Follow security incident response process |
| Level 6 - Supplier | Third-party failure, missed supplier response or unresolved dependency | Supplier Manager | Escalate with supplier and track contractual response |
| Level 7 - Executive | Severe business, customer, financial or reputational impact | CIO or delegated executive | Provide direction, resources and stakeholder communication |

### Emergency Actions

Emergency operational actions may be taken only when delay would create unacceptable business, safety, security or service impact.

Emergency actions must:

- Be authorised by the Operations Lead or appropriate on-call authority where practical.
- Be limited to what is necessary to stabilise or restore service.
- Be recorded immediately or as soon as practicable.
- Be reviewed after the event.
- Be linked to an emergency change, incident or security incident record as applicable.
- Include evidence of approval, actions taken, outcome and follow-up.

## Review

This procedure must be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to IT operations, including:

- Introduction or retirement of critical services.
- Significant change to operating model, outsourcing or support structure.
- New monitoring, backup, job scheduling or service management platform.
- Major incident or recurring operational failure.
- Audit finding or management review action.
- Significant supplier change.
- Change to business operating hours or service level expectations.
- Lessons learned from disaster recovery or resilience exercises.
- Identified gap in runbooks, handover or operational evidence.

The Operations Lead is responsible for coordinating the review. The Head of IT Operations is accountable for approval.

The review must confirm that:

- Scope remains accurate.
- Roles and responsibilities remain current.
- Escalation paths and contact lists are valid.
- Operational tasks reflect actual production services.
- Monitoring coverage is adequate.
- Evidence requirements are practical and complete.
- Runbooks are current and approved.
- Exceptions and recurring issues have been addressed.
- Supplier dependencies are reflected.
- The procedure remains aligned with business service expectations.

Review outcomes must be recorded, including:

| Review Item | Required Record |
|---|---|
| Review date | Date review was completed |
| Review participants | Roles or names of reviewers |
| Summary of changes | Material updates made or confirmed not required |
| Open actions | Owner, due date and status |
| Approval | Approver and approval date |
| Next review date | Planned review cycle |

Version history must be maintained.

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Author | Approved By |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Initial issue | [Author Name/Role] | [Approver Name/Role] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Ticket ID | Enter the unique ITSM ticket/reference number generated by the service management tool; format should match the system identifier, e.g. INC0001234 or REQ0005678. |
| Record Type | Enter the ticket type using allowed values only: Incident, Service Request. |
| Source Channel | Enter how the ticket was raised using allowed values such as Portal, Email, Phone, Chat, Monitoring Alert, Walk-up, API, Other. |
| Logged Date/Time | Enter the date and time the ticket was created in the ITSM tool; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM using 24-hour time and agreed organisational time zone. |
| Reported By | Enter the name, user ID, or email of the person or system that reported the ticket. |
| Requester/User Affected | Enter the name, user ID, or email of the user or group affected by the incident or requesting the service. |
| Business Unit | Enter the affected/requesting department, function, site, or business unit using the organisation's approved naming convention. |
| Service/Application | Enter the business service, IT service, or application affected/requested as recorded in the service catalogue or CMDB. |
| Configuration Item/Asset ID | Enter the CI name, asset tag, hostname, application ID, or CMDB reference associated with the ticket; enter Not Applicable if no CI applies. |
| Service Owner | Enter the accountable service owner or application owner for the affected/requested service. |
| Short Description | Enter a concise one-line summary of the request or incident, sufficient to identify the issue or requested service. |
| Detailed Description | Enter the detailed symptoms, request details, error messages, business impact, affected users, and any initial diagnostic information. |
| Category | Enter the approved high-level ticket classification from the ITSM taxonomy, e.g. Access, Hardware, Software, Network, Application, Facilities, Request Fulfilment. |
| Subcategory | Enter the approved lower-level classification under the selected category, e.g. Password Reset, Laptop, Email, VPN, Database, User Provisioning. |
| Impact | Enter assessed business impact using allowed values: 1-Enterprise/Critical, 2-High, 3-Medium, 4-Low, or the organisation's approved impact scale. |
| Urgency | Enter required speed of response using allowed values: 1-Critical, 2-High, 3-Medium, 4-Low, or the organisation's approved urgency scale. |
| Priority | Enter the calculated or approved priority derived from impact and urgency using allowed values: P1 Critical, P2 High, P3 Medium, P4 Low, P5 Planning. |
| Major Incident Flag | Enter Yes if the incident met the organisation's major incident criteria; otherwise enter No. For service requests enter Not Applicable unless the ITSM process requires otherwise. |
| Security/Privacy Flag | Enter Yes if the ticket involves suspected/confirmed information security, cyber, privacy, or data protection impact; otherwise enter No. |
| Known Error/Workaround Applied | Enter Yes if a known error record or documented workaround was used; enter No if not used; enter Not Applicable for service requests where not relevant. |
| Related Problem ID | Enter the linked problem record ID if the incident is associated with problem management/root cause analysis; enter Not Applicable if no problem record exists. |
| Related Change ID | Enter the linked change record ID where fulfilment, remediation, or resolution required an authorised change; enter Not Applicable if no change was required. |
| Assignment Group | Enter the support queue, resolver group, or fulfilment team responsible for the ticket at the time of export. |
| Assigned Analyst | Enter the named analyst currently or finally assigned to resolve/fulfil the ticket; enter Unassigned if not yet assigned. |
| Current Status | Enter current lifecycle status using allowed values such as New, Assigned, In Progress, Pending User, Pending Vendor, Pending Change, Resolved, Closed, Cancelled. |
| Status Reason | Enter the reason for the current status, especially for pending, cancelled, or closed tickets, e.g. Awaiting User, Awaiting Approval, Awaiting Supplier, Duplicate, Completed. |
| SLA Name | Enter the applicable SLA/OLA/UC name or service target applied by the ITSM tool; enter Not Applicable if no SLA applies. |
| SLA Target Resolution Date/Time | Enter the deadline for resolution or fulfilment according to the applicable SLA; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or Not Applicable if no SLA applies. |
| SLA Target Response Date/Time | Enter the deadline for first response according to the applicable SLA; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or Not Applicable if no SLA applies. |
| First Response Date/Time | Enter the date and time support first responded to the requester or acknowledged the ticket; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or blank if not yet responded. |
| Resolution Date/Time | Enter the date and time the incident was resolved or the service request was fulfilled; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or blank if not yet resolved/fulfilled. |
| Closure Date/Time | Enter the date and time the ticket was formally closed in the ITSM tool; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or blank if not yet closed. |
| SLA Met | Enter Yes if all applicable SLA targets were met, No if one or more SLA targets were breached, or Not Applicable if no SLA applies. |
| Escalation Level | Enter the highest escalation level reached using allowed values such as None, Functional Escalation, Hierarchical Escalation, Major Incident Escalation, Vendor Escalation. |
| Escalation Date/Time | Enter the date and time of first escalation; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or Not Applicable if no escalation occurred. |
| Approvals Required | Enter Yes if fulfilment or resolution required approval, such as access, standard request, financial, manager, or change approval; otherwise enter No. |
| Approval Status | Enter approval state using allowed values: Not Required, Pending, Approved, Rejected, Withdrawn. |
| Approval Date/Time | Enter the date and time final approval or rejection was recorded; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or Not Applicable if approval was not required. |
| Resolution Code | Enter the approved resolution/fulfilment code from the ITSM tool, e.g. Fixed, Workaround Provided, User Education, Access Granted, Hardware Replaced, Duplicate, Unable to Reproduce, Cancelled. |
| Resolution Summary | Enter a clear summary of actions taken, diagnostics performed, fulfilment completed, workaround provided, and evidence of service restoration or request completion. |
| Root Cause Category | For incidents, enter the confirmed or suspected root cause category where known, e.g. Hardware Failure, Software Defect, Configuration Error, Capacity, User Error, Supplier, Unknown; for service requests enter Not Applicable. |
| Customer Confirmation | Enter confirmation outcome using allowed values: Confirmed Resolved/Fulfilled, Auto-Closed After No Response, Not Confirmed, Not Applicable. |
| Reopened Flag | Enter Yes if the ticket was reopened after resolution/closure; otherwise enter No. |
| Reopen Count | Enter the number of times the ticket was reopened as a whole number, e.g. 0, 1, 2. |
| Closure Code | Enter the formal closure classification using allowed values defined by the organisation, e.g. Successful, Completed, Cancelled by User, Duplicate, No Fault Found, Rejected. |
| Knowledge Article Created/Updated | Enter Yes if a knowledge article, known error, FAQ, runbook, or workaround record was created or updated as a result of the ticket; otherwise enter No. |
| Audit Trail/Activity Log Reference | Enter the ITSM system link, export reference, or activity log identifier that evidences updates, communications, approvals, escalations, and status changes. |
| Last Updated Date/Time | Enter the latest date and time any field or activity on the ticket was updated in the ITSM tool; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the IT Service Management Process Owner, with oversight from Incident Management, Request Fulfilment, Problem Management, and Service Owners. Updated continuously from the ITSM ticketing tool and formally reviewed at least monthly for completeness, SLA performance, escalations, problem links, and closure quality.

field_guidance.Source Channel: Enter how the ticket was raised using allowed values such as Portal, Email, Phone, Chat, Monitoring Alert, Walk-up, API, Other.
field_guidance.Logged Date/Time: Enter the date and time the ticket was created in the ITSM tool; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM using 24-hour time and agreed organisational time zone.
field_guidance.Reported By: Enter the name, user ID, or email of the person or system that reported the ticket.
field_guidance.Requester/User Affected: Enter the name, user ID, or email of the user or group affected by the incident or requesting the service.
field_guidance.Business Unit: Enter the affected/requesting department, function, site, or business unit using the organisation's approved naming convention.
field_guidance.Service/Application: Enter the business service, IT service, or application affected/requested as recorded in the service catalogue or CMDB.
field_guidance.Configuration Item/Asset ID: Enter the CI name, asset tag, hostname, application ID, or CMDB reference associated with the ticket; enter Not Applicable if no CI applies.
field_guidance.Service Owner: Enter the accountable service owner or application owner for the affected/requested service.
field_guidance.Short Description: Enter a concise one-line summary of the request or incident, sufficient to identify the issue or requested service.
field_guidance.Detailed Description: Enter the detailed symptoms, request details, error messages, business impact, affected users, and any initial diagnostic information.
field_guidance.Category: Enter the approved high-level ticket classification from the ITSM taxonomy, e.g. Access, Hardware, Software, Network, Application, Facilities, Request Fulfilment.
field_guidance.Subcategory: Enter the approved lower-level classification under the selected category, e.g. Password Reset, Laptop, Email, VPN, Database, User Provisioning.
field_guidance.Impact: Enter assessed business impact using allowed values: 1-Enterprise/Critical, 2-High, 3-Medium, 4-Low, or the organisation's approved impact scale.
field_guidance.Urgency: Enter required speed of response using allowed values: 1-Critical, 2-High, 3-Medium, 4-Low, or the organisation's approved urgency scale.
field_guidance.Priority: Enter the calculated or approved priority derived from impact and urgency using allowed values: P1 Critical, P2 High, P3 Medium, P4 Low, P5 Planning.
field_guidance.Major Incident Flag: Enter Yes if the incident met the organisation's major incident criteria; otherwise enter No. For service requests enter Not Applicable unless the ITSM process requires otherwise.
field_guidance.Security/Privacy Flag: Enter Yes if the ticket involves suspected/confirmed information security, cyber, privacy, or data protection impact; otherwise enter No.
field_guidance.Known Error/Workaround Applied: Enter Yes if a known error record or documented workaround was used; enter No if not used; enter Not Applicable for service requests where not relevant.
field_guidance.Related Problem ID: Enter the linked problem record ID if the incident is associated with problem management/root cause analysis; enter Not Applicable if no problem record exists.
field_guidance.Related Change ID: Enter the linked change record ID where fulfilment, remediation, or resolution required an authorised change; enter Not Applicable if no change was required.
field_guidance.Assignment Group: Enter the support queue, resolver group, or fulfilment team responsible for the ticket at the time of export.
field_guidance.Assigned Analyst: Enter the named analyst currently or finally assigned to resolve/fulfil the ticket; enter Unassigned if not yet assigned.
field_guidance.Current Status: Enter current lifecycle status using allowed values such as New, Assigned, In Progress, Pending User, Pending Vendor, Pending Change, Resolved, Closed, Cancelled.
field_guidance.Status Reason: Enter the reason for the current status, especially for pending, cancelled, or closed tickets, e.g. Awaiting User, Awaiting Approval, Awaiting Supplier, Duplicate, Completed.
field_guidance.SLA Name: Enter the applicable SLA/OLA/UC name or service target applied by the ITSM tool; enter Not Applicable if no SLA applies.
field_guidance.SLA Target Resolution Date/Time: Enter the deadline for resolution or fulfilment according to the applicable SLA; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or Not Applicable if no SLA applies.
field_guidance.SLA Target Response Date/Time: Enter the deadline for first response according to the applicable SLA; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or Not Applicable if no SLA applies.
field_guidance.First Response Date/Time: Enter the date and time support first responded to the requester or acknowledged the ticket; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or blank if not yet responded.
field_guidance.Resolution Date/Time: Enter the date and time the incident was resolved or the service request was fulfilled; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or blank if not yet resolved/fulfilled.
field_guidance.Closure Date/Time: Enter the date and time the ticket was formally closed in the ITSM tool; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or blank if not yet closed.
field_guidance.SLA Met: Enter Yes if all applicable SLA targets were met, No if one or more SLA targets were breached, or Not Applicable if no SLA applies.
field_guidance.Escalation Level: Enter the highest escalation level reached using allowed values such as None, Functional Escalation, Hierarchical Escalation, Major Incident Escalation, Vendor Escalation.
field_guidance.Escalation Date/Time: Enter the date and time of first escalation; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or Not Applicable if no escalation occurred.
field_guidance.Approvals Required: Enter Yes if fulfilment or resolution required approval, such as access, standard request, financial, manager, or change approval; otherwise enter No.
field_guidance.Approval Status: Enter approval state using allowed values: Not Required, Pending, Approved, Rejected, Withdrawn.
field_guidance.Approval Date/Time: Enter the date and time final approval or rejection was recorded; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or Not Applicable if approval was not required.
field_guidance.Resolution Code: Enter the approved resolution/fulfilment code from the ITSM tool, e.g. Fixed, Workaround Provided, User Education, Access Granted, Hardware Replaced, Duplicate, Unable to Reproduce, Cancelled.
field_guidance.Resolution Summary: Enter a clear summary of actions taken, diagnostics performed, fulfilment completed, workaround provided, and evidence of service restoration or request completion.
field_guidance.Root Cause Category: For incidents, enter the confirmed or suspected root cause category where known, e.g. Hardware Failure, Software Defect, Configuration Error, Capacity, User Error, Supplier, Unknown; for service requests enter Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Customer Confirmation: Enter confirmation outcome using allowed values: Confirmed Resolved/Fulfilled, Auto-Closed After No Response, Not Confirmed, Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Reopened Flag: Enter Yes if the ticket was reopened after resolution/closure; otherwise enter No.
field_guidance.Reopen Count: Enter the number of times the ticket was reopened as a whole number, e.g. 0, 1, 2.
field_guidance.Closure Code: Enter the formal closure classification using allowed values defined by the organisation, e.g. Successful, Completed, Cancelled by User, Duplicate, No Fault Found, Rejected.
field_guidance.Knowledge Article Created/Updated: Enter Yes if a knowledge article, known error, FAQ, runbook, or workaround record was created or updated as a result of the ticket; otherwise enter No.
field_guidance.Audit Trail/Activity Log Reference: Enter the ITSM system link, export reference, or activity log identifier that evidences updates, communications, approvals, escalations, and status changes.
field_guidance.Last Updated Date/Time: Enter the latest date and time any field or activity on the ticket was updated in the ITSM tool; format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.

COB-026.title: Problem Management Records
COB-026.content:
## Problem Management Records (ITSM export template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Problem Record ID | Problem Title | Problem Description | Problem Source | Detection Date | Logged Date | Reported By | Problem Manager | Assigned Investigation Group | Affected Business Service | Affected Application or System | Affected Configuration Item IDs | Related Incident IDs | Incident Count Linked | Business Impact Description | Impact Rating | Urgency Rating | Priority | Risk Rating | Problem Category | Problem Subcategory | Problem Status | RCA Required | RCA Method | Investigation Start Date | Investigation Target Date | Symptoms Observed | Investigation Findings | Root Cause Identified | Root Cause Category | Known Error Record ID | Known Error Status | Workaround Available | Workaround Description | Workaround Published To | Permanent Resolution Required | Permanent Resolution Description | Corrective Action Owner | Corrective Action Due Date | Corrective Action Status | Related Change Request ID | Change Implementation Date | Resolution Verification Method | Resolution Verified By | Resolution Verification Date | Residual Risk Accepted | Residual Risk Acceptance Reference | Closure Summary | Closed Date | Closure Approved By | Lessons Learned | Preventive Actions Identified | SLA or OLA Breach | Major Problem Review Required | Major Problem Review Date | Evidence or Attachment Links | COBIT Control Reference | Last Updated Date | Last Updated By |
