pending approval.] | [EXAMPLE: Not Published] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Review and tune connection pool configuration after RCA confirmation.] | [EXAMPLE: Payments Engineering Lead] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-31] | [EXAMPLE: In Progress] | [EXAMPLE: CHG0007788] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: 14-day monitoring period following change, with no recurrence of linked incident symptom.] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: Not Applicable] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: Improve capacity alerting thresholds and review pre-peak performance testing.] | [EXAMPLE: Add connection pool utilisation dashboard and automated alerting.] | [EXAMPLE: Under Assessment] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: RCA-DOC-2026-004; LOG-BUNDLE-7788; MON-DASH-PAY-01] | [EXAMPLE: DSS03.01; DSS03.02; DSS03.03] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-12] | [EXAMPLE: jsmith] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Problem Record ID | Enter the unique identifier assigned by the ITSM tool for this problem record; use the system-generated format, e.g. PRB0001234. |
| Problem Title | Enter a concise title summarising the problem, including the affected service or technology and symptom. |
| Problem Description | Enter a clear description of the recurring, major, or underlying issue requiring root-cause analysis; include what is failing, where, and under what conditions. |
| Problem Source | Enter the origin of the problem record; allowed values: Incident Trend, Major Incident, Monitoring Alert, Service Review, Supplier Notification, Audit Finding, Risk Event, Proactive Analysis, Other. |
| Detection Date | Enter the date the issue pattern, major incident cause, or potential problem was first detected in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Logged Date | Enter the date the problem record was formally created in the ITSM system in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Reported By | Enter the name, role, team, or system that raised the problem record. |
| Problem Manager | Enter the named person accountable for coordinating the problem lifecycle and ensuring investigation, resolution, and closure. |
| Assigned Investigation Group | Enter the resolver group, technical team, supplier, or cross-functional team responsible for root-cause investigation. |
| Affected Business Service | Enter the business-facing service affected, using the official service catalogue name. |
| Affected Application or System | Enter the application, platform, infrastructure component, or technology domain affected. |
| Affected Configuration Item IDs | Enter the configuration item identifier(s) from the CMDB; separate multiple IDs with semicolons. |
| Related Incident IDs | Enter all incident, major incident, event, or alert references linked to this problem; separate multiple IDs with semicolons. |
| Incident Count Linked | Enter the number of incidents currently linked to this problem as a whole number. |
| Business Impact Description | Describe the business impact, including affected users, locations, processes, customer impact, financial impact, compliance impact, or operational disruption. |
| Impact Rating | Enter the assessed impact level; allowed values: 1-Critical, 2-High, 3-Medium, 4-Low. |
| Urgency Rating | Enter the urgency level based on time sensitivity and likelihood of recurrence; allowed values: 1-Critical, 2-High, 3-Medium, 4-Low. |
| Priority | Enter the priority derived from the approved impact/urgency matrix; allowed values: P1, P2, P3, P4. |
| Risk Rating | Enter the risk rating considering likelihood and consequence of recurrence; allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low. |
| Problem Category | Enter the high-level classification using the organisation's approved ITSM category taxonomy, e.g. Application, Infrastructure, Network, Security, Data, Supplier, Process. |
| Problem Subcategory | Enter the more specific classification under the selected category, using the organisation's approved ITSM taxonomy. |
| Problem Status | Enter the current lifecycle status; allowed values: New, Under Investigation, Root Cause Identified, Known Error, Workaround Available, Resolution In Progress, Pending Change, Resolved, Closed, Cancelled. |
| RCA Required | State whether formal root-cause analysis is required; allowed values: Yes, No. Use Yes for recurring incidents, major incidents, significant business impact, or unresolved underlying cause. |
| RCA Method | Enter the root-cause analysis method used; allowed values: 5 Whys, Fishbone/Ishikawa, Fault Tree Analysis, Kepner-Tregoe, Timeline Analysis, Pareto Analysis, Vendor Analysis, Other, Not Yet Started. |
| Investigation Start Date | Enter the date root-cause investigation began in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Investigation Target Date | Enter the target date for completing investigation or RCA in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Symptoms Observed | Record observable symptoms and evidence, such as error messages, monitoring alerts, degraded performance, outage behaviour, recurrence pattern, or affected transactions. |
| Investigation Findings | Record factual findings from logs, monitoring, diagnostics, interviews, supplier analysis, configuration review, trend analysis, or testing. |
| Root Cause Identified | Enter the confirmed root cause; if not yet confirmed, enter 'Not Yet Identified' and update when evidence confirms the cause. |
| Root Cause Category | Classify the confirmed or suspected root cause; allowed values: Software Defect, Hardware Failure, Configuration Error, Capacity Issue, Network Issue, Data Issue, Security Control Failure, Human Error, Process Failure, Supplier Failure, Environmental Issue, Unknown, Other. |
| Known Error Record ID | Enter the linked known error record identifier if the root cause is known but not yet permanently resolved; enter 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Known Error Status | Enter the known error status; allowed values: Not Applicable, Proposed, Registered, Published, Under Review, Retired. |
| Workaround Available | State whether an approved workaround exists; allowed values: Yes, No, Under Development, Not Applicable. |
| Workaround Description | Describe the approved workaround, including steps, limitations, risks, expiry conditions, and when it should be used; enter 'N/A' if none. |
| Workaround Published To | Record where the workaround has been communicated or published; allowed values or references may include Service Desk Knowledge Base, User Advisory, Operations Runbook, Supplier Portal, Not Published, N/A. |
| Permanent Resolution Required | State whether a permanent fix is required to remove the root cause; allowed values: Yes, No, To Be Determined. |
| Permanent Resolution Description | Describe the proposed or implemented permanent resolution, including design, configuration, code, process, capacity, supplier, or control changes. |
| Corrective Action Owner | Enter the named person, team, or supplier accountable for delivering the corrective action or permanent fix. |
| Corrective Action Due Date | Enter the agreed due date for the corrective action in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Corrective Action Status | Enter the implementation status of corrective actions; allowed values: Not Started, In Progress, Pending Approval, Pending Change, Implemented, Verified, Overdue, Cancelled. |
| Related Change Request ID | Enter the change request, release, deployment, or project reference used to implement the resolution; enter 'N/A' if no change is required. |
| Change Implementation Date | Enter the date the related change or fix was implemented in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter 'N/A' if not yet implemented or not applicable. |
| Resolution Verification Method | Describe how the organisation confirmed the root cause was removed or recurrence reduced, e.g. monitoring period, test results, incident trend review, user validation, supplier confirmation. |
| Resolution Verified By | Enter the name and role of the person who verified the resolution outcome. |
| Resolution Verification Date | Enter the date verification was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Residual Risk Accepted | State whether any remaining risk was formally accepted; allowed values: Yes, No, Not Applicable. |
| Residual Risk Acceptance Reference | Enter the risk acceptance, waiver, exception, or governance approval reference; enter 'N/A' if no residual risk acceptance applies. |
| Closure Summary | Summarise why the problem can be closed, including root cause, workaround status, permanent resolution, verification result, and any remaining risk. |
| Closed Date | Enter the formal closure date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until closure is approved. |
| Closure Approved By | Enter the name and role of the authorised approver for problem closure, such as Problem Manager, Service Owner, Change Authority, or Major Problem Review Chair. |
| Lessons Learned | Record lessons learned from the problem, including improvements to monitoring, design, process, knowledge articles, supplier management, testing, or controls. |
| Preventive Actions Identified | Record actions intended to prevent recurrence or reduce impact, including proactive monitoring, capacity management, process changes, training, automation, or control enhancements. |
| SLA or OLA Breach | State whether the problem caused or contributed to a service level or operational level breach; allowed values: Yes, No, Under Assessment. |
| Major Problem Review Required | State whether a formal major problem review or post-incident review is required; allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Major Problem Review Date | Enter the date of the major problem review in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter 'N/A' if not required. |
| Evidence or Attachment Links | Enter links or references to supporting evidence such as RCA document, logs, monitoring graphs, incident timeline, change records, test results, supplier report, approval record, or knowledge article. |
| COBIT Control Reference | Enter the applicable COBIT 2019 objective and practice reference; for this template use DSS03 and, where known, the specific management practice such as DSS03.01, DSS03.02, DSS03.03, DSS03.04, or DSS03.05. |
| Last Updated Date | Enter the date this record was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Updated By | Enter the name or user ID of the person who last updated the problem record. |

### Maintenance

The Problem Manager owns this template and ensures records are updated at each lifecycle event, with weekly review of open problem records and monthly quality review with service owners. The source system is the organisation's ITSM platform, drawing linked incident, change, CMDB, knowledge management, monitoring, and RCA evidence records where applicable.

COB-027.title: Continuity / Resilience Plans (IT)
COB-027.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [IT-BCP-PLAN-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Head of IT Service Continuity |

## Purpose & Objectives

This plan defines how the organisation will establish, maintain, test and improve IT continuity and resilience capabilities so that critical technology services can be recovered within agreed business tolerances following disruption.

The objectives of this plan are to:

- Identify and prioritise IT services that support critical business processes.
- Define recovery strategies for applications, infrastructure, data, networks, cloud services, end-user services and third-party technology dependencies.
- Establish documented IT continuity plans that are usable during incidents, outages, cyber events, disasters and major supplier failures.
- Align recovery capabilities with business impact analysis outcomes, agreed recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives.
- Ensure IT continuity arrangements are tested regularly through realistic exercises and technical recovery tests.
- Provide clear roles, responsibilities, escalation paths and decision-making authority during disruption.
- Maintain evidence that recovery plans, tests, lessons learned and improvement actions are managed effectively.
- Support business continuity, crisis management, disaster recovery and cyber incident response activities through coordinated IT recovery planning.
- Improve resilience by reducing single points of failure and strengthening preventive, detective and recovery controls.

This plan applies to the implementation and ongoing management of IT continuity and resilience planning. It is intended for IT leadership, service owners, infrastructure and application teams, information security, risk management, business continuity, crisis management, procurement, supplier management and audit stakeholders.

## Scope

This plan covers the development, implementation, testing, maintenance and continual improvement of IT continuity and resilience plans for technology services owned, operated, supported or consumed by the organisation.

In scope:

- Critical and important IT services supporting business operations.
- Business applications, databases, middleware and integration platforms.
- Data centres, cloud platforms, hosting environments and managed service environments.
- Network services, internet connectivity, remote access and telecommunications.
- Identity and access management services required for recovery.
- Backup, replication, restoration and archival services.
- End-user computing services required to support continuity of operations.
- Security monitoring, incident response and cyber recovery capabilities.
- Technology suppliers, outsourced service providers and cloud service providers.
- Recovery runbooks, contact lists, escalation procedures and communication arrangements.
- Technical recovery testing, tabletop exercises, failover tests and post-test reviews.
- Documentation, evidence retention, metrics and management reporting.

Out of scope:

- Full enterprise business continuity planning, except where IT recovery supports business continuity requirements.
- Physical facilities recovery planning, except for technology dependencies such as data centres, server rooms, network rooms and workplace connectivity.
- Detailed crisis communications plans, except for IT-specific inputs and escalation contacts.
- Safety, emergency response and evacuation planning.
- Financial contingency planning unrelated to technology recovery.

The scope will be reviewed at least annually and whenever there are significant changes to business services, technology architecture, outsourcing arrangements, regulatory obligations or risk exposure.

## Approach / Phases

The organisation will implement IT continuity and resilience planning through the following phased approach.

### Phase 1 - Mobilise and Govern

Establish governance, sponsorship and delivery structure for IT continuity planning.

Key activities:

- Confirm executive sponsor and plan owner.
- Define governance forums for oversight of continuity planning, testing and improvement.
- Agree scope, priorities, reporting cadence and escalation thresholds.
- Identify stakeholders across IT, business continuity, information security, risk, procurement and key business areas.
- Confirm document standards, evidence requirements and repository location.
- Establish a central IT continuity plan register.
- Define criteria for classifying IT services by criticality.
- Confirm alignment with business continuity, incident management and crisis management arrangements.

Expected outputs:

- Approved implementation approach.
- Stakeholder register.
- IT continuity plan register.
- Reporting and governance schedule.
- Evidence repository structure.

### Phase 2 - Identify Critical Services and Dependencies

Identify technology services that require continuity planning and understand their dependencies.

Key activities:

- Review business impact analysis outcomes and critical business processes.
- Map critical business processes to supporting IT services.
- Identify application, infrastructure, data, network, identity, supplier and security dependencies.
- Identify single points of failure and existing resilience features.
- Confirm service ownership and technical recovery ownership.
- Validate dependency information with service owners and technical teams.
- Prioritise services for recovery planning based on business criticality and risk exposure.

Expected outputs:

- Critical IT service inventory.
- Service-to-business process mapping.
- Dependency maps for critical services.
- Prioritised recovery planning list.
- Initial resilience risk log.

### Phase 3 - Define Recovery Requirements

Translate business needs into practical IT recovery requirements.

Key activities:

- Confirm recovery time objectives for each critical IT service.
- Confirm recovery point objectives for systems and data stores.
- Identify minimum service levels required during recovery.
- Identify maximum tolerable outage thresholds and escalation points.
- Define recovery sequence and interdependencies between systems.
- Identify manual workarounds or interim operating modes where available.
- Confirm regulatory, contractual, customer and internal commitments affecting recovery.
- Assess current recovery capabilities against required objectives.

Expected outputs:

- Recovery requirements matrix.
- Service recovery priority model.
- Gap assessment between required and current recovery capability.
- Initial remediation recommendations.

Example recovery requirements matrix:

| IT Service | Business Process Supported | Criticality | Recovery Time Objective | Recovery Point Objective | Minimum Recovery Capability | Service Owner |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| [Core ERP Platform] | Finance, procurement, inventory | Critical | [4 hours] | [1 hour] | Core transaction processing and reporting | [Service Owner] |
| [Customer Portal] | Customer self-service | High | [8 hours] | [2 hours] | Login, account view, service requests | [Service Owner] |
| [Identity Platform] | Enterprise authentication | Critical | [2 hours] | [30 minutes] | Authentication for priority applications | [Service Owner] |
| [Email and Collaboration] | Internal and external communications | High | [12 hours] | [4 hours] | Executive and incident team communications | [Service Owner] |
| [Security Monitoring Platform] | Threat detection and response | Critical | [4 hours] | [1 hour] | Alert intake, investigation and escalation | [Service Owner] |

### Phase 4 - Design Recovery Strategies

Define appropriate recovery strategies for critical IT services based on approved recovery requirements, risk appetite and available resources.

Key activities:

- Determine recovery strategies for each critical service, including failover, restoration, rebuild, replacement, manual workaround or supplier-led recovery.
- Confirm backup, replication, restoration and retention arrangements.
- Define requirements for alternate processing sites, cloud regions, availability zones or recovery environments.
- Confirm capacity requirements for recovery operations.
- Identify required recovery tooling, access permissions and administrative procedures.
- Define cyber recovery considerations, including clean restoration, isolation, malware scanning and credential reset.
- Confirm communication methods if primary collaboration tools are unavailable.
- Identify required supplier commitments and escalation contacts.
- Document accepted risks where recovery objectives cannot currently be met.
- Define remediation actions for material gaps.

Expected outputs:

- Approved recovery strategy for each critical IT service.
- Backup and restoration strategy alignment.
- Cyber recovery considerations.
- Supplier recovery dependency assessment.
- Resilience risk treatment plan.

Recovery strategy options may include:

| Strategy Type | Description | Typical Use Case | Key Considerations |
|---|---|---|---|
| High availability | Redundant components provide near-continuous service. | Identity, network, security monitoring, core platforms | Cost, complexity, monitoring, failover validation |
| Active/passive failover | Standby environment is activated during disruption. | Business-critical applications | Replication lag, activation procedures, licensing |
| Backup restoration | Service is rebuilt or restored from backup. | Lower-criticality systems or data recovery | Restore time, backup integrity, storage capacity |
| Rebuild from infrastructure templates | Systems are redeployed using standard images or automation. | Cloud workloads, standard platforms | Configuration accuracy, dependency sequencing |
| Supplier-managed recovery | Third party executes agreed recovery arrangements. | SaaS, outsourced hosting, managed services | Contractual clarity, test evidence, escalation |
| Manual workaround | Business continues using non-system processes temporarily. | Short-term operational continuity | Data reconciliation, error risk, process ownership |
| Cyber recovery environment | Isolated recovery environment used following compromise. | Ransomware or destructive attack scenarios | Clean backups, privileged access, forensics coordination |

### Phase 5 - Develop IT Continuity Plans and Runbooks

Create practical, role-based plans and recovery runbooks for use during disruption.

Key activities:

- Develop an overarching IT continuity plan describing governance, activation, escalation and coordination.
- Develop service-specific recovery runbooks for critical IT services.
- Define activation criteria and decision authority.
- Document recovery steps in the correct technical sequence.
- Include dependency checks, validation steps and rollback considerations.
- Include communication protocols, contact lists and escalation paths.
- Document supplier engagement steps and contractual support details.
- Define evidence to be captured during recovery execution.
- Confirm emergency access procedures and segregation of duties considerations.
- Validate plans with service owners, technical teams, information security and business continuity stakeholders.
- Store plans in accessible repositories, including offline or out-of-band access where appropriate.

Expected outputs:

- Approved IT continuity plan.
- Service-specific recovery runbooks.
- Contact and escalation directory.
- Recovery checklist templates.
- Plan validation records.

Minimum contents for each service recovery runbook:

| Section | Required Content |
|---|---|
| Service overview | Purpose, business owner, service owner, technical owner and criticality |
| Recovery objectives | Agreed recovery time, data loss tolerance and minimum operating capability |
| Dependencies | Applications, databases, infrastructure, network, identity, suppliers and data feeds |
| Activation criteria | Conditions under which the runbook is invoked |
| Roles and contacts | Primary and alternate contacts, escalation points and supplier contacts |
| Preconditions | Access, tools, backups, environments and approvals required |
| Recovery steps | Ordered technical steps to restore or fail over service |
| Validation steps | Checks to confirm service availability, data integrity and security status |
| Communications | Required updates to incident command, service desk, business owners and users |
| Fallback approach | Actions if primary recovery fails |
| Evidence required | Logs, screenshots, timestamps, decisions and approvals |
| Post-recovery actions | Monitoring, reconciliation, problem records and lessons learned |

### Phase 6 - Implement Resilience Improvements

Address gaps that prevent recovery objectives from being met or that create unacceptable operational risk.

Key activities:

- Prioritise resilience gaps based on business impact, likelihood and recovery requirement shortfall.
- Create remediation actions with accountable owners and due dates.
- Implement improvements such as redundancy, automated deployment, improved backup coverage, enhanced monitoring or supplier contract updates.
- Update architecture, configuration and operational documentation.
- Validate changes through testing or assurance activities.
- Track risk acceptance for gaps that cannot be remediated within agreed timeframes.
- Report progress to IT governance and risk oversight forums.

Expected outputs:

- Approved resilience improvement backlog.
- Funded remediation plan.
- Updated risk register entries.
- Evidence of completed improvements.
- Revised recovery plans and runbooks.

Example resilience improvement backlog:

| Gap ID | Gap Description | Affected Service | Risk Rating | Required Action | Owner | Target Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [GAP-001] | Backup restore time exceeds business tolerance. | [Core ERP Platform] | High | Implement storage replication and quarterly restore testing. | Infrastructure Manager | [Date] | Open |
| [GAP-002] | Supplier recovery commitment not contractually defined. | [Customer Portal Hosting] | Medium | Update contract to include recovery commitments and test evidence. | Supplier Manager | [Date] | In Progress |
| [GAP-003] | Recovery runbook lacks database validation steps. | [Data Warehouse] | Medium | Update runbook and complete technical walkthrough. | Data Platform Lead | [Date] | Open |

### Phase 7 - Test and Exercise

Test plans and technical recovery capabilities to confirm they are effective, understood and achievable.

Key activities:

- Develop an annual IT continuity test schedule.
- Select test types appropriate to service criticality and risk.
- Conduct tabletop exercises for decision-making, communication and coordination.
- Conduct technical recovery tests for backup restoration, failover, rebuild and supplier recovery where practical.
- Include cyber recovery scenarios, including ransomware, data corruption and credential compromise.
- Test emergency communications and out-of-band coordination methods.
- Include business representatives to validate minimum service capability where appropriate.
- Record actual recovery times, data recovery results, issues, decisions and deviations.
- Complete post-test reviews and assign improvement actions.
- Retain test evidence and management sign-off.

Expected outputs:

- Annual IT continuity test schedule.
- Test plans and scripts.
- Exercise attendance records.
- Test results and evidence.
- Lessons learned report.
- Corrective action plan.

Test types:

| Test Type | Purpose | Frequency Guidance | Typical Participants |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plan walkthrough | Confirm plan completeness and understanding. | At least annually for each critical service | Service owner, technical owner, business continuity, security |
| Tabletop exercise | Test decision-making, escalation and coordination. | At least annually for critical services and major scenarios | IT leadership, incident management, business representatives |
| Backup restore test | Confirm data can be restored within expectations. | Based on criticality, at least annually for critical systems | Infrastructure, database, application teams |
| Failover test | Confirm alternate processing capability works. | Based on risk and technical feasibility | Infrastructure, application, network, supplier teams |
| Cyber recovery exercise | Test recovery from malicious disruption or data corruption. | At least annually for high-risk services | Security, IT operations, legal, communications, business continuity |
| Supplier recovery validation | Confirm supplier recovery arrangements and evidence. | At least annually for critical suppliers | Supplier manager, service owner, supplier representative |

Minimum test record fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Test ID | Unique identifier for the test or exercise |
| Service or scenario tested | IT service, platform or scenario covered |
| Test type | Walkthrough, tabletop, restore, failover, cyber recovery or supplier validation |
| Date and duration | Start time, end time and elapsed time |
| Participants | Names or roles of attendees |
| Objectives | What the test intended to prove |
| Preconditions | Assumptions, environment, data and access requirements |
| Steps performed | Summary of actions taken |
| Results | Pass, partial pass or fail with explanation |
| Actual recovery time | Time required to restore minimum service capability |
| Actual data recovery point | Point to which data was restored |
| Issues identified | Defects, delays, gaps or failed assumptions |
| Decisions made | Key decisions and approvals during the test |
| Evidence retained | Logs, screenshots, tickets, reports and communications |
| Action items | Assigned corrective actions with owners and dates |
| Approval | Service owner and plan owner sign-off |

### Phase 8 - Maintain, Monitor and Improve

Ensure IT continuity plans remain accurate, tested and aligned with business and technology change.

Key activities:

- Review plans and runbooks on a defined schedule.
- Update plans following major incidents, exercises, system changes, supplier changes or business priority changes.
- Monitor completion of test schedules and corrective actions.
- Track recovery capability against agreed objectives.
- Maintain contact lists, escalation paths and supplier details.
- Verify that new or changed critical services include recovery planning before production release.
- Include continuity considerations in architecture, procurement, change and project delivery processes.
- Report key metrics and unresolved risks to management.
- Conduct periodic independent assurance or internal review.
- Retire obsolete plans when services are decommissioned.

Expected outputs:

- Updated plans and runbooks.
- Current plan register.
- Action tracking reports.
- Management performance reporting.
- Evidence of periodic review and approval.
- Continual improvement backlog.

| Security incident affecting recovery confidence | Review backup integrity, privileged access, recovery environment and clean restoration procedures. | CISO | As soon as practicable |
| Regulatory, contractual or customer commitment change | Assess impact on recovery requirements and reporting obligations. | Legal / Risk Manager | Within [30 days] of identification |
| Organisational restructure | Update ownership, escalation paths and contact information. | Head of IT Service Continuity | Within [30 days] |
| Contact list change | Update plan contacts and emergency communication records. | Service Desk Manager | Within [5 business days] |
| Audit or assurance finding | Update plan, controls, evidence or corrective actions as required. | IT Governance Manager | Based on agreed action due date |
| Service decommissioning | Retire related recovery runbooks and update plan register. | Service Owner | At decommissioning |

Plan maintenance requirements:

- The master copy of this plan must be stored in the approved document repository with version control.
- Service recovery runbooks must be accessible during outages, including through approved offline or alternate access methods.
- Changes to this plan must be reviewed by the Head of IT Service Continuity and approved by the CIO or delegated authority.
- Material changes to recovery objectives, recovery strategies or accepted risks must be reviewed through the appropriate governance forum.
- Superseded versions must be retained according to the organisation’s records retention requirements.
- Evidence of reviews, approvals, tests and updates must be retained for audit and assurance purposes.

COB-028.title: Security Operations Records
COB-028.content:
## What This Evidences

Security Operations Records evidence that the organisation is operating security monitoring, detection, response, malware protection, intrusion detection, and vulnerability management activities in support of COBIT 2019 DSS05. They demonstrate that security events are identified, analysed, escalated, and resolved; that endpoint and network protection tools are functioning; and that vulnerability scanning results are reviewed and actioned.

This artifact is **collected, not authored**. Do not create a narrative document as evidence. Export or capture operational records directly from the organisation’s security tools, log platforms, ticketing system, dashboards, or managed security service portal.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect records from the systems that operate or aggregate security monitoring, such as:

- SIEM or log management platform: [SIEM / Log Platform Name]
- Security orchestration or case management system: [SOAR / Case Tool Name]
- ITSM or incident ticketing system: [ITSM Tool Name]
- Vulnerability scanner: [Vulnerability Scanner Name]
- Endpoint protection / EDR / antivirus console: [EDR / AV Tool Name]
- IDS / IPS / NDR platform: [IDS / IPS / NDR Tool Name]
- Managed SOC / MSSP customer portal: [MSSP Portal Name]
- Cloud security monitoring tools: [Cloud Security Tool Name]
- Email security gateway: [Email Security Tool Name], where relevant

## How To Collect

1. Define the evidence period, for example [Start Date] to [End Date].
2. Log in to [SIEM / Log Platform Name] with an account that has read-only reporting access.
3. Export SOC alert records for the evidence period, including opened, investigated, escalated, and closed alerts.
4. Filter for significant alert types, such as malware, suspicious authentication, privilege misuse, data exfiltration indicators, IDS/IPS events, and high-risk detections.
5. Export associated incident or case records from [ITSM Tool Name] or [SOAR / Case Tool Name].
6. Export vulnerability scan summaries and detailed findings from [Vulnerability Scanner Name], including remediation status.
7. Export endpoint security / antivirus status from [EDR / AV Tool Name], including detections, quarantine actions, unresolved devices, and signature or sensor health.
8. Export IDS/IPS or network detection event summaries from [IDS / IPS / NDR Tool Name].
9. Save exports in non-editable format where possible, such as PDF or CSV with checksum, and include screenshots of dashboards showing date filters and system name.
10. Store all files in the approved evidence repository: [Evidence Repository Path].

## What To Capture

Capture enough detail to prove the activity occurred and was managed. Include:

- System or tool name and environment
- Evidence period and export timestamp
- Alert or event ID
- Date and time detected
- Severity or priority
- Asset, user, IP address, hostname, or application affected
- Event type or detection rule
- Alert status: open, triaged, escalated, contained, resolved, closed
- Analyst or owner assigned
- Investigation notes or case reference
- Response action taken
- Closure date and closure rationale
- Vulnerability scan date and scan scope
- Vulnerability severity, affected asset, and remediation status
- Endpoint protection status, malware detections, quarantine actions, and device coverage
- IDS/IPS detection summaries and blocked or allowed actions
- Dashboard screenshots showing filters, totals, and source system identity

## Frequency & Owner

- Collection frequency: Monthly, or quarterly where risk and audit requirements permit.
- Event-based collection: Immediately after major security incidents, critical vulnerabilities, malware outbreaks, or significant IDS/IPS alerts.
- Owner: Security Operations Manager or SOC Lead.
- Supporting owners: Vulnerability Management Lead, Endpoint Security Administrator, Network Security Engineer, and ITSM Administrator.

## Retention & Storage

Store records in [Evidence Repository Path] with restricted access for Security, Risk, Compliance, and Internal Audit personnel only. Retain records for [Retention Period], or longer where required for legal, contractual, insurance, or regulatory purposes.

Use a clear naming convention, for example:

- `Security-Operations-Records_[Tool]_[Period]_[ExportDate]`
- `SOC-Alerts_[SIEM]_[YYYY-MM]`
- `Vulnerability-Scan-Results_[Scanner]_[YYYY-MM]`

Protect evidence from alteration. Where possible, preserve original exports, audit timestamps, and hash values.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence if it:

- Comes directly from operational security systems, not from a manually written summary
- Covers the agreed evidence period
- Shows the source system name, date filters, and export timestamp
- Includes SOC alerts, vulnerability scan results, endpoint protection records, and IDS/IPS or equivalent detection evidence
- Shows alert handling status, ownership, actions taken, and closure outcomes
- Demonstrates that high-risk events and vulnerabilities were reviewed and tracked to resolution or accepted risk
- Is complete, readable, and stored in an access-controlled evidence repository
- Can be reconciled to incident tickets, change records, or remediation tasks where applicable

COB-029.title: Business Process Controls Evidence
COB-029.content:
## What This Evidences

Business Process Controls Evidence demonstrates that controls embedded in business processes are operating as intended. For COBIT 2019 DSS06, this evidence supports the management of business process controls by showing that key controls such as approvals, reconciliations, exception handling, segregation of duties, data validation, and transaction monitoring are configured, executed, reviewed, and followed up.

This artifact is **collected, not authored**. Do not create a narrative document as evidence. Collect actual operational records from the organisation’s own systems showing that business process controls ran in the normal course of operations.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect evidence from the systems where business processes and control activities are executed or monitored. Typical sources include:

- ERP or finance system: [ERP/Finance System Name]
- CRM or order management platform: [CRM/Order Platform Name]
- Procurement or supplier portal: [Procurement System Name]
- HR/payroll system: [HR/Payroll System Name]
- Workflow or approval platform: [Workflow Tool Name]
- ITSM/ticketing tool for control exceptions: [ITSM Tool Name]
- GRC or compliance monitoring tool: [GRC Tool Name]
- BI/dashboard/reporting platform: [Reporting Tool Name]
- SIEM/log store for system-based control activity: [SIEM/Log Platform Name]

Use the system of record for the process being tested. If dashboards are used, ensure the dashboard data can be traced back to underlying transactions or logs.

## How To Collect

1. Identify the business process being evidenced, such as purchase-to-pay, order-to-cash, payroll, inventory, or user access approval.
2. Identify the embedded controls in that process, such as mandatory approvals, tolerance checks, duplicate detection, reconciliations, exception queues, or restricted role execution.
3. Log in to [System Name] using an account with read-only reporting or audit access.
4. Select the relevant reporting period: [Start Date] to [End Date].
5. Run the standard control report, audit log, workflow history, exception report, or dashboard extract for the selected control.
6. Export the report in a non-editable or traceable format where possible, such as PDF, CSV with system metadata, or native audit export.
7. Capture screenshots showing report filters, date range, system name, and execution timestamp.
8. For sampled transactions, open the transaction record and capture the control trail showing approvals, validations, exceptions, or reconciliations.
9. If exceptions exist, collect related remediation tickets from [ITSM/GRC Tool Name] showing ownership, action taken, and closure.
10. Store the evidence package in the approved evidence repository using the naming convention: `[Process]_[Control]_[Period]_[System]_[ExportDate]`.

## What To Capture

Capture enough information to prove the control operated. Include:

- Process name and control name or description
- Source system name: [System Name]
- Report name, dashboard name, or log source
- Reporting period and filters applied
- Date and time the report was generated
- User or role generating the report
- Transaction IDs, request IDs, invoice IDs, order IDs, employee IDs, or workflow IDs
- Approval history, including approver, date/time, decision, and comments where applicable
- Control status, such as passed, failed, pending, rejected, overridden, or exception
- Exception details and ageing
- Evidence of follow-up or remediation for failed controls
- Reconciliation results, including matched/unmatched items and reviewer sign-off
- Screenshot of system header or metadata proving the source
- Exported report file and, where applicable, underlying sample records

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Collect monthly for high-volume operational controls, quarterly for management review controls, and per audit request for sample-based testing.
- **Owner:** The business process owner, such as [Finance Process Owner], [Procurement Lead], [HR Operations Manager], or [Sales Operations Manager].
- **Support:** System owner, application administrator, GRC team, internal audit, or data/reporting team as needed.

## Retention & Storage

Store evidence in [Evidence Repository Name] or [GRC Tool Name] with restricted access and version control. Retain according to the organisation’s audit and records retention schedule, typically [Retention Period], unless legal, regulatory, contractual, or investigation requirements require longer retention.

Maintain the original export where possible. Do not edit source evidence. If transformation is required for readability, retain both the raw export and the formatted working copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence when it:

- Comes directly from the relevant system of record
- Clearly shows the process, control activity, date range, and source system
- Includes transaction-level or workflow-level detail, not only a summary statement
- Demonstrates that the control operated during the review period
- Shows who performed, approved, reviewed, or remediated the activity
- Includes exceptions and their resolution where applicable
- Is complete, readable, time-bound, and traceable to the source system
- Is retained in an approved repository with appropriate access controls
- Has not been manually fabricated or recreated outside the operational system

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Report ID | Enter the unique identifier for this performance and conformance report, using format PCR-YYYY-NNN, e.g., PCR-2026-001. |
| Reporting Period | Enter the period covered by the report in YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Report Date | Enter the date the report is issued to the governance body in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Governance Body | Enter the name of the governance forum receiving the report, e.g., Board Risk Committee, IT Steering Committee, Audit Committee. |
| COBIT 2019 Objective Reference | Enter the COBIT 2019 objective being monitored, normally MEA01 for this report; if reporting supporting objectives, use format APOxx, BAIxx, DSSxx, MEAxx. |
| Enterprise Goal / Alignment Goal Reference | Enter the relevant COBIT enterprise goal or alignment goal reference linked to the measure, e.g., EG01, EG06, AG05, AG07, or the organisation’s approved equivalent reference. |
| Performance or Conformance Area | Enter the monitored area, using a specific description such as Service Performance, Project Delivery, Control Compliance, Policy Conformance, Risk Treatment, SLA Achievement, Audit Finding Closure, Regulatory Compliance. |
| KPI/KGI/Conformance Indicator Name | Enter the exact name of the metric, goal indicator, or conformance indicator being reported. |
| Indicator Definition | Define precisely how the indicator is calculated, including numerator, denominator, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and measurement scope. |
| Target / Threshold | Enter the approved target, tolerance, or threshold, including comparator and unit, e.g., >=98%, <=5 open high-risk exceptions, 100% completed by due date. |
| Actual Result | Enter the measured result for the reporting period using the same unit and basis as the target. |
| Unit of Measure | Enter the unit used for the target and actual result, e.g., %, count, days, hours, currency, RTO/RPO, maturity/capability rating. |
| Variance from Target | Enter the difference between actual and target, including direction and unit, e.g., -3%, +4 days, 2 exceptions above threshold. |
| Trend vs Previous Period | Enter one of: Improving, Stable, Deteriorating, New Measure, Not Available; base this on comparison with the immediately prior reporting period. |
| RAG Status | Enter one of: Green, Amber, Red; Green = within target, Amber = within tolerance or emerging concern, Red = outside tolerance or requires governance attention. |
| Data Source / System of Record | Enter the authoritative source used to produce the result, e.g., GRC tool, ITSM platform, SIEM, project portfolio tool, ERP, risk register, audit management system. |
| Data Extraction Date | Enter the date the data was extracted or refreshed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Data Owner | Enter the role or named owner accountable for the accuracy and completeness of the source data. |
| Result Owner | Enter the executive, process owner, service owner, or control owner accountable for performance or conformance against the target. |
| Root Cause / Commentary | Enter concise analysis explaining the result, especially for Amber or Red status; include known drivers, constraints, or assumptions. |
| Impact on Objectives or Risk | Enter the business, governance, risk, compliance, service, financial, or stakeholder impact of the reported result. |
| Exception / Non-Conformance Reference | Enter the linked exception, issue, risk, audit finding, incident, or non-conformance ID; enter N/A if none exists. |
| Corrective Action Required | Enter Yes or No; select Yes where the result is Amber/Red, outside target, or requires a management action to restore performance or conformance. |
| Corrective Action Owner | Enter the role or named person accountable for completing the corrective action; enter N/A if no corrective action is required. |
| Target Remediation Date | Enter the committed completion date for corrective action in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no corrective action is required. |
| Management Response / Recommendation | Enter management’s proposed response, recommendation, or action plan for governance consideration. |
| Governance Decision / Direction | Record the decision or direction given by the governance body, e.g., Accepted, Further analysis requested, Escalated, Additional funding approved, Risk accepted, Action plan rejected. |
| Escalation Required | Enter Yes or No; Yes means the matter must be escalated to a higher governance body, risk committee, audit committee, or executive owner. |
| Approval Status | Enter one of: Draft, Submitted, Reviewed, Approved, Rejected, Deferred. |
| Approved By | Enter the name and role of the person or governance chair approving the report; enter N/A until approved. |
| Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A until approved. |

### Maintenance

The template is owned by the Governance, Risk and Compliance Manager or MEA01 process owner, with inputs from process owners, service owners and control owners. It is updated each reporting cycle, typically monthly or quarterly, using approved source systems such as the GRC platform, ITSM tool, risk register, audit management system, project portfolio tool and operational performance dashboards.

COB-031.title: Internal Control Self-Assessment Report
COB-031.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | Head of Governance, Risk and Compliance | [Effective Date] | COBIT 2019 | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This Internal Control Self-Assessment Report presents the results of management’s assessment of the organisation’s internal control system for information and technology governance and management.

The report is intended to:

- Provide leadership with a clear view of the design and operating effectiveness of selected internal controls.
- Identify control weaknesses, improvement opportunities and emerging risk themes.
- Support informed decision-making on remediation priorities, investment and accountability.
- Provide evidence that control performance is being monitored, evaluated and improved.
- Support internal audit, external assurance, risk oversight and governance reporting activities.

This report is based on self-assessment performed by control owners, validated through review of supporting evidence and management challenge where required. It does not replace independent audit; however, it provides a structured management view of control health and control maturity.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Assessment period | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Fieldwork period | [Fieldwork Start Date] to [Fieldwork End Date] |
| Report date | [Report Date] |
| Assessment cycle | Quarterly / Semi-Annual / Annual |
| Previous assessment date | [Previous Assessment Date] |

### In-Scope Areas

The assessment covered internal controls supporting governance, risk management, security, service delivery, technology operations and compliance across the following areas:

| Area | In-Scope Activities |
|---|---|
| Governance and oversight | Decision rights, management review, reporting, escalation and accountability |
| Risk management | Identification, assessment, treatment, monitoring and acceptance of information and technology risks |
| Policy and standards | Approval, communication, review and adherence to internal requirements |
| Identity and access management | User access provisioning, modification, removal, privileged access and periodic access review |
| Change management | Change request approval, testing, implementation, emergency change handling and post-implementation review |
| Incident and problem management | Incident logging, classification, response, escalation, root cause analysis and corrective action |
| Service continuity | Backup, recovery, continuity planning, recovery testing and lessons learned |
| Third-party management | Supplier due diligence, contract controls, performance monitoring and risk reviews |
| Asset and configuration management | Asset ownership, inventory accuracy, configuration records and lifecycle management |
| Security operations | Vulnerability management, monitoring, logging, alert handling and security event response |
| Data protection | Data classification, handling, retention, disposal and privacy-related safeguards |
| Compliance monitoring | Regulatory, contractual and internal compliance obligations relevant to information and technology |

### In-Scope Business Units and Locations

| Business Unit / Function | Location / Region | Scope Inclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Information Technology | [Location/Region] | Included |
| Information Security | [Location/Region] | Included |
| Risk and Compliance | [Location/Region] | Included |
| Operations | [Location/Region] | Included |
| Finance Systems Support | [Location/Region] | Included |
| Human Resources Systems Support | [Location/Region] | Included |
| [Additional Business Unit] | [Location/Region] | Included |

### In-Scope Systems and Services

| System / Service | Business Owner | Technology Owner | Criticality |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Core Business Application] | [Owner] | [Owner] | High |
| [Identity Platform] | [Owner] | [Owner] | High |
| [Enterprise Resource Planning System] | [Owner] | [Owner] | High |
| [Customer Relationship Management System] | [Owner] | [Owner] | Medium |
| [Endpoint Management Platform] | [Owner] | [Owner] | Medium |
| [Security Monitoring Platform] | [Owner] | [Owner] | High |
| [Cloud Service / Platform] | [Owner] | [Owner] | High |

### Out-of-Scope Items

The following were excluded from this assessment:

- Newly implemented systems not yet operating for a full assessment cycle.
- Controls operated solely by external service providers where current assurance reports were not available during fieldwork.
- Projects in design or pre-production phase.
- Technical penetration testing and red-team activities.
- Independent audit testing.

Out-of-scope items may be included in future self-assessment cycles or reviewed separately based on risk.

### Assessment Rating Definitions

| Rating | Definition |
|---|---|
| Effective | Control is appropriately designed, consistently performed and supported by sufficient evidence. |
| Mostly Effective | Control is generally designed and operating as intended, with minor gaps that do not materially increase risk. |
| Partially Effective | Control exists but is inconsistently performed, inadequately evidenced or has design weaknesses requiring remediation. |
| Ineffective | Control is absent, poorly designed, not operating or not supported by reliable evidence. |
| Not Assessed | Control was not assessed during this period due to scope limitation, timing constraint or dependency. |

### Finding Severity Definitions

| Severity | Definition | Expected Management Response |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Significant control failure exposing the organisation to material operational, financial, regulatory, security or reputational impact. | Immediate executive attention and urgent remediation plan required. |
| High | Important control weakness that could lead to significant risk exposure if not addressed promptly. | Formal action plan required with senior management oversight. |
| Medium | Control weakness that increases risk but is unlikely to cause material impact in isolation. | Action plan required with defined owner and due date. |
| Low | Minor weakness, documentation gap or improvement opportunity. | Management action or acceptance required. |
| Observation | Good practice opportunity or advisory note with no current control failure identified. | Optional improvement decision by management. |

## Executive Summary

### Overall Assessment Result

The internal control system for information and technology governance and management is assessed as **Partially Effective** for the reporting period.

The organisation has established a recognisable internal control environment, including defined policy ownership, key operational processes, risk registers, governance forums and management reporting. Several control activities are operating adequately, particularly in change approval, incident logging, backup execution and periodic governance review.

However, the assessment identified recurring weaknesses in evidence quality, consistency of control performance, access recertification discipline, third-party monitoring and formal tracking of remediation actions. These issues do not indicate a complete breakdown of internal control, but they reduce management’s ability to demonstrate reliable, repeatable and risk-based control operation.

### Summary of Results by Control Domain

| Control Domain | Overall Rating | Key Result |
|---|---|---|
| Governance and oversight | Mostly Effective | Governance forums operate regularly, but action tracking needs stronger discipline. |
| Risk management | Partially Effective | Risks are identified, but treatment plans and acceptance records are inconsistent. |
| Policy and standards | Mostly Effective | Core policies are approved and published; review evidence requires improvement. |
| Identity and access management | Partially Effective | Provisioning is controlled, but access reviews and privileged access evidence are inconsistent. |
| Change management | Mostly Effective | Standard changes are well controlled; emergency change documentation is incomplete. |
| Incident and problem management | Mostly Effective | Incident response is timely; root cause analysis is not consistently completed. |
| Service continuity | Partially Effective | Backups are performed, but recovery testing coverage is incomplete. |
| Third-party management | Partially Effective | Supplier inventory exists, but risk reviews and assurance evidence are not consistently maintained. |
| Asset and configuration management | Partially Effective | Asset records exist, but reconciliation and ownership records require improvement. |
| Security operations | Partially Effective | Vulnerability scanning and monitoring are in place; remediation timeliness requires improvement. |
| Data protection | Mostly Effective | Data handling controls exist; retention monitoring requires enhancement. |
| Compliance monitoring | Partially Effective | Compliance obligations are known, but control evidence mapping is incomplete. |

### Key Strengths

The assessment identified the following strengths:

- Executive and management forums are in place to oversee technology risk, security, service performance and major initiatives.
- Core governance documents, including policies and standards, are available to employees through approved communication channels.
- Change requests are generally logged, assessed, approved and implemented through a defined workflow.
- Incident management processes are operational, with clear escalation routes for significant technology incidents.
- Backup processes are scheduled and monitored for key systems.
- Security monitoring capabilities exist for key infrastructure and cloud platforms.
- Management demonstrates awareness of major information and technology risks.

### Key Weaknesses

The most significant weaknesses identified were:

- Periodic access reviews are not consistently completed within expected timeframes.
- Privileged access activity review is not consistently evidenced.
- Supplier risk reviews are incomplete for several important technology service providers.
- Recovery testing does not cover all high-criticality systems.
- Vulnerability remediation performance is not consistently aligned with internal target timelines.
- Control owners retain evidence in inconsistent formats and locations, reducing assurance efficiency.
- Management action tracking lacks a single authoritative view across governance forums, risk registers and audit actions.

### Overall Risk Implication

The current internal control environment provides a reasonable foundation for governance and control, but inconsistent execution and evidence discipline may expose the organisation to:

- Increased likelihood of unauthorised access or excessive user privileges.
- Delayed response to unresolved vulnerabilities.
- Reduced confidence in recovery capability for critical systems.
- Insufficient visibility over risks introduced by third-party service providers.
- Difficulty demonstrating control effectiveness to auditors, regulators, customers or executive stakeholders.
- Fragmented remediation tracking and delayed closure of known issues.

### Priority Actions

Management should prioritise the following actions during the next reporting period:

1. Establish a centralised control evidence repository with defined evidence standards.
2. Complete overdue access reviews and implement automated escalation for missed recertifications.
3. Formalise privileged access monitoring and retain review evidence.
4. Refresh the third-party technology risk register and complete supplier assurance reviews for critical vendors.
5. Expand recovery testing coverage for high-criticality systems.
6. Implement a single management action tracker covering self-assessment, audit, risk and compliance actions.
7. Strengthen vulnerability remediation reporting and exception approval.

## Methodology

### Assessment Approach

The internal control self-assessment was performed using a management-led, evidence-based approach. Control owners completed self-assessment questionnaires and provided supporting evidence for selected controls. The Governance, Risk and Compliance function reviewed submissions, challenged ratings where required and consolidated results into this report.

The assessment included the following activities:

1. Defined assessment scope, rating criteria and reporting timetable.
2. Identified relevant control owners and process owners.
3. Issued self-assessment questionnaires and evidence requests.
4. Reviewed submitted responses and supporting documentation.
5. Conducted interviews and walkthroughs with selected control owners.
6. Performed limited sample-based validation for selected high-risk controls.
7. Rated control design and operating effectiveness.
8. Identified findings, root causes, risk implications and management actions.
9. Validated draft results with accountable managers.
10. Prepared the final report for governance review and distribution.

### Limitations

The assessment was subject to the following limitations:

- The assessment relied partly on management-provided evidence.
- Testing was sample-based and does not provide absolute assurance over all transactions.
- Some evidence was not retained in central repositories and required manual retrieval.
- External supplier assurance evidence was not available for all providers during the fieldwork period.
- The assessment did not include independent technical testing, forensic review or penetration testing.
- Control effectiveness may have changed after the reporting period due to process, system or organisational changes.

#### Condition

Periodic user access reviews are defined for key applications; however, not all reviews were completed within required timeframes. For some systems, review completion evidence did not clearly show reviewer approval, exceptions identified, actions taken or date of completion.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- Access recertification reports.
- User entitlement exports.
- Manager review confirmations.

#### Root Cause

Access review responsibilities are distributed across system owners and business managers without consistent escalation when reviews are overdue. The review process is partly manual, and evidence requirements are not standardised.

## Analysis

### Control Maturity Assessment

The assessment indicates that the organisation has moved beyond ad hoc control operation in most areas and has established repeatable practices for key governance and technology controls. However, several controls remain dependent on manual effort, individual knowledge and decentralised evidence retention.

| Maturity Theme | Current State | Target State |
|---|---|---|
| Governance discipline | Governance forums exist and meet regularly. | Governance decisions, actions and outcomes are consistently tracked to closure. |
| Control ownership | Control owners are generally identified. | Ownership is formally documented, current and linked to evidence obligations. |
| Evidence quality | Evidence exists but is inconsistent across areas. | Evidence is standardised, centrally retained and reviewed periodically. |
| Risk-based prioritisation | High-risk areas are known, but prioritisation is inconsistent. | Control monitoring frequency and remediation effort are based on risk and criticality. |
| Automation | Some controls use workflow tools. | Key controls use automated reminders, reporting, escalation and exception tracking. |
| Third-party oversight | Critical suppliers are identified. | Supplier risk, assurance and performance are reviewed through a consistent lifecycle. |
| Remediation management | Actions exist in multiple trackers. | Single action register provides authoritative status and overdue reporting. |

### Recurring Themes

The following recurring themes were observed across findings:

#### 1. Evidence Discipline Requires Improvement

Several controls appear to operate in practice, but evidence is incomplete, decentralised or inconsistently retained. This creates challenges for assurance, management review and regulatory response.

Examples include:

- Access review evidence lacking sign-off or exception closure.
- Emergency changes missing post-implementation review.
- Recovery testing records missing business approval.
- Supplier reviews not stored in a central location.
- Policy review evidence not consistently retained.

#### 2. Manual Control Processes Increase Execution Risk

Manual tracking is used for several important control activities, including access recertification, supplier reviews, action tracking and recovery test scheduling. Manual processes increase the likelihood of missed deadlines, inconsistent follow-up and incomplete evidence.

#### 3. Accountability Is Not Always Clear at the Right Level

Several findings relate to unclear or distributed ownership. Asset ownership, vulnerability remediation, supplier assurance and root cause analysis all require clearer assignment of accountable owners.

#### 4. Risk Acceptance and Exception Handling Are Inconsistent

Where control activities cannot be completed within defined expectations, exception approval and risk acceptance are not always documented. This may result in risks being tolerated informally without appropriate visibility.

#### 5. Control Monitoring Is Not Yet Fully Integrated

Governance reporting, risk management, audit action tracking and compliance evidence collection operate as related but separate activities. Integration would improve management visibility and reduce duplicated effort.

| Third-party management | Partially Effective | Partially Effective | No change | Supplier criticality classification improved, but assurance coverage remains incomplete. |
| Security operations | Partially Effective | Partially Effective | No change | Vulnerability visibility improved, but remediation timeliness remains below target. |
| Compliance monitoring | Partially Effective | Partially Effective | No change | Evidence mapping remains under development. |

### Overall Conclusion

The organisation’s internal control system is functioning but requires focused improvement in execution consistency, evidence quality, accountability and remediation governance. The most urgent areas are access governance, privileged access oversight, vulnerability remediation, supplier assurance and recovery testing.

Management should treat the current assessment as a baseline for strengthening continuous control monitoring. The recommendations below are designed to reduce operational risk, improve audit readiness and enhance leadership visibility over control effectiveness.

## Recommendations & Actions

### Management Action Plan

| Priority | Recommendation | Related Findings | Accountable Owner | Target Date | Expected Outcome |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Establish a central control evidence repository with defined evidence standards. | CSA-001, CSA-002, CSA-006, CSA-010, CSA-011 | Head of GRC | [Target Date] | Evidence is complete, current, retrievable and consistently retained. |
| 2 | Implement a single management action register for all control, risk, audit and compliance actions. | CSA-008 | Head of GRC | [Target Date] | Leadership has one authoritative view of open and overdue actions. |
| 3 | Complete overdue access reviews and automate reminder and escalation workflows. | CSA-001 | Identity and Access Manager | [Target Date] | Access reviews completed on time with clear evidence of exceptions and removals. |
| 4 | Strengthen privileged access governance through central inventory, periodic review and monitoring. | CSA-002 | Infrastructure Operations Manager | [Target Date] | Privileged access is known, approved, monitored and periodically validated. |
| 5 | Complete supplier assurance reviews for all critical technology suppliers. | CSA-003 | Vendor Management Lead | [Target Date] | Critical supplier risks are reviewed and supported by current assurance evidence. |
| 6 | Expand recovery testing for high-criticality systems and standardise reporting. | CSA-004 | IT Service Continuity Manager | [Target Date] | Recovery capability is demonstrated and approved by business owners. |
| 7 | Improve vulnerability remediation governance, reporting and exception approval. | CSA-005 | Security Operations Manager | [Target Date] | Critical and high-risk vulnerabilities are remediated on time or formally accepted. |
| 8 | Embed root cause analysis and problem management for major incidents. | CSA-007 | IT Service Desk Manager | [Target Date] | Recurring incidents are reduced through corrective action. |
| 9 | Improve asset ownership completeness and integrate ownership into lifecycle processes. | CSA-009 | IT Asset Manager | [Target Date] | Asset accountability supports risk, incident and vulnerability management. |
| 10 | Develop a control evidence catalogue and map key controls to recurring evidence sources. | CSA-010 | Compliance Manager | [Target Date] | Compliance reporting is supported by repeatable evidence collection. |

### Long-Term Actions - Next 6 to 12 Months

| Management actions reported through central register | 100% |

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution List

This report is intended for the following recipients:

| Recipient / Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Board Risk Committee | Oversight of material technology and control risks. |
| Executive Committee | Awareness of key control themes, remediation priorities and resource implications. |
| Chief Information Officer | Accountability for technology control improvement. |
| Chief Information Security Officer | Accountability for security-related control improvement. |
| Chief Risk Officer | Oversight of enterprise risk implications and acceptance decisions. |
| Head of Governance, Risk and Compliance | Ownership of control monitoring and reporting process. |
| Head of IT Operations | Ownership of operational remediation actions. |
| Internal Audit | Planning input and management assurance evidence. |
| External Auditors / Assessors | Provided only where approved by authorised management. |
| Relevant Control Owners | Action ownership and remediation execution. |

### Confidentiality Requirements

This report is classified as **Confidential - Internal Use Only**.

Recipients must:

- Use the report only for governance, risk, control, compliance, audit and remediation purposes.
- Not distribute the report outside the approved distribution list without written authorisation from the report owner.
- Protect the report from unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration or deletion.
- Store the report only in approved document repositories or secure collaboration platforms.
- Avoid extracting findings into unsecured documents, emails or messaging channels.
- Ensure that any external disclosure is reviewed and approved by Legal, Risk or Compliance as appropriate.

### Handling of Sensitive Information

This report may contain sensitive information about control weaknesses, security vulnerabilities, suppliers, systems and remediation activities. Detailed evidence supporting this report must be stored separately in the approved evidence repository and made available only to authorised personnel.

Where extracts are required for audit, customer assurance, regulatory response or supplier discussion, the extract must be limited to the minimum necessary information and approved by the report owner.

| Column | What to enter |

| External Requirement Type | Select the type of external requirement: Law, Regulation, Regulatory Guidance, Industry Standard, Contractual Requirement, Licence Requirement, Court Order, Other. |
| Jurisdiction / Authority | Enter the applicable country, region, regulator, supervisory authority, standards body, or contractual counterparty, for example UK ICO, EU, SEC, ISO, Customer Name. |

| Requirement Citation / Clause | Enter the exact article, section, clause, paragraph, schedule, or control reference, for example Art. 32, Section 404,. |
| Requirement Summary | Summarise the specific obligation in plain language, limited to the requirement being mapped, not the whole law or standard. |
| Applicability to Organisation | Select one value: Applicable, Not Applicable, Partially Applicable, Under Assessment. |

| Compliance Owner | Enter the accountable business or compliance owner responsible for interpreting and ensuring compliance with the external requirement; use role name or named individual per organisational convention. |
| Control Objective | Enter the internal control objective that addresses the requirement, written as the intended compliance outcome. |

| Mapped Internal Control Name | Enter the official name of the mapped internal control from the control library. |
| Control Type | Select one value: Preventive, Detective, Corrective, Directive, Compensating. |
| Control Frequency | Select or enter the operating frequency of the control: Continuous, Per Transaction, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annual, Annual, Event-Driven, Ad Hoc. |
| Control Owner | Enter the role or named individual accountable for operation of the mapped control. |
| Control Design Status | Select one value: Designed and Documented, Designed Not Documented, Design Gap Identified, Not Designed, Not Applicable, Under Review. |
| Control Operating Status | Select one value: Operating Effectively, Operating with Exceptions, Not Operating, Not Tested, Not Yet Implemented, Not Applicable. |
| Compliance Status | Select one value: Compliant, Partially Compliant, Non-Compliant, Not Assessed, Not Applicable. |
| Evidence Required | Describe the specific evidence needed to demonstrate compliance, for example approved policy, access review report, system configuration export, incident notification record, test result. |
| Evidence Location / Link | Enter the repository path, GRC record link, document management URL, ticket ID, or evidence reference where supporting evidence is stored. |
| Last Assessment Date | Enter the date the requirement/control mapping was last assessed, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |

| Gap Description | Describe the control, evidence, design, operating, ownership, or interpretation gap preventing full compliance; enter N/A if none. |
| Risk Rating | Select the residual compliance risk rating for the requirement: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Very Low, Not Rated. |
| Remediation Action | Enter the agreed corrective action required to close the gap or improve compliance; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Action Owner | Enter the role or named individual responsible for completing the remediation action; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Target Remediation Date | Enter the committed remediation due date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Current Remediation Status | Select one value: Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Overdue, Deferred, Cancelled, N/A. |
| Exception / Waiver Reference | Enter the approved exception or waiver ID if compliance is temporarily waived or a compensating control is accepted; enter N/A if none. |
| Exception Expiry Date | Enter the expiry date of the approved exception or waiver in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if none. |

| Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not yet approved. |

Owned by the Compliance Manager or GRC function, with requirement interpretation input from Legal and control status input from control owners. Updated at least quarterly and whenever laws, regulations, standards, contracts, or internal controls change, drawing from the GRC platform, legal/regulatory obligation register, contract repository, control library, ITSM tool, and evidence repository.

COB-033.title: Independent Assurance Reports
COB-033.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | Head of Internal Audit / Assurance | [Effective Date] | COBIT 2019 | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This report presents the results of independent assurance activities performed over the organisation’s governance and management of enterprise information and technology. It is intended to provide the Board, Audit and Risk Committee, executive management, and relevant control owners with an objective view of whether selected governance practices, management processes, controls, and evidence are designed and operating effectively.

The report supports management oversight by:

- Confirming whether technology governance activities are aligned with enterprise objectives, risk appetite, and agreed performance expectations.
- Identifying control weaknesses, governance gaps, process inefficiencies, and areas of non-conformance.
- Assessing whether accountabilities, decision rights, escalation paths, metrics, and reporting mechanisms are operating as intended.
- Providing practical recommendations and agreed actions to improve control effectiveness, resilience, compliance, value delivery, and risk management.
- Supporting transparency over the status of remediation activities and management accountability.

This report is not intended to replace management’s responsibility for designing, operating, monitoring, and improving controls. Independent assurance provides an objective assessment based on evidence available during the reporting period.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Reporting period covered | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Fieldwork period | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Report issue date | [Report Date] |
| Assurance provider | [Internal Audit Function / External Audit Firm / Independent Assurance Team] |
| Report sponsor | [Audit and Risk Committee / Chief Audit Executive / Board Sponsor] |
| Management owner | [Chief Information Officer / Chief Digital Officer / Chief Technology Officer] |

### Scope of Review

The assurance engagement covered selected governance and management practices relating to information and technology, with emphasis on the reliability of governance oversight, performance reporting, risk management, control monitoring, and improvement tracking.

The review included assessment of the following areas:

| Scope Area | Included Activities | Primary Owners |
|---|---|---|
| Governance oversight | Review of technology governance forums, decision records, escalation mechanisms, and oversight reporting | Board Technology Committee, Executive Committee, CIO |
| Risk and control monitoring | Evaluation of how technology risks, control issues, incidents, and exceptions are identified, reported, tracked, and escalated | Risk Management, Technology Risk, Control Owners |
| Performance and conformance reporting | Assessment of technology metrics, dashboards, key risk indicators, control attestations, and management reporting | IT Governance Office, Enterprise PMO, Service Owners |
| Assurance coordination | Review of coordination between internal audit, external audit, compliance, risk, security, and operational assurance activities | Internal Audit, Compliance, CISO, Risk Function |
| Issue and remediation management | Testing of issue logging, ownership assignment, action planning, target dates, closure evidence, and overdue escalation | Control Owners, Risk Function, Internal Audit |
| Management accountability | Review of defined responsibilities, approvals, action ownership, and evidence of management oversight | Executive Management, Process Owners |

### In-Scope Business Units and Functions

| Business Unit / Function | Included in Review | Notes |

| Corporate IT | Yes | Core technology governance and service management activities reviewed |
