## Executive Summary

### Overall Assurance Opinion

**Overall rating: Moderate assurance**

The organisation has established core mechanisms for technology governance oversight, risk reporting, issue tracking, and assurance coordination. Governance forums operate regularly, key technology risks are reported to senior stakeholders, and management has made progress in consolidating audit and risk findings into central trackers.

However, the review identified weaknesses in the consistency, completeness, and evidential quality of assurance reporting. Several governance and control monitoring activities are reliant on manual updates, informal follow-up, and inconsistent management attestations. In particular, issue closure evidence is not always independently validated, technology risk reporting lacks consistent linkage to business impact, and assurance activities across the three lines of accountability are not fully coordinated through an integrated plan.

As a result, executive management and governing bodies may not always receive a complete and timely view of technology-related control effectiveness, risk exposure, or remediation progress.

## Methodology

### Assurance Approach

The engagement was conducted using a risk-based assurance approach aligned to recognised governance, risk, control, and audit practices. The review considered both design effectiveness and operating effectiveness.

The work was performed through:

- Review of governance and management documentation.
- Interviews with executive stakeholders, process owners, control owners, risk personnel, audit personnel, and selected business representatives.
- Walkthroughs of issue management, risk reporting, committee reporting, and assurance coordination processes.
- Sample testing of audit findings, management actions, control attestations, risk records, and governance decisions.
- Review of performance metrics, management dashboards, and escalation records.
- Comparison of observed practices against the organisation’s governance expectations, policy requirements, risk appetite, and accepted good practice.

### Testing Performed

| Test Area | Test Objective | Sample / Evidence Reviewed |
|---|---|---|
| Governance forum operation | Confirm whether oversight forums meet as scheduled, receive relevant information, and record decisions | Committee packs, agendas, minutes, attendance logs, action trackers |
| Issue management | Confirm whether findings are logged, assigned, risk-rated, tracked, escalated, and closed with adequate evidence | Audit issue log, remediation plans, closure evidence, overdue reports |
| Assurance coordination | Confirm whether assurance activities are planned and coordinated to avoid gaps or duplication | Audit plans, compliance plans, risk review schedules, management monitoring plans |
| Risk reporting | Confirm whether technology risks are reported with clear ownership, business impact, trends, and treatment status | Risk registers, executive risk reports, board packs, key risk indicators |
| Control monitoring | Confirm whether controls are periodically assessed and results are reliable | Control self-assessments, attestations, testing evidence, exception reports |
| Third-party assurance | Confirm whether supplier assurance results are reviewed and acted upon | Service review packs, supplier reports, assurance summaries, issue logs |
| Prior finding follow-up | Confirm whether previous findings were remediated and whether closure was supported by evidence | Prior reports, action closure records, validation notes |

### Rating Definitions

Findings have been rated using the following criteria:

| Rating | Definition | Management Response Expectation |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | A severe control failure or governance breakdown that creates immediate and material risk to the organisation, customers, operations, compliance posture, or strategic objectives | Immediate executive attention, urgent containment, formal recovery plan, and frequent progress reporting |
| High | A significant weakness that may materially affect risk management, control reliability, decision-making, or compliance if not remediated promptly | Management action plan required, senior owner assigned, progress tracked to completion |
| Medium | A control weakness or process gap that increases risk but is not expected to cause immediate material impact if managed appropriately | Action plan required with defined owner and target date |
| Low | A minor weakness, inconsistency, or documentation gap with limited risk impact | Remediate through routine process improvement |
| Improvement Opportunity | A recommended enhancement to improve maturity, efficiency, insight, or consistency | Management to consider and implement where beneficial |

### Evidence Reliability Considerations

The following factors were considered when evaluating evidence:

- Whether the evidence was system-generated or manually prepared.
- Whether records were complete, dated, approved, and traceable.
- Whether evidence demonstrated performance of a control rather than only intent.
- Whether management assertions were supported by independent records.
- Whether closure evidence addressed the root cause of the original issue.
- Whether reports were produced consistently over time.
- Whether metrics were defined, repeatable, and subject to quality review.

## Detailed Findings / Results (with structure)

### Finding IA-01 - Issue Closure Evidence Is Inconsistent and Not Always Independently Validated

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Rating | High |
| Area | Issue and remediation management |
| Owner | [Role / Owner] |
| Target remediation date | [Date] |
| Status | Open |

#### Condition

The review identified that issue closure evidence is not consistently retained, validated, or linked to the original finding and agreed action. In several sampled cases, issues were marked as closed based on management confirmation without sufficient evidence to demonstrate that the remediation had been fully implemented and was operating effectively.

Examples observed included:

- Closure notes stating “completed” without supporting documentation.
- Evidence showing that a document had been updated, but no evidence that the revised process had been communicated or implemented.
- Remediation actions closed without independent review by risk, compliance, internal audit, or another appropriate assurance function.
- Target dates extended multiple times without clear rationale or senior approval.
- Action descriptions that did not fully address the root cause of the original finding.

#### Criteria

Effective assurance reporting requires reliable issue lifecycle management. Findings should remain open until management can demonstrate that agreed actions have been completed and that the underlying risk has been reduced to an acceptable level. Closure should be supported by appropriate evidence and, for significant findings, independent validation.

#### Cause

The issue closure process does not define minimum evidence requirements by finding severity. Responsibilities for validating closure are not consistently documented, and the central tracker does not require mandatory evidence fields before an issue can be closed.

#### Impact

If issues are closed without sufficient validation, management and governing bodies may receive an inaccurate view of control effectiveness and residual risk. This may result in unresolved weaknesses remaining undetected, repeat findings, delayed remediation, and reduced confidence in assurance reporting.

#### Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence Item | Observation |
|---|---|
| Audit issue tracker | Closure status updated for sampled issues, but supporting evidence was inconsistent |
| Closure evidence files | Some files contained incomplete or indirect evidence |
| Management action plans | Several actions did not clearly map to root cause |
| Committee reports | Closed issue counts reported without evidence quality indicators |
| Interview records | Stakeholders confirmed closure validation practices vary by team |

#### Recommendation

Define and implement a standard issue closure and validation process. The process should include evidence standards, closure approval requirements, validation responsibilities, and escalation rules for overdue or repeatedly extended actions.

### Finding IA-02 - Assurance Activities Are Not Fully Coordinated Through an Integrated Assurance Plan

| Field | Detail |

| Rating | High |

| Owner | [Role / Owner] |

#### Condition

The organisation performs several assurance activities across internal audit, risk management, compliance, cybersecurity, technology operations, external audit, and supplier oversight. However, these activities are not consolidated into a single integrated assurance plan that maps coverage to key technology risks, critical services, regulatory obligations, and management priorities.

The review found:

- Separate assurance plans maintained by different functions.
- Limited visibility of combined assurance coverage for technology risks.
- Potential duplication of assurance work in some areas.
- Limited assurance coverage over certain third-party and cloud service risks.
- No routine executive-level view of assurance gaps, overlaps, and planned coverage.

#### Criteria

Effective governance requires coordinated assurance that provides decision-makers with a clear view of whether key risks and controls are being independently reviewed. Assurance planning should be risk-based, coordinated across functions, and periodically reviewed by senior management.

#### Cause

No single function has been assigned responsibility for maintaining an integrated assurance view across technology-related assurance activities. Existing planning cycles are function-specific and not formally aligned.

#### Impact

Without integrated assurance planning, the organisation may over-assess lower-risk areas while under-assessing material risks. This can reduce efficiency, create assurance fatigue, and leave governing bodies without a complete view of coverage.

#### Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence Item | Observation |
|---|---|
| Internal audit plan | Contains technology audit activity but not full combined assurance coverage |
| Compliance monitoring plan | Maintained separately with limited technology risk mapping |
| Cybersecurity assurance schedule | Focused on security control testing but not integrated with audit planning |
| Supplier review schedule | Incomplete mapping to criticality and risk |
| Executive reporting | Does not provide a consolidated assurance coverage map |

#### Recommendation

Establish an integrated technology assurance plan covering internal audit, risk, compliance, cybersecurity, operations, supplier assurance, and external reviews. The plan should be risk-based, approved by appropriate governance forums, and updated regularly.

#### Recommendation

Create a technology metrics catalogue that defines each metric, owner, source, calculation method, threshold, reporting frequency, intended audience, and required management action when thresholds are breached.

## Analysis

### Overall Governance and Assurance Maturity

The organisation demonstrates a developing level of maturity in independent assurance over information and technology governance. Core structures are in place, including governance forums, risk reporting, audit tracking, and management ownership of remediation actions. However, practices are not yet consistently embedded across all relevant functions and business units.

The most important maturity gaps relate to:

- Consistency of evidence standards.
- Integration of assurance planning across functions.
- Quality and actionability of executive reporting.
- Traceability between findings, risks, actions, and control improvements.
- Independent validation of remediation for higher-risk issues.
- Visibility of supplier-related assurance results.

### Root Cause Themes

The findings indicate several recurring root cause themes:

| Theme | Description | Related Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Fragmented assurance ownership | Assurance activity is performed by multiple teams without a single consolidated view | IA-02, IA-06, IA-09 |
| Inconsistent evidence standards | Control and issue records vary in quality and completeness | IA-01, IA-04, IA-08 |
| Reporting not fully decision-oriented | Reports contain information but not always clear thresholds, trends, or required decisions | IA-03, IA-05, IA-09 |
| Limited validation discipline | Some management assertions are accepted without sufficient independent review | IA-01, IA-04 |
| Distributed third-party oversight | Supplier assurance information is not consistently assessed and escalated | IA-06 |
| Process documentation gaps | Expectations are not always formalised in templates, guidance, or standard operating practices | IA-04, IA-07, IA-08 |

### Risk Implications

If the findings remain unresolved, the organisation may face the following risks:

- Inaccurate reporting of remediation progress to senior management and governing bodies.
- Continued operation of ineffective or partially remediated controls.
- Assurance gaps over material technology risks and critical services.
- Duplication of assurance work and inefficient use of specialist resources.
- Weak visibility of supplier-related control issues.
- Reduced ability to demonstrate effective oversight to regulators, external auditors, customers, or contractual counterparties.
- Repeat findings and remediation fatigue.
- Delayed management response to deteriorating risk indicators.

### Management Capability Assessment

Management has demonstrated willingness to engage with the assurance process and has provided access to relevant stakeholders and records. There is evidence of active governance and an established intent to improve assurance reporting. However, management capability would be strengthened by assigning clearer ownership for integrated assurance coordination and by formalising consistent standards across issue management, control self-assessment, risk reporting, and supplier assurance.

### Prioritisation Assessment

Remediation should be prioritised as follows:

| Priority | Focus Area | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Issue closure and validation | Prevents inaccurate reporting of risk reduction and control effectiveness |
| 2 | Integrated assurance planning | Improves coverage of key risks and reduces duplication |
| 3 | Technology risk and metrics reporting | Improves decision quality and management oversight |
| 4 | Control self-assessment evidence standards | Strengthens reliability of management assurance |
| 5 | Third-party assurance integration | Improves visibility of supplier-related risk |
| 6 | Documentation and action tracking consistency | Improves traceability and governance discipline |

### Conclusion of Analysis

The organisation’s assurance arrangements provide a foundation for effective oversight, but current practices require standardisation and integration. Addressing the high-rated findings should materially improve the reliability of management reporting and the quality of assurance provided to governing bodies.

| Compliance Officer | Compliance monitoring and regulatory alignment |
| Relevant Process and Control Owners | Implementation of agreed actions |
| External Auditors | Where approved and relevant to audit coordination |
| Regulators or Supervisory Bodies | Only where legally required or formally authorised |

Additional distribution requires approval from [Report Owner / Chief Audit Executive / General Counsel].

### Confidentiality Requirements

This report is classified as **Confidential - Internal Use Only**. It contains sensitive information regarding governance practices, control weaknesses, risk exposure, audit observations, remediation status, and third-party assurance matters.

Recipients must:

- Use the report only for authorised governance, management, audit, risk, compliance, or remediation purposes.
- Not share the report externally without prior written approval from [Authorising Role].
- Store the report only in approved repositories with appropriate access controls.
- Avoid copying report extracts into lower-classification documents unless approved.
- Protect working papers and supporting evidence in accordance with organisational information handling requirements.
- Notify [Report Owner / Information Security Contact] immediately if unauthorised disclosure is suspected.

### External Release

External release of this report, in whole or in part, must be reviewed and approved by:

| Approver | Approval Required For |
|---|---|
| [Chief Audit Executive] | Release to external auditors or assurance providers |
| [General Counsel] | Release to regulators, litigants, counterparties, or public bodies |
| [Chief Information Security Officer] | Release of security-sensitive content |
| [Executive Sponsor] | Release to strategic partners or customers where contractually required |

### Record Retention

The final report, management responses, supporting evidence, and follow-up validation records must be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements for audit and assurance material.

Minimum retention expectations:

| Record Type | Retention Requirement | Repository |
|---|---|---|
| Final assurance report | [Retention Period] | [Approved Repository] |
| Management action plan | [Retention Period] | [Approved Repository] |
| Supporting workpapers | [Retention Period] | [Approved Repository] |
| Closure validation evidence | [Retention Period] | [Approved Repository] |
| Distribution and approval records | [Retention Period] | [Approved Repository] |

| Report Prepared By | [Name / Role] | [Date] |
| Reviewed By | [Name / Role] | [Date] |
| Approved By | [Name / Role] | [Date] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Minute Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for the minutes record, using the organisation’s naming convention, e.g. GOV-MIN-YYYY-NNN. |
| Governance Body | Enter the formal name of the board, steering committee, or governance forum holding the meeting. |
| Meeting Type | Enter one allowed value: Scheduled, Extraordinary, Emergency, Workshop, Review. |
| Meeting Date | Enter the date the meeting was held in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Meeting Start Time | Enter the meeting start time in 24-hour HH:MM format, including time zone if relevant. |
| Meeting End Time | Enter the meeting end time in 24-hour HH:MM format, including time zone if relevant. |
| Meeting Location / Channel | Enter the physical location or virtual meeting platform used, e.g. Boardroom 1, Microsoft Teams, Zoom. |
| Chair | Enter the full name and role/title of the person chairing the meeting. |
| Minute Taker | Enter the full name and role/title of the person preparing the minutes. |
| Attendees Present | List all attendees present, including full name, role/title, and organisation/function represented. |
| Apologies / Absentees | List invited members not present and record whether apologies were received; enter None if not applicable. |
| Quorum Confirmed | Enter Yes or No and, where applicable, state the quorum threshold met, e.g. Yes - 5 of 7 voting members present. |
| Conflicts of Interest Declared | Record any declared conflict of interest for the agenda item, including member name and mitigation; enter None if no conflict was declared. |
| Agenda Item Number | Enter the agenda reference number, using the meeting agenda sequence, e.g. 1.0, 2.1, 3.2. |
| Agenda Item Title | Enter the concise title of the matter discussed or decision requested. |
| COBIT 2019 Governance Objective Reference | Enter the relevant COBIT 2019 governance objective reference: EDM01, EDM02, EDM03, EDM04, EDM05, or multiple references if applicable. |
| EDM Focus Area | Enter the primary governance purpose using one allowed value: Governance Framework, Benefits Delivery, Risk Optimization, Resource Optimization, Stakeholder Transparency. |
| Paper / Evidence Reference | Enter the reference ID, title, version, and date of the board paper, dashboard, business case, risk report, performance report, or other evidence reviewed. |
| Summary of Discussion | Record a factual, concise summary of key matters discussed, questions raised, challenge provided, and information considered. |
| Decision / Resolution | Record the exact decision, resolution, direction, approval, rejection, or deferral agreed by the governance body. |
| Decision Type | Enter one allowed value: Approve, Reject, Defer, Note, Endorse, Escalate, Request Information, Assign Action. |
| Decision Outcome | Enter the final outcome using one allowed value: Approved, Rejected, Deferred, Noted, Endorsed, Escalated, Action Assigned. |
| Risk / Issue Considered | Record any material risk, issue, dependency, compliance matter, or control concern considered in the discussion; enter None if not applicable. |
| Approved Resources / Budget Impact | Record any approved funding, resource allocation, budget change, or capacity impact, including amount and currency where applicable; enter None if not applicable. |
| Policy / Framework / Strategy Impact | Record any impact on governance framework, enterprise strategy, IT strategy, policies, risk appetite, principles, or delegations of authority; enter None if not applicable. |
| Accountable Owner | Enter the named executive, committee member, or role accountable for the decision or governance outcome. |
| Action Required | Describe the specific follow-up action required, using clear task wording; enter None if no action is required. |
| Action Owner | Enter the full name and role/title of the person accountable for completing the action; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Action Due Date | Enter the agreed due date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Action Status | Enter one allowed value: Not Started, In Progress, Complete, Overdue, Deferred, Cancelled, N/A. |
| Follow-up Required | Enter Yes or No; if Yes, state the meeting or date when the item must return for review. |
| Escalation Required | Enter Yes or No; if Yes, state the escalation destination, e.g. Board, Audit Committee, Risk Committee, Executive Committee. |
| Approval of Previous Minutes | Record whether previous minutes were approved, amended, or deferred, and identify the previous minute record ID. |
| Minutes Approval Status | Enter one allowed value: Draft, Reviewed, Approved, Approved with Amendments, Rejected. |
| Minutes Approved By | Enter the full name and role/title of the chair or authorised approver; enter N/A while draft. |
| Minutes Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A while draft. |
| Record Classification | Enter the information classification according to the organisation’s classification scheme, e.g. Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. |
| Retention Requirement | Enter the applicable retention period and policy reference, e.g. 7 years per Records Retention Schedule GOV-01. |
| Supporting Attachments | List filenames, document IDs, or links to supporting papers, packs, dashboards, presentations, approvals, and evidence reviewed. |
| Version | Enter the document version number using the organisation’s convention, e.g. v0.1 Draft, v1.0 Approved. |
| Prepared Date | Enter the date the minutes were prepared in YYYY-MM-DD format. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Governance Office or Company Secretariat, with input from the CIO, CRO, and committee chair. Updated for every board or steering committee meeting and maintained from the board portal, meeting pack repository, action tracker, and approved document management system.

COB-035.title: Continual Improvement Register (IT Governance)
COB-035.content:
## Continual Improvement Register (IT Governance) (XLSX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Improvement ID | Date Raised | Raised By | Source of Improvement | Source Reference | COBIT 2019 Objective | Governance/Management Area | Related Policy/Process/Control | Current Issue or Gap | Root Cause | Improvement Action | Expected Outcome | Risk or Opportunity Addressed | Priority | Impact | Effort | Action Owner | Accountable Executive | Target Start Date | Target Completion Date | Actual Start Date | Actual Completion Date | Status | RAG | Progress Commentary | Dependencies | Resources Required | Success Measure/KPI | Baseline Value | Target Value | Post-Implementation Result | Evidence Location | Validation Method | Validator | Validation Date | Closure Decision | Closure Approval By | Closure Approval Date | Lessons Learned | Next Review Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [EXAMPLE: CI-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-15] | [EXAMPLE: Internal Audit] | [EXAMPLE: Internal Audit] | [EXAMPLE: IA-2026-ITG-03] | [EXAMPLE: MEA02] | [EXAMPLE: Internal control monitoring] | [EXAMPLE: IT Control Self-Assessment Procedure] | [EXAMPLE: Control testing evidence is not consistently retained for quarterly IT governance controls.] | [EXAMPLE: Evidence retention requirements are not defined in the procedure.] | [EXAMPLE: Update the control self-assessment procedure to define mandatory evidence types, retention location, and review responsibilities.] | [EXAMPLE: Control evidence is complete, consistently retained, and available for assurance review.] | [EXAMPLE: Reduced risk of ineffective control monitoring and failed audit evidence requests.] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: Medium] | [EXAMPLE: IT Governance Manager] | [EXAMPLE: CIO] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-01] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-31] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-03] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: In Progress] | [EXAMPLE: Amber] | [EXAMPLE: Procedure update drafted; awaiting review by control owners.] | [EXAMPLE: Approval from IT Risk Committee] | [EXAMPLE: Process owner time and SharePoint repository update] | [EXAMPLE: Percentage of quarterly controls with complete evidence retained] | [EXAMPLE: 62%] | [EXAMPLE: 95%] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: SharePoint/ITGovernance/Controls/CSA/2026] | [EXAMPLE: Evidence review and sample testing] | [EXAMPLE: IT Risk Manager] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: Not Ready] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-30] |
| [EXAMPLE: CI-2026-002] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-22] | [EXAMPLE: Risk Committee] | [EXAMPLE: KPI/KRI Review] | [EXAMPLE: ITGC-KRI-Q4-2025] | [EXAMPLE: EDM03] | [EXAMPLE: Risk optimisation] | [EXAMPLE: IT Risk Reporting Standard] | [EXAMPLE: IT risk reports do not clearly show overdue treatment actions by accountable executive.] | [EXAMPLE: Reporting template does not include executive accountability or ageing thresholds.] | [EXAMPLE: Revise the IT risk dashboard to include overdue treatment actions, ageing, accountable executive, and escalation status.] | [EXAMPLE: Executive governance bodies receive transparent and actionable IT risk information.] | [EXAMPLE: Improved oversight of overdue IT risk treatment actions.] | [EXAMPLE: Medium] | [EXAMPLE: Medium] | [EXAMPLE: Low] | [EXAMPLE: Head of IT Risk] | [EXAMPLE: Chief Risk Officer] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-10] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-15] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: Approved] | [EXAMPLE: Green] | [EXAMPLE: Approved by Risk Committee; implementation scheduled for next reporting cycle.] | [EXAMPLE: GRC reporting configuration change] | [EXAMPLE: GRC analyst support] | [EXAMPLE: Number of overdue IT risk treatment actions without executive owner] | [EXAMPLE: 14] | [EXAMPLE: 0] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: GRC Platform/Risk Dashboards/IT Risk Committee] | [EXAMPLE: Dashboard review and committee confirmation] | [EXAMPLE: Enterprise Risk Manager] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: Not Ready] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-15] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Improvement ID | Enter a unique identifier for the improvement action, using a consistent format such as CI-YYYY-###. |
| Date Raised | Enter the date the improvement was identified in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Raised By | Enter the name or role of the person, committee, audit team, or governance body that raised the improvement. |
| Source of Improvement | Select the origin of the improvement: Internal Audit, External Audit, Risk Assessment, Control Testing, KPI/KRI Review, Management Review, Incident/Post-Incident Review, Regulatory Finding, COBIT Capability Assessment, Stakeholder Feedback, or Other. |
| Source Reference | Enter the reference to the originating record, such as audit finding ID, risk ID, incident ID, assessment report section, meeting minute reference, or ticket number. |
| COBIT 2019 Objective | Enter the relevant COBIT 2019 objective reference, especially EDM or MEA objectives, e.g. EDM01, EDM02, EDM03, EDM04, EDM05, MEA01, MEA02, MEA03, or MEA04. |
| Governance/Management Area | Enter the governance or management area affected, such as governance framework, benefits delivery, risk optimisation, resource optimisation, stakeholder transparency, performance monitoring, internal control, compliance, or assurance. |
| Related Policy/Process/Control | Enter the specific internal policy, process, control, standard, procedure, or framework element affected by the improvement. |
| Current Issue or Gap | Describe the current weakness, deficiency, inefficiency, nonconformity, or improvement opportunity in clear audit-ready language. |
| Root Cause | Enter the underlying cause of the issue, such as unclear ownership, missing process, inadequate control design, inconsistent execution, tooling limitation, insufficient training, resource constraint, or data quality issue. |
| Improvement Action | Describe the specific corrective or improvement action to be completed, using clear action-oriented wording. |
| Expected Outcome | Describe the intended result of the improvement, including how governance, control effectiveness, monitoring, assurance, risk reduction, transparency, or performance will improve. |
| Risk or Opportunity Addressed | Enter the associated risk, control weakness, regulatory obligation, performance issue, or improvement opportunity addressed by the action. |
| Priority | Select one value: Critical, High, Medium, Low. |
| Impact | Select one value: High, Medium, Low, based on expected governance, risk, compliance, operational, or stakeholder impact. |
| Effort | Select one value: High, Medium, Low, based on estimated implementation effort, cost, resource demand, or complexity. |
| Action Owner | Enter the named individual or role responsible for implementing the improvement action. |
| Accountable Executive | Enter the senior accountable role or governance owner responsible for ensuring the action is completed, such as CIO, CISO, Head of IT Governance, Risk Owner, or Process Owner. |
| Target Start Date | Enter the planned start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Target Completion Date | Enter the planned completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Actual Start Date | Enter the actual start date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until work has started. |
| Actual Completion Date | Enter the actual completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until fully implemented. |
| Status | Select one value: New, Approved, In Progress, On Hold, Implemented Pending Validation, Closed, Rejected, Superseded. |
| RAG | Select one value: Red, Amber, Green, based on delivery health against target date, scope, dependency, and risk. |
| Progress Commentary | Enter concise current progress notes, including key actions completed, blockers, decisions needed, or reason for delay. |
| Dependencies | Enter any dependency required to complete the action, such as another project, system change, budget approval, third-party input, policy approval, or resource availability; enter None if not applicable. |
| Resources Required | Enter required people, budget, tools, data, training, or external support needed to complete the action. |
| Success Measure/KPI | Enter the metric or test that will prove the improvement has worked, such as control pass rate, audit issue reduction, SLA achievement, assessment score, reporting timeliness, or evidence completeness. |
| Baseline Value | Enter the starting measurement before improvement, including units or percentage where applicable, e.g. 65%, 12 open findings, 10 days, or Not measured. |
| Target Value | Enter the intended target measurement after implementation, including units or percentage where applicable, e.g. 95%, 0 overdue actions, 5 days. |
| Post-Implementation Result | Enter the measured result after implementation and validation, including units or percentage; leave blank until measured. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the document repository link, GRC record, ticket reference, SharePoint path, audit evidence ID, or system location where implementation evidence is stored. |
| Validation Method | Select or describe how completion will be verified, such as control retest, management attestation, evidence review, KPI review, audit validation, walkthrough, or sample testing. |
| Validator | Enter the independent person or role that validates completion, such as IT Governance Manager, Internal Audit, Risk Manager, Control Owner, Compliance Officer, or Assurance Lead. |
| Validation Date | Enter the date validation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until validated. |
| Closure Decision | Select one value: Not Ready, Accepted and Closed, Rework Required, Risk Accepted, Cancelled, Superseded. |
| Closure Approval By | Enter the name or role approving closure of the improvement action. |
| Closure Approval Date | Enter the closure approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until closure is approved. |
| Lessons Learned | Enter any lessons learned, recurring themes, process improvements, or preventive actions identified during implementation. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format, especially where the improvement requires monitoring after closure. |

### Maintenance

The Continual Improvement Register is owned by the IT Governance Manager, with action updates provided by assigned action owners and closure validated by IT Risk, Compliance, or Internal Audit as appropriate. It is updated at least monthly and after each audit, assessment, control review, KPI/KRI review, incident review, or governance committee meeting, drawing from the GRC platform, audit management system, risk register, control testing records, incident system, and governance committee minutes.

HIPAA-001.title: HIPAA Applicability & Entity Type Determination
HIPAA-001.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-HIPAA-001] | 1.0 | Privacy Officer | [Effective Date] | HIPAA | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes the mandatory requirements for determining and documenting the organisation’s status under HIPAA as a Covered Entity, Business Associate, Hybrid Entity, or non-regulated entity for each applicable business activity, function, service, product, and legal entity.

The purpose of this Policy is to ensure that the organisation:

- Correctly identifies when HIPAA applies to its operations.
- Determines whether it acts as a Covered Entity, Business Associate, or Hybrid Entity.
- Maintains accurate records supporting entity type determinations.
- Applies appropriate privacy, security, breach notification, contractual, and governance requirements based on the organisation’s role.
- Prevents under-classification, inconsistent treatment of protected health information, and unmanaged regulatory exposure.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All workforce members, including employees, contractors, temporary staff, interns, volunteers, and other personnel acting on behalf of the organisation.
- All legal entities, business units, subsidiaries, departments, programs, services, systems, applications, and products operated by or for the organisation.
- All activities involving the creation, receipt, maintenance, transmission, use, disclosure, storage, access, or processing of health information.
- All arrangements with customers, clients, providers, payers, vendors, subcontractors, partners, affiliates, and other third parties where health information may be involved.
- All new and existing services, system implementations, product launches, acquisitions, divestitures, outsourcing arrangements, and material business changes that may affect HIPAA applicability.

This Policy applies whether information is handled in electronic, paper, verbal, image, audio, video, or any other format.

This Policy does not replace separate HIPAA Privacy, Security, Breach Notification, Sanctions, Training, Risk Management, Vendor Management, or Incident Response policies. Entity type determination under this Policy shall be used to identify which of those additional requirements apply.

## Policy Statements

1. **The organisation shall perform a formal HIPAA applicability assessment before launching, acquiring, materially changing, or contracting for any service, business function, product, system, or relationship that involves health information.**

2. **The organisation shall determine whether it is acting as a Covered Entity, Business Associate, Hybrid Entity, or non-regulated entity based on the specific activity being performed and the relationship under which health information is created, received, maintained, transmitted, used, disclosed, or processed.**

3. **The organisation shall not assume that HIPAA does or does not apply based solely on industry sector, customer type, data sensitivity, internal terminology, or the presence of medical information.**

4. **The organisation shall classify itself as a Covered Entity for a function or legal entity when it performs regulated health plan, health care clearinghouse, or health care provider activities involving standard electronic health care transactions.**

5. **The organisation shall classify itself as a Business Associate when it creates, receives, maintains, transmits, uses, discloses, or otherwise handles protected health information on behalf of a Covered Entity or another Business Associate to perform services or functions involving that information.**

6. **The organisation shall classify itself as a Hybrid Entity only when it performs both regulated and non-regulated functions, formally designates its health care components, documents the designation, and implements safeguards to prevent impermissible access, use, or disclosure between regulated and non-regulated functions.**

7. **The organisation shall identify and document each health care component within a Hybrid Entity designation, including the departments, workforce groups, systems, data repositories, processes, and third-party relationships that perform regulated functions.**

8. **The organisation shall ensure that Hybrid Entity designations are approved by the Privacy Officer, Security Officer, Legal Counsel, and executive leadership before implementation.**

9. **The organisation shall treat any ambiguity in entity type or HIPAA applicability as requiring escalation to the Privacy Officer and Legal Counsel before health information is used, disclosed, processed, or contracted for.**

10. **The organisation shall maintain a HIPAA Applicability and Entity Type Register documenting each determination, the rationale, supporting evidence, approval date, accountable owner, and review date.**

11. **The organisation shall apply the most protective applicable HIPAA obligations when a business activity involves multiple roles, mixed data flows, or uncertainty regarding whether the organisation is acting as a Covered Entity or Business Associate.**

12. **The organisation shall not use a Business Associate classification to avoid Covered Entity obligations where the organisation directly performs regulated Covered Entity functions.**

13. **The organisation shall not use a non-regulated classification where the organisation handles protected health information on behalf of a Covered Entity or Business Associate for regulated functions or services.**

14. **The organisation shall ensure that contracts, statements of work, data processing arrangements, service descriptions, and customer commitments are consistent with the approved entity type determination.**

15. **The organisation shall execute a Business Associate Agreement before creating, receiving, maintaining, transmitting, using, disclosing, or otherwise handling protected health information as a Business Associate, unless Legal Counsel documents that no such agreement is required.**

16. **The organisation shall require downstream subcontractors that handle protected health information on behalf of the organisation to enter into written agreements imposing appropriate privacy, security, breach reporting, and permitted-use requirements.**

17. **The organisation shall ensure that entity type determinations address all relevant data flows, including intake, collection, storage, access, transmission, analytics, reporting, support, backup, archival, testing, disposal, and subcontractor processing.**

18. **The organisation shall identify whether health information becomes de-identified, aggregated, limited, or otherwise transformed, and shall document whether the transformed information remains subject to HIPAA requirements.**

19. **The organisation shall ensure that de-identification determinations are approved by qualified privacy, legal, or compliance personnel before information is treated as outside HIPAA scope.**

20. **The organisation shall ensure that systems containing protected health information are identified in asset inventories, risk assessments, access control reviews, incident response plans, retention schedules, and vendor management records.**

21. **The organisation shall assign a business owner for each regulated function, service, product, or system subject to HIPAA.**

22. **The organisation shall ensure that workforce members supporting regulated functions receive HIPAA training appropriate to their role and the organisation’s approved entity type.**

23. **The organisation shall restrict access to protected health information to authorised workforce members and approved third parties with a legitimate business need aligned to the applicable entity type determination.**

24. **The organisation shall ensure that non-regulated business units do not access protected health information from regulated components unless such access is permitted, approved, documented, and controlled.**

25. **The organisation shall evaluate mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, reorganisations, new customer relationships, and new lines of business for potential changes to HIPAA applicability before operational integration.**

26. **The organisation shall reassess entity type determinations when there is a material change in services, customers, contracts, data flows, systems, third parties, legal structure, or regulatory interpretation.**

27. **The organisation shall not begin processing protected health information for a new customer, client, or partner until HIPAA applicability, entity type, contractual requirements, and security responsibilities have been determined and approved.**

28. **The organisation shall ensure that marketing, sales, product, implementation, and customer success materials do not make representations about HIPAA status, compliance, or responsibilities unless approved by Privacy, Security, and Legal.**

29. **The organisation shall retain records of entity type determinations, approvals, related contracts, and supporting evidence in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements and applicable legal obligations.**

30. **The organisation shall monitor adherence to approved entity type determinations and shall remediate misclassifications, undocumented data flows, missing agreements, or inconsistent operational practices in a timely manner.**

The following classification guide shall be used as a baseline for entity type determination. Final classification shall be based on documented facts and approved by authorised reviewers.

| Classification | Practical Indicators | Typical Examples | Required Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Covered Entity | The organisation operates a health plan, health care clearinghouse, or certain health care provider functions involving standard electronic health care transactions. | Employee health plan administration, clinical services billing electronically, claims clearinghouse activity. | Apply HIPAA obligations directly to the regulated function or entity. |
| Business Associate | The organisation handles protected health information on behalf of a Covered Entity or another Business Associate to provide services or perform functions. | Claims processing, data hosting, analytics, billing support, legal services, accounting services, consulting, secure messaging, managed IT, document storage. | Execute appropriate written agreement and apply required privacy, security, and breach responsibilities. |
| Hybrid Entity | The organisation performs both regulated and non-regulated functions and formally designates the regulated health care components. | A university with a student health clinic, an employer with a self-insured health plan, a diversified company with a regulated health services division. | Document health care components, separate regulated functions, and control access and disclosures. |
| Non-Regulated Entity or Function | The organisation does not perform regulated functions and does not handle protected health information on behalf of a regulated entity. | General wellness services without regulated transactions, employment records held by an employer, consumer services not performed for a Covered Entity. | Document rationale and reassess upon change in data use, customer type, or service model. |

The HIPAA Applicability and Entity Type Register shall include, at a minimum, the following fields.

| Field | Required Content |
|---|---|
| Business function, product, service, or legal entity | Name and description of the activity being assessed. |
| Business owner | Accountable leader responsible for the activity. |
| Data involved | Types of health information, identifiers, source systems, and data subjects. |
| Data flows | How information is collected, received, created, used, stored, transmitted, disclosed, and disposed. |
| Relationship context | Whether the activity is performed directly, for a customer, for a Covered Entity, for another Business Associate, or internally. |
| Proposed classification | Covered Entity, Business Associate, Hybrid Entity, non-regulated, or requires legal review. |
| Rationale | Facts supporting the classification decision. |
| Required agreements | Business Associate Agreement, subcontractor agreement, customer agreement, data sharing agreement, or none. |
| Required safeguards | Key privacy, security, access, training, and monitoring requirements. |
| Approvers | Privacy Officer, Security Officer, Legal Counsel, business owner, and any additional required approver. |
| Approval date | Date of final approval. |
| Review trigger | Scheduled review date and event-based review triggers. |
| Evidence location | Link or reference to supporting records in [approved repository]. |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors or Governing Body | Provide oversight of HIPAA governance and receive escalation of material compliance risks related to entity type determination. |
| Executive Leadership | Ensure sufficient authority, resources, and accountability for accurate HIPAA applicability determinations across the organisation. |
| Privacy Officer | Own this Policy; lead HIPAA applicability assessments; approve entity type determinations; maintain the entity type register; oversee privacy obligations arising from each classification. |
| Security Officer | Identify security obligations associated with regulated functions; ensure systems and data flows involving protected health information are included in security risk management, access controls, monitoring, and incident response. |
| Legal Counsel | Provide legal interpretation; review ambiguous classifications; approve contractual language; determine when agreements are required; advise on regulatory risk. |
| Compliance Officer | Monitor compliance with this Policy; coordinate audits or reviews; track remediation actions; report unresolved issues to leadership. |
| Business Owners | Identify activities that may involve health information; initiate applicability assessments; maintain accurate service descriptions and data flow information; ensure operations align with approved classifications. |
| Product and Service Owners | Build entity type review into product design, service launch, configuration, implementation, and change management processes. |
| Sales, Marketing, and Customer-Facing Teams | Obtain approval before making statements about HIPAA applicability, compliance status, Business Associate responsibilities, or permitted uses of health information. |
| Procurement and Vendor Management | Ensure third-party arrangements involving protected health information are reviewed, approved, and supported by required agreements before work begins. |
| Information Technology | Maintain inventories of systems that create, receive, maintain, or transmit protected health information; implement technical safeguards according to approved classification. |
| Human Resources | Coordinate workforce training, sanctions, role changes, and onboarding or offboarding activities for personnel supporting regulated functions. |
| Workforce Members | Follow approved classifications, use protected health information only as authorised, report suspected misclassification or improper handling, and complete required training. |
| Internal Audit or Independent Assurance Function | Periodically assess whether entity type determinations are complete, accurate, approved, and operationally implemented. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

The organisation shall monitor compliance with this Policy through governance reviews, compliance testing, internal audits, contract reviews, system inventories, data flow assessments, access reviews, and change management oversight.

At a minimum, the following monitoring activities shall be performed.

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of HIPAA Applicability and Entity Type Register for completeness and currency | Quarterly | Privacy Officer | Updated register and review notes |
| Review of new products, services, contracts, and customer implementations for HIPAA applicability | Before approval or launch | Business Owner, Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel | Completed assessment and approvals |
| Review of Business Associate Agreements and subcontractor agreements | At contract initiation and upon material change | Legal Counsel, Vendor Management | Executed agreements and contract checklist |
| Review of Hybrid Entity health care component designation, if applicable | Annually and upon organisational change | Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, Executive Leadership | Approved designation record |
| Review of systems containing protected health information against asset inventory and risk assessment records | Semi-annually | Security Officer, IT Asset Owner | System inventory, risk records, remediation actions |
| Review of workforce access to protected health information | Quarterly or risk-based | Security Officer, Business Owner | Access review attestations |
| Review of sales, marketing, and customer commitments referencing HIPAA | Risk-based and prior to publication where applicable | Legal Counsel, Privacy Officer | Approved materials |
| Internal audit of entity type determination process | At least annually or as scheduled in the audit plan | Internal Audit or Compliance | Audit report and corrective action plan |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in corrective action, contract suspension, disciplinary action, removal of access, termination of vendor relationships, customer notification where required, or other actions permitted by organisational policy and applicable law.

Examples of non-compliance include, but are not limited to:

- Processing protected health information without an approved entity type determination.
- Failing to execute required Business Associate or subcontractor agreements.
- Misrepresenting the organisation’s HIPAA role to customers, vendors, or regulators.
- Allowing non-regulated business units to access protected health information without approval.
- Treating information as de-identified without proper review and approval.
- Launching or materially changing services involving health information without privacy, security, and legal review.
- Failing to update the entity type register after organisational, contractual, or technical changes.
- Ignoring or concealing suspected misclassification or unauthorised data handling.

Material misclassification, unmanaged protected health information processing, or repeated failure to follow this Policy shall be escalated to executive leadership and, where appropriate, the governing body.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be limited, documented, risk-assessed, time-bound, and approved before the exception is implemented.

An exception shall not be used to:

- Avoid determining whether HIPAA applies.
- Bypass required legal review.
- Process protected health information without appropriate contractual safeguards.
- Remove required privacy or security protections for protected health information.
- Permit unapproved access between regulated and non-regulated functions.
- Make unapproved representations about HIPAA compliance or entity status.

Exception requests shall include, at a minimum:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Name, role, business unit, and contact information. |
| Affected activity | Product, service, system, contract, customer, vendor, or business function. |
| Requested exception | Specific requirement from this Policy for which exception is requested. |
| Business justification | Reason the requirement cannot be met as written. |
| Data involved | Types and volume of health information, including whether protected health information is involved. |
| Risk assessment | Privacy, security, legal, contractual, operational, and reputational risks. |
| Compensating controls | Safeguards that will reduce risk during the exception period. |
| Duration | Start date, end date, and milestones for returning to compliance. |
| Required approvals | Business owner, Privacy Officer, Security Officer, Legal Counsel, and executive approver where required. |
| Review plan | Monitoring activities and reassessment date. |

All approved exceptions shall be recorded in the exception register maintained by [Compliance Function or Privacy Office]. Exceptions shall be reviewed at least monthly until closed, unless a more frequent review is required by the approvers.

Any exception that increases the risk of unauthorised use, disclosure, access, or transmission of protected health information shall require approval by the Privacy Officer, Security Officer, Legal Counsel, and [Executive Approver].

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change affecting HIPAA applicability, including changes to:

- Organisational structure, ownership, acquisitions, divestitures, or legal entities.
- Business models, products, services, or customer relationships.
- Health information data flows, systems, applications, or infrastructure.
- Contracts, subcontractors, vendors, or outsourced services.
- Regulated functions, health care components, or Hybrid Entity designation.
- Applicable law, regulatory expectations, enforcement trends, or legal interpretations.
- Internal audit findings, incidents, breaches, complaints, or risk assessments.

The Privacy Officer shall coordinate review and maintenance of this Policy with the Security Officer, Legal Counsel, Compliance Officer, business owners, and other stakeholders as appropriate.

Policy updates shall be approved by [Approving Authority] before publication. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.

The current approved version of this Policy shall be published in [policy repository] and made available to all workforce members who perform, support, sell, contract for, manage, or oversee activities involving health information.

| Process Owner | Enter the accountable business owner role or named owner responsible for accuracy of this entry; include title and team where possible. |
| System / Application / Repository Name | Enter the name of the system, application, database, file share, device, SaaS platform, paper repository, or other location where PHI/ePHI exists. |

| PHI/ePHI Created | Indicate whether PHI/ePHI is created at this location using allowed values: Yes, No, Unknown; if Yes, creation must be reflected in the process description. |

| PHI/ePHI Maintained | Indicate whether PHI/ePHI is stored, retained, archived, or otherwise maintained at this location using allowed values: Yes, No, Unknown. |
| PHI/ePHI Transmitted | Indicate whether PHI/ePHI is transmitted from this location using allowed values: Yes, No, Unknown; if Yes, identify recipient and transmission method. |
| PHI Data Categories | List the PHI/ePHI categories present, separated by semicolons; examples include name, address, date of birth, MRN, diagnosis, treatment notes, medication, lab result, imaging, billing, claims, insurance ID, SSN, payment data, provider notes, appointment data. |
| Patient Population / Scope | Describe whose PHI/ePHI is included, e.g., all patients, behavioral health patients, employees receiving care, minors, research subjects, specific facility patients. |
| Approximate Record Volume | Enter the approximate number of individuals or records affected; use a number or range, e.g., 25000 or 10000-50000; enter Unknown only if not available. |
