 Access shall be provisioned through approved ticketing, identity governance, access management, or documented manual processes. Informal requests through email, chat, verbal instruction, or direct administrator action shall not be sufficient unless documented and approved in accordance with this policy.

12. **Access rights shall match the approved request.** 
 Access administrators shall grant only the permissions approved in the access request. If additional permissions are needed, a new or amended approval shall be obtained before provisioning.

13. **Temporary access shall have an expiration date.** 
 Temporary access to ePHI shall be assigned a defined end date and shall be removed automatically where technically feasible. Temporary access shall not be extended without renewed approval.

14. **Privileged access shall be restricted and separately controlled.** 
 Administrative, super-user, database administrator, root, service management, security configuration, and other privileged access shall be limited to authorized personnel with a documented need. Privileged access shall be separately approved, monitored, and reviewed more frequently than standard access.

15. **Privileged accounts shall not be used for routine business activity.** 
 Workforce members with privileged access shall use standard user accounts for routine activities and privileged accounts only when performing authorized administrative functions.

16. **Access to ePHI shall be modified promptly when job duties change.** 
 Managers shall initiate access changes when a workforce member transfers departments, changes job responsibilities, changes employment status, changes work location, or no longer requires previously granted access.

17. **Access shall be removed promptly upon workforce separation.** 
 Access to ePHI shall be disabled or removed when a workforce member’s employment, contract, assignment, or affiliation ends.

18. **Access removal timelines shall be based on risk.** 
 Access changes and removals shall be completed within the following timeframes unless a stricter timeframe is required by [Organization Name]:

 | Event Type | Required Action | Maximum Completion Time |
 |---|---|---:|
 | Involuntary termination or high-risk separation | Disable all access to ePHI and remote access | Immediately upon notice, and no later than [1 hour] |
 | Voluntary termination | Disable access to ePHI | By end of last working day |
 | Contractor or vendor assignment end | Disable assigned access | By end of assignment or contract end date |
 | Department transfer | Remove access no longer required; grant approved new access | Within [1 business day] |
 | Role change with reduced need | Remove unnecessary access | Within [1 business day] |
 | Leave of absence where access is not required | Suspend or restrict access | Within [1 business day] |
 | Temporary access expiration | Remove temporary permissions | On expiration date |

19. **Emergency access shall be controlled and auditable.** 
 Emergency access to ePHI may be granted only when necessary to support patient care, urgent operational needs, system recovery, or other time-sensitive circumstances. Emergency access shall be limited in duration, logged, reviewed after use, and revoked when no longer needed.

20. **Emergency access use shall be reviewed after the event.** 
 All emergency or break-glass access events shall be reviewed by the system owner, Privacy Officer, Security Officer, or designated reviewer to confirm that access was appropriate and limited to the situation.

21. **Vendor and third-party access shall be formally authorized.** 
 Vendors, consultants, service providers, and other third parties shall not be granted access to ePHI unless a valid business need exists, required contractual protections are in place, access has been approved, and the access is limited to the services being performed.

22. **Third-party access shall be time-bound where practical.** 
 Vendor and third-party accounts shall be assigned expiration dates or periodically revalidated. Persistent vendor access shall require documented justification and enhanced monitoring.

23. **Remote access to ePHI shall be approved and secured.** 
 Remote access to systems containing ePHI shall be limited to authorized users, approved business purposes, and secure remote access methods authorized by [Organization Name].

24. **Access to non-production environments containing ePHI shall be controlled.** 
 Test, development, training, reporting, analytics, backup, archive, and disaster recovery environments containing ePHI shall be subject to access authorization requirements equivalent to production environments.

25. **Use of production ePHI in non-production environments shall be restricted.** 
 Production ePHI shall not be used in non-production environments unless approved by the Privacy Officer, Security Officer, and applicable system owner, and unless appropriate safeguards are applied.

26. **Service accounts shall be approved, documented, and controlled.** 
 Service accounts, application accounts, interface accounts, integration accounts, robotic process accounts, and system-to-system accounts that access ePHI shall have an assigned owner, documented purpose, approved access level, and appropriate technical protections.

27. **Service accounts shall not be used for interactive user activity.** 
 Service accounts shall not be used by individuals for routine login or interactive work unless specifically approved for a documented technical need and protected by compensating controls.

28. **Access to bulk export, reporting, and analytics capabilities shall be restricted.** 
 Capabilities that allow viewing, exporting, printing, downloading, transferring, or aggregating large volumes of ePHI shall be limited to authorized roles with a documented business need and appropriate oversight.

29. **Access to sensitive ePHI categories shall be further restricted where applicable.** 
 Additional access restrictions shall be applied to sensitive patient information where required by law, organizational policy, patient consent requirements, ethical obligations, contractual terms, or business rules.

30. **Access shall be reviewed periodically.** 
 User access to systems containing ePHI shall be reviewed on a scheduled basis to confirm that access remains appropriate, necessary, and authorized.

31. **Access review frequency shall be risk-based.** 
 Access reviews shall occur at least as frequently as follows:

 | Access Type | Minimum Review Frequency | Reviewer |
 |---|---:|---|
 | Standard user access to ePHI systems | Quarterly or [Frequency] | Manager and system owner |
 | Privileged access | Monthly or [Frequency] | System owner and Security Officer or delegate |
 | Vendor or third-party access | Quarterly or contract milestone | Vendor owner and system owner |
 | Emergency access events | After each use | Privacy Officer, Security Officer, or delegate |
 | Service accounts | Quarterly or [Frequency] | Account owner and system owner |
 | Bulk export, reporting, or analytics access | Quarterly or [Frequency] | Data owner and Privacy Officer or delegate |

32. **Access review results shall be documented.** 
 Reviewers shall document access reviewed, decisions made, access retained, access modified, access removed, review date, and reviewer identity.

33. **Inappropriate access identified during reviews shall be remediated promptly.** 
 Access that is excessive, outdated, unauthorized, unexplained, or inconsistent with job duties shall be removed or modified within defined remediation timelines.

34. **Access review remediation shall be tracked to closure.** 
 Findings from access reviews shall be recorded, assigned to responsible personnel, monitored, and closed only after corrective action is completed.

35. **Access logs shall be retained and available for review.** 
 Systems containing ePHI shall maintain records sufficient to determine who accessed ePHI, what access was performed, when access occurred, and whether access was successful or denied, where technically feasible.

36. **Access management records shall be retained.** 
 Records of access requests, approvals, modifications, removals, emergency access, access reviews, and related remediation shall be retained in accordance with [Organization Name]’s record retention requirements.

37. **Access shall be suspended when misuse is suspected.** 
 Access to ePHI may be suspended or restricted when unauthorized access, inappropriate use, workforce misconduct, compromised credentials, excessive permissions, or other access-related risk is suspected.

38. **Workforce members shall complete required training before receiving access.** 
 Workforce members shall complete required privacy, security, confidentiality, acceptable use, and role-specific training before access to ePHI is granted, unless an approved exception exists for urgent operational need.

39. **Workforce members shall use access only for authorized purposes.** 
 Workforce members shall access ePHI only as needed to perform assigned duties, support treatment, payment, healthcare operations, or other authorized organizational functions.

40. **Access to ePHI for curiosity, personal reasons, or unauthorized purposes is prohibited.** 
 Workforce members shall not access their own records, family member records, coworker records, celebrity records, public figure records, or any patient record unless access is required for assigned job duties and permitted by organizational policy.

41. **Segregation of duties shall be considered when granting access.** 
 Access shall be designed to reduce the risk of inappropriate activity, unauthorized changes, fraud, or concealment of activity. Conflicting permissions shall be avoided unless approved and monitored.

42. **Authentication and access control safeguards shall support authorization decisions.** 
 Systems containing ePHI shall use authentication and access control mechanisms appropriate to the risk of the system and the sensitivity of the ePHI.

43. **Access management processes shall be auditable.** 
 Access decisions and administrative actions shall be traceable to a request, approval, responsible individual, date, and business justification.

44. **Manual or local access processes shall follow the same authorization requirements.** 
 Where access is managed outside centralized identity management tools, system owners shall ensure equivalent approval, documentation, review, and removal controls are applied.

45. **Access shall not be granted based solely on seniority, convenience, or broad operational preference.** 
 Access to ePHI shall be based on legitimate job responsibilities, approved role requirements, and documented business need.

46. **Patient care continuity shall be balanced with privacy and security requirements.** 
 Access controls shall support timely care delivery while ensuring that access to ePHI remains appropriate, accountable, and limited to authorized purposes.

47. **Access management processes shall be coordinated with onboarding, transfer, and offboarding processes.** 
 Human Resources, management, Information Technology, Privacy, Security, and system owners shall coordinate workforce lifecycle events to ensure access remains accurate and timely.

48. **Access management failures shall be reported.** 
 Delayed terminations, unauthorized access, excessive access, missing approvals, failed access reviews, or other access control weaknesses shall be reported to the Security Officer, Privacy Officer, or designated governance channel.

49. **Access to ePHI shall be denied by default.** 
 Systems and processes shall be configured so that access is not granted unless explicitly approved and provisioned through an authorized process.

50. **Policy requirements shall apply to all methods of accessing ePHI.** 
 These requirements apply whether access occurs through a user interface, database query, application interface, file transfer, reporting tool, mobile application, API, administrative console, remote support session, or other access method.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Leadership | Provide oversight and resources to support effective information access management for ePHI. |
| Privacy Officer | Oversee privacy-related access requirements; advise on minimum necessary access; review high-risk, sensitive, or emergency access; support investigation of inappropriate access. |
| Security Officer | Oversee security-related access controls; approve or delegate approval for high-risk access; monitor access control effectiveness; coordinate remediation of access-related risks. |
| Information Technology | Implement approved access changes; maintain identity and access management tools; disable accounts; support logging, monitoring, and technical enforcement of access controls. |
| System Owners | Define system access roles; approve access to systems under their ownership; support access reviews; ensure system-level access controls are functioning appropriately. |
| Data Owners | Define appropriate access to ePHI data sets; approve access to sensitive, aggregated, reporting, or bulk data capabilities; participate in access reviews. |
| Managers and Supervisors | Validate business need; request access changes; ensure workforce access aligns with job duties; promptly notify appropriate teams of transfers, terminations, or role changes. |
| Human Resources | Notify responsible teams of workforce onboarding, role changes, leave, and separation events according to established processes and timelines. |
| Access Administrators | Provision, modify, disable, or remove access only after proper approval; maintain evidence of completed access actions; escalate incomplete or unclear requests. |
| Workforce Members | Use access only for authorized duties; protect credentials; complete required training; report suspected unauthorized access or access errors. |
| Vendor Owners | Sponsor and oversee third-party access; confirm business need; ensure vendor access remains appropriate; request timely removal when access is no longer required. |
| Internal Audit, Compliance, or Governance Function | Independently review access management practices, evidence, and adherence to this policy as part of monitoring and assurance activities. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy shall be monitored through a combination of operational controls, management oversight, system reports, access reviews, audit logs, incident investigations, and internal assessments.

Monitoring activities may include:

- Review of user access request records and approval evidence.
- Review of account creation, modification, and termination timeliness.
- Periodic access recertification for systems containing ePHI.
- Review of privileged, emergency, vendor, and service account access.
- Review of access to sensitive records or high-profile patient records.
- Comparison of active accounts against Human Resources and contractor records.
- Monitoring for inactive accounts, shared accounts, orphaned accounts, and excessive permissions.
- Review of access to reporting, bulk export, database query, and file transfer functions.
- Validation that terminated or transferred users no longer retain inappropriate access.
- Review of security events involving failed logins, unusual access patterns, or access outside expected work duties.

The following compliance metrics shall be maintained where practical:

| Metric | Target |
|---|---:|
| Access requests with documented approval before provisioning | 100% |
| Terminated workforce access disabled within required timeframe | 100% |
| Privileged accounts reviewed within required review cycle | 100% |
| Standard access reviews completed on schedule | At least [95%] |
| High-risk access exceptions with documented approval | 100% |
| Emergency access events reviewed after use | 100% |
| Inappropriate access findings remediated within assigned due date | At least [95%] |
| Vendor accounts with documented owner and business need | 100% |

Violations of this policy may result in corrective action, up to and including access suspension, disciplinary action, termination of employment or contract, legal action, and reporting to appropriate authorities where required.

Examples of policy violations include, but are not limited to:

- Granting access to ePHI without proper approval.
- Accessing ePHI without a valid work-related reason.
- Retaining access after a job change or termination.
- Sharing user credentials.
- Using another person’s account.
- Using privileged access for unauthorized purposes.
- Failing to complete required access reviews.
- Failing to remove access when no longer required.
- Circumventing approved access management processes.
- Granting vendor access without required authorization and oversight.

Suspected unauthorized access to ePHI shall be reported promptly to the Privacy Officer, Security Officer, Help Desk, Compliance function, or other designated reporting channel.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be limited, documented, risk-assessed, approved, time-bound, and reviewed periodically. Exceptions shall not be used to bypass access authorization requirements for convenience or routine operational preference.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception requester | Person or department requesting the exception |
| System or data involved | System, application, database, or ePHI data set affected |
| Policy requirement affected | Specific requirement that cannot be met |
| Business justification | Reason the exception is necessary |
| Risk assessment | Privacy, security, operational, and compliance risks |
| Compensating controls | Safeguards to reduce risk during the exception period |
| Requested duration | Start date and end date |
| Responsible owner | Person accountable for managing the exception |
| Required approvals | Privacy Officer, Security Officer, system owner, data owner, or executive approval as applicable |
| Review date | Date exception must be reviewed or closed |

Exceptions involving high-risk access, privileged access, vendor access, emergency access, bulk export capabilities, or sensitive ePHI shall require approval by the Privacy Officer and Security Officer, or their authorized delegates.

Approved exceptions shall be tracked in an exception register and reviewed at least quarterly, or more frequently based on risk. Expired exceptions shall be closed or reapproved before continuation.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect access to ePHI, including:

- Implementation of new systems containing ePHI.
- Major changes to identity and access management processes.
- Material changes to organizational structure or workforce roles.
- Significant privacy or security incidents involving access to ePHI.
- Changes in legal, regulatory, contractual, or business requirements.
- Audit findings or risk assessments identifying access management weaknesses.
- Adoption of new cloud services, integrations, remote access methods, or third-party support models.

The Privacy Officer and Security Officer shall jointly coordinate review and maintenance of this policy, with input from Information Technology, Human Resources, Compliance, system owners, data owners, and business leadership.

Policy revisions shall be documented through version control, approved by appropriate governance authority, and communicated to affected workforce members and third parties as applicable. Training, procedures, standards, and technical configurations shall be updated as needed to remain consistent with this policy.

HIPAA-015.title: Workstation Use & Security Policy
HIPAA-015.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-HIPAA-WS-001] | 1.0 | Privacy Officer / Security Officer | [Effective Date] | HIPAA | Internal Use |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Workstation Use & Security Policy is to establish mandatory requirements for the appropriate use, placement, configuration, and physical safeguarding of workstations that access, store, process, transmit, or display electronic protected health information.

This policy supports the organization’s obligation to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information by reducing the risk of unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, theft, loss, or viewing of information through workstation misuse or inadequate physical safeguards.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All workforce members, including employees, medical staff, contractors, consultants, interns, volunteers, temporary staff, and third parties who use organizational workstations.
- All workstations owned, leased, managed, or approved by the organization.
- Any workstation used to access organizational systems or electronic protected health information, including:
 - Desktop computers.
 - Laptop computers.
 - Thin clients.
 - Shared clinical workstations.
 - Registration, billing, scheduling, and administrative workstations.
 - Workstations on wheels and mobile clinical carts.
 - Kiosks or dedicated-use terminals.
 - Workstations used in remote or hybrid work locations.
- All locations where workstations may be used, including:
 - Clinical areas.
 - Administrative offices.
 - Patient intake and waiting areas.
 - Nursing stations.
 - Laboratories.
 - Pharmacies.
 - Billing and coding areas.
 - Home offices.
 - Third-party or hosted work environments, where approved.

This policy applies whether the workstation is connected to the organization’s network directly, remotely, wirelessly, through a virtual desktop, or through an approved cloud-based application.

This policy does not replace more detailed technical standards, acceptable use requirements, remote work requirements, device management standards, or incident response procedures. Where multiple requirements apply, the more protective requirement shall be followed.

## Policy Statements

1. The organization shall define and enforce appropriate workstation use requirements for all workstations that access, process, store, transmit, or display electronic protected health information.

2. Workforce members shall use workstations only for authorized business, clinical, operational, educational, or administrative purposes approved by the organization.

3. Workforce members shall not use workstations to access, view, retrieve, disclose, copy, download, print, transmit, or store electronic protected health information unless such access is necessary to perform assigned job duties.

4. Workforce members shall access only the minimum information necessary to perform their assigned responsibilities, except where broader access is required for treatment, authorized operations, or another approved business purpose.

5. Workforce members shall authenticate using their own assigned credentials before accessing any workstation, application, system, or service containing electronic protected health information.

6. Workforce members shall not share passwords, authentication tokens, smart cards, badges, multifactor authentication prompts, or other access credentials used to access workstations or systems.

7. Workforce members shall not allow another person to use a workstation under their authenticated session.

8. Workforce members shall log off, lock, or otherwise secure workstations before leaving them unattended, including for short periods.

9. Workstations shall be configured to automatically lock after a defined period of inactivity based on location and risk.

| Workstation Location or Use Case | Maximum Inactivity Period Before Lock | Additional Requirement |
|---|---:|---|
| Shared clinical workstation in patient care areas | [5 minutes] | Session shall require re-authentication or approved rapid secure re-entry |
| Registration, intake, billing, or reception workstation | [10 minutes] | Screen shall not be visible to unauthorized individuals |
| Administrative workstation in restricted office area | [15 minutes] | Screen lock shall require user re-authentication |
| Remote work workstation | [10 minutes] | Full device lock shall be enabled |
| Public-facing kiosk or dedicated terminal | [2 minutes] | Application shall restrict access to approved functions only |

10. Workstations shall be positioned, shielded, or otherwise arranged to reduce the likelihood that electronic protected health information can be viewed by patients, visitors, vendors, or unauthorized workforce members.

11. Workforce members shall use privacy screens, monitor positioning, workstation placement, or other approved safeguards when workstations are located in open, public, semi-public, or high-traffic areas.

12. Workstations located in patient rooms, hallways, nursing stations, waiting areas, registration areas, or other public-facing spaces shall be configured and positioned to limit unauthorized viewing of electronic protected health information.

13. Workstations shall not be left displaying electronic protected health information when the information is no longer actively needed.

14. Workforce members shall not discuss, display, or access electronic protected health information at a workstation in a manner that allows unauthorized individuals to view or overhear confidential information.

15. Workstations shall be physically protected against unauthorized access, tampering, theft, and environmental hazards using safeguards appropriate to the location and use of the workstation.

16. Desktop workstations in restricted areas shall be placed in controlled locations and secured through facility access controls, locked rooms, cable locks, locked cabinets, or other approved physical safeguards when warranted by risk.

17. Laptops, tablets, mobile workstations, and portable computing devices shall be physically secured when not in use, including storage in a locked drawer, cabinet, office, docking station, cart, or other approved secure location.

18. Workstations shall not be relocated, reassigned, repurposed, loaned, disposed of, or removed from organizational premises without approval from Information Technology or another authorized function.

19. Workforce members shall not connect unauthorized personal devices, removable media, peripherals, storage devices, or networking equipment to organizational workstations.

20. Workforce members shall not install, disable, bypass, or modify software, security tools, hardware, operating system settings, browser extensions, encryption settings, logging tools, endpoint protection, or configuration controls unless authorized by Information Technology.

21. Workstations used to access electronic protected health information shall be configured, managed, and maintained according to organization-approved security baselines.

22. Workstations shall use organization-approved endpoint protection, encryption, access control, patch management, logging, and monitoring capabilities appropriate to their purpose and risk.

23. Workstations shall not be used to store electronic protected health information locally unless there is a documented business need, the storage is approved, and required security safeguards are implemented.

24. Electronic protected health information stored locally on approved workstations shall be encrypted where technically feasible and shall be removed when no longer required for the approved business purpose.

25. Workforce members shall save electronic protected health information only in approved applications, repositories, network locations, electronic health record systems, document management systems, or other authorized storage locations.

26. Workforce members shall not store electronic protected health information on local desktops, personal folders, temporary folders, unapproved cloud storage, personal email, consumer messaging platforms, or unapproved removable media.

27. Printing, scanning, faxing, copying, downloading, exporting, or screen capturing electronic protected health information from a workstation shall be limited to approved business purposes and performed in a manner that prevents unauthorized access or disclosure.

28. Printed materials containing protected health information shall be retrieved promptly, secured during use, and disposed of in approved confidential disposal containers or through approved destruction methods.

29. Shared workstations shall be configured to support individual user authentication, session separation, access controls, and auditability.

30. Generic or shared workstation accounts shall not be used to access electronic protected health information unless specifically approved for a limited operational purpose and supported by compensating controls that preserve accountability.

31. Workstations used in clinical emergencies or time-sensitive care settings shall be configured to balance patient safety and information protection, including appropriate safeguards for emergency access, timeout, and audit review.

32. Public-access workstations, kiosks, guest devices, and patient-facing terminals shall not provide access to internal systems or electronic protected health information unless explicitly approved and technically restricted to the intended function.

33. Remote workstations used to access electronic protected health information shall comply with organization-approved remote access, device management, encryption, network security, and physical security requirements.

34. Workforce members working remotely shall protect workstation screens from unauthorized viewing by household members, visitors, roommates, public bystanders, or other unauthorized individuals.

35. Workforce members shall not access electronic protected health information from public or unsecured workstations, including hotel business centers, public libraries, shared personal computers, internet cafés, or unapproved borrowed devices.

36. Workforce members shall not leave organizational laptops or portable workstations unattended in vehicles, public locations, conference areas, airports, restaurants, hotel lobbies, or other unsecured environments unless secured in accordance with organizational requirements.

37. If temporary storage of a portable workstation in a vehicle is unavoidable, the device shall be powered off, locked, kept out of sight, and secured in the trunk or other concealed compartment for the minimum time necessary.

38. Workstations shall be protected from environmental risks, including spills, heat, water damage, electrical hazards, excessive dust, obstructed ventilation, and unsafe placement.

39. Workstations in clinical or operational environments shall be positioned so that cables, carts, and peripherals do not create safety hazards or obstruct care delivery, emergency access, exits, or required equipment.

40. Workstations that are lost, stolen, damaged, tampered with, infected with malware, accessed by an unauthorized person, or suspected of exposing electronic protected health information shall be reported immediately through the organization’s incident reporting process.

41. Workforce members shall promptly report any observed failure of workstation safeguards, including unattended active sessions, visible protected health information, missing devices, unauthorized software, suspicious activity, or physical security concerns.

42. Information Technology shall disable, isolate, recover, reimage, or remove from service any workstation suspected of compromise, unauthorized modification, malware infection, or other condition that may place electronic protected health information at risk.

43. Workstations shall be inventoried and assigned to an accountable owner, department, location, or user, as appropriate.

44. The organization shall maintain records sufficient to identify workstation assignment, location, configuration status, lifecycle state, and disposition.

45. Workstations shall be securely sanitized, reimaged, repurposed, returned, or disposed of using approved methods before reassignment, repair, recycling, return to vendor, donation, or destruction.

46. Vendors, contractors, and service personnel shall not access, repair, replace, or remove workstations that may contain or access electronic protected health information unless authorized and supervised or otherwise controlled according to organizational requirements.

47. Workforce members shall complete required privacy and security training before being granted access to workstations that access electronic protected health information.

48. Workforce members shall follow all workstation use and security requirements communicated through training, system banners, job aids, standards, procedures, and management instructions.

49. The organization shall implement additional workstation safeguards where risk assessments, incident history, audits, regulatory expectations, or operational changes indicate a need for stronger protection.

50. Department leaders shall ensure workstation placement and use within their areas support patient privacy, workforce productivity, safety, and information security.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Leadership | Approves and supports the enforcement of this policy; ensures sufficient resources are available to implement workstation safeguards. |
| Privacy Officer | Provides oversight for privacy requirements related to workstation use, viewing, disclosure, printing, and handling of protected health information. |
| Security Officer | Owns security governance for workstation safeguards; coordinates risk assessments, monitoring expectations, enforcement activities, and policy maintenance. |
| Information Technology | Configures, deploys, secures, monitors, patches, supports, inventories, and retires workstations; implements technical safeguards such as encryption, screen lock, endpoint protection, access control, and device management. |
| Facilities / Physical Security | Supports physical safeguards for workstation placement, restricted areas, locks, access controls, environmental protections, and secure storage. |
| Department Managers | Ensure workforce members follow this policy; approve workstation locations and use cases; report noncompliance; ensure local practices protect electronic protected health information. |
| Workforce Members | Use workstations appropriately; protect credentials; secure screens and devices; prevent unauthorized viewing; report incidents, lost devices, suspicious activity, and policy violations. |
| Compliance / Internal Audit | Performs periodic reviews, audits, and compliance assessments related to workstation use and physical safeguards. |
| Third Parties and Vendors | Follow contractual and organizational requirements when accessing, supporting, repairing, or handling workstations or systems containing electronic protected health information. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy is mandatory. The organization shall monitor adherence through a combination of technical, administrative, and physical review activities.

Monitoring activities may include:

- Review of workstation configuration compliance.
- Endpoint protection and patch status monitoring.
- Encryption and device management reporting.
- Screen lock and session timeout validation.
- Physical walkthroughs of clinical and administrative areas.
- Review of workstation placement in public or patient-facing areas.
- Audit log review for inappropriate access or unusual activity.
- Inventory reconciliation.
- Review of remote access and device compliance.
- Investigation of reported incidents, lost devices, or privacy concerns.
- Validation of secure disposal, reassignment, or return processes.
- Periodic privacy and security risk assessments.

Minimum expected review activities are:

| Activity | Frequency | Responsible Function | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workstation configuration compliance review | At least quarterly | Information Technology | Device compliance report, remediation ticket records |
| Physical workstation safeguard walkthrough | At least annually and after major layout changes | Security Officer / Privacy Officer / Facilities | Walkthrough checklist, findings, remediation actions |
| Inventory reconciliation | At least annually | Information Technology | Asset inventory report, exception list |
| Remote workstation compliance review | At least quarterly | Information Technology / Security Officer | Device management report, remote access report |
| Review of workstation-related incidents | Ongoing, with periodic trend review | Security Officer / Privacy Officer | Incident records, corrective action plans |
| Workforce training completion review | At least annually | Compliance / Human Resources | Training completion report |

Noncompliance may result in corrective action, up to and including suspension of access, disciplinary action, contract remedies, termination of employment or engagement, and legal action where appropriate.

Enforcement shall be based on the nature, severity, intent, recurrence, and impact of the violation. Examples of violations include, but are not limited to:

- Leaving an active workstation session unattended.
- Sharing credentials or allowing another person to use an authenticated session.
- Viewing protected health information without a job-related need.
- Positioning a workstation so protected health information is visible to unauthorized individuals.
- Removing a workstation from an approved location without authorization.
- Disabling endpoint protection, encryption, logging, or security settings.
- Storing protected health information in unapproved locations.
- Using an unauthorized device to access electronic protected health information.
- Failing to report a lost, stolen, compromised, or tampered workstation.
- Installing unauthorized software or connecting unauthorized peripherals.
- Failing to secure a workstation used for remote work.

Confirmed or suspected breaches involving protected health information shall be handled through the organization’s incident response and breach assessment processes.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be limited, documented, risk-assessed, time-bound, and approved before implementation unless emergency circumstances require immediate action to protect patient safety or critical operations.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Name, role, department, and contact information of the person requesting the exception |
| Workstation or Location | Asset identifier, location, department, or use case affected |
| Policy Requirement | Specific requirement that cannot be met |
| Business Justification | Reason the exception is necessary |
| Risk Description | Potential privacy, security, operational, and patient safety risks |
| Compensating Safeguards | Alternative controls to reduce risk |
| Requested Duration | Start date and end date of the exception |
| Approvals | Department leader, Security Officer, Privacy Officer, and other required approvers |
| Review Date | Date the exception will be reassessed |
| Remediation Plan | Steps and timeline to return to compliance |

The Security Officer and Privacy Officer shall review exception requests involving electronic protected health information. Information Technology shall review exceptions involving workstation configuration, endpoint security, device management, or technical feasibility.

Approved exceptions shall be recorded in an exception register and reviewed at defined intervals. Exceptions shall not be granted indefinitely unless formally approved by executive leadership and supported by documented risk acceptance.

Emergency deviations from this policy shall be reported to the Security Officer and Privacy Officer as soon as practical and shall be reviewed after the event to determine whether continued exception approval, remediation, or corrective action is required.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect workstation use or security, including:

- Changes to clinical workflows or workstation locations.
- Deployment of new workstation types, mobile carts, kiosks, or remote work technologies.
- Changes to electronic health record, billing, scheduling, or administrative systems.
- Significant privacy or security incidents involving workstations.
- Audit findings or risk assessment results.
- Facility renovations, relocations, or changes to public-facing areas.
- Changes in legal, regulatory, contractual, or organizational requirements.
- Introduction of new device management, endpoint security, or access control technologies.

The Security Officer is responsible for coordinating review and maintenance of this policy in consultation with the Privacy Officer, Information Technology, Facilities, Compliance, and department leadership.

Updates shall be documented through version control and communicated to affected workforce members. Material changes shall be supported by updated training, procedures, standards, or technical configurations where appropriate.

HIPAA-016.title: Device & Media Controls Policy
HIPAA-016.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-HIPAA-DMC-001] | 1.0 | [Privacy Officer / Security Officer] | [Effective Date] | HIPAA | Internal |

## Purpose

This policy establishes mandatory requirements for controlling devices and electronic media that create, receive, maintain, process, store, transmit, transport, reuse, or dispose of electronic protected health information.

The purpose of this policy is to ensure that electronic protected health information is protected throughout the full device and media lifecycle, including receipt, inventory, movement, removal from facilities, transfer, reuse, sanitization, destruction, and disposal.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All workforce members, including employees, contractors, temporary staff, volunteers, interns, and third parties who use or manage devices or media on behalf of [Organization Name].
- All facilities, offices, clinics, data centers, remote work locations, and third-party service locations where devices or media containing electronic protected health information are used, stored, transported, serviced, reused, or disposed of.
- All information systems and technology assets that create, receive, maintain, process, store, transmit, or access electronic protected health information.
- All electronic media, whether owned by [Organization Name], leased, personally owned if approved for business use, or managed by a vendor.

For the purposes of this policy, “devices and media” include, but are not limited to:

| Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| End-user devices | Laptops, desktops, tablets, smartphones, thin clients, workstations on wheels |
| Servers and infrastructure | Physical servers, storage arrays, network-attached storage, backup appliances, medical device controllers |
| Removable media | USB drives, external hard drives, memory cards, optical discs, tapes |
| Embedded storage | Drives inside printers, copiers, scanners, fax machines, diagnostic systems, imaging systems, medical devices |
| Backup and archival media | Backup tapes, external backup disks, replicated storage, offline archives |
| Virtual and cloud media | Virtual disks, snapshots, machine images, cloud storage volumes, container images where electronic protected health information may be stored |
| Returned, retired, or failed components | Hard drives, solid-state drives, mobile device storage, failed storage components, replacement parts |

This policy applies regardless of whether electronic protected health information is stored temporarily or permanently.

## Policy Statements

1. [Organization Name] shall maintain documented controls for the receipt, inventory, movement, removal, reuse, sanitization, destruction, and disposal of devices and media that may contain electronic protected health information.

2. [Organization Name] shall maintain an accurate inventory of devices and media that store, process, transmit, or may contain electronic protected health information.

3. The inventory shall record, at minimum, the following information where applicable:

 | Inventory Field | Requirement |
 |---|---|
 | Asset identifier | Unique asset tag, serial number, barcode, or system-generated identifier |
 | Asset type | Device or media category |
 | Assigned owner or custodian | Workforce member, department, system owner, or service provider responsible |
 | Physical or logical location | Facility, room, storage area, cloud environment, or remote user assignment |
 | Electronic protected health information status | Whether the asset stores, processes, transmits, or may contain electronic protected health information |
 | Encryption status | Encryption enabled, not applicable, or exception approved |
 | Lifecycle status | In service, in storage, in transit, pending reuse, pending disposal, destroyed, lost, or retired |
 | Receipt date | Date received or placed into service |
 | Transfer history | Chain of custody for reassignment, movement, service, return, or disposal |
 | Sanitization or destruction record | Method, date, approver, and evidence for reused or disposed media |

4. Devices and media that may contain electronic protected health information shall be uniquely identified and traceable from receipt through final disposition.

5. Devices and media shall be reviewed at receipt to determine whether they can store, process, transmit, or retain electronic protected health information.

6. Devices and media capable of storing electronic protected health information shall be entered into the approved asset inventory before being placed into production use.

7. Devices and media received from vendors, service providers, or external parties shall be inspected, logged, and assigned to an accountable internal owner before use.

8. Devices and media shall not be used to create, receive, maintain, process, store, or transmit electronic protected health information unless they are approved, inventoried, and configured in accordance with [Organization Name] security requirements.

9. Devices and media containing or reasonably expected to contain electronic protected health information shall be protected against unauthorized access, loss, theft, tampering, and environmental damage.

10. Devices and media containing electronic protected health information shall be stored in secure areas appropriate to the sensitivity of the information and the risk of unauthorized access.

11. Removable media containing electronic protected health information shall be minimized and used only when there is a documented business need and no reasonably secure alternative is available.

12. Removable media containing electronic protected health information shall be encrypted using organization-approved encryption before use, unless an approved exception is documented.

13. Workforce members shall not copy electronic protected health information to removable media, personal devices, unmanaged storage, or consumer cloud services unless specifically authorized by policy, role, and documented business need.

14. Devices and media containing electronic protected health information shall not be removed from [Organization Name] facilities unless removal is authorized, documented, and protected by appropriate safeguards.

15. The removal of devices or media from controlled facilities shall be recorded in a movement or chain-of-custody log when the device or media contains, or may contain, electronic protected health information.

16. The chain-of-custody record shall include, at minimum:

 | Chain-of-Custody Field | Requirement |
 |---|---|
 | Asset or media identifier | Unique identifier of the device or media |
 | Description | Type of device or media and purpose of movement |
 | Electronic protected health information status | Known, suspected, encrypted, or sanitized |
 | Released by | Name and role of person releasing the item |
 | Received by | Name and role of person receiving the item |
 | Date and time | Date and time of release and receipt |
 | Origin and destination | Facility, department, vendor, or shipping destination |
 | Transportation method | Hand delivery, courier, secure shipment, vendor pickup, or other approved method |
 | Protective measures | Encryption, sealed container, tracking number, tamper-evident packaging, or secure courier |
 | Approval reference | Service ticket, change record, disposal authorization, or management approval |
 | Final disposition | Returned, reassigned, sanitized, destroyed, lost, or pending closure |

17. Devices and media containing electronic protected health information shall be transported using secure methods appropriate to the risk, including encryption, tamper-evident packaging, tracking, and signature confirmation where applicable.

18. Devices and media containing electronic protected health information shall not be left unattended in public areas, unsecured vehicles, hotel rooms, conference rooms, waiting areas, or other locations where unauthorized access may occur.

19. Workforce members shall promptly report lost, stolen, damaged, missing, or unaccounted-for devices or media that contain or may contain electronic protected health information.

20. Lost, stolen, missing, or unaccounted-for devices or media shall be handled as a security incident and assessed to determine whether electronic protected health information may have been compromised.

21. Devices assigned to workforce members shall be returned to [Organization Name] upon termination, transfer, role change, device replacement, end of contract, or upon request.

22. Returned devices and media shall be tracked, secured, and evaluated before reassignment, reuse, repair, return to vendor, or disposal.

23. Devices and media that are no longer needed, obsolete, damaged, replaced, or removed from service shall follow an approved retirement, sanitization, and disposal process.

24. Devices and media containing or reasonably expected to contain electronic protected health information shall not be reused until electronic protected health information has been removed using an approved sanitization method.

25. Sanitization methods shall be selected based on media type, sensitivity of information, intended reuse, and technical feasibility.

26. Approved sanitization and destruction methods shall include, as appropriate:

 | Media Type | Approved Reuse Method | Approved Disposal Method |
 |---|---|---|
 | Magnetic hard drives | Secure overwrite or cryptographic erasure where supported | Degaussing, shredding, crushing, or certified destruction |
 | Solid-state drives | Cryptographic erasure or manufacturer-approved secure erase where validated | Shredding, crushing, disintegration, or certified destruction |
 | USB drives and memory cards | Secure erase only where effective and approved | Shredding, crushing, or certified destruction |
 | Optical discs | Not typically approved for reuse where electronic protected health information is present | Shredding or physical destruction |
 | Backup tapes | Approved overwrite or degaussing where technically suitable | Degaussing, shredding, or certified destruction |
 | Mobile devices | Factory reset plus cryptographic erasure and management system removal | Certified destruction if erasure cannot be verified |
 | Printers, copiers, scanners, and fax devices | Secure erase of embedded storage or replacement of storage component | Certified destruction of embedded storage if erasure cannot be verified |
 | Medical devices with embedded storage | Manufacturer-approved sanitization validated by [Information Security / Biomedical Engineering] | Certified destruction or vendor-attested destruction of storage components |

27. Simple deletion, formatting, moving files to trash, or removing file references shall not be considered acceptable sanitization for electronic protected health information.

28. If sanitization cannot be validated, the device or media shall be physically destroyed or managed under an approved exception with compensating safeguards.

29. Devices and media that are sent to a vendor for repair, warranty replacement, return, lease termination, or disposal shall be sanitized before release whenever technically feasible.

30. If a device or media item containing electronic protected health information cannot be sanitized before vendor release, the release shall require documented approval, chain-of-custody tracking, contractual safeguards, and risk acceptance by authorized management.

31. Disposal of devices and media containing or reasonably expected to contain electronic protected health information shall be performed only by authorized personnel or approved service providers.

32. Disposal service providers shall be subject to due diligence, contractual confidentiality and security obligations, and documented oversight appropriate to their access to electronic protected health information.

33. A certificate of destruction or equivalent evidence shall be obtained and retained for devices and media destroyed by a third-party service provider.

34. Destruction records shall identify the media or device destroyed, method of destruction, date, service provider or personnel performing the destruction, and authorizing party.

35. Devices and media pending sanitization, reuse, return, or destruction shall be stored securely and segregated from active inventory to prevent unauthorized access or accidental redeployment.

36. Devices and media that have been sanitized for reuse shall be validated and documented before reassignment.

37. Reused devices shall be configured according to approved security baselines before being issued or returned to service.

38. Electronic protected health information shall not be retained on replaced, reassigned, repurposed, loaned, demo, test, or training devices unless specifically approved and protected under applicable safeguards.

39. Test, training, development, demonstration, or loaner devices shall use de-identified, synthetic, or non-production data wherever feasible.

40. Personal devices shall not be used to store electronic protected health information unless explicitly authorized under an approved bring-your-own-device or mobile device management program.

41. Personal devices approved for access to electronic protected health information shall be subject to security controls, including encryption, access control, remote wipe capability, and removal of organization data when access is no longer authorized.

42. Cloud storage volumes, snapshots, backups, exports, and virtual machine images containing electronic protected health information shall be controlled, tracked, retained, sanitized, deleted, or destroyed according to approved lifecycle controls.

43. System owners shall ensure that electronic protected health information is removed from decommissioned applications, databases, storage repositories, virtual infrastructure, and cloud services according to approved data retention and disposal requirements.

44. Backup and archive media containing electronic protected health information shall be protected, tracked, encrypted where feasible, and disposed of securely when retention requirements have been met.

45. Media disposal shall not occur if the media is subject to legal hold, investigation hold, audit hold, contractual retention requirement, or approved business retention requirement.

46. The minimum retention of device and media control records shall be as follows, unless a longer period is required by legal, contractual, or organizational requirements:

 | Record Type | Minimum Retention |
 |---|---:|
 | Asset inventory records | Life of asset plus [6 years] |
 | Chain-of-custody logs | [6 years] |
 | Sanitization records | [6 years] |
 | Destruction certificates | [6 years] |
 | Vendor disposal records | [6 years] |
 | Exception approvals | [6 years] after exception closure |
 | Incident records involving devices or media | In accordance with incident response and legal retention requirements |

47. Device and media control records shall be accurate, complete, protected from unauthorized alteration, and available for audit, investigation, and compliance review.

48. Workforce members shall complete assigned privacy and security awareness training that includes responsibilities for protecting devices and media containing electronic protected health information.

49. Departments shall not establish separate device or media handling practices that conflict with this policy.

50. Any suspected violation of this policy shall be reported promptly to [Security Officer], [Privacy Officer], [Compliance Department], or through [Incident Reporting Channel].

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Leadership | Approves organizational commitment to protecting electronic protected health information and supports enforcement of this policy. |
| Security Officer | Owns technical safeguards for device and media controls; defines approved sanitization methods; reviews device and media risks; monitors compliance; coordinates security incident response involving lost, stolen, or improperly handled devices or media. |
| Privacy Officer | Assesses privacy impact involving electronic protected health information; supports breach assessment and notification processes; ensures handling aligns with privacy obligations and patient confidentiality expectations. |
| Compliance Officer | Oversees compliance monitoring; supports audit readiness; tracks policy exceptions and corrective actions; coordinates with Legal where required. |
| Information Technology | Maintains asset inventory; configures devices; enables encryption; manages endpoint protection and mobile device management; performs or verifies sanitization; supports secure disposal and redeployment. |
| Biomedical Engineering / Clinical Technology | Maintains inventory and lifecycle controls for medical devices and clinical systems with embedded storage; coordinates manufacturer-supported sanitization, repair, replacement, and disposal. |
| Facilities Management | Provides secure physical storage areas for devices and media awaiting deployment, repair, return, reuse, or disposal; supports secure vendor access and pickup. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Ensures vendors handling devices or media are reviewed, approved, and contractually obligated to protect electronic protected health information; obtains required disposal and destruction documentation. |
| Legal | Advises on legal holds, retention obligations, investigations, contractual requirements, and regulatory exposure involving devices and media. |
| Department Managers | Ensure workforce members follow this policy; approve business need for device or media use; ensure returned assets are collected during transfers and terminations. |
| System Owners | Identify systems and storage locations containing electronic protected health information; ensure secure decommissioning, deletion, retention, and disposal of system media and data. |
| Workforce Members | Protect assigned devices and media; use only approved storage and transfer methods; report loss, theft, damage, or suspected compromise; return devices and media when required. |
| Third-Party Service Providers | Handle devices and media only as authorized; protect electronic protected health information; maintain chain of custody; perform approved sanitization or destruction; provide required evidence and certifications. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

[Organization Name] shall monitor compliance with this policy through a combination of administrative, technical, and physical control activities.

Compliance monitoring shall include, as appropriate:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Responsible Role |
|---|---:|---|
| Review of device and media inventory completeness | At least quarterly | Information Technology |
| Reconciliation of assigned devices to workforce records | At least quarterly | Information Technology / Human Resources |
| Review of removable media use | At least quarterly | Security Officer |
| Review of encryption status for applicable devices | At least monthly | Information Technology / Security Officer |
| Review of devices pending disposal or sanitization | At least monthly | Information Technology |
| Sampling of sanitization and destruction records | At least quarterly | Compliance Officer |
| Review of vendor destruction certificates | Per disposal event and at least quarterly | Procurement / Vendor Management |
| Physical inspection of secure storage areas | At least semi-annually | Facilities Management / Security Officer |
| Review of exceptions and compensating safeguards | At least quarterly | Compliance Officer / Security Officer |
| Review of incidents involving lost, stolen, or mishandled devices or media | Per incident and during periodic trend review | Security Officer / Privacy Officer |

Audit and monitoring results shall be documented and retained according to organizational record retention requirements.

Identified gaps shall be tracked to remediation with assigned ownership, due dates, and evidence of completion.

Violations of this policy may result in corrective action, including retraining, suspension of access, disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment, contract remedies, vendor termination, civil action, or referral to law enforcement where appropriate.

Failure to report a lost, stolen, missing, improperly disposed, or improperly transferred device or media item may be treated as a policy violation.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only when there is a documented business, clinical, operational, technical, or legal need and the risk has been reviewed and approved by authorized personnel.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Name, role, department, and contact information |
| Asset or media involved | Asset identifier, media type, system, or data repository |
| Electronic protected health information involved | Description of the type and sensitivity of information, without including patient data in the request where avoidable |
| Reason for exception | Business, clinical, operational, legal, or technical justification |
| Requested duration | Start date and end date or event-based closure condition |
| Risk assessment | Security and privacy risks created by the exception |
| Compensating safeguards | Controls that reduce risk during the exception period |
| Approvals | Required authorization from Security, Privacy, Compliance, Legal, and business leadership as applicable |
| Review date | Date the exception will be reassessed |
| Closure evidence | Evidence that the exception has ended or been remediated |

Exceptions shall be time-limited and shall not exceed [maximum exception period] without reapproval.

Exceptions involving unencrypted devices or media containing electronic protected health information shall require approval by the Security Officer and Privacy Officer.

Exceptions involving vendor access to unsanitized devices or media shall require documented contractual safeguards and management risk acceptance.

Emergency exceptions may be granted when necessary to protect patient safety or restore critical operations, provided that the exception is documented and reviewed as soon as practical after the emergency condition is stabilized.

Expired exceptions shall be considered non-compliant unless formally renewed before expiration.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect device or media handling, including:

- Introduction of new systems, storage technologies, mobile devices, medical devices, or cloud services.
- Changes to electronic protected health information workflows.
- Significant security incidents involving devices or media.
- Changes in legal, regulatory, contractual, or organizational requirements.
- Audit findings or risk assessment results identifying gaps in device or media controls.
- Changes to approved sanitization, encryption, disposal, or vendor management practices.

The policy owner shall coordinate review with Information Technology, Privacy, Security, Compliance, Legal, Biomedical Engineering, Facilities, Procurement, and other stakeholders as appropriate.

Material changes shall be approved according to [Organization Name] policy governance requirements.

Superseded versions shall be retained according to organizational document retention requirements.

HIPAA-017.title: Audit Controls Policy
HIPAA-017.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| POL-HIPAA-AUDIT-CONTROLS | 1.0 | [Privacy and Security Officer] | [Effective Date] | HIPAA | Internal Use |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Audit Controls Policy is to establish mandatory requirements for implementing and maintaining hardware, software, and procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in systems that create, receive, maintain, transmit, or otherwise process electronic protected health information (ePHI).

This policy supports the organization’s ability to detect inappropriate access, investigate security and privacy incidents, demonstrate accountability, and maintain reliable evidence of system activity affecting ePHI.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All workforce members, including employees, contractors, temporary staff, volunteers, interns, and third parties who access systems containing ePHI.
- All information systems, applications, databases, cloud services, medical devices, infrastructure platforms, network devices, identity services, and end-user technologies that create, receive, maintain, transmit, or support access to ePHI.
- All environments where ePHI is processed, including production, staging, testing, backup, disaster recovery, remote access, and third-party hosted environments.
- All audit logs, security event records, access logs, administrative activity records, system alerts, and supporting evidence used to monitor and investigate activity involving ePHI.

This policy does not replace detailed operational procedures for log configuration, monitoring, incident response, or forensic investigation. Those procedures shall align with this policy.

## Policy Statements

1. The organization shall implement audit controls for all systems that create, receive, maintain, transmit, or support access to ePHI.

2. The organization shall use appropriate hardware, software, and procedural mechanisms to record user activity, administrative activity, system activity, and security-relevant events involving ePHI.

3. Audit logging shall be enabled before any system processing ePHI is placed into production use.

4. Systems processing ePHI shall not be approved for production deployment unless audit logging requirements have been reviewed and accepted by the Information Security function or another authorized control owner.

5. Audit logs shall record sufficient detail to support detection, investigation, and accountability, including, where technically feasible:
 - Unique user or service account identifier.
 - Date and time of activity.
 - Source location, device, network address, or session information.
 - System, application, database, file, or record accessed.
 - Type of activity performed.
 - Success or failure of the activity.
 - Privileged or administrative action performed.
 - Changes to security settings, permissions, accounts, roles, or audit configurations.

6. Systems containing ePHI shall log access to patient, member, client, or subject records where the system supports such logging.

7. The organization shall log authentication and access control events for systems containing ePHI, including successful logins, failed login attempts, account lockouts, password resets, multi-factor authentication events, session termination, and access denials.

8. The organization shall log privileged account activity in systems containing or supporting ePHI, including creation, modification, use, disablement, and deletion of administrative accounts.

9. The organization shall log changes to user access rights, role assignments, group memberships, access control lists, and authorization rules for systems containing or supporting ePHI.

10. The organization shall log changes to audit logging settings, log retention settings, time synchronization settings, security alerting rules, and log forwarding configurations.

11. The organization shall log security-relevant system events, including malware detections, firewall events, intrusion detection events, endpoint protection alerts, vulnerability exploitation attempts, unauthorized configuration changes, and abnormal system behavior affecting ePHI environments.

12. The organization shall log database activity involving ePHI where technically feasible, including privileged queries, bulk exports, direct database access, schema changes, permission changes, and access outside approved application workflows.

13. The organization shall log creation, modification, deletion, transmission, export, download, and printing of ePHI where supported by the applicable system.

14. Audit logging shall be configured in accordance with an approved logging standard or baseline that defines minimum event types, log detail, retention periods, protection requirements, and monitoring expectations.

15. Audit logs shall be protected against unauthorized access, modification, deletion, disabling, or destruction.

16. Access to audit logs shall be restricted to authorized personnel with a legitimate business need, such as security monitoring, privacy investigations, system administration, compliance review, audit, or incident response.

17. Workforce members shall not alter, delete, suppress, or disable audit logs unless explicitly authorized and documented for a legitimate operational purpose.

18. Administrative users shall not have unrestricted ability to modify or delete audit records related to their own activity without compensating controls, such as centralized log forwarding, independent monitoring, or separation of duties.

19. Systems processing ePHI shall forward security-relevant audit logs to an approved centralized logging, monitoring, or security information and event management platform where technically feasible.

20. Centralized log repositories shall be configured to preserve the integrity, availability, and confidentiality of audit records.

21. Audit logs shall be time-stamped using an approved and synchronized time source to support accurate event correlation and investigation.

22. Systems processing ePHI shall be configured to use consistent time zones or include clear time zone information in audit records.

23. Audit logs shall be retained for a period appropriate to legal, regulatory, contractual, operational, and investigative needs, and shall not be retained for less than the minimum period defined in the organization’s records retention requirements.

24. The following minimum retention requirements shall apply unless a longer period is required by law, contract, investigation, litigation hold, or organizational records retention schedule:

| Log Category | Minimum Retention Requirement | Example Sources |
|---|---:|---|
| Access logs for systems containing ePHI | [Minimum Retention Period] | EHR, practice management, billing, claims, care coordination platforms |
| Authentication and identity logs | [Minimum Retention Period] | Identity provider, directory services, single sign-on, multi-factor authentication |
| Privileged activity logs | [Minimum Retention Period] | Administrative consoles, servers, databases, cloud platforms |
| Security monitoring logs | [Minimum Retention Period] | SIEM, EDR, IDS/IPS, firewall, web gateway |
| Network and infrastructure logs supporting ePHI systems | [Minimum Retention Period] | Network devices, VPN, load balancers, cloud infrastructure |
| Audit trail exports used in investigations | Until investigation closure plus [Retention Period] | Case files, legal holds, incident response evidence repositories |

25. Audit records subject to investigation, legal hold, privacy complaint, security incident, breach assessment, or regulatory inquiry shall be preserved until formally released by Legal, Compliance, Privacy, or another authorized function.

26. Audit logs shall be reviewed on a risk-based basis to identify inappropriate access, unauthorized activity, anomalous behavior, suspicious activity, and control failures involving ePHI.

27. The organization shall define routine log review expectations, including frequency, responsible party, review method, escalation criteria, and evidence of completion.

28. At minimum, the following audit review activities shall be performed:

| Review Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence Required |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of high-risk security alerts involving ePHI systems | Daily business day or continuous monitoring where available | Security Operations | Alert records, ticket notes, disposition |
| Review of privileged access activity in critical ePHI systems | Monthly | Information Security or System Owner | Review report, exceptions, remediation actions |
| Review of user access to sensitive ePHI records where supported | Monthly or risk-based | Privacy Office or Compliance | Audit trail review log, investigation notes |
| Review of failed login trends and account lockouts | Monthly | IT Operations or Security Operations | Report, analysis, follow-up actions |
| Review of audit logging status for critical ePHI systems | Quarterly | Information Security | Control checklist, system evidence |
| Review of log retention and centralized forwarding coverage | Quarterly | Information Security | Coverage report, remediation plan |
| Review of audit control effectiveness | Annually | Privacy and Security Officer | Assessment results, corrective actions |

29. Automated alerts shall be configured for high-risk events involving ePHI systems where technically feasible.

30. High-risk events requiring alerting or prompt review shall include, as applicable:
 - Unauthorized or failed access attempts to ePHI systems.
 - Use of disabled, terminated, shared, generic, or emergency accounts.
 - Privileged access outside approved maintenance windows.
 - Unusual access to a large number of patient or member records.
 - Access to VIP, employee, family member, minor, restricted, or specially protected records where supported by business rules.
 - Access from unusual locations, devices, or networks.
 - Bulk export, download, transmission, or printing of ePHI.
 - Changes to audit logging, access control, encryption, firewall, or security monitoring settings.
 - Disabling of endpoint protection, logging agents, monitoring agents, or security tools.
 - Evidence of malware, ransomware, unauthorized scanning, or attempted exploitation.
 - Repeated failed login attempts or credential misuse indicators.
 - Use of service accounts outside expected patterns.

31. Alerts and audit review findings shall be triaged, documented, assigned, and resolved within defined timeframes based on risk.

32. Suspected inappropriate access, unauthorized disclosure, security incident, or breach involving ePHI shall be escalated in accordance with the organization’s incident response, privacy incident, and breach assessment procedures.

33. Audit logs and monitoring data shall be used only for authorized business purposes, including security operations, privacy monitoring, compliance, investigations, audits, system troubleshooting, fraud prevention, and legal support.

34. Workforce monitoring involving audit logs shall be conducted in a manner consistent with applicable law, organizational policies, human resources requirements, and privacy expectations.

35. System owners shall identify audit logging capabilities and limitations for systems processing ePHI and shall document any gaps that prevent required events from being captured.

36. Where a system cannot produce required audit logs, the organization shall implement compensating controls, such as network logging, database logging, access gateway logging, application-level monitoring, manual review procedures, or contractual requirements for vendor-provided reports.

37. Third-party service providers and business associates that host, process, maintain, or support ePHI on behalf of the organization shall maintain audit controls appropriate to the services provided.

38. Contracts or agreements with relevant third parties shall require access to audit information, security event notifications, investigation support, and evidence of audit control operation where appropriate.

39. The organization shall evaluate audit logging and monitoring capabilities during procurement, implementation, significant system change, and vendor risk assessment activities for systems involving ePHI.

40. Audit control requirements shall be included in system design, configuration, testing, and acceptance processes for new or materially changed ePHI systems.

41. Audit logs shall be backed up, replicated, or otherwise protected where required to meet availability, investigation, and retention needs.

42. Audit log storage shall be sized and monitored to prevent loss of audit records due to storage exhaustion, misconfiguration, ingestion failure, licensing constraints, or system malfunction.

43. Failures in audit logging, log forwarding, monitoring agents, or log storage for critical ePHI systems shall be treated as operational and security issues requiring timely remediation.

44. Critical audit control failures affecting ePHI systems shall be escalated to Information Security, the System Owner, and the Privacy and Security Officer.

45. Evidence of audit log reviews, alerts, investigations, exceptions, and remediation actions shall be retained in accordance with organizational records retention requirements.

46. The organization shall maintain procedures for requesting, retrieving, reviewing, exporting, preserving, and securely sharing audit logs for investigations and audits.

47. Audit logs containing ePHI or sensitive security information shall be handled, transmitted, stored, and disposed of securely.

48. Audit log exports shall be encrypted or otherwise protected when stored or transmitted outside approved logging platforms.

49. Audit data used in reports shall be limited to the minimum necessary information required for the business purpose.

50. Workforce members shall cooperate with authorized audit reviews, investigations, and requests for information related to system activity involving ePHI.

51. The organization shall provide training or awareness to relevant workforce members regarding acceptable system use, monitoring expectations, audit logging, and consequences for inappropriate access to ePHI.

52. The organization shall periodically test or validate that audit controls are operating as intended for critical systems containing ePHI.
