- Change in facility location, data center, alternate worksite, or remote work model.
- Material change to system dependencies, interfaces, integrations, or data flows.
- New or changed recovery time objectives or recovery point objectives.
- Backup failure trends, failed restore tests, or inability to meet recovery expectations.
- Completion of a tabletop exercise, technical recovery test, emergency mode exercise, or communications test with findings.
- Actual contingency plan activation, emergency mode operation, disaster recovery event, or significant outage.
- Cybersecurity incident affecting availability, integrity, backup repositories, recovery systems, or administrative access.
- Privacy incident involving contingency operations or emergency access.
- Changes in leadership, plan ownership, system ownership, vendor contacts, or escalation paths.
- Significant organizational changes, including mergers, acquisitions, new service lines, closures, or restructuring.
- Changes in legal, contractual, insurance, or regulatory obligations.
- Audit findings, risk analysis results, or management review decisions requiring plan changes.
- Lessons learned from industry incidents, threat intelligence, or healthcare sector disruptions.
- Changes to downtime forms, manual processes, or reconciliation procedures.
- Evidence that workforce members are not aware of their emergency responsibilities.

Review activities must include:

| Review Activity | Responsible Role | Minimum Frequency | Evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Confirm plan owner and approvers | Executive Sponsor | Annually | Approval record |
| Validate system inventory and covered systems | IT Lead / System Owners | Annually and upon major change | Updated inventory |
| Review criticality analysis | Plan Owner / Business Owners | Annually and upon major change | Criticality register |
| Review recovery objectives | IT Lead / Business Owners | Annually | Approved objective list |
| Review backup coverage and exceptions | Backup Administrator / Security Officer | Quarterly | Backup review record |
| Review recovery procedures | System Owners | Annually and after changes | Updated runbooks |
| Review downtime procedures | Operations Leaders | Annually | Downtime procedure attestation |
| Review vendor recovery information | Vendor Manager | Annually and at renewal | Vendor review record |
| Review contact lists | Communications Lead | Semi-annually | Contact list validation |
| Review test and exercise results | Plan Owner | After each test | Test report and action tracker |
| Review corrective actions | Plan Owner / Leadership | Monthly or quarterly | Corrective action status |
| Approve plan updates | Executive Sponsor / Security Officer | As needed | Version history and approval |

Version control must be maintained for this plan. Each update must record the version number, date, summary of changes, author, and approval.

| Version | Date | Summary of Changes | Author | Approved By |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [Date] | Initial release | [Author] | [Approver] |

HIPAA-020.title: Breach Notification Policy & Procedure
HIPAA-020.content:
# Breach Notification Policy & Procedure

| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [HIPAA-PR-###] | 1.0 | Privacy Officer | [YYYY-MM-DD] | HIPAA | Internal - Confidential |

## Purpose

This procedure defines how [Organization Name] identifies, investigates, assesses, documents, and notifies affected parties following a suspected or confirmed breach of unsecured protected health information (PHI).

The purpose is to ensure that:

- Suspected breaches are promptly reported and investigated.
- A consistent risk assessment is performed to determine whether notification is required.
- Affected individuals, regulators, and media outlets are notified when required.
- Notifications are accurate, timely, complete, and approved before release.
- Breach response activities are documented and retained for audit, legal, and compliance purposes.
- Workforce members understand their responsibilities for escalation, preservation of evidence, and cooperation during breach investigations.

For this procedure, “PHI” means individually identifiable health information that is created, received, maintained, or transmitted by [Organization Name] in any form or medium. “Unsecured PHI” means PHI that has not been rendered unusable, unreadable, or indecipherable to unauthorized persons through approved encryption, destruction, or equivalent protection methods.

## Scope

This procedure applies to:

- All workforce members of [Organization Name], including employees, contractors, temporary staff, volunteers, interns, trainees, and other persons under the organization’s direct control.
- All departments, locations, systems, applications, databases, devices, cloud services, paper records, communications channels, and business processes that create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI.
- All suspected or confirmed unauthorized access, use, disclosure, acquisition, loss, theft, alteration, or destruction of PHI.
- Breaches involving [Organization Name] as a covered entity.
- Breaches involving business associates, subcontractors, vendors, or other third parties that handle PHI on behalf of [Organization Name].
- Breaches involving electronic PHI, paper PHI, verbal disclosures, images, recordings, faxes, emails, patient portals, text messages, removable media, medical devices, backups, and logs.

This procedure covers:

- Initial reporting and triage.
- Containment and evidence preservation.
- Breach investigation.
- Risk assessment.
- Determination of whether notification is required.
- Notification to affected individuals.
- Notification to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
- Notification to prominent media outlets when required.
- Coordination with business associates and subcontractors.
- Documentation and record retention.
- Exceptions and executive escalation.

This procedure does not replace incident response procedures for security events, disaster recovery procedures, disciplinary procedures, or legal hold processes. Where those processes apply, they must be coordinated with this procedure.

## Prerequisites & Inputs

The following prerequisites must be in place to execute this procedure effectively:

| Prerequisite | Requirement | Owner |

| Privacy Officer assignment | A designated Privacy Officer must be responsible for breach assessment, notification coordination, and documentation oversight. | Executive Leadership |
| Security Officer assignment | A designated Security Officer must support technical investigation, containment, forensics, and evidence preservation for electronic PHI incidents. | Executive Leadership |
| Incident reporting channel | Workforce members must have a clear method to report suspected privacy or security incidents, such as [incident reporting system], [privacy hotline], or [security email address]. | Privacy Officer / Security Officer |
| Business associate agreements | Contracts with business associates must require timely reporting of suspected or confirmed breaches involving PHI. | Legal / Procurement |
| Breach response team | A cross-functional team must be available to support investigation, legal analysis, communications, operations, and notification. | Privacy Officer |
| Notification templates | Approved templates must be maintained for individual notices, substitute notices, regulator submissions, and media statements. | Privacy Officer / Legal / Communications |
| PHI inventory | Relevant systems, repositories, vendors, and business processes involving PHI must be known to support investigation and impact assessment. | Privacy Officer / Data Owners |
| Contact data sources | Reliable sources must exist for affected individual mailing addresses, email preferences where permitted, and next-of-kin or personal representative information where applicable. | Operations / Patient Services |
| Evidence preservation capability | Technical and administrative processes must exist to preserve logs, access records, emails, devices, paper records, and system snapshots when needed. | Security Officer / IT |

Inputs to this procedure may include:

- Workforce report of suspected unauthorized access, use, disclosure, or loss of PHI.
- Security monitoring alert.
- Vendor or business associate notification.
- Patient complaint.
- Returned mail, misdirected communication, or fax transmission report.
- Lost or stolen device report.
- Audit log anomaly.
- Law enforcement notice.
- Media inquiry.
- Regulator inquiry.
- Discovery during internal audit, compliance review, litigation, or quality assurance activity.

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

1. **Report the suspected breach immediately**

 1.1. Any workforce member who becomes aware of a suspected or confirmed unauthorized access, use, disclosure, loss, theft, or improper handling of PHI must report it immediately through one of the approved reporting channels:

 - [Incident reporting system]
 - [Privacy Officer email address]
 - [Security Operations email address]
 - [Privacy hotline number]
 - Direct manager escalation, if the standard channel is unavailable

 1.2. Workforce members must not delay reporting while attempting to confirm all facts.

 1.3. Workforce members must not delete, alter, forward, print, copy, or further disclose potentially affected PHI unless instructed by the Privacy Officer, Security Officer, or Legal Counsel.

 1.4. If a business associate reports a suspected breach, the recipient must forward the notice to the Privacy Officer and Legal Counsel immediately.

2. **Open a breach investigation record**

 2.1. The Privacy Officer or delegated incident coordinator must open a breach investigation record in [case management system] within one business day of discovery.

 2.2. Assign a unique case number.

 2.3. Record the discovery date. The discovery date is the date the incident was first known, or reasonably should have been known, to [Organization Name] or any workforce member other than the person who committed the act.

 2.4. Classify the case initially as one of the following:

 | Initial Classification | Description |
 |---|---|
 | Privacy incident - under review | Possible improper use or disclosure of PHI requiring investigation. |
 | Security incident involving PHI - under review | Technical event that may involve electronic PHI. |
 | Confirmed non-breach | Event involving PHI that does not meet breach criteria after review. |
 | Confirmed breach | Impermissible use or disclosure of unsecured PHI requiring notification unless an exception applies. |
 | Business associate reported event | Event reported by a third party that requires coordination and verification. |

 2.5. Notify the Security Officer when electronic PHI, systems, devices, networks, credentials, malware, hacking, cloud services, or logs may be involved.

 2.6. Notify Legal Counsel when facts suggest potential notification obligations, litigation risk, law enforcement involvement, contractual issues, or media exposure.

3. **Perform immediate containment and preservation**

 3.1. The Privacy Officer and Security Officer must coordinate containment actions appropriate to the incident.

 3.2. Containment may include:

 - Disabling or suspending user accounts.
 - Resetting passwords or revoking tokens.
 - Blocking unauthorized access.
 - Retrieving misdirected mail, fax, email, or documents.
 - Requesting deletion and written attestation from unintended recipients.
 - Isolating affected systems or devices.
 - Preserving email messages, logs, database records, call recordings, audit trails, and access records.
 - Securing paper records or physical evidence.
 - Contacting vendors to suspend processing or preserve evidence.
 - Placing relevant records under legal hold.

 3.3. Containment actions must be documented with date, time, owner, action taken, and outcome.

 3.4. Evidence must be preserved in a manner that maintains integrity, confidentiality, and chain of custody.

4. **Determine whether PHI was involved**

 4.1. The Privacy Officer must determine whether the information involved is PHI.

 4.2. Information is PHI when it relates to an individual’s past, present, or future health condition, health care, or payment for health care and can identify the individual directly or indirectly.

 4.3. Examples of PHI include, but are not limited to:

 - Patient name with appointment, diagnosis, treatment, provider, medication, lab, imaging, claim, or billing information.
 - Medical record number.
 - Health plan beneficiary number.
 - Account number linked to health care services.
 - Prescription information.
 - Clinical notes.
 - Images or recordings connected to care.
 - Device identifiers linked to a patient.
 - Dates of service or admission associated with an individual.
 - Demographic information maintained in a health care context.

 4.4. If no PHI was involved, document the conclusion, close the breach assessment, and route the event to any other applicable process.

5. **Determine whether the PHI was unsecured**

 5.1. The Security Officer must determine whether the PHI was protected by approved safeguards that rendered it unusable, unreadable, or indecipherable to unauthorized persons.

 5.2. For electronic PHI, verify whether it was encrypted using an approved method at the time of the incident.

 5.3. For paper or physical media, verify whether the information was destroyed using approved secure destruction methods before exposure.

 5.4. If PHI was secured using approved methods and there is no evidence that the protection was compromised, notification may not be required. The decision must be documented.

 5.5. If PHI was unsecured, continue the breach assessment.

6. **Assess whether the use or disclosure was impermissible**

 6.1. The Privacy Officer, with Legal Counsel as needed, must determine whether the incident involved an impermissible use or disclosure of PHI.

 6.2. Examples of potentially impermissible events include:

 - PHI sent to the wrong patient.
 - PHI mailed, faxed, or emailed to the wrong recipient.
 - Employee access to a record without a job-related reason.
 - Lost or stolen unencrypted laptop, phone, USB drive, or paper file.
 - Unauthorized disclosure to family member, employer, attorney, insurer, or third party.
 - Cyberattack involving systems that store or transmit PHI.
 - Business associate disclosure outside permitted purposes.
 - Public exposure of PHI on a website, portal, shared drive, or collaboration platform.

 6.3. If the use or disclosure was permitted, document the basis and close the breach assessment unless further corrective action is required.

7. **Check whether a recognized exception applies**

 7.1. The Privacy Officer must determine whether the incident fits a recognized exception where notification is not required.

 7.2. Exceptions may include:

 | Exception Type | Conditions to Confirm |
 |---|---|
 | Unintentional internal access or use | The access or use was made in good faith, within the workforce member’s authority, and did not result in further improper use or disclosure. |
 | Inadvertent disclosure between authorized persons | The disclosure occurred between persons authorized to access PHI within the organization or an organized health care arrangement, and the information was not further misused. |
 | Recipient could not reasonably retain the information | The unauthorized recipient could not reasonably have retained the PHI, such as a letter returned unopened or a document immediately retrieved before review. |

 7.3. If an exception applies, document the supporting facts and evidence.

 7.4. If no exception applies, proceed to the breach risk assessment.

8. **Conduct the breach risk assessment**

 8.1. The Privacy Officer must perform a documented risk assessment to determine the probability that the PHI has been compromised.

 8.2. The assessment must evaluate, at minimum, the following factors:

 | Risk Factor | Assessment Questions | Evidence Examples |
 |---|---|---|
 | Nature and extent of PHI | What types of PHI were involved? Was clinical, financial, identity, genetic, behavioral health, substance use, HIV, reproductive health, or other sensitive information included? Could the information increase risk of identity theft, stigma, discrimination, financial harm, or personal harm? | Data samples, file inventories, screenshots, records, system extracts. |
 | Identifiability | Could the individual be identified directly or indirectly? Were names, addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers, photographs, or other identifiers included? | Document review, metadata review, recipient confirmation. |
 | Unauthorized person | Who received, accessed, acquired, or used the PHI? Is the person obligated to protect confidentiality? Is the person known, trustworthy, or unknown? | Recipient details, contracts, attestations, access logs. |
 | Actual acquisition or viewing | Is there evidence that the PHI was actually accessed, viewed, downloaded, copied, printed, saved, transmitted, or retained? | Audit logs, email read receipts, download logs, device forensics, interviews. |
 | Mitigation | Was the PHI recovered, deleted, destroyed, returned, or otherwise contained? Did the recipient provide reliable written confirmation? | Deletion attestation, retrieval proof, forensic report, courier record. |

 8.3. The assessment must result in one of the following conclusions:

 | Conclusion | Meaning | Required Action |
 |---|---|---|
 | Low probability of compromise | Evidence supports that PHI was not likely compromised. | Document rationale, approve closure, complete corrective actions. |
 | More than low probability of compromise | Evidence does not support a low probability conclusion. | Treat as a breach requiring notification. |
 | Insufficient information | Facts are incomplete or unavailable. | Treat conservatively, escalate to Legal Counsel and Executive Leadership, and determine notification approach. |

 8.4. The assessment must not be based solely on whether harm has been proven. The focus is whether the PHI was compromised.

 8.5. If the assessment determines that notification is not required, the Privacy Officer must document the rationale and obtain Legal Counsel review for moderate or high sensitivity incidents.

9. **Determine affected individuals**

 9.1. The Privacy Officer, Data Owner, and relevant department must identify all individuals whose unsecured PHI was involved.

 9.2. The affected population must be validated through reliable sources, such as:

 - System audit logs.
 - Database queries.
 - File inventories.
 - Email distribution lists.
 - Mailing records.
 - Fax confirmation logs.
 - Vendor reports.
 - Paper file tracking records.
 - Access reports.
 - Forensic analysis.

 9.3. The affected individual list must include, where available:

 | Data Element | Purpose |
 |---|---|
 | Full name | Individual identification and notice preparation. |
 | Mailing address | Written notification. |
 | Email address | Electronic notice only where permitted and authorized. |
 | Phone number | Follow-up support or substitute contact where appropriate. |
 | Date of birth | Validation and deduplication. |
 | Medical record or account number | Internal identification only; avoid including in notice unless necessary. |
 | Personal representative details | Notification where the individual is deceased, a minor, or represented by another authorized person. |
 | Type of PHI involved | Notice content and risk assessment. |
 | State of residence | Identification of additional state notification considerations. |

 9.4. The affected individual list must be stored securely and access must be restricted to authorized personnel.

10. **Establish notification deadlines**

 10.1. The Privacy Officer must calculate notification deadlines from the discovery date.

 10.2. Notifications must be made without unreasonable delay and within the required outer timeframe.

 10.3. The following timeline must be used:

 | Notification Type | Trigger | Timing Requirement | Owner |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Individual notification | Breach of unsecured PHI affecting one or more individuals. | Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days from discovery. | Privacy Officer |
 | Regulator notification - 500 or more individuals | Breach affecting 500 or more individuals. | Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days from discovery. | Privacy Officer / Legal |
 | Regulator notification - fewer than 500 individuals | Breach affecting fewer than 500 individuals. | Maintain log and submit no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered. | Privacy Officer |
 | Media notification | Breach affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction. | Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days from discovery. | Communications / Privacy Officer |
 | Business associate notification to [Organization Name] | Business associate discovers breach involving [Organization Name] PHI. | As soon as possible and within the timeframe required by contract. | Business Associate |
 | Law enforcement delay | Law enforcement requests a delay in notification. | Delay only as directed and documented. | Legal Counsel |

 10.4. The Privacy Officer must create a notification schedule and track progress to completion.

11. **Decide whether law enforcement delay applies**

 11.1. If law enforcement states that notification would impede a criminal investigation or cause damage to national security, Legal Counsel must review the request.

 11.2. A written request from law enforcement must be retained and followed according to its stated duration.

 11.3. If a law enforcement request is made orally, Legal Counsel must document:

 - Name and agency of the official.
 - Date and time of request.
 - Scope of requested delay.
 - Reason provided.
 - Expected duration.

 11.4. Notification may be delayed only to the extent supported by the law enforcement request.

 11.5. The Privacy Officer must resume notification promptly when the delay expires or is lifted.

12. **Prepare individual notifications**

 12.1. The Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, and Communications must prepare written notice for affected individuals.

 12.2. Individual notices must be written in plain language and include:

 - A brief description of what happened.
 - The date of the breach, if known.
 - The date the breach was discovered.
 - The types of PHI involved.
 - Steps individuals should take to protect themselves.
 - What [Organization Name] is doing to investigate, mitigate harm, and prevent recurrence.
 - Contact procedures for questions, including toll-free number if available, email address, website, and postal address.
 - Any offered support services, such as credit monitoring, identity protection, call center support, or fraud guidance, where appropriate.

 12.3. Individual notices must not include unnecessary PHI.

 12.4. The tone must be accurate, transparent, respectful, and non-speculative.

 12.5. Notices must be approved by the Privacy Officer and Legal Counsel before distribution.

 12.6. Executive Leadership approval is required for breaches involving any of the following:

 - 500 or more individuals.
 - Sensitive diagnoses or specially protected information.
 - Cyberattack or extortion.
 - Media interest.
 - Regulator inquiry.
 - Material reputational impact.
 - High likelihood of identity theft or financial harm.
 - Significant operational disruption.

13. **Deliver individual notifications**

 13.1. Written notice must be sent by first-class mail to the affected individual’s last known address unless the individual has agreed to receive notices electronically.

 13.2. If the individual is deceased, notice must be sent to the next of kin or personal representative if known.

 13.3. If the individual is a minor or has a personal representative, notice must be sent to the authorized representative as appropriate.

 13.4. If there is insufficient or out-of-date contact information for fewer than 10 affected individuals, substitute notice may be provided by an alternative written, telephone, or electronic method.

 13.5. If there is insufficient or out-of-date contact information for 10 or more affected individuals, substitute notice must be provided through a conspicuous posting on [Organization Name]’s website or through major print or broadcast media in the affected area. The substitute notice must include contact information that remains available for at least 90 days.

 13.6. If the breach creates possible imminent misuse of unsecured PHI, additional urgent notice by telephone or other appropriate means may be provided in addition to written notice.

 13.7. Mailing files, vendor files, returned mail, publication records, call center scripts, and delivery evidence must be retained.

14. **Notify the regulator**

 14.1. The Privacy Officer must prepare regulator notification when a breach of unsecured PHI is confirmed.

 14.2. For breaches involving 500 or more individuals, notification must be submitted within the required timeframe and aligned with individual notification.

 14.3. For breaches involving fewer than 500 individuals, the Privacy Officer must maintain a breach log and submit required information according to the annual reporting deadline.

 14.4. Regulator submissions must be reviewed by Legal Counsel before submission.

 14.5. The submission must accurately reflect:

 - Covered entity name.
 - Contact information.
 - Breach type.
 - Location of breached information.
 - Number of individuals affected.
 - Date of breach.
 - Date of discovery.
 - Type of PHI involved.
 - Safeguards in place before the incident.
 - Actions taken in response.
 - Notification status.
 - Mitigation measures.
 - Corrective actions.

 14.6. Confirmation of submission must be retained in the breach case file.

15. **Notify media when required**

 15.1. If the breach affects more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction, the Communications Lead, Privacy Officer, and Legal Counsel must prepare notice to prominent media outlets serving the affected area.

 15.2. Media notice must be provided without unreasonable delay and within the required timeframe.

 15.3. The media notice must include the same general information required for individual notice, while avoiding unnecessary PHI and respecting individual privacy.

 15.4. Media statements, press releases, talking points, FAQs, website postings, and call center scripts must be approved by Legal Counsel and Executive Leadership before release.

 15.5. Communications must monitor media inquiries and coordinate all responses through the approved spokesperson.

16. **Coordinate business associate breach response**

 16.1. When a business associate reports a breach involving [Organization Name] PHI, the Privacy Officer must request sufficient information to assess and complete notification obligations.

 16.2. The business associate must provide, as available:

 | Required Information | Description |
 |---|---|
 | Description of incident | What happened and how it occurred. |
 | Discovery date | When the business associate discovered the incident. |
 | Breach date or date range | When the incident occurred, if known. |
 | Individuals affected | Names and contact information where available. |
 | PHI involved | Categories of information involved. |
 | Unauthorized recipient or actor | Known details of the recipient or threat actor. |
 | Containment actions | Actions taken to stop further disclosure or access. |
 | Mitigation actions | Retrieval, deletion, forensic remediation, monitoring, or other mitigation. |
 | Risk assessment | Business associate’s analysis and supporting evidence. |
 | Notification support | Whether the business associate will support mailing, call center, credit monitoring, or other services. |

 16.3. [Organization Name] remains responsible for ensuring required notifications are completed unless the business associate agreement assigns specific notification duties.

 16.4. Legal Counsel must review the contract to determine responsibility for notification costs, cooperation duties, indemnification, and regulator communication.

 16.5. Business associate performance during breach response must be documented and considered in vendor risk management.

17. **Address state, contractual, and special information requirements**

 17.1. Legal Counsel must assess whether additional notification obligations apply based on:

 - State residence of affected individuals.
 - Types of information involved, such as Social Security numbers, payment card data, driver’s license numbers, financial accounts, biometric data, or online credentials.
 - Substance use treatment records.
 - Mental health information.
 - HIV, genetic, reproductive health, or other sensitive categories.
 - Contractual commitments.
 - Payment card network requirements.
 - Law enforcement or public health considerations.

 17.2. If additional requirements apply, Legal Counsel must integrate them into the notification plan.

 17.3. Where multiple requirements apply, [Organization Name] must meet the most protective applicable obligation unless Legal Counsel approves a different approach.

18. **Implement mitigation and corrective actions**

 18.1. The Privacy Officer and responsible business owner must identify corrective actions to reduce the likelihood of recurrence.

 18.2. Corrective actions may include:

 - Workforce retraining.
 - Disciplinary action.
 - Access removal or role adjustment.
 - Encryption deployment.
 - Email loss prevention rules.
 - Fax number validation.
 - Mailing quality checks.
 - Minimum necessary process changes.
 - System configuration changes.
 - Audit logging improvements.
 - Vendor remediation plan.
 - Contract amendments.
 - Updated procedures or forms.
 - Enhanced monitoring.
 - Secure disposal improvements.

 18.3. Corrective actions must be assigned an owner, due date, and completion evidence.

 18.4. High-risk corrective actions must be tracked to closure through [risk register / compliance action tracker].

19. **Close the breach case**

 19.1. The Privacy Officer may close the case only after:

 - Investigation is complete or sufficiently resolved.
 - Breach determination is documented.
 - Required notifications are completed or scheduled.
 - Regulator submissions are completed or logged for annual reporting.
 - Media notification is completed, if required.
 - Business associate responsibilities are documented, if applicable.
 - Corrective actions are completed or formally tracked.
 - Legal Counsel has reviewed closure for reportable breaches.
 - Records are stored in the approved repository.

 19.2. The final case summary must include:

 | Case Summary Field | Required Content |
 |---|---|
 | Case number | Unique breach investigation identifier. |
 | Discovery date | Date the incident was first known or reasonably should have been known. |
 | Incident description | Concise factual summary. |
 | PHI involved | Categories and sensitivity of PHI. |
 | Individuals affected | Final count or reasonable estimate. |
 | Root cause | Human error, process failure, technical control failure, malicious activity, vendor failure, or other cause. |
 | Risk assessment conclusion | Low probability of compromise, reportable breach, exception, or secured PHI. |
 | Notification decision | Who was notified, how, and when. |
 | Mitigation | Actions taken to reduce potential harm. |
 | Corrective actions | Actions assigned and status. |
 | Approvals | Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, and other required approvers. |

20. **Perform post-incident lessons learned**

 20.1. For reportable breaches and significant non-reportable incidents, the Privacy Officer must conduct a lessons learned review within 30 days after closure or stabilization.

 20.2. The review should include Privacy, Security, Legal, Communications, Operations, affected department leaders, and business associate representatives where applicable.

 20.3. Lessons learned must evaluate:

 - Timeliness of reporting and escalation.
 - Adequacy of evidence preservation.
 - Accuracy of affected individual identification.
 - Notification quality and timeliness.
 - Effectiveness of containment.
 - Root cause and contributing factors.
 - Workforce training gaps.
 - Technical control gaps.
 - Vendor performance.
 - Policy or procedure improvements.

 20.4. Improvement actions must be assigned and tracked to completion.

Records containing PHI or sensitive investigation details must be access-controlled, encrypted where applicable, and shared only with personnel who have a need to know.

## Exceptions & Escalation

Exceptions to this procedure are permitted only when approved by the Privacy Officer and Legal Counsel, and only when consistent with applicable law, contractual obligations, and the protection of affected individuals.

Examples of situations requiring escalation:

| Escalation Trigger | Escalate To | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Suspected breach involving 500 or more individuals | Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, Executive Leadership, Communications Lead | Immediately upon reasonable suspicion |
| Cyberattack, ransomware, extortion, or threat actor activity involving PHI | Security Officer, Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, Executive Leadership | Immediately |
| Media inquiry or public exposure | Communications Lead, Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, Executive Leadership | Immediately |
| Regulator or law enforcement inquiry | Legal Counsel, Privacy Officer, Executive Leadership | Immediately |
| Business associate delay or refusal to provide information | Legal Counsel, Privacy Officer, Vendor Management, Executive Leadership | Within one business day |
| Uncertainty about whether notification is required | Legal Counsel, Privacy Officer | Before closure or notification decision |
| Potential imminent misuse of PHI | Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, Executive Leadership, Communications Lead | Immediately |
| Sensitive PHI categories involved | Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, Executive Leadership as needed | As soon as identified |
| Inability to meet notification timeline | Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, Executive Leadership | As soon as risk is known |
| Workforce member misconduct | Privacy Officer, Human Resources, Legal Counsel | As soon as substantiated |
| Evidence tampering or failure to cooperate | Legal Counsel, Human Resources, Security Officer | Immediately |
| Significant patient safety concern | Privacy Officer, Clinical Leadership, Legal Counsel | Immediately |

If an exception or escalation decision is made, the breach case file must document:

- The issue requiring exception or escalation.
- Facts known at the time.
- Decision made.
- Decision owner.
- Legal review, if applicable.
- Alternative actions taken.
- Impact on notification timing.
- Follow-up actions.

No workforce member may suppress, delay, or discourage reporting of a suspected breach. Retaliation against any person who reports a suspected breach in good faith is prohibited.

## Review

This procedure must be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a significant change to:

- HIPAA breach notification requirements.
- Organizational structure or assigned privacy/security roles.
- Systems or processes that create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI.
- Business associate relationships.
- Incident response processes.
- Notification vendors or communication channels.
- Lessons learned from a breach or significant privacy incident.
- Regulatory guidance or enforcement expectations.
- Applicable state breach notification requirements.

The Privacy Officer is responsible for coordinating the review with the Security Officer, Legal Counsel, Communications Lead, Operations, Human Resources, IT, and other stakeholders as appropriate.

Review activities must include:

- Confirming that breach response roles remain current.
- Validating reporting channels and contact lists.
- Testing notification templates for completeness and readability.
- Reviewing breach logs and incident trends.
- Confirming that annual regulator reporting is completed when required.
- Assessing whether corrective actions from prior incidents were completed.
- Updating procedures based on tabletop exercises or actual incidents.
- Verifying that workforce training references current reporting expectations.

Evidence of review must be retained, including the review date, participants, summary of changes, approval records, and updated version history.

| Version | Date | Summary of Changes | Approved By |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Initial release. | [Approver Name / Title] |

HIPAA-021.title: Business Associate Agreement (BAA) Template
HIPAA-021.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [HIPAA-BAA-TPL-001] | 1.0 | Privacy Officer / Legal Counsel | [Effective Date] | HIPAA | Confidential |

## Purpose

This Business Associate Agreement (BAA) Template is used to establish written assurances between [Organization Name] and a Business Associate that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits Protected Health Information (PHI) on behalf of [Organization Name].

The purpose of this template is to ensure that every Business Associate relationship includes documented obligations for safeguarding PHI, limiting use and disclosure, reporting privacy or security incidents, managing subcontractors, supporting individual rights, enabling oversight, and returning or destroying PHI when the relationship ends.

This template must be completed, reviewed, approved, and executed before PHI is disclosed to or accessed by a Business Associate, unless an approved exception has been documented by the Privacy Officer and Legal Counsel.

## Instructions

1. **Use this template for every Business Associate relationship.** 
 Complete this template whenever a vendor, contractor, consultant, service provider, platform, or other third party will create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI on behalf of [Organization Name].

2. **Do not use this template for ordinary service providers that do not access PHI.** 
 If a vendor has no access to PHI and does not perform services involving PHI, a BAA may not be required. The Privacy Officer or Legal Counsel must confirm the determination.

3. **Complete all required fields before routing for approval.** 
 Fields marked “Yes” in the Required column must be completed before the BAA is submitted for review or signature.

4. **Attach supporting documents where applicable.** 
 Attach the underlying services agreement, statement of work, data protection addendum, security questionnaire, risk assessment, subcontractor list, incident response contact details, and any relevant technical documentation.

5. **Confirm that the Business Associate’s services are accurately described.** 
 The BAA must clearly describe the services being provided and the specific PHI-related activities the Business Associate is permitted to perform.

6. **Limit PHI use and disclosure to the minimum necessary.** 
 The template must specify the permitted uses and disclosures of PHI and must not grant broad or unrestricted access unless justified by the services.

7. **Address electronic PHI safeguards.** 
 If the Business Associate will create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic PHI, the BAA must require appropriate administrative, physical, and technical safeguards.

8. **Include breach and incident reporting expectations.** 
 Reporting timelines, contact methods, required notification content, and cooperation obligations must be documented.

9. **Document subcontractor obligations.** 
 The Business Associate must ensure that any subcontractor with access to PHI agrees to written restrictions and safeguards that are no less protective than those in the BAA.

10. **Ensure alignment with the master agreement.** 
 The BAA must be consistent with the underlying contract, statement of work, data processing terms, insurance requirements, indemnity provisions, and termination rights.

11. **Do not alter standard legal language without approval.** 
 Any deviation from approved BAA language must be reviewed and approved by Legal Counsel and the Privacy Officer before execution.

12. **Retain the executed agreement.** 
 The fully executed BAA and supporting approval records must be stored in the approved contract repository.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| BAA Record ID | Text | Yes | Enter the unique internal tracking number for this BAA, such as [BAA-YYYY-###]. |
| Request Date | Date | Yes | Enter the date the BAA review was initiated. |
| Requesting Department | Text | Yes | Identify the department requesting the Business Associate relationship. |
| Business Owner | Name / Role | Yes | Enter the internal owner responsible for managing the relationship and confirming the services are needed. |
| Privacy Officer | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the person responsible for privacy review and approval. |
| Legal Reviewer | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the attorney or legal representative reviewing the agreement. |
| Security Reviewer | Name / Role | Conditional | Required when electronic PHI will be created, received, maintained, or transmitted by the Business Associate. |
| Procurement Contact | Name / Role | Conditional | Required if the agreement is processed through procurement or vendor management. |
| Business Associate Legal Name | Text | Yes | Enter the full legal name of the Business Associate as it should appear in the agreement. |
| Business Associate DBA or Trade Name | Text | No | Enter any “doing business as” name, product name, or service brand associated with the Business Associate. |
| Business Associate Address | Text | Yes | Enter the legal notice address for the Business Associate. |
| Business Associate Primary Contact | Name / Contact Details | Yes | Enter the main commercial or account contact. |
| Business Associate Privacy Contact | Name / Contact Details | Yes | Enter the individual or team responsible for privacy matters. |
| Business Associate Security Contact | Name / Contact Details | Conditional | Required where electronic PHI is involved. Include email, phone, and escalation details. |
| Business Associate Incident Reporting Contact | Name / Contact Details | Yes | Enter the required notification address for suspected or confirmed privacy or security incidents. |
| Covered Entity / Organization Legal Name | Text | Yes | Enter the full legal name of [Organization Name] or applicable covered entity. |
| Covered Entity Address | Text | Yes | Enter the legal notice address for [Organization Name]. |
| Underlying Agreement Title | Text | Yes | Enter the name of the master services agreement, statement of work, order form, purchase agreement, or other related contract. |
| Underlying Agreement Effective Date | Date | Yes | Enter the effective date of the related agreement. |
| BAA Effective Date | Date | Yes | Enter the date the BAA becomes effective. This should be on or before any PHI access begins. |
| BAA Term | Text / Date Range | Yes | State whether the BAA remains in effect for the duration of the underlying agreement or specify a fixed term. |
| Description of Services | Long Text | Yes | Describe the services the Business Associate will provide, including how those services involve PHI. |
| Business Associate Role | Selection | Yes | Select the role, such as claims processing, billing support, cloud hosting, analytics, transcription, legal services, consulting, utilization review, software support, data storage, call center, or other service. |
| PHI Access Required | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether the Business Associate requires access to PHI to perform services. If “No,” confirm whether a BAA is necessary. |
| Types of PHI Involved | Multi-select / Long Text | Yes | Identify the categories of PHI involved, such as demographics, medical records, claims data, billing data, treatment information, appointment information, lab data, images, member data, patient identifiers, or payment information. |
| Electronic PHI Involved | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether electronic PHI will be created, received, maintained, or transmitted. |
| Paper PHI Involved | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether paper records or printed PHI will be used. |
| Verbal PHI Involved | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether PHI will be discussed by phone, video, in-person, or other verbal channels. |
| Volume of PHI | Selection / Text | Yes | Estimate the quantity of PHI involved, such as single record, limited dataset, department-level, enterprise-level, or ongoing bulk access. |
| Patient / Member Population Affected | Text | Conditional | Required when a defined population is involved. Describe the affected patient, member, client, or workforce group. |
| Systems or Applications Used | Text | Conditional | Required if systems, portals, databases, APIs, file transfer tools, or hosted platforms will process PHI. |
| Data Hosting Location | Text | Conditional | Required where PHI is hosted or stored by the Business Associate or its subcontractors. Identify country, region, and hosting provider if known. |
| Remote Access Required | Yes / No | Conditional | Required if the Business Associate will access [Organization Name] systems remotely. |
| Data Transmission Method | Text | Yes | Describe how PHI will be exchanged, such as secure portal, encrypted email, secure file transfer, API, VPN, EHR access, courier, or other approved method. |
| Encryption Requirements | Text | Conditional | Required when electronic PHI is stored or transmitted. State encryption expectations for data in transit and at rest. |
| Authentication Requirements | Text | Conditional | Required for system access. Describe access controls such as unique user IDs, multi-factor authentication, least privilege access, and account review. |
| Minimum Necessary Access | Long Text | Yes | Describe how access to PHI will be limited to the minimum information needed for the services. |
| Permitted Uses of PHI | Long Text | Yes | State the specific purposes for which the Business Associate may use PHI, such as performing contracted services, managing operations as permitted by the agreement, or fulfilling legal obligations. |
| Permitted Disclosures of PHI | Long Text | Yes | State the specific circumstances under which the Business Associate may disclose PHI, such as to approved subcontractors, as directed by [Organization Name], or as required by law. |
| Prohibited Uses and Disclosures | Long Text | Yes | State that the Business Associate may not use or disclose PHI except as allowed by the BAA, the underlying agreement, written instructions from [Organization Name], or applicable law. |
| Sale of PHI Prohibited | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm that the Business Associate is prohibited from selling PHI unless specifically authorized in writing and legally permitted. |
| Marketing Use Prohibited | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm that PHI may not be used for marketing unless expressly authorized by [Organization Name] and legally permitted. |
| Use of PHI for Product Development or AI Tools | Long Text | Conditional | Required if the Business Associate uses analytics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, software improvement, model training, or product development. Specify restrictions and approval requirements. |
| De-Identification Allowed | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the Business Associate may de-identify PHI. If allowed, specify permitted purposes and method requirements. |
| Limited Data Set Use | Yes / No | Conditional | Required if a limited data set will be used. Identify the purpose and any separate data use requirements. |
| Business Associate Safeguards | Long Text | Yes | Require administrative, physical, and technical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity, volume, and format of PHI. |
| Security Program Confirmation | Yes / No | Conditional | Required when electronic PHI is involved. Confirm whether the Business Associate maintains a written information security program. |
| Workforce Access Controls | Long Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to limit workforce access to authorized personnel with a legitimate need to know. |
| Workforce Training | Text | Yes | Require privacy and security training for workforce members who handle PHI. |
| Sanctions and Workforce Accountability | Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to apply appropriate disciplinary or corrective action for workforce misuse of PHI. |
| Incident Detection and Response | Long Text | Yes | Require processes to detect, investigate, mitigate, and document suspected or confirmed unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of PHI. |
| Incident Reporting Timeline | Text | Yes | State the required timeline for reporting suspected or confirmed incidents to [Organization Name]. Use the organization’s standard requirement, such as without unreasonable delay and no later than [number] calendar days after discovery. |
| Breach Notification Content | Long Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to provide available facts, including individuals affected, PHI involved, incident dates, discovery date, cause, containment steps, mitigation actions, and contact person. |
| Ongoing Incident Updates | Long Text | Yes | Require timely updates as additional information becomes available until investigation and remediation are complete. |
| Mitigation Responsibilities | Long Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to mitigate harmful effects of any improper use, disclosure, security incident, or breach involving PHI. |
| Cooperation with Notifications | Long Text | Yes | Require cooperation with [Organization Name] in assessing notification obligations and supporting required notices to affected individuals, regulators, or other parties. |
| Subcontractors Used | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether subcontractors will create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI on behalf of the Business Associate. |
| Subcontractor List | Table / Attachment | Conditional | Required if subcontractors will access PHI. Include legal name, service provided, location, PHI involved, and confirmation of written obligations. |
| Subcontractor Approval Required | Yes / No | Yes | State whether prior written approval from [Organization Name] is required before subcontractors may access PHI. |
| Subcontractor Written Agreement | Yes / No | Conditional | Required when subcontractors are used. Confirm that subcontractors must be bound by written terms at least as protective as this BAA. |
| Individual Access Support | Long Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to assist [Organization Name] in responding to requests by individuals to access their PHI, where applicable. |
| Amendment Support | Long Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to support requests to amend PHI, where applicable. |
| Accounting of Disclosures Support | Long Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to maintain and provide information needed for an accounting of disclosures, where applicable. |
| Restriction Requests Support | Long Text | Conditional | Required if the Business Associate performs services that may be affected by individual restriction requests. |
| Confidential Communications Support | Long Text | Conditional | Required if the Business Associate communicates directly with individuals on behalf of [Organization Name]. |
| Direct Contact with Individuals | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether the Business Associate will communicate directly with patients, members, clients, or other individuals using PHI. |
| Notice of Privacy Practices Alignment | Yes / No | Conditional | Required if the Business Associate performs services involving individual communications or uses of PHI affected by [Organization Name] privacy notices. |
| Access to Books and Records | Long Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to make relevant records available to [Organization Name] and legally authorized oversight bodies when required for compliance verification. |
| Audit Rights | Long Text | Yes | State whether [Organization Name] may request evidence of compliance, review safeguards, assess incident records, or conduct reasonable audits. |
| Compliance Documentation | Long Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to maintain documentation showing compliance with privacy and security obligations. |
| Cybersecurity Insurance | Text | Conditional | Required if mandated by procurement, legal, risk management, or contract requirements. State minimum coverage and evidence requirements. |
| Indemnification | Text | Conditional | Complete as directed by Legal Counsel. Address responsibility for losses, claims, penalties, costs, or expenses resulting from the Business Associate’s acts or omissions. |
| Limitation of Liability Alignment | Text | Conditional | Required where the underlying agreement limits liability. Legal Counsel must confirm whether privacy, security, breach, confidentiality, and indemnity obligations are excluded from any cap. |
| Return or Destruction of PHI | Long Text | Yes | Require the Business Associate to return or destroy PHI at termination or expiration if feasible and as instructed by [Organization Name]. |
| Retained PHI After Termination | Long Text | Conditional | Required if return or destruction is not feasible. State that retained PHI remains protected and may only be used or disclosed for limited purposes that make return or destruction infeasible. |
| Certificate of Destruction Required | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the Business Associate must provide written certification that PHI has been destroyed. |
| Termination for Cause | Long Text | Yes | State that [Organization Name] may terminate the BAA and related services for material violation of privacy or security obligations, subject to applicable cure rights approved by Legal Counsel. |
| Transition Assistance | Long Text | Conditional | Required when services are operationally critical. Describe required cooperation to transition services without compromising PHI. |
| Survival of Obligations | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm that relevant confidentiality, privacy, security, return/destruction, and audit obligations survive termination as needed. |
| Governing Law / Venue | Text | Conditional | Complete as directed by Legal Counsel and align with the underlying agreement. |
| Order of Precedence | Text | Yes | State how conflicts between the BAA and underlying agreement will be resolved, ensuring PHI protections are not weakened. |
| Notice Method | Text | Yes | Specify approved methods for legal and incident notices, such as email plus written notice, secure portal notification, or overnight delivery. |
| Required Attachments | Checklist | Yes | Attach the underlying agreement, service description, security review, risk assessment, subcontractor list, incident contact details, and approved deviations if applicable. |
| Privacy Risk Assessment Completed | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether privacy risk review has been completed before approval. |
| Security Risk Assessment Completed | Yes / No | Conditional | Required when electronic PHI is involved or the Business Associate connects to systems, hosts data, or processes large volumes of PHI. |
| Vendor Due Diligence Completed | Yes / No | Conditional | Required if the Business Associate is subject to vendor risk management review. |
| Exceptions or Deviations | Long Text | Conditional | Required if any standard BAA language, safeguard requirement, reporting timeline, subcontractor requirement, or termination right has been changed. |
| Exception Approval | Name / Date | Conditional | Required where exceptions or deviations exist. Must include Privacy Officer and Legal Counsel approval. |
| Final BAA Version | Attachment / Link | Yes | Attach or link the final approved version before signature. |
| Signature Authority - Organization | Name / Title | Yes | Identify the person authorized to sign on behalf of [Organization Name]. |
| Signature Authority - Business Associate | Name / Title | Yes | Identify the person authorized to sign on behalf of the Business Associate. |
| Organization Signature Date | Date | Yes | Enter the date signed by [Organization Name]. |
| Business Associate Signature Date | Date | Yes | Enter the date signed by the Business Associate. |
| Fully Executed Agreement Stored | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the signed BAA has been uploaded to the approved contract repository. |
| Repository Location | Link / Text | Yes | Enter the storage location or contract management system record link. |
| Renewal / Review Date | Date | Yes | Enter the next scheduled review date, renewal date, or trigger for reassessment. |
| Relationship End Date | Date | Conditional | Complete when the relationship terminates or services end. |
| PHI Returned or Destroyed | Yes / No / Not Feasible | Conditional | Required at termination. Document whether PHI was returned, destroyed, or retained because return/destruction was not feasible. |
| Termination Certification Received | Yes / No | Conditional | Required if destruction or return certification is required. |
| Closure Approval | Name / Date | Conditional | Required when the relationship ends. Privacy Officer or delegate confirms closure requirements were completed. |

## Approval / Routing

The BAA must be routed and approved before execution and before PHI is made available to the Business Associate.

| Step | Reviewer / Approver | Required | Review Focus | Evidence Required |
|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Business Owner | Yes | Confirms business need, service description, PHI access requirement, and operational scope. | Completed request form and underlying agreement or statement of work. |
| 2 | Privacy Officer | Yes | Confirms BAA requirement, permitted uses and disclosures, minimum necessary scope, individual rights support, incident reporting, and termination handling. | Privacy review approval and documented privacy risk notes. |
| 3 | Security Officer / Information Security | Conditional | Reviews safeguards, electronic PHI processing, system access, hosting, encryption, authentication, incident response, and vendor security posture. | Security questionnaire, risk assessment, remediation plan, or approval note. |
| 4 | Procurement / Vendor Management | Conditional | Confirms vendor onboarding, due diligence, insurance, subcontractor disclosures, and contract repository requirements. | Vendor due diligence record and procurement approval. |
| 5 | Legal Counsel | Yes | Reviews legal terms, deviations, indemnity, liability, notice, termination, subcontractor obligations, and consistency with the underlying agreement. | Legal approval and final redline or clean agreement. |
| 6 | Executive / Delegated Contract Signatory | Conditional | Required when contract value, risk level, or internal authority matrix requires executive approval. | Approval record under the contract authority process. |
| 7 | Authorized Signatories | Yes | Executes the final approved BAA. | Fully signed BAA. |
| 8 | Contract Administrator / Records Owner | Yes | Stores the executed agreement and schedules renewal or review. | Repository entry and retention metadata. |

Approval may be withheld if any of the following conditions exist:

- The Business Associate refuses to sign an approved BAA.
- The services require PHI access but the permitted uses and disclosures are unclear.
- The Business Associate cannot demonstrate appropriate safeguards for PHI.
- Incident reporting obligations are missing, delayed, or inconsistent with [Organization Name] requirements.
- Subcontractors will access PHI without appropriate written obligations.
- The underlying agreement conflicts with required privacy or security protections.
- Legal Counsel, the Privacy Officer, or the Security Officer identifies unresolved high-risk issues.
- Required risk reviews or vendor due diligence have not been completed.

Approved exceptions must be documented in the form and retained with the executed BAA.

## Records & Retention

The completed BAA template, approval evidence, supporting due diligence, executed agreement, amendments, renewals, and termination records must be maintained as official compliance records.

| Record | Owner | Storage Location | Retention Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completed BAA Request Form | Privacy Officer / Contract Administrator | [Contract Repository or GRC System] | Retain for at least [Retention Period] after termination of the Business Associate relationship. | Must show required field completion and approval history. |
| Fully Executed BAA | Legal / Contract Administrator | [Contract Repository] | Retain for at least [Retention Period] after termination or longer if required by legal hold, contract, or organizational policy. | Must include signatures from authorized representatives. |
| Underlying Agreement and Statements of Work | Legal / Procurement | [Contract Repository] | Retain according to contract retention requirements. | Must be linked to the BAA record. |
| Privacy Review Evidence | Privacy Officer | [GRC System or Privacy Repository] | Retain for at least [Retention Period]. | Includes privacy risk notes, minimum necessary analysis, and approval decisions. |
| Security Review Evidence | Security Officer | [GRC System or Vendor Risk Platform] | Retain for at least [Retention Period]. | Required where electronic PHI, system access, hosting, or data transmission is involved. |
| Vendor Due Diligence Records | Procurement / Vendor Management | [Vendor Management System] | Retain according to vendor risk retention requirements. | Includes questionnaires, certifications, insurance evidence, and remediation tracking. |
| Subcontractor Disclosures | Business Owner / Privacy Officer | [Contract Repository or GRC System] | Retain while subcontractors are active and for at least [Retention Period] afterward. | Must identify subcontractors with PHI access. |
| Approved Exceptions or Deviations | Legal Counsel / Privacy Officer | [Contract Repository] | Retain with the executed BAA. | Must include rationale and approver names. |
| Incident Notices from Business Associate | Privacy Officer / Security Officer | [Incident Management System] | Retain according to incident and breach record retention requirements. | Must be linked to the relevant BAA and vendor record. |
| Amendments and Renewals | Legal / Contract Administrator | [Contract Repository] | Retain with the BAA record. | Includes revised terms, extensions, and updated approvals. |
| Termination, Return, or Destruction Evidence | Privacy Officer / Business Owner | [Contract Repository or GRC System] | Retain for at least [Retention Period] after relationship closure. | Includes certificates of destruction or documented infeasibility of return/destruction. |
| Closure Approval | Privacy Officer / Contract Administrator | [Contract Repository or GRC System] | Retain with the BAA record. | Confirms relationship end date and PHI disposition. |

Records must be protected from unauthorized access, alteration, deletion, or disclosure. Access to BAA records must be limited to personnel with a legitimate business need, such as Privacy, Legal, Security, Procurement, Vendor Management, Audit, and relevant business owners.

If litigation, investigation, audit, complaint, breach review, or regulatory inquiry is pending or reasonably anticipated, all related BAA records must be preserved until the hold is released by Legal Counsel, even if the normal retention period has expired.

| Column | What to enter |

| Request/Ticket ID | Enter the helpdesk, IAM, HR, or change-management ticket number that initiated the access grant or modification. |
| Request Date | Enter the date the access request or modification request was submitted in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Requested By | Enter the name or user ID of the person who submitted the request, e.g. manager, system owner, HR, or user. |
| Workforce Member/User ID | Enter the unique workforce member or account identifier for the individual whose access is being granted or modified. |
| Workforce Member Name | Enter the full legal or HR-recorded name of the workforce member receiving the access grant or modification. |
| Department/Function | Enter the workforce member’s department, unit, team, or business function requiring the access. |
| Employment/Engagement Type | Enter one allowed value: Employee, Contractor, Vendor, Clinician, Temporary Staff, Student/Intern, Service Account, Other. |
| Access Action | Enter one allowed value: New Grant, Role Change, Permission Addition, Permission Removal, Account Reinstatement, Transfer Change, Other Modification. |

| System/Application/Repository | Enter the name of the system, application, database, file share, platform, or repository where access is being granted or modified. |

| Access Level | Enter one allowed value: Read/View, Create, Update/Edit, Delete, Export/Download, Admin/Privileged, Break-Glass/Emergency, Other. |

| Authorising Manager/Owner | Enter the name and role of the authorised approver, such as workforce manager, data owner, system owner, Privacy Officer, or Security Officer. |
| Authorisation Decision | Enter one allowed value: Approved, Rejected, Approved with Conditions, Pending Additional Information. |
| Authorisation Date | Enter the date the authorising manager or owner approved or rejected the request in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Authorisation Evidence Location | Enter the link, ticket reference, approval workflow ID, email archive location, or document path where approval evidence is retained. |
| Identity/Eligibility Verified | Enter Yes or No to confirm that the requester and workforce member identity, employment status, role, and eligibility were verified before implementation. |
| Implemented By | Enter the name or user ID of the IAM, IT, application administrator, or authorised individual who implemented the access grant or modification. |
| Implementation Date | Enter the date the access change was technically implemented in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Effective Date | Enter the date the access became active or usable in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Expiry/Review Date | Enter the date access expires or must be reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A only for standard ongoing role-based access subject to periodic access review. |
| Technical Change Reference | Enter the IAM transaction ID, directory group change ID, application audit event ID, change record, or configuration reference proving implementation. |

| User Notified | Enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the workforce member was notified that access was granted or modified. |
| Related HIPAA Control Reference | Enter the applicable HIPAA reference; for this log use 45 CFR 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(B) and/or 45 CFR 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(C). |
| Comments/Exceptions | Enter any conditions, deviations, emergency context, compensating actions, rejection reasons, or follow-up required; enter N/A if none. |

Records should be reconciled at least monthly against IAM, helpdesk/change-management, HR, and application audit-log source systems.
