| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| BA Register ID | Enter a unique identifier for this business associate record, e.g. BA-0001; do not reuse IDs. |
| Business Associate Legal Name | Enter the full legal name of the business associate exactly as shown on the executed BAA or contract. |
| Doing Business As / Vendor Name | Enter the vendor trade name, product name, or DBA if different from the legal name; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| BA Type | Select one: Vendor, Consultant, Cloud Service Provider, Billing Service, Claims Processor, Legal Service, Accounting Service, Data Analytics Provider, Health Information Exchange, Subcontractor, Other. |
| Internal Business Owner | Enter the internal role or named owner accountable for the BA relationship, e.g. Revenue Cycle Manager; include department if useful. |
| Internal Contract Owner | Enter the internal role or named owner responsible for contract and BAA administration, typically Legal, Procurement, or Vendor Management. |
| Service / Function Provided | Briefly describe the service or function performed for the organisation that involves PHI, e.g. claims processing, hosted EHR, transcription, legal review. |
| PHI / ePHI Involved | Select one: PHI, ePHI, Both, None. If None, BAA Required should normally be No and rationale should be included in Notes. |
| PHI Data Categories | List the PHI categories involved, separated by semicolons, e.g. demographics; diagnosis; treatment records; billing data; claims; images; lab results. |
| Systems / Applications / Locations Used | List the systems, applications, portals, storage locations, or data exchange mechanisms used by the BA to receive, create, maintain, or transmit PHI. |
| BAA Required | Select Yes or No based on whether the party creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on behalf of the organisation under HIPAA. |
| BAA Status | Select one: Executed, Pending Execution, Not Required, Expired, Terminated, Exception Approved. |
| Executed BAA Document Name | Enter the exact file name or contract management title of the executed BAA; enter N/A if BAA Status is Not Required. |
| Executed BAA Repository Link / Path | Enter the controlled repository URL, contract management system link, or file path where the fully executed BAA is stored; do not link to local desktops or email attachments. |
| BAA Effective Date | Enter the BAA effective date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| BAA Expiration Date | Enter the BAA expiration date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or Perpetual if the BAA remains effective until termination. |
| Auto-Renewal / Renewal Terms | Enter renewal terms from the BAA or underlying agreement, e.g. annual auto-renewal with 60 days' notice; enter N/A if none. |
| Covered Entity Signatory | Enter the name and title of the organisation's authorised signatory on the BAA. |
| Business Associate Signatory | Enter the name and title of the business associate's authorised signatory on the BAA. |
| BAA Execution Date | Enter the date the BAA was fully executed by all required parties in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Underlying Contract / MSA Reference | Enter the contract, MSA, SOW, purchase order, or vendor record reference linked to the BAA. |
| Permitted Uses and Disclosures Defined | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA specifies the permitted and required uses and disclosures of PHI by the BA. |
| Prohibition on Unauthorized Use / Disclosure Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA prohibits the BA from using or disclosing PHI other than as permitted by the BAA or required by law. |
| Safeguards Requirement Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA requires the BA to use appropriate safeguards to prevent unauthorized use or disclosure of PHI. |
| Breach / Incident Reporting Requirement Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA requires the BA to report unauthorized uses/disclosures, security incidents, or breaches as required by HIPAA and the agreement. |
| Subcontractor Flow-Down Requirement Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA requires the BA to ensure subcontractors that handle PHI agree to the same restrictions and conditions. |
| Access to PHI Requirement Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA requires the BA to make PHI available as needed for individual access rights under HIPAA. |
| Amendment of PHI Requirement Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA requires the BA to make PHI available for amendment and incorporate approved amendments. |
| Accounting of Disclosures Requirement Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA requires the BA to document and provide information needed for an accounting of disclosures. |
| HHS Access to Books and Records Requirement Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA requires the BA to make internal practices, books, and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of HHS for compliance determination. |
| Return or Destruction of PHI on Termination Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA requires return or destruction of PHI at termination where feasible, and continued protection if return/destruction is infeasible. |
| Termination for Material Breach Included | Select Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the BAA authorizes termination if the BA materially breaches the agreement. |
| Subcontractors / Downstream BAs Used | Enter Yes, No, or Unknown; if Yes, list known subcontractors handling PHI or reference the approved subcontractor list. |
| Subcontractor BAA Assurance Status | Select one: Confirmed, Pending, Not Applicable, Unknown, Exception Approved; use Confirmed only where flow-down assurances or contractual terms are verified. |
| Last BAA Legal Review Date | Enter the most recent date Legal reviewed the BAA for required HIPAA terms in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Compliance Review Date | Enter the most recent date Compliance, Privacy, Security, or Vendor Risk reviewed the BA record in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Status | Select one: Current, Review Due, Remediation Open, Exception Approved, Terminated. |
| Exceptions / Gaps | Describe any missing BAA, missing clause, expired agreement, unsigned document, unverified subcontractor assurance, or other gap; enter None if no known gap. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the person or role responsible for resolving any exception or gap; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target date for resolving the exception or gap in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Termination Date | Enter the date the BA relationship ended in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if active. |
| PHI Returned or Destroyed Date | Enter the date PHI return or destruction was completed and evidenced in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if active or not yet applicable. |
| Record Status | Select one: Active, Pending Onboarding, Inactive, Terminated, Archived. |
| Notes | Enter concise supporting context, decisions, rationale for BAA not required, or references to approvals; do not include PHI in this field. |

### Maintenance

Owned by Privacy/Compliance with Legal and Vendor Management support; update at onboarding, contract change, renewal, termination, subcontractor change, and at least quarterly. Source data should come from the contract lifecycle management repository, vendor risk management system, procurement/vendor master, and controlled executed agreement storage location.

HIPAA-029.title: Authorisation Forms (PHI Use/Disclosure)
HIPAA-029.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [DOC-ID] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Privacy Officer |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | HIPAA |
| Classification | Internal - Confidential |

## Purpose

This template is used to obtain a valid individual authorization before the organization uses or discloses Protected Health Information (PHI) for purposes that require explicit written permission, including but not limited to:

- Marketing communications where authorization is required.
- Research uses or disclosures not covered by another permitted pathway.
- Disclosures to third parties at the individual’s request.
- Use or disclosure of psychotherapy notes, where applicable.
- Sale of PHI or disclosures involving remuneration, where applicable.
- Any use or disclosure of PHI not otherwise permitted by organizational policy or applicable privacy requirements.

This form is intended to ensure that authorizations are clear, specific, voluntary, documented, and revocable by the individual or their legally authorized representative.

## Instructions

1. **Use this form before the PHI is used or disclosed.** Do not process the requested use or disclosure until the authorization has been reviewed, signed, and approved according to the routing requirements below.

2. **Complete all required fields.** An authorization is not valid if required information is missing, unclear, expired, or inconsistent.

3. **Use plain language.** The individual must be able to understand what PHI will be used or disclosed, who will use or receive it, and for what purpose.

4. **Describe the PHI specifically.** Avoid broad phrases such as “all records” unless the individual clearly intends to authorize release of the complete designated record set. Specify dates, departments, providers, record types, conditions, or service episodes where applicable.

5. **Identify the recipient clearly.** If PHI will be disclosed to a person, organization, sponsor, researcher, vendor, media outlet, employer, school, attorney, insurer, or other third party, provide enough detail to identify the recipient.

6. **State the purpose.** The form must describe the purpose of the use or disclosure. If the individual requests the authorization and does not wish to state a purpose, “At the request of the individual” may be used.

7. **Include expiration.** Each authorization must include either a specific expiration date or a clear expiration event related to the purpose of the authorization.

8. **Explain revocation rights.** The individual must be informed that they may revoke the authorization in writing, except to the extent the organization has already acted in reliance on it.

9. **Explain potential redisclosure.** The individual must be informed that PHI disclosed under the authorization may be redisclosed by the recipient and may no longer be protected by the organization’s privacy obligations.

10. **Do not condition treatment, payment, enrollment, or eligibility on signing**, except where permitted by law and approved by the Privacy Officer.

11. **Provide a copy to the individual.** A signed copy of the authorization must be offered or provided to the individual or their legally authorized representative.

12. **Verify representative authority.** If signed by a personal representative, legal guardian, parent, executor, healthcare proxy, or other authorized party, confirm and document the basis of authority before processing.

13. **Special review is required** for authorizations involving:
 - Marketing.
 - Research.
 - Psychotherapy notes.
 - Sale of PHI or disclosures involving payment or other value to the organization.
 - Minors’ records.
 - Substance use disorder, reproductive health, genetic, mental health, HIV/AIDS, or other specially protected information.
 - Media, public relations, fundraising, employer, or law enforcement-related disclosures.
 - Requests involving large data sets or recurring disclosures.

14. **Do not alter signed authorization language after signature.** If changes are required, obtain a new authorization.

15. **File the completed authorization in the approved record location** and record the disclosure where required by organizational accounting and tracking processes.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---:|:---:|---|
| Authorization Form Identifier | Text | Yes | Unique tracking number assigned by Privacy, HIM, Compliance, or the records system. Example: AUTH-[YYYY]-[Sequential Number]. |
| Date Authorization Prepared | Date | Yes | Date the form is generated or prepared for signature. |
| Individual Full Legal Name | Text | Yes | Full name of the individual whose PHI is the subject of the authorization. |
| Individual Preferred Name | Text | No | Include if used by the organization to assist identification and communication. |
| Date of Birth | Date | Yes | Used to verify identity and match records accurately. |
| Medical Record Number / Patient ID | Text | Conditional | Required if the organization assigns a patient or member identifier. |
| Address | Text | Conditional | Required when needed for identity verification or mailing a copy. |
| Phone Number | Text | Conditional | Include if needed for follow-up or identity confirmation. |
| Email Address | Email | Conditional | Include only if email communication is requested or needed. Confirm secure communication preferences where applicable. |
| Identity Verified By | Dropdown / Text | Yes | Document verification method, such as government ID, patient portal authentication, existing registration verification, notarized request, or approved remote verification method. |
| Verification Date | Date | Yes | Date the identity or representative authority was verified. |
| Organization Authorized to Use or Disclose PHI | Text | Yes | Name the covered entity, department, clinic, provider group, health plan, business unit, or workforce area authorized to use or disclose PHI. |
| Specific Workforce Role or Department | Text | Conditional | Required if the authorization is limited to a particular department, researcher, treating provider, program, or business unit. |
| Recipient Name | Text | Yes | Name of the person or organization authorized to receive the PHI, if the authorization involves disclosure outside the organization. |
| Recipient Contact Person | Text | Conditional | Required where the recipient is an organization and a contact person is known. |
| Recipient Address | Text | Conditional | Required for mail, courier, legal, or formal disclosures. |
| Recipient Email | Email | Conditional | Required if disclosure will be made by email. Use only approved secure transmission methods unless the individual specifically requests otherwise after being informed of risks. |
| Recipient Phone Number | Text | Conditional | Include if needed to coordinate disclosure. |
| Recipient Fax Number | Text | Conditional | Required if disclosure will be made by fax. Confirm recipient fax number before sending. |
| Description of PHI to Be Used or Disclosed | Long Text | Yes | Describe the information specifically. Examples: lab results from [date range], discharge summary for [encounter], billing records for [date range], imaging reports, medication history, research data elements, marketing contact information. |
| Date Range of PHI | Date Range | Conditional | Required unless the authorization applies to a clearly defined event, episode, study, or record type. |
| Include Entire Medical Record | Checkbox | No | Use only if the individual specifically authorizes release of the complete record. Review for sensitive categories before release. |
| Sensitive Information Included | Checkbox Group | Conditional | Indicate if PHI includes specially sensitive information, such as mental health, substance use disorder, HIV/AIDS, genetic information, reproductive health, sexual health, minors’ confidential services, or psychotherapy notes. Follow additional review requirements. |
| Psychotherapy Notes Included | Yes/No | Conditional | Required if psychotherapy notes are requested or implicated. This should generally be authorized separately from other PHI unless Privacy Officer approves the format. |
| Purpose of Use or Disclosure | Long Text | Yes | State the purpose clearly. Examples: participation in research study, marketing communication, disclosure to attorney, insurance review, school accommodation, personal request, media story, care coordination not otherwise permitted. |
| Purpose Category | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Research, Marketing, Individual Request, Legal/Administrative, Media/Public Relations, Employer/School, Family/Personal Representative, Sale or Remunerated Disclosure, Other. |
| Marketing Involved | Yes/No | Yes | Select “Yes” if the PHI will be used to encourage purchase or use of a product or service and authorization is required. |
| Financial Remuneration Involved | Yes/No | Yes | Select “Yes” if the organization will receive direct or indirect payment or other value in exchange for the use or disclosure. Explain in the remuneration field. |
| Remuneration Description | Long Text | Conditional | Required if remuneration is involved. Describe the nature of payment or value in plain language. |
| Sale of PHI Involved | Yes/No | Yes | Select “Yes” if PHI will be exchanged for payment or other value in a manner requiring explicit authorization. Requires Privacy Officer and Legal review. |
| Research Study Name | Text | Conditional | Required for research authorizations. Use the protocol title or public-facing study name. |
| Research Principal Investigator | Text | Conditional | Required for research authorizations. |
| Research Sponsor | Text | Conditional | Required if the study is sponsored or funded by an external party. |
| Research Data Use Description | Long Text | Conditional | Required for research authorizations. Describe how PHI will be used, who will access it, and whether identifiable information will leave the organization. |
| Authorization Combined With Consent or Other Permission | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether this authorization is combined with another form, such as research consent. Combined forms must be reviewed for clarity and voluntariness. |
| Redisclosure Warning Provided | Checkbox | Yes | Confirm the individual has been informed that information disclosed to the recipient may be redisclosed and may no longer be protected by the organization. |
| Right to Revoke Explained | Checkbox | Yes | Confirm the individual has been informed of their right to revoke the authorization in writing. |
| Revocation Submission Method | Text | Yes | Provide where and how revocation must be submitted, such as Privacy Office address, patient portal, approved email address, or HIM department. |
| Effect of Revocation Explained | Checkbox | Yes | Confirm the individual has been informed that revocation will not affect actions already taken in reliance on the authorization. |
| Conditioning Statement Included | Checkbox | Yes | Confirm the form states whether treatment, payment, enrollment, or eligibility is conditioned on signing and, if so, describes the permitted reason. |
| Is Signing Required to Receive Treatment, Payment, Enrollment, or Benefits? | Yes/No | Yes | Must generally be “No” unless approved by Privacy Officer and Legal. If “Yes,” explain below. |
| Conditioning Explanation | Long Text | Conditional | Required if signing is a condition for a permitted activity, such as research-related treatment or eligibility for a service that requires the disclosure. |
| Expiration Date | Date | Conditional | Required unless an expiration event is used. Must be specific and reasonable for the stated purpose. |
| Expiration Event | Text | Conditional | Required if no expiration date is used. Example: end of research study, conclusion of legal matter, completion of requested disclosure, termination of participation in [program]. |
| One-Time Disclosure or Ongoing Authorization | Dropdown | Yes | Select one-time, recurring, continuous for defined period, or event-based. |
| Frequency of Disclosure | Text | Conditional | Required for recurring or ongoing authorizations. Example: monthly, each visit, upon update, at study milestones. |
| Disclosure Method | Checkbox Group | Conditional | Select applicable method: secure portal, encrypted email, mail, fax, secure file transfer, verbal disclosure, in-person pickup, API/electronic exchange, other approved method. |
| Individual Requests Unsecure Transmission | Yes/No | Conditional | Required if individual requests email or another method that may not be secure. Document risk warning and confirmation. |
| Risk Warning for Unsecure Transmission Provided | Checkbox | Conditional | Required where applicable. Confirm the individual was informed of risks and still requested the method. |
| Minimum Necessary Review Completed | Yes/No | Conditional | Required for workforce processing. Confirm the disclosure is limited to the PHI authorized and appropriate for the purpose. |
| Fees Disclosed, If Applicable | Yes/No/Not Applicable | Conditional | Indicate whether any permissible copying, media, or processing fee was disclosed to the individual before fulfillment. |
| Individual Signature | Signature | Yes | Signature of the individual whose PHI is being used or disclosed, unless signed by a verified personal representative. |
| Individual Signature Date | Date | Yes | Date the individual signs the authorization. The authorization is not valid without a signature date. |
| Personal Representative Name | Text | Conditional | Required if signed by someone other than the individual. |
| Personal Representative Relationship | Text | Conditional | Examples: parent, legal guardian, healthcare proxy, executor, power of attorney, court-appointed representative. |
| Authority Documentation Reviewed | Checkbox | Conditional | Required if signed by a personal representative. Confirm supporting authority was reviewed. |
| Description of Authority | Long Text | Conditional | Describe the document or basis of authority reviewed, such as court order, guardianship document, power of attorney, healthcare proxy, estate appointment, parental authority, or other recognized authority. |
| Personal Representative Signature | Signature | Conditional | Required if the individual does not sign personally. |
| Personal Representative Signature Date | Date | Conditional | Required if representative signs. |
| Witness Name | Text | Conditional | Required if organizational policy, state law, research protocol, or high-risk disclosure review requires witness documentation. |
| Witness Signature | Signature | Conditional | Required where witness is used. |
| Witness Signature Date | Date | Conditional | Required where witness is used. |
| Interpreter Used | Yes/No | Conditional | Required if interpretation was provided. |
| Interpreter Name or ID | Text | Conditional | Required if interpreter used. |
| Language Provided | Text | Conditional | Required if form was translated or interpreted. |
| Copy Provided to Individual | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether a copy of the signed authorization was provided or offered. |
| Copy Delivery Method | Dropdown / Text | Conditional | Required if copy was provided. Examples: paper copy, secure portal, encrypted email, mail. |
| Staff Member Receiving Authorization | Text | Yes | Name or ID of workforce member who received the completed form. |
| Department Receiving Authorization | Text | Yes | Department responsible for intake, such as HIM, Privacy Office, Research Office, Patient Access, Marketing, or clinic. |
| Intake Date | Date | Yes | Date completed authorization was received by the organization. |
| Privacy Review Required | Yes/No | Yes | Select “Yes” for high-risk or special categories identified in the instructions. |
| Privacy Review Decision | Dropdown | Conditional | Required when Privacy review is required. Select approved, approved with conditions, rejected, or returned for correction. |
| Privacy Review Notes | Long Text | Conditional | Document review rationale, restrictions, required safeguards, or reasons for rejection. |
| Legal Review Required | Yes/No | Conditional | Required for sale of PHI, remuneration, complex research, litigation-related disclosures, media, minors’ rights conflicts, or other high-risk matters. |
| Legal Review Decision | Dropdown | Conditional | Required when Legal review is required. |
| Fulfillment Approved By | Text | Conditional | Name or role approving the use or disclosure after validation. |
| Fulfillment Date | Date | Conditional | Date PHI was used or disclosed. |
| Disclosure Logged | Yes/No/Not Applicable | Conditional | Confirm whether the disclosure was recorded in the accounting or disclosure tracking process, where required. |
| Disclosure Log Reference | Text | Conditional | Link or identifier for the disclosure accounting record, if applicable. |
| Revocation Received | Yes/No | Conditional | Update if the individual later revokes the authorization. |
| Revocation Date | Date | Conditional | Required if revocation is received. |
| Revocation Processed By | Text | Conditional | Workforce member or department that processed the revocation. |
| Actions Stopped After Revocation | Long Text | Conditional | Describe future uses or disclosures stopped because of revocation. |
| Reliance Actions Already Completed | Long Text | Conditional | Document any actions already taken before revocation that cannot be reversed. |
| Record Location | Text | Yes | Approved system or repository where the authorization and related documentation are stored. |
| Retention Trigger Date | Date | Yes | Usually the signature date, expiration date, fulfillment date, or date last relied upon, as determined by retention policy. |

## Approval / Routing

Completed authorizations must follow the routing below before PHI is used or disclosed.

| Scenario | Required Review / Approval | Routing Destination | Key Review Points |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routine individual-directed disclosure to a third party | HIM or authorized records team | Health Information Management / Records Release | Identity verification, recipient details, PHI description, expiration, signature, secure delivery method. |
| Marketing use or disclosure requiring authorization | Privacy Officer and Marketing Owner | Privacy Office, then Marketing Department | Required authorization language, remuneration disclosure if applicable, opt-out coordination, recipient controls, campaign scope. |
| Research use or disclosure | Research Office, Privacy Officer, and study leadership | Research Administration / Privacy Office | Study purpose, data elements, participant authorization, sponsor access, combined consent clarity, revocation handling. |
| Psychotherapy notes | Privacy Officer and appropriate clinical leadership | Privacy Office | Separate authorization, sensitive content handling, recipient need, legal restrictions, clinical risk considerations. |
| Sale of PHI or disclosure involving remuneration | Privacy Officer and Legal Counsel | Privacy Office and Legal | Explicit disclosure of remuneration, permissibility, contract terms, individual understanding, reputational and compliance risk. |
| Media, public relations, or testimonial | Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, and Communications Lead | Privacy Office / Legal / Communications | Scope of PHI, images or recordings, publicity duration, withdrawal limits, future use, third-party platforms. |
| Minor’s record or personal representative signature | Privacy Officer or designated specialist | Privacy Office / HIM | Authority to sign, minor consent rights, sensitive services, custody or guardianship restrictions. |
| Specially protected information | Privacy Officer and Legal Counsel where needed | Privacy Office | Additional confidentiality obligations, segmentation, express inclusion, recipient limitations. |
| Employer, school, attorney, insurer, or administrative request | HIM or Privacy Officer depending on risk | HIM / Privacy Office | Voluntariness, specific recipient, date range, purpose, potential coercion, minimum necessary fulfillment. |
| Unsecure transmission requested by individual | HIM or Privacy Officer if high risk | HIM / Privacy Office | Risk warning provided, individual direction documented, correct recipient, transmission method. |
| Revocation of authorization | Privacy Officer or designated records team | Privacy Office / HIM / Relevant Department | Written revocation, identity verification, stop future uses/disclosures, notify affected teams, document reliance actions. |

Approval must be documented before fulfillment for any authorization requiring Privacy, Legal, Research, Marketing, Communications, or clinical leadership review.

A submitted authorization must be rejected or returned for correction if any of the following apply:

- The form is unsigned or undated.
- The individual or representative cannot be verified.
- Representative authority is not established.
- The PHI description is missing, vague, or inconsistent with the purpose.
- The recipient is not identifiable.
- The purpose is missing or unclear.
- No expiration date or expiration event is provided.
- Required statements about revocation, conditioning, or redisclosure are missing.
- The authorization has expired.
- The authorization is known to have been revoked.
- Material information is false or incomplete.
- Required special review has not been completed.
- The requested use or disclosure is not permitted by organizational policy or applicable law.

## Records & Retention

Completed authorizations and related review records must be retained as official privacy documentation.

| Record | Owner | Storage Location | Retention Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Signed authorization form | Privacy Officer / HIM | [Approved Records System] | Retain for at least six years from the date last in effect or longer if required by organizational retention schedule | Must be retrievable for audit, complaint investigation, and disclosure verification. |
| Identity verification evidence or notation | HIM / Intake Department | [Approved Records System] | Retain with the authorization record | Do not store unnecessary copies of identity documents unless required by policy. |
| Personal representative authority documentation | HIM / Privacy Office | [Approved Records System] | Retain with the authorization record | Include enough documentation to support authority to sign. |
| Privacy review notes and decision | Privacy Office | [Privacy Case Management System] | Retain for at least six years from decision date or longer if tied to the authorization record | Required for high-risk, sensitive, or escalated authorizations. |
| Legal review notes and decision | Legal Department | [Legal Matter System] | Retain according to legal record retention requirements | Cross-reference authorization identifier where appropriate. |
| Research authorization review documentation | Research Office | [Research Administration System] | Retain according to study and organizational retention requirements | Must align with study documentation and participant records. |
| Disclosure accounting entry, where applicable | HIM / Privacy Office | [Disclosure Tracking System] | Retain according to privacy accounting retention requirements | Include date, recipient, PHI disclosed, purpose, and authorization reference. |
| Revocation request | Privacy Office / HIM | [Approved Records System] | Retain with original authorization | Must include date received, validation, actions stopped, and reliance actions already completed. |
| Transmission confirmation | Fulfillment Department | [Approved Records System] | Retain with fulfillment record | Examples: fax confirmation, secure portal delivery receipt, certified mail tracking, secure transfer log. |
| Rejected or invalid authorization | Privacy Office / HIM | [Approved Records System] | Retain according to privacy documentation retention requirements | Record reason for rejection and any communication to requester. |

Access to authorization records must be limited to workforce members with a business need, such as Privacy, HIM, Legal, Research Administration, Compliance, and authorized department personnel.

Authorization records must be protected against unauthorized access, alteration, deletion, and disclosure. Electronic records must be stored in approved systems with access controls, audit logging, backup, and retention controls. Paper records must be stored in secure areas and scanned or filed according to organizational records management procedures.

If an authorization is revoked, the organization must promptly document the revocation, notify departments that may rely on the authorization, stop future uses or disclosures covered by the revocation, and retain evidence of any actions already taken before the revocation was received and processed.

HIPAA-030.title: Accounting of Disclosures Log
HIPAA-030.content:
## Accounting of Disclosures Log (XLSX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Disclosure Log ID | Individual/Patient ID | Individual/Patient Name | Disclosure Date | Recipient Name | Recipient Organization | Recipient Address | Recipient Type | Purpose of Disclosure | Purpose Source | PHI Disclosed Description | Disclosure Method | Disclosure Category | Accounting Required | Accounting Exclusion Reason | Multiple Disclosure Series | Series Start Date | Series End Date | Series Frequency/Periodicity | Last Disclosure Date in Series | Written Request/Authorization Reference | System of Record | Entered By | Entry Date | Reviewed By | Review Date | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [EXAMPLE: AOD-2026-0001] | [EXAMPLE: MRN123456] | [EXAMPLE: Doe, Jane] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-14] | [EXAMPLE: John Smith] | [EXAMPLE: County Public Health Department] | [EXAMPLE: 100 Main Street, Springfield, ST 12345] | [EXAMPLE: Public Health Authority] | [EXAMPLE: Communicable disease reporting required by state law] | [EXAMPLE: Legal Requirement] | [EXAMPLE: Patient demographics, diagnosis, lab result, and date of service] | [EXAMPLE: Secure Email] | [EXAMPLE: Public Health] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: PH-REQ-2026-0142] | [EXAMPLE: EHR and Privacy Ticketing System] | [EXAMPLE: jsmith] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-14] | [EXAMPLE: privacyofficer] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-16] | [EXAMPLE: Enter only operational notes needed for audit support] |
| [EXAMPLE: AOD-2026-0002] | [EXAMPLE: MRN987654] | [EXAMPLE: Roe, Richard] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-01] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: State Health Oversight Agency] | [EXAMPLE: 250 State Plaza, Capital City, ST 67890] | [EXAMPLE: Health Oversight Agency] | [EXAMPLE: Monthly disclosures for licensed facility oversight review] | [EXAMPLE: Written Request] | [EXAMPLE: Encounter dates, provider name, billing codes, and care plan summary] | [EXAMPLE: Portal] | [EXAMPLE: Health Oversight] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-01] | [EXAMPLE: Ongoing] | [EXAMPLE: Monthly] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-01] | [EXAMPLE: OVERSIGHT-2026-009] | [EXAMPLE: Release-of-Information System] | [EXAMPLE: mbrown] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-01] | [EXAMPLE: Pending] | [EXAMPLE: Pending] | [EXAMPLE: Series row used for repeated disclosures to same recipient for same oversight purpose] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Disclosure Log ID | Enter a unique identifier for this disclosure log entry, using a consistent format such as AOD-YYYY-####. |
| Individual/Patient ID | Enter the internal patient/member/client identifier for the individual whose PHI was disclosed; do not use SSN. |
| Individual/Patient Name | Enter the individual's full legal name in Last Name, First Name format. |
| Disclosure Date | Enter the date the disclosure occurred in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Recipient Name | Enter the full name of the person who received the PHI, if known; if the recipient is an organization only, enter N/A. |
| Recipient Organization | Enter the organization or entity that received the PHI, if applicable; if an individual only, enter N/A. |
| Recipient Address | Enter the recipient's mailing address or business address sufficient to identify the recipient; use N/A only if unavailable after reasonable effort. |
| Recipient Type | Select one: Public Health Authority, Health Oversight Agency, Law Enforcement, Coroner/Medical Examiner, Organ Procurement Organization, Research, Government Authority, Business Associate, Court/Legal, Other. |
| Purpose of Disclosure | Enter a brief statement of the purpose of the disclosure, such as public health reporting, health oversight audit, law enforcement request, or research disclosure. |
| Purpose Source | Select one: Written Request, Verbal Request Documented, Legal Requirement, Authorization, Internal Policy, Other. |
| PHI Disclosed Description | Enter a brief description of the PHI disclosed, specific enough to support an accounting, such as dates of service, diagnosis, lab result, medication list, demographic information, or full designated record set. |
| Disclosure Method | Select one: Secure Email, Fax, Mail, Portal, EHR Interface, HIE, Telephone, In Person, API, Other. |
| Disclosure Category | Select one: Required by Law, Public Health, Health Oversight, Judicial/Administrative Proceeding, Law Enforcement, Decedent Information, Organ/Tissue Donation, Research Without Authorization, Serious Threat, Specialized Government Function, Workers Compensation, Other. |
| Accounting Required | Select Yes or No to indicate whether this disclosure must be included in an accounting under HIPAA 45 CFR 164.528. |
| Accounting Exclusion Reason | If Accounting Required is No, enter the applicable exclusion, such as Treatment/Payment/Health Care Operations, Disclosure to Individual, Facility Directory, National Security/Intelligence, Correctional Institution/Law Enforcement Custody, Prior to HIPAA Compliance Date, or Other; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Multiple Disclosure Series | Select Yes if this row represents a series of multiple disclosures to the same recipient for the same purpose; otherwise select No. |
| Series Start Date | If Multiple Disclosure Series is Yes, enter the first disclosure date in the series in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Series End Date | If Multiple Disclosure Series is Yes and the series has ended, enter the final date in YYYY-MM-DD format; if ongoing enter Ongoing; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Series Frequency/Periodicity | If Multiple Disclosure Series is Yes, enter the frequency, periodicity, or number of disclosures, such as Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Event-based, or 12 disclosures; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Last Disclosure Date in Series | If Multiple Disclosure Series is Yes, enter the most recent disclosure date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Written Request/Authorization Reference | Enter the document ID, ticket number, subpoena number, authorization ID, or request reference supporting the disclosure; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| System of Record | Enter the source system where the disclosure evidence is maintained, such as EHR, release-of-information system, case management system, privacy ticketing system, HIE audit log, or legal matter system. |
| Entered By | Enter the name or user ID of the workforce member who recorded this disclosure. |
| Entry Date | Enter the date this log entry was created in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Reviewed By | Enter the name or user ID of the Privacy Officer or designee who reviewed the entry; enter Pending if not yet reviewed. |
| Review Date | Enter the review date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Pending if not yet reviewed. |
| Notes | Enter any additional facts needed to understand the disclosure or accounting treatment; do not duplicate full PHI content here. |

### Maintenance

The Privacy Officer or designated HIPAA Privacy Compliance Manager owns this template and updates it at the time each accountable disclosure is made, with formal review at least monthly and whenever an individual requests an accounting. Source data should be drawn from the EHR, release-of-information system, privacy ticketing system, HIE/API audit logs, legal request files, and any departmental disclosure tracking records.

HIPAA-031.title: Patient Rights Request Records (Access/Amend/Restrict)
HIPAA-031.content:

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Request Record ID | Enter a unique tracking number for the request, using the organisation’s case numbering format, e.g. PRR-YYYY-####. |
| Request Type | Select one allowed value: Access, Amendment, Restriction, Confidential Communication, Combined. |
| HIPAA Provision | Enter the applicable HIPAA citation: 164.524 for access, 164.526 for amendment, 164.522(a) for restriction, or 164.522(b) for confidential communications. |
| Date Request Received | Enter the calendar date the organisation received the request in YYYY-MM-DD format; this date starts the response timeline. |
| Receipt Channel | Select how the request was received: Portal, Email, Mail, Fax, In Person, Telephone, Other. |
| Receiving Department or Location | Enter the department, facility, clinic, or business unit that first received the request. |
| Requester Full Name | Enter the full legal name of the person making the request. |
| Requester Relationship to Individual | Select one allowed value: Individual, Personal Representative, Parent/Guardian, Executor/Administrator, Attorney, Other Authorized Person. |
| Individual/Patient Full Name | Enter the full legal name of the individual whose PHI is the subject of the request. |
| Individual/Patient Identifier | Enter the organisation’s patient identifier, medical record number, or other approved internal identifier; do not use Social Security number unless required by policy. |
| Personal Representative Authority Verified | Enter Yes, No, or N/A; if Yes, retain proof of authority in the documentation location. |
| Identity Verification Method | Describe the method used to verify identity and authority before disclosing or changing PHI, e.g. government ID checked, portal login authenticated, notarized authorization, known patient factors verified. |
| Request Description | Summarize exactly what the requester asked for, including the right being exercised and any specific records, amendment text, restriction, or communication preference requested. |
| Designated Record Set / PHI Scope | Identify the records or PHI covered, such as billing records, clinical notes, lab results, imaging, claims, or the full designated record set. |
| Requested Date Range of PHI | Enter the date range requested in YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD format, or enter All Available if no date range was specified. |
| Requested Form and Format | For access requests, enter the requested format, e.g. paper copy, PDF, portal download, electronic copy, CD/USB, inspection only; for other request types enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Requested Delivery Method or Restriction Method | For access, enter the requested delivery method, e.g. portal, encrypted email, mail, pickup, direct transmission to third party; for restriction, enter the requested limit on use/disclosure; for amendment enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Confidential Communication Request Details | For 164.522(b) requests, record the requested alternative address, phone number, email, contact method, or location; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Urgent or Safety Consideration | Enter Yes or No and briefly describe any urgent patient care, safety, domestic violence, endangerment, emergency treatment, or legal consideration affecting processing. |
| Responsible Workforce Member | Enter the name and role of the staff member responsible for processing the request. |
| Assigned Privacy Reviewer | Enter the Privacy Officer, HIM reviewer, compliance reviewer, or designee assigned to evaluate the request. |
| Initial Response Due Date | Enter the required response deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format, normally 30 calendar days from receipt unless a stricter state law or organisational policy applies. |
| Extension Used | Enter Yes or No; HIPAA permits one extension for access requests when the individual is notified in writing of the reason and expected completion date. |
| Extension Notice Date | If an extension is used, enter the date the written extension notice was sent in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Extended Due Date | If an extension is used, enter the new deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Fees Assessed | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether a permitted, reasonable, cost-based fee was assessed for access copies or delivery. |
| Fee Amount | Enter the amount charged in USD with two decimals, e.g. 25.00, or enter 0.00 if no fee was charged. |
| Fee Notice / Agreement Date | Enter the date the requester was notified of or agreed to applicable fees in YYYY-MM-DD format, or N/A if no fee applied. |
| Decision Status | Select one allowed value: Pending, Approved, Partially Approved, Denied, Withdrawn, Unable to Verify Identity, Completed. |
| Decision Date | Enter the date the decision was made in YYYY-MM-DD format, or leave blank until decided. |
| Approval / Partial Approval Details | If approved or partially approved, describe what was approved and any limits, exclusions, redactions, or agreed alternative format or timing. |
| Denial Basis | If denied or partially denied, state the specific basis, such as psychotherapy notes, information compiled for legal proceedings, CLIA restriction, inmate safety, protected source, endangerment, record not in designated record set, record not created by organisation, record accurate and complete, or other permitted basis; enter N/A if not denied. |
| Denial Reviewable | For access denials, enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the denial is reviewable under HIPAA; amendment denials should be marked N/A unless internal policy requires review. |
| Denial Notice Sent Date | If denied or partially denied, enter the date the written denial notice was sent in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Review Requested | Enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the individual requested review of a reviewable access denial. |
| Review Requested Date | If review was requested, enter the request date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Reviewing Official | If review was requested, enter the name and role of the licensed health care professional or other qualified official who was not involved in the original denial; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Review Decision Date | If review was requested, enter the date the review decision was made in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Review Outcome | If review was requested, enter Upheld, Overturned, Modified, or N/A. |
| Access Fulfillment Date | For approved access requests, enter the date access was provided in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Access Fulfillment Method | For approved access requests, enter how access was provided, e.g. portal release, paper mailed, encrypted email, in-person inspection, direct transmission to third party; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Amendment Accepted | For amendment requests, enter Yes, No, Partially, or N/A. |
| Amendment Action Taken | If amendment was accepted, describe the correction, addendum, or linkage made to the designated record set and the date completed; if denied, enter N/A. |
| Amendment Notification Recipients | For accepted amendments, list persons or entities notified or to be notified as requested by the individual or as required because they may have relied on or could rely on the information; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Amendment Denial Statement of Disagreement Received | For denied amendment requests, enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the individual submitted a written statement of disagreement. |
| Amendment Rebuttal Added | If the organisation prepared a rebuttal to a statement of disagreement, enter Yes and retain the rebuttal with the request file; otherwise enter No or N/A. |
| Restriction Accepted | For restriction requests, enter Yes, No, Partially, or N/A; note that certain paid-in-full out-of-pocket restrictions to health plans must be honored where applicable. |
| Restriction Implementation Details | If a restriction or confidential communication request was accepted, describe exactly how it was implemented, including flags, billing controls, disclosure blocks, contact instructions, or minimum necessary limits; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Restriction Termination Date | If an accepted restriction was terminated, enter the termination date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Restriction Termination Notice Date | If the organisation terminated a restriction, enter the date notice was provided to the individual in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Systems / Records Updated | List all systems, modules, files, or record repositories updated as part of the request, such as EHR, billing system, release-of-information platform, patient portal, paper chart, CRM, or consent management tool. |
| Third Parties Notified | List external recipients notified, such as business associates, health plans, providers, or requester-designated recipients; enter N/A if none. |
| Documentation Location | Enter the link, case file path, document management reference, or repository location where the request, correspondence, verification evidence, decision notices, and fulfillment evidence are stored. |
| Final Closure Date | Enter the date all actions were completed and the case was closed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Outcome Summary | Provide a concise final summary of the outcome, including whether the request was fulfilled, amended, restricted, denied, withdrawn, or unresolved. |
| Notes / Exceptions | Record any relevant exceptions, delays, state-law considerations, escalation notes, or unusual handling details; enter N/A if none. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Privacy Officer or Health Information Management/Release of Information lead, with entries updated at intake, decision, fulfillment, and closure and reviewed at least monthly for timeliness and completeness. Source data should be drawn from the privacy case management system, release-of-information platform, EHR/patient portal, identity verification records, correspondence repository, and applicable billing or consent/restriction systems.

HIPAA-032.title: Documentation Retention Records
HIPAA-032.content:
## What This Evidences

**Documentation Retention Records** evidence that the organisation retains required HIPAA policies, procedures, and related documentation for **at least 6 years** from the date of creation, last effective date, or last use, as applicable.

This artifact is **collected operational evidence**, not an authored document. It must be exported or captured from the organisation’s own document management system, records repository, compliance portal, or equivalent system of record. Do not create a manual spreadsheet unless it is a direct export or report generated from the authoritative system.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect this evidence from the organisation’s official documentation and records management source, typically one of:

- Document Management System: `[DMS Name]`
- Governance, Risk, and Compliance platform: `[GRC Tool Name]`
- Policy management portal: `[Policy Portal Name]`
- Records management repository: `[Records Repository Name]`
- SharePoint/Google Workspace/Confluence with governed retention controls: `[Collaboration Platform Name]`
- Legal hold or records retention system: `[Retention Tool Name]`

The preferred source is the system that stores approved HIPAA policies and procedures and applies retention rules, version history, approval status, and deletion controls.

## How To Collect

1. Log in to `[DMS/GRC/Policy System Name]` using an account with reporting or records administration access.
2. Navigate to the policy, procedure, or records retention area, such as `[Policies Library]`, `[HIPAA Documentation Repository]`, or `[Records Retention Dashboard]`.
3. Filter records to include HIPAA-related policies, procedures, standards, guidelines, forms, and supporting documentation.
4. Apply filters for:
 - Document category: HIPAA, Privacy, Security, Compliance, Risk, Incident Response, Access Management, or related categories
 - Status: Approved, Effective, Superseded, Archived, Retired
 - Retention rule: 6 years or greater
5. Generate the system report showing retention metadata and document lifecycle history.
6. Export the report in a controlled format such as PDF, CSV, XLSX, or native system audit report.
7. Capture screenshots of the retention rule configuration if the report does not show the retention period directly.
8. Save the exported report and screenshots to the approved audit evidence repository.
9. Record the collection date, collector name, system source, and report parameters used.

## What To Capture

The evidence should include enough detail to prove that documentation is retained for the required period. Capture the following fields where available:

- Document title
- Document unique ID or repository path
- Document type, such as policy, procedure, standard, or form
- HIPAA-related category or tag
- Version number
- Owner or responsible department
- Approval status
- Effective date
- Creation date
- Last reviewed date
- Superseded or archived date, if applicable
- Retention classification or retention label
- Retention period, showing **6 years minimum**
- Disposal or deletion eligibility date
- Legal hold status, if applicable
- Last modified date
- Version history availability
- Access control or permission group, if shown
- System-generated timestamp of the report
- Name of system or repository used

If available, also capture the retention policy configuration screen showing that HIPAA documentation is assigned to a 6-year retention rule.

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Quarterly, and additionally before HIPAA audits, compliance reviews, major policy updates, or repository migrations.
- **Primary Owner:** `[Compliance Officer / Privacy Officer]`
- **Supporting Owners:** `[Information Security Manager]`, `[Records Manager]`, `[Document Control Owner]`, `[IT System Administrator]`

The owner should verify that all active, superseded, and archived HIPAA policies and procedures remain covered by the 6-year retention rule.

## Retention & Storage

Store collected evidence in `[Audit Evidence Repository Name]` under a controlled location such as:

`[Repository Path]/HIPAA/Evidence/Documentation Retention/[Year]/`

Retain the evidence itself for at least 6 years, or longer if required by organisational policy, contract, litigation hold, or regulatory instruction.

Restrict access to authorised compliance, privacy, security, audit, and legal personnel. Do not store evidence only on a local workstation or in personal cloud storage.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence if it shows:

- The record was collected from an authoritative system, not manually fabricated
- HIPAA-related policies and procedures are identifiable
- Each record has sufficient lifecycle metadata, including creation, effective, review, version, and status information
- The retention period is clearly shown as **6 years or greater**
- Superseded, archived, and retired documentation remains retained and traceable
- The report is system-generated or supported by screenshots from the system
- The evidence includes collection date, source system, and report parameters
- Access to the repository and deletion controls are governed
- The evidence is complete enough to demonstrate that required documentation cannot be prematurely deleted or lost

HIPAA-033.title: Breach Notification to HHS / Individuals / Media
HIPAA-033.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [HIPAA-FRM-BREACH-NOTIFICATION-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Privacy Officer |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | HIPAA |
| Classification | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This template is used to document, prepare, approve, and track breach notifications required after an impermissible use or disclosure of unsecured protected health information has been determined to be a reportable breach.

The template supports notification to:

- Affected individuals
- The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
- Prominent media outlets, when required due to the number of affected individuals in a state or jurisdiction
- Business associates, covered entities, or other parties involved in notification coordination

This form is intended to ensure that breach notifications are accurate, complete, timely, consistent, and approved before release.

## Instructions

1. Complete this form after the breach risk assessment has concluded that a reportable breach of unsecured protected health information occurred.
2. Do not use this form to determine whether an incident is a breach. The breach determination must be documented separately in the incident investigation and risk assessment record.
3. Complete all required fields before submitting for approval.
4. Use plain language in notification content. Avoid technical jargon, speculation, or unsupported conclusions.
5. Ensure all dates are accurate and consistent with the incident record, investigation file, and notification deadlines.
6. Coordinate with Legal, Privacy, Security, Compliance, Communications, and affected business units before issuing any external notification.
7. If a business associate is involved, confirm whether the organization or the business associate is responsible for providing individual notifications and ensure this responsibility is documented.
8. If law enforcement has requested a delay in notification, attach the request or document the verbal request details, including the requesting official, agency, date, and scope of delay.
9. Notifications to individuals must be sent without unreasonable delay and within the required timeframe after discovery of the breach, unless a documented law enforcement delay applies.
10. If the breach affects a large number of individuals in a state or jurisdiction, coordinate with Communications and Legal to determine whether media notification is required.
11. Do not include Social Security numbers, full medical record numbers, full account numbers, or other unnecessary sensitive data in notification letters or email subject lines.
12. Retain completed copies of this form, approvals, final notification text, delivery evidence, and related correspondence according to the retention requirements in this template.

| Legal Counsel Assigned | Name / Role | Yes | Identify internal or external legal counsel reviewing the notification. |

| Business Associate Name | Text | Conditional | Required when a business associate caused, contributed to, discovered, or reported the breach. |
| Date Breach Discovered | Date | Yes | Enter the first date the breach was known, or reasonably should have been known, by the organization or workforce member other than the person who committed the breach. |

### Individual Notification Content Checklist

## Approval / Routing

The completed form and notification materials must be routed for review and approval before any external notification is issued, unless emergency circumstances require expedited approval as directed by Legal Counsel and the Privacy Officer.

## Records & Retention

The completed breach notification record must be retained as part of the official privacy incident file. Records must be complete enough to demonstrate what happened, how the breach decision was made, who was notified, when notification occurred, what content was provided, and what corrective actions were taken.

### Records to Retain

| Record | Required | Retention Location | Notes |
|---|:---:|---|---|
| Completed breach notification form | Yes | [System / Repository] | Retain final approved version. |
| Incident investigation record | Yes | [System / Repository] | Include factual investigation notes and timeline. |
| Breach risk assessment and determination | Yes | [System / Repository] | Retain signed or approved determination. |
| Affected individual population and recipient list | Yes | [Secure Repository] | Protect as confidential and limit access. |
| Data element analysis | Yes | [System / Repository] | Document categories of PHI and sensitive information involved. |
| Individual notification letter templates | Yes | [System / Repository] | Retain final approved versions. |
| Copies or samples of mailed notices | Yes | [System / Repository] | Retain sample letters and merge template evidence; avoid unnecessary duplicate PHI. |
| Mailing manifest or delivery certification | Yes | [System / Repository] | Retain vendor certification, postal records, or equivalent proof. |
| Email notification delivery evidence | Conditional | [System / Repository] | Required if email notification is used. |
| Substitute notice evidence | Conditional | [System / Repository] | Required if substitute notice is used. |
| HHS submission confirmation | Yes | [System / Repository] | Retain confirmation number, submission receipt, and submitted content. |
| Media notification evidence | Conditional | [System / Repository] | Required if media notification is made. |
| Law enforcement delay documentation | Conditional | [System / Repository] | Required if a delay is requested. |
| Legal and executive approvals | Yes | [System / Repository] | Retain approval emails, signatures, or workflow records. |
| Communications talking points and call scripts | Conditional | [System / Repository] | Required if call center, media, or public inquiries are expected. |
| Call center logs and inquiry metrics | Conditional | [System / Repository] | Retain summary metrics and escalated complaint records where applicable. |
| Vendor contracts, statements of work, or confidentiality terms | Conditional | [Contract Repository] | Required if vendors support notification or mitigation services. |
| Credit monitoring or identity protection records | Conditional | [System / Repository] | Retain service offer details and enrollment reporting where applicable. |
| Corrective action plan | Yes | [System / Repository] | Include owners, due dates, status, and completion evidence. |
| Lessons learned record | Conditional | [System / Repository] | Required for significant incidents or as directed by Privacy Officer. |
| Closure approval | Yes | [System / Repository] | Retain evidence that notification and follow-up actions were completed. |

### Retention Requirements

| Record Category | Minimum Retention Period | Retention Trigger | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Breach notification record and supporting documentation | 6 years | Date the record was created or last in effect, whichever is later | Privacy Officer |
| HHS submission evidence | 6 years | Date of submission | Privacy Officer |
| Individual and media notification evidence | 6 years | Date notification was issued | Privacy Officer |
| Law enforcement delay documentation | 6 years | Date notification record is closed | Privacy Officer / Legal Counsel |
| Corrective action evidence | 6 years | Date corrective action is completed | Compliance Officer |
| Vendor notification support records | 6 years | Date services are completed or contract record retention period, whichever is longer | Vendor Management |
| Legal advice and privileged communications | As directed by Legal Counsel | Date created | Legal Counsel |

### Storage and Protection Requirements

- Store this form and all related records in the approved privacy incident repository or governance, risk, and compliance system.
- Restrict access to personnel with a legitimate need to know, including Privacy, Legal, Security, Compliance, and assigned operational owners.
- Do not store breach notification working files on unmanaged local drives, personal cloud storage, or unapproved collaboration platforms.
- Mark drafts and final records according to the organization’s information classification standard.
- Protect affected individual lists and delivery files using encryption, access controls, and secure transfer methods.
- Remove unnecessary sensitive identifiers from working papers when they are no longer needed.
- Preserve records subject to legal hold, investigation hold, regulatory inquiry, litigation, or enforcement matter until Legal Counsel authorizes release.
- The Privacy Officer is responsible for confirming that the official breach notification file is complete before closure.

HIPAA-034.title: OCR / HHS Audit Response Pack
HIPAA-034.content:
## What This Evidences

The **OCR / HHS Audit Response Pack** evidences the organisation’s ability to respond to an OCR or HHS audit request under HIPAA by producing complete, accurate, and timely supporting records for privacy, security, breach response, and administrative compliance activities.

This is **operational evidence collected from existing organisational systems**. It must not be authored, recreated, or backfilled as a standalone document. The ZIP package should contain exported records, reports, screenshots, logs, policies, procedures, tickets, attestations, and other source evidence from approved systems of record.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect the audit response pack from the organisation’s authoritative systems, typically including:

- Governance, risk, and compliance platform: `[GRC Tool]`
- Policy management repository: `[Policy Portal / Document Management System]`
- Learning management system: `[LMS]`
- Identity and access management system: `[IAM / SSO Platform]`
- Security monitoring platform: `[SIEM / Log Management Tool]`
- Endpoint/security tooling: `[EDR / Vulnerability Management Tool]`
- Ticketing and workflow system: `[ITSM / Case Management Tool]`
- Incident and breach response repository: `[Incident Management System]`
- Business associate management repository: `[Vendor Risk / Contract Management Tool]`
- Risk assessment repository: `[Risk Register / Risk Assessment Tool]`
- Email or secure correspondence system for OCR/HHS communications: `[Secure Mailbox / eDiscovery Tool]`

## How To Collect

1. Review the OCR/HHS request letter or audit notification and list each requested evidence item.
2. Create an evidence index with request ID, requested item, source system, owner, export date, and file name.
3. Assign each item to the relevant system owner, Privacy Officer, Security Officer, Compliance Officer, HR, IT, or Legal contact.
4. Export evidence directly from the source system using native reporting, audit export, PDF export, CSV export, or screenshot functionality.
5. Where screenshots are required, include the full screen with system name, date/time, user context where appropriate, and the relevant record visible.
6. Preserve original file metadata where possible. Do not alter logs, timestamps, tickets, or system-generated reports.
7. Redact only where approved by Legal or Privacy, and retain an unredacted copy in restricted storage if required.
8. Name files consistently, for example: `[RequestID]_[EvidenceType]_[System]_[YYYY-MM-DD].pdf`.
9. Place all files into a structured folder set, then compress into a ZIP file.
10. Perform a completeness and quality review before submission.

## What To Capture

The ZIP should include, as applicable to the OCR/HHS request:

- Audit request letter and response tracker
- Current HIPAA policies and procedures, with approval and effective dates
- Security risk analysis and risk management action plans
- Workforce training completion records
- Sanctions, access review, and workforce clearance evidence
- System access logs, authentication records, and privileged access reports
- Incident, complaint, and breach investigation records
- Breach notification evidence, if applicable
- Business associate agreements and vendor due diligence records
- Asset, system, and application inventories involving ePHI
- Vulnerability scans, remediation tickets, and patching evidence
- Backup, contingency, and disaster recovery test records
- Audit log review reports and monitoring alerts
- Change management tickets for systems handling ePHI
- Encryption, endpoint protection, and device management evidence
- OCR/HHS correspondence and submission records

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Collected on demand when an OCR or HHS audit, investigation, inquiry, or data request is received. Maintain readiness through periodic compliance evidence reviews.
- **Primary Owner:** `[Privacy Officer]`
- **Supporting Owners:** `[Security Officer]`, `[Compliance Officer]`, `[Legal Counsel]`, `[IT Operations Lead]`, `[HR Lead]`, `[Vendor Risk Owner]`

## Retention & Storage

Store the final ZIP, evidence index, and submission record in `[Secure Compliance Repository]` with restricted access, encryption, and audit logging enabled.

Retain according to the organisation’s HIPAA documentation retention schedule and legal hold requirements, typically no less than the required HIPAA documentation retention period from the date of creation or last effective date. Do not delete while an audit, investigation, dispute, or legal hold remains active.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the pack as sufficient when:

- Each OCR/HHS request item is mapped to a specific evidence file.
- Evidence is exported from authoritative systems, not manually recreated.
- Reports show relevant dates, system names, record owners, and status.
- Logs, tickets, and records cover the requested audit period.
- Policies and procedures show approval, effective dates, and current ownership.
- Training, access, incident, and risk records are complete and traceable.
- Redactions are justified and do not prevent audit verification.
- The ZIP structure is organised, indexed, readable, and complete.
- The organisation can explain where each item came from and who approved submission.

HIPAA-035.title: Annual Risk Analysis Update
HIPAA-035.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| HIPAA-RPT-ARA-001 | 1.0 | Privacy Officer / Security Officer | [Effective Date] | HIPAA | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This report documents the annual update to the organization’s risk analysis for electronic protected health information (ePHI). The purpose of the annual risk analysis update is to identify and assess reasonably anticipated threats and vulnerabilities that could affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of ePHI, evaluate existing safeguards, determine current risk levels, and define actions needed to reduce risk to an acceptable level.

This report supports management decision-making, security planning, privacy oversight, audit readiness, and ongoing risk management. It is intended to provide a practical, evidence-based view of current risk across systems, people, processes, facilities, and third-party relationships that create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI.

The report also confirms whether prior risk treatment activities were completed, whether new risks have emerged since the last review, and whether existing safeguards remain appropriate given changes in operations, technology, workforce behavior, threat activity, and vendor dependencies.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Reporting Period Covered | [Start Date] through [End Date] |
| Risk Analysis Review Dates | [Review Start Date] through [Review Completion Date] |
| Prior Risk Analysis Date | [Prior Report Date] |
| Report Prepared By | [Name / Role / Department] |
| Report Reviewed By | [Name / Role / Committee] |
| Report Approval Authority | [Executive Sponsor / Risk Committee / Compliance Committee] |

### Scope

This annual risk analysis update covers administrative, physical, and technical safeguards related to ePHI across the organization’s operations. The scope includes all systems, applications, devices, processes, facilities, workforce roles, and business associate relationships that create, receive, maintain, access, store, process, or transmit ePHI.

In scope:

- Clinical, billing, administrative, and patient-facing systems containing ePHI.
- Electronic health record and practice management platforms.
- Patient portals, telehealth tools, messaging platforms, and scheduling systems.
- Cloud-hosted systems and managed service providers supporting ePHI.
- Workstations, mobile devices, removable media, and network infrastructure used to access ePHI.
- User access management, authentication, remote access, and privileged access processes.
- Backup, recovery, incident response, logging, monitoring, and vulnerability management processes.
- Physical locations where ePHI systems or devices are used or maintained.
- Third parties and business associates with access to ePHI.
- Workforce training, role-based access, sanctions, and security awareness practices.
- Changes to the environment since the prior risk analysis.

Out of scope:

- Systems confirmed not to create, receive, maintain, access, store, process, or transmit ePHI.
- De-identified data repositories where re-identification is not reasonably possible.
- Personal devices not approved or used for organizational business and not connected to organizational systems.
- Public-facing informational websites that do not collect patient information or authenticate users.

## Executive Summary

The annual risk analysis update found that the organization maintains a generally functioning security and privacy control environment for ePHI, with several effective safeguards in place, including role-based access, workforce privacy and security training, endpoint protection, backups, business associate agreements for major vendors, and documented incident response responsibilities.

However, the review identified areas requiring improvement to reduce the likelihood or impact of unauthorized access, data loss, service disruption, and delayed detection of security events. The highest-priority concerns relate to access review consistency, incomplete vendor risk documentation, limited centralized log review, uneven encryption verification for portable devices, and recovery testing documentation.

The risk environment has changed since the prior review due to increased use of cloud platforms, remote access, patient-facing digital services, and reliance on third-party service providers. These changes do not indicate unmanaged risk by themselves, but they require more formal evidence of monitoring, review, and accountability.

### Management Conclusion

No evidence was identified indicating systemic disregard for ePHI protection obligations. The organization has established foundational safeguards and demonstrates awareness of its responsibility to protect ePHI. However, certain practices are not sufficiently documented or consistently executed to support reliable risk reduction and audit defensibility.

Management should prioritize remediation of high-risk findings within the next reporting cycle and strengthen governance over recurring reviews, vendor oversight, access management, monitoring, and recovery validation.

## Methodology

The annual risk analysis update used a structured, evidence-based approach to evaluate risks to ePHI. The review considered the likelihood of reasonably anticipated threats exploiting known or potential vulnerabilities and the resulting impact to confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

The methodology included:

1. Confirming the inventory of systems, applications, services, workflows, and third parties involving ePHI.
2. Identifying changes since the prior risk analysis.
3. Reviewing prior findings and remediation status.
4. Conducting interviews with system owners, IT personnel, privacy and security leadership, compliance personnel, and selected operational managers.
5. Reviewing policies, procedures, technical configurations, access reports, training records, incident records, vendor documentation, and evidence of safeguards.
6. Evaluating administrative, physical, and technical safeguards.
7. Identifying threats and vulnerabilities relevant to ePHI.
8. Rating risk based on likelihood and impact.
9. Documenting findings, observations, recommendations, and assigned actions.
10. Presenting results to management for review and risk treatment decisions.

### Risk Rating Criteria

Risk ratings were assigned using likelihood and impact. The ratings reflect residual risk after considering safeguards already in place.

#### Likelihood

| Rating | Definition |
|---|---|
| Low | The threat is unlikely to occur, safeguards are strong, and there is limited exposure. |
| Medium | The threat could reasonably occur, safeguards are partially effective, or exposure is increasing. |
| High | The threat is likely, there is known exposure, safeguards are weak or inconsistent, or similar events have occurred. |

#### Impact

| Rating | Definition |
|---|---|
| Low | Limited operational disruption, limited ePHI exposure, minimal patient or organizational impact. |
| Medium | Meaningful operational disruption, potential unauthorized access to ePHI, compliance impact, or reputational concern. |
| High | Significant ePHI exposure, material service disruption, patient safety concern, reportable incident risk, legal exposure, or major reputational harm. |

#### Overall Risk

| Likelihood | Impact | Overall Risk |
|---|---|---|
| Low | Low | Low |
| Low | Medium | Low to Medium |
| Low | High | Medium |
| Medium | Low | Medium |
| Medium | Medium | Medium |
| Medium | High | High |
| High | Low | Medium |
| High | Medium | High |
| High | High | Critical |

### Limitations

This report reflects evidence available during the review period. It is not a penetration test, forensic investigation, financial audit, or legal opinion. Control effectiveness was assessed using interviews, records, sample evidence, and available system reports. Where documentation was unavailable, inconsistent, or incomplete, the risk rating reflects the uncertainty created by lack of evidence.

### ARA-01 - Periodic User Access Reviews Are Not Consistently Documented

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Area | Access Management |
| Risk Rating | High |
| Likelihood | Medium |
| Impact | High |
| Owner | [IT / System Owners] |
| Status | Open |

#### Observation

The organization has role-based access controls for major systems containing ePHI. However, evidence of periodic access review was incomplete or inconsistent across systems. Some systems had recent access review records, while others relied on informal manager confirmation or did not retain evidence of review.

#### Risk

Without documented access reviews, terminated users, transferred workforce members, excessive permissions, shared accounts, or unnecessary privileged access may remain active. This increases the risk of unauthorized access to ePHI and weakens the organization’s ability to demonstrate that workforce access is appropriate.

#### Existing Safeguards

- User provisioning requires manager approval for primary systems.
- Human Resources notifies IT of terminations.
- Role-based access templates exist for common job functions.
- Unique user accounts are generally used for workforce access.
- Some system owners perform ad hoc access reviews.

#### Recommendation

Implement a formal access review schedule for all systems containing ePHI. Require system owners and department managers to review active users, role assignments, privileged permissions, inactive accounts, and terminated workforce members. Retain review evidence, approvals, exceptions, and remediation actions.

#### Required Action
