### Risk Rating Criteria

| Rating | Description | Typical Indicators |
|---|---|---|
| Low | Risk is unlikely to materially affect individuals or the organisation, and safeguards are strong and operating effectively. | Limited personal data, low sensitivity, strong encryption, limited onward transfers, transparent recipient practices. |
| Medium | Risk could affect individuals or the organisation if safeguards fail or circumstances change. Additional controls or monitoring are required. | Moderate sensitivity, public authority access concerns, multiple sub-processors, incomplete evidence, reliance on contractual measures plus technical controls. |
| High | Risk may cause significant harm to individuals or expose the organisation to material compliance, legal, operational, or reputational impact. Transfer should not proceed without remediation or senior risk acceptance. | Highly sensitive data, weak safeguards, extensive onward transfers, problematic legal environment, inadequate recipient transparency or control. |
| Critical | Risk is unacceptable in the current state. Transfer should not proceed or should be suspended until controls are materially improved. | Sensitive data exposed to access without effective safeguards, no enforceable protections, no credible vendor cooperation, inability to meet individual rights or security obligations. |

### Limitations

This report is based on information available at the time of assessment. The conclusions may change if:

- The recipient changes hosting, support, or processing locations.
- New sub-processors are introduced.
- The destination country changes relevant laws or public authority access practices.
- The recipient materially changes its security or privacy controls.
- The personal data categories, processing purpose, volume, retention period, or data subject groups change.
- New regulatory guidance, court decisions, or enforcement trends affect the transfer risk position.
- Evidence provided by the vendor is inaccurate, incomplete, outdated, or not independently verifiable.

- Store the report in an approved document repository with access controls.
- Avoid copying report content into unmanaged systems, email threads, or collaboration spaces.
- Protect any vendor confidential information in line with contractual obligations.
- Follow secure disposal requirements when the report is superseded or no longer required.

### Retention

| Record | Retention Requirement | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Final approved TIA report | Retain for the life of the transfer plus [Retention Period] | Data Protection Officer |
| Evidence reviewed | Retain with assessment file or linked repository | Privacy / Legal / Security |
| Approval records | Retain with final report | Data Protection Officer |
| Remediation evidence | Retain until action closure and next review cycle | Action Owners |
| Superseded versions | Retain according to document retention schedule | Document Owner |

### Version Control

| Version | Date | Author | Summary of Changes | Approval Status |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | [Date] | [Author] | Initial draft | Draft |
| 0.2 | [Date] | [Author] | Stakeholder updates | Draft |
| 1.0 | [Date] | [Author] | Approved version | Approved |

GDPR-013.title: External Privacy Notice
GDPR-013.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [GDPR-POL-PRIV-001] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer | [DD Month YYYY] | GDPR | Public |

## Purpose

This Policy defines the mandatory requirements for providing clear, accurate and accessible privacy information to individuals whose personal data is processed by [Organisation Name].

The purpose of the External Privacy Notice is to ensure that individuals understand:

- who is responsible for processing their personal data;
- what personal data is collected or otherwise obtained;
- why the personal data is processed;
- the lawful basis relied upon for each processing purpose;
- where the personal data comes from, where it is not collected directly from the individual;
- who the personal data is shared with;
- whether the personal data is transferred internationally;
- how long the personal data is retained;
- what rights individuals have over their personal data; and
- how individuals can contact [Organisation Name] or raise a concern.

This Policy supports transparent, fair and accountable processing of personal data and sets minimum standards for the creation, approval, publication and maintenance of privacy notices.

## Scope

This Policy applies to all external privacy notices issued by [Organisation Name] to individuals whose personal data is processed by or on behalf of [Organisation Name], including but not limited to:

- customers, prospective customers and end users;
- website and mobile application users;
- marketing contacts and event attendees;
- suppliers, contractors and business contacts;
- visitors to [Organisation Name] premises;
- job applicants and recruitment candidates;
- complainants, enquirers and correspondents;
- individuals whose personal data is received from third parties; and
- individuals whose personal data is processed through online tracking technologies, analytics tools or similar technologies.

This Policy applies to personal data collected:

- directly from the individual;
- indirectly from another organisation, public source, referral, partner, customer or third-party provider;
- automatically through systems, devices, applications, cookies, logs or similar technologies; and
- through paper, telephone, email, web forms, applications, portals, social media, events or in-person interactions.

This Policy applies to all business units, employees, workers, contractors and third parties acting on behalf of [Organisation Name] who design, operate, procure or change processing activities involving personal data.

This Policy does not replace internal employee privacy notices, contract clauses, consent forms, cookie banners, just-in-time notices or product-specific notices, but it sets the minimum transparency requirements that those materials shall meet where applicable.

## Policy Statements

1. **Publication of External Privacy Notice**

 1.1. [Organisation Name] shall maintain an External Privacy Notice that is publicly available, easy to locate and written in clear, plain language.

 1.2. The External Privacy Notice shall be accessible from all primary public digital channels where personal data is collected, including [organisation website], customer portals, mobile applications and relevant online forms.

 1.3. The External Privacy Notice shall be provided or made available before or at the time personal data is collected directly from an individual, unless the individual already has the required information.

 1.4. Where personal data is not collected directly from the individual, [Organisation Name] shall provide the External Privacy Notice within a reasonable period after obtaining the personal data, unless a valid and documented reason applies for not doing so.

 1.5. The External Privacy Notice shall not be hidden within general terms and conditions or written in a way that makes privacy information difficult to identify or understand.

2. **Required Content of the External Privacy Notice**

 2.1. The External Privacy Notice shall identify [Organisation Name] as the organisation responsible for deciding how and why the relevant personal data is processed.

 2.2. The External Privacy Notice shall include the contact details of [Organisation Name] and the Data Protection Officer or privacy contact.

 2.3. The External Privacy Notice shall describe the categories of personal data processed in a way that is specific enough for individuals to understand what information is involved.

 2.4. The External Privacy Notice shall explain the purposes for which personal data is processed.

 2.5. The External Privacy Notice shall identify the lawful basis relied upon for each processing purpose.

 2.6. Where processing is based on legitimate interests, the External Privacy Notice shall explain the relevant interest pursued by [Organisation Name] or a third party.

 2.7. Where processing is based on consent, the External Privacy Notice shall explain that consent can be withdrawn at any time and how withdrawal can be requested.

 2.8. Where processing is necessary for a contract or a legal requirement, the External Privacy Notice shall explain whether the individual is required to provide the personal data and the possible consequences of not providing it.

 2.9. Where special category data or criminal offence-related data is processed, the External Privacy Notice shall describe the nature of that data and the additional condition relied upon for processing it.

 2.10. Where personal data is obtained from a source other than the individual, the External Privacy Notice shall identify the source or category of source, unless doing so would not be possible or would undermine a lawful confidentiality obligation.

 2.11. The External Privacy Notice shall identify the categories of recipients with whom personal data is shared, including service providers, professional advisers, public authorities, group companies, partners and other relevant third parties.

 2.12. The External Privacy Notice shall explain whether personal data is transferred outside the jurisdiction in which it was collected and the safeguards used to protect it.

 2.13. The External Privacy Notice shall state the period for which personal data is retained or, where a fixed period cannot be stated, the criteria used to determine the retention period.

 2.14. The External Privacy Notice shall explain the rights available to individuals in relation to their personal data and how those rights can be exercised.

 2.15. The External Privacy Notice shall explain the right to lodge a complaint with the relevant data protection supervisory authority.

 2.16. The External Privacy Notice shall explain whether automated decision-making, including profiling, is used to make decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects for individuals.

 2.17. Where significant automated decision-making is used, the External Privacy Notice shall provide meaningful information about the logic involved, the significance of the processing and the expected consequences for the individual.

 2.18. The External Privacy Notice shall include the effective date or last updated date.

3. **Minimum Notice Content Standard**

 3.1. Each External Privacy Notice shall meet the following minimum content standard:

| Notice Element | Mandatory Requirement | Example Wording Standard |
|---|---|---|
| Organisation identity | Shall clearly name the controller and provide contact details | “The organisation responsible for your personal data is [Organisation Name], located at [Registered Address].” |
| Privacy contact | Shall provide an accessible contact route for privacy questions and rights requests | “You can contact our Data Protection Officer at [privacy email address].” |
| Data categories | Shall describe the types of personal data processed | “We process contact details, account information, transaction records and communications with us.” |
| Source of data | Shall explain whether data is collected directly or obtained from others | “We may receive your details from [source category], such as referral partners or publicly available registers.” |
| Processing purposes | Shall explain each significant purpose of processing | “We use your personal data to provide services, manage accounts, respond to enquiries and meet legal obligations.” |
| Lawful basis | Shall link the lawful basis to each purpose | “We process billing information because it is necessary to perform our contract with you.” |
| Legitimate interests | Shall identify the relevant interest where relied upon | “We use limited business contact details to manage our relationship with corporate customers.” |
| Sharing | Shall identify recipient categories | “We share personal data with hosting providers, payment processors, delivery partners and professional advisers.” |
| International transfers | Shall explain where transfers may occur and safeguards used | “Where data is transferred internationally, we use approved contractual safeguards or other lawful protections.” |
| Retention | Shall state retention periods or criteria | “We keep account records for the duration of the relationship and for [X years] afterwards where required for legal or audit purposes.” |
| Individual rights | Shall describe available rights and how to exercise them | “You may request access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability or objection by contacting [privacy email address].” |
| Complaints | Shall explain escalation options | “You may contact us first, and you also have the right to complain to the relevant supervisory authority.” |
| Automated decisions | Shall explain whether significant automated decisions are made | “We do not use your personal data to make solely automated decisions that have legal or similarly significant effects on you.” |
| Updates | Shall state how changes are communicated | “We will update this notice when our processing changes materially.” |

4. **Timing of Privacy Information**

 4.1. Privacy information shall be provided at a time that allows the individual to make an informed decision about providing personal data or continuing to use the relevant service.

 4.2. Where personal data is collected directly from an individual through a form, portal, application, call script, paper document or in-person process, a link to or copy of the relevant privacy notice shall be provided at the point of collection.

 4.3. Where personal data is collected indirectly, the responsible business owner shall ensure that privacy information is provided within the required timeframe unless an approved exception applies.

 4.4. The following timing standard shall apply:

| Collection Scenario | Timing Requirement | Responsible Party |
|---|---|---|
| Website form, app form or portal registration | Privacy notice shall be linked before submission | Digital Product Owner |
| Marketing sign-up | Privacy information shall be provided before the individual subscribes | Marketing Owner |
| Sales enquiry | Privacy information shall be provided at or before first substantive interaction | Sales Owner |
| Customer onboarding | Privacy notice shall be provided before account activation or service start | Customer Operations Owner |
| Event registration | Privacy information shall be provided before registration is completed | Events Owner |
| Supplier contact onboarding | Privacy notice shall be provided before or at first collection of business contact details | Procurement Owner |
| Visitor registration | Privacy information shall be available before or at check-in | Facilities Owner |
| Data obtained from a third party | Privacy information shall be provided within a reasonable period and no later than first communication where communication occurs | Business Process Owner |
| Data intended for disclosure to another recipient | Privacy information shall be provided before first disclosure, unless already provided | Business Process Owner |

5. **Layered and Contextual Notices**

 5.1. [Organisation Name] shall use layered privacy notices where this improves clarity, including short notices at the point of collection supported by a full External Privacy Notice.

 5.2. Short-form notices shall include, at minimum, the identity of [Organisation Name], the main processing purpose, any unexpected or high-impact use of the data, a link to the full External Privacy Notice and a contact point.

 5.3. Just-in-time notices shall be used where personal data is collected in a context that may not be obvious to the individual, such as location data, device identifiers, behavioural analytics, optional profile information or sensitive information.

 5.4. Product-specific or service-specific notices shall be used where the general External Privacy Notice would not provide enough detail about a particular service, feature, audience or processing activity.

6. **Information Collected Directly from Individuals**

 6.1. When personal data is collected directly from an individual, [Organisation Name] shall ensure that the individual receives all relevant privacy information at the time the data is collected.

 6.2. Data collection forms shall include a link to the applicable privacy notice and shall not require the individual to accept unrelated terms as a substitute for receiving privacy information.

 6.3. Consent requests shall be presented separately from general privacy information where consent is relied upon as the lawful basis for processing.

 6.4. Consent wording shall be specific, unambiguous and separate from the External Privacy Notice.

 6.5. Where children or vulnerable individuals are likely to use a service, the privacy information shall be written in a way appropriate for the intended audience.

7. **Information Not Collected Directly from Individuals**

 7.1. Where [Organisation Name] receives personal data from third parties, public sources, referrals, business partners or other indirect sources, the External Privacy Notice shall explain the categories of source and the categories of personal data obtained.

 7.2. The business owner receiving indirectly collected personal data shall confirm that the source of the data was lawful and that privacy information can be provided to the individual where required.

 7.3. Where [Organisation Name] decides not to provide privacy information directly to an individual because it is impossible, would involve disproportionate effort, would seriously impair the purpose of processing, or is restricted by law, the rationale shall be documented and approved by the Data Protection Officer.

 7.4. Where direct notice is not provided due to disproportionate effort, [Organisation Name] shall consider appropriate alternative transparency measures, such as publishing clear public information, providing notice through the data source, or using communication channels already available.

8. **Lawful Basis Transparency**

 8.1. Each purpose of processing described in the External Privacy Notice shall be linked to a lawful basis.

 8.2. The External Privacy Notice shall not use broad or vague lawful basis statements that prevent individuals from understanding why their personal data is processed.

 8.3. Where more than one lawful basis applies across different purposes, the notice shall distinguish between those purposes.

 8.4. Where legitimate interests are relied upon, the privacy notice shall describe the nature of those interests in plain language.

 8.5. Where the lawful basis changes for an existing processing activity, the privacy notice shall be reviewed and updated before the changed processing begins, unless urgent legal or safety reasons require immediate action.

9. **Data Sharing and Processors**

 9.1. The External Privacy Notice shall describe the categories of third parties with whom personal data may be shared.

 9.2. Where sharing is material, unexpected, high-risk or central to the service, the notice shall provide more specific information about the recipient or recipient category.

 9.3. Where third-party service providers process personal data on behalf of [Organisation Name], the notice shall explain the types of providers used, such as hosting providers, customer support platforms, payment processors, analytics providers, communication tools or professional advisers.

 9.4. Personal data shall not be shared with a new category of recipient unless the relevant privacy notice has been reviewed and updated where necessary.

10. **International Transfers**

 10.1. The External Privacy Notice shall explain whether personal data may be transferred to or accessed from countries outside the individual’s jurisdiction.

 10.2. Where international transfers occur, the notice shall describe the safeguards used to protect the data in plain language.

 10.3. The notice shall provide a method for individuals to request further information about transfer safeguards where applicable.

 10.4. Business owners shall notify the Data Protection Officer before implementing new suppliers, systems or support arrangements that create new international transfer arrangements.

11. **Retention Transparency**

 11.1. The External Privacy Notice shall describe how long personal data is retained.

 11.2. Where exact retention periods are known, they shall be stated in the notice or in an accessible linked retention summary.

 11.3. Where exact periods cannot be stated, the notice shall explain the criteria used to determine retention, such as account duration, legal limitation periods, regulatory requirements, audit needs, dispute handling, security needs or user preferences.

 11.4. Retention statements in the External Privacy Notice shall align with the approved Records Retention Schedule.

12. **Individual Rights**

 12.1. The External Privacy Notice shall explain the rights individuals may have in relation to their personal data, including the right to request access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, objection and withdrawal of consent where applicable.

 12.2. The notice shall explain that some rights are subject to conditions and may not apply in every case.

 12.3. The notice shall provide a clear and accessible method for submitting rights requests.

 12.4. The notice shall state that [Organisation Name] may need to verify the identity of the requester before responding to a rights request.

 12.5. The notice shall not discourage individuals from exercising their rights or imply that rights requests are subject to unnecessary formalities.

13. **Automated Decision-Making and Profiling**

 13.1. The External Privacy Notice shall state whether [Organisation Name] uses automated decision-making or profiling that has legal or similarly significant effects on individuals.

 13.2. Where such processing occurs, the notice shall explain the decision involved, the data used, the general logic of the process, the potential effect on the individual and how the individual can request human review or challenge the decision.

 13.3. Where profiling is used for marketing, personalisation, risk assessment, fraud prevention or service optimisation, the privacy notice shall describe this in a way that is clear and proportionate to the impact on individuals.

14. **Cookies, Tracking and Similar Technologies**

 14.1. Where cookies, pixels, software development kits, device identifiers, analytics tools or similar technologies are used, the External Privacy Notice shall be consistent with the Cookie Notice, Cookie Banner and Cookie Preference Centre.

 14.2. The External Privacy Notice shall describe the main purposes for which tracking technologies are used, such as essential service operation, analytics, personalisation, advertising, security or fraud prevention.

 14.3. Non-essential tracking technologies shall not be described as essential where they are not strictly required to provide the requested service.

 14.4. Changes to tracking technologies shall trigger a review of relevant privacy and cookie notices before deployment.

15. **Accuracy and Change Control**

 15.1. The External Privacy Notice shall accurately reflect actual processing activities.

 15.2. Business owners shall notify the Data Protection Officer of any new or materially changed processing activity before it goes live.

 15.3. The External Privacy Notice shall be reviewed before launching new products, services, campaigns, systems, data-sharing arrangements, analytics tools, artificial intelligence features or international processing arrangements.

 15.4. Privacy notice updates shall be controlled through the approved document management process.

 15.5. Material changes to the External Privacy Notice shall be communicated to affected individuals where appropriate, taking account of the nature of the change and its impact on individuals.

16. **Accessibility and Plain Language**

 16.1. The External Privacy Notice shall be concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible.

 16.2. The notice shall be written in plain language suitable for the intended audience.

 16.3. The notice shall avoid unnecessary legal jargon, unexplained technical terms and vague statements such as “we may use your data for business purposes” without further explanation.

 16.4. The notice shall be available in accessible digital formats and shall support assistive technologies where published online.

 16.5. Where [Organisation Name] targets or regularly serves individuals in multiple languages or jurisdictions, translated or localised versions of the notice shall be provided where necessary.

17. **Evidence and Record Keeping**

 17.1. [Organisation Name] shall retain evidence of approved versions of the External Privacy Notice.

 17.2. Records shall include the notice version, approval date, effective date, publication location, approver and summary of changes.

 17.3. Where notices are provided through systems, forms, portals or applications, [Organisation Name] shall retain evidence that the notice was available at the point of collection.

 17.4. The Data Protection Officer shall maintain or have access to a register of published privacy notices and associated business owners.

| Record | Minimum Retention | Owner |
|---|---:|---|
| Approved privacy notice versions | [X years] after replacement | Data Protection Officer |
| Privacy notice change log | [X years] | Data Protection Officer |
| Evidence of publication | [X years] | Digital / Communications Owner |
| Approval records | [X years] | Data Protection Officer |
| Exceptions and rationale records | [X years] | Data Protection Officer |
| Business owner review confirmations | [X years] | Business Process Owner |

18. **Consistency with Other Documents**

 18.1. The External Privacy Notice shall be consistent with internal records of processing activities, data protection impact assessments, data sharing arrangements, supplier contracts, retention schedules, consent records and cookie documentation.

 18.2. Where inconsistency is identified, processing records and external notices shall be corrected promptly.

 18.3. Business units shall not publish separate privacy wording externally without review and approval by the Data Protection Officer or authorised privacy delegate.

19. **Approval and Publication**

 19.1. The External Privacy Notice shall be approved by the Data Protection Officer before publication.

 19.2. Legal review shall be obtained where the notice relates to high-risk processing, sensitive data, automated decision-making, international transfers, new jurisdictions, children’s data, large-scale profiling or complex data-sharing arrangements.

 19.3. Communications or Digital teams shall publish only the approved version provided through the agreed document management process.

 19.4. Superseded versions shall be removed from active publication unless there is a valid business or legal reason to retain them in an archive.

20. **Prohibited Practices**

 20.1. [Organisation Name] shall not collect personal data through external channels without providing appropriate privacy information.

 20.2. [Organisation Name] shall not rely on generic, incomplete or misleading privacy wording.

 20.3. [Organisation Name] shall not state or imply that personal data will be used only for limited purposes if additional processing purposes are planned or known.

 20.4. [Organisation Name] shall not bury important privacy information in documents that individuals are unlikely to read or cannot reasonably access.

 20.5. [Organisation Name] shall not launch new processing activities where required privacy notice updates have not been completed, unless approved through the exceptions process.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board / Executive Management | Provides oversight of privacy governance and ensures appropriate resources are available to meet transparency obligations. |
| Data Protection Officer | Owns this Policy; approves the External Privacy Notice; advises on transparency requirements; reviews exceptions; monitors compliance; maintains evidence of approved notices. |
| Legal Counsel | Provides legal advice on privacy notice wording, data-sharing disclosures, international transfers, sensitive processing, automated decision-making and jurisdiction-specific requirements. |
| Business Process Owners | Identify processing activities requiring privacy information; ensure the notice accurately reflects actual processing; notify the Data Protection Officer of changes before implementation. |
| Marketing Owner | Ensures privacy information is provided for marketing activities, campaigns, events, preference management, analytics and lead generation activities. |
| Digital / Product Owners | Ensure privacy notices are accessible through websites, applications, portals, forms, product interfaces and user journeys at the appropriate points. |
| Procurement Owner | Ensures supplier-related processing and third-party service provider arrangements are reflected in privacy notices where required. |
| Information Security Owner | Advises on security-related processing, logging, monitoring, fraud prevention and technical measures that may need to be described in privacy notices. |
| Human Resources / Recruitment Owner | Ensures external recruitment privacy information is provided to candidates and agency-referred applicants where applicable. |
| Customer Operations Owner | Ensures customers and service users receive appropriate privacy information during onboarding, support and service delivery. |
| Communications Team | Publishes approved privacy notices and supports clear, accessible external communication of material updates. |
| Employees and Contractors | Follow this Policy; use only approved privacy wording; escalate new or changed personal data processing to the relevant business owner and Data Protection Officer. |
| Third Parties Acting on Behalf of [Organisation Name] | Provide or display approved privacy information where required under contract or agreed process. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

1. Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all personnel and business units within scope.

2. The Data Protection Officer shall monitor compliance with this Policy through appropriate activities, which may include:

 - review of published privacy notices;
 - review of web forms, application screens and data collection points;
 - sampling of marketing, sales, recruitment and customer onboarding journeys;
 - comparison of privacy notices against processing records;
 - review of new project and change assessments;
 - supplier onboarding checks;
 - review of cookie and tracking technology disclosures;
 - review of rights request trends and complaints; and
 - internal audit or assurance reviews.

3. The following compliance indicators shall be maintained where practical:

| Compliance Indicator | Target / Expectation | Reporting Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| External Privacy Notice reviewed within scheduled period | 100% | At least annually |
| New processing activities reviewed for notice impact before launch | 100% | Quarterly |
| Published notice matches approved version | 100% | Quarterly |
| Data collection points include privacy notice link or approved wording | 100% | Quarterly |
| Material notice updates approved before publication | 100% | As required |
| Exceptions documented and approved | 100% | Quarterly |
| Identified notice defects remediated within agreed timeframe | [X business days] for high priority issues | Quarterly |

4. Non-compliance shall be reported to the Data Protection Officer and may be escalated to Legal Counsel, Risk Management, Information Security, Executive Management or the relevant governance forum.

5. Where a privacy notice deficiency creates a risk to individuals or to [Organisation Name], the Data Protection Officer shall require corrective action, which may include:

 - immediate update or withdrawal of inaccurate wording;
 - suspension of a data collection activity;
 - update to forms, scripts, portals or product interfaces;
 - communication of revised privacy information to affected individuals;
 - completion or update of a data protection impact assessment;
 - supplier remediation;
 - additional staff training; or
 - escalation for disciplinary or contractual action.

6. Breaches of this Policy by employees may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment, subject to applicable employment procedures.

7. Breaches by contractors, suppliers or partners may result in contractual remedies, suspension of access, remediation requirements or termination of the relevant agreement.

8. Where a deficiency may indicate a personal data breach or unlawful processing, it shall be escalated under the applicable incident response and data breach management process.

## Exceptions

1. Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented, lawful and risk-assessed reason.

2. Exceptions shall be approved by the Data Protection Officer before the relevant processing begins or continues, unless urgent circumstances require immediate action.

3. Exception requests shall include:

 - the processing activity concerned;
 - the individuals affected;
 - the privacy information that will not be provided or will be delayed;
 - the reason for the exception;
 - the risks to individuals;
 - proposed alternative transparency measures;
 - legal advice, where required;
 - the exception owner;
 - the expiry date or review date; and
 - required compensating controls.

4. Exceptions may be considered where providing privacy information directly to the individual is impossible, would involve disproportionate effort, would seriously impair a lawful processing objective, would conflict with a legal obligation, or would breach a valid duty of confidentiality.

5. Exceptions shall not be used to avoid inconvenience, cost, poor planning, system limitations or commercial sensitivity where privacy information can reasonably be provided.

6. Approved exceptions shall be recorded in the Privacy Exceptions Register.

| Exception Field | Required Information |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | [EXC-YYYY-###] |
| Business owner | [Name / role] |
| Processing activity | Description of the activity |
| Affected individuals | Category of individuals |
| Reason for exception | Specific lawful and practical reason |
| Risk assessment | Summary of risks and mitigation |
| Alternative transparency measures | Public notice, third-party notice, delayed notice or other approach |
| Approval | Data Protection Officer and Legal Counsel where required |
| Effective date | [DD Month YYYY] |
| Expiry / review date | [DD Month YYYY] |
| Status | Approved / Rejected / Expired / Withdrawn |

7. Exceptions shall be reviewed at least by their expiry date and withdrawn where they are no longer justified.

## Review & Maintenance

1. This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to legal requirements, organisational structure, processing activities, technology, products, services, jurisdictions, data-sharing arrangements or risk profile.

2. The External Privacy Notice shall be reviewed at least annually and before any material change to processing activities that affects individuals.

3. The Data Protection Officer shall coordinate Policy and notice reviews with relevant stakeholders, including Legal, Information Security, Marketing, Digital, Product, Procurement, Customer Operations and relevant business process owners.

4. Business process owners shall confirm, at least annually, whether the privacy information relating to their processing activities remains accurate and complete.

5. Updates to this Policy shall be approved by [Policy Approval Authority].

6. Updates to the External Privacy Notice shall be approved by the Data Protection Officer before publication.

7. Version history shall be maintained for this Policy and the External Privacy Notice.

| Version | Date | Summary of Changes | Approved By |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [DD Month YYYY] | Initial release | [Approver Name / Role] |

GDPR-014.title: Internal Data Protection Policy
GDPR-014.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-DP-001] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | [Effective Date] | GDPR | Internal |

## Purpose

This Internal Data Protection Policy establishes the organisation’s mandatory requirements for protecting personal data and demonstrating accountable, lawful, fair and transparent processing.

The purpose of this Policy is to ensure that the organisation:

- Processes personal data only for valid, clearly defined and lawful business purposes.
- Respects the rights and freedoms of individuals whose personal data is processed.
- Applies appropriate governance, security and oversight to personal data throughout its lifecycle.
- Maintains evidence that data protection obligations are understood, implemented and monitored.
- Embeds data protection into business activities, projects, systems, supplier relationships and operational decision-making.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All employees, workers, contractors, consultants, temporary staff, interns, officers and directors of the organisation.
- All business units, functions, locations and subsidiaries that process personal data on behalf of the organisation.
- All personal data processed by or for the organisation, whether in electronic, paper, audio, video or any other format.
- All systems, applications, databases, devices, networks, cloud services, collaboration platforms, archives and physical storage locations used to process personal data.
- All processing activities performed by third parties, suppliers, service providers, partners or other external parties on behalf of the organisation.

This Policy applies to personal data relating to, including but not limited to:

- Customers, prospects and website users.
- Employees, applicants, contractors and former personnel.
- Suppliers, partners and business contacts.
- Complainants, visitors and event participants.
- Any other identifiable individual whose data is processed by the organisation.

This Policy applies across the full data lifecycle, including collection, recording, storage, access, use, sharing, transfer, retention, archiving, anonymisation and deletion.

## Policy Statements

1. **The organisation shall process personal data lawfully, fairly and transparently.**

 1.1. The organisation shall identify and document a valid lawful basis before processing personal data.

 1.2. The organisation shall ensure individuals are provided with clear, concise and accessible information about how their personal data is used.

 1.3. The organisation shall not process personal data in a way that is unexpected, misleading or incompatible with the information provided to individuals.

 1.4. The organisation shall ensure that privacy notices are kept accurate, current and aligned with actual processing activities.

2. **The organisation shall process personal data only for specified and legitimate purposes.**

 2.1. The organisation shall define the business purpose for each processing activity before collecting or using personal data.

 2.2. The organisation shall not use personal data for new, incompatible purposes unless a lawful basis has been confirmed and appropriate transparency information has been provided.

 2.3. Business owners shall consult the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead before introducing materially new uses of personal data, including analytics, profiling, automation, marketing, monitoring or data sharing.

3. **The organisation shall collect and process only the personal data necessary for the intended purpose.**

 3.1. The organisation shall limit the collection of personal data to what is adequate, relevant and necessary for the stated purpose.

 3.2. Forms, systems, reports and data extracts shall be designed to avoid excessive or unnecessary personal data collection.

 3.3. Sensitive or high-risk personal data shall be collected only where there is a clear business need, a lawful basis, appropriate safeguards and documented approval.

4. **The organisation shall keep personal data accurate and up to date where necessary.**

 4.1. The organisation shall take reasonable steps to ensure personal data is accurate, complete and current in relation to the purpose for which it is processed.

 4.2. Individuals shall be provided with appropriate mechanisms to correct inaccurate personal data.

 4.3. Business owners shall ensure inaccurate personal data is corrected, restricted or deleted without undue delay where required.

5. **The organisation shall retain personal data only for as long as necessary.**

 5.1. Personal data shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s approved retention schedule.

 5.2. Retention periods shall be based on legal, regulatory, contractual, operational and evidential requirements.

 5.3. Personal data shall be securely deleted, anonymised or archived when it is no longer required.

 5.4. Personal data shall not be retained indefinitely unless there is a documented and approved legal or business justification.

6. **The organisation shall protect personal data against unauthorised or unlawful processing, loss, destruction or damage.**

 6.1. Personal data shall be protected using appropriate technical and organisational security measures proportionate to the risk.

 6.2. Access to personal data shall be granted on a need-to-know and least-privilege basis.

 6.3. Systems processing personal data shall use appropriate authentication, access controls, encryption, logging, backup and recovery controls.

 6.4. Personal data shall not be stored on unauthorised devices, personal email accounts, unmanaged cloud storage, removable media or unapproved messaging platforms.

 6.5. Physical records containing personal data shall be stored securely and protected from unauthorised access, loss or damage.

7. **The organisation shall maintain accountability for data protection compliance.**

 7.1. The organisation shall maintain documented evidence of its data protection governance, decisions, controls and compliance activities.

 7.2. Records of processing activities shall be maintained and kept current for all material processing activities.

 7.3. Each business area shall be responsible for understanding and documenting the personal data it processes, why it is processed, where it is stored, who it is shared with and how long it is retained.

 7.4. Data protection risks shall be identified, assessed, managed and reported through appropriate governance channels.

8. **The organisation shall apply data protection by design and by default.**

 8.1. Data protection requirements shall be considered at the start of all new projects, systems, products, services, processes and supplier engagements involving personal data.

 8.2. Default settings in systems and processes shall be configured to minimise personal data collection, visibility, retention and sharing.

 8.3. Project teams shall complete privacy assessments where processing is new, materially changed, high risk, large scale, sensitive, automated, intrusive or involves vulnerable individuals.

 8.4. Privacy risks shall be addressed before go-live unless an approved risk acceptance is in place.

9. **The organisation shall conduct privacy assessments for high-risk processing.**

 9.1. A privacy assessment shall be completed before commencing processing that may result in significant risk to individuals.

 9.2. Privacy assessments shall evaluate the purpose, necessity, proportionality, risks, safeguards and residual risk of the proposed processing.

 9.3. Processing shall not proceed where unacceptable privacy risks remain unresolved.

 9.4. Completed privacy assessments shall be retained as evidence of decision-making and risk management.

10. **The organisation shall respect and enable individual data protection rights.**

 10.1. The organisation shall provide individuals with clear channels to exercise their rights in relation to their personal data.

 10.2. Requests from individuals shall be logged, verified, assessed and fulfilled within required timeframes.

 10.3. The organisation shall not obstruct, discourage or penalise individuals for exercising their rights.

 10.4. Responses to rights requests shall be accurate, complete and appropriately reviewed before release.

 10.5. Where a request cannot be fulfilled in whole or in part, the organisation shall explain the reason in clear language unless legally restricted from doing so.

11. **The organisation shall manage consent appropriately where consent is used.**

 11.1. Consent shall be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous.

 11.2. Consent requests shall be separate from general terms and conditions and shall not use pre-ticked boxes, inactivity or implied acceptance.

 11.3. Individuals shall be able to withdraw consent as easily as they gave it.

 11.4. Records of consent shall be maintained, including what the individual was told, when consent was obtained, how it was obtained and whether it has been withdrawn.

 11.5. The organisation shall not rely on consent where there is a significant imbalance of power or where consent is not genuinely optional.

12. **The organisation shall apply additional safeguards for sensitive personal data.**

 12.1. Sensitive personal data shall be processed only where there is a lawful basis, a permitted condition and a documented business need.

 12.2. Sensitive personal data shall be subject to enhanced access controls, security measures and retention controls.

 12.3. Processing of sensitive personal data shall be reviewed by the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead before implementation.

 12.4. Sensitive personal data shall not be used for secondary purposes without appropriate assessment and approval.

13. **The organisation shall manage personal data breaches promptly and effectively.**

 13.1. All suspected or actual personal data breaches shall be reported immediately through the approved incident reporting channel.

 13.2. Employees and contractors shall not investigate, conceal, delete evidence of or delay reporting a suspected personal data breach.

 13.3. The organisation shall assess each reported incident to determine the nature, scope, impact, affected individuals, containment actions and notification requirements.

 13.4. Notifications to supervisory authorities, individuals, customers or other parties shall be made where required and within applicable deadlines.

 13.5. Lessons learned from personal data breaches shall be documented and used to improve controls.

14. **The organisation shall control sharing and disclosure of personal data.**

 14.1. Personal data shall be shared internally only where there is a legitimate business need and appropriate access authorisation.

 14.2. Personal data shall be disclosed externally only where there is a lawful basis, appropriate safeguards and a documented business justification.

 14.3. Data sharing arrangements shall define the purpose, data categories, roles of the parties, security requirements, retention expectations and handling of individual rights and incidents.

 14.4. Ad hoc disclosures of personal data to external parties shall be approved by the relevant business owner and, where necessary, reviewed by Legal or the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead.

15. **The organisation shall manage suppliers and processors that handle personal data.**

 15.1. Suppliers that process personal data on behalf of the organisation shall be subject to due diligence before engagement.

 15.2. Written contractual terms shall be in place before personal data is made available to a supplier.

 15.3. Supplier contracts shall require appropriate confidentiality, security, sub-processing, breach notification, assistance with rights requests, audit, retention and deletion obligations.

 15.4. Suppliers shall process personal data only on documented instructions from the organisation unless legally required to do otherwise.

 15.5. Supplier performance and data protection compliance shall be monitored based on risk.

16. **The organisation shall control international transfers of personal data.**

 16.1. Personal data shall not be transferred outside the approved jurisdictions or made accessible from another country unless appropriate safeguards have been assessed and approved.

 16.2. International transfer arrangements shall be documented and reviewed before implementation.

 16.3. Business owners shall consult the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead before using services, support teams, hosting locations or sub-processors that involve cross-border access to personal data.

17. **The organisation shall ensure personnel understand their data protection obligations.**

 17.1. All personnel shall complete mandatory data protection training at onboarding and at regular intervals thereafter.

 17.2. Personnel in roles with elevated data protection responsibilities shall receive role-specific training.

 17.3. Training completion shall be recorded and monitored.

 17.4. Personnel shall be reminded of data protection obligations through periodic awareness communications and targeted guidance.

18. **The organisation shall maintain confidentiality of personal data.**

 18.1. Personnel shall keep personal data confidential and use it only for authorised business purposes.

 18.2. Personal data shall not be discussed in public places, exposed on desks, displayed unnecessarily on screens or shared with unauthorised persons.

 18.3. Confidentiality obligations shall continue after employment or engagement ends.

19. **The organisation shall maintain appropriate records and evidence.**

 19.1. The organisation shall maintain records sufficient to demonstrate compliance with this Policy.

 19.2. Evidence shall include, as applicable, privacy notices, processing records, risk assessments, privacy assessments, training records, supplier due diligence, contracts, breach records, rights request logs, consent records and retention schedules.

 19.3. Data protection records shall be accurate, accessible to authorised personnel and retained in accordance with internal retention requirements.

20. **The organisation shall ensure personal data is securely disposed of.**

 20.1. Personal data shall be disposed of using methods appropriate to the format and sensitivity of the data.

 20.2. Electronic personal data shall be deleted, securely erased or anonymised using approved methods.

 20.3. Paper records containing personal data shall be shredded, pulped or disposed of through an approved secure destruction service.

 20.4. Disposal activities shall be documented where required by retention, legal, contractual or risk requirements.

21. **The organisation shall ensure employment-related personal data is handled responsibly.**

 21.1. Employee and applicant personal data shall be processed only for legitimate employment, workforce management, legal, security, benefits, payroll, recruitment or organisational purposes.

 21.2. Employee monitoring shall be proportionate, transparent and approved before implementation.

 21.3. Access to employee personal data shall be restricted to authorised personnel with a defined business need.

22. **The organisation shall ensure marketing activities comply with data protection expectations.**

 22.1. Marketing communications shall be sent only where the organisation has a valid basis to contact the individual.

 22.2. Marketing preferences, opt-ins and objections shall be recorded and respected.

 22.3. Individuals shall be provided with a clear and simple way to unsubscribe or opt out of direct marketing.

 22.4. Purchased, rented or third-party marketing lists shall not be used unless Legal or the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead has confirmed that appropriate permissions and evidence are in place.

23. **The organisation shall ensure automated decision-making and profiling are governed.**

 23.1. Automated decision-making or profiling involving personal data shall be assessed before use.

 23.2. Individuals shall be provided with meaningful information about significant automated processing where required.

 23.3. Appropriate safeguards shall be implemented, including human review where decisions may significantly affect individuals.

24. **The organisation shall maintain data protection governance reporting.**

 24.1. Data protection risks, incidents, compliance activities and material issues shall be reported to appropriate management forums.

 24.2. The Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead shall have sufficient independence, authority and access to senior management to perform the role effectively.

 24.3. Senior management shall support the implementation of this Policy and ensure adequate resources are available to meet data protection obligations.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board / Executive Leadership | Approves the organisation’s data protection direction, promotes a culture of accountability, ensures adequate resources are available and receives reporting on material data protection risks and issues. |
| Senior Management | Ensures this Policy is implemented within their business areas, assigns accountable owners for processing activities and ensures teams follow required data protection controls. |
| Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | Advises on data protection obligations, monitors compliance, supports privacy assessments, advises on high-risk processing, oversees rights requests and breach assessment, and reports material risks to management. |
| Legal | Provides legal advice on lawful basis, contracts, disclosures, regulatory engagement, data sharing, international transfers and disputes involving personal data. |
| Information Security | Implements and monitors technical and organisational security controls, supports breach response, performs security risk assessments and advises on secure processing of personal data. |
| IT | Ensures systems and infrastructure processing personal data are appropriately configured, maintained, access-controlled, backed up and decommissioned securely. |
| Human Resources | Manages employee and applicant personal data in accordance with this Policy, supports training, confidentiality obligations and workforce privacy requirements. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Ensures supplier due diligence, contractual controls and ongoing supplier monitoring are completed for suppliers that process personal data. |
| Business Process Owners | Own the lawful, fair and secure processing of personal data within their processes; maintain accurate processing records; ensure retention, access and sharing controls are followed. |
| Project Managers / Product Owners | Ensure data protection requirements are considered early in project and product lifecycles, complete required privacy assessments and implement agreed safeguards before launch. |
| Marketing / Communications | Ensures marketing activities, preference management, campaigns and communications comply with consent, opt-out and transparency requirements. |
| Records Management | Maintains retention schedules, supports disposal processes and ensures records containing personal data are retained and destroyed appropriately. |
| All Personnel | Follow this Policy, complete required training, protect personal data, use approved systems, report incidents immediately and seek guidance when unsure. |

The following operational accountability model shall apply:

| Activity | Accountable Owner | Required Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Maintaining records of processing activities | Business Process Owner | Current processing record |
| Approving new high-risk processing | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead and Business Owner | Completed privacy assessment and risk decision |
| Responding to individual rights requests | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead with relevant Business Owner | Rights request log and response record |
| Reporting suspected personal data breaches | All Personnel | Incident report entry |
| Assessing personal data breaches | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead, Information Security and Legal | Breach assessment record |
| Approving external data sharing | Business Owner with Legal or Privacy review where required | Data sharing record or agreement |
| Approving suppliers that process personal data | Procurement / Vendor Management and Business Owner | Due diligence and contract record |
| Managing retention and deletion | Business Process Owner and Records Management | Retention schedule and disposal evidence |
| Completing data protection training | All Personnel | Training completion record |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through proportionate governance, assurance and review activities, including:

- Periodic review of records of processing activities.
- Review of privacy notices and transparency materials.
- Monitoring completion of mandatory data protection training.
- Review of rights request handling and response timeliness.
- Review of personal data breach logs, root causes and corrective actions.
- Supplier due diligence and contract compliance reviews.
- Internal audits and control testing.
- Review of privacy assessments for new or changed processing.
- Access reviews for systems containing personal data.
- Retention and disposal compliance checks.
- Management reporting on material risks, incidents and remediation.

Minimum monitoring expectations are set out below:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Owner | Output |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Data protection training completion review | Monthly | Human Resources / Privacy Lead | Training compliance report |
| Personal data breach log review | Monthly | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | Breach trend and action report |
| Individual rights request log review | Monthly | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | Rights request status report |
| Records of processing review | At least annually and upon material change | Business Process Owners | Updated processing records |
| Privacy notice review | At least annually and upon material change | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead and Business Owners | Updated privacy notices |
| Supplier data protection review | Based on supplier risk rating | Procurement / Vendor Management | Supplier review record |
| Access review for high-risk systems | At least quarterly | System Owners | Access review evidence |
| Retention compliance review | At least annually | Records Management and Business Owners | Retention compliance report |
| Data protection risk reporting | Quarterly | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | Management risk report |
| Policy compliance audit | At planned audit intervals | Internal Audit / Compliance | Audit report and action plan |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in:

- Mandatory remedial training.
- Revocation or restriction of access to systems or data.
- Formal performance or disciplinary action.
- Contractual remedies for third parties.
- Escalation to senior management.
- Notification to affected customers, partners, regulators or individuals where required.
- Legal action where misconduct, negligence or unlawful activity is identified.

Any employee, contractor or third party who becomes aware of an actual or suspected breach of this Policy shall report it immediately to [reporting channel] or the Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead.

Managers shall ensure corrective actions are completed within agreed timeframes and shall provide evidence of remediation when requested.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy are permitted only where there is a documented and approved business justification and where the exception does not create unacceptable risk to individuals or the organisation.

Requests for exceptions shall be submitted to the Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead using the approved exception process and shall include:

- The specific Policy requirement for which an exception is requested.
- The business reason for the exception.
- The personal data involved.
- The individuals affected.
- The proposed duration of the exception.
- The risks to individuals and the organisation.
- Compensating controls or safeguards.
- Confirmation from the relevant Business Owner.
- Any legal, contractual or customer implications.

Exception approvals shall be time-bound and reviewed before expiry.

| Exception Type | Required Approval | Maximum Initial Duration | Minimum Safeguards |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Low-risk operational exception | Business Owner and Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | 90 days | Documented rationale and compensating control |
| System or technical constraint | System Owner, Information Security and Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | 180 days | Risk assessment, access control and remediation plan |
| Supplier-related exception | Procurement / Vendor Management, Business Owner and Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | 180 days | Contractual safeguards and supplier remediation plan |
| High-risk processing exception | Senior Management, Legal and Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | 90 days | Formal risk acceptance and documented safeguards |
| Retention exception | Records Management, Legal and Business Owner | As justified | Legal hold or documented retention rationale |

Exceptions shall not be used to bypass legal requirements, conceal non-compliance or avoid implementing reasonable data protection controls.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed through the approved process.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to:

- Data protection laws or regulatory expectations.
- The organisation’s business model, products, services or operating locations.
- Processing activities involving personal data.
- Technology platforms, systems or security architecture.
- Supplier arrangements involving personal data.
- Organisational structure, governance or accountability arrangements.
- Data protection risk profile or incident trends.

The Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead is responsible for coordinating the review and maintenance of this Policy. Policy updates shall be reviewed by relevant stakeholders, including Legal, Information Security, Human Resources, Procurement / Vendor Management and business representatives, as appropriate.

Material changes to this Policy shall be approved by [approval authority].

Previous versions of this Policy shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document retention requirements.

Personnel shall be informed of material changes to this Policy and may be required to complete additional training or acknowledgement where appropriate.

GDPR-015.title: Data Retention Policy & Schedule
GDPR-015.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [POL-GDPR-RET-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Data Protection Officer |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | GDPR |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

This Data Retention Policy & Schedule establishes the organisation’s mandatory requirements for retaining, archiving, and securely deleting personal data. It ensures that personal data is kept only for as long as necessary for defined business, legal, regulatory, contractual, employment, security, or legitimate operational purposes.

The policy supports the organisation’s obligation to prevent excessive storage of personal data, reduce privacy risk, maintain accurate records, and ensure personal data is securely disposed of when no longer required.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All employees, contractors, temporary workers, consultants, suppliers, and third parties who collect, access, process, store, transfer, archive, or delete personal data on behalf of the organisation.
- All personal data processed by the organisation, regardless of format, system, location, or medium, including:
 - Electronic records.
 - Paper records.
 - Emails and messaging records.
 - Databases and application data.
 - Backups and archives.
 - Audio, video, and image recordings.
 - System logs containing personal identifiers.
 - HR, customer, supplier, marketing, finance, legal, and security records.
- Personal data processed in:
 - Corporate systems.
 - Cloud services.
 - Local devices.
 - Shared drives and collaboration platforms.
 - Physical filing locations.
 - Third-party platforms and outsourced service environments.

This policy applies to personal data relating to customers, prospects, employees, workers, job applicants, suppliers, website users, business contacts, visitors, and any other identifiable individual whose personal data is processed by the organisation.

This policy does not override statutory, regulatory, contractual, litigation, tax, employment, or audit retention obligations. Where multiple retention periods apply to the same record, the longest applicable approved retention period shall be used unless deletion is legally required earlier.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall retain personal data only for as long as it is necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, used, or otherwise lawfully processed.

2. The organisation shall define and maintain a documented retention schedule covering all material categories of personal data processed by the organisation.

3. Each personal data category shall have:
 - A defined business or legal purpose.
 - An identified system or record location.
 - A designated business owner.
 - A documented retention period.
 - A defined retention trigger.
 - An approved disposal method.
 - Any applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, or operational rationale.

4. Personal data shall not be retained indefinitely unless there is a documented and approved legal or regulatory reason to do so.

5. Retention periods shall be proportionate to the purpose of processing and shall consider:
 - The nature and sensitivity of the personal data.
 - The expectations of the individual.
 - Legal, regulatory, tax, employment, contractual, or audit requirements.
 - Limitation periods for legal claims.
 - Operational need.
 - Security and privacy risks associated with continued retention.
 - Whether anonymisation can meet the business need instead of continued retention of identifiable data.

6. Personal data shall be deleted, destroyed, anonymised, or otherwise rendered irreversibly non-identifiable when the applicable retention period expires, unless a valid retention hold applies.

7. Business owners shall not create local, shadow, duplicate, or unmanaged repositories of personal data that bypass approved retention controls.

8. Personal data stored in emails, shared drives, collaboration tools, local folders, spreadsheets, messaging platforms, and exported reports shall be subject to the same retention requirements as data stored in core business applications.

9. Employees shall store personal data only in approved systems and repositories that support appropriate access control, retention management, backup, auditability, and secure disposal.

10. Personal data shall not be retained merely because storage is inexpensive, deletion is inconvenient, or the data might be useful in the future without a documented and lawful purpose.

11. The organisation shall apply the following standard retention schedule unless a more specific approved schedule, legal requirement, contractual obligation, or retention hold applies.

| Data Category | Examples | Retention Trigger | Standard Retention Period | Disposal Method | Business Owner |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Customer account records | Customer profile, contact details, account preferences, service history | Account closure or end of customer relationship | [6 years] | Secure deletion or anonymisation | Customer Operations |
| Customer transaction records | Orders, invoices, payment confirmations, delivery records | End of financial year in which transaction occurred | [7 years] | Secure deletion or restricted archive deletion | Finance |
| Customer support records | Support tickets, complaint history, call notes, chat transcripts | Closure of support case | [3 years] | Secure deletion or anonymisation | Customer Support |
| Marketing prospect records | Leads, campaign responses, event registrations, newsletter sign-ups | Last meaningful interaction or consent withdrawal | [24 months] | Secure deletion or suppression where required | Marketing |
| Marketing suppression records | Opt-out lists, unsubscribe records, do-not-contact preferences | Date of opt-out or objection | As long as needed to honour the preference | Retain minimal suppression record | Marketing |
| Website and cookie consent records | Cookie consent logs, preference settings, consent timestamp | Consent update or expiry | [13 months] | Secure deletion | Digital / Marketing |
| Recruitment records for unsuccessful applicants | CVs, application forms, interview notes, assessment results | Completion of recruitment process | [12 months] | Secure deletion or confidential shredding | Human Resources |
| Recruitment records for successful applicants | CVs, employment checks, offer letters, onboarding forms | Start of employment | Transfer to employee file and retain under employee retention period | Secure deletion of duplicates | Human Resources |
| Employee personnel records | Employment contract, role history, performance records, disciplinary records, training records | End of employment | [6 years] | Secure deletion or confidential shredding | Human Resources |
| Payroll and tax records | Salary records, tax information, pension contributions, benefits records | End of financial year | [7 years] | Secure deletion or confidential shredding | Finance / HR |
| Working time, absence, and leave records | Timesheets, sickness absence, holiday records, statutory leave records | End of employment or end of relevant leave year | [6 years] | Secure deletion | Human Resources |
| Health and occupational safety records | Workplace incident reports, health assessments, reasonable adjustment records | End of employment or incident closure | [6 years], or longer where required for health and safety claims | Secure deletion or confidential shredding | HR / Health & Safety |
| Supplier and vendor contact records | Supplier contacts, contract managers, account representatives | End of supplier relationship | [6 years] | Secure deletion | Procurement |
| Supplier due diligence records | Vendor assessments, security questionnaires, insurance records, compliance checks | End of supplier relationship | [6 years] | Secure deletion | Procurement / Information Security |
| Contracts and legal agreements | Customer, supplier, partner, employment, and confidentiality agreements | Contract expiry or termination | [6 years] | Secure deletion or confidential shredding | Legal |
| Legal dispute and claims records | Correspondence, evidence, settlement records, legal advice | Final resolution of matter | [6 years] or as directed by Legal | Secure deletion with Legal approval | Legal |
| Data protection request records | Access, deletion, correction, objection, portability, restriction, and consent records | Closure of request | [3 years] | Secure deletion | Data Protection Officer |
| Data breach and incident records | Breach assessments, investigation notes, notification records, remediation evidence | Closure of incident | [6 years] | Secure deletion or restricted archive deletion | Data Protection Officer / Information Security |
| CCTV and physical security footage | Video footage of premises, access points, restricted areas | Date of recording | [30 days] unless required for investigation | Automatic deletion or secure overwrite | Facilities / Security |
| Visitor records | Visitor logs, access badges, sign-in records | Date of visit | [12 months] | Secure deletion or confidential shredding | Facilities |
| Building access records | Badge access logs, entry and exit logs | Date of access event | [12 months] | Secure deletion | Facilities / Security |
| Authentication and access logs | User login records, privileged access logs, failed login events | Date of log event | [12 months] | Secure deletion or log rotation | Information Technology |
| Security monitoring logs | SIEM events, endpoint alerts, network security logs | Date of log event | [12 months] | Secure deletion or secure log expiry | Information Security |
| IT service desk records | Tickets, device assignments, access requests, support history | Ticket closure | [3 years] | Secure deletion | Information Technology |
| Backup data containing personal data | System backups, database backups, file backups | Backup creation date | [90 days] unless longer approved | Automatic overwrite or secure backup expiry | Information Technology |
| Corporate email records | Business emails containing personal data | Email creation or receipt | [7 years] unless deleted earlier under approved rules | Secure deletion or retention archive expiry | Information Technology / Business Owners |
| Collaboration platform records | Chat messages, shared documents, comments, recordings | Creation date or workspace closure | [3 years] unless business record retention applies | Secure deletion | Information Technology / Business Owners |
| Training and awareness records | Training completion logs, assessment results, policy acknowledgements | Completion date or end of employment | [6 years] | Secure deletion | Human Resources / Compliance |
| Audit and compliance records | Internal audits, control evidence, compliance attestations | Audit completion date | [6 years] | Secure deletion | Compliance |
| Board and governance records containing personal data | Meeting packs, minutes, registers, declarations of interest | Date of record creation | [10 years] or permanent where approved | Restricted archive or secure deletion | Company Secretary / Legal |

12. Where personal data is anonymised instead of deleted, the anonymisation shall be irreversible in practice and shall remove the organisation’s ability to identify the individual directly or indirectly using reasonably available means.

13. Pseudonymised data shall remain subject to this policy where re-identification is possible.

14. The organisation shall maintain an inventory of personal data repositories and shall link each repository to an approved retention category.

15. New systems, applications, processes, products, or services that process personal data shall not go live until applicable retention requirements have been defined and approved.

16. Retention requirements shall be incorporated into privacy assessments, procurement reviews, system design, change management, and supplier onboarding activities.

17. Systems processing personal data shall be configured, where technically feasible, to support automated retention, deletion, archiving, or anonymisation.

18. Where automated deletion is not technically feasible, the responsible business owner shall operate a documented manual review and deletion process at an approved frequency.

19. Manual deletion processes shall include evidence of:
 - Data reviewed.
 - Applicable retention rule.
 - Records deleted, anonymised, archived, or retained.
 - Date of action.
 - Person performing the action.
 - Approval where required.

20. Personal data pending deletion shall be protected against unauthorised access, alteration, loss, disclosure, or inappropriate restoration.

21. Personal data retained for archival, audit, dispute, or compliance purposes shall be access-restricted and used only for the purpose justifying retention.

22. Expired records shall not be reused for new purposes, analytics, marketing, profiling, product development, or research unless a lawful basis has been confirmed and the retention schedule has been updated.

23. The organisation shall use secure disposal methods appropriate to the data type, media, and sensitivity.

| Record or Media Type | Approved Disposal Method |
|---|---|
| Standard electronic records | Secure deletion from approved systems, including removal from active storage and scheduled expiry from backups |
| Sensitive electronic records | Secure deletion using approved tools, cryptographic erasure, or verified destruction process |
| Cloud-hosted records | Deletion through approved platform controls with confirmation where available |
| Paper records | Cross-cut shredding, confidential waste service, or secure destruction certificate |
| Removable media | Secure wipe, degaussing, physical destruction, or approved asset disposal process |
| Mobile devices and laptops | Secure wipe before reassignment, return, disposal, or repair |
| Backup media | Expiry, overwrite, secure erasure, or physical destruction in line with backup retention rules |
| Anonymised datasets | Retention permitted only where re-identification risk remains acceptably low and periodically reviewed |

24. Paper records containing personal data shall be stored securely during their retention period and disposed of through approved confidential disposal channels.

25. Personal data shall not be deleted where it is subject to a legal hold, regulatory hold, investigation hold, audit hold, contractual preservation requirement, or unresolved rights request requiring continued retention.

26. Retention holds shall be authorised by Legal, the Data Protection Officer, Compliance, or another authorised role depending on the reason for the hold.

27. A retention hold shall specify:
 - Data or record category affected.
 - System or location.
 - Reason for the hold.
 - Authorising person.
 - Start date.
 - Review date.
 - Conditions for release.

28. When a retention hold is released, the affected data shall return to the normal retention schedule and be deleted or retained according to the applicable approved rule.

29. The organisation shall maintain evidence of deletion, anonymisation, destruction, or retention review for records where such evidence is necessary to demonstrate compliance.

30. Suppliers and processors handling personal data on behalf of the organisation shall apply retention and deletion requirements consistent with this policy and the applicable contract.

31. Supplier contracts involving personal data shall include requirements for:
 - Defined retention periods or return/deletion instructions.
 - Secure deletion at the end of service.
 - Deletion of copies, extracts, and backups where feasible.
 - Confirmation of deletion where requested.
 - Assistance with data subject requests and regulatory obligations.
 - Restrictions on retaining personal data after contract termination except where required by law.

32. Suppliers shall not retain organisation personal data for their own purposes unless expressly authorised under a documented lawful arrangement.

33. Where personal data is transferred to or processed in another jurisdiction, the applicable retention and deletion requirements shall continue to apply.

34. The organisation shall respect valid requests from individuals for deletion, restriction, objection, or correction, subject to any lawful reason requiring continued retention.
