35. Where deletion cannot be completed due to legal, regulatory, contractual, security, or technical reasons, the organisation shall explain the limitation where required and restrict further processing where appropriate.

36. Backups shall be managed so that personal data is not retained in backups for longer than necessary for business continuity, disaster recovery, and security purposes.

37. Personal data deleted from active systems may remain in backups until the backup naturally expires, provided the data is not restored into active use unless a legitimate recovery need exists.

38. If deleted personal data is restored from backup, the organisation shall reapply applicable deletion requirements promptly where feasible.

39. The organisation shall not use expired backup data as a substitute archive or to avoid deletion requirements.

40. System logs containing personal data shall be retained for a defined security, operational, or audit purpose and shall not be retained indefinitely by default.

41. Test, development, and training environments shall not retain production personal data unless approved, protected, and subject to a defined retention period.

42. Personal data used for testing, development, analytics, research, or training shall be anonymised or minimised wherever feasible.

43. Reports, exports, dashboards, and extracts containing personal data shall have defined retention rules and shall be deleted when no longer needed.

44. Employees shall not download or export personal data unless required for an approved business purpose and shall delete the export once the purpose has been fulfilled.

45. Departing employees’ files, mailboxes, devices, and collaboration spaces shall be reviewed and managed according to applicable retention and access requirements.

46. Personal data contained in personal drives, local storage, unmanaged devices, or unapproved repositories shall be migrated to approved repositories or securely deleted.

47. The organisation shall maintain a deletion and retention review calendar for key systems and record categories.

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence Required |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review retention schedule | Annually | Data Protection Officer | Approved updated schedule or confirmation of no change |
| Review personal data inventory alignment | Annually | Data Protection Officer / Business Owners | Inventory update records |
| Review expired records in key systems | Quarterly | Business Owners | Deletion or retention review log |
| Review legal and regulatory hold register | Quarterly | Legal | Hold status report |
| Review backup retention settings | Annually | Information Technology | Backup configuration evidence |
| Review supplier deletion compliance | At contract end and as needed | Procurement / Contract Owner | Deletion confirmation or contract record |
| Review high-risk repositories | Semi-annually | Information Security / Business Owners | Access and retention review evidence |
| Test secure deletion capability | Annually | Information Technology | Test results and remediation actions |

48. Retention periods shall be reviewed whenever:
 - A new law, regulation, contractual requirement, or business obligation is identified.
 - A new system or processing activity is introduced.
 - A data protection assessment identifies a retention risk.
 - A data breach or audit finding relates to excessive retention.
 - A business process changes materially.
 - A supplier arrangement changes.
 - The organisation enters a new market or jurisdiction.

49. Retention decisions shall be documented and approved before implementation.

50. Where there is uncertainty about the correct retention period, the matter shall be referred to the Data Protection Officer and Legal before records are deleted or retained beyond the standard period.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board / Senior Management | Approves the organisation’s commitment to responsible data retention and ensures adequate resources are available to implement this policy. |
| Data Protection Officer | Owns this policy; advises on privacy requirements; maintains the retention schedule with business input; reviews retention risks; supports data subject requests; monitors compliance. |
| Legal | Advises on statutory, contractual, regulatory, litigation, and claims-related retention requirements; issues and releases legal holds; approves retention for legal matters. |
| Compliance | Supports monitoring activities; coordinates audit evidence; tracks remediation actions related to retention compliance. |
| Information Technology | Implements technical retention, archiving, backup, deletion, and secure disposal controls; supports system configuration; maintains evidence of technical deletion where required. |
| Information Security | Advises on secure disposal, access restrictions, logging, storage protection, and security risks associated with retained data. |
| Business Owners | Define business retention needs for their processes; ensure records are stored in approved repositories; perform periodic retention reviews; approve deletion actions where required. |
| Human Resources | Applies retention requirements to employee, worker, applicant, payroll-related, training, and occupational records in coordination with Legal and the Data Protection Officer. |
| Finance | Applies retention requirements to financial, accounting, invoicing, tax, payment, and transaction records. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Ensures supplier contracts include appropriate retention and deletion obligations; obtains supplier deletion confirmations where required. |
| Facilities / Physical Security | Manages retention and disposal of visitor records, access logs, CCTV, and physical security records. |
| Employees and Contractors | Store personal data only in approved locations; follow retention and disposal rules; delete unnecessary copies; report retention concerns or unmanaged repositories. |
| Internal Audit | Independently assesses compliance with this policy according to the approved audit plan. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy is mandatory. The organisation shall monitor adherence through a combination of technical controls, management review, audit activity, supplier assurance, and evidence-based retention reviews.

Monitoring activities may include:

- Review of system retention configurations.
- Sampling of records against approved retention periods.
- Review of shared drives, collaboration spaces, and email retention practices.
- Assessment of deletion logs and destruction certificates.
- Supplier compliance reviews.
- Review of backup expiry settings.
- Review of legal hold registers.
- Audit of records retained beyond approved periods.
- Investigation of excessive retention identified through privacy assessments, incidents, or data subject requests.

Non-compliance with this policy may result in:

- Required deletion or remediation of retained data.
- Suspension of processing activities.
- Additional training or supervision.
- Withdrawal of system access.
- Supplier remediation or contract action.
- Disciplinary action in accordance with the organisation’s HR policies.
- Escalation to senior management, Legal, or the Data Protection Officer.

Intentional destruction, concealment, alteration, or deletion of records subject to a legal hold, investigation, audit, regulatory requirement, or approved preservation instruction is strictly prohibited and may result in disciplinary action and legal consequences.

All suspected or confirmed breaches of this policy shall be reported promptly to the Data Protection Officer, Information Security, Legal, or [Reporting Channel].

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented and approved business, legal, regulatory, technical, or operational justification.

Exception requests shall include:

| Requirement | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Name, role, and business area requesting the exception |
| Data category | Type of personal data affected |
| System or location | Repository where the data is stored |
| Requested exception | Retention extension, retention reduction, delayed deletion, alternative disposal method, or other deviation |
| Justification | Business, legal, regulatory, contractual, technical, or operational reason |
| Risk assessment | Privacy, security, legal, and operational risks |
| Compensating controls | Measures to reduce risk during the exception period |
| Duration | Start date, end date, and review date |
| Approvals | Required approvals from the Data Protection Officer, Legal, business owner, and Information Security where applicable |

Exceptions shall be:

- Time-bound.
- Risk-assessed.
- Approved before implementation.
- Recorded in the exceptions register.
- Reviewed at defined intervals.
- Removed when no longer justified.

Permanent exceptions shall not be permitted unless approved by senior management, Legal, and the Data Protection Officer with a documented justification and periodic review.

Emergency exceptions may be approved verbally or by expedited written approval where immediate action is required, but shall be documented retrospectively within [5 business days].

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to:

- Applicable privacy, employment, tax, corporate, regulatory, or sector-specific requirements.
- Business processes involving personal data.
- Systems, applications, cloud platforms, or data storage locations.
- Supplier or processor arrangements.
- Data protection risk profile.
- Records management practices.
- Organisational structure or operating model.
- Audit findings, incidents, complaints, or regulatory feedback.

The Data Protection Officer is responsible for coordinating the review of this policy and the retention schedule with Legal, Information Technology, Information Security, Compliance, and relevant business owners.

Changes to the retention schedule shall be approved before implementation and communicated to affected teams. Material changes shall be reflected in related procedures, privacy notices, data inventories, supplier instructions, training materials, and system configurations.

The current approved version of this policy shall be stored in [Policy Repository]. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document control requirements.

GDPR-016.title: Consent Mgmt Policy & Records
GDPR-016.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [GDPR-POL-CONSENT-001] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer | [Effective Date] | GDPR | Internal |

## Purpose

This policy defines mandatory requirements for obtaining, recording, managing, evidencing, and withdrawing consent where the organisation relies on consent as the lawful basis for processing personal data.

The purpose of this policy is to ensure that consent is freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, demonstrable, and easy to withdraw, and that the organisation maintains reliable records showing how and when consent was obtained.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All personal data processing activities where consent is used as the lawful basis.
- All employees, contractors, temporary staff, consultants, service providers, and third parties acting on behalf of the organisation.
- All business functions that collect, use, store, share, or otherwise process personal data based on consent.
- All channels through which consent may be obtained, including websites, mobile applications, paper forms, call centres, events, in-person interactions, email, SMS, customer portals, and third-party platforms.
- All categories of data subjects, including customers, prospects, employees, job applicants, suppliers, website users, event attendees, and other individuals.
- All consent records maintained in systems, databases, customer relationship management platforms, marketing platforms, consent management platforms, document repositories, and manual records.

This policy applies only where consent is the lawful basis for processing. Where another lawful basis is relied upon, the relevant privacy, data protection, retention, and transparency requirements still apply, but the specific consent requirements in this policy do not replace those obligations.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall use consent as a lawful basis only where the individual has a genuine choice and control over whether their personal data is processed.

2. The organisation shall not use consent where there is a clear imbalance of power, coercion, detriment for refusal, or where the processing is necessary for a contract, legal obligation, vital interest, public task, or legitimate business purpose that is more appropriate than consent.

3. Business owners shall assess and document whether consent is the appropriate lawful basis before any processing activity relying on consent begins.

4. Consent shall be obtained before the relevant processing activity begins.

5. Consent shall be requested using clear, plain, and accessible language that an average member of the intended audience can understand.

6. Consent requests shall be separate from general terms and conditions, privacy notices, contractual terms, or other unrelated acknowledgements.

7. Consent shall not be bundled with acceptance of terms, account registration, service delivery, or other activities unless the consent is genuinely necessary for that specific processing purpose.

8. Consent shall be specific to each distinct processing purpose.

9. Separate consent shall be obtained for separate processing purposes where those purposes are not closely related.

10. Consent shall be given by a clear affirmative action, such as selecting an unticked checkbox, signing a consent form, choosing settings, clicking an acceptance button, or giving a clear verbal confirmation that is recorded in accordance with this policy.

11. Pre-ticked boxes, inactivity, silence, default settings, implied acceptance, or continued use of a service shall not be treated as valid consent.

12. Consent shall not be made a condition of receiving a product or service unless the processing based on consent is genuinely necessary to provide that product or service.

13. The organisation shall provide individuals with sufficient information at the point of consent to make an informed decision.

14. At a minimum, the consent request shall tell the individual:
 - The identity of the organisation requesting consent.
 - The specific purpose of the processing.
 - The type of personal data to be processed.
 - Any special category or sensitive data involved.
 - Whether data will be shared with third parties and the categories or names of those parties where appropriate.
 - Whether international transfers are involved where relevant.
 - That consent can be withdrawn at any time.
 - How consent can be withdrawn.
 - A link or reference to the applicable privacy notice.

15. Consent language shall be reviewed by the Data Protection Officer or an authorised privacy representative before use.

16. Where consent is obtained digitally, the relevant system shall record a timestamp, user identifier or contact identifier, consent wording presented, consent status, source channel, and method of capture.

17. Where consent is obtained on paper, the completed form shall be retained in a controlled repository and indexed against the relevant individual or record.

18. Where consent is obtained verbally, the organisation shall either record the call where legally and operationally permitted or capture a contemporaneous record of the consent statement, date, time, script version, staff member, and individual identifier.

19. The organisation shall maintain records sufficient to demonstrate that valid consent was obtained.

20. Consent records shall include, at a minimum, the following information:

| Consent Record Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Individual identifier | Unique reference linking the consent to the relevant individual |
| Consent status | Granted, refused, withdrawn, expired, refreshed, or superseded |
| Purpose | Specific processing purpose for which consent was requested |
| Data categories | Categories of personal data covered by the consent |
| Consent wording | Exact wording or version presented to the individual |
| Privacy notice version | Version or link to the privacy information provided at the time |
| Date and time | When consent was obtained, updated, withdrawn, or refreshed |
| Capture channel | Web, app, phone, paper, email, in-person, partner platform, or other channel |
| Capture method | Checkbox, signature, recorded call, preference setting, click-through, or other affirmative action |
| Source system | System or repository where the consent was captured |
| Staff or process owner | Person, team, workflow, or automated process responsible for capture |
| Third-party disclosure | Any third parties or categories of third parties covered by the consent |
| Withdrawal method | How the individual can withdraw or did withdraw consent |
| Evidence location | Link, record ID, file location, or audit trail reference |

21. Consent records shall be accurate, complete, and retrievable within a reasonable timeframe to support data subject requests, audits, investigations, complaints, and regulatory enquiries.

22. Consent records shall be protected against unauthorised access, alteration, deletion, or disclosure.

23. Consent records shall be retained for as long as necessary to demonstrate compliance and defend against claims, taking account of applicable retention schedules and limitation periods.

24. Consent shall be easy for individuals to withdraw.

25. The method for withdrawing consent shall be as easy and accessible as the method used to provide consent, wherever reasonably possible.

26. The organisation shall not charge a fee, impose unnecessary steps, require excessive information, or create unreasonable friction for withdrawing consent.

27. Withdrawal of consent shall be actioned promptly and without undue delay.

28. Where consent is withdrawn, processing based on that consent shall stop unless another lawful basis has been assessed, documented, and approved by the Data Protection Officer or authorised privacy representative.

29. Withdrawal of consent shall not affect processing that lawfully occurred before the withdrawal.

30. Systems and processes shall be designed to propagate consent withdrawals to relevant downstream systems, vendors, processors, marketing lists, analytics tools, and operational teams.

31. Where consent preferences are managed across multiple channels, the organisation shall maintain a single reliable view of current consent status or implement controlled synchronisation between systems.

32. Consent shall be refreshed where required because the purpose, processing method, data category, third-party sharing arrangement, technology, privacy notice, or context has materially changed.

33. Consent shall not be relied upon indefinitely where there has been no meaningful interaction with the individual or where the original consent may no longer be valid in context.

34. Business owners shall define appropriate consent refresh periods based on the nature of the processing, individual expectations, risk level, and applicable retention requirements.

35. The following consent review and refresh expectations shall apply unless a documented alternative has been approved:

| Consent Context | Minimum Review Expectation | Refresh Trigger |
|---|---:|---|
| Electronic marketing to customers or prospects | At least every 24 months | Material change in marketing purpose, channel, or third-party sharing |
| Special category or sensitive data processing based on consent | At least every 12 months | Change in processing purpose, risk level, or data category |
| Research, surveys, and optional feedback programmes | At project start and at material change | New research purpose or reuse beyond the original explanation |
| Cookies, tracking technologies, and online identifiers | At least every 12 months | Change in tracking purpose, vendor, technology, or preference mechanism |
| Event, webinar, and promotional consent | At each campaign or event series | New event series, sponsor sharing, or marketing purpose |
| Employee optional processing based on consent | At least every 12 months | Change in employment context, purpose, or voluntary nature |

36. Consent shall be renewed or re-obtained before processing expands beyond the scope of the original consent.

37. If valid consent cannot be demonstrated, the organisation shall stop the related processing until a lawful basis has been confirmed and documented.

38. Consent shall not be transferred to a new purpose, new controller, or new third party unless the original consent clearly covered that activity or new consent is obtained.

39. Where third parties collect consent on behalf of the organisation, contractual arrangements shall require them to comply with this policy and maintain evidence of consent.

40. The organisation shall not purchase, rent, or use third-party contact lists unless appropriate due diligence confirms that valid consent or another lawful basis exists for the intended processing.

41. Third-party consent evidence shall be reviewed before use of the relevant personal data for marketing, profiling, analytics, or other consent-based activities.

42. Consent collected by a third party shall be capable of being evidenced to the same standard as consent collected directly by the organisation.

43. Where the organisation acts as a processor and is instructed to support consent management on behalf of a controller, the organisation shall follow documented instructions and maintain agreed processing records.

44. Where children’s personal data is processed based on consent, the organisation shall apply enhanced safeguards appropriate to the age of the child and the nature of the service.

45. Where parental or guardian consent is required, the organisation shall take reasonable steps to verify that the person giving consent has authority to do so.

46. Consent requests aimed at children shall be written in age-appropriate language.

47. Special category personal data shall only be processed based on consent where the consent is explicit, clearly documented, and approved by the Data Protection Officer or authorised privacy representative.

48. Explicit consent shall require a clear statement confirming the individual’s agreement to the specific processing of the relevant sensitive data.

49. Consent mechanisms shall be tested before release to confirm that they capture the required evidence and do not use misleading, manipulative, or unfair design practices.

50. Consent interfaces shall not use confusing layouts, hidden refusal options, unequal button prominence, forced continuation, unnecessary repetition, or other designs that undermine free choice.

51. The organisation shall provide individuals with access to their consent preferences where appropriate and feasible.

52. Marketing communications shall only be sent where valid consent or another approved lawful basis exists for the channel, recipient, and purpose.

53. Suppression lists shall be maintained to ensure withdrawn consent, objections, and opt-outs are respected.

54. Suppression records shall be used only for the purpose of preventing unwanted processing or communications, unless another lawful basis has been documented.

55. Changes to consent wording, privacy notices, forms, preference centres, cookie banners, marketing platforms, or related workflows shall be subject to privacy review before implementation.

56. Consent evidence shall be made available to the Data Protection Officer, Legal, Internal Audit, and authorised management upon request.

57. Employees shall complete privacy and data protection training relevant to their role before collecting or managing consent.

58. Employees shall report suspected consent failures, inaccurate consent records, unauthorised processing, or improper withdrawal handling through the approved incident or privacy reporting channel.

59. Processing activities that rely on consent shall be recorded in the organisation’s data processing inventory.

60. The data processing inventory shall identify the purpose, data categories, data subjects, systems, recipients, retention period, consent mechanism, and business owner for consent-based processing.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board or Executive Leadership | Approves the organisation’s overall privacy governance direction and ensures adequate resources are available for consent management compliance. |
| Data Protection Officer | Owns this policy, advises on consent requirements, reviews high-risk consent activities, monitors compliance, and acts as a point of contact for privacy concerns. |
| Legal Counsel | Advises on legal interpretation, contractual requirements, third-party consent arrangements, complaints, disputes, and regulatory correspondence. |
| Privacy Team | Supports business teams with consent wording, privacy notices, records, assessments, training, monitoring, and remediation activities. |
| Business Process Owners | Ensure processing activities under their control use an appropriate lawful basis, implement compliant consent mechanisms, maintain records, and action withdrawals. |
| Marketing Team | Ensures marketing consents, opt-ins, opt-outs, preference centre records, campaign lists, and suppression lists are accurate and compliant. |
| Product and Digital Teams | Build consent requirements into websites, applications, platforms, cookie tools, preference centres, and user journeys by design. |
| IT and System Owners | Implement technical controls to capture, store, secure, synchronise, retrieve, and delete consent records in line with this policy. |
| Information Security Team | Ensures consent records and related systems are protected through appropriate access control, logging, monitoring, and security measures. |
| Procurement and Vendor Management | Ensures third parties that collect or process consent-based personal data are assessed, contracted, and monitored appropriately. |
| Human Resources | Ensures employee-related consent is used only where appropriate and that staff involved in collecting or managing consent receive relevant training. |
| Customer Service and Sales Teams | Capture and update consent preferences accurately, follow approved scripts, and handle withdrawal requests promptly. |
| Internal Audit or Compliance Function | Performs independent or periodic reviews of consent management controls, evidence, and remediation progress. |
| All Employees and Contractors | Follow this policy, use approved consent mechanisms, protect consent records, and report suspected non-compliance. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

The organisation shall monitor compliance with this policy through risk-based assurance activities, including system reviews, record sampling, consent journey testing, vendor checks, marketing campaign reviews, and audit activities.

Monitoring activities shall include, where applicable:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Owner | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of consent wording and capture mechanisms | Before launch and upon material change | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Team | Approved consent text, screenshots, form versions, sign-off records |
| Sampling of consent records for completeness | Quarterly | Privacy Team / Compliance | Sample results, exceptions, remediation actions |
| Marketing list consent validation | Before each campaign | Marketing Owner | Campaign approval, list validation evidence, suppression check |
| Withdrawal handling review | Quarterly | Business Process Owner | Withdrawal logs, processing times, completion evidence |
| Preference centre or consent platform review | Semi-annually | Product / IT System Owner | Configuration review, access logs, change records |
| Third-party consent evidence review | Annually or before use | Procurement / Privacy Team | Due diligence records, contractual clauses, vendor attestations |
| Data processing inventory reconciliation | Semi-annually | Business Process Owner / Privacy Team | Updated inventory records |
| Training completion monitoring | Annually | Human Resources / Privacy Team | Training reports and completion records |

Non-compliance with this policy may result in corrective action, including suspension of processing, withdrawal of campaign approval, removal of system access, mandatory retraining, contract remediation, vendor escalation, disciplinary action, or other action permitted by organisational policy and applicable law.

Suspected or confirmed breaches of this policy shall be reported promptly through [Privacy Incident Reporting Channel] or to the Data Protection Officer at [DPO Contact Details].

Where non-compliance creates a risk to individuals, the Data Protection Officer shall assess whether further action is required, including notification, remediation, suspension of processing, or engagement with relevant authorities.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business need, legal justification, and risk assessment approved by the Data Protection Officer or authorised delegate.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Name, role, department, and contact details |
| Processing activity | Description of the processing and personal data involved |
| Policy requirement affected | Specific requirement from this policy for which an exception is requested |
| Business justification | Reason the exception is necessary |
| Risk assessment | Privacy, legal, operational, reputational, and individual impact |
| Compensating controls | Measures to reduce or manage the risk |
| Duration | Requested start and end date |
| Approval | Data Protection Officer or authorised delegate decision |
| Review date | Date the exception will be reassessed |

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed [Maximum Exception Period] unless reapproved.

Permanent exceptions are not permitted unless this policy is formally updated through the review and approval process.

Emergency exceptions may be approved verbally by the Data Protection Officer or authorised delegate where immediate action is required, provided that the exception is documented within [Number] business days.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to:

- Applicable privacy or data protection law.
- Organisational processing activities.
- Consent management technology.
- Marketing, analytics, profiling, or tracking practices.
- Data sharing or third-party arrangements.
- Products, services, or user journeys involving consent.
- Regulatory guidance, enforcement trends, audit findings, or privacy risk profile.

The Data Protection Officer is responsible for coordinating the review and ensuring that updates are approved, communicated, and implemented.

Policy changes shall be recorded in the document history maintained by the policy owner.

The current approved version of this policy shall be made available to all relevant personnel through [Policy Repository or Intranet Location].

Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document retention requirements.

GDPR-017.title: Data Subject Rights Procedure (DSAR)
GDPR-017.content:
| Metadata | Details |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [GOV-PRC-DSAR-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Data Protection Officer |
| Effective Date | [DD-MMM-YYYY] |
| Framework | GDPR |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

This procedure defines how [Organisation Name] receives, verifies, assesses, fulfils, records, and escalates requests from individuals exercising their data protection rights.

The procedure is designed to ensure that data subject rights requests are handled consistently, lawfully, securely, and within required timeframes. It covers requests relating to:

- Access to personal data
- Confirmation of whether personal data is processed
- Rectification of inaccurate or incomplete personal data
- Erasure of personal data
- Restriction of processing
- Data portability
- Objection to processing
- Objection to direct marketing
- Objection to automated decision-making or profiling
- Withdrawal of consent
- Requests for information about how personal data is used

This procedure also supports appropriate documentation of decisions, exemptions, identity checks, communications, and evidence of completion.

## Scope

This procedure applies to:

- All employees, contractors, temporary staff, consultants, and third parties acting on behalf of [Organisation Name]
- All business units and functions that collect, use, store, disclose, archive, or delete personal data
- All personal data processed by [Organisation Name], whether held electronically, physically, in structured filing systems, applications, archives, emails, collaboration tools, backups, or third-party platforms
- Requests received from customers, employees, former employees, applicants, suppliers, website users, complainants, or any other identifiable individual
- Requests received through any channel, including email, post, telephone, web form, in person, social media, customer portal, helpdesk ticket, or through a legal representative

This procedure applies where [Organisation Name] acts as a controller for the personal data involved in the request.

Where [Organisation Name] acts only as a processor on behalf of a customer or another controller, the request must be forwarded promptly to the relevant controller in accordance with contractual obligations, and [Organisation Name] must not respond substantively to the individual unless authorised to do so.

This procedure does not apply to:

- Routine customer service updates that do not involve exercising a formal data subject right, unless the individual clearly requests use of a data protection right
- Legal disclosure requests from law enforcement, courts, regulators, or public authorities, which must be handled under the applicable disclosure or legal request procedure
- Internal employee record corrections performed as routine HR administration, unless the request is expressly made as a data protection rights request or requires formal assessment

## Prerequisites & Inputs

The following prerequisites must be in place to operate this procedure effectively:

| Prerequisite | Description | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| DSAR intake channel | A dedicated email address, web form, postal address, or service desk queue for receiving data subject rights requests | Data Protection Officer |
| DSAR register | A central log for all requests, deadlines, status updates, decisions, and evidence | Data Protection Officer |
| Identity verification process | Approved methods for confirming the identity and authority of requesters | Data Protection Officer / Customer Operations / HR |
| Data inventory | Current understanding of systems, repositories, business processes, and third-party processors that may contain personal data | Data Governance Lead / System Owners |
| Retention schedule | Approved retention rules to support erasure, restriction, and lawful refusal decisions | Records Manager / Data Protection Officer |
| Third-party processor list | Current list of vendors and service providers processing personal data on behalf of [Organisation Name] | Procurement / Vendor Management |
| Legal escalation route | Defined contact route for complex, high-risk, disputed, or legally sensitive requests | Legal Counsel |
| Secure response mechanism | Approved method for securely transmitting personal data to verified requesters | IT Security / Data Protection Officer |

Inputs to this procedure may include:

- A request submitted by the individual
- A request submitted by an authorised representative
- Proof of identity or authority, where required
- Details of the right being exercised
- Relevant identifiers, such as name, email address, customer number, employee ID, account number, phone number, or postal address
- Search parameters and date ranges
- System search results
- Copies of records containing personal data
- Internal notes from business owners
- Legal, HR, compliance, security, or fraud risk assessments
- Third-party processor responses
- Decision rationale and approval records

A request does not need to mention data protection law or use formal terminology to be valid. Any communication that reasonably indicates the individual wants to exercise control over their personal data must be treated as a potential data subject rights request.

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

1. **Recognise and route the request**

 Any staff member who receives a potential data subject rights request must forward it to the Data Protection Officer or the designated DSAR mailbox immediately and no later than one business day after receipt.

 Staff must not ignore, delete, delay, or attempt to fulfil the request independently unless they are part of the authorised DSAR handling team.

 Examples of statements that may indicate a request include:

 - “Send me all information you hold about me.”
 - “Delete my account and all my data.”
 - “Correct my address.”
 - “Stop using my data for marketing.”
 - “Give me my data in a format I can transfer.”
 - “I object to you using my information.”
 - “Do not use automated decisions about me.”
 - “Tell me who you shared my data with.”

2. **Log the request in the DSAR register**

 The DSAR Coordinator must create an entry in the DSAR register on the day the request is received by the DSAR team.

 The log must include, at minimum:

 | Field | Required Entry |
 |---|---|
 | DSAR reference number | Unique request identifier |
 | Date received | Date the request was first received by [Organisation Name] |
 | Date logged | Date entered into the DSAR register |
 | Requester name | Individual or representative making the request |
 | Data subject name | Individual whose data is requested |
 | Request channel | Email, post, web form, phone, in person, portal, or other |
 | Type of right | Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, marketing objection, automated decision review, consent withdrawal, or other |
 | Identity status | Verified, pending, failed, not required, or representative authority pending |
 | Business areas involved | Relevant departments or process owners |
 | Systems in scope | Known or suspected data locations |
 | Deadline | Response due date |
 | Status | Open, pending identity, gathering data, under review, awaiting approval, responded, closed, escalated |
 | Assigned owner | DSAR Coordinator or case handler |
 | Decision summary | Fulfilled, partially fulfilled, refused, no data found, or withdrawn |
 | Closure date | Date completed |
 | Evidence location | Link or reference to supporting records |

3. **Acknowledge receipt**

 The DSAR Coordinator must acknowledge the request without undue delay, unless the request can be completed immediately.

 The acknowledgement should include:

 - Confirmation that the request has been received
 - The assigned reference number
 - A plain-language summary of the request as understood
 - Any identity verification or authority evidence required
 - The expected timeframe for response
 - Contact details for questions
 - Notice that the response period may not begin or may pause where identity cannot reasonably be verified
 - Notice that complex or multiple requests may require additional time, where applicable

4. **Determine whether [Organisation Name] is the controller**

 The Data Protection Officer or DSAR Coordinator must determine whether [Organisation Name] decides why and how the relevant personal data is processed.

 - If [Organisation Name] is the controller, continue with this procedure.
 - If [Organisation Name] is a joint controller, coordinate with the other controller according to the applicable arrangement and ensure the individual receives a clear response.
 - If [Organisation Name] is only a processor, promptly notify the relevant controller and follow contractual instructions. Do not provide a substantive response to the individual unless authorised.
 - If the request relates to data not processed by [Organisation Name], inform the requester where appropriate and close the case.

5. **Clarify the request if necessary**

 If the request is unclear, overly broad, or does not provide enough information to identify the data subject or the relevant data, the DSAR Coordinator may ask the requester for clarification.

 Clarification should be requested only where genuinely necessary. The requester must not be required to complete a specific form if the original request is otherwise clear and valid.

 Examples of appropriate clarification include:

 - Which email address, account, or customer ID is associated with the request
 - Whether the request relates to customer, employee, applicant, or supplier records
 - Whether the requester wants all personal data or only data relating to a specific matter
 - Which date range or transaction is relevant
 - Whether the request concerns access, erasure, correction, objection, or another right

6. **Verify identity and authority**

 The DSAR Coordinator must verify the requester’s identity to a level appropriate to the sensitivity of the data and the risk of unauthorised disclosure or action.

 Identity verification must be proportionate. [Organisation Name] must not request excessive identity documentation where the requester can be verified using existing authenticated channels or account information.

 Acceptable verification methods may include:

 | Scenario | Verification Method |
 |---|---|
 | Logged-in customer portal request | Existing authenticated session plus confirmation of request intent |
 | Customer email request from registered email address | Match against account details and request confirmation where needed |
 | Employee request from corporate email | Confirm through HR record and corporate identity |
 | Former employee request | Verify using known HR identifiers and a suitable identity document if needed |
 | Postal request | Match identifiers and request additional proof where risk requires |
 | Telephone request | Verify through approved security questions and follow up in writing if needed |
 | Representative request | Verify data subject identity and obtain written authority for the representative |
 | Request involving sensitive or high-risk data | Enhanced verification approved by the Data Protection Officer |

 Identity documents must be handled securely and retained only as long as necessary to evidence verification. Copies should not be retained unless required and approved by the Data Protection Officer.

 If identity cannot be verified, the request must not be fulfilled. The requester must be informed of the issue and given a reasonable opportunity to provide appropriate verification.

7. **Identify the applicable right and response requirements**

 The DSAR Coordinator must classify the request and determine what actions are required.

 | Request Type | Required Handling |
 |---|---|
 | Access | Confirm whether personal data is processed and provide a copy of personal data, subject to review and applicable limitations |
 | Rectification | Correct inaccurate personal data or complete incomplete personal data where appropriate |
 | Erasure | Delete personal data where there is no overriding lawful reason to retain it |
 | Restriction | Temporarily limit processing while accuracy, objection, or legal grounds are assessed |
 | Portability | Provide eligible data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format where technically feasible |
 | Objection | Assess whether processing must stop or whether there are overriding legitimate grounds to continue |
 | Direct marketing objection | Stop direct marketing promptly and suppress the individual from future marketing |
 | Automated decision review | Assess the decision, provide meaningful information, and arrange human review where required |
 | Consent withdrawal | Stop processing based on consent where no other lawful basis applies |
 | Information request | Provide clear information about processing activities, purposes, categories, recipients, retention, rights, and complaint routes |

8. **Calculate and monitor the response deadline**

 The DSAR Coordinator must calculate the response deadline from the date the request is received by [Organisation Name], subject to any lawful pause or dependency for identity verification where applicable.

 Standard requests must be completed without undue delay and within the required response period.

 Where a request is complex or the individual has submitted multiple requests, the Data Protection Officer may approve an extension. The requester must be informed of the extension and the reasons before the original deadline expires.

 | Milestone | Target Timeframe |
 |---|---|
 | Request routed to DSAR team | Within 1 business day of receipt by any staff member |
 | Request logged | Same business day received by DSAR team |
 | Acknowledgement sent | Within 5 business days where practicable |
 | Identity verification requested | Without undue delay |
 | Internal data search initiated | Within 5 business days after sufficient information is available |
 | Business owner response to search request | Within 7 business days unless otherwise agreed |
 | Draft response prepared | At least 5 business days before deadline where practicable |
 | Legal or DPO review completed | Before final response is issued |
 | Final response issued | Within applicable response deadline |
 | Case closed and records completed | Within 5 business days after response |

9. **Assess whether the request is excessive, repetitive, or unfounded**

 The Data Protection Officer must review any proposal to refuse a request or charge a permitted administrative fee.

 A request must not be treated as excessive or unfounded merely because it is inconvenient, broad, or relates to a complaint.

 Relevant factors may include:

 - The frequency of similar requests
 - The volume of data requested
 - Whether the request duplicates a recently completed request
 - Whether the request appears intended to harass, disrupt, or abuse the process
 - Whether the individual has refused reasonable clarification
 - The burden compared with the value and purpose of the request

 Any decision to refuse or charge a fee must be documented with objective rationale and approved by the Data Protection Officer and Legal Counsel where appropriate. The response to the requester must explain the decision in plain language and provide available complaint routes.

10. **Identify systems, repositories, and business owners**

 The DSAR Coordinator must identify all likely locations of relevant personal data using the data inventory, system owner list, retention schedule, and input from relevant business areas.

 Potential locations include:

 - Customer relationship management systems
 - Enterprise resource planning systems
 - HR information systems
 - Payroll systems
 - Recruitment platforms
 - Email and calendars
 - Collaboration and messaging tools
 - Ticketing and support systems
 - Call recordings and transcripts
 - Access control and visitor management systems
 - CCTV systems
 - Marketing platforms
 - Data warehouses and reporting tools
 - Finance and billing systems
 - Security logs
 - Complaint management systems
 - Paper files and archived records
 - Third-party processors and cloud services

 Search scope must be reasonable, risk-based, and aligned with the nature of the request.

11. **Issue data collection instructions**

 The DSAR Coordinator must send written search and collection instructions to relevant system owners and business owners.

 Instructions must include:

 - DSAR reference number
 - Request type
 - Data subject identifiers
 - Search terms
 - Date ranges
 - Systems or repositories to search
 - Required response date
 - Secure method for returning results
 - Requirement to preserve relevant data
 - Reminder not to delete, alter, or withhold records without approval
 - Escalation contact

 Business owners must confirm whether relevant personal data has been located, provide copies or extracts securely, and identify any concerns about disclosure, third-party information, privilege, confidentiality, security, or business sensitivity.

12. **Preserve relevant data where required**

 If a request relates to disputed data, objection, restriction, complaint, legal claim, investigation, or erasure, the DSAR Coordinator must assess whether a temporary hold is needed.

 Data subject rights requests must not trigger routine deletion of relevant records before the request has been assessed. Where preservation is necessary, the Data Protection Officer must coordinate with Legal Counsel, Records Management, IT, HR, or system owners.

13. **Collect and consolidate relevant data**

 System owners must perform searches using approved search criteria and provide results to the DSAR Coordinator through secure channels.

 Collected data must be stored in a restricted DSAR case workspace accessible only to authorised personnel.

 The DSAR Coordinator must consolidate results, remove exact duplicates where appropriate, and maintain traceability to source systems.

 Search results must not be exported to unsecured locations, personal drives, removable media, or personal email accounts.

14. **Review personal data for relevance**

 The DSAR Coordinator, with input from business owners, must review collected records to determine whether they contain personal data relating to the requester.

 Information should generally be included where it identifies the individual directly or indirectly and relates to them.

 Information may be excluded where it does not relate to the requester, is purely business information, is a duplicate already represented elsewhere, or is outside the request scope.

15. **Review third-party personal data and confidential information**

 Before disclosure, the DSAR Coordinator must review whether records include personal data of other individuals or confidential information belonging to [Organisation Name], clients, staff, or third parties.

 [Organisation Name] must balance the requester’s rights against the rights and freedoms of others.

 Actions may include:

 - Redacting names, contact details, opinions, or identifiers of third parties
 - Seeking consent from the third party where appropriate
 - Providing summaries instead of full documents
 - Withholding specific content where disclosure would adversely affect others
 - Disclosing information where it is reasonable and lawful to do so

 Redactions must be applied securely and irreversibly. The reason for each material redaction must be recorded.

16. **Assess legal, security, and privilege limitations**

 The Data Protection Officer must consult Legal Counsel where records may involve:

 - Legal advice or litigation material
 - Ongoing investigations
 - Whistleblowing reports
 - Fraud prevention
 - Security monitoring
 - Confidential references
 - Regulatory inquiries
 - Intellectual property or trade secrets
 - Negotiations or settlement discussions
 - Records subject to legal hold
 - Information that may prejudice the prevention or detection of unlawful activity

 Any decision to withhold or limit disclosure must be documented, approved, and explained to the requester where appropriate without undermining the reason for the limitation.

17. **Prepare the response for access requests**

 For access requests, the DSAR Coordinator must prepare a response package containing, where applicable:

 - Confirmation whether [Organisation Name] processes the individual’s personal data
 - A copy of personal data in scope
 - Purposes for processing
 - Categories of personal data involved
 - Categories of recipients or parties to whom data has been disclosed
 - Retention periods or criteria used to determine retention
 - Information about the individual’s rights
 - Source of the data where not collected directly from the individual
 - Meaningful information about automated decision-making where applicable
 - Complaint routes, including internal contact details and supervisory authority information
 - Explanation of any redactions or withheld material, where appropriate

 Responses must be concise, transparent, intelligible, and written in plain language.

18. **Handle rectification requests**

 For rectification requests, the DSAR Coordinator must work with the relevant system owner or business owner to assess whether the data is inaccurate or incomplete.

 Actions may include:

 - Correcting factual inaccuracies
 - Completing missing data
 - Adding a supplementary statement where the accuracy is disputed
 - Notifying relevant recipients or processors of the correction where appropriate
 - Informing the requester of completion or explaining why no correction was made

 Where the accuracy of data is disputed and cannot be resolved immediately, processing may need to be restricted while the matter is assessed.

19. **Handle erasure requests**

 For erasure requests, the DSAR Coordinator must determine whether the personal data should be deleted and whether any lawful retention reason applies.

 Erasure may be appropriate where:

 - The data is no longer needed for the purpose collected
 - The individual withdraws consent and no other lawful basis applies
 - The individual successfully objects to processing
 - The data was processed unlawfully
 - Deletion is required to meet a legal obligation
 - The data relates to certain online services provided to a child

 Erasure may be refused or limited where retention is necessary for reasons such as:

 - Compliance with legal obligations
 - Establishing, exercising, or defending legal claims
 - Employment, tax, finance, audit, or regulatory recordkeeping
 - Freedom of expression or information considerations
 - Public interest obligations where applicable
 - Security, fraud prevention, or incident investigation needs
 - Contractual necessity where the individual still receives services

 Where deletion is approved, system owners must confirm completion. Where immediate deletion from backups is not feasible, the data must be protected from active use and deleted according to backup lifecycle processes.

20. **Handle restriction requests**

 For restriction requests, the DSAR Coordinator must determine whether processing should be temporarily limited.

 Restriction may be appropriate where:

 - The individual contests accuracy and verification is pending
 - Processing is unlawful but the individual prefers restriction instead of erasure
 - [Organisation Name] no longer needs the data but the individual needs it for a legal claim
 - The individual has objected and the balancing assessment is pending

 Restricted data must be clearly marked, access-limited, or technically controlled to prevent use except for permitted purposes. The requester must be informed before restriction is lifted where required.

21. **Handle portability requests**

 For portability requests, the DSAR Coordinator must assess whether the requested data is eligible for portability.

 Eligible data generally includes personal data:

 - Provided by the individual
 - Processed by automated means
 - Processed based on consent or contract
 - Not adversely affecting the rights and freedoms of others

 Where applicable, provide the data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format, such as CSV, JSON, XML, or another appropriate format.

 Where technically feasible and secure, [Organisation Name] may transmit the data directly to another controller at the individual’s request.

22. **Handle objection requests**

 For objection requests, the Data Protection Officer must assess the processing activity, the lawful basis, the individual’s circumstances, and whether [Organisation Name] has compelling grounds to continue.

 Processing must be paused where appropriate while the assessment is completed.

 If the objection relates to direct marketing, processing for direct marketing purposes must stop promptly. The individual should be added to an appropriate suppression list to prevent future marketing, unless they request complete deletion and deletion is appropriate.

 For non-marketing objections, the decision must be documented and communicated to the requester.

23. **Handle withdrawal of consent**

 Where an individual withdraws consent, the DSAR Coordinator must identify all processing activities relying on that consent and ensure they are stopped.

 Withdrawal of consent does not automatically require deletion of all personal data. The DSAR Coordinator must assess whether any personal data must be retained under another lawful basis.

 The requester must be informed of the action taken.

24. **Handle automated decision-making and profiling requests**

 Where the request concerns an automated decision or profiling activity, the Data Protection Officer must identify:

 - The decision or profiling process involved
 - Whether the decision has legal or similarly significant effects
 - The data used in the decision
 - The logic and main factors involved, explained in understandable terms
 - The impact on the individual
 - Whether human review is required
 - Whether the individual can contest the decision or provide additional information

 The case must be escalated to Legal Counsel where the decision affects employment, credit, eligibility, pricing, fraud outcomes, access to essential services, or other high-impact outcomes.

25. **Notify recipients and processors where required**

 Where personal data has been corrected, erased, or restricted, the DSAR Coordinator must determine whether recipients or processors should be notified.

 Notification may include:

 - Internal system owners
 - Service providers
 - Business partners
 - Joint controllers
 - Data recipients that received the affected personal data

 The DSAR Coordinator must record who was notified, when, what action was requested, and what confirmation was received.

26. **Prepare the draft response**

 The DSAR Coordinator must prepare a draft response using the approved DSAR response template.

 The response must include:

 - DSAR reference number
 - Summary of the request
 - Actions taken
 - Outcome of the request
 - Data provided, corrected, deleted, restricted, exported, or suppressed
 - Any information withheld or redacted, described where appropriate
 - Reasons for any refusal or partial fulfilment
 - Available internal review route
 - Right to lodge a complaint with the relevant supervisory authority
 - Contact details for the Data Protection Officer or privacy team

 The tone must be professional, clear, and helpful. Avoid legal jargon unless necessary.

27. **Quality check the response package**

 Before release, the DSAR Coordinator must complete quality checks to ensure:

 - The requester’s identity and authority were verified
 - The correct individual’s data is included
 - Searches were completed and evidenced
 - Data from all relevant systems was considered
 - Redactions are irreversible and appropriate
 - Third-party data is protected
 - Withheld information is supported by documented rationale
 - The response is complete and understandable
 - The response is addressed to the correct recipient
 - The delivery method is secure
 - Any extension, refusal, or partial response has been approved

28. **Obtain approval**

 The final response must be approved before release.

 Approval requirements are:

 | Case Type | Required Approval |
 |---|---|
 | Routine access request with no significant redactions | DSAR Coordinator or Data Protection Officer delegate |
 | Request involving sensitive personal data | Data Protection Officer |
 | Partial refusal or full refusal | Data Protection Officer and Legal Counsel |
 | Employee or former employee request | Data Protection Officer and HR representative |
 | Request involving legal claims or disputes | Legal Counsel |
 | Request involving security logs, fraud, or investigations | Data Protection Officer, Legal Counsel, and Information Security representative |
 | High-volume or complex request | Data Protection Officer |
 | Request from a representative | Data Protection Officer or delegate after authority verification |
 | Request involving media, regulator, executive, or reputational sensitivity | Data Protection Officer and Executive Sponsor as needed |

29. **Send the response securely**

 The DSAR Coordinator must send the final response using an approved secure method proportionate to the sensitivity of the data.

 Approved methods may include:

 - Secure portal
 - Encrypted email
 - Password-protected file with password sent separately
 - Registered post or courier
 - In-person collection with identity verification
 - Secure transfer to another controller for portability requests

 Personal data must not be sent to unverified addresses or through insecure channels where there is a risk of unauthorised access.

30. **Complete operational actions**

 Where the request requires changes to data or processing activities, the DSAR Coordinator must ensure the actions are completed and evidenced.

 Operational actions may include:

 - Updating inaccurate records
 - Deleting approved data
 - Applying restriction flags
 - Removing the individual from marketing lists
 - Adding the individual to a suppression list
 - Updating consent records
 - Exporting portable data
 - Triggering processor actions
 - Updating internal notes
 - Confirming backup handling
 - Updating data quality or system configuration issues identified during the request

31. **Close the request**

 The DSAR Coordinator may close the request when:

 - The final response has been sent
 - Required operational actions have been completed or scheduled
 - Evidence has been saved
 - The DSAR register has been updated
 - Any lessons learned or remediation actions have been recorded
 - Any complaint or appeal period tracking required by [Organisation Name] has been noted

 The closure record must include the final outcome, closure date, approver, evidence location, and any residual actions.

32. **Manage follow-up, complaint, or appeal**

 If the requester challenges the response, complains, or provides additional information, the Data Protection Officer must assess whether the case should be reopened, treated as a new request, or handled as a complaint.

 Complaints alleging delay, incomplete response, wrongful refusal, improper redaction, failure to erase, or inappropriate processing must be escalated to the Data Protection Officer and Legal Counsel as appropriate.

## Roles & RACI

| Activity | Data Subject / Representative | DSAR Coordinator | Data Protection Officer | System Owner / Business Owner | Legal Counsel | Information Security | HR | Processor / Vendor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Submit request | R | I | I | I | I | I | I | I |
| Log DSAR | I | R | A | I | I | I | I | I |
| Acknowledge request | I | R | A | I | I | I | I | I |
| Verify identity | R | R | A | C | C | C | C | I |
| Clarify scope | R | R | A | C | C | I | C | I |
| Determine controller or processor role | I | R | A | C | C | I | I | C |
| Calculate deadline | I | R | A | I | I | I | I | I |
| Identify systems and data locations | I | R | A | R | I | C | C | C |
| Search and collect data | I | C | A | R | I | C | R where HR data involved | R where instructed |
| Preserve relevant data | I | R | A | R | C | C | C | R where instructed |
| Review relevance and scope | I | R | A | C | C | I | C | I |
| Review redactions and limitations | I | R | A | C | C | C | C | I |
| Assess refusal or extension | I | C | A | C | R | C | C | I |
| Complete rectification, erasure, restriction, suppression, or portability actions | I | C | A | R | C | C | R where HR data involved | R where instructed |
| Prepare response | I | R | A | C | C | C | C | I |
| Approve response | I | C | A | C | R for legal matters | C for security matters | C for HR matters | I |
| Send response securely | I | R | A | I | I | C | I | I |
| Update DSAR register and close case | I | R | A | I | I | I | I | I |
| Handle complaint or escalation | R | C | A | C | R where legal risk exists | C | C | I |

RACI key:

- **R** - Responsible for performing the activity
- **A** - Accountable for the outcome and approval
- **C** - Consulted before or during the activity
- **I** - Informed of progress or outcome

## Records & Outputs

The DSAR Coordinator must maintain complete and accurate records for each request. Records must be stored securely in the approved DSAR case management location and retained according to the approved retention schedule.

Required records include:

| Record / Output | Description | Owner | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| DSAR register entry | Central record of request details, status, deadlines, decisions, and closure | Data Protection Officer | [Retention Period] |
| Original request | Copy of email, form, letter, call note, ticket, or other intake record | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Acknowledgement | Copy of acknowledgement sent to requester | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Identity verification evidence | Verification status and limited evidence of method used | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Representative authority evidence | Written authority, power of attorney, parental responsibility evidence, or equivalent | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Clarification correspondence | Requests for clarification and responses received | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Search instructions | Instructions sent to system owners and business owners | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Search results confirmation | Evidence of systems searched, search terms, dates, and results | System Owners / DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Data extracts | Copies of personal data collected for review | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Redaction log | Record of redactions and rationale | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Limitation or refusal assessment | Rationale and approval for withholding, limiting, extending, charging, or refusing | Data Protection Officer / Legal Counsel | [Retention Period] |
| Processor correspondence | Instructions to and confirmations from processors or vendors | DSAR Coordinator / Vendor Management | [Retention Period] |
| Action completion evidence | Proof of correction, deletion, restriction, suppression, export, or consent update | System Owners / DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Final response | Copy of response sent to requester | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Delivery evidence | Secure transmission confirmation, postal receipt, portal log, or equivalent | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Approval record | Evidence of DPO, Legal, HR, Information Security, or other approval | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |
| Closure record | Final status, closure date, residual actions, and lessons learned | DSAR Coordinator | [Retention Period] |

Outputs may include:

- A completed access response package
- Corrected personal data
- Deleted personal data or deletion instruction
- Restricted processing flag or control
- Portable data file
- Marketing suppression confirmation
- Consent withdrawal confirmation
- Automated decision review outcome
- Refusal or partial refusal response
- Extension notice
- Processor action confirmation
- Updated DSAR register
- Lessons learned or remediation action

DSAR records must be protected against unauthorised access, alteration, deletion, or disclosure. Access must be limited to personnel with a business need to know.

## Exceptions & Escalation

Exceptions to this procedure must be approved by the Data Protection Officer and documented in the DSAR register.

Examples of exceptions include:

- Delayed response due to complexity, multiple requests, or dependency on verified identity
- Refusal to fulfil all or part of a request
- Decision to charge a permitted administrative fee
- Inability to complete erasure due to legal retention obligations
- Inability to provide portability in the requested format
- Limitation of access due to third-party rights, privilege, security, fraud, or legal risk
- Deviation from standard identity verification methods
- Use of an alternative secure delivery method
- Delayed processor response
- Need to preserve data despite an erasure request

Escalation is mandatory in the following circumstances:

| Escalation Trigger | Escalate To | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Identity cannot be verified | Data Protection Officer | As soon as identified |
| Request from a legal representative | Data Protection Officer / Legal Counsel | Before substantive response |
| Request involving legal claims, litigation, or settlement | Legal Counsel | Immediately |
| Request involving employee relations, grievance, disciplinary, or termination matters | HR and Legal Counsel | Immediately |
| Request involving children or vulnerable individuals | Data Protection Officer / Legal Counsel | Immediately |
| Request involving special category or highly sensitive data | Data Protection Officer | Before disclosure or action |
| Request involving security logs, fraud, or investigations | Information Security / Legal Counsel / Data Protection Officer | Immediately |
| Request involving suspected data breach | Information Security / Data Protection Officer | Immediately |
| Request likely to miss deadline | Data Protection Officer | At least 5 business days before deadline where possible |
| Request from regulator, media, public figure, or executive | Data Protection Officer / Legal Counsel / Communications | Immediately |
| Proposed refusal, extension, or fee | Data Protection Officer / Legal Counsel | Before notifying requester |
| Processor fails to cooperate | Vendor Management / Legal Counsel / Data Protection Officer | As soon as delay is known |
| Request may affect rights of other individuals | Data Protection Officer / Legal Counsel | Before disclosure |
| Repeated, abusive, or excessive requests | Data Protection Officer / Legal Counsel | Before decision |

If a requester complains about the handling of a request, the Data Protection Officer must review the case file, confirm whether the original decision remains appropriate, and determine whether corrective action is required.

If a supervisory authority contacts [Organisation Name] regarding a data subject rights request, Legal Counsel and the Data Protection Officer must be notified immediately. All related records must be preserved.

## Review

This procedure must be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur, including:

- Changes to data protection law or regulatory expectations
- Changes to business processes involving personal data
- Implementation of new systems or major system changes
- Introduction of new processors or outsourcing arrangements
- Repeated DSAR handling issues or missed deadlines
- Findings from audits, complaints, incidents, or regulatory inquiries
- Changes to organisational structure, roles, or responsibilities
- Lessons learned from complex or high-risk requests

The Data Protection Officer is responsible for ensuring the review is completed, updates are approved, and relevant personnel are informed of material changes.

Review activities should include:

- Sampling closed DSAR cases for completeness and timeliness
- Checking whether deadlines were met
- Reviewing quality of identity verification evidence
- Assessing adequacy of searches and system owner responses
- Confirming redactions and refusals were properly approved
- Reviewing processor responsiveness
- Identifying recurring data quality or retention issues
- Confirming templates and response language remain current
- Updating training materials and staff guidance where needed

Version history must be maintained below.

| Version | Date | Author | Summary of Changes | Approved By |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Purpose

This procedure defines how [Organisation Name] detects, assesses, manages, records, and reports personal data breaches. It ensures that suspected or confirmed breaches involving personal data are handled promptly, consistently, and in a manner that protects affected individuals and meets statutory notification timelines.

This procedure is designed to ensure that:

- Personal data breaches are identified and escalated without delay.
- The Data Protection Officer and relevant stakeholders receive sufficient information to assess the breach.
- Notifications to the relevant Supervisory Authority are made within the required timeframe where legally required.
- Affected individuals are informed without undue delay where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms.
- All breaches, including those not notified externally, are documented with rationale, actions taken, and lessons learned.
- Remediation and prevention activities are tracked to completion.

## Scope

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, temporary staff, third-party service providers, and business units of [Organisation Name] that process personal data on behalf of the organisation or have access to systems, records, communications, devices, or services containing personal data.

This procedure applies to suspected or confirmed personal data breaches involving personal data in any format, including:

- Electronic records, databases, files, logs, backups, emails, messages, collaboration tools, and cloud platforms.
- Paper records, printed reports, notebooks, forms, identity documents, and physical files.
- Verbal disclosures or misdirected conversations involving personal data.
- Personal data processed by suppliers, processors, sub-processors, consultants, or other third parties acting for or with [Organisation Name].
- Personal data relating to customers, employees, contractors, applicants, suppliers, website users, patients, residents, students, members, or any other identifiable individuals.

For this procedure, a personal data breach means a security incident that results in accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data. Examples include, but are not limited to:

- Sending personal data to the wrong recipient.
- Loss or theft of a laptop, mobile device, USB drive, paper file, or access credential.
- Unauthorised access to systems containing personal data.
- Ransomware, malware, phishing, or account compromise involving personal data.
- Accidental publication of personal data on a website, portal, shared drive, or collaboration platform.
- Incorrect system permissions exposing personal data to unauthorised users.
- Supplier incidents affecting personal data processed for [Organisation Name].
- Loss of availability of personal data where the loss may affect individuals.
- Unauthorised alteration of personal data affecting accuracy, integrity, or decision-making.

This procedure must be followed in conjunction with, where applicable:

- Information Security Incident Response Procedure.
- Data Protection Policy.
- Records Retention Schedule.
- Supplier Management Procedure.
- Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery procedures.
- Legal Hold and Litigation Response Procedure.
- Communications and Media Handling procedures.

## Prerequisites & Inputs

The following prerequisites must be in place to support effective execution of this procedure:

| Prerequisite | Required Detail | Responsible Role |
|---|---|---|
| Breach reporting channels | Dedicated email, service desk category, hotline, or incident portal for reporting suspected personal data breaches | Data Protection Officer / IT Service Desk |
| Incident logging system | A system or register capable of recording breach details, timestamps, decisions, evidence, actions, and closure status | Data Protection Officer |
| Current contact list | Up-to-date contacts for Legal, Information Security, IT, HR, Communications, business owners, senior management, suppliers, and external advisers | Data Protection Officer |
| Supervisory Authority contact details | Approved contact route for the competent data protection authority | Data Protection Officer |
| Supplier breach notification obligations | Contractual terms requiring suppliers to notify [Organisation Name] promptly of suspected or confirmed breaches | Procurement / Legal |
| Data inventory | Records describing key processing activities, personal data categories, systems, data owners, locations, and processors | Data Protection Officer / Data Owners |
| Breach assessment template | Standard form for facts, timeline, affected individuals, risk assessment, notification decision, and remediation | Data Protection Officer |
| Communication templates | Approved templates for authority notifications, data subject notices, internal briefings, and supplier requests | Data Protection Officer / Legal / Communications |
| Evidence preservation capability | Ability to preserve logs, emails, screenshots, access records, forensic images, tickets, and supplier reports | Information Security / IT |

Inputs to this procedure may include:

- Employee, customer, supplier, or third-party breach reports.
- Alerts from security monitoring tools, endpoint detection, data loss prevention, identity systems, or cloud platforms.
- Service desk tickets.
- Supplier or processor notifications.
- Internal audit findings.
- Customer complaints or enquiries.
- Returned mail, misdirected emails, or access control reports.
- Legal, regulatory, law enforcement, or media enquiries.
- Business continuity, disaster recovery, or system availability incident reports.

The following timeline applies once [Organisation Name] becomes aware that a personal data breach has occurred. Awareness means the organisation has a reasonable degree of certainty that a security incident has led to personal data being compromised.

| Activity | Target Timing | Maximum Timing / Requirement |
|---|---:|---|
| Initial internal report by staff member or contractor | Immediately | No later than 2 hours after discovery |
| Service Desk / Security triage and escalation to DPO | Immediately | No later than 4 hours after receipt |
| Initial breach assessment started | Same business day | No later than 8 hours after awareness |
| Incident response team convened, where required | Same business day | No later than 12 hours after awareness |
| Decision on authority notification requirement | As soon as sufficient facts are available | In time to support notification within 72 hours of awareness |
| Supervisory Authority notification, where required | As soon as practicable | Within 72 hours of awareness |
| Data subject notification, where required | Without undue delay | As soon as accurate and helpful information can be provided |
| Breach record completed | During incident handling | Finalised within 10 business days of closure |
| Lessons learned review | After containment and immediate remediation | Within 20 business days of closure |

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

1. **Identify and report the suspected breach**
