| Department Heads / Business Unit Leaders | Own completion performance within their areas; identify high-risk roles; provide subject matter input; address systemic issues affecting compliance |
| Information Security | Provides input on secure handling, access control, breach reporting, phishing, remote working, and incident response content; coordinates with privacy training where risks overlap |
| Legal / Compliance | Reviews legal accuracy where required; supports training on rights requests, complaints, contracts, and regulatory obligations; advises on enforcement implications |
| IT / Identity and Access Management | Provides access data for reconciliation; supports restrictions or controls where training completion is tied to system access; supports platform integrations |
| Internal Communications | Supports launch messages, reminders, intranet updates, campaign branding, and targeted awareness communications |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Identifies third-party personnel requiring training; ensures contractual training expectations are reflected where applicable; supports supplier-related specialist content |
| System Owners / Process Owners | Identify users handling personal data in their systems or processes; ensure local procedures align with training; notify the Data Protection Officer of material changes |
| Employees and In-Scope Personnel | Complete training by the deadline; apply training in daily work; seek advice when unsure; report suspected personal data breaches immediately; follow approved policies and procedures |
| Internal Audit | May independently review programme design, completion evidence, escalation, and effectiveness as part of assurance activity |

Responsibility summary:

| Activity | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Programme approval | Executive Sponsor | Data Protection Officer | Legal, HR, Information Security | Department Heads |
| Training needs assessment | Data Protection Officer | Privacy Team / Department Heads | HR, IT, Process Owners | Managers |
| Content development | Data Protection Officer | Learning and Development / Privacy Team | Legal, HR, Information Security, SMEs | Learners |
| Training assignment | Learning and Development | Learning and Development | HR, Data Protection Officer | Managers, Learners |
| Completion monitoring | Data Protection Officer | Learning and Development | HR, Managers | Executive Sponsor |
| Non-completion escalation | Department Heads | Managers / Learning and Development | HR, Data Protection Officer | Executive Sponsor where material |
| Effectiveness review | Data Protection Officer | Privacy Team / Learning and Development | Internal Audit, Information Security, HR | Senior Leadership |
| Record retention | Learning and Development | Learning and Development / HR | Data Protection Officer | Internal Audit |

## Resources

The programme requires sufficient people, tools, budget, and supporting materials to deliver training reliably and maintain evidence.

### People Resources

| Resource | Purpose | Estimated Commitment |
|---|---|---|
| Data Protection Officer | Programme ownership, content approval, reporting, effectiveness review | [Hours / FTE estimate] during implementation, then ongoing |
| Privacy Team | Content support, learner queries, specialist modules, incident trend analysis | [Hours / FTE estimate] |
| Learning and Development Lead | LMS configuration, assignment, reporting, learner support | [Hours / FTE estimate] |
| HR Representative | Workforce data, onboarding integration, escalation support | [Hours / FTE estimate] |
| Information Security Representative | Security content and breach reporting alignment | [Hours / FTE estimate] |
| Legal / Compliance Reviewer | Legal accuracy and compliance review | [Hours / FTE estimate] |
| Internal Communications Support | Launch and reminder communications | [Hours / FTE estimate] |
| Department Subject Matter Experts | Role-based scenarios and process-specific examples | [Hours / FTE estimate] per function |
| IT / LMS Administrator | Platform configuration and troubleshooting | [Hours / FTE estimate] |

### Technology Resources

Required technology resources include:

- Learning management system or approved training tracking platform.
- Workforce data feed from HR system.
- Contractor and third-party user source data.
- Reporting dashboard or export capability.
- Training content authoring tool, where applicable.
- Secure repository for approved training materials and evidence.
- Communications channels such as email, intranet, collaboration platform, and manager dashboards.
- Helpdesk or support channel for access issues.
- Identity and access management reporting to support population reconciliation.

### Content and Materials

The following materials will be developed or maintained:

| Material | Purpose | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Core Data Protection Training Module | Mandatory baseline training for all in-scope personnel | Data Protection Officer |
| Annual Refresher Module | Reinforces key responsibilities and updates | Data Protection Officer |
| Induction Training Version | Supports onboarding and early awareness | Learning and Development / Data Protection Officer |
| Specialist Role-Based Modules | Addresses high-risk and function-specific processing | Data Protection Officer / SMEs |
| Manager Briefing Pack | Enables managers to reinforce obligations and manage completion | Data Protection Officer / HR |
| Executive Briefing | Supports leadership accountability and risk awareness | Data Protection Officer |
| Quick Reference Guides | Provides practical reminders for common tasks | Privacy Team |
| Breach Reporting Job Aid | Explains how to report suspected personal data breaches | Data Protection Officer / Information Security |
| Frequently Asked Questions | Answers common learner questions | Privacy Team |
| Communications Templates | Launch, reminders, escalation, and campaign updates | Internal Communications |
| Assessment Question Bank | Measures understanding and identifies weak areas | Learning and Development / Data Protection Officer |

### Budget Considerations

Budget planning should consider:

- Learning management system licensing or configuration costs.
- External training content, if used.
- Translation or localisation where needed.
- Accessibility adaptations.
- Content authoring tools.
- External legal or privacy review, if required.
- Time commitment from internal subject matter experts.
- Communications materials.
- Reporting or dashboard development.
- Backfill or operational coverage for high-volume teams completing training.
- Specialist training for high-risk teams.

### Accessibility and Inclusion

Training must be accessible to all in-scope personnel. The programme will consider:

- Accessible formats compatible with assistive technology.
- Captions or transcripts for video content.
- Alternative formats where required.
- Plain-language content.
- Translations where necessary for the workforce.
- Mobile-compatible delivery where appropriate.
- Options for personnel without regular computer access.
- Reasonable adjustments for learners requiring support.

## Success Metrics

The programme will be measured using completion, understanding, behavioural, and assurance indicators.

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Reporting Frequency | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Core induction completion for new starters | [Target %] within required timeframe | LMS / onboarding report | Monthly | Learning and Development |
| Annual refresher completion | [Target %] by campaign deadline | LMS completion dashboard | Weekly during campaign, monthly otherwise | Learning and Development |
| Specialist training completion for assigned roles | [Target %] by deadline | LMS role-based report | Monthly | Data Protection Officer |
| Manager briefing completion | [Target %] by deadline | LMS / attendance record | Monthly | Human Resources |
| Executive awareness completion | [Target %] by deadline | Attendance / completion record | Annually | Data Protection Officer |
| Assessment pass rate | [Target %] first-time pass or approved retry completion | LMS quiz report | Monthly during rollout | Learning and Development |
| Overdue training rate | Less than [Target %] after escalation | LMS overdue report | Weekly during campaign | Learning and Development |
| Training population accuracy | [Target %] reconciliation between HR, contractor, and access records | Reconciliation review | Quarterly | HR / IT / Data Protection Officer |
| Personal data breach reporting timeliness | Improvement against baseline | Incident records | Quarterly | Data Protection Officer / Information Security |
| Repeat privacy errors in same team or process | Reduction against baseline | Incident and audit trend analysis | Quarterly | Data Protection Officer |
| Learner satisfaction | [Target score] or above | Training feedback survey | After each campaign | Learning and Development |
| Staff confidence in reporting concerns | Improvement against baseline | Survey / pulse check | Annually | Data Protection Officer |
| Audit findings related to training evidence | No high-risk unresolved findings | Internal audit or assurance review | Annually | Data Protection Officer |
| Policy acknowledgement completion | [Target %] where required | LMS or attestation records | Annually | Learning and Development |
| Completion evidence availability | Evidence retrievable within [number] business days | Evidence sampling | Quarterly | Learning and Development |

Minimum success criteria for the first full programme cycle are:

- All in-scope personnel are assigned appropriate training.
- New starter training is embedded into onboarding.
- Annual refresher training is completed by the required population or formally escalated.
- High-risk roles receive additional role-based training.
- Completion records and training content versions are retained.
- Overdue training is actively managed and evidenced.
- Effectiveness is reviewed using more than completion rates alone.
- Improvement actions are documented and tracked.

Where targets are not met, the Data Protection Officer will agree corrective actions with relevant owners. Corrective actions may include targeted re-training, improved communications, manager escalation, access control changes, process updates, or additional assurance activity.

## Review & Update Triggers

This Plan will be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change affecting data protection training needs.

Scheduled review:

| Review Activity | Frequency | Owner | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Programme plan review | Annually | Data Protection Officer | Updated Plan or confirmation no change required |
| Core training content review | Annually | Data Protection Officer | Updated module and approval record |
| Specialist training content review | Annually or as needed | Data Protection Officer / SMEs | Updated role-based modules |
| Role-to-training matrix review | Quarterly or following significant organisational change | Data Protection Officer / HR / Department Heads | Updated assignment rules |
| Completion and exception review | Monthly | Learning and Development / Data Protection Officer | Completion dashboard and exception actions |
| Effectiveness review | Quarterly and annually | Data Protection Officer | Effectiveness report and improvement actions |
| Evidence retention review | Annually | Learning and Development / Data Protection Officer | Evidence completeness confirmation |

Update triggers include:

- Material changes to data protection law, regulatory expectations, or enforcement trends.
- New or revised organisational data protection policies or procedures.
- Significant personal data breach, near miss, or incident trend.
- Audit or assurance finding indicating training weakness.
- Introduction of new systems, tools, platforms, or technologies processing personal data.
- New uses of personal data, including analytics, profiling, monitoring, automation, or artificial intelligence.
- Launch of new products, services, business processes, or customer channels.
- New categories of personal data or higher-risk processing.
- Significant change in workforce model, such as remote working, outsourcing, insourcing, restructuring, merger, or acquisition.
- Expansion into new countries or markets.
- Changes to individual rights handling processes.
- Changes to breach reporting or incident management procedures.
- Supplier or third-party processing changes.
- Repeated non-completion or poor assessment results in a department or role group.
- Feedback indicating that training is unclear, outdated, inaccessible, or not practical.
- Technology changes affecting the learning platform or reporting capability.

Version control expectations:

- All approved training materials must have a version number and approval date.
- Superseded materials must be retained where needed to evidence what training was delivered at a point in time.
- Changes to mandatory training requirements must be communicated to affected personnel and managers.
- Material changes to this Plan must be approved by the Data Protection Officer and, where significant, by the Executive Sponsor.
- Review records must be retained as evidence of ongoing programme management.

GDPR-023.title: Data Processing Agreements (Art. 28 Contracts)
GDPR-023.content:
# Data Processing Agreements (Art. 28 Contracts)

| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DPA-TPL-001] | 1.0 | [Data Protection Officer / Privacy Office] | [Effective Date] | GDPR | Internal - Confidential |

## Purpose

This template is used to capture, review, approve and evidence the required contractual controls for any third party that processes personal data on behalf of the organisation.

It applies before engaging a new processor, materially changing an existing processing arrangement, renewing a supplier contract, adding new services, changing processing locations, introducing sub-processors, or expanding the categories of personal data processed.

The completed form supports confirmation that:

- A written data processing agreement or equivalent contract terms are in place before processing begins.
- Processing is limited to documented instructions from the organisation.
- The processor provides appropriate confidentiality, security, assistance, deletion, return, audit, breach notification and sub-processor controls.
- International transfers and onward processing are identified and appropriately governed.
- The agreement aligns with the organisation’s data protection, procurement, information security, vendor risk management and records management requirements.

## Instructions

1. Complete this template for every processor that will process personal data on behalf of the organisation.
2. Complete all required fields before contract signature, purchase order approval, onboarding or access provisioning.
3. Attach the proposed or executed agreement, data processing terms, security schedule, transfer mechanism, sub-processor list, and any relevant assessment evidence.
4. The business owner is responsible for initiating the form and confirming the business need, processing purpose and operational details.
5. The Privacy Office or Data Protection Officer is responsible for confirming that the data protection terms are adequate.
6. Information Security is responsible for reviewing technical and organisational security measures where the processing presents more than low risk.
7. Legal or Procurement is responsible for ensuring the approved terms are incorporated into the governing contract and signed by authorised parties.
8. Do not approve the processor to process personal data until all mandatory fields are complete, required reviews are recorded, and any high-risk issues are resolved or formally accepted.
9. If the processor uses its own standard data processing agreement, compare it against the mandatory requirements in this form and document any deviations.
10. If the processor will engage sub-processors, transfer personal data internationally, or process sensitive data, ensure the relevant sections are completed and reviewed.
11. If the processing changes after approval, update this form and route it for re-approval before the change is implemented.
12. Retain the completed form and all supporting records in the approved contract or vendor management repository.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Request ID | Text | Yes | Enter the unique internal request, procurement, legal matter or vendor risk reference. |
| Date Submitted | Date | Yes | Enter the date this form is submitted for review. |
| Business Owner | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the accountable internal owner for the processing activity and supplier relationship. |
| Business Unit / Department | Text | Yes | State the department requesting or managing the processor. |
| Processor Legal Name | Text | Yes | Enter the full legal entity name of the processor. Do not use only a trading name unless it is also the contracting entity. |
| Processor Trading Name | Text | No | Enter the brand, platform or service name if different from the legal entity. |
| Processor Address | Text | Yes | Provide the registered or principal business address of the processor. |
| Processor Contact | Name / Email | Yes | Provide the commercial or account contact responsible for the engagement. |
| Processor Privacy Contact | Name / Email | Yes | Provide the privacy, data protection or legal contact for contractual and data protection matters. |
| Processor Security Contact | Name / Email | No | Provide the contact for information security, incident response, audit and technical control matters. |
| Parent / Affiliate Involvement | Text | No | Identify any group companies or affiliates involved in providing the service or accessing personal data. |
| Contract Title | Text | Yes | Enter the name of the master agreement, order form, statement of work, terms of service or other governing contract. |
| Contract Reference | Text | Yes | Enter the contract number, procurement reference, vendor record or legal matter ID. |
| Contract Start Date | Date | Yes | Enter the intended or actual start date of the contract. |
| Contract End Date / Renewal Terms | Text | Yes | State the end date, renewal cycle, auto-renewal terms or termination notice period. |
| DPA Document Title | Text | Yes | Enter the title of the data processing agreement, data processing addendum, schedule or equivalent terms. |
| DPA Version / Date | Text | Yes | State the version number and date of the data processing terms being reviewed or executed. |
| DPA Execution Method | Dropdown | Yes | Select: signed agreement, click-through terms, incorporated schedule, supplier standard addendum, customer addendum, framework agreement, other. |
| DPA Status | Dropdown | Yes | Select: draft, under review, approved for signature, signed, rejected, renewal required, remediation required. |
| Processing Role Confirmed | Dropdown | Yes | Confirm that the supplier acts as processor for the described services. If the supplier is an independent controller, joint controller or mixed-role provider, document this and seek Privacy Office review. |
| Description of Services | Long Text | Yes | Describe the services the processor will provide and how those services involve personal data. |
| Purpose of Processing | Long Text | Yes | Describe the specific business purpose for which the processor is authorised to process personal data. Avoid broad descriptions such as “business purposes” without detail. |
| Processing Activities | Multi-select / Long Text | Yes | Identify activities such as collection, hosting, storage, access, support, analysis, transmission, enrichment, deletion, backup, archiving, communication, fulfilment or troubleshooting. |
| Processing Systems / Platforms | Text | Yes | Name the systems, applications, portals, integrations, environments or tools through which personal data will be processed. |
| Internal System Owner | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the owner of the internal system or process connected to the processor. |
| Data Subjects | Multi-select / Text | Yes | Identify affected individuals, such as customers, prospects, employees, contractors, website users, patients, students, suppliers, applicants or other individuals. |
| Categories of Personal Data | Long Text | Yes | List the personal data categories, such as contact details, identifiers, account data, employment records, transaction data, device data, usage data, communications, support tickets or location data. |
| Sensitive or High-Risk Data | Yes / No / Details | Yes | Indicate whether the processor will handle sensitive data, criminal records data, children’s data, financial account data, government identifiers, authentication credentials, health data, biometric data or other high-risk information. Provide details where applicable. |
| Estimated Volume of Records | Dropdown / Number | Yes | Estimate the number of individuals or records processed. Use ranges if exact figures are unavailable. |
| Frequency of Processing | Dropdown | Yes | Select: one-time, occasional, monthly, weekly, daily, continuous, real-time, other. |
| Duration of Processing | Text | Yes | State how long the processor is authorised to process personal data, including post-termination transition, backup and deletion periods. |
| Documented Instructions | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm that the processor may process personal data only on the organisation’s documented instructions, including instructions in the contract, order forms, statements of work and approved support requests. |
| Processor Use for Own Purposes Prohibited | Yes / No / Details | Yes | Confirm the agreement prohibits the processor from using personal data for its own purposes except where expressly authorised by the organisation or required by law. |
| Legal Requirement Notification | Yes / No / Details | Yes | Confirm the processor must notify the organisation if it is legally required to process personal data outside the organisation’s instructions, unless prohibited from doing so. |
| Confidentiality Commitment | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm that all personnel authorised to process personal data are bound by confidentiality obligations. Reference the relevant contract section or attachment. |
| Personnel Access Limited | Yes / No / Details | Yes | Confirm that access to personal data is limited to personnel who need it to provide the services. |
| Security Measures Attached | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm that technical and organisational security measures are included or attached. Reference the security schedule, supplier documentation, assessment or control summary. |
| Security Measures Adequacy | Dropdown | Yes | Select: adequate, adequate with conditions, remediation required, not adequate, review pending. Consider encryption, access controls, logging, network security, secure development, vulnerability management, backup, resilience and incident response. |
| Security Review Required | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether Information Security review is required based on data sensitivity, access level, connectivity, processing volume or criticality. |
| Security Review Outcome | Dropdown / Text | Conditional | Required if security review is needed. Select: approved, approved with conditions, rejected, pending, risk accepted. Document key conditions or exceptions. |
| Processor Assistance with Individual Rights | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the processor must assist the organisation with requests from individuals, including access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability and objection where applicable. |
| Processor Assistance with Privacy Obligations | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the processor must assist with privacy impact assessments, regulatory engagement, prior consultation, records, notices and other compliance obligations where relevant to the service. |
| Personal Data Breach Notification Requirement | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the processor must notify the organisation without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach. |
| Breach Notification Timeframe | Text | Yes | State the contractual notification timeframe. If the timeframe is not specific or is excessive, route for Privacy Office and Legal review. |
| Breach Notification Content | Yes / No / Details | Yes | Confirm the processor must provide sufficient information to support assessment, notification decisions, mitigation and communications. |
| Cooperation During Incident Response | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the processor must cooperate with investigation, containment, evidence preservation, remediation and communications. |
| Sub-Processors Permitted | Dropdown | Yes | Select: not permitted, permitted with specific prior approval, permitted with general prior approval and objection right, already approved list, unclear. |
| Sub-Processor List Provided | Yes / No / Link | Conditional | Required if sub-processors are permitted. Attach or link to the current sub-processor list. |
| Sub-Processor Notification Method | Text | Conditional | State how the processor notifies the organisation of new or changed sub-processors, such as email notice, portal update or contractual notice. |
| Sub-Processor Objection Right | Yes / No / Details | Conditional | Confirm whether the organisation can object to new or replacement sub-processors and state the process and timeframe. |
| Flow-Down Obligations Confirmed | Yes / No / Reference | Conditional | Confirm the processor is required to impose equivalent data protection obligations on sub-processors. |
| Processor Remains Liable for Sub-Processors | Yes / No / Reference | Conditional | Confirm the processor remains responsible for sub-processor performance and failures. |
| Approved Sub-Processors | Table / Attachment | Conditional | List or attach the approved sub-processors, their service role, processing location and data categories. |
| Processing Locations | Text / Table | Yes | Identify all countries or regions where personal data will be processed, stored, accessed, supported or backed up. |
| Remote Access Locations | Text | No | Identify countries or regions from which support or administrative personnel may access personal data remotely. |
| International Transfers Occur | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether personal data will be transferred to, accessed from, or stored in countries outside the organisation’s approved operating locations. |
| Transfer Mechanism | Dropdown / Details | Conditional | Required where international transfers occur. Identify the approved transfer mechanism, supporting terms, safeguards and any supplementary measures. |
| Transfer Impact Review Required | Yes / No | Conditional | Indicate whether a transfer risk assessment or equivalent review is required by organisational policy. |
| Transfer Impact Review Outcome | Dropdown / Text | Conditional | Select: approved, approved with safeguards, rejected, pending, risk accepted. Record key conditions. |
| Government or Law Enforcement Request Handling | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the processor must notify the organisation of requests for disclosure unless legally prohibited and must challenge or narrow requests where appropriate. |
| Data Return Requirement | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the processor must return personal data at the organisation’s request or upon termination where required. |
| Data Deletion Requirement | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the processor must delete personal data after services end or when instructed, unless retention is legally required. |
| Deletion Timeframe | Text | Yes | State the required deletion timeframe, including production data, backups, logs, support copies and archives where applicable. |
| Deletion Certification | Yes / No / Details | Yes | Confirm whether the processor must provide written confirmation or certification of deletion. |
| Backup Retention Handling | Text | Yes | Describe how personal data in backups will be protected, isolated from routine access, and deleted or overwritten according to backup cycles. |
| Audit Rights Included | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the organisation has rights to receive audit information, conduct audits, request assurance reports or otherwise verify compliance. |
| Audit Notice and Frequency | Text | Conditional | Required where audit rights are included. State notice periods, frequency limitations, evidence access and restrictions. |
| Third-Party Assurance Reports | Yes / No / Details | No | Identify available assurance reports, certifications, penetration test summaries or independent assessments. |
| Compliance Information Obligation | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the processor must make available information necessary to demonstrate compliance with contractual data protection obligations. |
| Processor Notice of Non-Compliance | Yes / No / Reference | Yes | Confirm the processor must notify the organisation if it believes an instruction is unlawful or cannot comply with its obligations. |
| Restrictions on Data Combination or Enrichment | Yes / No / Details | No | State whether the processor is prohibited from combining the organisation’s data with other datasets or using it for profiling, analytics, model training or product improvement. |
| Artificial Intelligence or Automated Processing Use | Yes / No / Details | No | Identify whether the processor uses AI, automated decision-making, machine learning, model training or automated analysis involving personal data. Include restrictions and approvals. |
| Production Data in Testing or Development | Yes / No / Details | No | State whether personal data may be used in test, development or staging environments. If yes, document controls such as masking, minimisation and access restrictions. |
| Data Minimisation Confirmed | Yes / No / Details | Yes | Confirm only personal data necessary for the service will be provided or made accessible. |
| Retention Alignment Confirmed | Yes / No / Details | Yes | Confirm the processor’s retention practices align with the organisation’s retention instructions and service need. |
| Special Restrictions or Instructions | Long Text | No | Record any additional organisation-specific restrictions, such as no offshore access, no email exports, no onward transfer, encryption requirements, segregation requirements or named support personnel only. |
| Standard Contract Deviations | Long Text | Yes | List deviations from approved data processing terms, missing provisions, supplier redlines or non-standard positions. Enter “None” if no deviations. |
| Privacy Risk Rating | Dropdown | Yes | Select: low, medium, high, critical. Consider data sensitivity, volume, individual impact, processing location, supplier maturity, service criticality and sub-processing complexity. |
| Residual Risks | Long Text | Conditional | Required where risks remain after review. Describe residual risks and proposed treatment. |
| Risk Treatment Decision | Dropdown | Conditional | Select: mitigate before signature, accept, transfer, avoid, escalate, monitor. |
| Risk Acceptance Owner | Name / Role | Conditional | Required if residual risk is accepted. Must be an authorised risk owner with sufficient accountability. |
| Conditions of Approval | Long Text | No | Record any conditions that must be met before go-live, within a specified timeframe, or before renewal. |
| Go-Live Approval Granted | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether the processor may begin processing personal data. Do not mark “Yes” until required approvals are complete. |
| Linked Privacy Impact Assessment | Link / ID | Conditional | Provide the related privacy impact assessment or screening reference if required by internal policy. |
| Linked Vendor Risk Assessment | Link / ID | Conditional | Provide the vendor risk assessment reference where applicable. |
| Linked Security Assessment | Link / ID | Conditional | Provide the security assessment or technical review reference where applicable. |
| Linked Contract Repository Record | Link / ID | Yes | Provide the record location where the executed contract and data processing agreement will be stored. |
| Attachments Provided | Checklist | Yes | Confirm attachment of relevant materials, including contract, DPA, security schedule, sub-processor list, transfer terms, assurance reports, assessment outputs and approval evidence. |
| Review Completion Date | Date | Yes | Enter the date all required reviews were completed. |
| Next Review Date | Date | Yes | Set the next review date based on risk, contract renewal, supplier review cycle or material change trigger. |
| Change Trigger Notes | Long Text | No | Record known upcoming changes that require re-review, such as new region, new module, new data category, new sub-processor, migration or contract renewal. |
| Final Determination | Dropdown | Yes | Select: approved, approved with conditions, rejected, deferred, not applicable, replacement terms required. |
| Final Determination Notes | Long Text | Yes | Summarise the basis for the decision, key obligations confirmed, unresolved issues and required follow-up actions. |

Example sub-processor schedule to complete or attach where applicable:

| Sub-Processor Name | Service Provided | Personal Data Processed | Processing Location | Approval Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Sub-Processor Name] | [Hosting / Support / Analytics / Communications] | [Data Categories] | [Country / Region] | [Approved / Pending / Rejected] | [Notes] |

Example processing location schedule to complete or attach where applicable:

| Location | Activity | Data Stored | Data Accessed | Transfer Mechanism / Safeguard | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| [Country / Region] | [Hosting / Support / Backup / Administration] | [Yes / No] | [Yes / No] | [Approved safeguard or internal approval reference] | [Notes] |

Example issue and remediation tracker to complete where gaps are identified:

| Issue ID | Requirement / Topic | Gap Identified | Risk Rating | Required Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DPA-001] | [Sub-processors / Security / Transfer / Deletion] | [Description of gap] | [Low / Medium / High / Critical] | [Action required] | [Owner] | [Date] | [Open / In Progress / Closed] |

## Approval / Routing

The completed form must be routed according to the risk and complexity of the processing arrangement. Approval may be completed through the organisation’s contract lifecycle management, procurement, vendor risk management, privacy management or ticketing system, provided the required approvals are recorded and retained.

| Review / Approval Step | Required When | Responsible Role | Approval Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Business Owner Review | All processor engagements | Business Owner | Confirmation of business purpose, processing description, data categories, service need and operational accuracy. |
| Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer Review | All processor engagements involving personal data | Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer | Confirmation that required data protection terms are present, adequate and aligned to the processing risk. |
| Legal Review | New contracts, supplier paper, redlines, deviations, high-risk processing, international transfers or non-standard terms | Legal Counsel | Approval of contract wording, negotiation position, deviations and execution readiness. |
| Procurement Review | New suppliers, renewals, purchase orders, sourcing events or supplier onboarding | Procurement | Confirmation that contract documents and supplier records are complete before onboarding or renewal. |
| Information Security Review | Medium, high or critical risk processing; sensitive data; system integration; privileged access; hosting; remote administration; or security concerns | Information Security | Security assessment outcome, required controls, exceptions and conditions. |
| Vendor Risk Management Review | Where required by supplier risk process | Vendor Risk Management | Vendor risk rating, due diligence outcome and monitoring requirements. |
| Transfer Review | Where personal data is transferred, stored or accessed internationally | Privacy Office / Legal | Confirmation that the transfer mechanism and safeguards are acceptable. |
| Risk Acceptance | Where residual risks remain after review | Authorised Risk Owner | Formal risk acceptance with rationale, expiry date and treatment plan. |
| Final Approval to Process | Before personal data is provided, accessed, migrated or made available | Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer and Business Owner | Final determination recorded as approved or approved with conditions. |

Approval record:

| Approver | Role | Decision | Conditions / Comments | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Approver Name] | Business Owner | [Approved / Rejected / Conditional] | [Comments] | [Date] |
| [Approver Name] | Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer | [Approved / Rejected / Conditional] | [Comments] | [Date] |
| [Approver Name] | Legal | [Approved / Rejected / Conditional / Not Required] | [Comments] | [Date] |
| [Approver Name] | Information Security | [Approved / Rejected / Conditional / Not Required] | [Comments] | [Date] |
| [Approver Name] | Vendor Risk Management | [Approved / Rejected / Conditional / Not Required] | [Comments] | [Date] |
| [Approver Name] | Authorised Risk Owner | [Accepted / Not Accepted / Not Required] | [Comments] | [Date] |

Minimum approval requirements:

- The Business Owner must approve all completed forms.
- The Privacy Office or Data Protection Officer must approve all processor arrangements before processing begins.
- Legal must approve any non-standard or supplier-provided data processing terms before signature.
- Information Security must approve processing involving elevated security risk before access is provisioned.
- Residual high or critical risks must be accepted only by an authorised risk owner and must include a defined review date.
- Conditional approvals must include named actions, accountable owners and due dates.
- Rejected arrangements must not proceed unless revised and resubmitted for approval.

## Records & Retention

The completed form and supporting documents are compliance records and must be retained in the approved repository.

Required records include:

- Completed Data Processing Agreement review form.
- Executed contract, order form, statement of work and data processing agreement or equivalent terms.
- Version of the data processing terms reviewed and approved.
- Security schedule or description of technical and organisational measures.
- Sub-processor list and approval or objection records.
- International transfer terms, safeguards and related review evidence, where applicable.
- Privacy, legal, security, procurement and vendor risk approvals.
- Risk assessments, risk acceptance records and remediation evidence.
- Breach notification terms and incident communication contacts.
- Deletion, return or termination evidence where services end.
- Material change reviews, renewal reviews and re-approvals.

Retention requirements:

| Record Type | Repository | Minimum Retention | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Completed DPA review form | [Contract / Privacy / Vendor Repository] | Duration of contract plus [retention period] | Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer | Retain final approved version and any material updates. |
| Executed DPA and governing contract | [Contract Repository] | Duration of contract plus [retention period] | Legal / Procurement | Retain signed or otherwise legally accepted version. |
| Supplier security and assurance evidence | [Vendor Risk Repository] | Duration of contract plus [retention period] | Information Security / Vendor Risk Management | Retain evidence used to support approval and monitoring. |
| Sub-processor approvals and notices | [Privacy / Vendor Repository] | Duration of contract plus [retention period] | Privacy Office / Business Owner | Retain initial list and subsequent change notices. |
| International transfer review records | [Privacy / Legal Repository] | Duration of contract plus [retention period] | Privacy Office / Legal | Retain transfer terms, assessments and safeguard evidence. |
| Risk acceptance records | [Risk Register / GRC System] | Until risk closure plus [retention period] | Risk Owner | Must include rationale, expiry date and treatment plan. |
| Deletion or return confirmation | [Contract / Privacy Repository] | [retention period] after service termination | Business Owner / Privacy Office | Retain certification or other evidence of completion. |

Record handling rules:

- Store records only in approved repositories with access restricted to personnel who require them for legal, privacy, security, procurement, audit or supplier management purposes.
- Do not store executed agreements or completed forms in personal drives, unmanaged email folders or unapproved collaboration spaces.
- Ensure records are searchable by processor name, contract reference, business owner, service name and review date.
- Preserve superseded versions where they evidence historical approvals, contractual positions or processing terms.
- Update the record whenever there is a material change to processing, including new data categories, new processing purposes, new sub-processors, new countries, new systems, new security risks or revised contract terms.
- Review active processor agreements at renewal and at intervals appropriate to the processing risk.
- Dispose of records only in accordance with the organisation’s approved retention schedule and legal hold requirements.

GDPR-024.title: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs)
GDPR-024.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DPO-FRM-SCC-001] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer | [Effective Date] | GDPR | Confidential |

## Purpose

This template is used to document, route, approve, execute, and retain Standard Contractual Clauses for international transfers of personal data from the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland to a country that does not benefit from an adequacy decision or equivalent recognised transfer mechanism.

The completed form supports the organisation in confirming that:

- The correct contractual arrangement is selected for the transfer relationship.
- The parties, roles, data categories, processing activities, and transfer locations are clearly documented.
- The transfer has been assessed for legal, technical, organisational, and security risks.
- Supplementary measures are identified where required.
- The Standard Contractual Clauses are executed without unauthorised modification.
- Ongoing monitoring, review, and recordkeeping obligations are assigned.

This template must be completed before any new restricted international transfer begins, before any material change to an existing international transfer, and during renewal or replacement of supplier, customer, affiliate, or intra-group agreements involving such transfers.

## Instructions

1. **Use this template before transfer commencement**
 - Complete this form before personal data is transferred internationally under Standard Contractual Clauses.
 - Do not begin the transfer until all mandatory fields are completed and required approvals are obtained.

2. **Confirm whether Standard Contractual Clauses are needed**
 - Use this template where personal data is exported from a protected jurisdiction to a recipient in a country that does not have a recognised adequacy status for the relevant transfer.
 - If another valid transfer mechanism applies, document that mechanism in the relevant field and obtain Data Protection Officer approval before proceeding.

3. **Select the correct transfer relationship**
 - Identify whether the transfer is:
 - Controller to controller.
 - Controller to processor.
 - Processor to processor.
 - Processor to controller.
 - If multiple relationships apply, complete separate entries or attach a transfer matrix.

4. **Do not alter mandatory Standard Contractual Clauses wording**
 - The official Standard Contractual Clauses text must not be changed except where the text expressly permits selection, completion, or addition of business details.
 - Any commercial terms, service levels, liability provisions, or operational provisions must be included outside the Standard Contractual Clauses and must not conflict with them.

5. **Complete all transfer details accurately**
 - Include all parties, affiliates, sub-processors, systems, countries, data categories, data subjects, processing purposes, transfer frequency, retention periods, and security measures.
 - Where details are maintained in an approved supplier management or privacy system, reference the exact system record and attach an export or evidence snapshot.

6. **Complete a transfer risk assessment**
 - Assess whether the recipient can comply with the Standard Contractual Clauses in practice.
 - Consider destination country laws, government access risks, sector-specific risks, technical controls, encryption, access management, data minimisation, onward transfers, and contractual enforceability.
 - Identify supplementary measures where the risk cannot be sufficiently mitigated by the clauses alone.

7. **Attach required evidence**
 - At minimum, attach:
 - Draft or final Standard Contractual Clauses.
 - Description of processing or data processing agreement.
 - Transfer risk assessment.
 - Security measures schedule.
 - Sub-processor list, where applicable.
 - Evidence of vendor due diligence, where applicable.
 - Approval records.
 - Executed agreement once signed.

8. **Route for approval**
 - The Data Protection Officer, Legal, Information Security, Procurement or Vendor Management, and the relevant Business Owner must review and approve as applicable.
 - Higher-risk transfers must be escalated to senior management before signature.

9. **Retain executed documents**
 - Store the signed Standard Contractual Clauses and supporting evidence in the approved contract repository or privacy governance system.
 - Maintain a record of periodic reviews and any changes to parties, purposes, locations, systems, sub-processors, or safeguards.

10. **Review and refresh**
 - Review each transfer at least annually, or sooner if there is a material change, security incident, regulatory development, new sub-processor, country risk change, or change in processing purpose.
 - Where the Standard Contractual Clauses are no longer adequate, suspend, modify, or replace the transfer mechanism as directed by Legal and the Data Protection Officer.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| SCC Record ID | Text | Yes | Enter the unique identifier for this SCC record, such as `[SCC-YYYY-###]`. |
| Request Date | Date | Yes | Enter the date the SCC assessment and approval request is initiated. |
| Requested By | Text | Yes | Enter the name, title, department, and contact details of the person requesting approval. |
| Business Owner | Text | Yes | Identify the accountable business owner responsible for the processing activity and ongoing transfer. |
| Legal Entity Exporting Personal Data | Text | Yes | Enter the full legal name, registered address, and country of the data exporter. Include all exporting affiliates if applicable. |
| Legal Entity Importing Personal Data | Text | Yes | Enter the full legal name, registered address, and country of the data importer. Include all importing affiliates if applicable. |
| Contracting Party Relationship | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Controller to Controller; Controller to Processor; Processor to Processor; Processor to Controller; Multiple Relationships. |
| Description of Business Arrangement | Long Text | Yes | Describe the contract, service, project, intra-group arrangement, or commercial relationship requiring the data transfer. |
| Master Agreement Reference | Text | Conditional | Enter the contract title, contract number, effective date, and repository link where the SCCs are attached to or incorporated into another agreement. Required where a master agreement exists. |
| SCC Execution Method | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Standalone SCC agreement; Addendum to master agreement; Data processing agreement attachment; Intra-group agreement; Other approved method. |
| Transfer Mechanism Status | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: New SCCs required; Existing SCCs under review; SCC renewal; SCC replacement; Alternative transfer mechanism documented. |
| Adequacy Check Completed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether the destination country has been checked for recognised adequacy status relevant to the transfer. |
| Adequacy Check Result | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Adequacy available; Adequacy not available; Partial adequacy only; Not applicable; Legal review required. |
| Reason SCCs Are Required | Long Text | Yes | Explain why SCCs are the appropriate transfer mechanism for this transfer. |
| Exporting Jurisdiction | Text | Yes | List the country or countries from which personal data will be exported. |
| Importing Jurisdiction | Text | Yes | List the country or countries where the importer will receive, access, host, support, or otherwise process the personal data. |
| Remote Access Locations | Long Text | Conditional | List any countries from which personnel, support teams, administrators, or subcontractors may remotely access the personal data. Required where remote access occurs. |
| Processing Purpose | Long Text | Yes | Describe the specific purpose of the processing, such as cloud hosting, payroll administration, customer support, analytics, HR management, fraud prevention, or professional services. |
| Processing Activities | Long Text | Yes | Describe the actions performed on the personal data, such as collection, storage, access, retrieval, transmission, analysis, deletion, support, backup, or archiving. |
| Data Subject Categories | Multi-select | Yes | Select and describe relevant categories, such as customers, prospects, employees, contractors, suppliers, website users, patients, students, minors, or other individuals. |
| Personal Data Categories | Long Text | Yes | List the types of personal data transferred, such as name, contact details, account identifiers, HR records, transaction data, device data, support tickets, or usage logs. |
| Sensitive or Special Category Data | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether the transfer includes more sensitive data, such as health data, biometric data, race or ethnicity, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, sexual orientation, or criminal offence data. |
| Sensitive Data Details | Long Text | Conditional | Required if sensitive or special category data is transferred. Describe the data types, necessity, safeguards, access restrictions, and lawful handling conditions. |
| Children’s Data Included | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether the transfer includes personal data relating to children or minors. |
| Children’s Data Safeguards | Long Text | Conditional | Required if children’s data is transferred. Describe additional protections, minimisation controls, access limits, and approval basis. |
| Data Volume | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Low; Medium; High; Very High. Include approximate number of records where known. |
| Transfer Frequency | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: One-time; Occasional; Monthly; Weekly; Daily; Continuous; On-demand. |
| Transfer Method | Multi-select | Yes | Select all that apply: API; Secure file transfer; Cloud platform access; Email; Remote support access; Replication; Backup; Manual upload; Other. |
| Systems or Platforms Used | Long Text | Yes | Identify the applications, infrastructure, databases, file stores, collaboration tools, support tools, or hosting platforms involved. |
| Data Hosting Location | Text | Yes | Identify the primary hosting region and backup or disaster recovery regions. |
| Retention Period | Text | Yes | State how long the importer will retain the personal data and the trigger for deletion or return. |
| Deletion or Return Method | Long Text | Yes | Describe how personal data will be returned, deleted, anonymised, or securely destroyed at the end of services or when no longer required. |
| Exporter Role | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Controller; Processor. |
| Importer Role | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Controller; Processor. |
| Importer Processing Instructions | Long Text | Conditional | Required where the importer acts as a processor or sub-processor. Describe the documented instructions governing the processing. |
| Onward Transfers Permitted | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether the importer may transfer personal data onward to another third party or location. |
| Onward Transfer Details | Long Text | Conditional | Required if onward transfers are permitted. List recipients, locations, purpose, transfer mechanism, and approval process. |
| Sub-processors Used | Yes/No | Conditional | Required where the importer acts as a processor or sub-processor. Indicate whether sub-processors are used. |
| Sub-processor List Attached | Yes/No | Conditional | Required if sub-processors are used. Attach the current sub-processor list, including legal names, locations, services, and data processed. |
| Sub-processor Approval Method | Dropdown | Conditional | Required if sub-processors are used. Select one: Specific prior approval; General approval with notice and objection right; Not approved; Other Legal-approved method. |
| Importer Contact for Data Protection Matters | Text | Yes | Provide the importer’s privacy, legal, or data protection contact details. |
| Exporter Contact for Data Protection Matters | Text | Yes | Provide the exporter’s privacy, legal, or data protection contact details. |
| Data Protection Officer Involved | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether the Data Protection Officer or privacy lead has reviewed or will review the transfer. |
| Data Processing Agreement Required | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether a separate data processing agreement is required in addition to the SCCs. |
| Data Processing Agreement Status | Dropdown | Conditional | Required if a data processing agreement is needed. Select one: Not started; Drafting; Under review; Approved; Executed; Not applicable. |
| SCC Text Source | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Approved internal template; External counsel template; Counterparty template reviewed by Legal; Other Legal-approved source. |
| SCC Text Modified | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether the official SCC wording has been modified. Any unauthorised modification must be rejected or escalated to Legal. |
| Permitted Selections Completed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm that only permitted selections, party details, appendices, schedules, and commercial attachments have been completed. |
| Conflicting Terms Check Completed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm Legal has checked that the master agreement, order form, data processing agreement, and SCCs do not contain conflicting terms. |
| Precedence Language Included | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm that the contract states the SCCs prevail where there is a conflict involving international transfer protections. |
| Transfer Risk Assessment Required | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether a transfer risk assessment is required. This will normally be required unless Legal and the Data Protection Officer approve an exception. |
| Transfer Risk Assessment Completed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether the transfer risk assessment has been completed and attached. |
| Destination Country Legal Environment Reviewed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm review of whether local laws or practices may affect the importer’s ability to comply with the SCCs. |
| Government Access Risk Rating | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Low; Medium; High; Critical; Legal review pending. Consider laws, sector, data type, recipient profile, and likelihood of access requests. |
| Importer Ability to Comply Confirmed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether the importer has represented that it can comply with the SCCs and notify the exporter if this changes. |
| Importer Transparency Report Reviewed | Yes/No/Not Applicable | Conditional | Review where available, especially for cloud, telecommunications, analytics, or large-scale service providers. |
| Law Enforcement Request Procedure Confirmed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm the importer has a procedure to assess, challenge where appropriate, and notify legally permissible government access requests. |
| Encryption in Transit | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether personal data is encrypted during transmission using approved protocols. |
| Encryption at Rest | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether personal data is encrypted while stored, backed up, or archived. |
| Key Management Responsibility | Dropdown | Conditional | Required where encryption applies. Select one: Exporter managed; Importer managed; Customer-controlled keys; Shared responsibility; Not applicable. |
| Access Controls | Long Text | Yes | Describe authentication, authorisation, least privilege, privileged access management, role reviews, and joiner-mover-leaver controls. |
| Multi-Factor Authentication | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether multi-factor authentication is enforced for administrative access and remote access to personal data. |
| Logging and Monitoring | Long Text | Yes | Describe audit logging, security monitoring, alerting, retention of logs, and review responsibilities. |
| Segregation Controls | Long Text | Conditional | Describe tenant segregation, environment segregation, network segmentation, or logical separation where relevant. |
| Data Minimisation Measures | Long Text | Yes | Describe how the transfer is limited to the minimum personal data necessary for the stated purpose. |
| Pseudonymisation or Anonymisation | Long Text | Conditional | Describe whether data is pseudonymised, tokenised, masked, aggregated, or anonymised before transfer, and who can re-identify it. |
| Backup and Recovery Controls | Long Text | Conditional | Describe backup locations, encryption, retention, restoration testing, and deletion from backups where relevant. |
| Security Certifications or Assurance Reports | Long Text | Conditional | List relevant independent assurance reports, certifications, penetration test summaries, or security attestations reviewed. |
| Incident Notification Commitment | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm contractual obligations require timely notification of personal data breaches or security incidents affecting transferred data. |
| Incident Notification Timeframe | Text | Yes | State the agreed timeframe and notification contact path. |
| Data Subject Rights Support | Long Text | Yes | Describe how the importer will assist with access, deletion, correction, objection, restriction, portability, or other individual rights requests. |
| Regulatory Cooperation Commitment | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm the importer agrees to support required cooperation with supervisory authorities where legally required. |
| Audit Rights Included | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm the exporter has appropriate rights to audit, request information, or obtain independent assurance regarding compliance. |
| Supplier Due Diligence Completed | Yes/No/Not Applicable | Yes | Confirm whether privacy, security, and vendor risk due diligence has been completed. |
| Supplier Risk Rating | Dropdown | Conditional | Required for third-party suppliers. Select one: Low; Medium; High; Critical; Pending. |
| Supplementary Measures Required | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether additional technical, contractual, or organisational measures are required to make the transfer acceptable. |
| Supplementary Measures Description | Long Text | Conditional | Required if supplementary measures are needed. Describe the measures, owner, implementation date, validation method, and residual risk. |
| Residual Transfer Risk Rating | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Low; Medium; High; Critical; Not approved. |
| Residual Risk Justification | Long Text | Yes | Explain why the residual risk is acceptable or why the transfer must be modified, suspended, or rejected. |
| Exceptions Requested | Yes/No | Yes | Indicate whether any exception to standard SCC process, security baseline, due diligence, or approval requirements is requested. |
| Exception Details | Long Text | Conditional | Required if an exception is requested. Describe the exception, reason, compensating controls, duration, and approver. |
| Data Protection Impact Assessment Link | Text | Conditional | Provide the reference or link if a data protection impact assessment exists or is required for the processing activity. |
| Records of Processing Link | Text | Yes | Provide the reference or link to the relevant record of processing activity or privacy inventory entry. |
| Privacy Notice Impact Reviewed | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether the relevant privacy notice or transparency language reflects the international transfer where required. |
| Customer or Client Notification Required | Yes/No | Conditional | Indicate whether customers, clients, or contractual counterparties must be notified or must approve the transfer. |
| Customer or Client Notification Status | Dropdown | Conditional | Required if notification or approval is required. Select one: Not started; In progress; Completed; Approval received; Not approved; Not applicable. |
| Insurance or Liability Review Required | Yes/No | Conditional | Indicate whether insurance, indemnity, or liability review is required due to transfer risk or contract value. |
| Legal Review Status | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Not submitted; Under review; Changes requested; Approved; Rejected; Escalated. |
| Information Security Review Status | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Not submitted; Under review; Remediation required; Approved; Rejected; Escalated. |
| Data Protection Officer Review Status | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Not submitted; Under review; Approved; Approved with conditions; Rejected; Escalated. |
| Procurement or Vendor Management Review Status | Dropdown | Conditional | Required for third-party suppliers. Select one: Not submitted; Under review; Approved; Rejected; Not applicable. |
| Business Owner Approval Status | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Pending; Approved; Approved with conditions; Rejected. |
| Conditions of Approval | Long Text | Conditional | Required if approval is conditional. List each condition, owner, due date, and evidence required for closure. |
| Signature Authority | Text | Yes | Identify the person authorised to sign the SCCs or related agreement on behalf of the organisation. |
| Counterparty Signatory | Text | Yes | Identify the counterparty signatory name, title, legal entity, and signing authority confirmation where known. |
| Execution Date | Date | Conditional | Enter the date the SCCs are fully executed. Required before the transfer goes live. |
| Go-Live Approval | Yes/No | Yes | Confirm whether the transfer may begin. Must be “Yes” only after all required reviews and signatures are complete. |
| Transfer Start Date | Date | Conditional | Enter the date the transfer is scheduled to begin or actually begins. |
| Next Review Date | Date | Yes | Set the next review date, normally no later than twelve months after approval or sooner for high-risk transfers. |
| Trigger Events for Early Review | Multi-select | Yes | Select all that apply: New country; New sub-processor; New data category; New processing purpose; Security incident; Regulatory development; Contract change; System change; Risk rating change; Other. |
| Attachments Included | Checklist | Yes | Attach all required evidence and list file names or repository links. |
| Repository Location | Text | Yes | Provide the approved storage location for the executed SCCs and supporting records. |
| Form Completed By | Text | Yes | Enter the name and role of the person completing this template. |
| Completion Date | Date | Yes | Enter the date this template is completed. |

### Transfer Relationship Selection Matrix

| Relationship | Use When | Required Supporting Documents | Key Review Focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Controller to Controller | Both parties independently determine purposes and means of processing for their respective activities. | SCCs, controller data sharing terms, transfer risk assessment, security measures schedule. | Transparency, lawful sharing, independent responsibilities, individual rights handling, onward transfer controls. |
| Controller to Processor | The importer processes personal data on documented instructions from the exporter. | SCCs, data processing agreement, processing instructions, sub-processor list, transfer risk assessment, security measures schedule. | Processor obligations, instruction controls, sub-processors, breach notification, deletion or return, audit rights. |
| Processor to Processor | The exporter acts as processor and engages the importer as sub-processor for a controller. | SCCs, data processing agreement chain, controller authorisation, sub-processor terms, transfer risk assessment. | Controller approval, flow-down obligations, onward transfers, incident escalation, audit support. |
| Processor to Controller | The exporter processes data for a controller and transfers data to an importing controller. | SCCs, role analysis, controller instructions where applicable, transfer risk assessment, commercial agreement. | Role clarity, lawful receipt by importer, purpose limitation, transparency, responsibility for individual rights. |
| Multiple Relationships | The arrangement includes more than one transfer role or several data flows. | Transfer matrix, SCCs for each applicable relationship, relevant data processing or sharing terms. | Accurate mapping, no gaps in transfer coverage, clear priority of terms, complete party details. |

### Required Attachment Checklist

| Attachment | Required | Evidence Standard | Attached / Link |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Draft or final SCCs | Yes | Current approved SCC text with all permitted selections and schedules completed. | [Repository Link] |
| Executed SCCs | Yes, before go-live | Fully signed agreement or legally valid execution evidence. | [Repository Link] |
| Master agreement or order form | Conditional | Current agreement governing the business relationship. | [Repository Link] |
| Data processing agreement | Conditional | Required where a processor or sub-processor relationship exists. | [Repository Link] |
| Transfer risk assessment | Yes | Completed assessment covering country, recipient, data, access risk, and safeguards. | [Repository Link] |
| Security measures schedule | Yes | Specific technical and organisational measures applicable to the transferred data. | [Repository Link] |
| Sub-processor list | Conditional | Current list with services, locations, and data processed. | [Repository Link] |
| Vendor due diligence evidence | Conditional | Privacy, security, financial, and operational due diligence as applicable. | [Repository Link] |
| Assurance reports or certifications | Conditional | Current independent reports or certifications relevant to the service. | [Repository Link] |
| Data protection impact assessment | Conditional | Required where the processing presents elevated privacy risk. | [Repository Link] |
| Records of processing entry | Yes | Privacy inventory or processing record updated to reflect transfer details. | [Repository Link] |
| Privacy notice review evidence | Conditional | Confirmation that required transparency information is accurate. | [Repository Link] |
| Customer or client approval | Conditional | Written approval or notice evidence where contractually required. | [Repository Link] |
| Approval records | Yes | Recorded approvals from required reviewers and approvers. | [Repository Link] |
| Supplementary measures evidence | Conditional | Proof of implementation and validation for required additional controls. | [Repository Link] |

### Supplementary Measures Register

| Measure ID | Measure Type | Description | Owner | Due Date | Validation Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [SM-001] | Technical | Apply customer-controlled encryption keys before transfer. | [Owner] | [Date] | Key management configuration screenshot or control attestation. | Open |
| [SM-002] | Organisational | Restrict importer support access to named personnel with approved access requests. | [Owner] | [Date] | Access control export and approval workflow evidence. | Open |
| [SM-003] | Contractual | Add commitment to notify the exporter of legally permissible government access requests. | [Owner] | [Date] | Signed contractual wording. | Open |

### Approval Decision Summary

| Review Area | Reviewer | Decision | Conditions / Notes | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business Ownership | [Business Owner] | Pending / Approved / Rejected | [Notes] | [Date] |
| Data Protection | [DPO / Privacy Lead] | Pending / Approved / Approved with Conditions / Rejected | [Notes] | [Date] |
| Legal | [Legal Reviewer] | Pending / Approved / Approved with Conditions / Rejected | [Notes] | [Date] |
| Information Security | [Security Reviewer] | Pending / Approved / Approved with Conditions / Rejected | [Notes] | [Date] |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | [Reviewer] | Pending / Approved / Rejected / Not Applicable | [Notes] | [Date] |
| Senior Management Escalation | [Approver] | Pending / Approved / Rejected / Not Applicable | [Notes] | [Date] |
| Signature Authority | [Authorised Signatory] | Pending / Approved to Sign / Not Approved | [Notes] | [Date] |

## Approval / Routing

The completed SCC form must be routed as follows.

| Step | Role / Function | Responsibility | Required For | Outcome |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Requester | Completes the initial form, gathers business details, and attaches available evidence. | All SCC requests. | Complete submission ready for review. |
| 2 | Business Owner | Confirms the business need, processing purpose, data scope, transfer necessity, and operational ownership. | All SCC requests. | Business approval or rejection. |
| 3 | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | Reviews role analysis, data categories, transparency, individual rights support, transfer risk assessment, supplementary measures, and ongoing review obligations. | All SCC requests. | Privacy approval, conditional approval, escalation, or rejection. |
| 4 | Legal | Confirms correct SCC selection, contract compatibility, execution approach, party details, precedence language, liability implications, and legal risk. | All SCC requests. | Legal approval to proceed to signature or required amendments. |
| 5 | Information Security | Reviews technical and organisational safeguards, encryption, access controls, logging, incident response, assurance evidence, and supplementary technical measures. | All transfers involving systems, suppliers, platforms, remote access, or sensitive data. | Security approval, remediation requirements, or rejection. |
| 6 | Procurement / Vendor Management | Confirms supplier due diligence, vendor risk rating, contract repository controls, and supplier lifecycle requirements. | Third-party supplier transfers. | Vendor approval or procurement hold. |
| 7 | Senior Management | Reviews elevated residual risk, high-volume or sensitive transfers, strategic suppliers, unresolved exceptions, or transfers rated high or critical. | High-risk transfers or exceptions. | Risk acceptance, rejection, or required remediation. |
| 8 | Authorised Signatory | Signs the SCCs or related contract only after all required approvals are complete. | All SCCs requiring execution. | Executed SCCs. |
| 9 | Contract / Privacy Operations | Stores executed documents, updates privacy records, records review date, and confirms transfer go-live status. | All approved SCCs. | Final record created and transfer approved for commencement. |

Approval rules:

- The transfer must not commence until the SCCs are fully executed and all required approvals are recorded.
- Conditional approval is not approval to commence unless the condition expressly permits go-live and the residual risk is accepted by the appropriate authority.
- Any modification to official SCC wording must be reviewed by Legal and either rejected or formally approved where legally permissible.
- Any high or critical residual risk must be escalated to senior management before signature or go-live.
- If the importer cannot confirm its ability to comply with the SCCs, the transfer must not proceed unless Legal and the Data Protection Officer approve an alternative lawful approach.
- If supplementary measures are required, the owner must provide implementation evidence before go-live unless a documented risk acceptance allows a defined temporary exception.
- If a material change occurs after approval, the SCC record must be reopened and reviewed before the changed transfer continues.

## Records & Retention

The organisation must retain a complete SCC record for each approved, rejected, expired, or suspended transfer.

| Record | Retention Requirement | Storage Location | Responsible Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Completed SCC form | Retain for the life of the transfer and for [Retention Period] after termination, expiry, or replacement. | [Privacy Governance System / Contract Repository] | Data Protection Officer |
| Executed SCCs | Retain for the life of the agreement and for [Retention Period] after agreement termination. | [Contract Repository] | Legal |
| Master agreement, data processing agreement, and related contract documents | Retain in accordance with contract retention requirements and no less than the SCC retention period. | [Contract Repository] | Legal / Procurement |
| Transfer risk assessment | Retain for the life of the transfer and for [Retention Period] after termination or replacement. | [Privacy Governance System] | Data Protection Officer |
| Security measures evidence | Retain while the transfer is active and for [Retention Period] after termination or replacement. | [GRC System / Security Repository] | Information Security |
| Supplementary measures evidence | Retain while measures remain relied upon and for [Retention Period] after the transfer ends. | [GRC System / Privacy Governance System] | Control Owner |
| Vendor due diligence records | Retain according to supplier risk management retention requirements and no less than the SCC retention period. | [Vendor Management System] | Procurement / Vendor Management |
| Approval records | Retain with the SCC record for the life of the transfer and for [Retention Period] after termination or replacement. | [Workflow System / Privacy Governance System] | Data Protection Officer |
| Review and monitoring records | Retain for [Retention Period] from the date of each review. | [Privacy Governance System] | Data Protection Officer |
| Rejected or withdrawn SCC requests | Retain for [Retention Period] from rejection or withdrawal date. | [Privacy Governance System] | Data Protection Officer |

Retention and recordkeeping requirements:

- SCC records must be stored in an approved repository with access limited to personnel who require access for legal, privacy, security, procurement, audit, or business purposes.
- Executed SCCs must be version-controlled and linked to the relevant supplier, customer, affiliate, project, processing activity, or contract record.
- The privacy inventory or records of processing must be updated to reflect the transfer, parties, countries, purposes, data categories, safeguards, and review date.
- Superseded SCCs must not be deleted where they evidence the lawful basis for historical transfers.
- If a transfer is terminated, the record must include confirmation of data return, deletion, anonymisation, or secure destruction where required.
- If a transfer is suspended due to legal, contractual, security, or privacy concerns, the suspension decision, scope, date, rationale, and remediation plan must be retained.
- Records must be made available to internal audit, external auditors, regulators, or supervisory authorities where legally required and approved through the appropriate disclosure process.
- Retention periods must be extended where a legal hold, regulatory inquiry, litigation, investigation, audit, or unresolved dispute applies.

GDPR-025.title: Joint Controller Arrangement
GDPR-025.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [Document ID] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer | [Effective Date] | GDPR | Internal - Confidential |

## Purpose

This template is used to document an arrangement between two or more organisations that jointly determine the purposes and essential means of processing personal data.

The completed arrangement should clearly describe:

- Which organisations are acting as joint controllers.
- The shared purpose for processing personal data.
- The key processing decisions made jointly.
- Each party’s responsibilities for transparency, lawful basis, individual rights, security, incident handling, retention, records, and cooperation.
- How individuals can understand the essence of the arrangement.
- How the parties will evidence compliance with data protection obligations.

This template is intended for use where the parties together decide why personal data is processed and how significant processing activities are carried out. It is not intended for standard controller-to-processor arrangements, independent controller disclosures, or data-sharing arrangements where each party determines its own separate purposes independently.

## Instructions

1. **Complete before processing begins**
 - Complete this form before launching any joint processing activity, campaign, platform, service, research initiative, shared database, or partnership involving personal data.
 - If the joint processing is already in place, complete this template as part of remediation and document the reason for retrospective completion.

2. **Confirm that joint controllership applies**
 - Use this template only where two or more parties jointly determine the purposes and essential means of processing.
 - Indicators of joint controllership include shared decisions about why data is collected, what categories of data are required, who the target individuals are, retention periods, transparency wording, access models, communication channels, or use of a shared system.
 - Where one party only processes personal data on documented instructions from another party, a processor agreement should be used instead.

3. **Involve the right stakeholders**
 - The business owner must complete the operational sections.
 - The Data Protection Officer or privacy lead must review the privacy, rights, transparency, and risk sections.
 - Information security must review security, access, hosting, and incident handling.
 - Legal must review liability, public-facing wording, governance, and termination provisions.
 - Procurement or vendor management should be involved where an external partner, supplier, platform provider, research body, charity, public authority, or commercial partner is involved.

4. **Be specific**
 - Avoid vague statements such as “the parties will comply with data protection law.”
 - Identify the responsible party for each obligation, the operational process, the contact point, and the timeframe.
 - Where responsibilities are shared, explain how they are shared and who coordinates each activity.

5. **Attach supporting documents**
