## Approval / Routing

The following routing must be completed before submission where time permits. Where the notification deadline is at risk, the Data Protection Officer or authorised incident executive may approve urgent submission and complete remaining reviews retrospectively.

| Role / Function | Responsibility | Required Before Submission | Name / Role | Approval / Review Timestamp | Comments |
|---|---|:---:|---|---|---|
| Incident Response Lead | Confirms incident facts, containment status, and technical evidence. | Yes | [Name / role] | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM] | [Comments] |
| Data Protection Officer | Assesses notification requirement, risk to individuals, content completeness, and regulatory communication approach. | Yes | [Name / role] | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM] | [Comments] |
| Legal Counsel | Reviews legal accuracy, privilege considerations, cross-border implications, and wording. | Recommended | [Name / role] | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM] | [Comments] |
| Business Owner | Confirms affected service, customer context, operational impact, and remediation ownership. | Recommended | [Name / role] | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM] | [Comments] |
| Information Security Lead | Confirms security controls, forensic position, threat status, and remediation actions. | Yes, where security-related | [Name / role] | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM] | [Comments] |
| Communications Lead | Reviews external messaging alignment and individual notification considerations. | Conditional | [Name / role] | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM] | [Comments] |
| Customer / Client Relationship Lead | Confirms contractual communications and customer handling where applicable. | Conditional | [Name / role] | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM] | [Comments] |
| Executive Sponsor | Approves submission for significant, high-risk, or public breaches. | Conditional | [Name / role] | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM] | [Comments] |
| Submission Owner | Submits notification through approved channel and records evidence. | Yes | [Name / role] | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM] | [Comments] |

**Urgent Submission Record**

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Was urgent submission required to avoid delay? | [Yes / No] |
| Reason urgent submission was required | [Explain deadline, information availability, or approval constraint] |
| Minimum reviews completed before submission | [List completed reviews] |
| Approver for urgent submission | [Name / role] |
| Approval date and time | [DD MMM YYYY HH:MM Time Zone] |
| Retrospective reviews required | [List roles and due dates] |

**Routing Rules**

- The Data Protection Officer must be informed of all suspected or confirmed personal data breaches without delay.
- Notifications to the Supervisory Authority must be submitted only by authorised personnel.
- Legal review should be obtained for significant breaches, cross-border incidents, law enforcement involvement, sensitive data, vulnerable individuals, high-volume breaches, likely public attention, or potential litigation.
- Executive approval should be obtained for breaches assessed as high or critical risk, unless waiting would delay timely notification.
- If the organisation is acting as a processor, the controller must be informed without delay according to contractual and operational escalation requirements. The organisation must not notify the Supervisory Authority on behalf of a controller unless authorised to do so.
- If multiple jurisdictions may be affected, the Data Protection Officer and Legal Counsel must determine the appropriate authority engagement strategy.
- All follow-up submissions must reference the original submission and clearly identify new, corrected, or final information.

## Records & Retention

Completed breach notification records must be retained as confidential compliance evidence and handled on a need-to-know basis.

| Record | Retention Requirement | Storage Location | Access Restrictions | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completed breach notification form | Retain for [X years] after breach closure, or longer if required for legal, regulatory, contractual, or litigation purposes. | [GRC system / secure repository] | DPO, Legal, Security, authorised incident stakeholders | Data Protection Officer |
| Submitted notification copy | Retain with submission timestamp and exact content submitted. | [GRC system / secure repository] | DPO, Legal, authorised compliance staff | Data Protection Officer |
| Supervisory Authority acknowledgement and correspondence | Retain for [X years] after final authority correspondence or case closure. | [GRC system / secure repository] | DPO, Legal, authorised compliance staff | Data Protection Officer |
| Incident investigation records | Retain according to incident management and legal hold requirements. | [Incident management system] | Security, Legal, DPO, authorised responders | Information Security Lead |
| Risk assessment and notification decision rationale | Retain whether or not notification was ultimately submitted. | [GRC system / secure repository] | DPO, Legal, Compliance | Data Protection Officer |
| Approval and routing evidence | Retain with the notification case file. | [GRC system / secure repository] | DPO, Legal, Compliance | Data Protection Officer |
| Individual notification assessment and communications | Retain with breach case file where individuals are notified or notification is considered. | [GRC system / secure repository] | DPO, Legal, Communications, authorised staff | Data Protection Officer |
| Corrective action plan and closure evidence | Retain until corrective actions are verified and for [X years] after closure. | [Risk / issue tracking system] | Risk owners, Security, DPO, Audit | Risk Owner |
| Post-incident review and lessons learned | Retain according to incident and audit record retention requirements. | [Incident management / GRC system] | Security, DPO, Legal, Audit | Information Security Lead |

Records must include enough information to demonstrate:

- When the organisation became aware of the breach.
- How the notification decision was reached.
- Whether notification was submitted within the required timeframe.
- What information was provided to the Supervisory Authority.
- What actions were taken to contain, remediate, and reduce harm.
- Whether follow-up updates were provided when facts changed or became available.
- Who reviewed, approved, and submitted the notification.

If a legal hold is issued, normal destruction schedules must be suspended for all related records until Legal Counsel confirms that the hold has been released.

GDPR-029.title: Breach Notification to Data Subject (Art. 34)
GDPR-029.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [GDPR-FRM-BNDS-001] |
| Version | |
| Owner | [Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead] |
| Effective Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Framework | GDPR |
| Classification | Confidential |

## Purpose

This template is used to notify an affected individual when a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms. It provides a consistent structure for clear, timely and understandable communication, enabling the individual to understand what happened, what data may be affected, the likely consequences, actions already taken by the organisation, and steps the individual can take to protect themselves.

This template should be used only after the incident response team, Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead, and relevant business stakeholders have assessed the breach and determined that direct notification to affected individuals is required or appropriate.

## Instructions

1. **Use clear and plain language**
 - Write for the affected individual, not for internal teams or regulators.
 - Avoid legal, technical or security jargon unless it is explained in simple terms.
 - Be specific enough to help the individual take protective action.

2. **Notify without undue delay**
 - Once a high risk to individuals has been confirmed, prepare and send the notification promptly.
 - Do not wait for the full investigation to be complete if enough facts are known to provide meaningful guidance.
 - If some details remain under investigation, state this clearly and explain that updates will be provided if necessary.

3. **Use the correct communication channel**
 - Send the notification directly to the affected individual where contact details are available.
 - Acceptable channels may include email, letter, secure portal message, SMS directing the individual to a secure notice, or another agreed communication method.
 - If direct contact is not practicable, seek approval for an alternative public communication method that is likely to reach affected individuals.

4. **Do not include unnecessary personal data**
 - Do not repeat sensitive data values in the notice unless necessary.
 - Avoid listing full identification numbers, financial account numbers, health details, passwords or other sensitive information.
 - Use partial identifiers where needed, such as “the last four digits of your account number”.

5. **Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders**
 - The notice must be reviewed by the Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead before issue.
 - Legal, Communications, Customer Support, Information Security and relevant business owners should review as required.
 - Where law enforcement has requested a delay to avoid prejudice to an investigation, document the request and obtain approval before delaying notification.

6. **Maintain consistency**
 - Ensure the notice aligns with:
 - The internal breach record.
 - Notifications made to the supervisory authority, if applicable.
 - Customer support scripts and FAQs.
 - Public statements or media responses.
 - Processor or third-party incident information, where relevant.

7. **Provide practical protective steps**
 - Include actions the individual can take, tailored to the nature of the breach.
 - Examples may include password resets, fraud monitoring, contacting their bank, watching for phishing attempts, reviewing account activity, or using identity protection services.

8. **Document all decisions**
 - Retain evidence of the risk assessment, approval, final message, delivery method, send date, recipient list, and any returned or failed notices.
 - Record reasons if notification is delayed, not sent, sent in phases, or made by public announcement.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Breach reference number | Text | Yes | Enter the unique internal breach or incident identifier, such as [INC-YYYY-NNN]. |
| Notice version | Text | Yes | Enter the version of the notification, for example “Version 1.0” or “Updated notice”. |
| Date notice prepared | Date | Yes | Enter the date this notification text was prepared. |
| Date notice approved | Date | Yes | Enter the date final approval was obtained before sending. |
| Date notice sent | Date | Yes | Enter the actual date the notice was sent or published. |
| Prepared by | Name / role | Yes | Identify the person or team drafting the notice. |
| Approved by | Name / role | Yes | Identify the final approver, normally the Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead or authorised delegate. |
| Affected individual name | Text | Conditional | Use where the notice is sent directly and personalisation is appropriate. Do not include if using a public notice. |
| Contact details used | Text | Yes | Record the delivery address, email domain, secure portal, SMS process or public notice location. Do not store more personal data than necessary. |
| Notification method | Dropdown | Yes | Select: Email, postal letter, secure portal, telephone, SMS, public notice, in-person, other. |
| Reason for notification | Text | Yes | Summarise why the breach is considered likely to create a high risk for the individual. Avoid internal scoring jargon. |
| Date breach occurred | Date / date range | Conditional | Enter the known or estimated date or period of the breach. If unknown, state “under investigation”. |
| Date breach discovered | Date | Yes | Enter when the organisation first became aware of the breach. |
| Date breach contained | Date / text | Conditional | Enter when containment occurred. If still ongoing, state what interim measures are in place. |
| Description of what happened | Long text | Yes | Provide a concise factual explanation of the breach. Include the nature of the event, affected service, and current status. |
| Categories of personal data affected | Checklist / text | Yes | List relevant categories such as contact details, account information, identity documents, financial information, health information, credentials, employment data, usage data or special category data. |
| Sensitive data involved | Yes / No / Under investigation | Yes | State whether particularly sensitive information is involved. If yes, describe the category without unnecessarily repeating the data itself. |
| Number of individuals affected | Number / estimate | Conditional | Include where relevant and appropriate. For individual notices, this may be recorded internally rather than included in the message. |
| How the breach may affect the individual | Long text | Yes | Explain likely consequences in plain language, such as fraud risk, identity misuse, phishing, financial loss, confidentiality impact, distress or account compromise. |
| Actions already taken by the organisation | Long text | Yes | Describe containment and remediation steps, such as securing accounts, disabling access, resetting credentials, notifying processors, improving monitoring, recovering data, or engaging forensic support. |
| Actions the individual should take | Long text | Yes | Provide practical, tailored steps. Include urgency, links to official support pages, and instructions for contacting banks or service providers if relevant. |
| Support offered by the organisation | Long text | Conditional | Describe helpdesk support, credit monitoring, identity protection, account review, replacement documents, counselling support or other assistance, where applicable. |
| Contact point for questions | Text | Yes | Provide the dedicated privacy, support or incident contact channel, including email, phone, postal address or secure portal. |
| Data Protection Officer / privacy contact | Text | Yes | Provide the relevant privacy contact details for follow-up questions. |
| Supervisory authority information | Text | Conditional | Include information about the individual’s right to contact the relevant supervisory authority where appropriate. Use plain language and local contact details if known. |
| Law enforcement delay considered | Yes / No | Yes | Record internally whether any law enforcement request affected timing or content. Do not include this field in the individual-facing notice unless approved. |
| Public communications required | Yes / No | Yes | Record whether a website notice, press statement, customer FAQ or other broad communication is required. |
| Attachments or links | Text | Conditional | Include approved FAQs, support pages, password reset pages or identity protection enrolment links. Ensure links use official domains only. |
| Translation required | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the notice must be translated for affected individuals. |
| Accessibility format required | Yes / No | Yes | State whether alternative formats are needed, such as large print, screen-reader compatible documents or telephone support. |
| Final notification text | Long text | Yes | Insert the approved individual-facing notice using the template below. |
| Delivery evidence location | Text | Yes | Record where evidence of sending, delivery logs, returned mail, publication screenshots or call logs is stored. |
| Follow-up required | Yes / No | Yes | State whether additional updates are expected after further investigation. |
| Follow-up owner | Name / role | Conditional | Assign a person responsible for updates, support tracking and closure communications. |
| Closure date | Date | Conditional | Enter when notification activities and follow-up actions are complete. |

### Individual-Facing Notification Template

| Section | Notification Text |
|---|---|
| Subject / heading | Important notice about your personal data |
| Greeting | Dear [Name], |
| Opening statement | We are writing to let you know about a personal data breach that may affect you. We take this matter seriously and want to explain what happened, what information may be involved, what we are doing, and the steps you can take to protect yourself. |
| What happened | On or around [date/date range], [brief description of incident in plain language]. We became aware of this on [date] and immediately began investigating and taking steps to secure our systems and information. |
| Information involved | Based on our investigation so far, the personal data that may have been affected includes: [categories of personal data]. We do not believe the following information was affected: [categories, if helpful and confirmed]. |
| How this may affect you | The possible risks to you may include [plain-language description of likely consequences, such as phishing attempts, identity misuse, unauthorised account access, financial fraud, confidentiality concerns or distress]. We are not aware of any misuse of your information at this time / We are aware of [brief description of misuse, if confirmed]. |
| What we have done | We have taken steps to respond to the breach, including [containment actions], [security actions], [investigation actions], and [support actions]. We are continuing to monitor the situation and will provide further updates if needed. |
| What you should do | We recommend that you: 1. [Action step]. 2. [Action step]. 3. [Action step]. 4. Be alert to unexpected emails, calls or messages asking for personal information or payment. 5. Contact us using the details below if you notice anything suspicious relating to your account or information. |
| Support available | To support you, we are offering [support services, if applicable]. You can access this support by [instructions]. |
| How to contact us | If you have questions or need assistance, please contact [team/contact point] at [email address], [telephone number] or [postal address]. Our reference for this matter is [breach reference number]. |
| Privacy contact | You may also contact our privacy team or Data Protection Officer at [privacy contact details]. |
| Supervisory authority | If you are not satisfied with our response, you may contact your local data protection supervisory authority. We encourage you to contact us first so we can try to address your concerns. |
| Closing | We regret that this happened and apologise for any concern or inconvenience it may cause. We are committed to protecting your personal data and have taken steps to reduce the risk of this happening again. |
| Sign-off | Yours sincerely, [Name / Role] on behalf of [Organisation] |

### Notification Timing and Delivery Log

| Activity | Owner | Target Date / Time | Actual Date / Time | Status | Evidence Location | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| High-risk assessment completed | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Notification text drafted | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Legal review completed | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Privacy review completed | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Communications review completed | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Customer support briefing completed | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Recipient list validated | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Notification approved | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Notifications sent | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Failed delivery review completed | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Follow-up communications issued, if required | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |
| Notification activity closed | [Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Not started / In progress / Complete] | [Location] | [Notes] |

## Approval / Routing

The notification must be reviewed and approved before issue according to the routing below. Emergency approvals may be given verbally or by secure message where timing is critical, but must be documented afterwards.

| Role / Function | Responsibility | Approval Required | Name / Role | Date / Time | Decision / Comments |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Incident Manager | Confirms incident facts, containment status and operational accuracy. | Yes | [Name / Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Approved / Changes required / Not applicable] |
| Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | Confirms whether notification is required, reviews content for completeness and individual clarity, and approves final privacy position. | Yes | [Name / Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Approved / Changes required / Not applicable] |
| Legal Counsel | Reviews legal risk, privilege considerations, liability-sensitive wording and any law enforcement constraints. | Conditional | [Name / Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Approved / Changes required / Not applicable] |
| Information Security | Confirms technical description, containment measures, residual risk and recommended individual actions. | Yes | [Name / Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Approved / Changes required / Not applicable] |
| Business Owner | Confirms customer, employee, supplier or service-specific accuracy and operational commitments. | Yes | [Name / Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Approved / Changes required / Not applicable] |
| Communications / PR | Reviews tone, readability, media alignment and public communications requirements. | Conditional | [Name / Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Approved / Changes required / Not applicable] |
| Customer Support / HR Support | Confirms scripts, FAQs, escalation routes and support readiness. | Conditional | [Name / Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Approved / Changes required / Not applicable] |
| Executive Sponsor | Approves high-impact notifications, public statements, major customer notices or material business commitments. | Conditional | [Name / Role] | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] | [Approved / Changes required / Not applicable] |

### Routing Rules

| Scenario | Required Routing |
|---|---|
| Breach affects customers or service users | Incident Manager, Privacy Lead, Information Security, Business Owner, Customer Support, Communications where needed. |
| Breach affects employees or contractors | Incident Manager, Privacy Lead, Information Security, HR, Legal where needed. |
| Breach involves financial data, credentials or identity documents | Incident Manager, Privacy Lead, Information Security, Legal, Customer Support, Executive Sponsor where impact is significant. |
| Breach involves health data, children’s data or other highly sensitive data | Incident Manager, Privacy Lead, Information Security, Legal, Executive Sponsor, specialist support function as needed. |
| Breach involves a processor or third party | Incident Manager, Privacy Lead, Information Security, Vendor Owner, Legal, Communications where needed. |
| Direct notification is not practicable | Privacy Lead, Legal, Communications and Executive Sponsor must approve the alternative communication approach. |
| Notification is delayed due to an external investigation request | Privacy Lead, Legal and Executive Sponsor must approve and document the reason for delay. |

## Records & Retention

The completed form and all supporting evidence must be retained as part of the organisation’s personal data breach record. Records must be accurate, complete, access-controlled and available for internal review, audit, regulatory engagement and lessons learned.

| Record | Minimum Content | Owner | Storage Location | Retention Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completed notification form | All required fields, approval trail, final notice text and closure status. | [Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead] | [Privacy breach register / GRC system] | Retain for [retention period] from closure of the breach, unless a longer period is required for legal, regulatory or litigation reasons. |
| Risk assessment supporting notification decision | Assessment of likely impact on individuals, reasoning for high-risk determination and decision date. | [Privacy Lead] | [GRC system / case file] | Retain with the breach record. |
| Final issued notification | Exact text sent or published, including language versions and accessibility formats. | [Privacy Lead / Communications] | [Case file / document repository] | Retain with the breach record. |
| Recipient and delivery evidence | Recipient list or distribution criteria, send logs, postal dispatch records, delivery failures, bounce reports, public notice screenshots and timestamps. | [Incident Manager / Communications] | [Case file / secure evidence repository] | Retain with the breach record. |
| Approval evidence | Emails, workflow approvals, meeting notes, secure messages or emergency approval records. | [Incident Manager] | [Case file / GRC workflow] | Retain with the breach record. |
| Customer or individual enquiries | Contact logs, complaints, support tickets, escalations and resolutions. | [Customer Support / HR Support] | [Support system] | Retain according to support record retention rules, linked to the breach record where appropriate. |
| Follow-up communications | Updated notices, FAQs, corrections, additional guidance and evidence of distribution. | [Privacy Lead / Communications] | [Case file] | Retain with the breach record. |
| Lessons learned and remediation evidence | Post-incident review, corrective actions, control improvements and completion evidence. | [Incident Manager / Information Security] | [Incident management system / GRC system] | Retain according to incident and risk management retention rules. |

Access to this form and related records must be limited to authorised personnel with a legitimate need to know. Where records contain personal data, they must be handled securely, protected against unauthorised disclosure, and disposed of safely at the end of the approved retention period.

| Participant Full Name | Enter the participant’s full legal or HR-recorded name. |
| Participant Work Email | Enter the participant’s organisation-issued work email address. |
| Job Title | Enter the participant’s current job title at the time the training was assigned or completed. |
| Department/Function | Enter the participant’s department or business function, e.g. HR, Finance, Marketing, IT, Legal, Customer Support. |
| Location/Jurisdiction | Enter the participant’s primary work location or jurisdiction, e.g. UK, Ireland, Germany, France, EU Remote. |
| Worker Type | Enter one of: Employee, Contractor, Temporary Worker, Intern, Board Member, Third-Party User, Other. |
| Line Manager | Enter the participant’s line manager name or manager ID. |

| Training Provider | Enter the provider name, e.g. internal DPO/privacy team, HR learning team, external training provider, LMS vendor, legal counsel. |
| Delivery Method | Enter one of: LMS E-Learning, Instructor-Led Classroom, Live Webinar, Recorded Webinar, Workshop, One-to-One Briefing, External Course, Other. |
| Course Version | Enter the course version or publication date used for the training, e.g. v1.3 or 2026-03. |
| Learning Objectives Covered | Briefly list the key GDPR topics covered, e.g. personal data principles, lawful basis, data subject rights, breach reporting, DPIA escalation, confidentiality, role-specific handling rules. |
| Mandatory Training | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether this training was mandatory for the participant. |
| Assigned Date | Enter the date the training was assigned in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Due Date | Enter the required completion deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Completion Date | Enter the date the participant completed the training in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if not completed. |
| Completion Status | Enter one of: Not Assigned, Assigned, In Progress, Completed, Completed Late, Overdue, Waived, Failed, Cancelled. |
| Assessment Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the course required a quiz, test, practical assessment, or acknowledgement. |

| Evidence of Completion | Enter the location or link to evidence, such as LMS completion record, attendance sheet, certificate repository link, signed acknowledgement, or HR training export reference. |

| Refresher Frequency | Enter the required refresher interval, e.g. On Joining, Annual, Biennial, Upon Material Policy Change, Role Change, DPO Directed, N/A. |
| Next Training Due Date | Enter the next required refresher or role-based training date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Overdue Days | Enter the number of calendar days overdue as a whole number; use 0 if completed on time or not overdue. |
| Exception/Waiver Approved | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether a formal exception or waiver has been approved. |
| Exception/Waiver Approver | Enter the name and role of the person approving the waiver, typically DPO, Privacy Lead, HR Learning Owner, or Senior Manager; enter N/A if no waiver. |
| Exception/Waiver Reason | Enter a concise reason for any waiver or exception, e.g. duplicate equivalent training completed, long-term leave, role no longer applicable; enter N/A if none. |
| Remediation/Follow-Up Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether follow-up action is required due to overdue, failed, incomplete, or role-inappropriate training. |
| Remediation/Follow-Up Details | Enter the required follow-up action, owner, and target date, e.g. reassigned module by YYYY-MM-DD, manager escalation, additional role-based briefing; enter N/A if none. |
| Record Created Date | Enter the date this row was first created in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record Last Updated Date | Enter the date this row was last reviewed or updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Record Owner | Enter the role responsible for maintaining this record, e.g. HR Learning Administrator, Privacy Office, DPO Office. |
| Retention Period | Enter the applicable retention period for training evidence, e.g. Employment duration plus 6 years, 6 years after completion, or as defined in the records retention schedule. |
| Notes | Enter any additional audit-relevant context not captured elsewhere; do not include unnecessary sensitive personal data. |

### Maintenance

The HR Learning Administrator owns the template with oversight from the DPO/Privacy Office. It is updated after each training assignment or completion and reviewed at least monthly, drawing from the LMS, HRIS, attendance records, certificates, and approved waiver records.

GDPR-031.title: Consent Records
GDPR-031.content:
## What This Evidences

Consent Records evidence that [Organisation Name] can demonstrate that a data subject gave valid consent where consent is used as the lawful basis for processing under GDPR Art. 7(1). This is operational evidence collected from live business systems, not a document to be authored manually.

The records should show who consented, what they consented to, when and how consent was obtained, which privacy notice or consent wording applied at the time, and whether consent was later withdrawn or changed.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect Consent Records from the system that captures and manages consent in [Organisation Name]’s environment. Typical sources include:

- Consent management platform: [Consent Management Platform]
- Customer identity and access management platform: [CIAM Tool]
- Marketing automation platform: [Marketing Platform]
- Customer relationship management system: [CRM]
- Website or app preference centre: [Preference Centre / Portal]
- Cookie consent platform: [Cookie Consent Tool]
- Data subject portal: [Privacy Portal]
- Audit log or data warehouse fed by the above systems: [Log Store / Reporting Database]

Where multiple systems capture consent, collect from the system of record first. If no single system of record exists, collect from each source relevant to the processing activity.

## How To Collect

1. Identify the processing activity where consent is the lawful basis, using the record of processing activities or privacy register in [Privacy Tool / GRC System].
2. Confirm which system captures consent for that activity with the relevant business owner or system owner.
3. Log in to [Consent System / CRM / Marketing Platform] using an account with reporting or audit access.
4. Navigate to the consent, preferences, privacy, subscription, or audit log module.
5. Filter records for the relevant processing purpose, product, service, campaign, channel, or consent category.
6. Select the audit period required, such as [start date] to [end date].
7. Export the consent records in CSV, PDF report, or system-generated audit report format.
8. If available, also export the version history for the consent language, privacy notice, or preference category in force during the period.
9. Save the export to the approved evidence repository at [Evidence Repository Path].
10. Record the extraction date, extractor name, source system, filters used, and any limitations in the evidence index or audit request tracker.

## What To Capture

Capture enough detail to prove consent was obtained and can be traced. The evidence should include:

- Data subject identifier, such as customer ID, user ID, email address, or hashed identifier
- Consent status, such as granted, refused, withdrawn, or updated
- Date and time of consent event
- Processing purpose or consent category
- Channel or collection method, such as web form, mobile app, call centre, paper form, or preference centre
- Consent wording shown to the individual, or a reference to the exact wording version
- Privacy notice version or link in effect at the time
- Source system and record ID
- IP address, device ID, session ID, user agent, or transaction ID where captured
- Staff user ID if consent was captured by an employee
- Withdrawal or preference-change history
- Timestamped audit trail showing creation and modification events
- Evidence that consent was not pre-ticked, bundled, or inferred where the system records this

## Frequency & Owner

- **Owner:** [Data Protection Officer / Privacy Manager] is accountable for ensuring consent evidence is available.
- **Operational owner:** [System Owner / Marketing Operations / Product Owner] is responsible for extracting records from [Consent System].
- **Frequency:** Collect on request for audits, complaints, investigations, or data subject queries. For ongoing assurance, collect a sample export at least [quarterly] for high-volume consent-based processing.
- **Trigger events:** New consent journey, major privacy notice update, system migration, campaign launch, regulatory inquiry, or consent-related complaint.

## Retention & Storage

Store exported Consent Records in [Evidence Repository / GRC Tool / Secure SharePoint Library] with access restricted to [Privacy Team], [Legal], [Internal Audit], and authorised system owners.

Retain records for as long as the consent-based processing continues and for [retention period] after consent is withdrawn or processing ends, unless a longer legal hold applies. Protect exports because they may contain personal data. Apply encryption, access logging, and secure deletion according to [Records Retention Policy] and [Information Security Policy].

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will normally accept Consent Records where the evidence:

- Comes directly from [Consent System / CRM / Marketing Platform] or an approved reporting database
- Covers the relevant processing activity, purpose, population, and audit period
- Shows the data subject, consent status, timestamp, purpose, collection channel, and source record
- Links consent to the wording or privacy notice version presented at the time
- Includes withdrawal and change history where applicable
- Is exported with system metadata showing source, extraction date, filters, and report parameters
- Is complete enough to demonstrate consent for sampled individuals without manual reconstruction
- Is stored in a controlled evidence location with restricted access
- Is consistent with privacy notices, preference-centre configuration, and processing records
- Is not a manually created spreadsheet unless it is a direct, traceable export from the source system

GDPR-032.content:

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this due diligence record, using the format VDD-YYYY-NNN, e.g. VDD-2026-001. |
| Vendor / Processor Legal Name | Enter the full registered legal name of the vendor or processor, not a trading name unless no legal name is available. |
| Vendor Type | Select one: New Vendor, Existing Vendor, Renewal, Material Change, Sub-processor Review. |
| Service / Processing Description | Describe the service provided and the processing activity supported, including why the organisation uses this processor. |
| Business Owner | Enter the internal role or named person accountable for the business use of the vendor. |
| Procurement / Contract Owner | Enter the internal role or named person responsible for procurement, onboarding, or contract management. |
| Processor Role | Select one: Processor, Sub-processor, Joint Controller, Independent Controller, To Be Confirmed. Use this log for Art. 28(1) only where the vendor acts as a processor or sub-processor. |
| Personal Data Involved | List the categories of personal data processed, e.g. name, email address, payroll data, customer ID, IP address, health data. |
| Data Subject Categories | List the categories of data subjects affected, e.g. employees, customers, prospects, suppliers, website users, children. |
| Special Category / Criminal Offence Data | Select one: None, Special Category Data, Criminal Offence Data, Both, Unknown. If not None, specify the relevant data type in the same cell. |
| Processing Location(s) | Enter the countries or regions where the processor stores, accesses, or otherwise processes personal data. |
| International Transfer Involved | Select one: Yes, No, Unknown. Mark Yes where personal data is transferred or remotely accessed outside the UK/EEA, as applicable to the organisation’s GDPR scope. |
| Transfer Safeguard | If international transfer is involved, enter the safeguard relied on, e.g. EU SCCs, UK IDTA, UK Addendum, Adequacy Decision, BCRs, Derogation, Not Applicable, To Be Confirmed. |
| Due Diligence Trigger | Select one: New Onboarding, Periodic Review, Contract Renewal, Change in Processing, Security Incident, New Sub-processor, Regulatory / Audit Request, Other. |
| Due Diligence Date | Enter the date the due diligence assessment was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Due Diligence Status | Select one: Not Started, In Progress, Evidence Requested, Under Review, Complete, Deferred, Rejected. |
| Evidence Reviewed | List the evidence reviewed to assess sufficient guarantees, including document names, versions, dates, or repository links where available. |
| Security Measures Assessed | Summarise the technical and organisational security measures assessed, such as access control, encryption, logging, backup, vulnerability management, secure development, endpoint security, and physical security. |
| Privacy / GDPR Measures Assessed | Summarise privacy governance measures assessed, such as data protection policies, staff training, confidentiality commitments, DPIA support, privacy by design, record keeping, and accountability controls. |
| Certifications / Attestations Reviewed | Record any certifications, reports, or attestations reviewed, e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, Cyber Essentials, CSA STAR, PCI DSS, including date or validity period. |
| Sub-processor Controls Reviewed | Record whether the processor’s sub-processor approval, notification, flow-down contract, and monitoring controls were reviewed. Use format: Yes / No / Not Applicable, followed by brief details. |
| Incident / Breach Management Reviewed | Record whether incident detection, reporting, investigation, and GDPR breach notification support were assessed. Use format: Yes / No, followed by any key timing commitment. |
| Data Subject Rights Support Reviewed | Record whether the processor can support controller obligations for access, deletion, rectification, restriction, portability, objection, and related requests. Use format: Yes / No / Partial, followed by brief details. |
| Deletion / Return Capability Reviewed | Record whether the processor can return or delete personal data at end of service and confirm deletion. Use format: Yes / No / Partial, followed by brief details. |
| Risk Rating | Select one: Low, Medium, High, Critical. Base the rating on data sensitivity, volume, processing purpose, location, security maturity, sub-processing, transfer risk, and identified gaps. |
| Identified Gaps / Concerns | Enter any gaps that may affect whether the processor provides sufficient guarantees. If none, enter None. |
| Remediation Actions Required | Enter specific actions required before approval or continued use, e.g. obtain SOC 2 report, add SCCs, complete DPA, confirm deletion process. If none, enter None. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the internal or vendor owner responsible for completing remediation actions. If no remediation is required, enter Not Applicable. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the due date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format, or Not Applicable if no remediation is required. |
| Sufficient Guarantees Conclusion | State the assessment conclusion on whether the processor provides sufficient guarantees under GDPR Art. 28(1), with a concise rationale. |
| Decision | Select one: Approved, Approved with Conditions, Rejected, Deferred, Existing Use to Continue, Existing Use to Cease. |
| Approver | Enter the named person or role approving the due diligence outcome, typically Data Protection Officer, Privacy Lead, Information Security Lead, or Vendor Risk Committee. |
| Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Linked Contract / DPA Reference | Enter the contract, purchase order, DPA, SCC, IDTA, or vendor management system reference that links this due diligence record to the binding agreement. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on risk rating and review frequency. |
| Review Frequency | Select one: Annual, Every 2 Years, Every 3 Years, On Material Change, On Renewal, Other. High-risk processors should normally be reviewed at least annually. |
| Record Last Updated | Enter the date this log entry was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |

### Maintenance

This template is owned by the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead, with input from Procurement, Legal, Information Security, and Vendor Risk Management. It is updated for each new processor onboarding, renewal, material processing change, new sub-processor, incident-driven reassessment, and at least according to the review frequency, drawing from the vendor management system, contract repository, security assessment tool, and privacy records of processing.

GDPR-033.title: Anonymisation / Pseudonymisation Standard
GDPR-033.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer | [Effective Date] | GDPR | Internal |

## Purpose

This procedure defines the required steps for applying anonymisation and pseudonymisation to personal data handled by [Organisation Name]. It supports privacy by design, data minimisation, secure processing, and controlled use of personal data for analytics, testing, research, reporting, product development, security monitoring, and operational processing.

The procedure ensures that:

- Personal data is transformed using appropriate technical and organisational measures before use or sharing where direct identification is not necessary.
- Pseudonymised data remains protected as personal data.
- Anonymised data is only treated as non-personal data where re-identification is not reasonably likely.
- Transformation methods are documented, tested, approved, and periodically reviewed.
- Re-identification risks, key management practices, access controls, and recipient obligations are properly managed.

## Scope

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, temporary staff, service providers, and third parties who process personal data on behalf of [Organisation Name].

It applies to:

- Customer, employee, supplier, partner, user, patient, applicant, visitor, and stakeholder personal data.
- Structured data, including databases, spreadsheets, data warehouses, logs, exports, and reporting datasets.
- Unstructured and semi-structured data, including documents, images, transcripts, free-text fields, emails, chat records, voice recordings, and application telemetry.
- Production, non-production, analytics, testing, development, research, training, and reporting environments.
- Internal transfers and external disclosures of datasets.
- Manual and automated anonymisation or pseudonymisation processes.

This procedure does not apply to data that never relates to an identified or identifiable natural person. However, where there is uncertainty, the dataset must be treated as personal data until the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Team confirms otherwise.

For this procedure:

- **Anonymisation** means transforming personal data so individuals are no longer identifiable by any party using means reasonably likely to be available, including by combining the data with other information.
- **Pseudonymisation** means replacing or separating direct identifiers so individuals cannot be identified without additional information, such as a lookup table, token vault, encryption key, or mapping file.
- **De-identification** is a general term covering techniques that reduce identifiability, including anonymisation and pseudonymisation.
- **Re-identification** means any process that links de-identified data back to an individual.

## Prerequisites & Inputs

Before anonymisation or pseudonymisation begins, the request owner must ensure the following prerequisites and inputs are available.

| Prerequisite / Input | Description | Responsible Role |
|---|---|---|
| Approved business purpose | Clear explanation of why the data is needed and why identifiable data is not required, or why pseudonymised data is sufficient. | Request Owner |
| Dataset inventory | Description of data sources, data fields, formats, volumes, locations, retention period, and planned recipients. | Data Owner |
| Data classification | Confirmation of whether the dataset contains personal data, special category data, criminal offence data, children’s data, employee data, financial data, location data, or other high-risk data. | Data Owner |
| Lawful processing confirmation | Confirmation that the proposed processing activity has a valid basis and aligns with privacy notices, records of processing, and internal approvals. | Privacy Team |
| Risk assessment | Assessment of re-identification risk, potential harm to individuals, and security impact. | Privacy Team / Information Security |
| Data protection impact assessment, where required | Completed or updated assessment for processing likely to create high risk for individuals. | Privacy Team |
| Technical design | Proposed anonymisation or pseudonymisation method, tools, algorithms, parameters, key management approach, and validation method. | Technical Owner |
| Access model | Defined users, roles, systems, service accounts, privileged access, and segregation requirements. | System Owner |
| Recipient assessment | Assessment of internal or external recipients, onward sharing restrictions, contractual controls, and transfer arrangements where applicable. | Data Owner / Legal |
| Retention requirements | Defined retention period for source data, transformed data, mapping files, keys, logs, and derived outputs. | Data Owner |
| Testing environment approval | Confirmation that non-production data handling requirements are met before transformed data is used in development or testing. | Information Security |
| Change approval, where applicable | Approval for new tools, scripts, pipelines, or recurring transformation processes. | Change Manager |

The following must be completed before implementation:

- Confirm whether the intended outcome is anonymisation or pseudonymisation.
- Identify all direct and indirect identifiers.
- Identify all parties that may receive or access the transformed dataset.
- Determine whether those parties have access to other datasets that could assist re-identification.
- Select transformation techniques appropriate to the sensitivity, context, volume, and intended use of the data.
- Define how success will be validated and recorded.
- Obtain required approvals before releasing the transformed dataset.

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

1. **Initiate the de-identification request**

 The request owner must submit a de-identification request using [Request System/Form Name] before personal data is anonymised, pseudonymised, exported, shared, or used in a new context.

 The request must include:

 - Business purpose.
 - Dataset name and source system.
 - Data fields requested.
 - Intended users and recipients.
 - Intended environment, such as production analytics, development, testing, reporting, research, or external sharing.
 - Whether anonymisation or pseudonymisation is requested.
 - Expected frequency, such as one-off extract, recurring feed, API, batch job, or dashboard.
 - Retention period.
 - Security requirements and any known constraints.

2. **Confirm necessity and minimise the dataset**

 The Data Owner must review the request and confirm that each requested field is necessary for the stated purpose.

 The Data Owner must:

 - Remove fields that are not required.
 - Reduce the dataset to the minimum time period, population, geography, or transaction range required.
 - Use aggregated data where individual-level records are not necessary.
 - Avoid including free-text fields unless reviewed and justified.
 - Avoid including special category data unless specifically required and approved.
 - Confirm that the transformed dataset will not be used for incompatible purposes.

 Where the purpose can be achieved without personal data, anonymisation must be preferred over pseudonymisation.

3. **Identify direct, indirect, and contextual identifiers**

 The Technical Owner, with support from the Privacy Team and Data Owner, must classify dataset fields as direct identifiers, indirect identifiers, sensitive attributes, operational attributes, or non-identifying attributes.

 Examples include:

 | Identifier Type | Examples | Required Action |
 |---|---|---|
 | Direct identifiers | Name, email address, phone number, national identifier, employee ID, customer ID, account number, device ID, IP address where it identifies a user | Remove, mask, encrypt, tokenize, or replace depending on purpose |
 | Indirect identifiers | Date of birth, postcode, job title, department, location, rare condition, timestamps, salary band, transaction pattern | Generalise, suppress, perturb, bucket, aggregate, or otherwise reduce uniqueness |
 | Sensitive attributes | Health data, ethnicity, biometric data, political opinions, union membership, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, criminal history | Apply heightened review and protection; include only where strictly necessary |
 | Linkage attributes | Persistent tokens, household IDs, transaction IDs, session IDs, correlation IDs | Assess whether they enable linking back to an individual |
 | Free-text or media fields | Notes, comments, chat logs, call transcripts, images, scanned documents, audio | Review using approved redaction or extraction tools before use |

4. **Determine target state: anonymisation or pseudonymisation**

 The Privacy Team must confirm whether the requested processing requires anonymisation or pseudonymisation.

 Use **anonymisation** where:

 - Individual-level identification is not required.
 - The organisation does not need to re-link records to individuals.
 - The dataset will be published, externally shared, used for broad analytics, or retained for long-term statistical purposes.
 - The recipient does not need identity restoration.

 Use **pseudonymisation** where:

 - Records must remain linkable over time.
 - Re-contact, correction, deletion, investigation, billing, service delivery, or operational linkage may be required.
 - The organisation needs controlled reversibility.
 - The dataset will remain under access-controlled processing as personal data.

 Pseudonymised data must continue to be handled as personal data. It must not be described or labelled as anonymous.

5. **Perform a re-identification risk assessment**

 The Privacy Team and Information Security must assess the likelihood and impact of re-identification before the transformed dataset is approved.

 The assessment must consider:

 - Dataset size and uniqueness of records.
 - Presence of rare combinations of attributes.
 - Sensitivity of the data.
 - Whether timestamps, locations, or event sequences reveal individuals.
 - Whether recipients have or can obtain other datasets for matching.
 - Publicly available information that could be used for linkage.
 - Internal access to source systems, mapping files, or identity services.
 - Strength of contractual, organisational, and technical restrictions.
 - Likelihood of motivated attackers, insider misuse, or accidental disclosure.
 - Consequences for individuals if re-identification occurs.

 A sample risk scoring approach is below.

 | Factor | Low Risk | Medium Risk | High Risk |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Population size | Large group with broad coverage | Moderate group or defined segment | Small group, rare population, or narrow cohort |
 | Attribute uniqueness | Common attributes only | Some distinguishing combinations | Unique or rare combinations likely |
 | Data sensitivity | Low sensitivity | Moderate sensitivity | Sensitive or high-impact data |
 | External data availability | Limited matching sources | Some matching sources available | Many public or recipient-held matching sources |
 | Recipient control | Internal controlled environment | Approved third party with contract | Public release or weak recipient controls |
 | Reversibility | No mapping retained | Mapping retained with strict controls | Mapping broadly accessible or poorly segregated |

 If residual risk is high, the dataset must not be released until risk is reduced or formally accepted through the exception process.

6. **Select appropriate transformation techniques**

 The Technical Owner must select one or more techniques suitable for the purpose and risk level. Techniques must be implemented using approved tools, reviewed scripts, or controlled data pipelines.

 Common techniques include:

 | Technique | Description | Typical Use | Key Considerations |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Suppression | Removing fields or values entirely | Removing names, emails, phone numbers, rare values | May reduce utility; must consider indirect identifiers |
 | Masking | Hiding part of a value | Displaying last four digits only | Usually pseudonymisation, not anonymisation |
 | Tokenisation | Replacing identifiers with generated tokens | Analytics requiring linkage across records | Token vault must be secured and access restricted |
 | Encryption | Protecting values with cryptographic keys | Reversible pseudonymisation | Key management and segregation are critical |
 | Hashing with salt or keyed hashing | Creating non-readable values from identifiers | Matching without revealing original values | Unsalted hashes of common values are vulnerable |
 | Generalisation | Reducing precision | Age band instead of date of birth; region instead of full address | Must be sufficient to reduce uniqueness |
 | Aggregation | Combining records into groups | Reporting counts, trends, statistics | Small cell counts must be suppressed |
 | Perturbation | Adding controlled noise | Statistical analysis | Must preserve analytical value while reducing identifiability |
 | Swapping | Exchanging values between records | Statistical datasets | Must be documented and tested |
 | Synthetic data generation | Creating artificial data with similar properties | Development, testing, modelling | Must be tested to ensure real individuals cannot be inferred |
 | Redaction | Removing identifiers from documents or media | Contracts, case files, transcripts, images | Manual quality checks are required |
 | Date shifting | Moving dates consistently by a random offset | Longitudinal analysis | Offsets must not reveal identity or key events |
 | Bucketing | Grouping granular values | Salary bands, age ranges, transaction bands | Buckets must avoid small groups |

 The method must be proportionate to the risk and must not rely on removal of direct identifiers alone where indirect identifiers remain sufficient to identify individuals.

7. **Apply anonymisation rules where the target is anonymous data**

 Where anonymisation is the approved target, the Technical Owner must implement controls so the dataset is not reasonably linkable to individuals by the organisation, recipients, or likely third parties.

 The following rules apply:

 - Remove all direct identifiers.
 - Remove or transform persistent identifiers that could support linkage.
 - Generalise dates, locations, job roles, and other quasi-identifiers.
 - Suppress rare attributes and outliers.
 - Aggregate data where individual-level detail is not required.
 - Suppress small group counts in reports and dashboards.
 - Avoid publishing exact timestamps where event timing may identify a person.
 - Remove metadata from files, images, documents, and exports.
 - Review free-text fields for hidden personal data.
 - Validate that the recipient cannot reasonably re-identify individuals using available information.
 - Do not retain mapping files if the output is to be treated as anonymised.
 - Do not label data as anonymised until validation has been completed and approved.

 Where the organisation retains a mapping file, key, lookup table, or other means to identify individuals from the dataset, the output is pseudonymised, not anonymised.

8. **Apply pseudonymisation rules where reversibility or linkage is required**

 Where pseudonymisation is the approved target, the Technical Owner must ensure identifiers are replaced or separated from the dataset and that additional information needed for re-identification is independently protected.

 The following rules apply:

 - Replace direct identifiers with pseudonyms, tokens, encrypted values, or keyed hashes.
 - Use different tokens for different contexts unless cross-context linkage is approved.
 - Avoid deterministic values across unrelated datasets unless linkage is necessary and approved.
 - Store mapping tables, token vaults, salts, and cryptographic keys separately from pseudonymised data.
 - Restrict access to re-identification materials to authorised roles only.
 - Log all access to mapping tables, keys, and tokenisation services.
 - Use strong access controls, privileged access management, and segregation of duties.
 - Rotate keys or tokens when compromise is suspected or where required by cryptographic standards.
 - Prevent developers, analysts, testers, or external parties from accessing both pseudonymised data and re-identification materials unless explicitly approved.
 - Define a documented process for authorised re-identification.
 - Treat pseudonymised datasets as personal data for storage, transfer, retention, incident response, and individual rights handling.

9. **Secure the transformation process**

 The Technical Owner and System Owner must ensure the transformation process is secure from source extraction through output delivery.

 Required controls include:

 - Use approved secure environments for extraction and transformation.
 - Prohibit local storage on unmanaged devices.
 - Encrypt data in transit and at rest.
 - Restrict access to source, interim, and output datasets.
 - Use managed service accounts where automation is required.
 - Avoid emailing datasets unless approved secure transfer methods are unavailable and an exception is approved.
 - Delete temporary files and staging data after validation and release.
 - Ensure scripts and pipelines are version controlled.
 - Conduct peer review for transformation logic.
 - Monitor privileged access and failed access attempts.
 - Maintain audit logs for dataset creation, access, modification, transfer, and deletion.
 - Apply data loss prevention controls where available.
 - Use approved secure file transfer, API, or data platform delivery methods.

10. **Validate the transformed dataset**

 Before release, the Technical Owner must validate that the transformation was correctly applied. The Privacy Team or delegated reviewer must review the results for privacy risk.

 Validation must include:

 - Confirmation that all direct identifiers were removed, replaced, or protected.
 - Sampling to verify transformed fields behave as expected.
 - Testing for uniqueness and small group counts.
 - Review of outliers and rare combinations.
 - Review of free-text, file metadata, and unstructured content where applicable.
 - Confirmation that mapping files or keys are not included in the output.
 - Confirmation that access permissions are correctly configured.
 - Confirmation that retention labels or deletion schedules are applied.
 - Verification that the output remains fit for the approved business purpose.

 Example validation checklist:

 | Validation Item | Pass / Fail | Evidence Location | Reviewer | Date |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | Direct identifiers removed or protected | [Pass/Fail] | [Link] | [Name] | [Date] |
 | Indirect identifiers generalised or controlled | [Pass/Fail] | [Link] | [Name] | [Date] |
 | Small groups and outliers addressed | [Pass/Fail] | [Link] | [Name] | [Date] |
 | Free-text reviewed where applicable | [Pass/Fail] | [Link] | [Name] | [Date] |
 | Mapping files or keys excluded from output | [Pass/Fail] | [Link] | [Name] | [Date] |
 | Access controls verified | [Pass/Fail] | [Link] | [Name] | [Date] |
 | Retention configured | [Pass/Fail] | [Link] | [Name] | [Date] |
 | Residual risk approved | [Pass/Fail] | [Link] | [Name] | [Date] |

11. **Approve release or use**

 The Data Owner, Privacy Team, and Information Security must approve release where required by risk level, recipient type, or data sensitivity.

 Minimum approval requirements are:

 | Scenario | Required Approval |
 |---|---|
 | Low-risk internal pseudonymised dataset | Data Owner and System Owner |
 | Medium-risk internal pseudonymised dataset | Data Owner, Privacy Team, and Information Security |
 | High-risk pseudonymised dataset | Data Owner, Privacy Team, Information Security, and Senior Risk Owner |
 | Any dataset claimed as anonymised | Data Owner and Privacy Team |
 | External sharing of de-identified data | Data Owner, Privacy Team, Legal, and Information Security |
 | Public release of aggregate or anonymised data | Data Owner, Privacy Team, Legal, Communications where applicable, and Senior Risk Owner |
 | Use of special category or other high-risk data | Data Owner, Privacy Team, and Information Security |
 | Use in non-production environments | Data Owner, System Owner, and Information Security |

 Release must not occur until all required approvals are recorded.

12. **Label and classify the output**

 The Technical Owner must apply clear labelling to the transformed dataset, reports, exports, dashboards, or files.

 Labels must state:

 - Dataset name.
 - Transformation type: anonymised, pseudonymised, aggregated, masked, synthetic, or redacted.
 - Data classification.
 - Approved purpose.
 - Approved recipients or access groups.
 - Retention period.
 - Restrictions on re-identification, onward sharing, or reuse.
 - Contact point for questions.

 Pseudonymised data must retain a personal data classification appropriate to its sensitivity. Anonymised data may only be reclassified after approval by the Privacy Team.

13. **Release or deploy through approved channels**

 The System Owner must release the dataset or deploy the recurring transformation process using approved channels only.

 Acceptable channels include:

 - Approved data platform with role-based access controls.
 - Secure managed file transfer.
 - Approved encrypted storage location.
 - Approved API with authentication, authorisation, logging, and rate controls.
 - Controlled analytics workspace.
 - Approved secure research or development environment.

 The release record must include:

 - Release date and time.
 - Recipient or access group.
 - Dataset version.
 - Location or delivery method.
 - Approval reference.
 - Retention expiry date.
 - Any contractual or usage restrictions.

14. **Manage re-identification requests**

 Re-identification of pseudonymised data is prohibited unless there is an approved business, legal, security, compliance, or individual rights reason.

 The requester must submit a re-identification request including:

 - Reason for re-identification.
 - Dataset and pseudonym reference.
 - Individuals or records affected.
 - Legal or operational justification.
 - Requested recipient of re-identified information.
 - Time period for access.
 - Confirmation that the minimum necessary records will be re-identified.

 Approval is required from the Data Owner and Privacy Team. Information Security approval is required where mapping files, token vaults, encryption keys, or privileged access are involved.

 Emergency re-identification for incident response, safety, fraud prevention, or legal hold may be authorised by [Emergency Approver Role], but must be retrospectively reviewed by the Privacy Team within [Number] business days.

15. **Monitor use and detect misuse**

 The System Owner and Information Security must monitor access to transformed datasets and re-identification materials.

 Monitoring must include:

 - Access by users, privileged users, service accounts, and third parties.
 - Downloads, exports, bulk queries, and unusual query patterns.
 - Failed access attempts.
 - Changes to access groups.
 - Attempts to combine datasets beyond the approved purpose.
 - Use of pseudonymised data in unauthorised environments.
 - Access to mapping tables, keys, token vaults, and salt values.
 - Expired datasets that remain accessible.

 Suspected unauthorised re-identification, misuse, or disclosure must be handled as a security and privacy incident.

16. **Retain and delete data according to approved periods**

 The Data Owner and System Owner must ensure source, interim, transformed, and mapping data are retained only for approved periods.

 Retention rules must specify:

 - Source data retention.
 - Temporary extraction and staging retention.
 - Transformed dataset retention.
 - Mapping table or token vault retention.
 - Key, salt, and secret retention.
 - Log retention.
 - Backup retention.
 - Deletion or anonymisation trigger events.

 At the end of the retention period, data must be securely deleted, anonymised, or renewed through documented approval. Deletion must be recorded.

17. **Maintain documentation and evidence**

 The request owner and Technical Owner must ensure the complete record of the de-identification activity is retained in [Repository/System Name].

 Documentation must include:

 - Request and approvals.
 - Dataset inventory and field classification.
 - Risk assessment.
 - Transformation design.
 - Transformation scripts, tool configuration, or pipeline details.
 - Validation results.
 - Release record.
 - Access controls.
 - Retention and deletion evidence.
 - Contracts or recipient restrictions where applicable.
 - Exception approvals, if any.

18. **Review recurring transformations**

 For recurring feeds, dashboards, pipelines, or shared datasets, the Data Owner must review the process at least every [Review Frequency] and when material changes occur.

 Triggers for review include:

 - Addition of new data fields.
 - Change in purpose.
 - New recipient or new external sharing arrangement.
 - Change in source system.
 - Change in transformation method.
 - Change in threat environment or known re-identification techniques.
 - Security incident or privacy incident.
 - Change in retention period.
 - New linkage to other datasets.
 - Material change in applicable legal, contractual, or business requirements.

## Roles & RACI

| Activity | Request Owner | Data Owner | Technical Owner | System Owner | Privacy Team / DPO | Information Security | Legal | Senior Risk Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Submit de-identification request | R | C | C | C | C | C | C | I |
| Confirm business purpose and necessity | C | A/R | C | C | C | I | I | I |
| Identify data fields and identifiers | C | A/R | R | C | C | C | I | I |
| Confirm anonymisation or pseudonymisation target | C | C | C | I | A/R | C | C | I |
| Perform re-identification risk assessment | C | C | C | C | A/R | R | C | I |
| Select transformation method | I | C | A/R | C | C | C | I | I |
| Implement transformation | I | C | A/R | R | C | C | I | I |
| Secure keys, salts, token vaults, or mapping tables | I | C | R | R | C | A/R | I | I |
| Validate transformed dataset | C | C | A/R | C | R | C | I | I |
| Approve release | I | A/R | C | C | R | R | C | A where high risk |
| Approve external sharing | I | A/R | C | C | R | R | R | A where high risk |
| Manage access controls | I | C | C | A/R | C | R | I | I |
| Approve re-identification | C | A/R | C | C | A/R | R where technical access required | C | I |
| Monitor use and misuse | I | C | C | A/R | C | R | I | I |
| Retain and delete data | I | A/R | C | R | C | C | I | I |
| Maintain records | R | A | R | C | C | C | C | I |
| Review recurring transformations | C | A/R | R | C | R | R | C | I |

RACI key:

- **R** - Responsible for performing the activity.
- **A** - Accountable for the outcome and approval.
- **C** - Consulted before or during the activity.
- **I** - Informed of the activity or outcome.

## Records & Outputs

The following records must be created and retained for each anonymisation or pseudonymisation activity.

| Record / Output | Description | Owner | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| De-identification request | Original request including purpose, dataset, recipient, environment, and frequency. | Request Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Dataset inventory | Source systems, data fields, data types, volume, and classification. | Data Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Field classification | Identification of direct identifiers, indirect identifiers, sensitive fields, and linkage fields. | Technical Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Necessity and minimisation review | Evidence that fields and records were reduced to the minimum required. | Data Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Re-identification risk assessment | Documented assessment of likelihood, impact, controls, and residual risk. | Privacy Team | [Retention Period] |
| Transformation design | Description of selected techniques, algorithms, parameters, tools, and logic. | Technical Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Approved scripts or configuration | Version-controlled scripts, code review evidence, tool configuration, and change records. | Technical Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Validation checklist | Evidence that transformation was tested and approved before release. | Technical Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Approval record | Data Owner, Privacy, Security, Legal, or senior risk approvals as applicable. | Data Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Release record | Date, recipient, location, dataset version, access group, and restrictions. | System Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Access control record | Users, roles, service accounts, privileged access, and review evidence. | System Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Mapping/key management record | Location, owner, access controls, rotation, and audit trail for re-identification materials. | Information Security | [Retention Period] |
| Re-identification request record | Requests, approvals, outputs, and audit logs for re-identification events. | Privacy Team | [Retention Period] |
| Recipient restrictions | Contractual, confidentiality, data sharing, or usage restrictions. | Legal | [Retention Period] |
| Retention and deletion evidence | Evidence of expiry, deletion, anonymisation, or approved extension. | Data Owner / System Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Review record | Periodic review of recurring transformations and any required remediation. | Data Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Exception record | Approved deviations, compensating controls, expiry date, and risk acceptance. | Privacy Team | [Retention Period] |

Required outputs may include:

- Anonymised dataset.
- Pseudonymised dataset.
- Aggregated report.
- Masked dataset.
- Redacted document set.
- Synthetic dataset.
- Tokenised or encrypted data extract.
- Validated dashboard or analytics workspace.
- Secure data feed or API output.
- Re-identification output, where separately approved.

All records must be stored in [Repository/System Name] with access limited to authorised personnel.

## Exceptions & Escalation

Exceptions to this procedure are permitted only where there is a documented business need and the associated privacy and security risks have been assessed and approved.

Examples of exceptions include:

- Use of identifiable production data in a non-production environment.
- Release of pseudonymised data without full validation.
- Retention of mapping files beyond the approved period.
- Access to both pseudonymised data and re-identification materials by the same user or team.
- Use of deterministic tokens across multiple purposes without approval.
- External sharing where contractual restrictions are not yet finalised.
- Use of free-text data without complete redaction.
- Delayed deletion of transformed datasets.
- Emergency re-identification before standard approval is completed.

Exception requests must include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception title | Short description of the requested deviation |
| Procedure requirement affected | Description of the requirement that cannot be met |
| Business justification | Why the exception is necessary |
| Dataset and individuals affected | Scope and sensitivity of the data |
| Risk assessment | Privacy, security, operational, and legal risk |
| Compensating controls | Measures to reduce risk during the exception period |
| Duration | Start date and expiry date |
| Approval required | Roles required to approve the exception |
| Review plan | How and when the exception will be reviewed or closed |

Approval requirements:

- Low-risk exceptions require approval from the Data Owner and Privacy Team.
- Medium-risk exceptions require approval from the Data Owner, Privacy Team, and Information Security.
- High-risk exceptions require approval from the Senior Risk Owner, with input from the Data Protection Officer, Information Security, and Legal.
- Exceptions involving external disclosure, public release, high-risk data, or possible significant impact to individuals must be escalated to [Executive Committee/Risk Committee Name].

Escalation must occur immediately where:

- Re-identification occurs without approval.
- Anonymised data is suspected to be re-identifiable.
- Mapping files, keys, salts, or token vaults are exposed.
- Transformed data is shared with an unauthorised recipient.
- A recipient breaches usage restrictions.
- Data is used for a purpose not approved in the request.
- A dataset is lost, stolen, or accessed by an unauthorised party.
- Individual rights cannot be fulfilled due to incomplete transformation records.
- A high residual risk remains unresolved.

Suspected privacy or security incidents must be reported through [Incident Reporting Channel] immediately and handled under the organisation’s incident management and breach response procedures.

## Review

This procedure must be reviewed at least annually by the Data Protection Officer, Privacy Team, Information Security, and relevant Data Owners.

The review must confirm that:

- The procedure remains aligned with organisational processing activities.
- Transformation techniques remain effective against current re-identification risks.
- Approved tools and scripts remain secure and supported.
- Access controls and segregation of duties remain appropriate.
- Mapping files, keys, salts, and token vaults are properly protected.
- Recurring transformations are reviewed and re-approved as required.
- Records are complete and retained according to approved periods.
- Exceptions are closed or renewed with valid justification.
- Lessons learned from incidents, audits, data subject requests, and third-party reviews are incorporated.
- Training and awareness materials remain current.

A review must also be performed when:

- New processing activities require large-scale anonymisation or pseudonymisation.
- New high-risk datasets are introduced.
- Existing datasets are linked in a new way.
- Data is shared with a new category of recipient.
- A new anonymisation, tokenisation, encryption, masking, or synthetic data tool is implemented.
- A significant privacy or security incident occurs.
- Material changes are made to systems, data architecture, analytics platforms, or cloud services.
- Legal, regulatory, contractual, or business requirements materially change.

Review outcomes must be documented in [Repository/System Name], including decisions, required updates, assigned actions, owners, and due dates.

GDPR-034.title: Internal Audit / Privacy Audit Reports
GDPR-034.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| PRIV-RPT-[YYYY]-[NN] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer | [Effective Date] | GDPR | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This report presents the results of the internal privacy audit performed to assess the effectiveness of [Organisation Name]’s privacy governance, data protection controls, and operational compliance with GDPR-aligned obligations.

The audit was designed to determine whether [Organisation Name]:

- Has established and maintained appropriate privacy governance arrangements.
- Can demonstrate accountability for the processing of personal data.
- Processes personal data lawfully, fairly, and transparently.
- Maintains accurate records of processing activities.
- Provides appropriate privacy notices and supports data subject rights.
- Applies privacy by design and privacy by default in business processes, systems, and projects.
- Identifies and manages privacy risks, including risks associated with vendors and third parties.
- Detects, assesses, and responds to personal data breaches within required timeframes.
