 13.4. Security monitoring shall be performed to detect suspicious activity, unauthorised access, data exfiltration attempts, malware, policy violations, and indicators of compromise.

 13.5. Alerts involving personal data, privileged accounts, critical systems, or external exposure shall be triaged and escalated according to incident response procedures.

 Minimum logging expectations are as follows:

 | Environment or System Type | Minimum Events to Capture | Minimum Retention |
 |---|---|---:|
 | Identity and access systems | Login attempts, privilege changes, account creation, account disablement, MFA events | [Retention Period] |
 | Systems processing personal data | Access to records, exports, administrative changes, failed access attempts | [Retention Period] |
 | Network and perimeter controls | Allowed and denied traffic, security alerts, configuration changes | [Retention Period] |
 | Cloud platforms | Administrative actions, API calls, access changes, storage access, security alerts | [Retention Period] |
 | Security tools | Malware events, vulnerability findings, policy violations, alert triage actions | [Retention Period] |

14. **Cybersecurity Incident Management**

 14.1. [Organisation Name] shall maintain a cybersecurity incident management process for detecting, reporting, triaging, containing, investigating, eradicating, recovering from, and learning from cybersecurity incidents.

 14.2. Suspected or confirmed incidents involving personal data shall be immediately escalated to the Information Security function and the Privacy or Data Protection function.

 14.3. Incident response activities shall preserve evidence, maintain confidentiality, document decisions, and support legal, regulatory, contractual, and data subject notification obligations.

 14.4. Incident severity shall be assessed based on impact to confidentiality, integrity, availability, personal data, business operations, legal obligations, reputation, and affected individuals.

 14.5. Post-incident reviews shall be conducted for significant incidents, and corrective actions shall be tracked to closure.

 14.6. Employees and third parties shall be required to report suspected cybersecurity incidents, personal data breaches, phishing, malware, unauthorised access, lost devices, and improper disclosures without delay.

15. **Business Continuity, Backup, and Resilience**

 15.1. [Organisation Name] shall implement resilience measures for critical systems and personal data processing environments to support continuity of operations.

 15.2. Backup processes shall be defined, performed, monitored, and tested for systems and data required to meet business, legal, regulatory, and recovery requirements.

 15.3. Backups containing personal data shall be protected using appropriate access controls, encryption, retention controls, and secure disposal methods.

 15.4. Recovery objectives shall be established for critical systems and shall be tested periodically.

 15.5. Cybersecurity scenarios, including ransomware, destructive malware, cloud service disruption, data corruption, and loss of privileged access, shall be considered in continuity and recovery planning.

16. **Third-Party and Processor Cybersecurity**

 16.1. Third parties that access, process, store, transmit, host, manage, or secure personal data on behalf of [Organisation Name] shall be subject to cybersecurity due diligence before engagement.

 16.2. Contracts with relevant third parties shall include cybersecurity, confidentiality, incident notification, audit support, data protection, secure disposal, sub-processing, and service continuity requirements.

 16.3. Third-party cybersecurity risk shall be assessed based on the nature of services, access level, data sensitivity, data volume, integration depth, hosting location, and operational dependency.

 16.4. Third parties shall be monitored periodically according to risk, including review of security attestations, audit reports, certifications, vulnerability posture, incident history, and remediation commitments.

 16.5. Third-party access to [Organisation Name] systems and personal data shall be approved, limited, monitored, and revoked when no longer required.

17. **Awareness and Training**

 17.1. All employees and relevant contractors shall complete cybersecurity awareness training at onboarding and periodically thereafter.

 17.2. Cybersecurity training shall include secure handling of personal data, phishing awareness, password and authentication practices, incident reporting, acceptable use, remote working, and protection of confidential information.

 17.3. Personnel with privileged access, security responsibilities, development responsibilities, or personal data processing responsibilities shall receive role-specific training.

 17.4. Training completion shall be tracked, and non-completion shall be escalated according to management procedures.

18. **Acceptable Use and Endpoint Security**

 18.1. Users shall use [Organisation Name] information assets only for authorised business purposes and in accordance with approved acceptable use requirements.

 18.2. Endpoints used to access organisational systems or personal data shall be secured, managed, monitored, and protected against malware and unauthorised access.

 18.3. Users shall not install unauthorised software, bypass security controls, disable security tools, use unauthorised storage services, or connect unmanaged devices to organisational networks without approval.

 18.4. Lost, stolen, compromised, or suspected compromised devices shall be reported immediately.

 18.5. Remote work shall be performed using approved devices, approved connectivity methods, and required security controls.

19. **Data Retention, Disposal, and Media Handling**

 19.1. Personal data shall be retained only for authorised business, legal, regulatory, or contractual purposes and shall be protected throughout the retention period.

 19.2. Storage media, backups, records, logs, and devices containing personal data shall be securely disposed of, sanitised, or destroyed when no longer required.

 19.3. Disposal activities for systems and media containing personal data shall be documented and, where applicable, certified by approved service providers.

 19.4. Removable media use shall be restricted, encrypted where permitted, logged where feasible, and approved based on business need.

20. **Compliance Evidence and Documentation**

 20.1. [Organisation Name] shall maintain evidence demonstrating implementation and operation of National Cybersecurity Authority-aligned controls.

 20.2. Evidence shall be accurate, complete, attributable, retrievable, and retained according to legal, regulatory, audit, and business requirements.

 20.3. Control owners shall provide evidence when requested by Information Security, Internal Audit, Compliance, Privacy, Legal, regulators, or authorised external assessors.

 20.4. Evidence shall not be falsified, backdated, altered, or withheld.

 Examples of required evidence include:

 | Control Area | Example Evidence |
 |---|---|
 | Governance | Approved policies, committee minutes, risk reports, cybersecurity roadmap |
 | Risk management | Risk assessments, risk registers, treatment plans, acceptance approvals |
 | Access control | Access approvals, access reviews, privileged access logs, termination records |
 | Vulnerability management | Scan reports, remediation tickets, patch records, exception approvals |
 | Incident management | Incident tickets, investigation reports, containment actions, lessons learned |
 | Third-party security | Due diligence records, contracts, security questionnaires, review results |
 | Awareness | Training records, phishing simulation results, communications |
 | Resilience | Backup reports, restore test results, continuity exercise records |

21. **Regulatory and Directive Management**

 21.1. [Organisation Name] shall monitor new and updated cybersecurity requirements, circulars, directives, and guidance issued by relevant Saudi authorities.

 21.2. New or updated requirements shall be assessed for applicability, impact, implementation effort, ownership, and target completion date.

 21.3. Material regulatory or directive changes affecting cybersecurity or personal data protection shall be reported to senior management.

 21.4. Internal policies, standards, procedures, control baselines, training, and assurance activities shall be updated where required to reflect applicable changes.

22. **Performance Measurement and Reporting**

 22.1. The Information Security function shall define cybersecurity metrics to measure adoption, implementation effectiveness, risk exposure, compliance status, and control performance.

 22.2. Cybersecurity metrics shall be reported periodically to management and governance forums.

 22.3. Metrics shall include both compliance indicators and operational effectiveness indicators.

 Example reporting metrics include:

 | Metric | Reporting Frequency | Responsible Owner |
 |---|---|---|
 | Percentage of applicable cybersecurity requirements implemented | Quarterly | CISO |
 | Number of overdue high and critical risk treatment actions | Monthly | Risk Owners |
 | Critical vulnerability remediation performance | Monthly | IT Operations |
 | Privileged access review completion rate | Quarterly | Identity and Access Management Owner |
 | Security awareness completion rate | Quarterly | Human Resources and Information Security |
 | Number of personal data-related security incidents | Monthly | Security Operations and Privacy Function |
 | Third-party security review completion rate | Quarterly | Vendor Management |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors / Executive Committee | Provide oversight of cybersecurity risk and compliance; approve strategic cybersecurity direction; ensure adequate resources are available; review significant risks, incidents, and compliance matters. |
| Chief Executive Officer | Ensure organisational commitment to cybersecurity and personal data protection; support enforcement of this Policy across all business units. |
| Chief Information Security Officer | Own this Policy; lead adoption of National Cybersecurity Authority-aligned standards; maintain cybersecurity governance; report cybersecurity posture; coordinate control implementation and assurance. |
| Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | Coordinate with Information Security on personal data protection requirements; advise on personal data breach implications; support privacy impact assessments and regulatory response. |
| Chief Information Officer / Technology Lead | Ensure technology environments implement required cybersecurity controls; support secure operations, patching, access management, backup, logging, and resilience. |
| Legal and Compliance | Monitor applicable legal and regulatory obligations; advise on contractual, notification, and regulatory matters; support interpretation of cybersecurity obligations affecting personal data. |
| Risk Management | Integrate cybersecurity risks into enterprise risk management; support risk assessment, treatment tracking, escalation, and reporting. |
| Internal Audit | Independently assess compliance with this Policy and related cybersecurity controls; report findings and track remediation. |
| Business Unit Heads | Ensure cybersecurity requirements are implemented within their areas; assign system and process owners; support risk treatment and compliance activities. |
| System Owners | Classify systems; approve access; ensure security requirements are implemented; support risk assessments, testing, logging, backup, and remediation activities. |
| Data Owners | Classify data; define authorised use and access; approve data sharing; support personal data protection and retention requirements. |
| IT Operations | Implement and operate technical security controls; maintain secure configurations; patch systems; monitor infrastructure; support incident response and recovery. |
| Security Operations | Monitor security events; triage alerts; coordinate incident response; maintain detection capabilities; report significant incidents. |
| Procurement and Vendor Management | Ensure cybersecurity requirements are included in supplier onboarding, contracts, renewals, and performance reviews. |
| Human Resources | Support onboarding and offboarding controls; coordinate training completion; enforce disciplinary processes where required. |
| Employees, Contractors, and Users | Comply with this Policy; protect personal data and information assets; complete required training; report incidents and weaknesses promptly. |
| Third Parties and Processors | Comply with contractual cybersecurity requirements; protect personal data; notify [Organisation Name] of incidents; support audits, assessments, and remediation activities. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory. [Organisation Name] shall monitor, test, and enforce compliance through governance reviews, control self-assessments, technical monitoring, internal audits, third-party reviews, risk assessments, vulnerability assessments, incident reviews, and management reporting.

The Information Security function shall maintain a compliance monitoring programme that includes:

- Periodic assessment of alignment with applicable National Cybersecurity Authority requirements.
- Review of control implementation and operating effectiveness.
- Monitoring of remediation actions, exceptions, and risk acceptances.
- Reporting of non-compliance to accountable owners and management.
- Escalation of overdue or high-risk issues to senior governance forums.
- Coordination with Privacy, Legal, Compliance, and Internal Audit where personal data or regulatory obligations are affected.

Minimum monitoring activities shall include:

| Activity | Frequency | Responsible Function |
|---|---:|---|
| Review of applicable cybersecurity standards and directives | Quarterly | Information Security and Compliance |
| Cybersecurity risk register review | Monthly | Information Security and Risk Management |
| Vulnerability and patch compliance reporting | Monthly | IT Operations and Information Security |
| Privileged access review | Quarterly | Identity and Access Management and System Owners |
| Third-party cybersecurity review for high-risk suppliers | At least annually | Vendor Management and Information Security |
| Security awareness completion review | Quarterly | Human Resources and Information Security |
| Cybersecurity incident trend review | Monthly | Security Operations |
| Policy compliance assessment | At least annually | Information Security |
| Independent audit or assurance review | According to audit plan | Internal Audit |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in one or more of the following actions:

- Required remediation within a defined timeframe.
- Increased monitoring or compensating controls.
- Suspension or removal of system access.
- Supplier corrective action or contractual remedies.
- Formal risk escalation to senior management.
- Disciplinary action in accordance with [Organisation Name] human resources policies.
- Legal or regulatory action where required.
- Termination of employment, contract, or supplier relationship in serious cases.

Any suspected violation of this Policy shall be reported to the Information Security function, Compliance function, Human Resources, or through [Organisation Name] approved reporting channel.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business need and where the associated risk has been assessed, approved, and controlled.

All exception requests shall include:

- The specific Policy requirement for which an exception is requested.
- Business justification for the exception.
- Affected systems, data, processes, users, locations, or third parties.
- Whether personal data or sensitive personal data is affected.
- Risk assessment and potential impact.
- Proposed compensating controls.
- Requested duration and expiry date.
- Remediation or transition plan.
- Approval from the relevant control owner, risk owner, Information Security, and other required stakeholders.

Exceptions shall not be open-ended. Each exception shall have an expiry date and shall be reviewed before renewal. Exceptions involving high or critical risk, personal data exposure, regulatory impact, or significant deviation from National Cybersecurity Authority expectations shall require senior management approval.

Exception records shall be maintained in an approved register.

| Exception Field | Required Information |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | [Exception ID] |
| Requesting Business Unit | [Business Unit] |
| Policy Requirement | [Requirement Description] |
| Affected Asset or Process | [System, Service, Process, or Supplier] |
| Personal Data Impact | [Yes/No and Description] |
| Risk Rating | [Low/Medium/High/Critical] |
| Compensating Controls | [Controls] |
| Approval Authority | [Approver Name or Role] |
| Expiry Date | [Date] |
| Remediation Plan | [Plan and Target Date] |
| Review Status | [Open/Approved/Rejected/Expired/Closed] |

Emergency exceptions may be granted for urgent operational needs, provided that they are documented as soon as practicable, reviewed by Information Security, time-limited, and subject to retrospective approval.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur, including:

- New or updated cybersecurity standards, directives, or guidance from Saudi authorities.
- Changes to Saudi personal data protection obligations.
- Significant changes to [Organisation Name] business operations, systems, data processing activities, or technology architecture.
- Major cybersecurity incidents, personal data breaches, audit findings, or regulatory findings.
- Material changes in threat landscape, risk exposure, outsourcing arrangements, or cloud adoption.
- Organisational restructuring or changes in accountability.

The Chief Information Security Officer is responsible for maintaining this Policy and coordinating reviews with relevant stakeholders, including Privacy, Legal, Compliance, Risk Management, Internal Audit, IT, Human Resources, Procurement, and business representatives.

Policy updates shall be approved according to [Organisation Name] governance requirements. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with document retention requirements.

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Approved By |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [Approval Date] | Initial release | [Approver Name or Committee] |

PDPL-021.title: Public Authority Disclosure Procedure
PDPL-021.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [PDPL-PROC-PA-DISC] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer | [Effective Date] | Saudi Personal Data Protection Law | Internal |

## Purpose

This procedure defines how [Organisation Name] receives, validates, approves, documents, and limits disclosures of personal data to public authorities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia or other competent authorities where legally applicable.

The procedure is intended to ensure that any disclosure to a public authority is:

- Lawful, necessary, and proportionate.
- Limited to the specific data required for the stated official purpose.
- Properly authorised before release, except where urgent legal circumstances require immediate action.
- Recorded in a manner that supports accountability, auditability, and regulatory inspection.
- Handled securely throughout request intake, review, transmission, and closure.
- Assessed for any impact on the rights and interests of data subjects.

## Scope

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, temporary workers, service providers, and business units of [Organisation Name] that receive or handle requests from public authorities for access to, copies of, confirmation of, preservation of, or disclosure of personal data.

This procedure covers requests from, or on behalf of, public authorities including but not limited to:

- Courts, judicial authorities, and dispute resolution bodies.
- Law enforcement and investigation authorities.
- Regulators and supervisory bodies.
- Ministries, government departments, municipalities, and public agencies.
- Tax, customs, labour, immigration, social insurance, and similar official bodies.
- Authorities requesting data for public interest, public health, safety, national security, fraud prevention, or statutory inspection purposes.

This procedure applies to personal data processed by [Organisation Name], whether held in:

- Business applications and databases.
- Customer relationship management systems.
- Human resources and payroll systems.
- Finance, procurement, and vendor management systems.
- Logs, monitoring records, access records, and security event data.
- Email, collaboration platforms, case management tools, and document repositories.
- Physical records, archives, and backup media.

This procedure applies to both routine and non-routine disclosures, including:

- Formal written demands, notices, summonses, warrants, court orders, inspection requests, and regulatory information requests.
- Requests received by email, secure portal, official letter, courier, in person, or through a recognised government platform.
- Urgent verbal or informal requests that require validation and subsequent written confirmation.
- Requests for direct system access, bulk data extracts, recurring reports, or preservation of records.

This procedure does not authorise employees to independently disclose personal data to a public authority. All such disclosures must follow this procedure unless an approved emergency exception applies.

## Prerequisites & Inputs

Before processing a disclosure request, the receiving team must ensure the following prerequisites and inputs are available or obtained.

### Required prerequisites

| Prerequisite | Description | Responsible Party |
|---|---|---|
| Designated intake channel | Public authority requests must be routed to [Designated Intake Email/System] or the Legal Department. | All staff |
| Request register | A central log must exist to track request receipt, assessment, approval, disclosure, and closure. | Data Protection Office |
| Authorised approvers | The organisation must maintain a list of roles authorised to approve disclosures. | Legal Department / Data Protection Officer |
| Data inventory | Relevant systems and data owners must be identifiable to determine where requested personal data is held. | Data Owners |
| Secure transfer method | Approved channels must be available for transferring personal data to authorised recipients. | Information Security |
| Retention rules | Retention requirements for request records and disclosed data packages must be defined. | Records Management |
| Escalation contacts | Legal, Privacy, Security, Executive, and Communications contacts must be current. | Data Protection Officer |

### Required inputs from the public authority

The requester must provide sufficient information to enable [Organisation Name] to validate the request and assess its scope.

| Required Input | Expected Detail |
|---|---|
| Authority identity | Name of public authority, department, address, and official contact details. |
| Requester identity | Name, title, employee or badge number where applicable, official email, phone number, and signature or seal where applicable. |
| Legal or official basis | The formal authority or official purpose under which the request is made. |
| Requested data | Clear description of the personal data requested, including data subjects, identifiers, date ranges, systems, transaction references, or case numbers. |
| Purpose of disclosure | The investigation, inspection, proceeding, statutory function, or official reason for requesting the data. |
| Deadline | Required response date and whether urgency is claimed. |
| Format and method | Preferred format for production and authorised method for delivery. |
| Confidentiality requirement | Any restriction on notifying data subjects, internal staff, or third parties. |
| Recipient details | The individual, office, portal, or secure endpoint authorised to receive the data. |

### Minimum internal inputs

| Internal Input | Source |
|---|---|
| Public Authority Disclosure Request Form | Receiving employee or Legal Department |
| Identity and authority validation evidence | Legal Department |
| Data location and owner confirmation | Data Owner |
| Necessity and proportionality assessment | Data Protection Officer and Legal Department |
| Security transfer assessment | Information Security |
| Approval record | Authorised approver |
| Disclosure package checklist | Data Owner / Records Management |
| Closure record | Data Protection Office |

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

1. **Receive and route the request**

 1.1. Any employee receiving a request from a public authority must immediately forward it to [Designated Intake Email/System] and notify the Legal Department.

 1.2. The receiving employee must not disclose, confirm, deny, extract, preserve, delete, alter, or discuss personal data in response to the request unless instructed by the Legal Department.

 1.3. If the request is received verbally, in person, by telephone, or through an informal channel, the employee must:
 
 - Record the requester’s name, role, authority, contact details, time, date, and stated purpose.
 - Ask the requester to submit the request through an official written channel.
 - Notify the Legal Department immediately.
 - Avoid confirming whether [Organisation Name] holds the requested personal data unless authorised.

 1.4. If the request appears urgent and involves risk to life, safety, public security, serious crime, or imminent harm, the employee must escalate immediately under the emergency escalation process in this procedure.

2. **Log the request**

 2.1. The Data Protection Office must create an entry in the Public Authority Disclosure Register within one business day of receipt, or immediately for urgent requests.

 2.2. The register entry must include, at minimum:

 | Field | Required Entry |
 |---|---|
 | Request ID | Unique reference number assigned by [Register/System]. |
 | Date and time received | Actual receipt date and time. |
 | Receiving person or channel | Employee, email, portal, courier, or office location. |
 | Public authority | Name and department of requesting authority. |
 | Requester | Name, title, contact details, and official identifier where available. |
 | Request type | Court order, regulator request, law enforcement request, inspection request, preservation request, emergency request, or other. |
 | Data subjects | Names, identifiers, account numbers, employee IDs, customer IDs, or other references where available. |
 | Requested data | Summary of data requested. |
 | Requested date range | Applicable period covered by the request. |
 | Deadline | Response deadline and urgency rating. |
 | Assigned owner | Legal case owner and supporting data owner. |
 | Status | New, validating, assessing, approved, rejected, disclosed, closed, or escalated. |

 2.3. All request documents, envelopes, emails, screenshots, portal notices, and related communications must be saved in the designated case folder.

3. **Acknowledge receipt where appropriate**

 3.1. The Legal Department must determine whether acknowledgment is appropriate or required.

 3.2. If acknowledgment is sent, it must:
 
 - Confirm receipt only.
 - Avoid committing to disclosure before assessment.
 - Request clarification or missing information where needed.
 - Use official contact details verified independently where possible.
 - Preserve any required confidentiality.

 3.3. Acknowledgment must be logged in the case file.

4. **Validate the identity and authority of the requester**

 4.1. The Legal Department must validate that the request comes from a genuine public authority and from an authorised official or office.

 4.2. Validation must use one or more of the following methods, depending on request sensitivity:

 | Validation Method | When to Use |
 |---|---|
 | Official government domain or portal verification | For routine written or portal-based requests. |
 | Call-back to published official number | For sensitive, urgent, unusual, or high-volume requests. |
 | Verification of seal, signature, reference number, or case number | For formal orders, notices, or summonses. |
 | Confirmation with known regulatory liaison | For regular supervisory or inspection requests. |
 | Review by external counsel | For unusual, cross-border, high-risk, or disputed requests. |

 4.3. If identity or authority cannot be validated, the request must be placed on hold and no personal data may be disclosed.

 4.4. Suspected fraudulent requests must be escalated to Information Security and handled as a potential security incident.

5. **Assess the legal and official basis**

 5.1. The Legal Department must assess whether the request has a valid legal, regulatory, judicial, supervisory, or official basis.

 5.2. The assessment must consider:

 - Whether the authority has jurisdiction over [Organisation Name], the data, the data subject, or the relevant activity.
 - Whether the request is mandatory, voluntary, investigatory, supervisory, judicial, or advisory.
 - Whether the request is sufficiently specific to identify the data sought.
 - Whether the deadline is legally binding or negotiable.
 - Whether disclosure is prohibited, restricted, or subject to additional conditions.
 - Whether the request conflicts with contractual confidentiality, professional secrecy, employment obligations, banking, health, telecommunications, or sector-specific restrictions.
 - Whether the request involves personal data located outside Saudi Arabia or recipients outside Saudi Arabia.
 - Whether the request requires data subject notification or prohibits notification.

 5.3. Where the request is unclear, overly broad, informal, or unsupported, the Legal Department must seek clarification, narrowing, formalisation, or additional documentation before disclosure.

 5.4. If the organisation is not legally required to disclose the data and voluntary disclosure is being considered, the Data Protection Officer must assess whether the disclosure is lawful, necessary, proportionate, and aligned with the rights and interests of the data subjects.

6. **Classify the request risk level**

 6.1. The Legal Department, in consultation with the Data Protection Officer, must assign a risk level.

 | Risk Level | Criteria | Minimum Approval |
 |---|---|---|
 | Low | Routine request from verified authority, limited dataset, clear official basis, no sensitive personal data, no confidentiality dispute. | Legal Department and Data Owner |
 | Medium | Request includes multiple data subjects, employee data, customer account data, moderate volume, unclear scope requiring interpretation, or tight deadline. | Legal Department, Data Protection Officer, and Data Owner |
 | High | Request includes sensitive personal data, large-scale data, direct system access, cross-border issues, secrecy order, disputed authority, media sensitivity, senior executive data, or significant impact on individuals. | General Counsel, Data Protection Officer, Information Security, and relevant Executive Owner |
 | Emergency | Immediate risk to life, safety, public security, serious crime, or imminent harm where delay may cause serious consequences. | Emergency approver with retrospective Legal and Data Protection Officer review |

 6.2. The assigned risk level must be documented in the register with rationale.

7. **Identify relevant data owners and systems**

 7.1. The Data Protection Office must identify the relevant Data Owner, System Owner, and Records Owner.

 7.2. Data Owners must confirm:
 
 - Whether [Organisation Name] holds the requested data.
 - Which systems, repositories, files, archives, or backups may contain the data.
 - The applicable data format and extraction options.
 - Whether the data includes third-party personal data not requested.
 - Whether the data includes sensitive personal data.
 - Whether the data includes privileged, confidential, proprietary, or legally protected information.
 - Whether the data can be isolated to the specific scope of the request.

 7.3. Data Owners must not extract or transmit data until the request is approved, except for preservation steps authorised by Legal.

8. **Preserve relevant records if required**

 8.1. If the request requires preservation, legal hold, suspension of deletion, or retention of relevant data, the Legal Department must issue a preservation instruction to relevant teams.

 8.2. The preservation instruction must specify:
 
 - Request ID.
 - Data subjects or identifiers.
 - Systems and records covered.
 - Date range.
 - Actions required.
 - Prohibited actions, including deletion, alteration, overwriting, or destruction.
 - Duration or review date.
 - Contact point for questions.

 8.3. Information Technology and Data Owners must confirm implementation of preservation instructions.

 8.4. Preservation must be limited to the scope required and must not be used as a basis for broader disclosure unless separately approved.

9. **Perform necessity, proportionality, and data minimisation review**

 9.1. The Data Protection Officer must review the requested disclosure to ensure it is limited to what is necessary for the stated official purpose.

 9.2. The review must address:

 | Assessment Area | Review Question |
 |---|---|
 | Specificity | Is the request clear enough to identify the required data? |
 | Purpose alignment | Does each category of data relate to the stated official purpose? |
 | Date range | Is the requested period limited and justified? |
 | Data subject scope | Are only relevant individuals included? |
 | Data category scope | Are unnecessary fields, attachments, metadata, logs, or comments excluded? |
 | Sensitive data | Is sensitive personal data requested, and is it strictly necessary? |
 | Third-party data | Can third-party personal data be redacted or excluded? |
 | Alternatives | Can confirmation, summary, anonymised, pseudonymised, or narrowed data satisfy the request? |
 | Impact | Could disclosure create disproportionate harm to data subjects? |

 9.3. If the request is too broad, the Legal Department must seek narrowing or clarification unless disclosure in full is legally mandatory and confirmed by Legal.

 9.4. Where redaction is appropriate, the Data Owner must prepare a redacted version and retain a record of the redaction rationale.

10. **Assess data subject notification requirements**

 10.1. The Data Protection Officer and Legal Department must determine whether affected data subjects should be notified of the disclosure.

 10.2. Notification must not be made where:
 
 - The public authority validly prohibits notification.
 - Notification would compromise an investigation, inspection, legal proceeding, public safety, national security, or another legitimate official purpose.
 - Notification is not legally required and would create unjustified risk.
 - Legal advice confirms notification should be deferred.

 10.3. Where notification is appropriate, the notice must be accurate and must not disclose confidential authority information. It should include:
 
 - The type of authority request received.
 - Categories of personal data disclosed.
 - Purpose of disclosure, where permitted.
 - Date or approximate timing of disclosure.
 - Contact point for questions.
 - Any rights available to the individual, subject to lawful restrictions.

 10.4. The decision to notify, defer, or withhold notification must be recorded.

11. **Prepare the disclosure package**

 11.1. The Data Owner must prepare the disclosure package only after approval to proceed with extraction.

 11.2. The package must contain only approved data fields, records, attachments, and date ranges.

 11.3. The Data Owner must apply data minimisation techniques, including where applicable:
 
 - Removing unrelated data subjects.
 - Redacting irrelevant personal data.
 - Excluding internal notes not requested.
 - Excluding privileged legal advice.
 - Removing unnecessary metadata.
 - Replacing direct identifiers with case references where permitted.
 - Providing summary information where accepted by the authority.

 11.4. The disclosure package must be labelled with:
 
 - Request ID.
 - Public authority name.
 - Confidentiality marking.
 - Date of preparation.
 - Prepared by.
 - Approved scope reference.
 - Page count, file count, or record count.

 11.5. The Data Owner must complete the Disclosure Package Checklist.

 | Checklist Item | Completed By | Evidence Required |
 |---|---|---|
 | Data matches approved scope | Data Owner | Extract query, file list, or sampling record |
 | Date range verified | Data Owner | Query parameters or search criteria |
 | Irrelevant data removed | Data Owner | Redaction log or exclusion note |
 | Sensitive data specifically approved | Data Protection Officer | Approval record |
 | Privileged or protected content reviewed | Legal Department | Legal review confirmation |
 | File integrity checked | Information Security or Data Owner | Hash value or checksum for high-risk packages |
 | Malware scan completed | Information Security or Data Owner | Scan result |
 | Secure transfer method selected | Information Security | Transfer approval |
 | Recipient details verified | Legal Department | Verification evidence |

12. **Review and approve the disclosure**

 12.1. The Legal Department must review the proposed disclosure package against the validated request.

 12.2. The Data Protection Officer must review the package for minimisation, sensitivity, proportionality, notification considerations, and documentation completeness.

 12.3. Information Security must review high-risk disclosures, bulk transfers, direct access requests, encrypted media, and any disclosure involving sensitive personal data.

 12.4. Approval must be documented before disclosure using the Public Authority Disclosure Approval Form.

 | Approval Field | Required Content |
 |---|---|
 | Request ID | Unique request reference. |
 | Authority | Name of requesting public authority. |
 | Data subjects | Identifiers or categories. |
 | Data approved for disclosure | Specific categories, files, fields, or report names. |
 | Exclusions | Data withheld, redacted, or narrowed. |
 | Legal basis decision | Summary of Legal assessment. |
 | Privacy assessment | Summary of necessity and proportionality review. |
 | Security method | Approved transfer mechanism. |
 | Notification decision | Notify, defer, do not notify, or not applicable. |
 | Approvers | Names, roles, dates, and approvals. |
 | Conditions | Any limitations, confidentiality statements, or handling instructions. |

 12.5. The disclosure must not proceed if any required approval is missing, unless handled under the emergency procedure.

13. **Select and validate secure transmission method**

 13.1. Information Security must ensure the disclosure method is appropriate to the sensitivity and volume of data.

 13.2. Approved methods include:

 | Disclosure Method | Permitted Use | Security Requirements |
 |---|---|---|
 | Official government secure portal | Preferred where available and validated. | Access by authorised user, upload confirmation retained. |
 | Encrypted email | Low to medium sensitivity and limited volume. | Strong encryption, verified recipient, separate password channel. |
 | Secure file transfer platform | Medium to high sensitivity or larger files. | Access expiry, recipient authentication, download logging. |
 | Encrypted removable media | Only where required by authority or approved by Information Security. | Encryption, chain of custody, courier tracking, password separation. |
 | Physical sealed documents | Where original or certified copies are required. | Tamper-evident packaging, courier or hand delivery receipt. |
 | Direct system access | Exceptional cases only. | Executive approval, least privilege, time-limited access, monitoring, audit logs. |

 13.3. Personal email, consumer messaging apps, unsecured removable media, unverified portals, and unofficial cloud links must not be used.

 13.4. Recipient address, portal, user account, or delivery location must be independently verified before transmission.

14. **Transmit the approved disclosure**

 14.1. The authorised sender must transmit only the approved disclosure package through the approved channel.

 14.2. Transmission must include a cover note, unless prohibited, stating:
 
 - The request ID or authority reference.
 - That the disclosure is provided in response to the specific request.
 - Any limitations on scope.
 - Any confidentiality or handling restrictions.
 - Contact point for clarification.

 14.3. The sender must retain proof of transmission, such as:
 
 - Portal submission receipt.
 - Secure transfer log.
 - Email delivery receipt.
 - Courier tracking and delivery confirmation.
 - Signed handover receipt.
 - Chain-of-custody record.

 14.4. For encrypted files, the password or decryption key must be sent through a separate approved channel.

 14.5. Where disclosure is made in person, two authorised representatives should attend where practicable, and a signed receipt must be obtained.

15. **Handle direct access requests**

 15.1. Requests from public authorities for direct access to systems, databases, live dashboards, APIs, logs, monitoring tools, or premises containing personal data must be treated as high risk.

 15.2. Direct access may only be granted where Legal confirms the authority is valid and the request cannot reasonably be satisfied through a controlled extract or supervised review.

 15.3. Before access is granted, the following controls must be applied:

 - Written approval from General Counsel, Data Protection Officer, Information Security, and relevant Executive Owner.
 - Named authorised public authority users only.
 - Least privilege access limited to approved data.
 - Defined start and end time.
 - No onward download, export, copy, screenshot, or print capability unless explicitly approved.
 - Supervised access where practicable.
 - Logging and monitoring of all access activity.
 - Immediate access removal at the end of the approved period.
 - Post-access review of logs.

 15.4. Standing or indefinite access to personal data by a public authority is not permitted unless specifically approved through a separate governance arrangement, legal review, privacy review, and security risk assessment.

16. **Handle emergency disclosures**

 16.1. Emergency disclosure may be considered where delay is likely to create serious risk to life, safety, public security, prevention of serious crime, or imminent harm.

 16.2. The employee receiving the emergency request must immediately contact:
 
 - Legal Department.
 - Data Protection Officer.
 - Information Security, if security logs, account data, or urgent transfer is involved.
 - [Emergency Executive Contact], if Legal or the Data Protection Officer is unavailable.

 16.3. Before emergency disclosure, the approver must make reasonable efforts to validate:
 
 - The requester’s identity.
 - The public authority’s official role.
 - The nature of the emergency.
 - The minimum data needed.
 - The authorised recipient and secure transfer method.

 16.4. Emergency disclosure must be limited to the minimum information necessary to address the emergency.

 16.5. A written request or confirmation must be obtained as soon as practicable after the disclosure.

 16.6. The Data Protection Officer and Legal Department must conduct a retrospective review within two business days and document:
 
 - Why emergency handling was necessary.
 - What data was disclosed.
 - Who approved and transmitted it.
 - Whether further data subject notification, containment, or corrective action is required.

17. **Respond to overbroad, invalid, or objectionable requests**

 17.1. If a request is overbroad, unclear, unsupported, invalid, or beyond the apparent authority of the requester, the Legal Department must determine the appropriate response.

 17.2. Potential responses include:
 
 - Requesting clarification.
 - Asking for formal written authority.
 - Seeking narrowing of scope.
 - Proposing an alternative format or summary.
 - Withholding unrelated or excessive personal data.
 - Challenging or objecting to the request through lawful channels.
 - Seeking external legal advice.
 - Escalating to executive management.

 17.3. Data must not be disclosed while an objection, clarification, or legal challenge is pending unless Legal confirms disclosure is required.

18. **Handle cross-border considerations**

 18.1. If the public authority request involves disclosure to an authority outside Saudi Arabia, transfer through a foreign platform, access by persons outside Saudi Arabia, or production of data stored outside Saudi Arabia, the Legal Department and Data Protection Officer must conduct an additional transfer assessment.

 18.2. The assessment must consider:
 
 - Whether the foreign authority has a valid legal basis to request the data.
 - Whether Saudi law, local law, contract terms, or sector rules restrict the disclosure.
 - Whether transfer outside Saudi Arabia is permitted for the stated purpose.
 - Whether approval, notification, contractual protections, or additional safeguards are needed.
 - Whether the data can be anonymised, minimised, or provided through a Saudi-based channel.
 - Whether data subjects may face increased risk.

 18.3. Cross-border disclosure must not proceed until Legal and the Data Protection Officer approve the transfer route and safeguards.

19. **Update the disclosure register**

 19.1. After transmission, the Data Protection Office must update the register with:

 | Field | Required Entry |
 |---|---|
 | Disclosure date and time | When the data was transmitted or handed over. |
 | Data disclosed | Summary of categories, files, fields, records, and date ranges. |
 | Data volume | Number of files, records, pages, or approximate size. |
 | Recipient | Verified authority recipient, office, portal, or delivery location. |
 | Transfer method | Approved method used. |
 | Security controls | Encryption, portal, courier, access control, or other safeguards. |
 | Approvals | Names, roles, and approval dates. |
 | Proof of delivery | Receipt, portal confirmation, email log, or courier record. |
 | Notification decision | Notified, deferred, prohibited, not required, or pending. |
 | Outstanding actions | Clarifications, follow-up requests, legal holds, or notification tasks. |
 | Closure status | Open, pending confirmation, closed, or escalated. |

 19.2. The register must be kept accurate and complete at all times.

20. **Notify data subjects where approved**

 20.1. If notification is approved, the Data Protection Officer must coordinate the notification with Legal and relevant business teams.

 20.2. Notification must be sent through an appropriate channel and must be recorded.

 20.3. If notification is deferred, the Data Protection Officer must set a review date and document the reason for deferral.

 20.4. If notification is prohibited or not appropriate, the reason must be recorded in the case file.

21. **Close the request**

 21.1. The Legal Department may close the request when:
 
 - The request has been fulfilled, rejected, withdrawn, superseded, or otherwise resolved.
 - Required disclosures and proof of delivery are recorded.
 - Preservation or legal hold status is confirmed.
 - Data subject notification decision is recorded.
 - Any follow-up communications are complete.
 - The case file contains all required evidence.

 21.2. The Data Protection Office must mark the register entry as closed and record the closure date.

 21.3. If the request results in a recurring disclosure obligation, recurring reporting arrangement, inspection programme, or ongoing authority access, the case must be escalated for governance approval rather than closed as a one-time disclosure.

22. **Conduct post-disclosure review for medium, high-risk, and emergency cases**

 22.1. The Data Protection Officer must conduct a post-disclosure review for:
 
 - Medium-risk disclosures.
 - High-risk disclosures.
 - Emergency disclosures.
 - Bulk disclosures.
 - Disclosures involving sensitive personal data.
 - Any disclosure where issues, delays, disputes, or errors occurred.

 22.2. The review must determine whether:
 
 - The procedure was followed.
 - The data disclosed matched the approved scope.
 - Transmission evidence is complete.
 - The authority received the data successfully.
 - Any excessive or erroneous disclosure occurred.
 - Additional notification, remediation, or reporting is required.
 - Process improvements are needed.

 22.3. Any suspected unauthorised, excessive, or erroneous disclosure must be escalated immediately as a potential personal data incident.

## Roles & RACI

### Role descriptions

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Receiving Employee | Routes requests immediately, avoids unauthorised disclosure, records initial details, escalates urgent matters. |
| Legal Department | Validates authority, assesses legal basis, manages communications with public authorities, approves or rejects requests, issues preservation instructions. |
| Data Protection Officer | Assesses privacy impact, necessity, proportionality, minimisation, notification, documentation completeness, and compliance with personal data obligations. |
| Data Owner | Identifies, extracts, reviews, minimises, redacts, and validates relevant data within approved scope. |
| System Owner | Supports system searches, access controls, extraction, logs, and preservation activities. |
| Information Security | Approves secure transfer methods, validates security controls, supports fraud detection, monitors direct access, and handles suspected security incidents. |
| Records Management | Ensures records are retained, archived, and disposed of according to retention requirements. |
| General Counsel | Approves high-risk, disputed, cross-border, or legally complex disclosures. |
| Executive Owner | Approves high-impact disclosures involving major business risk, direct system access, sensitive stakeholder groups, or reputational exposure. |
| Communications Lead | Supports external or internal communications only where authorised by Legal. |
| External Counsel | Provides specialist advice where required for complex, disputed, cross-border, or sector-specific matters. |

### RACI matrix

| Activity | Receiving Employee | Legal Department | Data Protection Officer | Data Owner | System Owner | Information Security | General Counsel | Executive Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Receive and route request | R | A | C | I | I | I | I | I |
| Log request | I | C | A/R | I | I | I | I | I |
| Validate authority | I | A/R | C | I | I | C | C | I |
| Assess legal basis | I | A/R | C | I | I | I | C | I |
| Assign risk level | I | R | A/R | C | I | C | C | I |
| Identify data sources | I | C | C | A/R | R | C | I | I |
| Preserve records | I | A/R | C | R | R | C | I | I |
| Perform minimisation review | I | C | A/R | R | C | C | I | I |
| Prepare disclosure package | I | C | C | A/R | R | C | I | I |
| Approve low-risk disclosure | I | A/R | C | R | C | I | I | I |
| Approve medium-risk disclosure | I | R | A/R | R | C | C | I | I |
| Approve high-risk disclosure | I | R | R | C | C | R | A | A/R |
| Approve emergency disclosure | I | A/R | R | R | C | C | C | A/R |
| Approve secure transfer method | I | C | C | I | C | A/R | I | I |
| Transmit approved package | I | A | C | R | C | R | I | I |
| Notify data subjects | I | C | A/R | C | I | I | I | C |
| Close case | I | A/R | R | C | C | C | I | I |
| Conduct post-disclosure review | I | C | A/R | C | C | C | I | I |

RACI key: R - Responsible, A - Accountable, C - Consulted, I - Informed.

## Records & Outputs

The following records must be created and retained for each public authority disclosure request, as applicable.

| Record / Output | Description | Owner | Minimum Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public Authority Disclosure Register entry | Central log of request handling, approvals, disclosure, and closure. | Data Protection Office | [Retention Period] |
| Original request | Written request, order, notice, email, portal notice, letter, or verbal request record. | Legal Department | [Retention Period] |
| Validation evidence | Evidence confirming authority identity and requester authorisation. | Legal Department | [Retention Period] |
| Legal assessment | Decision on authority, legal basis, jurisdiction, and conditions. | Legal Department | [Retention Period] |
| Necessity and proportionality assessment | Privacy review of scope, minimisation, sensitivity, and impact. | Data Protection Officer | [Retention Period] |
| Risk classification record | Documented risk rating and rationale. | Data Protection Office | [Retention Period] |
| Preservation instruction | Legal hold or preservation notice where applicable. | Legal Department | [Retention Period] |
| Data source confirmation | Confirmation of systems searched and data located. | Data Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Extraction record | Query criteria, search parameters, file list, or export record. | Data Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Redaction log | Record of data removed, masked, or withheld and rationale. | Data Owner / Legal Department | [Retention Period] |
| Disclosure package checklist | Confirmation that approved data package was reviewed and controlled. | Data Owner | [Retention Period] |
| Approval form | Evidence of required approvals before disclosure. | Data Protection Office | [Retention Period] |
| Transfer evidence | Portal receipt, email log, courier record, chain of custody, or handover receipt. | Legal Department / Information Security | [Retention Period] |
| Cover note | Written response sent with disclosed data. | Legal Department | [Retention Period] |
| Data subject notification record | Evidence of notification, deferral, prohibition, or decision not to notify. | Data Protection Officer | [Retention Period] |
| Direct access log | Access approval, user details, monitoring logs, and termination evidence. | Information Security | [Retention Period] |
| Emergency retrospective review | Post-event review for emergency disclosure. | Data Protection Officer / Legal Department | [Retention Period] |
| Closure record | Final status, closure date, and outstanding actions. | Data Protection Office | [Retention Period] |
| Lessons learned record | Improvement actions from post-disclosure review. | Data Protection Officer | [Retention Period] |

Records must be stored in [Case Management System/Repository] with access restricted to authorised Legal, Data Protection, Information Security, and relevant business personnel. Records must not be stored in personal drives, local desktops, informal messaging tools, or unmanaged repositories.

### Required outputs

Each completed case must produce, as applicable:

- Completed register entry.
- Validated request file.
- Legal assessment.
- Privacy assessment.
- Approved disclosure package or rejection response.
- Evidence of secure transmission or documented non-disclosure decision.
- Notification decision.
- Closure record.
- Corrective action record where required.

## Exceptions & Escalation

### Exceptions

Exceptions to this procedure are permitted only where justified, documented, and approved by the appropriate authority. Common exception scenarios include:

| Exception Scenario | Required Action | Approval Required |
|---|---|---|
| Emergency disclosure before full documentation | Limit disclosure to minimum necessary and complete retrospective review within two business days. | Legal Department or Emergency Executive Contact |
| Request received outside business hours | Escalate using [After-Hours Contact Process]. | On-call Legal or Executive Contact |
| Public authority refuses written request | Validate identity, record circumstances, disclose only if Legal confirms lawful necessity. | General Counsel |
| Transfer method mandated by authority is not secure | Seek alternative method or compensating controls. | Legal Department and Information Security |
| Deadline cannot be met | Seek extension or phased response. | Legal Department |
| Data cannot be isolated exactly | Use redaction, sampling, summary, or seek narrowing. | Data Protection Officer and Legal Department |
| Direct access requested | Treat as high risk and apply direct access controls. | General Counsel and Executive Owner |
| Cross-border authority request | Conduct additional transfer assessment. | General Counsel and Data Protection Officer |
| Conflict with other legal or contractual duties | Obtain legal advice and escalate. | General Counsel |

All exceptions must be recorded in the case file and the Public Authority Disclosure Register.

### Escalation triggers

The request must be escalated to General Counsel, the Data Protection Officer, Information Security, and the relevant Executive Owner where any of the following apply:

- The request involves sensitive personal data.
- The request involves children, vulnerable individuals, employees, executives, board members, or high-profile persons.
- The request is broad, vague, unusual, informal, or unsupported.
- The request seeks bulk data, historical archives, system logs, communications content, or behavioural monitoring data.
- The request seeks direct system access, live monitoring, credentials, API access, or standing access.
- The request is from an authority outside Saudi Arabia or involves cross-border disclosure.
- The request conflicts with another law, court order, contractual duty, or confidentiality obligation.
- The authority prohibits notification to the data subject or imposes secrecy restrictions.
- The request may create significant harm to individuals.
- The request may attract media, political, labour, customer, investor, or reputational sensitivity.
- The request appears fraudulent, coercive, or outside normal official channels.
- The organisation believes excessive data may have been disclosed.
- A deadline cannot be met without bypassing required checks.

### Incident escalation

If personal data is disclosed without authorisation, disclosed to the wrong recipient, disclosed in excess of approval, lost during transfer, accessed by unauthorised persons, or otherwise compromised, the matter must be reported immediately through [Incident Reporting Channel] and handled under the Personal Data Incident Response Procedure.

The disclosure case must not be closed until incident response actions are completed or formally assigned.

## Review

This procedure must be reviewed at least annually and whenever any of the following occur:

- Material changes to Saudi personal data protection requirements.
- New regulatory guidance affecting public authority disclosures.
- Significant organisational changes, including mergers, restructuring, new business lines, or new systems.
- Changes to public authority request channels, government platforms, or recurring reporting obligations.
- A significant public authority disclosure incident or near miss.
- Audit findings, regulator feedback, or management review requiring improvement.
- Changes to data retention, classification, encryption, or transfer standards.

The Data Protection Officer owns the review process and must coordinate input from Legal, Information Security, Records Management, and relevant business units.

Each review must verify that:

- Intake channels and escalation contacts remain current.
- The disclosure register is complete and consistently used.
- Approval thresholds remain appropriate.
- Secure transfer methods remain effective.
- Records are retained and access-controlled.
- Exceptions are tracked and addressed.
- Staff handling requests are trained.
- Lessons learned from disclosures and incidents are incorporated.

Changes to this procedure must be approved by the Data Protection Officer and General Counsel before publication. The current approved version must be made available to all relevant employees through [Policy Portal/Document Repository].

PDPL-022.title: Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) Template
PDPL-022.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer | [Effective Date] | Saudi Personal Data Protection Law | Confidential - Internal Use |

## Purpose

This Data Sharing Agreement template is used to document, approve and govern domestic sharing of personal data between [Organisation Name] and another entity operating within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

The template is intended for data-sharing relationships where personal data is disclosed, exchanged, made accessible, synchronised, reported, or otherwise transferred between organisations for a defined business, operational, legal, or public interest purpose. It helps ensure that personal data sharing is lawful, transparent, limited to what is necessary, protected by appropriate safeguards, and subject to clear accountability between the parties.

This template should be completed before any new domestic personal data sharing activity begins, and before any material change to an existing sharing arrangement, including changes to purpose, data categories, data subjects, access method, retention period, receiving party, processing location, or security arrangements.

This template may be used for:

- Controller-to-controller domestic data sharing.
- Sharing personal data with another Saudi-based entity for a joint or related purpose.
- Sharing personal data with government, regulatory, healthcare, financial, employment, education, logistics, insurance, or service partner entities where the receiving party determines or contributes to the purpose of use.
- Recurrent or systematic disclosures of personal data, including API integration, secure file exchange, portal access, shared workflow platforms, or scheduled reporting.

This template is not intended to replace a data processing agreement where a service provider processes personal data only on behalf of [Organisation Name] and does not determine its own purpose for using the data. Where the relationship includes both data sharing and processing services, Legal and the Privacy Office must determine whether both agreement types are required.

## Instructions

1. **Complete all required fields** before submitting the DSA for review and approval.
2. **Use plain, specific language**. Avoid broad descriptions such as “business purposes”, “customer data”, or “as required”. Clearly state the actual purpose, data categories, recipient, frequency, access method, and retention period.
3. **Confirm the legal basis** for the sharing activity before data is shared. The agreement must identify why sharing is permitted, including consent where required, contractual necessity, legal obligation, public interest, vital interest, legitimate interest where applicable, or another lawful basis approved by Legal and the Privacy Office.
4. **Assess whether sensitive personal data is involved**, including health data, biometric data, genetic data, financial data, credit data, location data, criminal or security-related data, data concerning children, or other data requiring heightened protection.
5. **Do not include more personal data than necessary**. Data fields must be limited to what is directly needed for the stated purpose.
6. **Verify transparency requirements**. The relevant privacy notice, collection notice, consent wording, or other data subject communication must support the proposed sharing unless an approved exception applies.
7. **Confirm domestic scope**. This template is for data sharing within Saudi Arabia. If any personal data will be accessed from, stored in, supported from, transferred to, or viewed outside Saudi Arabia, stop and consult the Privacy Office before proceeding.
8. **Complete a privacy risk review** for sharing that is new, high volume, involves sensitive personal data, uses automated decision-making, affects vulnerable individuals, or may significantly affect individuals’ rights or interests.
9. **Attach supporting documents**, such as privacy impact assessments, security assessment results, data flow diagrams, consent language, privacy notice excerpts, system architecture, API specifications, encryption details, or recipient due diligence results.
10. **Obtain all required approvals** listed in the Approval / Routing section before execution or operational launch.
11. **Keep the signed DSA and supporting records** in the approved contract and privacy records repository.
12. **Review the agreement at least annually**, or earlier if the purpose, recipient, data, legal basis, processing method, security controls, retention period, or applicable legal requirements change.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Agreement title | Text | Yes | Enter a clear name for the sharing arrangement, such as “Customer Eligibility Data Sharing with [Recipient Name]”. |
| DSA reference number | Text | Yes | Assign a unique reference number in accordance with [Organisation Name] document control or contract management procedures. |
| Date prepared | Date | Yes | Enter the date the draft DSA is created. |
| Requested effective date | Date | Yes | Enter the intended start date for data sharing. Data sharing must not begin until approval and execution are complete. |
| Review date | Date | Yes | Enter the next scheduled review date. Annual review is the default unless a shorter period is required due to risk. |
| Agreement expiry date | Date | Conditional | Required for time-limited sharing. If ongoing, state “Ongoing subject to annual review”. |
| Disclosing party legal name | Text | Yes | Enter the full legal name of the organisation disclosing personal data. |
| Disclosing party commercial registration or official identifier | Text | Yes | Enter the relevant registration number or official identifier. |
| Disclosing party address | Text | Yes | Enter the registered or principal business address in Saudi Arabia. |
| Disclosing party business owner | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the business accountable for the sharing activity. |
| Disclosing party privacy contact | Name / Email | Yes | Identify the Privacy Office or Data Protection Officer contact responsible for review and oversight. |
| Disclosing party security contact | Name / Email | Yes | Identify the information security contact responsible for technical and organisational safeguards. |
| Receiving party legal name | Text | Yes | Enter the full legal name of the receiving organisation. |
| Receiving party commercial registration or official identifier | Text | Yes | Enter the recipient’s registration number, licence number, or official identifier. |
| Receiving party address | Text | Yes | Enter the registered or principal business address in Saudi Arabia. |
| Receiving party business owner | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the recipient’s accountable business representative. |
| Receiving party privacy contact | Name / Email | Yes | Identify the recipient’s privacy or data protection contact. |
| Receiving party security contact | Name / Email | Yes | Identify the recipient’s information security contact. |
| Relationship type | Dropdown | Yes | Select: Controller-to-controller, joint purpose, statutory disclosure, regulated sector disclosure, public authority request, operational partner disclosure, or other approved relationship. |
| Description of the sharing activity | Long text | Yes | Describe what personal data will be shared, by whom, to whom, how often, through which channel, and for what operational outcome. |
| Business purpose | Long text | Yes | State the specific business, legal, regulatory, service delivery, public interest, or operational reason for sharing. Avoid vague or open-ended wording. |
| Lawful basis for sharing | Dropdown / Text | Yes | Identify the basis that permits the sharing. Include consent, contract performance, legal requirement, public interest, vital interest, approved legitimate interest, or another basis approved by Legal and the Privacy Office. |
| Supporting basis explanation | Long text | Yes | Explain why the selected basis applies and why the sharing is necessary for the stated purpose. |
| Consent required? | Yes / No / Not applicable | Yes | Indicate whether consent is required before sharing. If no, explain the approved reason. |
| Consent collection method | Text | Conditional | Required if consent is used. Describe where and how consent is collected, recorded, refreshed, and withdrawn. |
| Consent wording reference | Attachment / Link | Conditional | Required if consent is used. Attach or link to the approved consent statement. |
| Privacy notice updated? | Yes / No / Not applicable | Yes | Confirm whether the relevant privacy notice informs individuals about the sharing, recipient categories, purposes, rights, and contact channels. |
| Privacy notice reference | Attachment / Link | Conditional | Required unless an approved exception applies. Attach or link to the applicable privacy notice or collection notice. |
| Exception to transparency | Long text | Conditional | Required if the sharing is not described to individuals. Explain the approved legal or operational reason and attach Legal and Privacy Office approval. |
| Data subject categories | Multi-select / Text | Yes | Identify whose data will be shared, such as customers, employees, applicants, patients, students, suppliers, visitors, beneficiaries, users, or authorised representatives. |
| Estimated number of data subjects | Number / Range | Yes | Provide the expected number of individuals affected per month or per year. |
| Personal data categories | Long text / Table | Yes | List each data category and field to be shared. Use the detailed data field table below where possible. |
| Sensitive personal data included? | Yes / No | Yes | Select “Yes” if the sharing includes data needing heightened protection, such as health, biometric, genetic, financial, credit, location, criminal, security, children’s, or similarly sensitive data. |
| Sensitive personal data details | Long text | Conditional | Required if sensitive personal data is included. Describe the sensitive data and why it is necessary. |
| Children’s or vulnerable individuals’ data included? | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the sharing includes data relating to children, dependants, patients, elderly persons, persons with disabilities, or other vulnerable individuals. |
| Minimum necessary assessment completed? | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm that each data field has been assessed as necessary and proportionate for the stated purpose. |
| Data minimisation rationale | Long text | Yes | Explain why the data requested is the minimum needed. Identify any data excluded or masked to reduce risk. |
| Source system or record | Text | Yes | Identify the system, database, application, file store, or business process from which the personal data originates. |
| Receiving system or destination | Text | Yes | Identify where the receiving party will store, access, or process the data. |
| Data sharing method | Dropdown / Text | Yes | Specify the method, such as secure API, encrypted file transfer, secure portal, manual upload, system-to-system integration, secure email by exception, or physical transfer. |
| Frequency of sharing | Dropdown / Text | Yes | Specify one-time, real-time, daily, weekly, monthly, event-triggered, on request, or other defined frequency. |
| Data format | Text | Yes | State file, message, report, API payload, database extract, document type, or structured data format. |
| Encryption in transit | Text | Yes | Describe the encryption or secure channel used during transfer, such as approved secure protocol, VPN, private link, or equivalent secure mechanism. |
| Encryption at rest | Text | Yes | Describe how data will be encrypted or otherwise protected while stored by each party. |
| Identity and access controls | Long text | Yes | Describe user authentication, authorisation, privileged access controls, role-based access, access reviews, and removal of access when no longer needed. |
| Logging and monitoring | Long text | Yes | Describe audit logs, access logs, transfer logs, monitoring responsibilities, and log retention. |
| Segregation and environment controls | Long text | Conditional | Required where data will be processed in shared platforms, test environments, analytics environments, or multi-tenant systems. |
| Use in testing or development | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the data may be used outside production. Personal data should not be used in testing unless approved and appropriately masked or protected. |
| Data masking, pseudonymisation, or anonymisation | Long text | Conditional | Required where masking, pseudonymisation, aggregation, or anonymisation is used to reduce identifiability. |
| Automated decision-making or profiling | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the receiving party will use the data for automated decisions, scoring, profiling, eligibility checks, behavioural analysis, or similar activities. |
| Automated processing explanation | Long text | Conditional | Required if automated decision-making or profiling applies. Explain purpose, expected effect on individuals, safeguards, and human review process. |
| Artificial intelligence or advanced analytics use | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the data will be used for AI, machine learning, model training, analytics, prediction, segmentation, or decision support. |
| AI or analytics restrictions | Long text | Conditional | Required if AI or analytics applies. Define allowed and prohibited uses, model training restrictions, de-identification requirements, and output controls. |
| Sub-sharing permitted? | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the receiving party may share the data with any third party. Default should be “No” unless specifically approved. |
| Approved onward recipients | Table / Attachment | Conditional | Required if sub-sharing is permitted. List each onward recipient, purpose, location, data categories, safeguards, and approval evidence. |
| Cross-border access or transfer involved? | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether data will be accessed, stored, supported, backed up, or transferred outside Saudi Arabia. This domestic DSA must not be used to approve cross-border transfers. |
| Data localisation confirmation | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm that storage, access, support, backup, monitoring, and administration are within Saudi Arabia unless separately approved through the required transfer process. |
| Retention period by disclosing party | Text | Yes | State how long the disclosing party retains the data in relation to the sharing activity. |
| Retention period by receiving party | Text | Yes | State how long the receiving party may retain the shared data. Retention must be limited to the approved purpose. |
| Disposal or return method | Long text | Yes | Describe how the receiving party must return, delete, anonymise, or securely destroy the data at expiry, termination, or when no longer needed. |
| Evidence of disposal required? | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the receiving party must provide destruction certificates, deletion attestations, system logs, or other evidence. |
| Data accuracy responsibilities | Long text | Yes | Define how each party will ensure data is accurate, current, and complete for the sharing purpose. Include correction notification responsibilities. |
| Individual rights handling | Long text | Yes | Define how the parties will coordinate responses to access, correction, deletion, objection, withdrawal of consent, and other privacy requests. |
| Request response contact | Name / Email | Yes | Identify the operational mailbox or contact for rights requests involving shared data. |
| Complaint handling | Long text | Yes | Define how complaints from individuals about the sharing activity will be received, escalated, investigated, and resolved. |
| Incident notification requirement | Long text | Yes | Define how quickly each party must notify the other of suspected or confirmed data incidents involving shared data. Include minimum content for notification. |
| Incident contact | Name / Email / Phone | Yes | Identify 24/7 or business-hours incident contacts, depending on risk. |
| Regulatory notification responsibility | Long text | Yes | Define which party is responsible for assessing and making required notifications to authorities and affected individuals, and how the other party will support that process. |
| Security assessment completed? | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether Information Security has assessed the receiving party, transfer method, and system safeguards. |
| Privacy impact assessment completed? | Yes / No / Not required | Yes | Confirm whether a privacy risk assessment or privacy impact assessment has been completed. Attach evidence or rationale if not required. |
| Recipient due diligence completed? | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm that the recipient has been assessed for privacy, security, regulatory, and operational suitability. |
| Insurance or liability requirements | Text | Conditional | Include applicable insurance, indemnity, limitation of liability, or risk allocation requirements as advised by Legal. |
| Audit and assurance rights | Long text | Yes | Define whether [Organisation Name] may request evidence, conduct audits, review controls, or require independent assurance from the receiving party. |
| Permitted use restrictions | Long text | Yes | State that data may only be used for the approved purpose and may not be reused, sold, combined, enriched, profiled, disclosed, or retained for unrelated purposes unless approved in writing. |
| Confidentiality obligations | Long text | Yes | Confirm that personnel with access are bound by confidentiality obligations and receive appropriate privacy and security awareness training. |
| Operational owner | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the person responsible for day-to-day management of the sharing arrangement. |
| Contract owner | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the person responsible for contract recordkeeping, renewal, amendment, and termination management. |
| Privacy owner | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the Privacy Office representative responsible for privacy oversight. |
| Security owner | Name / Role | Yes | Identify the Information Security representative responsible for security oversight. |
| Key performance or compliance measures | Long text | Conditional | Include measures such as successful transfer rate, access review completion, incident reporting timeliness, deletion evidence, consent verification, or complaint handling. |
| Conditions precedent to launch | Long text | Yes | List all actions required before data sharing starts, such as signed agreement, privacy notice publication, consent capture, access provisioning, encryption validation, test transfer, and final approval. |
| Termination triggers | Long text | Yes | Define triggers such as purpose completion, expiry, breach, unlawful use, loss of lawful basis, security failure, regulatory direction, change in ownership, or withdrawal of required consent. |
