| Post-termination obligations | Long text | Yes | Define return, deletion, anonymisation, access revocation, certification, surviving confidentiality, audit, and incident support obligations. |
| Exceptions or deviations | Long text | Conditional | Document any exceptions to standard privacy, security, retention, localisation, or contractual requirements. Attach formal risk acceptance. |
| Supporting attachments | Attachment list | Conditional | Attach relevant documents, assessments, diagrams, approvals, consent wording, notices, technical specifications, and due diligence evidence. |
| Prepared by | Name / Role / Date | Yes | Identify the person completing the template. |
| Business owner acknowledgement | Signature / Date | Yes | Confirms business need, data accuracy, operational readiness, and accountability for the sharing activity. |
| Privacy Office review | Signature / Date | Yes | Confirms privacy requirements have been reviewed and required controls are defined. |
| Legal review | Signature / Date | Yes | Confirms contractual terms and lawful basis have been reviewed. |
| Information Security review | Signature / Date | Yes | Confirms technical and organisational safeguards have been reviewed. |
| Final approval | Signature / Date | Yes | Approval by the authorised signatory or delegated authority before execution and launch. |

**Detailed Data Field Register**

| Data Field | Data Category | Sensitive? | Source System | Recipient Use | Frequency Shared | Minimum Necessary Rationale | Retention by Recipient |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Field Name] | [Category] | Yes / No | [System] | [Purpose] | [Frequency] | [Rationale] | [Retention Period] |
| [Field Name] | [Category] | Yes / No | [System] | [Purpose] | [Frequency] | [Rationale] | [Retention Period] |
| [Field Name] | [Category] | Yes / No | [System] | [Purpose] | [Frequency] | [Rationale] | [Retention Period] |

**Approved Onward Sharing Register**

| Onward Recipient | Purpose | Data Categories | Location of Access and Storage | Sharing Method | Safeguards | Approval Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Recipient Name] | [Purpose] | [Data Categories] | Saudi Arabia | [Method] | [Safeguards] | [Approval Reference] |

**Transfer and Access Schedule**

| Activity | Party Responsible | Method / System | Frequency | Security Control | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Data extraction | [Party] | [System] | [Frequency] | Access restricted to authorised users | Extraction log |
| Data transfer | [Party] | [Method] | [Frequency] | Encrypted transfer channel | Transfer log |
| Receipt confirmation | [Party] | [System] | [Frequency] | Integrity check and reconciliation | Receipt confirmation |
| Access review | [Party] | [System] | [Frequency] | Role-based access review | Access review record |
| Deletion or return | [Party] | [System] | [Trigger / Frequency] | Secure deletion or approved return method | Deletion certificate or attestation |

**Incident Notification Minimum Content**

| Required Information | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Incident summary | Describe what happened, when detected, and current status. |
| Data affected | Identify data fields, categories, volume, and whether sensitive data is involved. |
| Individuals affected | Estimate number and categories of affected individuals. |
| Systems involved | Identify source, destination, transfer channel, or user accounts involved. |
| Likely impact | Describe potential harm to individuals or operational impact. |
| Immediate containment actions | State actions taken to stop or limit the incident. |
| Evidence preserved | Confirm logs, files, communications, and system evidence retained. |
| Contact person | Provide named incident lead and contact details. |
| Support required | State what assistance is required from the other party. |

**Individual Rights Coordination Matrix**

| Request Type | Lead Party | Supporting Party Responsibilities | Verification Requirement | Response Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access request | [Party] | Locate shared data and provide relevant records | Verify requester identity | Response record |
| Correction request | [Party] | Correct data and notify other party where applicable | Verify correction evidence | Correction log |
| Deletion request | [Party] | Delete where lawful and confirm completion | Verify legal eligibility | Deletion confirmation |
| Consent withdrawal | [Party] | Stop sharing or processing where consent is the basis | Verify consent record | Withdrawal record |
| Complaint | [Party] | Investigate and provide facts, logs, and communications | Verify complainant identity if needed | Complaint case record |

## Approval / Routing

The DSA must be routed and approved before personal data sharing begins. Approval confirms that the sharing activity has a defined purpose, lawful basis, appropriate notices or consent where needed, minimum necessary data fields, domestic data handling controls, security safeguards, retention limits, incident obligations, and accountable owners.

| Step | Reviewer / Approver | Review Focus | Required Before Launch? | Evidence |
|---:|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | Requesting Business Owner | Business purpose, necessity, operational scope, recipient details, data accuracy, launch readiness | Yes | Business owner acknowledgement |
| 2 | Data Owner | Data classification, approved data fields, minimum necessary data, source system authorisation | Yes | Data owner approval |
| 3 | Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer | Lawful basis, transparency, consent, individual rights, sensitive data, retention, privacy risk assessment, domestic scope | Yes | Privacy review approval |
| 4 | Legal | Contract enforceability, lawful basis support, liability, confidentiality, audit rights, termination, regulatory obligations | Yes | Legal approval or contract mark-up |
| 5 | Information Security | Transfer method, access control, encryption, logging, monitoring, recipient security posture, incident handling | Yes | Security assessment approval |
| 6 | Compliance / Risk Management | Risk acceptance, exceptions, regulatory exposure, audit evidence readiness | Conditional | Risk approval or exception record |
| 7 | Procurement / Vendor Management | Recipient due diligence, supplier records, commercial alignment where applicable | Conditional | Due diligence record |
| 8 | Executive or Delegated Authority | Final approval for high-risk, high-volume, sensitive, strategic, or exceptional sharing arrangements | Conditional | Signed approval |
| 9 | Authorised Signatories | Formal execution by both parties | Yes | Fully signed agreement |
| 10 | Operational Owner | Confirmation that pre-launch conditions are completed | Yes | Launch checklist and evidence |

**Approval Sign-Off**

| Role | Name | Decision | Conditions / Comments | Signature | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business Owner | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with Conditions | [Comments] | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Data Owner | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with Conditions | [Comments] | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with Conditions | [Comments] | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Legal | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with Conditions | [Comments] | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Information Security | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with Conditions | [Comments] | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Compliance / Risk Management | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with Conditions | [Comments] | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Authorised Signatory | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with Conditions | [Comments] | [Signature] | [Date] |

No data sharing may begin until all mandatory approvals are complete, the DSA is signed by authorised representatives of both parties, and all conditions precedent to launch have been satisfied.

Material changes must be submitted for re-review before implementation. Material changes include:

- New or changed purpose.
- New data categories or data fields.
- Inclusion of sensitive personal data not previously approved.
- Increased volume or frequency of sharing.
- New recipient, onward recipient, platform, or system.
- Change in lawful basis.
- Change to privacy notice or consent approach.
- Change to retention period.
- Change in security controls or transfer method.
- Any cross-border access, support, storage, backup, or transfer.
- Use for automated decision-making, profiling, artificial intelligence, or analytics not previously approved.
- Incident, complaint, audit finding, or regulatory concern affecting the sharing arrangement.

## Records & Retention

The completed and signed DSA, approval evidence, and supporting documents must be retained as official privacy and contract records. Records must be complete, accurate, searchable, access-controlled, and available for audit, legal review, incident response, and regulatory inquiry.

| Record | Owner | Repository | Retention Period | Access Restrictions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Signed Data Sharing Agreement | Contract Owner / Legal | [Contract Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Legal, Privacy Office, business owner, authorised auditors |
| Completed DSA template and field register | Privacy Office | [Privacy Records Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Privacy Office, Legal, business owner, authorised auditors |
| Approval sign-off records | Contract Owner | [Workflow or Approval System] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Approvers, Legal, Privacy Office, authorised auditors |
| Lawful basis assessment | Privacy Office / Legal | [Privacy Records Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Privacy Office, Legal |
| Consent evidence, where applicable | Business Owner / System Owner | [Consent Management System] | As long as sharing relies on consent plus [Retention Period] | Authorised privacy and operational personnel |
| Privacy notice or transparency evidence | Privacy Office | [Privacy Notice Repository] | Current version plus historical versions for [Retention Period] | Privacy Office, Legal |
| Privacy risk assessment or impact assessment | Privacy Office | [Risk Assessment Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Privacy Office, Risk, Legal, authorised auditors |
| Security assessment | Information Security | [Security GRC Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Information Security, Risk, authorised auditors |
| Recipient due diligence evidence | Procurement / Vendor Management | [Vendor Management Repository] | Duration of relationship plus [Retention Period] | Procurement, Legal, Risk, Privacy Office |
| Data flow diagram and technical specification | System Owner / Architecture | [Architecture Repository] | Current version plus historical versions for [Retention Period] | System owner, Information Security, Privacy Office |
| Transfer logs and receipt confirmations | System Owner | [Logging Platform or System Repository] | [Log Retention Period] | System owner, Information Security, authorised investigators |
| Access review records | System Owner / Receiving Party Contact | [Access Review Repository] | [Access Review Retention Period] | System owner, Information Security, authorised auditors |
| Individual rights request records | Privacy Office | [Privacy Case Management System] | [Rights Request Retention Period] | Privacy Office, Legal |
| Complaint records | Privacy Office / Customer Care / HR as applicable | [Case Management System] | [Complaint Retention Period] | Case handlers, Privacy Office, Legal |
| Incident records involving shared data | Information Security / Privacy Office | [Incident Management System] | [Incident Retention Period] | Incident response team, Legal, Privacy Office |
| Deletion, return, or destruction evidence | Contract Owner / System Owner | [Contract or Privacy Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Legal, Privacy Office, system owner |
| Audit and assurance evidence | Compliance / Internal Audit | [Audit Repository] | [Audit Retention Period] | Compliance, Internal Audit, Legal, authorised auditors |
| Exception and risk acceptance records | Risk Management | [Risk Register or GRC System] | Until risk closure plus [Retention Period] | Risk Management, Privacy Office, Legal, authorised auditors |

Records must not be deleted, altered, or destroyed while subject to an active investigation, dispute, audit, regulatory inquiry, legal hold, incident review, or unresolved data subject complaint.

At termination or expiry of the DSA, the Contract Owner must coordinate with the Business Owner, Privacy Office, Information Security, and the receiving party to confirm:

- Data sharing has stopped.
- Access credentials, API keys, accounts, tokens, integrations, and scheduled transfers have been disabled.
- Shared personal data has been returned, deleted, anonymised, or securely destroyed as required.
- Disposal evidence has been received and filed.
- Any continuing legal, regulatory, audit, or complaint obligations are documented.
- Surviving confidentiality, incident support, audit, and rights-handling obligations remain enforceable for the required period.

PDPL-023.title: Data Processing Agreement Template
PDPL-023.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DPA-TPL-001] | 1.0 | [Privacy Office / Legal Department] | [Effective Date] | Saudi Personal Data Protection Law | Confidential |

## Purpose

This Data Processing Agreement Template is used when [Organisation Name] engages any third party to process personal data on its behalf in connection with products, services, operations, technology, support, outsourcing, analytics, hosting, consulting, or other business activities.

The purpose of this template is to ensure that every processor is contractually bound to process personal data only in accordance with documented instructions from [Organisation Name], protect personal data using appropriate safeguards, support data subject rights, assist with incident response and compliance obligations, and return or securely delete personal data at the end of the engagement.

This template is required for all processors that access, collect, store, host, transmit, analyse, modify, disclose, erase, or otherwise handle personal data for or on behalf of [Organisation Name], including processors located inside or outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

## Instructions

1. Complete this template before the processor is authorised to process personal data for [Organisation Name].
2. Use this template as:
 - a standalone data processing agreement;
 - an addendum to a master services agreement, outsourcing agreement, statement of work, purchase order, cloud services agreement, or similar contract; or
 - a schedule to a broader commercial contract.
3. The business owner must complete the processing details accurately before Legal, Privacy, Information Security, Procurement, and other required approvers review the agreement.
4. Do not remove mandatory processor obligations unless approved by Legal and the Privacy Office.
5. If the processor will transfer, host, access, or support personal data from outside Saudi Arabia, obtain Privacy Office and Legal approval before execution.
6. If the processor will use sub-processors, the processor must identify them and accept contractual responsibility for their acts and omissions.
7. If sensitive personal data, national identification data, health data, financial data, children’s data, location data, biometric data, or large-scale processing is involved, complete the required privacy and security risk assessment before execution.
8. If the processing involves high risk to individuals, new technology, automated decision-making, profiling, or systematic monitoring, complete a data protection impact assessment before execution.
9. The agreement must be signed by authorised representatives of both parties before any live personal data is shared or accessed.
10. Retain the completed and executed agreement in the approved contract repository.

The following template clauses should be completed and incorporated into the agreement.

### 1. Parties

This Data Processing Agreement is entered into between:

- **Controller:** [Organisation Name], with its principal place of business at [Organisation Address].
- **Processor:** [Processor Legal Name], with its principal place of business at [Processor Address].

The Controller determines the purposes and means of processing personal data. The Processor processes personal data on behalf of the Controller under the Controller’s documented instructions.

### 2. Relationship to Main Agreement

This Data Processing Agreement forms part of and is incorporated into the agreement between the parties titled [Main Agreement Name] dated [Main Agreement Date], including any statements of work, schedules, purchase orders, or service descriptions issued under it.

If there is a conflict between this Data Processing Agreement and the main agreement regarding the processing or protection of personal data, this Data Processing Agreement takes precedence to the extent of the conflict.

### 3. Processing Instructions

The Processor shall process personal data only:

- for the purposes described in this agreement;
- in accordance with the documented instructions of the Controller;
- as necessary to provide the agreed services; and
- as required by applicable law, provided that the Processor informs the Controller before processing unless legally prohibited from doing so.

The Processor shall not process personal data for its own purposes, including product improvement, analytics, advertising, profiling, model training, resale, benchmarking, or other secondary use, unless expressly authorised in writing by the Controller.

The Processor shall promptly inform the Controller if it believes an instruction violates applicable privacy or data protection requirements.

### 4. Processing Description

The parties shall complete the processing description in the Form Fields section of this template. The completed processing description forms part of this Data Processing Agreement.

### 5. Confidentiality

The Processor shall ensure that all personnel authorised to process personal data:

- are subject to binding confidentiality obligations;
- receive appropriate privacy and security training;
- access personal data only where necessary for their assigned duties;
- understand restrictions on unauthorised access, use, copying, disclosure, alteration, or deletion; and
- remain bound by confidentiality obligations after their employment or engagement ends.

### 6. Security Measures

The Processor shall implement and maintain appropriate technical, organisational, and administrative measures to protect personal data against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, unauthorised access, misuse, or other unauthorised processing.

At a minimum, the Processor shall maintain safeguards covering:

| Security Area | Minimum Expected Measure |
|---|---|
| Access control | Unique user accounts, least privilege access, periodic access reviews, and prompt removal of access when no longer required |
| Authentication | Strong password controls and multi-factor authentication for administrative, remote, privileged, and high-risk access |
| Encryption | Encryption of personal data in transit and at rest where technically feasible and appropriate to the risk |
| Logging and monitoring | Logging of access, administrative activity, security events, and relevant data handling actions |
| Network security | Firewalls, secure configurations, segmentation where appropriate, and protection against unauthorised network access |
| Vulnerability management | Regular vulnerability scanning, timely remediation, patch management, and secure configuration management |
| Secure development | Secure coding, testing, change control, and vulnerability remediation for systems developed or configured by the Processor |
| Data segregation | Logical or physical segregation of Controller data from other customers’ data where applicable |
| Backup and recovery | Secure backups, tested recovery processes, and protection of backups from unauthorised access or alteration |
| Malware protection | Anti-malware, endpoint protection, and monitoring appropriate to the service environment |
| Physical security | Controls to prevent unauthorised physical access to facilities, devices, and media containing personal data |
| Incident response | Documented incident management procedures, defined escalation paths, and trained response personnel |
| Data minimisation | Processing only the personal data necessary for the agreed services |
| Secure disposal | Secure deletion, destruction, or return of personal data and media at the end of processing |
| Supplier security | Due diligence and ongoing oversight of sub-processors and other suppliers involved in processing |
| Business continuity | Continuity and disaster recovery arrangements proportionate to the services and risks |

The Processor shall provide evidence of its security measures upon request, including relevant certifications, audit summaries, security policies, penetration test summaries, risk assessments, or equivalent documentation, subject to reasonable confidentiality protections.

### 7. Sub-Processors

The Processor shall not appoint, replace, or materially change a sub-processor that will process personal data without prior written authorisation from the Controller.

The Processor shall provide the Controller with:

- the legal name of each sub-processor;
- the services performed by each sub-processor;
- the categories of personal data processed;
- the locations where personal data will be processed or accessed;
- the security and privacy safeguards applied; and
- any proposed changes to sub-processors before the change takes effect.

The Processor shall ensure that each approved sub-processor is bound by written obligations no less protective than those in this Data Processing Agreement. The Processor remains fully responsible for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.

The Controller may object to a proposed sub-processor on reasonable privacy, security, legal, operational, or regulatory grounds. If the parties cannot resolve the objection, the Controller may suspend the affected processing or terminate the affected services without penalty.

### 8. Cross-Border Processing and Transfers

The Processor shall not transfer, host, remotely access, support, disclose, or otherwise make personal data available outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia unless expressly authorised in writing by the Controller.

Where cross-border processing is authorised, the Processor shall:

- process personal data only in the approved countries, territories, hosting regions, and support locations;
- implement transfer safeguards approved by the Controller;
- ensure that any overseas recipient protects personal data to a standard required by this agreement;
- maintain a current record of all cross-border processing locations and recipients;
- notify the Controller before any change to approved cross-border processing locations or recipients;
- provide information needed by the Controller to assess the necessity, risk, and legality of the transfer; and
- immediately notify the Controller of any request, order, or legal demand from a foreign authority seeking access to personal data, unless legally prohibited.

### 9. Assistance with Data Subject Rights

The Processor shall assist the Controller in responding to requests from individuals regarding their personal data, including requests to access, correct, complete, update, erase, restrict, or otherwise exercise rights available under applicable privacy requirements.

The Processor shall not respond directly to an individual regarding personal data processed on behalf of the Controller unless instructed by the Controller, except to acknowledge receipt and refer the individual to the Controller.

The Processor shall notify the Controller of any data subject request within [2 business days] of receipt and provide all information reasonably required to support the Controller’s response.

### 10. Assistance with Compliance Obligations

The Processor shall provide reasonable assistance to the Controller in relation to:

- privacy notices and transparency information;
- records of processing activities;
- privacy and security risk assessments;
- data protection impact assessments;
- regulator enquiries, inspections, or requests;
- data breach assessment and notification;
- data minimisation and retention controls;
- secure deletion and return of personal data;
- verification of processing locations and sub-processors; and
- evidence of compliance with this agreement.

### 11. Personal Data Breach and Security Incident Notification

The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay, and in any case within [24 hours], after becoming aware of any actual or suspected personal data breach or security incident affecting personal data processed under this agreement.

The notification shall include, to the extent known at the time:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Incident summary | What happened, when it was discovered, and current status |
| Date and time | Date and time of occurrence, detection, and containment where known |
| Affected services | Systems, applications, databases, environments, or services involved |
| Affected data | Categories and approximate volume of personal data affected |
| Affected individuals | Categories and approximate number of individuals affected |
| Likely impact | Potential harm, misuse, identity risk, financial risk, reputational impact, or other consequences |
| Containment actions | Immediate steps taken to contain, stop, or reduce the incident |
| Remediation actions | Corrective actions completed or planned |
| Evidence preservation | Logs, forensic images, investigation records, and other relevant evidence preserved |
| Third parties | Sub-processors, suppliers, or other parties involved |
| Contact point | Processor incident lead and escalation contacts |

The Processor shall:

- investigate the incident promptly;
- take immediate steps to contain and remediate the incident;
- preserve evidence;
- provide regular updates to the Controller;
- not notify affected individuals, regulators, media, or other external parties without the Controller’s prior written approval unless legally required;
- cooperate with the Controller’s breach assessment and notification process; and
- implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

### 12. Audit and Verification

The Processor shall make available information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with this Data Processing Agreement.

The Controller, or an independent auditor appointed by the Controller, may audit the Processor’s compliance where reasonably required due to risk, incident, regulatory request, material change, or periodic assurance needs. Audits shall be conducted with reasonable notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that minimises disruption.

The Processor shall promptly address any material deficiencies identified through audit, assessment, or review and provide evidence of remediation.

### 13. Data Retention, Return, and Deletion

The Processor shall retain personal data only for the duration authorised by the Controller and only as necessary to provide the services.

Upon termination, expiry, or written instruction from the Controller, the Processor shall, at the Controller’s choice:

- return personal data in a commonly used, secure, and readable format;
- securely delete or destroy personal data;
- securely delete or destroy backups according to an agreed schedule; or
- continue to retain limited personal data only where legally required, protected from further processing except as required by law.

The Processor shall certify completion of return, deletion, or destruction in writing within [30 days] unless otherwise agreed.

### 14. Records of Processing

The Processor shall maintain accurate and up-to-date records of processing performed on behalf of the Controller, including:

- processing purposes;
- categories of personal data;
- categories of individuals;
- systems and locations used;
- sub-processors involved;
- cross-border processing locations;
- retention periods;
- security measures;
- incidents affecting personal data; and
- deletion or return actions.

The Processor shall provide relevant records to the Controller upon request.

### 15. Restrictions on Disclosure

The Processor shall not disclose personal data to any third party unless:

- authorised in writing by the Controller;
- necessary for an approved sub-processor to provide the services;
- required by applicable law; or
- required by a valid order of a competent authority.

If the Processor receives a legal demand, regulatory request, court order, law enforcement request, or similar request for personal data, it shall notify the Controller promptly before disclosure unless legally prohibited. The Processor shall disclose only the minimum personal data required.

### 16. Accuracy and Integrity

The Processor shall not modify, corrupt, degrade, combine, enrich, or derive personal data except as instructed by the Controller or necessary to provide the agreed services.

Where the Processor becomes aware that personal data is inaccurate, incomplete, outdated, or compromised, it shall promptly notify the Controller and assist with correction, completion, update, restriction, or deletion as instructed.

### 17. Personnel and Training

The Processor shall ensure that personnel with access to personal data:

- are vetted according to the sensitivity of their role and applicable law;
- receive privacy and security training before handling personal data and periodically thereafter;
- understand incident escalation requirements;
- use approved systems and secure working practices;
- are subject to disciplinary or contractual consequences for unauthorised processing; and
- are removed from access promptly when access is no longer required.

### 18. Use of Artificial Intelligence, Analytics, or Automated Tools

The Processor shall not use personal data for artificial intelligence, machine learning, profiling, automated decision-making, training datasets, analytics unrelated to the services, or service improvement unless expressly authorised in writing by the Controller.

Where such processing is authorised, the Processor shall provide sufficient information to allow the Controller to assess transparency, fairness, accuracy, security, explainability, data minimisation, retention, and risk to individuals.

### 19. Business Continuity and Availability

Where the Processor provides systems, hosting, managed services, critical operations, or other services affecting the availability of personal data, the Processor shall maintain business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities appropriate to the agreed services.

The Processor shall test continuity and recovery arrangements periodically and provide evidence of testing upon request.

### 20. Indemnity and Liability

The Processor shall be responsible for losses, costs, damages, claims, penalties, investigation costs, notification costs, remediation costs, and reasonable legal expenses arising from the Processor’s breach of this Data Processing Agreement, unauthorised processing, security failure, or acts or omissions of its sub-processors, subject to the liability terms agreed in the main agreement unless Legal approves different terms.

### 21. Term and Survival

This Data Processing Agreement remains in effect for as long as the Processor processes personal data on behalf of the Controller.

Obligations relating to confidentiality, security, return or deletion, audit evidence, incident cooperation, and restrictions on use or disclosure survive termination for as long as the Processor retains or can access personal data.

### 22. Signatures

| Party | Authorised Signatory | Title | Signature | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Organisation Name] | [Name] | [Title] | [Signature] | [Date] |
| [Processor Legal Name] | [Name] | [Title] | [Signature] | [Date] |

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|

| Controller security contact | Name / email | Yes | Enter the Information Security contact for incidents and assurance requests. |

| Processor address | Text | Yes | Enter the processor’s principal address and any relevant local office address. |

| Processor privacy contact | Name / email / phone | Yes | Identify the processor’s privacy or data protection contact. |
| Processor security contact | Name / email / phone | Yes | Identify the processor’s incident response or security contact. |
| Main agreement name | Text | Yes | Enter the title of the related commercial agreement, order form, statement of work, or master agreement. |
| Main agreement date | Date | Yes | Enter the date the related agreement was signed or will be signed. |
| Service description | Long text | Yes | Describe the services the processor will provide and how they involve personal data. |
| Processing purpose | Long text | Yes | State the specific business purpose for processing. Avoid broad statements such as “business operations” unless explained. |
| Processing activities | Multi-select / long text | Yes | Identify activities such as collection, hosting, storage, access, retrieval, support, analysis, transmission, deletion, archiving, migration, or reporting. |
| Processing start date | Date | Yes | Enter when the processor may first access or receive personal data. Processing must not start before agreement execution. |
| Processing end date | Date / event | Yes | Enter the scheduled end date or event triggering termination of processing. |
| Duration of processing | Text | Yes | State the expected duration, including any transition, backup, or post-termination period. |
| Categories of individuals | Multi-select / long text | Yes | Identify whose data is processed, such as customers, employees, contractors, job applicants, suppliers, patients, visitors, users, or beneficiaries. |
| Categories of personal data | Long text | Yes | List all personal data fields or data types, such as name, contact details, account ID, transaction data, usage logs, employment data, or support tickets. |
| Sensitive personal data involved | Yes / No | Yes | Mark “Yes” if processing includes health data, genetic data, biometric data, religious data, criminal data, financial data, precise location data, or other highly sensitive data. |
| Sensitive personal data description | Long text | Conditional | Required if sensitive personal data is involved. Describe the data and why it is necessary. |
| National identification data involved | Yes / No | Yes | Mark “Yes” if national ID, residency number, passport number, or similar official identifier is processed. |
| Children’s data involved | Yes / No | Yes | Mark “Yes” if personal data relates to minors or services used by minors. |
| Volume of personal data | Number / range | Yes | Provide an approximate number of records or individuals affected, such as “up to 10,000 employees” or “approximately 2 million customer records”. |
| Frequency of processing | Select | Yes | Select one: one-time, daily, weekly, monthly, continuous, event-based, or other. |
| Source of personal data | Text | Yes | Identify whether data comes from [Organisation Name], individuals, systems, affiliates, public sources, or third parties. |
| Systems used by processor | Long text | Yes | List applications, platforms, databases, ticketing systems, cloud services, storage locations, and environments used for processing. |
| Hosting location | Country / region | Yes | State where production personal data is hosted. Include cloud region where applicable. |
| Backup location | Country / region | Yes | State where backups, archives, replicas, and disaster recovery copies are stored. |
| Support access location | Country / region | Yes | Identify countries from which support personnel may access personal data remotely. |
| Cross-border processing required | Yes / No | Yes | Mark “Yes” if personal data will be transferred, hosted, accessed, supported, or viewed outside Saudi Arabia. |
| Cross-border processing justification | Long text | Conditional | Required if cross-border processing is requested. Explain the operational necessity and why local processing is not sufficient. |
| Approved countries and locations | List | Conditional | Required if cross-border processing is approved. List each country, city, data centre, cloud region, or support location. |

| Data subject request support timeframe | Number | Yes | Enter the maximum time for the processor to notify the Controller of a request, such as [2 business days]. |
| Incident notification timeframe | Number | Yes | Enter the maximum time for the processor to notify the Controller after becoming aware of an actual or suspected incident, such as [24 hours]. |
| Retention period during services | Text | Yes | State how long the processor may retain personal data during the contract. |
| Post-termination return period | Number | Yes | State how quickly personal data must be returned after termination or instruction. |
| Post-termination deletion period | Number | Yes | State how quickly personal data must be securely deleted after termination or instruction. |
| Backup deletion period | Number | Yes | State how long encrypted backups may remain before routine deletion, where immediate deletion is technically impracticable. |
| Deletion certificate required | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether the processor must provide written certification of deletion or destruction. This should normally be “Yes”. |
| Audit rights accepted | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the processor accepts audit and assurance obligations. Any exception requires Legal and Privacy Office approval. |

### Sub-Processor Register

| Storage | [Describe storage of live data, logs, backups, or archives] | [System / location] | [Data categories] | [Categories of individuals] | [Frequency] |
