### Minimum Contractual Obligations Checklist

| Obligation | Included | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Processor acts only on documented Controller instructions | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Processor cannot use personal data for its own purposes | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Confidentiality obligations apply to authorised personnel | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Security measures are documented and enforceable | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Sub-processors require prior authorisation | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Processor remains liable for sub-processors | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Cross-border processing is prohibited unless approved | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Data subject request assistance is required | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Breach notification timeframe is stated | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Processor must cooperate with incident investigation and remediation | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Audit and assurance rights are included | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Return and deletion obligations are included | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Deletion certification is required | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Records of processing must be maintained | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Legal demand notification is required where permitted | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| AI, analytics, profiling, or secondary use is restricted | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |
| Agreement is executed before processing begins | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |

### Processor Exception Log

| Exception Requested | Clause / Topic | Business Justification | Risk Assessment | Required Approval | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Exception description] | [Topic] | [Justification] | [Low / Medium / High / Critical] | [Legal / Privacy / Security / Procurement] | [Approved / Rejected / Conditional] |

## Approval / Routing

The completed Data Processing Agreement must be routed and approved before signature according to the risk and nature of the processing.

| Review / Approval Step | Responsible Role | Required When | Approval Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Business owner review | [Business Owner] | All processor engagements | Confirmation that service description and processing details are accurate |
| Procurement review | [Procurement Lead] | All new suppliers, renewals, or material contract changes | Supplier onboarding approval and contract routing confirmation |
| Privacy review | [Privacy Office] | All processing of personal data | Privacy approval, risk assessment, and confirmation of required privacy terms |
| Legal review | [Legal Counsel] | All agreements and all deviations from template terms | Legal approval of contract wording and exceptions |
| Information Security review | [Information Security] | All processors with system access, hosting, integrations, sensitive data, or high-risk processing | Security assessment, risk rating, and remediation requirements |
| Data governance review | [Data Governance Owner] | Large-scale processing, master data, analytics, or data quality impact | Confirmation of data ownership, minimisation, retention, and classification |
| Compliance review | [Compliance Officer] | Regulated activities, regulator-facing services, or high-risk processing | Compliance approval and any required control actions |
| Executive approval | [Executive Sponsor] | Critical suppliers, high-risk exceptions, sensitive data, or cross-border processing | Executive sign-off or risk acceptance |
| Contract execution | [Authorised Signatory] | After required approvals are complete | Signed agreement by both parties |
| Repository filing | [Contract Administrator] | After execution | Upload to approved repository with metadata completed |

No personal data may be transferred to or accessed by the processor until all required approvals are complete and the agreement has been executed.

## Records & Retention

The completed and executed Data Processing Agreement, including approvals, attachments, processing descriptions, assessments, exceptions, sub-processor lists, security evidence, and related correspondence, must be retained as an official contract and privacy compliance record.

| Record | Owner | Storage Location | Retention Period | Disposal Method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Executed Data Processing Agreement | [Legal Department] | [Contract Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion or archival disposal according to legal hold status |
| Completed processing description | [Privacy Office] | [Privacy Governance Repository] | Duration of processing plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion or controlled archive disposal |
| Supplier privacy assessment | [Privacy Office] | [Privacy Governance Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion according to retention schedule |
| Supplier security assessment | [Information Security] | [Security GRC Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion according to retention schedule |
| Sub-processor approvals | [Privacy Office / Procurement] | [Supplier Management Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion or archive disposal |
| Cross-border processing approval | [Privacy Office / Legal Department] | [Privacy Governance Repository] | Duration of authorised transfer plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion subject to legal hold |
| Processor exception approvals | [Legal Department] | [Contract Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion or archive disposal |
| Breach and incident notices from processor | [Information Security / Privacy Office] | [Incident Management System] | [Incident Retention Period] | Secure deletion subject to investigation or legal hold |
| Audit reports and assurance evidence | [Information Security / Privacy Office] | [Security GRC Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion according to retention schedule |
| Return, deletion, or destruction certificate | [Legal Department / Privacy Office] | [Contract Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion according to retention schedule |
| Approval and routing evidence | [Contract Administrator] | [Contract Repository] | Duration of agreement plus [Retention Period] | Secure deletion according to retention schedule |

Records must be protected according to their classification and access must be limited to personnel with a legitimate business need. If litigation, regulatory enquiry, investigation, audit, or dispute is pending or reasonably anticipated, disposal must be suspended until the legal hold or investigation hold is released.

PDPL-024.title: Standard Contractual Clauses for Cross-Border Transfer
PDPL-024.content:
# Standard Contractual Clauses for Cross-Border Transfer

| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [PDPL-SCC-TPL-001] | 1.0 | [Privacy Office / Legal Department] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Saudi Personal Data Protection Law | Confidential |

## Purpose

This template is used to document and execute standard contractual clauses for any transfer, disclosure, hosting, remote access, support activity, or other processing of personal data outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

The purpose of these clauses is to ensure that cross-border transfers of personal data are performed lawfully, securely, transparently, and only where the importing party provides appropriate contractual commitments to protect the personal data in accordance with Saudi personal data protection requirements and the organisation’s privacy governance obligations.

This template applies where:

- Personal data collected or processed by the organisation in Saudi Arabia will be transferred to, accessed from, stored in, or processed in another country.
- A third party outside Saudi Arabia will receive, host, support, analyse, maintain, or otherwise process personal data.
- A foreign affiliate, cloud provider, technology service provider, outsourcing partner, professional adviser, or other recipient will access personal data from outside Saudi Arabia.
- The transfer requires contractual safeguards because the receiving country, recipient, or transfer arrangement must be assessed and controlled before transfer.

This template is intended to be attached to or incorporated into a master services agreement, data processing agreement, intra-group agreement, statement of work, cloud services agreement, outsourcing agreement, or other binding contract.

## Instructions

1. Complete all required fields in the **Form Fields** section before issuing the clauses for review or signature.
2. Use this template only after the business owner has confirmed that the transfer is necessary for a legitimate and documented purpose.
3. Do not use this template as a substitute for a transfer impact assessment, privacy impact assessment, vendor due diligence, or security assessment where those activities are required by the organisation.
4. The Legal Department must review any proposed changes to the standard wording before execution.
5. The Privacy Office must confirm that the transfer purpose, categories of personal data, data subjects, destination country, recipient role, onward transfers, and security measures have been documented.
6. Information Security must review the technical and organisational safeguards for medium-risk, high-risk, sensitive, large-scale, or externally hosted processing.
7. Procurement must ensure the executed clauses are linked to the relevant supplier contract, purchase order, or vendor record.
8. Business owners must not permit transfer, access, migration, integration, or production use until approval has been completed and the executed record is stored in the designated contract repository.
9. Where the recipient will engage sub-processors or onward recipients, the business owner must ensure they are identified, controlled, and contractually bound before any onward transfer occurs.
10. If the transfer involves sensitive personal data, children’s data, health data, biometric data, financial data, location data, national identification data, criminal records, or other high-risk data, additional review and approvals are required.
11. If any field is not applicable, record “Not applicable” and provide a short justification where relevant.
12. Do not delete audit-relevant sections, approval records, transfer descriptions, safeguards, or retention details.
13. Executed clauses must be retained with the relevant contract and linked to the transfer register or privacy inventory.
14. Any actual or suspected breach affecting transferred personal data must be escalated immediately under the organisation’s incident response and personal data breach management process.
15. Renew, revalidate, or re-execute the clauses when the recipient, country, processing purpose, system, data categories, sub-processors, transfer method, or applicable contract materially changes.

The following standard contractual commitments should be included in the final agreement or attached schedule. Wording may be adapted by Legal only where required for the specific contract structure, provided the level of protection is not reduced.

| Standard Clause Area | Required Contractual Commitment |
|---|---|
| Parties | The agreement must clearly identify the data exporter, data importer, their legal names, addresses, registration details, authorised representatives, and contact points for privacy and security matters. |
| Roles | The agreement must state whether each party acts as controller, processor, joint controller, sub-processor, or independent recipient for the transfer and related processing. |
| Transfer purpose | The agreement must limit the transfer to the documented business purpose and prohibit processing for unrelated, incompatible, unauthorised, or undisclosed purposes. |
| Personal data categories | The agreement must describe the personal data categories transferred, including whether sensitive or high-risk data is involved. |
| Data subject categories | The agreement must identify the categories of individuals whose personal data is transferred, such as customers, employees, contractors, patients, users, visitors, or applicants. |
| Processing activities | The agreement must define the permitted processing operations, including collection, access, storage, hosting, support, maintenance, analysis, transmission, deletion, return, anonymisation, or archival. |
| Destination and access locations | The agreement must identify the destination countries and all countries from which the recipient or its authorised personnel may access the personal data. |
| Transfer method | The agreement must specify approved transfer mechanisms, systems, interfaces, encryption channels, file exchange methods, remote access tools, or hosting environments. |
| Confidentiality | The recipient must ensure that personnel with access to personal data are bound by confidentiality obligations and receive appropriate privacy and security instructions. |
| Lawful and limited processing | The recipient must process personal data only on documented instructions, within the agreed scope, and in a manner consistent with the exporter’s obligations. |
| Security measures | The recipient must implement appropriate technical, organisational, and physical safeguards to protect personal data against unauthorised access, alteration, loss, disclosure, destruction, misuse, or unlawful processing. |
| Access control | The recipient must restrict access to authorised users with a business need, use unique accounts, apply strong authentication, regularly review access, and promptly remove access when no longer required. |
| Encryption | Personal data must be encrypted in transit and, where appropriate based on risk, encrypted at rest using organisation-approved cryptographic standards. |
| Logging and monitoring | The recipient must maintain logs for access, administrative actions, transfers, changes, and security events involving the personal data where technically feasible and proportionate to risk. |
| Data minimisation | The recipient must not request, receive, retain, or process more personal data than is necessary for the documented transfer purpose. |
| Accuracy and correction | The recipient must assist the exporter in maintaining accurate personal data and must support correction, completion, restriction, deletion, or update requests where applicable. |
| Data subject rights support | The recipient must promptly assist the exporter in responding to valid individual rights requests and must not respond directly unless authorised or legally required. |
| Notice and transparency support | The recipient must provide information reasonably required for the exporter to maintain accurate privacy notices, transfer disclosures, and processing records. |
| Sub-processing and onward transfer | The recipient must not appoint sub-processors or onward recipients, or transfer the data to another country or entity, without prior written authorisation and equivalent contractual protections. |
| Sub-processor obligations | Approved sub-processors must be subject to written obligations that are no less protective than those imposed on the recipient. |
| Government and legal requests | The recipient must promptly notify the exporter of legally binding requests for disclosure of personal data unless prohibited by law, and must challenge or narrow requests where legally appropriate. |
| Breach notification | The recipient must notify the exporter without undue delay after becoming aware of any actual or suspected personal data breach affecting transferred data and provide details needed for investigation, containment, notification, and remediation. |
| Incident cooperation | The recipient must cooperate with breach response activities, preserve relevant evidence, support forensic investigation, implement corrective actions, and provide incident reports. |
| Audit and assurance | The recipient must provide reasonable evidence of compliance, including security certifications, audit reports, policies, test results, or completed questionnaires, and permit audits where required by contract or risk. |
| Transfer impact cooperation | The recipient must provide information needed to assess the risks of the transfer, including legal environment, access controls, sub-processors, security posture, and operational safeguards. |
| Data retention | The recipient must retain personal data only for the approved period and must return or securely delete it at the end of services, on instruction, or when no longer required. |
| Secure deletion | Deletion must be performed using secure methods appropriate to the media and system type, and the recipient must provide confirmation where requested. |
| Data return | On termination or expiry, the recipient must return personal data in a usable and secure format if requested by the exporter. |
| Business continuity | The recipient must maintain continuity and disaster recovery controls appropriate to the criticality of the processing and must protect data during disruption or recovery. |
| Location changes | The recipient must not change hosting location, support location, remote access location, or processing country without prior written notice and approval. |
| Personnel controls | The recipient must ensure that personnel with access to personal data are appropriately screened, trained, authorised, supervised, and subject to disciplinary processes for misuse. |
| Records of processing | The recipient must maintain records sufficient to demonstrate compliance with the agreed processing instructions and transfer restrictions. |
| Conflict with law | The recipient must notify the exporter if it cannot comply with the clauses, local law prevents compliance, or circumstances arise that materially affect the protection of personal data. |
| Suspension and termination | The exporter may suspend transfers, require remediation, restrict access, or terminate the relevant processing where the recipient cannot comply or where unacceptable risk exists. |
| Liability and remedies | The agreement must include appropriate responsibility, indemnity, cooperation, and remedy provisions for privacy, security, confidentiality, and breach failures. |
| Survival | Confidentiality, security, audit, deletion, return, cooperation, and liability obligations must survive termination for as long as the recipient retains or can access personal data. |

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| SCC request reference | Text | Yes | Assign a unique internal reference for this cross-border transfer request. |
| Related contract reference | Text | Yes | Enter the master agreement, data processing agreement, statement of work, purchase order, or supplier record linked to these clauses. |
| Business owner | Person / Team | Yes | Identify the accountable internal owner for the processing activity and transfer. |
| Requesting department | Text | Yes | State the department requesting or relying on the transfer. |
| Data exporter legal name | Text | Yes | Enter the full legal name of the Saudi entity or organisation exporting or making the personal data available. |
| Data exporter address | Text | Yes | Enter the registered or principal business address of the exporting entity. |
| Data exporter authorised representative | Person | Yes | Name the person authorised to approve or sign on behalf of the data exporter. |
| Data exporter privacy contact | Email / Person | Yes | Provide the contact responsible for privacy queries relating to the transfer. |
| Data exporter security contact | Email / Person | Yes | Provide the contact responsible for security queries relating to the transfer. |
| Data importer legal name | Text | Yes | Enter the full legal name of the foreign recipient, service provider, affiliate, or processor. |
| Data importer address | Text | Yes | Enter the registered or principal business address of the importer. |
| Data importer country | Country | Yes | State the country where the importer is legally established. |
| Data importer privacy contact | Email / Person | Yes | Provide the importer’s privacy or data protection contact. |
| Data importer security contact | Email / Person | Yes | Provide the importer’s information security contact. |
| Importer role | Dropdown | Yes | Select controller, processor, sub-processor, joint controller, independent recipient, or other approved role. |
| Exporter role | Dropdown | Yes | Select controller, processor, joint controller, or other approved role for the exporting organisation. |
| Transfer type | Dropdown | Yes | Select remote access, hosting, support, outsourcing, cloud service, analytics, intra-group transfer, professional service, backup, integration, or other. |
| Transfer description | Long text | Yes | Describe what personal data is transferred, why it is transferred, how it is transferred, and what the importer will do with it. |
| Business purpose | Long text | Yes | Explain the specific business need for the transfer and why the purpose cannot be achieved without cross-border processing. |
| Legal and privacy basis for processing | Long text | Yes | Summarise the documented basis for collecting, using, and transferring the personal data. |
| Transfer necessity assessment completed | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether the business need, proportionality, and alternatives have been assessed. |
| Transfer impact assessment reference | Text | Conditional | Required for medium-risk, high-risk, sensitive, large-scale, critical, or new international transfers. |
| Privacy impact assessment reference | Text | Conditional | Required where the transfer forms part of new, changed, high-risk, or sensitive processing. |
| Vendor due diligence reference | Text | Conditional | Required where the importer is a supplier, outsourced provider, cloud provider, or managed service provider. |
| Information security assessment reference | Text | Conditional | Required where systems, networks, applications, hosting, or remote access are involved. |
| Countries of storage | Country list | Yes | List every country where personal data will be stored, backed up, replicated, archived, or hosted. |
| Countries of remote access | Country list | Yes | List every country from which support teams, administrators, affiliates, contractors, or sub-processors may access the data. |
| Countries of onward transfer | Country list | Conditional | Required where the importer will transfer or provide access to another party or country. |
| Hosting environment | Dropdown / Text | Conditional | Required where data will be hosted. State cloud provider, region, data centre, tenancy model, and environment type. |
| System or application name | Text | Yes | Enter the name of the system, platform, database, repository, application, or file share involved. |
| System owner | Person / Team | Yes | Identify the accountable owner of the system used for transfer or processing. |
| Transfer start date | Date | Yes | State the expected date when transfer, access, migration, or processing will begin. |
| Transfer end date | Date / Text | Yes | State the end date or indicate ongoing processing with review frequency. |
| Transfer frequency | Dropdown | Yes | Select one-time, ad hoc, daily, weekly, monthly, real-time, continuous, or other. |
| Transfer method | Dropdown / Text | Yes | Describe the approved secure method, such as encrypted API, secure file transfer, managed VPN, private link, encrypted email, or controlled portal. |
| Personal data categories | Multi-select / Long text | Yes | List the personal data involved, such as name, contact details, identifiers, employment data, financial data, health data, account data, transaction data, location data, or usage data. |
| Sensitive personal data included | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether sensitive or high-risk data is included. If yes, complete the sensitive data details field. |
| Sensitive data details | Long text | Conditional | Required if sensitive data is included. Describe the data types, volume, risk, and additional safeguards. |
| Data subject categories | Multi-select / Text | Yes | Identify individuals affected, such as customers, employees, contractors, suppliers, applicants, patients, users, visitors, or dependants. |
| Approximate number of data subjects | Number / Range | Yes | Provide the expected number or range of individuals whose data will be transferred. |
| Approximate data volume | Text | Yes | Estimate record count, file size, database size, or transaction volume. |
| Children’s data included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether personal data of minors is included. If yes, additional privacy review is required. |
| National identification data included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether national identity, residency, passport, or government-issued identifier data is included. |
| Health or biometric data included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether health, genetic, biometric, or medical information is included. |
| Financial data included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether bank, payment, salary, credit, insurance, or financial transaction data is included. |
| Criminal or disciplinary data included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether criminal history, investigations, sanctions, or disciplinary records are included. |
| Data minimisation confirmed | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm that only the minimum necessary personal data will be transferred. |
| Anonymisation or pseudonymisation used | Yes / No / Not applicable | Yes | State whether data will be anonymised, aggregated, masked, tokenised, or pseudonymised before transfer. |
| Encryption in transit | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm that approved encryption will protect data during transmission and remote access. |
| Encryption at rest | Yes / No / Not applicable | Yes | Confirm whether approved encryption protects stored data in the importer’s environment. |
| Key management owner | Text | Conditional | Required where encryption is used. State who controls and manages encryption keys. |
| Access control model | Long text | Yes | Describe role-based access, least privilege, privileged access management, approval workflow, and access review frequency. |
| Authentication method | Text | Yes | State whether multi-factor authentication, single sign-on, certificates, keys, or other approved authentication methods are used. |
| Logging and monitoring controls | Long text | Yes | Describe audit logging, security monitoring, alerting, retention, and review arrangements for the transferred data. |
| Network security controls | Long text | Conditional | Required where systems are interconnected or remotely accessed. Describe segmentation, firewall rules, private connectivity, VPN, or API gateway controls. |
| Endpoint and administrator controls | Long text | Conditional | Required where personnel access personal data from endpoints or administer systems. Describe managed devices, hardening, malware protection, and privileged access controls. |
| Backup and replication locations | Text | Conditional | Required where data is backed up or replicated. List countries, systems, retention periods, and protection measures. |
| Retention period at importer | Text | Yes | State how long the importer may retain personal data and the trigger for deletion or return. |
| Deletion method | Text | Yes | Describe how data will be securely deleted from production, backup, logs, archives, and temporary locations where applicable. |
| Return requirement | Yes / No | Yes | State whether the importer must return a copy of the data at termination, expiry, or on request. |
| Sub-processors used | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether the importer will use any sub-processors or onward recipients. |
| Approved sub-processor list | Table / Attachment | Conditional | Required if sub-processors are used. Include legal name, country, service, data access, and approval status. |
| Sub-processor approval mechanism | Dropdown / Text | Conditional | State whether approval is specific written approval, general written authorisation with objection right, or prohibited. |
| Onward transfer restrictions included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the contract prohibits onward transfer without written approval and equivalent protections. |
| Government access notification obligation included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the importer must notify the exporter of legally binding access or disclosure requests unless prohibited. |
| Breach notification timeframe | Text | Yes | State the contractual timeframe for notifying the exporter after becoming aware of an actual or suspected breach. |
| Incident cooperation obligations included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the importer must cooperate with investigation, containment, reporting, remediation, and evidence preservation. |
| Audit rights included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the exporter has appropriate rights to obtain assurance, review evidence, or conduct audits. |
| Assurance evidence provided | Text / Attachment | Conditional | Include recent security certifications, independent audit reports, penetration test summaries, privacy attestations, or completed questionnaires where applicable. |
| Data subject rights support included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the importer must assist with access, correction, deletion, restriction, complaint handling, and other individual requests. |
| Confidentiality obligations included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the importer’s personnel and sub-processors are bound by confidentiality obligations. |
| Training obligations included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm personnel with access to personal data receive appropriate privacy and security training. |
| Business continuity controls reviewed | Yes / No / Not applicable | Yes | Confirm whether continuity and disaster recovery arrangements are appropriate for the processing. |
| Insurance requirements included | Yes / No / Not applicable | Conditional | Required where the supplier contract requires cyber, professional indemnity, or liability insurance. |
| Liability provisions reviewed | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm Legal has reviewed privacy, confidentiality, security, indemnity, and limitation of liability terms. |
| Suspension right included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the exporter may suspend transfer or access where compliance or security risk is unacceptable. |
| Termination assistance included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the importer must support transition, return, deletion, and continuity at termination. |
| Local law conflict notification included | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the importer must notify the exporter if local law or circumstances prevent compliance with the contractual obligations. |
| Contract language | Text | Yes | State the contract language and whether a translation is required. |
| Governing law and dispute forum | Text | Yes | Enter the governing law and dispute resolution forum agreed by Legal. |
| Deviations from standard wording | Long text | Yes | Describe any changes to the standard clauses. If none, state “No deviations”. |
| Legal deviation approval | Person / Date | Conditional | Required if any standard wording has been changed. |
| Residual privacy risk rating | Dropdown | Yes | Select low, medium, high, or critical after safeguards and contractual controls are considered. |
| Residual security risk rating | Dropdown | Yes | Select low, medium, high, or critical after technical and organisational controls are considered. |
| Risk acceptance required | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm whether residual risk requires formal acceptance before transfer. |
| Risk acceptance owner | Person | Conditional | Required where residual risk is high, critical, or outside tolerance. |
| Required remediation actions | Long text | Conditional | List actions required before approval, such as encryption changes, access restrictions, contract amendments, or sub-processor removal. |
| Remediation due date | Date | Conditional | Required where actions must be completed before or after approval. |
| Pre-transfer approval status | Dropdown | Yes | Select draft, under review, approved, conditionally approved, rejected, suspended, or expired. |
| Effective date of clauses | Date | Yes | Enter the date the clauses become contractually effective. |
| Expiry or review date | Date | Yes | Enter the date for periodic review, renewal, or revalidation of the transfer arrangement. |
| Signature method | Dropdown | Yes | Select wet ink, electronic signature, contract management workflow, or other approved method. |
| Executed document location | Link / Repository path | Yes | Provide the location of the signed clauses in the approved contract repository. |
| Transfer register updated | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm the transfer register, privacy inventory, or processing record has been updated. |
| Post-approval monitoring owner | Person / Team | Yes | Identify who will monitor ongoing compliance, vendor performance, access, and changes. |
| Next review trigger | Multi-select | Yes | Select annual review, contract renewal, supplier change, country change, system change, data category change, sub-processor change, incident, audit finding, or business change. |
| Additional notes | Long text | No | Record any additional context, assumptions, constraints, or reviewer comments. |

Where sub-processors or onward recipients are involved, complete the following table and attach it to the executed agreement or contract schedule.

| Sub-processor / Onward Recipient | Country | Service Provided | Data Access Level | Personal Data Categories | Approval Status | Contractual Safeguards Confirmed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Legal entity name] | [Country] | [Service description] | View / Process / Store / Support / Admin | [Categories] | Approved / Rejected / Pending | Yes / No |
| [Legal entity name] | [Country] | [Service description] | View / Process / Store / Support / Admin | [Categories] | Approved / Rejected / Pending | Yes / No |

Where remediation or pre-transfer conditions are required, complete the following action table.

| Action ID | Required Action | Owner | Due Date | Dependency | Completion Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACT-001 | [Action description] | [Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Dependency] | [Evidence] | Open / In progress / Complete / Deferred |
| ACT-002 | [Action description] | [Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Dependency] | [Evidence] | Open / In progress / Complete / Deferred |

## Approval / Routing

The completed template must follow the routing below before any personal data is transferred, accessed, hosted, migrated, or otherwise processed outside Saudi Arabia.

| Step | Reviewer / Approver | Required For | Review Focus | Approval Evidence |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Business Owner | All transfers | Business purpose, necessity, scope, data minimisation, operational need, budget, and ownership. | Workflow approval or signed request. |
| 2 | Privacy Office | All transfers | Privacy basis, transfer justification, data categories, data subject categories, transparency, rights support, transfer register update, and residual privacy risk. | Privacy approval record. |
| 3 | Legal Department | All transfers | Contractual enforceability, SCC wording, deviations, liability, governing law, termination, audit rights, breach obligations, and onward transfer restrictions. | Legal approval and approved contract draft. |
| 4 | Information Security | Transfers involving systems, hosting, remote access, sensitive data, high-risk data, or suppliers | Encryption, access control, authentication, logging, monitoring, incident response, continuity, supplier security posture, and technical safeguards. | Security assessment approval. |
| 5 | Procurement / Vendor Management | Supplier or outsourced processing | Supplier record, due diligence, purchase order, contract linkage, sub-processor tracking, insurance, and renewal controls. | Procurement approval or supplier file update. |
| 6 | Data Governance / Records Management | Transfers involving records, archives, deletion, retention, or large datasets | Retention schedule, deletion method, data quality, records classification, return requirements, and archival controls. | Records review confirmation. |
| 7 | Risk Management | High or critical residual risk, exceptions, or risk acceptance | Risk rating, compensating controls, risk acceptance, escalation, and monitoring obligations. | Risk acceptance or risk committee decision. |
| 8 | Executive Sponsor | High-risk, strategic, sensitive, large-scale, or material outsourcing transfers | Business accountability, material risk, strategic alignment, and approval to proceed. | Executive sign-off. |
| 9 | Authorised Signatories | All executed clauses | Formal execution by authorised representatives of the exporter and importer. | Signed agreement or approved electronic execution certificate. |
| 10 | Contract Repository Administrator | All executed clauses | Storage of executed record, metadata capture, linkage to supplier and transfer register, and access restriction. | Repository record and document link. |

Approval outcome must be documented as one of the following:

| Outcome | Meaning | Transfer Permission |
|---|---|---|
| Approved | All required reviews are complete and no blocking conditions remain. | Transfer may proceed within the approved scope. |
| Conditionally approved | Transfer may proceed only after specified conditions are completed or within agreed temporary restrictions. | Transfer may proceed only as stated in the approval. |
| Rejected | The transfer is not permitted due to legal, privacy, security, contractual, or business concerns. | Transfer must not proceed. |
| Suspended | Previously approved transfer is paused due to incident, non-compliance, material change, audit finding, or unacceptable risk. | Transfer must stop until reinstated. |
| Expired | Approval is no longer valid because the review date, contract term, or approved scope has expired. | Transfer must not continue until renewed. |

Minimum approval rules:

- No cross-border transfer may begin until the Business Owner, Privacy Office, and Legal Department have approved the completed template and contractual wording.
- Information Security approval is mandatory where the transfer involves technology platforms, hosting, administrator access, remote support, APIs, cloud services, sensitive personal data, or high-volume processing.
- Any deviation from standard wording must be approved by Legal before signature.
- Any high or critical residual risk must be accepted by the appropriate risk owner before transfer.
- Any unapproved sub-processor or unapproved destination country must be resolved before transfer.
- Any material change after approval must be resubmitted for review before implementation.
- Emergency transfers must still be documented, approved by an authorised executive and the Privacy Office, and retrospectively completed within the timeframe set by the organisation’s privacy governance process.

Execution block for attachment to the contract:

| Party | Name | Title | Signature | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Data Exporter | [Authorised signatory name] | [Title] | [Signature] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Data Importer | [Authorised signatory name] | [Title] | [Signature] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

Internal approval record:

| Role | Name | Decision | Conditions / Comments | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business Owner | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Conditional | [Comments] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Privacy Office | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Conditional | [Comments] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Legal Department | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Conditional | [Comments] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Information Security | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Conditional / Not applicable | [Comments] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Conditional / Not applicable | [Comments] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Risk Management | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Conditional / Not applicable | [Comments] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Executive Sponsor | [Name] | Approved / Rejected / Conditional / Not applicable | [Comments] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

## Records & Retention

The completed and executed template is a controlled privacy and legal record. It must be retained in the approved repository and protected according to its classification.

| Record | Repository | Owner | Minimum Retention | Access Restrictions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completed SCC template | [Contract repository / privacy governance system] | Privacy Office | Duration of the contract plus [retention period] | Privacy, Legal, Business Owner, authorised auditors. |
| Executed contractual clauses | [Contract repository] | Legal Department | Duration of the contract plus [retention period] | Legal, Procurement, Privacy, authorised executives, authorised auditors. |
| Related master agreement or data processing agreement | [Contract repository] | Legal Department | Duration of the contract plus [retention period] | Legal, Procurement, Business Owner, authorised auditors. |
| Transfer impact assessment | [Privacy governance system] | Privacy Office | Duration of the transfer plus [retention period] | Privacy, Legal, Information Security, Risk Management, authorised auditors. |
| Privacy impact assessment | [Privacy governance system] | Privacy Office | Duration of the processing activity plus [retention period] | Privacy, Legal, Business Owner, authorised auditors. |
| Vendor due diligence and security assessment | [Vendor management system / GRC platform] | Procurement / Information Security | Supplier lifecycle plus [retention period] | Procurement, Information Security, Privacy, Legal, authorised auditors. |
| Sub-processor approvals | [Contract repository / vendor management system] | Procurement / Privacy Office | Duration of sub-processing plus [retention period] | Procurement, Privacy, Legal, Business Owner. |
| Approval workflow evidence | [Workflow system / GRC platform] | Privacy Office | Duration of the transfer plus [retention period] | Approvers, Privacy, Legal, Risk Management, authorised auditors. |
| Risk acceptance record | [Risk register / GRC platform] | Risk Management | Duration of accepted risk plus [retention period] | Risk Management, Privacy, Legal, Executive Sponsor, authorised auditors. |
| Breach or incident records related to transferred data | [Incident management system] | Information Security / Privacy Office | Duration required by incident and legal hold requirements | Information Security, Privacy, Legal, Incident Response Team, authorised investigators. |
| Deletion or return certificate | [Contract repository / privacy governance system] | Business Owner / Legal Department | Duration of the contract plus [retention period] | Legal, Privacy, Business Owner, authorised auditors. |

Retention and recordkeeping requirements:

- Records must be complete, accurate, dated, and traceable to the relevant contract, supplier, system, and transfer register entry.
- Executed clauses must not be stored only in email, shared drives, or local devices unless those locations are approved records repositories.
- Access to records must be limited to personnel with a legitimate business need.
- Superseded versions must be retained where needed to evidence the contractual terms that applied at the time of transfer.
- Records must be made available for internal audit, regulatory response, legal review, incident investigation, and supplier review when authorised.
- Where litigation hold, regulatory inquiry, investigation, dispute, audit, or incident response is active, deletion of relevant records must be suspended until released by Legal.
- At the end of the retention period, records must be securely disposed of in accordance with the organisation’s records management and secure disposal requirements.
- The Privacy Office must ensure the transfer register or processing inventory reflects the executed clauses, transfer scope, destination countries, review date, and approval status.
- The Business Owner must notify the Privacy Office and Legal Department before renewing, terminating, materially changing, expanding, or replacing the transfer arrangement.
- The template must be reviewed at least annually or sooner if Saudi personal data protection requirements, regulatory expectations, organisational risk appetite, transfer practices, or approved contract standards change.

PDPL-025.title: Vendor / Processor Due Diligence Records
PDPL-025.content:
## Vendor / Processor Due Diligence Records (DOCX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Record ID | Vendor / Processor Legal Name | Commercial Registration / Registration Number | Country of Establishment | Vendor Role | Business Owner | Procurement / Contract Owner | Service / Processing Description | Personal Data Processing Purpose | PDPL Controller / Processor Relationship | Data Subject Categories | Personal Data Categories | Sensitive Personal Data Involved | Criminal / Security Data Involved | Children / Minors Data Involved | Estimated Data Volume | Processing Locations | Cross-Border Transfer Involved | Cross-Border Transfer Countries | Cross-Border Transfer Legal Basis / Assessment Reference | Sub-Processors Used | Sub-Processor Approval Status | Due Diligence Initiation Date | Due Diligence Status | Due Diligence Reviewer | Security Questionnaire Completed | Privacy / PDPL Questionnaire Completed | Evidence Reviewed | Technical and Organisational Measures Assessed | Access Control Assessment | Encryption / Pseudonymisation Assessment | Logging and Monitoring Assessment | Data Segregation Assessment | Backup and Business Continuity Assessment | Vulnerability / Penetration Testing Evidence | Incident and Breach Notification Capability | Data Subject Rights Support Capability | Retention and Deletion Capability | Return / Deletion on Termination Capability | Audit / Inspection Rights Confirmed | Confidentiality Obligations Confirmed | Staff Training / Awareness Evidence | Processor Contract / DPA Required | Processor Contract / DPA Status | Mandatory PDPL Contract Clauses Confirmed | Contract Effective Date | Contract Expiry / Renewal Date | Residual Risk Rating | Risk Treatment Decision | Approver | Approval Date | Conditions / Remediation Actions | Remediation Owner | Remediation Due Date | Remediation Status | Ongoing Monitoring Frequency | Last Review Date | Next Review Date | Offboarding Date | Offboarding Evidence Reference | Record Status | Document / Evidence Repository Link | Comments |

deletion certificate wording to be added] | [EXAMPLE: Satisfactory] | [EXAMPLE: Satisfactory] | [EXAMPLE: Satisfactory] | [EXAMPLE: Satisfactory] | [EXAMPLE: Satisfactory] | [EXAMPLE: 2025-11 penetration test executive summary reviewed] | [EXAMPLE: Satisfactory] | [EXAMPLE: Satisfactory] | [EXAMPLE: Gap Identified - deletion certificate required] | [EXAMPLE: Gap Identified - certificate wording pending] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Annual privacy and security training attestation reviewed] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Executed] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-15] | [EXAMPLE: 2027-02-14] | [EXAMPLE: Medium] | [EXAMPLE: Mitigate] | [EXAMPLE: Data Protection Lead - Fahad Al-Salem] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-20] | [EXAMPLE: Add deletion certificate obligation to service schedule] | [EXAMPLE: Legal - Contract Manager] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-15] | [EXAMPLE: In Progress] | [EXAMPLE: Annual] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-20] | [EXAMPLE: 2027-02-20] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: Approved with Conditions] | [EXAMPLE: GRC/Vendors/ABCCloud/VDD-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: Approval conditional on contract schedule update before production go-live] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this due diligence record, using format VDD-YYYY-NNN, e.g. VDD-2026-001. |
| Vendor / Processor Legal Name | Enter the full legal name of the vendor, processor, or service provider as shown in the contract or commercial registration. |
| Commercial Registration / Registration Number | Enter the Saudi commercial registration number, foreign company registration number, or equivalent official identifier; enter N/A only if not available. |
| Country of Establishment | Enter the country where the vendor legal entity is incorporated or registered, using the full country name. |
| Vendor Role | Select one: Processor, Sub-Processor, Independent Controller, Joint Controller, Service Provider with No Personal Data Access, Other. |
| Business Owner | Enter the internal business function and named owner accountable for the service, in format Department - Full Name. |
| Procurement / Contract Owner | Enter the internal procurement, legal, or contract management owner, in format Department - Full Name. |
| Service / Processing Description | Describe the service provided and the processing activity in one concise sentence, including the system or platform name if applicable. |
| Personal Data Processing Purpose | State the specific, lawful business purpose for which personal data will be processed; do not use generic wording such as 'business purposes'. |
| PDPL Controller / Processor Relationship | Describe the PDPL relationship and instruction model, e.g. 'Organisation is Controller; vendor processes only on documented instructions'. |
| Data Subject Categories | List the categories of individuals whose personal data is processed, e.g. Employees, Customers, Website Users, Suppliers, Patients, Applicants. |
| Personal Data Categories | List the categories of personal data processed, e.g. name, national ID/Iqama, contact details, payroll data, account credentials, location data. |
| Sensitive Personal Data Involved | Select Yes or No; if Yes, specify the categories such as health data, biometric data, genetic data, religious data, credit data, or similar PDPL-sensitive data. |
| Criminal / Security Data Involved | Select Yes or No; if Yes, describe the criminal, security, or related records processed and confirm additional approvals or controls where applicable. |
| Children / Minors Data Involved | Select Yes or No; if Yes, describe the age group and any guardian consent or additional protection requirements. |
| Estimated Data Volume | Enter the approximate number of data subjects or records processed, using a number or defined range such as <1,000, 1,000-10,000, 10,001-100,000, >100,000. |
| Processing Locations | List all countries and hosting regions where personal data is stored, accessed, supported, backed up, or processed. |
| Cross-Border Transfer Involved | Select Yes or No based on whether personal data is transferred, accessed, stored, supported, or backed up outside Saudi Arabia. |
| Cross-Border Transfer Countries | If cross-border transfer is Yes, list each destination country; if No, enter N/A. |
| Cross-Border Transfer Legal Basis / Assessment Reference | Enter the approved transfer basis and reference to the transfer assessment or approval record, e.g. TIA-YYYY-NNN; enter N/A if no transfer. |
| Sub-Processors Used | Select Yes or No; if Yes, list the sub-processors or reference the approved sub-processor list. |
| Sub-Processor Approval Status | Select one: Not Applicable, Pending Review, Approved, Approved with Conditions, Rejected; include approval reference if applicable. |
| Due Diligence Initiation Date | Enter the date due diligence started in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Due Diligence Status | Select one: Not Started, In Progress, Awaiting Vendor Response, Under Review, Approved, Approved with Conditions, Rejected, Expired. |
| Due Diligence Reviewer | Enter the name and role of the privacy, legal, information security, or risk reviewer completing the assessment. |
| Security Questionnaire Completed | Select Yes, No, or Not Required; if Yes, reference the questionnaire file or ticket ID. |
| Privacy / PDPL Questionnaire Completed | Select Yes, No, or Not Required; if Yes, reference the completed PDPL/privacy questionnaire. |
| Evidence Reviewed | List the evidence reviewed, such as ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 report, penetration test summary, privacy notice, policies, DPA, deletion procedure, or audit report. |
| Technical and Organisational Measures Assessed | Summarise whether the vendor provides sufficient technical and organisational measures appropriate to the processing risk; include key gaps if any. |
| Access Control Assessment | Record the assessment outcome for identity, authentication, authorisation, privileged access, and access review controls; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed. |
| Encryption / Pseudonymisation Assessment | Record whether encryption in transit, encryption at rest, key management, masking, anonymisation, or pseudonymisation controls are adequate; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed. |
| Logging and Monitoring Assessment | Record whether activity logging, security monitoring, alerting, and log retention are adequate; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed. |
| Data Segregation Assessment | Record whether customer or controller data is logically or physically segregated and protected from unauthorised access; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed. |
| Backup and Business Continuity Assessment | Record whether backup, recovery, disaster recovery, and continuity arrangements are adequate for the service risk; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed. |
| Vulnerability / Penetration Testing Evidence | Enter the date and type of vulnerability assessment or penetration testing evidence reviewed, or enter Not Provided / Not Required. |
| Incident and Breach Notification Capability | Record whether the vendor can promptly notify the organisation of personal data breaches and security incidents within contractual and regulatory timelines; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, or Not Reviewed. |
| Data Subject Rights Support Capability | Record whether the vendor can support access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection, portability where applicable, and other PDPL data subject requests within required timelines. |
| Retention and Deletion Capability | Record whether the vendor can apply controller-defined retention periods and securely delete or anonymise personal data when no longer needed. |
| Return / Deletion on Termination Capability | Record whether the vendor can return, delete, or certify deletion of personal data at contract termination or controller instruction. |
| Audit / Inspection Rights Confirmed | Select Yes, No, or Not Applicable; confirm whether the contract gives the organisation audit, inspection, assurance, or evidence review rights over the processor. |
| Confidentiality Obligations Confirmed | Select Yes or No; confirm whether vendor personnel and sub-processors are bound by confidentiality obligations covering personal data. |
| Staff Training / Awareness Evidence | Record evidence that relevant vendor personnel receive privacy, data protection, information security, or confidentiality training; enter Not Provided if absent. |
| Processor Contract / DPA Required | Select Yes or No based on whether the vendor processes personal data on behalf of the organisation. |
| Processor Contract / DPA Status | Select one: Not Applicable, Not Started, In Negotiation, Executed, Executed with Exceptions, Expired, Rejected. |
| Mandatory PDPL Contract Clauses Confirmed | Select Yes, No, or Not Applicable; confirm the contract includes documented instructions, confidentiality, security measures, sub-processing controls, breach notification, data subject support, return/deletion, audit rights, and cross-border transfer restrictions where applicable. |
| Contract Effective Date | Enter the contract or DPA effective date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not executed. |
| Contract Expiry / Renewal Date | Enter the contract expiry, renewal, or next renewal date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A for evergreen contracts and note review date separately. |
| Residual Risk Rating | Select one: Low, Medium, High, Critical, based on remaining privacy and security risk after controls and contractual protections. |
| Risk Treatment Decision | Select one: Accept, Mitigate, Transfer, Avoid, Reject Vendor; include decision rationale if the rating is High or Critical. |
| Approver | Enter the name and role of the person approving use of the vendor, typically Privacy Officer, Data Protection Lead, CISO, Legal Counsel, or Risk Owner. |
| Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until approval is granted. |
| Conditions / Remediation Actions | List any required conditions before or after onboarding, such as contract clause changes, encryption enablement, sub-processor removal, deletion certificate, or transfer approval. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the internal or vendor owner responsible for completing remediation, in format Organisation/Vendor - Full Name or Team. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the remediation target completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation actions. |
| Remediation Status | Select one: Not Applicable, Open, In Progress, Overdue, Completed, Accepted Risk. |
| Ongoing Monitoring Frequency | Select one: Annual, Semi-Annual, Quarterly, Event-Driven, Contract Renewal Only, Not Applicable, based on vendor risk and processing sensitivity. |
| Last Review Date | Enter the most recent due diligence or monitoring review date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format, aligned to the monitoring frequency and risk rating. |
| Offboarding Date | Enter the date the vendor was offboarded or service ended in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank for active vendors. |
| Offboarding Evidence Reference | Enter the reference to evidence of data return, deletion, access revocation, or deletion certificate; enter N/A if vendor is active. |
| Record Status | Select one: Draft, Active, Approved for Use, Approved with Conditions, Rejected, Suspended, Offboarded, Archived. |
| Document / Evidence Repository Link | Enter the URL, document management path, GRC record link, or contract repository reference where supporting evidence is stored. |
| Comments | Enter any additional audit-relevant notes, exceptions, assumptions, or follow-up items not captured elsewhere. |

### Maintenance

The Privacy Officer or Data Protection Lead owns this template, with inputs from Legal, Procurement, Information Security, and the relevant Business Owner. It is updated at onboarding, contract renewal, material processing change, sub-processor change, cross-border transfer change, security incident, offboarding, and at the risk-based monitoring frequency, drawing from the GRC tool, procurement/vendor management system, contract repository, security assessment platform, and evidence document repository.

field_guidance.Record ID: Enter a unique identifier for this due diligence record, using format VDD-YYYY-NNN, e.g. VDD-2026-001.
field_guidance.Vendor / Processor Legal Name: Enter the full legal name of the vendor, processor, or service provider as shown in the contract or commercial registration.
field_guidance.Commercial Registration / Registration N: Enter the Saudi commercial registration number, foreign company registration number, or equivalent official identifier; enter N/A only if not available.
field_guidance.Country of Establishment: Enter the country where the vendor legal entity is incorporated or registered, using the full country name.
field_guidance.Vendor Role: Select one: Processor, Sub-Processor, Independent Controller, Joint Controller, Service Provider with No Personal Data Access, Other.
field_guidance.Business Owner: Enter the internal business function and named owner accountable for the service, in format Department - Full Name.
field_guidance.Procurement / Contract Owner: Enter the internal procurement, legal, or contract management owner, in format Department - Full Name.
field_guidance.Service / Processing Description: Describe the service provided and the processing activity in one concise sentence, including the system or platform name if applicable.
field_guidance.Personal Data Processing Purpose: State the specific, lawful business purpose for which personal data will be processed; do not use generic wording such as 'business purposes'.
field_guidance.PDPL Controller / Processor Relationship: Describe the PDPL relationship and instruction model, e.g. 'Organisation is Controller; vendor processes only on documented instructions'.
field_guidance.Data Subject Categories: List the categories of individuals whose personal data is processed, e.g. Employees, Customers, Website Users, Suppliers, Patients, Applicants.
field_guidance.Personal Data Categories: List the categories of personal data processed, e.g. name, national ID/Iqama, contact details, payroll data, account credentials, location data.
field_guidance.Sensitive Personal Data Involved: Select Yes or No; if Yes, specify the categories such as health data, biometric data, genetic data, religious data, credit data, or similar PDPL-sensitive data.
field_guidance.Criminal / Security Data Involved: Select Yes or No; if Yes, describe the criminal, security, or related records processed and confirm additional approvals or controls where applicable.
field_guidance.Children / Minors Data Involved: Select Yes or No; if Yes, describe the age group and any guardian consent or additional protection requirements.
field_guidance.Estimated Data Volume: Enter the approximate number of data subjects or records processed, using a number or defined range such as <1,000, 1,000-10,000, 10,001-100,000, >100,000.
field_guidance.Processing Locations: List all countries and hosting regions where personal data is stored, accessed, supported, backed up, or processed.
field_guidance.Cross-Border Transfer Involved: Select Yes or No based on whether personal data is transferred, accessed, stored, supported, or backed up outside Saudi Arabia.
field_guidance.Cross-Border Transfer Countries: If cross-border transfer is Yes, list each destination country; if No, enter N/A.
field_guidance.Cross-Border Transfer Legal Basis / Asse: Enter the approved transfer basis and reference to the transfer assessment or approval record, e.g. TIA-YYYY-NNN; enter N/A if no transfer.
field_guidance.Sub-Processors Used: Select Yes or No; if Yes, list the sub-processors or reference the approved sub-processor list.
field_guidance.Sub-Processor Approval Status: Select one: Not Applicable, Pending Review, Approved, Approved with Conditions, Rejected; include approval reference if applicable.
field_guidance.Due Diligence Initiation Date: Enter the date due diligence started in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Due Diligence Status: Select one: Not Started, In Progress, Awaiting Vendor Response, Under Review, Approved, Approved with Conditions, Rejected, Expired.
field_guidance.Due Diligence Reviewer: Enter the name and role of the privacy, legal, information security, or risk reviewer completing the assessment.
field_guidance.Security Questionnaire Completed: Select Yes, No, or Not Required; if Yes, reference the questionnaire file or ticket ID.
field_guidance.Privacy / PDPL Questionnaire Completed: Select Yes, No, or Not Required; if Yes, reference the completed PDPL/privacy questionnaire.
field_guidance.Evidence Reviewed: List the evidence reviewed, such as ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 report, penetration test summary, privacy notice, policies, DPA, deletion procedure, or audit report.
field_guidance.Technical and Organisational Measures As: Summarise whether the vendor provides sufficient technical and organisational measures appropriate to the processing risk; include key gaps if any.
field_guidance.Access Control Assessment: Record the assessment outcome for identity, authentication, authorisation, privileged access, and access review controls; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed.
field_guidance.Encryption / Pseudonymisation Assessment: Record whether encryption in transit, encryption at rest, key management, masking, anonymisation, or pseudonymisation controls are adequate; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed.
field_guidance.Logging and Monitoring Assessment: Record whether activity logging, security monitoring, alerting, and log retention are adequate; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed.
field_guidance.Data Segregation Assessment: Record whether customer or controller data is logically or physically segregated and protected from unauthorised access; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed.
field_guidance.Backup and Business Continuity Assessmen: Record whether backup, recovery, disaster recovery, and continuity arrangements are adequate for the service risk; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, Not Applicable, or Not Reviewed.
field_guidance.Vulnerability / Penetration Testing Evid: Enter the date and type of vulnerability assessment or penetration testing evidence reviewed, or enter Not Provided / Not Required.
field_guidance.Incident and Breach Notification Capabil: Record whether the vendor can promptly notify the organisation of personal data breaches and security incidents within contractual and regulatory timelines; use Satisfactory, Gap Identified, or Not Reviewed.
field_guidance.Data Subject Rights Support Capability: Record whether the vendor can support access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection, portability where applicable, and other PDPL data subject requests within required timelines.
field_guidance.Retention and Deletion Capability: Record whether the vendor can apply controller-defined retention periods and securely delete or anonymise personal data when no longer needed.
field_guidance.Return / Deletion on Termination Capabil: Record whether the vendor can return, delete, or certify deletion of personal data at contract termination or controller instruction.
field_guidance.Audit / Inspection Rights Confirmed: Select Yes, No, or Not Applicable; confirm whether the contract gives the organisation audit, inspection, assurance, or evidence review rights over the processor.
field_guidance.Confidentiality Obligations Confirmed: Select Yes or No; confirm whether vendor personnel and sub-processors are bound by confidentiality obligations covering personal data.
field_guidance.Staff Training / Awareness Evidence: Record evidence that relevant vendor personnel receive privacy, data protection, information security, or confidentiality training; enter Not Provided if absent.
field_guidance.Processor Contract / DPA Required: Select Yes or No based on whether the vendor processes personal data on behalf of the organisation.
field_guidance.Processor Contract / DPA Status: Select one: Not Applicable, Not Started, In Negotiation, Executed, Executed with Exceptions, Expired, Rejected.
field_guidance.Mandatory PDPL Contract Clauses Confirme: Select Yes, No, or Not Applicable; confirm the contract includes documented instructions, confidentiality, security measures, sub-processing controls, breach notification, data subject support, return/deletion, audit rights, and cross-border transfer restrictions where applicable.
field_guidance.Contract Effective Date: Enter the contract or DPA effective date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not executed.
field_guidance.Contract Expiry / Renewal Date: Enter the contract expiry, renewal, or next renewal date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A for evergreen contracts and note review date separately.
field_guidance.Residual Risk Rating: Select one: Low, Medium, High, Critical, based on remaining privacy and security risk after controls and contractual protections.
field_guidance.Risk Treatment Decision: Select one: Accept, Mitigate, Transfer, Avoid, Reject Vendor; include decision rationale if the rating is High or Critical.
field_guidance.Approver: Enter the name and role of the person approving use of the vendor, typically Privacy Officer, Data Protection Lead, CISO, Legal Counsel, or Risk Owner.
field_guidance.Approval Date: Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until approval is granted.
field_guidance.Conditions / Remediation Actions: List any required conditions before or after onboarding, such as contract clause changes, encryption enablement, sub-processor removal, deletion certificate, or transfer approval.
field_guidance.Remediation Owner: Enter the internal or vendor owner responsible for completing remediation, in format Organisation/Vendor - Full Name or Team.
field_guidance.Remediation Due Date: Enter the remediation target completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation actions.
field_guidance.Remediation Status: Select one: Not Applicable, Open, In Progress, Overdue, Completed, Accepted Risk.
field_guidance.Ongoing Monitoring Frequency: Select one: Annual, Semi-Annual, Quarterly, Event-Driven, Contract Renewal Only, Not Applicable, based on vendor risk and processing sensitivity.
field_guidance.Last Review Date: Enter the most recent due diligence or monitoring review date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Next Review Date: Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format, aligned to the monitoring frequency and risk rating.

field_guidance.Offboarding Evidence Reference: Enter the reference to evidence of data return, deletion, access revocation, or deletion certificate; enter N/A if vendor is active.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| DSR Reference ID | Enter a unique case reference for the request, using a consistent format such as DSR-YYYY-0001. |
| Request Received Date | Enter the calendar date the organisation first received the DSR in YYYY-MM-DD format; this starts the 30-day response period. |
| Request Received Time | Enter the time the request was received in 24-hour format HH:MM using local Saudi Arabia time. |
| Intake Channel | Select the channel used to submit the request: Web Form, Email, Phone, In Person, Mobile App, Postal Mail, Regulator Referral, Other. |
| Requester Type | Select who submitted the request: Data Subject, Legal Representative, Guardian, Attorney, Authorized Agent, Other. |
| Data Subject Name | Enter the full name of the individual whose personal data is the subject of the request. |
| Data Subject Identifier | Enter the internal customer, employee, patient, user, or account ID used to locate the data subject; do not enter unnecessary sensitive identifiers unless required for verification. |
| Representative Name | If the requester is not the data subject, enter the representative’s full name; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Representative Authority Verified | Record whether authority to act for the data subject has been verified: Yes, No, Pending, Not Applicable. |
| Contact Details for Response | Enter the approved contact point for the response, such as verified email address, postal address, account inbox, or phone number. |
| Right Exercised | Select the PDPL right requested: Access/Obtain Copy, Correction/Completion/Update, Destruction/Deletion, Withdraw Consent, Objection/Restriction where applicable, Information About Processing, Other. |
| Request Summary | Briefly describe what the data subject is asking for, including relevant dates, accounts, services, or data categories. |
| Personal Data / Processing Activity in Scope | Identify the personal data categories, records, service, processing purpose, or activity covered by the request. |
| Related System(s) / Data Owner(s) | List the systems, applications, repositories, business units, or data owners that must search, assess, correct, export, or delete data. |
| Identity Verification Status | Record the verification status before acting on the request: Not Started, In Progress, Verified, Failed, Not Required. |
| Identity Verification Completed Date | Enter the date identity verification was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format, or Not Applicable if verification is not required. |
| Request Validity Status | Record whether the request is valid and actionable: Valid, Partially Valid, Invalid, Duplicate, Withdrawn, Awaiting Clarification. |
| Clarification Requested | Record whether additional information was needed to process the request: Yes or No. |
| Clarification Requested Date | If clarification was requested, enter the date sent in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Clarification Received Date | If clarification was received, enter the date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter Not Applicable or Pending. |
| Statutory Response Due Date | Enter the initial deadline for response in YYYY-MM-DD format, calculated as 30 days from receipt unless internal policy applies a shorter period. |
| Extension Applied | Record whether the additional 30-day extension was applied: Yes or No. |
| Extension Notice Sent Date | If an extension was applied, enter the date the data subject was notified in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Extended Due Date | If an extension was applied, enter the extended deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format, not exceeding an additional 30 days; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Reason for Extension | If an extension was applied, state the reason such as complexity, volume of records, multiple systems, third-party consultation, or legal review; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Assigned Case Owner | Enter the name or role of the person accountable for coordinating and closing the DSR case. |
| Department(s) Consulted | List functions consulted, such as Privacy, Legal, IT, HR, Customer Service, Security, Records Management, Marketing, Operations, or specific business units. |
| Assessment Outcome | Record the decision after assessment: Fulfil in Full, Fulfil in Part, Refuse, No Data Found, Request Withdrawn, Duplicate Closed. |
| Refusal / Limitation Ground | If refused or partly fulfilled, enter the lawful reason and internal/legal reference; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Action Taken | Describe the operational action completed, such as copy exported, data corrected, data deleted, processing stopped, consent withdrawn, or information notice sent. |
| Response Sent Date | Enter the date the final response was sent to the requester in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Response Method | Select the method used to send the response: Secure Portal, Encrypted Email, Registered Mail, In Person, Account Inbox, Phone Confirmation, Other. |
| Response Summary | Summarise what was communicated to the requester, including whether the request was fulfilled, partly fulfilled, refused, or no data was found. |
| Data Provided / Corrected / Destroyed | Record the data package, correction, deletion, or other outcome delivered, including file name, record ID, or description where applicable. |
| Third Parties Notified | Record whether processors, controllers, recipients, or other third parties were notified to correct, delete, restrict, or otherwise action the request: Yes, No, Not Applicable. |
| Third Party Notification Details | If third parties were notified, list the recipient organisation, date notified, requested action, and confirmation status; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Data Subject Complaint / Escalation | Record whether the requester complained or the case was escalated: Yes or No. |
| Complaint / Escalation Details | If applicable, enter escalation route, complaint reference, regulator involvement, issue summary, and current status; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the case was fully closed in YYYY-MM-DD format after all actions, approvals, evidence capture, and communications are complete. |
| Final Status | Select the final case status: Open, Awaiting Requester, In Progress, Pending Approval, Closed - Fulfilled, Closed - Part Fulfilled, Closed - Refused, Closed - Withdrawn, Closed - Duplicate. |
| Days to Close | Enter the number of calendar days from Request Received Date to Closure Date as a whole number. |
| SLA Status | Record timeliness status: Within 30 Days, Within Extended Deadline, Overdue, Not Yet Due. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the secure repository path, case management link, ticket number, or document management reference containing request evidence, verification, assessment, response, approvals, and communications. |
| Approver | Enter the name or role of the person who approved the response or refusal, such as Data Protection Officer, Privacy Lead, Legal Counsel, or Business Owner. |
| Approval Date | Enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or Not Applicable if approval was not required by procedure. |
| Notes | Enter any additional audit-relevant context, dependencies, risks, or follow-up actions; avoid recording unnecessary personal data. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Office, with case-level updates made immediately upon each DSR event and reviewed at least monthly for SLA compliance and completeness. Source data should be drawn from the DSR case management workflow, privacy mailbox/web form, CRM/HR systems, identity verification records, legal assessments, and evidence repository.

PDPL-027.title: Personal Data Breach Register
PDPL-027.content:
## Personal Data Breach Register (XLSX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Breach ID | Incident/Ticket Reference | Date/Time Discovered | Discovered By | Date/Time Breach Occurred | Date/Time Breach Contained | Business Unit / Process Owner | System / Application / Location | Breach Description | Breach Type | Root Cause Category | Personal Data Categories Involved | Sensitive Personal Data Involved | Special Category Details | Estimated Number of Data Subjects Affected | Data Subject Categories | Estimated Number of Records Affected | Saudi Residents / Individuals in KSA Affected | Cross-Border Impact | Third Party / Processor Involved | Confidentiality Impact | Integrity Impact | Availability Impact | Risk of Harm to Data Subjects | Risk Assessment Rationale | PDPL Art. 20 Classification | SDAIA Notification Required | SDAIA Notification Deadline | SDAIA Notification Submitted Date/Time | SDAIA Notification Reference | Data Subject Notification Required | Data Subject Notification Date/Time | Data Subject Notification Method | Notification Content Summary | Immediate Containment Actions | Corrective / Remediation Actions | Responsible Action Owner | Target Remediation Date | Remediation Status | Residual Risk Rating | Evidence / Document Link | Legal / DPO Review Completed | Management Approval / Escalation | Closure Date | Lessons Learned | Record Last Updated |
