| [EXAMPLE: PDB-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: INC-445812] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-15 14:30 AST] | [EXAMPLE: SOC Analyst] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-15 13:50 AST] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-15 16:10 AST] | [EXAMPLE: Customer Operations / Head of Customer Service] | [EXAMPLE: CRM system] | [EXAMPLE: Customer records were accessed using a compromised support account before the account was disabled.] | [EXAMPLE: Unauthorised Access] | [EXAMPLE: Phishing/Compromise] | [EXAMPLE: Name, mobile number, email address, customer ID] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: 250] | [EXAMPLE: Customers] | [EXAMPLE: 250] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: Medium] | [EXAMPLE: Contact details were exposed but no credentials or sensitive personal data were involved; phishing risk exists.] | [EXAMPLE: Personal Data Breach - SDAIA Notifiable] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-18 14:30 AST] | [EXAMPLE: Pending] | [EXAMPLE: Pending] | [EXAMPLE: Pending Legal/DPO Review] | [EXAMPLE: Pending] | [EXAMPLE: Pending] | [EXAMPLE: Nature of breach, affected data categories, containment actions, recommended vigilance against phishing, contact channel.] | [EXAMPLE: Account disabled, password reset, active sessions revoked, access logs preserved.] | [EXAMPLE: MFA enforcement for support portal and targeted phishing retraining.] | [EXAMPLE: IT Security Manager] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-04-05] | [EXAMPLE: In Progress] | [EXAMPLE: Medium] | [EXAMPLE: GRC repository link to INC-445812 investigation folder] | [EXAMPLE: Yes - 2026-03-16 - DPO] | [EXAMPLE: Escalated to Privacy Incident Committee on 2026-03-16] | [EXAMPLE: Pending] | [EXAMPLE: Improve privileged support account monitoring and phishing controls.] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-16 - DPO] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Breach ID | Enter a unique register identifier for the breach using a consistent format, e.g. PDB-YYYY-###. |
| Incident/Ticket Reference | Enter the linked security, privacy, legal, or service desk ticket number; use N/A if no separate ticket exists. |
| Date/Time Discovered | Enter the date and time the organisation first became aware of the suspected or confirmed personal data breach in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format with time zone, e.g. 2026-03-15 14:30 AST. |
| Discovered By | Enter the name or role/team that discovered or reported the breach, e.g. SOC Analyst, Customer Support, Processor, Employee. |
| Date/Time Breach Occurred | Enter the known or estimated date and time the breach occurred in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM time zone format; if unknown, state Unknown and record the best estimated range if available. |
| Date/Time Breach Contained | Enter the date and time containment was completed in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM time zone format; use Pending if not yet contained. |
| Business Unit / Process Owner | Enter the accountable business unit and process owner for the affected processing activity. |
| System / Application / Location | Enter the affected system, database, application, physical location, or repository where the personal data was held or processed. |
| Breach Description | Enter a concise factual summary of what happened, how it was identified, and the current known scope; do not include unnecessary personal data in this field. |
| Breach Type | Select the main breach type: Unauthorised Access, Unauthorised Disclosure, Loss, Theft, Alteration, Destruction, Unavailability, Misdelivery, Malware/Ransomware, Phishing/Compromise, Other. |
| Root Cause Category | Select the primary root cause: Human Error, Process Failure, Technical Vulnerability, Malicious Insider, External Attack, Third-Party Failure, Physical Security Failure, Misconfiguration, Unknown, Other. |
| Personal Data Categories Involved | List the categories of personal data involved, e.g. name, national ID/Iqama, contact details, financial data, employment data, location data, account credentials. |
| Sensitive Personal Data Involved | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether sensitive personal data under Saudi PDPL is involved. |
| Special Category Details | If sensitive personal data is involved, specify the type, e.g. health data, biometric data, genetic data, credit data, religious belief, security data; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Estimated Number of Data Subjects Affected | Enter the confirmed or best estimated number of individuals affected as a whole number; if unknown, enter Unknown and update when confirmed. |
| Data Subject Categories | List affected categories of individuals, e.g. customers, employees, contractors, patients, website users, applicants, suppliers’ contacts. |
| Estimated Number of Records Affected | Enter the confirmed or estimated number of personal data records affected as a whole number; if unknown, enter Unknown. |
| Saudi Residents / Individuals in KSA Affected | Enter Yes, No, or Unknown to indicate whether the breach affects individuals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia or Saudi residents. |
| Cross-Border Impact | Enter Yes, No, or Unknown; if Yes, list countries or overseas recipients involved in the breach. |
| Third Party / Processor Involved | Enter Yes or No; if Yes, identify the processor, vendor, controller, or other third party involved and their role. |
| Confidentiality Impact | Select impact level: None, Low, Medium, High, Critical, based on unauthorised access or disclosure of personal data. |
| Integrity Impact | Select impact level: None, Low, Medium, High, Critical, based on unauthorised or accidental alteration of personal data. |
| Availability Impact | Select impact level: None, Low, Medium, High, Critical, based on loss, destruction, or unavailability of personal data. |
| Risk of Harm to Data Subjects | Select risk level: Low, Medium, High, Critical, based on potential harm to individuals’ rights, privacy, safety, finances, reputation, or other interests. |
| Risk Assessment Rationale | Record the reasoning for the risk rating, including sensitivity of data, volume, identifiability, misuse likelihood, affected individuals, safeguards, and likely consequences. |
| PDPL Art. 20 Classification | Classify the event for Saudi PDPL Article 20 purposes as: Not a Personal Data Breach, Personal Data Breach - No Notifiable Harm Expected, Personal Data Breach - SDAIA Notifiable, Personal Data Breach - Data Subject Notifiable, Personal Data Breach - SDAIA and Data Subject Notifiable. |
| SDAIA Notification Required | Enter Yes, No, or Pending Legal/DPO Review based on whether the breach may cause harm to personal data or data subjects and therefore requires notification to the competent authority under PDPL Art. 20. |
| SDAIA Notification Deadline | Enter the applicable regulatory notification deadline in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM time zone format, calculated from awareness according to Saudi PDPL/Implementing Regulation requirements; enter N/A if not required. |
| SDAIA Notification Submitted Date/Time | Enter the actual submission date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM time zone format; enter N/A if not required or Pending if not yet submitted. |
| SDAIA Notification Reference | Enter the authority submission reference number, portal reference, email reference, or other proof of notification; enter N/A if not required. |
| Data Subject Notification Required | Enter Yes, No, or Pending Legal/DPO Review based on whether the breach is likely to cause damage or harm requiring notification to affected data subjects under PDPL Art. 20. |
| Data Subject Notification Date/Time | Enter the date and time affected data subjects were notified in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM time zone format; enter N/A if not required or Pending if not yet completed. |
| Data Subject Notification Method | Enter the method used to notify affected individuals, e.g. email, SMS, phone, postal letter, in-app notice, website notice; enter N/A if not required. |
| Notification Content Summary | Summarise the key notification content, including nature of breach, affected data, likely consequences, measures taken, recommended steps for individuals, and contact point; do not paste full notices unless linked as evidence. |
| Immediate Containment Actions | Record urgent actions taken to stop or limit the breach, e.g. account disabled, access revoked, system isolated, email recalled, vendor instructed, password reset. |
| Corrective / Remediation Actions | Record planned or completed actions to address root cause and prevent recurrence, e.g. patching, policy change, access review, encryption, staff training, processor corrective action. |
| Responsible Action Owner | Enter the named role or person accountable for completing remediation actions. |
| Target Remediation Date | Enter the planned completion date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Remediation Status | Select status: Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Overdue, Accepted Risk, Cancelled. |
| Residual Risk Rating | Select the remaining risk after remediation: Low, Medium, High, Critical; update at closure. |
| Evidence / Document Link | Enter the link or reference to supporting evidence, including investigation report, screenshots, logs, notification copies, approvals, and remediation proof. |
| Legal / DPO Review Completed | Enter Yes, No, or N/A; if Yes, include review date in YYYY-MM-DD format and reviewer role/name. |
| Management Approval / Escalation | Record any escalation to executive management, crisis team, board, or risk committee, including approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the breach record was formally closed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank or enter Pending until all required actions and notifications are complete. |
| Lessons Learned | Record concise lessons learned and control improvements identified from the breach investigation. |
| Record Last Updated | Enter the most recent update date in YYYY-MM-DD format and initials or role of the updater. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Office, with updates made immediately upon breach discovery and at each investigation, notification, remediation, and closure milestone; the register is reviewed at least monthly and after every major incident. Source data should be drawn from the incident management system, SIEM/security logs, service desk tickets, processor/vendor notifications, legal/DPO assessments, and regulatory notification evidence.

PDPL-028.title: SDAIA Breach Notification
PDPL-028.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-PRIV-FRM-XXX] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer / Privacy Office | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Saudi Personal Data Protection Law | Confidential |

## Purpose

This form is used to prepare, review, approve, and submit a personal data breach notification to the Saudi Data & AI Authority when a personal data breach is likely to cause harm to individuals, affect their rights or interests, or otherwise require notification under applicable Saudi personal data protection requirements.

The form supports timely, consistent, and complete breach notification by capturing:

- The nature and circumstances of the personal data breach.
- The categories and approximate volume of affected personal data and individuals.
- The likely consequences for affected individuals.
- Immediate containment, mitigation, and corrective actions.
- The organisation’s assessment of notification requirement and urgency.
- Details of the notification submitted to the authority.
- Internal approvals, routing, evidence, and retention records.

This template is intended for use by the Privacy Office, Data Protection Officer, Legal, Information Security, Incident Response, Compliance, and business process owners involved in responding to a personal data breach.

## Instructions

1. **Open this form immediately when a suspected or confirmed personal data breach is identified.**
 - Do not wait for full forensic completion before starting the form.
 - Complete known information first and mark unknown items as “Under investigation”.
 - Update the form as additional facts are confirmed.

2. **Use this form for breaches involving personal data processed by or on behalf of the organisation.**
 - Personal data includes any data that can directly or indirectly identify an individual.
 - Sensitive personal data requires heightened review and escalation.
 - Breaches may include unauthorised access, disclosure, loss, alteration, destruction, ransomware, misdirected communications, insecure publication, theft, accidental deletion, or compromise of systems containing personal data.

3. **Notify the Privacy Office and Information Security Incident Response team without delay.**
 - Initial internal escalation must occur as soon as the incident is detected.
 - Where facts are incomplete, provide the best available estimate and state the assumptions used.

4. **Assess whether notification to the authority is required.**
 Notification is required where the breach may cause harm to individuals, affect their rights or interests, involve sensitive or high-risk personal data, affect a significant number of individuals, or otherwise create material privacy risk. The assessment must consider:
 - Type and sensitivity of personal data involved.
 - Number and categories of affected individuals.
 - Ease of identifying affected individuals from the data.
 - Risk of identity theft, fraud, financial loss, discrimination, reputational damage, physical harm, distress, or loss of confidentiality.
 - Whether the data was encrypted, anonymised, tokenised, or otherwise protected.
 - Whether the data has been accessed, acquired, disclosed, copied, exfiltrated, published, or misused.
 - Whether containment has been completed.
 - Whether the recipient is trusted, bound by confidentiality, and has confirmed secure deletion or non-use.

5. **Submit notification without undue delay once notification is determined to be required.**
 - Notification must not be delayed solely because all details are not yet available.
 - Where information is incomplete, submit an initial notification with available facts and planned follow-up.
 - Submit supplementary updates when material new information becomes available.

6. **Coordinate individual notification separately where required.**
 - This form is for authority notification.
 - If the breach may result in material harm to affected individuals or requires individuals to take protective action, complete the organisation’s data subject breach communication process and template.

7. **Maintain evidence.**
 Attach or reference supporting records, including incident tickets, forensic reports, logs, screenshots, email evidence, vendor communications, risk assessments, approval records, submitted notification copies, and authority correspondence.

8. **Do not include unnecessary personal data in this form.**
 - Use summaries, counts, and categories wherever possible.
 - Do not paste full datasets, national identification numbers, credentials, health records, financial account details, or other sensitive values into this form unless explicitly required and approved by Legal and the Privacy Office.
 - Store the completed form only in approved restricted-access repositories.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Breach Reference ID | Text | Yes | Unique internal reference, aligned to the incident ticket or case management number. Example: `PB-[YYYY]-[###]`. |
| Related Incident / Ticket ID | Text | Yes | Link or reference to the security, privacy, legal, customer service, or operational incident record. |
| Date and Time Breach Detected | Date/time | Yes | Record when the organisation first became aware of facts indicating a potential personal data breach. Include time zone. |
| Date and Time Breach Occurred | Date/time | Conditional | Provide actual or estimated start and end times. If unknown, state “Under investigation” and provide best available range. |
| Date and Time Privacy Office Notified | Date/time | Yes | Record when the Privacy Office or Data Protection Officer was first notified. |
| Date and Time Incident Response Activated | Date/time | Yes | Record when formal incident response began. |
| Prepared By | Name / role | Yes | Person completing this form. Include department and contact details. |
| Business Owner | Name / role | Yes | Owner of the affected business process, product, service, or dataset. |
| Data Controller Role | Dropdown / text | Yes | State whether the organisation is acting as controller, processor, joint controller, or another role. If acting as processor, identify the controller and contractual notification obligations. |
| Affected Business Process | Text | Yes | Name the process, service, system, location, project, vendor, or business unit involved. |
| Affected System(s) / Repository | Text | Yes | Identify applications, databases, storage locations, collaboration platforms, email systems, devices, paper files, or third-party environments involved. |
| Breach Status | Dropdown | Yes | Select: Suspected, Confirmed, Contained, Ongoing, Closed, Reopened. |
| Breach Type | Multi-select | Yes | Select all that apply: Unauthorised access, unauthorised disclosure, accidental disclosure, loss, theft, alteration, deletion, destruction, ransomware, malware, phishing, credential compromise, misconfiguration, exposed storage, misdirected communication, physical records breach, third-party breach, other. |
| Breach Description | Long text | Yes | Provide a concise factual description of what happened, how it was detected, and what is currently known. Avoid speculation. |
| Root Cause Summary | Long text | Conditional | Provide confirmed or preliminary cause, such as human error, system misconfiguration, compromised credentials, inadequate access control, vendor failure, malicious insider, external attack, or process failure. |
| Personal Data Involved | Long text | Yes | List categories of personal data involved, not individual records. Examples: name, contact details, national ID, account details, employment data, location data, device identifiers, images, health data, financial data, biometric data. |
| Sensitive Personal Data Involved | Yes/no + text | Yes | State whether sensitive personal data is involved. If yes, describe categories and safeguards in place. |
| Children’s Data Involved | Yes/no/unknown | Yes | Indicate whether personal data of minors is involved or may be involved. |
| Approximate Number of Affected Individuals | Number / estimate | Yes | Provide confirmed number or reasonable estimate. State the basis of calculation. |
| Categories of Affected Individuals | Multi-select / text | Yes | Examples: customers, employees, contractors, job applicants, patients, students, suppliers, visitors, app users, citizens, residents, dependants, other. |
| Geographic Scope | Text | Yes | State whether affected individuals are in Saudi Arabia, outside Saudi Arabia, or both. Include relevant countries if known. |
| Approximate Number of Records Involved | Number / estimate | Conditional | Provide where different from number of individuals. State whether count is confirmed or estimated. |
| Data Format | Multi-select | Yes | Select: Electronic structured data, electronic documents, email, logs, backups, images/video/audio, paper records, portable media, endpoint device, cloud storage, other. |
| Data Protection Measures in Place | Multi-select / text | Yes | Identify protections relevant to the breached data: encryption, hashing, masking, pseudonymisation, access controls, MFA, DLP, logging, network segmentation, secure deletion, physical controls, contractual confidentiality, other. |
| Was Data Encrypted or Rendered Unreadable? | Yes/no/partial/unknown | Yes | State whether protection was effective at the time of breach. Include encryption status, key exposure status, and whether data could realistically be read or used. |
| Evidence of Access or Exfiltration | Dropdown + text | Yes | Select: Confirmed, Suspected, No evidence, Under investigation. Summarise logs, alerts, forensic findings, recipient confirmation, or other evidence. |
| Unauthorised Recipient / Actor | Text | Conditional | Identify known or suspected recipient or threat actor, where appropriate. If unknown, state unknown. Do not include unnecessary personal details. |
| Data Published or Made Publicly Accessible? | Yes/no/unknown | Yes | If yes, include location, duration of exposure, takedown actions, and whether indexing or downloads occurred. |
| Breach Contained? | Yes/no/partial | Yes | State containment status and time of containment. If not contained, explain outstanding exposure. |
| Immediate Containment Actions | Long text | Yes | Examples: disabled accounts, revoked tokens, removed public access, isolated systems, reset passwords, recovered device, contacted unintended recipient, suspended vendor connection, blocked IPs, restored access controls. |
| Mitigation Actions Completed | Long text | Yes | Describe actions taken to reduce harm to individuals and prevent further exposure. |
| Corrective Actions Planned | Long text | Yes | Include longer-term remediation such as access review, system hardening, user training, process redesign, vendor corrective action, monitoring, audit, disciplinary review, or policy update. |
| Likely Impact on Individuals | Long text | Yes | Describe potential harms in practical terms, such as fraud, identity theft, financial loss, account compromise, embarrassment, reputational harm, discrimination, emotional distress, physical safety risk, loss of confidentiality, service disruption, or inability to exercise rights. |
| Risk Severity Assessment | Dropdown | Yes | Select: Low, Medium, High, Critical. Base on likelihood and impact to affected individuals, not only business impact. |
| Risk Assessment Rationale | Long text | Yes | Explain why the severity rating was assigned. Include sensitivity of data, volume, exposure duration, protection measures, evidence of misuse, and individual vulnerability. |
| Notification to Authority Required? | Yes/no/under review | Yes | Record the decision. If “No”, provide rationale and obtain Privacy and Legal approval. If “Under review”, set decision deadline and owner. |
| Reason for Authority Notification Decision | Long text | Yes | Explain the decision in plain language. Include whether the breach may harm individuals or affect their rights or interests. |
| Date and Time Notification Decision Made | Date/time | Yes | Record when the decision was made and by whom. |
| Notification Urgency | Dropdown | Yes | Select: Immediate, Same day, Next business day, Awaiting material facts. Delays must be justified and approved. |
| Reason for Any Delay | Long text | Conditional | Complete if notification is not submitted promptly after decision. Include operational, legal, evidentiary, or technical reason and approval. |
| Authority Notification Type | Dropdown | Conditional | Select: Initial notification, supplementary update, correction, closure update. |
| Proposed Notification Summary | Long text | Conditional | Draft the notification narrative for submission. Include what happened, when it happened, data involved, affected individuals, consequences, actions taken, and contact point. |
| Information Not Yet Available | Long text | Conditional | Identify missing facts and when updates will be provided. Use this for initial notifications where investigation is ongoing. |
| Contact Point for Authority | Name / role / email / phone | Conditional | Provide the organisation’s authorised contact for follow-up questions. |
| Submitted to Authority? | Yes/no/not applicable | Yes | Record whether notification has been submitted. |
| Submission Date and Time | Date/time | Conditional | Include time zone and submission method. |
| Submission Method | Text | Conditional | Record portal, email, official form, letter, or other approved channel used. |
| Authority Reference Number | Text | Conditional | Record acknowledgement, case, or reference number issued by the authority. |
| Copy of Submitted Notification Stored | Link / location | Conditional | Provide secure repository link or record location. Do not attach unnecessary personal data. |
| Follow-Up Required by Authority? | Yes/no/pending | Conditional | Record requests, deadlines, and assigned owners. |
| Supplementary Notification Required? | Yes/no/under review | Conditional | Indicate whether updates will be submitted due to missing facts, changed risk, increased affected population, new evidence, or remediation updates. |
| Data Subject Notification Required? | Yes/no/under review | Yes | Record whether individuals must be notified. If yes, reference the separate communication plan and approved message. |
| Customer / Regulator / Contractual Notifications | Long text | Conditional | Identify other required notifications, such as contractual customers, sector regulator, insurer, law enforcement, or partner organisations. |
| Processor / Vendor Involvement | Yes/no | Yes | State whether a processor, supplier, cloud provider, consultant, or outsourced service provider is involved. |
| Vendor Name and Contact | Text | Conditional | Provide vendor name, service, contact, incident reference, and contractual obligations triggered. |
| Vendor Notification Received Date and Time | Date/time | Conditional | If breach was reported by a vendor, record when notice was received and whether it was timely. |
| Cross-Border Data Transfer Involved | Yes/no/unknown | Yes | State whether the breached data was stored, accessed, processed, or disclosed outside Saudi Arabia. |
| Law Enforcement Involvement | Yes/no/under review | Yes | Record whether law enforcement has been or should be contacted, especially for criminal activity, extortion, theft, or threat to safety. |
| Cybersecurity Incident Linkage | Yes/no | Yes | State whether the breach is part of a cybersecurity incident requiring separate technical or regulatory reporting. |
| Media / Public Exposure | Yes/no/monitoring | Yes | Record whether the incident is public, likely to become public, or requires communications monitoring. |
| Communications Lead | Name / role | Conditional | Identify internal communications or public relations owner if external messaging may be required. |
| Legal Privilege Requested | Yes/no | Yes | Indicate whether Legal has directed privileged handling of investigation materials. |
| Attachments / Evidence Index | Long text / links | Yes | List supporting documents and secure storage locations. Examples: incident timeline, logs, forensic report, screenshots, vendor notices, notification copy, approval emails. |
| Open Actions | Table / text | Yes | List all open actions, owners, due dates, and status. See action tracker below. |
| Final Closure Summary | Long text | Conditional | Complete when investigation and notifications are closed. Summarise outcome, final affected population, notifications completed, remediation status, and lessons learned. |
| Closure Date | Date | Conditional | Date the Privacy Office closes the breach notification record. |
| Closure Approved By | Name / role | Conditional | Privacy Office, Legal, DPO, or authorised approver confirming closure. |

**Incident Timeline**

| Event | Date and Time | Owner / Source | Evidence Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Breach occurred or estimated start | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / team] | [Link / reference] | [Known facts or estimate basis] |
| Breach detected | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / team] | [Link / reference] | [Detection method] |
| Internal escalation made | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / team] | [Link / reference] | [Recipients / channels] |
| Containment initiated | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / team] | [Link / reference] | [Actions started] |
| Containment completed | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / team] | [Link / reference] | [If partial, explain] |
| Notification decision made | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / role] | [Link / reference] | [Required / not required / under review] |
| Authority notified | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / role] | [Link / reference] | [Submission method and reference] |
| Supplementary update submitted | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / role] | [Link / reference] | [If applicable] |
| Individual notification issued | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / role] | [Link / reference] | [If applicable] |
| Case closed | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Name / role] | [Link / reference] | [Closure rationale] |

**Open Action Tracker**

| Action ID | Action Description | Owner | Due Date | Status | Evidence / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BA-001 | [Containment or remediation action] | [Name / team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Not started / In progress / Complete | [Link / notes] |
| BA-002 | [Notification or investigation action] | [Name / team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Not started / In progress / Complete | [Link / notes] |
| BA-003 | [Corrective or preventive action] | [Name / team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Not started / In progress / Complete | [Link / notes] |

**Authority Notification Content Checklist**

| Notification Element | Included? | Location in Submission | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Organisation legal name and contact details | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Authorised contact point for follow-up | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Breach reference number | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Date and time of detection | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Actual or estimated breach period | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Description of what happened | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Categories of personal data involved | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Sensitive personal data identified | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Approximate number of affected individuals | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Categories of affected individuals | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Likely consequences for individuals | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Measures taken to contain the breach | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Measures taken or planned to reduce harm | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Whether breach is ongoing or contained | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Information still under investigation | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Expected timing of supplementary update | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Data subject notification status | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Vendor or processor involvement | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |
| Cross-border processing relevance | Yes / No / N/A | [Section / page] | [Notes] |

## Approval / Routing

The completed form must be routed according to the following table. Approval may be captured through electronic workflow, digital signature, email approval, or an approved case management system. All approvals must be retained with the breach record.

| Role / Function | Responsibility | Approval Required? | Timing |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Incident Lead | Confirms incident facts, containment status, affected systems, and technical evidence. | Yes | Before notification submission where feasible; otherwise as soon as available. |
| Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer | Owns breach assessment, notification decision, authority notification content, and privacy risk rationale. | Yes | Required before submission or documented emergency submission. |
| Legal Counsel | Reviews legal risk, notification requirement, wording, privilege handling, and external communications implications. | Yes | Required before submission unless emergency notification is approved by the authorised executive. |
| Information Security | Validates technical breach details, containment, evidence, and remediation status. | Yes | Required for cybersecurity-related breaches. |
| Business Owner | Confirms affected process, individuals, business impact, and remediation ownership. | Yes | Required for affected business area. |
| Compliance / Risk Management | Reviews regulatory, enterprise risk, and governance implications. | Conditional | Required for high or critical severity breaches. |
| Communications / Public Relations | Reviews external messaging if public or customer communication may be needed. | Conditional | Required where media, customer, or public statements are expected. |
| Vendor Management / Procurement | Coordinates processor or supplier obligations and corrective actions. | Conditional | Required where a vendor or processor is involved. |
| Executive Sponsor | Approves high-risk, critical, sensitive, public, or strategically significant notifications. | Conditional | Required for high or critical severity breaches or where directed by Legal or the Privacy Office. |

**Approval Record**

| Approval Step | Name | Role | Decision | Date and Time | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Incident facts validated | [Name] | [Role] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with conditions | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Comments] |
| Privacy assessment approved | [Name] | [Role] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with conditions | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Comments] |
| Legal review completed | [Name] | [Role] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with conditions | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Comments] |
| Authority notification approved | [Name] | [Role] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with conditions | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Comments] |
| Submission confirmed | [Name] | [Role] | Submitted / Not submitted / Deferred | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Submission reference] |
| Closure approved | [Name] | [Role] | Approved / Rejected / Approved with conditions | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ] | [Comments] |

**Escalation Rules**

| Trigger | Escalation Required | Escalate To | Target Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Breach involves sensitive personal data | Yes | Privacy Office, Legal, Information Security, Executive Sponsor | Immediately upon identification |
| Breach may cause material harm to individuals | Yes | Privacy Office, Legal, Executive Sponsor | Immediately upon assessment |
| Large number of individuals affected | Yes | Privacy Office, Legal, Compliance, Executive Sponsor | Same day |
| Breach is ongoing or containment is uncertain | Yes | Incident Response Lead, CISO, Privacy Office, Legal | Immediately |
| Breach involves ransomware, extortion, theft, or malicious actor | Yes | CISO, Legal, Privacy Office, Executive Sponsor | Immediately |
| Breach involves processor or supplier | Yes | Vendor Management, Legal, Privacy Office | Same day |
| Breach is public or likely to attract media attention | Yes | Communications, Legal, Privacy Office, Executive Sponsor | Immediately |
| Authority requests additional information | Yes | Privacy Office, Legal, Incident Lead | Based on authority deadline; immediately if urgent |

## Records & Retention

The completed form and all supporting records must be retained as part of the official privacy incident record. Records must be stored in an approved repository with restricted access limited to personnel with a legitimate need to know.

**Records to Retain**

| Record Type | Minimum Content | Owner | Storage Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Completed breach notification form | Final approved form and all material updates | Privacy Office | [Approved repository / case system] |
| Incident response record | Tickets, timelines, containment records, forensic summaries, and technical evidence | Information Security | [Approved repository / case system] |
| Risk assessment | Harm assessment, notification decision, severity rating, and rationale | Privacy Office | [Approved repository / case system] |
| Approval evidence | Workflow approvals, emails, signatures, executive approvals, emergency approval notes | Privacy Office | [Approved repository / case system] |
| Authority notification copy | Submitted notification, acknowledgement, reference number, correspondence, supplementary updates | Privacy Office | [Approved repository / case system] |
| Data subject communication records | Approved messages, delivery evidence, FAQs, call centre scripts, response tracking | Privacy Office / Communications | [Approved repository / case system] |
| Vendor records | Vendor notices, contractual correspondence, investigation updates, corrective action evidence | Vendor Management / Legal | [Approved repository / case system] |
| Remediation evidence | Corrective actions, testing results, access reviews, configuration changes, training records, closure evidence | Action owners | [Approved repository / case system] |
| Lessons learned | Post-incident review, control improvements, accountable owners, completion tracking | Privacy Office / Information Security | [Approved repository / case system] |

**Retention Requirements**

| Record Category | Retention Period | Retention Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Breach notification forms and authority correspondence | [Retention period] | Retain long enough to demonstrate compliance, decision-making, and regulatory response. |
| Incident evidence and forensic materials | [Retention period] | Preserve integrity and chain of custody where legal, disciplinary, or enforcement action is possible. |
| Approval and decision records | [Retention period] | Retain with the breach case file. |
| Remediation and closure evidence | [Retention period] | Retain until corrective actions are completed and for the defined compliance retention period thereafter. |
| Drafts and duplicate working copies | [Retention period] | Remove or archive according to legal hold, privilege, and records management instructions. |

**Access and Handling Requirements**

- Classify completed forms as **Confidential** unless Legal or Information Security requires a higher classification.
- Restrict access to the Privacy Office, Legal, Information Security, Compliance, relevant business owners, and approved executives.
- Do not store the form in personal drives, unmanaged email folders, local desktops, or unauthorised collaboration spaces.
- Do not include unnecessary personal data in attachments or evidence summaries.
- Apply legal hold immediately if directed by Legal.
- Maintain a clear audit trail of updates, approvals, submissions, and closure decisions.
- If the form is updated after submission to the authority, retain both the original submitted version and the updated version.
- Close the record only after required notifications, follow-up responses, and agreed remediation actions have been completed or formally assigned to tracked governance actions.

PDPL-029.title: Data Subject Breach Notification
PDPL-029.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [Document ID] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Data Protection Officer |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | Saudi Personal Data Protection Law |
| Classification | Confidential - Personal Data Incident Response |

## Purpose

This template is used to prepare and approve a notification to affected data subjects when a personal data breach is likely to cause substantial harm to their rights, interests, privacy, safety, financial position, or reputation.

It supports a consistent, timely, accurate, and evidence-based communication to affected individuals, including sufficient information to help them understand the breach, assess the potential impact, and take protective action.

This template applies to confirmed personal data breaches involving individuals whose personal data is processed by, or on behalf of, the organisation in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including breaches affecting employees, customers, beneficiaries, patients, users, suppliers, contractors, or other identifiable individuals.

## Instructions

1. **Use this template only after breach assessment**
 - Complete this notification after the incident response team has determined that a personal data breach occurred and that affected data subjects should be notified due to the likelihood of substantial harm.
 - Do not send a notification based on speculation. If facts are incomplete, state clearly what is known and what remains under investigation.

2. **Coordinate with incident response and legal teams**
 - The Data Protection Officer, Legal, Information Security, Communications, and relevant business owner must review the content before release.
 - Where the breach involves third-party processors, coordinate facts with the processor before communicating to affected data subjects.

3. **Use clear and accessible language**
 - The notification must be understandable to the intended audience.
 - Avoid technical jargon unless necessary. Where technical terms are used, explain them in plain language.
 - Use Arabic where required for the affected audience. Provide English or other languages where appropriate.

4. **Include minimum required content**
 - The notification should explain:
 - What happened.
 - When it happened or when it was discovered.
 - What categories of personal data were affected.
 - The likely consequences or risks to the individual.
 - What the organisation has done or is doing to contain and remediate the breach.
 - What the individual can do to protect themselves.
 - How the individual can contact the organisation for further information.

5. **Avoid disclosing sensitive operational details**
 - Do not include information that could increase risk, such as detailed security architecture, exploit methods, internal system names, credentials, investigation tactics, or information about other affected persons.
 - Do not include personal data of other individuals.

6. **Verify affected population and delivery method**
 - Confirm the affected data subject list before distribution.
 - Use a delivery channel appropriate to the urgency and sensitivity of the breach, such as SMS, email, secure portal message, registered mail, call centre outreach, or in-person communication.
 - Where direct contact information is unavailable or unreliable, escalate to the Data Protection Officer and Legal for an alternative notification approach.

7. **Timing**
 - Send the notification without undue delay after the organisation confirms that affected data subjects should be notified, unless Legal or an authorised authority advises that a short delay is necessary to protect the investigation or reduce risk to individuals.
 - Document any delay, reason for delay, approver, and revised notification time.

8. **Preserve evidence**
 - Retain the completed form, approval record, final notification copy, distribution logs, delivery evidence, returned messages, call scripts, FAQs, and any follow-up communications.

9. **Do not alter approved wording after sign-off**
 - Any material change to breach facts, risk description, recommended actions, contact details, or timing must be re-approved before release.

## Form Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Guidance |
|---|---:|:---:|---|
| Breach Notification Reference | Text | Yes | Unique reference linking this notification to the incident record, breach assessment, and regulatory notification file, if applicable. Example: `BN-[YYYY]-[###]`. |
| Incident Reference | Text | Yes | Internal incident ticket, case number, or investigation reference. |
| Notification Status | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Draft, Under Review, Approved for Release, Released, Superseded, Withdrawn. |
| Prepared By | Name / Role | Yes | Person drafting the notification. |
| Date Prepared | Date / Time | Yes | Date and time the first notification draft was prepared. |
| Business Owner | Name / Role | Yes | Business function accountable for the affected processing activity. |
| Data Protection Officer | Name / Role | Yes | Responsible person reviewing privacy content and notification adequacy. |
| Legal Reviewer | Name / Role | Yes | Legal counsel reviewing accuracy, liability, confidentiality, and regulatory sensitivity. |
| Information Security Lead | Name / Role | Yes | Security representative validating breach facts, containment, and technical accuracy. |
| Communications Lead | Name / Role | Conditional | Required where a large population, media interest, call centre support, or public messaging is expected. |
| Third-Party Processor Involved | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether a vendor, processor, cloud provider, service partner, or outsourced provider is involved. |
| Third-Party Name | Text | Conditional | Required if a third party is involved. Include legal entity name, not informal vendor nickname. |
| Third-Party Contact | Name / Contact Details | Conditional | Required if a third party is involved. Include incident liaison and escalation contact. |
| Breach Discovery Date and Time | Date / Time | Yes | When the organisation first became aware of facts indicating a possible personal data breach. |
| Breach Occurrence Date and Time | Date / Time / Range | Conditional | State known or estimated date and time of breach occurrence. If unknown, state “Unknown - under investigation”. |
| Breach Confirmation Date and Time | Date / Time | Yes | When the organisation confirmed that a personal data breach occurred. |
| Summary of What Happened | Long Text | Yes | Plain-language description of the breach. Include only validated facts. Avoid unnecessary technical details or speculative statements. |
| Breach Type | Multi-select | Yes | Select all that apply: Unauthorised access, Unauthorised disclosure, Loss, Theft, Alteration, Destruction, Ransomware, Phishing, Misdelivery, System misconfiguration, Insider misuse, Other. |
| Breach Source | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Internal error, Malicious external actor, Malicious insider, Third-party failure, System failure, Physical loss or theft, Unknown, Other. |
| Affected Systems or Processing Activity | Text | Yes | Describe the business service, application, database, file repository, device, or process affected using business-friendly wording. Avoid sensitive security details. |
| Location of Processing | Text | Yes | Identify country or region where affected processing, storage, or access occurred, where known. |
| Affected Data Subject Categories | Multi-select | Yes | Select all that apply: Customers, Employees, Job applicants, Contractors, Suppliers, Patients, Students, Beneficiaries, Website users, Mobile app users, Dependants, Other. |
| Estimated Number of Affected Data Subjects | Number / Range | Yes | Provide best current estimate. Use a range if final count is not available. Update before final release if material changes occur. |
| Basis for Affected Population Estimate | Long Text | Yes | Explain how the estimate was calculated, such as affected records extracted, access logs, email distribution list, vendor report, or forensic analysis. |
| Categories of Personal Data Affected | Multi-select | Yes | Select all that apply: Name, national ID or residency ID, contact details, address, date of birth, financial data, bank details, health data, employment data, family data, location data, account credentials, biometric data, images or video, transaction data, government identifiers, other. |
| Sensitive or High-Risk Data Involved | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether the breach includes data that may increase risk to individuals, such as identity documents, health information, financial information, credentials, children’s data, location data, or highly private information. |
| Details of Sensitive or High-Risk Data | Long Text | Conditional | Required if sensitive or high-risk data is involved. Describe categories only. Do not include actual personal data values. |
| Credentials Compromised | Yes / No / Unknown | Yes | State whether passwords, one-time passwords, API keys linked to individuals, security questions, PINs, or other account access credentials were compromised. |
| Credentials Reset or Disabled | Yes / No / Not Applicable | Conditional | Required if credentials were compromised or suspected to be compromised. |
| Likelihood of Substantial Harm | Dropdown | Yes | Select one: Likely, Highly Likely, Confirmed Harm Occurred. Use this template where harm threshold is met. |
| Harm Assessment Summary | Long Text | Yes | Explain why affected individuals may suffer substantial harm. Consider identity theft, fraud, financial loss, reputational harm, discrimination, distress, safety risk, loss of confidentiality, account takeover, or misuse of sensitive information. |
| Known Consequences to Date | Long Text | Yes | Record confirmed consequences, if any. If none are known, state “No confirmed misuse identified at the time of notification”. |
| Ongoing Risks to Data Subjects | Long Text | Yes | Describe realistic risks that may continue after notification, such as phishing attempts, fraud attempts, unauthorised account access, social engineering, or exposure of confidential information. |
| Containment Actions Completed | Long Text | Yes | Describe actions already taken, such as disabling access, resetting credentials, isolating systems, recovering data, recalling messages, revoking links, patching vulnerabilities, or engaging forensic support. |
| Remediation Actions Planned or Underway | Long Text | Yes | Describe additional actions underway to prevent recurrence and reduce individual risk. Do not overpromise or include unapproved commitments. |
| Actions Recommended for Data Subjects | Long Text | Yes | Provide practical steps affected individuals should take. Tailor to the breach, such as changing passwords, enabling multi-factor authentication, monitoring bank accounts, contacting banks, watching for phishing, reviewing official account activity, or reporting suspicious activity. |
| Support Offered to Data Subjects | Long Text | Conditional | Describe support such as helpline, dedicated email, account monitoring, credential reset support, replacement cards, identity protection assistance, or complaint handling. Required where support is being offered. |
| Contact Channel for Data Subjects | Text | Yes | Provide approved email address, telephone number, portal link, office address, or support centre details. Use monitored channels only. |
| Contact Hours | Text | Yes | State support availability, including time zone. Example: Sunday to Thursday, 9:00 to 17:00, Saudi Arabia time. |
| FAQ Required | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether an FAQ is required for support teams, call centre, front desk, account managers, or public website. |
| Call Script Required | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether a call script is needed for outbound or inbound communication. |
| Notification Language | Multi-select | Yes | Select language versions to be issued, such as Arabic, English, or other languages relevant to affected individuals. |
| Translation Reviewed | Yes / No / Not Applicable | Conditional | Required where more than one language version is used. Confirm that translations match approved meaning and do not omit key information. |
| Notification Delivery Method | Multi-select | Yes | Select all that apply: Email, SMS, secure portal, registered mail, courier, telephone, in-person, public notice, mobile app notification, other. |
| Rationale for Delivery Method | Long Text | Yes | Explain why the chosen method is appropriate considering urgency, reliability, sensitivity, and available contact data. |
| Notification Audience List Owner | Name / Role | Yes | Person accountable for preparing and validating the affected data subject distribution list. |
| Audience List Validation Completed | Yes / No | Yes | Confirm that the distribution list has been checked for accuracy, duplicates, exclusions, and contact details. |
| Date and Time Notification Approved | Date / Time | Conditional | Completed after final approval. |
| Planned Release Date and Time | Date / Time | Yes | Target release date and time. Consider urgency, support availability, and coordination with any authority communications. |
| Actual Release Date and Time | Date / Time | Conditional | Completed after release. |
| Reason for Delay, if Any | Long Text | Conditional | Required if release is delayed after approval or after decision to notify. Include reason, approving role, and revised timing. |
| Regulatory Notification Made | Yes / No / Pending / Not Applicable | Yes | State whether the competent authority has been notified, if applicable. Do not include legal citations. |
| Regulatory Notification Reference | Text | Conditional | Required if a related regulatory notification has been submitted. |
| Consistency with Regulatory Notification Confirmed | Yes / No / Not Applicable | Conditional | Confirm that facts in the data subject notification are consistent with authority notification, unless differences are documented and approved. |
| Law Enforcement Involved | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether law enforcement is involved. |
| Law Enforcement Delay Requested | Yes / No / Not Applicable | Conditional | Indicate whether any communication delay has been requested to protect an investigation. Attach evidence of request or instruction where available. |
| Media or Public Interest Expected | Yes / No | Yes | Indicate whether media attention, social media escalation, or public concern is expected. |
| Public Statement Required | Yes / No | Conditional | Required if media or public interest is expected. |
| Final Notification Text | Long Text / Attachment | Yes | Insert the final text or attach the final approved version. Use the notification content section below as the standard structure. |
| Attachments | Attachment List | Conditional | Include approved FAQ, call script, distribution list evidence, translation, legal approval, processor confirmation, and delivery logs as applicable. |
| Post-Notification Monitoring Plan | Long Text | Yes | Describe how the organisation will monitor responses, complaints, bounce-backs, support contacts, evidence of misuse, and new facts after notification. |
| Follow-Up Notification Required | Yes / No / To Be Determined | Yes | Indicate whether a further update to affected data subjects is required if new material facts emerge. |
| Form Completed By | Name / Role | Yes | Person completing the final form record. |
| Completion Date | Date | Yes | Date the form was completed for records retention. |

### Notification Content Template

| Section | Required Content | Draft Text |
|---|---|---|
| Subject Line / Opening Statement | Clear and direct statement that the organisation is notifying the individual about a personal data breach. Avoid alarming language unless urgent action is required. | [Draft subject line or opening statement] |
| What Happened | Plain-language summary of the incident, including what was affected and how the organisation discovered it, where appropriate. | [Draft text] |
| When It Happened | Date or estimated date range of occurrence and discovery, if known. | [Draft text] |
| What Personal Data Was Involved | Categories of personal data affected. Do not include actual personal data values. | [Draft text] |
| What This May Mean for You | Specific, realistic risks to the individual based on the data involved and breach circumstances. | [Draft text] |
| What We Have Done | Containment, investigation, remediation, and support actions already taken or underway. | [Draft text] |
| What You Should Do | Practical protective steps the individual should take. Make recommendations specific to the breach. | [Draft text] |
| How to Contact Us | Dedicated contact channels, support hours, and reference number to quote. | [Draft text] |
| Closing Statement | Reassurance, apology where approved, and commitment to protecting personal data. | [Draft text] |

### Recommended Protective Actions by Breach Scenario

| Breach Scenario | Recommended Actions for Data Subjects |
|---|---|
| Contact details exposed | Be alert for suspicious calls, emails, or SMS messages; do not click unknown links; verify messages through official channels. |
| National ID, residency ID, or identity documents exposed | Monitor for identity misuse; be cautious of requests for additional identity information; report suspected fraud to relevant authorities and service providers. |
| Bank details or payment information exposed | Monitor bank and card statements; notify the bank of suspicious transactions; consider card replacement where advised; report unauthorised activity promptly. |
| Account credentials exposed | Change passwords immediately; use a strong unique password; enable multi-factor authentication; avoid reusing passwords across services. |
| Health or highly private information exposed | Watch for targeted scams or blackmail attempts; report suspicious contact; contact the organisation’s support channel for confidential assistance. |
| Employment or salary information exposed | Be alert to impersonation attempts, payroll diversion scams, or fraudulent requests to change bank details. |
| Children’s or dependants’ data exposed | Parents or guardians should monitor unusual contact or account activity and report suspicious approaches immediately. |
| Location or travel data exposed | Be alert to safety risks, stalking, or targeted fraud; contact the organisation if there is concern about personal safety. |

## Approval / Routing

The following approvals are required before the notification is released to affected data subjects.

| Approval Step | Approver / Role | Required | Approval Criteria | Date / Time | Signature / Evidence |
|---|---|:---:|---|---|---|
| Breach Facts Validation | Information Security Lead | Yes | Confirms technical facts, affected systems, containment actions, and no sensitive security details are disclosed. | [Date / Time] | [Signature / Evidence] |
| Affected Population Validation | Business Owner | Yes | Confirms affected data subject categories, estimated numbers, and distribution list accuracy. | [Date / Time] | [Signature / Evidence] |
| Privacy Review | Data Protection Officer | Yes | Confirms notification is necessary, complete, clear, and proportionate to the risk of substantial harm. | [Date / Time] | [Signature / Evidence] |
| Legal Review | Legal Counsel | Yes | Confirms legal accuracy, privilege considerations, liability-sensitive wording, and alignment with other notifications. | [Date / Time] | [Signature / Evidence] |
| Communications Review | Communications Lead | Conditional | Required for large-scale notifications, public attention, media interest, or executive-sensitive matters. | [Date / Time] | [Signature / Evidence] |
| Customer / Employee Support Readiness | Support Owner | Conditional | Required where call centre, HR, account management, or helpdesk support is needed. Confirms scripts, FAQs, escalation paths, and staffing are ready. | [Date / Time] | [Signature / Evidence] |
| Executive Approval | [Authorised Executive Role] | Conditional | Required for high-impact incidents, sensitive groups, strategic customers, public exposure, or significant financial or reputational risk. | [Date / Time] | [Signature / Evidence] |
| Final Release Authorisation | Data Protection Officer or Authorised Delegate | Yes | Confirms all required approvals are complete and notification may be issued. | [Date / Time] | [Signature / Evidence] |

### Routing Checklist

| Routing Item | Owner | Completed | Evidence / Notes |
|---|---|:---:|---|
| Incident record updated with notification decision | Incident Manager | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Breach assessment completed and attached | Data Protection Officer | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Affected population list validated | Business Owner | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Notification text approved | Data Protection Officer | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Legal review completed | Legal Counsel | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Translation completed and reviewed, if applicable | Communications Lead | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Support channels prepared | Support Owner | ☐ | [Notes] |
| FAQ and call script approved, if applicable | Communications Lead | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Regulatory notification alignment checked, if applicable | Data Protection Officer | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Distribution method tested | Communications Lead / IT Owner | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Notification released | Communications Lead / Business Owner | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Delivery evidence retained | Records Owner | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Bounce-backs or failed deliveries triaged | Support Owner | ☐ | [Notes] |
| Post-notification monitoring started | Incident Manager | ☐ | [Notes] |

## Records & Retention

All records related to this notification must be retained securely and made available to authorised reviewers, auditors, regulators, or investigators where required.

| Record | Owner | Retention Requirement | Storage Location | Access Restrictions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completed Data Subject Breach Notification form | Data Protection Officer | Retain for at least [Retention Period] after incident closure, or longer if required for legal, regulatory, contractual, or litigation purposes. | [Repository / System] | Data Protection, Legal, Incident Response, authorised audit personnel. |
| Final approved notification text | Data Protection Officer | Retain with the breach case file. | [Repository / System] | Restricted to authorised personnel. |
| Draft versions and review comments | Legal Counsel / Data Protection Officer | Retain where needed to evidence review and decision-making. Mark privileged material appropriately where applicable. | [Repository / System] | Legal and authorised privacy personnel. |
| Approval records | Data Protection Officer | Retain with the notification file. | [Repository / System] | Restricted to authorised personnel. |
| Affected data subject distribution list | Business Owner | Retain only as long as required to evidence notification and manage follow-up. Protect as confidential personal data. | [Repository / System] | Strictly limited to personnel with a need to know. |
| Delivery logs and proof of sending | Communications Lead / IT Owner | Retain with the notification file, including timestamps, channel used, and delivery status where available. | [Repository / System] | Restricted to authorised personnel. |
| Failed delivery and bounce-back records | Support Owner | Retain until resolution and then with the notification file. | [Repository / System] | Restricted to authorised personnel. |
| Call scripts, FAQs, and support guidance | Communications Lead | Retain final approved versions and material updates. | [Repository / System] | Support teams and authorised reviewers. |
| Data subject enquiries and complaints | Support Owner / Data Protection Officer | Retain in line with complaint handling and privacy request retention requirements. | [Repository / System] | Restricted to authorised support, privacy, and legal personnel. |
| Evidence of follow-up notifications | Data Protection Officer | Retain with the breach case file. | [Repository / System] | Restricted to authorised personnel. |
| Regulatory correspondence, if applicable | Data Protection Officer / Legal Counsel | Retain with related breach notification file. | [Repository / System] | Data Protection, Legal, and authorised executive personnel only. |
| Post-incident review and lessons learned | Incident Manager | Retain with incident closure records. | [Repository / System] | Incident Response, Risk, Compliance, and authorised management. |

Records must be protected against unauthorised access, alteration, deletion, or disclosure. Personal data contained in notification records must not be reused for unrelated purposes. Access must be reviewed periodically and removed when no longer required.

Where a legal hold, investigation, regulatory inquiry, dispute, insurance claim, or litigation is active or reasonably anticipated, normal disposal must be suspended until Legal authorises release of the hold.

PDPL-030.title: Consent Records
PDPL-030.content:
## What This Evidences

Consent Records evidence that [Organisation Name] has captured, stored, and can demonstrate how, when, and for what purpose a data subject gave, refused, or withdrew consent for processing personal data under the Saudi PDPL control requirements.

This artifact is **collected from operational systems**, not authored as a standalone document. Do not create or manually fabricate consent records. The evidence must be extracted from the actual system of record where consent events are captured and maintained.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect Consent Records from the system that records data subject consent events in your environment. Typical sources include:

- Customer portal or mobile application consent database - [Customer Portal / Mobile App Platform]
- Consent management platform - [Consent Management Tool]
- CRM or marketing preference centre - [CRM / Marketing Platform]
- Identity and access management or profile management system - [IAM / CIAM Tool]
- Data privacy management platform - [Privacy Management Tool]
- Web cookie consent platform, where applicable - [Cookie Consent Tool]
- Service desk or ticketing system for offline/manual consent updates - [ITSM Tool]

The preferred source is the authoritative consent repository used by [Organisation Name] to determine whether personal data processing is permitted.

## How To Collect

1. Identify the relevant processing activity, service, campaign, form, portal, or data subject group being reviewed.
2. Log in to [Consent Management Tool / CRM / Portal Admin Console] using an approved privileged or reporting account.
3. Navigate to the consent, preferences, privacy, or data subject profile section.
4. Filter records for the audit period: [Start Date] to [End Date].
5. Export the consent event history in CSV, XLSX, JSON, PDF report, or system-generated audit report format.
6. Where the system supports it, include both current consent status and full consent history.
7. If consent is captured through multiple systems, repeat the extraction for each source and reconcile using data subject ID, customer ID, mobile number, email address, or other approved identifier.
8. Capture screenshots showing the report filters, source system name, export timestamp, and a sample record view.
9. Store the export and screenshots in the approved evidence repository: [GRC Evidence Repository / Secure SharePoint / DMS].
10. Record the collection details in [Evidence Tracker], including collector name, date collected, system source, period covered, and file location.

## What To Capture

Capture sufficient fields to demonstrate consent validity and traceability, including:

- Data subject identifier, such as [Customer ID] or [Data Subject ID]
- Consent status: granted, refused, withdrawn, expired, or updated
- Date and time consent was given, changed, or withdrawn
- Consent purpose or processing activity
- Consent wording, notice version, privacy notice version, or form version presented
- Channel of collection, such as web, mobile app, call centre, paper form, branch, or email
- Source system or application name
- Method of authentication or verification, where available
- User, agent, or system that recorded the consent event
- IP address, device ID, session ID, transaction ID, or request ID, where available
- Language of notice or consent text, where relevant
- Evidence of withdrawal mechanism and withdrawal timestamp, where applicable
- Record creation and last modified timestamps
- Export timestamp and report parameters

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Collect at least quarterly, and additionally before audits, after major consent process changes, or following a privacy incident involving consent.
- **Owner:** Data Protection Officer or Privacy Lead.
- **Supporting owners:** CRM Owner, Digital Platform Owner, Marketing Operations, IT Application Owner, and Records Management.

## Retention & Storage

Store consent record extracts in [GRC Evidence Repository] with access restricted to authorised privacy, compliance, audit, and legal personnel.

Retain records for the duration required by [Organisation Name]’s retention schedule and applicable Saudi PDPL obligations. Retention should cover the period needed to demonstrate lawful processing, handle data subject disputes, and support regulatory or audit enquiries.

Protect exported files using encryption, access control, and integrity safeguards. Avoid unnecessary duplication of personal data. Where full personal data is not required for audit, use masked or pseudonymised exports while preserving traceability.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor should accept the evidence where it shows:

- Records are exported from the live or authoritative consent system, not manually recreated.
- The audit period, source system, export date, and collection method are clear.
- Each consent record links a data subject to a specific consent purpose and consent status.
- The record shows when consent was given, changed, or withdrawn.
- The consent wording, notice version, or form version can be traced.
- Withdrawals and preference changes are captured with timestamps.
- The evidence is complete for the sampled population or clearly scoped extract.
- Screenshots or metadata prove the records came from [Consent Management Tool / CRM / Portal].
- Access to the evidence is controlled and retained according to the approved retention schedule.

Update upon each training assignment or completion, review monthly for overdue items, and reconcile at least quarterly against the LMS, HRIS, attendance records, and approved exception register.
