### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Request Log ID | Enter a unique sequential identifier for this disclosure request, e.g. PDR-YYYY-0001. |
| Request Received Date | Enter the calendar date the organisation received the request in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Request Received Time | Enter the local Saudi time the request was received in 24-hour HH:MM format. |
| Receiving Business Unit | Enter the internal department or function that first received the request, e.g. Legal, Compliance, Customer Operations, Security. |
| Receiving Channel | Select the channel used to receive the request: Official letter, Secure email, Government portal, Court order, In-person delivery, Telephone followed by written confirmation, Other. |
| Requesting Public Authority Name | Enter the full official name of the Saudi public authority or competent authority making the request. |
| Requesting Public Authority Type | Select the authority type: Court/Judicial Authority, Law Enforcement, Regulator, Government Ministry, Supervisory Authority, National Security Authority, Other Public Authority. |
| Requesting Officer Name | Enter the full name of the official named in the request or verified as handling the request. |
| Requesting Officer Title/Department | Enter the officer’s official role, title, unit, or department as stated in the request or verified separately. |
| Requesting Officer Contact Details | Enter official contact information only, such as government email, direct office number, postal address, or portal account reference. |
| Authority Request Reference Number | Enter the reference number, case number, order number, circular number, or official correspondence number assigned by the requesting authority. |
| Request Document/File Reference | Enter the internal document management link, file path, or evidence ID for the request letter, order, warrant, or portal submission. |
| Officer Identity and Authority Verified | Select Yes, No, or Not applicable; record Yes only where the officer identity and authority to make the request were verified before disclosure. |
| Verification Method | Describe how the request and officer authority were verified, e.g. official domain check, call-back to published authority number, government portal authentication, signed/stamped letter validation, legal order review. |
| Verification Date | Enter the date verification was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Legal Basis Cited by Authority | Enter the law, regulation, court order, official mandate, or statutory power cited by the authority; quote article/order references where available. |
| Saudi PDPL Disclosure Ground Relied On | Select the applicable PDPL disclosure ground, e.g. disclosure required by law/regulation, disclosure requested by a public entity for security purposes, disclosure necessary to protect public health/safety, disclosure necessary to protect life/health of an individual, disclosure for judicial requirements, or other permitted PDPL basis. |
| Purpose of Disclosure Requested | Enter the specific purpose stated by the authority, such as investigation, enforcement, regulatory supervision, litigation, national security, public health, or judicial proceedings. |
| Urgency Classification | Select Routine, Urgent, Emergency, or Immediate threat; use Emergency/Immediate threat only where the request states or evidence supports imminent harm, legal deadline, or public interest urgency. |
| Response Due Date | Enter the authority-imposed or internally agreed response deadline in YYYY-MM-DD format; if no deadline exists, enter the internally assigned target date. |
| Data Subject Category | Describe whose personal data is requested, e.g. employee, customer, visitor, vendor contact, patient, applicant, beneficiary, platform user. |
| Number of Data Subjects Affected | Enter the exact number of individuals if known; if not known, enter a reasonable estimate and mark as estimate, e.g. Approx. 250. |
| Data Subject Identifiers Requested | List identifiers requested or used to locate the records, e.g. national ID/Iqama, customer ID, employee ID, mobile number, email, account number, vehicle plate, IP address. |
| Personal Data Categories Requested | List the categories of personal data requested, e.g. identity data, contact data, transaction records, account history, location data, access logs, CCTV, communications metadata. |
| Sensitive Personal Data Included | Select Yes, No, or To be determined; mark Yes if the request includes health, biometric, genetic, criminal, financial/credit, religious, political, or other sensitive data under Saudi PDPL. |
| Sensitive Data Categories | If sensitive personal data is included, list the sensitive categories; if none, enter Not applicable. |
| Requested Disclosure Period/Date Range | Enter the time period requested by the authority in YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD format, or enter Specific date(s), Ongoing, or Not specified as applicable. |
| Systems/Repositories Containing Requested Data | List the internal systems, databases, archives, physical files, email repositories, CCTV systems, or third-party platforms where the requested data is held. |
| Data Controller Role Confirmed | Select Controller, Joint Controller, Processor, or Not confirmed; record the organisation’s role for the requested data before disclosure. |
| Processor/Third Party Involvement | Enter any processor, service provider, joint controller, or data custodian involved in locating, extracting, reviewing, transmitting, or hosting the requested data; enter None if not applicable. |
| Necessity Assessment Outcome | Select Necessary, Partially necessary, Not necessary, or Not assessed due to mandatory legal order; base this on whether the requested data is required for the stated lawful purpose. |
| Proportionality/Data Minimisation Assessment | Record whether the scope was limited to the minimum data, individuals, and date range necessary; include any narrowing, filtering, aggregation, or redaction applied. |
| Confidentiality or Restriction Considerations | Record any confidentiality duties, contractual restrictions, legal privilege, secrecy requirements, court restrictions, or sector rules considered before disclosure. |
| Conflict With Other Legal Obligations | Select Yes, No, or Unknown; if Yes or Unknown, briefly describe the potential conflict and escalation taken. |
| Internal Legal Review Required | Select Yes or No based on internal policy, sensitivity, uncertainty of legal basis, volume, urgency, or conflict risk. |
| Internal Legal Reviewer | Enter the name/title of the legal reviewer or legal team that reviewed the request; enter Not applicable if no legal review was required. |
| DPO/Privacy Review Required | Select Yes or No based on PDPL governance policy, sensitive data, high volume, unusual disclosure, overseas element, or risk level. |
| DPO/Privacy Reviewer | Enter the name/title of the DPO, privacy officer, or privacy team reviewer; enter Not applicable if no privacy review was required. |
| Risk Rating | Select Low, Medium, High, or Critical based on data sensitivity, volume, legal uncertainty, urgency, disclosure channel, and potential impact on data subjects. |
| Decision | Select Approved, Approved with redactions/limitations, Rejected, Partially rejected, Clarification requested, Withdrawn by authority, or Escalated/pending. |
| Decision Rationale | Summarise the reason for the decision, including the verified legal basis, PDPL disclosure ground, necessity/proportionality conclusion, and any limitations imposed. |
| Decision Date | Enter the date the disclosure decision was made in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Approving Authority/Role | Enter the internal role or committee that approved the decision, e.g. General Counsel, DPO, Compliance Director, CEO delegate, Disclosure Review Committee. |
| Approval Evidence Reference | Enter the internal approval record link, ticket ID, email approval reference, workflow ID, or signed decision memo reference. |
| Data Disclosed | Describe exactly what data was disclosed, including fields, records, files, date range, and number of records; if no data disclosed, enter None. |
| Data Withheld or Redacted | Describe any requested data not provided, redacted, masked, anonymised, aggregated, or excluded; enter None if all requested data was disclosed. |
| Reason for Withholding/Redaction | Enter the reason for any withholding or redaction, such as not covered by legal basis, excessive scope, unrelated third-party data, privilege, unavailable data, or minimisation requirement. |
| Disclosure Method | Select Secure portal upload, Encrypted email, Secure file transfer, Physical sealed delivery, Direct system access, In-person handover, Registered courier, Other. |
| Security Measures Applied | Record the technical and organisational safeguards used, e.g. encryption, password shared separately, access control, file integrity hash, sealed envelope, recipient authentication, audit logging. |
| Recipient Confirmation Obtained | Select Yes, No, or Not applicable; if Yes, ensure the acknowledgement receipt, portal confirmation, or signed handover evidence is referenced. |
| Disclosure Completion Date | Enter the date the disclosure was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until completed. |
| Disclosure Completion Time | Enter the local Saudi time the disclosure was completed in 24-hour HH:MM format; leave blank until completed. |
| Disclosure Evidence Reference | Enter the evidence ID, portal receipt number, email ID, courier tracking number, handover form reference, or transfer log confirming disclosure. |
| Data Subject Notification Required | Select Yes, No, Deferred, or To be determined based on PDPL, Implementing Regulations, the nature of the request, and any legal restriction on notification. |
| Data Subject Notification Status | Select Not applicable, Pending, Completed, Deferred, Prohibited by authority/law, or Not required. |
| Reason Notification Not Provided or Deferred | If notification is not provided or is deferred, record the reason, such as legal prohibition, investigation confidentiality, public interest, court order, risk to safety/security, or not required under applicable PDPL basis. |
| Retention Period for Request File | Enter the retention period for the disclosure request file in months/years or cite the approved retention schedule reference. |
| Retention/Deletion Action Date | Enter the planned date for secure deletion, archival review, or retention reassessment in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Related Incident/Breach Reference | Enter any linked privacy incident, security incident, or breach case ID; enter None if unrelated. |
| Related Data Subject Request Reference | Enter any linked data subject rights request, complaint, objection, or inquiry reference; enter None if unrelated. |
| Status | Select Open, Awaiting clarification, Under review, Approved pending disclosure, Disclosed, Rejected, Withdrawn, Closed, or Archived. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the request file was formally closed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Closure Notes | Record final closure comments, outstanding issues, lessons learned, follow-up actions, or confirmation that evidence and approvals are complete. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the DPO/Privacy Office with Legal as mandatory reviewer for public-authority requests; update the log upon receipt, verification, decision, disclosure, and closure, with a formal completeness review monthly. Source records should be drawn from the legal matter management system, privacy/GRC workflow tool, document management repository, government portal receipts, secure transfer logs, and approval workflow records.

PDPL-033.title: Privacy Programme Internal Audit Report
PDPL-033.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-PRV-AUD-001] | 1.0 | [Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Saudi Personal Data Protection Law and Implementing Regulations | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This Privacy Programme Internal Audit Report presents the results of the periodic internal assurance review of [Organisation Name]’s privacy programme against the requirements and expectations of the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law and its Implementing Regulations.

The purpose of this report is to:

- Assess whether [Organisation Name] has designed and implemented effective governance, processes, records, and controls for protecting personal data.
- Evaluate operational compliance with privacy obligations applicable to the collection, use, disclosure, retention, transfer, and disposal of personal data.
- Identify control gaps, process weaknesses, and improvement opportunities.
- Provide management with prioritised recommendations and agreed actions.
- Support ongoing accountability, management oversight, and continuous improvement of the privacy programme.

This report is intended for internal assurance and management decision-making. It does not constitute legal advice and should be reviewed with Legal where interpretation of statutory obligations is required.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Audit period covered | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Fieldwork period | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Report date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Previous audit date | [YYYY-MM-DD / Not applicable] |
| Next planned audit | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

### Organisational Scope

The audit covered the following functions, locations, and business activities:

| Area | Included in Scope | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Privacy governance and oversight | Yes | Privacy roles, accountability, reporting, issue tracking |
| Personal data inventory and processing records | Yes | Coverage of key processing activities and data flows |
| Privacy notices and transparency | Yes | Customer, employee, vendor, and digital-channel notices |
| Consent and lawful basis management | Yes | Consent capture, withdrawal, and alternatives to consent |
| Data subject rights handling | Yes | Intake, identity verification, fulfilment, and response tracking |
| Data sharing and processor management | Yes | Contracts, due diligence, and monitoring |
| Cross-border personal data transfers | Yes | Transfer approvals, risk assessment, safeguards, and records |
| Privacy impact assessment process | Yes | High-risk processing assessment and approval |
| Personal data breach management | Yes | Detection, escalation, assessment, notification, and lessons learned |
| Retention and disposal | Yes | Retention schedule, implementation, exception management |
| Marketing and digital tracking | Yes | Opt-in, opt-out, preference management, cookies and similar technologies |
| Training and awareness | Yes | Mandatory training, targeted training, completion records |
| Information security alignment | Limited | Privacy-related security controls only |
| HR processing | Yes | Employee and candidate personal data processing |
| Customer processing | Yes | Customer onboarding, service delivery, support, and marketing |
| Vendor processing | Yes | Third-party service providers handling personal data |

### Systems and Repositories Reviewed

The audit included a sample review of the following systems, repositories, and records:

| System / Repository | Purpose | Review Performed |
|---|---|---|
| [CRM System] | Customer profile, contact, service and marketing data | Access, notice linkage, consent fields, retention indicators |
| [HR System] | Employee and candidate data | Privacy notice, access controls, retention, data subject request handling |
| [Service Desk Tool] | Data subject requests, incidents, complaints | Workflow, evidence, timeliness, escalation records |
| [Vendor Management System] | Supplier due diligence and contracts | Processor classification, contract terms, review status |
| [Document Management Repository] | Policies, procedures, templates, approvals | Version control, ownership, implementation evidence |
| [Data Inventory Tool / Spreadsheet] | Processing records and data mapping | Completeness, accuracy, update cadence |
| [Security Incident Platform] | Security and privacy incident tracking | Breach triage, privacy assessment, notifications |

### Exclusions and Limitations

The following items were outside the scope of this audit:

- Technical penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, or full security architecture review.
- Legal interpretation of contractual positions outside the privacy compliance context.
- Detailed audit of every business application or every processing activity.
- Assurance over third-party controls beyond available contract, due diligence, and monitoring evidence.
- Validation of regulatory submissions not available during the fieldwork period.

The audit was conducted using sampling. As a result, findings may not identify every instance of non-compliance or control weakness.

## Executive Summary

### Overall Audit Opinion

**Overall rating: Needs Improvement**

[Organisation Name] has established several foundational privacy programme components, including defined privacy ownership, approved privacy policies, documented breach escalation channels, and initial records of personal data processing. However, the audit identified gaps in operational consistency, evidence retention, processor oversight, cross-border transfer governance, retention implementation, and data subject rights handling.

The privacy programme is progressing, but current control maturity is not yet sufficient to demonstrate consistent, repeatable compliance across all in-scope business areas. Management attention is required to strengthen accountability, improve documentation quality, and embed privacy controls into business processes and technology workflows.

### Summary of Results

| Rating | Count | Description |
|---|---:|---|
| Critical | 0 | No issue identified that presents immediate severe legal, operational, or reputational exposure requiring emergency action. |
| High | 4 | Significant gaps requiring prompt management action due to elevated compliance, operational, or individual-rights risk. |
| Medium | 7 | Control weaknesses requiring corrective action within the agreed remediation timeframe. |
| Low | 5 | Improvement opportunities or documentation gaps with limited immediate risk. |
| Positive Observations | 6 | Effective practices observed during the audit. |

### Key Strengths

The audit identified the following positive practices:

- A designated privacy owner is in place with visible support from Legal, Compliance, Information Security, and HR.
- Core privacy governance documents exist, including a privacy policy, breach response procedure, and data subject rights procedure.
- Mandatory privacy awareness training has been launched for employees.
- A breach escalation path exists and is known by Information Security and Customer Support teams.
- The organisation has started building a personal data inventory for major business processes.
- Vendor onboarding includes privacy-related questions for new suppliers.

### Key Areas Requiring Improvement

The most significant improvement areas are:

1. **Incomplete and inconsistent personal data inventory** 
 Records of processing are not complete for several functions, and some entries lack data categories, retention periods, transfer details, or responsible owners.

2. **Data subject rights process not fully operationalised** 
 Procedures exist, but evidence of request tracking, identity verification, deadline monitoring, and consistent response templates is incomplete.

3. **Cross-border transfer governance requires strengthening** 
 Transfers to external service providers and group entities are not consistently identified, risk-assessed, approved, and documented.

4. **Processor contracts and monitoring are inconsistent** 
 Several vendors handling personal data do not have complete privacy terms, documented instructions, breach notification commitments, or evidence of periodic review.

5. **Retention schedule not fully implemented in systems** 
 Retention rules exist for some data types, but technical enforcement and exception tracking are limited.

### Management Attention Required

Management should prioritise remediation of high-rated findings within [30-60] days and medium-rated findings within [90-120] days. The Privacy Office should maintain a formal remediation tracker and report progress to the [Privacy Steering Committee / Risk Committee] monthly until closure.

## Methodology

### Audit Approach

The internal audit was performed using a risk-based assurance approach. The review assessed both design effectiveness and operating effectiveness of privacy controls.

The audit included:

- Review of approved policies, procedures, templates, and governance records.
- Interviews with process owners and control performers.
- Walkthroughs of selected privacy processes.
- Sample testing of personal data processing activities, contracts, requests, incidents, training records, and transfer records.
- Assessment of evidence against organisational privacy requirements and Saudi PDPL implementation expectations.
- Validation of management responses and proposed remediation actions.

### Audit Criteria

The audit criteria included:

- Requirements of the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law and Implementing Regulations.
- [Organisation Name]’s approved privacy policies, procedures, standards, and contractual commitments.
- Internal governance expectations for privacy accountability, risk management, incident management, records management, and third-party oversight.
- Recognised good practice for privacy programme governance, documentation, monitoring, and assurance.

### Finding 1 - Personal Data Inventory Is Incomplete and Not Consistently Maintained

| Field | Details |

| Rating | High |

| Status | Open |

#### Condition

The organisation has established a personal data inventory, but it is incomplete and not consistently maintained across all business functions. Of 20 processing records sampled, 11 were missing one or more key elements such as processing purpose, data categories, individual categories, source of data, retention period, recipient categories, transfer location, system owner, or lawful handling rationale.

Some business processes involving customer support, recruitment, vendor onboarding, and analytics were not fully reflected in the inventory. Several records had not been reviewed or updated within the expected review cycle.

#### Risk / Impact

An incomplete inventory limits the organisation’s ability to:

- Demonstrate accountability over personal data processing.
- Provide accurate privacy notices.
- Respond to data subject requests completely and within expected timelines.
- Identify cross-border transfers and third-party disclosures.
- Apply retention and disposal requirements.
- Assess risk before introducing new or changed processing.

#### Evidence

- Data inventory extract dated [YYYY-MM-DD].
- Sample of 20 processing activity records.
- Interviews with [HR], [Marketing], [Customer Support], and [IT].
- Absence of documented review dates for selected records.

#### Root Cause

Privacy inventory maintenance is not embedded into business change, project intake, vendor onboarding, or system implementation processes. Ownership of individual inventory entries is not consistently assigned or monitored.

#### Recommendation

Update the personal data inventory to include all material processing activities and require each record to include mandatory fields. Assign accountable business owners and establish a periodic attestation process. Integrate inventory updates into new project approvals, vendor onboarding, system changes, and process changes.

#### Management Response

Management agrees. The Privacy Office will conduct a structured refresh of the inventory and assign accountable owners for all entries.

| Action | Owner | Due Date | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Configure privacy complaint categories | [Customer Support / IT] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Ticket category configuration |
| Train support agents on categorisation | [Customer Support / Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Training records |
| Report privacy complaint trends monthly | [Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Monthly dashboard |

---

### Finding 16 - Positive Observation: Breach Escalation Awareness Is Strong in Security Operations

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Rating | Positive Observation |
| Area | Incident management |
| Owner | [Information Security] |

Security operations personnel demonstrated clear awareness of when to escalate suspected personal data incidents to the Privacy Office. Interviews confirmed that privacy escalation is included in incident triage discussions, and several sampled incidents showed timely referral to the Privacy Office.

This practice should be maintained and reinforced through tabletop exercises and periodic refresher training.

---

### Finding 17 - Positive Observation: Privacy Office Engagement in Vendor Onboarding Has Improved

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Rating | Positive Observation |
| Area | Vendor management |
| Owner | [Procurement / Privacy Office] |

The Privacy Office is increasingly involved in reviewing vendors that may process personal data. Newer vendor files showed better documentation than legacy files, including privacy questionnaires and evidence of Legal review.

This improvement should be formalised through mandatory workflow checkpoints.

---

### Finding 18 - Positive Observation: Employees Demonstrate General Awareness of Privacy Escalation Channels

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Rating | Positive Observation |
| Area | Training and awareness |
| Owner | [HR / Privacy Office] |

Most interviewed employees understood that suspected privacy incidents, unusual personal data requests, or unclear data handling situations should be escalated to [Privacy Office Contact / Privacy Mailbox]. This indicates that awareness communications are having a positive effect.

The organisation should continue recurring awareness campaigns and include practical examples relevant to each function.

## Analysis

### Overall Control Maturity

The privacy programme has moved beyond initial policy development and has several foundational elements in place. However, the audit indicates that the programme remains partially dependent on manual effort, informal coordination, and individual knowledge rather than embedded, system-supported controls.

| Domain | Maturity Assessment | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| Governance and accountability | Developing | Roles exist, but metrics and committee reporting require strengthening. |
| Processing records | Developing | Inventory exists but lacks completeness, quality control, and integration with change processes. |
| Transparency | Developing | Notices are in place but require standardisation and review governance. |
| Consent and preferences | Developing | Controls exist in some channels but are not consistently integrated. |
| Individual rights | Developing | Procedure exists, but workflow evidence and deadline controls require improvement. |
| Vendor management | Developing | New onboarding has improved, but legacy vendor remediation is needed. |
| Cross-border transfers | Basic to developing | Transfer activity occurs, but documentation and approval are inconsistent. |
| Breach management | Developing | Escalation works, but assessment documentation must improve. |
| Retention and disposal | Basic to developing | Retention rules are documented but not fully implemented in systems. |
| Training and awareness | Developing | General awareness is in place; role-based training is needed. |
| Monitoring and assurance | Developing | Internal audit performed; ongoing metrics and control testing should be formalised. |

### Risk Themes

The findings indicate five main risk themes:

1. **Evidence and documentation gaps** 
 Several controls may be performed in practice, but evidence is not consistently retained. This affects auditability and management confidence.

2. **Limited workflow automation** 
 Data subject requests, breach assessments, transfer approvals, and retention activities rely heavily on manual tracking. This increases the likelihood of missed deadlines, inconsistent handling, and incomplete records.

3. **Insufficient integration with business change** 
 Privacy checkpoints are not consistently embedded into project initiation, procurement, system change, and new process design. This creates a risk that privacy requirements are addressed late or not at all.

4. **Third-party and transfer exposure** 
 Vendor and transfer governance are the highest-priority areas because they involve personal data outside direct organisational control and may create external compliance exposure.

5. **Retention implementation lag** 
 Retention requirements are not yet consistently enforced within systems. This increases the volume of personal data held and may amplify breach or complaint impact.

### Root Cause Summary

| Root Cause | Related Findings |
|---|---|
| Privacy controls not embedded into business workflows | Findings 1, 3, 4, 9 |
| Manual tracking and fragmented evidence storage | Findings 2, 6, 8, 15 |
| Lack of standardised templates and quality criteria | Findings 1, 2, 3, 5, 12 |
| Limited system configuration for privacy controls | Findings 6, 7, 8 |
| Insufficient role-based training and ownership | Findings 10, 13, 14 |
| Legacy vendor and system environment not remediated | Findings 3, 4, 7 |

### Residual Risk View

If the high-rated findings are not remediated promptly, residual privacy risk will remain elevated in the following areas:

- Inability to demonstrate full knowledge of personal data processing activities.
- Inconsistent response to individual rights requests.
- Unapproved or insufficiently documented cross-border transfers.
- Inadequate contractual and monitoring controls over processors.
- Retention of personal data beyond business and legal need.

Once agreed actions are implemented and validated, residual risk is expected to reduce to a manageable level, provided that privacy governance reporting and periodic monitoring are sustained.

### Comparison with Previous Audit

| Area | Previous Status | Current Status | Trend |
|---|---|---|---|
| Privacy governance | [Not assessed / Developing] | Developing | Improving |
| Data inventory | [Not assessed / Partial] | Partial | Stable |
| Data subject requests | [Not assessed / Partial] | Partial | Stable |
| Breach management | [Not assessed / Developing] | Developing | Improving |
| Vendor management | [Not assessed / Partial] | Partial | Improving for new vendors, weak for legacy vendors |
| Retention | [Not assessed / Limited] | Limited implementation | Needs attention |
| Training | [Not assessed / Developing] | Developing | Improving |

Where prior results are unavailable, this report should be treated as the baseline for future audit comparisons.

## Recommendations & Actions

### Priority Recommendations

Management should implement the following priority improvements:

1. **Complete and govern the personal data inventory**
 - Make the inventory the central record for processing activities, systems, owners, vendors, transfers, retention, and notices.
 - Require business owner attestation at least quarterly or when material changes occur.

2. **Operationalise data subject rights handling**
 - Use a central workflow tool.
 - Track deadlines automatically.
 - Retain evidence of identity verification, searches, responses, and closure approvals.

3. **Formalise cross-border transfer approval**
 - Maintain a transfer register.
 - Require documented assessment and approval before transfers begin.
 - Link transfers to vendor files, system records, and processing inventory entries.

4. **Remediate processor contracts and monitoring**
 - Prioritise high-risk vendors and those handling sensitive, high-volume, or business-critical personal data.
 - Require clear processing instructions, breach notification obligations, sub-processor controls, security commitments, and data return or deletion terms.

5. **Implement retention controls**
 - Translate the retention schedule into system-level configuration, deletion workflows, and exception approvals.
 - Obtain periodic certification from system and business owners.

6. **Strengthen monitoring and reporting**
 - Establish privacy metrics and monthly dashboard reporting.
 - Track all remediation actions to closure.
 - Escalate overdue actions to the governance committee.

### Consolidated Action Plan

| Ref | Action Summary | Rating | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Refresh and complete personal data inventory | High | [Privacy Office / Business Owners] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 2 | Implement data subject rights workflow and evidence checklist | High | [Privacy Office / Customer Support / HR] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 3 | Establish cross-border transfer assessment and approval process | High | [Legal / Privacy Office / IT / Procurement] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 4 | Remediate high-risk vendor privacy contract gaps | High | [Procurement / Legal] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 5 | Refresh privacy notices and create notice register | Medium | [Legal / Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 6 | Standardise consent and preference management | Medium | [Marketing / IT / Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 7 | Implement retention controls for priority systems | Medium | [IT / Records Management / System Owners] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 8 | Enhance breach assessment documentation in incident workflow | Medium | [Information Security / Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 9 | Embed privacy impact assessment triggers into project intake | Medium | [PMO / Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 10 | Launch role-based privacy training | Medium | [HR / Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 11 | Implement privacy dashboard and management metrics | Medium | [Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 12 | Apply document control to privacy artefacts | Low | [Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 13 | Add data minimisation reviews to collection forms | Low | [Business Owners / Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 14 | Issue sensitive personal data handling guidance | Low | [Privacy Office / HR / Information Security] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| 15 | Configure privacy complaint categories and trend reporting | Low | [Customer Support / Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |

### Remediation Governance

The Privacy Office shall maintain the remediation tracker and coordinate status updates with action owners. Evidence of completion must be reviewed before actions are closed.

Minimum closure evidence should include:

- Updated or approved documents, where applicable.
- System screenshots or configuration evidence, where applicable.
- Completed registers, logs, or records.
- Training completion reports, where applicable.
- Sample testing results demonstrating operating effectiveness.
- Governance committee acknowledgement for high-rated finding closure.

### Follow-Up Review

A follow-up review should be performed after the target closure dates for high and medium findings. The follow-up should validate:

- Whether agreed actions were completed.
- Whether evidence is sufficient and retained.
- Whether controls are operating consistently.
- Whether residual risk has been reduced.
- Whether any overdue actions require escalation or revised risk acceptance.

| Follow-Up Activity | Responsible Party | Planned Date |
|---|---|---|
| Validate closure evidence for high-rated findings | [Internal Audit / Compliance] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Validate closure evidence for medium-rated findings | [Internal Audit / Compliance] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Report remediation status to governance committee | [Privacy Office] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Conduct targeted retesting | [Internal Audit] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Issue follow-up assurance memo | [Internal Audit] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

### Risk Acceptance

Where remediation cannot be completed by the agreed due date, the action owner must submit a documented risk acceptance or extension request. The request must include:

- Reason for delay or non-remediation.
- Interim controls.
- Residual risk assessment.
- Revised target date.
- Approval by the appropriate management authority.
- Confirmation that Legal and Privacy have reviewed the impact where privacy compliance risk is involved.

High-rated findings should not be risk accepted without senior management approval.

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution

This report is distributed to the following internal stakeholders:

| Recipient / Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Chief Executive Officer / Managing Director] | Executive oversight and accountability |
| [Chief Legal Officer / General Counsel] | Legal review and compliance oversight |
| [Chief Information Security Officer] | Security and incident-related remediation |
| [Chief Compliance Officer / Risk Officer] | Risk management and monitoring |
| [Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer] | Programme ownership and remediation coordination |
| [Head of Procurement] | Vendor management remediation |
| [Head of HR] | Employee data, training, and HR process remediation |
| [Head of Marketing] | Consent, notices, and preference management remediation |
| [Head of IT / CIO] | System workflow, retention, and technical implementation |
| [Internal Audit] | Assurance records and follow-up review |
| [Privacy Steering Committee / Risk Committee] | Governance oversight and status tracking |

### Confidentiality Requirements

This report is classified as **Confidential - Internal Use Only** and contains sensitive assurance findings relating to privacy governance, compliance posture, internal controls, systems, vendors, and operational processes.

Recipients must:

- Use the report only for authorised governance, remediation, assurance, and legal compliance purposes.
- Not distribute the report outside the approved recipient list without written approval from [Report Owner].
- Not share the report with external parties, vendors, consultants, or regulators unless approved by Legal and authorised management.
- Store the report only in approved internal repositories with access restricted to authorised personnel.
- Protect extracts, screenshots, working papers, and supporting evidence with the same confidentiality level as this report.
- Ensure any printed copies are secured and destroyed when no longer required.

### External Disclosure

Any external disclosure of this report, including disclosure to regulators, auditors, customers, insurers, legal counsel, or business partners, must be approved in advance by:

- [General Counsel / Legal Department]
- [Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer]
- [Chief Compliance Officer / Risk Officer]
- [Executive Sponsor], where required

### Record Retention

The final report, management responses, working papers, evidence, and follow-up validation records shall be retained in accordance with [Organisation Name]’s audit and records retention requirements.

| Record | Minimum Retention Location | Responsible Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Final audit report | [GRC Repository / Audit System] | [Internal Audit] |
| Supporting evidence | [Secure Evidence Repository] | [Internal Audit] |
| Management responses | [GRC Repository / Audit System] | [Privacy Office / Internal Audit] |
| Remediation tracker | [GRC Tool / Privacy Programme Repository] | [Privacy Office] |
| Follow-up validation records | [GRC Repository / Audit System] | [Internal Audit] |

PDPL-034.title: SDAIA Inquiry / Complaint Response Pack
PDPL-034.content:
## What This Evidences

The **SDAIA Inquiry / Complaint Response Pack** evidences that the organisation can cooperate with SDAIA and respond to regulator inquiries or complaints within short response windows under Saudi PDPL expectations. It demonstrates that the organisation can identify the inquiry, assign ownership, investigate relevant personal data processing activities, prepare an approved response, submit it through the appropriate channel, and retain proof of submission.

This artifact is **operational evidence collected from live organisational systems**. It is **not authored as a standalone document** and must not be fabricated. The final evidence should be exported and packaged as a ZIP containing tickets, communications, approvals, logs, submissions, and supporting records from the organisation’s own systems.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect the evidence from the systems used to receive, manage, investigate, approve, and respond to regulator matters, typically:

- [ITSM / case management system], such as [ServiceNow / Jira Service Management / Freshservice]
- [Privacy request / compliance portal], if SDAIA inquiries are tracked there
- [Email system], such as [Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace], for regulator communications
- [Document management system], such as [SharePoint / Google Drive / Box]
- [DLP / data discovery / privacy management platform], where relevant investigation evidence is stored
- [SIEM / log management platform], where access or activity logs support the investigation
- [Approval workflow tool], such as [Power Automate / DocuSign / internal GRC platform]
- [SDAIA portal or official submission channel], if applicable

## How To Collect

1. Identify the SDAIA inquiry or complaint reference number, received date, due date, and response owner.
2. Search [ITSM / case management system] for the relevant case using the reference number, complainant name, data subject identifier, email subject, or incident/request ID.
3. Export the full case record, including status history, assignment history, comments, attachments, timestamps, and closure details.
4. From [email system], export the inbound SDAIA communication and all outbound responses, including message headers, dates, recipients, and attachments.
5. From [document management system], collect the response draft, final approved response, investigation notes, evidence pack, and any legal or DPO review records.
6. From [approval workflow tool], export approval history showing who reviewed and approved the response and when.
7. From [SIEM / log store / privacy platform], export only the logs or reports directly relevant to the inquiry, such as access records, consent records, deletion records, disclosure logs, or processing activity evidence.
8. From [SDAIA portal / submission channel], capture submission confirmation, portal receipt, reference number, timestamp, and any acknowledgement.
9. Save all exports into a single folder using a consistent naming convention.
10. Compress the folder into a ZIP named: `SDAIA_Response_Pack_[ReferenceID]_[YYYY-MM-DD].zip`.

## What To Capture

The ZIP should include:

- SDAIA inquiry or complaint reference number
- Date and time received
- Response deadline and actual submission date
- Case/ticket ID and full case timeline
- Assigned owner, reviewers, approvers, and escalation contacts
- Original inquiry or complaint communication
- Investigation notes and supporting evidence
- Relevant personal data, system, or processing activity records
- Internal decision logs and legal/DPO review comments
- Approved response text or response letter
- Evidence of submission to SDAIA
- Confirmation receipt, acknowledgement, or portal screenshot
- Closure notes and final case status
- Any delay justification or escalation record, if applicable

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Collect for every SDAIA inquiry, complaint, clarification request, or follow-up.
- **Primary Owner:** [Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead]
- **Operational Owner:** [Compliance Operations / ITSM Case Owner]
- **Supporting Teams:** [Legal], [Information Security], [IT Operations], [Business System Owner], [Customer Support]

The pack should be assembled immediately after response submission and completed before the case is closed.

## Retention & Storage

Store the ZIP in [secure compliance evidence repository / GRC platform / restricted SharePoint library] with access limited to [Privacy], [Legal], [Compliance], and authorised audit personnel.

Apply the organisation’s regulatory evidence retention period, or retain for at least [retention period] from case closure, whichever is longer. Ensure the ZIP is protected against unauthorised modification and deletion. Where available, enable versioning, access logging, and retention lock.

Do not store unnecessary personal data. Redact or segregate sensitive personal data where full detail is not required for audit purposes.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will accept the evidence where the ZIP clearly shows:

- The SDAIA inquiry or complaint was received and logged promptly
- Ownership, escalation, and response deadlines were assigned
- The organisation investigated the matter using relevant internal records
- The response was reviewed and approved by appropriate personnel
- The response was submitted within the required timeframe or delay was justified
- Submission proof or acknowledgement is included
- The case was formally closed with a complete timeline
- Evidence comes from authoritative systems, not manually recreated files
- File names, timestamps, ticket IDs, and references are consistent across records
- Access to the retained evidence is controlled and auditable

PDPL-035.title: Annual Programme Review
PDPL-035.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [PDPL-RPT-APR-001] | 1.0 | Data Protection Officer | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Saudi Personal Data Protection Law | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This Annual Programme Review reports on the maturity, effectiveness, and operating performance of [Organisation Name]’s personal data protection programme for the reporting period. It provides management with a consolidated view of compliance with the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law and its Implementing Regulations, including the status of governance activities, privacy risk management, data subject rights handling, data sharing controls, cross-border transfer arrangements, incident readiness, and the refresh of Data Protection Impact Assessments.

The report is intended to:

- Confirm whether the privacy programme remains suitable for the nature, scale, and sensitivity of personal data processed by [Organisation Name].
- Assess progress against the prior year privacy plan, remediation actions, and management commitments.
- Identify material compliance gaps, control weaknesses, operational issues, and emerging risks.
- Provide a year-end view of privacy risk exposure, including high-risk processing activities.
- Recommend actions for the next reporting cycle with accountable owners and target completion dates.
- Support evidence-based oversight by executive management, the Privacy Steering Committee, Internal Audit, Legal, Information Security, Risk Management, and relevant business owners.

This report is not a legal opinion. Legal interpretations and regulatory engagement decisions remain the responsibility of the Legal Department in consultation with the Data Protection Officer and executive management.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

This review covers the period from **[Start Date] to [End Date]**.

Where relevant, the report also references significant events occurring after the reporting period up to **[Report Finalisation Date]**, where those events affect risk, compliance posture, or management decisions.

### Organisational Scope

The review covers personal data processing activities conducted by:

- [Organisation Name] headquarters and Saudi operations.
- Business units that collect, use, disclose, store, archive, or delete personal data.
- Shared service functions including Human Resources, Finance, Legal, Procurement, Information Technology, Marketing, Customer Operations, and Compliance.
- Digital channels, customer platforms, employee systems, vendor-managed services, and internally hosted applications.
- Third parties processing personal data on behalf of [Organisation Name].
- Data sharing arrangements with partners, affiliates, regulators, service providers, and other authorised recipients.

### Data Categories in Scope

The programme review considered controls relating to the following personal data categories:

| Data Category | Examples | Primary Business Owners | Risk Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer personal data | Names, contact details, account identifiers, service history | [Customer Operations / Business Unit] | Medium |
| Employee personal data | Employment records, payroll information, performance data | Human Resources | Medium |
| Sensitive personal data | Health data, biometric data, financial information, national identifiers, special category records where applicable | [Relevant Business Owner] | High |
| Children’s or minors’ data | Guardian information, age-related records where applicable | [Relevant Business Owner] | High |
| Digital identifiers | Device IDs, IP addresses, cookies, application logs, user IDs | Information Technology / Digital | Medium |
| CCTV and physical access data | Visitor records, camera footage, access logs | Facilities / Security | Medium |
| Vendor and contact data | Supplier representatives, contract contacts, billing contacts | Procurement / Finance | Low to Medium |

### Processing Activities in Scope

The review included the following activities:

- Personal data collection and transparency practices.
- Consent management and other approved bases for processing.
- Data subject rights request handling.
- Privacy notices and communication materials.
- Records of processing activities and data inventory maintenance.
- Data Protection Impact Assessments, including annual refresh.
- Personal data sharing and disclosure controls.
- Third-party privacy due diligence and contract controls.
- Cross-border personal data transfer governance.
- Direct marketing and electronic communications practices.
- Retention, archiving, and secure disposal.
- Personal data breach response readiness and incident handling.
- Privacy training and awareness.
- Governance, monitoring, reporting, and issue remediation.

### Out of Scope

The following areas were not independently tested as part of this annual review, except where they directly affected privacy controls:

- Full technical penetration testing of systems.
- Full financial audit procedures.
- Detailed employment law compliance review.
- Full information security control certification assessment.
- Non-personal commercial data governance.

## Executive Summary

### Overall Conclusion

[Organisation Name] has established the core components of a Saudi PDPL-aligned privacy programme and demonstrated measurable progress during the reporting period. Governance structures, privacy documentation, data subject rights processes, incident escalation channels, and third-party review practices are in place. The organisation has also completed a refresh of priority Data Protection Impact Assessments for high-risk processing activities.

However, the programme remains in a maturing stage. The most significant areas requiring management attention are:

- Inconsistent maintenance of records of processing activities across business units.
- Limited evidence of periodic review for some privacy notices and consent records.
- Gaps in documenting the business justification and safeguards for certain data sharing and cross-border transfer arrangements.
- Uneven completion of vendor privacy reassessments.
- Retention schedules not fully implemented in all systems.
- Need for stronger metrics and management dashboards to evidence ongoing compliance.

No confirmed material personal data breach requiring external notification was recorded during the reporting period. Several privacy incidents and near misses were identified and resolved internally; these demonstrate that reporting channels are functioning, but root cause analysis indicates recurring issues with access management, email handling, and manual data extraction.

### Programme Maturity Rating

| Domain | Current Rating | Prior Rating | Direction of Travel | Summary |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Governance and accountability | 3 - Defined | 2 - Developing | Improving | Roles, committees, and reporting are established; evidence quality should improve. |
| Data inventory and processing records | 2 - Developing | 2 - Developing | Stable | Inventory exists but requires business owner refresh and reconciliation. |
| Transparency and consent | 3 - Defined | 2 - Developing | Improving | Key notices updated; consent evidence requires strengthening. |
| Data subject rights | 3 - Defined | 3 - Defined | Stable | Process is operating, with minor timeliness and tracking improvements needed. |
| DPIA and privacy risk management | 3 - Defined | 2 - Developing | Improving | High-risk assessments refreshed; action tracking requires more discipline. |
| Third-party and data sharing controls | 2 - Developing | 2 - Developing | Stable | Due diligence is in place but reassessment and contract evidence are incomplete. |
| Cross-border transfer governance | 2 - Developing | 1 - Initial | Improving | Transfer register created; justification and safeguard packs need completion. |
| Retention and disposal | 2 - Developing | 2 - Developing | Stable | Retention standard exists but technical implementation is inconsistent. |
| Breach response and incident management | 3 - Defined | 2 - Developing | Improving | Escalation and triage improved; tabletop exercise actions remain open. |
| Training and awareness | 3 - Defined | 2 - Developing | Improving | General training completed; targeted training should be expanded. |

Rating scale:

| Rating | Description |
|---:|---|
| 1 - Initial | Activities are ad hoc, undocumented, or dependent on individuals. |
| 2 - Developing | Core processes exist but are inconsistently applied or evidenced. |
| 3 - Defined | Processes are documented, communicated, and generally operating effectively. |
| 4 - Managed | Processes are measured, monitored, and consistently improved. |
| 5 - Optimised | Processes are embedded, automated where appropriate, and independently validated. |

### Key Achievements During the Reporting Period

| Achievement | Evidence Reviewed | Business Impact |
|---|---|---|
| Privacy governance forum established | Privacy Steering Committee terms of reference, meeting minutes, action logs | Improved accountability and executive oversight. |
| Core privacy policies updated | Approved policy set, publication records, staff acknowledgement reports | Increased consistency of expected behaviours. |
| Data subject rights workflow implemented | Ticketing records, response templates, request register | Improved ability to respond to individuals within expected timelines. |
| DPIA refresh completed for priority processing | DPIA register, updated assessments, risk treatment actions | Better visibility of high-risk processing and required safeguards. |
| Cross-border transfer register created | Transfer inventory, supplier mapping, contract extracts | Improved control over overseas access and hosting arrangements. |
| Privacy training delivered | Learning management reports, attendance records | Increased staff awareness of handling obligations. |
| Incident triage process improved | Incident logs, escalation matrix, tabletop exercise records | Faster identification and handling of privacy incidents. |

### Key Risks Requiring Management Attention

| Risk | Current Exposure | Potential Impact | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incomplete processing records | Medium | Inability to evidence lawful and transparent processing; delays in responding to regulator or data subject enquiries | High |
| Weak evidence of consent and preference management | Medium | Disputed marketing or optional processing activities; increased complaints | High |
| Incomplete cross-border transfer documentation | Medium to High | Regulatory scrutiny, data sharing delays, contractual exposure | High |
| Vendor privacy reassessments overdue | Medium | Unidentified processor risks, weak contractual protections, breach exposure | Medium |
| Retention rules not technically enforced in all systems | Medium | Over-retention, increased breach impact, difficulty honouring deletion requests | Medium |
| Manual data exports without consistent controls | Medium | Accidental disclosure, excessive access, loss of tracking | Medium |

### Overall Management Assessment

The privacy programme is directionally sound and materially stronger than at the beginning of the reporting period. The next cycle should focus on operational discipline: completing evidence packs, embedding privacy checks into procurement and change management, strengthening technical enforcement of retention and access controls, and improving management reporting.

## Methodology

### Review Approach

The annual programme review was conducted using a risk-based methodology combining document review, interviews, sample testing, metrics analysis, and action tracking. The assessment focused on whether privacy controls were designed appropriately and whether they were operating in practice.

The review was coordinated by the Data Protection Officer with input from Legal, Information Security, Internal Audit, Compliance, Risk Management, Procurement, Human Resources, Marketing, Customer Operations, and relevant system owners.

### Review Activities Performed

| Activity | Description | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Governance document review | Reviewed policies, standards, procedures, committee records, and approval evidence | Governance effectiveness observations |
| Processing inventory review | Assessed completeness and currency of records of processing activities | Inventory gap list |
| DPIA refresh | Revalidated high-risk and materially changed processing activities | Updated DPIA register and risk treatment plan |
| Data subject rights sample testing | Reviewed a sample of requests for timeliness, accuracy, identity verification, and closure evidence | Data subject rights testing results |
| Incident log review | Analysed privacy incidents, near misses, root causes, and response timelines | Incident trend analysis |
| Vendor sample review | Reviewed selected vendors handling personal data for due diligence, contract terms, and reassessment status | Third-party control findings |
| Cross-border transfer review | Identified transfers, overseas access, hosting arrangements, and documented safeguards | Transfer register status |
| Training review | Analysed completion rates and targeted awareness activities | Training effectiveness observations |
| Stakeholder interviews | Conducted interviews with process owners and control operators | Qualitative findings |
| Action plan validation | Reviewed progress against prior remediation commitments | Action status report |

### Evidence Sources

The following evidence sources were reviewed:

- Approved privacy and data protection policies.
- Data protection governance meeting minutes and action logs.
- Records of processing activities.
- Privacy notices and consent language.
- Data subject rights request register and case records.
- DPIA register, completed assessments, and risk treatment plans.
- Vendor due diligence questionnaires and contract extracts.
- Data sharing agreements and internal approval records.
- Cross-border transfer register and supporting documentation.
- Incident and breach management logs.
- Training completion reports and awareness communications.
- Retention schedule and disposal records.
- System access review records where relevant.
- Procurement and change management records for selected projects.

### Sampling

Testing was performed on a sample basis and does not represent exhaustive validation of every processing activity, system, vendor, or record.

| Test Area | Population | Sample Size | Selection Basis |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Data subject rights requests | [Number] requests | [Number] cases | Mix of access, correction, deletion, objection, and withdrawal requests |
| DPIAs | [Number] assessments | [Number] assessments | High-risk, materially changed, and overdue assessments |
| Vendors processing personal data | [Number] vendors | [Number] vendors | High-risk vendors, cross-border vendors, and recent onboarding |
| Privacy incidents | [Number] incidents / near misses | [Number] cases | Severity, recurrence, and business unit spread |
| Processing records | [Number] processing activities | [Number] records | High-volume, sensitive, and customer-facing activities |
| Privacy notices | [Number] notices | [Number] notices | External, employee-facing, digital channel, and marketing notices |

### Limitations

The review was subject to the following limitations:

- Some evidence was provided by business units on a self-attestation basis.
- Technical validation of all system configurations was not performed.
- Vendor evidence was limited to documentation available at the time of review.
- Some legacy systems do not support automated reporting for retention, deletion, or access review controls.

## Analysis

### Programme Strengths

The annual review identified the following strengths:

1. **Governance foundation is in place** 
 The organisation has defined privacy leadership, committee oversight, reporting lines, and documented responsibilities.

2. **Core documentation has improved** 
 Key policies, notices, procedures, and templates have been developed or refreshed during the period.

3. **DPIA practice is becoming embedded** 
 High-risk processing is more visible, and the DPIA refresh has identified practical remediation actions.

4. **Data subject rights process is operating** 
 Requests are logged, tracked, and generally handled within internal targets.

5. **Incident response channels are functioning** 
 Employees are reporting suspected incidents, and the DPO is involved in triage and assessment.

6. **Cross-border transfer awareness has increased** 
 The organisation has better visibility of overseas hosting, support, and affiliate access than in the prior year.

7. **Training coverage has improved** 
 General awareness completion rates have increased and role-based sessions have begun.

### Programme Weaknesses

The review identified recurring weaknesses that should be addressed in the next cycle:

1. **Evidence discipline remains inconsistent** 
 Many controls are being performed, but evidence is not always complete, centralised, approved, or easy to retrieve.

2. **Business unit ownership needs reinforcement** 
 The privacy programme remains too dependent on the DPO for operational follow-up. Business owners must take clearer responsibility for their processing activities.

3. **Inventory, DPIA, vendor, and transfer records are not fully integrated** 
 Records are maintained in separate trackers, creating risk of inconsistency and outdated information.

4. **Technical enforcement is uneven** 
 Retention, access controls, logging, and deletion practices vary across systems.

5. **Manual handling remains a significant risk** 
 Email, spreadsheets, shared folders, and file exports continue to create recurring incident and near-miss patterns.

6. **Consent and preference records require improvement** 
 The organisation needs more reliable evidence of when and how individuals agreed to optional processing and how withdrawals are propagated.

The risk level is considered manageable if the recommended actions are completed within agreed timelines and executive management reinforces business ownership.

## Recommendations & Actions

### Priority Recommendations

Management should approve the following priority recommendations for the next reporting cycle:

1. **Complete a full refresh of the processing inventory** 
 Require each business unit to validate processing purposes, data categories, systems, recipients, vendors, retention periods, sensitive data indicators, and cross-border data flows.

2. **Strengthen DPIA governance and action tracking** 
 Move all DPIA remediation actions into a central action tracker with clear ownership, due dates, escalation, and risk acceptance requirements.

3. **Complete cross-border transfer documentation** 
 Finalise transfer records and safeguard evidence for all overseas hosting, remote access, affiliate access, and vendor-managed processing.

4. **Improve consent and preference evidence** 
 Establish a central standard for consent capture, proof, withdrawal, and downstream synchronisation.

5. **Embed privacy checks into procurement and change management** 
 Make privacy screening mandatory for new systems, vendors, campaigns, integrations, analytics initiatives, and material process changes.

6. **Implement retention controls for high-risk systems** 
 Prioritise automated deletion, archival rules, and disposal evidence for systems containing sensitive, high-volume, or customer data.

7. **Strengthen vendor lifecycle management** 
 Implement reassessment schedules for high-risk vendors and require completion before contract renewal or service expansion.

8. **Reduce manual handling risk** 
 Introduce secure file transfer tools, restricted sharing, email controls, labelling, and targeted training for teams handling large exports.

9. **Improve privacy metrics and executive reporting** 
 Develop a dashboard covering inventory status, DPIA actions, rights requests, incidents, training, vendor reviews, transfers, and retention implementation.

10. **Build a central evidence repository** 
 Maintain audit-ready evidence for policies, approvals, notices, DPIAs, incidents, rights requests, vendor reviews, and transfer decisions.

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution

This report is intended for internal use by authorised personnel with a legitimate business need to review privacy programme performance, risk, and remediation activity.

Approved recipients include:

| Recipient Group | Purpose |

| Board or Board Committee, where applicable | Oversight of material privacy risk and remediation progress |

| Internal Audit | Independent assurance planning and evidence review |
| Business Unit Owners | Ownership of findings and remediation actions |
| Procurement | Vendor privacy risk management and contractual remediation |
| Human Resources | Employee data processing and training actions |

Any distribution outside the approved recipient groups requires prior approval from the Data Protection Officer and Legal Department.

### Confidentiality Requirements

This report is classified as **Confidential - Internal Use Only**. It contains sensitive information regarding privacy risks, incidents, vendors, systems, processing activities, and compliance gaps. Unauthorised disclosure may create legal, regulatory, commercial, operational, or reputational risk for [Organisation Name].

Recipients must:

- Store the report only in approved repositories with access controls.
- Not forward the report externally without written approval from Legal and the DPO.
- Not copy report content into external communications unless approved.
- Use the report only for governance, remediation, assurance, or authorised management purposes.
- Protect any extracts, slides, dashboards, or action trackers derived from this report with equivalent confidentiality.
- Report any suspected unauthorised disclosure of the report through the organisation’s incident reporting channel.

### External Disclosure

This report must not be disclosed to customers, vendors, regulators, auditors, consultants, affiliates, or other external parties unless:

- The disclosure has been reviewed and approved by Legal and the DPO.
- The recipient has a legitimate need to know.
- Appropriate confidentiality protections are in place.
- Sensitive internal findings are redacted where necessary.
- Executive approval is obtained where disclosure may create material risk.

### Record Retention

The final approved version of this report, supporting evidence, management approvals, and action tracking records must be retained in accordance with [Organisation Name]’s retention schedule.

The official record copy must be stored in [Approved Repository / System] under the ownership of the Data Protection Officer.
