PDPL-005.title: PDPL Gap Assessment
PDPL-005.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [PDPL-GAP-ASSMT-001] | 1.0 | [Privacy Office / Data Protection Officer] | [DD Month YYYY] | Saudi Personal Data Protection Law, Implementing Regulations, and Personal Data Transfer Regulations | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This report presents the results of the PDPL Gap Assessment conducted for [Organisation Name] to evaluate readiness against the requirements of the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law, its Implementing Regulations, and the rules governing transfer of personal data outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

The assessment identifies current practices, compliance gaps, risk exposure, priority remediation actions, and accountable owners. It is intended to support executive decision-making, implementation planning, privacy governance, regulatory readiness, and evidence preparation for potential inspection, inquiry, or audit by the competent authority.

The report focuses on practical readiness across the full personal data lifecycle, including collection, use, disclosure, retention, destruction, data subject rights, breach management, vendor processing, direct marketing, data transfer, and governance oversight.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Assessment period | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Report issue date | [DD Month YYYY] |
| Business units reviewed | [List business units, e.g., Human Resources, Customer Operations, Marketing, IT, Procurement, Legal, Compliance] |
| Locations covered | [Saudi Arabia offices, branches, data centres, remote operations, overseas processing locations if applicable] |
| Assessment lead | [Name / Role] |
| Report owner | [Name / Role] |
| Executive sponsor | [Name / Role] |

### Scope

The assessment covered [Organisation Name]’s current operating environment for personal data processing involving individuals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia or personal data otherwise subject to Saudi PDPL obligations.

The scope included:

- Personal data governance and accountability.
- Inventory of personal data processing activities.
- Identification and classification of personal data, including sensitive personal data.
- Lawful basis and purpose limitation for processing.
- Privacy notices, transparency, and data subject communications.
- Consent management where consent is required.
- Data subject rights handling.
- Processing of children’s data, if applicable.
- Direct marketing and advertising communications.
- Data minimisation and retention.
- Data accuracy and correction processes.
- Security safeguards for personal data.
- Breach detection, assessment, notification, and response.
- Processor and third-party management.
- Personal data sharing and disclosures.
- Cross-border personal data transfers and external access from outside Saudi Arabia.
- Records, evidence, approvals, and governance documentation.
- Training, awareness, and operational adoption.

### Systems and Data Repositories Reviewed

| System / Repository | Business Owner | Data Type | Approximate Data Volume | Hosting / Processing Location | In Scope |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| [CRM Platform] | [Customer Operations] | Customer contact details, preferences, transaction history | [Number] records | [Saudi Arabia / Cloud Region] | Yes |
| [HR System] | [Human Resources] | Employee records, payroll, performance, medical leave data | [Number] records | [Location] | Yes |
| [Marketing Platform] | [Marketing] | Prospects, consent status, campaign activity | [Number] records | [Location] | Yes |
| [ERP / Finance System] | [Finance] | Vendor, invoice, payment and tax-related personal data | [Number] records | [Location] | Yes |
| [Data Warehouse / BI Platform] | [IT / Analytics] | Consolidated operational and reporting datasets | [Number] records | [Location] | Yes |
| [Customer Support Tool] | [Service Operations] | Complaints, call recordings, identity verification records | [Number] records | [Location] | Yes |
| [File Shares / Collaboration Tools] | [IT] | Mixed business records containing personal data | Unknown | [Location] | Yes |

### Out of Scope

The following were not assessed in detail and should be addressed through separate review or future assessment:

- Deep technical penetration testing of systems.
- Full legal review of all customer, vendor, and employment contracts.
- Certification of information security controls.
- Exhaustive review of paper archives at all physical sites.
- Detailed review of overseas subsidiaries not involved in Saudi personal data processing, unless they access or process Saudi personal data.
- Validation of every individual data record for accuracy.

## Executive Summary

[Organisation Name] has established several foundational privacy and information security practices; however, the organisation is not yet fully ready to demonstrate comprehensive compliance with Saudi PDPL requirements. The most significant gaps relate to formal privacy governance, completeness of processing records, cross-border transfer controls, data subject rights operations, privacy notices, processor contracts, retention enforcement, and breach notification readiness.

The assessment found that personal data is processed across multiple systems and business functions, including customer management, employee administration, marketing, vendor management, analytics, and service delivery. While some controls exist through information security, legal contracting, and operational procedures, they are not consistently designed or evidenced as PDPL-specific controls.

### Overall Readiness Rating

| Readiness Area | Rating | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| Governance and accountability | Partially Ready | Roles exist informally, but formal privacy governance, decision rights, and reporting need strengthening. |
| Data inventory and processing records | Not Ready | Processing activities are not fully documented across all systems, purposes, categories, recipients, retention periods, and transfer locations. |
| Lawful processing and transparency | Partially Ready | Privacy notices and lawful basis mapping require revision to reflect actual processing practices. |
| Consent management | Partially Ready | Consent is captured in some channels, but evidence, withdrawal handling, and purpose-level tracking are inconsistent. |
| Data subject rights | Not Ready | No fully operational end-to-end workflow with identity verification, deadlines, exceptions, and audit trail. |
| Sensitive personal data | Partially Ready | Sensitive data exists in HR, health-related, identity, and potentially financial contexts; enhanced controls are not consistently defined. |
| Direct marketing | Partially Ready | Opt-out handling exists in some systems, but consent and suppression processes are not consistently governed. |
| Retention and disposal | Not Ready | Retention periods are not consistently mapped to processing purposes, and disposal evidence is limited. |
| Security safeguards | Partially Ready | Baseline security controls exist, but privacy-specific safeguards and access reviews need improvement. |
| Breach response | Partially Ready | Incident response exists, but PDPL-specific breach assessment, notification, and affected individual communication criteria require formalisation. |
| Processor and third-party management | Not Ready | Contracts and due diligence do not consistently include PDPL-aligned processor obligations and transfer restrictions. |
| Cross-border transfers | Not Ready | External hosting, support access, cloud platforms, and group sharing require formal transfer assessment and documented approvals. |
| Training and awareness | Partially Ready | General security awareness exists, but role-based PDPL training is not mature. |

### Overall Assessment Conclusion

Overall readiness is assessed as **Partially Ready with material remediation required**.

The organisation should implement a structured remediation programme led by the Privacy Office, Legal, Information Security, IT, Procurement, HR, Marketing, and relevant business owners. Priority should be given to high-risk areas where personal data is transferred outside Saudi Arabia, sensitive personal data is processed, individuals interact directly with the organisation, or regulatory notification obligations may be triggered.

### Key High-Priority Gaps

| Priority | Gap | Business Impact |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | No complete record of personal data processing activities | The organisation cannot reliably demonstrate what personal data it processes, why, where, for how long, and with whom it is shared. |
| 2 | Cross-border transfers not formally assessed or approved | Transfers or remote access may occur without adequate justification, safeguards, or required documentation. |
| 3 | Data subject rights process not operationalised | Requests may be delayed, mishandled, or answered inconsistently. |
| 4 | Privacy notices do not fully reflect actual processing | Individuals may not receive clear information about purposes, disclosures, retention, rights, and transfer practices. |
| 5 | Processor contracts lack required privacy obligations | Vendors may process personal data without sufficient restrictions, security commitments, breach notice duties, or transfer controls. |
| 6 | Retention schedule not implemented across systems | Personal data may be kept longer than necessary, increasing regulatory, security, and litigation risk. |
| 7 | PDPL-specific breach process incomplete | The organisation may fail to assess, escalate, notify, or evidence breach handling within required expectations. |

## Methodology

### Assessment Approach

The assessment was conducted using a structured review of governance documents, operational processes, system information, stakeholder interviews, and sample evidence. The objective was to determine whether current practices are designed and operating effectively to meet Saudi PDPL expectations.

The assessment methodology included:

1. **Document review** - policies, procedures, notices, contracts, incident plans, records, consent language, retention schedules, vendor templates, and system documentation.
2. **Stakeholder interviews** - discussions with business, technical, legal, compliance, HR, marketing, procurement, and security representatives.
3. **Data flow review** - identification of personal data sources, systems, recipients, processors, hosting locations, access patterns, and transfer routes.
4. **Control mapping** - comparison of current practices against PDPL compliance expectations.
5. **Evidence sampling** - review of selected records, workflows, contracts, tickets, training logs, access reports, and incident records.
6. **Risk rating** - classification of gaps by impact, likelihood, regulatory exposure, and implementation urgency.
7. **Action planning** - development of recommended remediation actions, ownership, and indicative timelines.

### Assessment Ratings

| Rating | Definition |
|---|---|
| Ready | Control is designed, implemented, documented, and supported by evidence. Minor improvement may be beneficial but is not essential for readiness. |
| Partially Ready | Some practices exist, but they are incomplete, inconsistent, not fully documented, or not operating across all relevant areas. |
| Not Ready | Required control is absent, undocumented, not implemented, or materially ineffective. |
| Not Applicable | Requirement does not apply based on confirmed business activities, data types, or processing context. |

### Risk Ratings

| Risk Rating | Description | Typical Response |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Immediate exposure to regulatory, legal, reputational, or individual harm risk; urgent executive attention required. | Remediate immediately with executive oversight. |
| High | Significant compliance gap or control weakness affecting important processing activity. | Remediate through priority action plan. |
| Medium | Moderate gap requiring planned improvement and monitoring. | Remediate within agreed programme timeline. |
| Low | Limited issue or enhancement opportunity. | Address through continuous improvement. |

### Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence Category | Examples Reviewed | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Governance documentation | Privacy policy, information security policy, compliance committee terms, risk register | Partially Available |
| Processing records | Data inventories, system lists, business process maps | Incomplete |
| Privacy notices | Website notice, employee notice, customer forms, application notices | Partially Available |
| Consent records | Marketing opt-ins, cookie preferences, signed forms, consent language | Inconsistent |
| Contracts | Vendor agreements, data processing terms, cloud service contracts, support agreements | Partially Available |
| Security records | Access control reports, encryption standards, vulnerability summaries, incident tickets | Partially Available |
| Breach response | Incident response plan, escalation contacts, prior incident logs | Partially Available |
| Retention records | Records retention schedule, disposal logs, archival rules | Incomplete |
| Transfer records | Cloud hosting information, vendor locations, remote access details | Incomplete |
| Training records | Security training logs, compliance training material | Partially Available |

### Stakeholders Consulted

| Function | Role / Representative | Topics Covered |
|---|---|---|
| Legal | [Name / Role] | Lawful basis, notices, contracts, regulatory engagement |
| Compliance | [Name / Role] | Governance, monitoring, evidence, reporting |
| Information Security | [Name / Role] | Security controls, breach response, access management |
| IT | [Name / Role] | Systems, hosting, integrations, access, data repositories |
| Human Resources | [Name / Role] | Employee data, recruitment, payroll, benefits, retention |
| Marketing | [Name / Role] | Campaigns, consent, opt-out, profiling, cookies |
| Customer Operations | [Name / Role] | Customer records, complaints, service channels, rights requests |
| Procurement | [Name / Role] | Vendor onboarding, contracts, due diligence |
| Data / Analytics | [Name / Role] | Reporting, dashboards, data warehouse, anonymisation |
| Internal Audit | [Name / Role] | Assurance, control testing, risk tracking |

## Detailed Findings / Results (with structure)

### 1. Governance, Accountability, and Privacy Operating Model

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-01 | Privacy governance is not formally established as an operating model. | Responsibilities are distributed between Legal, Compliance, IT, and Information Security, but there is no approved privacy governance structure defining ownership, escalation, reporting, decision rights, and accountability for PDPL compliance. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-02 | No formal PDPL implementation roadmap exists. | Several privacy-related activities are underway, but there is no consolidated plan with milestones, owners, dependencies, and executive oversight. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-03 | Privacy risk is not consistently recorded in enterprise risk management. | Some privacy risks are discussed informally, but they are not consistently documented, rated, monitored, or escalated. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Without a formal privacy operating model, compliance may depend on individual judgement rather than repeatable governance. This increases the risk of inconsistent decisions, missed obligations, limited evidence, and slow remediation.

**Recommended Control Design**

- Appoint an accountable privacy lead or Data Protection Officer function appropriate to the organisation’s size and risk profile.
- Establish a privacy governance committee or include PDPL as a standing agenda item in an existing risk and compliance forum.
- Define roles for Legal, Compliance, Information Security, IT, Procurement, HR, Marketing, Customer Operations, and business data owners.
- Create a PDPL compliance register, risk register, and remediation tracker.
- Require periodic executive reporting on privacy risk, incidents, rights requests, vendor issues, and transfer approvals.

---

### 2. Personal Data Inventory and Records of Processing

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-04 | Personal data processing activities are not comprehensively documented. | System lists exist, but they do not consistently capture processing purposes, data categories, individual categories, sources, recipients, processors, locations, retention periods, and transfer arrangements. | Critical | Not Ready |
| PDPL-05 | Data flows are not mapped end-to-end. | Business teams understand their local processes, but there is no organisation-wide view of data collection, internal sharing, external disclosure, storage, archiving, or deletion. | High | Not Ready |
| PDPL-06 | Sensitive personal data is not centrally identified. | HR and certain customer processes handle sensitive data, but there is no central register of sensitive personal data processing or enhanced safeguards. | High | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

The organisation cannot demonstrate control over the personal data lifecycle without complete processing records. This affects privacy notices, lawful basis decisions, rights responses, retention, transfer assessments, breach assessment, and vendor management.

**Minimum Data Inventory Fields Required**

| Field | Description | Current Status |
|---|---|---|
| Processing activity name | Clear business process name | Incomplete |
| Business owner | Accountable business function and owner | Incomplete |
| Processing purpose | Specific reason for collecting and using personal data | Incomplete |
| Individual category | Customers, employees, applicants, visitors, vendors, beneficiaries, users | Partially Captured |
| Personal data category | Contact, identity, financial, employment, health, location, behavioural, biometric if applicable | Incomplete |
| Sensitive data indicator | Identification of sensitive personal data and justification | Incomplete |
| Source of data | Individual, employer, government source, third party, system-generated | Incomplete |
| Collection channel | Website, mobile app, branch, call centre, form, API, email | Incomplete |
| Lawful basis / justification | Documented legal or operational basis for processing | Incomplete |
| Recipients | Internal teams, external vendors, public authorities, partners | Incomplete |
| Processor details | Vendor name, service, location, contract status | Incomplete |
| Transfer outside Saudi Arabia | Whether data is hosted, accessed, disclosed, or supported from outside the Kingdom | Incomplete |
| Retention period | Approved retention duration and trigger | Incomplete |
| Disposal method | Deletion, anonymisation, archival, secure destruction | Incomplete |
| Security safeguards | Access restrictions, encryption, logging, segregation | Partially Captured |

---

### 3. Lawful Processing, Purpose Limitation, and Data Minimisation

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-07 | Lawful basis for processing is not consistently documented. | Some processing is based on contract, employment need, legal obligation, consent, or legitimate operational necessity, but these justifications are not consistently recorded by activity. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-08 | Purpose limitation controls are not fully embedded. | Personal data collected for one purpose may be reused for reporting, analytics, marketing, or service improvement without formal compatibility review. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-09 | Data minimisation is not consistently applied. | Forms and systems may collect optional or historical fields without documented necessity. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Processing without clear purpose and justification increases regulatory exposure and may result in excessive, unexpected, or unfair use of personal data.

**Examples of Areas Requiring Review**

| Area | Potential Issue | Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| Customer onboarding | Collection of identity documents or demographic data beyond service need | Validate necessity and remove unnecessary fields |
| Marketing registration | Consent language may be bundled with service terms | Separate marketing consent from mandatory service processing |
| HR records | Historical documents may be retained indefinitely | Align collection and retention with employment and legal needs |
| Analytics | Production data may be reused for broad reporting | Confirm purpose, apply minimisation, and use anonymised or aggregated data where possible |
| Call recordings | Retention and use for training or quality may not be clearly disclosed | Update notices and define retention |

---

### 4. Privacy Notices and Transparency

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-10 | Privacy notices do not fully describe actual processing. | Website and customer notices exist, but they may not fully describe purposes, categories of data, recipients, retention, rights, complaint channels, and transfer practices. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-11 | Employee and candidate privacy notices require enhancement. | HR-related notices are not consistently provided at recruitment, onboarding, benefits administration, performance management, or monitoring points. | Medium | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-12 | Notices are not consistently presented at the point of collection. | Data may be collected through forms, call centres, applications, email, events, and branches without standardised privacy wording. | High | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Insufficient transparency may undermine the validity of processing, increase complaints, and weaken the organisation’s ability to defend its data practices.

**Privacy Notice Content Expectations**

| Notice Element | Required Practical Content | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Identity of organisation | Legal entity name and contact details | Partially Available |
| Purpose of processing | Clear and specific purposes | Incomplete |
| Data categories | Types of personal data collected | Incomplete |
| Collection sources | Whether data is collected directly or from third parties | Incomplete |
| Recipients and disclosures | Categories of internal and external recipients | Incomplete |
| Transfer information | Whether personal data may be transferred or accessed outside Saudi Arabia | Incomplete |
| Retention | How long data is kept or how retention is determined | Incomplete |
| Individual rights | Available rights and how to exercise them | Partially Available |
| Complaint route | How individuals can complain or escalate concerns | Incomplete |
| Consequences of refusal | Where applicable, impact of not providing required data | Incomplete |

---

### 5. Consent Management

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-13 | Consent is not managed consistently across channels. | Consent may be captured in digital platforms, forms, and call scripts, but there is no central consent standard or consistent evidence trail. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-14 | Withdrawal of consent is not consistently operationalised. | Individuals can unsubscribe from some marketing channels, but withdrawal across related systems and processing purposes is not fully controlled. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-15 | Consent wording is not consistently granular. | Consent may be combined with terms of service or general acknowledgements rather than purpose-specific statements. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Where processing relies on consent, the organisation may be unable to prove that consent was informed, specific, freely given, and capable of withdrawal.

**Consent Control Requirements**

| Control | Expected Practice | Current Status |
|---|---|---|
| Consent capture | Record who consented, when, how, to what wording, and for which purpose | Inconsistent |
| Consent evidence | Preserve proof of consent and version of language shown | Incomplete |
| Consent withdrawal | Provide easy withdrawal through comparable channels | Partially Available |
| Suppression | Ensure withdrawn individuals are not contacted for the withdrawn purpose | Partially Available |
| Consent refresh | Reconfirm consent where purpose materially changes | Not Formalised |
| Children or guardian consent | Apply enhanced verification where applicable | Not Assessed |

---

### 6. Data Subject Rights

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-16 | Data subject rights workflow is not fully implemented. | There is no central intake, triage, verification, fulfilment, exception handling, and closure process supported by templates and evidence. | Critical | Not Ready |
| PDPL-17 | System capability to locate and export personal data is inconsistent. | Some systems can retrieve records by identifier, while unstructured repositories and legacy systems require manual search. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-18 | Staff are not consistently trained to recognise rights requests. | Requests may be received by email, call centre, branches, social media, HR, or customer service without clear routing. | High | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Failure to respond accurately and on time to rights requests may lead to complaints, regulatory scrutiny, operational disruption, and reputational damage.

**Rights Request Process Expectations**

| Step | Expected Practice | Current Status |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | Central channel for requests, including email or web form | Not Formalised |
| Logging | Unique request ID, date received, requester identity, right type, due date | Not Formalised |
| Identity verification | Risk-based verification before disclosure or action | Not Formalised |
| Scope confirmation | Clarify request and affected systems | Not Formalised |
| Search and retrieval | Search structured and unstructured systems | Partially Available |
| Legal review | Apply lawful limitations or exceptions where appropriate | Informal |
| Response | Provide clear response in appropriate language and format | Not Standardised |
| Closure | Record outcome, date closed, evidence, and quality review | Not Formalised |

---

### 7. Sensitive Personal Data and High-Risk Processing

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-19 | Sensitive personal data processing is not subject to a consistent enhanced review. | HR, health, identity, financial, and potentially biometric or location data may be processed without a dedicated review of necessity, access, retention, and disclosure. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-20 | Privacy impact assessments are not consistently performed. | New projects and systems undergo technical and procurement review, but privacy risk assessment is not embedded as a standard gate. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-21 | Profiling, analytics, and automated decisioning have not been fully assessed. | Analytics activities exist, but the use of personal data for segmentation, behavioural analysis, scoring, or automated decisions is not centrally documented. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Sensitive or high-risk processing may create greater harm to individuals and higher regulatory exposure if not governed carefully.

**High-Risk Processing Triggers**

| Trigger | Example | Required Review |
|---|---|---|
| Sensitive personal data | Health data, biometric identifiers, genetic data, religious information, security-related records | Enhanced privacy impact review |
| Large-scale processing | Customer databases, employee monitoring, loyalty platforms | Privacy risk assessment and executive approval |
| Monitoring or tracking | CCTV, location tracking, online behavioural tracking | Transparency, necessity, access, retention controls |
| Automated decisions | Eligibility scoring, fraud flags, automated rejection | Fairness, transparency, review mechanism |
| Data matching | Combining data from multiple sources | Purpose compatibility and minimisation review |
| Vulnerable individuals | Children, patients, beneficiaries, employees in dependent relationship | Additional safeguards and clear notices |

---

### 8. Direct Marketing, Cookies, and Communications Preferences

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-22 | Marketing consent and preferences are not consistently governed. | Email unsubscribe exists in some tools, but SMS, call campaigns, app notifications, and third-party campaigns are not consistently controlled through a unified preference framework. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-23 | Suppression lists are not consistently synchronised. | Withdrawal or opt-out in one channel may not automatically prevent outreach through another channel or vendor campaign. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-24 | Website cookies and tracking technologies require review. | Cookies, analytics tags, pixels, and advertising technologies have not been fully inventoried or aligned with notice and consent expectations. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Improper marketing practices can result in complaints, unwanted contact, reputational harm, and regulatory scrutiny.

**Marketing Control Expectations**

| Area | Expected Practice | Current Status |
|---|---|---|
| Consent | Obtain clear consent where required for direct marketing | Inconsistent |
| Preference centre | Allow individuals to manage channels and topics | Not Fully Available |
| Suppression | Maintain reliable opt-out and do-not-contact controls | Partially Available |
| Vendor campaigns | Ensure agencies and platforms honour consent and opt-out | Incomplete |
| Cookie notice | Inform users about tracking technologies and choices | Incomplete |
| Campaign approvals | Require privacy review before launch | Informal |

---

### 9. Retention, Archiving, and Disposal

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-25 | Retention schedule is incomplete or not implemented. | Some legal and financial retention requirements are known, but personal data retention is not consistently defined by processing purpose and system. | High | Not Ready |
| PDPL-26 | System deletion capability is inconsistent. | Some systems support deletion or anonymisation, while others require manual intervention or retain backups beyond business need. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-27 | Disposal evidence is limited. | Secure destruction records, deletion logs, and anonymisation evidence are not consistently retained. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Retaining personal data longer than necessary increases security exposure, storage cost, operational burden, and regulatory risk.

**Retention Implementation Requirements**

| Requirement | Expected Practice | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Retention schedule | Approved schedule by data category, purpose, and legal requirement | Incomplete |
| System configuration | Automated retention or archival rules where feasible | Inconsistent |
| Legal hold | Ability to suspend deletion when legally required | Partially Available |
| Secure destruction | Documented destruction of electronic and paper records | Incomplete |
| Backup retention | Defined retention and recovery limits | Partially Available |
| Anonymisation | Use irreversible anonymisation where data is retained for analytics | Not Standardised |
| Evidence | Maintain deletion and destruction logs | Incomplete |

---

### 10. Information Security Safeguards for Personal Data

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-28 | Security controls exist but are not fully mapped to personal data risk. | Access control, monitoring, endpoint security, and network controls exist; however, privacy-specific risk alignment is not consistently documented. | Medium | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-29 | Access reviews for personal data systems require improvement. | Access is reviewed for some key systems, but frequency, evidence, privileged access, and joiner-mover-leaver controls are inconsistent. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-30 | Encryption and masking practices are inconsistent. | Encryption is used in some systems, but standards for encryption at rest, encryption in transit, masking in non-production, and secure file exchange are not consistently enforced. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-31 | Logging and monitoring of personal data access is incomplete. | Critical systems generate logs, but monitoring for inappropriate access, bulk export, or unusual activity is not fully implemented. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Security weaknesses may increase the likelihood or impact of personal data breaches and reduce the organisation’s ability to detect and investigate misuse.

**Priority Security Improvements**

| Control Area | Required Improvement |
|---|---|
| Access management | Role-based access, least privilege, periodic reviews, removal of dormant accounts |
| Privileged access | Strong authentication, approval workflow, logging, session monitoring where appropriate |
| Encryption | Encrypt personal data in transit and at rest based on risk |
| Data masking | Mask or anonymise personal data in development, testing, and analytics environments |
| Secure transfer | Use approved secure channels for file exchange and API transmission |
| Monitoring | Alert on bulk downloads, unusual access, failed logins, and high-risk exports |
| Endpoint and mobile security | Protect devices accessing personal data through approved controls |
| Physical security | Restrict access to paper files, archives, and workspaces containing personal data |

---

### 11. Personal Data Breach Management

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-32 | Breach response plan is not fully aligned to PDPL expectations. | A general incident response process exists, but it does not include PDPL-specific assessment criteria, regulatory escalation, affected individual communication, and evidence requirements. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-33 | Breach notification decision-making is not formally documented. | There is no standard breach assessment template to determine severity, affected individuals, data categories, containment, and notification need. | High | Not Ready |
| PDPL-34 | Processor breach notification obligations are inconsistent. | Vendor contracts do not consistently require prompt breach notification, cooperation, investigation support, and evidence preservation. | High | Not Ready |

**Impact**

A personal data breach may not be identified, escalated, assessed, notified, or documented in a timely and defensible manner.

**Breach Response Components Required**

| Component | Expected Practice | Current Status |
|---|---|---|
| Definition of personal data breach | Includes unauthorised access, disclosure, loss, alteration, destruction, or misuse | Incomplete |
| Intake and escalation | Clear reporting channels for staff, vendors, and service desks | Partially Available |
| Assessment template | Data type, volume, individuals, harm risk, containment, notification decision | Not Available |
| Regulatory notification | Defined owner, approval path, content, timing, and evidence | Not Formalised |
| Individual notification | Clear criteria and communication templates | Not Formalised |
| Breach register | Central record of incidents, decisions, actions, and lessons learned | Incomplete |
| Testing | Tabletop exercises for privacy breach scenarios | Not Conducted |

---

### 12. Processor, Vendor, and Third-Party Management

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-35 | Vendor privacy due diligence is incomplete. | Procurement conducts commercial and security review for some vendors, but privacy-specific due diligence is not consistently required. | High | Not Ready |
| PDPL-36 | Data processing terms are not consistently included in contracts. | Some agreements include confidentiality and security language, but processor obligations, instructions, sub-processing, audit rights, breach notice, deletion, and transfer restrictions are inconsistent. | High | Not Ready |
| PDPL-37 | Sub-processors are not centrally tracked. | Vendors may use cloud hosting, support teams, affiliates, or subcontractors without a complete register or approval process. | High | Not Ready |

**Impact**

Third-party processing creates significant compliance and operational risk, particularly where vendors host, access, support, analyse, or transmit Saudi personal data.

**Vendor Privacy Control Requirements**

| Requirement | Expected Practice | Current Status |
|---|---|---|
| Vendor classification | Identify vendors processing personal data and rate risk | Incomplete |
| Due diligence | Review security, privacy, hosting, sub-processors, transfer locations | Inconsistent |
| Contract terms | Include clear processing instructions and PDPL-aligned obligations | Incomplete |
| Sub-processor control | Require disclosure, approval, and flow-down obligations | Incomplete |
| Breach notice | Require prompt notice and cooperation | Inconsistent |
| Return or deletion | Require data return, deletion, and certification at termination | Incomplete |
| Audit and assurance | Reserve right to review evidence or conduct assessments | Inconsistent |
| Ongoing monitoring | Periodic reassessment for high-risk vendors | Not Formalised |

---

### 13. Cross-Border Personal Data Transfers

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-38 | Transfers outside Saudi Arabia are not fully identified. | Cloud hosting, vendor support, group access, analytics platforms, and remote administration may involve access or processing outside the Kingdom, but these are not fully recorded. | Critical | Not Ready |
| PDPL-39 | Transfer assessments are not performed consistently. | There is no standard process to assess necessity, legal basis, destination, safeguards, risk, proportionality, and approvals before transfer. | Critical | Not Ready |
| PDPL-40 | Transfer safeguards and documentation are incomplete. | Contracts may not include adequate restrictions on onward transfer, sub-processing, confidentiality, security, breach notification, and return or deletion. | High | Not Ready |
| PDPL-41 | Existing cloud and support arrangements require remediation. | Several systems may be hosted or supported from outside Saudi Arabia without documented transfer justification and evidence. | High | Not Ready |

**Impact**

Cross-border transfers are one of the highest-risk areas under Saudi PDPL. Unassessed hosting, remote support, data replication, group sharing, or vendor processing outside Saudi Arabia may expose the organisation to regulatory action and business disruption.

**Transfer Scenarios Requiring Assessment**

| Scenario | Example | Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud hosting | SaaS platform hosted outside Saudi Arabia | Confirm hosting location and perform transfer assessment |
| Remote support | Vendor engineers outside Saudi Arabia accessing production data | Restrict access, log sessions, minimise data, and document necessity |
| Group company access | Overseas affiliate accessing customer or employee data | Define purpose, role, safeguards, and approval |
| Analytics processing | Data exported to external analytics or BI platform | Minimise, anonymise where possible, and assess transfer |
| Backups and replication | Disaster recovery copy stored outside Saudi Arabia | Confirm location and safeguards |
| Customer service outsourcing | Offshore call centre or support provider | Contract controls, training, access restrictions, and monitoring |
| Marketing platforms | Campaign tools processing contact lists outside Saudi Arabia | Consent, notice, contract controls, and transfer review |

**Minimum Transfer Assessment Fields**

| Field | Required Information |
|---|---|
| Data exporter | Saudi entity or function disclosing or enabling access |
| Data importer | Recipient, processor, group company, or vendor |
| Destination country | Country where data is hosted, accessed, stored, or supported |
| Transfer mechanism | Hosting, remote access, API, file transfer, support, replication |
| Purpose | Specific business need requiring transfer |
| Data categories | Personal and sensitive personal data involved |
| Individual categories | Customers, employees, applicants, vendors, visitors, users |
| Volume and frequency | One-time, recurring, continuous, high-volume |
| Necessity assessment | Why processing cannot reasonably occur within Saudi Arabia |
| Risk assessment | Potential harm, destination risk, recipient maturity, security posture |
| Safeguards | Contract, encryption, access restriction, logging, minimisation, retention |
| Onward transfer | Whether recipient may further disclose or sub-process data |
| Approval | Legal, Privacy, Security, Business Owner, Executive where required |
| Review date | Date for reassessment and renewal |

---

### 14. Data Sharing, Disclosure, and Government Requests

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-42 | Data sharing decisions are not consistently documented. | Disclosures to partners, vendors, public authorities, auditors, insurers, and group companies may occur without a formal sharing assessment. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-43 | Government and law enforcement request handling requires formalisation. | Legal is typically involved, but there is no standard procedure to verify authority, scope requests, preserve evidence, and limit disclosure to what is required. | Medium | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-44 | Internal access and disclosure are not always purpose-limited. | Internal teams may access shared files, reports, or dashboards containing personal data beyond their operational need. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Uncontrolled disclosure may lead to excessive sharing, lack of transparency, breach exposure, and inability to demonstrate accountability.

**Required Disclosure Controls**

| Control | Expected Practice |
|---|---|
| Disclosure register | Record recurring disclosures and recipients |
| Approval workflow | Require Legal and Privacy review for new sharing arrangements |
| Data minimisation | Share only necessary fields |
| Secure transfer | Use approved encrypted channels |
| Purpose restriction | Define permitted use and prohibit incompatible use |
| Evidence | Retain request, approval, disclosure details, and legal basis |
| Government request procedure | Verify validity, authority, scope, and proportionality |

---

### 15. Training, Awareness, and Culture

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-45 | PDPL-specific training is not fully implemented. | General information security or compliance training exists, but staff are not consistently trained on PDPL obligations, rights requests, breach reporting, consent, and handling sensitive data. | Medium | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-46 | Role-based privacy training is limited. | High-risk functions such as HR, Marketing, Customer Operations, Procurement, IT, and Data Analytics have not received tailored training. | Medium | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-47 | Awareness materials are not embedded into daily operations. | There are limited quick reference guides, intranet pages, FAQs, or process checklists for staff. | Low | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Staff may fail to recognise privacy risks, mishandle personal data, delay escalation, or provide inaccurate information to individuals.

**Training Plan Requirements**

| Audience | Required Topics | Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| All staff | PDPL basics, personal data handling, breach reporting, confidentiality, phishing and secure sharing | Onboarding and annually |
| HR | Employee notices, sensitive data, retention, access requests, disciplinary records, medical data | Annually and upon process change |
| Marketing | Consent, opt-out, direct marketing, cookies, campaign approvals, suppression lists | Semi-annually |
| Customer Operations | Rights requests, identity verification, complaint handling, call recordings | Semi-annually |
| IT and Security | Privacy by design, access control, logging, masking, breach investigation | Annually |
| Procurement | Vendor due diligence, processor terms, transfer risks | Annually |
| Executives | Accountability, risk appetite, breach escalation, transfer decisions | Annually |

---

### 16. Privacy by Design and Change Management

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-48 | Privacy review is not embedded into project delivery. | New systems and changes are reviewed for technical, budgetary, and security considerations, but privacy is not consistently included as a required approval gate. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-49 | Privacy impact assessments are not standardised. | There is no approved template or trigger matrix for assessing privacy risks before launching new processing activities. | High | Not Ready |
| PDPL-50 | System design does not consistently support rights, retention, and minimisation. | Requirements for deletion, export, consent, audit logs, and field minimisation are not always included in system requirements. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Privacy risks may be introduced into new products, systems, campaigns, or integrations without adequate review, leading to costly rework or non-compliant processing.

**Required Privacy by Design Gates**

| Project Stage | Privacy Requirement |
|---|---|
| Idea / initiation | Determine whether personal data is involved |
| Requirements | Define purposes, data fields, lawful basis, retention, notices, rights support |
| Vendor selection | Conduct privacy and transfer due diligence |
| Design | Apply minimisation, access control, logging, masking, and security safeguards |
| Testing | Avoid use of live personal data unless approved and protected |
| Go-live | Confirm notices, consent, contracts, transfer assessment, and support model |
| Post-implementation | Review actual processing against approved design |

---

### 17. Documentation, Evidence, and Audit Readiness

| Finding ID | Finding | Current State | Risk Rating | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDPL-51 | Compliance evidence is fragmented. | Evidence exists across Legal, IT, Security, HR, Procurement, and business teams, but there is no central evidence repository or ownership model. | Medium | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-52 | Policies and procedures require PDPL alignment. | Current policies cover confidentiality and security, but do not fully address PDPL-specific processing obligations. | High | Partially Ready |
| PDPL-53 | Periodic monitoring and assurance are not defined. | There is no recurring privacy control testing plan, KPI reporting, or management review cycle. | Medium | Partially Ready |

**Impact**

Even where controls exist, lack of evidence may prevent the organisation from demonstrating compliance to management, auditors, customers, or the competent authority.

**Core Documentation Required**

| Document / Record | Current Status | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| Privacy governance charter | Not Available | High |
| PDPL compliance policy | Not Available / Draft Required | High |
| Records of processing activities | Incomplete | Critical |
| Data inventory and data flow maps | Incomplete | Critical |
| Privacy notices | Partially Available | High |
| Consent management standard | Not Available | High |
| Data subject rights procedure | Not Available | Critical |
| Personal data breach procedure | Incomplete | High |
| Vendor data processing agreement template | Incomplete | High |
| Cross-border transfer assessment template | Not Available | Critical |
| Retention schedule | Incomplete | High |
| Privacy impact assessment template | Not Available | High |
| Training records | Partially Available | Medium |
| Privacy risk register | Incomplete | Medium |
| Compliance monitoring plan | Not Available | Medium |

## Analysis

### Overall Maturity Assessment

The organisation demonstrates an emerging privacy control environment, supported by existing information security, legal, procurement, and compliance practices. However, PDPL readiness requires a more integrated and evidence-based operating model. The current state is heavily dependent on informal processes, system-specific practices, and individual business knowledge.

The most significant maturity issue is the lack of an authoritative view of personal data processing. Without a complete inventory and data flow map, other privacy obligations cannot be implemented reliably. Privacy notices, consent controls, retention rules, rights responses, transfer assessments, vendor contracts, and breach response all depend on knowing what personal data exists, why it is processed, where it is stored, who accesses it, and when it should be deleted.

### Primary Risk Themes

| Risk Theme | Description | Affected Areas |
|---|---|---|
| Accountability gap | Privacy roles and decision rights are not formalised. | Governance, risk management, reporting, remediation |
| Data visibility gap | Processing activities and data flows are not comprehensively documented. | Inventory, notices, retention, rights, breach response |
| Transfer exposure | Cross-border hosting, access, and support are not fully assessed. | Cloud, vendors, group companies, remote administration |
| Third-party dependency | Vendor processing obligations are not consistently controlled. | Procurement, contracts, outsourcing, sub-processors |
| Operational readiness gap | Rights requests, breach notification, consent withdrawal, and deletion are not fully operationalised. | Customer service, HR, IT, Legal, Compliance |
| Evidence weakness | Controls may exist but are not consistently documented or retained. | Audit readiness, regulatory response, management assurance |

### Root Cause Analysis

| Root Cause | Evidence Observed | Resulting Impact |
|---|---|---|
| No central privacy operating model | Responsibilities spread across functions without formal ownership | Delayed decisions and inconsistent practices |
| Limited data lifecycle mapping | Systems known but processing details incomplete | Inaccurate notices, weak retention, uncertain transfers |
| Procurement not privacy-led | Vendor review focused primarily on commercial and security factors | Processor and transfer risks not consistently addressed |
| Legacy systems and unstructured data | File shares, email, archives, and legacy applications contain personal data | Difficult rights fulfilment and disposal |
| Limited privacy awareness | Staff rely on general security training | Missed escalation of requests and incidents |
| Lack of templates and workflows | No standard forms for rights, breach, transfers, privacy impact assessments | Inconsistent evidence and decision-making |

### High-Risk Processing Areas

| Area | Risk Drivers | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Customer platforms | Large volumes, direct individual interaction, marketing, support records | High priority for inventory, notices, rights, consent, retention |
| HR and recruitment | Sensitive employee data, medical information, performance records, dependency relationship | High priority for notices, minimisation, access control, retention |
| Cloud applications | Potential hosting or support outside Saudi Arabia | Critical priority for transfer assessment and contract review |
| Marketing technologies | Consent, profiling, cookies, suppression lists, third-party platforms | High priority for preference governance |
| Analytics and reporting | Reuse of data, aggregation, dashboards, possible excessive access | Medium to high priority for minimisation and anonymisation |
| Vendor processing | Outsourcing, SaaS, support providers, agencies, sub-processors | High priority for due diligence and contractual remediation |

### Regulatory Readiness Assessment

The organisation would currently face challenges demonstrating:

- A complete and accurate record of personal data processing.
- Clear evidence of the lawful basis and purpose for each processing activity.
- Adequate transparency to individuals at all collection points.
- Operational ability to respond to individual rights requests within expected timelines.
- Documented justification and safeguards for cross-border transfers.
- PDPL-aligned contractual controls for processors.
- Evidence-based breach assessment and notification decisions.
- Consistent retention and deletion of personal data.
- Privacy risk review for new projects and high-risk processing.

### Dependencies and Constraints

| Dependency / Constraint | Impact on Remediation |
|---|---|
| System ownership clarity | Required to complete inventory, retention, rights handling, and deletion controls |
| Vendor cooperation | Needed to confirm hosting, sub-processors, support locations, and contract amendments |
| Legal review capacity | Needed for notices, lawful basis mapping, contracts, transfer assessments, and response templates |
| IT capability | Needed for access controls, logging, deletion, export, consent integration, and data discovery |
| Business process variation | Different channels and departments require tailored implementation |
| Legacy data repositories | May require manual clean-up, archival review, or phased remediation |
| Executive sponsorship | Needed to resolve cross-functional conflicts and prioritise budget |

## Recommendations & Actions

### Remediation Strategy

[Organisation Name] should establish a formal PDPL remediation programme with executive sponsorship and a defined implementation timeline. The programme should prioritise activities that reduce the highest regulatory and operational risks while building sustainable privacy governance.

The remediation strategy should follow four phases:

1. **Stabilise** - establish governance, assign ownership, stop high-risk unmanaged activities, and create core templates.
2. **Discover** - complete processing inventory, data flow maps, vendor register, and transfer register.
3. **Implement** - update notices, contracts, rights workflows, breach procedures, retention controls, and training.
4. **Assure** - test controls, monitor KPIs, review high-risk processing, and maintain evidence.

### Priority Action Plan

| Action ID | Action | Priority | Owner | Target Date | Expected Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACT-01 | Appoint accountable privacy lead and approve privacy governance model. | Critical | [Executive Sponsor / Compliance] | [Date] | Appointment record, governance terms, reporting cadence |
| ACT-02 | Establish PDPL remediation programme with workstreams, milestones, budget, and executive reporting. | Critical | [Privacy Office] | [Date] | Programme plan, steering committee minutes, risk tracker |
| ACT-03 | Build complete records of processing activities across all business units and systems. | Critical | [Privacy Office / Business Owners] | [Date] | Approved processing register |
| ACT-04 | Map personal data flows, including collection points, internal transfers, external recipients, storage, and deletion. | Critical | [IT / Business Owners] | [Date] | Data flow diagrams and system mapping |
| ACT-05 | Create cross-border transfer register and assess all hosting, vendor support, group access, and cloud arrangements. | Critical | [Legal / Privacy / IT] | [Date] | Transfer register, completed assessments, approvals |
| ACT-06 | Update customer, employee, candidate, website, and channel-specific privacy notices. | High | [Legal / Privacy / Marketing / HR] | [Date] | Approved notices, publication evidence |
| ACT-07 | Implement data subject rights procedure, intake channel, request log, identity verification process, and response templates. | Critical | [Privacy Office / Customer Operations / HR] | [Date] | Procedure, request register, templates, training records |
| ACT-08 | Develop consent management standard and remediate marketing consent and opt-out processes. | High | [Marketing / Legal / IT] | [Date] | Consent standard, consent records, suppression process |
| ACT-09 | Review and amend high-risk vendor contracts to include PDPL-aligned processor obligations. | High | [Procurement / Legal] | [Date] | Contract addenda, vendor register, due diligence files |
| ACT-10 | Implement vendor privacy due diligence and sub-processor approval workflow. | High | [Procurement / Privacy / Security] | [Date] | Due diligence questionnaire, approval records |
| ACT-11 | Develop and implement PDPL-aligned personal data breach procedure and breach assessment template. | High | [Information Security / Privacy / Legal] | [Date] | Procedure, breach register, tabletop exercise results |
| ACT-12 | Create retention schedule for personal data and implement deletion or archival rules in priority systems. | High | [Records Management / Legal / IT] | [Date] | Retention schedule, system configuration evidence, deletion logs |
| ACT-13 | Implement privacy impact assessment process for new systems, projects, campaigns, and high-risk processing. | High | [Privacy Office / PMO / IT] | [Date] | Assessment template, completed assessments, project gate evidence |
| ACT-14 | Perform access review for systems containing sensitive or high-volume personal data. | High | [IT / Information Security / System Owners] | [Date] | Access review results, remediation evidence |
| ACT-15 | Establish privacy training programme, including role-based modules for HR, Marketing, Customer Operations, IT, Procurement, and executives. | Medium | [Privacy Office / HR] | [Date] | Training content, completion logs |
| ACT-16 | Create privacy evidence repository and compliance monitoring dashboard. | Medium | [Compliance / Privacy Office] | [Date] | Repository structure, KPI dashboard, evidence index |
| ACT-17 | Review cookies, tracking technologies, pixels, and analytics tools. | Medium | [Marketing / IT / Privacy] | [Date] | Cookie inventory, updated notice, consent configuration |
| ACT-18 | Define anonymisation and masking standards for analytics, testing, and reporting. | Medium | [Data / IT / Security] | [Date] | Standard, system evidence, test data controls |

### Quick Wins - First 30 Days

| Quick Win | Benefit | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Create a central PDPL action tracker | Immediate visibility of ownership and progress | [Privacy Office] |
| Freeze onboarding of new high-risk processors without privacy review | Prevents creation of new unmanaged risk | [Procurement / Legal] |
| Issue staff guidance on recognising rights requests and privacy incidents | Reduces risk of missed escalation | [Compliance / HR] |
| Identify all cloud platforms and support locations | Supports urgent transfer risk assessment | [IT] |
| Publish interim rights request email address and escalation route | Enables controlled request handling | [Privacy Office] |
| Start inventory workshops with high-risk functions | Accelerates core compliance foundation | [Business Owners] |
| Update breach escalation contact list | Improves incident response readiness | [Information Security] |

### 90-Day Target State

By the end of the first 90 days, [Organisation Name] should aim to have:

- Approved privacy governance model and named accountable owners.
- Central PDPL remediation plan with executive oversight.
- Completed processing inventory for high-risk business functions.
- Initial transfer register covering all known cloud and vendor arrangements.
- Draft updated privacy notices for customer, employee, candidate, and website contexts.
- Operational rights request intake and logging process.
- Draft breach assessment and notification procedure.
- Vendor privacy due diligence embedded into procurement intake.
- Initial review of high-risk vendor contracts.
- Training delivered to high-risk functions.
- Privacy impact assessment template approved for new projects.

### 180-Day Target State

By the end of 180 days, [Organisation Name] should aim to have:

- Complete processing records across all in-scope business units.
- Approved and published privacy notices across all major collection channels.
- Operational data subject rights workflow tested through sample requests.
- Completed transfer assessments for all material cross-border processing.
- Amended or risk-accepted high-risk vendor contracts.
- Approved retention schedule and implementation plan for priority systems.
- Privacy impact assessment integrated into project and procurement governance.
- PDPL-specific breach tabletop exercise completed.
- Role-based training programme completed for relevant functions.
- Compliance dashboard reporting to executive management.

### Key Performance Indicators

| KPI | Target | Reporting Frequency |
|---|---:|---|
| Processing activities documented | 100% of in-scope activities | Monthly during implementation, quarterly thereafter |
| High-risk transfers assessed | 100% of known high-risk transfers | Monthly |
| High-risk vendor contracts remediated | 90% or approved exception | Monthly |
| Rights requests completed on time | 100% | Monthly |
| Privacy notices updated | 100% of priority notices | Monthly during remediation |
| Staff privacy training completion | 95% minimum | Monthly until complete, quarterly thereafter |
| Breach assessments documented | 100% of suspected personal data breaches | Per incident and quarterly |
| Access reviews completed for priority systems | 100% | Quarterly |
| Retention rules implemented for priority systems | 80% by target date | Monthly |
| Privacy impact assessments completed for applicable new projects | 100% | Monthly |

### Management Decisions Required

| Decision | Required By | Decision Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm accountable privacy leadership role and reporting line | [Date] | [Executive Sponsor] |
| Approve PDPL remediation budget and resources | [Date] | [Executive Committee] |
| Approve risk appetite for cross-border transfers and vendor exceptions | [Date] | [Risk Committee / Legal] |
| Confirm priority systems for retention and access remediation | [Date] | [CIO / Business Owners] |
| Approve external legal or consulting support, if needed | [Date] | [Executive Sponsor / Procurement] |
| Approve customer-facing notice publication plan | [Date] | [Legal / Marketing / Business Owner] |

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution

This report is intended for internal use by authorised personnel of [Organisation Name]. Distribution should be limited to individuals with a legitimate business need to review, approve, implement, or monitor PDPL remediation activities.

| Recipient Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Board / Executive Committee | Oversight, risk acceptance, funding, and strategic direction |
| Risk and Compliance Committee | Monitoring, governance, and remediation tracking |
| Legal | Legal interpretation, notices, contracts, transfer assessments, regulatory response |
| Privacy Office / Data Protection Function | Programme ownership and implementation |
| Information Security | Security safeguards, breach response, access control, monitoring |
| IT | Systems inventory, data flows, retention, access, logging, transfer assessment |
| Procurement | Vendor due diligence, contract remediation, sub-processor management |
| Human Resources | Employee data processing, notices, training, retention |
| Marketing | Consent, communications preferences, cookies, direct marketing |
| Customer Operations | Rights requests, complaints, service data handling |
| Internal Audit | Independent assurance planning and follow-up |

### Confidentiality Requirements

This report is classified as **Confidential - Internal Use Only**. It contains sensitive information regarding privacy compliance posture, control weaknesses, system processing, vendor arrangements, data flows, and remediation priorities.

The following handling rules apply:

- Do not distribute this report outside [Organisation Name] without written approval from [Report Owner / Legal].
- Do not upload this report to unauthorised collaboration platforms or external file-sharing tools.
- Store the report only in approved repositories with access restricted to authorised recipients.
- Do not extract findings for external communication without Legal and Privacy Office review.
- Redact sensitive system, vendor, incident, and personal data details before any approved external sharing.
- Treat remediation status, risk ratings, and identified gaps as confidential management information.
- Retain this report according to [Organisation Name]’s approved records retention schedule.
- If this report is requested by a regulator, customer, auditor, court, or third party, immediately refer the request to [Legal Department / Privacy Office].

### Report Limitations

This assessment was based on information made available during the reporting period, stakeholder representations, sampled evidence, and the systems and processes identified within scope. The findings reflect the state of readiness at the time of assessment and may change as business processes, systems, vendors, regulations, or evidence mature.

This report does not constitute legal advice. Legal interpretation and regulatory engagement should be managed by [Legal Department] with support from qualified Saudi legal counsel where required.

### Approval

| Role | Name | Signature / Approval Method | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Report Owner | [Name] | [Signature / Email Approval] | [Date] |
| Privacy Lead | [Name] | [Signature / Email Approval] | [Date] |
| Legal Reviewer | [Name] | [Signature / Email Approval] | [Date] |
| Executive Sponsor | [Name] | [Signature / Email Approval] | [Date] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique register identifier for this processing activity in the format DI-YYYY-###, e.g. DI-2026-001. |
| Processing Activity Name | Enter the short, specific name of the processing activity, e.g. employee payroll, customer onboarding, marketing consent management. |
| Business Owner | Enter the accountable business owner role or named individual responsible for the processing activity. |
| Department / Function | Enter the department or function that performs or owns the processing, e.g. HR, Finance, Sales, Customer Support, IT. |
| Process Description | Describe what happens to the personal data from collection to use, sharing, storage, and deletion in 1-3 sentences. |
| Data Controller Entity | Enter the legal entity determining the purpose and means of processing; include full registered name and country. |
| Processor / Joint Controller / Recipient Entity | Enter any third party or internal group entity that processes, receives, or jointly determines processing; use 'None' if not applicable. |
| Role of External Entity | Select one value: Processor, Sub-processor, Joint Controller, Independent Controller, Recipient, Government Authority, Internal Group Entity, None. |
| KSA Resident Data Involved | Select Yes or No to indicate whether the processing includes personal data of individuals residing in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. |
| Data Subject Categories | List the categories of individuals whose data is processed, e.g. customers, employees, job applicants, suppliers, visitors, patients, website users. |
| Personal Data Categories | List non-sensitive personal data categories processed, e.g. name, contact details, account ID, transaction history, employment records, device identifiers. |
| Sensitive Personal Data Categories | List any sensitive personal data processed under Saudi PDPL, such as health data, biometric data, genetic data, credit data, religious belief, security data, or enter 'None'. |
| National ID / Iqama / Official Identifier Used | Select Yes or No; if Yes, state the identifier type and why it is necessary for this activity. |
| Children / Minors Data Involved | Select Yes, No, or Unknown; if Yes, describe the age range and guardian consent/control process where applicable. |
| Data Source | State where the personal data originates, e.g. directly from data subject, employer, government platform, CRM import, third-party data provider, public source. |
| Collection Method / Channel | Enter the method used to collect the data, e.g. web form, mobile app, paper form, API, email, call recording, HR portal, physical access system. |
| Data Origin Location | Enter the country or location from which the data is collected or first received, e.g. Saudi Arabia, UAE, EU, Global. |
| Purpose of Processing | State the specific, explicit purpose for processing; avoid broad phrases such as 'business purposes'. |
| PDPL Lawful Basis | Select the applicable basis under Saudi PDPL: Consent, Contractual/Service Requirement, Legal Obligation, Vital Interest, Actual Interest/Legitimate Interest where permitted, Public Interest, Other; add a brief justification. |
| Consent Required | Select Yes, No, or Conditional based on the PDPL basis and nature of processing, especially for sensitive data, marketing, or disclosure. |
| Consent Capture Method | If consent is required, record how consent is captured and evidenced, e.g. tick-box with timestamp, signed form, recorded verbal consent; enter 'Not applicable' if consent is not required. |
| Consent Withdrawal Method | Record how individuals can withdraw consent, e.g. preference centre, unsubscribe link, email request, call centre; enter 'Not applicable' if consent is not used. |
| Privacy Notice Provided | Select Yes or No to indicate whether the data subject receives a PDPL-compliant notice at or before collection. |
| Privacy Notice Reference / URL | Enter the document title, version, URL, or repository link for the privacy notice used for this processing activity. |
| Data Minimisation Justification | Explain why each major data category is necessary and proportionate for the stated purpose. |
| Automated Decision-Making / Profiling | Select Yes or No; if Yes, describe the decision logic at a high level, impact on individuals, and human review option. |
| System / Application Name | Enter the system, application, platform, or manual file where the data is processed, e.g. SAP SuccessFactors, Salesforce, Oracle ERP. |
| Database / Repository / Storage Location | Enter the specific repository, database, file share, SaaS tenant, archive, or physical storage location holding the data. |
| Hosting Location | Enter the country or region where the system or repository is hosted, including cloud region if known, e.g. KSA, AWS me-south-1, EU-West, On-prem Riyadh. |
| Internal Data Flow | Describe internal movement of data between departments, systems, databases, or group entities, including source and destination. |
| External Disclosure / Sharing | Describe any disclosure or sharing outside the controller entity, including recipient name, purpose, data categories, and transfer method; enter 'None' if not applicable. |
| Recipient Country | Enter the country where each external recipient accesses or stores the data; use 'KSA only' if no foreign recipient exists. |
| Cross-Border Transfer Involved | Select Yes or No to indicate whether personal data is transferred, accessed, stored, or otherwise processed outside Saudi Arabia. |
| Cross-Border Transfer Justification | If Yes, enter the PDPL-compatible reason for transfer, e.g. contractual necessity, service delivery, public interest, regulatory requirement, or other approved exception; enter 'Not applicable' if No. |
| Transfer Safeguard / Approval Reference | Record the safeguard, approval, assessment, SCC-like clause, regulatory approval, or internal cross-border transfer assessment reference; enter 'Not applicable' if no cross-border transfer. |
| Processor Agreement / DPA Reference | Enter the contract, data processing agreement, or vendor privacy schedule reference governing processor obligations; enter 'Not applicable' if no processor. |
| Access Roles / User Groups | List the roles, teams, or user groups with access to the data and whether access is read-only, edit, admin, export, or privileged. |
| Security Controls Applied | List key technical and organisational controls, e.g. RBAC, MFA, logging, segregation of duties, masking, backup, secure disposal, vendor security review. |
| Encryption Applied | Select one value: At rest, In transit, At rest and in transit, Tokenised/hashed, Not encrypted, Unknown; add brief details if needed. |
| Retention Period | Enter the approved retention period in months or years, e.g. 7 years, 24 months, Until contract termination plus 5 years. |
| Retention Trigger | Enter the event that starts the retention clock, e.g. account closure, employment termination, transaction date, consent withdrawal, case closure. |
| Disposal / Deletion Method | Describe how the data is securely deleted, anonymised, archived, or destroyed at end of retention, including system automation or manual process. |
| Data Subject Rights Handling Process | Describe how access, correction, deletion, destruction, withdrawal of consent, and other PDPL rights requests are routed and fulfilled for this processing activity. |
| Accuracy / Update Mechanism | State how the organisation keeps the data accurate and up to date, e.g. self-service portal, periodic verification, integration with source of truth. |
| Data Quality Owner | Enter the role or team responsible for ensuring accuracy and completeness of the personal data in this activity. |
| Risk Assessment / DPIA Required | Select Yes, No, or To be assessed, based on sensitivity, scale, new technology, profiling, vulnerable individuals, or cross-border transfer risk. |
| Risk Assessment / DPIA Reference | Enter the risk assessment, privacy impact assessment, DPIA, or transfer impact assessment reference number or link; enter 'Not applicable' if not required. |
| Known PDPL Compliance Gaps | Record any known gaps such as missing notice, unclear lawful basis, excessive retention, missing DPA, unapproved transfer, or enter 'None'. |
| Remediation Action Owner | Enter the person or role accountable for closing any compliance gaps; enter 'Not applicable' if no gaps. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the due date for closing compliance gaps in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter 'Not applicable' if no gaps. |
| Processing Status | Select one value: Planned, Active, Suspended, Retired, Under Remediation. |
| Last Reviewed Date | Enter the most recent review date of this register entry in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Evidence / Document Links | Provide links or references to supporting evidence, e.g. data flow diagram, contract, DPA, privacy notice, consent log, system screenshot, retention schedule. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Data Protection Officer or Privacy Office with accountable input from each business process owner and system owner; updated before any new or materially changed processing, vendor, system, data category, retention period, or cross-border transfer, and reviewed at least quarterly. Source inputs should be drawn from the CMDB/application inventory, vendor register, contract repository, consent management platform, records retention schedule, access management system, privacy rights workflow, and data discovery/classification tools.

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._
