Data Retention Schedule; DSAR Procedure; Breach Response Procedure] | [EXAMPLE: ExampleCRM Cloud Platform] | [EXAMPLE: KSA cloud region database] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-15] | [EXAMPLE: 2027-01-15] | [EXAMPLE: Draft] | [EXAMPLE: Privacy Officer] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: Confirm retention period with Legal by 2026-02-01.] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| RoPA Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this processing activity, using a consistent format such as ROPA-YYYY-###. |
| Processing Activity Name | Enter the clear business name of the processing activity, e.g. employee payroll, customer onboarding, CCTV monitoring. |
| Business Owner / Department | Enter the accountable business function and named owner responsible for the processing activity, e.g. HR - Payroll Manager. |
| Controller Entity | Enter the legal entity determining the purpose and means of processing, including full registered name and country. |
| Processor / Joint Controller Involved | Enter any processor, sub-processor, or joint controller involved; if none, enter 'None'. |
| Role of Organisation | Select one allowed value: Controller, Processor, Joint Controller, Controller and Processor. |
| Processing Description | Briefly describe what personal data is collected, used, stored, disclosed, transferred, or deleted in this activity. |
| Processing Purpose(s) | Enter the specific, lawful, and explicit purpose(s) for processing; avoid vague terms such as 'business purposes'. |
| PDPL Legal Basis / Permitted Ground | Enter the PDPL basis or permitted ground relied upon, such as Consent, Contractual necessity, Legal obligation, Vital interest, Legitimate interest where permitted, Public interest, or Other PDPL-permitted basis; include article/control reference if known. |
| Data Subject Category(ies) | List the categories of individuals whose data is processed, e.g. employees, job applicants, customers, website users, suppliers, patients. |
| Personal Data Category(ies) | List the categories of personal data processed, e.g. name, national ID/Iqama, contact details, financial data, employment data, location data, device identifiers. |
| Sensitive Personal Data Involved | Select Yes or No based on whether sensitive personal data is processed. |
| Sensitive Data Category | If sensitive data is involved, list the category, e.g. health, genetic, biometric, religious belief, credit data, criminal/security data; otherwise enter 'N/A'. |
| Children / Minors Data Involved | Select Yes, No, or Unknown, based on whether the activity involves personal data of children or minors. |
| Source of Personal Data | Enter where the data originates, e.g. directly from data subject, employer records, government platform, third party vendor, public source. |
| Collection Method / Channel | Enter the collection channel, e.g. web form, mobile app, paper form, API, email, call recording, CCTV, HR system. |
| Notice / Privacy Information Provided | Enter where and how the privacy notice is provided to the data subject, including link, form reference, or script reference; if not provided, enter gap/action needed. |
| Data Subject Consent Required | Select Yes, No, or Not Applicable, based on whether consent is required for this processing purpose under PDPL. |
| Consent Capture Method / Record Location | If consent is required, enter how consent is captured and where the evidence is stored, e.g. CRM consent log, signed form, app timestamp; otherwise enter 'N/A'. |
| Recipients / Disclosure Parties | List internal or external recipients to whom personal data is disclosed, including processors, affiliates, authorities, service providers, or third parties. |
| Recipient Location | Enter the country or region where each recipient is located; use 'Saudi Arabia' where local only. |
| Cross-Border Transfer Involved | Select Yes or No based on whether personal data is transferred, accessed, hosted, or disclosed outside Saudi Arabia. |
| Cross-Border Transfer Country(ies) | If cross-border transfer is involved, list destination country/countries; otherwise enter 'N/A'. |
| Cross-Border Transfer Mechanism / Exception | If transfer is involved, enter the PDPL-compliant transfer basis, safeguard, exception, approval, or mechanism relied upon; otherwise enter 'N/A'. |
| Transfer Risk / SDAIA Requirement Status | Enter status of any required transfer assessment, approval, safeguard, or SDAIA-related requirement using allowed values: Not Required, Required - Not Started, In Progress, Approved, Rejected, Expired, Unknown. |
| Processor Contract / Data Processing Terms in Place | Select Yes, No, In Progress, or Not Applicable; record whether written processor/data processing terms are in place covering PDPL obligations. |
| Retention Period | Enter the retention duration for the personal data, using a defined period such as '7 years', '1 year after account closure', or 'until consent withdrawal plus 30 days'; do not enter 'indefinite'. |
| Retention Trigger / Start Point | Enter the event from which retention is calculated, e.g. contract end date, employee termination date, transaction date, case closure date. |
| Disposal / Deletion Method | Enter the approved disposal method, e.g. secure deletion, anonymisation, cryptographic erasure, physical shredding, backup expiry cycle. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Privacy Officer/Data Protection Lead with accountable input from business process owners, Legal, Information Security, and IT application owners. Update at onboarding of any new processing activity, material change, new vendor/transfer, incident or regulatory change, and review at least annually using inputs from the data inventory, application register, vendor register, consent platform, retention schedule, DPIA log, and data subject rights workflow.

CIS-001.title: Implementation Group (IG1/IG2/IG3) Determination
CIS-001.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-CIS-IG-001] | 1.0 | [Chief Information Security Officer] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | CIS Controls v8 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes the mandatory requirements for determining, approving, documenting, and maintaining the organisation’s CIS Controls v8 Implementation Group designation: IG1, IG2, or IG3.

The Implementation Group designation shall be used to define the minimum required cybersecurity safeguard baseline for the organisation based on:

- The sensitivity, criticality, and regulatory exposure of the data the organisation processes, stores, or transmits.
- The scale and complexity of the technology environment.
- The organisation’s threat exposure and operational risk profile.
- The resources, capabilities, and maturity available to implement and sustain safeguards.

This Policy ensures that the organisation applies a cybersecurity baseline that is proportionate to risk, defensible to auditors and stakeholders, and practical to implement.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All business units, subsidiaries, departments, and functions within the organisation.
- All information systems, cloud services, networks, applications, endpoints, operational technology, and third-party hosted environments used to process, store, or transmit organisational data.
- All data types owned, managed, processed, or protected by the organisation, including public, internal, confidential, regulated, sensitive, and mission-critical data.
- All personnel, contractors, service providers, and third parties responsible for governance, risk management, information security, technology management, compliance, data ownership, or control implementation.
- Initial Implementation Group determination, periodic reassessment, reassessment following material change, and approval of any Implementation Group exceptions.

This Policy does not prescribe detailed technical implementation procedures for each safeguard. Those requirements shall be addressed in supporting standards, procedures, implementation plans, risk treatment plans, and control evidence records.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain a formally approved CIS Controls v8 Implementation Group designation as the minimum cybersecurity safeguard baseline for the in-scope environment.

2. The organisation shall determine its Implementation Group using a documented assessment of data sensitivity, business criticality, threat exposure, technology complexity, compliance obligations, and available implementation resources.

3. The organisation shall not select an Implementation Group based solely on convenience, budget preference, tool availability, or current control maturity.

4. The organisation shall assign one of the following Implementation Group designations:

 | Implementation Group | Required Use |
 |---|---|
 | IG1 | May be used where the organisation has limited cybersecurity resources, relatively low data sensitivity, limited technology complexity, and no material processing of regulated or highly sensitive data. |
 | IG2 | Shall be used where the organisation processes sensitive business data, supports important business services, has moderate technology complexity, uses cloud or third-party service environments, or has meaningful regulatory, contractual, or customer security expectations. |
 | IG3 | Shall be used where the organisation processes highly sensitive, regulated, mission-critical, or high-value data; operates complex or distributed environments; faces elevated threat exposure; provides critical services; or would experience severe business, legal, safety, financial, or reputational harm from a cybersecurity incident. |

5. The organisation shall treat IG1 as the minimum acceptable baseline only where a documented risk assessment confirms that higher Implementation Group safeguards are not required for the organisation’s risk profile.

6. The organisation shall adopt IG2 as the default baseline where the organisation’s risk profile is uncertain, where data sensitivity is mixed, or where the environment includes both low-risk and moderate-risk systems.

7. The organisation shall adopt IG3 where any of the following conditions apply:

 - The organisation processes large volumes of confidential, regulated, financial, health, government, customer, authentication, intellectual property, or commercially sensitive data.
 - A cybersecurity incident could materially affect life, safety, essential services, legal standing, market confidence, or business continuity.
 - The organisation is a likely target for advanced, persistent, organised, or sector-specific threat actors.
 - The organisation operates critical infrastructure, high-availability platforms, public-facing transactional services, or environments requiring strong assurance.
 - Contractual, insurance, customer, regulatory, or board expectations require a high level of cybersecurity maturity.
 - The organisation has sufficient security, technology, governance, and operational capability to implement and sustain the higher baseline.

8. The organisation shall document the rationale for its Implementation Group determination in an approved assessment record.

9. The Implementation Group determination shall include, at minimum, assessment of the following factors:

 | Assessment Factor | Required Considerations |
 |---|---|
 | Data sensitivity | Classification of data, regulated data, confidential business data, personal data, financial data, intellectual property, authentication data, and customer data. |
 | Business criticality | Importance of systems and data to revenue, operations, customer delivery, safety, legal obligations, and continuity of service. |
 | Threat exposure | Internet exposure, remote access, sector targeting, geopolitical exposure, fraud risk, ransomware exposure, and history of security events. |
 | Technology complexity | Number of users, locations, systems, networks, cloud platforms, third-party integrations, privileged accounts, and externally accessible services. |
 | Legal and contractual obligations | Customer requirements, regulatory expectations, cyber insurance conditions, supplier obligations, and contractual security commitments. |
 | Security resources | Personnel, budget, tools, governance capacity, operational maturity, monitoring capability, and ability to maintain safeguards. |
 | Impact of compromise | Potential financial, operational, legal, safety, privacy, customer, and reputational harm. |
 | Existing control maturity | Current safeguard coverage, known gaps, compensating measures, and remediation capacity. |

10. The organisation shall use the following decision criteria when determining the Implementation Group:

 | Criterion | IG1 Indicator | IG2 Indicator | IG3 Indicator |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Data sensitivity | Mostly public or internal operational data | Confidential, customer, financial, or sensitive business data | Highly sensitive, regulated, mission-critical, or high-value data |
 | Business impact | Limited disruption if systems are unavailable or compromised | Material disruption to operations, customers, or obligations | Severe disruption, safety concern, major loss, or public impact |
 | Environment size and complexity | Small, simple, mostly standard technology environment | Moderate environment with cloud, third parties, multiple systems, or distributed users | Large, complex, highly integrated, high-availability, or multi-region environment |
 | Threat profile | Opportunistic threats expected | Moderate targeting or meaningful exposure | Advanced, targeted, persistent, or sector-specific threats likely |
 | Compliance and customer expectations | Limited formal obligations | Defined regulatory, customer, insurance, or contractual expectations | Strong assurance obligations or high external scrutiny |
 | Security capability | Limited staff and tools | Defined security ownership and moderate capability | Mature security governance, tooling, monitoring, and response capability |

11. The organisation shall select the highest Implementation Group indicated by the assessment where criteria point to different Implementation Groups, unless a documented risk-based justification is approved by the designated authority.

12. The organisation shall not reduce the Implementation Group designation without a documented risk assessment, evidence supporting the reduction, and formal approval by the designated authority.

13. The organisation shall identify whether the Implementation Group designation applies to the entire organisation or to defined segments, business units, systems, or environments.

14. Where different parts of the organisation have materially different risk profiles, the organisation may assign different Implementation Groups to different scoped environments, provided that segmentation, ownership, boundaries, and applicability are clearly documented.

15. Where multiple Implementation Groups apply across the organisation, shared services shall meet the highest Implementation Group required by any dependent environment unless an approved exception or alternative architecture is documented.

16. Systems that process or provide access to data from a higher Implementation Group environment shall be treated as part of that higher Implementation Group unless effective segregation and access controls are in place.

17. The approved Implementation Group shall establish the minimum required safeguard baseline; business owners, system owners, and risk owners may require additional safeguards where risk warrants stronger protection.

18. The organisation shall maintain a mapping between the approved Implementation Group and the safeguards selected for implementation, including ownership, status, evidence location, and target completion dates.

19. The organisation shall establish an implementation plan for any safeguards required by the approved Implementation Group that are not yet implemented or not operating effectively.

20. The implementation plan shall prioritise safeguards based on risk, dependency, feasibility, and protection of the most sensitive and critical assets.

21. The organisation shall ensure that resource constraints are documented as implementation risks and managed through risk treatment, phased delivery, compensating controls, or approved exceptions.

22. The organisation shall not use lack of resources as the sole justification for permanently excluding safeguards required by the approved Implementation Group.

23. The organisation shall ensure that the Implementation Group determination is reviewed during annual cybersecurity planning, risk assessment, budgeting, and control assurance activities.

24. The organisation shall reassess its Implementation Group following any material change, including:

 - Acquisition, merger, divestment, or significant restructuring.
 - Introduction of new regulated data, sensitive data, or high-value business processes.
 - Significant cloud migration or technology transformation.
 - Material expansion in users, locations, systems, customers, or jurisdictions.
 - Major cybersecurity incident or material audit finding.
 - New contractual, insurance, customer, or legal security obligation.
 - Change in threat exposure or sector risk.
 - Significant change in available security resources or operational capability.

25. The organisation shall retain evidence of Implementation Group determination, approval, reassessment, implementation planning, exceptions, and management review.

26. The Implementation Group determination shall be approved before it is used to define control scope, security budgets, audit readiness activities, or risk treatment commitments.

27. The organisation shall communicate the approved Implementation Group and related baseline requirements to relevant stakeholders, including technology, security, risk, compliance, procurement, project delivery, and business leadership teams.

28. The organisation shall ensure that new systems, services, projects, and third-party arrangements align with the applicable Implementation Group before production use or formal acceptance.

29. Third-party services that process, store, transmit, or provide privileged access to organisational data shall be assessed against the applicable Implementation Group expectations or equivalent security outcomes.

30. The organisation shall maintain a record of the current Implementation Group designation using the following minimum data fields:

 | Field | Required Content |
 |---|---|
 | Assessment name | Name of the Implementation Group assessment. |
 | Assessment date | Date the assessment was completed. |
 | Scope | Organisation, business unit, system, service, or environment covered. |
 | Data classification | Highest classification of data in scope. |
 | Business criticality | Summary of operational importance and impact of compromise. |
 | Threat exposure | Summary of relevant threat conditions. |
 | Technology complexity | Summary of environment size and complexity. |
 | Resource assessment | Summary of security and technology resources available. |
 | Recommended Implementation Group | IG1, IG2, or IG3. |
 | Approved Implementation Group | IG1, IG2, or IG3. |
 | Rationale | Business and risk-based justification. |
 | Required actions | Key remediation, implementation, or governance actions. |
 | Approver | Name and role of approving authority. |
 | Approval date | Date of approval. |
 | Next review date | Date by which reassessment is required. |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board or Executive Leadership | Provides oversight of cybersecurity risk posture, endorses the organisation’s risk appetite, and ensures appropriate resources are available to meet the approved Implementation Group baseline. |
| Chief Information Security Officer | Owns this Policy, leads the Implementation Group determination process, recommends the appropriate designation, ensures alignment with cybersecurity strategy, and reports status to leadership. |
| Chief Information Officer or Technology Leader | Provides information about technology scope, complexity, architecture, platforms, operational constraints, and resource requirements for implementation. |
| Risk Management Function | Supports risk assessment, validates risk rationale, ensures alignment with enterprise risk management practices, and tracks accepted risks related to Implementation Group decisions. |
| Compliance or Legal Function | Identifies relevant legal, regulatory, contractual, privacy, insurance, and customer obligations that influence the Implementation Group determination. |
| Data Owners | Identify data sensitivity, classification, business value, regulatory relevance, and potential impact of compromise for data within their responsibility. |
| Business Owners | Define business criticality, service impact, operational dependencies, customer commitments, and acceptable risk levels for systems and processes. |
| System Owners | Provide system inventory, architecture, dependency, access, exposure, and control maturity information needed for assessment and implementation planning. |
| Security Operations | Provides threat, vulnerability, incident, monitoring, detection, and response information relevant to determining threat exposure and implementation capability. |
| Internal Audit or Independent Assurance | Reviews the design and operating effectiveness of the Implementation Group determination process and validates evidence where included in the audit plan. |
| Project and Change Owners | Ensure new initiatives, systems, and material changes are assessed against the applicable Implementation Group before go-live or acceptance. |
| Procurement and Third-Party Risk Management | Ensures suppliers and service providers meet applicable safeguard expectations or equivalent security outcomes for the Implementation Group in scope. |
| All Personnel | Support accurate information gathering, comply with approved security requirements, and escalate known changes that may affect the Implementation Group determination. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through governance reviews, risk assessments, control assurance activities, project reviews, third-party assessments, and internal audit activities where applicable.

At minimum, the following monitoring activities shall be performed:

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review approved Implementation Group designation | Annually | [Chief Information Security Officer] | Approved assessment record and review minutes |
| Validate data sensitivity and business criticality inputs | Annually or upon material change | Data Owners and Business Owners | Data classification records and business impact analysis |
| Review safeguard implementation status against approved Implementation Group | Quarterly | Security Governance Function | Control status dashboard and remediation plan |
| Review exceptions related to Implementation Group requirements | Quarterly | Risk Management Function | Exception register and risk acceptance records |
| Validate new projects and material changes against applicable Implementation Group | Before approval or go-live | Project Owner and Security Architecture Function | Security review record |
| Report implementation progress and material risks to leadership | Quarterly | [Chief Information Security Officer] | Management report |
| Independent review of determination process | As scheduled in audit plan | Internal Audit or Independent Assurance | Audit report or assurance memo |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in one or more of the following actions:

- Required remediation within an approved timeframe.
- Escalation to business, technology, risk, or executive leadership.
- Formal risk acceptance by an authorised risk owner.
- Suspension or delay of system go-live, service onboarding, project approval, or supplier engagement.
- Additional monitoring, compensating controls, or targeted assurance.
- Disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policies and applicable employment agreements.
- Contractual remedies for supplier non-compliance, where applicable.

Material non-compliance shall be documented, risk assessed, assigned an accountable owner, and tracked to closure.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business need, a completed risk assessment, and formal approval by the appropriate authority.

Exceptions may include:

- Temporary deferral of a safeguard required by the approved Implementation Group.
- Use of a compensating control that achieves an equivalent security outcome.
- Scoped application of a lower Implementation Group to a defined environment.
- Temporary operation of a system that does not yet meet the applicable Implementation Group baseline.
- Acceptance of supplier security capability that does not fully align with the applicable baseline but is supported by equivalent controls or risk treatment.

Exception requests shall include, at minimum:

| Field | Required Content |
|---|---|
| Exception request ID | Unique identifier for the exception. |
| Requestor | Name, role, and business unit of the requestor. |
| Scope | System, service, business process, supplier, or environment affected. |
| Policy requirement affected | Description of the requirement that cannot be met. |
| Business justification | Explanation of why the exception is needed. |
| Risk assessment | Confidentiality, integrity, availability, legal, operational, financial, and reputational risk impact. |
| Compensating controls | Existing or proposed measures that reduce risk. |
| Duration | Requested start date and expiry date. |
| Remediation plan | Actions, owners, milestones, and target completion date. |
| Risk owner | Person accountable for accepting the residual risk. |
| Approval authority | Person or committee authorised to approve the exception. |
| Review frequency | Frequency for reassessing the exception while active. |

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed [maximum exception period, e.g., 12 months] without renewed assessment and approval.

Permanent exceptions shall not be granted where they would undermine the integrity of the approved Implementation Group baseline. Where a long-term deviation is unavoidable, the organisation shall reassess the Implementation Group scope, document the residual risk, and obtain executive-level approval.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed or remediated before expiry.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever a material change occurs that could affect the organisation’s Implementation Group determination or cybersecurity baseline.

The review shall consider:

- Changes in business strategy, products, services, or operating model.
- Changes in data sensitivity, data volume, data locations, or regulatory exposure.
- Significant changes to technology architecture, cloud usage, third-party reliance, or system interconnectivity.
- Changes in threat landscape, incident trends, vulnerability exposure, or sector risk.
- Results from audits, assessments, risk reviews, penetration tests, incidents, and control monitoring.
- Changes in available cybersecurity resources, tools, staffing, and operational maturity.
- Progress against safeguard implementation plans and remediation commitments.
- Approved exceptions and recurring non-compliance.
- Feedback from business, technology, risk, compliance, and assurance stakeholders.

The Policy Owner shall be responsible for maintaining this Policy, coordinating stakeholder review, obtaining approval for material updates, and ensuring the current approved version is available to relevant personnel.

Superseded versions of this Policy and related Implementation Group determination records shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.

At minimum, the following maintenance records shall be retained:

| Record | Minimum Retention |
|---|---:|
| Approved Implementation Group assessment records | [Retention period, e.g., 7 years] |
| Implementation Group approval records | [Retention period, e.g., 7 years] |
| Annual review evidence | [Retention period, e.g., 7 years] |
| Material change reassessments | [Retention period, e.g., 7 years] |
| Exception requests and approvals | [Retention period, e.g., 7 years] |
| Implementation plans and remediation tracking | [Retention period, e.g., 7 years] |
| Management reporting and meeting minutes | [Retention period, e.g., 7 years] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Assessment ID | Enter a unique identifier for this self-assessment or gap report, e.g. CISV8-SA-YYYY-###. |
| Assessment Period | Enter the period covered by the assessment in format YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD. |
| Assessment Date | Enter the date the safeguard was assessed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Assessor Name | Enter the full name of the person performing or recording the assessment. |
| Assessor Role/Team | Enter the assessor’s role, department, or team, e.g. GRC Analyst, Security Operations, IT Infrastructure. |
| Business Unit/Scope | Enter the business unit, legal entity, site, service, or organisational scope assessed. |
| In-Scope Environment | Enter the environment assessed, e.g. Enterprise, Corporate IT, Cloud, SaaS, OT, Production, Development, Endpoints, Network. |
| CIS Control Number | Enter the CIS Controls v8 control number from 1 to 18. |
| CIS Control Name | Enter the official CIS Controls v8 control name, e.g. Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets. |
| CIS Safeguard Number | Enter the CIS Controls v8 safeguard reference in format x.y, e.g. 1.1, 5.4, 18.5. |
| CIS Safeguard Title | Enter the official CIS Controls v8 safeguard title. |
| Implementation Group Applicability | Enter the CIS Implementation Group applicability for the safeguard: IG1, IG2, IG3, IG1/IG2/IG3, IG2/IG3, or IG3 only. |
| Safeguard Requirement Summary | Summarise what the safeguard requires the organisation to implement, using concise requirement language. |
| Control Owner | Enter the accountable owner for the CIS control or safeguard, normally a role or named owner such as CISO, IT Operations Manager, IAM Lead. |
| Process Owner | Enter the owner of the business or IT process that performs the control activity. |
| Technology/System Owner | Enter the owner of the system, platform, tooling, or repository used to operate or evidence the safeguard. |
| Applicable to Organisation | Enter Yes, No, or Partially to indicate whether the safeguard applies to the assessed organisation/scope. |
| Applicability Rationale | If not fully applicable, explain why; reference business model, technology scope, outsourcing, regulatory scope, or absence of relevant assets. |
| Current Implementation Status | Enter one allowed value: Implemented, Partially Implemented, Not Implemented, Not Applicable, Planned, Unknown. |
| Implementation Coverage % | Enter the estimated percentage of applicable assets, users, systems, or processes covered by the safeguard as a whole number from 0 to 100. |
| Implementation Maturity | Enter one allowed value: Ad Hoc, Repeatable, Defined, Managed, Optimised, or Not Applicable. |
| CSAT/Assessment Score | Enter the score from CIS CSAT or equivalent assessment method, using the organisation’s scoring convention, e.g. 0-100, 0-5, or Pass/Partial/Fail. |
| Assessment Method | Enter how the status was determined: Interview, Document Review, Technical Testing, Tool Export, Observation, Sampling, CSAT Entry, or Combination. |
| Evidence Available | Enter Yes, No, or Partial to indicate whether sufficient evidence exists to support the assessment conclusion. |
| Evidence Reference/Link | Enter the document ID, ticket number, repository path, URL, screenshot reference, report name, or system export reference supporting the assessment. |
| Evidence Date | Enter the date of the evidence reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format, or leave blank if no evidence is available. |
| Evidence Owner | Enter the person, team, or system owner responsible for maintaining the evidence. |
| Observed Current State | Describe the current implemented process, configuration, tooling, or operating practice observed during the assessment. |
| Gap Description | Describe the specific gap between the CIS safeguard requirement and the current state; use 'No gap identified' where fully implemented. |
| Gap Root Cause | Enter the primary cause of the gap, e.g. No assigned owner, Tool limitation, Process not defined, Incomplete rollout, Lack of monitoring, Resource constraint, Legacy system. |
| Risk Statement | State the risk created by the gap in cause-event-impact format, e.g. 'If inactive accounts are not removed, unauthorised access may occur, leading to data exposure.' |
| Risk Rating | Enter the inherent/current risk rating using allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational, or Not Applicable. |
| Likelihood | Enter the assessed likelihood using allowed values: Very High, High, Medium, Low, Very Low, or Not Applicable. |
| Impact | Enter the assessed impact using allowed values: Very High, High, Medium, Low, Very Low, or Not Applicable. |
| Affected Assets/Processes | List the asset classes, systems, applications, data types, users, locations, or processes affected by the gap. |
| Related Policies/Standards | Reference any internal policies, standards, or external requirements related to the safeguard, using document names or IDs. |
| Related Procedures/Runbooks | Reference operational procedures, work instructions, playbooks, or runbooks used to perform the safeguard. |
| Related Tools/Systems | List the tools, platforms, repositories, or systems used to implement or monitor the safeguard, e.g. CMDB, EDR, SIEM, IAM, vulnerability scanner. |
| Dependencies/Prerequisites | Record dependencies required before remediation can be completed, e.g. asset inventory completion, budget approval, tool deployment, vendor action. |
| Recommended Remediation Action | Enter the specific action required to close the gap, written as an actionable task or set of tasks. |
| Remediation Type | Enter one allowed value: Policy/Standard, Process, Technical Configuration, Tooling, Training, Monitoring, Third-Party, Documentation, Governance. |
| Remediation Priority | Enter one allowed value: P1 Critical, P2 High, P3 Medium, P4 Low, or Backlog. |
| Target Implementation Date | Enter the planned completion date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the named person, role, or team accountable for completing the remediation. |
| Estimated Effort | Enter estimated effort using a consistent unit, e.g. hours, person-days, or T-shirt sizing XS/S/M/L/XL. |
| Estimated Cost | Enter estimated cost and currency, e.g. USD 5000, GBP 12000, EUR 0, or Unknown. |
| Compensating Control Exists | Enter Yes, No, or Partial to indicate whether another control reduces the risk while the safeguard is not fully implemented. |
| Compensating Control Description | Describe the compensating control and how it reduces the risk; leave blank if none exists. |
| Residual Risk After Remediation | Enter expected residual risk after remediation using allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational, or Not Applicable. |
| Exception/Waiver Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether management acceptance or a formal exception is required for any remaining gap. |
| Exception/Waiver Reference | Enter the approved exception, waiver, risk acceptance, or governance ticket reference; leave blank if not applicable. |
| Management Response | Enter management’s response to the gap, e.g. Accept, Remediate, Transfer, Avoid, Defer, or Not Applicable, with brief context if needed. |
| Management Approval | Enter the approving manager, committee, or risk authority for the response or exception. |
| Approval Date | Enter the date management approved the response or exception in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Remediation Status | Enter one allowed value: Not Started, In Progress, Blocked, Completed, Deferred, Accepted Risk, Not Applicable. |
| Completion Date | Enter the actual remediation completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or leave blank until completed. |
| Validation/Test Performed | Describe the validation activity used to confirm implementation, e.g. configuration review, sample test, report export, walkthrough, technical scan. |
| Validation Result | Enter one allowed value: Pass, Partial Pass, Fail, Not Tested, Not Applicable. |
| Validator Name | Enter the name of the person who independently validated remediation or assessment conclusion. |
| Validation Date | Enter the date validation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date for this safeguard in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Comments/Notes | Enter any additional context, assumptions, limitations, sampling notes, or cross-references relevant to the assessment. |

### Maintenance

The template is owned by the GRC or Security Assurance function, with input from control owners across IT, Security Operations, IAM, Infrastructure, Cloud, Legal, HR, Procurement, and Business Continuity. It should be updated at least quarterly and after major technology or organisational changes, drawing from CIS CSAT or equivalent assessment tooling, CMDB/asset inventory, vulnerability management platform, IAM, SIEM, ticketing system, policy repository, risk register, and evidence repositories.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Asset Inventory ID | Enter the unique internal inventory identifier for this asset; use a consistent format such as AST-000001. |
| Asset Name / Hostname | Enter the configured hostname, device name, or asset label exactly as detected or assigned. |
| Asset Type | Select the hardware category; allowed values: Server, Workstation, Laptop, Mobile Device, Network Device, Printer, IoT/OT Device, Virtual Host, Hypervisor, Storage Device, Security Appliance, Other. |
| Hardware Manufacturer | Enter the manufacturer or vendor name, such as Dell, HP, Cisco, Apple, Lenovo, VMware, or Unknown if not yet identified. |
| Hardware Model | Enter the hardware model, appliance model, or virtual hardware type; enter Unknown if not yet identified. |
| Serial Number / Service Tag | Enter the serial number, service tag, asset tag, IMEI, or equivalent manufacturer identifier; enter N/A only where no such identifier exists. |
| Unique Device Identifier | Enter any additional unique device identifier such as UUID, cloud instance ID, hypervisor VM ID, EDR device ID, or MDM device ID. |
| MAC Address(es) | Enter one or more MAC addresses in colon-separated format, for example AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF; separate multiple values with semicolons. |
| IP Address(es) | Enter the current or most recently observed IPv4/IPv6 address(es); separate multiple values with semicolons. |
| Network Segment / VLAN | Enter the network segment, subnet, VLAN ID/name, wireless SSID, cloud VPC/subnet, or equivalent location where the asset was observed. |
| Physical / Logical Location | Enter the site, building, room, data centre, cloud region, remote user assignment, or other location relevant to locating the asset. |
| Asset Owner | Enter the accountable business or technical owner by name, role, or team; do not leave blank for authorized assets. |
| Business Unit | Enter the department, business unit, subsidiary, or service area that owns or uses the asset. |
| Custodian / Support Team | Enter the IT, security, operations, facilities, or managed service team responsible for day-to-day support of the asset. |
| Authorization Status | Select the current approval state; allowed values: Authorized, Unauthorized, Unknown, Pending Approval, Retired. |
| Asset Lifecycle Status | Select the lifecycle state; allowed values: In Service, Build, Staging, Quarantined, Lost, Retired, Disposed, Decommissioning. |
| Approved Use / Business Purpose | Enter the approved purpose or service supported by the asset, such as Finance laptop, domain controller, branch router, CCTV camera, or test server. |
| Criticality | Select the business criticality of the asset; allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Unknown. |
| Data Sensitivity | Select the highest data classification processed, stored, or transmitted by the asset; allowed values: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, Regulated, Unknown. |
| Operating System / Firmware | Enter the operating system, appliance OS, mobile OS, hypervisor, or firmware family, such as Windows, Ubuntu, iOS, Cisco IOS, FortiOS, ESXi, or Unknown. |
| OS / Firmware Version | Enter the specific OS, build, firmware, or image version where known; use vendor version format. |
| Discovery Method | Select how the asset was identified; allowed values: Active Discovery, Passive Discovery, DHCP Log, CMDB Import, EDR/Agent, MDM, Manual Entry, Cloud Inventory, Network Authentication, Other. |
| Discovery Source System | Enter the tool, platform, or log source that provided the record, such as vulnerability scanner, NAC, DHCP server, SIEM, CMDB, EDR, MDM, cloud console, or passive sensor. |
| First Discovered Date | Enter the date the asset was first observed or added to inventory in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Seen Date | Enter the most recent date the asset was observed by discovery tooling, DHCP logs, passive monitoring, agent check-in, or manual validation in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Inventory Validation Date | Enter the date this inventory record was last reviewed and confirmed accurate in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| DHCP Scope / Server | Enter the DHCP server, scope, pool, or relay source that issued or logged the lease; enter N/A for assets not using DHCP. |
| DHCP Lease Start | Enter the DHCP lease start timestamp in ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, or N/A if not applicable. |
| DHCP Lease End | Enter the DHCP lease end or expiry timestamp in ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, or N/A if not applicable. |
| DHCP Hostname | Enter the hostname recorded in the DHCP lease log; enter N/A if not applicable or not recorded. |
| Passive Discovery Evidence | Enter the passive discovery reference, sensor name, alert ID, SIEM event ID, packet metadata reference, or N/A if not applicable. |
| Active Discovery Evidence | Enter the active scan job ID, scan date, discovery tool record link, scanner result reference, or N/A if not applicable. |
| Unauthorized / Unknown Asset Action | For Unauthorized or Unknown assets, enter the required response such as Investigate, Approve, Quarantine, Remove, Block, Reimage, or Transfer to Owner; enter N/A for Authorized assets. |
| Action Owner | Enter the person or team responsible for completing the remediation or investigation action; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Action Due Date | Enter the due date for the action in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Action Status | Select the current action state; allowed values: N/A, Open, In Progress, Blocked, Completed, Overdue. |
| Exception / Risk Acceptance ID | Enter the approved exception, waiver, or risk acceptance reference if the asset remains outside normal requirements; enter N/A if none. |
| Related CMDB / Asset Record ID | Enter the linked CMDB, procurement, finance, EDR, MDM, or asset management system record ID where applicable. |
| Notes | Enter concise additional information needed to understand the record, investigation, or reconciliation status; avoid sensitive credentials or secrets. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the IT Asset Management owner with Security Operations and Network Operations as contributors; update continuously from discovery sources and formally reconcile at least weekly, with unauthorized or unknown assets reviewed daily. Source systems should include CMDB/ITAM, active discovery or vulnerability scanners, passive discovery/NAC tooling, DHCP lease logs, EDR/MDM, cloud inventory, and network authentication logs.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Software Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this software inventory record, using a consistent format such as SW-0001. |
| Software Name | Enter the official product/application name as shown by the vendor or software discovery tool. |
| Publisher / Vendor | Enter the legal publisher or vendor name responsible for the software. |
| Software Category | Enter the functional category, such as Operating System, Productivity, Security Tool, Browser, Development Tool, Database, Remote Access, Cloud Client, Utility, or Other. |
| Business Purpose | Describe the approved business use for the software in one concise sentence. |
| Authorised Status | Select one value: Authorised, Unauthorised, Pending Review, Prohibited, or Retired. |
| Authorisation Date | Enter the date the software was approved for use in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank only if not yet authorised. |
| Authorising Owner | Enter the role or named person who approved the software for organisational use. |
| Business Owner | Enter the business role or team accountable for the need and continued use of the software. |
| Technical Owner | Enter the IT, application, endpoint, or platform owner responsible for technical administration and lifecycle management. |
| Approved Version / Version Range | Enter the approved version, minimum version, or version range, such as 12.4.1, >= 12.4, or 12.x only. |
| Installed Version Detected | Enter the version detected on assets by the inventory/discovery tool; use Multiple if more than one version exists and list details in Notes or a supporting export. |
| Installation Scope | Select one value: Enterprise-wide, Department-specific, Role-specific, Asset-specific, Server-only, Workstation-only, or Other. |
| Approved Platforms / OS | Enter the operating systems or platforms on which the software is approved, such as Windows 11, macOS 14, Ubuntu 22.04, iOS, Android, or SaaS. |
| Approved Asset Groups | Enter the approved asset group, OU, device collection, business unit, or endpoint group where installation is permitted. |
| Licence Type | Select one value: Freeware, Open Source, Per Device, Per User, Subscription, Enterprise Agreement, OEM, Trial, SaaS, or Other. |
| Licence Entitlement / Count | Enter the authorised licence entitlement count or subscription quantity; enter N/A where not applicable. |
| Licence Expiry Date | Enter the licence or subscription expiry date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A for perpetual or non-licensed software. |
| Support Status | Select one value: Supported, Unsupported, End-of-Life, End-of-Support Pending, Unknown, or N/A. |
| Vendor Support End Date | Enter the vendor support or end-of-life date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Unknown if not confirmed. |
| Patch / Update Method | Enter how updates are applied, such as Auto-update, Central Patch Management, MDM, Manual, Vendor Console, Package Manager, or Not Patchable. |
| Latest Approved Patch Level | Enter the latest approved patch, build, release, or update level required by the organisation. |
| Discovery Source | Enter the system of record or tool where the software presence was identified, such as EDR, MDM, CMDB, SAM Tool, Vulnerability Scanner, Endpoint Management, or Manual Attestation. |
| Discovery Date | Enter the date this software record or detection was last obtained from the discovery source in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Number of Installations Detected | Enter the total number of detected installations across organisational assets as a whole number. |
| Unauthorised Installation Detected | Select Yes or No to indicate whether any installation exists outside the approved authorisation, version, asset group, or platform. |
| Unauthorised Installation Count | Enter the number of detected unauthorised installations as a whole number; enter 0 if none. |
| Blocking / Allowlisting Control | Enter the preventative or detective control used, such as Application Allowlisting, EDR Block Rule, MDM Restriction, Software Restriction Policy, Package Manager Control, CASB, or None. |
| Blocking Status | Select one value: Blocking Enforced, Monitoring Only, Not Enforced, Exception Approved, Not Applicable, or Unknown. |
| Exception Required | Select Yes or No to indicate whether continued use requires a formal exception. |
| Exception Reference | Enter the approved exception/ticket/risk acceptance reference; enter N/A if no exception applies. |
| Exception Expiry Date | Enter the exception expiry date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no exception applies. |
| Risk Rating | Select one value: Low, Medium, High, Critical, or Not Assessed, based on security, licensing, supportability, and business risk. |
| Remediation Action | Enter the required action, such as Approve, Remove, Upgrade, Patch, Block, Licence True-up, Investigate, or No Action Required. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the person, team, or role responsible for completing the remediation action. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the remediation due date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A where no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Status | Select one value: Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Overdue, Accepted Risk, or N/A. |
| Last Review Date | Enter the date this software record was last reviewed for accuracy, authorisation, licence, support, and blocking status in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| CIS Control Reference | Enter the applicable CIS Controls v8 safeguard reference, such as 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, or 2.5. |
| Notes | Enter any concise additional context, assumptions, links to evidence, or references to supporting tickets or exports. |

### Maintenance

The Software Asset Management Owner or IT Asset Manager owns this register, with Security Operations accountable for unauthorised software detection and blocking status. Update from automated software discovery sources such as endpoint management, EDR, MDM, CMDB/SAM tooling, vulnerability scanners, and application allowlisting platforms at least monthly and whenever new software is requested, approved, detected, blocked, retired, or excepted.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this inventory record, using a consistent format such as DI-0001. |
| Data Asset Name | Enter the business-recognised name of the dataset, repository, database, file store, application data store, or information asset. |
| Data Asset Description | Briefly describe what the data asset contains and its business use; do not enter actual sensitive data values. |
| Business Process / Purpose | Enter the business process, service, or operational purpose for which the data is collected, stored, processed, or transmitted. |
| Data Owner | Enter the accountable business owner role or named individual responsible for classification, handling decisions, retention, and access approval. |
| Data Custodian / System Owner | Enter the technical owner, platform owner, or system administrator responsible for operating and protecting the repository. |
| Business Unit | Enter the department, function, or legal entity that owns or primarily uses the data. |
| Data Category | Select the main category of data: Public, Internal Business, Confidential Business, Personal Data, Sensitive Personal Data, Financial, Authentication/Secrets, Intellectual Property, Regulated, Operational/Log Data, Other. |
| Data Elements Included | List the key types of data elements present, such as name, email, national ID, payment card data, health data, credentials, customer contracts, source code, or system logs. |
| Data Classification | Enter the approved classification label used by the organisation, such as Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, or Highly Restricted. |
| Sensitivity Rationale | Explain why the classification was assigned, referencing business impact, confidentiality risk, privacy impact, regulatory obligation, contractual requirement, or security risk. |
| Regulatory / Contractual Applicability | List applicable obligations such as GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, GLBA, CCPA/CPRA, contractual NDA, customer contract, data processing agreement, or enter None. |
| Primary System / Repository | Enter the authoritative system, application, database, SaaS platform, shared drive, object store, document management system, or data warehouse where the data resides. |
| Storage Location | Enter the logical or physical storage location, such as database name, share path, cloud bucket/container, SaaS workspace, data lake zone, or document library. |
| Hosting Model | Select one: On-premises, Private Cloud, Public Cloud, SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, Hybrid, Third Party Hosted. |
| Geographic Location / Jurisdiction | Enter the country, region, or legal jurisdiction where the data is stored or primarily processed, such as US, EU, UK, Canada, Global, or specific data centre region. |
| Data Format | Select one or more: Structured Database, Spreadsheet, Document, Email, Image/Scan, Log File, Backup, Source Code, Object Storage, SaaS Record, Other. |
| Source of Data | Enter where the data originates, such as customer input, employee record, third-party feed, system-generated log, API integration, manual upload, or migrated legacy data. |
| Data Subjects / Population | Enter whose data is represented, such as customers, employees, contractors, suppliers, patients, students, prospects, users, or Not Applicable. |
| Approximate Record Count | Enter an estimated number of records or data subjects as a whole number or range, such as 50000 or 10000-50000. |
| Access Groups / Roles | List the approved business or technical roles, directory groups, or application roles with access to the data; do not list passwords or secrets. |
| Privileged Access Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether administrative, elevated, service account, or privileged access is needed to manage or access the data. |
| External Sharing | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether data is shared outside the organisation, including vendors, regulators, customers, partners, processors, or cloud services. |
| Third Party / Recipient Name | If External Sharing is Yes, enter the recipient organisation or third-party service name; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Data Transfer Method | Enter how data is transmitted or shared, such as HTTPS, SFTP, API, VPN, email with encryption, managed file transfer, SaaS integration, physical media, or Not Applicable. |
| Encryption at Rest | Enter Yes, No, Partial, or Not Applicable; if Yes or Partial, include the encryption mechanism or service where known, such as AES-256, TDE, KMS, or platform-managed encryption. |
| Encryption in Transit | Enter Yes, No, Partial, or Not Applicable; if Yes or Partial, include the protocol where known, such as TLS 1.2+, HTTPS, SFTP, or VPN. |
| Handling Requirements | Enter required handling rules for this classification, such as approved storage only, no public sharing, encryption required, need-to-know access, masking/tokenisation, secure transfer only, or printing restricted. |
| Retention Period | Enter the required retention duration in years/months/days or enter Permanent if formally approved; examples of format: 7 years, 90 days, 18 months. |
| Retention Trigger | Enter the event that starts the retention clock, such as account closure, contract termination, employee termination, transaction date, consent withdrawal, record creation date, or legal hold release. |
| Disposal / Destruction Method | Enter the approved disposal method, such as secure deletion, cryptographic erasure, media sanitisation, shredding, anonymisation, purge job, vendor-certified destruction, or Not Applicable. |
| Backup Included | Enter Yes, No, or Unknown to indicate whether this data is included in backup, snapshot, archive, or disaster recovery copies. |
| Backup Location | If Backup Included is Yes, enter where backups are stored, such as backup platform name, cloud region, vault, tape storage, DR site, or SaaS backup provider; otherwise enter Not Applicable. |
| Logging / Monitoring Enabled | Enter Yes, No, Partial, or Unknown to indicate whether access, modification, export, deletion, or administrative activity is logged and monitored. |
| DLP / Data Protection Control Applied | Enter applicable protection controls, such as DLP policy, classification label, rights management, masking, tokenisation, CASB rule, database activity monitoring, access review, or None. |
| Last Reviewed Date | Enter the most recent date this inventory record was validated by the data owner, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the scheduled next review date in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on classification and organisational review frequency. |
| Lifecycle Status | Select one: Proposed, Active, In Migration, Archived, Pending Deletion, Retired. |
| Exceptions / Gaps | Record any known non-compliance, missing classification, unclear ownership, excessive access, absent encryption, unapproved sharing, retention gap, or enter None. |
| Related CIS Control 3 Safeguard | Enter the applicable CIS Controls v8 Control 3 safeguard reference, such as 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, or 3.14. |
| Evidence / Reference Link | Enter a link or reference to supporting evidence, such as system record, data flow diagram, access review, classification policy, retention schedule, vendor contract, or repository URL. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Data Governance Owner or Chief Data Officer, with each Data Owner responsible for validating their entries at least quarterly and whenever a new system, dataset, integration, classification change, retention change, or sharing arrangement is introduced. Source data should be drawn from the CMDB/application inventory, data discovery/classification tools, DLP/CASB platforms, IAM access groups, records of processing activities, retention schedule, vendor register, and system owner attestations.
