SOX-001.title: ITGC Scoping Memo
SOX-001.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [ITGC-SCOPE-MEMO-001] | 1.0 | [SOX Compliance Owner / IT Governance Owner] | [Effective Date] | SOX IT General Controls | Internal Confidential |

## Purpose

This policy establishes the mandatory requirements for defining, approving, maintaining, and evidencing the scope of IT General Controls supporting internal control over financial reporting.

The purpose of this ITGC Scoping Memo is to ensure that the organisation consistently identifies:

- Financially significant systems that process, store, transmit, or report financial data.
- Key reports, interfaces, and automated calculations used in financial reporting controls.
- Technology layers that support the reliability, integrity, availability, and restricted access of in-scope financial systems.
- Service providers, end-user computing tools, and data flows that may affect financial reporting.
- Ownership, documentation, and approval requirements for the annual SOX ITGC scope.

This policy supports management’s responsibility to maintain effective controls over systems and technology components that could materially affect financial reporting.

## Scope

This policy applies to all business units, finance functions, information technology teams, system owners, control owners, and third parties involved in operating, administering, supporting, or relying on systems and reports used for financial reporting.

The policy applies to the identification and scoping of ITGCs for systems, applications, infrastructure, databases, reports, interfaces, and supporting technology services that may impact the completeness, accuracy, validity, authorisation, processing, or reporting of financial information.

The scope shall include, at a minimum:

| Scope Area | Description | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Financial applications | Systems that initiate, record, process, approve, consolidate, or report financial transactions or balances | Enterprise resource planning system, consolidation platform, revenue system, procurement system, payroll system |
| Key reports | Reports used as evidence in financial controls or management review controls, or used to prepare financial statements and disclosures | Revenue listing, journal entry report, aged receivables report, user access report, close checklist report |
| Interfaces and data transfers | Automated or manual data movements between financial systems or from operational systems into financial reporting systems | Order-to-cash interface, payroll-to-general-ledger feed, bank file upload, data warehouse load |
| Databases | Databases storing financial data, configuration, user access, transaction records, or reporting data | Production financial database, reporting database, data mart supporting close reporting |
| Infrastructure | Operating systems, servers, cloud services, network components, and storage supporting in-scope systems | Cloud environment, virtual servers, file storage, authentication services |
| Security and identity services | Tools and services used to authenticate users, assign privileges, enforce access, or monitor security events | Single sign-on, directory service, privileged access management tool, multi-factor authentication |
| Change and release tools | Tools used to develop, approve, test, migrate, or deploy changes to in-scope systems | Ticketing system, source code repository, release pipeline, deployment tool |
| Job scheduling and batch processing | Tools and processes used to run recurring financial jobs, interfaces, calculations, or reconciliations | Batch scheduler, automated posting jobs, nightly interface runs |
| Third-party services | Outsourced technology or business process providers supporting financially relevant systems or controls | SaaS provider, managed hosting provider, outsourced payroll provider, outsourced IT operations provider |
| End-user computing tools | Spreadsheets, databases, scripts, or local tools used in financial reporting controls or calculations | Close workbook, tax provision model, revenue allocation spreadsheet |
| Reporting and analytics platforms | Data warehouses, business intelligence platforms, and report-generation tools used for key financial reporting | BI dashboards, consolidation reports, management review reports |

This policy applies during:

- Annual SOX scoping and planning.
- New system implementation or major system change.
- Acquisition, divestiture, or restructuring activity.
- New financial reporting process implementation.
- Outsourcing, migration to cloud services, or major technology platform change.
- Identification of a new key report, interface, automated control, or financially relevant data source.
- Any event that could materially change technology risk to financial reporting.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain a documented ITGC scope for each SOX compliance year.

2. The ITGC scope shall be based on the financial reporting risk profile of systems, reports, interfaces, and supporting technology layers.

3. The ITGC scope shall identify all financially significant applications that initiate, authorise, process, record, consolidate, transmit, or report financial data.

4. The ITGC scope shall include systems that directly support significant financial statement accounts, disclosures, transaction classes, or management review controls.

5. The ITGC scope shall include systems that generate, store, or transmit data used by key financial reporting controls, even where the system does not post directly to the general ledger.

6. The ITGC scope shall include key reports used in the execution, review, or evidence of financial reporting controls.

7. Each key report shall have a documented report owner, source system, purpose, frequency, data population, report logic owner, and control usage.

8. Reports shall be assessed to determine whether they are standard system reports, configurable reports, custom reports, queries, dashboards, extracts, spreadsheets, or other end-user reporting tools.

9. The ITGC scope shall identify whether each key report relies on completeness and accuracy controls over source data, report logic, parameters, interfaces, or manual adjustments.

10. The ITGC scope shall include automated application controls and system-generated calculations that are relied upon to prevent or detect material misstatement.

11. The ITGC scope shall identify key interfaces and data transfers that move financially relevant information between systems, applications, databases, reporting platforms, or third-party providers.

12. Interfaces shall be evaluated for the risk of incomplete, inaccurate, unauthorised, duplicate, rejected, or untimely processing of financial data.

13. The ITGC scope shall include databases and data repositories supporting in-scope financial systems, key reports, automated controls, and financially relevant data processing.

14. The ITGC scope shall include operating systems, cloud platforms, servers, storage, middleware, networks, and infrastructure components that directly support in-scope applications and databases.

15. The ITGC scope shall include identity and access management services used to authenticate users, manage privileged access, enforce password requirements, or approve access to in-scope systems.

16. The ITGC scope shall include change management tools, release management tools, source code repositories, deployment pipelines, and job scheduling tools supporting in-scope systems.

17. The ITGC scope shall include IT operations controls over batch jobs, backups, incident management, problem management, monitoring, and disaster recovery where those activities support financial reporting system reliability and data integrity.

18. The ITGC scope shall include third-party technology providers and outsourced business process providers where their services affect financial reporting systems, key controls, transaction processing, hosting, system administration, report generation, or data storage.

19. The organisation shall obtain and evaluate relevant third-party assurance reports, bridge letters, complementary user-entity control requirements, service descriptions, and subservice provider dependencies for in-scope service providers.

20. The ITGC scope shall identify user departments, control owners, system owners, process owners, IT owners, and service providers responsible for each in-scope system, report, interface, and technology layer.

21. Each in-scope system shall be assigned a documented financial relevance rating based on its impact on financial reporting.

22. The scoping assessment shall consider quantitative financial significance and qualitative risk factors, including transaction volume, complexity, susceptibility to error or fraud, level of automation, reliance on system calculations, and degree of manual intervention.

23. The organisation shall document the rationale for including or excluding financially relevant systems, reports, interfaces, technology layers, and service providers.

24. Exclusions from ITGC scope shall be supported by documented analysis demonstrating that the excluded item does not create a reasonable risk to financial reporting reliability.

25. Systems used only for operational reporting shall be excluded from SOX ITGC scope only where the organisation has documented that they are not relied upon for financial reporting controls, financial statement preparation, or disclosure support.

26. Read-only reporting tools, data warehouses, and analytics platforms shall be included where their outputs are relied upon for financial reporting, management review controls, reconciliations, or disclosure support.

27. Spreadsheets and end-user computing tools shall be assessed for inclusion where they perform financially significant calculations, aggregate financial data, transform report outputs, or support key control evidence.

28. The ITGC scope shall clearly map in-scope systems and reports to related business processes, financial statement areas, and control activities.

29. The ITGC scope shall define the relevant ITGC domains applicable to each in-scope technology environment, including access management, change management, computer operations, backup and recovery, incident management, job processing, and third-party oversight.

30. The ITGC scope shall distinguish between controls performed by the organisation and controls performed by third parties.

31. The organisation shall maintain an inventory of in-scope systems, reports, interfaces, technology layers, and service providers.

32. The inventory shall be updated when new systems are implemented, systems are retired, financial reporting processes change, or technology dependencies are materially modified.

33. New systems supporting financial reporting shall be assessed for SOX ITGC scope before production use or before reliance on the system for financial reporting controls.

34. Material changes to in-scope systems, including cloud migration, major version upgrades, significant configuration changes, new modules, new interfaces, or changes in hosting arrangements, shall trigger a scoping reassessment.

35. Acquisitions, divestitures, legal entity changes, shared service transitions, or process migrations shall trigger a reassessment of the ITGC scope.

36. The SOX Compliance Owner shall coordinate the annual ITGC scoping process with Finance, Internal Audit, IT, system owners, business process owners, and external audit stakeholders as appropriate.

37. The annual ITGC Scoping Memo shall be reviewed and approved by accountable Finance and IT leadership before control testing begins for the fiscal year.

38. The approved ITGC Scoping Memo shall be retained as formal SOX compliance evidence.

39. Changes to the approved ITGC scope during the fiscal year shall be documented, justified, risk-assessed, approved, and communicated to impacted control owners and testing teams.

40. The organisation shall ensure that the ITGC scope is aligned with the financial reporting risk assessment, control matrix, system inventory, report inventory, service provider inventory, and testing plan.

41. The ITGC scope shall be sufficiently detailed to allow management, Internal Audit, and external auditors to understand why each system, report, interface, or technology layer is included or excluded.

42. The organisation shall not rely on undocumented verbal representations as the sole basis for scoping decisions.

43. All scoping decisions shall be supported by current evidence, including system inventories, process narratives, data flow diagrams, control matrices, report listings, architecture diagrams, service provider documentation, and management inquiry records where applicable.

44. The ITGC scope shall be maintained in a controlled repository with version history, access restrictions, and retention aligned to SOX evidence retention requirements.

45. The organisation shall prohibit unauthorised changes to the approved ITGC Scoping Memo.

46. The ITGC Scoping Memo shall include, or reference, the following minimum content:

| Required Content | Mandatory Requirement |
|---|---|
| Fiscal year and reporting period | The memo shall identify the SOX year and reporting period covered. |
| Scoping methodology | The memo shall explain how systems, reports, interfaces, and technology layers were evaluated. |
| Financial reporting linkage | The memo shall map in-scope items to relevant financial reporting processes or control areas. |
| In-scope systems | The memo shall list each in-scope application and its purpose. |
| Key reports | The memo shall list key reports and their use in financial controls. |
| Interfaces | The memo shall identify financially relevant interfaces and data flows. |
| Technology layers | The memo shall identify supporting databases, infrastructure, security services, and operational tools. |
| Third parties | The memo shall identify service providers supporting financial systems or controls. |
| Exclusions | The memo shall document excluded systems or components and the rationale. |
| Changes from prior year | The memo shall summarise additions, removals, and significant changes. |
| Approvals | The memo shall evidence review and approval by accountable stakeholders. |

47. The organisation shall maintain the following minimum scoping attributes for each in-scope application:

| Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| System name | The official application name shall be recorded. |
| System owner | The accountable business or IT owner shall be identified. |
| Business process | The supported financial reporting process shall be documented. |
| Financial relevance | The nature of financial reporting reliance shall be described. |
| Transaction type | Key financial transaction types processed by the system shall be identified. |
| Key controls supported | Relevant financial reporting controls shall be referenced by business description. |
| Hosting model | The environment shall be identified as on-premises, cloud, SaaS, or hosted by a third party. |
| Key dependencies | Databases, infrastructure, identity services, interfaces, and reporting tools shall be listed. |
| ITGC domains | Applicable ITGC areas shall be defined. |
| Service provider involvement | Any outsourced operation, administration, hosting, or processing shall be documented. |

48. The organisation shall maintain the following minimum scoping attributes for each key report:

| Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Report name | The report or extract name shall be recorded. |
| Report owner | The accountable business owner shall be identified. |
| Source system | The originating system or data repository shall be documented. |
| Purpose | The financial reporting use shall be described. |
| Frequency | The generation and use frequency shall be recorded. |
| Report type | The report shall be classified as standard, configurable, custom, query, dashboard, extract, or end-user tool. |
| Parameters | Key report parameters or filters shall be documented where relevant. |
| Logic owner | The owner of report logic, configuration, query, or calculation shall be identified. |
| Control usage | The related financial reporting control activity shall be described. |
| Completeness and accuracy approach | The method for validating report reliability shall be documented. |

49. The organisation shall maintain the following minimum scoping attributes for each in-scope interface:

| Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Interface name | The interface or data transfer name shall be recorded. |
| Source system | The originating system shall be identified. |
| Destination system | The receiving system shall be identified. |
| Data type | The financial data transferred shall be described. |
| Frequency | The interface schedule or trigger shall be documented. |
| Transfer method | The mechanism shall be identified, such as API, file transfer, batch job, middleware, or manual upload. |
| Error handling | The process for identifying and resolving rejects or failures shall be described. |
| Reconciliation | The applicable completeness and accuracy checks shall be documented. |
| Ownership | Business and IT owners shall be identified. |
| Financial reporting impact | The risk to financial reporting shall be described. |

50. The organisation shall maintain a documented change log for the ITGC Scoping Memo.

| Change Type | Examples | Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| New financial system | New revenue platform, new consolidation tool, new payroll system | Perform scoping assessment before reliance for financial reporting. |
| System retirement | Legacy system decommissioned after migration | Confirm no remaining financial reporting reliance before removal. |
| New key report | New management review report or disclosure support report | Assess report logic, source data, and completeness and accuracy controls. |
| Interface change | New general ledger feed or modified data mapping | Reassess interface controls and affected systems. |
| Hosting change | Migration from on-premises to cloud or managed hosting | Reassess infrastructure, access, operations, and third-party dependencies. |
| New service provider | Outsourced payroll, SaaS provider, managed IT provider | Evaluate assurance reports and user control responsibilities. |
| Acquisition or divestiture | Newly acquired entity or disposed business unit | Reassess system and process scope. |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Audit Committee / Board Oversight Body | Provides oversight of management’s responsibilities for internal control over financial reporting and receives escalation of significant ITGC scoping issues. |
| Chief Financial Officer | Owns management accountability for financial reporting control scope and approves significant scoping decisions affecting financial reporting. |
| Chief Information Officer / Technology Executive | Owns IT accountability for systems, infrastructure, and technology services supporting financial reporting. |
| SOX Compliance Owner | Leads the annual ITGC scoping process, maintains the ITGC Scoping Memo, coordinates stakeholder input, documents scoping decisions, and ensures approval and retention of the final memo. |
| Controller / Finance Process Owners | Identify financial reporting processes, significant accounts, disclosures, key reports, management review controls, and reliance on system-generated information. |
| IT Control Owner | Confirms applicable ITGC domains, control ownership, technology dependencies, and operational control coverage for in-scope systems. |
| System Owner | Provides system purpose, ownership, data flow, interface, report, access, change, and operational dependency information for assigned systems. |
| Report Owner | Confirms report usage, parameters, source data, logic, frequency, and financial reporting control reliance. |
| Data Owner | Confirms data lineage, data transformation, data quality dependencies, and financial relevance of data used in reporting. |
| Information Security | Provides input on identity services, privileged access, authentication mechanisms, security monitoring, and access risk for in-scope environments. |
| Infrastructure / Cloud Operations | Identifies servers, databases, networks, storage, cloud services, backups, job processing, monitoring, and recovery dependencies supporting in-scope systems. |
| Application Development / DevOps | Identifies change management, release management, configuration, source code, deployment, and automated pipeline dependencies for in-scope systems. |
| Third-Party Risk Management / Procurement | Identifies service providers supporting financial reporting systems and obtains relevant third-party assurance documentation. |
| Internal Audit | Provides independent challenge, testing alignment, and advisory input on scoping completeness and documentation sufficiency. |
| External Audit Liaison | Coordinates responses to external audit inquiries and ensures management-approved scoping materials are available for audit review. |
| Business Control Owners | Confirm the use of systems, reports, and interfaces in financial reporting control execution and evidence. |

Approval responsibility shall be assigned as follows:

| Approval Item | Required Approver |
|---|---|
| Annual ITGC Scoping Memo | Chief Financial Officer or delegate, Chief Information Officer or delegate, SOX Compliance Owner |
| Inclusion or exclusion of financially relevant systems | SOX Compliance Owner, Finance Process Owner, IT Control Owner |
| Removal of a system from scope | SOX Compliance Owner, Finance Process Owner, System Owner, IT Control Owner |
| Addition of new in-scope system during the year | SOX Compliance Owner, System Owner, Finance Process Owner, IT Control Owner |
| Third-party service provider scope decision | SOX Compliance Owner, Third-Party Risk Management, Finance Process Owner, IT Control Owner |
| Key report scope decision | SOX Compliance Owner, Report Owner, Finance Process Owner |
| Exception to this policy | SOX Compliance Owner, Chief Financial Officer or delegate, Chief Information Officer or delegate |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy is mandatory for all personnel involved in financial reporting, IT operations, application ownership, system administration, change management, report ownership, and SOX control execution.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through the following activities:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Responsible Party | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual ITGC scope refresh | Annually before SOX testing begins | SOX Compliance Owner | Approved ITGC Scoping Memo |
| System inventory reconciliation | At least annually and upon material change | IT Governance / System Owners | Reconciled system inventory |
| Financial process and system mapping review | At least annually | Finance Process Owners / SOX Compliance Owner | Process-to-system mapping |
| Key report inventory review | At least annually and upon new report reliance | Report Owners / Finance Process Owners | Approved key report inventory |
| Interface inventory review | At least annually | System Owners / IT Control Owners | Interface inventory and data flow documentation |
| Third-party provider review | At least annually and upon onboarding | Third-Party Risk Management / SOX Compliance Owner | Assurance reports, bridge letters, user control mapping |
| Change impact assessment | Upon material system, process, or technology change | System Owner / SOX Compliance Owner | Change impact assessment and scope decision |
| Scope approval review | Annually and upon major amendment | CFO delegate, CIO delegate, SOX Compliance Owner | Approval record |
| Evidence retention check | At least annually | SOX Compliance Owner | Repository evidence listing |

Non-compliance with this policy may result in:

- Reassessment of SOX ITGC scope.
- Additional management review or control testing.
- Control deficiency evaluation.
- Remediation plan requirements.
- Escalation to Finance, IT, Internal Audit, Legal, or executive leadership.
- Restriction on reliance upon a system, report, or tool for financial reporting purposes until appropriate controls and documentation are established.
- Disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policy where non-compliance is deliberate, repeated, or negligent.

The following events shall be escalated to the SOX Compliance Owner within five business days of identification:

| Escalation Event | Required Escalation Detail |
|---|---|
| New system used for financial reporting | System name, owner, purpose, go-live date, affected controls |
| New key report relied upon for SOX controls | Report name, source system, owner, control usage |
| Material change to in-scope system | Nature of change, implementation date, affected controls and dependencies |
| New or changed interface | Source, destination, data type, timing, financial impact |
| Change in service provider | Provider name, service description, affected systems or processes |
| Unsupported or missing third-party assurance report | Provider, affected controls, compensating evidence |
| System retirement | Retirement date, replacement process, data retention impact |
| Control owner change | Former owner, new owner, affected controls |
| Unidentified reporting dependency | Description of dependency, source data, financial reporting use |

Management shall evaluate identified scoping gaps to determine whether they indicate a control design issue, operating effectiveness issue, documentation deficiency, or broader governance concern.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only where a documented business justification exists and the residual risk to financial reporting has been assessed and accepted by authorised management.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception requester | Name and role of person requesting the exception |
| Date requested | Date the exception was submitted |
| Policy requirement affected | Specific policy statement or requirement affected |
| System, report, interface, or provider | Item affected by the exception |
| Business justification | Reason the requirement cannot be met |
| Financial reporting impact | Description of potential impact on financial reporting reliability |
| Risk assessment | Evaluation of likelihood and impact |
| Compensating controls | Controls that reduce the risk during the exception period |
| Duration requested | Start date and end date |
| Remediation plan | Actions required to return to compliance |
| Responsible owner | Person accountable for remediation |
| Required approvals | Authorised approvers and approval dates |

Exceptions shall not be open-ended. Each exception shall have an expiry date, an accountable owner, and documented compensating controls where applicable.

Exceptions affecting financial reporting reliability, key reports, privileged access, change management, system operations, or third-party assurance shall be reviewed by the SOX Compliance Owner and approved by Finance and IT leadership.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless formally renewed and reapproved before expiry.

The SOX Compliance Owner shall maintain an exception register and review open exceptions at least quarterly.

| Exception Status | Required Action |
|---|---|
| Submitted | Review for completeness and assign reviewer |
| Under review | Assess risk, compensating controls, and remediation plan |
| Approved | Track expiry date and remediation progress |
| Rejected | Communicate decision and required compliance action |
| Expired | Escalate as non-compliance |
| Closed | Retain evidence of remediation and approval closure |

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and updated when there are material changes to financial reporting processes, technology architecture, systems, outsourcing arrangements, control strategy, organisational structure, or SOX compliance methodology.

The SOX Compliance Owner shall coordinate the policy review with Finance, IT, Internal Audit, Information Security, Third-Party Risk Management, and other relevant stakeholders.

The annual review shall confirm that:

- The policy remains aligned to the organisation’s SOX ITGC approach.
- Scoping requirements reflect current financial reporting processes and technology dependencies.
- Roles and responsibilities remain accurate.
- Required scoping attributes remain sufficient for management and audit purposes.
- Monitoring and escalation requirements remain effective.
- Exception and approval requirements remain appropriate.
- Related inventories and evidence repositories remain current.

Policy updates shall be version-controlled and approved before publication.

| Maintenance Activity | Frequency | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Formal policy review | Annually | SOX Compliance Owner |
| Review following major system implementation | As needed | SOX Compliance Owner / System Owner |
| Review following acquisition or divestiture | As needed | SOX Compliance Owner / Finance Leadership |
| Review following major outsourcing or cloud migration | As needed | SOX Compliance Owner / IT Leadership |
| Update of scoping templates and inventories | At least annually | SOX Compliance Owner |
| Review of exception register | Quarterly | SOX Compliance Owner |
| Approval of policy changes | As needed | CFO delegate, CIO delegate, SOX Compliance Owner |

The current approved version of this policy shall be stored in [Policy Repository / GRC Platform]. Superseded versions, approval records, change history, and supporting review evidence shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements for SOX documentation.

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Application ID | Enter the unique application identifier used by IT or enterprise architecture, e.g. CMDB ID, application code, or asset ID. Use a stable value that does not change year to year. |
| Application Name | Enter the official production application name as recorded in the CMDB, application inventory, or system of record. |
| Application Description / Business Purpose | Briefly describe what the application does and why the business uses it, focusing on financial reporting relevance where applicable. |
| Business Process Supported | Enter the business process(es) supported by the application, e.g. Order to Cash, Procure to Pay, Record to Report, Payroll, Treasury, Tax, Inventory, Financial Close. |
| Financial Statement Area(s) / Significant Account(s) Impacted | Enter the financial statement area or significant account impacted, e.g. Revenue, Accounts Receivable, Inventory, Payroll Expense, Cash, Journal Entries, Consolidation. |
| SOX Relevance | Select one: Directly Impacts Financial Reporting, Indirectly Supports Financial Reporting, Generates Key Report/IPE, Supports Relevant Interface, Infrastructure/Supporting System, Not SOX Relevant. |
| Basis for SOX Inclusion / Exclusion | Document the rationale for including or excluding the application from SOX scope, including how it impacts financial reporting, key reports, interfaces, calculations, postings, or reliance by controls. |
| In-Scope for SOX ITGC? | Select one: Yes, No, Pending Assessment. Mark Yes only where the application is relied upon for financial reporting or supports relevant automated controls, reports, interfaces, or financially significant processing. |
| ITGC Domains Applicable | Enter applicable ITGC domains using comma-separated values from: Access Management, Change Management, IT Operations, Program Development, Computer Operations, Backup/Recovery, Vendor Controls, Interface Controls. Use N/A if not in scope. |
| Application Type | Select one: ERP, Financial Close/Consolidation, Subledger, Billing, Payroll, Treasury, Tax, Data Warehouse/Reporting, Middleware/Interface, Database, Infrastructure Tool, SaaS, Custom Application, Other. |
| Technology Platform / Product | Enter the primary product, platform, or technology stack, e.g. SAP S/4HANA, Oracle EBS, Workday, Microsoft SQL Server, Salesforce, BlackLine, custom Java application. |
| Version / Release | Enter the current production version, release, or major build number where applicable. Use N/A for SaaS platforms where versioning is not customer-managed. |
| Hosting Model | Select one: On-Premise, Private Cloud, Public Cloud IaaS, Public Cloud PaaS, SaaS, Managed Service, Hybrid. |
| Production Environment Location | Enter the production hosting location, data center, cloud region, or tenant location, e.g. AWS us-east-1, Azure West Europe, Company DC1, Vendor-hosted SaaS. |
| Application Owner | Enter the accountable application owner name or role responsible for the application inventory record and SOX scoping confirmation. |
| Business Process Owner | Enter the business owner responsible for the financial process supported by the application. |
| IT Owner / Support Owner | Enter the IT operations, application support, or platform owner responsible for production support and ITGC operation. |
| Vendor / Service Provider | Enter the external vendor or service provider name if applicable; otherwise enter N/A. |
| SOC Report Reliance? | Select one: Yes, No, N/A, Pending. Use Yes if the organisation relies on a vendor SOC report to address relevant ITGCs or complementary user entity controls. |
| SOC Report Type and Period | If SOC reliance is Yes, enter report type and coverage period in format SOC 1 Type 2 YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD or SOC 2 Type 2 YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD. Enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Key Reports / IPE Produced | List financially relevant reports, extracts, dashboards, or information produced by the entity used in SOX controls or financial reporting. Enter report names/IDs or N/A. |
| Key Interfaces / Data Feeds | List financially relevant inbound or outbound interfaces, feeds, APIs, files, or integrations. Include interface IDs where available or enter N/A. |
| Upstream Source System(s) | Enter systems that send financially relevant data into this application. Use comma-separated official application names or N/A. |
| Downstream Target System(s) | Enter systems that receive financially relevant data from this application. Use comma-separated official application names or N/A. |
| Database Name / Platform | Enter the production database name and platform supporting the application where applicable, e.g. FINDB01 / Oracle 19c. Enter N/A for SaaS if not visible or not managed by the organisation. |
| Operating System / Infrastructure Dependency | Enter key operating system, server, cloud service, or infrastructure dependency relevant to ITGC scope. Use N/A for SaaS if not customer-managed. |
| Authentication Method | Select or describe authentication method, e.g. SSO, Active Directory, LDAP, Local Application Accounts, MFA, Vendor Managed, Service Accounts Only. |
| Privileged Access Exists? | Select one: Yes, No, Unknown. Mark Yes if admin, superuser, developer, database, OS, cloud, or support privileged access exists for the application or supporting platform. |
| Change Management Tool / Repository | Enter the tool or repository used to manage production changes, e.g. ServiceNow, Jira, Azure DevOps, GitHub Enterprise, SAP ChaRM. Enter N/A if not applicable or vendor-managed. |
| Job Scheduler / Batch Dependency | Enter relevant batch scheduler, job automation, or recurring processing dependency, e.g. Control-M, Autosys, SAP jobs, cron. Enter N/A if none or vendor-managed. |
| End-User Computing Dependency? | Select one: Yes, No, Unknown. Mark Yes if spreadsheets, databases, macros, or manual EUC tools materially depend on data from this application or feed data into it for financial reporting. |
| Data Retention / Evidence Location | Enter where SOX-relevant evidence, logs, reports, access listings, change records, or processing evidence is retained, e.g. ServiceNow, SharePoint SOX repository, GRC tool, vendor portal. |
| Application Status | Select one: Active Production, Implementation, Read-Only, Decommission Planned, Decommissioned, Archived. |
| Go-Live Date | Enter the original production go-live date or most recent major implementation date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Use Unknown if not available. |
| Decommission Date | Enter planned or actual decommission date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Last SOX Scope Assessment Date | Enter the date the SOX relevance and ITGC scope assessment was last completed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Scope Assessment Performed By | Enter the name and role/team of the person who performed or approved the SOX scoping assessment. |
| Financial Reporting Risk Notes | Enter concise notes on the financial reporting risk, e.g. posts journal entries, calculates revenue, stores payroll master data, generates key SOX report, transmits subledger balances. Enter N/A if excluded. |
| Related SOX Control IDs | Enter applicable SOX control references mapped to the application, e.g. ITGC-AC-01, ITGC-CM-02, ITGC-OPS-03, AC-REV-05. Use comma-separated values or N/A. |
| Last Updated Date | Enter the date this register row was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Updated By | Enter the name or role of the person who last updated the register row. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the IT SOX Lead or GRC Application Controls Owner, with certification by Application Owners and Business Process Owners. Update at least quarterly and whenever applications are implemented, materially changed, retired, or newly relied upon for financial reporting; primary sources should be the CMDB/application inventory, enterprise architecture repository, GRC tool, SOX scoping assessment, vendor/SOC report inventory, and finance process/control documentation.

SOX-003.title: IT Process & Risk Walkthroughs
SOX-003.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| SOX-ITGC-RPT-001 | 1.0 | IT Compliance Manager | [Effective Date] | SOX IT General Controls | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This report documents the IT process and risk walkthroughs performed to support the organisation’s SOX IT General Controls program for the reporting period. The walkthroughs were conducted to confirm that key IT processes supporting financially relevant systems are understood, appropriately designed, and capable of addressing risks that could impact the reliability, integrity, availability, and security of financial reporting data.

The objectives of the walkthroughs were to:

- Validate current-state process flows for key IT General Control domains.
- Confirm the existence and design of controls relied upon for financial reporting.
- Identify risks, control gaps, inconsistencies, or process deviations requiring remediation.
- Assess whether control owners understand their responsibilities and perform activities as described.
- Trace selected transactions or activities from initiation through completion to confirm end-to-end control design.
- Support management’s assessment of IT controls relevant to financial reporting.

This report is intended for use by IT management, control owners, SOX program management, internal audit, and external audit stakeholders, as appropriate.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Attribute | Details |
|---|---|
| Reporting Period Covered | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Walkthrough Fieldwork Dates | [Fieldwork Start Date] to [Fieldwork End Date] |
| Report Date | [Report Date] |
| Prepared By | [Preparer Name / Team] |
| Reviewed By | [Reviewer Name / Team] |

### In-Scope ITGC Domains

The walkthroughs covered the following IT General Control areas relevant to financial reporting systems:

| ITGC Domain | Scope Description |
|---|---|
| User Access Management | Provisioning, modification, periodic access review, termination, privileged access, and segregation of duties considerations. |
| Change Management | Standard application, database, infrastructure, and emergency changes supporting financially relevant systems. |
| IT Operations | Job scheduling, batch processing, backup monitoring, incident handling, problem escalation, and operational monitoring. |
| Program Development / System Implementation | New system implementations, major enhancements, testing, approval, migration, and financial reporting impact assessment. |
| Logical Security Administration | Authentication, password settings, account lockout, service accounts, administrative accounts, and security configuration management. |
| Interfaces and Data Transfers | Key automated interfaces, file transfers, reconciliations, error handling, and monitoring of financial data movement. |

### In-Scope Systems and Platforms

| System / Platform | Business Purpose | Financial Reporting Relevance | Primary IT Owner | Primary Business Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ERP System] | General ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, procurement, and financial close activities. | High | [IT Owner] | [Business Owner] |
| [Financial Reporting System] | Consolidation, reporting, and financial statement preparation. | High | [IT Owner] | [Business Owner] |
| [Payroll System] | Payroll processing and payroll-related financial postings. | Medium / High | [IT Owner] | [Business Owner] |
| [Database Platform] | Hosts financially relevant application data. | High | [IT Owner] | [Business Owner] |
| [Identity Management Platform] | Centralised access provisioning and authentication. | High | [IT Owner] | [Business Owner] |
| [Job Scheduling Tool] | Executes scheduled processing and data transfer activities. | Medium / High | [IT Owner] | [Business Owner] |

### Out-of-Scope Items

The following items were not included in this walkthrough cycle:

- Systems not supporting financially relevant processes.
- Business process controls outside the ITGC scope, except where they intersect with IT-dependent controls.
- Detailed operating effectiveness testing, except where limited sample tracing was performed to support process understanding.
- Cybersecurity controls not directly relevant to financial reporting reliability, unless they affect in-scope systems.
- Third-party service provider controls where separate assurance reports or vendor control documentation are relied upon, unless complementary user entity activities were assessed.

### Walkthrough Participants

| Name | Role | Department | Walkthrough Area |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Name] | IT Compliance Manager | IT Governance / Compliance | Overall SOX ITGC coordination |
| [Name] | Application Owner | IT Applications | ERP access and change management |
| [Name] | Security Administrator | IT Security | User access provisioning and termination |
| [Name] | Infrastructure Manager | IT Operations | Backups, monitoring, batch operations |
| [Name] | Database Administrator | IT Infrastructure | Database access and changes |
| [Name] | Financial Systems Manager | Finance | Financial system ownership and approvals |
| [Name] | Internal Audit Representative | Internal Audit | Observation and challenge |

## Executive Summary

Walkthroughs were completed for the key IT processes supporting financial reporting during the reporting period. Overall, the organisation has established foundational ITGC processes across access management, change management, IT operations, and system implementation. Control owners were generally able to describe their responsibilities, demonstrate relevant tools and records, and provide examples of control performance.

The walkthroughs confirmed that several controls are designed to address key risks, including unauthorised access to financially relevant systems, inappropriate changes to production environments, incomplete processing of scheduled jobs, and insufficient monitoring of privileged activities. However, the walkthroughs also identified process inconsistencies and documentation gaps that should be remediated before or during operating effectiveness testing.

### Overall Walkthrough Conclusion

| Area | Walkthrough Result | Summary Conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| User Access Management | Partially Effective Design | Core provisioning and termination activities exist, but evidence consistency and timely removal monitoring require improvement. |
| Change Management | Generally Effective Design | Standard change process is defined and supported by workflow tooling, but emergency change documentation requires strengthening. |
| IT Operations | Partially Effective Design | Monitoring, job scheduling, and backup processes are in place, but exception documentation and review evidence are inconsistent. |
| Program Development / System Implementation | Generally Effective Design | Project controls exist for major changes, with opportunities to improve financial reporting impact assessment documentation. |
| Logical Security Administration | Partially Effective Design | Authentication controls are configured, but privileged and service account governance requires enhanced review. |
| Interfaces and Data Transfers | Partially Effective Design | Key interfaces are monitored, but reconciliation ownership and error resolution evidence require clarification. |

### Key Themes Identified

- **Control activities exist but are not always supported by consistent evidence.**
- **Approvals are generally embedded in workflow tools, but rationale and review notes are not always sufficiently documented.**
- **Privileged access oversight requires additional discipline and periodic validation.**
- **Operational exceptions are addressed in practice, but closure evidence is inconsistent.**
- **Several processes depend on key individuals, increasing reliance on informal knowledge.**
- **Control descriptions should be refreshed to align with actual system workflows and tool configurations.**

### High-Priority Items

| Priority | Issue | Impact | Required Management Attention |
|---|---|---|---|

## Methodology

The walkthroughs were conducted using a risk-based approach focused on IT processes that support the confidentiality, integrity, availability, and reliability of financially relevant systems and data.

### Walkthrough Approach

The following activities were performed:

1. **Process Inquiry**
 - Interviewed control owners, system administrators, IT operations personnel, application owners, and business stakeholders.
 - Confirmed roles, responsibilities, process frequency, escalation paths, and dependencies.

2. **Process Observation**
 - Observed system workflows, ticket queues, approval paths, access request screens, change records, job schedules, monitoring dashboards, and logs.
 - Confirmed how control activities are initiated, performed, reviewed, and retained.

3. **Document Review**
 - Reviewed policies, procedures, control narratives, risk and control matrices, access review records, change tickets, incident records, backup logs, and monitoring evidence.
 - Compared documented procedures to actual process execution.

4. **Transaction Tracing**
 - Selected representative examples and traced them from initiation through completion.
 - Confirmed that key control points were present, including authorisation, review, approval, execution, monitoring, and evidence retention.

5. **Risk Identification**
 - Identified process points where errors, unauthorised activity, or incomplete processing could affect financial reporting.
 - Assessed whether existing controls are designed to prevent or detect those risks.

6. **Design Assessment**
 - Evaluated whether each process, as described and demonstrated, is suitably designed to address relevant IT and financial reporting risks.
 - Identified design gaps, evidence gaps, process inconsistencies, and improvement opportunities.

### Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence Type | Examples Reviewed |
|---|---|
| Access Requests | New user requests, access modification tickets, manager approvals, role assignments. |
| Termination Records | HR termination notifications, deactivation records, identity management logs. |
| Access Reviews | Quarterly review files, reviewer sign-offs, exceptions, remediation tracking. |
| Change Records | Change tickets, approvals, testing evidence, deployment logs, rollback plans. |
| Emergency Changes | Emergency approval records, post-implementation reviews, retrospective testing evidence. |
| Job Monitoring Records | Batch completion logs, failure alerts, rerun records, exception notes. |
| Backup Evidence | Backup schedules, success/failure logs, restoration test records. |
| Incident Records | Incident tickets, severity classification, escalation evidence, closure notes. |
| Interface Monitoring | Transfer logs, reconciliation reports, error queues, issue resolution records. |
| Security Configuration | Password settings, account lockout settings, privileged account listings. |

### Walkthrough Rating Definitions

| Rating | Definition |
|---|---|
| Effective Design | Process and controls are clearly defined, consistently understood, and suitably designed to address identified risks. Evidence expectations are clear. |
| Generally Effective Design | Process and controls are largely suitable, with minor documentation, evidence, or consistency improvements required. |
| Partially Effective Design | Process addresses some risks, but gaps or inconsistencies could affect reliability, auditability, or timely detection of issues. |
| Ineffective Design | Process does not adequately address key risks or lacks defined control ownership, performance expectations, or evidence. |
| Not Assessed | Area was not fully assessed due to scope limitation, unavailable evidence, or pending process change. |

### Limitations

The walkthroughs were designed to assess process understanding and control design. They do not represent full operating effectiveness testing across the reporting period. Any conclusions in this report are based on evidence made available during the walkthrough period and may require further validation through sample-based testing.

## Analysis

### Overall Control Design Maturity

The walkthroughs indicate that the organisation has established core SOX ITGC processes and that control owners generally understand the expected activities. The organisation has implemented workflow tools for access requests, change management, incident handling, and operational monitoring. These tools provide an appropriate foundation for consistent control performance and evidence retention.

However, several process areas rely on informal knowledge, manual tracking, or inconsistent evidence practices. This creates audit risk because management may be unable to demonstrate that controls were performed as designed throughout the reporting period, even where operational teams performed the underlying activity.

### Risk Concentration by Domain

| Domain | Risk Level | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| User Access Management | High | Access controls directly affect the ability to initiate, approve, modify, or conceal financially relevant activity. Termination and privileged access evidence gaps require prompt remediation. |
| Change Management | High | Emergency change process gaps could allow production changes without sufficient review. Standard change management is stronger but requires improved financial impact documentation. |
| IT Operations | Medium | Monitoring activities are in place, but failure resolution evidence and business impact assessment require improvement. |
| Program Development / System Implementation | Medium | Governance exists, but testing should more clearly cover financial reporting requirements and control dependencies. |
| Logical Security Administration | Medium | Authentication settings are established, but privileged, service, and dormant account governance should be strengthened. |
| Interfaces and Data Transfers | Medium | Monitoring exists, but reconciliation ownership and interface inventory quality require improvement. |

### Root Cause Themes

The findings appear to be driven by the following common root causes:

1. **Evidence Standards Are Not Fully Defined**
 - Teams often perform the activity but do not retain evidence in a consistent, audit-ready format.
 - Closure notes, approvals, and review comments are not always sufficient to demonstrate the nature and quality of review.

2. **Tool Workflows Do Not Enforce All Required Fields**
 - Some tools allow tickets or reviews to be closed without retrospective approval, financial impact assessment, remediation notes, or reviewer comments.

3. **Ownership Boundaries Are Not Always Clear**
 - Interface monitoring, reconciliation, service account governance, and privileged access review involve multiple teams.
 - Responsibilities are not always clearly documented between IT, Finance, system owners, and business process owners.

4. **Financial Reporting Relevance Is Not Always Explicit**
 - IT teams often assess technical risk but do not consistently document whether a change, interface, job, or access role affects financial reporting.

5. **Periodic Reviews Require More Reviewer Challenge**
 - Access and privileged account reviews are occurring, but evidence does not always show meaningful evaluation of appropriateness, exceptions, and remediation.

### Potential Impact on SOX ITGC Program

If not remediated, the identified gaps may affect management’s ability to rely on ITGCs for financial reporting purposes. The most significant impact relates to controls where the activity may occur but evidence may not sufficiently demonstrate:

- Who performed the control.
- When the control was performed.
- What population was reviewed.
- What exceptions were identified.
- How exceptions were resolved.
- Whether the reviewer had sufficient knowledge and authority.
- Whether the review was completed before the control deadline.
- Whether the control addressed the relevant financial reporting risk.

The areas requiring immediate attention before operating effectiveness testing are termination access removal, privileged access review, emergency change closure, and evidence standards for operational exceptions.

### Positive Observations

The walkthroughs also identified several strengths:

- Workflow tools are in place for key IT processes.
- Control owners were available and generally knowledgeable.
- Standard change records usually include approval, testing, and implementation evidence.
- Scheduled job and backup monitoring activities are performed.
- Access review cycles are established.
- Production migration access is restricted to authorised personnel.
- Major projects include business stakeholder involvement.
- Incident management is supported by a defined ticket workflow.

These strengths provide a practical base for remediation and control maturity improvement.

### Recommended Control Evidence Standards

To improve audit readiness, management should establish standard evidence requirements for all ITGC activities. At a minimum, evidence should show:

- The population or item reviewed.
- The date the control was performed.
- The individual who performed the activity.
- The individual who reviewed or approved the activity, where applicable.
- The criteria used to perform the review.
- Exceptions identified.
- Actions taken to resolve exceptions.
- Date of resolution.
- Linkage to relevant ticket, request, system log, or report.
- Evidence that the activity was completed within the required timeframe.

### Confidentiality Requirements

- This report must not be shared outside approved distribution without written authorisation from [Authorising Role].
- Extracts from this report must retain the same classification unless formally reclassified.
- Findings and remediation details must not be distributed to individuals without a legitimate business need.
- Evidence referenced in this report must be stored in approved repositories with access restricted to authorised personnel.
- Any external sharing must follow the organisation’s legal, audit, and confidentiality review process.
- Draft versions, working papers, and interview notes must be retained or disposed of in accordance with applicable records management requirements.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| RACM_ID | Enter the unique register row identifier in the format RACM-YYYY-NNN, where YYYY is the SOX year and NNN is a sequential number. |
| SOX_Scope_Year | Enter the SOX compliance year in YYYY format. |
| Business_Process_or_ITGC_Domain | Enter the SOX ITGC domain or business area affected; allowed values: Access Management, Change Management, IT Operations, Program Development, Cybersecurity, Entity-Level IT Controls, Third-Party IT Services, Other. |
| IT_Process | Enter the specific IT process addressed by the risk/control, such as user access provisioning, privileged access review, emergency change, batch monitoring, backup restore, job scheduling, or incident management. |
| System_or_Application | Enter the in-scope financially relevant system, application, platform, or service name exactly as listed in the SOX system inventory. |
| Infrastructure_or_Database_In_Scope | Enter relevant infrastructure, database, operating system, middleware, cloud platform, or network component in scope; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Financial_Statement_Impact | Enter the financial reporting area affected, such as revenue, inventory, payroll, general ledger, financial close, accounts payable, or all financial reporting. |
| Relevant_Assertion | Enter the financial statement assertion impacted; allowed values: Completeness, Accuracy, Validity, Existence, Occurrence, Rights and Obligations, Cut-off, Classification, Presentation and Disclosure, Authorization, All. |
| Risk_ID | Enter the unique risk identifier in the format RISK-ITGC-NNN. |
| Risk_Statement | Enter a concise risk statement describing what could go wrong and its financial reporting impact, using the format: If [condition/event], then [impact to system/data/control], resulting in [financial reporting risk]. |
| Inherent_Risk_Rating | Enter the risk rating before considering controls; allowed values: High, Medium, Low. |
| Control_ID | Enter the unique control identifier in the format ITGC-XX-NNN, where XX represents the domain abbreviation such as AM, CM, OPS, PD, CYB, or ELC. |
| Control_Title | Enter a short control name that clearly identifies the activity performed. |
| Control_Objective | Enter the objective of the control, stating the risk it mitigates and the intended outcome. |
| Control_Description | Enter a detailed description of who performs the control, what is performed, when/how often it is performed, what evidence is retained, and how exceptions are resolved. |
| COSO_Component | Map the control to one COSO component; allowed values: Control Environment, Risk Assessment, Control Activities, Information and Communication, Monitoring Activities. |
| COSO_Principle | Enter the applicable COSO principle number and short name, for example P11 - Selects and develops general controls over technology. |
| COBIT_Objective | Enter the applicable COBIT objective reference and name, such as APO12 Managed Risk, BAI06 Managed IT Changes, DSS05 Managed Security Services, DSS06 Managed Business Process Controls, MEA02 Managed System of Internal Control. |
| Control_Category | Enter the ITGC category; allowed values: Logical Access, Privileged Access, User Access Review, Change Management, SDLC, Computer Operations, Backup and Recovery, Incident Management, Job Scheduling, Interface Monitoring, Security Configuration, Third-Party Service Organization, Other. |
| Control_Type | Enter the control execution type; allowed values: Manual, Automated, IT-Dependent Manual, Configuration, Hybrid. |
| Control_Nature | Enter whether the control is Preventive, Detective, or Corrective. |
| Control_Frequency | Enter how often the control operates; allowed values: Real-time, Per Transaction, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annual, Annual, Ad hoc, Event-driven. |
| Preventive_or_Detective | Enter the primary timing of the control; allowed values: Preventive, Detective. |
| Key_Control | Enter Yes if the control is relied upon to address a material SOX risk; otherwise enter No. |
| Entity_Level_or_Process_Level | Enter whether the control operates at Entity-Level, IT General Control Level, Application Level, Infrastructure Level, or Process Level. |
| Control_Owner | Enter the accountable role or named owner responsible for control design and operation, such as IT Security Manager or Change Manager. |
| Control_Performer | Enter the role or team that performs the control activity; use role/team names rather than personal names where possible. |
| Control_Reviewer | Enter the role or team that reviews or approves the control evidence; enter N/A if there is no separate reviewer. |
| Segregation_of_Duties_Consideration | Describe relevant SoD considerations, including incompatible duties, required independence of reviewer, or compensating control; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Population_Definition | Define the complete population subject to the control for the period, such as all production changes, all active users, all terminated users, all privileged accounts, or all failed batch jobs. |
| Evidence_Produced | List the specific evidence retained to prove operation, such as approved ticket, access review certification, change approval, implementation log, monitoring report, backup report, or exception tracker. |
| Evidence_Location | Enter the repository or system path where evidence is retained, such as GRC tool, ServiceNow, Jira, SharePoint, SIEM, IAM tool, or file path. |
| IPE_or_Report_Used | Enter the name of any information-produced-by-entity report, query, dashboard, or export used in the control; enter N/A if none. |
| IPE_or_Report_Validation_Required | Enter Yes if the control relies on a system-generated report or query that requires completeness and accuracy validation; otherwise enter No. |
| Control_Dependency | Enter any upstream or dependent control, system, report, or configuration required for this control to operate effectively; enter N/A if none. |
| Related_Application_Control | Enter related application control ID(s) that depend on or are supported by this ITGC; enter N/A if none. |
| Related_Manual_Control | Enter related business manual control ID(s) supported by this ITGC; enter N/A if none. |
| Control_Start_Date | Enter the date the control became effective in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Control_End_Date | Enter the date the control was retired or superseded in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if active. |
| Control_Status | Enter current status; allowed values: Draft, Active, In Remediation, Retired, Superseded. |
| Design_Effectiveness_Assessment | Enter the current design assessment; allowed values: Effective, Ineffective, Not Assessed, Not Applicable. |
| Operating_Effectiveness_Testing_Approach | Describe the planned audit/testing procedure, including inquiry, inspection, observation, reperformance, or automated evidence testing. |
| Sample_Selection_Method | Enter the sampling approach; allowed values: Full Population, Random Sample, Haphazard Sample, Judgmental Sample, Exception-Based, Not Applicable. |
| Testing_Frequency | Enter how often SOX testing is performed; allowed values: Quarterly, Semi-Annual, Annual, Continuous, Not Tested. |
| Last_Test_Date | Enter the most recent control test completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not yet tested. |
| Test_Result | Enter the latest testing outcome; allowed values: Pass, Pass with Observation, Fail, Not Tested, Not Applicable. |
| Deficiency_ID | Enter linked deficiency or issue identifier in the format DEF-YYYY-NNN; enter N/A if no deficiency exists. |
| Deficiency_Severity | Enter the assessed severity; allowed values: None, Control Deficiency, Significant Deficiency, Material Weakness, Not Assessed. |
| Remediation_Owner | Enter the role or named owner accountable for remediation; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation_Due_Date | Enter the committed remediation due date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Management_Response | Enter management’s response, action plan, or rationale for risk acceptance; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| External_Auditor_Reliance | Enter whether external auditors are expected to rely on this control; allowed values: Yes, No, TBD. |
| Last_Updated_Date | Enter the date this RACM row was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last_Updated_By | Enter the name, role, or user ID of the person who last updated this RACM row. |

### Maintenance

The IT SOX Manager or GRC Control Owner owns and maintains this RACM, with input from IT control owners, application owners, process owners, internal audit, and external audit. Update at least quarterly and whenever systems, risks, controls, scope, deficiencies, or remediation plans change, using source data from the SOX scoping inventory, GRC platform, ticketing/change tools, IAM systems, CMDB, audit testing workpapers, and deficiency tracker.

SOX-005.title: IT Risk Assessment (Financial Reporting)
SOX-005.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | [IT Risk and Controls Owner] | [Effective Date] | SOX IT General Controls | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This report documents the results of the IT risk assessment performed to support management’s assessment of internal control over financial reporting.

The assessment applies a top-down, risk-based scoping approach to identify the systems, infrastructure, IT processes, service providers, and IT general controls that are relevant to the reliability, integrity, completeness, and availability of financial reporting data.

The objectives of this report are to:

- Identify technology risks that could materially affect financial reporting.
- Determine which applications, databases, interfaces, infrastructure components, and IT services are in scope for SOX IT General Controls.
- Link financially significant business processes to supporting technology.
- Assess the design relevance of IT general control areas, including access management, change management, computer operations, job processing, backup and recovery, interface controls, and privileged access.
- Identify control gaps, scoping changes, or risk areas requiring remediation, enhancement, or management attention.
- Provide a documented basis for SOX ITGC testing scope for the reporting period.

This report is intended for use by management, internal audit, external audit, compliance, IT control owners, and relevant process owners.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Assessment period | [Fiscal Year / Quarter / Reporting Period] |
| Assessment performed during | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Financial reporting period supported | [Fiscal Year Ending Date] |
| Prior assessment reference | [Prior Report Name / Version / Date, if applicable] |

### Organisational Scope

This assessment covers technology supporting financial reporting for the following organisational areas:

| Area | Included in Scope | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Corporate finance and accounting | Yes | Includes general ledger, consolidation, close, reporting, and journal entry processes. |
| Revenue and billing | Yes | Includes order-to-cash systems and billing platforms that initiate or modify financial transactions. |
| Procurement and accounts payable | Yes | Includes procure-to-pay applications and vendor payment workflows. |
| Payroll and benefits accounting | [Yes/No] | Included where payroll postings materially affect financial statements. |
| Inventory and cost accounting | [Yes/No] | Included where inventory valuation or cost of goods sold is material. |
| Treasury and cash management | [Yes/No] | Included where cash, debt, investments, or hedging activities are material. |
| Tax accounting | [Yes/No] | Included where tax calculations or reporting are supported by key systems. |
| Financial planning and analysis | [Yes/No] | Included only where outputs feed directly into recorded financial statements or disclosures. |

### Financially Relevant Business Processes

The following business processes were considered for IT dependency and SOX relevance:

| Business Process | Financial Statement Impact | IT Dependency | SOX IT Relevance |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Record-to-report | General ledger, consolidation, financial close, adjustments, financial reporting | High | High |
| Order-to-cash | Revenue, receivables, cash receipts, deferred revenue | High | High |
| Procure-to-pay | Expenses, liabilities, cash disbursements | High | High |
| Hire-to-retire / payroll | Compensation expense, payroll liabilities, taxes | [High/Medium/Low] | [High/Medium/Low] |

## Methodology

### Assessment Approach

The risk assessment followed a top-down, risk-based approach. Management first identified financially significant accounts, disclosures, and business processes, then assessed which technology components support those processes. IT risks were evaluated based on their potential to affect the completeness, accuracy, validity, authorisation, and availability of financial reporting data.

The methodology included the following steps:

1. Identify financially significant accounts, disclosures, and related business processes.
2. Map significant business processes to supporting applications, databases, interfaces, reporting tools, infrastructure, and service providers.
3. Determine whether each system initiates, authorises, processes, records, stores, transforms, transmits, or reports financially relevant data.
4. Assess the likelihood and potential impact of IT risks affecting financial reporting.
5. Evaluate whether automated controls, system-generated reports, configurable controls, or interface controls depend on underlying ITGC.
6. Consider changes in systems, processes, vendors, infrastructure, personnel, and access models during the period.
7. Determine in-scope and out-of-scope systems based on risk, materiality, dependency, and control reliance.
8. Identify control domains required for each in-scope system or technology component.
9. Document findings, risk ratings, scope conclusions, and required actions.

### Risk Rating Criteria

Risks were assessed using likelihood and financial reporting impact.

#### Likelihood

| Rating | Criteria |
|---|---|
| High | The event is reasonably possible due to high change volume, complex access model, prior issues, limited monitoring, weak process maturity, or significant third-party dependence. |
| Medium | The event could occur, but existing processes, oversight, or controls reduce the likelihood. |
| Low | The event is unlikely due to stable systems, limited access, low change activity, strong monitoring, or limited financial reporting dependency. |

#### Impact

| Rating | Criteria |
|---|---|
| High | Could result in a material or significant financial reporting error, unauthorised financial transaction, inaccurate consolidation, or inability to complete financial close. |
| Medium | Could result in financial reporting errors requiring correction, delayed close activity, or reliance on compensating controls. |
| Low | Limited effect on financial reporting due to immateriality, read-only use, independent reconciliation, or downstream validation. |

#### Overall Risk

| Overall Rating | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| High | Requires SOX scope inclusion and management attention; control design and operating effectiveness should be tested. |
| Medium | Generally requires scope consideration; inclusion depends on dependency, compensating controls, and management reliance. |
| Low | May be excluded where there is no significant financial reporting dependency or where risks are sufficiently mitigated outside ITGC. |

### Scope Decision Criteria

A system or component is generally included in SOX ITGC scope when it:

- Supports a financially significant business process.
- Initiates, authorises, records, processes, stores, transforms, transmits, or reports financial data.
- Hosts or supports an in-scope financial application or database.
- Is used to operate automated controls relied upon for financial reporting.
- Produces system-generated reports used as evidence for financial reporting controls.
- Manages authentication, authorisation, privileged access, or security administration for in-scope systems.
- Supports interfaces transferring financially relevant data.
- Supports job scheduling, batch processing, or system operations that affect financial completeness or accuracy.
- Is operated by a third-party provider whose services affect financial reporting reliability.

A system or component may be excluded when:

- It does not support financially significant accounts, disclosures, or business processes.
- It is used only for management analytics and does not feed financial records or disclosures.
- It is read-only and does not transform, approve, calculate, or record financial data.
- Financial data from the system is independently validated before use in financial reporting.
- The related process is immaterial and not otherwise sensitive.
- The system is not relied upon for automated controls, key reports, or financial close activities.

The organisation’s financial reporting environment is technology-dependent, with key reliance on [ERP / General Ledger System], [Consolidation System], and related systems supporting revenue, procurement, payroll, reporting, and close activities. The level of IT dependency requires a structured SOX ITGC scope that covers the applications and underlying technology components that could affect financial reporting accuracy, completeness, validity, and availability.

The assessment confirms that a risk-based ITGC scope is appropriate for the reporting period. In-scope systems are those that support financially significant processes, automated controls, system-generated reports, financial data interfaces, or core financial records. Supporting databases, infrastructure, identity services, job processing tools, and third-party services are also relevant where they directly support in-scope financial systems.

### Key Risk Themes

#### Access Management

Access management remains a critical risk area because inappropriate access to financial applications, databases, or privileged administrative functions could allow unauthorised transaction entry, approval, configuration changes, or direct data modification.

The assessment indicates that control emphasis should remain on:

- Timely user provisioning and deprovisioning.
- Business approval of access requests.
- Periodic access reviews for financially sensitive roles.
- Monitoring and restriction of privileged access.
- Segregation of duties conflicts.
- Service account ownership and review.
- Authentication requirements for in-scope systems.

#### Change Management

Change management is a key risk area due to the potential for unauthorised, inadequately tested, or improperly approved changes to affect financial processing, reporting, interfaces, security configuration, and automated controls.

The assessment indicates that control emphasis should remain on:

- Approval before development and deployment.
- Documented testing for financially relevant changes.
- Business approval for changes affecting financial processes.
- Restricted production migration access.
- Retrospective review of emergency changes.
- Configuration management for financial rules and workflows.
- Separation of duties between development, approval, and deployment.

#### Operations and Interface Processing

Operations controls are relevant where scheduled jobs, interfaces, batch processes, file transfers, and close activities support financial reporting. Failed or incomplete processing may affect transaction completeness, data accuracy, and timely financial close.

The assessment indicates that control emphasis should remain on:

- Identification of critical financial jobs and interfaces.
- Monitoring of scheduled jobs and interface processing.
- Timely resolution of failures and exceptions.
- Reconciliation of transferred data where appropriate.
- Escalation of incidents affecting financial systems.
- Backup monitoring and recovery readiness.

#### Third-Party Reliance

The organisation relies on third-party providers for [SaaS applications / cloud hosting / managed services / payroll processing / payment processing]. Where third-party services support financially relevant systems or data, management remains responsible for evaluating the provider’s control environment and performing internal complementary responsibilities.

The assessment indicates that control emphasis should remain on:

- Obtaining and reviewing current third-party control reports.
- Assessing report scope, period covered, exceptions, and subservice providers.
- Obtaining bridge letters where report coverage does not align to the reporting period.
- Performing complementary user responsibilities.
- Evaluating vendor incidents, service changes, and contract changes.
- Documenting management’s conclusion on reliance.
