| Interfaces | [Description of financially relevant inbound and outbound data flows] |
| Reports | [Description of key financial, reconciliation, operational, or management reports generated by the system] |
| Automated Controls | [Description of automated approvals, validations, calculations, limits, workflows, or system-enforced rules] |
| Manual Dependencies | [Description of manual reconciliations, reviews, approvals, or exception handling that mitigate system risk] |

The primary financial reporting risk is that deficiencies in implementation controls could result in inaccurate data migration, unauthorised configuration changes, excessive access, incomplete transaction processing, or unreliable reporting. The risk level is increased where controls have not yet been evidenced, where exceptions remain unresolved, or where post-go-live monitoring is not sufficiently defined.

### Readiness Analysis by Risk Theme

| Risk Theme | Analysis | Residual Risk |
|---|---|---|
| Change Governance | [Assess whether changes are authorised, tested, segregated, and deployed through controlled procedures.] | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical] |
| Logical Access | [Assess whether access is approved, role-based, least-privilege, and properly controlled for privileged users.] | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical] |
| Segregation of Duties | [Assess whether conflicting roles have been removed, mitigated, or formally accepted.] | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical] |
| Data Migration | [Assess whether migrated data is complete, accurate, reconciled, and approved.] | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical / Not Applicable] |
| Interfaces | [Assess whether interfaces are tested, monitored, reconciled, and recoverable.] | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical / Not Applicable] |
| Key Reports | [Assess whether report logic is validated and protected from unauthorised change.] | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical / Not Applicable] |
| IT Operations | [Assess whether the system can be supported after go-live through documented monitoring, backup, incident, and escalation procedures.] | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical] |
| Third-Party Dependency | [Assess whether external provider responsibilities, access, and assurance have been reviewed.] | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical / Not Applicable] |

### Go-Live Decision Analysis

The appropriate go-live decision should be based on the following criteria:

| Decision Option | Conditions |
|---|---|
| Proceed | No critical or high findings remain open; medium and low findings have accountable owners and target remediation dates; evidence is sufficient to support SOX readiness |
| Proceed with Conditions | One or more high or medium findings remain open but compensating controls, monitoring, and management acceptance are documented; unresolved items do not create an unacceptable risk of material financial reporting error |
| Defer Go-Live | Critical findings remain open, high-risk issues lack compensating controls, financial data cannot be reconciled, privileged access is uncontrolled, testing is incomplete for key processes, or operational support is not ready |

Based on the current findings and evidence, the recommended decision is **[Proceed / Proceed with Conditions / Defer Go-Live]**.

If go-live proceeds with conditions, management should formally approve the residual risk, document compensating controls, and require daily or weekly tracking of open actions until closure.

### Residual Risk Assessment

| Residual Risk | Rating | Rationale | Acceptance Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unauthorised changes after go-live | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical] | [Rationale] | [Yes / No] |
| Excessive or inappropriate access | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical] | [Rationale] | [Yes / No] |
| Inaccurate migrated data | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical / Not Applicable] | [Rationale] | [Yes / No] |
| Incomplete or failed interfaces | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical / Not Applicable] | [Rationale] | [Yes / No] |
| Unreliable key financial reports | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical / Not Applicable] | [Rationale] | [Yes / No] |
| Inadequate operational monitoring | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical] | [Rationale] | [Yes / No] |
| Incomplete audit evidence | [Low / Moderate / High / Critical] | [Rationale] | [Yes / No] |

### Conditions for Go-Live, if Applicable

If the decision is to proceed with conditions, the following conditions must be satisfied:

| Condition | Required Before Go-Live? | Owner | Evidence Required | Due Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Condition 1] | [Yes / No] | [Owner] | [Evidence] | [Date] |
| [Condition 2] | [Yes / No] | [Owner] | [Evidence] | [Date] |
| [Condition 3] | [Yes / No] | [Owner] | [Evidence] | [Date] |

## Recommendations & Actions

### Management Action Plan

| Action ID | Recommendation / Required Action | Related Finding | Priority | Owner | Due Date | Status | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACT-001 | [Action description] | [Finding 1] | [Critical / High / Medium / Low] | [Owner] | [Date] | [Open / In Progress / Closed] | [Evidence required] |
| ACT-002 | [Action description] | [Finding 2] | [Critical / High / Medium / Low] | [Owner] | [Date] | [Open / In Progress / Closed] | [Evidence required] |
| ACT-003 | [Action description] | [Finding 3] | [Critical / High / Medium / Low] | [Owner] | [Date] | [Open / In Progress / Closed] | [Evidence required] |

### Required Pre-Go-Live Actions

The following actions must be completed before production deployment unless formally approved as residual risk by authorised management:

| Required Action | Reason | Accountable Owner | Evidence Required | Completion Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Confirm final production access list and remove unnecessary implementation access | Prevent excessive or inappropriate access at go-live | [Identity and Access Owner] | Approved access listing and removal evidence | [Date] |
| Obtain formal approval of deployment and rollback plan | Confirm controlled production implementation and recovery path | [Change Manager] | Approved change record and cutover plan | [Date] |
| Complete business sign-off for key testing and unresolved defects | Confirm system supports intended financial processes | [Business Process Owner] | UAT sign-off and defect disposition approval | [Date] |
| Complete data migration reconciliation and exception approval | Confirm migrated data is complete and accurate | [Data Migration Owner] | Reconciliation reports and business approval | [Date] |
| Confirm interface monitoring and escalation procedures | Detect and correct failed or incomplete financial data flows | [Integration Owner] | Monitoring procedure and support assignment | [Date] |
| Confirm backup and restore readiness | Support recovery from implementation or operational failure | [Infrastructure / Cloud Operations Owner] | Backup configuration and restore readiness evidence | [Date] |
| Confirm hypercare support and emergency change process | Ensure issues are handled quickly and under control | [Service Owner] | Hypercare plan and emergency change workflow | [Date] |

### Post-Go-Live Actions

The following actions should be tracked after implementation:

| Action | Timing | Owner | Expected Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Perform first post-go-live privileged access review | Within [number] business days after go-live | [Access Control Owner] | Reviewed privileged access listing and remediation evidence |
| Perform first user access recertification for financially relevant roles | Within [number] days after go-live | [Business Role Owners] | Certified access review results |
| Review emergency changes raised during hypercare | Weekly during hypercare | [Change Manager] | Emergency change log, approvals, and retrospective reviews |
| Monitor interface failures and reconciliations | Daily for first [number] business days | [Integration Owner] | Monitoring logs and reconciliation evidence |
| Review data migration exceptions and financial reconciliations | At first close cycle after go-live | [Finance Process Owner] | Reconciliation results and exception resolution |
| Validate key financial reports in production | Before reliance in financial close or reporting | [Report Owner] | Production validation and approval evidence |
| Confirm control operation evidence is retained | Throughout first reporting cycle | [Control Owners] | Evidence repository with complete control records |
| Conduct post-implementation review | Within [number] days after go-live | [IT GRC / Project Sponsor] | Post-implementation review report |

### Recommended Go-Live Approval Record

The following approval record should be completed before final production deployment:

| Approval Role | Name | Decision | Date | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | [Name] | [Approve / Approve with Conditions / Reject] | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Finance Process Owner | [Name] | [Approve / Approve with Conditions / Reject] | [Date] | [Comments] |
| IT System Owner | [Name] | [Approve / Approve with Conditions / Reject] | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Information Security Owner | [Name] | [Approve / Approve with Conditions / Reject] | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Change Manager | [Name] | [Approve / Approve with Conditions / Reject] | [Date] | [Comments] |
| IT Operations Owner | [Name] | [Approve / Approve with Conditions / Reject] | [Date] | [Comments] |
| SOX / IT GRC Lead | [Name] | [Approve / Approve with Conditions / Reject] | [Date] | [Comments] |
| Internal Audit Observer, if applicable | [Name] | [Noted / Comments Provided] | [Date] | [Comments] |

### Risk Acceptance, if Applicable

Where management elects to proceed with unresolved high or critical items, formal risk acceptance is required before go-live.

| Risk Accepted | Business Justification | Compensating Controls | Approver | Expiry / Review Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Risk] | [Justification] | [Controls] | [Approver] | [Date] |

Risk acceptance must:

- Be approved by a sufficiently senior business and IT executive.
- Include a clear description of the unresolved risk.
- Identify compensating controls and monitoring activities.
- Define the remediation owner and target completion date.
- Expire automatically if remediation is not completed by the agreed date.
- Be retained with the project and SOX evidence repository.

### Evidence Retention Requirements

All evidence supporting this review must be retained in the approved repository for the required retention period. Evidence must be complete, traceable, and accessible for management review, external audit, and internal assurance activities.

Required retained evidence includes:

- Final signed version of this report.
- Management action plan and status updates.
- Final go-live approval record.
- Risk acceptance approvals, if applicable.
- Change approval and deployment evidence.
- Testing and business sign-off evidence.
- Access review and provisioning evidence.
- Privileged access approval and monitoring evidence.
- Data migration reconciliation and approval evidence.
- Interface monitoring and reconciliation evidence.
- Key report validation evidence.
- Operational readiness and hypercare evidence.
- Post-go-live review evidence.

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution

This report is intended for authorised internal stakeholders with responsibility for SOX compliance, financial reporting, system ownership, implementation governance, and operational readiness.

| Recipient Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | Go-live decision and risk acceptance |
| Finance Leadership | Financial reporting impact assessment and business approval |
| IT Leadership | System readiness and remediation oversight |
| System Owner | Accountability for control readiness and ongoing operation |
| Business Process Owners | Validation of process readiness, reports, reconciliations, and access |
| IT Governance, Risk and Compliance | SOX readiness oversight and evidence retention |
| Information Security | Access, privileged account, logging, and security configuration oversight |
| Change Management | Deployment approval and release governance |
| IT Operations / Service Management | Production support and operational readiness |
| Internal Audit | Independent review planning and advisory visibility |
| External Audit, if authorised | Audit evidence and SOX reliance planning |

### Confidentiality

This report is classified as **Confidential - Internal Use Only**. It may contain sensitive information regarding system controls, access rights, security configuration, implementation risks, audit evidence, financial reporting dependencies, and unresolved control gaps.

Recipients must:

- Use the report only for authorised governance, compliance, audit, remediation, and go-live decision purposes.
- Not distribute the report outside the approved recipient list without written approval from [Document Owner / SOX Lead].
- Store the report only in approved repositories with access restricted to authorised personnel.
- Avoid forwarding the report through unsecured channels.
- Redact sensitive system, access, or security details before any approved external distribution.
- Retain the report and supporting evidence in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.

### External Sharing

External sharing is permitted only where:

- The request is related to audit, regulatory, legal, or contractual obligations.
- Approval is obtained from [Authorised Approver].
- Sensitive operational details are redacted where appropriate.
- The shared copy is logged, including recipient, purpose, date, and version.

### Report Integrity

This report must not be altered after issuance except through formal version control. Any updates to findings, actions, or go-live status after the report date must be recorded in an updated version or addendum and retained with the original report.

SOX-024.title: Vendor / SOC Reports (3rd-party financial systems)
SOX-024.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [SOX-ITGC-REP-004] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [SOX IT Compliance Owner] |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | SOX IT General Controls |
| Classification | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This report documents management’s review of third-party SOC 1 reports for outsourced technology services that support financial reporting, including systems, applications, infrastructure, and managed services relied upon by the organisation’s SOX IT general controls program.

The purpose of this report is to:

- Identify in-scope third-party service providers supporting financially relevant systems and processes.
- Confirm whether current SOC 1 reports have been obtained and reviewed.
- Evaluate the suitability of the SOC 1 report scope, audit period, opinion, control objectives, testing results, and user entity responsibilities.
- Identify exceptions, gaps, complementary user entity controls, subservice organisation dependencies, and carve-outs that may affect financial reporting reliance.
- Document management’s conclusions regarding whether outsourced ITGCs may be relied upon for the reporting period.
- Define remediation actions, compensating controls, and follow-up activities where reliance is limited or unsupported.

This report is intended to support management’s SOX assessment, external audit coordination, vendor risk oversight, and evidence retention for outsourced ITGCs.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

This report covers the SOX reporting period from **[Start Date]** to **[End Date]**.

SOC 1 reports were assessed for relevance to the organisation’s financial reporting reliance during the reporting period. Where a SOC 1 report period did not fully align with the SOX reporting period, bridge letters, management attestations, or complementary internal controls were evaluated.

### In-Scope Vendor Services

The review includes third-party vendors that provide applications, platforms, infrastructure, hosting, managed operations, or other IT services that support financial systems or processes relevant to the organisation’s financial statements.

In-scope services include, as applicable:

- Financial close, consolidation, and reporting platforms.
- Enterprise resource planning applications.
- Payroll processing platforms.
- Revenue, billing, invoicing, and receivables platforms.
- Procurement, payables, and expense management platforms.
- Cloud hosting or managed infrastructure supporting financially relevant applications.
- Managed database, access administration, batch processing, backup, or change deployment services.
- External service providers performing control activities on behalf of management.

### In-Scope Vendors Reviewed

| Vendor / Service Provider | Service / System Supported | Financial Reporting Relevance | SOC 1 Report Obtained | Report Period Covered | Report Type | Review Status |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [Vendor 1] | [ERP Hosting / Managed Services] | High | Yes | [Date] to [Date] | Type 2 | Complete |
| [Vendor 2] | [Payroll Processing Platform] | High | Yes | [Date] to [Date] | Type 2 | Complete |
| [Vendor 3] | [Revenue Billing System] | High | Yes | [Date] to [Date] | Type 2 | Complete |
| [Vendor 4] | [Financial Reporting Tool] | Medium | Yes | [Date] to [Date] | Type 2 | Complete |
| [Vendor 5] | [Cloud Infrastructure Provider] | Medium | Yes | [Date] to [Date] | Type 2 | Complete |
| [Vendor 6] | [Managed Database Services] | Medium | Pending | [Date] to [Date] | Type 2 | In Progress |

### Out-of-Scope Areas

The following areas were not included in this report unless explicitly noted:

- SOC 2 reports, except where reviewed as supporting context for security, availability, or confidentiality controls that indirectly support SOX-relevant systems.
- Vendor financial condition, contract pricing, or commercial performance.
- Operational service-level performance unless it directly affects ITGC reliance.
- Business process controls performed by vendors unless included in a SOC 1 report and relevant to financial reporting.
- Vendors that do not support systems, interfaces, data, or operations relevant to financial reporting.

## Executive Summary

Management reviewed SOC 1 reports for third-party service providers supporting financially relevant systems and outsourced ITGC activities. The review focused on whether the reports provide sufficient evidence to support reliance on vendor-operated controls for the SOX reporting period.

Overall, the reviewed SOC 1 reports provide a reasonable basis for reliance on outsourced ITGCs for the majority of in-scope vendors, subject to completion of identified user entity controls and remediation of open findings. No report reviewed contained a qualified or adverse opinion. However, several matters require management attention, including timing gaps between SOC report coverage and the SOX year-end period, user entity control responsibilities requiring formal evidence, and subservice organisation carve-outs requiring additional assessment.

### Overall Conclusion

| Area | Conclusion |
|---|---|
| SOC 1 report availability | Current SOC 1 reports were obtained for most in-scope vendors. One report remains pending and requires follow-up. |
| Report suitability | Reports generally align to services used by the organisation and include ITGC areas relevant to financial reporting. |
| Auditor opinion | No adverse or qualified opinions were identified in the reports reviewed. |
| Control exceptions | Exceptions were noted in selected vendor reports; none currently indicate a material inability to rely, but management action is required. |
| User entity responsibilities | Several complementary user controls must be documented and evidenced internally. |
| Coverage gaps | Bridge letters or management representations are required where report periods do not cover the full SOX assessment period. |
| Reliance decision | Conditional reliance is supported for most vendors, pending completion of required actions. |

### Key Findings Summary

| Finding ID | Vendor | Finding Theme | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | [Vendor 1] | SOC report period does not fully cover SOX year-end | Medium | Open |
| F-02 | [Vendor 2] | Complementary user entity controls not fully evidenced | Medium | Open |
| F-03 | [Vendor 3] | Vendor access review exception noted in SOC report | Medium | Open |
| F-04 | [Vendor 4] | Subservice organisation carved out of SOC report | Medium | Open |
| F-05 | [Vendor 6] | SOC 1 report not yet received | High | Open |
| F-06 | [Vendor 5] | No significant exceptions identified | Low | Closed |

### Management Assessment

Based on the review performed, management has determined that:

- Reliance on outsourced ITGCs is appropriate where SOC 1 reports were current, relevant, unqualified, and exceptions did not undermine control effectiveness.
- Reliance is conditional where bridge letters, user entity control evidence, or remediation follow-up remains outstanding.
- Reliance should not be finalised for vendors where SOC 1 reports have not been received or where report scope does not sufficiently cover the services used by the organisation.
- Action owners must complete remediation and evidence collection before SOX year-end control reliance is formally concluded.

## Methodology

The SOC 1 review was performed using a standardised SOX ITGC vendor assessment approach. Each report was evaluated for relevance, completeness, timing, control coverage, test results, exceptions, management responses, subservice organisation dependencies, and user entity responsibilities.

### Review Steps Performed

| Step | Review Activity | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vendor population validation | Confirmed vendors supporting financially relevant systems through application inventory, SOX scoping, procurement records, and vendor risk data. |
| 2 | SOC 1 report request | Requested current SOC 1 reports, bridge letters, and related management attestations from vendors or internal vendor owners. |
| 3 | Report authenticity check | Confirmed reports were issued by an independent service auditor and were complete, final, and not restricted to unrelated services. |
| 4 | Scope assessment | Compared report scope to the specific services, systems, locations, and control activities used by the organisation. |
| 5 | Period coverage assessment | Compared report coverage period to the organisation’s SOX reporting period and identified any gap periods. |
| 6 | Opinion review | Reviewed service auditor opinion and management assertion for adverse, qualified, or disclaimed conclusions. |
| 7 | Control objective mapping | Mapped relevant vendor control objectives to ITGC domains relied upon by the organisation. |
| 8 | Exception analysis | Reviewed test exceptions, deviation descriptions, population impact, management responses, and remediation status. |
| 9 | User entity control evaluation | Identified complementary user entity controls and assessed whether internal control evidence exists. |
| 10 | Subservice organisation assessment | Identified carve-outs and inclusive subservice organisations and assessed additional reliance needs. |
| 11 | Reliance conclusion | Determined whether controls may be relied upon, conditionally relied upon, or not relied upon for SOX purposes. |
| 12 | Action tracking | Documented open actions, owners, due dates, and required evidence. |

### Assessment Criteria

The following criteria were applied when evaluating each SOC 1 report:

- The report is a SOC 1 Type 2 report for the relevant service period.
- The report covers the services, applications, infrastructure, or operations used by the organisation.
- The report period overlaps substantially with the organisation’s SOX assessment period.
- Any gap between the report end date and the SOX reporting date is supported by a bridge letter or other appropriate evidence.
- The service auditor opinion does not indicate pervasive deficiencies.
- Control objectives and controls are relevant to financial reporting reliance.
- Exceptions are understood, assessed for impact, and remediated or compensated where necessary.
- Complementary user entity controls are identified, owned, and evidenced internally.
- Subservice organisations are reviewed where their controls are necessary to support reliance.
- Report restrictions are respected, and distribution is limited to authorised personnel.

### ITGC Areas Considered

SOC 1 reports were evaluated for outsourced controls in the following ITGC areas where applicable:

| ITGC Area | Relevant Vendor Control Activities Reviewed |
|---|---|
| Logical access | User provisioning, privileged access, access reviews, password configuration, authentication, termination processing |
| Change management | Change approval, testing, segregation of duties, migration to production, emergency changes |
| Computer operations | Job monitoring, incident management, backups, recovery, batch processing, interface monitoring |
| System development | Development lifecycle controls, testing, production migration, project governance |
| Data processing integrity | Transaction processing, file transfers, reconciliations, error handling, interface completeness |
| Security monitoring | Logging, alert review, vulnerability management, intrusion monitoring where relevant to financial systems |
| Physical and environmental controls | Data centre access, environmental safeguards, media protection where relevant to hosted services |
| Business continuity | Backup restoration, disaster recovery testing, recovery governance where required for financial reporting continuity |

## Detailed Findings / Results (with structure)

### Vendor SOC 1 Review Results

| Vendor | Report Obtained | Report Period Alignment | Opinion / Conclusion | Exceptions Noted | User Entity Controls Required | Subservice Considerations | Reliance Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Vendor 1] | Yes | Partial coverage; bridge required | Unmodified | Limited exceptions | Yes | None material | Conditional reliance |
| [Vendor 2] | Yes | Full coverage | Unmodified | No material exceptions | Yes | Carve-out noted | Conditional reliance |
| [Vendor 3] | Yes | Full coverage | Unmodified | Access review exception | Yes | None material | Conditional reliance |
| [Vendor 4] | Yes | Partial coverage; bridge required | Unmodified | No significant exceptions | Yes | Subservice carved out | Conditional reliance |
| [Vendor 5] | Yes | Full coverage | Unmodified | No significant exceptions | Limited | Inclusive method used | Reliance supported |
| [Vendor 6] | No | Not assessed | Not assessed | Not assessed | Unknown | Unknown | Reliance not yet supported |

---

### Finding F-01 - SOC Report Period Does Not Fully Cover SOX Year-End

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor | [Vendor 1] |
| Service / System | [ERP Hosting / Managed Services] |
| Finding Type | Period coverage gap |
| Severity | Medium |
| Status | Open |
| Owner | [Vendor Owner / SOX IT Compliance Owner] |
| Target Resolution Date | [Date] |

#### Condition

The SOC 1 report for [Vendor 1] covers the period from [Date] to [Date], which does not fully cover the organisation’s SOX reporting period through [Year-End Date]. A gap exists from [Date] to [Date].

#### Risk

Controls operated by the vendor during the gap period may not be independently tested. Without additional evidence, management may not have sufficient basis to rely on the vendor’s ITGCs for the full SOX period.

#### Impact

The affected areas may include:

- Logical access administration for the hosted financial system.
- Production change management.
- Backup and job monitoring.
- Incident response and operational controls.

#### Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Date Reviewed | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| SOC 1 Type 2 report | [Date] | Report obtained and reviewed |
| Vendor bridge letter | [Date] | Not yet received |
| Vendor management representation | [Date] | Requested |
| Internal monitoring evidence | [Date] | Partially available |

#### Management Conclusion

Reliance is conditional pending receipt and review of a bridge letter covering the gap period. If a bridge letter is not received, management must perform additional procedures, such as obtaining vendor attestations, reviewing complementary internal monitoring controls, or limiting reliance on vendor-operated controls.

---

### Finding F-02 - Complementary User Entity Controls Not Fully Evidenced

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor | [Vendor 2] |
| Service / System | [Payroll Processing Platform] |
| Finding Type | User entity control evidence gap |
| Severity | Medium |
| Status | Open |
| Owner | [Payroll Control Owner / SOX Control Owner] |
| Target Resolution Date | [Date] |

#### Condition

The SOC 1 report identifies complementary user entity controls that must be performed by the organisation for the vendor’s controls to operate effectively. Evidence was not complete for all required internal responsibilities.

#### Required User Entity Controls

| User Entity Control Responsibility | Internal Owner | Evidence Status | Required Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Timely notification of employee terminations | [HR Operations Owner] | Complete | Termination report and access removal evidence |
| Review of payroll system user access | [Payroll Manager] | Incomplete | Quarterly access review certification |
| Approval of payroll configuration changes | [Payroll Systems Owner] | Incomplete | Approved change tickets |
| Validation of payroll input and output files | [Payroll Operations Owner] | Complete | Reconciliation evidence |
| Review of exception reports | [Payroll Manager] | Partial | Exception report review sign-off |

#### Risk

If user entity controls are not performed or evidenced, vendor controls may not fully address risks to payroll processing, access appropriateness, or financial reporting completeness and accuracy.

#### Impact

Management may be unable to rely on vendor controls unless the organisation can demonstrate that its own responsibilities were performed consistently during the period.

#### Management Conclusion

Reliance is conditional. Internal control owners must provide complete evidence for all required user entity controls before final SOX reliance is concluded.

---

### Finding F-03 - Vendor Access Review Exception Noted in SOC Report

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor | [Vendor 3] |
| Service / System | [Revenue Billing System] |
| Finding Type | Vendor control exception |
| Severity | Medium |
| Status | Open |
| Owner | [Application Owner / Vendor Manager] |
| Target Resolution Date | [Date] |

#### Condition

The SOC 1 report identified an exception related to periodic access reviews. The service auditor noted that for a sample of privileged users, evidence of timely review or approval was not available.

#### Risk

Inadequate review of privileged access may increase the risk of unauthorised changes to billing configuration, revenue data, user permissions, or system processing rules.

#### Impact Assessment

| Factor | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Control area affected | Logical access |
| User type affected | Privileged vendor users |
| Financial reporting relevance | High |
| Population impact | Limited based on report details |
| Compensating controls | Internal review of organisation-managed users; vendor access restriction process |
| Residual risk | Moderate until remediation evidence is obtained |

#### Evidence Reviewed

- SOC 1 exception description.
- Vendor management response.
- Vendor remediation statement.
- Internal access review evidence for organisation-managed accounts.
- Access listing provided by [Vendor 3], where available.

#### Management Conclusion

The exception does not automatically preclude reliance, but additional follow-up is required. Management must obtain vendor remediation evidence or a written confirmation that the access review process was corrected and operated effectively after remediation.

---

### Finding F-04 - Subservice Organisation Carved Out of SOC Report

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor | [Vendor 4] |
| Service / System | [Financial Reporting Tool] |
| Finding Type | Subservice organisation carve-out |
| Severity | Medium |
| Status | Open |
| Owner | [Vendor Risk Manager / System Owner] |
| Target Resolution Date | [Date] |

#### Condition

The SOC 1 report for [Vendor 4] excludes certain control activities performed by a subservice organisation that supports hosting, infrastructure, security monitoring, or data processing services.

#### Risk

Controls performed by the subservice organisation may be necessary to support reliance on the outsourced service. If those controls are not reviewed, management may have an incomplete view of the end-to-end ITGC environment.

#### Impact

Potential affected control areas include:

- Data centre and hosting controls.
- Network and infrastructure security.
- Backup and recovery operations.
- Logical access to infrastructure components.
- Change management for hosted environments.

#### Required Follow-Up

| Required Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Identify carved-out subservice organisation and services provided | [Vendor Owner] | [Date] | Open |
| Determine whether subservice controls are relevant to SOX reliance | [SOX IT Compliance Owner] | [Date] | Open |
| Obtain subservice SOC 1 or other suitable assurance report if required | [Vendor Risk Manager] | [Date] | Open |
| Document compensating controls if report is unavailable | [System Owner] | [Date] | Open |

#### Management Conclusion

Reliance is conditional until management determines whether the carved-out subservice organisation performs controls required to support financial reporting reliance.

---

### Finding F-05 - SOC 1 Report Not Yet Received

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor | [Vendor 6] |
| Service / System | [Managed Database Services] |
| Finding Type | Missing assurance report |
| Severity | High |
| Status | Open |
| Owner | [Vendor Manager] |
| Target Resolution Date | [Date] |

#### Condition

A current SOC 1 report has not yet been received for [Vendor 6]. The vendor supports services used by [Financial System], which is relevant to financial reporting.

#### Risk

Without a current SOC 1 report or equivalent evidence, management may be unable to assess whether outsourced ITGCs operated effectively during the SOX reporting period.

#### Impact

The absence of a report may affect reliance on:

- Database access controls.
- Privileged administration.
- Change deployment support.
- Backup monitoring.
- Incident management.
- Service availability for financial close activities.

#### Interim Procedures

Until the SOC 1 report is obtained, management should perform the following interim procedures:

| Procedure | Owner | Evidence Required | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Obtain vendor management assertion over relevant controls | [Vendor Manager] | Signed attestation | Open |
| Request listing of privileged vendor administrators | [System Owner] | Access listing and review evidence | Open |
| Review internal monitoring of vendor change tickets | [Application Owner] | Approved change records | Open |
| Confirm backup and recovery monitoring responsibilities | [Infrastructure Owner] | Backup monitoring evidence | Open |
| Assess incident history during reporting period | [IT Operations Owner] | Incident report and review sign-off | Open |

#### Management Conclusion

Reliance is not currently supported. Final reliance requires receipt and review of the SOC 1 report or completion of sufficient alternative procedures approved by SOX management and, where applicable, aligned with external audit expectations.

---

### Finding F-06 - No Significant Exceptions Identified

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor | [Vendor 5] |
| Service / System | [Cloud Infrastructure Provider] |
| Finding Type | No significant exception |
| Severity | Low |
| Status | Closed |
| Owner | [Cloud Platform Owner] |
| Target Resolution Date | Not applicable |

#### Condition

The SOC 1 report was obtained, reviewed, and found to be relevant to the services used by the organisation. The report period aligns with the SOX reporting period, and no exceptions were identified that affect reliance on relevant outsourced ITGCs.

#### Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Result |
|---|---|
| SOC 1 Type 2 report | Complete and current |
| Report scope | Relevant to services used |
| Auditor opinion | Unmodified |
| Exceptions | No significant exceptions affecting reliance |
| Subservice organisations | Included or not relevant to SOX reliance |
| User entity controls | Limited and addressed internally |

#### Management Conclusion

Reliance is supported for relevant vendor-operated controls, subject to continued performance of internal monitoring and user entity responsibilities.

## Analysis

### Overall SOC 1 Coverage

The review indicates that the organisation has established a functioning process to obtain and evaluate SOC 1 reports for third-party providers supporting financial reporting. Most high-risk vendors have current SOC 1 reports available, and the reports generally cover logical access, change management, operations, and security controls relevant to SOX ITGC reliance.

However, the process requires continued attention in the following areas:

- Timely collection of reports before SOX testing and year-end reliance deadlines.
- Formal tracking of report period gaps and bridge letter requirements.
- Consistent mapping of complementary user entity controls to internal SOX control evidence.
- Review of subservice organisation carve-outs where vendor services depend on third-party infrastructure or processing.
- Documentation of management’s reliance conclusion for each vendor.

### Report Period Alignment

SOC 1 reporting periods rarely align perfectly with the organisation’s SOX reporting period. Where reports end before SOX year-end, management must obtain bridge letters or perform additional procedures covering the gap. Period gaps are not necessarily control failures, but unresolved gaps may reduce the evidence available to support reliance.

| Coverage Scenario | Management Response |
|---|---|
| SOC 1 period fully covers SOX period | Reliance may be supported if scope and results are acceptable |
| SOC 1 period covers most but not all of SOX period | Obtain bridge letter or perform gap-period procedures |
| SOC 1 period is outdated | Request current report and consider alternative procedures |
| SOC 1 report unavailable | Reliance not supported until sufficient evidence is obtained |
| Report scope does not match services used | Determine whether other evidence is required or reliance should be limited |

### Complementary User Entity Controls

SOC 1 reports commonly assume that the user organisation performs certain controls. These controls are not optional; they are necessary for the vendor’s controls to be effective in the organisation’s environment.

Common responsibilities identified across reports include:

- Approving and periodically reviewing user access.
- Notifying vendors promptly of user terminations and role changes.
- Restricting privileged access requests to authorised personnel.
- Reviewing system-generated reports and processing exceptions.
- Reconciling input and output files.
- Approving configuration and master data changes.
- Monitoring vendor service issues and incidents.
- Maintaining internal policies and procedures for system use.

Where these responsibilities are not evidenced, the organisation’s ability to rely on the vendor’s controls may be impaired even if the vendor’s SOC 1 report is otherwise clean.

### Exception Severity Assessment

SOC 1 exceptions were assessed based on nature, frequency, population impact, financial reporting relevance, and whether compensating controls exist.

| Severity | Description | Typical Management Response |
|---|---|---|
| High | Exception affects a key outsourced control and may materially impact reliance | Do not rely until remediated or alternative procedures are completed |
| Medium | Exception affects a relevant control but appears limited or compensating controls may exist | Conditional reliance with follow-up and documented mitigation |
| Low | Exception does not affect controls relied upon or has minimal impact | Reliance may continue with monitoring |
| Informational | Observation does not indicate control failure but may improve oversight | Track as improvement item |

### Subservice Organisation Considerations

Subservice organisations may perform controls that are important to the vendor’s service delivery. If such organisations are carved out of the vendor’s SOC 1 report, management must determine whether their controls are relevant to SOX reliance.

Examples include:

- Cloud infrastructure providers hosting financial systems.
- Data centre operators supporting vendor applications.
- Payment processors supporting transaction flows.
- Managed security providers monitoring vendor environments.
- Third-party database or platform administrators.

Where relevant subservice controls are not included in the vendor’s report, management should obtain additional assurance reports, vendor confirmations, or evidence of compensating controls.

### Reliance Determination Summary

| Reliance Category | Vendors | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Reliance supported | [Vendor 5] | Report obtained, relevant scope, acceptable period, no significant exceptions, user entity controls addressed |
| Conditional reliance | [Vendor 1], [Vendor 2], [Vendor 3], [Vendor 4] | Report obtained but follow-up required for gap period, user controls, exceptions, or subservice carve-outs |
| Reliance not yet supported | [Vendor 6] | SOC 1 report not received or sufficient alternative evidence not yet available |

## Recommendations & Actions

### Priority Recommendations

Management should complete the following actions before finalising SOX reliance on outsourced ITGCs:

1. Obtain all outstanding SOC 1 reports and bridge letters.
2. Complete documented reviews for each in-scope report using a standard review template.
3. Map all complementary user entity controls to internal SOX controls and evidence.
4. Obtain remediation evidence for SOC 1 exceptions that affect relevant ITGCs.
5. Review subservice organisation carve-outs and obtain additional assurance where needed.
6. Document formal reliance conclusions for each vendor.
7. Escalate unresolved high-risk gaps to SOX leadership and external audit stakeholders.
8. Maintain a central repository for SOC reports, bridge letters, reviews, conclusions, and related evidence.

### Action Plan

| Action ID | Action | Priority | Owner | Due Date | Required Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| A-01 | Obtain bridge letter for [Vendor 1] covering [Date] to [Date] | High | [Vendor Owner] | [Date] | Signed bridge letter | Open |
| A-02 | Complete evidence collection for payroll user entity controls | High | [Payroll Control Owner] | [Date] | Access review, change approvals, reconciliations | Open |
| A-03 | Obtain remediation evidence for [Vendor 3] access review exception | Medium | [Application Owner] | [Date] | Vendor remediation confirmation | Open |
| A-04 | Assess [Vendor 4] subservice carve-out and obtain additional report if required | Medium | [Vendor Risk Manager] | [Date] | Subservice assessment and report | Open |
| A-05 | Obtain current SOC 1 report for [Vendor 6] | High | [Vendor Manager] | [Date] | SOC 1 report and completed review | Open |
| A-06 | Perform alternative procedures for [Vendor 6] if report is delayed | High | [SOX IT Compliance Owner] | [Date] | Alternative testing evidence | Open |
| A-07 | Finalise reliance conclusions for all vendors | High | [SOX IT Compliance Owner] | [Date] | Signed reliance summary | Open |
| A-08 | Update vendor SOC 1 tracking register | Medium | [GRC Analyst] | [Date] | Updated tracker | Open |

### Required Evidence Package

For each in-scope vendor, the evidence package should include:

| Evidence Item | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Current SOC 1 Type 2 report | Yes | Must cover relevant services used by the organisation |
| Bridge letter | If applicable | Required where report period does not cover SOX year-end |
| SOC report review checklist | Yes | Must document scope, period, opinion, exceptions, and conclusion |
| Complementary user entity control mapping | Yes | Must identify internal owners and related evidence |
| Exception impact assessment | If applicable | Required for any relevant SOC 1 exception |
| Subservice organisation assessment | If applicable | Required where subservice controls are carved out or critical |
| Vendor remediation evidence | If applicable | Required where exceptions affect reliance |
| Management reliance conclusion | Yes | Must be approved by SOX IT Compliance Owner |
| External audit correspondence | If applicable | Retain where reliance approach was discussed |

### Escalation Criteria

Issues should be escalated to [SOX Program Lead], [Controller], [CIO], or [Audit Committee Liaison] when any of the following occur:

- A high-risk vendor does not provide a current SOC 1 report.
- A SOC 1 report contains a qualified, adverse, or otherwise concerning opinion.
- Exceptions affect key outsourced controls without effective remediation.
- Required user entity controls were not performed or cannot be evidenced.
- A significant subservice organisation is carved out and no additional assurance is available.
- Vendor management refuses to provide sufficient assurance evidence.
- External audit raises concerns regarding reliance on outsourced controls.
- Remediation will not be completed before SOX year-end reporting deadlines.

### Target Completion Timeline

| Milestone | Target Date | Owner |
|---|---:|---|
| Confirm in-scope vendor population | [Date] | [SOX IT Compliance Owner] |
| Obtain SOC 1 reports and bridge letters | [Date] | [Vendor Owners] |
| Complete SOC 1 reviews | [Date] | [GRC Analyst / SOX IT Team] |
| Complete user entity control evidence collection | [Date] | [Control Owners] |
| Complete exception and carve-out assessments | [Date] | [SOX IT Compliance Owner] |
| Finalise management reliance conclusions | [Date] | [SOX Program Lead] |
| Provide evidence package to external audit | [Date] | [SOX IT Compliance Owner] |

## Distribution & Confidentiality

This report contains confidential information regarding third-party control environments, vendor assurance reports, financial systems, SOX control reliance, and internal control assessments. Distribution must be limited to personnel with a legitimate business need.

### Approved Distribution

| Recipient Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [SOX Program Lead] | Oversight of SOX control reliance and remediation |
| [SOX IT Compliance Team] | Review, evidence management, and action tracking |
| [System Owners] | Resolution of system-specific findings |
| [Vendor Owners] | Vendor follow-up and assurance collection |
| [Finance Control Owners] | Completion of user entity controls |
| [Internal Audit] | Independent review and SOX coordination |
| [External Audit] | Audit reliance and evidence review |
| [Executive Management, as required] | Escalation of significant unresolved risks |

### Confidentiality Requirements

- SOC 1 reports and related vendor assurance materials must be handled in accordance with vendor confidentiality restrictions.
- Reports must not be forwarded outside approved distribution without authorisation from [Legal / Vendor Management / SOX Program Lead].
- SOC 1 reports must be stored only in approved repositories with restricted access.
- Extracts from SOC 1 reports should be limited to information necessary for SOX review and audit evidence.
- Vendor reports must not be uploaded to unauthorised collaboration tools, public repositories, or unmanaged storage locations.
- Any suspected unauthorised disclosure must be reported immediately to [Information Security Contact] and [Legal Contact].

### Retention

This report and supporting evidence must be retained in accordance with the organisation’s SOX evidence retention requirements and legal hold obligations. At a minimum, the retained evidence should include:

- Final version of this report.
- SOC 1 reports reviewed.
- Bridge letters and vendor attestations.
- Completed SOC report review checklists.
- User entity control evidence.
- Exception assessments and remediation evidence.
- Subservice organisation assessments.
- Final reliance conclusions and approvals.

SOX-025.title: Internal Audit ITGC Test Workpapers
SOX-025.content:
## What This Evidences

Internal Audit ITGC Test Workpapers evidence the internal audit team’s independent testing of the design and operating effectiveness of SOX IT general controls supporting financial reporting. This includes testing over access management, change management, computer operations, job scheduling, backups, incident handling, and privileged access, as applicable to the in-scope systems.

This artifact is collected, not authored as a standalone policy or narrative. The workpapers must be obtained from the organisation’s audit management platform, internal audit repository, or approved evidence storage location where actual test procedures, samples, results, exceptions, and reviewer approvals are maintained.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect from the organisation’s official internal audit evidence sources, typically:

- Audit management system: [Audit Management Tool]
- GRC platform: [GRC Platform]
- Internal audit SharePoint or document repository: [Repository Name]
- SOX testing workspace or audit binder: [SOX Workspace]
- Workpaper management tool: [Workpaper Tool]
- Supporting source systems referenced by the workpapers, where needed:
 - ITSM/change ticketing: [ITSM Tool]
 - Identity and access management: [IAM Tool]
 - Privileged access management: [PAM Tool]
 - SIEM/log management: [SIEM Tool]
 - Backup or job scheduling console: [Operations Tool]

## How To Collect

1. Confirm the audit period and in-scope SOX applications, infrastructure, databases, and ITGC controls with [SOX Owner/Internal Audit Lead].
2. Log in to [Audit Management Tool] or [SOX Workspace] using an account with read-only evidence access.
3. Navigate to the relevant audit engagement, such as `[FY YYYY SOX ITGC Testing]`.
4. Filter or search for ITGC workpapers by control area, system, process owner, or control ID used internally by the organisation.
5. Export or download the completed workpaper package for each in-scope ITGC, including:
 - Test plan or test script
 - Population used for testing
 - Sample selection
 - Evidence examined
 - Test results
 - Exception details
 - Reviewer sign-off
6. Where workpapers link to external evidence, open the referenced ticket, report, log extract, access listing, or screenshot in the source system and export it if it is not already embedded.
7. Confirm that each file includes preparer and reviewer information, testing dates, conclusion, and any remediation status.
8. Save the collected package to the approved SOX evidence repository using the organisation’s naming convention.
9. Record the collection date, collector name, audit period, source system, and file location in the evidence tracker.

## What To Capture

Capture enough detail to show both design and operating effectiveness testing, including:

- Audit engagement name and fiscal year or testing period
- Control name and internal control identifier
- In-scope system, application, database, platform, or infrastructure component
- Control objective or risk addressed
- Test procedure performed
- Population definition and source
- Population report or listing with extraction date
- Sample selection methodology and selected items
- Evidence reviewed for each sample
- Test result for each sample item
- Pass/fail conclusion for each control
- Identified exceptions, root cause, impact, and remediation status
- Management response, if applicable
- Retest evidence, if applicable
- Preparer name and preparation date
- Reviewer name, review date, and approval status
- Version history or audit trail from [Audit Management Tool]

## Frequency & Owner

- Frequency: At least annually for SOX year-end testing, with interim and roll-forward testing where applicable.
- Owner: Internal Audit or SOX Compliance team.
- Evidence collector: [SOX PMO/Evidence Coordinator].
- Review owner: [Internal Audit Manager] or [SOX ITGC Lead].
- Control owners provide supporting evidence but should not alter internal audit workpapers.

## Retention & Storage

Store collected workpapers in the approved SOX evidence repository: [SOX Evidence Repository].

Retention should align with the organisation’s SOX audit retention policy and legal hold requirements. Access must be restricted to Internal Audit, SOX Compliance, External Audit, and authorised control owners where appropriate.

Maintain files in read-only format where possible. Preserve system-generated timestamps, approval history, and audit trails. Do not overwrite prior versions; retain superseded files with clear version labels.

## Acceptance Criteria

Auditors generally accept the evidence as sufficient when:

- Workpapers are collected from the official audit or GRC system, not recreated manually.
- The testing period clearly matches the SOX audit period under review.
- Each in-scope ITGC has a completed test procedure and documented conclusion.
- Population and sample evidence are traceable to authoritative source systems.
- Test results support both design and operating effectiveness conclusions.
- Exceptions are clearly documented, evaluated, and remediated or risk-accepted.
- Preparer and independent reviewer sign-offs are present.
- Dates, systems, control owners, and sample details are complete and consistent.
- Evidence is retained in an approved repository with restricted access and version control.
- The package can be re-performed or traced from workpaper to source evidence without unsupported assumptions.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Deficiency ID | Enter a unique sequential identifier for the deficiency, e.g., ITGC-DEF-FY2026-001; do not reuse IDs. |
| Date Identified | Enter the date the deficiency was first identified in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Reporting Period / Fiscal Year | Enter the SOX reporting period or fiscal year impacted, e.g., FY2026, Q2 FY2026. |
| Source of Identification | Enter the source that identified the issue; allowed values: Management Testing, Internal Audit, External Audit, Control Owner Self-Assessment, Incident / Event, Regulatory Review, Other. |
| ITGC Domain | Enter the ITGC area impacted; allowed values: Access Management, Change Management, IT Operations, Program Development, Computer Operations, Cybersecurity, Third-Party / SOC Reliance, Other. |
| Application / System / Infrastructure Scope | Enter the specific in-scope SOX application, database, operating system, network device, job scheduler, interface, or infrastructure component affected. |
| Related SOX Process / Financial Statement Area | Enter the impacted business process or financial reporting area, e.g., Revenue, Inventory, Payroll, Financial Close, Treasury, General Ledger. |
| Control ID(s) Impacted | Enter the SOX control reference number(s) impacted, separated by semicolons, e.g., ITAC-01; ITGC-AM-03. |
| Control Objective Impacted | Enter the control objective that failed or was not fully achieved, e.g., only authorized users have privileged access to SOX systems. |
| Deficiency Title | Enter a short, specific title describing the deficiency, e.g., Incomplete quarterly privileged access review. |
| Deficiency Description | Enter a factual description of what failed, including condition, criteria, affected control, and why it represents a deficiency; avoid speculation. |
| Deficiency Type | Enter the nature of the issue; allowed values: Design Deficiency, Operating Effectiveness Deficiency, Missing Control, Insufficient Evidence, Scope Gap, Other. |
| Deficiency Classification | Enter the evaluated classification; allowed values: Inherent Deficiency, Control Deficiency, Significant Deficiency, Material Weakness. Use Significant Deficiency or Material Weakness only after formal evaluation under PCAOB AS 2201 and management/auditor assessment. |
| Severity Rationale | Enter the basis for classification, including likelihood, magnitude, affected accounts/disclosures, compensating controls, duration, and aggregation with other deficiencies. |
| Root Cause Category | Enter the primary cause; allowed values: Process Design, Control Execution, Insufficient Review, System Configuration, Access Governance, Change Governance, Evidence Retention, Resource / Training, Third Party, Other. |
| Root Cause Description | Enter a concise explanation of why the deficiency occurred, supported by facts from investigation. |
| Population / Period Affected | Enter the population and time period affected, e.g., all privileged users for Jan-Mar 2026, 18 production changes from 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31. |
| Number of Exceptions / Items Affected | Enter the count of exceptions and total population where known, e.g., 4 of 25; if unknown, enter TBD and update when determined. |
| Compensating Controls Identified | Enter Yes, No, or TBD to indicate whether compensating controls have been identified. |
| Compensating Control ID(s) | Enter the control reference number(s) for compensating controls, separated by semicolons; enter N/A if none. |
| Compensating Control Effectiveness | Enter the assessed effectiveness of compensating controls; allowed values: Effective, Partially Effective, Ineffective, Not Tested, N/A. |
| Likelihood of Misstatement | Enter the assessed likelihood that the deficiency could result in a material misstatement; allowed values: Remote, Reasonably Possible, Probable. |
| Magnitude / Potential Impact | Enter the potential financial reporting impact, including affected accounts/disclosures and estimated exposure if quantifiable; use currency and amount where available, otherwise qualitative description. |
| Aggregation Consideration | Enter whether this deficiency aggregates with related deficiencies; allowed values: Standalone, Aggregates with Other Deficiencies, TBD. If aggregating, reference related Deficiency IDs. |
| Management Owner | Enter the accountable remediation owner by role/name and function, e.g., IT Security Manager - Jane Smith. |
| Remediation Action Plan | Enter the specific corrective actions management will perform to remediate the deficiency, including process, system, control, evidence, and ownership changes. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target remediation completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Remediation Status | Enter current status; allowed values: Not Started, In Progress, Pending Validation, Remediated - Awaiting Retest, Retested - Effective, Retested - Ineffective, Closed, Deferred. |
| Interim Mitigation | Enter temporary mitigating actions in place until remediation is complete; enter N/A if none. |
| Actual Remediation Completion Date | Enter the date management completed remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until complete. |
| Management Validation Date | Enter the date management validated remediation readiness/evidence in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until validated. |
| Evidence of Remediation | Enter the evidence file names, links, ticket IDs, screenshots, reports, approvals, or repository location supporting remediation; do not embed evidence in the cell. |
| Retesting Owner | Enter the person or team responsible for independent retesting, e.g., SOX PMO, Internal Audit, External Audit. |
| Retesting Start Date | Enter the date retesting began in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if not started. |
| Retesting Completion Date | Enter the date retesting was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if not completed. |
| Retesting Result | Enter the retesting conclusion; allowed values: Pass, Fail, Partially Pass, Not Started, N/A. |
| Residual Deficiency / Remaining Gap | Enter any remaining issue after remediation/retesting; enter N/A if no residual deficiency remains. |
| External Auditor Status | Enter the external auditor's current position if applicable; allowed values: Not Provided, Under Review, Agreed, Disagreed, Pending Evidence, N/A. |
| Audit Committee / Disclosure Committee Reporting Required | Enter Yes, No, or TBD based on severity, disclosure implications, and governance reporting requirements. |
| Final Disposition | Enter the final outcome; allowed values: Closed - Remediated, Closed - Compensated, Open - In Remediation, Open - Deferred, Reclassified, Accepted Risk Pending Further Action. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the deficiency was formally closed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until closed. |
| Comments / Updates | Enter concise dated updates, decisions, dependencies, or escalation notes; include date and author initials for each update. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the SOX PMO or ITGC Compliance Lead, with remediation accountability assigned to IT control owners; update at least weekly during SOX testing/remediation cycles and immediately upon classification, remediation, validation, or retesting changes. Source data should be drawn from the GRC/SOX tool, internal audit workpapers, external auditor findings, ITSM tickets, IAM reports, change management tools, incident records, and remediation evidence repositories.

SOX-027.title: Remediation Tracker
SOX-027.content:
## Remediation Tracker (XLSX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Remediation ID | Issue/Finding ID | Issue Title | Source of Finding | SOX Application / IT Process | ITGC Domain | Related Control ID(s) | Related Financial Statement Assertion / Risk | Deficiency Type | Severity / Deficiency Assessment | Issue Description | Root Cause | Remediation Action Plan | Remediation Owner | Business Owner | Target Completion Date | Original Due Date | Revised Due Date | Due Date Change Reason | Priority | Remediation Status | Percent Complete | Key Milestones | Milestone Status | Dependencies / Blockers | Interim Compensating Control | Evidence Required for Closure | Evidence Location / Link | Management Validation Owner | Management Validation Date | Validation Result | Retesting Required | Retesting Owner | Retesting Date | Retesting Result | Residual Risk After Remediation | Closure Approval Owner | Closure Approval Date | Closure Status | Aging Days | Last Updated Date | Last Updated By | Comments / Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [EXAMPLE: REM-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: IA-2026-ITGC-004] | [EXAMPLE: Quarterly privileged access review not evidenced] | [EXAMPLE: Internal Audit] | [EXAMPLE: Active Directory] | [EXAMPLE: Logical Access] | [EXAMPLE: ITGC-LA-03] | [EXAMPLE: Unauthorized access could impact completeness and accuracy of financial reporting data] | [EXAMPLE: Operating Effectiveness Deficiency] | [EXAMPLE: Control Deficiency] | [EXAMPLE: Q2 privileged access review was performed late and approval evidence was incomplete for 3 of 25 users tested.] | [EXAMPLE: Access review ownership was not formally assigned after team reorganization.] | [EXAMPLE: Assign control owner, update access review procedure, implement quarterly review calendar reminders, and retain approval evidence in GRC.] | [EXAMPLE: Jane Smith, IT Access Manager] | [EXAMPLE: Finance Systems Owner] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-09-30] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-09-30] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: In Progress] | [EXAMPLE: 60] | [EXAMPLE: Owner assigned by 2026-08-15; procedure updated by 2026-09-01; Q3 review completed by 2026-09-30] | [EXAMPLE: On Track] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: IT Security Manager performs monthly spot-check of privileged users until quarterly control is remediated.] | [EXAMPLE: Updated procedure, Q3 access review evidence, reviewer approval, user population extract, exception resolution evidence] | [EXAMPLE: GRC/SOX/2026/Remediation/REM-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: Mark Lee, SOX PMO Manager] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: Not Performed] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: SOX PMO] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: Not Performed] | [EXAMPLE: Medium pending retest] | [EXAMPLE: SOX PMO Lead] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: Open] | [EXAMPLE: 35] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-08-20] | [EXAMPLE: Jane Smith] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-08-20: Procedure update drafted and under review.] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Remediation ID | Enter a unique tracker identifier for the remediation item, e.g. REM-YYYY-###; do not reuse IDs. |
| Issue/Finding ID | Enter the linked audit issue, deficiency, or finding reference from the source report or GRC system, e.g. IA-2026-ITGC-004. |
| Issue Title | Enter a short descriptive title of the remediation item, limited to one concise sentence. |
| Source of Finding | Select the origin of the issue: Internal Audit, External Audit, SOX PMO Testing, Management Self-Assessment, Regulatory Review, Incident/Post-Mortem, Other. |
| SOX Application / IT Process | Enter the in-scope SOX application, infrastructure component, or IT process affected, e.g. SAP ECC, Active Directory, Change Management, Job Scheduling. |
| ITGC Domain | Select the SOX ITGC domain: Logical Access, Change Management, IT Operations, Program Development, Computer Operations, Backup/Recovery, Interface Controls, Other. |
| Related Control ID(s) | Enter the SOX control reference(s) impacted, e.g. ITGC-LA-01; separate multiple IDs with semicolons. |
| Related Financial Statement Assertion / Risk | Enter the financial reporting risk or assertion affected by the control deficiency, e.g. completeness/accuracy of revenue processing, unauthorized changes to financial data. |
| Deficiency Type | Select the type of issue: Design Deficiency, Operating Effectiveness Deficiency, Missing Control, Documentation Deficiency, Evidence Deficiency, Other. |
| Severity / Deficiency Assessment | Enter management’s SOX deficiency assessment: Control Deficiency, Significant Deficiency, Material Weakness, Not Yet Evaluated; align with PCAOB AS 2201/SOX evaluation conclusions. |
| Issue Description | Describe the specific condition requiring remediation, including what failed, period affected, population/sample impact, and why it matters to SOX. |
| Root Cause | Enter the underlying cause, not just the symptom, e.g. unclear access review ownership, missing automated workflow enforcement, incomplete change approval procedure. |
| Remediation Action Plan | Enter the specific corrective actions management will perform to address the root cause and restore control design/operating effectiveness. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the accountable individual responsible for completing remediation; include name and role or team, e.g. Jane Smith, IT Access Manager. |
| Business Owner | Enter the SOX process or application business owner accountable for accepting the remediated control, if different from remediation owner. |
| Target Completion Date | Enter the planned completion date for all remediation activities in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Original Due Date | Enter the first approved due date assigned to the remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; do not overwrite when dates change. |
| Revised Due Date | Enter the latest approved revised due date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if no revision has occurred. |
| Due Date Change Reason | If Revised Due Date is populated, enter the business reason and approver for the date change; otherwise leave blank. |
| Priority | Select remediation priority: Critical, High, Medium, Low, based on SOX risk, severity, and reporting deadline impact. |
| Remediation Status | Select current status: Not Started, In Progress, Pending Evidence, Pending Management Validation, Pending Retest, Completed, Closed, Overdue, On Hold, Cancelled. |
| Percent Complete | Enter estimated completion percentage as a whole number from 0 to 100; use 100 only when remediation activities are complete and evidence is available. |
| Key Milestones | List major interim steps with target dates, e.g. policy updated by YYYY-MM-DD; workflow configured by YYYY-MM-DD; access review completed by YYYY-MM-DD. |
| Milestone Status | Select overall milestone position: On Track, At Risk, Delayed, Complete, Not Applicable. |
| Dependencies / Blockers | Enter any dependency preventing completion, such as vendor change, system release window, resource constraint, or business approval; enter None if no blocker. |
| Interim Compensating Control | Describe any temporary compensating control operating until remediation is complete, including owner and frequency; enter None if not applicable. |
| Evidence Required for Closure | Specify the exact evidence needed to support closure, e.g. approved procedure, access review sign-off, change ticket samples, system configuration screenshot, retest results. |
| Evidence Location / Link | Enter the repository path, GRC object link, ticket URL, or evidence folder location where closure evidence is stored. |
| Management Validation Owner | Enter the person responsible for confirming management’s remediation is complete and evidence is adequate. |
| Management Validation Date | Enter the date management validation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until performed. |
| Validation Result | Select result of management validation: Pass, Fail, Partially Complete, Not Performed, Not Applicable. |
| Retesting Required | Select Yes or No to indicate whether independent SOX PMO/Internal Audit/External Audit retesting is required before closure. |
| Retesting Owner | Enter the individual or team responsible for retesting, e.g. SOX PMO, Internal Audit, External Audit; leave blank if Retesting Required is No. |
| Retesting Date | Enter the date retesting was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until performed or if not required. |
| Retesting Result | Select retesting outcome: Pass, Fail, Not Performed, Not Applicable. |
| Residual Risk After Remediation | Enter management’s assessment of remaining SOX risk after remediation: Low, Medium, High, or None; include brief rationale if not Low/None. |
| Closure Approval Owner | Enter the role or person authorized to approve closure, e.g. SOX PMO Lead, Control Owner, Internal Audit Manager. |
| Closure Approval Date | Enter the formal closure approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until approved. |
| Closure Status | Select closure state: Open, Ready for Closure, Closed, Reopened, Cancelled. |
| Aging Days | Enter the number of calendar days from Issue/Finding open date to current date or closure date; use numeric whole days, ideally system-calculated. |
| Last Updated Date | Enter the date this tracker row was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Updated By | Enter the name or user ID of the person who last updated the row. |
| Comments / Notes | Enter concise updates, decisions, escalations, or context not captured elsewhere; include date-stamped notes where useful. |

### Maintenance

The SOX PMO or GRC Manager owns this remediation tracker, with updates required at least weekly and immediately after status, date, evidence, validation, or retesting changes. Source data should be drawn from the GRC/SOX compliance platform, internal and external audit findings, issue management tickets, control testing results, and approved closure evidence repositories.
