SOX-028.title: Management Quarterly Sub-Cert
SOX-028.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | [SOX Compliance Owner / Internal Controls Lead] | [Effective Date] | SOX IT General Controls | Internal - Confidential |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Management Quarterly Sub-Cert is to obtain formal quarterly confirmation from responsible control owners that assigned IT General Controls supporting financial reporting have operated effectively, exceptions have been identified and escalated, and supporting evidence is complete, accurate, and retained.

This attestation supports management’s quarterly financial reporting certification process by confirming that key technology controls over financially relevant systems have been performed as designed during the reporting period.

This document is intended to provide a consistent, auditable record of management accountability over SOX ITGC activities, including access management, change management, computer operations, job scheduling, backup and recovery, incident management, and other technology-dependent controls within the organisation’s SOX scope.

## Scope

This attestation applies to all control owners, control performers, application owners, infrastructure owners, and responsible managers assigned to SOX ITGC activities for in-scope systems, applications, databases, operating systems, networks, cloud platforms, interfaces, and supporting services that impact financial reporting.

The quarterly sub-certification covers the following areas, where applicable to the signatory’s assigned responsibilities:

| Control Area | In-Scope Activities |
|---|---|
| User access administration | New access, access modification, termination processing, privileged access, emergency access, and periodic access reviews |
| Change management | Application, database, infrastructure, configuration, and emergency changes affecting in-scope systems |
| Computer operations | Job monitoring, batch processing, interface monitoring, incident handling, problem escalation, and operational issue resolution |
| Backup and recovery | Backup completion, restoration testing, recovery monitoring, and retention of backup evidence |
| Security administration | Role design, segregation of duties considerations, administrative account usage, password configuration, and authentication settings |
| System development and deployment | Testing evidence, approval records, migration logs, and production implementation controls |
| Third-party and hosted services | Vendor-operated controls, service reports, complementary user entity controls, and management review of service performance |
| Evidence management | Preparation, review, retention, completeness, and accuracy of control evidence supporting the reporting period |

This attestation applies to the quarterly reporting period ending [Quarter End Date] and covers activity from [Period Start Date] through [Period End Date].

The attestation does not replace detailed control performance documentation, management review procedures, testing by Internal Audit, or external audit procedures. It serves as a management representation by the accountable control owner that assigned responsibilities have been fulfilled and that known issues have been disclosed.

## Attestation Statement

By signing this Management Quarterly Sub-Cert, I attest that, to the best of my knowledge after reasonable inquiry:

1. I am responsible for the ITGC activities, systems, processes, or controls assigned to me for the reporting period identified in this document.

2. The controls assigned to me were performed during the reporting period in accordance with approved procedures, documented control descriptions, management expectations, and applicable company policies.

3. The evidence supporting each assigned control is complete, accurate, legible, attributable to the correct period, and retained in the designated repository.

4. I have reviewed the control evidence or have confirmed that an appropriate delegated reviewer has performed the review.

5. All required approvals, review sign-offs, timestamps, system reports, tickets, logs, screenshots, reconciliation records, or other evidence items are available for inspection.

6. Any deviations, delays, missed controls, incomplete evidence, control failures, system incidents, unauthorized access events, emergency changes, failed jobs, backup exceptions, or other matters that may affect financial reporting have been disclosed to [SOX Compliance Owner / Internal Controls Lead].

7. I am not aware of any unreported control deficiency, material system issue, unauthorized access, unapproved change, unresolved operational incident, or evidence integrity concern affecting in-scope systems during the reporting period.

8. Where a control exception occurred, I have ensured that:
 - The exception was documented;
 - The business and financial reporting impact was assessed;
 - Appropriate management personnel were notified;
 - Corrective action was assigned;
 - Target remediation dates were established;
 - Compensating controls were identified where applicable.

9. I have disclosed any known changes to systems, infrastructure, vendors, control ownership, control frequency, control operation, evidence sources, automated reports, key spreadsheets, scripts, interfaces, or system-generated data that may affect the design or operation of assigned controls.

10. I have disclosed any known changes in personnel, roles, responsibilities, administrator assignments, privileged access, segregation of duties conflicts, or reliance on third-party service providers that may affect assigned controls.

11. I have not knowingly withheld information relevant to the evaluation of internal control over financial reporting.

12. I understand that management relies on this sub-certification as part of the quarterly financial reporting governance process.

13. I understand that inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading certification may result in management escalation and may be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with company policy.

The following certification response must be completed by the signatory:

| Certification Response | Select One |
|---|---|
| I certify without exception that all assigned controls operated effectively and all required evidence is complete and retained. | [Yes / No] |
| I certify with exceptions, and all exceptions have been disclosed in the exception log or attached schedule. | [Yes / No] |
| I am unable to certify for the reporting period and have provided an explanation to management. | [Yes / No] |

If certification is provided with exceptions or cannot be provided, complete the table below:

| Exception ID | Control / Process Area | Description of Exception | Period Affected | Financial Reporting Impact Assessment | Corrective Action | Owner | Target Completion Date | Current Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [EX-001] | [Access Review / Change Management / Operations / Other] | [Description] | [Quarter / Dates] | [None / Low / Moderate / Significant / To Be Assessed] | [Action] | [Owner] | [Date] | [Open / In Progress / Complete] |

## Signatory & Authority

The signatory must be the individual with management responsibility for the assigned control activities or an authorised delegate formally approved by the relevant process owner and SOX compliance function.

The signatory must have sufficient knowledge of the control activity to provide a reliable certification. If control execution was delegated, the signatory remains accountable for confirming that the delegated activities were performed, reviewed, evidenced, and escalated as required.

| Role | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Control Owner | Certifies operating effectiveness, evidence completeness, and disclosure of exceptions for assigned controls |
| Control Performer | Performs assigned control activity and provides timely, accurate evidence |
| Control Reviewer | Reviews evidence for completeness, accuracy, and appropriateness |
| Application / System Owner | Confirms relevant system changes, access activity, operational matters, and system dependencies |
| SOX Compliance Owner | Coordinates certification process, tracks responses, follows up on exceptions, and retains completed attestations |
| Finance Control Owner | Assesses potential impact of ITGC issues on financial reporting processes |
| Internal Audit / Testing Team | May inspect completed attestations and supporting evidence as part of independent testing |
| External Auditor | May request completed attestations and related evidence during audit procedures |

Certification must be completed by the following authorised signatory:

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Reporting Quarter | [Q1 / Q2 / Q3 / Q4] |
| Reporting Period | [Period Start Date] to [Period End Date] |
| Signatory Name | [Name] |
| Title | [Title] |
| Department / Function | [Department] |
| Assigned Control Areas | [Control Areas] |
| In-Scope Systems / Platforms | [Systems / Platforms] |
| Certification Response | [Certified Without Exception / Certified With Exceptions / Unable to Certify] |
| Signature | [Electronic Signature / Wet Signature] |
| Date Signed | [Date] |

Where an authorised delegate signs on behalf of the accountable owner, the following must also be completed:

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Accountable Owner Name | [Name] |
| Delegate Name | [Name] |
| Delegation Approved By | [Name / Role] |
| Delegation Approval Date | [Date] |
| Reason for Delegation | [Reason] |
| Period Covered by Delegation | [Dates] |

## Evidence Referenced

The signatory must reference the evidence reviewed or relied upon when completing this attestation. Evidence must be sufficient to allow an independent reviewer to verify control performance, timing, scope, accuracy, and approval.

Evidence should be stored in the approved SOX evidence repository and must be clearly labelled using the organisation’s standard naming convention.

Minimum expected evidence may include, as applicable:

| Control Area | Typical Evidence |
|---|---|
| User access provisioning | Approved access request tickets, role assignment records, manager approvals, system access logs, workflow history |
| User access removal | Termination reports, deactivation logs, service desk tickets, HR termination feeds, privileged account removal evidence |
| Periodic access review | Review population, reviewer sign-off, evidence of review completion, exceptions identified, remediation evidence |
| Privileged access management | Administrator account listings, approval records, usage logs, break-glass access records, review evidence |
| Change management | Change tickets, approvals, risk assessment, testing evidence, migration records, implementation logs, backout plans, post-implementation review |
| Emergency changes | Emergency approval records, implementation evidence, retrospective approval, testing confirmation, incident linkage |
| Job and batch monitoring | Job schedules, completion reports, failed job logs, rerun evidence, escalation records |
| Interface monitoring | Interface reconciliations, exception reports, transfer logs, failure resolution records |
| Backup monitoring | Backup completion logs, failure reports, remediation evidence, restore test results |
| Incident management | Incident tickets, severity assessment, escalation records, resolution notes, root cause analysis where applicable |
| Automated controls and reports | Report parameters, report generation evidence, source system validation, completeness and accuracy checks |
| Third-party services | Service reports, management review evidence, bridge letters where applicable, vendor issue tracking, complementary control evidence |

Evidence referenced for this quarterly attestation:

| Evidence ID | Control Area | Evidence Description | Repository Location / Link | Evidence Owner | Period Covered | Reviewed By | Review Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [EV-001] | [Control Area] | [Description] | [Repository Path / Link] | [Owner] | [Dates] | [Reviewer] | [Date] |
| [EV-002] | [Control Area] | [Description] | [Repository Path / Link] | [Owner] | [Dates] | [Reviewer] | [Date] |
| [EV-003] | [Control Area] | [Description] | [Repository Path / Link] | [Owner] | [Dates] | [Reviewer] | [Date] |

The signatory must confirm the following evidence requirements:

| Evidence Requirement | Confirmation |
|---|---|
| Evidence covers the full reporting period. | [Yes / No / Not Applicable] |
| Evidence is stored in the approved repository. | [Yes / No / Not Applicable] |
| Evidence is complete and readable. | [Yes / No / Not Applicable] |
| Evidence includes required approvals or review sign-offs. | [Yes / No / Not Applicable] |
| Evidence can be traced to the control activity performed. | [Yes / No / Not Applicable] |
| Evidence exceptions have been documented and escalated. | [Yes / No / Not Applicable] |
| System-generated reports used as evidence were reviewed for completeness and accuracy. | [Yes / No / Not Applicable] |

## Frequency

This Management Quarterly Sub-Cert must be completed every fiscal quarter for each control owner or accountable manager with assigned SOX ITGC responsibilities.

The certification process must follow the quarterly close timetable established by Finance, SOX Compliance, and Internal Controls management.

| Activity | Responsible Party | Target Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm quarterly certification population | SOX Compliance Owner | Prior to quarter-end close process |
| Distribute sub-certification requests | SOX Compliance Owner | Within [X] business days after quarter-end |
| Complete control owner review of assigned controls and evidence | Control Owner | Within [X] business days after request |
| Submit signed sub-certification | Control Owner | No later than [Submission Deadline] |
| Review submitted certifications for completeness | SOX Compliance Owner | Within [X] business days after receipt |
| Follow up on missing, incomplete, or qualified certifications | SOX Compliance Owner | Within [X] business days after review |
| Escalate unresolved exceptions or non-responses | SOX Compliance Owner / Management | Prior to quarterly management certification |
| Retain final certification package | SOX Compliance Owner | After management review and acceptance |

Late, incomplete, or missing attestations must be escalated to [SOX Program Leader], [IT Leadership], and [Finance Leadership] in accordance with the quarterly certification timeline.

If a control owner changes during the reporting period, the outgoing and incoming owners must coordinate to ensure coverage for the full period. Where necessary, separate attestations may be required for partial-period responsibilities.

If an in-scope system, process, or control is newly implemented, decommissioned, outsourced, or materially changed during the quarter, the control owner must disclose the change as part of the attestation and provide supporting evidence.

## Records & Retention

Completed Management Quarterly Sub-Certs and related evidence are formal SOX records and must be retained in the approved repository.

Records must be protected against unauthorised modification, deletion, or loss. Access to completed certifications must be restricted to personnel with a legitimate business need, including SOX Compliance, Finance management, Internal Audit, Legal, authorised IT management, and external auditors.

The following records must be retained:

| Record Type | Minimum Retention Requirement | Repository |
|---|---:|---|
| Signed quarterly sub-certifications | [Retention Period] | [SOX Repository / GRC Tool] |
| Evidence referenced in the certification | [Retention Period] | [Evidence Repository] |
| Exception logs and remediation plans | [Retention Period] | [GRC Tool / Issue Tracker] |
| Management review notes and follow-up records | [Retention Period] | [SOX Repository] |
| Delegation approvals | [Retention Period] | [SOX Repository] |
| Late submission or escalation records | [Retention Period] | [SOX Repository / Email Archive] |

Retention must be sufficient to support management review, internal testing, external audit requests, regulatory inquiries, and historical traceability of control operation.

Records must not be deleted, overwritten, or materially altered during an active audit, investigation, legal hold, remediation review, or management assessment. If a legal hold or audit preservation notice is issued, the applicable records must be preserved until the hold is formally released.

The SOX Compliance Owner is responsible for maintaining the final quarterly certification package, including:

- Completed and signed attestations;
- Certification response tracker;
- Exception summary;
- Evidence index;
- Escalation records;
- Management review notes;
- Remediation status updates;
- Final sign-off confirming the package is complete.

Final quarterly certification package approval:

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Prepared By | [Name / Role] |
| Reviewed By | [Name / Role] |
| Approved By | [Name / Role] |
| Approval Date | [Date] |
| Repository Location | [Repository Path / Link] |
| Package Status | [Complete / Complete with Open Exceptions / Incomplete] |

SOX-029.title: Management Assertion (404)
SOX-029.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | [Chief Financial Officer / SOX Program Owner] | [Effective Date] | SOX ITGC | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This Management Assertion documents management’s annual assertion regarding the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, including relevant Information Technology General Controls supporting systems, applications, infrastructure, databases, interfaces, reports, and service providers that materially support financial reporting.

This attestation is intended to provide a formal, evidence-based statement that management has:

- Accepted responsibility for establishing and maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting.
- Identified the financially relevant technology environment supporting significant accounts, disclosures, and financial reporting processes.
- Designed, implemented, and evaluated IT general controls that support the reliability, integrity, availability, and controlled operation of financial reporting systems.
- Assessed the operating effectiveness of in-scope controls for the annual reporting period.
- Evaluated identified control deficiencies, including their severity, financial reporting impact, remediation status, and disclosure implications.
- Reached a conclusion on whether internal control over financial reporting was effective as of the assessment date.

This assertion is prepared for use by the Audit Committee, executive management, internal audit, external audit, and other authorised stakeholders involved in financial reporting governance and assurance.

## Scope

This assertion applies to the annual management assessment of internal control over financial reporting for the fiscal year ending [Fiscal Year-End Date].

The scope includes IT general controls and related technology-dependent controls that support the preparation, processing, recording, consolidation, reporting, and disclosure of financial information. In-scope areas include, where relevant to financial reporting:

- User access management for financially significant applications, databases, operating systems, and supporting platforms.
- Privileged access management, including administrator access, service accounts, emergency access, and elevated permissions.
- Change management for application, database, configuration, infrastructure, reporting, and interface changes.
- Computer operations, including batch processing, job scheduling, backup monitoring, incident handling, interface monitoring, and system availability controls.
- Program development and system implementation activities for systems introduced or materially changed during the reporting period.
- Logical security controls supporting segregation of duties and restricted access to financial data and system functions.
- Interfaces, automated workflows, calculations, and system-generated reports relied upon in financial reporting processes.
- Information produced by the entity and end-user computing tools relied upon in key financial reporting controls.
- Third-party technology service providers that host, process, manage, or support financially relevant systems or data.
- Complementary user entity controls required to operate effectively within outsourced or cloud-hosted environments.
- Remediation activities related to ITGC deficiencies identified during the reporting period.

The assertion covers the following financially significant systems and supporting technology components:

| System / Component | Financial Reporting Relevance | Control Areas in Scope | System Owner | IT Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ERP / General Ledger System] | General ledger, journal entries, consolidation, financial close | Access, changes, operations, reports, interfaces | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |
| [Revenue System] | Revenue recognition, billing, customer transactions | Access, changes, operations, interfaces | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |
| [Procurement / Accounts Payable System] | Vendor master data, purchase orders, invoices, payments | Access, changes, operations, reports | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |
| [Payroll System] | Payroll expense, accruals, employee master data | Access, changes, operations, service provider oversight | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |
| [Financial Reporting / Consolidation Tool] | Consolidation, eliminations, reporting packages, disclosures | Access, changes, reports, operations | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |
| [Data Warehouse / Reporting Platform] | Financial reports, dashboards, reconciliations, data extracts | Access, changes, data integrity, report logic | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |
| [Infrastructure / Cloud Platform] | Hosting and operation of financially significant systems | Privileged access, changes, operations, backup, monitoring | [Name / Role] | [Name / Role] |

Out-of-scope systems, processes, or locations are excluded only where management has determined they do not materially support significant financial statement accounts, disclosures, or relevant assertions for the reporting period. Any exclusions are documented in the SOX scoping assessment and approved by the SOX Program Owner.

This assertion is made as of [Assessment Date] and relates to controls operating during the period from [Start Date] to [End Date], subject to any control frequency requirements and applicable testing windows.

## Attestation Statement

Management acknowledges its responsibility for establishing, maintaining, and evaluating internal control over financial reporting. This responsibility includes ensuring that technology supporting financial reporting is appropriately controlled, monitored, and governed.

Management has conducted an annual assessment of internal control over financial reporting, including IT general controls relevant to financial reporting systems, using a recognised internal control framework and a risk-based SOX ITGC testing approach. The assessment included consideration of financially significant systems, related infrastructure, databases, reports, interfaces, service organisations, and relevant business process dependencies.

Based on management’s evaluation, including the evidence referenced in this document, management asserts that, as of [Assessment Date]:

1. Internal control over financial reporting was designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external reporting purposes.
2. In-scope IT general controls were designed to address relevant risks to the completeness, accuracy, validity, restricted access, integrity, and availability of financial reporting systems and data.
3. Management evaluated the operating effectiveness of in-scope IT general controls for the annual reporting period through inquiry, inspection of evidence, observation, reperformance, and review of control-owner certifications, as appropriate.
4. Control exceptions identified during testing were evaluated individually and in aggregate to determine their impact on financial reporting risk.
5. Deficiencies were assessed based on the likelihood and magnitude of potential financial statement misstatement, including consideration of compensating controls, mitigating business process controls, actual errors identified, and remediation performed.
6. Remediation actions for identified deficiencies were tracked, assigned to accountable owners, and evaluated for completion and sustainability where remediation occurred before the assessment date.
7. Management considered the impact of third-party service providers on financially relevant systems and evaluated available assurance reports, complementary user entity responsibilities, control exceptions, and bridging procedures, where applicable.
8. Management considered whether information used in the operation of key controls, including system-generated reports and data extracts, was complete and accurate for its intended purpose.
9. Management has disclosed to the Audit Committee and external auditor all known significant control deficiencies, material weaknesses, relevant fraud matters, and changes in internal control over financial reporting that could materially affect financial reporting.

Subject to the matters described below, management asserts that internal control over financial reporting was effective as of [Assessment Date].

| Area | Management Conclusion | Notes / Exceptions |
|---|---|---|
| ITGC design effectiveness | [Effective / Effective with exceptions / Not effective] | [Summary of design exceptions, if any] |
| ITGC operating effectiveness | [Effective / Effective with exceptions / Not effective] | [Summary of operating exceptions, if any] |
| Financial reporting system access controls | [Effective / Effective with exceptions / Not effective] | [Summary] |
| Change management controls | [Effective / Effective with exceptions / Not effective] | [Summary] |
| Computer operations controls | [Effective / Effective with exceptions / Not effective] | [Summary] |
| Service organisation oversight | [Effective / Effective with exceptions / Not effective] | [Summary] |
| Information produced by the entity | [Effective / Effective with exceptions / Not effective] | [Summary] |
| Deficiency remediation | [Complete / In progress / Not applicable] | [Summary] |
| Overall ICFR conclusion | [Effective / Not effective] | [Basis for conclusion] |

If management has identified one or more material weaknesses, the overall conclusion must state that internal control over financial reporting was not effective as of [Assessment Date]. In that case, management’s assertion must include a clear summary of each material weakness, its financial reporting impact, remediation status, and planned corrective actions.

| Deficiency ID | Deficiency Description | Severity | Financial Reporting Impact | Remediation Status | Owner | Target Completion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DEF-001] | [Description] | [Control deficiency / Significant deficiency / Material weakness] | [Impact] | [Open / Remediated / In validation] | [Name / Role] | [Date] |
| [DEF-002] | [Description] | [Control deficiency / Significant deficiency / Material weakness] | [Impact] | [Open / Remediated / In validation] | [Name / Role] | [Date] |

Management confirms that this assertion is based on information available as of [Assertion Date]. Events, control failures, system incidents, organisational changes, cyber events, or financial reporting matters identified after this date must be evaluated separately to determine whether they affect this assertion or require additional disclosure.

## Signatory & Authority

This assertion is made by management under the authority of the organisation’s executive leadership and governance responsibilities for financial reporting.

The Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer retain ultimate accountability for the annual assessment of internal control over financial reporting. The SOX Program Owner coordinates the assessment process and ensures that testing, deficiency evaluation, remediation tracking, and reporting are completed in accordance with the approved SOX methodology. IT management and business process owners are responsible for the accuracy, completeness, and timely provision of control evidence within their areas of responsibility.

The following signatories confirm that they have reviewed the assessment results, considered known control deficiencies and remediation status, and support the management assertion stated in this document.

| Role | Name | Attestation Responsibility | Signature | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chief Executive Officer | [Name] | Executive accountability for financial reporting and ICFR assertion | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Chief Financial Officer | [Name] | Executive accountability for financial reporting controls and disclosure implications | [Signature] | [Date] |
| SOX Program Owner | [Name] | Coordination of SOX assessment, testing status, deficiency evaluation, and reporting | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Chief Information Officer / Chief Technology Officer | [Name] | Accountability for ITGC design, operation, remediation, and technology control environment | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Controller / Head of Accounting | [Name] | Accountability for financial close, accounting controls, and system dependencies | [Signature] | [Date] |
| Internal Audit Executive, if applicable | [Name] | Independent assessment support and reporting to governance bodies, where applicable | [Signature] | [Date] |

By signing this document, each signatory confirms that, to the best of their knowledge:

- Relevant information has not been knowingly withheld from the SOX Program Owner, Audit Committee, executive management, internal audit, or external auditor.
- Known ITGC failures, financial reporting incidents, access violations, unauthorised changes, service provider issues, and remediation concerns have been communicated through the established governance process.
- Evidence provided to support this assertion is complete, accurate, and representative of control performance for the period under review.
- Any limitations, unresolved issues, or areas requiring management judgement have been documented and escalated appropriately.
- The conclusion reached in this assertion is reasonable based on the work performed and evidence reviewed.

## Evidence Referenced

This assertion is supported by the SOX assessment file, control testing results, management review documentation, deficiency evaluations, remediation evidence, and governance records maintained for the reporting period.

Evidence referenced includes, at a minimum:

| Evidence Category | Description | Evidence Owner | Repository / Location | Review Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOX scoping assessment | Identification of significant accounts, disclosures, locations, processes, systems, and IT dependencies | [SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Risk and control matrix | Documented ITGC risks, control objectives, control activities, frequency, owners, and evidence requirements | [SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Process narratives and walkthroughs | Documentation of financial reporting process flows, IT dependencies, automated controls, reports, and interfaces | [Process Owners] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| ITGC testing workpapers | Design and operating effectiveness testing for access, change management, operations, and related control areas | [Internal Audit / SOX Team] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Access review evidence | User access review results, privileged access reviews, joiner-mover-leaver samples, remediation records | [IT Control Owners] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Change management evidence | Change tickets, approvals, testing evidence, deployment records, emergency change reviews, segregation evidence | [IT Control Owners] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Operations evidence | Job monitoring logs, incident records, backup evidence, restoration testing, interface monitoring, batch processing reviews | [IT Operations] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Report and interface validation | Completeness and accuracy validation for key reports, data extracts, interfaces, and automated calculations | [Report Owners / IT Owners] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Service provider assurance | Service organisation reports, bridge letters, complementary control assessments, vendor exception evaluations | [Vendor Owner / IT Owner] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Deficiency evaluation records | Exception analysis, severity assessment, aggregation analysis, compensating control evaluation, disclosure assessment | [SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Remediation evidence | Corrective action plans, implementation evidence, retesting results, management sign-off | [Control Owners] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Governance reporting | SOX steering committee minutes, Audit Committee materials, management certifications, external audit communications | [SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |
| Management sub-certifications | Certifications from control owners and business process owners regarding completeness and accuracy of evidence | [Control Owners] | [Repository Path] | [Reviewed / Pending] |

Management’s assessment considered the following control areas and evidence expectations:

| Control Area | Evidence Considered | Typical Evaluation Performed |
|---|---|---|
| User access provisioning | Access requests, approvals, role assignment evidence, segregation considerations | Whether access was authorised, appropriate, and timely |
| User access removal | Termination reports, access removal tickets, deactivation timestamps | Whether access was removed promptly after termination or transfer |
| Periodic access reviews | Review sign-offs, reviewer evidence, access listings, remediation tickets | Whether access remained appropriate and exceptions were resolved |
| Privileged access | Administrator listings, approval records, monitoring logs, emergency access records | Whether elevated access was restricted, approved, monitored, and reviewed |
| Change management | Change requests, business approvals, technical approvals, testing evidence, deployment records | Whether changes were authorised, tested, approved, and implemented as intended |
| Emergency changes | Emergency change logs, post-implementation approvals, testing or validation evidence | Whether urgent changes were reviewed after implementation and appropriately controlled |
| Production access restrictions | Developer access listings, production permission reviews, deployment controls | Whether inappropriate development or direct change access was prevented or monitored |
| Batch processing and interfaces | Job schedules, exception logs, reconciliation evidence, incident tickets | Whether financial data processing completed accurately and exceptions were resolved |
| Backup and recovery | Backup job evidence, monitoring records, restore test results | Whether financial systems and data could be recovered within business expectations |
| Incident management | Incident tickets, root cause analysis, resolution evidence, financial impact assessment | Whether incidents affecting financial systems were escalated and resolved appropriately |
| Reports and data extracts | Report logic, parameters, source data validation, reconciliation evidence | Whether reports used in key controls were complete and accurate |
| Service organisations | Assurance reports, bridge letters, vendor exception analysis, user control mapping | Whether outsourced controls were understood and appropriately addressed |

Management confirms that evidence limitations, missing samples, population completeness concerns, inconsistent documentation, or reliance on compensating controls have been identified and evaluated as part of the deficiency assessment process.

## Frequency

This Management Assertion is prepared and approved annually in connection with the organisation’s year-end financial reporting cycle.

The annual assertion process follows the timetable below unless adjusted by the SOX Program Owner and approved by the Chief Financial Officer.

| Activity | Responsible Party | Target Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm SOX scope, significant systems, and IT dependencies | SOX Program Owner, Finance, IT Leadership | [Q1 / Planning Period] |
| Update ITGC risk and control matrix | SOX Program Owner, IT Control Owners | [Q1-Q2] |
| Complete walkthroughs and confirm control design | SOX Team, Control Owners | [Q2] |
| Perform interim operating effectiveness testing | SOX Team / Internal Audit | [Q2-Q3] |
| Communicate interim exceptions and remediation actions | SOX Program Owner, Control Owners | [Q3] |
| Perform year-end roll-forward testing | SOX Team / Internal Audit | [Q4 / Year-End] |
| Evaluate service provider assurance reports and bridge letters | SOX Program Owner, Vendor Owners, IT Owners | [Q4] |
| Complete deficiency aggregation and severity assessment | SOX Program Owner, Finance Leadership, IT Leadership | [Q4 / Pre-Filing] |
| Report results to executive management and Audit Committee | CFO, SOX Program Owner | [Pre-Filing] |
| Obtain management assertion signatures | CEO, CFO, CIO/CTO, SOX Program Owner | [Before Annual Report Filing] |
| Archive final assertion and supporting records | SOX Program Owner | [Within 30 Days of Filing] |

Management may issue an interim or updated assertion if there is a material acquisition, divestiture, system implementation, cyber incident, significant control failure, financial restatement, material change in financial reporting systems, or other event that could significantly affect internal control over financial reporting.

Any significant change to the control environment after the annual assessment date must be evaluated to determine whether additional testing, disclosure, remediation, or governance reporting is required.

## Records & Retention

The approved Management Assertion and supporting records must be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention policy, legal hold requirements, audit requirements, and financial reporting obligations.

At a minimum, the following records must be retained:

| Record Type | Required Retention | Custodian | Storage Location |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Signed Management Assertion | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] |
| Final SOX scoping assessment | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] |
| ITGC risk and control matrix | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] |
| Walkthrough documentation | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [SOX Team / Internal Audit] | [Repository Path] |
| Testing workpapers and sample evidence | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [SOX Team / Internal Audit] | [Repository Path] |
| Deficiency evaluations and remediation records | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] |
| Management certifications and sub-certifications | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] |
| Service provider assurance reports and evaluations | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [Vendor Owner / SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] |
| Audit Committee and governance reporting materials | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [Corporate Secretary / SOX Program Owner] | [Repository Path] |
| External audit correspondence relevant to ICFR | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [Finance Leadership] | [Repository Path] |

Records must be:

- Complete, accurate, and traceable to the control, population, sample, assessment, or conclusion they support.
- Protected from unauthorised access, modification, deletion, or disclosure.
- Stored in an approved repository with appropriate access controls and retention settings.
- Available for authorised management review, internal audit review, external audit review, regulatory inquiry, or legal request.
- Preserved immediately if subject to legal hold, investigation, restatement review, enforcement matter, or audit dispute.

Draft versions of this assertion may be retained only where required by policy, legal hold, or audit protocol. The final signed version is the authoritative record.

Disposal of records after the retention period must follow approved records management procedures and must not occur while any audit, investigation, litigation, regulatory inquiry, or financial reporting review remains open.

SOX-030.title: External Auditor Walkthrough Pack
SOX-030.content:
## What This Evidences

The **External Auditor Walkthrough Pack** evidences that the organisation has provided complete, traceable, and current documentation to the external auditor for SOX ITGC walkthrough purposes. It supports the control objective that IT general controls are designed, documented, and available for auditor inspection, including evidence of the systems, processes, control owners, and supporting artifacts used in the walkthrough.

This artifact is **collected, not authored**. Do not create or reconstruct evidence manually. The ZIP must be assembled from the organisation’s actual source systems, repositories, ticketing tools, dashboards, and approved control documentation locations.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect the walkthrough pack from the relevant systems used in the SOX ITGC environment, typically including:

- GRC or audit management platform: [GRC Tool Name]
- IT service management system: [ITSM Tool Name]
- Identity and access management system: [IAM Tool Name]
- Privileged access management system: [PAM Tool Name]
- Change management or DevOps platform: [Change Tool / DevOps Tool Name]
- Configuration management database: [CMDB Name]
- Logging, monitoring, or SIEM platform: [SIEM / Log Platform Name]
- Document repository: [SharePoint / Confluence / Document Management System]
- Evidence repository or auditor portal: [Evidence Portal Name]

## How To Collect

1. Confirm the walkthrough scope with [SOX Manager / ITGC Lead], including systems, applications, control areas, audit period, and requested auditor items.
2. Retrieve the latest approved process narratives, control descriptions, RACI documents, policies, and procedure documents from [Document Repository].
3. Export relevant population reports from source systems, such as user listings, privileged access listings, change tickets, incident tickets, job schedules, configuration items, and monitoring alerts.
4. Download selected sample records requested by the auditor from [ITSM Tool], [IAM Tool], [PAM Tool], [Change Tool], or other applicable systems.
5. Capture screenshots showing system-generated dates, filters, report parameters, and user/session context where exports alone do not evidence source authenticity.
6. Include walkthrough meeting materials, agendas, attendee lists, screen-share captures, or read-only demo extracts where these are stored in [Audit Portal / Collaboration Tool].
7. Name files consistently using: `[Control Area]_[System]_[Evidence Type]_[Period]_[YYYYMMDD]`.
8. Place all files into a single folder structure by control area and source system.
9. Create a ZIP file named: `[Organisation]_External_Auditor_Walkthrough_Pack_[Audit Period]_[YYYYMMDD].zip`.
10. Upload the ZIP to [Evidence Repository / Auditor Portal] and record the submission reference or upload confirmation.

## What To Capture

The ZIP should contain sufficient evidence to allow an auditor to understand and trace the walkthrough, including:

- Approved SOX ITGC process narratives and control descriptions
- Current policies and procedures relevant to access, change, operations, backups, monitoring, and incident handling
- System-generated reports with report name, source system, run date, parameters, and period covered
- Screenshots showing filters, timestamps, system name, and logged-in user where required
- Representative tickets or records used during walkthroughs
- User access and privileged access extracts for in-scope systems
- Change records showing request, approval, testing, implementation, and closure
- Job monitoring, backup, incident, or alert records where relevant
- Application and infrastructure inventory or CMDB extracts for in-scope systems
- Auditor request list or walkthrough agenda, if available
- Evidence submission confirmation from [Evidence Portal]

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Collected for each external audit walkthrough cycle and refreshed whenever the auditor requests updated evidence.
- **Primary Owner:** [SOX ITGC Lead / IT Compliance Manager]
- **Contributors:** [System Owners], [IT Operations Lead], [IAM Administrator], [Change Manager], [Security Operations Lead]
- **Reviewer:** [SOX Manager / Internal Controls Lead]

## Retention & Storage

Store the final ZIP and supporting collection notes in [Evidence Repository / GRC Tool] under the relevant audit period. Restrict access to authorised audit, compliance, IT control, and external auditor personnel only.

Retain the walkthrough pack in line with the organisation’s SOX evidence retention schedule, legal hold requirements, and audit record retention policy. Do not store the only copy on local drives, email inboxes, or unmanaged collaboration folders.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the walkthrough pack as sufficient when:

- Evidence is sourced directly from approved systems of record
- Files are complete, readable, and clearly named
- Reports show source system, period covered, extraction date, and relevant filters
- Screenshots include timestamps or other indicators of authenticity where needed
- Evidence aligns to the requested SOX ITGC scope and audit period
- Sample records can be traced back to source systems
- The pack includes approved documentation and operational records, not manually recreated substitutes
- Submission is uploaded to the authorised evidence repository or auditor portal with a clear submission date and reference
- Any redactions are approved, documented, and do not obscure control-relevant information

SOX-031.title: External Auditor ITGC Test Reliance Memo
SOX-031.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-ID] | 1.0 | [External Audit Engagement Partner / IT Audit Lead] | [Effective Date] | SOX IT General Controls | Confidential - Audit Restricted |

## Purpose

This report documents the external auditor’s position on the planned and actual reliance on Information Technology General Controls (ITGCs) relevant to the audit of internal control over financial reporting and the financial statement audit for [Organisation Name].

The purpose of this memo is to:

- Summarise the IT systems, infrastructure, and IT processes considered relevant to financial reporting.
- Document the external auditor’s assessment of ITGC design and operating effectiveness.
- State the extent to which the external auditor intends to rely on ITGCs for the reporting period.
- Identify exceptions, deficiencies, control gaps, compensating controls, and audit implications.
- Support the planned nature, timing, and extent of application control testing, reports testing, substantive procedures, and other financial audit procedures.
- Provide management and audit stakeholders with a clear view of ITGC reliance limitations and required remediation actions.

This report is prepared for audit planning, execution, conclusion, and governance purposes. It is not intended to replace detailed test workpapers, exception logs, system walkthroughs, population completeness procedures, or management’s own internal control assessment documentation.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

This report covers ITGC testing and reliance assessment for the period:

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Fiscal year under audit | [Fiscal Year] |
| ITGC testing period | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Interim testing date, if applicable | [Interim Testing Date] |
| Roll-forward testing period, if applicable | [Roll-forward Period] |
| Report issue date | [Report Date] |
| External audit firm | [Audit Firm Name] |
| Client organisation | [Organisation Name] |

### In-Scope Systems

The following systems were assessed because they support financially significant processes, generate financial reporting data, host financially relevant applications, or provide infrastructure services relied upon by in-scope applications.

| System / Platform | Business Purpose | Financial Reporting Relevance | Hosting Model | In Scope for Reliance? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Methodology

### Approach

The external auditor performed procedures to evaluate whether ITGCs relevant to financial reporting were designed and operating effectively during the reporting period. The methodology included risk assessment, system scoping, process walkthroughs, control design evaluation, sample-based testing, population validation, evidence inspection, inquiry, observation, reperformance where applicable, and evaluation of exceptions.

The assessment considered:

- The role of each system in initiating, authorising, processing, recording, reporting, or storing financial information.
- The dependence of financial reporting controls on automated application controls, interfaces, calculations, workflows, and system-generated reports.
- The risk of unauthorised access, unauthorised changes, failed processing, data loss, or inappropriate system administration.
- The extent to which management’s IT processes prevent or detect errors or unauthorised activity that could affect financial reporting.
- The reliability of evidence produced by systems used in the audit.
- The impact of third-party providers and outsourced technology services.

### Procedures Performed

| Procedure Area | Procedures Performed |
|---|---|
| Planning and scoping | Obtained system inventory, financial process mapping, application dependency mapping, infrastructure diagrams, and prior-year ITGC results |
| Walkthroughs | Conducted walkthroughs with IT, security, application owners, business process owners, and control performers |
| Design assessment | Evaluated whether controls were appropriately designed to address identified risks and whether control owners understood performance requirements |
| Population completeness | Assessed completeness and accuracy of populations used for testing, including user listings, change listings, incident logs, job schedules, and privileged access reports |
| Sample selection | Selected samples based on control frequency, risk, population size, and prior exception history |
| Evidence inspection | Reviewed tickets, approvals, access requests, system logs, review sign-offs, test evidence, migration records, monitoring alerts, and management review documentation |
| Reperformance | Reperformed selected access review checks, change approval validations, user termination comparisons, and report parameter validations where appropriate |
| Third-party review | Reviewed relevant service organisation reports, bridge letters, subservice considerations, and management’s evaluation of vendor controls |
| Exception evaluation | Assessed exceptions for cause, frequency, pervasiveness, compensating controls, and potential financial reporting impact |
| Reliance conclusion | Determined whether reliance is supported, limited, unsupported, or pending for each domain and system |

### Testing Strategy

The testing strategy was risk-based and considered control frequency, control automation, prior-year results, extent of financial reporting reliance, and whether controls were preventive or detective.

| Control Frequency | Typical Testing Approach |
|---|---|
| Continuous / automated | Validate configuration, access to modify configuration, change history, and monitoring of exceptions |
| Daily | Test a representative sample across the period, including higher-risk dates or periods |
| Weekly | Test a sample across multiple months or quarters |
| Monthly | Test selected months, including close periods where applicable |
| Quarterly | Test selected quarters, including at least one period close where relevant |
| Annual | Test the annual occurrence and evaluate timeliness, completeness, and review quality |
| Event-driven | Test a risk-based sample from the complete population of events |

### Evidence Standards

Evidence was considered sufficient and appropriate when it demonstrated:

- The control was performed by an authorised and competent individual or automated process.
- The control was performed at the required frequency.
- The control covered the complete and accurate population.
- The reviewer had sufficient information to identify exceptions.
- Exceptions were investigated and resolved timely.
- Approval occurred before access, change migration, or other relevant control event unless a defined emergency process applied.
- Evidence was retained in a reliable system or repository.
- The timing of evidence aligned to the period under audit.
- System-generated evidence was supported by access controls and report reliability procedures.

### Reliance Decision Criteria

Reliance was evaluated using the following criteria:

| Criterion | Consideration |
|---|---|
| Design suitability | Whether the control is capable of preventing or detecting relevant financial reporting risks |
| Operating consistency | Whether the control operated as designed throughout the period |
| Evidence quality | Whether documentation is complete, clear, retained, and independently verifiable |
| Exception severity | Whether exceptions indicate isolated performance issues or broader control failure |
| Compensating controls | Whether other controls sufficiently reduce the same risk |
| Deficiency pervasiveness | Whether the issue affects one system, one control, one period, or multiple financial processes |
| Management review precision | Whether review controls are performed at a level of detail sufficient to identify meaningful errors or unauthorised activity |
| Period coverage | Whether testing covers the full audit period or whether roll-forward procedures are required |
| Third-party assurance | Whether service provider controls and management’s user responsibilities are adequately addressed |
