# Scope & TSC Selection Memo

## Purpose

This Policy establishes the mandatory scope and Trust Services Criteria selection for the organisation’s SOC 2 program. It defines the systems, services, people, processes, locations, data types, service commitments, and selected criteria categories that shall be included in SOC 2 readiness, control design, control operation, evidence collection, management review, and external examination activities.

The purpose of this Policy is to ensure that the SOC 2 examination scope is accurate, defensible, aligned with customer commitments, and consistently applied across business, technology, security, privacy, and operational teams.

## Scope

This Policy applies to all organisational units, personnel, contractors, systems, processes, third-party services, and data flows that support the delivery, security, availability, confidentiality, processing integrity, or privacy of the in-scope service.

The in-scope service for SOC 2 is:

| Scope Element | Description |
|---|---|
| In-Scope Service | [Name of product, platform, application, managed service, or service offering] |
| Service Description | [Brief description of the service provided to customers] |
| Primary Customers | [Customer segments, industries, or user groups] |
| Examination Type | [Type I / Type II] |
| Intended Reporting Period | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Primary Business Owner | [Business Owner] |
| Primary Technical Owner | [Technical Owner] |
| Primary Compliance Owner | [Compliance Owner] |

The SOC 2 program shall include the following selected Trust Services categories:

| Category | Selection Status | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Security | Mandatory - Included | Required for every SOC 2 examination and applicable to protection of systems and data against unauthorized access, unauthorized disclosure, and damage that could affect the organisation’s ability to meet its service commitments. |
| Availability | Included | Selected because the organisation makes commitments regarding service uptime, resilience, continuity, incident response, backup, recovery, monitoring, and capacity management. |
| Confidentiality | Included | Selected because the organisation stores, processes, or transmits confidential customer information, business data, contractual information, or other restricted information requiring controlled access and protection from unauthorized disclosure. |
| Processing Integrity | Included | Selected because the organisation processes customer transactions, workflows, records, data transformations, reports, integrations, or automated outputs where completeness, accuracy, validity, timeliness, and authorization are material to customer commitments. |
| Privacy | Included | Selected because the organisation collects, uses, retains, discloses, or disposes of personal information on behalf of customers, users, employees, or other individuals and has privacy commitments or regulatory obligations. |

The SOC 2 system boundary shall include the following components where they support the in-scope service:

| Component Type | Included Scope |
|---|---|
| Applications | Customer-facing applications, administrative consoles, APIs, worker services, background jobs, reporting modules, and internal service components supporting the in-scope service. |
| Infrastructure | Cloud environments, virtual networks, compute resources, containers, databases, object storage, logging platforms, identity services, secrets management, backup systems, and monitoring tools supporting the in-scope service. |
| Data | Customer data, confidential information, personal information, system logs, metadata, configuration data, support data, audit records, and operational data used to provide or secure the service. |
| People | Employees, contractors, temporary staff, administrators, developers, support personnel, security personnel, privacy personnel, and operations personnel with responsibilities for the in-scope service. |
| Processes | Governance, risk management, access control, change management, secure development, incident response, vendor management, business continuity, data protection, privacy operations, support operations, monitoring, and management review processes. |
| Locations | [Headquarters], [office locations], remote work environments, cloud regions, data processing locations, and support locations relevant to the in-scope service. |
| Third Parties | Cloud hosting providers, managed service providers, payment processors, identity providers, monitoring providers, support platforms, analytics providers, subprocessors, and other vendors materially supporting the in-scope service. |

The SOC 2 scope shall exclude only those systems, services, entities, geographies, or processes that do not support the in-scope service, do not affect the selected criteria, and do not materially influence the organisation’s ability to meet its service commitments and system requirements.

Any excluded component shall be documented with a business justification, risk assessment, and approval from the Compliance Owner and Executive Sponsor.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain a formally approved SOC 2 scope that identifies the in-scope service, examination type, intended reporting period, selected Trust Services categories, business processes, technology components, supporting personnel, physical and remote locations, and relevant third-party services.

2. The organisation shall include Security as a mandatory SOC 2 category for the in-scope service.

3. The organisation shall include Availability as a selected SOC 2 category where the organisation commits to service uptime, performance, disaster recovery, backup, business continuity, monitoring, or operational resilience.

4. The organisation shall include Confidentiality as a selected SOC 2 category where confidential customer data, restricted business information, proprietary information, credentials, secrets, contractual data, or sensitive operational information is stored, processed, transmitted, or accessed.

5. The organisation shall include Processing Integrity as a selected SOC 2 category where the service performs transaction processing, data ingestion, data transformation, workflow execution, reporting, synchronization, automated decision support, integration handling, or other processing activities that must be complete, accurate, valid, timely, and authorized.

6. The organisation shall include Privacy as a selected SOC 2 category where personal information is collected, received, stored, used, disclosed, retained, deleted, anonymized, or otherwise processed as part of the in-scope service.

7. The organisation shall define service commitments and system requirements for each selected category in plain business terms and shall align control design, evidence collection, and management assertions to those commitments and requirements.

8. The organisation shall maintain a current description of the in-scope system, including the nature of the service, principal service commitments, system components, data flows, user groups, boundaries, subservice organisations, complementary user responsibilities, and relevant controls.

9. The organisation shall identify and document all material systems, applications, infrastructure, databases, networks, repositories, administrative tools, security tools, logging sources, backup systems, and monitoring platforms that support the in-scope service.

10. The organisation shall maintain an inventory of material data types processed by the in-scope service, including customer data, confidential information, personal information, authentication data, system data, support data, and audit data.

11. The organisation shall maintain a data flow view for the in-scope service that identifies major data entry points, processing activities, storage locations, transmission paths, integrations, outputs, deletion points, and third-party transfers.

12. The organisation shall identify all roles with privileged, administrative, development, support, operational, security, compliance, or privacy responsibilities for the in-scope service.

13. The organisation shall identify all third-party providers that materially support the in-scope service and shall classify whether their services affect security, availability, confidentiality, processing integrity, privacy, or multiple selected categories.

14. The organisation shall define whether third-party controls are addressed through direct organisational controls, complementary controls, contractual commitments, vendor assurance reports, security reviews, privacy reviews, or other oversight mechanisms.

15. The organisation shall not exclude a material system, process, location, team, data type, or third-party dependency from the SOC 2 scope solely for convenience, lack of control maturity, lack of evidence, or anticipated audit difficulty.

16. The organisation shall document all scope exclusions and shall ensure each exclusion is supported by a clear rationale demonstrating that the excluded item does not materially affect the in-scope service or selected categories.

17. The organisation shall reassess SOC 2 scope when significant changes occur, including new products, new customer commitments, acquisitions, major architecture changes, migration to new hosting environments, new regulated data processing, new subprocessors, new regions, or material changes to service delivery.

18. The organisation shall ensure SOC 2 scope decisions are approved before the beginning of each examination period, unless a change during the period requires formal reapproval.

19. The organisation shall ensure that all controls mapped to the selected categories are implemented, owned, evidenced, monitored, and retained in a manner that supports the intended examination type and reporting period.

20. The organisation shall ensure that SOC 2 evidence is collected from authoritative sources and covers the full reporting period for recurring controls, population-based controls, access reviews, change management activities, incidents, vendor reviews, risk assessments, and privacy operations.

21. The organisation shall ensure that management’s description of the system does not overstate control coverage, service commitments, privacy practices, availability commitments, processing guarantees, or confidentiality protections.

22. The organisation shall ensure that customer contracts, service-level commitments, public security statements, privacy notices, data processing terms, support terms, and product documentation are reviewed for alignment with the selected SOC 2 categories.

23. The organisation shall ensure that privacy commitments included in SOC 2 scope are consistent with actual personal information practices, including notice, choice where applicable, collection, use, retention, disclosure, access, correction, deletion, and disposal.

24. The organisation shall ensure that availability commitments included in SOC 2 scope are supported by monitoring, alerting, incident response, backup, recovery, capacity management, and business continuity processes.

25. The organisation shall ensure that confidentiality commitments included in SOC 2 scope are supported by access controls, encryption, secure transmission, data classification, need-to-know access, secure disposal, and third-party confidentiality obligations.

26. The organisation shall ensure that processing integrity commitments included in SOC 2 scope are supported by controls over input validation, authorization, completeness checks, error handling, reconciliation, exception handling, processing monitoring, and output review where applicable.

27. The organisation shall ensure that Security controls apply across all selected categories and include governance, risk management, logical access, change management, secure development, vulnerability management, incident response, monitoring, endpoint security, network security, and vendor oversight as applicable to the in-scope service.

28. The organisation shall maintain traceability between selected categories, service commitments, system requirements, control objectives, control activities, evidence sources, control owners, and review frequencies.

29. The organisation shall communicate the approved SOC 2 scope and selected categories to relevant executives, control owners, engineering leaders, operations teams, support teams, privacy personnel, legal personnel, and vendor management personnel.

30. The organisation shall retain scope approval records, category selection rationale, scope diagrams, system descriptions, data flow documentation, third-party dependency lists, and related approvals in accordance with the organisation’s evidence retention requirements.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors or Executive Leadership | Provides oversight of the SOC 2 program, ensures adequate resources are available, and receives material updates on SOC 2 scope, readiness, exceptions, and examination outcomes. |
| Executive Sponsor | Approves the SOC 2 scope, selected categories, examination objectives, reporting period, and material scope changes. Resolves cross-functional issues affecting SOC 2 readiness or examination completion. |
| Compliance Owner / GRC Lead | Owns this Policy, coordinates SOC 2 scoping activities, maintains scope documentation, validates evidence expectations, coordinates with auditors, and monitors compliance with this Policy. |
| Service Owner | Confirms that the in-scope service description, service commitments, customer obligations, system requirements, and operational dependencies are accurate and complete. |
| Security Owner | Ensures security controls are designed, implemented, evidenced, and monitored across the in-scope service and supporting environments. |
| Infrastructure / Operations Owner | Maintains availability-related controls including monitoring, alerting, capacity management, backups, recovery, resilience, incident response support, and operational procedures. |
| Engineering Owner | Ensures application, development, deployment, code review, testing, processing integrity, and change management controls operate effectively for the in-scope service. |
| Privacy Owner | Ensures privacy practices, notices, personal information inventories, data subject request processes, retention practices, disclosure controls, and subprocessors are reflected accurately in SOC 2 scope. |
| Legal / Contract Owner | Reviews customer commitments, contractual obligations, confidentiality terms, data processing terms, privacy notices, and public statements for consistency with SOC 2 scope. |
| Vendor Management Owner | Maintains oversight of third-party providers and subprocessors that materially support the in-scope service, including due diligence, contracts, assurance reviews, and risk tracking. |
| Control Owners | Operate assigned controls, maintain evidence, remediate deficiencies, participate in readiness activities, and notify the Compliance Owner of control changes or failures. |
| Internal Audit or Independent Reviewer | Performs independent readiness reviews, control testing, or advisory reviews where assigned and reports findings to management. |
| All Personnel Supporting the In-Scope Service | Comply with applicable SOC 2 control requirements, protect in-scope data and systems, complete assigned training, follow approved processes, and report issues promptly. |

The following approval authorities shall apply to SOC 2 scope decisions:

| Decision Area | Required Approver |
|---|---|
| Initial SOC 2 scope approval | Executive Sponsor and Compliance Owner |
| Selection of Trust Services categories | Executive Sponsor, Compliance Owner, Service Owner, and relevant category owners |
| Addition of a material system or service | Compliance Owner and Service Owner |
| Removal or exclusion of a material system or service | Executive Sponsor and Compliance Owner |
| Addition or removal of a material third-party provider | Compliance Owner, Vendor Management Owner, and Service Owner |
| Material change to service commitments | Executive Sponsor, Service Owner, Legal Owner, and Compliance Owner |
| Material privacy scope change | Privacy Owner, Legal Owner, and Compliance Owner |
| Examination period confirmation | Executive Sponsor and Compliance Owner |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all personnel and third parties supporting the in-scope SOC 2 service.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through periodic governance reviews, readiness assessments, control owner attestations, evidence reviews, risk assessments, internal audits, vendor reviews, management reviews, and external examination activities.

At a minimum, the following monitoring activities shall be performed:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Responsible Role | Expected Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| SOC 2 scope review | At least annually and before each examination period | Compliance Owner | Approved scope record and category selection rationale |
| Service commitment review | At least annually and upon material contract or product change | Service Owner, Legal Owner, Compliance Owner | Updated service commitments and system requirements |
| System inventory review | Quarterly | Technical Owner, Security Owner | Updated in-scope system inventory |
| Data flow and data type review | At least annually and upon material architecture change | Privacy Owner, Security Owner, Engineering Owner | Updated data inventory and data flow documentation |
| Third-party dependency review | At least annually and upon onboarding or material change | Vendor Management Owner | Updated vendor list and assurance status |
| Control ownership review | Quarterly | Compliance Owner | Updated control owner register |
| Evidence completeness review | Monthly during readiness and examination periods | Compliance Owner | Evidence status report and remediation tracker |
| Scope change review | Upon trigger event | Compliance Owner and affected owners | Approved or rejected scope change decision |
| Management review of SOC 2 readiness | At least quarterly during active examination preparation | Executive Sponsor and Compliance Owner | Management review minutes and action items |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in corrective action, management escalation, remediation plans, disciplinary action, contract remedies, suspension of access, vendor remediation requirements, or other actions permitted by organisational policy and applicable agreements.

Material issues that may affect SOC 2 scope, control operation, examination readiness, or management’s assertion shall be escalated to the Executive Sponsor and Compliance Owner without undue delay.

Examples of material issues include:

- Discovery of an unscoped system that stores or processes in-scope customer data.
- Use of an unapproved third-party provider supporting the in-scope service.
- A material service outage affecting availability commitments.
- A security incident affecting customer data, confidential information, or personal information.
- A significant change to data processing activities or privacy commitments.
- Inability to provide evidence for a key control during the reporting period.
- A material change in product architecture or hosting environment.
- A mismatch between customer commitments and actual control coverage.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business need, risk assessment, compensating control plan, defined owner, and approved time-bound remediation or acceptance decision.

Exceptions shall not be used to misrepresent SOC 2 scope, exclude material risks without justification, avoid required controls, or conceal control deficiencies from management or external examiners.

All exception requests shall include:

| Required Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | Unique identifier assigned by the Compliance Owner |
| Requestor | Individual requesting the exception |
| Business Owner | Accountable owner for the affected service, process, or system |
| Description | Clear explanation of the requested exception |
| Affected SOC 2 Category | Security, Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity, Privacy, or multiple categories |
| Affected System or Process | System, service, process, vendor, location, or data type impacted |
| Business Justification | Reason the exception is required |
| Risk Assessment | Potential impact to customers, service commitments, systems, data, compliance, and examination readiness |
| Compensating Controls | Controls that reduce the risk while the exception is active |
| Remediation Plan | Actions required to eliminate the exception or reduce the risk |
| Expiration Date | Date by which the exception must be resolved or reapproved |
| Required Approval | Appropriate approval based on risk and scope impact |

Exception approval shall follow this authority model:

| Exception Risk Level | Required Approval |
|---|---|
| Low | Compliance Owner and relevant Control Owner |
| Medium | Compliance Owner, Service Owner, and relevant category owner |
| High | Executive Sponsor, Compliance Owner, Service Owner, and relevant category owner |
| Critical or customer-impacting | Executive Sponsor, Legal Owner, Compliance Owner, and applicable senior leadership |

Approved exceptions shall be tracked to closure. Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless formally reapproved before expiration.

The Compliance Owner shall maintain the exception register and shall report material exceptions to the Executive Sponsor during management review.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever a material change occurs that could affect SOC 2 scope, selected categories, service commitments, system boundaries, data processing, third-party dependencies, or control responsibilities.

Material change events include, but are not limited to:

- Launch of a new product, module, service, region, or customer-facing capability.
- Expansion into new customer segments or regulated industries.
- Introduction of new personal information processing activities.
- New or changed availability, confidentiality, processing, security, or privacy commitments.
- Material architecture redesign, cloud migration, or infrastructure change.
- Acquisition, divestiture, or organisational restructuring.
- Onboarding or offboarding of a material third-party provider or subprocessor.
- Significant incident, outage, breach, or privacy event.
- Auditor feedback indicating scope ambiguity or incomplete documentation.
- Management decision to change examination type or reporting period.

The Compliance Owner shall be responsible for maintaining this Policy, coordinating stakeholder review, updating scope records, and ensuring approved changes are communicated to relevant personnel.

Policy changes shall be approved by the Executive Sponsor and Compliance Owner. Changes affecting privacy commitments shall also be reviewed by the Privacy Owner and Legal Owner. Changes affecting customer contractual commitments shall also be reviewed by the Legal Owner and Service Owner.

The organisation shall maintain version history for this Policy.

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Author | Approver |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [Effective Date] | Initial version | [Author Name] | [Approver Name] |

SOC2-002.title: Type 1 vs Type 2 Decision Document
SOC2-002.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [SOC2-POL-001] | 1.0 | [Compliance Owner / GRC Lead] | [Effective Date] | SOC 2 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes the mandatory requirements for selecting, approving, and maintaining the organisation’s SOC 2 report type and audit period. It ensures that decisions between a Type 1 and Type 2 SOC 2 examination are made consistently, based on business need, customer commitments, service maturity, control readiness, and audit feasibility.

The Policy is intended to support credible assurance over the organisation’s system, services, controls, and commitments to customers and other stakeholders. It defines when a Type 1 report is appropriate, when a Type 2 report is required, and how the audit period for a Type 2 examination shall be determined.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All SOC 2 examinations undertaken by the organisation.
- All services, products, platforms, systems, processes, and business units included or proposed for inclusion in the SOC 2 system description.
- All Trust Services Criteria selected for the SOC 2 examination, including security and any additional categories such as availability, confidentiality, processing integrity, or privacy.
- All personnel, contractors, service owners, control owners, executive sponsors, and third-party service providers involved in SOC 2 readiness, audit planning, evidence collection, control operation, or customer assurance.
- All decisions relating to:
 - Initial SOC 2 report type selection.
 - Transition from Type 1 to Type 2.
 - Type 2 audit period length.
 - Changes to the audit period.
 - Re-performance of a Type 1 examination.
 - Deferral, cancellation, or modification of a SOC 2 examination.

This Policy does not define detailed SOC 2 control operating procedures, evidence collection steps, auditor testing methods, or customer-facing distribution rules. Those requirements are addressed in supporting procedures, control documentation, and report distribution guidance.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall formally determine whether a SOC 2 Type 1 or Type 2 examination is required before engaging an independent auditor for each SOC 2 reporting cycle.

2. The organisation shall document the decision rationale for the selected report type, including business drivers, customer requirements, control maturity, audit readiness, service scope, timing constraints, and any known limitations.

3. The organisation shall use a SOC 2 Type 1 examination when the primary objective is to provide assurance that controls are suitably designed and implemented at a specific point in time.

4. The organisation shall not use a Type 1 report as a substitute for ongoing operating effectiveness assurance when customers, contractual obligations, market expectations, or risk levels require evidence that controls operated over a defined period.

5. The organisation shall use a SOC 2 Type 2 examination when the primary objective is to provide assurance that controls are suitably designed, implemented, and operating effectively over a defined review period.

6. The organisation shall maintain Type 2 reporting as the default long-term SOC 2 assurance position for mature in-scope services that are commercially offered to customers or relied upon for customer data processing.

7. The organisation shall consider a Type 1 examination appropriate only where one or more of the following conditions apply:

 | Condition | Type 1 Use Case |
 |---|---|
 | First-time SOC 2 examination | The organisation has not previously completed a SOC 2 examination and requires an initial independent assessment of control design and implementation. |
 | Newly launched service | The in-scope system, platform, or service has been recently launched and has not operated long enough to support a Type 2 period. |
 | Material control redesign | Significant changes have been made to controls, architecture, or business processes, and the organisation requires point-in-time assurance before a Type 2 period begins. |
 | Customer interim assurance | A customer requires a SOC 2 report before sufficient operating history exists for a Type 2 examination. |
 | Acquisition or integration | A newly acquired or integrated service requires baseline assurance before being added to the recurring Type 2 scope. |
 | Readiness validation | Management requires independent confirmation that the control environment is ready before committing to a Type 2 audit period. |

8. The organisation shall consider a Type 2 examination required where one or more of the following conditions apply:

 | Condition | Type 2 Requirement |
 |---|---|
 | Customer or contract requirement | Customer agreements, procurement processes, or due diligence requests require evidence of control operating effectiveness. |
 | Established production service | The in-scope service has operated in production long enough to support testing over an audit period. |
 | Recurring assurance commitment | The organisation has committed to periodic SOC 2 reporting for customers, partners, regulators, or internal governance. |
 | Elevated risk profile | The service processes sensitive customer data, supports critical customer operations, or has significant availability, confidentiality, privacy, or integrity commitments. |
 | Prior Type 1 completion | A Type 1 examination has been completed and management has committed to progressing to operating effectiveness assurance. |
 | Market expectation | Prospective customers or industry norms reasonably expect a Type 2 report for the service being offered. |

9. The organisation shall not commence a Type 2 audit period unless management has concluded that key controls are implemented, control owners are assigned, evidence generation is operating, and known control gaps have been assessed.

10. The organisation shall select a Type 2 audit period that is long enough to demonstrate consistent control operation and appropriate for the assurance expectations of customers and stakeholders.

11. The organisation shall use an audit period of at least six months for a Type 2 examination unless a shorter period is formally approved as an exception.

12. The organisation shall use an audit period of twelve months for recurring Type 2 examinations once the SOC 2 programme has reached steady-state maturity, unless a different period is justified and approved.

13. The organisation shall define the Type 2 audit period before the period starts, unless the examination is specifically planned as a retrospective audit based on sufficient existing evidence and auditor agreement.

14. The organisation shall not select a Type 2 audit period based solely on convenience, sales timelines, or customer pressure where doing so would compromise the reliability, completeness, or credibility of the examination.

15. The organisation shall consider the following factors when selecting the Type 2 audit period:

 | Factor | Requirement |
 |---|---|
 | Control frequency | The audit period shall allow recurring controls to operate enough times for meaningful testing. |
 | Service maturity | The period shall reflect how long the in-scope service has been stable in production. |
 | Evidence availability | Evidence shall be generated and retained for the full period or otherwise be supportable through reliable records. |
 | Customer expectations | The period shall align with customer assurance needs and contractual commitments. |
 | Prior audit history | Prior Type 1 or Type 2 results shall be considered when determining period length. |
 | Control changes | Major changes during the period shall be assessed for impact on audit scope and control testing. |
 | Auditor feasibility | The independent auditor shall be able to perform appropriate testing over the selected period. |
 | Reporting deadline | The period shall allow sufficient time for management review, auditor testing, report drafting, and final issuance. |

16. The organisation shall apply the following standard decision model unless an exception is approved:

 | Scenario | Required Decision |
 |---|---|
 | First SOC 2 examination and controls recently implemented | Type 1, followed by Type 2 after a defined operating period. |
 | First SOC 2 examination and controls have operated reliably for at least six months | Type 2 may be selected if evidence is complete and auditor-ready. |
 | Existing Type 1 report with customer demand for operating effectiveness | Type 2 shall be planned as the next examination. |
 | Existing Type 2 programme with no material scope change | Annual Type 2 shall be maintained. |
 | New product added to mature SOC 2 programme | Management shall decide whether to include it in the next Type 2 period or obtain separate Type 1 assurance first. |
 | Material platform or control redesign | Management shall assess whether a Type 1 reset, bridge communication, modified Type 2 period, or scoped exclusion is required. |
 | Significant evidence gaps during planned Type 2 period | Management shall assess whether to remediate and continue, shorten the period by exception, delay the report, or revert to Type 1. |

17. The organisation shall obtain approval from the Executive Sponsor, Compliance Owner, and relevant service leadership before finalising the report type and audit period.

18. The organisation shall consult the independent auditor before confirming the audit period to validate that the proposed period, scope, and evidence approach are suitable for examination.

19. The organisation shall document the approved report type and audit period in a SOC 2 Decision Record before audit planning activities are finalised.

20. The SOC 2 Decision Record shall include, at minimum:

 | Decision Record Field | Required Content |
 |---|---|
 | Service or system name | Name of the in-scope service, platform, or system. |
 | Report type | Type 1 or Type 2. |
 | Reporting period | Point-in-time date for Type 1 or start and end dates for Type 2. |
 | Selected Trust Services Categories | Categories included in the examination. |
 | Business rationale | Reason the selected report type meets current assurance needs. |
 | Customer or contractual drivers | Relevant customer commitments, sales requirements, or contract obligations. |
 | Control readiness assessment | Summary of control implementation and operating maturity. |
 | Evidence readiness | Confirmation that evidence is available or will be generated for the required period. |
 | Known limitations | Any exclusions, constraints, unresolved gaps, or scope caveats. |
 | Auditor consultation | Confirmation that the auditor has been consulted on feasibility. |
 | Approvals | Required management approvals and approval dates. |

21. The organisation shall maintain a SOC 2 audit planning timeline for each reporting cycle.

22. The SOC 2 audit planning timeline shall include realistic milestones for readiness, period start, evidence collection, audit fieldwork, management review, report issuance, and customer availability.

23. The organisation shall use the following planning baseline unless an alternative timeline is approved:

 | Milestone | Type 1 Baseline | Type 2 Baseline |
 |---|---:|---:|
 | Confirm report scope and categories | 8-12 weeks before target report date | 4-8 weeks before audit period start |
 | Complete readiness assessment | 6-10 weeks before target report date | Before audit period start |
 | Finalise auditor engagement | 6-8 weeks before target report date | Before audit period start |
 | Confirm system description owner | 4-6 weeks before target report date | Before audit period start |
 | Begin audit period | Not applicable | Approved audit period start date |
 | Perform evidence quality checks | 3-4 weeks before fieldwork | Monthly or quarterly during audit period |
 | Complete fieldwork | As scheduled with auditor | After audit period end |
 | Management review of draft report | Before final issuance | Before final issuance |
 | Final report issuance | Target date approved by management | Target date approved by management |

24. The organisation shall not represent a SOC 2 examination as covering controls, systems, services, locations, entities, or time periods that are not included in the approved audit scope.

25. The organisation shall ensure that customer-facing statements about SOC 2 report type, audit period, status, or expected issuance date are accurate, approved, and not misleading.

26. The organisation shall not commit to providing a Type 2 report to customers unless the audit period, report scope, auditor engagement, and expected issuance timeline have been approved by authorised management.

27. The organisation shall maintain evidence supporting the report type and audit period decision for each SOC 2 reporting cycle.

28. The organisation shall retain approved SOC 2 Decision Records, audit planning materials, management approvals, auditor communications, readiness results, and related evidence in the designated compliance repository.

29. The organisation shall review material changes to the in-scope system during a Type 2 audit period to determine whether the audit period, report scope, or report type remains appropriate.

30. The organisation shall escalate any event that may materially affect the SOC 2 report type, audit period, audit scope, or issuance timeline to the Executive Sponsor and Compliance Owner within a reasonable timeframe.

31. The organisation shall assess whether bridge letters, customer notices, modified reporting timelines, or additional assurance activities are required when there is a gap between SOC 2 report periods or a delay in report issuance.

32. The organisation shall not rely on bridge letters as a permanent replacement for timely Type 2 reporting.

33. The organisation shall ensure that Type 2 report periods are planned to minimise assurance gaps between reporting cycles wherever commercially and operationally feasible.

34. The organisation shall document any decision to delay, cancel, shorten, extend, or materially modify a SOC 2 examination.

35. The organisation shall ensure that SOC 2 report type and audit period decisions are aligned with the organisation’s risk appetite, customer assurance strategy, contractual commitments, and control maturity.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | Provides executive ownership for SOC 2 reporting strategy; approves the selected report type and audit period; resolves conflicts involving customer commitments, resources, timing, or risk acceptance. |
| Compliance Owner / GRC Lead | Owns this Policy; coordinates SOC 2 decision-making; prepares the SOC 2 Decision Record; validates readiness inputs; maintains audit planning documentation; coordinates with the independent auditor. |
| Security Leader | Confirms security control readiness; identifies material control gaps; assesses the impact of security incidents, control changes, and technical risks on the selected report type and audit period. |
| Privacy Leader | Provides input where privacy commitments are included in scope; confirms readiness of privacy-related controls, notices, data handling processes, and evidence. |
| Engineering / Technology Leader | Confirms platform and infrastructure readiness; identifies material system changes; ensures technical evidence is available for the audit period. |
| Product or Service Owner | Defines the in-scope service boundaries; confirms production status, customer commitments, service changes, and customer-facing assurance needs. |
| Legal / Contracts | Reviews customer contractual obligations, report commitments, confidentiality restrictions, and customer communications relating to SOC 2 report availability. |
| Sales / Customer Success | Provides customer assurance requirements and deadlines; ensures customer-facing commitments are aligned with approved SOC 2 decisions. |
| Control Owners | Operate assigned controls; maintain evidence; notify the Compliance Owner of control failures, delays, or changes affecting SOC 2 readiness. |
| Internal Audit or Risk Function, where applicable | Provides independent challenge or advisory input on readiness, risk, and governance of SOC 2 decisions. |
| Independent Auditor | Provides professional input on audit feasibility, report type implications, evidence expectations, and audit period suitability. The auditor does not approve management’s business decision. |
| Senior Management | Reviews and approves significant changes to SOC 2 reporting strategy, including exceptions, deferrals, or deviations from standard Type 2 reporting expectations. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all personnel involved in SOC 2 planning, readiness, reporting, customer assurance, and control operation.

The Compliance Owner shall monitor compliance with this Policy by:

- Maintaining an approved SOC 2 Decision Record for each examination.
- Confirming that report type and audit period decisions are approved before auditor fieldwork begins.
- Performing periodic readiness checks before and during a Type 2 audit period.
- Confirming that control owners understand evidence expectations for the selected report type.
- Reviewing customer-facing SOC 2 commitments for consistency with approved decisions.
- Tracking open readiness gaps, audit period risks, evidence issues, and report issuance risks.
- Reporting material SOC 2 planning risks to the Executive Sponsor and senior management.

The organisation shall monitor the following minimum indicators:

| Monitoring Area | Minimum Expectation |
|---|---|
| Approved decision record | Completed before audit engagement is finalised or audit period begins. |
| Audit period readiness | Confirmed before Type 2 period start. |
| Evidence collection | Reviewed periodically during the audit period. |
| Control owner accountability | Control ownership documented and current. |
| Scope stability | Material system or process changes assessed for SOC 2 impact. |
| Customer commitments | SOC 2 commitments reviewed before being communicated externally. |
| Reporting timeline | Milestones tracked against approved target dates. |
| Assurance gaps | Gaps between report periods identified and managed. |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in:

- Rejection or deferral of a proposed SOC 2 examination.
- Requirement to complete a Type 1 examination before proceeding to Type 2.
- Extension, delay, or restart of a Type 2 audit period.
- Management review of customer commitments and external assurance statements.
- Corrective action plans for control owners or business leaders.
- Escalation to senior management.
- Disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policy where non-compliance is deliberate, negligent, or materially misleading.

The organisation shall treat inaccurate or unauthorised statements about SOC 2 report type, report period, report availability, or scope as a compliance issue requiring prompt correction.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be formally documented, risk-assessed, approved, and time-bound.

Exceptions may include, but are not limited to:

- Use of a Type 2 audit period shorter than six months.
- Deferral of a planned Type 2 examination.
- Selection of a Type 1 examination where a Type 2 report was expected by customers.
- Material change to an approved audit period.
- Extension of an assurance gap between report periods.
- Retrospective selection of a Type 2 audit period.
- Exclusion of a service, system, location, process, or control area previously expected to be in scope.

Exception requests shall include:

| Exception Field | Required Content |
|---|---|
| Exception description | Clear statement of the requested deviation. |
| Business justification | Reason the exception is necessary. |
| Affected report | SOC 2 report type, scope, and period affected. |
| Risk assessment | Impact on customers, contracts, assurance, control reliability, and audit feasibility. |
| Compensating actions | Steps to reduce risk, such as additional readiness testing, customer communication, or enhanced monitoring. |
| Duration | Defined start date and end date or review date. |
| Approvals | Approval by the Executive Sponsor, Compliance Owner, and any other required stakeholders. |
| Auditor consultation | Confirmation of whether the independent auditor has been consulted, where relevant. |

The Compliance Owner shall maintain an exception register for SOC 2 reporting decisions.

Exceptions shall not be used to conceal control failures, misrepresent assurance coverage, avoid customer commitments, or create misleading external statements about the organisation’s SOC 2 status.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to the organisation’s SOC 2 programme, services, customer commitments, control environment, audit strategy, or risk profile.

The Compliance Owner is responsible for coordinating review and maintenance of this Policy. Review shall include input from relevant stakeholders, including security, privacy, technology, product, legal, sales, customer success, executive leadership, and the independent auditor where appropriate.

The review shall assess whether:

- The Type 1 and Type 2 decision criteria remain suitable.
- The standard Type 2 audit period expectations remain appropriate.
- Customer and contractual assurance requirements have changed.
- SOC 2 reporting timelines remain realistic.
- Evidence collection and readiness practices support the selected report type.
- Recent audit outcomes indicate a need to revise decision criteria.
- Exceptions or assurance gaps indicate recurring planning issues.
- Roles and responsibilities remain accurate.
- Supporting templates and decision records remain current.

All material updates to this Policy shall be approved by the Executive Sponsor and Compliance Owner before publication.

Version history shall be maintained as follows:

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Approved By |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [Effective Date] | Initial release | [Approver Name / Role] |

SOC2-003.title: System Description Outline (Section III)
SOC2-003.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-SOC2-SYS-DESC] | 1.0 | [Compliance Owner / Trust Services Owner] | [Effective Date] | SOC 2 | Confidential |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes mandatory requirements for preparing, approving, maintaining, and using the System Description included in Section III of the organisation’s SOC 2 report.

The System Description is the organisation’s formal description of the services, systems, processes, people, technologies, controls, and boundaries relevant to the SOC 2 examination. It shall be accurate, complete, clear, and suitable for inclusion in a report provided to customers, auditors, regulators, partners, and other authorised stakeholders.

This Policy ensures that the System Description:

- Represents management’s description of the system fairly and consistently.
- Defines the services and system boundaries covered by the SOC 2 report.
- Describes the control environment and relevant trust services commitments.
- Identifies key components, dependencies, user responsibilities, and complementary controls.
- Is maintained through the reporting period and updated when material changes occur.
- Supports the independent auditor’s examination without relying on informal or undocumented explanations.

## Scope

This Policy applies to all personnel, contractors, service owners, control owners, process owners, and business functions involved in designing, operating, supporting, documenting, reviewing, or approving the systems and services included in the SOC 2 report.

This Policy applies to the System Description for the following in-scope service or services:

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| In-Scope Service(s) | [Name of product, platform, managed service, or business service] |
| Legal Entity | [Legal entity name] |
| Report Type | [Type I / Type II] |
| Reporting Period | [Start date] to [End date] |
| Trust Services Categories | [Security, Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity, Privacy, as applicable] |
| Primary Locations | [Corporate offices, data centres, cloud regions, remote workforce locations, as applicable] |
| Primary Cloud / Hosting Providers | [Provider names, if applicable] |
| Primary Customer Base | [Customer segment or industry, if appropriate] |

This Policy covers the content, ownership, evidence expectations, change management, approval requirements, and maintenance process for the System Description.

This Policy does not replace detailed operational policies, procedures, standards, control descriptions, network diagrams, system inventories, incident response plans, business continuity plans, privacy notices, or contractual documents. Those documents shall support and align with the System Description.

## Policy Statements

1. **Ownership and Accountability**
 1. The organisation shall assign an accountable owner for the SOC 2 System Description.
 2. The System Description Owner shall ensure the document is accurate, current, internally consistent, and approved by management before it is provided to the independent auditor.
 3. Each in-scope business, technology, security, compliance, privacy, and operations function shall provide timely and accurate information to support the System Description.
 4. Management shall take responsibility for the final System Description included in the SOC 2 report.

2. **Required System Description Content**
 1. The System Description shall include a clear overview of the organisation, the in-scope service, and the purpose of the system.
 2. The System Description shall identify the period covered by the report and whether the description supports a point-in-time or period-of-time examination.
 3. The System Description shall describe the nature of services provided to customers and the principal service commitments communicated through contracts, service descriptions, policies, or other formal customer-facing materials.
 4. The System Description shall describe the trust services categories included in the report and how they relate to the organisation’s service commitments.
 5. The System Description shall define the boundaries of the system, including in-scope products, applications, infrastructure, locations, teams, processes, and supporting technologies.
 6. The System Description shall identify material system components, including applications, databases, infrastructure, networks, data stores, monitoring tools, identity systems, ticketing systems, and relevant third-party services.
 7. The System Description shall describe the types of data processed, stored, transmitted, or otherwise handled by the in-scope system.
 8. The System Description shall describe the principal classes of users, including internal users, customers, administrators, support personnel, and third parties, as applicable.
 9. The System Description shall describe relevant user entity responsibilities, including customer responsibilities that are necessary for the controls to operate effectively.
 10. The System Description shall describe complementary controls expected to be performed by customers, subservice organisations, or other external parties, where applicable.
 11. The System Description shall identify subservice organisations used to deliver, secure, operate, monitor, or support the in-scope service.
 12. The System Description shall describe whether subservice organisations are included within or excluded from the SOC 2 examination boundary.
 13. The System Description shall describe significant control activities relevant to the in-scope trust services categories.
 14. The System Description shall describe the organisation’s control environment, risk assessment activities, communication practices, monitoring activities, and change management practices at an appropriate level.
 15. The System Description shall include sufficient detail for a reader to understand how the system is designed and operated without disclosing sensitive information that would create unnecessary security or commercial risk.

3. **System Boundary Requirements**
 1. The System Description shall clearly distinguish in-scope systems, processes, teams, and locations from out-of-scope items.
 2. The boundary shall align with the services covered by customer commitments and the auditor’s examination scope.
 3. The boundary shall be supported by current inventories, architecture diagrams, data flow diagrams, vendor lists, and service ownership records.
 4. The System Description shall not imply coverage of services, systems, regions, environments, products, or control activities that are not included in the SOC 2 examination.
 5. If shared corporate services support the in-scope system, the System Description shall describe the relevant shared services and their relationship to the system.

4. **Accuracy and Evidence Requirements**
 1. Statements in the System Description shall be supported by evidence, documented processes, approved policies, system records, service inventories, contracts, diagrams, or other reliable source materials.
 2. Control descriptions shall reflect actual control design and operation, not aspirational practices or planned future improvements.
 3. The System Description shall not include unsupported claims about control maturity, service performance, security outcomes, availability, confidentiality, privacy, or processing integrity.
 4. The System Description shall avoid marketing language and shall use factual, auditable, and balanced wording.
 5. The System Description shall be reconciled to the control matrix, control narratives, policy set, risk register, vendor inventory, architecture records, and auditor-provided drafts before approval.
 6. Material inconsistencies identified during review shall be resolved before the System Description is issued.

5. **Drafting Standards**
 1. The System Description shall be written in clear business language suitable for customers, auditors, and other authorised report users.
 2. The System Description shall be structured consistently across reporting periods unless changes are required due to changes in services, systems, commitments, or audit scope.
 3. The System Description shall describe what the organisation does, how the system is organised, and how relevant controls are designed, without presenting step-by-step operational procedures.
 4. The System Description shall distinguish between management processes, automated controls, manual controls, customer responsibilities, and third-party responsibilities.
 5. The System Description shall use defined terms consistently, including names of services, platforms, environments, customer roles, data categories, and subservice organisations.
 6. The System Description shall identify the period or point in time to which the description applies.
 7. The System Description shall disclose significant changes during the reporting period that affect the system or controls, where relevant to report users.

6. **Minimum Outline Requirements**
 1. The System Description shall follow an approved outline that includes, at minimum, the following sections:

| Required Section | Minimum Content Requirement |
|---|---|
| Overview of the Organisation | Legal entity, business purpose, service model, customer base, and operating model relevant to the SOC 2 report. |
| Description of the In-Scope Service | Products, services, features, and service commitments included in the report. |
| Report Scope and Boundaries | Reporting period, trust services categories, in-scope systems, excluded systems, locations, and organisational units. |
| Principal Service Commitments | Commitments made to customers regarding security, availability, confidentiality, processing integrity, privacy, or other in-scope areas. |
| System Components | Applications, infrastructure, data stores, networks, tooling, environments, and supporting technologies. |
| Data Processed by the System | Types of customer data, confidential data, operational data, logs, metadata, and personal information, as applicable. |
| People and Organisational Structure | Teams and roles responsible for governance, operations, engineering, support, security, compliance, and service delivery. |
| Processes and Procedures | High-level description of processes supporting the system, including access management, change management, incident response, monitoring, vendor management, backup, recovery, and risk management. |
| Control Environment | Management oversight, policies, standards, ethics, accountability, and governance practices. |
| Risk Assessment | How risks relevant to the in-scope service are identified, assessed, treated, and reviewed. |
| Information and Communication | Internal and external communication channels, customer communications, policy communication, security awareness, and reporting practices. |
| Monitoring Activities | Control monitoring, management review, internal assessments, vulnerability management, logging, alerts, and remediation tracking. |
| Subservice Organisations | Third parties that support the service, their role, and whether they are included or excluded from the examination boundary. |
| Complementary Controls | Responsibilities expected of customers, users, and third parties for the system to achieve its service commitments. |
| Significant Changes | Material changes to systems, controls, service commitments, infrastructure, organisational structure, or subservice organisations during the reporting period. |
| Incidents and Relevant Events | Significant incidents, outages, security events, or control-impacting events that are relevant to the report, described in a factual and approved manner. |
| Applicable Criteria Mapping Summary | A plain-language explanation of how described controls support the in-scope trust services categories, without detailed audit testing results. |

7. **Subservice Organisation Requirements**
 1. The System Description shall identify subservice organisations that are material to delivery, security, availability, confidentiality, privacy, processing integrity, or operation of the in-scope service.
 2. For each material subservice organisation, the System Description shall describe the nature of services provided.
 3. The System Description shall state whether the subservice organisation’s controls are included within the SOC 2 examination boundary or whether the organisation relies on complementary controls performed by that subservice organisation.
 4. The System Description shall describe the organisation’s vendor governance and monitoring practices at a level appropriate to the role of the subservice organisation.
 5. The organisation shall maintain supporting evidence for subservice organisation identification, risk assessment, due diligence, contracting, monitoring, and review.

8. **Complementary User Entity Control Requirements**
 1. The System Description shall identify customer or user responsibilities that are necessary for the organisation’s controls and service commitments to operate effectively.
 2. Complementary user entity controls shall be specific, realistic, and directly related to how customers use the in-scope service.
 3. The System Description shall not shift responsibility to customers for controls that the organisation has committed to perform.
 4. Complementary user entity controls shall be reviewed by Legal, Customer Success, Security, Compliance, and relevant service owners before approval.
 5. Customer responsibilities described in the System Description shall align with customer agreements, product documentation, security guides, acceptable use terms, and service configuration guidance.

9. **Control Description Requirements**
 1. The System Description shall describe control activities at a level that enables report users to understand the design of controls relevant to the in-scope service.
 2. Control descriptions shall align with the organisation’s approved control inventory and auditor-facing control matrix.
 3. The System Description shall describe both preventive and detective control activities where relevant.
 4. The System Description shall address logical access, authentication, authorisation, privileged access, change management, incident management, vulnerability management, logging and monitoring, vendor management, risk management, data protection, backup and recovery, business continuity, and security governance where relevant to scope.
 5. The System Description shall not include confidential implementation details, secrets, exploit-enabling information, private network details, or information that would materially increase risk if disclosed.

10. **Change and Event Disclosure Requirements**
 1. The System Description shall disclose significant changes during the reporting period when those changes are relevant to understanding the system or its controls.
 2. Significant changes may include new products, major architecture changes, migration of hosting environments, material vendor changes, major organisational restructuring, new control platforms, material changes to customer commitments, or significant incident-driven changes.
 3. The System Description shall describe significant changes factually, including the nature and timing of the change and its relevance to the in-scope system.
 4. The System Description shall be reviewed when any material system change is approved through change management.
 5. The organisation shall maintain a change log for System Description updates.

11. **Confidentiality and Disclosure Requirements**
 1. The System Description shall be classified at least as Confidential unless a higher classification is required by the organisation’s information classification policy.
 2. Drafts and final versions shall be stored only in approved repositories with access restricted to authorised personnel.
 3. The System Description shall not be distributed externally except as part of an authorised SOC 2 report release process or with approval from Legal, Compliance, and Executive Management.
 4. The System Description shall be reviewed for sensitive information before external release.
 5. The System Description shall not contain passwords, cryptographic keys, detailed firewall rule sets, exploit paths, sensitive network diagrams, unredacted incident forensic details, or other information unsuitable for external report users.

12. **Version Control Requirements**
 1. The System Description shall be version controlled.
 2. Each material draft and approved version shall include an owner, version number, date, reviewer list, and approval status.
 3. Changes shall be traceable through a documented revision history.
 4. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.
 5. The final version provided to the auditor shall be clearly identifiable and protected from unauthorised modification.

13. **Review and Approval Requirements**
 1. The System Description shall be reviewed by all required stakeholders before submission to the auditor.
 2. At minimum, the following functions shall review the System Description where applicable: Security, Compliance, Legal, Privacy, Engineering, Infrastructure, Product, Operations, Customer Support, Vendor Management, Human Resources, and Executive Management.
 3. The System Description shall be approved by an authorised management representative before being included in the SOC 2 report.
 4. Review comments shall be tracked to closure.
 5. The System Description shall not be represented as final until all required approvals are completed.

14. **Required Review Timeline**
 1. The organisation shall maintain a planning timeline for drafting, reviewing, and approving the System Description.
 2. The timeline shall provide sufficient time for stakeholder review, auditor review, management approval, and remediation of inconsistencies.
 3. The following minimum timeline shall be used unless a different timeline is formally approved by the System Description Owner:

| Activity | Minimum Timing | Responsible Party |
|---|---:|---|
| Confirm SOC 2 scope and report type | Before audit planning begins | Compliance Owner |
| Confirm in-scope systems and services | Before evidence request launch | System Description Owner and Service Owners |
| Collect source documentation and control narratives | At least 60 days before auditor draft due date | Control Owners |
| Prepare initial System Description draft | At least 45 days before auditor draft due date | System Description Owner |
| Conduct functional stakeholder review | At least 30 days before auditor draft due date | Required Reviewers |
| Resolve review comments and inconsistencies | At least 20 days before auditor draft due date | System Description Owner and Control Owners |
| Submit management-approved draft to auditor | At least 15 days before auditor draft due date | Compliance Owner |
| Review auditor comments and update draft | As requested during audit | System Description Owner |
| Final management approval | Before report issuance | Executive Sponsor |
| Archive final approved version | Within 10 business days after report issuance | Compliance Owner |

15. **Alignment with SOC 2 Report and Audit Evidence**
 1. The System Description shall align with management’s written assertion, the auditor’s report scope, and the final SOC 2 report.
 2. The System Description shall align with evidence provided during the examination.
 3. If the auditor identifies discrepancies between the System Description and audit evidence, the System Description Owner shall coordinate resolution with relevant stakeholders.
 4. The organisation shall not knowingly provide a System Description that is incomplete, misleading, outdated, or inconsistent with actual practices.
 5. Any unresolved disagreement about the accuracy or wording of the System Description shall be escalated to Executive Management, Legal, and Compliance before report issuance.

16. **Restrictions on Unsupported Future-State Statements**
 1. The System Description shall not describe future initiatives as current controls.
 2. Planned enhancements may be included only when necessary for context and clearly identified as future-state, not current-state.
 3. Control improvements implemented after the reporting period shall not be presented as having operated during the reporting period.
 4. Management shall ensure that any descriptions of remediation, improvement, or corrective action are accurate and approved.

17. **Records Retention**
 1. The organisation shall retain the approved System Description, drafts provided to the auditor, review records, approvals, evidence of reconciliations, and supporting source documents.
 2. Records shall be retained for at least [retention period] or longer where required by contract, law, audit needs, or internal policy.
 3. Records shall be protected against unauthorised access, alteration, and deletion.
 4. Records shall be retrievable for audits, customer assurance requests, management reviews, and regulatory inquiries, where authorised.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board / Executive Leadership | Provides oversight for the SOC 2 programme; supports accurate external reporting; approves significant matters where required. |
| Executive Sponsor | Ensures the System Description accurately represents the in-scope service and management’s commitments; approves the final version or delegates approval to an authorised executive. |
| System Description Owner | Owns drafting, coordination, version control, stakeholder review, comment resolution, and readiness for auditor review. |
| Compliance Owner | Coordinates the SOC 2 programme; aligns the System Description with audit scope, evidence, control matrix, auditor requests, and report deliverables. |
| Security Leadership | Reviews security control descriptions, security governance statements, incident handling content, monitoring practices, and sensitive disclosure risks. |
| Privacy Owner | Reviews privacy-related content, personal information handling, customer and data subject responsibilities, privacy commitments, and related disclosures. |
| Legal Counsel | Reviews external disclosure risk, customer commitment language, contractual alignment, report distribution restrictions, incident wording, and reliance on third parties. |
| Product Owner | Confirms service descriptions, feature scope, product boundaries, customer responsibilities, and relevant product changes. |
| Engineering Owner | Confirms application architecture, development lifecycle, change management, environments, deployment practices, and technical system components. |
| Infrastructure / Cloud Operations Owner | Confirms hosting model, cloud services, network architecture, capacity, availability, backup, recovery, monitoring, and operational controls. |
| IT Operations Owner | Confirms endpoint, identity, productivity platform, support tooling, access management, and internal IT control descriptions. |
| Vendor Management Owner | Confirms subservice organisations, vendor roles, vendor monitoring, due diligence, and third-party risk management descriptions. |
| Human Resources Owner | Confirms personnel screening, onboarding, offboarding, training, disciplinary process, and employee lifecycle descriptions. |
| Customer Support Owner | Confirms customer support processes, escalation paths, customer communications, and support access controls. |
| Control Owners | Validate control descriptions, provide supporting evidence, identify changes, and resolve discrepancies. |
| Internal Audit / Independent Assurance Function | Performs independent review where applicable; identifies inconsistencies, control description gaps, or evidence concerns. |
| Document Control / Records Management | Maintains approved versions, retention records, access controls, and archival processes. |
| All Personnel Supporting SOC 2 | Provide accurate information, promptly report inaccuracies, and avoid unauthorised modification or distribution of the System Description. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all personnel and functions involved in the SOC 2 programme.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through:

- SOC 2 readiness reviews.
- Management review of the System Description.
- Reconciliation of the System Description against the control matrix and evidence inventory.
- Stakeholder sign-off tracking.
- Auditor feedback and issue logs.
- Internal quality reviews before report issuance.
- Periodic review of system, vendor, and service changes.
- Access reviews for repositories containing drafts and final versions.
- Post-report lessons learned.

The following compliance checks shall be performed for each SOC 2 reporting cycle:

| Compliance Check | Frequency | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Scope confirmation completed | Each reporting cycle | Approved scope document or audit planning record |
| System inventory reconciled to description | Each reporting cycle and after material change | Inventory export, architecture review, reconciliation notes |
| Subservice organisation list validated | Each reporting cycle and after material vendor change | Vendor inventory, risk review, review sign-off |
| Control descriptions reconciled to control matrix | Each reporting cycle | Control matrix, review notes, change log |
| Stakeholder review completed | Each reporting cycle | Review tracker, approval records |
| Sensitive disclosure review completed | Before external release | Legal/Security review approval |
| Final management approval obtained | Before report issuance | Approval record |
| Final version archived | After report issuance | Repository record, version history |

Non-compliance may include, but is not limited to:

- Submitting an inaccurate or incomplete System Description.
- Omitting material systems, services, vendors, changes, incidents, or customer responsibilities.
- Including unsupported claims or aspirational control descriptions.
- Failing to obtain required reviews or approvals.
- Distributing drafts or final reports to unauthorised parties.
- Modifying approved content without authorisation.
- Failing to preserve records supporting the System Description.

Violations of this Policy may result in corrective action, removal of document access, escalation to management, retraining, audit issue reporting, disciplinary action, contract remedies, or other action consistent with organisational policy and applicable law.

Material inaccuracies identified after report issuance shall be escalated immediately to the Executive Sponsor, Legal Counsel, Compliance Owner, Security Leadership, and the independent auditor for assessment and response.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business justification, risk assessment, compensating control, and approval by authorised management.

Exception requests shall include:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | Unique identifier assigned by Compliance or Document Control |
| Requestor | Name and role of the person requesting the exception |
| Policy Requirement | Specific requirement for which exception is requested |
| Business Justification | Explanation of why compliance is not feasible or appropriate |
| Risk Assessment | Description of confidentiality, integrity, availability, privacy, audit, contractual, and customer impact |
| Compensating Controls | Measures that reduce the risk created by the exception |
| Duration | Start date and end date; permanent exceptions are not permitted without executive approval |
| Approvals | Required approvals from Compliance, Legal, Security, System Description Owner, and Executive Sponsor, as applicable |
| Review Date | Date on which the exception will be reassessed |
| Closure Criteria | Conditions required to close or remediate the exception |

Exceptions shall not be used to conceal known inaccuracies, omit material information, misrepresent control operation, or bypass required management approval for the SOC 2 report.

Any exception affecting the accuracy, completeness, or fairness of the System Description shall be disclosed to the independent auditor before report issuance.

Approved exceptions shall be tracked to closure and reviewed at least quarterly until resolved.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever there is a material change to the SOC 2 programme, report scope, services, system architecture, trust services categories, organisational structure, legal obligations, customer commitments, or auditor expectations.

The System Description Owner and Compliance Owner shall jointly ensure that this Policy remains aligned with the organisation’s SOC 2 reporting process and current operating practices.

At minimum, the annual review shall assess:

- Whether required System Description content remains appropriate.
- Whether ownership and approval roles remain current.
- Whether drafting and review timelines remain practical.
- Whether lessons learned from the prior SOC 2 examination require updates.
- Whether subservice organisation and complementary control requirements remain complete.
- Whether confidentiality, disclosure, and distribution requirements remain adequate.
- Whether records retention requirements remain aligned with business, legal, contractual, and audit needs.
- Whether changes to services, systems, or customer commitments require updates to this Policy.

Policy changes shall be documented in a revision history and approved by the Policy Owner or authorised delegate.
