| Data Owners | Classify information, approve access to data, define handling requirements, and ensure data is retained and disposed of appropriately. |
| People or Human Resources Team | Supports onboarding, screening, policy acknowledgement, security awareness tracking, disciplinary processes, and termination access coordination. |
| Legal and Compliance Team | Advises on legal, contractual, privacy, regulatory, and customer requirements related to information security and data protection. |
| IT and Engineering Teams | Implement and operate technical controls, maintain secure configurations, manage vulnerabilities, perform backups, support monitoring, and execute approved changes. |
| Procurement or Vendor Management Team | Ensures third-party security requirements are incorporated into procurement, due diligence, contracts, reviews, and offboarding activities. |
| Managers | Ensure personnel understand and comply with this Policy, approve access based on business need, report security concerns, and support remediation activities. |
| All Personnel | Comply with this Policy and supporting requirements, protect organisation and customer information, complete training, use systems responsibly, and report suspected security incidents promptly. |
| Third Parties | Comply with contractual security obligations, protect organisation and customer information, report incidents as required, and cooperate with security reviews where applicable. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory. The organisation shall monitor compliance through a combination of management oversight, automated controls, manual reviews, internal assessments, operational metrics, security testing, incident analysis, access reviews, vendor reviews, audit activities, and control evidence review.

The following monitoring activities shall be performed at minimum:

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of information security risks and remediation status | Quarterly | Security Leader | Risk register, action tracker, management meeting notes |
| User access review for material systems | Quarterly | System Owners | Access review records, approvals, removal evidence |
| Privileged access review | Quarterly | System Owners and Security Team | Privileged access review records |
| Security awareness training completion review | Quarterly | People Team and Security Team | Training reports, completion records |
| Vulnerability review and remediation tracking | Monthly | IT, Engineering, Security Team | Scan results, remediation tickets, exception records |
| Security incident review | As incidents occur and at least quarterly | Security Team | Incident records, post-incident reviews, corrective actions |
| Vendor security review for critical providers | At onboarding and at least annually | Vendor Management and Security Team | Due diligence records, security documentation, risk ratings |
| Backup and restoration testing | At least annually | IT or Platform Team | Test records, recovery results, issue tracking |
| Policy acknowledgement review | At onboarding and at least annually | People Team | Acknowledgement records |
| Review of open audit findings and control deficiencies | Monthly until closure | Control Owners | Finding tracker, remediation evidence |

The organisation shall investigate actual or suspected non-compliance with this Policy. Confirmed violations may result in corrective action, access restriction, mandatory retraining, contractual remedies, disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or engagement, and legal action where warranted.

Enforcement shall be proportionate to the nature and severity of the violation, the sensitivity of affected information, the degree of negligence or intent, prior conduct, customer or business impact, legal obligations, and the risk to the organisation.

Material security risks, significant policy violations, unresolved control deficiencies, and significant incidents shall be reported to executive management in a timely manner.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy are permitted only when there is a documented business justification and the risk has been reviewed, approved, and formally accepted by authorised management.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Individual requesting the exception |
| Affected system, process, vendor, or data | Scope of the exception |
| Policy requirement affected | Specific requirement that cannot be met |
| Business justification | Reason the exception is needed |
| Risk assessment | Security, operational, customer, legal, and compliance impact |
| Compensating controls | Alternative measures that reduce risk |
| Duration | Requested start date and expiry date |
| Approver | Authorised risk owner or executive approver |
| Review date | Date by which the exception will be reassessed |
| Remediation plan | Actions required to return to compliance, where applicable |

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not be granted indefinitely. The maximum approval period for an exception shall be [90 days] unless a longer duration is approved by executive management based on documented business need and risk acceptance.

Approved exceptions shall be recorded in an exception register, reviewed before expiry, and tracked until closure. Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed through the approved exception process.

Exceptions involving customer data, production systems, critical services, significant third-party risk, legal obligations, or material business risk shall require review by the Security Leader and approval by an appropriate executive risk owner.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that could affect the organisation’s information security obligations, risk environment, systems, services, business operations, legal requirements, customer commitments, or control environment.

The Policy Owner is responsible for coordinating review, obtaining stakeholder input, submitting material changes for approval, communicating updates, and maintaining version history.

At minimum, the review shall consider:

- Changes to business strategy, services, products, customers, and operating locations.
- Changes to systems, infrastructure, cloud services, applications, and data flows.
- Results of risk assessments, audits, incidents, penetration tests, vulnerability assessments, and control monitoring.
- Changes in customer commitments, contracts, legal obligations, and privacy requirements.
- Changes in personnel responsibilities, organisational structure, vendors, and outsourced services.
- Lessons learned from security incidents, policy exceptions, control failures, and remediation activities.
- The continued suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of this Policy and supporting documents.

Material changes to this Policy shall be approved by [Executive Management / Security Steering Committee / Board-delegated authority]. Non-material administrative updates, such as formatting, owner title changes, or clarification of wording that does not change policy intent, may be approved by the Policy Owner.

All superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document retention requirements. Personnel shall be notified of material updates and may be required to re-acknowledge the Policy after significant changes.

SOC2-008.title: Acceptable Use Policy
SOC2-008.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [AUP-POL-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [Chief Information Security Officer] |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | SOC 2 |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Acceptable Use Policy is to define mandatory requirements for the appropriate, secure, and lawful use of [Organisation Name] information assets, technology resources, systems, networks, applications, data, and facilities.

This Policy supports the protection of customer data, company information, employee information, systems, and services from unauthorised access, misuse, loss, disruption, disclosure, or damage. It establishes clear rules for users who access or handle [Organisation Name] assets and information as part of their work responsibilities.

## Scope

This Policy applies to all users who access, use, manage, or support [Organisation Name] information assets or technology resources, including:

- Employees, contractors, consultants, temporary workers, interns, service providers, and third parties.
- Corporate-owned and approved personally owned devices used to access [Organisation Name] systems or data.
- Cloud services, software-as-a-service platforms, business applications, infrastructure, networks, endpoints, collaboration tools, email, messaging platforms, storage locations, databases, source code repositories, and administrative consoles.
- Information in all forms, including electronic, printed, verbal, visual, and recorded information.
- Use of [Organisation Name] assets from office locations, remote locations, customer sites, public places, and home networks.

This Policy applies whether systems and data are hosted internally, by a cloud provider, by a managed service provider, or by another authorised third party.

## Policy Statements

1. **Authorised Business Use**
 1. [Organisation Name] information assets and technology resources shall be used primarily for authorised business purposes.
 2. Limited personal use may be permitted only where it:
 - Does not interfere with work responsibilities.
 - Does not consume excessive resources.
 - Does not create security, legal, reputational, or operational risk.
 - Does not violate this Policy or any other [Organisation Name] policy.
 3. Users shall use systems, data, and services only for purposes consistent with their assigned role and authorised responsibilities.

2. **User Accountability**
 1. Users shall be accountable for all activity performed using their assigned accounts, credentials, access tokens, devices, and authentication methods.
 2. Users shall not share passwords, passphrases, authentication codes, access tokens, private keys, security badges, or other authentication mechanisms with any other person.
 3. Users shall not allow another individual to use their account, device session, privileged access, or security badge.
 4. Users shall lock screens, log out, or otherwise secure sessions when devices are left unattended.
 5. Users shall promptly report suspected unauthorised use of their account, credentials, device, or access rights to [Security Team/Service Desk].

3. **Acceptable Access and Authorisation**
 1. Users shall access only systems, applications, repositories, environments, data, and physical areas for which they have been formally authorised.
 2. Users shall not attempt to bypass, disable, alter, or evade access controls, security monitoring, authentication requirements, network restrictions, or logging mechanisms.
 3. Users shall not attempt to gain unauthorised access to any account, system, data, network, application, or service.
 4. Users shall not use another person’s credentials or access privileges.
 5. Users shall use privileged or administrative access only for approved administrative activities and only through authorised methods.

4. **Protection of Company and Customer Information**
 1. Users shall handle [Organisation Name] information and customer data in accordance with its classification, sensitivity, contractual obligations, and approved handling requirements.
 2. Users shall store company and customer information only in approved systems, repositories, or storage locations.
 3. Users shall not copy, transfer, upload, synchronise, print, photograph, record, or share confidential information unless there is a legitimate business need and an approved method is used.
 4. Users shall not disclose company, customer, employee, or third-party confidential information to unauthorised individuals or organisations.
 5. Users shall verify recipient identity and authorisation before sharing sensitive information.
 6. Users shall use approved secure transfer methods when transmitting confidential, restricted, regulated, or customer data.
 7. Users shall not use personal email accounts, unauthorised messaging applications, personal cloud storage, or unapproved file-sharing services to store or transmit company or customer information.

5. **Use of Devices and Endpoints**
 1. Users shall use only approved, managed, and appropriately secured devices to access [Organisation Name] systems and data, unless explicitly authorised.
 2. Corporate devices shall remain configured with required security controls, including approved endpoint protection, device encryption, screen lock, patching, logging, and management software.
 3. Users shall not remove, disable, alter, or interfere with security tools, device management agents, encryption, monitoring controls, or required configurations.
 4. Users shall not install unauthorised software, browser extensions, utilities, scripts, or services on corporate devices.
 5. Users shall not connect unauthorised storage devices, network equipment, peripherals, or removable media to corporate systems.
 6. Users shall protect devices from theft, loss, damage, and unauthorised viewing or access.
 7. Users shall report lost, stolen, compromised, or damaged devices immediately to [Security Team/Service Desk].
 8. Users shall return corporate devices and equipment upon request, role change, contract end, or termination.

6. **Personal Devices and Bring Your Own Device Use**
 1. Personal devices shall not be used to access [Organisation Name] systems or data unless approved under the organisation’s device access requirements.
 2. Approved personal devices shall meet minimum security requirements before access is granted, including authentication, screen lock, encryption where supported, current operating system updates, and required management or security controls.
 3. Users shall consent to reasonable security enforcement on approved personal devices used for business access, including access removal, session revocation, and remote wipe of business data where technically supported.
 4. Users shall not store company or customer information locally on personal devices unless specifically authorised and protected by approved controls.
 5. [Organisation Name] reserves the right to restrict, suspend, or revoke access from personal devices that do not meet security requirements.

7. **Email, Messaging, and Collaboration Tools**
 1. Users shall use approved corporate email, messaging, meeting, and collaboration platforms for business communications.
 2. Users shall exercise care when opening attachments, clicking links, responding to messages, or approving requests, particularly where messages are unexpected, urgent, unusual, or request sensitive information.
 3. Users shall not send confidential or sensitive information to personal accounts or unauthorised external recipients.
 4. Users shall not use corporate communications tools to send, store, or distribute content that is unlawful, discriminatory, harassing, threatening, defamatory, obscene, malicious, or otherwise inconsistent with [Organisation Name] standards of conduct.
 5. Users shall not automatically forward corporate email to external or personal email accounts unless explicitly approved.
 6. Users shall report suspected phishing, impersonation, fraud, malicious messages, or suspicious communication activity using the approved reporting method.

8. **Internet and Network Use**
 1. Users shall use [Organisation Name] internet and network services in a lawful, ethical, and secure manner.
 2. Users shall not use corporate networks or systems to access, create, download, store, transmit, or distribute material that is illegal, malicious, discriminatory, harassing, sexually explicit, exploitative, extremist, or otherwise prohibited by company policy.
 3. Users shall not conduct unauthorised scanning, interception, monitoring, probing, exploitation, password cracking, denial-of-service activity, or vulnerability testing.
 4. Users shall not operate unauthorised network services, wireless access points, servers, tunnelling tools, proxies, anonymisers, cryptocurrency mining tools, or peer-to-peer file-sharing services.
 5. Users shall connect remotely to [Organisation Name] systems only through approved remote access methods.
 6. Users shall not connect corporate devices to untrusted public networks without using required protective controls, such as approved secure remote access.

9. **Software, Applications, and Cloud Services**
 1. Users shall use only approved software, applications, cloud services, artificial intelligence tools, and third-party platforms for business purposes.
 2. Users shall not procure, subscribe to, configure, or process company or customer data in new applications or services without required approval.
 3. Users shall not upload, paste, enter, or process confidential, proprietary, regulated, or customer information in public or unauthorised artificial intelligence, analytics, translation, transcription, or automation tools.
 4. Users shall comply with software licensing terms and shall not install, copy, distribute, or use unlicensed or pirated software.
 5. Users shall not introduce open-source, third-party, or externally sourced software into company products, repositories, environments, or workflows except through approved processes.

10. **Data Storage, Transfer, and Disposal**
 1. Users shall store business records, work products, and customer information in approved repositories that support access control, backup, retention, and monitoring.
 2. Users shall not store the only copy of business-critical information on local drives, removable media, personal storage, or unauthorised systems.
 3. Users shall transfer sensitive information only through approved secure methods.
 4. Users shall dispose of information, documents, media, and devices using approved disposal or sanitisation methods.
 5. Users shall not delete, alter, destroy, or conceal information that is subject to legal hold, investigation, audit, contractual requirement, or retention obligation.

11. **Physical Asset Use**
 1. Users shall protect physical assets, including laptops, mobile devices, access cards, documents, removable media, security keys, and office equipment.
 2. Users shall not lend, transfer, discard, sell, donate, or repurpose [Organisation Name] assets without approval.
 3. Users shall display, store, transport, and dispose of confidential printed information in a manner that prevents unauthorised access.
 4. Users shall challenge or report unauthorised individuals in restricted areas where safe and appropriate to do so.
 5. Users shall not tailgate or permit others to tailgate into controlled facilities.

12. **Remote Work and Public Location Use**
 1. Users shall maintain appropriate security when working remotely, travelling, or using systems in public or shared locations.
 2. Users shall prevent unauthorised viewing of screens and documents, including through the use of privacy screens where required.
 3. Users shall avoid discussing confidential matters where they may be overheard by unauthorised persons.
 4. Users shall ensure home or remote working environments provide reasonable protection against unauthorised access, loss, theft, and disclosure.
 5. Users shall not leave corporate devices, documents, security keys, or storage media unattended in public locations or unsecured vehicles.

13. **Prohibited Activities**
 1. Users shall not use [Organisation Name] assets or systems to engage in activities that are unlawful, fraudulent, malicious, deceptive, abusive, or contrary to business ethics.
 2. Users shall not create, store, transmit, or distribute malware, unauthorised scripts, credential harvesting tools, exploit code, or hacking tools except where explicitly authorised for legitimate security testing.
 3. Users shall not access, store, transmit, or distribute material that violates intellectual property rights, privacy rights, contractual obligations, or applicable law.
 4. Users shall not use company systems to harass, threaten, discriminate against, impersonate, defame, or intimidate any person or organisation.
 5. Users shall not use company resources for unauthorised commercial activities, political campaigning, gambling, personal profit, or excessive non-business activities.
 6. Users shall not intentionally degrade, disrupt, overload, or damage [Organisation Name] systems, networks, applications, or data.

14. **Security Incident Reporting**
 1. Users shall immediately report suspected or actual security incidents, policy violations, data loss, unauthorised disclosure, malware infection, phishing, credential compromise, lost devices, or suspicious activity.
 2. Users shall report incidents through approved channels, including [Security Email], [Service Desk Portal], [Incident Hotline], or [Messaging Channel].
 3. Users shall preserve relevant information and shall not investigate, alter, delete, or attempt to remediate suspected security incidents unless authorised to do so.
 4. Users shall cooperate with incident response, investigation, audit, legal, and compliance activities.

15. **Privacy and Monitoring Notice**
 1. Users shall have no expectation of personal privacy when using [Organisation Name] systems, networks, applications, devices, or accounts, except where privacy rights are protected by applicable law.
 2. [Organisation Name] may monitor, log, inspect, restrict, preserve, and disclose activity on company systems and networks for security, compliance, operational, legal, and investigative purposes.
 3. Monitoring shall be conducted in accordance with applicable law, approved business purposes, and authorised access requirements.
 4. Users shall not attempt to disable, evade, or interfere with monitoring, logging, data loss prevention, endpoint management, or security alerting.

16. **Legal, Contractual, and Ethical Use**
 1. Users shall use [Organisation Name] assets and information in compliance with applicable laws, regulations, contractual obligations, confidentiality commitments, intellectual property requirements, and company policies.
 2. Users shall respect third-party rights, including software licences, copyrights, trademarks, patents, trade secrets, and confidentiality obligations.
 3. Users shall not use customer environments, customer data, or customer-provided access for any purpose other than authorised service delivery.

17. **Training and Acknowledgement**
 1. Users shall complete required security and acceptable use training within assigned timeframes.
 2. Users shall acknowledge this Policy upon onboarding and periodically thereafter as required by [Organisation Name].
 3. Users shall seek guidance from [Security Team/Compliance Team/Legal] when acceptable use requirements are unclear.

18. **Asset Return and Access Termination**
 1. Users shall return all [Organisation Name] assets, documents, devices, access cards, removable media, security keys, and records upon request, role change, contract end, or termination.
 2. Users shall not retain, copy, transfer, or destroy company or customer information when leaving [Organisation Name] or changing roles unless authorised.
 3. Users shall cooperate with access removal, asset recovery, device inspection, data transfer, and information preservation activities.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors / Executive Leadership | Provide oversight for acceptable use expectations and support enforcement of security and compliance obligations. |
| [Chief Information Security Officer] | Own this Policy, approve material changes, define acceptable use security requirements, and oversee monitoring and enforcement activities. |
| Information Security Team | Establish security controls supporting acceptable use, monitor for misuse, investigate suspected violations, maintain awareness materials, and advise users on secure practices. |
| IT Operations | Manage corporate devices, networks, approved software, endpoint controls, remote access, account provisioning support, and technical enforcement mechanisms. |
| Human Resources | Support policy acknowledgement, employee onboarding and offboarding, disciplinary processes, and communication of conduct expectations. |
| Legal / Compliance | Advise on legal, contractual, privacy, evidence preservation, and regulatory implications of acceptable use matters. |
| Managers | Ensure personnel understand and comply with this Policy, approve appropriate business use where required, report concerns, and support timely asset return and access changes. |
| Users | Use assets and information responsibly, comply with this Policy, complete required training, protect credentials and devices, and report suspected incidents or violations promptly. |
| Third Parties and Contractors | Comply with this Policy and applicable contractual requirements when accessing [Organisation Name] systems, facilities, or information. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory. [Organisation Name] shall implement reasonable administrative, technical, and physical controls to support acceptable use requirements and detect potential misuse.

Monitoring and enforcement activities may include:

- Review of access logs, authentication events, endpoint activity, network traffic, email security events, data transfer activity, and administrative actions.
- Detection of unauthorised software, unapproved cloud services, malicious activity, unusual data movement, policy violations, and suspicious user behaviour.
- Periodic review of device compliance, software inventory, access rights, remote access activity, and security tool status.
- Investigation of suspected security incidents, data loss, fraud, harassment, unauthorised access, or misuse of assets.
- Verification of policy acknowledgement and completion of required training.

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Party | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| User acknowledgement of this Policy | Upon onboarding and at least annually | Human Resources / Compliance | Acknowledgement records |
| Security awareness and acceptable use training | Upon onboarding and at least annually | Information Security / Human Resources | Training completion records |
| Review of device compliance | Continuous or at least monthly | IT Operations / Information Security | Device compliance reports |
| Review of unauthorised software or services | At least quarterly | IT Operations / Information Security | Software inventory and exception records |
| Review of security alerts related to misuse | Ongoing | Information Security | Alert records and investigation notes |
| Review of access and activity logs for high-risk systems | At least quarterly or risk-based | Information Security / System Owners | Log review records |
| Review of remote access activity | At least quarterly | Information Security / IT Operations | Remote access reports |
| Review of policy exceptions | At least quarterly | Policy Owner / Compliance | Exception register |

Violations of this Policy may result in one or more of the following actions, depending on severity, intent, impact, contractual obligations, and applicable law:

- Coaching, retraining, or management counselling.
- Temporary or permanent restriction of access.
- Removal of unauthorised software, services, data, or devices.
- Device quarantine, reconfiguration, inspection, or recovery.
- Formal disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract.
- Contractual remedies for third parties.
- Referral to law enforcement or regulatory authorities where appropriate.
- Legal action to recover losses or protect [Organisation Name], customers, or affected parties.

[Organisation Name] may preserve and review relevant records, systems, communications, and devices where required for investigation, legal, compliance, security, or operational purposes.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business need, risk assessment, and approval by authorised personnel.

1. Exception requests shall be submitted before the non-compliant activity occurs, unless an emergency requires immediate action to protect life, safety, systems, or customer service.
2. Exceptions shall include:
 - Description of the requested exception.
 - Business justification.
 - Assets, systems, users, data, and locations affected.
 - Risk assessment and potential impact.
 - Compensating controls.
 - Requested duration.
 - Approval from the Policy Owner or delegated authority.
3. Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed [maximum exception period, e.g., 90 days] unless renewed through formal review.
4. Approved exceptions shall be recorded in the exception register.
5. Expired exceptions shall be closed, remediated, or re-approved before continued use.
6. Exceptions involving customer data, regulated data, legal commitments, or material security risk shall require review by [Legal/Compliance] and [Information Security].

| Exception Field | Required Information |
|---|---|
| Request ID | [Exception ID] |
| Requestor | Name, role, department, and contact details |
| Date Requested | [Date] |
| Policy Requirement | Specific requirement for which exception is requested |
| Business Justification | Reason the exception is necessary |
| Scope | Users, systems, devices, locations, data, and duration |
| Risk Assessment | Security, privacy, operational, legal, and customer impact |
| Compensating Controls | Controls used to reduce risk during the exception period |
| Approver(s) | Policy Owner and any required additional approvers |
| Expiry Date | Date exception must be reviewed or closed |
| Closure Evidence | Remediation, removal, renewal, or other closure action |

Emergency exceptions shall be documented as soon as practicable after the event and shall be reviewed by the Policy Owner.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect acceptable use requirements, including:

- Changes to business operations, workforce model, technology environment, or customer obligations.
- Introduction of new systems, cloud services, collaboration tools, remote access methods, or artificial intelligence tools.
- Material security incidents or recurring policy violations.
- Changes to legal, regulatory, contractual, privacy, or insurance requirements.
- Significant changes to security risks, threats, or control expectations.

The Policy Owner shall ensure that this Policy remains accurate, approved, communicated, and available to all in-scope users. Material changes shall be approved by [Approval Authority]. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with [Document Retention Policy].

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Author | Approver |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [Effective Date] | Initial release | [Author Name/Role] | [Approver Name/Role] |

SOC2-009.title: Access Control Policy
SOC2-009.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| POL-AC-001 | 1.0 | [Information Security Owner] | [Effective Date] | SOC 2 | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Access Control Policy is to define mandatory requirements for granting, managing, monitoring, and revoking logical and physical access to [Organization Name] systems, facilities, networks, applications, data, and supporting infrastructure.

This policy is intended to ensure that access is limited to authorized individuals based on business need, job responsibility, least privilege, and approved risk decisions. It supports the confidentiality, integrity, availability, privacy, and security commitments made to customers, personnel, partners, and other stakeholders.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All employees, contractors, consultants, temporary workers, vendors, service providers, and other workforce members who access [Organization Name] resources.
- All production and non-production systems, applications, databases, cloud services, networks, endpoints, administrative consoles, source code repositories, collaboration platforms, and security tools owned, operated, or managed by [Organization Name].
- All physical locations, offices, data centers, secure work areas, server rooms, network closets, and storage areas where company systems, data, or sensitive information are accessed, processed, stored, or transmitted.
- All forms of access, including interactive user access, privileged administrative access, service accounts, application programming interfaces, remote access, emergency access, and physical access credentials.
- Third-party access to company systems, facilities, data, or environments, including managed service providers, outsourced support teams, contractors, and customer-authorized users where applicable.

This policy does not replace more detailed procedures, standards, or technical configuration baselines. Where stricter requirements exist in customer contracts, legal obligations, regulatory requirements, or approved internal standards, the stricter requirement shall apply.

## Policy Statements

1. **Access control governance**
 1. [Organization Name] shall implement and maintain logical and physical access controls that restrict access to authorized users and authorized business purposes.
 2. Access control requirements shall be documented, approved, communicated, and enforced for systems, applications, facilities, and information assets.
 3. Access privileges shall be based on least privilege, need to know, segregation of duties, and role-based access where practical.
 4. Access rights shall be traceable to an approved business justification, an authorized request, and an accountable access owner.
 5. Access control decisions shall consider the sensitivity of the system or data, user role, employment status, location, device posture, authentication strength, and business risk.

2. **User identification and accountability**
 1. Each individual user shall be assigned a unique user identifier before access is granted to company systems or facilities.
 2. Shared user accounts shall be prohibited except where explicitly approved for a documented business or technical reason and protected by compensating controls.
 3. User activity on company systems shall be attributable to a unique individual wherever technically feasible.
 4. Generic, anonymous, or group accounts shall not be used for routine access to systems containing confidential, customer, production, financial, employee, or security-relevant data.
 5. Account ownership shall be documented for all non-personal accounts, including service accounts, automation accounts, integration accounts, and emergency accounts.

3. **Access request and approval**
 1. Access to systems, applications, data, facilities, and restricted areas shall be requested through an approved access management process.
 2. Access requests shall include the user identity, requested access, business justification, duration if temporary, approving manager or system owner, and any required security review.
 3. Access shall be approved by an appropriate authority before provisioning, such as the user’s manager, system owner, data owner, or physical security owner.
 4. Access to sensitive systems, production environments, confidential data, customer data, financial systems, security tools, and administrative functions shall require explicit approval by the relevant system or data owner.
 5. Access shall not be granted based solely on informal communication, verbal requests, or untracked messages unless an emergency access process is followed and documented after the event.
 6. Access approvals shall be retained as evidence in [Access Request System] or another approved system of record.

4. **Provisioning of logical access**
 1. Logical access shall be provisioned only after required approvals have been obtained.
 2. Access provisioning shall be performed by authorized personnel or automated workflows under controlled conditions.
 3. Provisioned access shall match the approved request and shall not exceed the access necessary for the user’s assigned responsibilities.
 4. Default access profiles shall be reviewed and approved by system owners before use.
 5. New user access shall be based on an authorized onboarding event, such as an approved hire, contractor engagement, vendor authorization, or customer authorization.
 6. Access to production systems shall be restricted to personnel with a demonstrated business need and approved operational responsibility.
 7. Access to security administration functions shall be restricted to designated personnel with appropriate training and authorization.

5. **Physical access control**
 1. Physical access to [Organization Name] offices, secure work areas, data centers, server rooms, network closets, and other restricted locations shall be limited to authorized individuals.
 2. Physical access credentials, including badges, keys, access cards, biometric access, visitor passes, and mobile access tokens, shall be issued only after approval by the appropriate physical security or facilities owner.
 3. Access to restricted areas shall be granted based on job role, business need, and least privilege.
 4. Visitors shall be registered, approved where required, identified, and escorted in areas where sensitive systems, data, or operations may be accessible.
 5. Visitor logs shall be maintained for restricted areas and retained according to the organization’s retention requirements.
 6. Physical access credentials shall not be shared, loaned, copied, or used by anyone other than the assigned individual.
 7. Lost, stolen, or suspected compromised physical access credentials shall be reported immediately to [Facilities/Security Contact] and disabled as soon as practicable.
 8. Physical access to data centers or third-party hosting facilities shall be managed according to approved vendor and internal access requirements.

6. **Authentication requirements**
 1. Users shall authenticate before accessing company systems, networks, applications, or restricted resources.
 2. Authentication mechanisms shall be appropriate to the sensitivity of the system and the risk of unauthorized access.
 3. Multi-factor authentication shall be required for remote access, privileged access, administrative consoles, cloud management platforms, production environments, source code repositories, security tools, and systems containing sensitive or customer data where supported.
 4. Passwords and other authentication secrets shall be protected against disclosure, reuse, unauthorized sharing, and storage in insecure locations.
 5. Password requirements shall be defined in an approved authentication standard or configuration baseline and enforced technically where feasible.
 6. Initial passwords, temporary passwords, recovery codes, and enrollment links shall be transmitted securely and changed or invalidated upon first use where supported.
 7. Authentication credentials shall not be embedded in source code, scripts, tickets, documentation, or unapproved storage locations.
 8. Users shall not share passwords, multi-factor authentication tokens, access cards, session tokens, private keys, or other authentication credentials.

7. **Privileged access management**
 1. Privileged access shall be restricted to authorized personnel with a documented business need.
 2. Privileged access shall be approved separately from standard user access.
 3. Privileged accounts shall be uniquely assigned to individuals wherever technically feasible.
 4. Administrative privileges shall not be used for routine business activities such as email, web browsing, document editing, or general collaboration.
 5. Privileged access shall be time-bound, role-based, or just-in-time where practical for high-risk systems.
 6. Privileged access to production systems, security tools, cloud administration consoles, databases, identity platforms, and infrastructure management systems shall be logged and subject to review.
 7. Privileged credentials shall be protected using approved secure methods, such as privileged access management tools, vaulting solutions, strong authentication, encryption, and access logging.
 8. The number of privileged users shall be limited to the minimum necessary to operate, support, and secure the environment.
 9. Emergency privileged access shall be approved, logged, time-limited, and reviewed after use.

8. **Service accounts and non-human access**
 1. Service accounts, automation accounts, application accounts, integration accounts, API keys, tokens, certificates, and other non-human credentials shall be approved, documented, and assigned an accountable owner.
 2. Non-human access shall be limited to the specific systems, functions, and data required for the intended service or integration.
 3. Service accounts shall not be used for interactive human login unless explicitly approved and technically required.
 4. Credentials used by non-human accounts shall be stored securely using approved secret management or credential vaulting solutions.
 5. Non-human credentials shall be rotated periodically, upon suspected compromise, upon owner change where appropriate, or when required by risk or system capability.
 6. Unused, orphaned, expired, or unnecessary service accounts and tokens shall be disabled or removed.
 7. Service account activity shall be logged and monitored commensurate with the sensitivity and risk of the account.

9. **Remote access**
 1. Remote access to company systems and networks shall be permitted only through approved secure access methods.
 2. Remote access shall require strong authentication and shall be restricted to authorized users and approved devices where technically feasible.
 3. Remote access sessions shall be encrypted using approved protocols.
 4. Remote administrative access to production systems and infrastructure shall be limited to authorized personnel and logged.
 5. Split tunneling, unmanaged devices, personal devices, or external networks may be restricted based on security requirements, business risk, and approved technology standards.
 6. Remote access shall be disabled promptly when no longer required or when a user is terminated, transferred, suspended, or no longer authorized.

10. **Access to customer and sensitive data**
 1. Access to customer data, confidential information, personal information, financial data, security data, and other sensitive information shall be restricted to authorized users with a legitimate business need.
 2. Access to sensitive data shall be granted using role-based permissions where practical.
 3. Users shall access only the data necessary to perform assigned responsibilities.
 4. Direct access to production customer data shall be limited, approved, logged where feasible, and subject to periodic review.
 5. Use of production data in non-production environments shall be restricted and shall follow approved data handling, masking, anonymization, or authorization requirements.
 6. Data exports, bulk downloads, and administrative access to sensitive records shall be limited to authorized users and monitored where feasible.
 7. Access to customer environments or customer-specific data shall comply with contractual commitments and approved support processes.

11. **Segregation of duties**
 1. Access rights shall be designed to reduce conflicts of interest and prevent inappropriate concentration of authority.
 2. No user shall be granted access that enables the user to initiate, approve, execute, and review the same sensitive transaction or control activity without compensating controls.
 3. Incompatible access combinations shall be identified for critical systems and reviewed during access approvals and periodic access reviews.
 4. Where segregation of duties cannot be fully enforced due to operational constraints, compensating controls shall be documented, approved, and monitored.

12. **Access modification**
 1. Access rights shall be modified when a user’s role, responsibilities, employment status, contract status, location, department, or business need changes.
 2. Managers, Human Resources, Procurement, Vendor Management, and system owners shall notify access administrators of changes that affect access requirements.
 3. Access that is no longer required shall be removed promptly.
 4. Role changes and transfers shall trigger review of existing access to determine whether privileges remain appropriate.
 5. Temporary access shall have an expiration date or be reviewed at the end of the approved period.

13. **Access termination and revocation**
 1. Logical and physical access shall be revoked when a user is terminated, contractually disengaged, no longer authorized, or no longer has a business need.
 2. Access revocation shall be initiated by an authoritative event, such as notice from Human Resources, Legal, Procurement, Vendor Management, the user’s manager, or the relevant business owner.
 3. Access for involuntary terminations or high-risk departures shall be revoked at or before the effective termination time.
 4. Access for voluntary terminations shall be revoked no later than the user’s final working day unless an earlier time is required.
 5. Contractor, vendor, temporary worker, and third-party access shall be disabled upon engagement end date or earlier when access is no longer required.
 6. Physical access credentials, company devices, keys, tokens, badges, and other access media shall be returned or disabled at the end of employment or engagement.
 7. Former users shall not retain access to company systems, facilities, data, or credentials after their authorization ends.
 8. Account disabling shall be preferred over deletion where log preservation, audit evidence, investigation, or operational continuity requires retained account history.

14. **Periodic access reviews**
 1. Access to systems, applications, data repositories, physical locations, and privileged functions shall be reviewed periodically by appropriate owners.
 2. Reviews shall validate that access remains appropriate based on user role, business need, least privilege, employment or contract status, and segregation of duties.
 3. System owners, data owners, managers, and physical security owners shall certify, modify, or revoke access during reviews.
 4. Privileged access and access to sensitive or production environments shall be reviewed more frequently than standard access.
 5. Access review results, reviewer decisions, remediation actions, and completion evidence shall be retained.
 6. Access identified as inappropriate, excessive, unused, or unauthorized shall be removed or remediated within approved timeframes.

| Access Category | Minimum Review Frequency | Reviewer |
|---|---:|---|
| Privileged access to production, cloud administration, identity platforms, security tools, and databases | Quarterly | System Owner or Security Owner |
| Access to customer data, confidential data, financial systems, and sensitive repositories | Quarterly | Data Owner or Business Owner |
| Standard user access to business applications | Semi-annually | Application Owner or Department Manager |
| Service accounts, API keys, tokens, and automation credentials | Semi-annually | Technical Owner |
| Physical access to restricted areas | Semi-annually | Facilities or Physical Security Owner |
| General office access | Annually | Facilities or HR Representative |

15. **Logging and monitoring**
 1. Access events for critical systems, privileged activities, remote access, authentication attempts, account changes, and physical access to restricted areas shall be logged where technically feasible.
 2. Logs shall capture sufficient information to support investigation, monitoring, and accountability, including user identity, timestamp, source, target resource, action performed, and success or failure status where available.
 3. Access logs shall be protected against unauthorized alteration, deletion, and disclosure.
 4. Security-relevant access events shall be monitored using approved processes, tools, and alerting mechanisms.
 5. Suspected unauthorized access, unusual access patterns, excessive failed login attempts, privilege escalation, and access outside expected business patterns shall be investigated.
 6. Log retention periods shall be defined and aligned with legal, contractual, operational, and security requirements.

16. **Third-party access**
 1. Third-party access shall be granted only when supported by a valid business requirement, approved engagement, and appropriate contractual or security obligations.
 2. Third-party users shall be uniquely identified and authenticated.
 3. Third-party access shall be limited to the systems, data, facilities, and time period necessary to perform the authorized service.
 4. Third-party access shall be reviewed periodically and removed promptly when no longer required.
 5. Third-party remote access to company environments shall use approved secure access methods and shall be logged where feasible.
 6. Vendors shall not be permitted unsupervised access to restricted physical areas unless explicitly approved and covered by appropriate security requirements.

17. **Access to development and production environments**
 1. Access to development, test, staging, and production environments shall be controlled based on role and business need.
 2. Production access shall be limited to authorized personnel responsible for operating, supporting, deploying, securing, or monitoring production systems.
 3. Developers shall not be granted standing administrative access to production unless approved based on role and business need.
 4. Changes to production access shall follow approved access request, change management, or privileged access processes.
 5. Access between environments shall be restricted to prevent unauthorized movement of data, code, or credentials.
 6. Non-production environments shall not be treated as unrestricted environments when they contain sensitive data, production-like configurations, customer information, or access paths to production systems.

18. **Device and endpoint access**
 1. Access to company systems shall be limited to approved users and, where required, approved devices.
 2. Devices used to access sensitive systems or data shall meet applicable security configuration, encryption, endpoint protection, patching, and management requirements.
 3. Administrative access to endpoints shall be restricted to authorized personnel or approved support processes.
 4. Local administrator rights shall not be granted to users unless there is a documented business need and approval.
 5. Lost or stolen devices that may provide access to company systems or data shall be reported immediately.

19. **Access records and evidence**
 1. Records of access requests, approvals, provisioning, modifications, revocations, reviews, exceptions, and related evidence shall be retained in approved repositories.
 2. Access records shall be complete, accurate, and available for audit, investigation, and control monitoring purposes.
 3. Evidence shall demonstrate that access was authorized, appropriate, reviewed, and revoked when no longer required.
 4. Records shall be retained for at least [Retention Period] unless a longer period is required by contract, legal obligation, investigation hold, or internal retention policy.

20. **User responsibilities**
 1. Users shall use access privileges only for authorized business purposes.
 2. Users shall protect credentials, access cards, tokens, devices, and authentication factors from unauthorized use.
 3. Users shall report suspected unauthorized access, credential compromise, lost credentials, lost devices, or suspicious access activity immediately to [Security Contact].
 4. Users shall not attempt to bypass access controls, escalate privileges without authorization, access information outside their role, or use another person’s credentials.
 5. Users shall complete required security awareness and access-related training as assigned.

21. **Minimum access control timelines**
 1. Access control activities shall be completed within the timeframes below unless a stricter requirement applies or an approved exception is in place.

| Activity | Required Timeframe |
|---|---:|
| Disable access for involuntary termination or high-risk departure | At or before termination notification time |
| Disable access for voluntary termination | No later than final working day |
| Disable contractor or vendor access at engagement end | No later than engagement end date |
| Remove access no longer required after role change or transfer | Within [5 business days] of notification |
| Remove inappropriate access identified during review | Within [10 business days] of review decision |
| Disable lost or stolen physical access credential | As soon as practicable, not to exceed [1 business day] |
| Disable suspected compromised account or credential | Immediately upon confirmation or credible suspicion |
| Complete privileged access review | Quarterly |
| Complete standard application access review | At least semi-annually |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Management | Approves risk appetite for access control; supports enforcement of access control requirements; ensures adequate resources are available. |
| Information Security Owner | Owns this policy; defines access control requirements; monitors access control effectiveness; reviews exceptions; supports investigations and audit activities. |
| IT Operations / System Administration | Provisions, modifies, disables, and monitors logical access according to approved requests; maintains identity and access management tools; protects administrative credentials. |
| Human Resources | Notifies relevant teams of employee onboarding, transfers, leaves of absence, and terminations; supports timely access changes and revocations. |
| Managers | Request and approve access for personnel under their responsibility; ensure access aligns with job duties; notify access administrators of changes; participate in access reviews. |
| System Owners | Approve access to systems under their ownership; define appropriate roles and permissions; review access periodically; ensure remediation of inappropriate access. |
| Data Owners | Approve access to sensitive data; define data access requirements; review access to data repositories; ensure access aligns with business need and data handling obligations. |
| Facilities / Physical Security | Manages physical access credentials, visitor access, restricted area access, and physical access logs; disables physical access when no longer authorized. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Notifies responsible teams of vendor onboarding, contract changes, and engagement termination; ensures third-party access is supported by approved business relationships. |
| Users | Protect credentials and access media; use access only for authorized purposes; report suspected compromise or unauthorized access; comply with this policy. |
| Internal Audit / Compliance | Independently assesses access control processes and evidence; reports control gaps and remediation status to management. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy is mandatory. [Organization Name] shall monitor adherence through a combination of automated controls, manual reviews, system logs, access certifications, physical access logs, security alerts, management oversight, and periodic assessments.

Monitoring activities may include:

- Review of access requests, approvals, and provisioning evidence.
- Review of user access listings for critical systems and sensitive data repositories.
- Review of privileged access assignments and administrative activity.
- Review of terminated user access removal evidence.
- Monitoring of authentication events, failed login attempts, suspicious access patterns, and privilege escalations.
- Review of service accounts, API keys, and non-human credentials.
- Review of physical access logs and visitor records for restricted areas.
- Testing of access revocation, role changes, and access review completion.
- Investigation of unauthorized access attempts and policy violations.

Non-compliance may result in one or more of the following actions, depending on severity and circumstances:

- Immediate suspension or revocation of access.
- Mandatory remediation or retraining.
- Notification to the user’s manager, system owner, Human Resources, Legal, or executive management.
- Disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract.
- Vendor remediation, access restriction, contract action, or termination of services.
- Incident response investigation and reporting where unauthorized access, data exposure, or credential compromise is suspected.

Access control weaknesses, control failures, and policy violations shall be tracked to remediation. High-risk issues shall be escalated to appropriate management until resolved.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only when there is a documented business or technical justification and the risk has been reviewed and approved by authorized personnel.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Individual requesting the exception |
| Business Owner | Manager or owner accountable for the business need |
| System, Data, or Facility | Resource affected by the exception |
| Policy Requirement | Requirement that cannot be met |
| Business Justification | Reason the exception is necessary |
| Risk Assessment | Security, operational, customer, legal, or compliance risks created by the exception |
| Compensating Controls | Controls used to reduce risk while the exception is active |
| Duration | Start date and expiration date |
| Approval | Required approval from [Information Security Owner] and relevant owner |
| Review Requirement | Frequency or condition for reassessing the exception |

Exception requirements:

1. Exceptions shall be approved before implementation unless emergency conditions prevent prior approval.
2. Emergency exceptions shall be documented and submitted for review as soon as practicable after implementation.
3. Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not remain open indefinitely.
4. Exceptions affecting customer data, production environments, privileged access, authentication, or physical restricted areas shall require security review.
5. Expired exceptions shall be remediated, renewed through approval, or escalated.
6. Exception records shall be retained as audit evidence.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect access control requirements, including:

- Material changes to systems, architecture, identity platforms, facilities, or cloud environments.
- Introduction of new applications, sensitive data repositories, or production environments.
- Significant changes to workforce structure, third-party access, or remote work practices.
- Security incidents involving unauthorized access, credential compromise, privilege misuse, or physical access failure.
- Audit findings, customer commitments, legal requirements, or risk assessment results indicating a need for update.
- Changes to authentication, logging, access review, or privileged access technologies.

The [Information Security Owner] is responsible for coordinating the review and update of this policy. Material changes shall be approved by [Approving Authority]. Updated versions shall be communicated to affected personnel and made available in the approved policy repository.

Policy review evidence, approval records, and version history shall be retained according to [Organization Name] document retention requirements.

SOC2-010.title: Code of Conduct / Ethics
SOC2-010.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| POL-ETH-001 | 1.0 | [Chief Executive Officer / General Counsel / Chief People Officer] | [Effective Date] | SOC 2 | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Code of Conduct / Ethics Policy is to define the standards of integrity, professional behavior, accountability and ethical decision-making expected across [Organisation Name].

This Policy supports a culture in which personnel act honestly, comply with applicable obligations, protect customers and stakeholders, safeguard information, avoid conflicts of interest, report concerns in good faith and make decisions consistent with the organisation’s values.

This Policy is intended to ensure that ethical expectations are clearly communicated, consistently applied and embedded into day-to-day business operations, including service delivery, customer support, product development, sales, procurement, finance, security, privacy and leadership activities.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All employees, officers, executives, board members and directors of [Organisation Name].
- Contractors, consultants, temporary workers, interns and agency personnel.
- Third parties acting on behalf of [Organisation Name], including suppliers, service providers, resellers, implementation partners and outsourced support providers, where contractually applicable.
- All business activities conducted on behalf of [Organisation Name], whether on-site, remote, hybrid, at customer locations, during business travel or through digital communication channels.
- All company systems, collaboration platforms, communication tools, information assets and records used to conduct business.

This Policy applies globally, subject to applicable local laws and employment requirements. Where local law imposes a higher standard than this Policy, the higher standard shall apply. Where this Policy imposes a higher standard than local practice, this Policy shall apply unless prohibited by law.

## Policy Statements

1. **General ethical conduct**
 1. [Organisation Name] shall conduct business honestly, fairly, transparently and in a manner that maintains stakeholder trust.
 2. Personnel shall act with integrity, professionalism and sound judgment in all work-related activities.
 3. Personnel shall not engage in behavior that could reasonably be expected to damage the reputation, credibility, security posture or customer trust of [Organisation Name].
 4. Personnel shall comply with this Policy, applicable laws, contractual commitments, approved internal policies and lawful instructions issued by authorised management.

2. **Respectful and inclusive workplace**
 1. Personnel shall treat colleagues, customers, partners, suppliers and other stakeholders with dignity, respect and professionalism.
 2. [Organisation Name] shall prohibit discrimination, harassment, bullying, intimidation, retaliation and abusive conduct in any work-related setting.
 3. Personnel shall not engage in conduct that creates a hostile, offensive, exclusionary or unsafe working environment.
 4. Managers shall promote inclusive, respectful and psychologically safe team environments where personnel can raise questions and concerns without fear of retaliation.

3. **Compliance with laws and obligations**
 1. Personnel shall comply with applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, privacy, security, employment, anti-corruption, competition, export, sanctions and financial obligations relevant to their roles.
 2. Personnel shall seek guidance from Legal, Compliance, People, Security or management when they are uncertain about applicable obligations.
 3. Personnel shall not knowingly assist, conceal or ignore unlawful, unethical or non-compliant conduct.
 4. Personnel shall cooperate truthfully and promptly with internal reviews, audits, investigations and lawful external inquiries.

4. **Conflicts of interest**
 1. Personnel shall avoid actual, potential or perceived conflicts between personal interests and the interests of [Organisation Name].
 2. Personnel shall disclose conflicts of interest promptly through the approved disclosure process before taking action that could be affected by the conflict.
 3. Personnel shall not use their position, access, authority or company information for improper personal gain or to benefit family members, friends or affiliated organisations.
 4. Personnel involved in hiring, procurement, vendor selection, contracting, compensation, investment decisions or customer negotiations shall disclose any personal, financial or relationship-based interests that could influence their judgment.
 5. [Organisation Name] shall review disclosed conflicts and document required mitigation actions, recusals or approvals.

5. **Bribery, corruption and improper payments**
 1. Personnel shall not offer, promise, give, request, accept or authorise bribes, kickbacks, facilitation payments or anything of value intended to improperly influence a business decision.
 2. Personnel shall not use third parties to perform actions that would be prohibited if performed directly by [Organisation Name].
 3. Gifts, meals, entertainment, travel, charitable donations, sponsorships and political contributions shall not be used to obtain improper advantage or influence.
 4. Personnel shall obtain required approvals before providing or accepting gifts, hospitality or other benefits above established thresholds.
 5. Payments and expenses shall be accurately recorded and supported by appropriate business documentation.

6. **Gifts, hospitality and business courtesies**
 1. Personnel shall ensure that gifts, hospitality and business courtesies are reasonable, infrequent, lawful, transparent and directly related to a legitimate business purpose.
 2. Personnel shall not accept or provide cash, cash equivalents, personal loans or extravagant benefits in connection with company business.
 3. Personnel shall not provide or accept gifts or hospitality during active procurement, tender, renewal, audit, dispute or contract negotiation activities if the benefit could appear to influence a decision.
 4. Personnel shall record and seek approval for gifts and hospitality in accordance with the thresholds below.

| Item Type | Permitted Without Prior Approval | Requires Prior Written Approval | Prohibited |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Promotional items of nominal value | Up to [Amount] | Above [Amount] | If intended to influence a decision |
| Business meals | Up to [Amount] per person | Above [Amount] per person | Excessive, frequent or unrelated to business |
| Event attendance | Up to [Amount] | Above [Amount] | Adult entertainment or inappropriate venues |
| Travel or accommodation paid by a third party | Not permitted without approval | Always required | If tied to a pending decision |
| Cash or cash equivalents | Not permitted | Not applicable | Always prohibited |

7. **Accurate records and truthful reporting**
 1. Personnel shall create, maintain and submit complete, accurate and timely business records.
 2. Personnel shall not falsify, conceal, backdate, improperly alter or destroy company records.
 3. Financial transactions, expenses, time records, customer communications, security evidence, audit records and operational metrics shall reflect the true nature of the activity.
 4. Personnel shall follow approved retention, legal hold and disposal requirements for company records.
 5. Personnel shall immediately report suspected fraud, misstatement, improper accounting, unauthorised record alteration or evidence tampering.

8. **Protection of confidential information**
 1. Personnel shall protect confidential, proprietary, customer, employee, partner and non-public business information from unauthorised access, use, disclosure, alteration or loss.
 2. Personnel shall use confidential information only for authorised business purposes and only to the extent required for their assigned responsibilities.
 3. Personnel shall not discuss confidential information in public places, unsecured channels or with unauthorised individuals.
 4. Personnel shall comply with information security, privacy, acceptable use, data classification, access control, incident reporting and secure handling requirements.
 5. Personnel shall continue to protect confidential information after their relationship with [Organisation Name] ends.

9. **Privacy and personal information**
 1. Personnel shall collect, use, store, share, retain and dispose of personal information only for lawful, authorised and clearly defined business purposes.
 2. Personnel shall limit access to personal information to individuals with a legitimate business need.
 3. Personnel shall promptly report suspected or confirmed unauthorised access, disclosure, loss or misuse of personal information through the approved incident reporting channels.
 4. Personnel shall respect customer, employee and user privacy expectations and shall not use personal information for unauthorised monitoring, profiling, marketing or personal purposes.

10. **Security-conscious behavior**
 1. Personnel shall comply with all approved security policies, standards and procedures applicable to their work.
 2. Personnel shall protect credentials, devices, company systems, customer environments and information assets from misuse, compromise or unauthorised access.
 3. Personnel shall not bypass security controls, disable protection mechanisms, share passwords or grant unauthorised access.
 4. Personnel shall promptly report suspected phishing, malware, unauthorised access, security weaknesses, policy violations or unusual system behavior.
 5. Personnel shall complete required security and ethics training within assigned timelines.

11. **Responsible use of company assets**
 1. Personnel shall use company assets, systems, funds, equipment, information, software, intellectual property and working time responsibly and primarily for authorised business purposes.
 2. Personnel shall not use company assets for illegal, unethical, offensive, fraudulent, discriminatory or unauthorised personal activities.
 3. Personnel shall protect company assets from theft, waste, misuse, unauthorised modification and loss.
 4. Personnel shall return company assets and information upon request, role change or termination of employment or engagement.

12. **Fair dealing with customers and stakeholders**
 1. Personnel shall communicate honestly and accurately with customers, prospects, partners, auditors, regulators and suppliers.
 2. Personnel shall not make misleading claims about products, services, security capabilities, certifications, compliance status, pricing, performance, availability or contractual obligations.
 3. Personnel shall escalate customer commitments, service limitations, security concerns or delivery risks that cannot be met as represented.
 4. Personnel shall honour approved contractual commitments and shall not knowingly create side agreements or informal commitments that conflict with authorised contracts.

13. **Competition and market conduct**
 1. Personnel shall compete fairly and shall not engage in collusion, price fixing, bid rigging, market allocation, improper exchange of competitively sensitive information or other anti-competitive conduct.
 2. Personnel shall not obtain competitor, customer or supplier information through deception, unauthorised access, improper inducement or breach of confidentiality.
 3. Personnel shall seek guidance before participating in industry meetings, benchmarking activities or competitor-facing discussions that may involve commercially sensitive topics.

14. **Intellectual property and work product**
 1. Personnel shall respect the intellectual property rights of [Organisation Name], customers, suppliers, partners, competitors and third parties.
 2. Personnel shall not use unlicensed software, unauthorised code, copyrighted material, confidential third-party information or open-source components contrary to approved requirements.
 3. Work product created within the scope of employment or engagement shall be handled in accordance with employment agreements, contractor agreements and applicable company policy.
 4. Personnel shall protect source code, designs, documentation, models, algorithms, product plans and other proprietary materials from unauthorised disclosure or use.

15. **Use of artificial intelligence and automated tools**
 1. Personnel shall use artificial intelligence, automation and analytics tools only in accordance with approved company requirements.
 2. Personnel shall not input confidential, customer, personal, regulated or proprietary information into external tools unless such use has been approved by authorised Security, Privacy and Legal functions.
 3. Personnel shall review AI-generated or automated outputs for accuracy, bias, confidentiality, intellectual property concerns and suitability before using them for business purposes.
 4. Personnel shall not represent machine-generated output as verified fact without appropriate human review.

16. **External communications and public statements**
 1. Personnel shall not speak on behalf of [Organisation Name] unless authorised to do so.
 2. Public statements, media responses, investor communications, regulatory communications, public security statements, customer-facing trust claims and legal positions shall be issued only by authorised individuals.
 3. Personnel shall use social media responsibly and shall not disclose confidential information, make misleading statements or create the impression that personal views represent official company positions unless authorised.
 4. Personnel shall refer media inquiries, legal notices, regulatory requests and unauthorised external audit requests to the appropriate internal function.

17. **Political, charitable and community activities**
 1. Personnel may participate in lawful political, charitable and community activities in a personal capacity, provided such activities do not create a conflict of interest, misuse company resources or imply company endorsement without authorisation.
 2. Company funds, assets, name, brand or personnel time shall not be used for political contributions, lobbying, sponsorships or charitable donations unless approved through authorised channels.
 3. Personnel shall not pressure colleagues, suppliers, customers or partners to support personal political, charitable or social causes.

18. **Reporting concerns and seeking guidance**
 1. Personnel shall promptly report suspected or actual violations of this Policy, law, contract, company policy or ethical standards.
 2. Personnel may raise concerns through management, People, Legal, Compliance, Security, Finance, the confidential reporting channel or any other approved reporting route.
 3. Personnel shall provide truthful information when reporting concerns or participating in investigations.
 4. Personnel shall not knowingly make false or malicious reports.
 5. [Organisation Name] shall make reporting channels reasonably accessible and shall communicate them to personnel during onboarding and periodic training.

| Reporting Channel | Appropriate For | Contact / Location | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| Direct manager | Routine questions, minor concerns, coaching | [Manager / HRIS] | Business hours |
| People / HR | Workplace conduct, harassment, discrimination, employment concerns | [HR Email / System] | Business hours |
| Legal or Compliance | Conflicts, bribery, gifts, regulatory concerns, ethics questions | [Legal / Compliance Email] | Business hours |
| Security or Privacy | Security incidents, data handling, access misuse, privacy concerns | [Security / Privacy Email or Portal] | 24/7 for incidents |
| Confidential reporting channel | Sensitive concerns, anonymous reporting where permitted | [Hotline / Web Portal] | [Availability] |
| Finance | Fraud, expense misuse, accounting irregularities | [Finance Email] | Business hours |

19. **Non-retaliation**
 1. [Organisation Name] shall prohibit retaliation against any person who raises a concern in good faith, seeks guidance, refuses to participate in misconduct or cooperates with an investigation.
 2. Retaliation shall include dismissal, demotion, reduced opportunities, threats, intimidation, harassment, exclusion, adverse scheduling, negative performance treatment or any other adverse action linked to protected reporting or cooperation.
 3. Personnel shall report suspected retaliation immediately through any approved reporting channel.
 4. Confirmed retaliation shall result in corrective or disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contract.

20. **Investigation cooperation and confidentiality**
 1. Personnel shall cooperate fully, honestly and promptly with authorised internal investigations, audits and reviews.
 2. Personnel shall preserve relevant records and shall not delete, alter, conceal or destroy information related to a reported concern or investigation.
 3. Investigation information shall be treated as confidential and shared only with individuals who have a legitimate need to know.
 4. Personnel shall not interfere with investigations, coach witnesses, intimidate participants or attempt to influence outcomes improperly.

21. **Manager and leadership responsibilities**
 1. Leaders and managers shall model ethical conduct and reinforce this Policy through decisions, communications and actions.
 2. Managers shall ensure personnel understand applicable ethical, security, privacy and compliance expectations for their roles.
 3. Managers shall respond promptly and appropriately to concerns raised by personnel and shall escalate matters requiring specialist review.
 4. Leaders shall not direct, encourage, approve or tolerate misconduct in pursuit of business objectives.
 5. Performance expectations and incentives shall be designed and administered in a manner that does not encourage unethical behavior.

22. **Training and acknowledgement**
 1. Personnel shall complete Code of Conduct / Ethics training during onboarding and periodically thereafter.
 2. Personnel in higher-risk roles, including sales, procurement, finance, leadership, customer support, engineering, security, privacy and legal roles, shall complete additional training where assigned.
 3. Personnel shall acknowledge that they have read, understood and agree to comply with this Policy.
 4. Completion and acknowledgement records shall be maintained as evidence of communication and accountability.

| Activity | Required Audience | Frequency / Trigger | Evidence Retained |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code of Conduct acknowledgement | All personnel | Onboarding and upon material policy update | Signed or electronic acknowledgement |
| Ethics and compliance training | All personnel | Onboarding and at least annually | Training completion record |
| Anti-bribery and conflict training | Higher-risk roles | Onboarding and periodically based on risk | Training completion record |
| Security and privacy conduct training | All personnel with system access | Onboarding and at least annually | Training completion record |
| Manager ethics briefing | People managers and leaders | At least annually | Attendance or completion record |

23. **Disciplinary and corrective action**
