| SOC 2 evidence package prepared | Compile plan, training, exercises, sample tickets, response records, and remediation evidence | Prior to audit readiness review | GRC Lead | SOC 2 evidence package |
| Ongoing operational review | Review incidents, trends, open corrective actions, and plan effectiveness | Monthly or quarterly based on risk | Security Leadership | Metrics report and improvement actions |
| Annual refresh | Review and update plan, contacts, playbooks, templates, and lessons learned | Annually | Security Incident Response Manager | Updated plan and approval record |

Incident response target timeline during active incidents:

| Activity | Critical | High | Medium | Low |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Initial triage | Within 15 minutes | Within 1 hour | Within 4 business hours | Within 1 business day |
| Incident Commander assigned | Within 30 minutes | Within 2 hours | Within 1 business day | As needed |
| Containment strategy agreed | Within 1 hour | Same business day | Within 2 business days | As needed |
| Executive notification | Within 2 hours | Same business day if material | As requested | Usually not required |
| Legal and privacy assessment | As soon as potential data impact is known | Same business day if data impact suspected | As needed | Usually not required |
| Customer impact assessment | Within 4 hours | Same business day | As needed | Usually not required |
| Recovery validation | Before service restoration | Before service restoration | Before closure if applicable | As needed |
| Post-incident review | Within 10 business days of recovery | Within 15 business days of recovery | As determined | Aggregate review |
| Corrective action assignment | Within 5 business days of review | Within 5 business days of review | Within 10 business days if required | As needed |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | Provides senior leadership support, approves major decisions, accepts material residual risk, supports customer and board-level communications where required. |
| Security Incident Response Manager | Owns this plan, maintains readiness, coordinates exercises, monitors metrics, ensures incident records and corrective actions are maintained. |
| Incident Commander | Leads the active response, confirms severity, coordinates teams, facilitates decisions, maintains the incident timeline, and approves transition between response phases. |
| Security Operations | Monitors alerts, performs triage, collects evidence, investigates suspicious activity, recommends containment actions, and updates detection rules. |
| IT Operations | Supports endpoint, network, identity, and corporate system containment and recovery; executes account resets, device isolation, patching, and restoration actions. |
| Engineering / DevOps | Supports investigation and recovery for production systems, applications, cloud services, deployment pipelines, and source code repositories. |
| System Owner | Provides business and technical context for affected systems, validates recovery, and accepts operational risk related to restoration. |
| Data Owner | Assesses data sensitivity, validates data integrity, supports impact analysis, and advises on customer or business implications. |
| Legal Counsel | Advises on legal obligations, privilege, evidence preservation, contracts, law enforcement, customer commitments, and external notification requirements. |
| Privacy Officer | Assesses personal data impact, notification requirements, data subject considerations, and privacy-related remediation. |
| Communications Lead | Prepares and coordinates approved messaging for internal and external audiences, including status updates and public statements where required. |
| Customer Success Lead | Coordinates customer-specific communications, tracks customer impact, supports customer inquiries, and ensures consistent customer messaging. |
| Vendor Management | Coordinates with third-party providers, confirms contractual obligations, obtains vendor incident details, and tracks vendor remediation commitments. |
| Human Resources | Supports incidents involving personnel misconduct, insider risk, disciplinary action, or employee communications. |
| Business Continuity Owner | Coordinates continuity actions where service disruption or business process impact requires alternate operating arrangements. |
| GRC Lead | Maintains evidence for SOC 2 readiness, validates control operation, tracks remediation commitments, and supports audit requests. |
| Employees and Contractors | Report suspected incidents promptly, preserve relevant information, follow instructions from the Incident Response Team, and do not independently investigate or communicate externally. |
| Third-Party Service Providers | Report relevant incidents affecting organisation systems or data, support investigation, provide timely updates, and complete agreed remediation actions. |

Decision authority matrix:

| Decision | Primary Authority | Required Consultation |
|---|---|---|
| Activate this plan | Security Incident Response Manager or Incident Commander | Security Leadership |
| Assign or change incident severity | Incident Commander | Security Operations, affected system owner |
| Disable account or revoke access | Incident Commander / IT Operations | System Owner where feasible |
| Isolate production system | Incident Commander | Engineering Lead, System Owner, Executive Sponsor for major impact |
| Restore affected service | System Owner / Engineering Lead | Security Incident Response Manager, Business Owner |
| Notify customers | Executive Sponsor / Customer Success Lead | Legal, Privacy, Communications, Security |
| Notify regulator or law enforcement | Legal / Privacy | Executive Sponsor, Security |
| Engage external forensic firm | Security Leadership | Legal, Procurement, Executive Sponsor where material |
| Accept material residual risk | Executive Sponsor | Security Leadership, Legal, Business Owner |
| Close incident | Incident Commander | Security Incident Response Manager, System Owner, Legal or Privacy where applicable |

## Resources

The organisation will maintain resources necessary to support timely and effective incident response.

People resources:

- Designated Incident Response Team with primary and backup members.
- 24x7 or risk-based on-call coverage for critical systems.
- Access to Legal, Privacy, Communications, Customer Success, Engineering, IT, and executive stakeholders.
- External forensic, legal, public relations, and managed security service support where internal capability is insufficient.
- Trained employees who understand how to identify and report suspected incidents.

Technology resources:

| Resource | Purpose | Minimum Capability |
|---|---|---|
| Security monitoring and alerting | Detect suspicious activity and support investigation | Alerts, dashboards, log search, retention, escalation |
| Endpoint protection and management | Detect, isolate, and remediate endpoint threats | Malware detection, quarantine, isolation, telemetry |
| Identity and access management | Contain account compromise | Account disablement, session revocation, MFA, audit logs |
| Cloud security tooling | Investigate and contain cloud incidents | Activity logs, configuration history, resource isolation |
| Ticketing or case management | Track incidents and response evidence | Incident workflow, timestamps, owners, attachments |
| Secure communications | Coordinate response securely | Restricted channels, backup communications, access control |
| Backup and recovery platform | Restore systems and data | Tested backups, recovery logs, integrity validation |
| Vulnerability management tools | Identify and confirm remediation | Scanning, prioritisation, remediation tracking |
| Evidence repository | Preserve investigation records | Restricted access, retention controls, audit trail |
| Asset inventory | Identify ownership and criticality | System owner, data classification, environment, dependencies |

Documentation resources:

- Incident Response Policy & Plan.
- Incident response playbooks.
- Severity matrix and escalation guide.
- Contact lists and on-call schedules.
- System architecture diagrams and data flow diagrams.
- Asset inventory and data classification records.
- Backup and recovery procedures.
- Business continuity and disaster recovery plans.
- Vendor escalation contacts and contract summaries.
- Customer notification templates.
- Evidence handling guidance.
- Post-incident review template.
- Corrective action tracker.

Budget and procurement considerations:

- External incident response retainer or emergency procurement path.
- Cyber insurance contact details and notification process.
- Emergency approval process for forensic services, legal support, cloud capacity, tooling, or communications support.
- Budget for tabletop exercises, training, and tooling improvements.
- Pre-approved access to critical vendor support plans where required.

Training and awareness resources:

| Audience | Training Topic | Frequency |
|---|---|---:|
| All personnel | How to identify and report suspected incidents, phishing, data handling expectations | At onboarding and annually |
| Incident Response Team | Incident lifecycle, roles, evidence preservation, severity classification, escalation | Annually and after major updates |
| Security Operations | Alert triage, investigation methods, containment tools, documentation requirements | Ongoing |
| Engineering / IT | Production containment, secure recovery, logging, credential rotation, vulnerability remediation | Annually |
| Executives | Decision-making during major incidents, communication approval, risk acceptance | Annually or through tabletop exercises |
| Communications / Customer Success | Approved messaging, customer impact handling, confidentiality expectations | Annually |
| Legal / Privacy | Incident workflow, technical evidence, notification decision process | Annually or as needed |

## Success Metrics

The effectiveness of this plan will be measured through operational, readiness, communication, recovery, and improvement metrics.

| Metric | Description | Target / Expectation | Reporting Frequency |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Incident triage timeliness | Percentage of reported incidents triaged within target time based on severity | 95% or greater | Monthly |
| Time to contain | Elapsed time from incident confirmation to containment | Trending downward or within severity targets | Monthly / per incident |
| Time to recover | Elapsed time from containment to approved recovery | Within agreed recovery expectations | Per incident |
| Detection source coverage | Percentage of incidents detected through approved monitoring versus ad hoc discovery | Improvement over time | Quarterly |
| Incident documentation completeness | Percentage of incidents with required fields, timeline, evidence, actions, and closure approval | 95% or greater | Monthly |
| Post-incident review completion | Percentage of required reviews completed within target timeframe | 100% for High and Critical incidents | Quarterly |
| Corrective action closure | Percentage of corrective actions closed by due date | 90% or greater | Monthly |
| Repeat incident rate | Number of recurring incidents with same or similar root cause | Trending downward | Quarterly |
| Evidence preservation compliance | Incidents with required evidence stored in approved repository | 100% for High and Critical incidents | Quarterly |
| Exercise completion | Required tabletop or technical exercises completed on schedule | At least annually | Annually |
| Training completion | Required personnel completing incident response or security awareness training | 95% or greater | Quarterly |
| Contact list accuracy | Key contacts validated and updated | 100% of critical contacts current | Quarterly |
| Communication approval compliance | External communications approved through required workflow | 100% | Per incident |
| Customer impact assessment timeliness | Customer impact evaluated within target time for High and Critical incidents | 100% | Per incident |
| Monitoring improvement actions | Detection improvements implemented from incidents and exercises | Tracked to completion | Quarterly |

Qualitative indicators of success include:

- Responders understand their roles and can activate the plan without ambiguity.
- Incident records provide a clear, defensible timeline of what happened and what decisions were made.
- Customers receive accurate and approved information when they are affected.
- Recovery actions do not reintroduce the threat or create unacceptable residual risk.
- Lessons learned result in measurable control improvements.
- Auditors can trace incidents from detection through closure, including evidence of communication, remediation, and management oversight.

## Review & Update Triggers

This plan must be reviewed at least annually and updated whenever changes materially affect incident response readiness or requirements.

Review and update triggers include:

- Completion of a High or Critical incident.
- Post-incident review identifying gaps in roles, procedures, controls, communications, or evidence handling.
- Significant changes to production architecture, cloud environments, identity systems, logging, monitoring, or backup capabilities.
- Launch of a new product, service, geography, or customer segment with materially different security or notification considerations.
- Material change in customer contractual obligations related to security incidents or notifications.
- Material change in applicable legal, privacy, regulatory, insurance, or industry expectations.
- Change in key incident response personnel, executive sponsor, legal counsel, privacy officer, communications lead, or on-call model.
- Change in material third-party providers supporting production, security monitoring, hosting, customer support, identity, or data processing.
- Tabletop exercise or audit identifying improvement opportunities.
- Evidence that incident response metrics are not meeting defined targets.
- Discovery that contact lists, playbooks, templates, or escalation paths are inaccurate.
- Changes to data classification, customer data handling, or critical business processes.
- Introduction of new threat scenarios requiring specific playbooks, such as ransomware, source code compromise, supply chain attack, cloud account takeover, or data extortion.

Review process:

1. The Security Incident Response Manager initiates the review and collects feedback from Security Operations, IT, Engineering, Legal, Privacy, Communications, Customer Success, GRC, and relevant business owners.
2. Open incidents, incident trends, corrective actions, exercises, audit findings, and monitoring gaps are assessed.
3. Updates are drafted and reviewed by required stakeholders.
4. Security leadership approves material changes.
5. The updated plan is published to the approved document repository.
6. A change summary is communicated to affected stakeholders.
7. Training, playbooks, templates, and exercises are updated where required.
8. Superseded versions are retained according to document retention requirements.

SOC2-014.title: Business Continuity & DR Policy
SOC2-014.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | POL-BCDR-001 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [Business Continuity Manager / Head of Operations] |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | SOC 2 |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery Policy is to establish mandatory requirements for maintaining the availability and recoverability of critical business operations, systems, data, and services in the event of disruption.

This policy supports the organisation’s commitment to delivering reliable services to customers by ensuring that foreseeable interruptions are planned for, response responsibilities are defined, recovery strategies are tested, and continuity capabilities are maintained in line with business, customer, contractual, and operational requirements.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All employees, contractors, temporary staff, and third parties who support or operate business processes, technology services, infrastructure, applications, data, facilities, or customer-facing services.
- All production systems, supporting infrastructure, cloud services, networks, endpoints, data repositories, communication platforms, and operational processes required to deliver services to customers.
- All business functions that support service delivery, customer support, security operations, finance operations, people operations, vendor management, and executive decision-making during a disruption.
- All locations and remote working arrangements used by the organisation.
- All third-party service providers whose services are material to the organisation’s ability to meet availability, recovery, customer, legal, or contractual commitments.

This policy covers planning, ownership, risk assessment, business impact analysis, continuity strategies, disaster recovery planning, communications, backup and restoration, testing, incident escalation, lessons learned, and ongoing maintenance of business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain a documented Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery program that is approved by management, aligned to business objectives, and proportionate to the organisation’s service delivery obligations and operational risk profile.

2. The organisation shall identify critical business processes, systems, applications, data, infrastructure, personnel, facilities, vendors, and dependencies required to deliver services and support customers during normal and disrupted operations.

3. The organisation shall perform and maintain a Business Impact Analysis for critical business processes and technology services to determine the operational, financial, legal, security, customer, and reputational impact of service disruption.

4. The Business Impact Analysis shall define recovery requirements for each critical process and service, including Recovery Time Objectives, Recovery Point Objectives, minimum operating requirements, key dependencies, required personnel, and acceptable workarounds.

5. The organisation shall maintain documented Business Continuity Plans for critical business functions and documented Disaster Recovery Plans for critical technology services.

6. Business Continuity Plans shall include, at minimum, activation criteria, response roles, escalation paths, continuity procedures, manual workarounds where applicable, communication requirements, resource needs, and restoration priorities.

7. Disaster Recovery Plans shall include, at minimum, system recovery procedures, backup restoration steps, infrastructure rebuild or failover instructions, data validation activities, dependency sequencing, access requirements, vendor escalation contacts, and recovery verification criteria.

8. Recovery strategies shall be designed to meet approved recovery objectives and shall consider redundancy, backup, alternative processing arrangements, remote access, manual workarounds, alternate suppliers, and cloud or infrastructure resilience capabilities where appropriate.

9. The organisation shall establish and maintain the following minimum continuity and disaster recovery planning elements:

| Planning Element | Minimum Requirement |
|---|---|
| Business Impact Analysis | Completed for critical business processes and systems and reviewed at least annually |
| Business Continuity Plans | Maintained for critical business functions |
| Disaster Recovery Plans | Maintained for critical production systems and supporting infrastructure |
| Recovery Objectives | Defined and approved for critical processes and services |
| Backup Strategy | Documented and aligned to approved recovery objectives |
| Communication Plan | Maintained for internal, customer, vendor, and stakeholder communications |
| Testing Program | Conducted at planned intervals and after material changes |
| Lessons Learned | Documented after exercises and actual disruptions |

10. The organisation shall assign ownership for each Business Continuity Plan and Disaster Recovery Plan to an accountable business or technology owner.

11. Plan owners shall ensure that continuity and recovery plans remain accurate, actionable, and accessible to authorised personnel during a disruption.

12. The organisation shall maintain emergency and crisis communication procedures to support timely coordination with employees, management, customers, vendors, regulators where applicable, and other relevant stakeholders.

13. Communication procedures shall include approved communication channels, escalation contacts, notification templates or guidance, decision-making authority, and requirements for protecting confidential information during a disruption.

14. The organisation shall maintain current contact information for personnel and third parties required to execute Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery plans.

15. Critical continuity and recovery documentation shall be stored in a manner that remains accessible during loss of primary systems, primary facilities, corporate network access, or normal collaboration tools.

16. The organisation shall implement backup and restoration capabilities for critical data and systems that support approved recovery objectives.

17. Backup processes shall be monitored for successful completion, and backup failures affecting critical systems shall be investigated and remediated in a timely manner.

18. Restoration of backups for critical systems shall be tested periodically to confirm that data can be recovered within approved recovery objectives and that restored data is complete and usable.

19. Backup data shall be protected against unauthorised access, alteration, deletion, corruption, and loss, including appropriate access controls, encryption where required, retention controls, and separation from production environments where feasible.

20. The organisation shall define severity levels and escalation criteria for disruptions affecting availability of critical business processes, systems, or services.

21. Events that may require activation of Business Continuity or Disaster Recovery Plans shall be promptly assessed and escalated to the appropriate decision-makers.

22. The organisation shall define authority for declaring a business continuity event, disaster recovery event, major service disruption, or crisis.

23. The organisation shall prioritise safety of personnel, protection of customer data, restoration of critical services, preservation of evidence where relevant, and clear communication during disruptive events.

24. The organisation shall establish continuity and recovery requirements for third-party providers that support critical operations or services.

25. Material third-party providers shall be assessed for their ability to support the organisation’s continuity and recovery requirements before onboarding and periodically thereafter.

26. Contracts or service agreements with material third-party providers shall include appropriate availability, incident notification, continuity, disaster recovery, data protection, and support commitments where commercially feasible.

27. The organisation shall consider concentration risk and single points of failure in vendors, infrastructure, personnel, facilities, data stores, network connectivity, and operational processes.

28. The organisation shall maintain alternate operating arrangements for critical business functions where loss of a facility, system, vendor, or key personnel would materially affect service delivery.

29. Remote working capabilities used as part of continuity arrangements shall be secured, tested, and capable of supporting critical operations during disruption.

30. Access required for continuity and disaster recovery activities shall be authorised, controlled, logged where technically feasible, and limited to personnel with a legitimate business need.

31. Emergency access granted during a disruption shall be reviewed after the event and revoked when no longer required.

32. The organisation shall conduct Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery testing at planned intervals to validate the effectiveness of plans, procedures, personnel readiness, communication channels, recovery objectives, and technical recovery capabilities.

33. Testing shall include an appropriate mix of tabletop exercises, technical recovery tests, backup restoration tests, communication exercises, failover tests, and scenario-based simulations based on the organisation’s risk profile.

34. At minimum, the organisation shall perform the following testing activities:

| Test Type | Minimum Frequency | Expected Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Business continuity tabletop exercise | Annually | Scenario, attendees, decisions, issues, action items |
| Disaster recovery technical exercise for critical systems | Annually | Test plan, execution evidence, recovery results, issues |
| Backup restoration test for critical data | At least annually, or more frequently based on risk | Restoration result, validation evidence, defects |
| Emergency contact and communication test | At least annually | Contact validation, delivery results, exceptions |
| Plan walkthrough with plan owners | Annually | Review notes, updates, approvals |

35. Test results shall be documented and retained as evidence, including scope, scenario, participants, timeline, recovery results, issues identified, deviations from expected outcomes, and corrective actions.

36. Corrective actions identified through testing, actual incidents, audits, risk assessments, vendor reviews, or management reviews shall be assigned an owner, target date, and priority.

37. Corrective actions shall be tracked to completion and verified for effectiveness where appropriate.

38. The organisation shall conduct post-incident reviews after significant disruptions, disaster recovery activations, major outages, or failed continuity exercises.

39. Post-incident reviews shall identify root causes where feasible, response effectiveness, communication effectiveness, customer impact, recovery performance, policy or plan gaps, and required improvements.

40. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery planning shall be integrated with incident management, security incident response, change management, vendor risk management, risk assessment, asset management, and corporate communications processes.

41. Material changes to critical systems, infrastructure, business processes, facilities, vendors, operating models, or customer commitments shall trigger review and update of applicable continuity and recovery plans.

42. The organisation shall consider continuity and recovery requirements during design, implementation, and change approval for critical systems and services.

43. New production systems or materially changed systems shall not be classified as critical without defined recovery ownership, recovery objectives, backup requirements, and recovery procedures.

44. The organisation shall ensure personnel with assigned continuity or recovery responsibilities receive appropriate awareness, training, and access to relevant plans and tools.

45. Personnel participating in continuity or disaster recovery activities shall understand their assigned responsibilities, escalation paths, communication requirements, and decision-making authority.

46. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery records shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s record retention requirements and shall be available for internal review, external audit, and management oversight.

47. The organisation shall protect continuity and recovery documentation from unauthorised disclosure where it contains sensitive operational, security, vendor, infrastructure, customer, or personal information.

48. The organisation shall report significant continuity and disaster recovery risks, testing results, incidents, plan deficiencies, and remediation status to management on a periodic basis.

49. The organisation shall maintain evidence sufficient to demonstrate that continuity and recovery requirements are implemented, tested, monitored, and improved over time.

50. The organisation shall not rely solely on untested assumptions, undocumented procedures, individual knowledge, or informal communications for recovery of critical services.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Management | Approves the Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery program; provides resources; sets risk tolerance; supports crisis decision-making; reviews significant risks and remediation status. |
| Business Continuity Manager / Program Owner | Owns the overall continuity program; coordinates Business Impact Analysis activities; maintains policy and program standards; facilitates exercises; tracks corrective actions; reports program status to management. |
| Disaster Recovery Lead / Technology Recovery Owner | Owns technology recovery planning; coordinates technical recovery procedures; ensures disaster recovery plans align with recovery objectives; leads technical recovery testing and restoration validation. |
| Business Process Owners | Identify critical processes, dependencies, manual workarounds, staffing requirements, and operational impacts; maintain Business Continuity Plans for their areas; participate in testing and post-incident reviews. |
| System Owners | Define system criticality, recovery objectives, dependencies, backup requirements, and recovery procedures; ensure system recovery documentation is current and tested. |
| Information Security | Advises on security requirements during continuity and recovery activities; ensures emergency access and recovery actions maintain appropriate protection of systems and data; supports incident coordination where disruption involves security events. |
| IT Operations / Infrastructure Teams | Maintain resilient infrastructure, backups, monitoring, recovery tooling, access mechanisms, and technical procedures; execute recovery actions during disaster recovery events. |
| Customer Support / Customer Success | Supports customer communications during service disruptions; provides customer impact information; escalates customer availability concerns through approved channels. |
| Communications / Legal / Compliance | Supports stakeholder notifications, external messaging, contractual communication obligations, regulatory considerations where applicable, and review of sensitive communications. |
| Vendor Management | Identifies material third-party dependencies; obtains and reviews continuity and recovery information from vendors; supports vendor escalation during disruptions. |
| Human Resources / People Operations | Supports employee communications, workforce continuity planning, emergency contact processes, and personnel availability considerations. |
| Employees and Contractors | Follow continuity instructions during disruptions; maintain awareness of emergency communications; report disruptions promptly; participate in training and exercises when assigned. |
| Internal Audit / Assurance Function | Provides independent review of continuity and recovery controls where applicable; validates evidence and reports findings to management. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy shall be monitored through governance reviews, management reporting, testing activities, audit evidence review, operational monitoring, and periodic assessment of continuity and recovery capabilities.

The following evidence shall be maintained to demonstrate compliance:

| Evidence Type | Minimum Content |
|---|---|
| Business Impact Analysis records | Critical processes, systems, dependencies, impact ratings, recovery objectives, approvals |
| Business Continuity Plans | Current plan versions, owners, activation criteria, procedures, contact lists |
| Disaster Recovery Plans | Recovery steps, dependency sequencing, backup and restoration procedures, validation criteria |
| Test records | Test scope, scenario, participants, execution details, results, issues, action items |
| Backup and restoration records | Backup status, failures, remediation, restoration test results |
| Incident and post-incident records | Timeline, decisions, impact, recovery actions, lessons learned, corrective actions |
| Third-party continuity assessments | Vendor recovery capabilities, availability commitments, identified risks, remediation actions |
| Management reporting | Program status, risk issues, test outcomes, remediation progress |

Management shall review Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery program performance at planned intervals. Reviews should consider:

- Current critical processes and systems.
- Status of Business Impact Analysis updates.
- Test completion and test outcomes.
- Recovery performance against objectives.
- Backup and restoration reliability.
- Open corrective actions and overdue items.
- Material continuity risks.
- Third-party dependency concerns.
- Significant incidents or service disruptions.
- Resource requirements and improvement priorities.

Non-compliance with this policy may result in corrective action, including remediation plans, additional training, access restrictions, vendor escalation, contractual remedies, disciplinary action, or other management action appropriate to the severity and impact of the non-compliance.

Intentional disregard of continuity, disaster recovery, backup, communication, or escalation requirements may be treated as a serious violation of organisational policy.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be documented, risk-assessed, approved, time-bound, and reviewed periodically.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception description | The specific requirement that cannot be met |
| Business justification | Why the exception is necessary |
| Affected processes or systems | Services, data, customers, vendors, or locations impacted |
| Risk assessment | Potential impact to availability, recovery, customers, security, compliance, and operations |
| Compensating controls | Alternative measures used to reduce risk |
| Exception owner | Person accountable for managing the exception |
| Expiry date | Date by which the exception must be remediated or re-approved |
| Approval | Authorised approver based on risk level |

Exceptions that materially affect the organisation’s ability to recover critical services, meet customer commitments, restore data, or communicate during disruptions shall require approval from executive management or an authorised risk governance body.

Expired exceptions shall not be considered valid unless formally re-assessed and re-approved.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and updated as needed to remain aligned with business operations, customer commitments, technology architecture, risk profile, service availability requirements, and organisational changes.

The policy shall also be reviewed following:

- Significant service disruption or disaster recovery activation.
- Major change to critical systems, infrastructure, facilities, vendors, or business processes.
- Material change in customer or contractual availability commitments.
- Significant organisational restructuring.
- Results from testing that identify major policy or program gaps.
- Audit findings or management concerns related to continuity or disaster recovery.
- Changes to applicable legal, regulatory, or business requirements.

The policy owner is responsible for coordinating reviews, obtaining stakeholder input, maintaining version history, securing required approvals, and communicating material policy changes to affected personnel.

Superseded versions of this policy shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s record retention requirements.

SOC2-015.title: Confidentiality Policy
SOC2-015.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-CONF-001] | 1.0 | [Chief Information Security Officer] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | SOC 2 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Confidentiality Policy establishes mandatory requirements for protecting confidential information entrusted to, created by, processed by, or stored by [Organization Name]. The policy supports the organization’s commitments to customers, business partners, employees, and other stakeholders by ensuring confidential information is identified, used appropriately, protected from unauthorized access or disclosure, and retained or disposed of in accordance with contractual, legal, regulatory, and business requirements.

This policy is intended to ensure that confidential information is protected throughout its lifecycle, including collection, classification, access, use, transmission, storage, sharing, retention, archival, and destruction.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All employees, contractors, consultants, temporary workers, interns, and other personnel who access, process, manage, or support [Organization Name] information assets.
- All information systems, applications, infrastructure, networks, databases, repositories, endpoints, collaboration platforms, cloud services, and third-party services used to store, process, transmit, or manage confidential information.
- All confidential information in any form, including electronic, paper, verbal, visual, and recorded formats.
- Confidential information owned by [Organization Name], customers, business partners, suppliers, employees, or other authorized third parties.
- All environments where confidential information may reside, including production, non-production, development, testing, support, backup, archive, and disaster recovery environments.

For the purposes of this policy, confidential information includes information that is not intended for public disclosure and that could cause harm to [Organization Name], its customers, business partners, employees, or other stakeholders if disclosed, altered, lost, or accessed without authorization.

Examples include, but are not limited to:

- Customer data and customer-provided confidential information.
- Contractual terms, pricing, statements of work, and customer-specific service information.
- Business plans, financial information, forecasts, and strategic materials.
- Intellectual property, product designs, source code, algorithms, architecture diagrams, and technical documentation.
- Security information, including vulnerability information, security configurations, access credentials, incident details, and monitoring data.
- Employee and contractor records.
- Legal, compliance, and audit materials.
- Non-public operational procedures and internal reports.
- Authentication secrets, encryption keys, tokens, certificates, and API credentials.

## Policy Statements

1. **Confidentiality obligations shall be formally established.** 
 [Organization Name] shall define, approve, communicate, and enforce requirements for protecting confidential information. All workforce members and relevant third parties shall be bound by confidentiality obligations before receiving access to confidential information.

2. **Confidential information shall be identified and classified.** 
 Information shall be classified based on sensitivity, business value, contractual obligations, and potential impact of unauthorized disclosure. Classification labels shall be applied where technically or operationally feasible.

3. **Information classification levels shall be consistently applied.** 
 The following classification model shall be used unless a formally approved alternative is required for a specific business, customer, or regulatory need:

 | Classification | Description | Examples | Minimum Handling Requirements |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Public | Approved for public release with no expected harm from disclosure. | Published marketing materials, public website content, approved press releases. | May be shared externally after approval through authorized channels. |
 | Internal | Intended for internal business use and not approved for public disclosure. | Internal procedures, general business communications, non-sensitive internal reports. | Access limited to authorized workforce members and approved service providers. |
 | Confidential | Sensitive business, customer, personnel, legal, security, or technical information requiring restricted access. | Customer data, contracts, source code, security documentation, financial records. | Access shall be granted based on business need; encryption and controlled sharing shall be used. |
 | Restricted | Highly sensitive information requiring the strongest level of protection due to contractual, legal, security, or business impact. | Credentials, encryption keys, regulated data, sensitive incident details, privileged access records. | Access shall be tightly limited, logged, encrypted, and subject to enhanced approval and monitoring. |

4. **Access to confidential information shall be based on least privilege.** 
 Access shall be limited to individuals, systems, and third parties with a legitimate business need. Access shall be approved, provisioned, reviewed, modified, and removed in accordance with the organization’s access management requirements.

5. **Access to confidential information shall be uniquely attributable.** 
 Users shall access confidential information using uniquely assigned accounts wherever technically feasible. Shared accounts shall be prohibited unless formally approved, risk-assessed, controlled, and monitored.

6. **Privileged access to confidential information shall be restricted and monitored.** 
 Administrative, elevated, or service-level access that can view, modify, export, delete, or disclose confidential information shall be limited to authorized personnel and systems. Privileged access shall be approved, logged, reviewed, and removed when no longer required.

7. **Confidential information shall only be used for authorized business purposes.** 
 Personnel shall not access, use, copy, extract, transfer, disclose, or retain confidential information except as required to perform assigned job responsibilities or authorized business activities.

8. **Customer confidential information shall be protected in accordance with commitments.** 
 Customer information shall be handled in accordance with applicable contracts, service descriptions, data processing terms, confidentiality agreements, and documented customer instructions.

9. **Confidential information shall not be disclosed without authorization.** 
 Disclosure of confidential information to external parties shall require appropriate authorization, a valid business purpose, and an executed agreement containing confidentiality protections unless disclosure is legally compelled or otherwise approved by Legal.

10. **Confidential information shall be protected during transmission.** 
 Confidential and Restricted information shall be transmitted using approved secure methods, such as encrypted email, secure file transfer, encrypted APIs, virtual private networks, or other approved encrypted communication channels.

11. **Confidential information shall be protected at rest.** 
 Confidential and Restricted information shall be stored only in approved systems and repositories. Encryption shall be used for stored confidential information where supported and appropriate based on sensitivity, contractual obligations, and risk.

12. **Confidential information shall be stored only in approved locations.** 
 Confidential information shall not be stored in unauthorized personal accounts, unmanaged devices, consumer file-sharing services, removable media, or unapproved cloud platforms.

13. **Confidential information shall be protected in non-production environments.** 
 Production confidential information shall not be used in development, testing, training, sandbox, or demonstration environments unless approved, required for a legitimate business purpose, protected with equivalent safeguards, and minimized or de-identified where feasible.

14. **Confidential information shall be minimized.** 
 The organization shall collect, access, process, retain, and disclose only the confidential information necessary for approved business purposes, contractual obligations, legal requirements, or service delivery.

15. **Confidential information shall be accurate and complete where relied upon.** 
 Processes that use confidential information for customer service delivery, reporting, billing, security, compliance, or operational decisions shall include reasonable measures to preserve integrity and prevent unauthorized modification.

16. **Confidential information shall be protected against unauthorized copying and extraction.** 
 Bulk exports, downloads, printing, screenshots, data replication, and extraction of Confidential or Restricted information shall be limited to authorized business needs and may be subject to additional approval, monitoring, and technical restrictions.

17. **Confidential information shall be protected on endpoints and mobile devices.** 
 Devices used to access confidential information shall meet organizational security requirements, including access control, encryption where required, endpoint protection, patching, screen locking, and remote wipe capability where applicable.

18. **Physical records containing confidential information shall be protected.** 
 Paper records and physical media containing confidential information shall be stored securely, protected from unauthorized viewing or removal, transported using approved methods, and destroyed using secure disposal processes.

19. **Conversations involving confidential information shall be conducted appropriately.** 
 Personnel shall avoid discussing confidential information in public areas or with unauthorized individuals. Meetings involving confidential information shall be limited to authorized participants.

20. **Confidential information shall be shared internally only with authorized recipients.** 
 Internal sharing shall be restricted to personnel who require the information for assigned responsibilities. Distribution lists, shared drives, collaboration workspaces, and messaging channels shall be configured to prevent unauthorized access.

21. **Confidential information shall be shared externally only through approved methods.** 
 External sharing shall occur only through approved tools, approved recipients, and appropriate contractual or legal safeguards. External recipients shall be verified before confidential information is disclosed.

22. **Third parties shall protect confidential information.** 
 Vendors, service providers, contractors, and other third parties that access or process confidential information shall be subject to due diligence, contractual confidentiality obligations, security requirements, and ongoing oversight proportionate to risk.

23. **Confidential information shall be retained only as long as required.** 
 Retention periods shall be defined and followed based on business, contractual, legal, regulatory, tax, audit, and operational requirements. Information shall not be retained indefinitely unless formally required and approved.

24. **Confidential information shall be securely disposed of.** 
 Confidential information that is no longer required shall be securely deleted, destroyed, anonymized, or otherwise rendered unrecoverable using approved disposal methods.

25. **Backups containing confidential information shall be protected.** 
 Backup, archive, and recovery copies containing confidential information shall be protected using access controls, encryption where appropriate, retention controls, and secure destruction practices.

26. **Confidentiality risks shall be considered in system design and change management.** 
 New systems, applications, integrations, business processes, and significant changes involving confidential information shall include appropriate confidentiality requirements, risk assessment, access control design, logging, and data protection measures before implementation.

27. **Confidentiality requirements shall be included in contracts where applicable.** 
 Agreements with customers, partners, suppliers, contractors, and service providers shall include confidentiality terms appropriate to the nature of the information, permitted use, protection requirements, breach notification expectations, return or destruction obligations, and survival of confidentiality duties.

28. **Confidentiality training shall be required.** 
 Workforce members shall complete confidentiality and information security awareness training upon onboarding and periodically thereafter. Training shall include handling expectations, acceptable use, reporting obligations, phishing awareness, secure sharing, and consequences for policy violations.

29. **Personnel shall report suspected confidentiality incidents promptly.** 
 Any actual or suspected unauthorized access, disclosure, loss, theft, misuse, alteration, or exposure of confidential information shall be reported immediately through approved incident reporting channels.

30. **Confidentiality incidents shall be investigated and managed.** 
 Suspected or confirmed confidentiality incidents shall be assessed, contained, investigated, remediated, documented, and escalated in accordance with the organization’s incident response requirements.

31. **Logs and monitoring shall be used to support confidentiality protection.** 
 Systems that store or process Confidential or Restricted information shall generate and retain appropriate logs to support detection, investigation, accountability, and auditability.

32. **Confidential information shall be protected during personnel changes.** 
 Access to confidential information shall be modified or removed when personnel change roles, transfer departments, go on extended leave, or separate from the organization.

33. **Confidentiality obligations shall continue after termination.** 
 Personnel and third parties shall remain responsible for protecting confidential information after their relationship with [Organization Name] ends, as required by agreements and applicable law.

34. **Secrets and credentials shall be treated as Restricted information.** 
 Passwords, API keys, encryption keys, private certificates, tokens, recovery codes, and similar secrets shall not be stored in source code, shared documents, tickets, chat messages, or other unapproved locations.

35. **Confidential information shall be protected from public disclosure through technical and administrative safeguards.** 
 Public repositories, public storage buckets, public websites, external knowledge bases, and publicly accessible collaboration spaces shall not contain confidential information unless formally approved for release.

36. **Data loss prevention and protective technologies shall be used where appropriate.** 
 The organization shall implement technical controls proportionate to risk, such as access controls, encryption, logging, monitoring, data loss prevention, watermarking, rights management, or export restrictions.

37. **Confidential information shall be returned or destroyed upon request where required.** 
 Customer, partner, or third-party confidential information shall be returned, deleted, or destroyed in accordance with contractual commitments, documented instructions, and applicable retention obligations.

38. **Legal holds shall override standard disposal requirements.** 
 Confidential information subject to legal hold, investigation, audit, dispute, or regulatory inquiry shall be preserved until Legal authorizes release from hold.

39. **Confidentiality requirements shall be documented and available.** 
 Supporting standards, procedures, guidelines, and approved handling methods shall be maintained and made available to personnel who process confidential information.

40. **Non-compliance shall be addressed.** 
 Violations of this policy shall be reviewed and may result in corrective action, access restriction, disciplinary action, contract termination, legal action, or other remedies appropriate to the severity and circumstances.

The following table summarizes minimum handling expectations:

| Activity | Internal | Confidential | Restricted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access | Authorized workforce and approved third parties | Business need and approved access | Strict need-to-know with enhanced approval |
| Storage | Approved business systems | Approved secured systems only | Approved secured systems with strong access controls |
| Transmission | Approved business channels | Encrypted or approved secure channels | Encrypted approved channels only |
| External Sharing | Business-approved | Requires authorization and confidentiality protections | Requires explicit approval and documented safeguards |
| Printing | Permitted for business need | Limited and securely stored | Strongly restricted and tracked where feasible |
| Disposal | Normal business disposal | Secure deletion or shredding | Verified secure destruction |
| Monitoring | Standard monitoring | Access and activity logging where feasible | Enhanced logging and periodic review |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors or Executive Leadership | Provides oversight of confidentiality risk management and supports the organization’s confidentiality commitments. |
| Chief Executive Officer | Ensures business accountability for protecting confidential information and supports enforcement of this policy. |
| Chief Information Security Officer | Owns this policy, establishes confidentiality safeguards, oversees implementation, monitors compliance, and reports confidentiality risks to leadership. |
| Legal Counsel | Advises on confidentiality obligations, contractual requirements, legal holds, compelled disclosures, regulatory matters, and breach notification requirements. |
| Privacy Officer or Data Protection Lead | Advises on handling requirements where confidential information includes personal information or regulated data. |
| Information Asset Owners | Classify information assets, approve access, define handling requirements, validate retention needs, and ensure appropriate safeguards are in place. |
| System Owners | Implement technical controls for systems that store, process, or transmit confidential information, including access control, encryption, logging, retention, and secure disposal capabilities. |
| Managers | Ensure team members understand and comply with confidentiality requirements, approve access based on business need, and promptly request access changes when roles change. |
| Human Resources | Ensures workforce confidentiality obligations are acknowledged, supports training completion, and coordinates disciplinary processes where required. |
| Procurement and Vendor Management | Ensures third parties with access to confidential information undergo appropriate review and are subject to confidentiality and security obligations. |
| Information Technology | Supports secure configuration, endpoint protection, identity management, backups, logging, monitoring, and approved collaboration tools. |
| Security Operations | Monitors for potential unauthorized access or disclosure, investigates alerts, and supports incident response involving confidential information. |
| Employees and Contractors | Protect confidential information, follow approved handling procedures, complete required training, use only approved systems, and promptly report suspected incidents. |
| Third Parties | Protect confidential information in accordance with agreements, approved instructions, and applicable security requirements. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy shall be monitored through a combination of management oversight, technical controls, access reviews, security monitoring, vendor oversight, training records, incident metrics, internal assessments, and audit activities.

Monitoring activities may include:

- Review of access to repositories, systems, applications, databases, and collaboration platforms containing confidential information.
- Review of privileged user activity and administrative actions.
- Monitoring for unauthorized sharing, public exposure, unusual downloads, mass exports, or abnormal access patterns.
- Periodic review of user access rights against business need.
- Review of third-party access and contractual confidentiality obligations.
- Validation of encryption, logging, backup, and retention controls.
- Review of incident reports involving unauthorized disclosure or suspected exposure.
- Training completion tracking and follow-up.
- Review of exceptions and remediation actions.
- Internal audits or readiness assessments related to confidentiality commitments.

Minimum monitoring expectations are as follows:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Workforce confidentiality training completion review | At onboarding and annually | Human Resources and Security | Training completion reports |
| User access review for key systems containing confidential information | At least quarterly | System Owners and Managers | Access review records and approvals |
| Privileged access review | At least quarterly | Security and System Owners | Privileged access review evidence |
| Third-party access review | At least annually or upon contract change | Vendor Management and System Owners | Vendor access review records |
| Confidentiality incident review | As incidents occur and at least quarterly in aggregate | Security Operations | Incident tickets, root cause analysis, corrective actions |
| Public exposure review for externally accessible repositories and storage | At least quarterly | Security and IT | Scan results, remediation records |
| Policy compliance assessment | At least annually | Information Security | Assessment report and action plan |
| Exception review | At least quarterly | Information Security and Risk Management | Exception register and approvals |

Enforcement shall be proportionate to the severity, intent, recurrence, and impact of the violation. Enforcement actions may include:

- Coaching or retraining.
- Removal or restriction of access.
- Formal corrective action.
- Disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.
- Termination of vendor or contractor access.
- Contractual remedies.
- Legal action where appropriate.
- Notification to customers, partners, regulators, or affected parties where required.

Personnel who become aware of a violation or suspected violation of this policy shall report it promptly to [Security Contact], [Service Desk], [Incident Reporting Channel], or their manager.

Retaliation against any person who reports a suspected confidentiality concern in good faith is prohibited.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only when there is a documented business justification, risk assessment, compensating controls where feasible, and formal approval from authorized personnel.

Exception requests shall include:

- Description of the policy requirement for which an exception is requested.
- Business justification.
- Scope of affected information, systems, users, third parties, or processes.
- Confidentiality risks and potential impact.
- Proposed compensating controls.
- Duration of the exception.
- Remediation or transition plan.
- Approval from the Information Security owner and relevant business or system owner.
- Legal, Privacy, or Risk approval where required based on the nature of the information.

Exceptions shall be time-bound and reviewed periodically. Permanent exceptions are not permitted unless the policy is updated to reflect an approved change in organizational requirements.

| Exception Risk Level | Maximum Approval Period | Required Approval |
|---|---:|---|
| Low | Up to 12 months | Information Security and Business Owner |
| Medium | Up to 6 months | Information Security, Business Owner, and Risk Management |
| High | Up to 90 days | CISO, Business Executive, and Legal or Privacy where applicable |
| Critical | Not permitted unless approved by Executive Leadership | Executive Leadership and CISO |

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed through the formal exception process before expiration.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect confidentiality requirements, including:

- Changes to products, services, systems, or business processes.
- New or changed customer commitments.
- New or changed legal, regulatory, contractual, or compliance obligations.
- Significant security incidents involving confidential information.
- Material changes in technology, infrastructure, or third-party services.
- Audit findings or risk assessments requiring policy updates.
- Changes in organizational structure, roles, or responsibilities.

The [Chief Information Security Officer] is responsible for maintaining this policy and ensuring it remains aligned with organizational commitments, business objectives, risk appetite, and operational practices.

Policy updates shall be approved by [Approving Authority] and communicated to affected personnel. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organization’s document retention requirements.

SOC2-016.title: Privacy Policy & Notice
SOC2-016.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-PRIV-001] | 1.0 | [Privacy Officer / Legal Counsel] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | SOC 2 | Internal Use |

## Purpose

This Privacy Policy & Notice establishes the mandatory requirements for how [Organisation Name] collects, uses, retains, discloses, protects, and disposes of personal information in connection with its products, services, websites, applications, business operations, and customer engagements.

This policy is intended to ensure that [Organisation Name]:

- Provides clear and accurate notice about privacy practices.
- Collects and uses personal information only for appropriate, disclosed, and authorised purposes.
- Respects individual privacy rights and preferences.
- Protects personal information throughout its lifecycle.
- Shares personal information only with authorised parties and under appropriate safeguards.
- Maintains evidence that privacy commitments are implemented and operating effectively.
- Meets contractual, legal, regulatory, and trust service commitments related to privacy.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All employees, contractors, temporary workers, consultants, officers, and third parties acting on behalf of [Organisation Name].
- All business units, departments, and functions that collect, access, use, store, transmit, disclose, or dispose of personal information.
- All systems, applications, databases, collaboration platforms, storage locations, paper records, backups, logs, and reporting tools that contain personal information.
- Personal information processed in any capacity, including information about customers, customer end users, employees, job applicants, suppliers, partners, website visitors, prospects, and other individuals.
- Personal information processed by service providers, subprocessors, vendors, and other third parties on behalf of [Organisation Name].
- Privacy notices, consent mechanisms, preference centres, data subject request processes, customer contracts, and related privacy communications.

For the purposes of this policy:

- **Personal information** means any information that identifies, relates to, describes, can reasonably be associated with, or could reasonably be linked to an identified or identifiable individual.
- **Sensitive personal information** means personal information that requires heightened protection due to its nature, applicable law, contractual commitments, or risk of harm if misused or disclosed. This may include government identifiers, financial information, health information, biometric information, precise location information, account credentials, children’s information, or information revealing protected characteristics.
- **Processing** means any operation performed on personal information, including collection, recording, organisation, storage, access, use, modification, transmission, disclosure, retention, deletion, and destruction.
- **Privacy notice** means an external or internal communication that describes how [Organisation Name] processes personal information and how individuals may exercise privacy choices or rights.

## Policy Statements

1. **Privacy Governance**

 1.1. [Organisation Name] shall maintain a documented privacy program aligned with its business activities, contractual commitments, risk profile, and obligations to customers and individuals.

 1.2. [Organisation Name] shall assign accountable ownership for privacy governance to a designated Privacy Officer, Legal Counsel, Data Protection Officer, or equivalent role.

 1.3. [Organisation Name] shall maintain documented privacy policies, standards, and operating procedures that support this policy and address collection, use, access, retention, disclosure, disposal, individual rights, incident response, and third-party processing.

 1.4. [Organisation Name] shall ensure that privacy requirements are incorporated into relevant business processes, product development activities, vendor management processes, customer onboarding, employee onboarding, and system change processes.

 1.5. [Organisation Name] shall maintain records sufficient to demonstrate that privacy requirements are implemented, reviewed, and monitored.

2. **Privacy Notice and Transparency**

 2.1. [Organisation Name] shall provide clear, complete, and reasonably accessible privacy notices before or at the time personal information is collected, unless another timing is required by applicable law or contractual obligation.

 2.2. Privacy notices shall describe, at minimum, the categories of personal information collected, the purposes of processing, the categories of recipients, retention practices, individual rights and choices, contact details for privacy inquiries, and the effective date of the notice.

 2.3. Privacy notices shall be written in plain language appropriate to the intended audience and shall not be misleading, deceptive, or inconsistent with actual processing practices.

 2.4. [Organisation Name] shall publish the public privacy notice on its website and make relevant internal privacy notices available to employees, contractors, and applicants.

 2.5. [Organisation Name] shall update privacy notices before materially changing how personal information is collected, used, disclosed, or retained.

 2.6. [Organisation Name] shall maintain evidence of privacy notice publication, approval, and change history.

 2.7. Where [Organisation Name] processes personal information on behalf of a customer, [Organisation Name] shall support the customer’s notice obligations as required by contract, but shall not make unauthorised representations on the customer’s behalf.

3. **Purpose Limitation**

 3.1. [Organisation Name] shall collect and process personal information only for legitimate, documented, and disclosed business purposes.

 3.2. [Organisation Name] shall not use personal information for purposes that are incompatible with the purposes disclosed at collection unless appropriate notice, consent, contractual authorisation, or other valid basis has been established.

 3.3. Business owners shall document the purpose for collecting personal information before initiating a new collection activity, product feature, campaign, integration, or data transfer.

 3.4. [Organisation Name] shall prohibit the use of personal information for personal, unauthorised, discriminatory, deceptive, or unlawful purposes.

4. **Data Minimisation**

 4.1. [Organisation Name] shall collect only the personal information that is necessary and proportionate for the stated business purpose.

 4.2. [Organisation Name] shall avoid collecting sensitive personal information unless it is specifically required for an approved business purpose and appropriate safeguards have been implemented.

 4.3. Forms, workflows, integrations, reports, logs, and analytics tools shall be designed to avoid unnecessary collection or exposure of personal information.

 4.4. Default system configurations shall limit personal information collection to what is required for the approved service, transaction, or operational purpose.

 4.5. Where feasible, [Organisation Name] shall use de-identified, anonymised, aggregated, masked, or tokenised information instead of directly identifiable personal information.

5. **Consent, Choice, and Preferences**

 5.1. [Organisation Name] shall obtain valid consent where consent is required by law, contract, customer instruction, or organisational commitment.

 5.2. Consent requests shall be specific, informed, unambiguous, and separate from unrelated terms where required.

 5.3. [Organisation Name] shall maintain records of consent where consent is relied upon for processing.

 5.4. [Organisation Name] shall provide reasonable mechanisms for individuals to exercise available privacy choices, including marketing preferences, cookie preferences, communication preferences, and withdrawal of consent where applicable.

 5.5. [Organisation Name] shall honour opt-out and withdrawal requests within required timelines and shall not penalise individuals for exercising available privacy choices unless the requested service cannot reasonably be provided without the relevant information.

 5.6. Preference settings shall be applied consistently across relevant systems, platforms, and business processes.

6. **Collection of Personal Information**

 6.1. [Organisation Name] shall collect personal information through lawful, fair, and transparent means.

 6.2. [Organisation Name] shall identify whether personal information is collected directly from individuals, from customers, from third-party sources, through automated technologies, or through system-generated records.

 6.3. [Organisation Name] shall not knowingly collect personal information from children or other restricted categories of individuals unless explicitly approved by Legal or the Privacy Officer and appropriate controls are implemented.

 6.4. [Organisation Name] shall review new or materially changed data collection activities before implementation to confirm privacy notice, consent, security, retention, and contractual requirements.

7. **Use of Personal Information**

 7.1. [Organisation Name] shall use personal information only as authorised by this policy, applicable privacy notices, customer agreements, internal approvals, and documented business purposes.

 7.2. Personal information shall not be used for automated decision-making, profiling, artificial intelligence model training, marketing, product analytics, or secondary analytics unless the activity has been reviewed and approved through the applicable privacy review process.

 7.3. [Organisation Name] shall maintain appropriate safeguards when using personal information in testing, development, training, troubleshooting, reporting, or demonstration environments.

 7.4. Production personal information shall not be used in non-production environments unless approved by Security and Privacy leadership and protected by controls equivalent to production.

8. **Accuracy and Quality**

 8.1. [Organisation Name] shall take reasonable steps to ensure personal information is accurate, complete, and current for the purpose for which it is used.

 8.2. Individuals shall be provided reasonable means to request correction or update of their personal information where applicable.

 8.3. Business owners shall maintain processes to correct inaccurate personal information when inaccuracies are identified.

 8.4. [Organisation Name] shall not knowingly use inaccurate personal information where doing so could adversely affect an individual, customer, employee, or business partner.

9. **Access to Personal Information**

 9.1. Access to personal information shall be limited to authorised personnel and systems with a legitimate business need.

 9.2. Access to personal information shall be granted based on role, job function, customer authorisation, and least privilege principles.

 9.3. Access to sensitive personal information shall require additional approval and shall be reviewed periodically.

 9.4. [Organisation Name] shall remove or modify access promptly when personnel change roles, no longer require access, or separate from the organisation.

 9.5. Administrative access to systems containing personal information shall be restricted, monitored, and protected with strong authentication.

 9.6. Personnel shall not access personal information out of curiosity, for personal purposes, or outside assigned responsibilities.

10. **Security and Protection of Personal Information**

 10.1. [Organisation Name] shall protect personal information using administrative, technical, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity, volume, processing context, and risk of harm.

 10.2. Personal information shall be protected against unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, loss, misuse, destruction, and unavailability.

 10.3. Systems containing personal information shall be subject to security controls including access management, encryption where appropriate, logging, vulnerability management, secure configuration, backup, monitoring, and incident response.

 10.4. Personal information transmitted over public or untrusted networks shall be protected using approved encryption or secure transfer mechanisms.

 10.5. Personal information stored on endpoints, removable media, portable devices, or local storage shall be avoided unless required and explicitly protected by approved security controls.

 10.6. Personnel shall not store personal information in unauthorised repositories, personal email accounts, personal cloud storage, unmanaged devices, or unapproved collaboration tools.

11. **Disclosure and Sharing**

 11.1. [Organisation Name] shall disclose personal information only to authorised recipients and only for approved business purposes.

 11.2. Disclosures of personal information to customers, service providers, partners, regulators, law enforcement, affiliates, or other third parties shall be supported by appropriate legal, contractual, business, and security review.

 11.3. [Organisation Name] shall not sell personal information unless explicitly approved by executive leadership and Legal, disclosed in the applicable privacy notice, and supported by required individual choices.

 11.4. [Organisation Name] shall not share personal information with third parties for their independent marketing purposes unless permitted by applicable law, contract, notice, and individual choice requirements.

 11.5. [Organisation Name] shall verify the identity and authority of requesting parties before disclosing personal information.

 11.6. [Organisation Name] shall maintain records of material personal information disclosures where required for operational, contractual, legal, or audit purposes.

12. **Third-Party and Subprocessor Management**

 12.1. [Organisation Name] shall conduct privacy and security due diligence before engaging third parties that process personal information on behalf of [Organisation Name] or its customers.

 12.2. Contracts with third parties that process personal information shall include appropriate privacy, confidentiality, security, breach notification, retention, disposal, audit, and subprocessing requirements.

 12.3. Third parties shall be authorised to process personal information only for documented purposes and in accordance with written instructions or contractual terms.

 12.4. [Organisation Name] shall maintain an inventory of third parties and subprocessors that process personal information.

 12.5. [Organisation Name] shall monitor third-party privacy and security posture based on risk, data sensitivity, service criticality, and contractual commitments.

 12.6. Material changes to subprocessors, processing locations, or third-party data handling practices shall be reviewed and communicated as required by customer contracts and privacy commitments.

13. **Cross-Border Transfers**

 13.1. [Organisation Name] shall identify where personal information is stored, accessed, supported, or processed across countries or regions.

 13.2. Cross-border transfers of personal information shall be reviewed by Legal or the Privacy Officer to confirm appropriate contractual, organisational, and technical safeguards.

 13.3. [Organisation Name] shall communicate relevant international transfer practices in applicable privacy notices, customer agreements, or subprocessor disclosures.

 13.4. Personnel shall not transfer personal information to unauthorised countries, systems, vendors, or affiliates outside approved business processes.

14. **Retention and Disposal**

 14.1. [Organisation Name] shall retain personal information only for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes for which it was collected, meet contractual obligations, support legitimate business needs, comply with legal requirements, or resolve disputes.

 14.2. Retention periods shall be documented in an approved retention schedule or equivalent record.

 14.3. Personal information shall be securely deleted, anonymised, returned, archived, or destroyed at the end of its retention period unless subject to a legal hold, contractual requirement, or approved exception.

 14.4. Disposal methods shall be appropriate to the media type, sensitivity of information, and risk of recovery.

 14.5. Backups containing personal information shall be protected from unauthorised access and retained according to approved backup and recovery requirements.

 14.6. The following minimum retention guidance shall apply unless superseded by law, contract, customer instruction, or approved retention schedule:

| Information Type | Typical Retention Period | Disposal Method | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Customer account and billing records | [7 years after account closure] | Secure deletion or archival purge | Finance / Customer Operations |
| Customer service data processed on behalf of customers | Per customer agreement or instruction | Return, deletion, or secure purge | Product / Customer Success |
| Website visitor analytics | [25 months] | Automated deletion or aggregation | Marketing / Product Analytics |
| Marketing contact records | Until opt-out, inactivity threshold, or [3 years] | Suppression, deletion, or anonymisation | Marketing |
| Employee personnel records | [7 years after separation] | Secure deletion or physical destruction | Human Resources |
| Recruitment records | [2 years after role closure] | Secure deletion | Human Resources |
| Security logs containing personal information | [12-24 months] | Secure deletion or log rotation | Information Security |
| Vendor contact records | Duration of relationship plus [7 years] | Secure deletion or archival purge | Procurement |

15. **Individual Rights Requests**

 15.1. [Organisation Name] shall maintain a documented process for receiving, verifying, tracking, fulfilling, denying, and closing individual privacy rights requests.
