 15.2. Available rights may include access, correction, deletion, portability, restriction, objection, consent withdrawal, marketing opt-out, or other rights required by law, contract, or organisational commitment.

 15.3. [Organisation Name] shall verify the identity and authority of the requester before disclosing, correcting, deleting, or otherwise acting on personal information.

 15.4. [Organisation Name] shall respond to individual rights requests within required timelines and shall document the basis for fulfilment, denial, extension, or partial response.

 15.5. Where [Organisation Name] processes personal information on behalf of a customer, [Organisation Name] shall refer or support requests according to the applicable customer agreement.

 15.6. [Organisation Name] shall not discriminate against individuals for exercising available privacy rights.

 15.7. The following response targets shall apply unless a stricter legal, contractual, or customer requirement applies:

| Request Type | Target Acknowledgement | Target Completion | Approval or Review Required |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Access request | 5 business days | 30 calendar days | Privacy Officer / Legal as needed |
| Correction request | 5 business days | 30 calendar days | Data Owner |
| Deletion request | 5 business days | 30 calendar days | Privacy Officer and Data Owner |
| Marketing opt-out | As soon as practicable | 10 business days | Marketing Operations |
| Consent withdrawal | 5 business days | 30 calendar days | Privacy Officer as needed |
| Customer end-user request | Per customer contract | Per customer contract | Customer Success / Privacy Officer |
| Employee privacy request | 5 business days | 30 calendar days | Human Resources / Legal |

16. **Privacy by Design and Change Management**

 16.1. [Organisation Name] shall consider privacy requirements during product design, system implementation, business process changes, data integrations, vendor onboarding, marketing campaigns, analytics initiatives, and new uses of personal information.

 16.2. New or materially changed processing activities involving personal information shall be reviewed for privacy risk before launch.

 16.3. Privacy reviews shall evaluate, as applicable, notice, consent, purpose, minimisation, access, retention, third-party sharing, security safeguards, international transfers, individual rights, and customer commitments.

 16.4. High-risk processing activities shall require documented approval from the Privacy Officer, Legal, Security, and relevant business owner before implementation.

 16.5. Product and engineering teams shall implement privacy-supporting features where required, such as data export, deletion, access controls, configurable retention, tenant separation, audit logging, consent capture, and preference management.

17. **Records of Processing and Data Inventory**

 17.1. [Organisation Name] shall maintain an inventory of systems, repositories, business processes, and third parties that process personal information.

 17.2. The data inventory shall identify, where practical, categories of personal information, purposes of processing, data sources, data owners, systems of record, recipients, retention periods, processing locations, and security classification.

 17.3. Business owners shall keep inventory information accurate and shall update it when processing activities are created, changed, transferred, or retired.

 17.4. The data inventory shall be reviewed periodically to support privacy notices, rights requests, retention, risk assessment, vendor management, and audit activities.

18. **Privacy Incidents and Breach Response**

 18.1. Personnel shall promptly report suspected or confirmed unauthorised access, disclosure, loss, misuse, alteration, destruction, or compromise of personal information through [incident reporting channel].

 18.2. [Organisation Name] shall investigate privacy incidents in coordination with Information Security, Legal, Privacy, Communications, Customer Success, Human Resources, and business owners as appropriate.

 18.3. Privacy incidents shall be assessed for affected individuals, data types, volume, likelihood of harm, containment status, contractual obligations, notification requirements, and remediation actions.

 18.4. Notifications to customers, individuals, regulators, law enforcement, or other parties shall be approved by Legal and executive leadership as appropriate.

 18.5. Incident response records shall document facts, decisions, approvals, containment actions, notifications, remediation, lessons learned, and closure.

 18.6. [Organisation Name] shall not delay internal reporting of suspected privacy incidents because details are incomplete.

19. **Training and Awareness**

 19.1. All personnel shall complete privacy and data protection training during onboarding and at least annually thereafter.

 19.2. Personnel with elevated privacy responsibilities, including Human Resources, Customer Support, Sales, Marketing, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Procurement, and Finance, shall receive role-based privacy training as appropriate.

 19.3. Training shall address appropriate handling of personal information, privacy notices, individual rights, consent and preferences, secure sharing, incident reporting, phishing and social engineering risks, data minimisation, and confidentiality.

 19.4. [Organisation Name] shall maintain training completion records and follow up on overdue training.

20. **Confidentiality and Workforce Obligations**

 20.1. Personnel shall protect personal information as confidential information.

 20.2. Personnel shall access, use, discuss, transmit, or disclose personal information only as necessary to perform assigned duties.

 20.3. Personnel shall comply with approved privacy, security, acceptable use, data classification, access control, records retention, and incident response requirements.

 20.4. Personnel shall sign confidentiality, acceptable use, employment, contractor, or equivalent agreements before receiving access to personal information.

 20.5. Personnel shall promptly report privacy concerns, suspected misuse, unauthorised disclosure, inaccurate notices, or potential policy violations.

21. **Customer Data Processing Commitments**

 21.1. Where [Organisation Name] processes personal information on behalf of customers, [Organisation Name] shall process such information only according to customer agreements, documented instructions, approved product functionality, and applicable commitments.

 21.2. [Organisation Name] shall not access customer personal information except to provide contracted services, support customers, maintain security and availability, comply with law, prevent abuse, or as otherwise authorised.

 21.3. [Organisation Name] shall maintain controls to logically separate customer data where required by product architecture and customer commitments.

 21.4. [Organisation Name] shall support customer privacy obligations, including deletion, export, access, and subprocessor transparency, as defined in applicable agreements.

 21.5. Customer personal information shall not be used for unrelated marketing, resale, or independent profiling unless explicitly authorised by contract and applicable notice requirements.

22. **Marketing, Tracking, and Communications**

 22.1. Marketing activities involving personal information shall comply with applicable notice, consent, opt-out, and preference requirements.

 22.2. [Organisation Name] shall provide a clear and functional unsubscribe or opt-out mechanism for electronic marketing communications where required.

 22.3. Cookie banners, tracking technologies, pixels, tags, analytics tools, and advertising technologies shall be reviewed and configured according to applicable privacy requirements and disclosed in the relevant notice.

 22.4. Marketing lists shall be obtained from approved sources and shall be screened against applicable opt-out, suppression, and consent records before use.

 22.5. [Organisation Name] shall not use sensitive personal information for targeted advertising or marketing without explicit approval from Legal and the Privacy Officer.

23. **Human Resources Privacy**

 23.1. [Organisation Name] shall provide employees, contractors, and job applicants with appropriate privacy notices describing workforce-related personal information processing.

 23.2. Human Resources personal information shall be used only for legitimate employment, contractor management, legal, payroll, benefits, security, compliance, performance, recruiting, and workforce administration purposes.

 23.3. Access to workforce personal information shall be restricted to authorised Human Resources, Finance, Legal, Security, IT, management, and service provider personnel with a legitimate need.

 23.4. Employee monitoring, background checks, workplace investigations, and similar activities shall be reviewed by Legal or Human Resources leadership before implementation.

24. **Privacy Risk Assessment**

 24.1. [Organisation Name] shall assess privacy risks associated with personal information processing activities on a periodic basis and when material changes occur.

 24.2. Privacy risk assessments shall consider likelihood and impact of unauthorised disclosure, misuse, excessive collection, inaccurate notices, inappropriate retention, third-party failure, individual harm, customer impact, and contractual non-compliance.

 24.3. Identified privacy risks shall be documented, assigned an owner, prioritised, and remediated or accepted through approved risk management processes.

 24.4. High-risk privacy issues shall be reported to appropriate leadership.

25. **Documentation and Evidence**

 25.1. [Organisation Name] shall retain documentation and evidence demonstrating operation of privacy controls, including notices, approvals, consent records, rights request logs, training records, incident records, vendor reviews, data inventories, retention records, and privacy review outputs.

 25.2. Privacy records shall be protected against unauthorised modification or deletion.

 25.3. Evidence shall be retained for the period required by audit, legal, contractual, and business requirements.

26. **Prohibited Activities**

 26.1. Personnel shall not collect personal information without a valid business purpose and required notice or approval.

 26.2. Personnel shall not disclose personal information to unauthorised individuals, vendors, customers, colleagues, or public channels.

 26.3. Personnel shall not copy personal information into unauthorised tools, unmanaged artificial intelligence services, personal accounts, personal devices, or unapproved storage locations.

 26.4. Personnel shall not override privacy preferences, suppressions, or consent records without documented approval.

 26.5. Personnel shall not retain personal information beyond approved retention periods for convenience.

 26.6. Personnel shall not use customer personal information for personal research, curiosity, competitive analysis, unrelated analytics, or unauthorised product development.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors / Executive Leadership | Provide oversight of privacy risk, approve material privacy program direction, support resources for privacy compliance, and review significant privacy issues where escalated. |
| Privacy Officer / Data Protection Officer | Own the privacy program; maintain this policy; oversee privacy notices, rights requests, privacy reviews, data inventory, risk assessments, privacy training, and privacy monitoring; advise business teams on privacy requirements. |
| Legal Counsel | Interpret legal and contractual privacy obligations; review privacy notices, agreements, incidents, disclosures, international transfers, high-risk processing, and regulatory communications. |
| Chief Information Security Officer / Security Lead | Implement and monitor security safeguards protecting personal information; support incident response, access control, encryption, logging, vulnerability management, and vendor security review. |
| Data Owners / Business Process Owners | Identify personal information processed in their areas; define business purposes; maintain accurate data inventory entries; approve access; support retention, deletion, rights requests, and privacy reviews. |
| Product and Engineering Teams | Embed privacy requirements into product design, development, testing, release, logging, data retention, data export, deletion, and access management capabilities. |
| Information Technology | Manage systems and infrastructure containing personal information; enforce approved access, device, backup, retention, and disposal controls. |
| Human Resources | Protect workforce personal information; provide employee and applicant notices; manage HR privacy requests; ensure workforce confidentiality and training requirements are completed. |
| Marketing | Manage marketing consents, preferences, suppression lists, website tracking disclosures, campaign data use, and compliant marketing communications. |
| Sales and Customer Success | Ensure customer privacy commitments are understood; route privacy inquiries appropriately; avoid unauthorised statements about privacy practices; support customer requests according to contract. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Ensure vendors processing personal information are reviewed, approved, contracted, monitored, and offboarded according to privacy and security requirements. |
| Incident Response Team | Investigate and respond to privacy incidents; coordinate containment, assessment, notification, remediation, and documentation. |
| Managers | Ensure team members understand and follow privacy requirements; approve access only where needed; escalate privacy concerns and suspected violations. |
| All Personnel | Comply with this policy; protect personal information; complete training; report suspected privacy incidents; use approved systems and processes only. |
| Internal Audit / Compliance | Independently assess privacy program design and operating effectiveness; report findings; track remediation of issues. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

[Organisation Name] shall monitor compliance with this policy through a combination of governance reviews, technical controls, operational metrics, audits, management oversight, and exception tracking.

Monitoring activities shall include, as appropriate:

- Review of privacy notices for accuracy and completeness.
- Review of personal information inventories and processing records.
- Testing of individual rights request handling.
- Review of consent and preference management records.
- Access reviews for systems containing personal information.
- Vendor and subprocessor monitoring.
- Review of privacy training completion.
- Review of privacy incident response records.
- Assessment of retention and disposal activities.
- Review of privacy risk assessments and remediation plans.
- Monitoring of marketing compliance, including opt-out and suppression processes.
- Product and system change reviews for privacy impact.

Key privacy compliance activities shall be performed according to the following minimum schedule unless a higher frequency is required by risk, contract, or law:

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Privacy policy review | Annually | Privacy Officer | Approved policy version history |
| Public privacy notice review | At least annually and before material changes | Privacy Officer / Legal | Notice approval record and publication evidence |
| Data inventory review | At least annually | Data Owners / Privacy Officer | Updated inventory record |
| Individual rights request log review | Quarterly | Privacy Officer | Request log and closure metrics |
| Privacy training completion review | Quarterly | Privacy Officer / HR | Training completion report |
| Vendor privacy review | At onboarding and periodically based on risk | Procurement / Privacy Officer | Due diligence and contract records |
| Access review for high-risk systems | At least quarterly | System Owners | Access review evidence |
| Retention compliance review | At least annually | Data Owners / Records Owner | Retention review and deletion evidence |
| Marketing preference review | Quarterly | Marketing Operations | Suppression and preference testing results |
| Privacy incident trend review | Quarterly | Privacy Officer / Security Lead | Incident metrics and lessons learned |
| Privacy risk assessment | At least annually and upon material change | Privacy Officer / Risk Owner | Risk assessment and remediation plan |

Policy violations may result in corrective action, including access removal, mandatory retraining, disciplinary action up to and including termination, contract termination, legal action, or notification to affected customers, individuals, regulators, or law enforcement where appropriate.

Suspected violations shall be reported to [privacy reporting email], [security reporting channel], [ethics hotline], or a manager. [Organisation Name] shall prohibit retaliation against individuals who report privacy concerns in good faith.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business need, risk assessment, compensating control, and approval by the appropriate authority.

Exception requests shall include:

- Description of the requirement for which an exception is requested.
- Business justification.
- Personal information affected.
- Systems, processes, vendors, or teams affected.
- Risk assessment and potential impact to individuals, customers, and [Organisation Name].
- Proposed compensating controls.
- Requested duration.
- Remediation plan or path to compliance.
- Approval from the Data Owner, Privacy Officer, Security Lead, and Legal where applicable.

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed [12 months] unless renewed through a formal review. Permanent exceptions are not permitted unless incorporated into an approved policy revision.

The Privacy Officer shall maintain an exceptions register.

| Exception Field | Required Content |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | Unique tracking number |
| Requester | Name, role, department |
| Policy Requirement | Requirement affected |
| Business Justification | Reason compliance is not currently feasible |
| Data Involved | Categories and sensitivity of personal information |
| Risk Rating | Low, medium, high, or critical |
| Compensating Controls | Safeguards implemented during exception period |
| Approvers | Required approval names and dates |
| Expiration Date | Date exception ends |
| Remediation Plan | Actions required to return to compliance |
| Status | Open, approved, rejected, expired, or closed |

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed or closed with evidence of remediation.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever material changes occur to [Organisation Name]’s business operations, products, systems, processing activities, privacy commitments, customer requirements, legal obligations, risk environment, or organisational structure.

The Privacy Officer shall coordinate the review with Legal, Information Security, Product, Human Resources, Marketing, Procurement, Customer Success, and other relevant stakeholders.

Policy updates shall be approved by [approval authority] before publication. Material updates shall be communicated to affected personnel and, where applicable, customers, individuals, vendors, or other stakeholders.

Version history shall be maintained as follows:

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Approved By |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Initial release | [Name / Role] |

SOC2-017.title: Processing Integrity Policy
SOC2-017.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-PI-001] | 1.0 | [Head of Engineering / Head of Operations] | [Effective Date] | SOC 2 | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Processing Integrity Policy is to establish mandatory requirements to ensure that systems and services process data and transactions completely, accurately, timely, and in accordance with authorised business rules and customer commitments.

This Policy supports the organisation’s SOC 2 programme by defining governance expectations for processing controls across application workflows, integrations, batch jobs, data pipelines, operational procedures, and error handling. It is intended to reduce the risk of incomplete, inaccurate, duplicated, unauthorised, delayed, or otherwise inappropriate processing of customer, operational, and business-critical information.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All production systems, applications, platforms, databases, data pipelines, integrations, APIs, automated workflows, and batch processing activities that process customer data or business-critical operational data.
- All personnel, contractors, temporary workers, service providers, and third parties who design, develop, operate, support, monitor, or manage in-scope processing activities.
- All stages of processing, including data input, validation, transformation, calculation, transmission, storage, output, reporting, reconciliation, correction, and retention.
- Processing activities performed by third-party service providers where those activities support the organisation’s customer commitments or internal control environment.
- Changes to processing logic, business rules, system configurations, interface mappings, scheduled jobs, automation scripts, and data transformation rules.

This Policy does not replace detailed operational procedures, system design standards, data governance standards, incident response procedures, change management procedures, or customer contractual requirements. Where requirements conflict, the more restrictive requirement shall apply unless an approved exception has been granted.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall define and maintain documented processing integrity requirements for in-scope systems, including expectations for completeness, accuracy, timeliness, validity, authorisation, and traceability.

2. In-scope processing activities shall be designed to operate in accordance with approved business rules, customer commitments, product specifications, contractual obligations, and documented operational requirements.

3. Processing logic, calculation rules, validation rules, data mappings, workflow conditions, and system-generated outputs shall be documented at a level sufficient to support implementation, testing, troubleshooting, and audit review.

4. Data accepted into in-scope systems shall be subject to appropriate input validation controls to confirm that required fields, permitted formats, value ranges, data types, source authenticity, and business rule conditions are met before processing proceeds.

5. Systems shall reject, quarantine, flag, or route invalid, incomplete, unauthorised, duplicate, or inconsistent inputs for review in accordance with documented operational procedures.

6. Data received from external systems, customers, vendors, APIs, file transfers, or manual uploads shall be subject to validation proportionate to the sensitivity, volume, business impact, and risk of the processing activity.

7. Automated processing shall include appropriate controls to prevent, detect, and correct duplicate processing, missing records, partial processing, sequence errors, calculation errors, and unauthorised manipulation of processing logic.

8. Where processing depends on scheduled jobs, queues, pipelines, event streams, or batch routines, the organisation shall implement monitoring to confirm that processing completes successfully and within expected timeframes.

9. Critical processing jobs shall have defined success criteria, expected frequency, dependency requirements, error conditions, and escalation paths.

10. The organisation shall maintain procedures to identify and respond to failed, delayed, incomplete, or abnormal processing events in a timely manner.

11. Processing errors shall be logged, investigated, corrected, and tracked through resolution in accordance with their severity and business impact.

12. Error correction activities shall preserve the integrity of data and shall be authorised, tested where appropriate, documented, and traceable to the underlying issue.

13. Manual corrections to production data shall be restricted to authorised personnel, performed only through approved methods, and supported by a documented business justification and approval record.

14. Direct changes to production data outside approved application workflows shall be prohibited unless explicitly authorised through an approved operational support, incident, or emergency change process.

15. Processing outputs, including reports, customer-facing data, invoices, statements, notifications, exports, dashboards, and downstream data feeds, shall be subject to controls that support completeness, accuracy, and appropriate distribution.

16. Reconciliations shall be performed for processing activities where there is material risk of lost, duplicated, corrupted, incomplete, or mismatched data between systems or process stages.

17. Reconciliation frequency shall be based on processing criticality, data sensitivity, transaction volume, customer impact, financial impact, and operational risk.

18. Reconciliation differences shall be investigated, resolved, and retained as evidence in accordance with applicable operational procedures and record retention requirements.

19. Interfaces and integrations between systems shall include controls to confirm that data transmitted is complete, accurate, appropriately formatted, protected against unauthorised alteration, and received by the intended destination.

20. Data transformations, calculations, aggregations, and derivations shall be traceable to source data and approved business logic where practical and relevant to the processing risk.

21. Changes to processing logic, system configurations, automation scripts, data mappings, validation rules, reconciliation rules, and scheduled processing routines shall follow the organisation’s approved change management process.

22. Changes that may materially affect processing integrity shall be assessed for risk, tested prior to deployment, approved by authorised personnel, and supported by rollback or remediation plans where appropriate.

23. Emergency changes affecting processing activities shall be documented after implementation, reviewed for appropriateness, and validated to confirm that processing integrity was not adversely affected.

24. The organisation shall segregate duties where practical so that no individual can independently develop, approve, deploy, and validate material changes to critical processing activities without oversight.

25. Access to configure, operate, override, or correct in-scope processing activities shall be limited to authorised users based on job responsibilities and the principle of least privilege.

26. Privileged access that can alter processing outcomes, bypass validations, modify processing rules, or update production data shall be controlled, monitored, and periodically reviewed.

27. The organisation shall maintain logging and audit trails for critical processing activities sufficient to support issue investigation, operational monitoring, security review, and audit evidence requirements.

28. Logs for in-scope processing activities shall capture relevant information such as processing date and time, user or system identity, transaction identifiers, input source, processing status, error messages, correction activity, and approval references where applicable.

29. Logs and processing records shall be protected against unauthorised modification and retained in accordance with approved retention requirements.

30. Processing incidents that may affect customers, financial reporting, contractual commitments, regulatory obligations, data quality, or service availability shall be escalated through the incident management process.

31. Customer-impacting processing errors shall be assessed for notification obligations, contractual service commitments, corrective actions, and customer support requirements.

32. The organisation shall establish recovery and reprocessing procedures for critical processing activities to address failed jobs, corrupted data, interrupted workflows, incomplete transactions, and unavailable dependencies.

33. Reprocessing activities shall be controlled to prevent duplication, omission, unauthorised alteration, or inconsistent results.

34. Production data used for testing, troubleshooting, analysis, or reconciliation shall be handled in accordance with the organisation’s data protection, privacy, access control, and confidentiality requirements.

35. Where synthetic or anonymised test data can reasonably be used, it shall be preferred over production data for testing processing changes.

36. In-scope processing activities performed by third-party service providers shall be subject to appropriate vendor risk management, contractual requirements, performance oversight, and review of relevant assurance information.

37. The organisation shall identify key processing dependencies, including upstream data sources, downstream consumers, third-party services, infrastructure components, job schedulers, queues, APIs, and data storage platforms.

38. Processing dependencies shall be monitored and managed to reduce the risk of unplanned interruption, delayed processing, or inaccurate outputs.

39. Operational teams shall maintain runbooks or equivalent documentation for critical processing activities, including normal processing steps, expected outcomes, known failure modes, escalation contacts, and recovery actions.

40. Evidence of processing integrity controls shall be retained in a complete and auditable manner, including approvals, test results, monitoring records, exception reports, reconciliation records, error logs, incident records, and corrective action documentation.

41. Metrics and alerts shall be established for critical processing activities where appropriate, including job success rates, processing latency, error rates, rejected records, reconciliation breaks, retry volumes, and unresolved exceptions.

42. Processing integrity controls shall be reviewed periodically to confirm that they remain appropriate to current system architecture, business processes, customer commitments, transaction volumes, and risk levels.

43. Personnel responsible for designing, operating, monitoring, or supporting in-scope processing activities shall receive appropriate training or guidance on processing integrity requirements and relevant procedures.

44. The organisation shall maintain an inventory of in-scope systems and critical processing activities sufficient to support ownership, risk assessment, control operation, monitoring, and audit readiness.

45. Processing integrity risks shall be considered during system design, product development, data migration, integration onboarding, process automation, and material business process changes.

46. Data migrations, bulk uploads, backfills, and mass updates shall be planned, validated, approved, monitored, and reconciled to confirm completeness and accuracy.

47. The organisation shall maintain defined severity levels and target response expectations for processing failures and data quality issues based on customer impact, operational impact, financial impact, and urgency.

48. Processing activities shall not be knowingly operated in a manner that materially compromises completeness, accuracy, timeliness, or validity unless an approved risk-based exception or incident response decision is documented.

49. Control failures, recurring processing defects, or material data quality issues shall be subject to root cause analysis and corrective action tracking.

50. The organisation shall ensure that processing integrity requirements are considered before launching new services, major features, integrations, or customer-facing workflows.

The following minimum monitoring and evidence expectations apply unless a stricter system-specific requirement has been approved:

| Processing Area | Minimum Control Expectation | Minimum Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Input validation | Required fields, formats, ranges, source checks, and business rules validated before processing | Validation rules, rejected record logs, error reports |
| Scheduled jobs and batch processing | Job completion, failures, delays, and retries monitored | Scheduler logs, alerts, job status reports |
| Data pipelines and integrations | Transfer completeness, transformation accuracy, and destination receipt verified | Pipeline logs, reconciliation reports, interface monitoring records |
| Calculations and transformations | Business logic documented, tested, and approved before production use | Requirements, test results, approval records |
| Manual corrections | Corrections authorised, justified, traceable, and independently reviewed where material | Ticket records, approval evidence, audit trail |
| Reconciliations | Differences identified, investigated, resolved, and retained | Reconciliation worksheets, exception logs, resolution evidence |
| Processing errors | Errors triaged, assigned, resolved, and reviewed for recurrence | Incident or ticket records, root cause analysis, corrective actions |
| Customer-impacting outputs | Outputs reviewed or controlled for completeness, accuracy, and appropriate delivery | Report controls, delivery logs, review evidence |

Severity and target handling expectations for processing integrity events shall be defined and maintained as follows:

| Severity | Description | Examples | Target Initial Response | Escalation Requirement |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Critical | Material customer, financial, contractual, regulatory, or service impact; widespread or unrecoverable processing failure | Incorrect customer balances, failed billing run, mass data corruption, lost transaction set | [1 hour] | Executive, Legal, Security, Customer Support, and relevant business owner |
| High | Significant processing defect with limited scope or recoverable impact | Delayed critical batch job, recurring integration failure, inaccurate customer-facing report for subset of customers | [4 hours] | System owner, business owner, Engineering or Operations leadership |
| Medium | Processing issue affecting internal operations or limited non-critical outputs | Reconciliation break, failed non-critical job, isolated duplicate record | [1 business day] | System owner and operational process owner |
| Low | Minor processing anomaly with no material impact | Non-urgent validation warning, cosmetic report discrepancy, isolated rejected record with known cause | [3 business days] | Operational queue or service owner |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Management | Approves organisational commitment to processing integrity, ensures adequate resources, and supports enforcement of this Policy. |
| Policy Owner | Maintains this Policy, coordinates periodic review, monitors alignment with business needs, and ensures policy updates are communicated. |
| System Owners | Define processing requirements, identify critical processing activities, approve business rules, ensure appropriate controls are implemented, and retain evidence of control operation. |
| Process Owners | Define operational workflows, reconciliation needs, exception handling requirements, timeliness expectations, and escalation paths for business processes. |
| Engineering and Development Teams | Design, build, test, document, and maintain processing logic, validation rules, automation, integrations, and recovery capabilities in accordance with this Policy. |
| Operations and Support Teams | Monitor processing activities, respond to errors and exceptions, perform reconciliations, execute approved corrections, and maintain operational evidence. |
| Data Owners | Define data quality expectations, approve material data transformations, support reconciliation requirements, and review data integrity issues affecting their domains. |
| Information Security | Advises on access control, logging, monitoring, secure configuration, incident response, and protection of processing records. |
| Compliance / GRC | Coordinates audit readiness, reviews control evidence, tracks policy compliance, and supports management reporting on processing integrity control performance. |
| Change Approvers | Review and approve changes that may affect processing integrity, including risk, testing, rollback, and validation evidence. |
| Third-Party Risk Management / Vendor Management | Ensures relevant service providers are assessed, contracted, monitored, and reviewed for processing commitments that affect in-scope services. |
| Internal Audit or Independent Review Function | Performs independent review of processing integrity controls, evidence, and remediation activities as assigned. |
| All Personnel | Follow approved procedures, report processing errors or suspected control failures, protect processing records, and avoid unauthorised changes to data or processing logic. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all in-scope personnel, systems, and processing activities.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through a combination of automated monitoring, management review, operational evidence review, access reviews, change review, incident analysis, reconciliation review, and periodic control testing.

At a minimum, the following compliance activities shall be performed:

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Role | Expected Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review inventory of critical processing activities | Quarterly | System Owners / GRC | Updated inventory, review record |
| Review failed, delayed, or abnormal processing events | Monthly | Operations / System Owners | Exception report, ticket summary, remediation status |
| Review reconciliation exceptions and aged differences | Monthly | Process Owners / Data Owners | Reconciliation reports, exception ageing, resolution evidence |
| Review changes affecting processing logic or data transformation | Per change and quarterly sample review | Change Approvers / GRC | Change records, approvals, test evidence |
| Review privileged access affecting processing outcomes | Quarterly | System Owners / Information Security | Access review certification, remediation evidence |
| Review third-party processing performance and exceptions | At least annually, or per contract | Vendor Management / System Owners | Vendor review records, assurance reports, issue tracking |
| Test key processing integrity controls | At least annually | GRC / Internal Audit | Test plans, samples, results, remediation actions |
| Review processing incidents and root causes | Quarterly | Operations / Engineering / GRC | Incident records, root cause analysis, corrective action tracking |
| Review this Policy and supporting procedures | Annually | Policy Owner | Review and approval record |

Non-compliance may result in corrective action, including but not limited to:

- Required remediation plans and management tracking.
- Temporary suspension of access or elevated privileges.
- Additional monitoring or approval requirements.
- Mandatory retraining.
- Escalation to senior management.
- Disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policy.
- Contractual remedies for third-party service providers.
- Risk acceptance review where immediate remediation is not practical.

Material non-compliance, control failures, or recurring processing integrity issues shall be reported to appropriate management and tracked to resolution. Where customer, legal, contractual, financial, or regulatory impacts are suspected, Legal, Compliance, Security, and relevant business leadership shall be consulted promptly.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business justification, risk assessment, compensating control assessment, defined expiration date, and approval by appropriate authority.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Name, role, department, and contact information of the individual requesting the exception |
| System or Process | In-scope system, workflow, integration, job, report, or processing activity affected |
| Policy Requirement | Specific requirement that cannot be met |
| Business Justification | Reason the exception is needed and why standard compliance is not practical |
| Risk Assessment | Potential impact to completeness, accuracy, timeliness, validity, authorisation, customers, operations, contracts, or reporting |
| Compensating Controls | Alternative controls that reduce risk during the exception period |
| Duration | Requested start date and expiration date |
| Remediation Plan | Actions and timeline to return to compliance |
| Approval | Required approvals based on risk and business impact |

Exceptions shall not be open-ended. Approved exceptions shall be reviewed at least quarterly and upon material change to the affected system, process, risk level, or business requirement.

High-risk exceptions shall require approval from the Policy Owner, relevant business owner, system owner, and an appropriate risk or executive authority. Exceptions that may materially affect customers, contractual commitments, regulated data, or financial outcomes shall also be reviewed by Legal, Compliance, or other relevant stakeholders before approval.

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed through the approved exception process before expiration.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect processing integrity requirements, including:

- Launch of new products, services, platforms, or customer-facing workflows.
- Material changes to system architecture, data flows, integrations, or automation.
- Significant changes to business rules, calculations, reporting, or customer commitments.
- Major incidents involving processing failures, data corruption, inaccurate outputs, or delayed processing.
- Changes to legal, contractual, regulatory, audit, or customer requirements.
- Results from audits, risk assessments, control testing, incidents, or management reviews indicating the Policy is no longer effective.

The Policy Owner shall coordinate review with relevant stakeholders, including Engineering, Operations, Product, Data, Information Security, Compliance, Legal, and business process owners as appropriate.

Updates to this Policy shall be approved by [Approving Authority] before publication. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s record retention requirements.

The current approved version of this Policy shall be made available to all relevant personnel. Material changes shall be communicated to affected teams, and additional training or guidance shall be provided where necessary.

SOC2-018.title: HR Policies (Hiring, Onboarding, Termination)
SOC2-018.content:
| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [HR-POL-001] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Human Resources |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | SOC 2 |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

This policy establishes mandatory requirements for hiring, onboarding, employment changes, and termination practices to ensure that personnel are qualified, appropriately vetted, informed of their responsibilities, granted access based on business need, and removed from systems and facilities in a timely manner when employment or engagement ends.

The policy supports the organisation’s commitment to trustworthy operations by ensuring people-related controls are consistently applied throughout the workforce lifecycle.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All employees, contractors, temporary staff, interns, consultants, and other workforce members who perform work for or on behalf of [Organisation Name].
- All hiring, onboarding, role transfer, promotion, leave of absence, disciplinary, and termination activities.
- All departments involved in workforce management, including Human Resources, Legal, Information Security, Information Technology, Finance, Facilities, department managers, and executive leadership.
- All systems, applications, facilities, records, equipment, accounts, credentials, and information assets made available to workforce members.

This policy applies regardless of employment type, work location, or whether work is performed remotely, in-office, or at a customer or third-party location.

## Policy Statements

1. **Workforce Planning and Role Definition**

 1.1. The organisation shall define and approve each role before recruitment begins.

 1.2. Each role shall have a documented job description that includes, at minimum:

 - Job title.
 - Department or business function.
 - Reporting line.
 - Key responsibilities.
 - Required qualifications, experience, or certifications.
 - Security, privacy, compliance, or customer-facing responsibilities, where applicable.
 - Expected access to systems, data, facilities, or privileged functions.
 - Employment or engagement type.

 1.3. Hiring managers shall confirm that the role is necessary, budgeted, and authorised prior to initiating recruitment.

 1.4. Roles involving access to sensitive information, production systems, customer environments, financial systems, administrative privileges, or regulated data shall be identified as sensitive roles.

 1.5. Sensitive roles shall be subject to enhanced screening, role-specific training, and access approval requirements.

2. **Equal Opportunity and Fair Hiring**

 2.1. The organisation shall conduct hiring in a fair, consistent, and non-discriminatory manner.

 2.2. Employment decisions shall be based on job-related qualifications, skills, experience, performance, and legitimate business requirements.

 2.3. Interviewers and hiring managers shall not make selection decisions based on protected characteristics, personal relationships, conflicts of interest, or other inappropriate factors.

 2.4. Human Resources shall maintain standard hiring practices to promote consistency across departments and locations.

 2.5. Hiring records shall be retained in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory, and internal retention requirements.

3. **Recruitment Approval and Candidate Selection**

 3.1. New hires and replacement hires shall be approved by authorised management before an offer is made.

 3.2. Recruitment activities shall be coordinated through Human Resources or an approved recruiting process.

 3.3. Candidates shall be evaluated using job-related criteria.

 3.4. Hiring managers shall document the basis for candidate selection.

 3.5. Where recruitment agencies or third-party hiring platforms are used, they shall be approved in accordance with the organisation’s vendor management and privacy requirements.

4. **Employment Eligibility and Right to Work**

 4.1. The organisation shall verify employment eligibility and right to work before employment begins or within the legally permitted timeframe.

 4.2. Workforce members shall provide accurate and complete information required for employment verification, payroll, tax, and legal compliance purposes.

 4.3. Human Resources shall retain evidence of employment eligibility verification in accordance with applicable retention requirements.

 4.4. Workforce members shall not begin work or receive access to organisation systems until required employment eligibility checks have been completed or formally authorised under an approved exception.

5. **Background Screening**

 5.1. Background screening shall be completed for workforce members before they are granted access to organisation systems, customer data, production environments, or confidential information, unless an approved exception is documented.

 5.2. Background checks shall be conducted in accordance with applicable law, local employment requirements, candidate consent requirements, and privacy obligations.

 5.3. The level of background screening shall be proportionate to the nature of the role, location, and access required.

 5.4. Background screening for employees shall include, where legally permissible and role-appropriate:

 - Identity verification.
 - Employment history verification.
 - Education or credential verification, where required for the role.
 - Criminal history screening, where legally permitted.
 - Professional licence or certification verification, where applicable.
 - Reference checks, where appropriate.

 5.5. Background screening for contractors and consultants shall be completed either by [Organisation Name] or by the contracting organisation under written agreement.

 5.6. Sensitive roles shall be subject to enhanced screening where permitted by law and justified by business risk.

 5.7. Human Resources shall review background screening results and determine employment eligibility in consultation with Legal when required.

 5.8. Adverse results shall be handled confidentially, fairly, and in accordance with applicable legal requirements.

 5.9. Workforce members shall not be permitted to bypass background screening requirements due to urgency, seniority, or business pressure without documented approval.

6. **Employment Agreements and Confidentiality Obligations**

 6.1. Workforce members shall sign an employment agreement, contractor agreement, offer letter, statement of work, or equivalent written agreement before beginning work.

 6.2. Workforce members shall sign confidentiality, non-disclosure, intellectual property, acceptable use, and security acknowledgement documents as applicable to their role.

 6.3. Agreements shall clearly communicate the workforce member’s obligations to protect organisation, customer, employee, and third-party information.

 6.4. Workforce members shall agree to comply with applicable organisation policies as a condition of employment or engagement.

 6.5. Contractors, consultants, and third-party personnel shall be bound by contractual terms that impose confidentiality, security, privacy, and acceptable use obligations consistent with organisation requirements.

7. **Onboarding Requirements**

 7.1. All workforce members shall complete an approved onboarding process before being considered fully active.

 7.2. Onboarding shall be coordinated by Human Resources and supported by Information Technology, Information Security, Facilities, Finance, Legal, and the hiring manager as applicable.

 7.3. The onboarding process shall include, at minimum:

 - Verification that required hiring approvals are complete.
 - Confirmation of completed background screening or approved exception.
 - Execution of required employment or engagement agreements.
 - Completion of payroll, tax, benefits, and administrative setup, where applicable.
 - Assignment of a manager and department.
 - Provision of required equipment.
 - Setup of approved user accounts and access.
 - Delivery of required security, privacy, compliance, and role-specific training.
 - Acknowledgement of required policies.
 - Communication of job responsibilities, performance expectations, and reporting lines.

 7.4. Workforce members shall not receive access to systems, applications, facilities, customer data, production environments, or confidential information until onboarding prerequisites for the role have been satisfied.

 7.5. Hiring managers shall ensure that new workforce members understand their role responsibilities, required conduct, escalation paths, and security obligations.

 7.6. Onboarding tasks shall be tracked to completion using [HRIS/System of Record] or another approved tracking mechanism.

8. **Access Provisioning During Onboarding**

 8.1. Access for new workforce members shall be requested, approved, provisioned, and documented in accordance with the organisation’s access management requirements.

 8.2. Access shall be granted based on least privilege, business need, role responsibilities, and employment status.

 8.3. Managers shall approve access requests before access is provisioned.

 8.4. Privileged access, access to production environments, access to customer data, and access to sensitive systems shall require additional approval by the system owner or other authorised approver.

 8.5. Generic, shared, or unmanaged accounts shall not be assigned to new workforce members unless specifically approved for a documented business need and protected by compensating controls.

 8.6. Access provisioning shall be completed only by authorised personnel or approved automated workflows.

 8.7. Access granted during onboarding shall be documented and retained for audit and review purposes.

9. **Required Policy Acknowledgements**

 9.1. Workforce members shall acknowledge required policies before or during onboarding and at least annually thereafter.

 9.2. Required acknowledgements shall include, as applicable:

 - Code of Conduct.
 - Information Security Policy.
 - Acceptable Use Policy.
 - Confidentiality or Non-Disclosure Agreement.
 - Data Protection and Privacy Policy.
 - Remote Work Policy.
 - Incident Reporting Policy.
 - Anti-Harassment and Non-Discrimination Policy.
 - Conflict of Interest Policy.
 - Any role-specific policies required by the organisation.

 9.3. Policy acknowledgement records shall be retained in [HRIS/System of Record] or another approved repository.

 9.4. Workforce members who fail to acknowledge required policies within the defined timeframe shall be escalated to their manager and Human Resources.

10. **Security, Privacy, and Compliance Training**

 10.1. Workforce members shall complete required security, privacy, and compliance training as part of onboarding.

 10.2. Workforce members shall complete recurring training at least annually.

 10.3. Workforce members in sensitive roles shall complete additional role-specific training before performing sensitive duties, where required.

 10.4. Training shall cover, at minimum:

 - Protection of confidential and customer information.
 - Acceptable use of organisation systems.
 - Password and authentication requirements.
 - Phishing and social engineering awareness.
 - Incident and suspected breach reporting.
 - Secure handling of data.
 - Privacy responsibilities.
 - Physical and remote work security.
 - Reporting of conflicts of interest, misconduct, or policy violations.

 10.5. Training completion shall be tracked and reported to management.

 10.6. Workforce members who fail to complete required training by the due date shall be subject to escalation, access restrictions, or disciplinary action as appropriate.

11. **Probationary Period and Initial Performance Expectations**

 11.1. Where applicable, workforce members shall be subject to a probationary or introductory period in accordance with employment agreements and local law.

 11.2. Managers shall set clear initial performance, conduct, and security expectations for new workforce members.

 11.3. Managers shall provide timely feedback during the initial employment period.

 11.4. Concerns regarding performance, conduct, policy adherence, or suitability for continued employment shall be escalated to Human Resources promptly.

12. **Workforce Records Management**

 12.1. Human Resources shall maintain accurate and complete workforce records.

 12.2. Workforce records shall include, as applicable:

 - Job application and recruiting records.
 - Offer letters or engagement agreements.
 - Background screening status and results handling records.
 - Employment eligibility documentation.
 - Policy acknowledgements.
 - Training records.
 - Role and department information.
 - Compensation and benefits records.
 - Performance and disciplinary records.
 - Employment status changes.
 - Termination documentation.

 12.3. Workforce records shall be stored securely and accessible only to authorised personnel with a legitimate business need.

 12.4. Workforce records shall be retained and disposed of in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements and applicable law.

 12.5. Sensitive personnel information shall be protected from unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.

13. **Employment Status and Role Changes**

 13.1. Human Resources shall maintain current records of workforce member status, including active, inactive, leave, suspended, transferred, terminated, contractor, or temporary status.

 13.2. Managers shall notify Human Resources promptly of role changes, department transfers, promotions, demotions, reporting line changes, location changes, contract end dates, and leave status changes.

 13.3. Access rights shall be reviewed and adjusted when a workforce member changes role, department, location, manager, employment type, or business responsibilities.

 13.4. Access no longer required for the new role shall be removed promptly.

 13.5. Sensitive role changes shall not become effective until required approvals, training, and access reviews are completed.

 13.6. Human Resources shall notify Information Technology, Information Security, Facilities, Finance, and other relevant functions of employment status changes that require account, facility, payroll, asset, or access updates.

14. **Leave of Absence and Suspension**

 14.1. Human Resources shall document approved leaves of absence and suspensions.

 14.2. Managers shall notify Human Resources and Information Technology of workforce members going on extended leave, administrative leave, or suspension.

 14.3. Access shall be reviewed and may be temporarily disabled or restricted during extended leave, suspension, or other periods of inactivity based on business need and risk.

 14.4. Workforce members on suspension or involuntary leave shall have access disabled or restricted as directed by Human Resources, Legal, or management.

 14.5. Access shall be restored only after Human Resources confirms the workforce member’s return and the manager confirms business need.

15. **Conduct and Professional Responsibilities**

 15.1. Workforce members shall conduct themselves professionally, ethically, and in accordance with organisation policies.

 15.2. Workforce members shall protect organisation assets, customer data, confidential information, intellectual property, and personal information.

 15.3. Workforce members shall report suspected policy violations, security incidents, privacy incidents, conflicts of interest, harassment, discrimination, fraud, or unethical conduct through approved reporting channels.

 15.4. Retaliation against any person who reports concerns in good faith shall be prohibited.

 15.5. Managers shall model expected behaviour and reinforce compliance with policies and security responsibilities.

16. **Performance Management and Disciplinary Action**

 16.1. Managers shall address performance, conduct, and policy compliance concerns in a timely and documented manner.

 16.2. Disciplinary action shall be proportionate to the nature and severity of the issue, prior conduct, business impact, legal requirements, and risk to the organisation.

 16.3. Human Resources shall be consulted before formal disciplinary action is taken.

 16.4. Disciplinary actions may include coaching, written warning, access restriction, suspension, termination, legal action, or other appropriate measures.

 16.5. Security or privacy violations shall be escalated to Information Security, Privacy, Legal, or executive management as appropriate.

17. **Termination Types and Approval**

 17.1. Terminations shall be classified and managed according to type, including voluntary resignation, involuntary termination, contract end, retirement, reduction in force, abandonment, or death.

 17.2. Human Resources shall coordinate termination activities and ensure appropriate approvals are obtained.

 17.3. Involuntary terminations shall be reviewed with Legal or authorised leadership before execution when required.

 17.4. Managers shall notify Human Resources immediately when they become aware of a resignation, intended termination, contract end, or employment status change.

 17.5. Contractor end dates shall be tracked and reviewed to ensure access does not remain active after engagement ends.

18. **Termination Notification and Coordination**

 18.1. Human Resources shall notify Information Technology, Information Security, Facilities, Finance, Legal, and relevant managers of terminations in time to complete offboarding activities.

 18.2. Termination notifications shall include, at minimum:

 - Workforce member name.
 - Employee or contractor identifier.
 - Manager.
 - Department.
 - Termination type.
 - Last working day.
 - Effective termination date and time.
 - Required access removal timing.
 - Equipment return requirements.
 - Any legal hold or investigation requirements.
 - Any special risk considerations.

 18.3. Termination notifications shall be handled confidentially and disclosed only to personnel with a business need to know.

 18.4. High-risk or involuntary terminations shall be coordinated in advance to ensure access is removed at or before the time of notification.

19. **Access Removal During Termination**

 19.1. Logical access shall be disabled or removed promptly upon termination or when access is no longer required.

 19.2. For involuntary terminations, high-risk terminations, or terminations involving personnel with privileged access, access shall be disabled at or before the termination notification.

 19.3. For voluntary terminations, access shall be removed no later than the workforce member’s final working day unless an approved business need requires earlier removal.

 19.4. Access removal shall include, as applicable:

 - Identity provider and single sign-on accounts.
 - Email and collaboration tools.
 - Virtual private network access.
 - Cloud platforms.
 - Production systems.
 - Source code repositories.
 - Customer support tools.
 - Administrative and privileged accounts.
 - Financial systems.
 - Human Resources systems.
 - Ticketing systems.
 - Physical access badges and facility access.
 - Mobile device management enrolment.
 - Shared folders and file repositories.
 - Third-party applications and vendor portals.

 19.5. Managers and system owners shall assist Information Technology and Information Security in identifying all access requiring removal.

 19.6. Access removal shall be documented and retained as evidence.

 19.7. Where access cannot be removed immediately due to technical constraints, compensating controls shall be implemented and documented.

20. **Return of Organisation Property**

 20.1. Workforce members shall return all organisation property upon termination or when requested.

 20.2. Organisation property includes, as applicable:

 - Laptops, desktops, tablets, and mobile phones.
 - Security keys, tokens, smart cards, and authentication devices.
 - Access badges, keys, parking passes, and facility credentials.
 - Storage media and removable drives.
 - Documents, records, notebooks, and printed materials.
 - Corporate credit cards.
 - Tools, peripherals, and office equipment.
 - Customer or third-party property issued through the organisation.

 20.3. Managers and Human Resources shall coordinate recovery of assets from remote workers, contractors, and personnel at off-site locations.

 20.4. Information Technology shall verify receipt of technology assets and assess whether data preservation, device wiping, reimaging, or forensic retention is required.

 20.5. Failure to return organisation property shall be escalated to Human Resources, Legal, Finance, or management as appropriate.

21. **Exit Process**

 21.1. Human Resources shall conduct an exit process for departing employees where appropriate and legally permissible.

 21.2. The exit process shall include confirmation of:

 - Final working day.
 - Return of organisation property.
 - Ongoing confidentiality obligations.
 - Intellectual property obligations.
 - Post-employment restrictions, where applicable.
 - Final pay, benefits, and administrative matters.
 - Contact information for post-employment communications.
 - Revocation of access.
 - Completion of required exit documentation.

 21.3. Exit interviews may be conducted to collect feedback and identify potential workplace, security, compliance, or operational concerns.

 21.4. Any concerns identified during exit interviews that indicate misconduct, control weakness, security risk, privacy issue, or legal exposure shall be escalated to appropriate management.

22. **Post-Termination Confidentiality and Data Protection**

 22.1. Departing workforce members shall remain bound by confidentiality, intellectual property, data protection, and other continuing obligations after termination.

 22.2. Workforce members shall not retain, use, copy, transmit, disclose, or destroy organisation, customer, employee, or third-party information except as authorised.

 22.3. Departing workforce members shall certify return or deletion of organisation information from personal devices, personal accounts, removable media, or other unauthorised locations where applicable.

 22.4. Human Resources and Legal shall coordinate any post-employment restrictions, litigation hold requirements, or regulatory obligations.

23. **Timelines for Workforce Lifecycle Activities**

 The following minimum timelines shall apply unless a stricter requirement is defined by law, contract, risk assessment, or another approved policy:

 | Activity | Required Timing | Responsible Party | Evidence Required |
 |---|---:|---|---|
 | Role approval before recruitment | Before job posting or sourcing begins | Hiring Manager / Finance / Human Resources | Approved requisition |
 | Background screening initiation | After conditional offer and before start date, where legally permitted | Human Resources | Screening request and status |
 | Employment agreement execution | Before first working day | Human Resources / Legal | Signed agreement |
 | Policy acknowledgements | Before or within [X] business days of start date | Workforce Member / Human Resources | Acknowledgement record |
 | Initial security and privacy training | Before or within [X] business days of start date | Workforce Member / Human Resources / Information Security | Training completion record |
 | Standard access provisioning | On or after approval and start date | Information Technology | Access request and approval |
 | Privileged access provisioning | After business owner and security approval | Information Technology / Information Security | Approved access record |
 | Role change notification | Within [X] business days of approval | Manager / Human Resources | HR status update |
 | Access review after role change | Within [X] business days of effective change | Manager / System Owner | Access review evidence |
 | Voluntary termination access removal | No later than final working day | Information Technology / System Owners | Deprovisioning record |
 | Involuntary or high-risk termination access removal | At or before termination notification | Human Resources / Information Technology / Information Security | Deprovisioning record |
 | Contractor access removal | On contract end date or earlier if no longer required | Manager / Information Technology | Deprovisioning record |
 | Asset return | On or before final working day, or within [X] business days for remote personnel | Workforce Member / Manager / Information Technology | Asset receipt record |
 | Final offboarding checklist completion | Within [X] business days after termination | Human Resources | Completed checklist |

24. **Minimum Hiring and Onboarding Evidence**

 24.1. Human Resources shall maintain evidence that hiring and onboarding requirements have been completed.

 24.2. Minimum evidence shall include, as applicable:

 | Evidence Item | Required For | System or Repository | Owner |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Approved role requisition | Employees and long-term contractors | [HRIS/ATS] | Human Resources |
 | Job description | All roles | [HRIS/Document Repository] | Hiring Manager |
 | Candidate selection documentation | Employees | [ATS] | Hiring Manager / Human Resources |
 | Signed offer or engagement agreement | All workforce members | [HRIS/Contract Repository] | Human Resources / Legal |
 | Background screening status | Roles requiring screening | [Background Check Provider/HRIS] | Human Resources |
 | Employment eligibility verification | Employees, where applicable | [HRIS] | Human Resources |
 | Confidentiality agreement | All workforce members | [HRIS/Contract Repository] | Human Resources / Legal |
 | Policy acknowledgements | All workforce members | [Policy Management System] | Human Resources |
 | Training completion record | All workforce members | [LMS] | Human Resources / Information Security |
 | Access approval records | Users requiring system access | [Ticketing/IAM System] | Information Technology |
 | Equipment assignment record | Personnel issued equipment | [Asset Management System] | Information Technology |

25. **Minimum Termination and Offboarding Evidence**

 25.1. Human Resources shall maintain evidence that termination and offboarding requirements have been completed.

 25.2. Minimum evidence shall include, as applicable:

 | Evidence Item | Required For | System or Repository | Owner |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Termination notice or resignation record | All departing workforce members | [HRIS] | Human Resources |
 | Approved termination documentation | Involuntary terminations | [HRIS/Legal Repository] | Human Resources / Legal |
 | Offboarding checklist | All departing workforce members | [HRIS/Ticketing System] | Human Resources |
 | Access deprovisioning ticket | All users with system access | [Ticketing/IAM System] | Information Technology |
 | Privileged access removal evidence | Users with privileged access | [IAM/PAM/Ticketing System] | Information Technology / Information Security |
 | Physical access removal evidence | Personnel with facility access | [Badge System/Facilities System] | Facilities |
 | Asset return record | Personnel issued assets | [Asset Management System] | Information Technology |
 | Exit interview notes, where conducted | Employees | [HRIS] | Human Resources |
 | Confidentiality reminder or certification | Departing workforce members | [HRIS/Document Repository] | Human Resources |
 | Legal hold instruction, where applicable | Personnel subject to hold | [Legal Repository] | Legal |

26. **Segregation of Duties in HR Processes**

 26.1. Hiring approval, candidate selection, access approval, access provisioning, payroll setup, and termination processing shall be performed by appropriately authorised personnel.

 26.2. No individual shall approve their own hiring, compensation, access, promotion, transfer, or termination record.

 26.3. Changes to compensation, title, reporting line, employment status, and termination date shall require approval by authorised personnel.

 26.4. Human Resources shall maintain controls to prevent unauthorised changes to workforce records.

27. **Use of HR and Workforce Management Systems**

 27.1. Approved systems shall be used to manage recruiting, workforce records, training, policy acknowledgements, access requests, and offboarding activities.

 27.2. Access to HR systems shall be restricted to authorised personnel with a legitimate business need.

 27.3. HR system access shall be reviewed periodically.

 27.4. Workforce data shall be protected against unauthorised access, disclosure, modification, deletion, and loss.

 27.5. Integration between HR systems and identity or access management systems shall be monitored to support timely account provisioning and deprovisioning.

28. **Contractors, Temporary Staff, and Third-Party Personnel**

 28.1. Contractors, temporary staff, consultants, and third-party personnel shall be subject to onboarding, confidentiality, access approval, training, and offboarding requirements appropriate to their role and access.

 28.2. Each non-employee workforce member shall have an assigned internal sponsor or manager.

 28.3. Contractor and temporary worker engagements shall have defined start and end dates.

 28.4. Access for non-employee workforce members shall expire automatically where technically feasible or be reviewed before extension.

 28.5. Managers shall confirm continued business need before contractor access is extended.

 28.6. Third-party organisations providing personnel shall be contractually required to conduct appropriate screening, ensure confidentiality, and notify [Organisation Name] promptly of personnel changes.

29. **Remote and Hybrid Workforce Requirements**

 29.1. Remote and hybrid workforce members shall comply with the same hiring, onboarding, security, confidentiality, training, and termination requirements as on-site personnel.

 29.2. Equipment shipment, identity verification, asset assignment, and asset return processes shall be documented for remote personnel.

 29.3. Remote workforce members shall use organisation-approved systems and security controls when accessing organisation or customer information.

 29.4. Remote workforce members shall protect confidential information from unauthorised viewing, access, loss, or disclosure in home and public work environments.

30. **Privacy and Confidentiality of HR Information**

 30.1. Personal information collected during hiring, employment, and termination shall be limited to what is necessary for legitimate business, legal, contractual, and security purposes.

 30.2. Workforce members involved in HR processes shall protect candidate and employee information from unauthorised disclosure.

 30.3. Background screening, disciplinary, medical, accommodation, investigation, and termination records shall be handled with heightened confidentiality.

 30.4. Candidate and workforce member information shall be shared only with personnel who have a legitimate need to know.

 30.5. Personal information shall be retained only as long as required by law, contract, or approved retention schedules.

31. **Incident Reporting Related to Workforce Matters**

 31.1. Human Resources shall notify Information Security, Legal, Privacy, or executive management of workforce matters that may create security, privacy, fraud, insider threat, legal, or compliance risk.

 31.2. Workforce-related incidents requiring escalation may include:

 - Suspected theft or misuse of information.
 - Unauthorised access or attempted access.
 - Failure to return assets.
 - Threatening behaviour or workplace violence.
 - Policy violations involving sensitive systems or data.
 - Misrepresentation of employment credentials.
 - Conflicts of interest affecting trust or independence.
 - Termination of personnel with privileged or sensitive access.
 - Lost or stolen devices.
 - Use of personal accounts to store or transmit organisation information.

 31.3. Security and privacy incidents shall be managed through the organisation’s incident response process.

32. **Retention of Audit Evidence**

 32.1. Evidence supporting hiring, onboarding, training, access approval, role changes, and termination controls shall be retained for audit and compliance purposes.

 32.2. Evidence shall be complete, accurate, attributable, and retrievable.

 32.3. Evidence shall be protected from unauthorised modification or deletion.

 32.4. Human Resources, Information Technology, Information Security, Facilities, and system owners shall provide evidence upon authorised request for audits, assessments, investigations, or management reviews.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors / Executive Leadership | Set expectations for ethical conduct, workforce accountability, and resourcing of HR controls. Approve significant policy changes where required. |
| Human Resources | Own this policy; manage hiring, onboarding, workforce records, training coordination, policy acknowledgements, employee relations, termination processing, and offboarding coordination. |
| Hiring Managers / People Managers | Define role requirements; participate in fair candidate selection; approve access based on business need; set expectations; notify HR of status changes; support onboarding and offboarding. |
| Workforce Members | Provide accurate employment information; complete required training and acknowledgements; follow policies; protect organisation and customer information; return assets upon request or termination. |
| Information Technology | Provision and deprovision accounts; issue and recover equipment; maintain asset records; support access changes; maintain evidence of account and device actions. |
| Information Security | Define security training requirements; advise on sensitive roles and high-risk terminations; monitor access control effectiveness; support investigations and incident response. |
| Legal | Advise on employment agreements, background screening, disciplinary matters, terminations, privacy requirements, litigation holds, and contractual obligations. |
| Facilities / Physical Security | Issue and revoke physical access; recover badges and keys; support on-site onboarding and offboarding activities. |
| Finance / Payroll | Confirm budget approvals; process payroll setup and termination payments; manage corporate cards and expense access. |
| System Owners | Approve access to systems under their ownership; ensure access is appropriate; support access removal during role changes and termination. |
| Compliance / Internal Audit | Monitor adherence to this policy; test control evidence; report findings and remediation status to management. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy is mandatory.

Human Resources, Information Technology, Information Security, and Compliance shall monitor adherence through periodic reviews, control testing, reporting, and management oversight.

Monitoring activities shall include, at minimum:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Owner | Expected Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of new hire onboarding completion | Monthly | Human Resources | Onboarding completion report |
| Review of background screening completion for applicable roles | Monthly | Human Resources | Screening status report |
| Review of policy acknowledgement completion | Quarterly | Human Resources / Compliance | Acknowledgement report |
| Review of required training completion | Monthly or quarterly | Human Resources / Information Security | Training report |
| Review of access provisioning evidence for new hires | Quarterly | Information Technology / Compliance | Access request samples |
| Review of role change access updates | Quarterly | Information Technology / System Owners | Access change tickets |
| Review of terminated user access removal | Monthly | Information Technology / Information Security | Deprovisioning report |
| Review of contractor end dates and access | Monthly | Human Resources / Managers / Information Technology | Contractor access report |
| Review of physical access removal for terminations | Quarterly | Facilities | Badge deactivation report |
| Review of HR system privileged access | Quarterly | Human Resources / Information Technology | Access review evidence |
