| Audit of HR lifecycle controls | At least annually | Compliance / Internal Audit | Audit workpapers and findings |

Policy violations may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contract, loss of access privileges, legal action, financial recovery, or referral to law enforcement where appropriate.

Examples of violations include:

- Hiring or engaging personnel without required approval.
- Granting system access before onboarding requirements are satisfied.
- Failing to complete required background screening where applicable.
- Failing to complete security or privacy training.
- Failing to notify HR or IT of terminations or role changes in a timely manner.
- Failing to remove access upon termination or role change.
- Retaining organisation information after termination.
- Misusing workforce or candidate personal information.
- Falsifying employment, screening, training, or offboarding records.
- Circumventing HR, access, or termination controls.

Identified control gaps shall be documented, assigned an owner, prioritised based on risk, and remediated within approved timeframes.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only when there is a documented business need, legal constraint, operational necessity, or technical limitation.

Exception requests shall include:

- Description of the requested exception.
- Business justification.
- Personnel, systems, data, or facilities affected.
- Risk assessment.
- Compensating controls.
- Requested duration.
- Approval from Human Resources.
- Approval from Information Security where security or access controls are affected.
- Approval from Legal where employment, privacy, contractual, or regulatory risk is involved.
- Approval from the relevant business owner or executive sponsor.

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed [X] days unless renewed through the approved exception process.

Standing or permanent exceptions shall not be allowed unless approved by executive leadership and reviewed at least annually.

Emergency exceptions may be approved verbally or through an expedited workflow, but shall be documented within [X] business days.

Exception records shall be retained in [Exception Register/System of Record].

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur, including:

- Changes to business operations or organisational structure.
- Changes to hiring, onboarding, or termination processes.
- Changes to HR, identity management, access management, training, or asset management systems.
- Material security or privacy incidents involving workforce members.
- Audit findings or control deficiencies.
- Legal, regulatory, contractual, or customer requirement changes.
- Significant workforce model changes, such as remote work expansion, outsourcing, or international hiring.

The policy owner shall coordinate reviews with Human Resources, Information Security, Information Technology, Legal, Compliance, and relevant business stakeholders.

Updates shall be approved by [Approving Authority] before publication.

The current approved version shall be made available to all workforce members through [Policy Portal/Repository].

Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.

SOC2-019.title: Training & Awareness Policy
SOC2-019.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| POL-TRAIN-AWARE | 1.0 | [Security/GRC Owner] | [Effective Date] | SOC 2 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Training & Awareness Policy establishes mandatory requirements for security, privacy, confidentiality, availability, and processing integrity training and awareness activities across [Organization Name]. The policy ensures personnel understand their responsibilities for protecting systems, data, customers, and business operations, and that training is completed at appropriate intervals and tailored to job responsibilities.

This policy supports a consistent culture of risk awareness by requiring baseline training for all personnel, role-based training for personnel with elevated or specialized responsibilities, ongoing awareness communications, and evidence of completion suitable for internal oversight and external audit.

## Scope

This policy applies to all personnel who access [Organization Name] systems, networks, facilities, applications, customer data, company data, or third-party hosted environments, including:

- Employees, officers, directors, interns, temporary workers, and contractors.
- Third-party personnel and managed service providers with access to company systems or data.
- Personnel with privileged, administrative, development, engineering, customer support, security, finance, legal, human resources, or operational responsibilities.
- Personnel working remotely, on-site, or from third-party locations.

This policy applies to training and awareness activities related to:

- Information security.
- Privacy and protection of personal data.
- Confidentiality of company, customer, and third-party information.
- Secure use of technology resources.
- Acceptable use and handling of company assets.
- Incident identification and reporting.
- Phishing and social engineering awareness.
- Secure software development and change practices, where applicable.
- Role-based responsibilities for access, operations, compliance, customer support, vendor management, and system administration.

This policy does not replace detailed procedures, job-specific work instructions, human resources policies, or contractual training obligations, but it establishes the minimum mandatory training and awareness requirements.

## Policy Statements

1. **Mandatory baseline training**
 1. All personnel shall complete baseline security and awareness training before being granted routine access to production systems, customer data, sensitive company data, or internal business systems, unless a documented exception is approved.
 2. Baseline training shall include, at minimum:
 - Acceptable use of company systems and devices.
 - Password, passphrase, and authentication expectations.
 - Multi-factor authentication responsibilities.
 - Phishing, social engineering, and business email compromise awareness.
 - Safe handling, storage, transmission, and disposal of confidential information.
 - Privacy and personal data protection responsibilities.
 - Incident, suspicious activity, and policy violation reporting.
 - Secure remote work practices.
 - Physical security and workspace expectations.
 - Use of approved tools, software, and communication channels.
 - Consequences of non-compliance.

2. **Annual refresher training**
 1. All personnel shall complete security and awareness refresher training at least annually.
 2. Annual training shall be updated to reflect material changes in the threat environment, company systems, business operations, policies, regulatory obligations, and lessons learned from incidents or control findings.
 3. Personnel shall complete annual training within the assigned due date, normally no later than [Number] calendar days from assignment.

3. **Role-based training**
 1. Personnel shall complete role-based training appropriate to their job duties, system access, data handling responsibilities, and risk exposure.
 2. Role-based training shall be assigned before or promptly after personnel assume responsibilities requiring specialized knowledge.
 3. Role-based training shall be refreshed at least annually or when significant changes occur to relevant systems, processes, technologies, threats, or responsibilities.
 4. Role-based training shall be required for, at minimum, the following groups where applicable:

| Role or Function | Required Training Topics | Minimum Frequency | Trigger Events |
|---|---|---:|---|
| All personnel | Baseline security, privacy, confidentiality, acceptable use, incident reporting, phishing awareness | Annually | New hire, policy change, significant incident |
| Managers and people leaders | Security responsibilities for teams, access approval, onboarding and offboarding responsibilities, reporting obligations | Annually | Promotion to manager, process change |
| System administrators and privileged users | Privileged access responsibilities, secure administration, logging and monitoring expectations, change controls, secrets handling | Annually | Privileged access assignment, major platform change |
| Engineering and development personnel | Secure development practices, code review expectations, secure configuration, vulnerability remediation, secrets management, change management | Annually | Assignment to development role, SDLC change |
| Security and IT operations personnel | Incident response, vulnerability management, monitoring, identity and access processes, backup and recovery responsibilities | Annually | Assignment to operational role, tool or process change |
| Customer support and success personnel | Customer data handling, identity verification, secure support processes, confidentiality, escalation procedures | Annually | Access to customer support platforms, process change |
| Human resources personnel | Employee data protection, onboarding and offboarding controls, confidentiality, secure records handling | Annually | HR system access, employment process change |
| Finance and procurement personnel | Fraud prevention, payment security, vendor risk awareness, invoice fraud and social engineering | Annually | Financial system access, payment process change |
| Legal, compliance, and privacy personnel | Confidential information handling, privacy obligations, records handling, reporting responsibilities | Annually | New compliance responsibility, material legal requirement change |

4. **Training during onboarding**
 1. New personnel shall be assigned required training as part of onboarding.
 2. Hiring managers and onboarding coordinators shall ensure personnel understand training requirements before access is granted to sensitive systems or data.
 3. Where immediate access is required for business reasons, compensating supervision or restricted access shall be implemented until training is completed.

5. **Training upon role change**
 1. Personnel changing roles, departments, responsibilities, or access levels shall be assessed for additional role-based training needs.
 2. Required additional training shall be assigned when the role change introduces new access, data handling responsibilities, administrative privileges, customer-facing responsibilities, development duties, or compliance obligations.
 3. Managers shall notify Human Resources, IT, Security, or the training administrator of role changes that affect training requirements.

6. **Training for contractors and third parties**
 1. Contractors and third-party personnel with access to company systems or data shall complete appropriate training before access is granted or shall provide acceptable evidence of equivalent training from their employer.
 2. Third-party training obligations shall be addressed in contracts, statements of work, onboarding instructions, or access approval workflows where applicable.
 3. Third-party personnel shall comply with company security and data handling requirements while performing work for [Organization Name].

7. **Awareness communications**
 1. The organization shall maintain an ongoing security and awareness program in addition to formal training.
 2. Awareness activities shall address current risks, common mistakes, seasonal threats, policy reminders, incident lessons learned, and practical guidance for personnel.
 3. Awareness communications may include emails, intranet posts, collaboration messages, posters, briefings, newsletters, simulations, workshops, or team meeting content.
 4. Awareness messages shall be written in clear business language and tailored to the audience where appropriate.

8. **Phishing and social engineering awareness**
 1. Personnel shall receive periodic phishing and social engineering awareness content.
 2. The organization shall conduct phishing simulations or equivalent practical exercises at a frequency determined by risk and business needs, but at least annually where feasible.
 3. Results of phishing exercises shall be used to improve awareness and identify personnel or groups requiring additional guidance.
 4. Phishing simulation results shall be handled respectfully and used for risk reduction, not public embarrassment.

9. **Incident reporting awareness**
 1. Training shall instruct personnel how to report suspected security incidents, privacy incidents, phishing attempts, lost or stolen devices, unauthorized access, malware, suspicious activity, and accidental disclosure of information.
 2. Reporting channels shall be clearly communicated and shall include [Incident Reporting Channel], [Security Email Address], or [Service Desk System].
 3. Personnel shall be instructed to report concerns promptly, even when facts are incomplete.

10. **Training content management**
 1. Training content shall be reviewed for accuracy, relevance, and completeness before assignment.
 2. Training content shall align with company policies, procedures, customer commitments, legal obligations, and operational practices.
 3. Content shall be updated when there are material changes to:
 - Company policies or standards.
 - Systems, tools, or access methods.
 - Threats or incident trends.
 - Regulatory, contractual, or customer obligations.
 - Business processes or services.
 4. Training materials shall be understandable to the intended audience and available in appropriate formats for personnel who require accessibility accommodations.

11. **Training assignment and completion tracking**
 1. Required training shall be assigned, tracked, and recorded in [Learning Management System] or another approved tracking mechanism.
 2. Training records shall identify, at minimum:
 - Individual assigned.
 - Department or function.
 - Training title or module.
 - Assignment date.
 - Due date.
 - Completion date.
 - Completion status.
 - Evidence of completion, such as system record, attestation, quiz result, certificate, or attendance record.
 3. Training completion evidence shall be retained in accordance with the organization’s records retention requirements and shall be available for compliance review and audit.

12. **Training completion deadlines**
 1. Baseline onboarding training shall be completed within [Number] calendar days of start date, unless required earlier based on access needs.
 2. Annual refresher training shall be completed within [Number] calendar days of assignment.
 3. Role-based training shall be completed within [Number] calendar days of assignment or before performing high-risk activities where required by the process owner.
 4. Remedial training assigned due to policy violations, incident involvement, phishing simulation results, or audit findings shall be completed within [Number] calendar days of assignment.

| Training Type | Required Audience | Standard Due Date | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Onboarding baseline training | New personnel with system or data access | Within [Number] days of start date | Completion record or signed acknowledgement |
| Annual refresher training | All active personnel in scope | Within [Number] days of assignment | Completion record |
| Role-based training | Personnel in designated roles | Within [Number] days of assignment or before high-risk activity | Completion record, attendance, certificate, or attestation |
| Remedial training | Personnel assigned corrective training | Within [Number] days of assignment | Completion record and manager confirmation if required |
| Third-party equivalent training | Contractors or third-party personnel | Before access or within approved onboarding window | Vendor attestation, certificate, or company training record |

13. **Assessment and acknowledgement**
 1. Training shall include an acknowledgement, quiz, knowledge check, certification of completion, attendance record, or other method to demonstrate participation and understanding.
 2. Personnel shall acknowledge applicable policies where required, including acceptable use, confidentiality, privacy, and information security responsibilities.
 3. Failure to pass required assessments may result in reassignment of the module, supplemental training, manager notification, or access restrictions.

14. **Non-completion escalation**
 1. Personnel who do not complete required training by the due date shall be subject to escalation.
 2. Escalation shall include reminders to the individual, notification to the manager, and notification to Human Resources, Security, Compliance, or executive management where required.
 3. Continued non-completion may result in suspension of access to systems or data, performance management, disciplinary action, or contract remedies.

| Days After Due Date | Escalation Action | Responsible Party |
|---:|---|---|
| 1-7 days | Reminder to individual and manager | Training Administrator |
| 8-14 days | Formal escalation to department leader and Security/GRC | Training Administrator |
| 15-30 days | Access review and potential restriction of non-essential access | Security, IT, Manager |
| More than 30 days | HR or contract management action; executive reporting where appropriate | HR, Legal, Department Leader |

15. **Access dependency**
 1. Access to sensitive systems, production environments, customer data, administrative functions, or regulated data may be withheld, restricted, or removed if required training is not completed.
 2. Managers shall not approve access that conflicts with training prerequisites unless a documented exception has been approved.
 3. IT and Security shall support access restriction or removal when directed through approved processes.

16. **Remedial and targeted training**
 1. Remedial training shall be assigned when personnel demonstrate a need for additional guidance due to:
 - Repeated phishing simulation failures.
 - Policy violations.
 - Involvement in a security or privacy incident.
 - Mishandling of confidential information.
 - Audit or monitoring findings.
 - Manager or Security recommendation.
 2. Targeted training shall be risk-based, relevant to the issue identified, and completed within the assigned deadline.
 3. Remedial training completion shall be tracked as compliance evidence.

17. **Management participation**
 1. Managers shall ensure their teams complete required training by the assigned due dates.
 2. Managers shall reinforce security and awareness expectations during team operations and shall support attendance at required sessions.
 3. Managers shall notify the training owner of changes in role, responsibility, or access that may require updated training assignments.

18. **Confidentiality and privacy of training records**
 1. Training records shall be treated as internal business records and protected from unauthorized access.
 2. Access to individual completion status and assessment results shall be limited to personnel with a legitimate business need, such as Human Resources, Security, Compliance, IT, Legal, auditors, managers, and designated administrators.
 3. Reporting shall use aggregated data where individual-level detail is not necessary.

19. **Metrics and reporting**
 1. The organization shall maintain training metrics to assess participation, completion, overdue items, role-based coverage, phishing exercise outcomes, and remedial training status.
 2. Training compliance status shall be reported to management on a defined schedule.
 3. Significant training gaps, overdue trends, or high-risk findings shall be escalated for corrective action.

20. **Records retention**
 1. Training records, acknowledgements, completion evidence, attendance records, and related reports shall be retained for at least [Retention Period] or longer where required by contract, law, audit, or business need.
 2. Records shall be stored in approved systems and protected against unauthorized alteration or deletion.
 3. Historical records shall remain accessible for audits, investigations, and compliance reviews.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Management | Approves and supports the training and awareness program; ensures adequate resources; reinforces accountability for completion. |
| Security/GRC Owner | Owns this policy; defines security and awareness training requirements; reviews program effectiveness; supports audit evidence collection; escalates material gaps. |
| Human Resources | Integrates required training into onboarding, role change, and offboarding processes; supports escalation and disciplinary processes; maintains personnel status information. |
| Training Administrator | Assigns training; maintains the training platform or tracking mechanism; monitors completion; issues reminders; produces reports; retains completion evidence. |
| Department Managers | Ensure personnel complete required training; identify role-based training needs; communicate role changes; support remediation for overdue or failed training. |
| IT and Security Operations | Enforce access restrictions where training prerequisites are not met; provide technical input for role-based content; support phishing simulations and incident reporting awareness. |
| Privacy, Legal, and Compliance Teams | Provide content requirements related to privacy, confidentiality, contractual obligations, records handling, and compliance commitments. |
| System and Process Owners | Identify training requirements for users of specific systems or processes; ensure high-risk activities include appropriate prerequisites. |
| Procurement and Vendor Management | Ensure third-party training obligations are included in vendor onboarding or contractual requirements where applicable. |
| Personnel | Complete required training by assigned deadlines; follow company policies; report suspected incidents; apply training in daily work; ask questions when responsibilities are unclear. |
| Third-Party Personnel | Complete required or equivalent training; comply with company security and data handling expectations; report incidents or concerns through approved channels. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy shall be monitored through training records, learning management system reports, onboarding checklists, access approval workflows, phishing simulation results, internal reviews, audit requests, management reporting, and exception tracking.

The Security/GRC Owner, Human Resources, Training Administrator, and relevant managers shall review training completion status periodically. Reviews shall include, as appropriate:

- Completion rates for baseline, annual, role-based, remedial, and third-party training.
- Overdue training by department, manager, role, or risk category.
- Personnel with access to sensitive systems who have not completed required training.
- Role changes requiring additional training.
- Results and trends from phishing or social engineering exercises.
- Effectiveness of reminders and escalation activities.
- Evidence availability for audit and management review.
- Corrective actions for recurring non-compliance.

Non-compliance with this policy may result in one or more of the following actions:

- Required completion of overdue training.
- Assignment of remedial or supplemental training.
- Notification to the individual’s manager.
- Restriction, suspension, or removal of access to systems, applications, production environments, or data.
- Performance management or disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.
- Contractual remedies, access removal, or termination of engagement for contractors or third-party personnel.
- Corrective action tracking for control deficiencies or audit findings.

Enforcement shall be applied consistently, proportionately, and in accordance with applicable employment agreements, contracts, laws, and company policies.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy shall be limited, risk-based, documented, time-bound, and approved before deviation occurs whenever possible.

Exception requests shall include:

- Name and role of the individual or group requiring the exception.
- Training requirement affected.
- Business reason for the exception.
- Systems, data, or processes involved.
- Risk assessment and potential impact.
- Compensating controls, such as restricted access, supervision, alternate training, or temporary access limits.
- Requested duration and expiration date.
- Approval from the Security/GRC Owner and the relevant business owner.
- Additional approvals from Human Resources, Legal, Privacy, or executive management where appropriate.

Exceptions shall not be used to avoid mandatory training permanently. Expired exceptions shall either be closed by completing the required training or renewed through a new review and approval. Exceptions involving access to sensitive systems, customer data, production environments, or privileged accounts shall receive heightened scrutiny.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and updated as needed to remain aligned with business operations, risk conditions, customer commitments, legal obligations, and the organization’s control environment.

The Security/GRC Owner shall coordinate the review with Human Resources, IT, Security Operations, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, and relevant business stakeholders. The review shall consider:

- Changes in organizational structure, roles, systems, and services.
- Results of audits, assessments, incidents, and investigations.
- Training completion trends and recurring gaps.
- Feedback from personnel, managers, and auditors.
- Changes in threats, common attack techniques, and industry practices.
- Updates to company policies, procedures, and contractual commitments.
- Effectiveness of role-based and remedial training.

Material changes to this policy shall be approved by [Approving Authority]. Version history, approvals, and publication records shall be maintained in accordance with document management requirements. The current approved version shall be made available to all personnel through [Policy Repository or Intranet Location].

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Review ID | Enter a unique identifier for the access review cycle, using format UAR-YYYY-Q#-SYSTEM or UAR-YYYY-MM-SYSTEM, e.g. UAR-2026-Q1-OKTA. |
| Review Period Start Date | Enter the first date covered by the review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Period End Date | Enter the last date covered by the review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Type | Enter the type of review performed; allowed values: Quarterly, Semi-Annual, Annual, Triggered, Post-Implementation. |
| System / Application Name | Enter the exact name of the system, application, database, infrastructure platform, or directory being reviewed. |
| System Owner | Enter the accountable business or technical owner of the system who is responsible for validating access appropriateness. |
| Access Population Extract Date | Enter the date the user access listing was exported from the source system in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Access Population Source | Enter the authoritative source used for the access listing, such as Okta, Azure AD, AWS IAM, GitHub, Salesforce admin export, or application admin report. |
| User ID / Account Name | Enter the unique account identifier exactly as shown in the source system. |
| User Full Name | Enter the user's full legal or HR-recognised name; for service accounts, enter the service account display name. |
| User Email | Enter the user's corporate email address; for service or non-human accounts, enter the owner email or distribution list. |
| User Type | Enter the account type; allowed values: Employee, Contractor, Vendor, Service Account, Shared Account, Admin Account, Break-Glass Account. |
| Department / Team | Enter the user's department, function, or team from HR or the identity source. |
| Manager | Enter the user's current manager or accountable sponsor; for service accounts, enter the named business or technical owner. |
| Employment / Engagement Status | Enter the current status from HR or vendor records; allowed values: Active, Terminated, Leave of Absence, Contractor Active, Contractor Ended, Unknown. |
| Role / Group / Permission Assigned | Enter the specific role, group, profile, entitlement, permission set, or access level assigned in the reviewed system. |
| Privilege Level | Classify the access level; allowed values: Standard User, Elevated User, Administrator, Super Administrator, Read-Only, Service, Unknown. |
| Access Description | Briefly describe what the assigned role or permission allows the user to do, focusing on security-relevant capabilities. |
| Business Justification | Enter the business reason the user requires this access, tied to job role, team responsibility, or approved operational need. |
| Last Login Date | Enter the most recent login or activity date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if the system does not track last login. |
| Reviewer Name | Enter the full name of the person who reviewed and certified the access. |
| Reviewer Role | Enter the reviewer's role, such as System Owner, Application Owner, Department Manager, Data Owner, or Security Reviewer. |
| Reviewer Independence | Indicate whether the reviewer is appropriate and not the same person as the access holder for their own access; allowed values: Independent, Self-Review Exception, Not Applicable. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the reviewer made the access decision in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Decision | Enter the certification outcome; allowed values: Approved - Retain, Remove, Modify, Suspend, Investigate, Exception Approved. |
| Decision Rationale | Enter a concise reason supporting the review decision, especially where access is retained, modified, removed, or excepted. |
| Access Change Required | Enter whether action is required as a result of the review; allowed values: Yes, No. |
| Remediation Action | If access change is required, describe the exact action to perform, such as remove admin role, disable account, downgrade to read-only, or transfer ownership; enter N/A if no action is required. |
| Remediation Owner | Enter the person or team responsible for completing the access change; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Due Date | Enter the target completion date for required remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Completion Date | Enter the actual date the remediation was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until completed or enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Remediation Evidence Reference | Enter the ticket number, change request ID, screenshot filename, audit log export name, or repository path proving the remediation was completed; enter N/A if no remediation is required. |
| Exception Approved | Indicate whether access was retained through an approved exception; allowed values: Yes, No, N/A. |
| Exception Approver | If an exception was approved, enter the approver's full name and role; enter N/A if no exception applies. |
| Exception Expiry Date | If an exception was approved, enter the expiry or re-review date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no exception applies. |
| Final Status | Enter the final review status after all decisions and remediation are complete; allowed values: Open, Pending Remediation, Remediated, Certified, Exception Active, Overdue. |

| Notes | Enter any additional context relevant to the review, such as limitations, unusual access patterns, compensating controls, or follow-up items. |

### Maintenance

The template is owned by the Information Security or GRC team, with completion input from system owners, application owners, managers, and IT administrators. It is updated each access review cycle, at least quarterly or per the organisation's access review policy, using authoritative exports from identity providers, HRIS, and in-scope application or infrastructure admin consoles.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique log identifier for this onboarding or termination event, e.g. NHT-YYYY-###. |
| Person ID | Enter the unique employee, contractor, or workforce ID from the HRIS or identity source of truth. |
| Full Name | Enter the individual's legal or HRIS-recorded full name. |
| Worker Type | Enter one allowed value: Employee, Contractor, Intern, Temporary, Vendor, Other. |
| Department | Enter the department or business unit from the HRIS. |
| Job Title | Enter the person's job title for new hires or most recent job title for terminations. |
| Manager | Enter the name of the direct manager or sponsor responsible for the individual's access. |
| Event Type | Enter one allowed value: New Hire, Rehire, Transfer, Termination, Contractor End, Role Change. |
| Employment Status | Enter one allowed value: Pending Start, Active, Leave, Terminated, Contractor Ended. |
| Hire Date | For new hire or rehire events, enter the effective start date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A for termination-only records. |
| Termination Date | For termination or contractor end events, enter the HR-effective termination date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A for new hire-only records. |
| Last Working Date | For termination events, enter the last day the individual performed work in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Access Request Ticket ID | Enter the service desk, IAM, or workflow ticket number used to request, approve, and track access changes. |
| HR Source Record ID | Enter the HRIS transaction, personnel action, or workflow ID that triggered the access provisioning or de-provisioning activity. |
| Request Submitted Date | Enter the date the onboarding, access, or termination request was submitted in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Requested By | Enter the person or system that submitted the request, typically HR, the hiring manager, or the manager/sponsor. |
| Business Justification | Enter the reason access is required or removed, tied to job responsibilities, termination, or role change. |
| Access Profile / Role Requested | Enter the standard role, access group, job profile, or access bundle requested or removed; avoid vague descriptions such as 'standard access'. |
| Systems / Applications In Scope | List each system, application, directory group, SaaS platform, infrastructure account, or privileged tool included in the provisioning or de-provisioning action. |
| Data Classification / Privilege Level | Enter one allowed value or equivalent internal label: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, Privileged/Admin. |
| Approver Name | Enter the name of the authorized approver for access provisioning or removal, typically manager, system owner, or data owner. |
| Approver Role | Enter the approver's role, such as Hiring Manager, Department Head, System Owner, Data Owner, HR, or IT Security. |
| Approval Date | Enter the date approval was granted in YYYY-MM-DD format; approval must occur before provisioning unless an approved exception exists. |
| Provisioning Due Date | For new hire, rehire, transfer, or role change events, enter the target completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Provisioning Completed Date | Enter the date access was fully provisioned in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A for de-provisioning-only records. |
| Provisioned By | Enter the name, team, automation process, or IAM workflow that completed the provisioning. |
| Provisioning Evidence Link | Enter a link or reference to evidence showing approved and completed provisioning, such as IAM workflow, ticket, screenshot, audit log, or access change report. |
| Termination Notification Date | For termination events, enter the date HR or management notified IT/IAM in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A for new hire-only records. |
| De-provisioning Due Date | For termination or access removal events, enter the required completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format based on policy or SLA; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| De-provisioning Completed Date | Enter the date all in-scope logical access was disabled, removed, or transferred in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A for provisioning-only records. |
| De-provisioned By | Enter the name, team, automation process, or IAM workflow that completed de-provisioning. |
| Accounts Disabled / Removed | Enter a concise list of disabled, removed, transferred, or retained accounts and groups; include N/A only where no accounts existed. |
| Shared / Privileged Access Reviewed | Enter one allowed value: Yes, No, N/A; use Yes only if shared credentials, admin accounts, service accounts, tokens, keys, and elevated groups were reviewed and remediated where required. |
| Physical Access Removed | Enter one allowed value: Yes, No, N/A; use Yes when badges, building access, office keys, and physical access rights were disabled or returned. |
| Company Assets Returned | Enter one allowed value: Yes, No, Partial, N/A; track whether laptops, mobile devices, security tokens, badges, and other company assets were returned. |
| Exception Required | Enter one allowed value: Yes, No; use Yes if access was provisioned without prior approval, de-provisioning was late, access was temporarily retained, or any policy/SLA requirement was not met. |
| Exception Description | If Exception Required is Yes, describe the exception, root cause, compensating controls, and affected systems; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Exception Approval | If Exception Required is Yes, enter the name and role of the authorized exception approver and approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Exception Target Resolution Date | If Exception Required is Yes, enter the target remediation date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Final Status | Enter one allowed value: Open, Pending Approval, In Progress, Completed On Time, Completed Late, Exception Open, Exception Closed, Cancelled. |
| Reviewer Name | Enter the name of the HR, IT, IAM, Security, or compliance reviewer who verified the record for completeness and evidence. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the record was reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Notes | Enter any additional audit-relevant context, such as delayed HR notification, automated workflow details, retained mailbox approval, or cross-reference to related records. |

### Maintenance

Owned by HR Operations and IT/IAM, with Security or Compliance performing periodic review. Update per personnel event and reconcile at least monthly against the HRIS, IAM/SSO platform, service desk tickets, and key application access logs.

| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this background check record, e.g., BGC-YYYY-###. |
| Worker ID | Enter the employee, contractor, or candidate ID from the HRIS or applicant tracking system; use 'Pending' if not yet assigned. |
| Worker Name | Enter the worker's full legal name or HRIS display name; avoid entering sensitive background check details in this log. |
| Employment Type | Enter one allowed value: Employee, Contractor, Intern, Temporary, Third-Party, Other. |
| Job Title | Enter the official job title associated with the role requiring the background check. |
| Department | Enter the worker's department or business function, e.g., Engineering, Finance, Customer Support. |
| Work Location / Country | Enter the primary work location and country because background check requirements may vary by jurisdiction. |
| Hiring Manager | Enter the name or employee ID of the hiring manager responsible for the role. |
| Background Check Requirement Level | Enter the HR policy requirement level applicable to the role, e.g., Standard, Enhanced, Executive, Regulated, Not Required. |
| Checks Required by HR Policy | List the required check types for the role per HR policy, e.g., identity verification, employment verification, education verification, criminal record check, sanctions screening, reference check, credit check where legally permitted. |
| Offer Date | Enter the date the offer was issued in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Planned Start Date | Enter the worker's planned start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Consent / Authorization Obtained | Enter Yes, No, or Not Required to indicate whether legally required worker consent or authorization was obtained before initiating the check. |
| Consent Date | Enter the date consent or authorization was obtained in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not required. |
| Background Check Vendor / Source | Enter the approved background check vendor or source system used, e.g., Checkr, Sterling, HireRight, internal HR verification. |
| Check Initiated Date | Enter the date the background check was initiated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Check Completed Date | Enter the date the background check was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until complete. |
| Overall Result | Enter one allowed value: Pending, Clear, Meets Requirements, Review Required, Does Not Meet Requirements, Cancelled, Not Required. |
| Adjudication Decision | Enter the final HR decision based on policy and applicable law: Approved, Approved with Exception, Not Approved, Pending, N/A. |
| Adjudication Decision Date | Enter the date the adjudication decision was made in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Adjudicator / HR Reviewer | Enter the name or employee ID of the HR reviewer or authorized adjudicator who reviewed the result. |
| Exception Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the worker started or was approved outside the standard background check policy requirement. |
| Exception Approval Reference | Enter the ticket ID, approval record ID, or document link for the exception; enter N/A if no exception. |
| Exception Approver | Enter the name or role of the authorized approver for the exception; enter N/A if no exception. |
| Exception Approval Date | Enter the date the exception was approved in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no exception. |
| Cleared Before Start Date | Enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether the worker was cleared or formally excepted before their start date. |
| Evidence Location | Enter a secure link, HRIS record reference, vendor report ID, or document repository path showing evidence of completion and adjudication; do not attach sensitive report contents in this log unless approved by HR/legal. |
| Confidentiality / Access Restriction Confirmed | Enter Yes or No to confirm that background check evidence is stored in a restricted HR/legal repository with access limited to authorized personnel. |
| Retention / Disposal Date | Enter the scheduled retention expiry or disposal date in YYYY-MM-DD format based on HR/legal retention policy. |
| Notes | Enter brief administrative notes only; do not include criminal history, medical information, protected-class information, or other sensitive background check findings. |

### Maintenance

Owned by HR Operations or People Operations, with restricted access for HR/legal and audit reviewers. Update upon each new hire, contractor onboarding, role transfer requiring re-screening, exception approval, or check completion, and reconcile at least monthly against the HRIS, applicant tracking system, onboarding workflow, and approved background check vendor portal.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this training completion record, using a consistent format such as TRN-YYYY-####. |
| Learner Employee ID | Enter the learner’s unique employee or contractor ID exactly as shown in the HRIS or identity system. |
| Learner Full Name | Enter the learner’s full legal or HRIS name in the format Last Name, First Name. |
| Learner Email | Enter the learner’s organisation-issued email address. |
| Employment Status | Enter the learner’s status at the time of assignment using one of: Active, New Hire, Leave of Absence, Terminated, Contractor Active, Contractor Ended. |
| Department | Enter the learner’s department or business unit exactly as recorded in the HRIS. |
| Job Title | Enter the learner’s job title exactly as recorded in the HRIS. |
| Manager | Enter the learner’s direct manager full name in the format Last Name, First Name. |
| Worker Type | Enter one of: Employee, Contractor, Temporary Worker, Intern, Third-Party User. |
| Training Audience Group | Enter the group that determines training requirement, such as All Workforce, Engineering, Customer Support, Privileged Access Users, New Hires, Managers. |
| Training Course Name | Enter the exact name of the required training course assigned, such as Annual Security Awareness Training or Secure Development Training. |
| Training Course Version | Enter the course version, publication date, or annual edition, using the LMS value where available, such as v2026.1 or 2026 Annual. |
| Training Category | Enter the training category using one of: Security Awareness, Privacy, Code of Conduct, Secure Development, Incident Reporting, Role-Based Security, Acceptable Use, Other. |
| SOC 2 Control Reference | Enter the relevant SOC 2 control reference supported by the training record, normally CC2.2; include additional internal control IDs if applicable, such as CC2.2 / SEC-TRN-01. |
| Training Period | Enter the annual training period covered in YYYY format or YYYY-Q# if the organisation tracks quarterly campaigns. |
| Assignment Date | Enter the date the training was assigned to the learner in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Due Date | Enter the date by which the learner was required to complete the training in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Completion Date | Enter the date the learner completed the training in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if not completed. |
| Completion Status | Enter one of: Not Assigned, Assigned, In Progress, Completed On Time, Completed Late, Overdue, Exempted, Not Applicable. |
| Completion Method | Enter how completion was evidenced using one of: LMS Completion, Live Session Attendance, Signed Attestation, External Certificate, Manual HR Confirmation. |
| Passing Score Required | Enter the minimum required passing score as a percentage, such as 80%; enter N/A if the course does not require a score. |
| Score Achieved | Enter the learner’s achieved score as a percentage, such as 95%; enter N/A if the course does not require a score. |
| Certificate or Evidence Link | Enter a hyperlink or repository path to the completion certificate, LMS report, attendance record, attestation, or other evidence supporting completion. |
| LMS Record ID | Enter the unique LMS transaction, enrolment, or completion record ID; enter N/A if the evidence did not come from an LMS. |
| Late Completion Reason | If Completion Status is Completed Late or Overdue, enter the documented reason; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Exception Approved By | If the learner is exempted or completion is waived, enter the approver’s full name and role; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Exception Approval Date | If an exception was approved, enter the approval date in YYYY-MM-DD format; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Follow-Up Action Required | Enter any required remediation or follow-up action, such as Manager escalation or Reassign training; enter None if no action is required. |
| Follow-Up Action Owner | Enter the role or person responsible for follow-up action; enter N/A if no follow-up is required. |
| Follow-Up Due Date | Enter the due date for the follow-up action in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no follow-up is required. |
| Notes | Enter concise additional context relevant to audit evidence, such as data correction notes or links to related communications; enter N/A if none. |

### Maintenance

The People Operations or Security Awareness Program Owner owns this template, with review by Compliance/GRC. It is updated for each annual training campaign and reconciled at least monthly during the campaign using the LMS as the primary source, supplemented by HRIS worker data and approved exception records.

SOC2-024.title: Change Tickets & Approvals
SOC2-024.content:
## What This Evidences

**Change Tickets & Approvals** evidence demonstrates that the organisation manages system changes through a controlled process, including documented requests, review, approval, implementation, testing, and closure.

For SOC 2 control **CC8.1**, this evidence supports that changes to infrastructure, applications, databases, configurations, and production environments are authorised, tracked, tested, and approved before or after implementation as appropriate.

This artifact is **collected, not authored**. It must be exported or captured from the organisation’s operational IT service management system, change management workflow, DevOps platform, or integrated ticketing tool. Do not create a manual spreadsheet or narrative as a substitute for system-generated change records.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect the evidence from the organisation’s primary change management or ITSM platform, such as:

- [ITSM platform name], for example ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Freshservice, Zendesk, or ManageEngine
- [DevOps/change workflow tool], for example Azure DevOps, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Jenkins, if approvals are managed there
- [Configuration/deployment platform], where production deployments are linked to approved change tickets
- [CAB/change approval dashboard], if formal change approval board records are maintained separately

The preferred source is the system of record used to request, approve, schedule, implement, and close production changes.

## How To Collect

1. Log in to [ITSM/change management system] with an account that has read access to change records and approval history.
2. Navigate to the change management module, for example **Changes**, **Change Requests**, **Production Changes**, or **Release Tickets**.
3. Set the reporting period to [audit period start date] through [audit period end date].
4. Filter for changes affecting production systems, security-relevant systems, customer-facing services, infrastructure, databases, CI/CD pipelines, or access-control configurations.
5. Include all change types in scope, such as standard, normal, emergency, and retrospective/emergency approvals.
6. Export the change ticket list to CSV, XLSX, or PDF from the system.
7. For the auditor’s sample, open each selected ticket and export or capture the full ticket detail, including approval workflow and activity history.
8. Where deployments are managed in a separate tool, capture the linked deployment, pull request, build, or release record showing traceability to the change ticket.
9. Save all exports and screenshots to the designated audit evidence repository using the agreed naming convention.

## What To Capture

For each change ticket, capture enough detail to show the full lifecycle:

- Change ticket ID or reference number
- Title and description of the change
- Requestor and change owner
- Affected system, application, service, or environment
- Change category and type, including emergency status where applicable
- Business or technical justification
- Risk and impact assessment
- Implementation plan
- Backout or rollback plan
- Testing or validation plan
- Scheduled implementation date and actual completion date
- Approval history, including approver names, roles, timestamps, and approval decisions
- Evidence of segregation between requestor, implementer, and approver where applicable
- Deployment, release, pull request, or build reference
- Post-implementation review or validation outcome
- Final status, closure notes, and closure timestamp
- System-generated activity log or audit trail showing workflow progression

## Frequency & Owner

- **Collection frequency:** At least quarterly during control operation reviews, and at audit request for the defined audit period.
- **Evidence owner:** [Change Manager] or [IT Service Management Owner].
- **Supporting owners:** [Engineering Lead], [Infrastructure Lead], [DevOps Lead], and [System Owner] for linked technical deployment evidence.

## Retention & Storage

Store collected exports and screenshots in [evidence repository name], such as a GRC platform, secure SharePoint site, Google Drive folder, or audit evidence vault.

Retain evidence for at least [retention period], or longer if required by customer, legal, regulatory, or audit obligations. Access should be restricted to authorised compliance, audit, IT, and management personnel. Evidence files should be read-only where possible and named using a consistent format, for example:

`SOC2_CC8.1_ChangeTickets_[period]_[system]_[export date]`

## Acceptance Criteria

Auditors typically accept this evidence when it:

- Comes directly from the system of record, not a manually prepared substitute
- Covers the full audit period or the specific sample period requested
- Shows a complete population of in-scope production changes
- Demonstrates that changes were documented, reviewed, approved, implemented, tested, and closed
- Includes timestamps and named individuals for key workflow events
- Shows approval occurred before implementation, except for documented emergency changes
- Includes emergency change review and retrospective approval where applicable
- Provides traceability between change tickets and deployments, pull requests, releases, or configuration updates
- Contains sufficient detail for the auditor to reperform or verify the change control process independently

| Scan Name | Enter the descriptive name of the scan, including environment or scope, e.g. Monthly External Perimeter Scan. |
| Scan Type | Enter the scan category; allowed values: Internal Network, External Network, Web Application, Cloud Configuration, Container/Image, Endpoint, Database, Other. |
| SOC 2 Control Reference | Enter the applicable SOC 2 control reference; for this template use CC7.1 unless mapped to an additional internal control ID. |

SOC2-026.title: Penetration Test Report (Annual)
SOC2-026.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-SOC2-PT-ANNUAL] | 1.0 | [Security Owner / CISO] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | SOC 2 | Confidential - Restricted Distribution |

## Purpose

This Penetration Test Report documents the results of the annual security assessment performed against [Organization Name] systems, applications, infrastructure, and supporting services within the defined scope. The purpose of the test was to identify exploitable security weaknesses that could affect the confidentiality, integrity, availability, or privacy of customer data and business operations.

This report is intended to provide management, security, engineering, and audit stakeholders with:

- A clear summary of the security posture of the tested environment.
- Validated vulnerabilities and exploitability evidence.
- Business risk analysis for identified issues.
- Remediation recommendations and accountable action plans.
- Evidence that periodic offensive security testing is performed to support the organization’s trust services commitments.

This report is not a certification or guarantee that the environment is free of vulnerabilities. It represents the results of testing performed during the reporting period, using the agreed scope, methods, time window, access level, and constraints.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Assessment Name | Annual Penetration Test |
| Reporting Period | [YYYY-MM-DD] to [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Testing Window | [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM Time Zone] to [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM Time Zone] |
| Report Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Testing Provider | [Internal Security Team / Third-Party Provider Name] |
| Lead Tester | [Name / Role] |
| Organization Contact | [Name / Role] |
| Retest Window | [YYYY-MM-DD] to [YYYY-MM-DD], where applicable |

### Scope Overview

The assessment covered externally accessible and selected internal components that support [Organization Name]’s in-scope services, customer data processing, administrative access, and production operations.

| Scope Area | Included Assets / Description | Testing Type |
|---|---|---|
| Web Applications | [Application names, URLs, portals, APIs] | Authenticated and unauthenticated testing |
| External Network | [IP ranges, domains, cloud endpoints] | External network penetration testing |
| Internal Network | [Internal subnets, VPN-accessible systems, shared services] | Internal network penetration testing |
| Cloud Infrastructure | [Cloud accounts, subscriptions, VPCs/VNETs, storage, IAM configurations] | Configuration and attack path review |
| APIs | [Public/private API endpoints, API gateways] | Authenticated and unauthenticated testing |
| Authentication Services | [SSO, MFA, identity provider, privileged access tooling] | Access control and session testing |
| Administrative Interfaces | [Admin consoles, management portals, bastion hosts] | Role-based authorization testing |
| Supporting Services | [CI/CD, logging platform, monitoring, ticketing integrations] | Limited security review |

### Out-of-Scope Items

The following systems, activities, or techniques were excluded from testing:

| Exclusion | Reason |
|---|---|
| Denial-of-service and stress testing | Avoid disruption to production services |
| Physical security testing | Covered by separate assessment or not applicable |
| Social engineering | Not approved for this engagement |
| Destructive exploit execution | Avoid data loss or service interruption |
| Third-party systems not controlled by [Organization Name] | Legal and contractual limitations |
| Production data extraction beyond proof of access | Protect customer and sensitive data |
| Persistence mechanisms or malware simulation | Not required for this annual test |

### Testing Assumptions and Constraints

- Testing was performed only against systems explicitly approved by [Organization Name].
- The assessment team did not intentionally modify, destroy, or exfiltrate production data.
- Where exploitation was demonstrated, evidence was limited to the minimum necessary to confirm impact.
- Some findings may be influenced by the access level granted, environmental state, rate limits, monitoring alerts, or testing time constraints.
- Vulnerabilities discovered after the testing window are not reflected unless specifically noted.
- Automated scanning results were manually validated where feasible to reduce false positives.
- Testing was conducted in a manner designed to minimize operational disruption.

### Asset Inventory Reviewed

| Asset Identifier | Environment | Owner | Data Sensitivity | In Scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [app.example.com] | Production | [Application Owner] | Customer Data | Yes |
| [api.example.com] | Production | [Engineering Team] | Customer Data | Yes |
| [admin.example.com] | Production | [Operations Team] | Restricted Administrative Access | Yes |
| [VPN / Internal CIDR] | Production | [Infrastructure Team] | Internal Systems | Yes |
| [Cloud Account / Subscription] | Production | [Cloud Platform Team] | Customer and Operational Data | Yes |

## Executive Summary

### Overall Assessment

The annual penetration test identified [number] findings across the in-scope environment, including [number] Critical, [number] High, [number] Medium, [number] Low, and [number] Informational findings.

The assessment found that [Organization Name] has implemented several effective security controls, including:

- Centralized authentication for key administrative interfaces.
- Multi-factor authentication for privileged user access.
- Segmented access to selected production resources.
- Logging and monitoring coverage for externally facing services.
- Secure development practices for common web application risk areas.
- Vulnerability management processes for routine patching.

However, the test also identified areas requiring improvement, particularly in:

- [Example: authorization enforcement within selected application workflows].
- [Example: cloud identity permissions and service account privilege management].
- [Example: exposure of administrative metadata or debug information].
- [Example: remediation timelines for externally exposed vulnerabilities].
- [Example: consistency of security headers and secure session configuration].

Based on the observed results, the tested environment demonstrates a [Strong / Moderate / Developing] security posture. No evidence of active compromise was identified during the assessment; however, several findings could increase the likelihood of unauthorized access, privilege escalation, or sensitive data exposure if left unremediated.

### Summary of Findings by Severity

| Severity | Count | Definition |
|---|---:|---|
| Critical | [0] | Immediate risk of compromise or material business impact; urgent remediation required |
| High | [0] | Significant exploitability or impact; prioritized remediation required |
| Medium | [0] | Meaningful security weakness requiring planned remediation |
| Low | [0] | Limited impact or exploitability; remediate as part of normal security improvement |
| Informational | [0] | Observation or best-practice improvement with minimal direct risk |

### Key Risk Themes

| Theme | Summary | Business Impact |
|---|---|---|
| Access Control | [Example: Inconsistent object-level authorization controls were observed in selected API workflows.] | Potential unauthorized access to customer or administrative data |
| Cloud Permissions | [Example: Several service identities had broader privileges than required for their business function.] | Increased blast radius if credentials are compromised |
| External Exposure | [Example: Legacy services remained reachable from the internet.] | Increased attack surface and likelihood of automated exploitation |
| Secure Configuration | [Example: Security headers and session attributes were inconsistently applied.] | Higher exposure to client-side or session-based attacks |
| Vulnerability Management | [Example: Patch gaps were identified on selected internet-facing systems.] | Increased likelihood of exploitation using known techniques |

### Management Conclusion

Management should prioritize remediation of Critical and High findings immediately, with verified closure through retesting. Medium findings should be remediated through planned engineering or infrastructure work within approved service-level targets. Low and Informational findings should be tracked to completion where they align with risk reduction, defense-in-depth, or compliance commitments.

Remediation ownership should be assigned to accountable business and technical owners, and progress should be tracked through [ticketing system name] until validation is complete.

## Methodology

### Testing Approach

The penetration test followed a risk-based methodology designed to simulate realistic attack techniques while operating within approved legal, operational, and safety constraints. The assessment included both automated and manual testing.

Testing activities included:

1. Scope confirmation and rules of engagement review.
2. Reconnaissance and asset discovery.
3. External attack surface review.
4. Network and service enumeration.
5. Web application and API testing.
6. Authentication and authorization testing.
7. Cloud and identity configuration review.
8. Vulnerability validation and exploitability assessment.
9. Privilege escalation and lateral movement analysis, where approved.
10. Evidence collection and risk rating.
11. Remediation guidance development.
12. Final reporting and stakeholder review.

### Testing Perspectives

| Perspective | Description |
|---|---|
| Unauthenticated External User | Testing from the internet without valid credentials |
| Authenticated Standard User | Testing using a standard user account with typical permissions |
| Authenticated Administrative User | Testing using approved privileged test accounts |
| Internal Network User | Testing from an approved internal or VPN-connected position |
| Cloud Identity Reviewer | Review of selected identity, permission, and configuration paths |
| API Consumer | Testing using approved API credentials and documentation where provided |

### Risk Rating Method

Findings were rated based on a combination of exploitability, business impact, exposure, control effectiveness, affected data, affected users, and likelihood of successful attack.

| Severity | Criteria |
|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitation is straightforward or already demonstrated, with potential for broad compromise, sensitive data exposure, administrative takeover, or material service disruption |
| High | Exploitation is practical and could result in unauthorized access, privilege escalation, significant data exposure, or compromise of important systems |
| Medium | Exploitation requires specific conditions or access but could weaken security controls, expose limited data, or support further compromise |
| Low | Limited exploitability or limited impact, generally requiring additional weaknesses to create meaningful risk |
| Informational | No direct vulnerability confirmed, but improvement is recommended for security posture, consistency, or operational maturity |

### Tools and Techniques Used

The assessment used a combination of commercial tools, open-source tools, custom scripts, and manual testing techniques. Tool output was reviewed by the testing team and validated where practical.

| Category | Examples of Techniques |
|---|---|
| Reconnaissance | DNS review, certificate transparency review, metadata inspection, subdomain discovery |
| Network Testing | Port scanning, service fingerprinting, protocol review, misconfiguration checks |
| Web Application Testing | Input validation testing, session review, access control testing, client-side review |
| API Testing | Endpoint enumeration, token handling review, object access testing, rate-limit review |
| Authentication Testing | MFA workflow review, password policy assessment, session lifecycle testing |
| Authorization Testing | Horizontal and vertical privilege testing, role boundary review |
| Cloud Review | IAM privilege review, storage exposure checks, network security group review |
| Vulnerability Validation | Manual reproduction, exploitability confirmation, compensating control review |

### Evidence Handling

All evidence collected during testing was handled as confidential security information. Evidence was limited to the minimum necessary to demonstrate the finding and support remediation.

Evidence handling requirements included:

- No unnecessary extraction of customer data.
- Redaction of secrets, tokens, personal data, and sensitive business information where possible.
- Storage in [approved secure repository].
- Access limited to authorized personnel.
- Deletion or archival according to [Organization Name] retention requirements.
- Secure transfer of report materials to approved recipients only.

### Operational Safety

The testing team followed the agreed rules of engagement and avoided intentionally disruptive activities. If potentially disruptive behavior was required to validate a finding, the testing team sought approval from [Organization Contact] before proceeding.

Any suspected active compromise, unexpected data exposure, system instability, or critical vulnerability discovered during testing was to be escalated immediately through [incident response contact/channel].

## Detailed Findings / Results (with structure)

### Findings Register

| ID | Finding Title | Severity | Affected Asset(s) | Status | Owner | Target Remediation Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PT-2025-001 | [Example: Broken Object-Level Authorization in Customer API] | High | [api.example.com] | Open | [Engineering Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| PT-2025-002 | [Example: Excessive Cloud Service Account Permissions] | High | [Cloud Account / Project] | Open | [Cloud Platform Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| PT-2025-003 | [Example: Missing Security Headers on Web Application] | Medium | [app.example.com] | Open | [Application Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| PT-2025-004 | [Example: Legacy TLS Configuration on External Service] | Medium | [service.example.com] | Open | [Infrastructure Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| PT-2025-005 | [Example: Verbose Error Messages Disclose Internal Details] | Low | [admin.example.com] | Open | [Engineering Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

---

### Finding PT-2025-001 - [Broken Object-Level Authorization in Customer API]

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Status | Open |
| Affected Asset(s) | [api.example.com], [API endpoint(s)] |
| Environment | Production |
| Business Owner | [Name / Team] |
| Technical Owner | [Name / Team] |
| Date Identified | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Target Remediation Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Validation Method | Authenticated API testing and manual request manipulation |

#### Description

The assessment identified an authorization weakness in [API endpoint/workflow] where an authenticated user could modify request parameters to access or perform actions against resources associated with another user or tenant.

The application authenticated the request successfully but did not consistently verify that the authenticated user was authorized to access the requested object.

#### Evidence

- A standard user account was created or provided for testing: `[test-user-1]`.
- A second standard user account was used as the target object owner: `[test-user-2]`.
- The tester submitted a valid request using `[test-user-1]` credentials.
- The tester modified `[object_id / account_id / tenant_id]` in the request.
- The application returned data or allowed an action associated with `[test-user-2]`.

Sensitive data values were redacted from retained evidence.

#### Impact

If exploited, this weakness could allow an authenticated user to access or manipulate data belonging to another user or tenant. Depending on the affected workflow, this may result in unauthorized disclosure, unauthorized modification, loss of customer trust, contractual impact, and reportable security events.

#### Likelihood

Likelihood is assessed as High because exploitation requires only a valid low-privilege account and predictable or obtainable object identifiers.

#### Root Cause

The likely root cause is insufficient server-side authorization enforcement at the object or tenant boundary. The application appears to rely on request parameters without consistently validating resource ownership against the authenticated user context.

#### Recommendation

Implement centralized server-side authorization checks for all object access and state-changing API requests. Ensure each request validates:

- Authenticated user identity.
- User role and permissions.
- Tenant or account membership.
- Ownership or permitted relationship to the requested object.
- Action-specific authorization.

Add automated regression tests for horizontal and vertical access control scenarios. Review similar endpoints for the same pattern.

#### Remediation Plan

| Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disable or restrict affected endpoint if immediate risk is unacceptable | [Engineering Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Implement object-level authorization checks | [Engineering Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Review related endpoints for similar authorization gaps | [Engineering Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Add automated authorization test coverage | [QA / Engineering Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Retest and validate closure | [Security Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |

### Finding PT-2025-002 - [Excessive Cloud Service Account Permissions]

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Status | Open |
| Affected Asset(s) | [Cloud account/subscription/project], [service account name] |
| Environment | Production |
| Business Owner | [Name / Team] |
| Technical Owner | [Cloud Platform Team] |
| Date Identified | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Target Remediation Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Validation Method | Cloud identity and permission review |

#### Description

The assessment identified one or more service accounts with permissions broader than required for their stated operational purpose. The permissions assigned could allow the service account to read, modify, or administer resources outside its business function.

#### Evidence

The following permission conditions were observed:

| Identity | Observed Permission Concern | Intended Function |
|---|---|---|
| [service-account-1] | [Example: broad administrative permissions across production resources] | [Application deployment] |
| [service-account-2] | [Example: read/write access to multiple storage locations not used by the service] | [Data processing job] |

No exploitation or privilege escalation was performed beyond review and validation of assigned permissions.

#### Impact

If credentials, tokens, workload identity bindings, or execution contexts associated with these service accounts are compromised, an attacker may gain excessive access to production resources. This could lead to unauthorized data access, modification of application components, persistence, or disruption of services.

#### Likelihood

Likelihood is assessed as Medium to High depending on exposure of the service account and how credentials are managed. The potential impact is significant due to the breadth of assigned permissions.

#### Root Cause

The likely root cause is role assignment drift, use of convenience roles during deployment, or lack of periodic review of service account privileges against current operational requirements.

#### Recommendation

Apply least-privilege access for all service accounts and workload identities. Replace broad permissions with scoped custom roles or narrowly assigned managed roles. Implement periodic permission review and alerting for high-risk privilege assignments.

#### Remediation Plan

| Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identify active permissions used by affected service accounts | [Cloud Platform Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Remove unused or excessive permissions | [Cloud Platform Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Replace broad roles with least-privilege alternatives | [Cloud Platform Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Validate application functionality after permission changes | [Engineering Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Add recurring review for privileged service identities | [Security / Cloud Governance] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |

---

### Finding PT-2025-003 - [Missing or Inconsistent Web Security Headers]

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Status | Open |
| Affected Asset(s) | [app.example.com], [admin.example.com] |
| Environment | Production |
| Business Owner | [Name / Team] |
| Technical Owner | [Application / Infrastructure Team] |
| Date Identified | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Target Remediation Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Validation Method | HTTP response inspection and browser-based testing |

#### Description

Selected web application responses did not consistently include recommended browser security headers. These headers help reduce exposure to certain client-side attacks, downgrade risks, content injection, clickjacking, and unintended data handling by browsers.

#### Evidence

| Header | Observed Condition | Affected Asset |
|---|---|---|
| Content Security Policy | [Missing / overly permissive] | [app.example.com] |
| Strict Transport Security | [Missing / incomplete] | [app.example.com] |
| X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors directive | [Missing] | [admin.example.com] |
| Referrer-Policy | [Missing / overly permissive] | [app.example.com] |
| Permissions-Policy | [Missing] | [app.example.com] |

#### Impact

Missing security headers do not typically result in compromise by themselves, but they reduce browser-enforced protections and may increase the impact of other vulnerabilities such as cross-site scripting, clickjacking, or mixed-content issues.

#### Likelihood

Likelihood is assessed as Medium because exploitation usually requires a second weakness or user interaction, but the affected assets are externally accessible.

#### Root Cause

Security header configuration appears to be inconsistently applied across application routes, domains, or reverse proxy configurations.

#### Recommendation

Define and enforce a standard security header baseline across all web applications and administrative portals. Apply headers at a centralized reverse proxy, content delivery network, or application middleware layer where feasible.

#### Remediation Plan

| Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Define approved security header baseline | [Security Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Apply baseline to affected domains | [Infrastructure / Engineering Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Test for application compatibility | [QA / Engineering Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Add automated header checks to deployment pipeline | [DevOps Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Validate remediation | [Security Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |

---

### Finding PT-2025-004 - [Legacy TLS Configuration on External Service]

| Field | Details |
|---|---|

#### Description

The assessment identified legacy or weak transport security configuration on [service.example.com]. The service accepted older protocol versions or cipher suites that do not align with current organizational security expectations.

#### Evidence

Observed configuration included:

| Item | Observed Condition |
|---|---|
| Protocol Support | [Example: legacy protocol accepted] |
| Cipher Suites | [Example: weak or deprecated cipher suites supported] |
| Certificate Chain | [Valid / issue noted] |
| Certificate Expiration | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Redirect Behavior | [HTTP to HTTPS enforced / not enforced] |

#### Impact

Weak transport security settings may expose sessions to downgrade risks, interception under specific network conditions, or noncompliance with customer security expectations. The practical risk depends on client compatibility requirements and exposure.

#### Likelihood

Likelihood is assessed as Medium due to internet exposure and ease of detection by automated tools.

#### Root Cause

The likely root cause is outdated load balancer, web server, or managed service configuration that has not been updated to match the current approved baseline.

#### Recommendation

Update the affected service to use the organization’s approved transport security configuration. Disable legacy protocols and weak cipher suites, enforce secure redirects, and monitor certificate validity.

#### Remediation Plan

| Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Confirm client compatibility requirements | [Product / Engineering Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Update TLS policy on affected service | [Infrastructure Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Validate configuration after deployment | [Security Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Add recurring external configuration checks | [Security Operations] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
