### Finding PT-2025-005 - [Verbose Error Messages Disclose Internal Details]

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Severity | Low |
| Status | Open |
| Affected Asset(s) | [admin.example.com], [app.example.com] |
| Environment | Production |
| Business Owner | [Name / Team] |
| Technical Owner | [Engineering Team] |
| Date Identified | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Target Remediation Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Validation Method | Manual application testing |

#### Description

The application returned verbose error messages that disclosed internal implementation details, such as stack traces, framework versions, database field names, internal paths, or service identifiers.

#### Evidence

Example information disclosed in error responses included:

- [Example: internal class or function name].
- [Example: database table or field reference].
- [Example: backend service hostname].
- [Example: framework version or library name].

Sensitive evidence has been redacted.

#### Impact

Verbose error messages typically do not provide direct access by themselves, but they can assist attackers in reconnaissance and vulnerability development. Internal details may help identify technologies, versions, code paths, or backend components.

#### Likelihood

Likelihood is assessed as Medium because error conditions may be triggered remotely, but impact is limited unless combined with other weaknesses.

#### Root Cause

The likely root cause is insufficient production error handling or debug logging configuration exposed to end users.

#### Recommendation

Configure production applications to return generic user-facing error messages while logging detailed diagnostics securely to internal logging systems. Ensure debug mode is disabled in production.

#### Remediation Plan

| Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disable verbose error output in production | [Engineering Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Confirm detailed errors are routed to secure logs only | [Engineering / Operations Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Review application routes for similar behavior | [Engineering Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |
| Validate remediation | [Security Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Open/In Progress/Complete] |

---

### Positive Security Observations

The following controls were observed to be operating effectively during the assessment:

| Area | Observation |
|---|---|
| Multi-Factor Authentication | MFA was enforced for tested administrative accounts |
| Account Lockout / Rate Limiting | Authentication workflows included controls to reduce automated guessing |
| Logging | Security-relevant events were visible in centralized logging for selected systems |
| Network Segmentation | Direct access to selected internal resources was restricted |
| Secret Handling | No hardcoded production secrets were identified in the tested web responses |
| Patch Management | Most externally visible services appeared to be maintained on supported versions |

### No-Finding Test Areas

The following areas were tested, and no exploitable finding was confirmed during the assessment window:

| Area Tested | Result |
|---|---|
| SQL injection testing on selected forms and API endpoints | No exploitable condition confirmed |
| Cross-site scripting testing on selected workflows | No exploitable condition confirmed |
| Authentication bypass attempts | No successful bypass confirmed |
| Password reset workflow testing | No material weakness confirmed |
| Session termination testing | No material weakness confirmed |
| Public storage exposure checks | No publicly accessible sensitive storage confirmed |
| Basic external port exposure review | No unexpected high-risk open services confirmed |

## Analysis

### Security Posture Assessment

The results indicate that [Organization Name] maintains a functioning security control environment with several effective preventive and detective controls. The organization demonstrates attention to authentication, monitoring, and secure configuration in key areas.

The most significant risk identified relates to authorization consistency in application and API workflows. Authorization defects can create direct exposure to customer data and are often difficult for perimeter controls to detect or prevent. These issues should be prioritized for remediation and regression testing.

Cloud identity permissions were also identified as an important risk area. Excessive permissions increase the potential impact of credential compromise, software defects, or misconfigured workloads. A structured least-privilege review should be performed, especially for production service accounts and automation identities.

Configuration issues such as security headers, TLS settings, and verbose errors represent defense-in-depth gaps. While these findings are less likely to cause direct compromise independently, they reduce the organization’s resilience and may increase the effectiveness of other attacks.

### Severity Distribution

| Severity | Count | Percentage |
|---|---:|---:|
| Critical | [0] | [0%] |
| High | [2] | [40%] |
| Medium | [2] | [40%] |
| Low | [1] | [20%] |
| Informational | [0] | [0%] |
| Total | [5] | [100%] |

### Risk by Environment

| Environment | Finding Count | Highest Severity | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Production | [5] | High | Primary focus of testing and remediation |
| Staging | [0] | N/A | [Not included / No findings] |
| Development | [0] | N/A | [Not included / No findings] |
| Corporate/Internal | [0] | N/A | [Not included / No findings] |

### Risk by Control Theme

| Theme | Finding Count | Highest Severity | Analysis |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Authorization | [1] | High | Requires immediate engineering focus and regression testing |
| Identity and Access Management | [1] | High | Cloud privilege scope should be reduced and monitored |
| Secure Configuration | [2] | Medium | Baseline standards should be applied consistently |
| Information Disclosure | [1] | Low | Production error handling should be hardened |
| Monitoring and Detection | [0] | N/A | No finding raised, but alert validation should continue |

### Exploitability Summary

| Finding ID | Exploitability | Attack Prerequisites |
|---|---|---|
| PT-2025-001 | Practical | Valid user account and object identifier |
| PT-2025-002 | Conditional | Compromise or misuse of service account context |
| PT-2025-003 | Conditional | User interaction or supporting client-side weakness |
| PT-2025-004 | Conditional | Network position or client downgrade opportunity |
| PT-2025-005 | Easy to trigger, limited direct impact | Ability to submit malformed or unexpected requests |

### Business Impact Summary

The identified findings could affect the business in the following ways:

- Unauthorized access to customer or tenant-specific data.
- Increased impact of compromised cloud identities.
- Greater exposure of externally accessible systems to automated reconnaissance.
- Reduced customer confidence if findings are not remediated promptly.
- Increased effort required to demonstrate effective risk management during customer, audit, or due diligence reviews.

No confirmed evidence of active exploitation, malware, unauthorized persistence, or material data exfiltration was identified during the assessment.

### Control Effectiveness Observations

| Control Area | Observed Effectiveness | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Preventive Controls | Partially Effective | Authentication and perimeter protections were present, but authorization gaps were identified |
| Detective Controls | Generally Effective | Logging was present, though alert validation was not fully tested for every finding |
| Corrective Controls | To Be Determined | Effectiveness depends on timely remediation and retesting |
| Configuration Management | Needs Improvement | Inconsistent secure configuration was observed across services |
| Access Management | Needs Improvement | Service account privileges require tightening |

## Recommendations & Actions

### Remediation Priorities

| Priority | Required Action | Target Timeline |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate | Address any Critical findings, if identified | Within [7] calendar days |
| High | Remediate High findings and perform security retesting | Within [30] calendar days |
| Medium | Remediate Medium findings through planned release or infrastructure change | Within [60-90] calendar days |
| Low | Remediate Low findings as part of normal backlog and hardening work | Within [120] calendar days |
| Informational | Track improvement items where appropriate | As agreed by management |

### Consolidated Action Plan

| Action ID | Related Finding(s) | Action | Owner | Due Date | Success Criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AP-001 | PT-2025-001 | Implement server-side object-level authorization for affected API workflows | [Engineering Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Unauthorized cross-user or cross-tenant access is no longer possible |
| AP-002 | PT-2025-001 | Add automated access control regression tests | [Engineering / QA Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Test suite covers horizontal and vertical authorization scenarios |
| AP-003 | PT-2025-002 | Reduce excessive service account privileges | [Cloud Platform Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Service identities have only required permissions |
| AP-004 | PT-2025-002 | Establish recurring privileged identity review | [Security Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Review evidence is retained and exceptions are approved |
| AP-005 | PT-2025-003 | Apply standard web security headers | [Infrastructure / Engineering Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | All in-scope web assets pass approved header baseline checks |
| AP-006 | PT-2025-004 | Update external TLS configuration | [Infrastructure Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Legacy protocol and weak cipher support removed |
| AP-007 | PT-2025-005 | Replace verbose user-facing errors with generic production errors | [Engineering Owner] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Internal diagnostic details are no longer exposed to users |
| AP-008 | All | Complete retesting of remediated findings | [Security Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Closure evidence is documented and approved |

### Recommended Management Actions

Management should ensure that:

- Each finding has a named technical owner and business owner.
- Remediation timelines are approved based on risk and operational feasibility.
- Exceptions or delays are documented, risk accepted by appropriate management, and assigned an expiration date.
- Remediation evidence is retained in [ticketing system / GRC platform / evidence repository].
- High-risk findings are retested by the security team or independent tester.
- Lessons learned are fed into secure development, cloud governance, and vulnerability management processes.
- Similar assets not included in the test are reviewed for the same weaknesses.

### Recommended Engineering Actions

Engineering teams should:

- Review authorization controls across all application and API endpoints, not only the sampled endpoints.
- Add automated test coverage for role, tenant, account, and object boundary enforcement.
- Use centralized middleware or shared authorization services where feasible.
- Ensure production debug behavior is disabled by default.
- Include secure header and TLS checks in build, deployment, or infrastructure validation processes.
- Review logging to confirm suspicious authorization failures and privilege changes are detectable.

### Recommended Cloud and Infrastructure Actions

Cloud and infrastructure teams should:

- Perform a least-privilege review of all production service accounts and workload identities.
- Identify and remove unused permissions, stale identities, and unnecessary administrative assignments.
- Enforce approved baseline configurations for externally exposed services.
- Monitor for creation or assignment of high-risk privileges.
- Maintain evidence of privilege reviews and remediation activities.
- Apply configuration compliance checks through infrastructure-as-code or cloud posture management tooling where available.

### Retesting Plan

| Retest Activity | Responsible Party | Planned Date | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validate PT-2025-001 remediation | [Security Team / Testing Provider] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Reproduction attempt fails; authorization tests pass |
| Validate PT-2025-002 remediation | [Security Team / Cloud Platform Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Permission comparison before and after remediation |
| Validate PT-2025-003 remediation | [Security Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Header scan results and manual confirmation |
| Validate PT-2025-004 remediation | [Security Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | TLS configuration scan results |
| Validate PT-2025-005 remediation | [Security Team] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Error handling screenshots or response samples |

### Exception Handling

If a finding cannot be remediated within the target timeline, the owner must document:

- Business reason for delay.
- Compensating controls in place.
- Residual risk assessment.
- Revised remediation date.
- Approver name and role.
- Expiration date for the exception.

Exceptions must be reviewed periodically and must not be treated as permanent unless formally approved by executive risk ownership.

### Evidence Retention

The following evidence should be retained for audit and management review:

| Evidence Type | Location | Retention Expectation |
|---|---|---|
| Final penetration test report | [Secure repository / GRC platform] | [Retention period] |
| Rules of engagement | [Secure repository] | [Retention period] |
| Scope approval | [Secure repository / ticket] | [Retention period] |
| Finding evidence | [Secure evidence repository] | [Retention period] |
| Remediation tickets | [Ticketing system] | [Retention period] |
| Retest evidence | [Secure repository / GRC platform] | [Retention period] |
| Risk acceptance records | [GRC platform] | [Retention period] |

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Classification

This report is classified as Confidential - Restricted Distribution. It contains sensitive security information, including vulnerabilities, affected assets, technical evidence, and remediation details. Unauthorized disclosure could increase risk to [Organization Name], its customers, and its service environment.

### Approved Recipients

### Handling Requirements

Recipients must:

- Not forward the report outside approved distribution without authorization.
- Not upload the report to public or unapproved external platforms.
- Redact sensitive details before sharing excerpts with customers or third parties.
- Use secure transfer methods for any approved external distribution.

### External Sharing

External sharing requires approval from [CISO / Security Owner / Legal Contact]. Where customer or third-party sharing is required, [Organization Name] should provide an executive summary or sanitized attestation-style version unless the full report is contractually required and approved.

The information contained in this report must not be disclosed, copied, distributed, or used for any purpose other than authorized remediation, governance, or assurance activities.

SOC2-027.title: Backup & Restore Records
SOC2-027.content:
## What This Evidences

Backup & Restore Records evidence that the organisation performs backups and validates restoration capability to support system availability under SOC 2 A1.2 (Availability). This artifact demonstrates that critical systems and data can be recovered in line with defined recovery objectives.

This is operational evidence and must be collected from the organisation’s actual backup, monitoring, logging, or ticketing systems. It must not be authored manually as a policy-style document or fabricated after the fact.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect Backup & Restore Records from the systems that generate or track backup execution and restore testing, such as:

- Backup platform: [Backup Tool Name], for example cloud backup, database backup, snapshot, or endpoint backup tooling
- Cloud provider console: [Cloud Provider Name], for example snapshot, image, object storage, or managed database backup logs
- SIEM or log store: [SIEM/Log Platform Name], where backup job events are forwarded
- ITSM/ticketing system: [ITSM Tool Name], where restore tests, incidents, and recovery activities are tracked
- Monitoring/dashboard tool: [Monitoring Tool Name], where backup success/failure alerts and job status are displayed
- Database administration tools: [Database Platform Name], for transaction log backups, point-in-time recovery, or dump files

## How To Collect

1. Identify the in-scope systems supporting customer-facing services and critical internal operations.
2. In [Backup Tool Name] or [Cloud Provider Name], filter backup jobs for the audit period: [Start Date] to [End Date].
3. Export backup job history showing successful, failed, and retried jobs for the in-scope systems.
4. Filter by system, workload, database, storage bucket, virtual machine, container volume, or application name as applicable.
5. Export restore activity logs for the same period, including production restores, test restores, and disaster recovery exercises.
6. In [ITSM Tool Name], export restore test tickets or change records linked to recovery testing.
7. In [SIEM/Log Platform Name], export corroborating logs if backup or restore events are forwarded centrally.
8. Capture screenshots of relevant dashboards only where exports are unavailable or where dashboard status is needed to show configuration and scope.
9. Save all exports in their native report format where possible, such as CSV, PDF, JSON, or system-generated audit report.
10. Record the collection date, collector name, source system, filters used, and audit period covered.

## What To Capture

Evidence should include enough detail to prove backups occurred and restore capability was tested. Capture:

- Backup job name or identifier
- System, application, database, storage location, or asset backed up
- Backup type, such as full, incremental, differential, snapshot, image, transaction log, or object replication
- Scheduled date/time and actual start/end time
- Backup status: success, failure, warning, retry, or cancelled
- Failure reason and remediation where applicable
- Backup retention period or expiry date
- Backup destination, vault, repository, region, or storage account
- Encryption status, where visible
- Restore job name or identifier
- Restore test date/time
- Restored system, dataset, database, file, snapshot, or object
- Restore target environment, such as test, staging, recovery environment, or production
- Restore result: successful, partially successful, failed, or aborted
- Evidence of validation, such as application start, database consistency check, file integrity check, user acceptance, or monitoring confirmation
- Operator or approver name
- Related ITSM ticket, change record, incident, or test plan reference
- Screenshots or exports showing date filters and system scope

## Frequency & Owner

- Collection frequency: At least quarterly for audit evidence, and after each formal restore test or material recovery event.
- Backup monitoring frequency: Daily or continuous, depending on system criticality.
- Restore testing frequency: At least annually for critical systems, and more frequently where recovery objectives require it.
- Evidence owner: [Infrastructure/Platform Operations Owner]
- Supporting teams: [Database Team], [Cloud Operations Team], [Security Operations Team], [Service Desk/ITSM Owner]

## Retention & Storage

Store collected evidence in [Evidence Repository Name] under a restricted-access folder for the relevant audit period. Retain records for [Retention Period], or longer if required by customer commitments, legal obligations, or audit requirements.

Evidence should be read-only after collection where practical. Access should be limited to authorised personnel in [GRC Team], [IT Operations], and [Audit Support Team]. Preserve original exports and avoid editing raw logs.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence when it:

- Comes directly from [Backup Tool Name], [Cloud Provider Name], [SIEM/Log Platform Name], or [ITSM Tool Name]
- Covers the full audit period or a clearly defined sample period requested by the auditor
- Shows backup activity for all in-scope critical systems
- Includes both successful and failed backup events, with remediation for failures
- Shows that restore testing occurred, not only that backups exist
- Includes restore validation results demonstrating usable recovery
- Identifies dates, systems, job status, operators, and related tickets or approvals
- Is complete, timestamped, and traceable to source systems
- Is stored in the approved evidence repository with collection metadata
- Does not rely solely on manual statements or screenshots without supporting system-generated records

SOC2-028.content:
## Disaster Recovery Test Records (DOCX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| DR Test Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this DR test record, using a consistent format such as DR-YYYY-###. |
| Exercise Name | Enter the formal name of the annual disaster recovery exercise. |
| Exercise Type | Enter the type of DR exercise performed; allowed values: Tabletop, Technical Failover, Backup Restore, Full Interruption, Partial Interruption, Other. |
| Test Date | Enter the date the DR exercise was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Test Start Time | Enter the time the test began in 24-hour format with timezone, e.g., 09:00 UTC. |
| Test End Time | Enter the time the test ended in 24-hour format with timezone, e.g., 13:30 UTC. |
| Business Process or Service Tested | Enter the customer-facing or internal business process supported by the system tested, e.g., Production SaaS Platform, Customer Support Portal, Billing Operations. |
| System or Application Tested | Enter the specific system, application, platform, database, or infrastructure component included in scope. |
| Environment Tested | Enter the environment used for the exercise; allowed values: Production, Staging, DR Environment, Test, Other. |
| DR Scenario Simulated | Describe the disruption scenario tested, such as region outage, database corruption, ransomware recovery, loss of primary cloud service, or backup restore failure. |
| Test Objective | State the specific objective of the test, including what recovery capability was intended to be demonstrated. |
| Criticality Tier | Enter the business criticality assigned to the system or service; allowed values: Tier 1 Critical, Tier 2 High, Tier 3 Medium, Tier 4 Low, Not Classified. |
| Defined RTO | Enter the approved recovery time objective for the system or service using hours/minutes, e.g., 4 hours or 30 minutes. |
| Defined RPO | Enter the approved recovery point objective for the system or service using hours/minutes, e.g., 1 hour or 15 minutes. |
| Actual Recovery Time | Enter the elapsed time from declared start of recovery to confirmed service restoration using hours/minutes; enter N/A if not measured in the exercise type. |
| Actual Data Loss | Enter the measured data loss or recovery point gap using hours/minutes or state 0 if no data loss occurred; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| RTO Met | Indicate whether actual recovery time met the defined RTO; allowed values: Yes, No, N/A. |
| RPO Met | Indicate whether actual data loss met the defined RPO; allowed values: Yes, No, N/A. |
| Recovery Procedure or Runbook Used | Enter the name, version, and location of the disaster recovery plan, runbook, or documented procedure followed during the test. |
| Recovery Steps Performed | Summarise the key recovery steps actually performed, including failover, restore, validation, rollback, or communications steps. |
| Primary Personnel Involved | List internal roles or names involved in the exercise, such as Incident Commander, Infrastructure Lead, Database Administrator, Application Owner. |
| Third Parties or Vendors Involved | List any external service providers, cloud providers, managed service providers, or vendors involved; enter None if not applicable. |
| Communications Tested | Describe the internal or external communications tested, such as incident bridge, executive notifications, customer status page, vendor escalation; enter Not Tested if out of scope. |
| Monitoring and Alerting Tested | Describe monitoring, alerting, or logging mechanisms used to detect, track, or validate the recovery; enter Not Tested if out of scope. |
| Backup or Replication Source Used | Identify the backup set, snapshot, replica, region, storage location, or recovery source used during the exercise. |
| Validation Performed | Describe how successful recovery was validated, such as application health checks, user acceptance testing, transaction testing, data integrity checks, or monitoring confirmation. |
| Test Result | Enter the overall outcome; allowed values: Pass, Pass with Exceptions, Fail, Incomplete. |
| Issues or Exceptions Identified | Record any gaps, delays, failed steps, missing documentation, tooling issues, communication failures, or control exceptions; enter None if no issues were identified. |
| Corrective Action Required | Describe the remediation or improvement required to address identified issues; enter None if no corrective action is required. |
| Corrective Action Owner | Enter the role or named individual responsible for completing the corrective action; enter N/A if no corrective action is required. |
| Corrective Action Due Date | Enter the due date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no corrective action is required. |
| Corrective Action Status | Enter the current remediation status; allowed values: Not Started, In Progress, Complete, Overdue, Accepted Risk, N/A. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the link or repository path to supporting evidence such as test plan, meeting notes, screenshots, logs, tickets, backup restore reports, monitoring dashboards, approvals, and post-exercise review. |
| Management Review Date | Enter the date management reviewed the DR test results in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Management Reviewer | Enter the name and role of the management reviewer who assessed the exercise results and exceptions. |
| Approval Status | Enter management approval status for the completed record; allowed values: Draft, Reviewed, Approved, Rejected. |
| Last Updated | Enter the date this record was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |

### Maintenance

The Business Continuity or Information Security owner maintains this template, with input from Engineering, Infrastructure, and application owners. It is updated at least annually after the DR exercise and whenever DR procedures, RTO/RPO targets, critical systems, or source evidence repositories change; source data is drawn from the DR plan/runbooks, backup and replication platforms, monitoring tools, incident management system, ticketing system, and evidence repository.

field_guidance.Business Process or Service Tested: Enter the customer-facing or internal business process supported by the system tested, e.g., Production SaaS Platform, Customer Support Portal, Billing Operations.
field_guidance.System or Application Tested: Enter the specific system, application, platform, database, or infrastructure component included in scope.
field_guidance.Environment Tested: Enter the environment used for the exercise; allowed values: Production, Staging, DR Environment, Test, Other.
field_guidance.DR Scenario Simulated: Describe the disruption scenario tested, such as region outage, database corruption, ransomware recovery, loss of primary cloud service, or backup restore failure.
field_guidance.Test Objective: State the specific objective of the test, including what recovery capability was intended to be demonstrated.
field_guidance.Criticality Tier: Enter the business criticality assigned to the system or service; allowed values: Tier 1 Critical, Tier 2 High, Tier 3 Medium, Tier 4 Low, Not Classified.
field_guidance.Defined RTO: Enter the approved recovery time objective for the system or service using hours/minutes, e.g., 4 hours or 30 minutes.
field_guidance.Defined RPO: Enter the approved recovery point objective for the system or service using hours/minutes, e.g., 1 hour or 15 minutes.
field_guidance.Actual Recovery Time: Enter the elapsed time from declared start of recovery to confirmed service restoration using hours/minutes; enter N/A if not measured in the exercise type.
field_guidance.Actual Data Loss: Enter the measured data loss or recovery point gap using hours/minutes or state 0 if no data loss occurred; enter N/A if not applicable.
field_guidance.RTO Met: Indicate whether actual recovery time met the defined RTO; allowed values: Yes, No, N/A.
field_guidance.RPO Met: Indicate whether actual data loss met the defined RPO; allowed values: Yes, No, N/A.
field_guidance.Recovery Procedure or Runbook Used: Enter the name, version, and location of the disaster recovery plan, runbook, or documented procedure followed during the test.
field_guidance.Recovery Steps Performed: Summarise the key recovery steps actually performed, including failover, restore, validation, rollback, or communications steps.
field_guidance.Primary Personnel Involved: List internal roles or names involved in the exercise, such as Incident Commander, Infrastructure Lead, Database Administrator, Application Owner.
field_guidance.Third Parties or Vendors Involved: List any external service providers, cloud providers, managed service providers, or vendors involved; enter None if not applicable.
field_guidance.Communications Tested: Describe the internal or external communications tested, such as incident bridge, executive notifications, customer status page, vendor escalation; enter Not Tested if out of scope.
field_guidance.Monitoring and Alerting Tested: Describe monitoring, alerting, or logging mechanisms used to detect, track, or validate the recovery; enter Not Tested if out of scope.
field_guidance.Backup or Replication Source Used: Identify the backup set, snapshot, replica, region, storage location, or recovery source used during the exercise.
field_guidance.Validation Performed: Describe how successful recovery was validated, such as application health checks, user acceptance testing, transaction testing, data integrity checks, or monitoring confirmation.
field_guidance.Test Result: Enter the overall outcome; allowed values: Pass, Pass with Exceptions, Fail, Incomplete.
field_guidance.Issues or Exceptions Identified: Record any gaps, delays, failed steps, missing documentation, tooling issues, communication failures, or control exceptions; enter None if no issues were identified.
field_guidance.Corrective Action Required: Describe the remediation or improvement required to address identified issues; enter None if no corrective action is required.
field_guidance.Corrective Action Owner: Enter the role or named individual responsible for completing the corrective action; enter N/A if no corrective action is required.
field_guidance.Corrective Action Due Date: Enter the due date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no corrective action is required.
field_guidance.Corrective Action Status: Enter the current remediation status; allowed values: Not Started, In Progress, Complete, Overdue, Accepted Risk, N/A.
field_guidance.Evidence Location: Enter the link or repository path to supporting evidence such as test plan, meeting notes, screenshots, logs, tickets, backup restore reports, monitoring dashboards, approvals, and post-exercise review.
field_guidance.Management Review Date: Enter the date management reviewed the DR test results in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Management Reviewer: Enter the name and role of the management reviewer who assessed the exercise results and exceptions.
field_guidance.Approval Status: Enter management approval status for the completed record; allowed values: Draft, Reviewed, Approved, Rejected.
field_guidance.Control Reference: Enter the applicable control reference, e.g., SOC 2 A1.3.
field_guidance.Last Updated: Enter the date this record was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format.

SOC2-029.title: Capacity Monitoring Records
SOC2-029.content:
## What This Evidences

Capacity Monitoring Records evidence that the organisation monitors infrastructure and service capacity to support system availability commitments under SOC 2 availability control A1.1. This shows that capacity trends, utilisation thresholds, and potential resource constraints are tracked so the organisation can plan scaling, remediation, or service changes before availability is affected.

This artifact is collected evidence, not an authored document. Do not create a narrative record manually. Collect screenshots, exports, or reports directly from the organisation’s monitoring, observability, cloud, or operational dashboard systems.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect capacity monitoring evidence from the operational systems that track infrastructure and application utilisation, such as:

- Observability or monitoring platform: [Datadog/New Relic/Dynatrace/Prometheus/Grafana/CloudWatch/Azure Monitor/Google Cloud Monitoring]
- Cloud provider dashboards: [AWS/Azure/GCP] capacity, compute, storage, database, network, and autoscaling metrics
- Kubernetes/container platform: [EKS/AKS/GKE/OpenShift] cluster, node, pod, CPU, memory, and storage dashboards
- Database monitoring: [RDS/Cloud SQL/Azure SQL/Oracle/SQL Server monitoring tool]
- ITSM or operations portal: [ServiceNow/Jira Service Management] for capacity-related alerts, incidents, or change records
- BI or executive operations dashboard: [internal portal/tool name] if it aggregates capacity metrics from source systems

Use the system of record where capacity data is generated or automatically aggregated.

## How To Collect

1. Log in to [monitoring/tool name] using an account with read-only or reporting access.
2. Navigate to the production environment dashboard for [system/service/application name].
3. Set the time range to the required review period, typically the prior [30/60/90] days or the audit sample period.
4. Filter to production workloads only, unless the control scope includes non-production environments.
5. Open dashboards showing key capacity dimensions, including compute, memory, storage, database, network, queue depth, and scaling activity as applicable.
6. Confirm the dashboard displays timestamps, metric names, system names, and thresholds or alert indicators.
7. Export the dashboard/report to PDF or CSV where supported.
8. If export is not available, capture full-screen screenshots showing the browser URL, timestamp, dashboard title, environment, and metric legends.
9. Collect related alert or ticket records for any threshold breaches, saturation events, or scaling actions during the period.
10. Save the evidence package to the approved audit evidence repository using the naming standard: `[YYYY-MM-DD] Capacity Monitoring - [System] - [Period]`.

## What To Capture

Capture enough detail to prove active capacity monitoring and planning. Include:

- Dashboard name and source system: [tool name]
- Environment: production / customer-facing / in-scope service
- System, application, cluster, database, or service name
- Time period covered
- CPU utilisation trends
- Memory utilisation trends
- Disk/storage utilisation and growth trends
- Database capacity metrics, where applicable
- Network throughput or bandwidth utilisation, where applicable
- Queue depth, connection pool, worker, or thread utilisation, where applicable
- Autoscaling group or container scaling activity, where applicable
- Capacity thresholds, alert levels, or saturation indicators
- Current utilisation versus provisioned capacity
- Forecasting, trendline, or growth projection, if available
- Alert history for capacity-related events
- Linked incident, problem, or change tickets for capacity actions
- Evidence timestamp and collector name, if available from the tool or export

## Frequency & Owner

- Frequency: collect at least monthly, and additionally before each SOC 2 audit evidence request or after major infrastructure changes.
- Owner: [Infrastructure Operations Owner / SRE Manager / Cloud Operations Lead].
- Reviewer: [Head of Engineering / Platform Owner / Information Security Manager], where formal review is required.
- Backup Owner: [Named backup role].

## Retention & Storage

Store exported reports, screenshots, and related tickets in [GRC platform/evidence repository/document management system]. Restrict access to authorised audit, security, and operations personnel.

Retain records for at least [retention period, e.g. 12-24 months] or longer if required by customer commitments, audit cycle, or legal requirements. Preserve original exports where possible and avoid editing screenshots or reports except for approved redaction of secrets or personal data.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence when it:

- Comes directly from an operational monitoring, cloud, observability, or ITSM system
- Covers the relevant SOC 2 audit period or requested sample period
- Clearly identifies the in-scope production system or service
- Shows capacity metrics over time, not only a single point-in-time value
- Includes key utilisation dimensions such as compute, memory, storage, database, and network where applicable
- Shows thresholds, alerts, trendlines, or scaling indicators used for capacity management
- Demonstrates that capacity issues are detected and followed up through alerts, tickets, changes, or scaling actions
- Includes timestamps and source system context
- Is retained in the approved evidence repository with a clear file name and collection date
- Is complete enough for the auditor to understand how the organisation monitors capacity to support availability commitments

SOC2-030.title: Incident Tickets & Post-Mortems
SOC2-030.content:
## What This Evidences

Incident Tickets & Post-Mortems evidence that [Organization Name] identifies, tracks, responds to, resolves, and reviews security incidents in a controlled and repeatable manner. For SOC 2 control CC7.4, this record demonstrates that potential and confirmed security incidents are investigated, assigned, escalated where necessary, remediated, and reviewed for lessons learned.

This artifact is **collected, not authored**. Do not create a standalone document to satisfy this evidence request. Collect the actual operational records from [ITSM/Ticketing System], [Incident Management Platform], [SIEM/Log Management Platform], and any associated post-incident review documentation used by the organization.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect records from the systems where incident response activity is actually managed, such as:

- ITSM or ticketing system: [Jira Service Management / ServiceNow / Zendesk / Freshservice / Other]
- Incident management platform: [PagerDuty / Opsgenie / FireHydrant / Rootly / Other]
- Security monitoring system: [SIEM Tool / EDR Console / Cloud Security Platform]
- Documentation or knowledge base: [Confluence / SharePoint / Google Drive / Notion / Other]
- Communications archive, if used for incident coordination: [Slack / Microsoft Teams / Email]

The primary source should be the system of record for incidents, typically [ITSM/Ticketing System] or [Incident Management Platform].

## How To Collect

1. Log in to [ITSM/Ticketing System] or [Incident Management Platform] using an account with read access to incident records.
2. Filter records for the audit period: [Start Date] to [End Date].
3. Apply filters for security-related incidents, such as:
 - Type/category: `Security Incident`, `Security Event`, `Privacy Incident`, `Data Incident`
 - Priority/severity: [Severity Levels Used]
 - Assignment group: [Security Team / SOC / IT Operations]
4. Export the filtered incident list to CSV, XLSX, or PDF.
5. For a representative sample, open each selected ticket and export or save the full ticket detail.
6. Collect linked evidence referenced in the ticket, such as SIEM alerts, EDR detections, investigation notes, containment actions, change records, and closure approvals.
7. For incidents requiring review, collect the associated post-mortem, after-action review, or lessons-learned record from [Documentation Platform].
8. Save all exports and supporting files to the audit evidence location: [Evidence Repository Path].
9. Ensure file names include the audit period and collection date, for example: `incident-tickets-postmortems-[YYYY-MM-DD].pdf`.

## What To Capture

Capture enough detail to show the incident lifecycle from detection through closure. Include:

- Incident/ticket ID
- Title or summary
- Date and time opened
- Detection source, such as SIEM alert, user report, EDR alert, vendor notification, or monitoring dashboard
- Incident category/type
- Severity or priority
- Assigned owner/team
- Timeline of investigation and response activity
- Impact assessment, including affected systems, users, data, or services
- Containment, eradication, and recovery actions
- Escalations and approvals, if applicable
- Communications or stakeholder notifications, if applicable
- Root cause or suspected cause
- Closure date and closure rationale
- Linked alerts, logs, screenshots, or forensic notes
- Post-mortem or lessons learned, where applicable
- Corrective actions, follow-up tasks, and their completion status

## Frequency & Owner

- **Collection frequency:** At least quarterly for audit readiness, and additionally at the end of the SOC 2 review period.
- **Operational update frequency:** Incident tickets should be updated throughout the incident lifecycle.
- **Owner:** [Security Operations Manager / Incident Response Lead / IT Operations Manager].
- **Evidence collector:** [GRC Owner / Compliance Manager / Security Analyst].

## Retention & Storage

Store exported evidence in [Evidence Repository] with access limited to [Security], [GRC], and authorized audit stakeholders. Retain incident tickets, post-mortems, and supporting evidence for at least [Retention Period], or longer if required by customer, legal, contractual, or regulatory obligations.

Preserve records in a read-only or access-controlled location to prevent alteration. Do not delete, overwrite, or modify source incident records after collection.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will typically accept this evidence if it shows:

- Actual incident records from the organization’s operational systems, not manually recreated summaries
- Coverage of the SOC 2 review period
- Clear linkage between detected events and tracked incident response activity
- Assigned ownership and documented investigation steps
- Evidence of containment, remediation, recovery, and closure
- Severity or priority classification
- Timely updates and resolution activity
- Post-mortems or lessons learned for significant incidents
- Follow-up corrective actions tracked to completion or documented as in progress
- Exported records with timestamps, ticket IDs, system source, and sufficient detail to verify authenticity and completeness

SOC2-031.content:

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Vendor / Subservice Organization Name | Enter the legal or contracted name of the vendor, service provider, or subservice organization whose SOC report or due diligence evidence is being reviewed. |
| Service Provided | Describe the outsourced service, platform, infrastructure, processing activity, or dependency provided by the vendor; be specific enough to link the service to business processes or systems. |
| Business Owner | Enter the internal business owner accountable for the relationship or service consumption; use name and role/title. |
| Vendor Owner | Enter the internal procurement, vendor management, or third-party risk owner responsible for maintaining the vendor record; use name and role/title. |
| Criticality / Inherent Risk Rating | Enter the vendor risk tier before considering SOC report results; allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low. |
| Data / System Access Type | Describe the type of data processed or system access provided; include whether the vendor accesses confidential data, customer data, production systems, cloud infrastructure, or no sensitive access. |
| SOC Report Type | Enter the report type reviewed; allowed values: SOC 1 Type I, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type I, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISO 27001, Other Due Diligence Evidence, Not Available. |
| SOC Report Period Start | Enter the first day of the audit period covered by the SOC report in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no SOC report is available. |
| SOC Report Period End | Enter the last day of the audit period covered by the SOC report in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no SOC report is available. |
| SOC Report Issue Date | Enter the date the independent auditor issued the report in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no SOC report is available. |
| Report Coverage / Scope Reviewed | Summarize the systems, locations, services, control domains, and boundaries covered by the report, and note any exclusions relevant to the organization’s use of the vendor. |
| Trust Services Criteria Covered | For SOC 2 reports, list the Trust Services Criteria covered; allowed values include Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, Privacy; enter N/A for non-SOC 2 evidence. |
| Complementary User Entity Controls (CUECs) Applicable | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the report identifies CUECs that the organization must operate for the vendor’s controls to be effective. |
| CUEC Owner(s) | If CUECs are applicable, enter the internal control owner(s) responsible for implementing and evidencing them; enter N/A if none apply. |
| CUEC Implementation Status | Record whether applicable CUECs have been mapped and implemented; allowed values: Implemented, Partially Implemented, Not Implemented, Not Assessed, N/A. |
| Complementary Subservice Organization Controls (CSOCs) Noted | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the report identifies controls expected to be performed by downstream subservice organizations. |
| Subservice Organizations Identified | List material subservice organizations named in the report that support the vendor’s service, or enter None Identified; include any relevant dependency such as cloud hosting, data center, payment processor, or managed service provider. |
| Subservice Method | Enter the SOC reporting method used for subservice organizations; allowed values: Inclusive, Carve-Out, Mixed, Not Stated, N/A. |
| Auditor Opinion | Record the independent service auditor’s opinion; allowed values: Unqualified, Qualified, Adverse, Disclaimer, N/A. |
| Exceptions / Deviations Identified | Summarize control exceptions, testing deviations, qualifications, significant observations, or note No Exceptions Identified; include report section or control reference where possible. |
| Exception Severity | Assess the severity of identified exceptions to the organization; allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low, None. |
| Management Response / Remediation Summary | Summarize vendor management’s response, remediation plan, compensating controls, or explanation for noted exceptions; enter N/A if no exceptions. |
| Impact Assessment on Organization | Document the internal assessment of whether report gaps, exceptions, scope exclusions, CUECs, or subservice dependencies affect the organization’s security, availability, confidentiality, processing integrity, or privacy commitments. |
| Follow-Up Actions Required | List required follow-up actions such as request clarification, obtain bridge letter, validate CUECs, perform compensating review, escalate risk acceptance, or enter None. |
| Action Owner | Enter the internal person or role responsible for completing follow-up actions; enter N/A if no follow-up is required. |
| Action Due Date | Enter the target completion date for follow-up actions in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no follow-up is required. |
| Action Status | Track the current status of follow-up actions; allowed values: Not Started, In Progress, Pending Vendor, Complete, Overdue, N/A. |
| Bridge Letter Required | Enter Yes or No based on whether the SOC report period end date does not cover the current review period or contract period sufficiently. |
| Bridge Letter Received | Enter Yes, No, or N/A to indicate whether a bridge letter or equivalent attestation covering the gap period has been obtained. |
| Bridge Period Covered | If a bridge letter is received, enter the period covered in YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| NDA / Access Restrictions Met | Enter Yes, No, or N/A to confirm whether confidentiality, NDA, portal access, or report-handling restrictions required by the vendor have been satisfied. |
| Evidence Storage Location | Enter the controlled repository path, GRC record ID, vendor management system link, or document management reference where the SOC report, bridge letter, review notes, and approvals are stored. |
| Reviewer | Enter the name and role/title of the person who reviewed the SOC report or due diligence evidence. |
| Review Completion Date | Enter the date the due diligence review was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Due Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format based on vendor risk tier, contract requirements, or annual SOC report cycle. |
| Overall Due Diligence Decision | Record the final review outcome; allowed values: Approved, Approved with Conditions, Risk Accepted, Rejected, Pending Additional Information. |
| Approval / Acceptance By | Enter the name and role/title of the authorized approver or risk acceptor for the due diligence decision. |
| Approval / Acceptance Date | Enter the date the approval or risk acceptance was recorded in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Notes | Enter any additional context relevant to the review, such as contract clauses, monitoring requirements, vendor portal limitations, upcoming reassessment triggers, or rationale for using alternative evidence. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Third-Party Risk Management or Vendor Risk Manager, with Security Compliance review for SOC 2 control alignment. Updated at onboarding, annually for critical/high-risk vendors, upon receipt of new SOC reports or bridge letters, and when material vendor/service changes occur; source data comes from the vendor management/GRC platform, contract repository, vendor portals, and secured SOC report evidence repository.

SOC2-032.title: Encryption Configuration Evidence
SOC2-032.content:
## What This Evidences

Encryption Configuration Evidence demonstrates that [Organisation Name] has configured encryption to protect sensitive data both at rest and in transit, supporting SOC 2 CC6.7 expectations for protecting information during storage, processing, and transmission.

This evidence is not authored manually. It must be collected from [Organisation Name]’s operational systems, cloud platforms, security tools, infrastructure consoles, or configuration management sources. The purpose is to show actual implemented encryption settings, not a policy statement or intended design.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect this evidence from the systems that enforce or record encryption configuration, typically including:

- Cloud provider consoles such as [AWS Console], [Azure Portal], or [Google Cloud Console]
- Infrastructure-as-code repositories such as [GitHub], [GitLab], or [Bitbucket]
- Configuration management or posture management tools such as [CSPM Tool], [Terraform Cloud], or [Ansible Tower]
- Database administration consoles such as [RDS Console], [Azure SQL], [Cloud SQL], [MongoDB Atlas], or [Snowflake]
- Storage service consoles such as [S3], [Azure Storage], [Google Cloud Storage], or [Backup Platform]
- Certificate and TLS management tools such as [Certificate Manager], [Load Balancer Console], [CDN Console], or [Web Application Firewall]
- Endpoint or server management platforms such as [MDM/EDR Tool], where disk encryption is centrally enforced
- SIEM or log store such as [SIEM Tool], if encryption configuration changes are logged there

## How To Collect

1. Identify the in-scope systems handling confidential, customer, production, or regulated data in [Asset Inventory/CMDB].
2. For each in-scope data store, open the relevant platform console or configuration tool.
3. Export or screenshot the encryption-at-rest configuration showing encryption is enabled.
4. For cloud storage, databases, backups, and volumes, capture the encryption status and key management configuration.
5. For systems using customer-managed keys, capture the key identifier, key status, rotation setting, and access policy summary.
6. For encryption in transit, open the configuration for public endpoints, load balancers, APIs, ingress controllers, CDNs, VPNs, or service mesh components.
7. Capture TLS/HTTPS enforcement settings, accepted protocol versions, certificate details, and redirect or secure transport rules.
8. Where available, export configuration reports from [CSPM Tool], [Cloud Security Dashboard], or [Infrastructure-as-Code Pipeline].
9. Record the collection date, collector name, source system, and scope covered.
10. Save the exported files or screenshots to the approved evidence repository.

## What To Capture

Capture enough detail to prove actual encryption configuration, including:

- System, service, application, database, bucket, volume, endpoint, or asset name
- Environment, such as production, staging, or corporate
- Encryption-at-rest status: enabled/disabled
- Encryption algorithm or service-managed encryption setting, where visible
- Key type: platform-managed key, customer-managed key, or HSM-backed key
- Key identifier, alias, or name, with sensitive secrets redacted
- Key status, rotation setting, and last rotation date, if applicable
- Storage/database/backup encryption settings
- Disk or volume encryption status for servers and endpoints
- TLS/HTTPS enforcement status for web, API, and service endpoints
- TLS certificate issuer, subject/common name, expiry date, and covered hostname
- Minimum TLS version and disabled legacy protocols, where visible
- Security group, listener, ingress, or load balancer rule enforcing secure transport
- Timestamp of export or screenshot
- Name of source system/tool used to collect the evidence

## Frequency & Owner

- Frequency: At least quarterly, and after material infrastructure, application, network, certificate, or key management changes.
- Primary owner: [Security Engineering Owner] or [Cloud Platform Owner].
- Supporting owners: [Infrastructure Owner], [DevOps Owner], [Database Owner], and [IT Operations Owner].
- Review owner: [GRC Owner] or [Compliance Owner].

## Retention & Storage

Store collected evidence in [Evidence Repository/GRC Tool] under the SOC 2 evidence folder for the relevant audit period.

Evidence should be:

- Read-only or access-controlled after upload
- Retained for at least [Retention Period], or longer if required by customer, legal, or audit obligations
- Linked to the applicable system, control, collection date, and owner
- Protected from unauthorised modification or deletion
- Redacted only for secrets, private keys, passwords, tokens, or sensitive connection strings

Do not store private encryption keys, plaintext secrets, or credentials as evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will typically accept the evidence if it:

- Comes directly from operational systems, not a manually created description
- Covers all material in-scope production systems that store, process, transmit, or back up sensitive data
- Shows encryption at rest is enabled for relevant databases, storage, backups, disks, and volumes
- Shows encryption in transit is enforced for externally exposed and sensitive internal communications
- Includes clear system names, environments, timestamps, and source tools
- Demonstrates appropriate key management, including key status and rotation where applicable
- Shows TLS certificates are valid and not expired at the time of collection
- Confirms weak or obsolete transport protocols are not permitted where configurable
- Is recent enough for the audit period and aligned to the agreed evidence frequency
- Is stored in the approved evidence repository with access controls and audit trail enabled

SOC2-033.title: Logging & Monitoring Configurations
SOC2-033.content:
## What This Evidences

**Logging & Monitoring Configurations** evidence demonstrates that the organisation has configured logging, monitoring, alerting, and retention mechanisms to detect, analyse, and respond to security events in support of **SOC 2 CC7.2**.

This artifact is **collected from operational systems**, not authored as a standalone document. It should be exported or captured directly from the organisation’s logging, SIEM, monitoring, cloud, endpoint, or infrastructure platforms.

The evidence should show that relevant security events are being ingested, monitored through defined rules or alerts, retained for an appropriate period, and available for investigation.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect this evidence from the systems used to manage logs, alerts, and monitoring, such as:

- SIEM or log management platform: [SIEM/log platform name]
- Cloud logging and monitoring services: [cloud provider logging service]
- Endpoint detection and response platform: [EDR tool name]
- Infrastructure monitoring platform: [monitoring tool name]
- Identity provider logs and alerting: [IdP name]
- Security orchestration or incident response tooling: [SOAR/ITSM tool name]
- Configuration management or policy-as-code repositories, if monitoring rules are managed in version control: [repository name]

The primary source should be the authoritative platform where security logs are centralised and detection rules are configured.

## How To Collect

1. Log in to [SIEM/log platform name] using an account with read-only administrator or security analyst access.
2. Navigate to the section showing log sources, data connectors, or ingestion status.
3. Export or capture evidence showing enabled log sources, ingestion health, and last event received.
4. Navigate to detection rules, correlation rules, saved searches, or alert policies.
5. Export the active monitoring rules or take screenshots showing key enabled rules and their configuration.
6. Navigate to retention, index, storage, or data lifecycle settings.
7. Export or capture the configured log retention period for relevant log types.
8. If alert routing is configured, capture the integration settings showing alerts sent to [ITSM/ticketing tool], [on-call platform], or [security mailbox].
9. If rules are managed through configuration files or version control, export the relevant configuration files and commit history from [repository name].
10. Save all exports and screenshots in the approved evidence repository with the collection date and collector noted.

## What To Capture

Capture enough detail to prove that logging and monitoring are operationally configured. Evidence should include:

- Tool name and environment: [SIEM/log platform name], [production environment]
- Collection date and timestamp
- Log source inventory, including:
 - Source name
 - System type
 - Status enabled/disabled
 - Last event received
 - Event volume or ingestion rate, where available
- Monitored event categories, such as:
 - Authentication events
 - Privileged access activity
 - Administrative actions
 - Endpoint security events
 - Network security events
 - Cloud control plane events
 - Application security logs
- Active detection or alert rules, including:
 - Rule name
 - Description or purpose
 - Severity
 - Enabled status
 - Query or detection logic summary
 - Trigger threshold or condition
 - Alert destination or escalation path
- Log retention configuration, including:
 - Log index, bucket, table, or storage location
 - Retention period
 - Archive setting, if applicable
 - Deletion or lifecycle policy
- Evidence of alert routing to [ITSM/ticketing tool], [SOAR platform], [on-call tool], or [security distribution list]
- User or role showing the configuration was viewed by an authorised operator

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Collect at least quarterly and after major changes to logging, monitoring, SIEM rules, cloud environments, or retention settings.
- **Owner:** Security Operations Manager or designated Security Engineering owner.
- **Reviewer:** Information Security, Compliance, or GRC owner responsible for SOC 2 evidence review.

## Retention & Storage

Store the collected evidence in [evidence repository/GRC platform name] under the SOC 2 evidence folder for the relevant audit period.

Recommended storage requirements:

- Retain for the full audit period plus the organisation’s evidence retention period.
- Restrict access to Security, Compliance, and authorised auditors.
- Preserve original exports where possible.
- Use dated filenames, for example: `logging-monitoring-configurations-[YYYY-MM-DD]`.
- Do not alter screenshots or exports after collection.
- Redact secrets, tokens, credentials, or sensitive payload data before sharing externally.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept this evidence if it shows that:

- Evidence was collected directly from [SIEM/log platform name] or another authoritative logging and monitoring system.
- Relevant production systems are sending logs to a central platform.
- Log ingestion is enabled and active, with recent event timestamps.
- Security monitoring rules or alerts are enabled and aligned to meaningful security events.
- Alert routing is configured to a responsible team or response workflow.
- Log retention settings are visible and meet the organisation’s stated retention requirement.
- The evidence is dated, attributable, and clearly tied to the audit period.
- Screenshots or exports are complete enough to verify configuration without relying only on management assertions.
- Any configuration-as-code evidence includes repository path, file content, and recent commit history where applicable.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Meeting ID | Enter the unique identifier for the committee meeting, using a consistent format such as RC-YYYY-MM-DD or RC-###. |
| Meeting Date | Enter the date the meeting occurred in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Meeting Time and Time Zone | Enter the start and end time plus time zone, for example 10:00-11:00 UTC. |
| Committee Name | Enter the formal name of the committee, for example Internal Risk Committee. |
| Meeting Chair | Enter the full name and role/title of the person chairing the meeting. |
| Minute Taker | Enter the full name and role/title of the person responsible for preparing the minutes. |
| Attendees Present | List full names and roles of all attendees present; separate multiple attendees with semicolons. |
| Required Attendees Absent | List required members who were absent, including role/title; enter N/A if none. |
| Quorum Confirmed | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the required quorum was met before decisions were made. |
| Meeting Purpose | Briefly state the purpose of the meeting, focused on risk governance, risk review, risk decisions, and communication of relevant information. |
| Agenda Item ID | Enter a unique identifier for each agenda item, for example AI-001. |
| Agenda Topic | Enter the specific topic discussed, such as enterprise risk register review, vendor risk update, security incident trends, control exceptions, or risk treatment approvals. |
| Information Pack or Inputs Reviewed | Record the information used by the committee, such as risk register extract, KPI/KRI dashboard, incident report, audit finding, vulnerability report, vendor assessment, or management update; include version/date where applicable. |
| Risk Area or Process | Enter the affected business area, system, service, process, or SOC 2 trust services area, for example Security, Availability, Confidentiality, Engineering, HR, Vendor Management, or Change Management. |
| Risk ID | Enter the linked risk register ID if applicable; enter N/A if the discussion is not tied to a specific risk. |
| Risk Summary | Provide a concise description of the risk, issue, trend, exception, or opportunity discussed. |
| Risk Rating Reviewed | Enter the rating reviewed by the committee using the organisation’s approved scale, for example Critical, High, Medium, Low or a numeric inherent/residual score. |
| Key Discussion Points | Summarise the material points discussed, including assumptions, relevant information considered, challenge by committee members, and any changes to risk understanding. |
| Decision or Outcome | Record the committee’s decision or outcome, such as Accept, Mitigate, Transfer, Avoid, Monitor, Escalate, Defer, Approve, Reject, or No Decision. |
| Control or Policy Reference | Enter any related SOC 2 control ID, internal control reference, policy, standard, or procedure discussed; enter N/A if not applicable. |
| Action Item ID | Enter a unique action identifier for any follow-up item, for example ACT-001; enter N/A if no action was assigned. |
| Action Item Description | Describe the required follow-up action in specific, measurable terms; enter N/A if no action was assigned. |
| Action Owner | Enter the named individual and role accountable for completing the action; do not enter a team name only unless the organisation permits team ownership. |
| Action Due Date | Enter the agreed completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no action was assigned. |
| Action Priority | Enter Critical, High, Medium, Low, or N/A based on the urgency and risk impact of the action. |
| Action Status | Enter Not Started, In Progress, Blocked, Complete, Deferred, Closed, or N/A. |
| Escalation Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the item must be escalated to executive management, the board, audit committee, risk owner, or another governance forum. |
| Escalation Owner or Forum | If escalation is required, enter the person, role, or forum receiving the escalation; enter N/A if escalation is not required. |
| Evidence or Attachment Link | Enter the link or document reference to supporting evidence such as agenda, slide deck, risk report, dashboard, action tracker, or approval record. |
| Minutes Approval Status | Enter Draft, Pending Review, Approved, or Rejected. |
| Approved By | Enter the full name and role/title of the approver of the minutes; enter N/A until approved. |
| Approval Date | Enter the date the minutes were approved in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A until approved. |
| Next Meeting Date | Enter the scheduled next committee meeting date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or TBD if not yet scheduled. |

### Maintenance

The GRC Manager or Risk Committee Secretary owns this template and updates it for every scheduled or ad hoc risk committee meeting, with approval by the meeting chair after review. Source information should be drawn from the risk register, action tracker, GRC platform, meeting agenda pack, KPI/KRI dashboards, incident and audit finding systems, vendor risk records, and approved policy/control repositories.
