SOC2-038.title: Bridge Letter (between report periods)
SOC2-038.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-SOC2-ATT-001] | 1.0 | [Compliance / Trust Office] | [Effective Date] | SOC 2 | Customer Confidential |

## Purpose

This Bridge Letter provides customers, prospective customers, auditors, and other authorised stakeholders with a management attestation covering the period between the end date of [Organisation Name]’s most recent SOC 2 report and the effective date of this letter.

This document is intended to help stakeholders understand whether any material changes, significant control issues, or relevant security events occurred after the covered SOC 2 examination period and before the next SOC 2 report becomes available.

This Bridge Letter does not replace the independent SOC 2 report issued by [Audit Firm Name]. It is a management representation only and has not been examined or tested by the independent service auditor unless explicitly stated in a separate auditor-issued document.

## Scope

This Bridge Letter applies to the services, systems, locations, teams, and control environment included in the most recent SOC 2 report for [Organisation Name].

| Scope Area | Description |
|---|---|
| Organisation | [Organisation Name] |
| Service Covered | [Service / Platform Name] |
| Most Recent SOC 2 Report Type | [Type I / Type II] |
| SOC 2 Report Period Covered | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Bridge Period Covered by this Letter | [Day After Report End Date] to [Bridge Letter Date] |
| Trust Services Categories Covered | [Security, Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity, Privacy - as applicable] |
| Independent Service Auditor | [Audit Firm Name] |
| Report Distribution | Available under non-disclosure agreement or other approved confidentiality terms |

This attestation is limited to the control environment described in the most recent SOC 2 report and the bridge period identified above. It does not extend to systems, services, subsidiaries, third-party environments, or product lines that were not included in the scope of the most recent SOC 2 report.

Where [Organisation Name] uses third-party service providers to support delivery of the in-scope service, this Bridge Letter does not provide an independent attestation over those providers’ control environments. Management has, however, continued to operate its vendor risk management and monitoring processes during the bridge period.

## Attestation Statement

Management of [Organisation Name] represents that, to the best of its knowledge and based on internal review of governance, risk, compliance, security, operational, and incident management records, the following statements are accurate for the bridge period from [Day After Report End Date] to [Bridge Letter Date]:

1. The control environment supporting the in-scope service remained materially consistent with the environment described in the most recent SOC 2 report.

2. The policies, procedures, and control activities relevant to the in-scope Trust Services Categories continued to be maintained and operated during the bridge period.

3. No material changes occurred that would significantly affect the design or operation of controls described in the most recent SOC 2 report, except as disclosed below.

4. No significant security incident, data breach, service disruption, or unauthorised disclosure affecting customer data within the in-scope service occurred during the bridge period, except as disclosed below.

5. No material control deficiency was identified during the bridge period that would materially affect the conclusions presented in the most recent SOC 2 report, except as disclosed below.

6. Control monitoring, vulnerability management, access review, change management, incident response, business continuity, vendor management, risk management, and policy governance activities continued to be performed in the normal course of business.

7. Customer data continued to be handled in accordance with [Organisation Name]’s contractual commitments, documented security policies, and applicable data protection obligations.

8. Any routine operational changes made during the bridge period were managed through established change management, security review, testing, approval, and deployment processes.

9. [Organisation Name] is not aware of any matter that would cause customers to reasonably conclude that the most recent SOC 2 report is materially misleading when considered together with this Bridge Letter.

The following table records management’s disclosure position for the bridge period:

| Area Reviewed | Management Attestation | Disclosure Required |
|---|---|---|
| Material changes to in-scope systems or services | [No material changes identified / See disclosure below] | [Yes / No] |
| Significant changes to control ownership or governance | [No significant changes identified / See disclosure below] | [Yes / No] |
| Significant customer-impacting security incidents | [No significant incidents identified / See disclosure below] | [Yes / No] |
| Material control failures or exceptions | [No material failures identified / See disclosure below] | [Yes / No] |
| Major changes to data hosting or processing locations | [No major changes identified / See disclosure below] | [Yes / No] |
| Significant vendor or subservice organisation changes | [No significant changes identified / See disclosure below] | [Yes / No] |
| Significant availability or resilience events | [No significant events identified / See disclosure below] | [Yes / No] |
| Material legal, regulatory, or contractual security matters | [No material matters identified / See disclosure below] | [Yes / No] |

If applicable, management discloses the following matters for the bridge period:

| Date / Period | Matter | Impact Assessment | Remediation / Current Status | Customer Notification Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Date] | [Description of disclosed change, event, exception, or issue] | [Summary of impact on customers, data, services, or controls] | [Remediation completed / In progress / Compensating controls in place] | [Not required / Completed on Date / In progress] |
| [Date] | [Description] | [Impact] | [Status] | [Status] |

If no disclosures are required, the table above should state: “No matters requiring disclosure were identified for the bridge period.”

This Bridge Letter is provided solely for the benefit of authorised stakeholders who have received, or are entitled to receive, [Organisation Name]’s most recent SOC 2 report. It should be read together with that report, including its description of the system, management’s assertion, the independent service auditor’s opinion, testing period, complementary user entity responsibilities, and any noted exceptions.

## Signatory & Authority

This Bridge Letter is issued by authorised management of [Organisation Name]. The signatory confirms that they have appropriate responsibility and authority for the governance, oversight, and representation of the control environment supporting the in-scope service.

| Role | Responsibility for Attestation |
|---|---|
| [Chief Information Security Officer / Head of Security] | Confirms security control operation, incident review, vulnerability management, and security governance activities during the bridge period. |
| [Chief Technology Officer / VP Engineering] | Confirms material technology changes, platform operations, change management, and service availability matters. |
| [Chief Compliance Officer / GRC Lead] | Confirms review of compliance evidence, SOC 2 scope alignment, control monitoring, and customer assurance records. |
| [Executive Sponsor / Chief Operating Officer] | Confirms executive accountability for the accuracy and release of this management attestation. |

Authorised signatory:

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Name | [Authorised Signatory Name] |
| Title | [Authorised Signatory Title] |
| Organisation | [Organisation Name] |
| Signature | [Signature or Approved Electronic Signature] |
| Date Signed | [Signature Date] |
| Contact for Assurance Requests | [Trust / Compliance Contact Email] |

By signing this Bridge Letter, the authorised signatory represents that reasonable internal enquiries have been completed and that the statements in this document are accurate to the best of management’s knowledge as of the date signed.

## Evidence Referenced

Management’s attestation is based on review of relevant internal records and control evidence maintained during the bridge period. Evidence may include, but is not limited to, the following:

| Evidence Category | Example Evidence Reviewed | Evidence Owner | Review Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Security governance | Security steering committee records, risk register updates, policy exception logs | [Security / GRC] | [Monthly / Quarterly] |
| Access management | User access reviews, privileged access reviews, joiner-mover-leaver records, access approval logs | [IT / Security Operations] | [Monthly / Quarterly] |
| Change management | Change tickets, deployment approvals, testing evidence, emergency change reviews | [Engineering / IT Operations] | [Continuous / Monthly] |
| Vulnerability management | Vulnerability scan results, remediation tracking, risk acceptance records, penetration test remediation status | [Security Operations] | [Continuous / Monthly] |
| Incident management | Incident tickets, security event reviews, incident response records, post-incident reviews | [Security Operations] | [Continuous / As needed] |
| Availability and resilience | Uptime reports, monitoring alerts, backup job records, disaster recovery test results, capacity review records | [Infrastructure / SRE] | [Continuous / Monthly] |
| Vendor management | Vendor assessments, due diligence records, SOC reports or equivalent assurance documents, vendor risk reviews | [Procurement / GRC] | [Annual / Event-driven] |
| Data protection | Data handling reviews, encryption configuration records, data retention reviews, privacy impact reviews | [Privacy / Security] | [Periodic / Event-driven] |
| Compliance monitoring | Internal control testing results, exception tracking, remediation plans, management review records | [GRC / Compliance] | [Monthly / Quarterly] |
| Customer assurance | Customer security questionnaires, contractual security commitments, assurance request logs | [Trust / Legal / Sales Operations] | [As needed] |

Management has considered whether the evidence reviewed indicates any material change, control failure, customer-impacting security event, or other matter that should be disclosed in this Bridge Letter.

This Bridge Letter does not include copies of the underlying evidence. Supporting records are retained internally and may be made available to authorised reviewers at [Organisation Name]’s discretion, subject to confidentiality, legal, security, and contractual restrictions.

## Frequency

A Bridge Letter may be issued when there is a time gap between the end of the most recent SOC 2 report period and the availability of the next SOC 2 report.

| Trigger | Expected Action |
|---|---|
| Customer requests assurance after the SOC 2 report period has ended | Issue the current approved Bridge Letter if the requester is authorised. |
| New SOC 2 report has been issued | Retire the prior Bridge Letter and provide the new SOC 2 report through the approved distribution process. |
| Material change or significant issue occurs during the bridge period | Review and update the Bridge Letter before further distribution. |
| Bridge period exceeds [90 / 120 / 180] days | Reassess whether issuing or extending the Bridge Letter remains appropriate. |
| New product, service, or environment is added | Confirm whether it is within the SOC 2 scope before including it in any customer assurance communication. |

Unless otherwise approved by [Compliance / Legal / Executive Sponsor], this Bridge Letter should not cover a bridge period longer than [Maximum Bridge Period, e.g., 180 days]. If a longer gap exists, management should evaluate whether additional assurance procedures, a refreshed SOC 2 report, a targeted customer communication, or other evidence is appropriate.

This Bridge Letter must be reviewed before each external distribution to confirm that the statements remain accurate as of the distribution date.

## Records & Retention

[Organisation Name] shall retain this Bridge Letter and related approval records in accordance with its records retention, legal, contractual, and audit requirements.

| Record | Retention Period | System of Record | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Final signed Bridge Letter | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [GRC Repository / Document Management System] | [Compliance / GRC] |
| Review and approval evidence | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [Workflow Tool / Ticketing System] | [Compliance / GRC] |
| Supporting control evidence referenced | [Retention Period, e.g., 3-7 years depending on evidence type] | [GRC Tool / Evidence Repository] | [Control Owners] |
| Customer distribution records | [Retention Period, e.g., 3 years] | [CRM / Trust Portal / Ticketing System] | [Trust / Sales Operations] |
| Superseded Bridge Letters | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [Document Management System] | [Compliance / GRC] |
| Related exception or disclosure records | [Retention Period, e.g., 7 years] | [Risk Register / Issue Tracker] | [Risk / Compliance] |

Bridge Letters shall be version-controlled and protected from unauthorised modification. External distribution must occur only through approved channels, such as [Trust Portal], [Customer Success], [Legal], or [Compliance], and only after confirmation that the recipient is authorised to receive customer-confidential assurance materials.

Superseded versions must be clearly marked as retired or archived to prevent accidental distribution. If a previously issued Bridge Letter is later found to contain a material inaccuracy, [Compliance / Legal / Executive Sponsor] must assess whether customer notification, corrective communication, or other action is required.

SOC2-039.title: Continuous Monitoring Dashboard
SOC2-039.content:
## What This Evidences

The Continuous Monitoring Dashboard evidences that the organisation performs ongoing monitoring of security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy-relevant controls throughout the year. It supports SOC 2 control expectations by showing that control health, exceptions, incidents, vulnerabilities, access risks, system performance, and operational alerts are tracked and reviewed on a continuous basis.

This artifact is **collected, not authored**. Do not create a manual dashboard for audit purposes. Collect evidence directly from the organisation’s operational monitoring systems, such as the SIEM, cloud security platform, ITSM tool, vulnerability scanner, endpoint platform, uptime monitoring tool, or governance dashboard.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect the dashboard from the system or portal used for continuous control monitoring in the organisation. Typical sources include:

- SIEM or log analytics platform - [SIEM/log platform name]
- Cloud security posture management tool - [CSPM tool name]
- Vulnerability management platform - [vulnerability scanner name]
- Endpoint detection and response tool - [EDR tool name]
- ITSM or incident management system - [ITSM tool name]
- Uptime, availability, or application monitoring platform - [monitoring tool name]
- Compliance automation or GRC platform - [GRC/compliance tool name]
- Internal security operations dashboard - [internal dashboard name]

Where multiple tools are used, collect the primary executive or operational dashboard plus supporting drill-downs for key metrics.

## How To Collect

1. Log in to [tool/system name] using an account with read-only or reporting access.
2. Navigate to the continuous monitoring, security operations, compliance, service health, or control status dashboard.
3. Set the reporting period to the audit evidence window, typically [start date] to [end date], or capture the current rolling view if the dashboard is live.
4. Confirm filters are set to include the relevant production environment, business units, systems, applications, and cloud accounts.
5. Capture the main dashboard view showing overall control status and key risk indicators.
6. Export the dashboard as PDF, image, CSV, or native report if the tool supports export.
7. If export is not available, take screenshots showing the full browser window, timestamp, URL or tool name, logged-in user, filters, and date range.
8. Capture supporting drill-down views for any exceptions, failed checks, critical alerts, overdue tickets, unresolved vulnerabilities, or degraded services.
9. Save the evidence using a standard filename, such as `[YYYY-MM-DD] Continuous Monitoring Dashboard - [tool name] - [period].pdf`.
10. Store the file in the approved audit evidence repository.

## What To Capture

Capture enough information to show continuous monitoring was operating and reviewed. Include:

- Dashboard title and source tool name
- Date and time of capture
- Reporting period or live timestamp
- Environment or scope filters, such as production, cloud account, application, or region
- Overall control health or compliance status
- Open alerts, exceptions, incidents, or failed checks
- Severity levels and risk ratings
- Vulnerability counts by severity and remediation status
- Incident or ticket counts by status, priority, and age
- Availability, uptime, error rate, or service health indicators where applicable
- Access, identity, or privileged activity alerts where applicable
- Assigned owners or responsible teams
- Evidence of trend, aging, SLA status, or overdue items
- Drill-down records for material exceptions
- Export metadata, report ID, or URL where available

## Frequency & Owner

- **Frequency:** Collect at least monthly during the SOC 2 review period, and additionally at quarter-end, year-end, and before audit fieldwork. For high-risk environments, collect weekly or retain automated daily snapshots.
- **Owner:** [Security Operations Manager], [GRC Manager], or [Control Owner].
- **Reviewer:** [CISO], [Head of Engineering], [IT Operations Lead], or delegated risk owner.

## Retention & Storage

Store collected dashboards in [evidence repository name] under the SOC 2 evidence folder for the relevant review period. Restrict access to authorised audit, security, and compliance personnel.

Retain evidence for at least [retention period], or longer if required by customer contracts, legal obligations, or internal policy. Preserve the exported file or screenshot in its original format. Do not edit screenshots or manually modify exported reports. If redaction is required, retain an unredacted original in a restricted location and provide a redacted copy for audit sharing.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept the evidence if it:

- Comes directly from an operational monitoring, ticketing, logging, security, or compliance system
- Shows the source system, dashboard name, date, timestamp, and reporting period
- Covers the in-scope systems, applications, environments, and services
- Shows continuous monitoring of relevant control areas, not a one-time manually prepared summary
- Includes meaningful metrics, alerts, exceptions, incidents, vulnerabilities, or service health indicators
- Shows status, severity, ownership, aging, or remediation information for exceptions
- Includes drill-down evidence for material open or failed items
- Is collected consistently throughout the review period
- Is stored in the approved evidence repository with a clear filename and collection date
- Can be reconciled to source records if the auditor requests follow-up testing

SOC2-040.title: Annual SOC 2 Renewal Cycle Plan
SOC2-040.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [DOC-SOC2-PLAN-001] | 1.0 | [Compliance Owner / GRC Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | SOC 2 | Internal |

## Purpose & Objectives

The purpose of this Annual SOC 2 Renewal Cycle Plan is to define the activities, timeline, responsibilities, resources, and success criteria required to complete the organisation’s annual SOC 2 renewal in a controlled, predictable, and audit-ready manner.

This plan supports the renewal of the organisation’s SOC 2 report by ensuring that control operation, evidence collection, management review, remediation, auditor coordination, and report issuance activities are planned and executed consistently.

The objectives of this plan are to:

- Maintain continuous readiness for the annual SOC 2 examination.
- Confirm that in-scope services, systems, processes, people, and control activities remain current and accurately documented.
- Ensure that controls are operating effectively throughout the examination period.
- Coordinate timely evidence collection, review, and submission to the external auditor.
- Identify and remediate control gaps before they become audit findings.
- Support management’s ability to make accurate representations to the auditor.
- Minimise business disruption during the audit cycle.
- Deliver the SOC 2 report within the planned reporting window to support customer, contractual, and market commitments.
- Preserve a reliable audit trail of planning decisions, evidence, approvals, and remediation activity.

This plan is intended to be used by the GRC, security, technology, operations, people, legal, vendor management, and business teams involved in preparing for and completing the annual SOC 2 renewal.

## Scope

This plan applies to the annual SOC 2 renewal cycle for the organisation’s in-scope products, services, infrastructure, personnel, locations, vendors, and control activities.

The scope includes:

- Annual SOC 2 renewal planning and governance.
- Review and confirmation of the SOC 2 system description.
- Validation of in-scope services, platforms, environments, applications, infrastructure, and supporting tools.
- Review of applicable trust service categories selected for the report.
- Review of control design and operating effectiveness.
- Control owner readiness activities.
- Evidence request planning, collection, quality review, and submission.
- Internal testing, readiness reviews, and gap remediation.
- External auditor coordination and audit support.
- Management review and approval of audit-related deliverables.
- Tracking of audit issues, exceptions, remediation actions, and lessons learned.
- Post-report distribution and customer response support.

The scope of this plan includes the following organisational areas, where applicable:

| Area | Included Activities |
|---|---|
| Governance, Risk & Compliance | Audit planning, control framework maintenance, evidence coordination, issue tracking, auditor liaison |
| Information Security | Security operations, monitoring, access control, vulnerability management, incident response, security awareness |
| Engineering / Product Development | Change management, secure development, code review, deployment controls, production access |
| IT Operations / Infrastructure | Asset management, system configuration, backups, endpoint management, network security |
| Cloud Operations | Cloud access, logging, monitoring, encryption, environment segregation, infrastructure changes |
| People / HR | Hiring, onboarding, background checks where applicable, training, role changes, offboarding |
| Legal / Privacy | Contractual commitments, customer terms, privacy obligations, confidentiality commitments |
| Vendor Management | Third-party risk assessment, supplier monitoring, contract reviews, service provider oversight |
| Business Operations | Customer commitments, report distribution, customer security questionnaire support |
| Executive Management | Risk acceptance, management representation, audit oversight, final approval |

The following are out of scope unless separately approved by [Compliance Owner / GRC Lead]:

- New certification or attestation initiatives outside the SOC 2 renewal.
- Major redesign of the compliance programme unrelated to audit readiness.
- Customer-specific audits not relying on the annual SOC 2 report.
- Assessments of systems, services, or business units not included in the SOC 2 system description.
- Regulatory examinations unrelated to SOC 2.

If there is uncertainty about whether a system, process, vendor, or team is in scope, the matter must be escalated to [Compliance Owner / GRC Lead] for determination and documented in the SOC 2 scope register.

## Assumptions & Dependencies

The successful execution of this plan depends on the following assumptions and dependencies.

### Assumptions

- The organisation intends to renew its SOC 2 report annually.
- The audit period is expected to cover [audit period start date] through [audit period end date].
- The external audit firm will be engaged before the beginning of fieldwork.
- Control owners understand their assigned control responsibilities and are available to support evidence collection.
- Key systems supporting the in-scope service remain materially consistent during the audit period unless changes are formally assessed.
- Evidence will be retained in approved repositories and will be available for auditor inspection.
- Management will support timely remediation of identified gaps.
- The organisation will maintain sufficient staffing and budget to complete the renewal cycle.
- Any material changes to services, architecture, operating model, vendors, or control environment will be communicated to the GRC team promptly.
- The SOC 2 report will be intended for restricted distribution to customers, prospects, partners, and other authorised recipients under appropriate confidentiality arrangements.

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Description | Owner | Required By |
|---|---|---|---|
| External auditor engagement | Signed engagement letter, audit scope alignment, examination period confirmation, and audit calendar | [Compliance Owner / Finance / Legal] | [Date] |
| Current system description | Accurate description of the in-scope service, infrastructure, boundaries, commitments, and control environment | [Compliance Owner] | [Date] |
| Control register | Current list of controls, owners, frequency, evidence expectations, and mapped processes | [GRC Lead] | [Date] |
| Evidence repository | Approved location for storing and tracking audit evidence | [GRC Lead / IT Owner] | [Date] |
| Control owner availability | Confirmed participation from process and system owners | Department Heads | Throughout cycle |
| Access to logs and reports | Availability of system-generated evidence for access, change, monitoring, vulnerability, incident, and operational controls | System Owners | Throughout cycle |
| Risk register | Current view of security, availability, confidentiality, privacy, and operational risks relevant to the SOC 2 scope | [Risk Owner] | [Date] |
| Vendor inventory | Current inventory of in-scope third-party service providers and their assurance documentation | [Vendor Management Owner] | [Date] |
| HR records | Access to onboarding, training, role change, and offboarding evidence for sampled personnel | [People / HR Owner] | During evidence collection |
| Change records | Complete records for production changes, approvals, testing, and deployments | [Engineering / IT Owner] | During evidence collection |
| Incident records | Complete record of security, availability, confidentiality, or privacy-related incidents and response activity | [Security Operations Owner] | During evidence collection |
| Management review cadence | Scheduled governance reviews for audit readiness, gaps, and key decisions | [Executive Sponsor] | Monthly or as required |

### Key Constraints

- Auditor fieldwork dates may affect internal resource availability and evidence submission deadlines.
- Evidence that is not system-generated may require additional validation and management approval.
- Changes to the product, infrastructure, vendors, or operating model during the audit period may require scope reassessment.
- Delays in remediation may result in audit exceptions or report qualifications.
- Late customer commitments may require report delivery timelines to be prioritised by management.

## Approach / Phases

The SOC 2 renewal cycle will be executed through structured phases. Each phase has defined outcomes, owners, and deliverables to ensure the organisation remains prepared before, during, and after the audit period.

### Phase 1 - Planning and Mobilisation

The planning and mobilisation phase establishes the audit foundation for the annual renewal cycle.

Key activities include:

- Confirm executive sponsor and SOC 2 renewal owner.
- Confirm target report type, audit period, and expected report issuance date.
- Engage or re-confirm the external auditor.
- Review prior-year report, management responses, exceptions, and observations.
- Review customer commitments and contractual deadlines requiring SOC 2 report availability.
- Confirm budget for auditor fees, tooling, remediation, and internal support.
- Establish project governance, meeting cadence, escalation paths, and status reporting.
- Confirm evidence repository, naming conventions, access permissions, and retention expectations.
- Prepare and approve the annual audit project plan.
- Identify known changes since the prior audit cycle.

Expected deliverables:

- Approved SOC 2 renewal project plan.
- Confirmed audit timeline.
- Confirmed external auditor engagement.
- Prior-year findings and observations review.
- Stakeholder and control owner list.
- Project communication plan.
- Initial risk and dependency log.

### Phase 2 - Scope and System Description Review

This phase confirms that the SOC 2 scope accurately reflects the organisation’s current services, commitments, systems, people, processes, locations, and third-party dependencies.

Key activities include:

- Validate in-scope products, services, and customer-facing commitments.
- Confirm trust service categories included in the report.
- Review system boundaries, infrastructure, applications, data flows, and integrations.
- Confirm in-scope environments, including production, staging, administrative, and supporting systems where relevant.
- Validate supporting functions such as engineering, security operations, IT, HR, legal, vendor management, and customer support.
- Review material changes to architecture, service delivery, operating model, or vendors.
- Update system description narratives, diagrams, and supporting appendices.
- Confirm complementary customer responsibilities and third-party responsibilities where applicable.
- Obtain management review of proposed scope updates.

Expected deliverables:

- Updated SOC 2 scope statement.
- Updated system description.
- Updated system architecture and data flow diagrams.
- Updated in-scope systems and vendors list.
- Documented scope decisions and exclusions.
- Management approval of scope.

### Phase 3 - Control Review and Readiness Assessment

This phase verifies that controls are suitably designed, assigned, documented, and operating as intended before auditor testing.

Key activities include:

- Review each control for current relevance, design, frequency, and ownership.
- Confirm control owners and backup owners.
- Confirm evidence expectations and source systems for each control.
- Remove obsolete controls and add controls for new risks, services, or processes.
- Review policies, standards, and procedures supporting SOC 2 controls.
- Perform internal readiness testing on selected controls.
- Validate that recurring control activities have been performed according to schedule.
- Confirm that evidence exists for the audit period to date.
- Identify control gaps, missing evidence, unclear ownership, and process inconsistencies.
- Document readiness results and assign remediation actions.

Expected deliverables:

- Updated control register.
- Control owner acknowledgement.
- Readiness testing results.
- Evidence availability assessment.
- Gap and remediation tracker.
- Updated policy and procedure inventory.
- Management briefing on readiness status.

### Phase 4 - Remediation and Control Stabilisation

This phase addresses identified gaps before external auditor testing begins and ensures that remediation is completed, documented, and sustainable.

Key activities include:

- Prioritise gaps based on audit impact, risk, customer commitments, and operational dependency.
- Assign remediation owners and due dates.
- Implement corrective actions for missing or ineffective controls.
- Update processes, procedures, workflows, tickets, automation, or ownership as needed.
- Re-perform control activities where appropriate and permissible.
- Document compensating controls where primary controls cannot be remediated immediately.
- Obtain risk acceptance for items that cannot be remediated before audit fieldwork, where appropriate.
- Validate remediation effectiveness through targeted retesting.
- Escalate overdue or high-impact remediation items to executive management.

Expected deliverables:

- Remediation tracker with status and evidence.
- Corrective action documentation.
- Retesting results.
- Risk acceptance records, where applicable.
- Executive status updates.
- Final pre-fieldwork readiness decision.

### Phase 5 - Evidence Collection and Quality Review

This phase prepares audit evidence in a complete, accurate, consistent, and traceable manner before submission to the external auditor.

Key activities include:

- Launch evidence request list to control owners.
- Confirm requested evidence period, sample population, and source system.
- Collect evidence in the approved repository.
- Check evidence for completeness, accuracy, date coverage, readability, and relevance.
- Validate that evidence aligns to the control activity being tested.
- Confirm that screenshots, reports, exports, tickets, logs, and approvals include sufficient context.
- Redact sensitive information only where appropriate and without impairing auditor review.
- Track missing, late, or rejected evidence.
- Obtain control owner certification for key evidence submissions where necessary.
- Maintain evidence submission logs and version control.

Expected deliverables:

- Completed evidence request list.
- Evidence quality review records.
- Evidence submission tracker.
- Control owner certifications, where applicable.
- Exception log for missing or incomplete evidence.
- Final evidence package submitted to auditor.

### Phase 6 - Auditor Fieldwork Support

This phase supports the external auditor’s testing activities and ensures responses are timely, accurate, and coordinated.

Key activities include:

- Conduct audit kickoff with auditor and internal stakeholders.
- Review audit request process, communication channels, deadlines, and escalation rules.
- Assign each auditor request to an internal owner.
- Coordinate walkthroughs, interviews, and control demonstrations.
- Respond to follow-up requests within agreed timeframes.
- Review draft auditor observations for factual accuracy.
- Track potential exceptions, management explanations, and additional evidence.
- Escalate unresolved matters to management.
- Maintain a complete record of auditor requests, responses, and supporting evidence.

Expected deliverables:

- Auditor request tracker.
- Interview and walkthrough schedule.
- Meeting notes and action items.
- Follow-up evidence submissions.
- Potential exception log.
- Management responses to auditor inquiries.
- Weekly fieldwork status reports.

### Phase 7 - Report Review, Management Representation, and Issuance

This phase manages the review and release of the SOC 2 report and related management responsibilities.

Key activities include:

- Review draft report for accuracy of scope, period, system description, responsibilities, control descriptions, and auditor observations.
- Confirm that management statements are accurate and supported.
- Validate that any exceptions are factually correct and appropriately described.
- Coordinate legal, executive, security, and business review as needed.
- Prepare management representation materials.
- Obtain required management approvals.
- Confirm final report issuance date and distribution restrictions.
- Store the final report in the approved repository.
- Update customer-facing security and compliance response materials.

Expected deliverables:

- Draft report review comments.
- Final management representation.
- Executive approval records.
- Final SOC 2 report.
- Report distribution guidance.
- Updated customer response materials.
- Final audit closure confirmation.

### Phase 8 - Post-Audit Improvement and Next Cycle Preparation

This phase captures lessons learned and prepares the organisation for continuous readiness in the next annual cycle.

Key activities include:

- Conduct post-audit retrospective with internal stakeholders.
- Review auditor comments, exceptions, observations, and management recommendations.
- Update control activities, ownership, and evidence procedures based on lessons learned.
- Add improvement actions to the compliance roadmap.
- Update training for control owners and evidence contributors.
- Review tooling, automation, and evidence collection efficiency.
- Archive audit records according to retention requirements.
- Confirm next audit cycle planning dates.
- Provide management with final audit performance summary.

Expected deliverables:

- Post-audit lessons learned report.
- Improvement action plan.
- Updated control register and evidence guide.
- Archived audit documentation.
- Next-cycle planning calendar.
- Final executive summary.

## Milestones & Timeline

The following timeline provides a standard annual renewal cycle. Dates should be adjusted based on the planned audit period, auditor availability, customer deadlines, and organisational change calendar.

| Milestone | Target Timing | Key Activities | Primary Owner | Deliverables |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Renewal planning kickoff | 6 months before audit period end | Confirm objectives, sponsor, audit approach, target dates, stakeholders, and budget | [Compliance Owner] | Kickoff notes, draft renewal plan, stakeholder list |
| External auditor engagement confirmed | 5-6 months before audit period end | Execute engagement, align on audit period, confirm audit approach and fieldwork expectations | [Compliance Owner / Legal / Finance] | Signed engagement, auditor contact list, audit calendar |
| Prior-year report and findings review | 5 months before audit period end | Review exceptions, observations, remediation commitments, and customer feedback | [GRC Lead] | Prior-year review summary, carried-forward actions |
| Scope validation completed | 4-5 months before audit period end | Confirm services, systems, locations, vendors, trust service categories, and organisational changes | [Compliance Owner] | Approved scope statement, updated in-scope inventory |
| System description refresh completed | 4 months before audit period end | Update service description, boundaries, architecture, commitments, dependencies, and diagrams | [Compliance Owner / System Owners] | Updated system description and diagrams |
| Control register review completed | 3-4 months before audit period end | Validate control design, ownership, frequency, evidence sources, and changes from prior year | [GRC Lead] | Updated control register and control owner assignments |
| Internal readiness testing begins | 3 months before audit period end | Test selected controls, review evidence availability, identify gaps | [GRC Lead / Internal Audit if applicable] | Readiness testing results, gap tracker |
| Remediation plan approved | 2-3 months before audit period end | Prioritise gaps, assign owners, set due dates, confirm escalation process | [Compliance Owner] | Approved remediation tracker |
| Key remediation completed | 1-2 months before audit period end | Complete corrective actions and retest control operation | Control Owners | Remediation evidence, retest results |
| Evidence request list finalised | 1 month before audit period end | Confirm auditor evidence requests, population requirements, formats, and deadlines | [GRC Lead] | Final evidence request list |
| Evidence collection window opens | Audit period end to 2 weeks after audit period end | Collect recurring control evidence, reports, tickets, approvals, logs, and samples | Control Owners | Evidence package in approved repository |
| Evidence quality review completed | 2-4 weeks after audit period end | Review completeness, accuracy, period coverage, and traceability | [GRC Lead] | Evidence quality review log, issue list |
| Audit kickoff meeting | 3-5 weeks after audit period end | Confirm fieldwork schedule, request process, auditor expectations, and communication protocols | [Compliance Owner] | Kickoff agenda, attendance record, fieldwork plan |
| Auditor fieldwork begins | 4-6 weeks after audit period end | Support testing, walkthroughs, inquiries, and follow-up requests | [GRC Lead] | Auditor request tracker, weekly status reports |
| Auditor fieldwork substantially complete | 8-10 weeks after audit period end | Resolve follow-ups, review potential exceptions, provide additional evidence | [Compliance Owner] | Potential exception log, management responses |
| Draft report received | 10-12 weeks after audit period end | Review report details, system description, control descriptions, and exceptions | [Compliance Owner / Legal / Executive Sponsor] | Draft report comments |
| Management representation completed | Before final report issuance | Confirm management assertions, representations, and approvals | [Executive Sponsor] | Signed management representation |
| Final report issued | 12-14 weeks after audit period end | Receive final report, store securely, approve distribution process | [Compliance Owner] | Final SOC 2 report, distribution record |
| Post-audit retrospective completed | Within 30 days after report issuance | Capture lessons learned, update roadmap, archive records | [GRC Lead] | Lessons learned report, improvement plan |
| Next renewal cycle scheduled | Within 45 days after report issuance | Establish next cycle dates and readiness cadence | [Compliance Owner] | Next-cycle calendar |

## Roles & Responsibilities

The following roles are responsible for planning, executing, reviewing, and approving SOC 2 renewal activities. One person may hold multiple roles depending on organisational size and structure.

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | Provides executive oversight, approves major decisions, removes obstacles, accepts residual risk where appropriate, approves final management representation and report release |
| Compliance Owner / GRC Lead | Owns the SOC 2 renewal cycle, maintains this plan, coordinates stakeholders, manages audit timeline, tracks evidence and remediation, liaises with auditor |
| Control Owners | Operate assigned controls, provide timely evidence, explain control operation, remediate deficiencies, confirm accuracy of submitted evidence |
| Security Lead | Supports security controls, monitoring, incident response, vulnerability management, access reviews, logging, risk treatment, and security policy updates |
| Engineering Lead | Supports change management, secure development, deployment processes, production access, code review, release evidence, and technical walkthroughs |
| IT Operations Lead | Supports endpoint management, internal IT access, asset management, identity management, backup processes, and IT service management evidence |
| Cloud / Infrastructure Owner | Provides evidence for cloud configuration, network security, logging, monitoring, access control, encryption, backups, and infrastructure changes |
| People / HR Lead | Provides evidence for onboarding, training, confidentiality commitments, role changes, termination processes, and workforce-related controls |
| Vendor Management Owner | Maintains third-party inventory, collects supplier assurance reports, tracks vendor reviews, and supports vendor risk evidence |
| Legal / Privacy Lead | Reviews contractual commitments, confidentiality obligations, report distribution terms, privacy-related content, and customer-facing statements |
| Finance / Procurement Lead | Supports auditor engagement, purchase orders, vendor contracts, and budget management |
| Internal Audit or Independent Reviewer, if applicable | Performs readiness testing, independent control review, and validation of remediation activities |
| System Owners | Provide system reports, logs, access records, configuration evidence, and explanations of system functionality |
| Risk Owner | Maintains risk register inputs relevant to SOC 2, supports risk acceptance and remediation prioritisation |
| External Auditor | Performs independent examination, issues evidence requests, conducts testing and walkthroughs, communicates observations, and issues the final report |
| Customer-Facing Teams | Use approved report distribution process, manage customer requests, and escalate customer commitments or deadlines to the compliance team |

### Responsibility Matrix

| Activity | Executive Sponsor | Compliance / GRC | Control Owners | Security / IT / Engineering | Legal / Privacy | External Auditor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Approve renewal plan | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Informed |
| Confirm audit scope | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted |
| Maintain control register | Informed | Accountable | Responsible | Responsible | Consulted | Informed |
| Operate controls | Informed | Oversight | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Not applicable |
| Collect evidence | Informed | Accountable | Responsible | Responsible | Consulted | Not applicable |
| Review evidence quality | Informed | Responsible | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Not applicable |
| Conduct readiness testing | Informed | Responsible | Consulted | Consulted | Informed | Not applicable |
| Remediate gaps | Accountable for high-risk items | Tracks | Responsible | Responsible | Consulted | Not applicable |
| Manage auditor requests | Informed | Responsible | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Responsible for request issuance |
| Review draft report | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Consulted | Responsible for legal review | Responsible for report preparation |
| Approve management representation | Accountable | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Receives representation |
| Release final report | Accountable | Responsible | Informed | Informed | Consulted | Issues report |
| Complete post-audit improvement plan | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Consulted | Consulted | Informed |

## Resources

The following resources are required to execute the annual SOC 2 renewal cycle effectively.

### People Resources

| Resource | Estimated Commitment | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Executive Sponsor | 2-4 hours per month during planning and fieldwork; additional time for approvals | Oversight, escalation, risk acceptance, final approval |
| Compliance Owner / GRC Lead | 25-50% allocation during planning; 50-100% during evidence collection and fieldwork | Overall project management and audit coordination |
| Control Owners | 2-6 hours per month; higher during evidence collection | Control operation, evidence submission, walkthrough support |
| Security Team | 4-10 hours per month; higher during testing | Security evidence, risk treatment, incident and monitoring support |
| Engineering / DevOps | 4-10 hours per month; higher during change and deployment evidence review | Change, deployment, code review, production access, infrastructure evidence |
| IT Operations | 4-8 hours per month | Identity, endpoint, backup, asset, and internal IT control evidence |
| HR / People Team | 2-6 hours per month during evidence collection | Workforce lifecycle and training evidence |
| Vendor Management | 2-4 hours per month | Supplier assurance and third-party risk evidence |
| Legal / Privacy | As needed; typically 5-15 hours during report review | Contract, confidentiality, privacy, and report distribution support |
| External Auditor | As defined in engagement | Independent examination and reporting |

### Technology and Tools

| Tool / Repository | Purpose | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| GRC platform or compliance tracker | Control register, evidence requests, readiness tracking, audit workflow | [GRC Lead] |
| Document management repository | Policies, procedures, system description, report storage, approvals | [Compliance Owner] |
| Ticketing system | Change records, incidents, service requests, access requests, remediation tracking | [IT / Engineering Owner] |
| Identity provider | User access listings, access reviews, authentication settings, administrative access | [IT Owner] |
| Cloud platform | Infrastructure, logging, configuration, encryption, backup, monitoring evidence | [Cloud Owner] |
| Source code repository | Code review, pull requests, branch protections, release evidence | [Engineering Owner] |
| CI/CD platform | Build, test, approval, and deployment evidence | [Engineering / DevOps Owner] |
| Security monitoring tools | Alerts, incident records, logging, detection, and response evidence | [Security Lead] |
| Vulnerability management tool | Scans, findings, remediation records, exception tracking | [Security Lead] |
| Endpoint management tool | Device inventory, configuration, encryption, patching, and compliance evidence | [IT Owner] |
| HR information system | Onboarding, role changes, terminations, training assignments, employment records | [HR Owner] |
| Vendor management repository | Vendor inventory, risk reviews, contracts, assurance reports | [Vendor Management Owner] |

### Documentation Resources

The following documents should be maintained and available for the renewal cycle:

- SOC 2 system description.
- SOC 2 scope statement.
- In-scope systems inventory.
- In-scope vendor inventory.
- Control register.
- Risk register.
- Policy and procedure inventory.
- Security policies and standards.
- Incident response plan and incident records.
- Access management procedures and access review records.
- Change management procedures and change records.
- Secure development procedures.
- Vulnerability management procedures and scan records.
- Business continuity and backup procedures.
- Vendor risk management procedures and reviews.
- HR onboarding, training, and offboarding procedures.
- Prior-year SOC 2 report.
- Prior-year audit issue tracker.
- Customer commitments and security obligation register, where applicable.
- Evidence collection guide.
- Audit communication plan.
- Report distribution procedure.

### Budget Considerations

The annual SOC 2 renewal budget should account for:

- External auditor fees.
- GRC or compliance tooling.
- Security tooling needed to support control operation and evidence generation.
- Independent readiness assessment support, if used.
- Remediation costs for control gaps.
- Legal review support, if required.
- Staff time and temporary support during evidence collection and fieldwork.
- Training for control owners and evidence contributors.
- Customer trust portal or secure report distribution mechanism, if used.

### Meeting Cadence

| Meeting | Frequency | Participants | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| SOC 2 renewal steering meeting | Monthly during planning; bi-weekly during fieldwork | Executive Sponsor, Compliance Owner, key leads | Oversight, decisions, escalation, timeline review |
| GRC working session | Weekly during readiness and evidence collection | GRC Lead, control owners, system owners | Evidence status, blockers, remediation tracking |
| Remediation review | Weekly or as needed | Compliance Owner, remediation owners, risk owner | Track gaps, due dates, retesting, escalations |
| Auditor coordination meeting | Weekly during fieldwork or as agreed | GRC Lead, auditor, relevant SMEs | Review requests, follow-ups, exceptions, schedule |
| Draft report review meeting | As needed during report review | Executive Sponsor, Compliance, Legal, Security, auditor | Review draft report and resolve comments |
| Post-audit retrospective | Once after report issuance | All key stakeholders | Lessons learned and improvement planning |

## Success Metrics

Success will be measured using quantitative and qualitative indicators that demonstrate timely execution, audit readiness, effective control operation, and continuous improvement.

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Renewal plan approved on time | Approved at least 5 months before audit period end | Plan approval record | [Compliance Owner] |
| External auditor engaged on time | Engagement completed at least 5 months before audit period end | Signed engagement documentation | [Compliance Owner / Finance] |
| Scope validation completed on time | Completed at least 4 months before audit period end | Approved scope statement | [Compliance Owner] |
| Control ownership confirmed | 100% of controls have named owner and backup owner | Control register review | [GRC Lead] |
| Evidence expectations documented | 100% of controls have defined evidence source and frequency | Control register / evidence guide | [GRC Lead] |
| Readiness testing completed | At least 90% of planned readiness tests completed before fieldwork | Readiness testing tracker | [GRC Lead] |
| High-risk gaps remediated before fieldwork | 100% or formally risk accepted | Remediation tracker | [Compliance Owner] |
| Evidence submitted on time | At least 95% of evidence submitted by internal deadline | Evidence request tracker | Control Owners / GRC |
| Evidence rejected during quality review | Less than 10% requiring rework | Evidence quality log | [GRC Lead] |
| Auditor follow-up response time | Responses provided within agreed service level, typically 3-5 business days | Auditor request tracker | [GRC Lead] |
| Unresolved auditor requests past due | Zero material overdue requests at fieldwork close | Auditor request tracker | [Compliance Owner] |
| Material surprises during fieldwork | Zero unplanned material scope or control issues | Fieldwork status reports | [Compliance Owner] |
| Draft report review completed on time | Completed within 5 business days of receipt, unless otherwise agreed | Draft report comment log | [Compliance Owner / Legal] |
| Final report issued by target date | Issued on or before [target report date] | Final report date | [Executive Sponsor] |
| Post-audit retrospective completed | Completed within 30 days of report issuance | Retrospective minutes | [GRC Lead] |
| Improvement actions assigned | 100% of lessons learned actions assigned with due dates | Improvement tracker | [Compliance Owner] |

Additional qualitative success indicators include:

- Control owners understand their responsibilities and can explain control operation during walkthroughs.
- Evidence is traceable to source systems and clearly demonstrates control operation.
- The system description accurately reflects the in-scope service and supporting environment.
- Management has timely visibility into audit risks, blockers, and decisions.
- Auditor questions are resolved through documented evidence rather than informal explanations.
- Customer-facing teams can confidently use the final report according to approved distribution rules.
- Lessons learned are incorporated into the next renewal cycle and ongoing compliance operations.

## Review & Update Triggers

This plan must be reviewed at least annually as part of the SOC 2 renewal planning process. It must also be reviewed and updated when changes occur that may affect the audit scope, timeline, control environment, or readiness approach.

### Scheduled Reviews

| Review Activity | Frequency | Owner | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual plan review | Annually before renewal kickoff | [Compliance Owner] | Updated and approved renewal plan |
| Timeline review | Monthly during planning; weekly during fieldwork | [GRC Lead] | Updated project schedule and status report |
| Scope review | At least annually and upon material change | [Compliance Owner] | Updated scope statement and system description |
| Control register review | At least annually and upon process or system change | [GRC Lead] | Updated control register |
| Resource review | At planning kickoff and before fieldwork | [Executive Sponsor / Compliance Owner] | Confirmed staffing and budget |
| Lessons learned review | After final report issuance | [GRC Lead] | Improvement plan for next cycle |

### Update Triggers

This plan must be reassessed when any of the following occur:

- A new product, service, environment, or customer-facing feature is added to the SOC 2 scope.
- A significant change is made to system architecture, hosting model, cloud provider, network design, or data flow.
- A material vendor or outsourced service provider is added, removed, or changed.
- The organisation changes the trust service categories included in the SOC 2 report.
- The target audit period or report issuance date changes.
- The external auditor changes.
- Key control owners, executive sponsors, or responsible teams change.
- A significant security, availability, confidentiality, or privacy incident occurs.
- A major control failure, audit exception, or recurring evidence issue is identified.
- New customer commitments create timing or scope requirements for the SOC 2 report.
- A merger, acquisition, divestiture, restructuring, or major operating model change affects the in-scope environment.
- Significant changes occur in tooling used for identity, logging, monitoring, vulnerability management, change management, or evidence collection.
- Management accepts risk for a control gap that may affect the audit outcome.
- Post-audit lessons learned indicate that the renewal process requires improvement.

### Change Management for This Plan

Changes to this plan must be documented, reviewed, and approved before implementation.

| Change Type | Review Required | Approval Required |
|---|---|---|
| Administrative updates, such as owner names, dates, or tool names | [GRC Lead] | [Compliance Owner] |
| Timeline changes that do not affect report issuance | [Compliance Owner] | [Executive Sponsor if material] |
| Scope, audit period, or report objective changes | [Compliance Owner], Legal, relevant business owners | [Executive Sponsor] |
| Changes to roles, responsibilities, or escalation paths | [Compliance Owner], affected department leads | [Executive Sponsor] |
| Changes resulting from audit findings or significant incidents | [Compliance Owner], Security Lead, Risk Owner | [Executive Sponsor] |
| Changes affecting customer commitments or report distribution | [Compliance Owner], Legal, Customer-Facing Leadership | [Executive Sponsor] |

The current approved version of this plan must be retained in [approved document repository]. Superseded versions must be archived in accordance with the organisation’s document retention requirements.

| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
