| Confirm target maturity and implementation timeline | [Date] | Action plan may not align with business expectations or funding |
| Approve cyber risk appetite thresholds | [Date] | Risk treatment and exception decisions remain inconsistent |
| Confirm critical business services | [Date] | Recovery, monitoring, and asset prioritisation may be misdirected |
| Approve funding and resource allocation | [Date] | Critical remediation actions may not start or complete on time |
| Approve supplier security enforcement approach | [Date] | High-risk suppliers may continue without adequate assurance |

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution

This report contains sensitive information about the organisation’s cybersecurity posture, control gaps, risk exposure, suppliers, systems, and remediation priorities. Distribution must be limited to authorised personnel with a business need to know.

| Recipient / Group | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Executive Leadership | Governance, funding, risk acceptance, and strategic oversight |
| Cybersecurity Team | Remediation planning, control improvement, monitoring, and assurance |
| IT Leadership and Operations | Technical remediation, asset management, recovery, and configuration improvements |
| Risk and Compliance | Risk register management, assurance tracking, and reporting |
| Internal Audit | Audit planning and validation of remediation progress |
| Legal and Privacy | Incident readiness, supplier obligations, and data protection considerations |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Supplier risk remediation and contract improvements |
| Business System Owners | Ownership of application, data, access, and recovery actions |
| External Advisors / Auditors | Only where authorised under confidentiality agreement |

### Confidentiality Requirements

- This report is classified as **Internal Confidential** unless reclassified by the document owner.
- The report must not be shared externally without approval from [Document Owner] and [Legal / Compliance Owner].
- Extracts from this report must not be distributed without confirming that sensitive system names, risk details, supplier information, and security weaknesses are appropriately protected.
- Recipients must store this report only in approved repositories with access restricted to authorised users.
- Printed copies must be avoided where possible and securely destroyed when no longer required.
- Any suspected unauthorised disclosure of this report must be reported immediately to [Security Contact / Incident Reporting Channel].
- Remediation status updates derived from this report must maintain the same confidentiality classification unless formally approved for wider distribution.

### Record Retention

| Record | Retention Requirement |
|---|---|
| Final report | Retain for [Retention Period] in the approved governance repository |
| Evidence reviewed | Retain according to audit and legal requirements in approved evidence locations |
| Action plan updates | Retain until all actions are closed, superseded, or formally accepted |
| Management approvals | Retain with governance meeting records and risk acceptance records |
| Follow-up reassessments | Retain with cybersecurity assurance records |

### Report Review and Update

This report should be reviewed and updated when any of the following occur:

- Completion of major remediation phases.
- Significant change to business operations, technology architecture, suppliers, or threat exposure.
- Material cybersecurity incident or near miss.
- Major audit finding or regulatory inquiry.
- Change in executive risk appetite or cybersecurity strategy.
- At least annually as part of cybersecurity programme planning.

NIST-006.title: Cybersecurity Risk Strategy & Appetite
NIST-006.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| POL-CYB-RISK-001 | 1.0 | [Chief Information Security Officer] | [Effective Date] | NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes the organisation’s mandatory requirements for cybersecurity risk strategy, risk appetite, risk tolerance, and risk register management. It ensures cybersecurity risk is identified, assessed, prioritised, treated, monitored, and reported in a consistent manner aligned with business objectives, legal and contractual obligations, operational resilience needs, and stakeholder expectations.

The Policy supports informed decision-making by defining how much cybersecurity risk the organisation is prepared to accept, when escalation is required, and how cybersecurity risks shall be recorded and governed throughout their lifecycle.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All business units, functions, subsidiaries, and controlled entities of the organisation.
- All employees, contractors, consultants, temporary staff, and third parties who manage, operate, or influence organisation information systems, data, processes, or services.
- All information assets, technology assets, operational technology, cloud services, third-party services, applications, networks, data repositories, and business processes that create, process, transmit, store, or protect organisational information.
- Cybersecurity risks arising from internal operations, external threats, technology change, supplier relationships, mergers and acquisitions, regulatory obligations, business transformation, and material changes to the threat environment.

This Policy applies to cybersecurity risk at enterprise, business process, system, project, supplier, product, and service levels.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain a documented cybersecurity risk strategy that defines how cybersecurity risk supports and constrains business objectives, operational resilience, customer trust, legal compliance, and protection of critical services.

2. The cybersecurity risk strategy shall be approved by executive management and reviewed at least annually, and whenever there is a material change to the business, technology environment, threat landscape, regulatory obligations, or organisational risk profile.

3. The organisation shall define, approve, communicate, and maintain cybersecurity risk appetite statements that describe the level and type of cybersecurity risk the organisation is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives.

4. Cybersecurity risk appetite shall be expressed in practical business terms and shall include measurable or observable thresholds where possible, including thresholds for confidentiality, integrity, availability, privacy, safety, regulatory exposure, financial loss, service disruption, reputational harm, and third-party dependency.

5. The organisation shall define risk tolerance thresholds that support the approved cybersecurity risk appetite and enable consistent risk escalation, prioritisation, acceptance, and treatment decisions.

6. The organisation shall maintain a central cybersecurity risk register as the authoritative record of identified cybersecurity risks, risk ratings, owners, treatment decisions, action plans, due dates, residual risk, acceptance status, and monitoring activity.

7. All material cybersecurity risks shall be recorded in the cybersecurity risk register, including risks associated with critical assets, high-value data, privileged access, internet-facing services, cloud platforms, third-party providers, unsupported technologies, known vulnerabilities, control deficiencies, and significant security incidents.

8. Cybersecurity risks shall be assessed using an approved risk assessment methodology that considers likelihood, impact, existing controls, control effectiveness, inherent risk, residual risk, and business context.

9. The organisation shall classify cybersecurity risks using a consistent rating scale approved by the [Cybersecurity Risk Committee] or equivalent governance body.

10. The following minimum cybersecurity risk rating scale shall be used unless a formally approved enterprise risk scale supersedes it:

| Risk Rating | Description | Minimum Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Risk could cause severe business disruption, significant legal or regulatory consequences, major financial loss, safety impact, or substantial loss of stakeholder trust. | Immediate executive escalation, documented treatment plan, active monitoring until reduced or formally accepted by authorised executive authority. |
| High | Risk could cause material business disruption, regulatory concern, significant data compromise, notable financial loss, or reputational harm. | Senior management escalation, documented treatment plan, target remediation date, and periodic progress reporting. |
| Medium | Risk could cause limited business disruption, moderate control weakness, or manageable exposure requiring planned treatment. | Assigned owner, documented action or acceptance rationale, and review within standard risk governance cycles. |
| Low | Risk is within routine operational tolerance and unlikely to cause material harm. | Managed through standard controls, monitoring, or local operational processes. |

11. Cybersecurity risk appetite and tolerance shall be approved for the following minimum domains:

| Risk Domain | Appetite Position | Example Tolerance Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Protection of regulated, confidential, or sensitive data | Very low appetite for unauthorised disclosure, misuse, or loss. | No known untreated high-risk exposure affecting sensitive data shall remain open beyond approved remediation timeframes. |
| Critical business services availability | Low appetite for preventable disruption to critical services. | Recovery and resilience requirements shall be defined and tested for critical services. |
| Identity and privileged access | Very low appetite for unmanaged privileged access or weak authentication. | Privileged access shall be approved, monitored, periodically reviewed, and protected with strong authentication. |
| Internet-facing systems | Low appetite for exploitable weaknesses on externally exposed services. | Critical exploitable vulnerabilities shall be remediated or mitigated within approved emergency timelines. |
| Third-party and cloud services | Low appetite for unassessed or unmanaged supplier cybersecurity risk. | Material suppliers shall undergo risk assessment before onboarding and periodically thereafter. |
| Regulatory and contractual obligations | Very low appetite for avoidable non-compliance. | Control gaps affecting legal, regulatory, or contractual commitments shall be escalated and tracked to closure. |
| Security monitoring and incident response | Low appetite for undetected or unmanaged security events. | Critical systems shall be covered by appropriate logging, alerting, and incident response processes. |
| Legacy and unsupported technology | Limited appetite where business need is documented and compensating controls are effective. | Unsupported technology shall have approved risk acceptance, a retirement or upgrade plan, and enhanced monitoring. |

12. The organisation shall ensure cybersecurity risk appetite is aligned with enterprise risk management, business continuity, privacy, legal, compliance, procurement, technology, and operational risk processes.

13. Business leaders shall own cybersecurity risks that affect their business processes, data, services, suppliers, or outcomes, even where technical controls are operated by information technology or security teams.

14. Cybersecurity risk decisions shall be based on documented evidence, including asset criticality, business impact, threat exposure, control performance, vulnerability information, incident history, regulatory obligations, and supplier risk information.

15. Cybersecurity risks shall be prioritised based on potential business impact, likelihood of occurrence, threat activity, exploitability, asset criticality, control gaps, and proximity to approved risk appetite and tolerance thresholds.

16. Risk treatment decisions shall use one or more of the following approved options:

| Treatment Option | Required Use |
|---|---|
| Mitigate | Implement or improve controls to reduce likelihood or impact. |
| Avoid | Stop, defer, redesign, or discontinue the activity causing the risk. |
| Transfer | Shift part of the financial or operational exposure through insurance, contracts, outsourcing, or other approved mechanisms, while retaining accountability for oversight. |
| Accept | Formally acknowledge and retain the residual risk within authorised limits. |

17. Cybersecurity risks rated Critical or High shall have documented treatment plans unless formally accepted by an authorised risk acceptance authority.

18. Cybersecurity risk treatment plans shall identify the risk owner, treatment owner, planned actions, target completion dates, interim controls, dependencies, funding requirements, success criteria, and reporting frequency.

19. Risk treatment deadlines shall be proportionate to risk severity and business impact. The following default timelines shall apply unless stricter requirements are defined by law, contract, or management direction:

| Risk Rating | Treatment Plan Required By | Target Treatment Completion | Progress Reporting |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Critical | 5 business days | 30 calendar days or sooner where exposure is active | Weekly until reduced or accepted |
| High | 10 business days | 90 calendar days | Monthly until reduced or accepted |
| Medium | 30 business days | 180 calendar days | At least quarterly |
| Low | As determined by the risk owner | Managed through routine operations | As required |

20. If a risk cannot be remediated within the default target timeframe, the risk owner shall document the rationale, interim controls, revised due date, and approval by the appropriate governance authority.

21. Risk acceptance shall be permitted only where the residual risk is understood, documented, within authorised limits, and approved by an accountable business authority with sufficient seniority.

22. Risk acceptance shall not be used to bypass mandatory legal, regulatory, contractual, or safety obligations.

23. Risk acceptance shall include an expiry date and shall be reviewed before expiry, upon material change, or after a relevant security incident.

24. The following minimum approval authorities shall apply to cybersecurity risk acceptance unless replaced by a formally approved enterprise delegation of authority:

| Residual Risk Rating | Minimum Acceptance Authority | Maximum Acceptance Period |
|---|---|---:|
| Critical | [Chief Executive Officer] or executive risk committee | 90 days |
| High | [Chief Information Security Officer] and accountable executive business owner | 180 days |
| Medium | Accountable business owner and cybersecurity risk function | 12 months |
| Low | System owner or process owner | 24 months |

25. Accepted risks shall remain visible in the cybersecurity risk register and shall not be closed solely because they have been accepted.

26. The organisation shall define risk indicators and metrics to monitor whether cybersecurity risk remains within approved appetite and tolerance.

27. Cybersecurity risk metrics shall include, at minimum, overdue high-risk treatment actions, critical vulnerabilities outside remediation timeframes, material supplier risks, unresolved audit findings, security incidents by severity, privileged access review outcomes, coverage of critical assets by monitoring, and exceptions approaching expiry.

28. Cybersecurity risk reporting shall be provided to management and governance forums at a frequency appropriate to risk severity, with Critical and High risks reported to senior leadership until reduced, accepted, transferred, or avoided.

29. The cybersecurity risk register shall be reviewed at least monthly by the cybersecurity risk function and at least quarterly by the relevant governance forum.

30. New or changed systems, services, suppliers, applications, infrastructure, data processing activities, or business processes shall undergo cybersecurity risk assessment before production use or contractual commitment where they may materially affect the organisation’s risk profile.

31. Projects and change initiatives shall identify cybersecurity risks early enough to influence design, budget, procurement, architecture, control selection, and implementation decisions.

32. Cybersecurity risks associated with third parties shall be assessed before onboarding, upon material service change, periodically during the relationship, and before renewal where the supplier supports critical services or handles sensitive data.

33. The organisation shall maintain risk escalation criteria to ensure risks exceeding appetite or tolerance are reported promptly to the appropriate level of management.

34. The following events shall trigger risk review and, where appropriate, escalation:

| Trigger Event | Required Action |
|---|---|
| Security incident with material business impact or exposure | Reassess related risks and update treatment plans. |
| Identification of a critical vulnerability affecting important assets | Record or update risk and define urgent mitigation. |
| Major technology, cloud, supplier, or architecture change | Perform risk assessment before approval or implementation. |
| Regulatory, legal, or contractual change affecting cybersecurity obligations | Reassess affected controls and risks. |
| Audit finding or control failure indicating systemic weakness | Record risk and assign treatment ownership. |
| Risk treatment deadline missed | Escalate to accountable management and revise plan. |
| Business decision to operate outside approved tolerance | Obtain formal risk acceptance or executive direction. |

35. Cybersecurity risk information shall be protected from unauthorised disclosure, alteration, or deletion because it may contain sensitive information about vulnerabilities, business exposure, suppliers, and control weaknesses.

36. The cybersecurity risk register shall include, at minimum, the following fields:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Risk ID | Unique identifier for tracking and reporting. |
| Risk Title | Concise description of the risk scenario. |
| Risk Description | Clear statement of cause, event, and potential impact. |
| Asset, Process, Supplier, or Service | Affected business or technology area. |
| Risk Owner | Accountable business owner responsible for the risk. |
| Treatment Owner | Person responsible for executing treatment actions. |
| Inherent Risk Rating | Risk level before considering existing controls. |
| Existing Controls | Current controls reducing likelihood or impact. |
| Control Effectiveness | Assessment of whether controls are operating as intended. |
| Residual Risk Rating | Risk level after considering existing controls. |
| Risk Appetite Status | Whether the risk is within, near, or outside appetite. |
| Treatment Decision | Mitigate, avoid, transfer, or accept. |
| Treatment Plan | Actions required to address the risk. |
| Due Dates | Target dates for treatment actions and reviews. |
| Acceptance Details | Approval authority, rationale, and expiry date where applicable. |
| Status | Open, treating, accepted, transferred, avoided, closed, or retired. |
| Review Date | Next scheduled review date. |
| Evidence Links | Supporting assessment, approval, testing, or remediation evidence. |

37. Cybersecurity risks shall be closed only when the risk owner and cybersecurity risk function agree that the risk has been treated, avoided, transferred, retired, or is no longer applicable, and supporting evidence has been retained.

38. Closed cybersecurity risks shall remain available for audit, trend analysis, incident review, and management reporting in accordance with organisational record retention requirements.

39. The organisation shall retain evidence of cybersecurity risk assessments, risk acceptance approvals, treatment plans, governance decisions, and risk reporting for at least [retention period] unless a longer period is required by law, contract, or internal policy.

40. Cybersecurity risk management activities shall be integrated with security architecture, vulnerability management, incident response, business continuity, disaster recovery, supplier management, privacy impact assessment, procurement, and change management processes.

41. The organisation shall consider threat intelligence, incident lessons learned, audit outcomes, control testing, and vulnerability trends when updating risk ratings and treatment priorities.

42. Risk appetite shall not be interpreted as permission to disregard security policies, standards, legal requirements, contractual commitments, customer obligations, or ethical responsibilities.

43. Where conflict exists between business objectives and cybersecurity risk requirements, the matter shall be escalated to the appropriate governance forum for decision and documented resolution.

44. Cybersecurity risk information used for executive reporting shall be accurate, timely, traceable to source records, and presented in a manner that supports informed decision-making.

45. Personnel involved in cybersecurity risk management shall receive appropriate guidance or training on risk identification, assessment, treatment, acceptance, escalation, and register usage.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors or Governing Body | Provides oversight of cybersecurity risk strategy and confirms that cybersecurity risk is considered in organisational governance and major business decisions. |
| Executive Management | Approves cybersecurity risk strategy and risk appetite; ensures adequate resources are available to manage cybersecurity risk; makes decisions on risks exceeding approved tolerance where required. |
| [Chief Information Security Officer] | Owns this Policy; leads cybersecurity risk management; maintains the cybersecurity risk methodology; reports material cybersecurity risks; advises management on treatment, acceptance, and escalation. |
| [Chief Risk Officer] or Enterprise Risk Function | Ensures cybersecurity risk is aligned with enterprise risk management practices, risk taxonomy, reporting, and governance expectations. |
| Cybersecurity Risk Function | Maintains the cybersecurity risk register; facilitates risk assessments; monitors risk treatment; validates risk records; prepares risk reporting; tracks risk acceptance and exceptions. |
| Business Risk Owners | Own risks affecting their business processes, data, services, and outcomes; approve treatment plans; provide resources; accept residual risk within delegated authority. |
| Technology and System Owners | Identify and assess technology risks; implement treatment actions; maintain asset and control information; support evidence collection and risk review. |
| Data Owners | Define data sensitivity and business impact; support assessment of risks to data confidentiality, integrity, availability, and lawful use. |
| Project and Change Owners | Ensure cybersecurity risks are identified and addressed during planning, design, procurement, testing, implementation, and transition to operations. |
| Supplier Relationship Owners | Ensure supplier cybersecurity risks are assessed, treated, monitored, and escalated throughout the supplier lifecycle. |
| Legal, Privacy, and Compliance Functions | Advise on legal, regulatory, privacy, contractual, and compliance implications of cybersecurity risk decisions. |
| Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance over the design and operating effectiveness of cybersecurity risk management processes, as approved in the audit plan. |
| All Personnel | Report suspected cybersecurity risks, control weaknesses, policy breaches, and incidents through approved channels. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory. The organisation shall monitor compliance through governance reviews, risk register quality checks, management reporting, control testing, internal audits, third-party assessments, vulnerability management outputs, incident reviews, and exception tracking.

The following compliance indicators shall be monitored:

| Compliance Indicator | Target or Expectation | Monitoring Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| Critical and High risks recorded in the risk register | 100% of known material risks recorded | Monthly |
| Critical risks with current treatment plan or approved acceptance | 100% | Weekly while open |
| High risks with current treatment plan or approved acceptance | 100% | Monthly |
| Overdue treatment actions for Critical and High risks | Reported and escalated | Monthly or sooner |
| Risk acceptances with valid approval and expiry date | 100% | Monthly |
| Risk register records with assigned risk owner | 100% | Monthly |
| Material changes assessed for cybersecurity risk | Evidence retained for applicable changes | Quarterly |
| Supplier risks assessed before onboarding for material suppliers | 100% | Quarterly |
| Risk appetite breaches escalated | 100% | As identified |
| Risk register reviewed by governance forum | At least quarterly | Quarterly |

Failure to comply with this Policy may result in one or more of the following actions:

- Escalation to the relevant manager, executive owner, or governance forum.
- Requirement to complete overdue risk assessment, treatment, acceptance, or reporting activities.
- Suspension or delay of projects, changes, supplier onboarding, system go-live, or production release until risk requirements are satisfied.
- Revocation of risk acceptance authority where misuse or repeated non-compliance occurs.
- Corrective action plans, performance management, contractual remedies, or disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policies and applicable law.

Material breaches of this Policy shall be reported to [Chief Information Security Officer], [Chief Risk Officer], and other stakeholders as appropriate.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business justification, the risk is assessed, compensating controls are defined where feasible, and approval is obtained from the appropriate authority before the exception is relied upon.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Person and business area requesting the exception. |
| Policy Requirement | Specific requirement that cannot be met. |
| Business Justification | Reason the exception is necessary. |
| Risk Assessment | Likelihood, impact, affected assets, data, services, and stakeholders. |
| Compensating Controls | Alternative measures to reduce risk during the exception period. |
| Duration | Requested start date, end date, and review date. |
| Treatment or Remediation Plan | Actions required to return to compliance, with owner and due date. |
| Approval | Authorised approver based on residual risk level. |

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not exceed 12 months unless renewed through reassessment and approval. Exceptions involving Critical or High residual risk shall be escalated to executive management and reviewed at least monthly until closed, reduced, or formally accepted.

No exception shall be approved where it would knowingly violate applicable law, regulatory obligation, binding contractual commitment, or safety requirement.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually by the [Chief Information Security Officer] and updated as needed to remain aligned with organisational objectives, cybersecurity risk appetite, threat conditions, technology changes, legal and contractual obligations, and governance expectations.

This Policy shall also be reviewed following:

- A material cybersecurity incident.
- A significant change in business strategy, operating model, technology architecture, supplier dependency, or data processing activity.
- A major audit finding or recurring control failure.
- A material change in legal, regulatory, contractual, or customer requirements.
- A significant change in the organisation’s risk appetite or enterprise risk management approach.

Policy changes shall be approved by [approval authority]. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with organisational record retention requirements. The current approved version shall be made available to all relevant personnel and communicated to stakeholders with cybersecurity risk management responsibilities.

NIST-007.title: Enterprise Risk Register (cyber)
NIST-007.content:
## Enterprise Risk Register (cyber) (XLSX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Risk ID | Risk Title | Risk Statement | Risk Category | NIST CSF 2.0 Function | NIST CSF 2.0 Category/Subcategory Reference | Asset / Process / Service Affected | Business Owner | Risk Owner | Threat Source / Threat Actor | Threat Event / Scenario | Vulnerability / Predisposing Condition | Business Impact Description | Confidentiality Impact | Integrity Impact | Availability Impact | Legal / Regulatory / Contractual Impact | Inherent Likelihood | Inherent Impact | Inherent Risk Rating | Existing Controls | Control Effectiveness | Residual Likelihood | Residual Impact | Residual Risk Rating | Risk Appetite / Tolerance Alignment | Risk Treatment Decision | Treatment Plan / Mitigation Actions | Treatment Owner | Target Residual Risk Rating | Due Date | Treatment Status | Exception / Acceptance Reference | Key Risk Indicators | Monitoring Frequency | Last Review Date | Next Review Date | Risk Status | Escalation Required | Escalation / Governance Forum | Related Incident / Finding / Vulnerability References | Evidence / Supporting Documentation Link | Date Opened | Date Closed | Comments / Update Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [EXAMPLE: CYR-0001] | [EXAMPLE: Ransomware risk to finance file shares] | [EXAMPLE: If a cybercriminal compromises user credentials and deploys ransomware to finance file shares, then financial reporting operations may be disrupted and sensitive data may be exposed.] | [EXAMPLE: Data Security] | [EXAMPLE: Identify] | [EXAMPLE: ID.RA-01; ID.RA-04; GV.RM-04] | [EXAMPLE: Finance shared drive and month-end reporting process] | [EXAMPLE: Finance Director] | [EXAMPLE: Head of IT Operations] | [EXAMPLE: Cybercriminal] | [EXAMPLE: Credential compromise followed by ransomware deployment] | [EXAMPLE: Incomplete MFA coverage and legacy file permissions] | [EXAMPLE: Month-end reporting delay, potential data disclosure, recovery cost, and reputational impact.] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: Medium] | [EXAMPLE: High] | [EXAMPLE: Customer confidentiality obligations and potential regulatory notification requirements] | [EXAMPLE: 4-High] | [EXAMPLE: 5-Severe] | [EXAMPLE: 20-Critical] | [EXAMPLE: MFA for remote access CTRL-IAM-004; EDR CTRL-END-002; daily backups CTRL-RES-006] | [EXAMPLE: Partially Effective] | [EXAMPLE: 3-Medium] | [EXAMPLE: 4-Major] | [EXAMPLE: 12-High] | [EXAMPLE: Outside Appetite - exceeds approved cyber disruption tolerance] | [EXAMPLE: Mitigate] | [EXAMPLE: Expand MFA to all finance users; remediate excessive permissions; test restore of finance shares.] | [EXAMPLE: IT Operations Manager] | [EXAMPLE: 6-Medium] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-31] | [EXAMPLE: In Progress] | [EXAMPLE: N/A] | [EXAMPLE: Critical backup restore failures > 0; privileged finance users > approved baseline] | [EXAMPLE: Monthly] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-15] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-02-15] | [EXAMPLE: Treatment In Progress] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: Cyber Risk Committee] | [EXAMPLE: VULN-2026-014; AUD-2025-IT-07] | [EXAMPLE: https://grc.example.com/risks/CYR-0001/evidence] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-10] | [EXAMPLE: ] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-01-15 rating confirmed following access review.] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Risk ID | Enter a unique identifier for the risk using a consistent format, e.g. CYR-0001; do not reuse retired IDs. |
| Risk Title | Enter a short descriptive title for the cyber risk, limited to one clear phrase. |
| Risk Statement | Enter the risk in cause-event-impact format, e.g. 'If [threat/event] exploits [vulnerability], then [business impact] may occur.' |
| Risk Category | Select the primary category: Governance, Identity and Access, Data Security, Third Party, Cloud, Network, Endpoint, Application, Operational Resilience, Incident Response, Privacy, Compliance, Physical/Environmental, Other. |
| NIST CSF 2.0 Function | Enter the relevant NIST CSF 2.0 Function: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, or Recover. |
| NIST CSF 2.0 Category/Subcategory Reference | Enter the applicable NIST CSF 2.0 category or subcategory reference, e.g. GV.RM-01, GV.RM-02, ID.RA-01, ID.RA-04; multiple references may be separated by semicolons. |
| Asset / Process / Service Affected | Enter the business process, information asset, system, application, service, data set, or technology environment affected by the risk. |
| Business Owner | Enter the accountable business owner for the affected asset/process/service, using name and role or team name. |
| Risk Owner | Enter the individual accountable for managing the risk through its lifecycle, using name and role. |
| Threat Source / Threat Actor | Enter the relevant source of threat, e.g. cybercriminal, insider, nation-state, supplier, human error, system failure, natural event, or unknown. |
| Threat Event / Scenario | Describe the specific event or scenario that could trigger the risk, e.g. ransomware infection, credential compromise, supplier outage, data exfiltration. |
| Vulnerability / Predisposing Condition | Describe the weakness, gap, exposure, or condition that makes the threat event plausible, e.g. missing MFA, unpatched system, excessive privileges, unsupported software. |
| Business Impact Description | Describe the expected business consequence if the risk materialises, including operational, financial, customer, reputational, safety, legal, or strategic effects. |
| Confidentiality Impact | Select the expected confidentiality impact: None, Low, Medium, High, Critical. |
| Integrity Impact | Select the expected integrity impact: None, Low, Medium, High, Critical. |
| Availability Impact | Select the expected availability impact: None, Low, Medium, High, Critical. |
| Legal / Regulatory / Contractual Impact | Enter applicable obligations or consequences, e.g. GDPR notification, PCI DSS non-compliance, customer SLA breach, contractual penalty; enter 'None identified' if not applicable. |
| Inherent Likelihood | Rate likelihood before considering existing controls using the organisation's approved scale, e.g. 1-Very Low, 2-Low, 3-Medium, 4-High, 5-Very High. |
| Inherent Impact | Rate impact before considering existing controls using the organisation's approved scale, e.g. 1-Insignificant, 2-Minor, 3-Moderate, 4-Major, 5-Severe. |
| Inherent Risk Rating | Enter the calculated inherent risk score or band using the approved risk methodology, e.g. likelihood x impact = 16 or High. |
| Existing Controls | List current preventive, detective, corrective, and governance controls that reduce the risk; include control IDs where available, separated by semicolons. |
| Control Effectiveness | Assess how well existing controls operate: Effective, Partially Effective, Ineffective, Not Tested, or Not Applicable. |
| Residual Likelihood | Rate likelihood after considering existing controls using the approved scale, e.g. 1-Very Low to 5-Very High. |
| Residual Impact | Rate impact after considering existing controls using the approved scale, e.g. 1-Insignificant to 5-Severe. |
| Residual Risk Rating | Enter the calculated residual risk score or band using the approved risk methodology, e.g. likelihood x impact = 9 or Medium. |
| Risk Appetite / Tolerance Alignment | State whether the residual risk is within appetite: Within Appetite, At Tolerance Limit, Outside Appetite, or Not Assessed; reference the applicable appetite statement if available. |
| Risk Treatment Decision | Select the approved treatment approach: Mitigate, Accept, Transfer/Share, Avoid, or Monitor. |
| Treatment Plan / Mitigation Actions | Enter specific planned actions to change the risk level, including deliverables or control improvements; enter 'None - accepted' only where formally accepted. |
| Treatment Owner | Enter the person or team responsible for completing the treatment actions. |
| Target Residual Risk Rating | Enter the intended residual risk score or band after treatment, using the same approved risk methodology as residual risk. |
| Due Date | Enter the target completion date for treatment actions in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Treatment Status | Select current status: Not Started, In Progress, Blocked, Completed, Overdue, Deferred, or Not Applicable. |
| Exception / Acceptance Reference | Enter the formal exception, waiver, or risk acceptance approval reference and expiry date where applicable; enter 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Key Risk Indicators | Enter measurable indicators used to monitor the risk, including threshold where possible, e.g. number of critical vulnerabilities over SLA > 10. |
| Monitoring Frequency | Enter how often the risk or KRIs are reviewed: Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annually, Annually, Event-Driven. |
| Last Review Date | Enter the date the risk was last reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Risk Status | Select lifecycle status: Open, Under Review, Accepted, Treatment In Progress, Closed, Retired. |
| Escalation Required | Enter Yes or No based on whether residual risk exceeds appetite, is overdue, has material business impact, or requires governance approval. |
| Escalation / Governance Forum | Enter the forum or authority for escalation or approval, e.g. Cyber Risk Committee, Enterprise Risk Committee, CISO, Board Risk Committee; enter 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Related Incident / Finding / Vulnerability References | Enter IDs or links to related audit findings, incidents, penetration test findings, vulnerabilities, third-party issues, or control failures; enter 'N/A' if none. |
| Evidence / Supporting Documentation Link | Enter a link or repository path to supporting evidence such as assessment notes, risk analysis, control testing, treatment plan, or approval record. |
| Date Opened | Enter the date the risk was first recorded in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Date Closed | Enter the closure date in YYYY-MM-DD format when the risk is closed or retired; leave blank while open. |
| Comments / Update Notes | Enter brief dated notes for material updates, decisions, changes in rating, delays, or review outcomes. |

### Maintenance

The template is owned by the CISO or Head of Cyber Risk, with risk entries maintained by assigned Risk Owners and reviewed at least monthly for high/critical risks and quarterly for all others. Source data should be drawn from the GRC platform or enterprise risk system, supported by vulnerability management, incident management, asset inventory, control testing, audit, third-party risk, and compliance systems.

field_guidance.Due Date: Enter the target completion date for treatment actions in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Treatment Status: Select current status: Not Started, In Progress, Blocked, Completed, Overdue, Deferred, or Not Applicable.
field_guidance.Exception / Acceptance Reference: Enter the formal exception, waiver, or risk acceptance approval reference and expiry date where applicable; enter 'N/A' if not applicable.
field_guidance.Key Risk Indicators: Enter measurable indicators used to monitor the risk, including threshold where possible, e.g. number of critical vulnerabilities over SLA > 10.
field_guidance.Monitoring Frequency: Enter how often the risk or KRIs are reviewed: Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annually, Annually, Event-Driven.
field_guidance.Last Review Date: Enter the date the risk was last reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Next Review Date: Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Risk Status: Select lifecycle status: Open, Under Review, Accepted, Treatment In Progress, Closed, Retired.
field_guidance.Escalation Required: Enter Yes or No based on whether residual risk exceeds appetite, is overdue, has material business impact, or requires governance approval.
field_guidance.Escalation / Governance Forum: Enter the forum or authority for escalation or approval, e.g. Cyber Risk Committee, Enterprise Risk Committee, CISO, Board Risk Committee; enter 'N/A' if not applicable.
field_guidance.Related Incident / Finding / Vulnerabili: Enter IDs or links to related audit findings, incidents, penetration test findings, vulnerabilities, third-party issues, or control failures; enter 'N/A' if none.
field_guidance.Evidence / Supporting Documentation Link: Enter a link or repository path to supporting evidence such as assessment notes, risk analysis, control testing, treatment plan, or approval record.
field_guidance.Date Opened: Enter the date the risk was first recorded in YYYY-MM-DD format.
field_guidance.Date Closed: Enter the closure date in YYYY-MM-DD format when the risk is closed or retired; leave blank while open.
field_guidance.Comments / Update Notes: Enter brief dated notes for material updates, decisions, changes in rating, delays, or review outcomes.

NIST-008.content:
## Asset Inventory (Hardware/Software/Data/Services) (XLSX template)

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Asset ID | Enter the unique inventory identifier for the asset; use a consistent format such as AST-000001 and do not reuse retired IDs. |
| Asset Name | Enter the human-readable name used by the organisation, such as hostname, application name, database name, service name, dataset name, or OT device name. |
| Asset Category | Select one: Hardware, Software, Data, Service. |
| Asset Type | Enter the specific type, such as Server, Laptop, PLC, HMI, Network Device, SaaS Application, Database, Dataset, API, Business Service, Cloud Service, Virtual Machine, Container, Storage, Mobile Device. |
| Description | Enter a concise description of what the asset is and its primary purpose. |
| Business Service / Process Supported | Enter the business service, operational process, mission function, or production process the asset supports; use the approved service catalogue name where available. |
| Asset Owner | Enter the accountable business owner role or named person responsible for risk decisions for the asset. |
| Technical Custodian | Enter the technical role, team, or person responsible for day-to-day administration and maintenance. |
| Managing Team / Department | Enter the department or team that manages the asset, such as IT Infrastructure, OT Engineering, Finance Systems, Data Office, Security Operations. |
| Environment | Select one: Production, Pre-Production, Test, Development, Disaster Recovery, Lab, Training, Archive. |
| ICT / OT Classification | Select one: ICT, OT, IoT, Hybrid ICT/OT, Other. |
| Location / Hosting Model | Select one: On-Premises, Colocation, Cloud IaaS, Cloud PaaS, SaaS, Edge, Remote Site, Mobile, Third-Party Hosted. |
| Physical Location | Enter the site, building, room, rack, production line, facility, country/region, or 'N/A' for purely logical/cloud assets. |
| Network Zone / Segment | Enter the network zone, VLAN, subnet, security domain, OT cell/area, cloud VPC/VNet, or 'N/A' if not network-connected. |
| IP Address / URL / Endpoint | Enter primary IP address, FQDN, URL, API endpoint, or management endpoint; use 'N/A' where not applicable. |
| Manufacturer / Vendor | Enter the manufacturer, software publisher, cloud provider, or service provider name. |
| Model / Product Name | Enter the hardware model, software product, SaaS product, platform name, dataset name, or service name. |
| Version / Firmware / Release | Enter installed software version, firmware version, build number, release, schema version, or 'N/A' where not applicable. |
| Serial Number / Instance ID | Enter serial number, asset tag, VM instance ID, cloud resource ID, database ID, SaaS tenant ID, or 'N/A' where not applicable. |
| Operating System / Platform | Enter operating system and version, platform, runtime, cloud platform, database platform, or 'N/A' where not applicable. |
| Software License / Subscription Status | Select one: Licensed, Subscription Active, Open Source, Freeware, Evaluation, Expired, Not Applicable; include license identifier if available. |
| Data Classification | Select the approved organisational classification, such as Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, Highly Restricted, or 'N/A' if the asset does not store/process/transmit data. |
| Data Types Stored / Processed / Transmitted | Enter the main data types handled, such as customer data, employee data, financial data, health data, payment card data, intellectual property, telemetry, production data, safety data, or 'N/A'. |
| Personal Data Indicator | Select one: Yes, No, Unknown; use Yes where the asset stores, processes, or transmits personal data. |
| Criticality | Select one: Critical, High, Medium, Low based on approved business impact criteria. |
| Business Impact if Unavailable | Enter the expected operational, financial, safety, legal, customer, or reputational impact if the asset is unavailable or compromised. |
| Recovery Time Objective (RTO) | Enter the maximum tolerable outage using format such as 4 hours, 1 day, 72 hours, or 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Recovery Point Objective (RPO) | Enter the maximum tolerable data loss using format such as 15 minutes, 4 hours, 1 day, or 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Internet Exposure | Select one: Public Internet-Facing, Private/Internal Only, Partner/Extranet, Remote Access Only, Unknown. |
| Authentication Method | Enter the primary authentication method, such as SSO, MFA, Local Accounts, Certificate-Based, API Key, Service Account, None, N/A. |
| Privileged Access Present | Select one: Yes, No, Unknown; use Yes if administrative, root, domain, cloud admin, vendor admin, or OT engineering privileged access exists. |
| Dependencies / Upstream Assets | Enter key assets, systems, services, networks, suppliers, data feeds, or infrastructure this asset depends on; use asset IDs where known. |
| Dependent Services / Downstream Assets | Enter key services, processes, systems, or assets that depend on this asset; use asset IDs where known. |
| Third-Party / Supplier Managed | Select one: Yes, No, Partially, Unknown. |
| Supplier Name | Enter supplier, managed service provider, cloud provider, vendor, or 'N/A' if not third-party managed. |
| Contract / SLA Reference | Enter contract ID, service agreement reference, SLA reference, or 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Support Status | Select one: Supported, Extended Support, Unsupported, End-of-Life, Unknown, Not Applicable. |
| End-of-Life Date | Enter vendor end-of-life or end-of-support date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or 'N/A' if not applicable or not announced. |
| Patch / Update Responsibility | Enter the role, team, supplier, or service provider responsible for patching or updates. |
| Last Patch / Update Date | Enter the last successful patch, firmware update, software update, or configuration update date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or 'Unknown' if not known. |
| Backup Required | Select one: Yes, No, Not Applicable. |
| Backup Method / Frequency | Enter backup method and frequency, such as daily snapshot, weekly full backup, SaaS export monthly, replicated database, or 'N/A'. |
| Monitoring / Logging Enabled | Select one: Yes, No, Partial, Unknown; indicate whether operational/security monitoring or logs are collected. |
| Security Baseline / Configuration Standard | Enter the applicable secure build, hardening, benchmark, configuration standard, or 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Vulnerability Scanner Coverage | Select one: In Scope and Scanned, In Scope Not Scanned, Excluded by Exception, Not Applicable, Unknown. |
| Last Vulnerability Scan Date | Enter the most recent vulnerability scan or assessment date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Known Risk / Exception Reference | Enter linked risk ID, vulnerability exception, policy exception, accepted risk reference, or 'None'. |
| Regulatory / Compliance Relevance | Enter applicable obligations or frameworks, such as GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, NIS2, safety regulation, export control, customer contractual requirement, or 'None'. |
| Disaster Recovery Included | Select one: Yes, No, Not Applicable, Unknown; use Yes if included in tested DR or continuity plans. |
| Asset Status | Select one: Planned, Active, In Maintenance, Suspended, Retiring, Retired, Disposed, Lost/Stolen. |
| Date Added to Inventory | Enter the date the asset was first recorded in the inventory in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Last Verified Date | Enter the date the asset record was last validated against source evidence in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format based on criticality and policy. |
| Retirement / Disposal Date | Enter the retirement, decommissioning, disposal, or data destruction date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or 'N/A' if active. |
| Inventory Source | Enter the authoritative source used to populate or verify the record, such as CMDB, EDR, MDM, cloud asset inventory, SaaS admin portal, OT asset discovery, data catalogue, procurement system, or manual attestation. |
| Notes | Enter any additional information needed to support identification, ownership, dependencies, lifecycle status, or audit traceability; use 'None' if not required. |

### Maintenance

The Asset Management Owner or CMDB/IT Asset Management Lead owns this register, with input from OT Engineering, Application Owners, Data Owners, Procurement, Security Operations, and Supplier Management. Update on asset creation/change/retirement and reconcile at least monthly for critical assets and quarterly for all assets, drawing from the CMDB, endpoint/EDR, MDM, cloud asset inventory, SaaS admin portals, OT discovery tools, data catalogue, procurement records, and supplier attestations.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Risk ID | Enter a unique identifier for the supplier risk record, using a consistent format such as SCR-0001. |
| Date Identified | Enter the date the risk was first identified in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Supplier Name | Enter the legal or contracted name of the supplier introducing or associated with the risk. |
| Supplier ID | Enter the unique supplier/vendor identifier from the procurement, vendor management, or ERP system. |
| Supplier Type | Enter the supplier category, such as Cloud Service Provider, Managed Service Provider, Software Vendor, Hardware Supplier, Data Processor, Subcontractor, Logistics Provider, or Other. |
| Product / Service Provided | Describe the product, platform, service, component, or outsourced process provided by the supplier. |
| Business Owner | Enter the internal business function or named role accountable for the service or process supported by the supplier. |
| Supplier Relationship Owner | Enter the internal person or role responsible for managing the supplier relationship and contract. |
| Criticality to Organisation | Select the supplier criticality rating: Critical, High, Medium, or Low, based on operational dependency, data sensitivity, substitutability, and business impact. |
| Supply Chain Tier | Enter the supplier tier: Tier 1 for direct supplier, Tier 2 for subcontractor or supplier to a Tier 1 supplier, Tier 3+ for deeper dependency, or Unknown if not confirmed. |
| NIST CSF 2.0 Reference | Enter the applicable NIST CSF 2.0 supply chain reference, such as GV.SC-01, GV.SC-02, GV.SC-03, GV.SC-04, GV.SC-05, GV.SC-06, GV.SC-07, GV.SC-08, GV.SC-09, GV.SC-10, or relevant ID.SC reference if used internally. |
| Risk Scenario | Describe the specific supplier-introduced cyber risk scenario in a clear cause-event-impact format, for example: Supplier remote access compromise may lead to unauthorized access to production systems. |
| Supplier-Introduced Cyber Risk Category | Select the main category: Third-Party Access, Fourth-Party Dependency, Software Vulnerability, Cloud Misconfiguration, Data Breach, Service Disruption, Concentration Risk, Counterfeit / Tampered Component, Inadequate Security Controls, Non-Compliance, Contractual Gap, or Other. |
| Affected Assets / Services / Data | List the internal systems, business services, applications, infrastructure, data sets, or processes that could be affected by the supplier risk. |
| Data Classification Involved | Select the highest classification of data accessible to or processed by the supplier, such as Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, Regulated, Personal Data, or No Data Access. |
| Access Type | Describe the supplier's access, such as No Access, Physical Access, Network Access, Remote Admin Access, API Access, Application Access, Privileged Access, Source Code Access, Production Data Access, or Customer Data Access. |
| Dependency Description | Describe how the organisation depends on the supplier, including whether the dependency is operational, technical, data-processing, software, infrastructure, support, or continuity-related. |
| Existing Supplier Controls | Summarise controls already in place to manage this supplier risk, such as MFA, encryption, logging, SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 certification, vulnerability management, incident notification clause, right to audit, or BCP testing. |
| Control Evidence / Assurance Source | Enter the evidence source used to validate supplier controls, such as SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, SIG questionnaire, CAIQ, penetration test summary, audit report, contract clause, security assessment, or attestation. |
| Inherent Likelihood | Select the likelihood before considering mitigating controls: 1-Very Low, 2-Low, 3-Medium, 4-High, or 5-Very High. |
| Inherent Impact | Select the impact before considering mitigating controls: 1-Very Low, 2-Low, 3-Medium, 4-High, or 5-Very High. |
| Inherent Risk Rating | Enter the inherent risk rating based on the organisation's risk matrix, such as Low, Medium, High, or Critical; if numeric scoring is used, enter Likelihood x Impact. |
| Residual Likelihood | Select the likelihood after considering existing controls: 1-Very Low, 2-Low, 3-Medium, 4-High, or 5-Very High. |
| Residual Impact | Select the impact after considering existing controls: 1-Very Low, 2-Low, 3-Medium, 4-High, or 5-Very High. |
| Residual Risk Rating | Enter the residual risk rating based on the organisation's risk matrix, such as Low, Medium, High, or Critical; if numeric scoring is used, enter Likelihood x Impact. |
| Risk Appetite Alignment | Select whether the residual risk is Within Appetite, Outside Appetite, or Pending Determination. |
| Treatment Decision | Select the approved treatment approach: Accept, Mitigate, Transfer, Avoid, Monitor, or Escalate. |
| Treatment Actions Required | Record specific actions needed to reduce, transfer, avoid, or monitor the supplier risk, including control enhancements, contract changes, supplier remediation, additional assurance, or contingency actions. |
| Action Owner | Enter the person or role responsible for completing the treatment actions. |
| Target Completion Date | Enter the agreed due date for treatment actions in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Contractual / Legal Requirements | Record applicable contract, regulatory, legal, privacy, security, or customer requirements relevant to this supplier risk, including breach notification, data processing, audit rights, security controls, or resilience obligations. |
| Required Supplier Obligations | List specific obligations that must be imposed on or confirmed with the supplier, such as incident notification timeframe, MFA, encryption, vulnerability remediation SLA, subcontractor disclosure, audit rights, secure development, data return, data deletion, or BCP requirements. |
| Assessment Status | Select the current assessment state: Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Overdue, Deferred, Exception Approved, or Not Required. |
| Last Assessment Date | Enter the most recent supplier risk or security assessment date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if no assessment has been completed. |
| Next Assessment Due Date | Enter the next required supplier assessment date in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on supplier criticality and review frequency. |
| Open Issues / Findings | Summarise any unresolved supplier security findings, control gaps, overdue remediation, missing evidence, audit concerns, or contractual gaps. |
| Exception / Waiver Reference | Enter the approved exception or waiver identifier if the risk, missing control, overdue action, or non-standard supplier arrangement has been formally accepted; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Incident History | Record any relevant past supplier-related cyber incidents, service disruptions, data breaches, or near misses, including date and brief description; enter None if not known. |
| Exit / Contingency Considerations | Describe contingency, portability, substitution, exit, data return, data deletion, or transition considerations if the supplier fails, is compromised, or must be replaced. |
| Risk Owner | Enter the internal role or named individual accountable for accepting, treating, and monitoring the supplier risk. |
| Risk Status | Select the current status: Open, In Treatment, Accepted, Closed, Escalated, Overdue, or Retired. |
| Review Frequency | Select the review cadence based on supplier criticality and risk rating: Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annual, Annual, Event-Driven, or Other. |
| Last Reviewed Date | Enter the most recent date this risk record was reviewed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the next scheduled review date in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Approver | Enter the person, committee, or role that approved the risk rating, treatment decision, exception, or acceptance. |
| Approval Date | Enter the date of approval in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Comments | Enter any additional context, assumptions, decisions, dependencies, or notes relevant to the supplier risk record. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Third-Party Risk Management or Supply Chain Risk function, with each risk record accountable to the assigned Risk Owner and Supplier Relationship Owner. Updated at onboarding, contract renewal, material supplier change, supplier incident, control assessment, and at least quarterly for critical/high-risk suppliers, drawing from the vendor management system, procurement/ERP records, supplier security assessments, contract repository, GRC platform, and incident management system.
