Exceptions to this policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business need, technical constraint or operational requirement that prevents full compliance.

All exceptions shall:

1. Be requested using the approved exception process.
2. Include a clear description of the policy requirement that cannot be met.
3. Include business justification and the affected systems, users, data or services.
4. Identify the risk created by the exception.
5. Define compensating controls to reduce risk to an acceptable level.
6. Identify an accountable business owner and technical owner.
7. Be approved by the Chief Information Security Officer or delegated authority.
8. Have a defined expiry date.
9. Be reviewed before expiry, renewal or closure.
10. Be recorded in the organisation’s risk or exception register.

Standing or indefinite exceptions shall not be permitted unless formally approved by executive management and subject to periodic review.

Emergency exceptions may be approved verbally or through expedited channels where required to protect life, safety, critical operations or material business continuity. Emergency exceptions shall be documented and reviewed retrospectively within [5 business days].

Exception records shall include, at minimum:

| Field | Required Information |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | Unique identifier assigned by the exception register |
| Requester | Name and business area of person requesting exception |
| Policy Requirement | Specific requirement that cannot be met |
| Business Justification | Explanation of why the exception is necessary |
| Affected Assets | Systems, applications, data, users or services affected |
| Risk Assessment | Summary of security, operational, legal or compliance risk |
| Compensating Controls | Controls implemented to reduce risk |
| Owner | Accountable business or system owner |
| Approver | Authorised approver |
| Approval Date | Date exception is approved |
| Expiry Date | Date exception must be remediated, renewed or closed |
| Review Date | Date exception will be reassessed |
| Status | Open, closed, expired, rejected or renewed |

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect identity management or access control requirements.

Review triggers include, but are not limited to:

- Significant changes to organisational structure, business processes or workforce model.
- Implementation of new identity platforms, authentication methods, cloud services or privileged access technologies.
- Material cybersecurity incidents involving unauthorised access, credential compromise or privilege misuse.
- Significant audit findings, control weaknesses or risk assessment results.
- Changes to legal, regulatory, contractual or customer requirements.
- New or changed technology architecture affecting authentication, authorisation or access logging.
- Changes in threat environment, including increased credential theft, phishing or identity-based attacks.

The Chief Information Security Officer shall be responsible for ensuring this policy remains current, approved and communicated to relevant stakeholders.

Policy updates shall be reviewed by appropriate stakeholders, which may include Information Security, IT Operations, Legal, Human Resources, Privacy, Internal Audit, business leadership and system owners.

Material changes shall be approved in accordance with the organisation’s governance process before publication.

The current approved version of this policy shall be made available to all relevant users and stakeholders through the organisation’s approved policy repository.

NIST-014.title: Awareness & Training Programme
NIST-014.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [Document ID] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 |
| Classification | Internal |

# Awareness & Training Programme

## Purpose & Objectives

The purpose of this plan is to establish a structured, measurable, and role-appropriate cyber security awareness and training programme for [Organisation Name]. The programme is designed to ensure that personnel understand their cyber security responsibilities, can recognise common threats, and are equipped to perform their roles in a way that protects the organisation’s information, systems, operations, customers, partners, and reputation.

This plan supports the organisation’s cyber risk management objectives by embedding security knowledge and expected behaviours across the workforce and by providing targeted training for roles with elevated cyber security responsibilities.

The objectives of the Awareness & Training Programme are to:

- Ensure all workforce members understand their responsibility to protect organisational information and technology assets.
- Provide baseline cyber security awareness to employees, contractors, temporary staff, interns, and other users with access to organisational systems.
- Deliver role-based training to personnel whose duties create, manage, operate, administer, protect, or govern technology and information assets.
- Promote secure behaviours in daily work, including phishing resistance, secure data handling, password and authentication hygiene, safe use of collaboration tools, incident reporting, and acceptable use of technology.
- Ensure managers, executives, technical teams, and business process owners understand their specific cyber risk responsibilities.
- Support compliance with internal policies, customer commitments, contractual obligations, and applicable legal or regulatory requirements.
- Maintain auditable evidence of training assignment, completion, exceptions, communications, and effectiveness.
- Continuously improve the programme using completion data, incident trends, phishing simulation results, user feedback, audit findings, threat intelligence, and business changes.

## Scope

This plan applies to all personnel who access [Organisation Name] information, systems, facilities, networks, applications, or services, including:

- Full-time and part-time employees.
- Contractors, consultants, agency workers, and temporary personnel.
- Interns, apprentices, and trainees.
- Executive leadership and Board-level stakeholders, where applicable.
- Privileged users, system administrators, developers, engineers, and IT support personnel.
- Personnel handling sensitive, regulated, confidential, customer, employee, financial, or operational data.
- Third-party users with access to organisational systems, where contractual arrangements require training or awareness.

The programme covers the following awareness and training areas:

- General cyber security awareness for all users.
- New starter cyber security induction.
- Annual refresher training.
- Phishing and social engineering awareness.
- Secure handling and classification of information.
- Reporting suspected incidents, phishing attempts, data loss, and policy breaches.
- Acceptable use of organisational technology and collaboration platforms.
- Authentication practices, including secure password use and multi-factor authentication.
- Safe remote and hybrid working practices.
- Privacy and data protection awareness relevant to job responsibilities.
- Physical security behaviours that affect cyber risk.
- Secure use of removable media, personal devices, and approved cloud services.
- Role-based training for:
 - Executives and senior leaders.
 - People managers.
 - System administrators and privileged users.
 - Software developers and DevOps personnel.
 - Security operations and incident response personnel.
 - Procurement, vendor management, and contract owners.
 - Human Resources personnel.
 - Finance and payment-processing personnel.
 - Legal, compliance, and privacy personnel.
 - Customer-facing and support teams.
 - Business continuity and crisis management participants.
- Targeted awareness campaigns in response to emerging threats or observed weaknesses.

The following are outside the direct scope of this plan but may provide input to it:

- Formal professional certification programmes, unless required for defined roles.
- Detailed technical operating procedures.
- Disciplinary processes for policy violations.
- Performance management processes, except where training completion or repeated risky behaviour must be escalated through management.
- Vendor-managed training programmes not controlled by [Organisation Name], unless the organisation relies on those programmes for evidence of third-party user competence.

## Assumptions & Dependencies

The successful implementation of this programme depends on the following assumptions:

- Executive leadership supports cyber security awareness as a business risk management activity, not only an IT activity.
- All workforce members can be uniquely identified in the organisation’s identity, HR, contractor, or learning management records.
- Managers are accountable for ensuring their teams complete assigned training within required timeframes.
- Training assignments can be tracked through a learning management platform or equivalent auditable tracking method.
- Personnel with elevated access or specialised responsibilities can be identified accurately through HR records, identity and access management data, job role mapping, system ownership records, or manager attestation.
- Training materials will be accessible to personnel with disabilities and suitable for the organisation’s working languages and geographic locations.
- The organisation will allocate time during working hours for personnel to complete required training.
- Contractors and third-party users will be subject to appropriate awareness requirements through onboarding processes, contracts, or access approval workflows.
- Awareness content will be kept current with changes in threats, technology, policies, business operations, and legal obligations.

Key dependencies include:

| Dependency | Description | Owner | Impact if Not Available |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workforce identity records | Accurate list of employees, contractors, and other users requiring training | Human Resources / Identity & Access Management | Users may be missed, resulting in incomplete coverage |
| Learning management platform | Tool to assign, deliver, track, and evidence training completion | Human Resources / Learning & Development | Manual tracking may reduce auditability and increase administrative effort |
| Security policy suite | Current policies and standards that define expected behaviours | Information Security | Training may not reflect approved organisational requirements |
| Role mapping | Defined mapping of job functions to role-based training requirements | Information Security / HR / Department Heads | Personnel may receive insufficient or irrelevant training |
| Executive sponsorship | Visible support for mandatory training and campaigns | Executive Leadership | Lower participation and weaker cultural adoption |
| Communications channels | Email, intranet, collaboration tools, digital signage, team briefings, or town halls | Corporate Communications | Awareness campaigns may not reach the intended audience |
| Incident and phishing data | Trends used to target training and measure effectiveness | Security Operations | Programme may not address actual organisational weaknesses |
| Procurement and third-party processes | Ability to set training expectations for third-party users | Procurement / Vendor Management | External users may create unmanaged risk |
| Local legal and labour requirements | Requirements for employee monitoring, training records, accessibility, and communications | Legal / HR | Programme may create compliance or employee relations issues |

## Approach / Phases

The Awareness & Training Programme will be implemented through structured phases to establish governance, define training needs, deploy content, measure effectiveness, and continuously improve.

### Phase 1 - Programme Initiation and Governance

The organisation will establish ownership, decision-making, and operating expectations for the programme.

Key activities:

- Confirm the programme owner and accountable executive sponsor.
- Define programme governance, including reporting cadence and escalation routes.
- Identify stakeholders from Information Security, HR, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, IT, Communications, Learning & Development, Procurement, and business units.
- Confirm mandatory training requirements for employees, contractors, privileged users, and high-risk roles.
- Define training frequency, completion deadlines, exception handling, and evidence retention expectations.
- Align the programme with the organisation’s security policies, acceptable use requirements, incident reporting process, privacy obligations, and workforce onboarding/offboarding processes.
- Agree how non-completion and repeated high-risk behaviour will be escalated to line management and, where appropriate, HR.

Expected outputs:

- Approved programme plan.
- Stakeholder register.
- Training governance model.
- Training assignment rules.
- Evidence and reporting requirements.

### Phase 2 - Audience and Role-Based Needs Assessment

The organisation will identify the audiences requiring awareness or specialised training and determine the learning outcomes for each group.

Key activities:

- Build an audience inventory covering employees, contractors, executives, privileged users, technical staff, business roles, and third-party users.
- Map job families and system access types to training needs.
- Identify high-risk roles based on access privileges, data handled, transaction authority, customer impact, operational dependency, and exposure to targeted attacks.
- Review recent cyber incidents, phishing results, audit findings, policy exceptions, and helpdesk trends to identify priority topics.
- Determine whether existing training content is adequate, requires tailoring, or must be replaced.
- Define minimum training requirements for new starters, annual refreshers, privileged access approval, and role changes.
- Identify accessibility, localisation, and language needs.

Role-based training categories will include, at minimum:

| Audience | Training Focus | Example Learning Outcomes | Minimum Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|
| All workforce members | Core cyber security awareness | Recognise phishing, report incidents, handle information securely, use approved tools | On hire and annually |
| Executives and senior leaders | Cyber risk governance and crisis leadership | Understand cyber risk decisions, support incident response, sponsor secure culture | Annually and during crisis exercises |
| People managers | Team accountability and escalation | Monitor completion, reinforce expectations, escalate risky behaviour | Annually |
| Privileged users and administrators | Secure administration practices | Protect privileged credentials, use approved admin workstations, follow change and logging expectations | On assignment and annually |
| Developers and DevOps personnel | Secure design and coding | Apply secure development practices, manage secrets, remediate vulnerabilities | On assignment and annually |
| Security operations and incident response teams | Detection, response, and evidence handling | Triage alerts, preserve evidence, communicate incidents, use response playbooks | At least annually and after major process changes |
| Finance and payment teams | Fraud and payment security | Identify business email compromise, verify payment changes, follow approval controls | Annually and targeted campaigns |
| HR personnel | Sensitive employee data and onboarding/offboarding | Protect personnel records, support access lifecycle controls, report suspicious requests | Annually |
| Procurement and vendor managers | Third-party cyber risk | Include security expectations in vendor engagement and monitor supplier access | Annually |
| Customer-facing teams | Safe customer support and data handling | Verify identity, avoid over-disclosure, report suspicious customer interactions | Annually |
| Legal, privacy, and compliance teams | Breach response and obligations | Support incident assessment, preserve records, advise on notifications | Annually |
| Business continuity and crisis teams | Cyber disruption scenarios | Execute communication and continuity responsibilities during cyber events | During exercises and annually |

Expected outputs:

- Audience and role mapping.
- Training needs assessment.
- High-risk role list.
- Training curriculum matrix.
- Prioritised content development backlog.

### Phase 3 - Curriculum Design and Content Development

The organisation will design practical, relevant, and accessible content that reflects its operating environment and risk profile.

Key activities:

- Develop or procure baseline awareness training covering common threats and expected behaviours.
- Create role-based modules for personnel with specialised responsibilities.
- Include realistic examples that reflect the organisation’s technologies, data types, workflows, and threat landscape.
- Integrate organisational policies, reporting channels, and approved tools into training content.
- Ensure training includes clear calls to action, such as how to report suspicious emails, lost devices, suspected data disclosure, unauthorised access, or social engineering attempts.
- Design short awareness campaigns to reinforce key behaviours throughout the year.
- Create phishing simulation templates aligned to common attack themes while avoiding inappropriate or harmful lures.
- Ensure training materials meet accessibility, language, and cultural requirements.
- Review training content with Legal, HR, Privacy, Communications, and relevant business stakeholders before release.
- Define pass scores, retake rules, and acknowledgement requirements where applicable.

Core curriculum topics will include:

| Topic | Applies To | Content Type | Key Behaviour Reinforced |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phishing and social engineering | All users | E-learning, simulations, briefings | Pause, verify, and report suspicious messages |
| Incident reporting | All users | E-learning, quick reference guide | Report promptly using approved channels |
| Information handling | All users and data handlers | E-learning, job aids | Classify, store, share, and dispose of information appropriately |
| Authentication and access | All users | E-learning, campaign messaging | Use strong authentication and never share credentials |
| Remote and hybrid working | Remote-capable users | E-learning, checklist | Protect devices, networks, conversations, and printed material |
| Acceptable use | All users | Policy acknowledgement | Use only approved systems and services for business information |
| Secure administration | Privileged users | Role-based module, workshop | Use privileged access securely and follow change controls |
| Secure development | Developers and DevOps | Role-based module, labs | Prevent common software and configuration weaknesses |
| Fraud prevention | Finance, executives, assistants | Scenario-based training | Verify payment, supplier, and executive requests |
| Cyber incident leadership | Executives, crisis teams | Tabletop exercise | Make timely decisions during disruptive cyber events |

Expected outputs:

- Approved annual curriculum.
- Training content and job aids.
- Campaign calendar.
- Phishing simulation plan.
- Role-based training materials.
- Training acknowledgement wording, where required.

### Phase 4 - Deployment and Communications

The organisation will deploy training in a controlled and measurable manner using approved communication channels and training platforms.

Key activities:

- Configure training assignments in the learning management platform or approved tracking mechanism.
- Assign training based on employment status, job role, department, location, access privileges, and system ownership.
- Integrate training into onboarding workflows so new users complete required awareness within defined timeframes.
- Require role-based training before or shortly after granting elevated access, depending on operational necessity and risk approval.
- Communicate the purpose, deadlines, expectations, and support routes for training completion.
- Provide managers with completion dashboards or periodic reports for their teams.
- Issue reminders before due dates and escalate overdue training according to the defined escalation model.
- Deliver targeted awareness campaigns using email, intranet, collaboration platforms, team briefings, posters, or digital signage.
- Conduct phishing simulations and provide immediate learning prompts where appropriate.
- Record all completions, acknowledgements, exceptions, campaign evidence, and simulation results.

Minimum deployment expectations:

| Training Type | Completion Requirement | Deadline | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| New starter awareness | Mandatory for all new workforce members | Within [Number] days of start date | Completion record |
| Annual awareness refresher | Mandatory for all active workforce members | By annual campaign deadline | Completion record and acknowledgement |
| Role-based training | Mandatory for identified roles | Within [Number] days of role assignment or access approval | Completion record |
| Privileged access training | Mandatory for privileged users | Before access or within approved exception period | Completion record and access approval evidence |
| Targeted remedial training | Assigned based on incidents, simulation results, or management request | Within [Number] days of assignment | Completion record |
| Executive cyber briefing | Required for executive leadership | At least annually | Attendance record and briefing materials |
| Incident or crisis exercise participation | Required for designated response roles | Per exercise schedule | Attendance record, scenario, and lessons learned |

Expected outputs:

- Training launch communications.
- Assigned training records.
- Completion dashboards.
- Reminder and escalation records.
- Campaign evidence.
- Phishing simulation reports.

### Phase 5 - Measurement, Reporting, and Assurance

The organisation will measure programme performance and report results to management and relevant governance forums.

Key activities:

- Track completion rates across the total workforce and by business unit, geography, role type, and employment type.
- Monitor overdue training and escalation effectiveness.
- Measure phishing simulation susceptibility, reporting rates, repeat click rates, and credential submission rates where simulated.
- Review incident data to identify whether user behaviour contributed to events or near misses.
- Compare role-based training completion against privileged access and high-risk role lists.
- Validate a sample of training records for completeness and accuracy.
- Review exceptions and overdue items with accountable managers.
- Report key metrics to the cyber risk governance forum and executive leadership.
- Provide evidence for internal audit, external audit, customer assurance, and regulatory enquiries where required.

Reporting will include:

| Report | Audience | Frequency | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workforce training completion report | Information Security, HR, department managers | Monthly during campaigns; otherwise quarterly | Completion, overdue items, exceptions, trends |
| Executive dashboard | Executive leadership / risk committee | Quarterly | Key metrics, risks, overdue areas, campaign outcomes |
| Role-based training compliance report | Information Security, IT, system owners | Quarterly | Completion by privileged and high-risk role |
| Phishing simulation report | Information Security, managers, leadership | After each simulation | Susceptibility, reporting rate, repeat behaviour, recommended actions |
| Annual programme effectiveness report | CISO, executive sponsor, governance forum | Annually | Outcomes, improvements, risks, next year priorities |
| Audit evidence pack | Internal audit, external auditors, assurance stakeholders | As required | Policy linkage, training records, reports, communications, exceptions |

Expected outputs:

- Programme metrics.
- Management reports.
- Exception log.
- Audit evidence pack.
- Improvement actions.

### Phase 6 - Continuous Improvement

The organisation will use evidence and feedback to improve the relevance, effectiveness, and efficiency of the programme.

Key activities:

- Review training content at least annually and after material changes in threats, policies, systems, business operations, or legal requirements.
- Update training topics based on incident trends, phishing outcomes, audit findings, vulnerability patterns, user feedback, and changes in organisational risk appetite.
- Retire outdated training materials and archive evidence in line with retention requirements.
- Improve role-based training assignments where role mapping or access reviews identify gaps.
- Conduct lessons learned reviews after major cyber incidents, significant phishing campaigns, or crisis exercises.
- Assess whether awareness campaigns are changing behaviour, not merely achieving completion.
- Benchmark programme maturity and coverage against recognised good practice.
- Maintain a forward-looking annual training plan and campaign calendar.

Expected outputs:

- Annual improvement plan.
- Updated curriculum and campaign calendar.
- Revised role mapping.
- Lessons learned records.
- Updated metrics and targets.

## Milestones & Timeline

The following timeline provides a practical implementation path for the first programme year. Dates should be adjusted to align with [Organisation Name] planning cycles, budget windows, onboarding cadence, and audit commitments.

| Milestone | Key Activities | Owner | Target Date | Deliverables | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Programme kick-off | Confirm sponsor, stakeholders, objectives, and governance cadence | CISO | [Date] | Kick-off minutes, stakeholder list | Planned |
| Approve programme plan | Review and approve this plan with HR, Legal, Privacy, IT, and Communications | CISO / Executive Sponsor | [Date] | Approved plan | Planned |
| Confirm workforce population | Validate employee, contractor, and third-party user data sources | HR / Identity & Access Management | [Date] | User population baseline | Planned |
| Complete training needs assessment | Identify audiences, high-risk roles, required learning outcomes, and training gaps | Information Security / HR | [Date] | Training needs assessment | Planned |
| Define curriculum matrix | Map audiences to mandatory and role-based modules | Information Security | [Date] | Curriculum matrix | Planned |
| Select or update training content | Procure, configure, or develop baseline and role-based content | Information Security / Learning & Development | [Date] | Approved content set | Planned |
| Configure tracking and reporting | Set up learning assignments, dashboards, reminders, and completion reports | Learning & Development / HR Systems | [Date] | LMS configuration, reports | Planned |
| Launch new starter training process | Embed awareness training into onboarding workflow | HR / Information Security | [Date] | Onboarding training workflow | Planned |
| Launch annual awareness campaign | Communicate requirements and assign baseline training | Information Security / Communications | [Date] | Launch message, assigned training | Planned |
| First completion checkpoint | Review completion rates and overdue users; issue reminders | Information Security / Managers | [Date] | Completion report, reminders | Planned |
| Escalate overdue training | Escalate overdue users to managers and business leaders | Information Security / HR | [Date] | Escalation log | Planned |
| Deliver first phishing simulation | Run approved simulation and provide learning prompts | Information Security | [Date] | Simulation report | Planned |
| Deploy role-based training | Assign modules to privileged users, developers, finance, HR, and other priority groups | Information Security / Department Heads | [Date] | Role-based completion records | Planned |
| Executive cyber briefing | Deliver leadership-focused cyber risk and incident readiness session | CISO | [Date] | Attendance record, briefing deck | Planned |
| Mid-year programme review | Assess metrics, incidents, feedback, and content effectiveness | CISO / Governance Forum | [Date] | Review minutes, action plan | Planned |
| Conduct incident response tabletop | Exercise cyber incident roles and decision-making | Information Security / Crisis Management | [Date] | Exercise report, lessons learned | Planned |
| Annual refresher completion close | Confirm completion, exceptions, and residual overdue items | Information Security / HR | [Date] | Final completion report | Planned |
| Annual effectiveness assessment | Review results against metrics and define improvements for next year | CISO | [Date] | Annual effectiveness report | Planned |
| Next-year planning | Update curriculum, campaign calendar, budget, and priorities | Information Security / Learning & Development | [Date] | Next-year programme plan | Planned |

## Roles & Responsibilities

The following roles are responsible for planning, delivering, supporting, and evidencing the Awareness & Training Programme.

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | Provides visible support for the programme; reinforces mandatory participation; resolves cross-functional barriers; reviews programme performance and risk implications. |
| Chief Information Security Officer | Owns the programme; approves curriculum priorities; ensures alignment with cyber risk objectives; reports performance to governance forums; accepts or escalates material risks. |
| Information Security Awareness Lead | Manages day-to-day programme delivery; develops the campaign calendar; coordinates content; tracks metrics; prepares reports; manages phishing simulations; maintains evidence. |
| Human Resources | Supports workforce population accuracy; embeds training into onboarding and role-change processes; assists with manager escalations; advises on employee relations and accessibility considerations. |
| Learning & Development | Administers the learning platform; supports content delivery; maintains completion records; assists with training design and learner experience. |
| Legal | Advises on legal considerations, employee monitoring, evidence retention, contractual obligations, and incident-related training content. |
| Privacy / Data Protection Lead | Ensures training appropriately covers personal data handling, privacy incident reporting, and role-specific privacy responsibilities. |
| Corporate Communications | Supports communication planning, campaign messaging, intranet content, leadership messages, and awareness branding. |
| IT Operations | Identifies privileged users and administrators; supports role-based training for operational technology and infrastructure roles; assists with access-related training prerequisites. |
| Identity & Access Management | Provides user and access data for training assignment; supports validation of privileged and high-risk user populations. |
| Security Operations | Provides incident trends, phishing data, and threat intelligence; supports targeted training following incidents or observed risky behaviour. |
| Software Engineering / DevOps Leadership | Ensures developers and engineering personnel complete secure development training; integrates training expectations with engineering practices. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Ensures third-party access arrangements include appropriate awareness and training expectations; supports tracking for external users where required. |
| Department Heads | Ensure personnel in their areas complete training; nominate role-based training participants; address overdue items and recurring risky behaviour. |
| Line Managers | Reinforce training expectations; allow time for completion; follow up on overdue training; support remedial actions where needed. |
| System Owners | Identify users with elevated or sensitive access; confirm role-based training requirements; support enforcement of training prerequisites for access. |
| Workforce Members | Complete assigned training by deadlines; apply secure behaviours; report suspected incidents and suspicious activity promptly; comply with security policies. |
| Internal Audit | May independently review programme design, evidence, completion rates, and effectiveness as part of assurance activities. |

Escalation for non-completion will follow the sequence below unless a stricter requirement applies:

| Escalation Stage | Trigger | Action | Responsible Party |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reminder | Training due within [Number] days | Automated or manual reminder to learner | Learning & Development |
| First escalation | Training overdue by [Number] days | Notify line manager with completion deadline | Information Security / HR |
| Second escalation | Training overdue by [Number] days | Notify department head and HR business partner | Information Security / HR |
| Risk escalation | Persistent non-completion or high-risk role overdue | Escalate to CISO and relevant executive | CISO |
| Access review | Role-based or privileged training not completed | Review whether access should be suspended, restricted, or exception-approved | System Owner / Identity & Access Management |
| HR action | Repeated refusal or policy breach | Manage through applicable HR process | HR / Line Manager |

## Resources

The programme requires the following resources to operate effectively.

### People

| Resource | Purpose | Estimated Commitment |
|---|---|---|
| Information Security Awareness Lead | Programme management, campaigns, reporting, content coordination | [Full-time/part-time estimate] |
| CISO or delegated security leader | Oversight, approvals, executive reporting | [Hours per month] |
| Learning & Development administrator | LMS configuration, assignments, records, learner support | [Hours per month] |
| HR representative | Workforce data, onboarding, escalation support | [Hours per month] |
| Communications specialist | Awareness messaging and campaign support | [Hours per campaign] |
| Security Operations representative | Threat trends, phishing data, incident insights | [Hours per month] |
| Technical subject matter experts | Role-based training input for IT, engineering, cloud, and operational systems | [Hours per module] |
| Legal and Privacy reviewers | Review content and monitoring considerations | [Hours per review cycle] |
| Department representatives | Validate role mappings and support completion | [Hours per quarter] |

### Technology

| Tool or System | Purpose | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Learning management system | Assign, deliver, track, and evidence training | Must support reporting, reminders, completion records, and learner access |
| Identity and access management system | Identify active users, privileged users, and role changes | Must provide accurate user and access data |
| HR information system | Identify workforce status, department, manager, location, and start date | Must integrate or reconcile with training assignments |
| Phishing simulation platform | Conduct simulations and track reporting behaviour | Must support safe, approved simulations and actionable reporting |
| Security incident management platform | Provide incident trends and training triggers | Must allow analysis of user-related incident patterns |
| Collaboration and communication tools | Distribute awareness messages and job aids | Must reach target audiences effectively |
| Reporting dashboard | Present programme metrics to managers and leadership | May be LMS-native or developed using business intelligence tools |

### Content and Materials

Required materials include:

- Baseline cyber security awareness module.
- New starter security induction content.
- Annual refresher module.
- Role-based modules for privileged users, developers, executives, finance, HR, procurement, and incident response participants.
- Quick reference guides for incident reporting, phishing reporting, secure information sharing, and remote working.
- Awareness campaign templates.
- Phishing simulation templates and landing page content.
- Manager briefing notes.
- Executive briefing materials.
- Policy acknowledgement wording.
- Frequently asked questions and learner support guidance.

### Budget

The programme budget should include:

| Budget Item | Description | Estimated Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Training platform licensing | LMS or security awareness platform subscriptions | [Amount] |
| Phishing simulation licensing | Simulation and reporting capability | [Amount] |
| Content licensing or development | Purchased modules, custom content, translation, accessibility adaptation | [Amount] |
| Communications materials | Digital assets, posters, videos, intranet design, campaign branding | [Amount] |
| Professional services | Specialist content development, tabletop facilitation, programme maturity review | [Amount] |
| Staff time | Internal labour to administer, review, and deliver the programme | [Amount or effort estimate] |
| Contingency | Emerging threat campaigns or urgent content updates | [Amount] |

### Evidence Retention

The programme will retain sufficient evidence to demonstrate assignment, completion, communication, exceptions, and effectiveness. Evidence will be retained in accordance with [Organisation Name] record retention requirements and applicable legal obligations.

Minimum evidence includes:

| Evidence Type | Examples |
|---|---|
| Training assignment records | Assigned users, module names, assignment dates, due dates |
| Completion records | Completion status, completion dates, scores, acknowledgements |
| Communications | Launch emails, reminders, intranet posts, manager briefings |
| Role mapping | Audience criteria, high-risk role lists, privileged user training population |
| Exception records | Approved delays, alternative training, business justification, expiry dates |
| Phishing simulation records | Approved scenarios, dates, target groups, results, learning prompts |
| Reports | Monthly dashboards, quarterly reports, annual effectiveness assessment |
| Content approvals | Review records from Information Security, HR, Legal, Privacy, or Communications |
| Improvement actions | Lessons learned, action owners, closure evidence |

## Success Metrics

The programme will use a combination of completion, coverage, behaviour, quality, and outcome metrics. Metrics will be reviewed regularly and used to drive improvements.

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Reporting Frequency |
|---|---:|---|---|
| New starter awareness completion | At least [Target]% within required timeframe | LMS or tracking report | Monthly |
| Annual awareness completion | At least [Target]% by campaign deadline | LMS or tracking report | During campaign and at close |
| Role-based training completion | At least [Target]% for identified roles | LMS report matched to role mapping | Quarterly |
| Privileged user training completion | 100% or formally approved exception | LMS report matched to privileged access list | Monthly |
| Executive briefing attendance | At least [Target]% of required leaders | Attendance record | Annually |
| Manager follow-up on overdue training | At least [Target]% actioned within escalation timeframe | Escalation log | Monthly during campaigns |
| Phishing simulation reporting rate | Year-on-year improvement or target of [Target]% | Phishing platform report | After each simulation |
| Phishing simulation click rate | Reduction against baseline or below [Target]% | Phishing platform report | After each simulation |
| Repeat simulation failure rate | Reduction against prior period | Phishing platform report | Quarterly |
| Incident reporting timeliness | Improvement against baseline | Incident management records | Quarterly |
| User-caused incident trend | Reduction in repeat preventable incidents | Incident trend analysis | Quarterly |
| Training satisfaction score | At least [Target] out of [Scale] | Learner feedback survey | After major modules |
| Content review completion | 100% of core content reviewed within annual cycle | Content review log | Annually |
| Training population accuracy | Reconciliation differences below [Target]% | HR/IAM/LMS reconciliation | Quarterly |
| Audit evidence completeness | No material evidence gaps | Internal review or audit sampling | Annually |

Additional qualitative indicators of success include:

- Managers actively reinforce cyber security expectations during team meetings.
- Users report suspicious emails and incidents through approved channels.
- Personnel understand where to find security policies, reporting channels, and help.
- Privileged and high-risk users can explain key security responsibilities relevant to their roles.
- Awareness content reflects current organisational systems and real threat scenarios.
- Training outcomes inform broader cyber risk decisions and improvement plans.

Where targets are not met, the Information Security Awareness Lead will document the issue, likely cause, corrective action, owner, and due date.

## Review & Update Triggers

This plan will be reviewed at least annually by the CISO or delegated programme owner in consultation with HR, Legal, Privacy, Learning & Development, IT, Communications, and relevant business stakeholders.

The plan must also be reviewed and updated when any of the following triggers occur:

- A material cyber incident, data breach, fraud event, or near miss indicates awareness or training gaps.
- Phishing simulation results show persistent high-risk behaviour or ineffective reporting.
- Significant changes occur to the organisation’s technology environment, such as new collaboration platforms, cloud services, identity systems, remote working tools, or operational systems.
- New or revised security policies introduce different user responsibilities.
- Organisational restructuring, mergers, acquisitions, divestments, outsourcing, or workforce model changes affect training populations.
- New legal, regulatory, contractual, customer, or insurance obligations affect awareness or training expectations.
- Audit, assurance, risk assessment, or customer review findings identify deficiencies in training coverage, records, role mapping, or effectiveness.
- A new threat campaign targets the organisation, sector, suppliers, executives, finance personnel, developers, or privileged users.
- Changes to onboarding, offboarding, access management, HR systems, or learning platforms affect assignment or evidence processes.
- Repeated non-completion or exception trends indicate that the escalation model is ineffective.
- Feedback from learners, managers, or business units indicates that training is unclear, inaccessible, outdated, or not relevant.
- New high-risk roles or business processes are introduced.
- Significant changes occur to incident response, business continuity, crisis management, or third-party risk processes.

Updates to this plan will be version-controlled. Material changes require approval by the CISO and, where they affect workforce obligations or monitoring, review by HR and Legal before implementation.

NIST-015.title: Data Security Policy
NIST-015.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-DS-001] | 1.0 | [Chief Information Security Officer] | [Effective Date] | NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Data Security Policy is to establish mandatory requirements for protecting organisational data throughout its lifecycle, including when data is created, stored, processed, transmitted, backed up, archived, shared, retained and securely deleted.

This Policy is intended to ensure that:

- Data is protected against unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, loss and destruction.
- Data confidentiality, integrity and availability are maintained in accordance with business, legal, regulatory and contractual obligations.
- Sensitive data is encrypted or otherwise protected when stored and transmitted.
- Data integrity is preserved through approved technical and administrative controls.
- Data is retained only for authorised business purposes and securely disposed of when no longer required.
- Data security responsibilities are clearly assigned and consistently enforced.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All employees, contractors, consultants, temporary workers, third-party users and service providers who create, access, process, store, transmit, manage or dispose of organisational data.
- All organisational data, regardless of format, location or ownership of the technology used to process it.
- All information systems, applications, databases, endpoints, servers, cloud services, collaboration platforms, removable media, backups, logs, archives and network services that store, process or transmit organisational data.
- Data held within production, development, testing, staging, analytics, reporting and backup environments.
- Data shared with or processed by third parties on behalf of the organisation.

This Policy covers data security requirements for:

- Data at rest.
- Data in transit.
- Data integrity.
- Data retention and deletion.
- Encryption and cryptographic key protection.
- Secure handling of sensitive and regulated information.
- Backup and archival protection.
- Data transfer and sharing.
- Sanitisation and disposal of storage media.

This Policy does not replace detailed technical standards, data handling procedures, records retention schedules or incident response procedures. Where those documents impose more specific or stringent requirements, they shall take precedence.

## Policy Statements

1. **Data Classification and Handling**

 1.1. The organisation shall classify data according to its sensitivity, business value, legal obligations and potential impact if disclosed, altered, lost or destroyed.

 1.2. Data owners shall ensure that data is assigned an appropriate classification before it is stored, processed, transmitted or shared.

 1.3. Data handling requirements shall be defined for each classification level, including permitted storage locations, transmission methods, access restrictions, encryption requirements, retention periods and disposal methods.

 1.4. Sensitive, confidential, regulated or business-critical data shall be handled only through approved systems and services that meet the organisation’s security requirements.

 1.5. Users shall not store organisational data in unauthorised personal accounts, unmanaged devices, consumer file-sharing services, personal email accounts or unapproved cloud services.

2. **Protection of Data at Rest**

 2.1. The organisation shall protect data at rest using controls appropriate to the data classification, system criticality and risk exposure.

 2.2. Sensitive, confidential and regulated data shall be encrypted at rest when stored on servers, databases, endpoints, mobile devices, removable media, backups, cloud storage and other persistent storage locations.

 2.3. Encryption at rest shall use organisation-approved cryptographic algorithms, configurations and key lengths.

 2.4. Full-disk encryption shall be enabled on organisation-managed laptops, mobile devices and removable media that may store organisational data.

 2.5. Databases, file repositories and storage platforms containing sensitive or regulated data shall apply access controls, logging, encryption and segregation appropriate to the sensitivity of the data.

 2.6. Production data shall not be copied into development, testing or training environments unless formally approved and protected to the same level as production, or unless the data has been masked, anonymised, tokenised or otherwise de-identified.

 2.7. Backups containing sensitive, confidential or regulated data shall be encrypted, access-controlled and protected from unauthorised modification or deletion.

 2.8. Storage locations for sensitive data shall be inventoried, approved and periodically reviewed.

3. **Protection of Data in Transit**

 3.1. The organisation shall protect data in transit against unauthorised interception, alteration and disclosure.

 3.2. Sensitive, confidential and regulated data shall be encrypted when transmitted over public networks, wireless networks, third-party networks or any network not fully controlled by the organisation.

 3.3. Approved secure transmission methods shall be used for sensitive data, such as secure web protocols, managed file transfer, virtual private network connections, secure email gateways or other approved encrypted channels.

 3.4. Unencrypted protocols shall not be used to transmit credentials, sensitive information, regulated data or administrative traffic.

 3.5. System-to-system data transfers shall be authenticated, encrypted, logged and restricted to approved source and destination systems.

 3.6. Remote administrative access shall use encrypted channels and strong authentication.

 3.7. Data sent to third parties shall be transmitted only through approved methods and only where a valid business purpose, contractual basis and appropriate security controls exist.

 3.8. Email transmission of sensitive data shall be avoided where secure alternatives are available. Where email must be used, approved encryption or secure delivery controls shall be applied.

4. **Cryptographic Key Management**

 4.1. Cryptographic keys shall be generated, stored, distributed, rotated, revoked and destroyed using approved key management processes.

 4.2. Cryptographic keys shall be protected from unauthorised access, disclosure, modification, loss and misuse.

 4.3. Access to encryption keys shall be restricted to authorised personnel and systems with a documented business need.

 4.4. Keys used to protect sensitive or regulated data shall not be stored with the encrypted data unless protected by an approved key management mechanism.

 4.5. Key rotation shall be performed according to defined schedules, upon suspected compromise, upon personnel changes affecting privileged key access, and where required by contractual or regulatory obligations.

 4.6. Default, shared, hard-coded or embedded cryptographic keys shall not be used in production systems.

 4.7. Loss, exposure or suspected compromise of cryptographic keys shall be reported as a security incident.

5. **Data Integrity**

 5.1. The organisation shall implement controls to protect data from unauthorised or accidental alteration, corruption and destruction.

 5.2. Systems that process business-critical, financial, operational, regulated or security-relevant data shall include integrity controls appropriate to their risk, such as validation checks, audit logging, reconciliation, checksums, digital signatures, version control or database integrity constraints.

 5.3. Applications shall validate input, processing logic and output to reduce the risk of inaccurate, incomplete, unauthorised or malicious data changes.

 5.4. Administrative and privileged changes to critical data shall be logged and attributable to an individual user or authorised service account.

 5.5. Data modification, deletion and restoration activities shall be traceable where required for business, legal, audit or security purposes.

 5.6. Unauthorised or unexpected changes to critical data shall be investigated and, where appropriate, treated as security incidents.

 5.7. Data synchronisation, replication and integration processes shall include error handling, reconciliation and monitoring to detect failed, incomplete or inconsistent transfers.

 5.8. Integrity checks shall be performed for backups, critical files, system images and data repositories where corruption or unauthorised modification could materially affect the organisation.

6. **Access Control for Data**

 6.1. Access to data shall be granted based on business need, least privilege and approved role-based or attribute-based access models.

 6.2. Data owners shall approve access to sensitive, confidential, regulated and business-critical data.

 6.3. Access rights to sensitive data shall be reviewed periodically and whenever users change roles, leave the organisation or no longer require access.

 6.4. Privileged access to data stores, databases, storage platforms, backups and encryption key systems shall be restricted, monitored and reviewed.

 6.5. Shared accounts shall not be used to access sensitive data unless formally approved, technically controlled and logged in a manner that preserves accountability.

 6.6. Service accounts with access to data shall be uniquely identifiable, limited to required functions, protected with strong authentication mechanisms and reviewed periodically.

 6.7. Data access permissions shall be removed promptly when no longer required.

7. **Data Sharing and Third-Party Processing**

 7.1. Data shall be shared internally or externally only for authorised business purposes and in accordance with classification, contractual, legal and privacy requirements.

 7.2. Sensitive, confidential or regulated data shall not be shared with third parties unless an approved agreement is in place that defines security, confidentiality, retention, breach notification, deletion and return obligations.

 7.3. Third parties that store, process or transmit organisational data shall be subject to risk-based due diligence before engagement and ongoing monitoring during the relationship.

 7.4. Data shared with third parties shall be limited to the minimum necessary for the approved purpose.

 7.5. Third-party access to organisational data shall be removed or disabled when the business need ends or the agreement terminates.

 7.6. The organisation shall maintain records of approved third-party data sharing arrangements involving sensitive, confidential or regulated data.

8. **Data Minimisation and Retention**

 8.1. The organisation shall collect, create, store and process only the data necessary for approved business, legal, regulatory or contractual purposes.

 8.2. Data shall be retained only for the period required by the approved records retention schedule, legal hold requirements, contractual obligations or documented business need.

 8.3. Data owners shall ensure that retention requirements are defined and applied to data under their responsibility.

 8.4. Systems that store data shall support retention and deletion requirements appropriate to the type and classification of data held.

 8.5. Data shall not be retained indefinitely unless a documented and approved justification exists.

 8.6. Legal holds shall override normal retention and deletion schedules until formally released by authorised Legal or Compliance personnel.

9. **Secure Deletion and Disposal**

 9.1. Data shall be securely deleted, destroyed, anonymised or otherwise rendered unrecoverable when it is no longer required and retention obligations have been satisfied.

 9.2. Secure deletion methods shall be appropriate to the media type, data classification and recovery risk.

 9.3. Storage media containing sensitive, confidential or regulated data shall be sanitised before reuse, redeployment, return, disposal or transfer outside organisational control.

 9.4. Physical media destruction shall be performed using approved methods and, where appropriate, by vetted service providers.

 9.5. Disposal of systems, storage devices and removable media shall be recorded where the media contained or may have contained sensitive, confidential, regulated or business-critical data.

 9.6. Cloud, hosted and third-party services shall provide reasonable assurance that organisational data is securely deleted or returned when no longer required or upon service termination.

 9.7. Users shall not delete data subject to legal hold, investigation, audit request or regulatory preservation requirement.

10. **Backup, Recovery and Archival Data Protection**

 10.1. Backup and archival data shall be protected according to the highest classification of data contained within the backup or archive.

 10.2. Backups shall be encrypted where they contain sensitive, confidential, regulated or business-critical data.

 10.3. Backup repositories shall be access-controlled, monitored and protected against unauthorised deletion, modification and ransomware-related destruction.

 10.4. Backup restoration processes shall include controls to prevent unauthorised access to restored data.

 10.5. Backup integrity and restoration capability shall be tested periodically based on system criticality and recovery requirements.

 10.6. Retention periods for backups and archives shall align with approved business, legal, regulatory and contractual requirements.

11. **Logging, Monitoring and Evidence**

 11.1. Systems that store, process or transmit sensitive, confidential, regulated or business-critical data shall generate logs sufficient to support security monitoring, investigation and audit activities.

 11.2. Logs shall record relevant data access, administrative changes, failed access attempts, data exports, privileged actions, deletion events and integrity-related alerts where technically feasible and legally permitted.

 11.3. Security logs shall be protected against unauthorised access, alteration and deletion.

 11.4. Monitoring shall be implemented to detect unusual or unauthorised data access, transfer, modification, deletion or exfiltration.

 11.5. Log retention periods shall be defined based on investigation, audit, legal and business requirements.

 11.6. Access to logs containing sensitive data shall be restricted to authorised personnel.

12. **Data Loss Prevention and Exfiltration Controls**

 12.1. The organisation shall implement risk-based controls to prevent, detect and respond to unauthorised disclosure or movement of sensitive, confidential or regulated data.

 12.2. Data loss prevention controls shall be applied to high-risk channels where appropriate, including email, web uploads, endpoint transfers, removable media, collaboration platforms and cloud storage.

 12.3. Bulk export, mass download or unusual transfer of sensitive data shall be monitored and investigated where suspicious.

 12.4. Removable media use shall be restricted, encrypted and approved where sensitive data may be stored or transferred.

 12.5. Users shall not bypass data protection controls, disable security tools or use unauthorised transfer methods to move organisational data.

13. **Endpoint and Mobile Data Protection**

 13.1. Endpoints and mobile devices used to store or access organisational data shall be managed, configured and protected according to organisational security standards.

 13.2. Organisation-managed laptops and mobile devices shall use encryption, access control, screen lock, anti-malware protection and remote wipe capability where supported.

 13.3. Sensitive data stored locally on endpoints shall be minimised and protected from unauthorised access.

 13.4. Lost or stolen devices that may contain or access organisational data shall be reported immediately through approved incident reporting channels.

 13.5. Personal devices used to access organisational data shall comply with approved bring-your-own-device or mobile access requirements.

14. **Cloud and SaaS Data Security**

 14.1. Cloud and software-as-a-service platforms used to store, process or transmit organisational data shall be approved before use.

 14.2. Cloud services containing sensitive, confidential or regulated data shall support appropriate encryption, identity management, access logging, administrative controls, backup, retention and deletion capabilities.

 14.3. Cloud storage and collaboration permissions shall be configured to prevent unauthorised public access or excessive sharing.

 14.4. Publicly accessible storage locations shall not contain sensitive, confidential or regulated data unless formally approved and protected by compensating controls.

 14.5. Cloud tenant configurations that affect data security shall be monitored and reviewed periodically.

15. **Security of Test, Development and Analytics Data**

 15.1. Sensitive, confidential or regulated production data shall not be used in non-production environments unless approved by the data owner and protected by equivalent security controls.

 15.2. Where feasible, test, development, analytics and training environments shall use synthetic, anonymised, masked or tokenised data.

 15.3. Non-production environments containing sensitive data shall be included in access reviews, vulnerability management, logging, backup, retention and deletion processes.

 15.4. Extracts used for reporting, analytics or troubleshooting shall be secured, limited to the minimum necessary and deleted when no longer required.

16. **Incident Reporting and Response**

 16.1. Suspected or confirmed unauthorised access, disclosure, modification, loss, destruction or exfiltration of organisational data shall be reported immediately through approved incident reporting channels.

 16.2. Personnel shall not attempt to conceal, independently investigate or remediate suspected data security incidents without coordination with authorised response personnel.

 16.3. Data security incidents shall be handled in accordance with the organisation’s incident response process.

 16.4. Evidence related to suspected data compromise shall be preserved where required for investigation, legal, regulatory or disciplinary purposes.

17. **Minimum Data Security Requirements**

 The following minimum requirements shall apply unless a documented exception has been approved:

 | Data Security Area | Minimum Mandatory Requirement |
 |---|---|
 | Sensitive data at rest | Encrypted using approved encryption methods |
 | Sensitive data in transit | Transmitted only through approved encrypted channels |
 | Removable media | Restricted, encrypted and approved before use |
 | Backups | Encrypted, access-controlled and periodically tested |
 | Production data in non-production environments | Prohibited unless approved and protected, masked or anonymised |
 | Third-party sharing | Covered by approved agreement and limited to minimum necessary data |
 | Data deletion | Performed using approved secure deletion or destruction methods |
 | Critical data changes | Logged and attributable to an authorised user or service |
 | Encryption keys | Protected using approved key management processes |
 | Legal hold data | Preserved until formal release by authorised personnel |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors or Executive Leadership | Provide oversight and support for the protection of organisational data; ensure adequate resources are available for data security capabilities. |
| Chief Information Security Officer | Own this Policy; define data security requirements; oversee encryption, monitoring, data loss prevention and related controls; report material risks and non-compliance. |
| Chief Information Officer / IT Leadership | Ensure that technology platforms, infrastructure and services implement required data protection controls; support secure storage, transmission, backup and deletion capabilities. |
| Data Owners | Classify data; approve access; define retention needs; authorise data sharing; ensure data is protected according to sensitivity and business requirements. |
| System Owners | Implement and maintain data security controls for assigned systems; ensure logging, access control, encryption, backup and deletion requirements are met. |
| Legal and Compliance | Advise on legal, regulatory, contractual and records retention obligations; approve legal holds; support breach notification and evidence preservation requirements. |
| Privacy Officer / Data Protection Lead | Advise on privacy requirements; ensure personal data is processed, retained, shared and deleted in accordance with applicable privacy obligations. |
| Security Operations | Monitor for data security events; investigate suspicious access, transfer, modification or deletion activity; support incident response and evidence collection. |
| IT Operations | Configure and maintain storage, network, endpoint, backup and cloud security controls; perform approved deletion, media sanitisation and disposal activities. |
| Procurement and Vendor Management | Ensure third-party contracts include appropriate data security, confidentiality, retention, deletion, return and breach notification obligations. |
| Human Resources | Support workforce awareness, onboarding, role changes and offboarding processes affecting data access. |
| Managers | Ensure personnel understand and follow data handling requirements; request access only where required for business purposes; report suspected non-compliance. |
| Users | Protect organisational data; follow approved handling, storage, transmission and deletion requirements; report suspected data security incidents promptly. |
| Third Parties | Protect organisational data in accordance with contractual obligations, approved security requirements and applicable law; report suspected data compromise promptly. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through a risk-based combination of technical controls, management reviews, audits, assessments, testing and security monitoring activities. Monitoring shall be proportionate to the sensitivity of the data, system criticality and risk exposure.

Compliance activities may include:

| Compliance Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Party | Evidence Examples |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of access to sensitive data repositories | At least quarterly | Data Owners / System Owners | Access review records, approval evidence, removal records |
| Review of privileged access to databases, storage and backup systems | At least quarterly | IT Operations / Security | Privileged access reports, ticket records, remediation evidence |
| Encryption status review for endpoints and storage platforms | At least quarterly | IT Operations | Encryption compliance reports, device management records |
| Backup integrity and restoration testing | At least annually, or more frequently for critical systems | IT Operations / System Owners | Test results, restore logs, corrective actions |
| Review of cloud sharing and public exposure settings | At least quarterly | Cloud Platform Owners / Security | Configuration reports, remediation records |
| Data loss prevention alert review | Ongoing | Security Operations | Alert records, investigation notes, incident tickets |
| Third-party data security review | At onboarding and periodically based on risk | Vendor Management / Security | Due diligence records, contract reviews, assessment results |
| Secure disposal and media sanitisation review | At least annually | IT Operations / Compliance | Disposal certificates, asset records, sanitisation logs |
| Key management review | At least annually | Security / IT Operations | Key inventory, rotation records, access review evidence |
| Policy compliance assessment | At least annually | Information Security / Internal Audit | Assessment report, findings, remediation plan |

Non-compliance may result in corrective action, including access revocation, mandatory training, disciplinary action, contract remedies or termination of services. Serious or intentional violations may result in legal action or referral to appropriate authorities.

The organisation shall investigate suspected violations of this Policy. Confirmed violations shall be documented, risk-assessed and remediated within a timeframe appropriate to the severity of the issue.

Security control failures, data exposure, unauthorised disclosure, unauthorised modification, data loss or suspected compromise shall be managed through the organisation’s incident response process.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business need and the risk has been assessed, approved and accepted by authorised management.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Name, role and business unit of the person requesting the exception |
| Affected data | Type, classification and volume of data affected |
| Affected system or process | System, service, process, third party or environment involved |
| Policy requirement impacted | Specific requirement that cannot be met |
| Business justification | Reason the exception is required |
| Risk assessment | Security, privacy, legal, operational and business impact of the exception |
| Compensating controls | Alternative measures that reduce the risk |
| Duration | Requested start date and end date |
| Approvals | Data owner, system owner, security and other required approvals |
| Review date | Date when the exception will be reassessed |
| Remediation plan | Actions required to return to compliance, where applicable |

Exceptions shall:

- Be approved before implementation unless emergency action is required to protect the organisation.
- Be time-bound and reviewed before expiry.
- Include compensating controls where feasible.
- Not override legal, regulatory or contractual obligations unless approved by Legal and executive management.
- Be recorded in the organisation’s exception register.
- Be revoked if the accepted risk materially changes or compensating controls are not maintained.

Emergency exceptions may be granted by [Authorised Emergency Approver] where delay would create greater risk to the organisation. Emergency exceptions shall be documented and reviewed retrospectively within [number] business days.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect data security requirements, including:

- Changes to business operations, technology architecture or data processing activities.
- Introduction of new systems, cloud services or third-party data processors.
- Material security incidents, audit findings or control failures.
- Changes to legal, regulatory, contractual or privacy obligations.
- Significant changes to data classification, retention or records management requirements.
- Changes in threat landscape or organisational risk appetite.

The Policy Owner shall coordinate review and maintenance activities with relevant stakeholders, including Information Security, IT, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, Data Owners, System Owners and Internal Audit where applicable.

Policy changes shall be approved by [Approving Authority] before publication. Superseded versions shall be retained according to the organisation’s document retention requirements.

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Author | Approval |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [Effective Date] | Initial release | [Author Name / Role] | [Approver Name / Role] |

NIST-016.title: Platform Security Policy
NIST-016.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [POL-PLAT-SEC] | 1.0 | [Chief Information Security Officer] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this Platform Security Policy is to establish mandatory requirements for secure configuration, system hardening, vulnerability remediation, and patch management across organisational technology platforms.

This policy is intended to ensure that servers, endpoints, cloud platforms, network devices, containers, applications, databases, and supporting infrastructure are securely deployed, maintained, and monitored throughout their lifecycle. It supports consistent reduction of security weaknesses caused by misconfiguration, unsupported software, missing updates, excessive services, insecure defaults, and unauthorised changes.

## Scope

This policy applies to all technology platforms owned, managed, hosted, or operated by the organisation, including those operated by third parties on the organisation’s behalf.

In scope assets include, but are not limited to:

- Physical and virtual servers
- End-user computing devices, including desktops, laptops, mobile devices, and tablets
- Cloud infrastructure, platform services, and software-as-a-service administrative configurations
- Network infrastructure, including routers, switches, firewalls, wireless controllers, load balancers, and remote access gateways
- Identity and access management platforms
- Databases, middleware, application platforms, and web servers
- Containers, container orchestration platforms, images, registries, and serverless services
- Operational technology, where supported by operational and safety requirements
- Security tools and management platforms
- Backup, logging, monitoring, and administrative systems
- Development, test, staging, and production environments

This policy applies to:

- Employees, contractors, consultants, temporary workers, and third parties who configure, administer, support, or maintain in-scope platforms
- New platform deployments
- Existing platforms
- Platform changes, upgrades, migrations, and decommissioning activities
- Managed services and outsourced technology operations

This policy does not replace detailed technical standards, build guides, secure baseline documents, or operating procedures. Those documents shall support and align with this policy.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain an accurate inventory of in-scope platforms sufficient to support secure configuration, patching, vulnerability management, ownership assignment, and lifecycle management.

2. Each platform shall have an assigned business owner and technical owner accountable for ensuring the platform is securely configured, maintained, monitored, and supported.

3. Platforms shall be built and maintained using approved secure configuration baselines appropriate to the platform type, operating environment, business criticality, and data sensitivity.

4. Secure configuration baselines shall define, at minimum:
 - Approved operating system and software versions
 - Required security settings
 - Authentication and access control requirements
 - Logging and monitoring settings
 - Network exposure and service restrictions
 - Encryption requirements
 - Malware protection or equivalent protective controls
 - Administrative interface restrictions
 - Backup and recovery configuration requirements
 - Time synchronisation settings
 - Unnecessary service and feature removal requirements

5. Default vendor credentials, shared administrative passwords, insecure sample accounts, and unnecessary default accounts shall be removed, disabled, or changed before platforms are connected to production networks or made available to users.

6. Unnecessary services, protocols, ports, packages, software components, scripts, utilities, and administrative tools shall be disabled or removed unless there is a documented business requirement and approved risk acceptance.

7. Platforms shall be hardened before production use and whenever materially changed, rebuilt, upgraded, or migrated.

8. Platforms shall not be deployed to production unless they meet approved minimum security configuration requirements or have an approved exception.

9. Configuration baselines shall be reviewed and updated periodically and when significant threats, technology changes, vendor guidance, or organisational requirements change.

10. The organisation shall implement configuration management controls to ensure that platform configurations are defined, approved, documented, version-controlled where appropriate, and protected from unauthorised change.

11. All material platform configuration changes shall follow the organisation’s change management process, including risk assessment, testing, approval, implementation planning, rollback planning, and post-implementation validation.

12. Emergency changes shall be documented, reviewed, and formally approved as soon as practicable after implementation.

13. Administrative access to platforms shall be restricted to authorised personnel based on job responsibilities and the principle of least privilege.

14. Privileged access shall use approved secure authentication methods, including multi-factor authentication where technically supported and risk-appropriate.

15. Shared administrative accounts shall be prohibited unless technically unavoidable, formally approved, and controlled using compensating safeguards such as credential vaulting, session logging, and individual accountability.

16. Administrative interfaces shall not be exposed to the public internet unless explicitly approved, protected by strong authentication, monitored, and restricted by network access controls.

17. Platforms shall be configured to generate security-relevant logs that support monitoring, investigation, accountability, and incident response.

18. Security logs shall be protected from unauthorised modification, retained according to organisational retention requirements, and forwarded to approved monitoring or log management platforms where technically feasible.

19. Platforms shall use approved time synchronisation sources to support reliable logging, monitoring, and forensic analysis.

20. The organisation shall maintain a patch management process covering operating systems, firmware, hypervisors, applications, libraries, containers, appliances, network devices, security tools, and cloud-managed components under organisational responsibility.

21. Patches and security updates shall be assessed, prioritised, tested where appropriate, deployed, and verified within timeframes based on severity, exploitability, asset criticality, and business impact.

22. Unless a more stringent requirement is defined by the organisation, security patches shall be remediated within the following maximum timeframes:

| Severity | Typical Criteria | Maximum Remediation Timeframe |
|---|---|---:|
| Critical | Actively exploited, remotely exploitable, internet-facing exposure, or likely to cause significant compromise | 7 calendar days |
| High | Significant security impact, privilege escalation, sensitive data exposure, or high-value platform exposure | 14 calendar days |
| Medium | Moderate security impact or limited exploitability | 30 calendar days |
| Low | Limited security impact, low likelihood, or defence-in-depth improvement | 90 calendar days |

23. Where active exploitation is confirmed or credible threat intelligence indicates imminent exploitation, the organisation shall accelerate remediation and apply emergency mitigation measures as directed by Security.

24. If a patch cannot be applied within the required timeframe, the technical owner shall implement approved compensating controls and submit an exception request.

25. Patch testing shall be proportionate to platform criticality and shall not be used to unreasonably delay remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities.

26. Patch deployment shall include validation to confirm that updates were successfully installed and that the platform remains operational.

27. Firmware, appliance software, network device operating systems, and management plane software shall be included in patch and lifecycle management activities.

28. Container images, base images, software dependencies, and runtime components shall be maintained using approved sources and updated to remediate known security weaknesses.
