- Scan name, scan date/time, scanner used, and scan policy/template.
- In-scope assets scanned, including hostname, IP address, cloud resource ID, application, or container image.
- Asset owner or responsible team, where available.
- Vulnerability identifier, title, affected asset, severity, risk score, and description.
- Detection date, first seen date, last seen date, and current status.
- Remediation recommendation or required action.
- Remediation due date or service-level target.
- Ticket ID or workflow reference linking the finding to remediation tracking.
- Assigned owner, ticket status, status history, closure date, and closure notes.
- Evidence of fix validation, such as rescan result, patch status, or “no longer detected” status.
- Records of risk acceptance, exception approval, compensating controls, and expiry date, where remediation is deferred.
- Summary metrics: total open vulnerabilities, critical/high count, remediated count, overdue count, and ageing.

## Frequency & Owner

- Collection frequency: monthly at minimum; weekly for critical environments or externally exposed assets.
- Scan frequency: as defined by the vulnerability management process, with continuous or frequent scanning preferred for internet-facing, cloud, and critical systems.
- Evidence owner: [Security Operations Manager] or [Vulnerability Management Lead].
- Supporting owners: [IT Operations], [Cloud Operations], [Application Owners], and [Service Desk/ITSM Owner].

## Retention & Storage

Store exported records in [Evidence Repository Name], such as a GRC platform, secure SharePoint site, document management system, or audit evidence folder.

Retention should be at least [Retention Period], or longer if required by contract, regulation, or internal policy. Access must be limited to authorised security, IT, compliance, and audit personnel. Preserve files in read-only PDF format where possible, with supporting CSV/XLSX exports retained for sampling and traceability.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will typically accept this evidence when it shows:

- Vulnerability scans were performed during the review period.
- The scope includes relevant systems, applications, endpoints, cloud assets, or networks.
- Findings include severity, affected asset, detection date, and remediation guidance.
- Vulnerabilities are tracked through a defined workflow or ticketing process.
- Critical and high-risk findings have owners, due dates, and current status.
- Closed findings include evidence of remediation or validation through rescan or patch status.
- Overdue vulnerabilities are visible and explainable.
- Risk acceptances or exceptions are approved, time-bound, and documented.
- Reports are system-generated from [Vulnerability Scanner Name], [ITSM Tool Name], or other authoritative operational tools.
- Evidence files are dated, complete for the selected period, and stored in a controlled repository.

| Policy / Standard / Procedure Covered | Enter the internal policy, standard, procedure, or code of conduct addressed by the training, including document name and version where available. |
| Required For | State the population required to complete the training, such as All workforce, New starters, Privileged users, Developers, Executives, Finance staff, HR staff, Contractors, or named role group. |
| Assignment Trigger | Select one value: Onboarding, Annual Recertification, Role Change, Privileged Access Granted, Policy Change, Incident / Corrective Action, Campaign, Contractual Requirement, Other. |
| Delivery Method | Select one value: LMS E-learning, Instructor-Led, Webinar, Workshop, Phishing Simulation, Tabletop Exercise, Policy Acknowledgement, Email Campaign, External Course, Other. |
| Training Provider / Owner | Enter the internal team or external provider responsible for delivering the training, e.g. Security Awareness Team, HR Learning, CISO Office, External Vendor Name. |
| Assigned Date | Enter the date the training was assigned to the learner in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Due Date | Enter the date by which the learner must complete the training in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Completion Date | Enter the actual completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank if not completed. |
| Completion Status | Select one value: Not Assigned, Assigned, In Progress, Completed, Completed Late, Overdue, Exempted, Deferred, Failed, Cancelled. |
| Assessment Required | Select one value: Yes, No. |
| Assessment Score | Enter the learner’s assessment score as a percentage from 0 to 100; enter N/A if no assessment is required. |
| Pass Mark | Enter the required passing score as a percentage from 0 to 100; enter N/A if no assessment is required. |
| Pass / Fail Result | Select one value: Pass, Fail, N/A, Pending. |
| Acknowledgement Required | Select one value: Yes, No. Use Yes where the learner must acknowledge a policy, standard, code of conduct, or training completion statement. |
| Acknowledgement Completed | Select one value: Yes, No, N/A. Use Yes only where acknowledgement evidence is available. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the link, file path, LMS record URL, ticket reference, or repository location where completion evidence, attendance record, certificate, acknowledgement, or assessment result is retained. |
| Certificate / Completion ID | Enter the certificate number, LMS completion ID, campaign result ID, attendance sheet reference, or N/A if not issued. |
| Exception / Deferral Reference | Enter the approved exception, waiver, or deferral reference if the learner did not complete by the required date; enter N/A if none. |
| Next Training Due Date | Enter the next required completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format based on the required refresher cycle; enter N/A if not recurring. |
| Manager / Approver | Enter the manager, course owner, or authorised approver responsible for confirming completion, exception, or deferral where applicable. |
| Record Last Updated | Enter the date this row was last updated in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Notes | Enter brief audit-relevant comments only, such as reason for late completion, reassignment, role change, duplicate record correction, or evidence clarification. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Security Awareness or GRC lead with HR Learning/LMS support; update after each training assignment, completion, exception, or campaign closeout, and review at least monthly. Source data should come from the LMS, HRIS, IAM/PAM role lists, phishing simulation platform, attendance records, and approved exception repository.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this access review record, using a consistent format such as AR-YYYY-###. |
| Review Cycle | Enter the scheduled review cycle, using allowed values: Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annual, Annual, Ad Hoc. |
| Review Period Start | Enter the first date covered by the access review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Review Period End | Enter the final date covered by the access review in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| System/Application | Enter the name of the system, application, platform, database, directory, or service whose access is being reviewed. |
| Environment | Enter the environment reviewed, using allowed values: Production, Non-Production, Development, Test, UAT, DR, Cloud, SaaS, Other. |
| Data/Asset Classification | Enter the highest classification of information or assets accessible through this account or role, using the organisation's approved classification scheme such as Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, Highly Restricted. |
| Account/User ID | Enter the exact account identifier, username, privileged account name, service account name, or unique identity value as shown in the source system. |
| User Full Name | Enter the legal or HR-recorded full name of the user; for non-human accounts enter Service Account, Shared Account, Break Glass Account, or System Account as applicable. |
| User Type | Enter the type of identity, using allowed values: Employee, Contractor, Third Party, Service Account, Shared Account, Privileged Account, Break Glass, Guest, Other. |
| Employment/Engagement Status | Enter the current status from HR/vendor records, using allowed values: Active, Leave, Transferred, Terminated, Contract Ended, Unknown, Not Applicable. |
| Department/Business Unit | Enter the user's current department, team, business unit, or vendor organisation responsible for the account. |
| Manager/Business Owner | Enter the name of the user's manager or the business owner accountable for approving the access. |
| Role/Group/Profile Reviewed | Enter the role, group, entitlement, permission set, profile, policy, or access package being reviewed exactly as named in the source system. |
| Privilege Level | Enter the level of access, using allowed values: Standard User, Power User, Administrator, Privileged Administrator, Read Only, Write/Modify, Approver, Developer, Service, Other. |
| Access Purpose/Business Justification | Enter the business reason the user or account requires the access; this must be specific enough to support least privilege and role appropriateness. |
| Access Granted Date | Enter the date the access was originally granted in YYYY-MM-DD format; if unavailable, enter Unknown. |
| Last Login Date | Enter the most recent successful login or use date in YYYY-MM-DD format; if unavailable or not applicable, enter Unknown or N/A. |
| Access Source | Enter where the access data came from, such as IAM export, Active Directory, Entra ID, Okta, HRIS, PAM tool, application admin report, database query, or ticketing system. |
| Review Date | Enter the date the reviewer assessed this access in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Reviewer Name | Enter the full name of the person who reviewed and certified or challenged the access. |
| Reviewer Role | Enter the reviewer's authority for the review, using values such as Line Manager, System Owner, Data Owner, Application Owner, Information Security, IAM Administrator, Compliance. |
| Review Decision | Enter the outcome of the review, using allowed values: Retain, Modify, Remove, Suspend, Investigate, Exception Approved. |
| Decision Rationale | Enter a concise reason supporting the review decision, including why the access remains appropriate or why a change is required. |
| Exception Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether the access deviates from policy, least privilege, segregation of duties, or standard role design and requires formal exception approval. |
| Exception ID | If Exception Required is Yes, enter the approved exception or risk acceptance identifier; otherwise enter N/A. |
| Required Change Type | Enter the access change required, using allowed values: None, Add, Modify, Remove, Disable, Suspend, Reassign Owner, Recertify, Investigate. |
| Change Request/Ticket ID | Enter the workflow, ITSM, IAM, or change ticket reference used to perform or track the access change; enter N/A if no change is required. |
| Change Description | Describe the exact change to be made, such as remove admin group, disable terminated user account, reduce role from approver to read only, or update service account owner. |
| Change Owner | Enter the person or team responsible for implementing the access change, such as IAM Operations, Application Admin, System Owner, Database Admin, or PAM Administrator. |
| Change Due Date | Enter the target completion date for the required access change in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no change is required. |
| Change Completion Date | Enter the actual date the access change was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if not completed or no change is required. |
| Change Status | Enter the current state of the change, using allowed values: Not Required, Open, In Progress, Completed, Overdue, Cancelled, Deferred. |
| Validation Method | Enter how completion was verified, such as system export, screenshot, access recertification report, IAM audit log, ticket closure evidence, PAM report, or application admin confirmation. |
| Validator Name | Enter the full name of the person who validated that the review decision or access change was correctly completed. |
| Validation Date | Enter the date validation was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if validation has not yet occurred or is not required. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the repository path, URL, ticket link, report name, or evidence reference where supporting evidence is stored; do not paste sensitive credentials or personal data beyond what is necessary. |
| Residual Risk Rating | Enter the remaining risk after review and any change action, using allowed values: Low, Medium, High, Critical, N/A. |
| Approver Name | Enter the name of the accountable approver for retained privileged access, exceptions, deferred removals, or review sign-off. |
| Approval Date | Enter the date approval or certification was given in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A where approval is not required. |
| Comments | Enter any additional context needed for audit traceability, such as dependency notes, compensating controls, delayed action reason, or follow-up required. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the IAM Manager or Access Control Process Owner, with review sign-off by system/application owners and oversight from Information Security or GRC. Updated at each scheduled access review cycle and whenever access changes are identified, using source data from IAM directories, HRIS, PAM tools, application access exports, ITSM/change tickets, and relevant audit logs.

NIST-025.title: Detection / SOC Alerts Logs
NIST-025.content:
## What This Evidences

Detection / SOC Alerts Logs evidence that the organisation is identifying and recording anomalous activity, security events, and potential incidents through monitoring and detection processes aligned to NIST CSF 2.0 DE.AE and DE.CM. This includes SIEM-generated events, correlation alerts, endpoint/network/cloud detections, and anomaly indicators reviewed by security operations.

This artifact is collected from operational systems. It is not authored manually and must not be recreated or fabricated. The evidence should be exported directly from the organisation’s monitoring, SIEM, SOAR, EDR, cloud security, or ticketing platforms.

## Where To Collect It From

Collect the evidence from the primary systems used to monitor and triage security alerts, typically including:

- SIEM or log analytics platform: [SIEM/log platform name]
- SOAR or SOC case management platform: [SOAR/case tool name]
- ITSM or security ticketing system: [ITSM/ticketing tool name]
- EDR/XDR platform: [EDR/XDR tool name]
- Cloud security monitoring platform: [cloud security tool name]
- Network detection and response platform: [NDR/IDS/IPS tool name]
- Identity monitoring platform: [IdP/identity security tool name]

Use the system of record for SOC alerting where alerts are generated, correlated, triaged, and closed.

## How To Collect

1. Log in to [SIEM/log platform name] or the designated SOC alerting platform using an authorised account.
2. Navigate to the alerts, detections, incidents, notable events, or security monitoring dashboard.
3. Set the date range for the audit sample period, such as [start date] to [end date].
4. Apply filters to include relevant alert types, such as anomaly detection, correlation rules, high-risk events, endpoint detections, identity alerts, cloud security alerts, and network intrusion detections.
5. Include all severities, or at minimum capture medium, high, and critical alerts, depending on the monitoring process.
6. Export the alert list in CSV, JSON, PDF, or native report format.
7. For selected sample alerts, open each alert record and capture the detailed alert page, investigation timeline, linked events, affected assets, user accounts, and disposition.
8. If alerts are converted into tickets or cases, export the linked records from [ITSM/ticketing tool name] or [SOAR/case tool name].
9. Save the export and screenshots to the approved evidence repository using the agreed naming convention.
10. Record the collection date, collector name, source system, query/filter used, and audit period covered.

## What To Capture

The evidence should include enough detail to show detection occurred and was handled. Capture:

- Alert ID, event ID, incident ID, or case reference
- Detection rule, correlation rule, analytic name, or alert title
- Alert severity, priority, risk score, or confidence level
- Date and time detected, including time zone
- Source log type or detection source
- Affected host, application, cloud resource, IP address, user account, or identity
- Description of suspicious or anomalous activity
- Raw or related event references where available
- Alert status, such as open, acknowledged, investigating, escalated, closed, or false positive
- Assigned analyst, team, or queue
- Triage notes, investigation comments, or disposition
- Response action taken, if applicable
- Closure reason and closure timestamp
- Links to related tickets, cases, incidents, or change records
- Screenshot of dashboard summary for the period
- Exported alert list for the selected period

## Frequency & Owner

- Frequency: Collect monthly for ongoing control evidence, and additionally for each audit request, incident review, or control assessment.
- Owner: SOC Manager, Security Operations Lead, or designated Detection Engineering owner.
- Collector: Authorised SOC analyst or GRC evidence coordinator with read-only access to the relevant platforms.
- Reviewer: Information Security Manager or Security Operations Manager.

## Retention & Storage

Store exported logs, reports, and screenshots in [evidence repository name] under restricted access. Retain them for [retention period], or longer if required for legal hold, incident investigation, customer commitment, or regulatory obligation.

Preserve exports in their original format where possible. Do not edit raw exports. If screenshots are used, ensure timestamps, filters, and source system names are visible. Protect evidence containing personal data, credentials, IP addresses, or sensitive security information according to the organisation’s data handling requirements.

## Acceptance Criteria

An auditor will generally accept this evidence when:

- The evidence is exported directly from [SIEM/log platform name], [SOAR/case tool name], [EDR/XDR tool name], or another approved monitoring system.
- The date range clearly covers the assessment period.
- Alerts show actual detection of anomalies, suspicious events, or security-relevant activity.
- Alert records include timestamps, severity, source, affected asset or user, and status.
- Sample alerts show triage, investigation notes, escalation, closure, or disposition.
- Links to tickets or cases are present where the process requires them.
- Screenshots or exports show the source system, filters, and collection date.
- Evidence is complete, unaltered, access-controlled, and traceable to the organisation’s operational monitoring environment.

EVID-INC-2026-0001] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Incident ID | Enter the unique incident reference using the organisation’s incident numbering format, e.g. INC-YYYY-0001. |
| Incident Title | Enter a short, specific title describing the incident, e.g. phishing email compromise, ransomware detection, cloud storage exposure. |
| Incident Type | Select the primary category: Malware, Phishing, Credential Compromise, Unauthorized Access, Data Loss/Leakage, Denial of Service, Insider Threat, Third-Party Incident, Vulnerability Exploitation, Physical/Safety, Availability Outage, Policy Violation, Other. |
| Detection Source | Record how the incident was identified, e.g. SIEM alert, EDR alert, user report, helpdesk ticket, third-party notification, audit finding, vulnerability scan, law enforcement, customer notification. |
| Date/Time Detected | Enter the date and time the organisation first detected or was notified of the incident in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ. |
| Date/Time Incident Started | Enter the estimated or confirmed start date/time of the incident in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ; use 'Unknown' if not known. |
| Date/Time Incident Ended | Enter the date/time malicious activity or incident condition ended in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ; use 'Open' if ongoing or 'Unknown' if not known. |
| Reported By | Enter the name, role/team, or source that reported the incident; use a ticket ID if reported via service desk or monitoring workflow. |
| Incident Owner | Enter the accountable response owner by role or named individual, e.g. Incident Commander, SOC Lead, IT Operations Manager. |
| Business Service / Asset Affected | List affected business services, applications, systems, networks, data stores, or assets; include asset IDs/CMDB references where available. |
| Asset Owner | Enter the business or technical owner responsible for the affected asset or service. |
| Location / Environment | Specify where the incident occurred: Production, Development, Test, Corporate IT, Cloud, SaaS, OT/ICS, Remote Endpoint, Third Party, Physical Site; include region/site if relevant. |
| Initial Severity | Record severity assigned at triage using the organisation’s scale, e.g. Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational, with rationale if required by procedure. |
| Final Severity | Record final validated severity after investigation using the same scale as Initial Severity. |
| Priority | Record response priority based on severity and business impact, e.g. P1, P2, P3, P4, according to the incident response procedure. |
| Incident Status | Select the current lifecycle status: New, Triage, Investigation, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, Monitoring, Post-Incident Review, Closed. |
| Incident Description | Provide a factual summary of what happened, including timeline highlights, affected scope, and known attacker or failure activity; do not include speculation unless labelled as such. |
| Indicators of Compromise / Evidence References | Record IOCs and evidence locations, e.g. IPs, domains, hashes, filenames, alert IDs, log locations, forensic image IDs, screenshots, email headers, SIEM case references. |
| Data Impact | Describe whether data confidentiality, integrity, or availability was affected; identify data types involved, e.g. personal data, customer data, financial data, credentials, intellectual property; state 'No known data impact' if applicable. |
| Systems Impact | Describe affected system functionality and technical impact, e.g. unavailable, degraded, encrypted, misconfigured, unauthorized change, isolated, rebuilt. |
| Business Impact | Describe operational impact, affected users/customers, downtime, transaction impact, financial estimate, SLA impact, or reputational impact; use 'None identified' if applicable. |
| Safety / Legal / Regulatory Impact | Record any safety, contractual, legal, privacy, regulatory, law enforcement, or sector reporting implications; state 'None identified' if assessed and not applicable. |
| Containment Actions Taken | Record actions used to limit impact, e.g. account disabled, host isolated, firewall block, token revoked, email purged; include dates/times and responsible teams where possible. |
| Eradication Actions Taken | Record actions used to remove the cause or threat, e.g. malware removed, vulnerability patched, credentials reset, persistence removed, misconfiguration corrected. |
| Recovery Actions Taken | Record actions used to restore normal operations, e.g. restore from backup, rebuild system, validate integrity, return host to network, user access restored, enhanced monitoring enabled. |
| Communications Sent | Record internal and external communications issued, including audience, date/time, channel, and reference to approved message or communication log. |
| External Parties Involved | List third parties involved in response or affected by the incident, e.g. MSSP, cloud provider, insurer, legal counsel, regulator, law enforcement, supplier, customer; state 'None' if not applicable. |
| Notification / Reporting Required | Record required notifications or reporting obligations, e.g. regulator, data protection authority, customers, insurer, law enforcement, board, contractual party; include deadline where applicable. |
| Notification / Reporting Completed | Record whether required notifications were completed: Yes, No, Not Applicable, Pending; include completion date/time and evidence reference if completed. |
| Root Cause | Enter the validated root cause after investigation, e.g. unpatched vulnerability, compromised credential, misconfiguration, process failure, user error, vendor failure; use 'Pending PIR' until confirmed. |
| Contributing Factors | Record conditions that increased likelihood or impact, e.g. weak monitoring, excessive privileges, missing MFA, delayed patching, insufficient backups, unclear escalation path. |
| Lessons Learned Summary | Summarize the key lessons from the post-incident review, including what worked well, what did not work, and what should change in people, process, or technology. |
| Corrective / Improvement Actions | List specific remediation or improvement actions agreed from the incident and lessons learned; each action should be measurable and trackable. |
| Action Owner | Enter the person or role accountable for completing the corrective/improvement action; use 'Multiple - see linked action tracker' if more than one owner exists. |
| Action Due Date | Enter the target completion date for the corrective/improvement action in YYYY-MM-DD format; use 'Not Applicable' only where no action is required. |
| Action Status | Select the action status: Not Started, In Progress, Blocked, Complete, Accepted Risk, Cancelled, Not Applicable. |
| Residual Risk | Record the remaining risk after response and corrective actions using the organisation’s risk scale, e.g. Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Accepted; include risk register ID where applicable. |
| Management Approval / Closure | Record the name/role of the approver confirming incident closure and acceptance of residual risk, if any; include approval date or reference. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the incident record was formally closed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until closure is approved. |
| Linked Records / References | Enter links or IDs for related tickets, SIEM cases, forensic reports, communications logs, risk register entries, change records, problem records, evidence folders, and post-incident review minutes. |

### Maintenance

Owned by the Incident Response Manager or SOC Manager, with review by Legal/Privacy and Business Continuity as required. Updated for every incident at each response phase and formally completed after the post-incident review; source data should be drawn from the incident management platform, SIEM/SOAR, EDR, service desk, communications log, evidence repository, and post-incident review records.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Record ID | Enter a unique identifier for this supplier due diligence record, using format SCDD-YYYY-NNN, for example SCDD-2026-001. |
| Supplier Legal Name | Enter the supplier's full registered legal entity name exactly as shown in procurement, contract, or company registry records. |
| Supplier Trading Name | Enter the supplier's common trading, brand, or DBA name if different from the legal name; enter 'N/A' if not applicable. |
| Supplier Unique Identifier | Enter the internal vendor ID, ERP supplier number, DUNS number, company registration number, or equivalent unique identifier. |
| Business Owner | Enter the internal business owner accountable for the supplier relationship, including name and role or function. |
| Procurement Owner | Enter the procurement or vendor management contact responsible for onboarding or contract management. |
| Assessment Owner | Enter the individual or team responsible for completing the cybersecurity supply chain due diligence assessment. |
| Assessment Type | Select one value: New Supplier, Renewal, Periodic Review, Material Change, Incident-Driven Review, Offboarding Review. |
| Assessment Trigger | Describe why the assessment is being performed, such as new onboarding, contract renewal, new data access, service expansion, regulatory requirement, incident, or scheduled review. |
| Assessment Status | Select one value: Not Started, In Progress, Evidence Requested, Under Review, Remediation Required, Approved, Approved with Conditions, Rejected, Closed. |
| Date Assessment Started | Enter the date the due diligence assessment began in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Date Assessment Completed | Enter the date assessment review was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until complete. |
| Next Review Due Date | Enter the next scheduled reassessment date in YYYY-MM-DD format, based on supplier criticality and risk. |
| Product or Service Provided | Describe the product, service, platform, outsourced function, or technology supplied to the organisation. |
| Business Process Supported | Identify the internal business process, system, product line, or operational service that depends on this supplier. |
| Supplier Criticality | Select one value: Critical, High, Medium, Low; rate based on business impact if the supplier fails, is disrupted, or is compromised. |
| Inherent Risk Rating | Select one value: Critical, High, Medium, Low before considering supplier controls, based on service criticality, data sensitivity, connectivity, concentration, geography, and regulatory exposure. |
| Cybersecurity Risk Rating | Select one value: Critical, High, Medium, Low based on the likelihood and impact of supplier compromise, access level, control maturity, and assurance evidence. |
| Privacy Risk Rating | Select one value: Critical, High, Medium, Low, N/A based on whether the supplier processes personal data, special category data, customer data, employee data, or regulated personal information. |
| Operational Resilience Risk Rating | Select one value: Critical, High, Medium, Low based on dependency on the supplier for availability, continuity, recovery, service delivery, or customer impact. |
| Data Access or Processing | Select one value: No Data, Public Data Only, Internal Data, Confidential Data, Restricted Data, Personal Data, Regulated Data; choose the highest sensitivity category involved. |
| Data Classification | Enter the organisation-approved data classification label applicable to the data shared with or processed by the supplier; enter 'N/A' if no data is involved. |
| System or Network Access | Select one value: None, User Portal Only, API Access, Privileged Access, Remote Network Access, Direct System Integration, Administrative Access. |
| Cloud or Hosting Model | Select one value: N/A, SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, Managed Service, On-Premises Supplier Hosted, Organisation Hosted, Hybrid. |
| Geographic Processing Locations | List countries or regions where services are delivered, data is stored, data is processed, or support personnel access systems; use comma-separated country names. |
| Fourth-Party or Subcontractor Dependency | State whether the supplier uses material subcontractors or fourth parties for the service; use Yes, No, or Unknown, and name key subcontractors where known. |
| Due Diligence Evidence Received | List the evidence received for the assessment, such as questionnaire, SOC 2, ISO certificate, penetration test summary, BCP test, policy documents, DPIA, SIG, CAIQ, or contract addendum. |
| Security Questionnaire Status | Select one value: Not Required, Not Sent, Sent, Received, Reviewed, Clarification Required, Accepted, Rejected. |
| Independent Assurance Reviewed | Select one value: SOC 2 Type II, SOC 2 Type I, ISO 27001 Certificate, PCI DSS AOC, CSA STAR, Independent Penetration Test, Other, None. |
| Independent Assurance Report Date | Enter the issue date or reporting period end date of the most relevant independent assurance report in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter 'N/A' if none. |
| Key Certifications or Attestations | List applicable certifications or attestations reviewed, including standard name, scope, and expiry date where available. |
| Vulnerability Management Evidence | Summarise evidence reviewed for vulnerability identification, patching, remediation SLAs, scanning, penetration testing, and vulnerability disclosure; enter 'Not Provided' if absent. |
| Incident Response Evidence | Summarise evidence reviewed for incident response plans, roles, escalation, customer notification, testing, and recent incident handling; enter 'Not Provided' if absent. |

| Encryption Evidence | Summarise evidence reviewed for encryption in transit, encryption at rest, key management, certificate management, and cryptographic standards. |
| Logging and Monitoring Evidence | Summarise evidence reviewed for security logging, monitoring, alerting, SIEM/SOC coverage, retention periods, and response procedures. |
| Privacy and Data Protection Evidence | Summarise evidence reviewed for privacy notices, data processing controls, retention, deletion, cross-border transfers, data subject rights, DPIA, or equivalent privacy review. |

NIST-028.title: BC/DR Test Results
NIST-028.content:
## BC/DR Test Results (DOCX template)

_Editable template — add your own rows. The example row(s) below are placeholders to replace._

| Test ID | Test Name | Recovery Plan Reference | NIST CSF 2.0 Reference | Test Type | Scenario Tested | Business Service or Process | System or Asset in Scope | Criticality Rating | Test Objective | Test Scope | Test Date | Test Start Time | Test End Time | Test Coordinator | Business Owner | Technical Recovery Owner | Participants | Recovery Point Objective Target | Recovery Time Objective Target | Actual Recovery Point Achieved | Actual Recovery Time Achieved | Recovery Procedure Steps Executed | Deviations from Approved Plan | Dependencies Tested | Communications Tested | Evidence Location | Test Result | Success Criteria Met | Issues or Gaps Identified | Impact of Issues | Corrective Action Reference | Corrective Action Owner | Corrective Action Due Date | Retest Required | Retest Date | Lessons Learned | Recovery Plan Updates Required | Approval Status | Approved By | Approval Date | Next Scheduled Test Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [EXAMPLE: BCDR-TEST-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: Finance System Backup Restore Exercise] | [EXAMPLE: DRP-FIN-APP-v3.0] | [EXAMPLE: RC.RP] | [EXAMPLE: Backup Restore Test] | [EXAMPLE: Simulated database corruption requiring restore from backup] | [EXAMPLE: Month-End Financial Close] | [EXAMPLE: FIN-APP-001 / FIN-DB-001] | [EXAMPLE: Critical] | [EXAMPLE: Validate restoration of the finance database within approved RTO and RPO] | [EXAMPLE: Included production-equivalent recovery environment and backup platform; excluded full user acceptance testing] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-18] | [EXAMPLE: 09:00 UTC] | [EXAMPLE: 11:20 UTC] | [EXAMPLE: Jane Smith, BC/DR Manager] | [EXAMPLE: Mark Patel, Finance Operations Director] | [EXAMPLE: Alex Chen, Infrastructure Recovery Lead] | [EXAMPLE: Finance Operations, Infrastructure, Database Administration, Service Desk] | [EXAMPLE: 1 hour] | [EXAMPLE: 4 hours] | [EXAMPLE: 30 minutes data loss] | [EXAMPLE: 2 hours 20 minutes] | [EXAMPLE: Restore checklist DR-CHK-FIN-001 completed] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: Backup platform, privileged access, database services, network connectivity] | [EXAMPLE: Incident bridge and recovery status email distribution list] | [EXAMPLE: GRC repository / BCDR Tests / 2026 / BCDR-TEST-2026-001] | [EXAMPLE: Pass] | [EXAMPLE: Yes] | [EXAMPLE: None] | [EXAMPLE: No adverse impact identified] | [EXAMPLE: Not applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Not applicable] | [EXAMPLE: No] | [EXAMPLE: Not applicable] | [EXAMPLE: Recovery evidence should be captured during each step rather than after the exercise] | [EXAMPLE: Yes - update runbook to add evidence capture prompts] | [EXAMPLE: Approved] | [EXAMPLE: Mark Patel, Finance Operations Director] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-03-21] | [EXAMPLE: 2026-09-18] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Test ID | Enter a unique identifier for the recovery exercise record, using a consistent format such as BCDR-TEST-YYYY-###. |
| Test Name | Enter the short name of the exercise, for example the application, service, or scenario being tested. |
| Recovery Plan Reference | Enter the identifier and version of the approved BC/DR or recovery plan tested, for example DRP-PAYROLL-v2.1. |
| NIST CSF 2.0 Reference | Enter the applicable NIST CSF 2.0 control reference; for this template use RC.RP unless the organisation maps additional references. |
| Test Type | Select the type of exercise performed: Tabletop, Walkthrough, Technical Recovery Test, Backup Restore Test, Failover Test, Full Interruption Test, Communications Test, or Other. |
| Scenario Tested | Describe the simulated disruption or recovery scenario tested, such as ransomware event, loss of primary site, corrupted database, cloud region outage, or key supplier outage. |
| Business Service or Process | Enter the business service, process, or function whose recovery capability was tested. |
| System or Asset in Scope | Enter the application, infrastructure, data store, platform, site, or asset covered by the test; use asset register names or IDs where available. |
| Criticality Rating | Enter the approved business criticality rating for the service or asset, using the organisation’s scale such as Critical, High, Medium, or Low. |
| Test Objective | State the specific recovery objective being validated, such as restore service from backup within RTO, validate failover procedure, or confirm recovery communications. |
| Test Scope | Describe what was included and excluded from the exercise, including locations, systems, teams, data sets, environments, and limitations. |
| Test Date | Enter the date the test was performed in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Test Start Time | Enter the actual start time of the test in 24-hour format with time zone, for example 09:30 UTC. |
| Test End Time | Enter the actual end time of the test in 24-hour format with time zone, for example 13:45 UTC. |
| Test Coordinator | Enter the name and role of the person responsible for coordinating the test. |
| Business Owner | Enter the name and role of the accountable business owner for the service or process tested. |
| Technical Recovery Owner | Enter the name and role of the person accountable for technical recovery execution. |
| Participants | List the teams, roles, and key individuals who participated in the exercise. |
| Recovery Point Objective Target | Enter the approved RPO target for the service or system, using time units such as 15 minutes, 4 hours, or 1 business day. |
| Recovery Time Objective Target | Enter the approved RTO target for the service or system, using time units such as 1 hour, 4 hours, or 24 hours. |
| Actual Recovery Point Achieved | Enter the actual point to which data was restored or recovered, expressed as data loss duration or timestamp, for example 10 minutes data loss or restored to 2026-06-30 22:00 UTC. |
| Actual Recovery Time Achieved | Enter the measured elapsed time from declared test start or simulated incident declaration to verified recovery, using hours and minutes. |
| Recovery Procedure Steps Executed | Summarise the approved recovery procedure steps completed, or reference the completed checklist ID/location. |
| Deviations from Approved Plan | Record any steps skipped, changed, performed out of order, manually improvised, or not applicable; enter None if there were no deviations. |
| Dependencies Tested | Record key dependencies validated during the test, such as identity services, DNS, network connectivity, backup platform, third-party provider, facilities, or privileged access. |
| Communications Tested | Record the recovery communications channels and escalation paths tested, such as call tree, incident bridge, crisis management tool, email, SMS, or executive notifications. |
| Evidence Location | Enter the repository link, ticket number, folder path, or system reference where test evidence is stored, such as screenshots, logs, meeting notes, completed checklists, and approvals. |
| Test Result | Select the overall result: Pass, Pass with Issues, Fail, Partial, or Cancelled. |
| Success Criteria Met | Enter Yes, No, or Partial, based on whether the predefined test objectives and acceptance criteria were achieved. |
| Issues or Gaps Identified | Describe any recovery gaps, control weaknesses, procedural failures, missing access, tooling failures, timing failures, communication issues, or documentation errors; enter None if no issues were found. |
| Impact of Issues | Describe the risk or operational impact of the issues found, including whether RTO/RPO, service availability, data integrity, communications, or regulatory obligations were affected. |
| Corrective Action Reference | Enter the linked action, risk, issue, audit finding, or ticket ID created to remediate identified gaps; enter Not applicable if no corrective action is required. |
| Corrective Action Owner | Enter the name and role of the person accountable for completing the corrective action; enter Not applicable if no corrective action is required. |
| Corrective Action Due Date | Enter the agreed due date for remediation in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not applicable if no corrective action is required. |
| Retest Required | Enter Yes or No to indicate whether a follow-up test is required to confirm remediation or recovery capability. |
| Retest Date | Enter the planned or completed retest date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter Not scheduled if not yet planned or Not applicable if no retest is required. |
| Lessons Learned | Record concise lessons learned from the exercise, including improvements to people, process, technology, documentation, or communications. |
| Recovery Plan Updates Required | Enter Yes or No and briefly state what recovery plan, procedure, contact list, dependency map, or runbook updates are required. |
| Approval Status | Select the review status of the test result record: Draft, Under Review, Approved, Rejected, or Superseded. |
| Approved By | Enter the name and role of the authorised approver for the test results, typically the business owner, BC/DR manager, or risk owner. |
| Approval Date | Enter the date the test result was approved in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until approved. |
| Next Scheduled Test Date | Enter the next planned recovery exercise date for the service or system in YYYY-MM-DD format. |

### Maintenance

The BC/DR Manager or Resilience Lead owns this template and updates it after each recovery exercise, failed test, significant system change, plan change, or at least annually. The log should draw from the BC/DR planning repository, test evidence repository, incident management system, asset register, backup/recovery tools, and corrective action or GRC tracking system.
