- Where recovery requirements exceed current capability, the gap must be documented and either remediated, deferred with approved action planning, or formally accepted as residual risk.
- Material budget changes require approval from the Executive Sponsor.
- Spend must follow [Organisation Name] procurement and financial approval processes.
- The project will distinguish between implementation costs and ongoing BCMS operating costs.

### Tools and Facilities

The project will use the following resources:

| Resource Type | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Document repository | Controlled, access-managed repository for BCMS records, approvals, evidence, and plan versions |
| Collaboration tools | Workshop scheduling, shared drafting, action tracking, and stakeholder communication |
| BCMS templates | Standard templates for BIA, risk assessment, continuity plans, exercise records, action logs, and management reporting |
| Notification capability | Mechanism for emergency communications, call tree testing, and stakeholder notification, where available |
| Data sources | Asset inventories, application lists, supplier registers, organisation charts, risk registers, service catalogues, incident records, and contracts |
| Meeting facilities | Physical or virtual workshop facilities suitable for confidential discussion and scenario exercises |
| Evidence management | Structured approach for retaining approvals, attendance records, reviews, exercise outcomes, issue logs, and improvement evidence |

### Project Governance

Project governance will operate as follows:

| Governance Activity | Frequency | Participants | Output |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Project status reporting | Weekly or fortnightly | BCMS Project Manager, Business Continuity Manager | Status report, risks, issues, actions |
| Steering Committee meeting | Monthly or at key decision points | Sponsor, senior stakeholders, project leads | Decisions, approvals, escalations |
| Workstream meetings | Weekly or as required | Relevant functional leads | Task progress, dependencies, blockers |
| Risk and issue review | At each project status meeting | Project Manager, relevant owners | Updated risk and issue log |
| Deliverable review | At planned checkpoints | Deliverable owner, reviewers, approvers | Comments, approval, rework actions |
| Management review | Before project closure and then periodically | Executive Sponsor, leadership, BCMS owner | BCMS performance and readiness decision |

## Success Metrics

The BCMS project will be considered successful when it delivers a practical, approved, and operating BCMS that supports the continuity of priority products and services and is embedded into ongoing management arrangements.

| Metric | Target | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Project charter approval | Approved by Executive Sponsor by target date | Signed or recorded approval |
| Scope approval | BCMS scope and exclusions approved | Approved scope statement |
| Stakeholder engagement | All in-scope business units represented | Stakeholder register, workshop attendance |
| Business Impact Analysis completion | 100% of in-scope functions completed and validated | Approved BIA records |
| Recovery objectives agreed | Recovery objectives approved for all priority activities | BIA summary and Steering Committee decision record |
| Dependency mapping | Critical people, technology, suppliers, premises, data, and process dependencies identified | Dependency maps and BIA records |
| Continuity risk assessment completion | All priority activities and material dependencies assessed | Risk assessment and treatment plan |
| Strategy approval | Continuity strategies approved for all priority activities | Approved strategy document |
| Capability gap management | All material gaps assigned to an owner, due date, and treatment decision | Gap register and action plan |
| Plan completion | Approved continuity plans for all priority functions | Controlled plan documents |
| Incident escalation alignment | Activation and escalation arrangements defined and approved | Incident response arrangements and contact lists |
| Training completion | At least [Target %] of assigned participants complete required training | Training records and attendance logs |
| Exercise completion | Initial exercise completed for each priority plan or representative scenario set | Exercise reports and lessons learned |
| Corrective action tracking | 100% of exercise and review actions logged; overdue actions escalated | Improvement log |
| Internal review completion | Internal review or audit completed before go-live | Review or audit report |
| Leadership review | Management review completed with readiness decision | Management review minutes |
| Evidence readiness | Required BCMS evidence available in controlled repository | Evidence index |
| Business-as-usual transition | Ongoing owner, calendar, and reporting cadence confirmed | BAU handover record |
| Certification readiness, if applicable | No unresolved critical readiness gaps | Readiness assessment and remediation log |

Qualitative success indicators:

- Leadership can clearly explain why the BCMS is needed and what it is intended to protect.
- Business units understand their recovery priorities and continuity responsibilities.
- Recovery objectives are based on business impact and are not arbitrary.
- Continuity plans are concise, accessible, role-based, and usable under pressure.
- Technology recovery plans and business recovery expectations are aligned or gaps are formally managed.
- Supplier continuity risks are visible and integrated into business continuity planning.
- Exercises produce meaningful learning and improvement, not only attendance records.
- BCMS documentation is controlled, current, and supported by evidence of implementation.
- The organisation can demonstrate that business continuity is part of normal management and not a one-time project.

## Review & Update Triggers

This BCMS Project Charter must be reviewed and updated when there are material changes that affect project mandate, scope, resources, budget, schedule, ownership, or success criteria.

Scheduled review:

| Review Type | Frequency / Timing | Owner | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Project status review | Weekly or fortnightly during implementation | BCMS Project Manager | Updated status report, risk and issue log |
| Steering Committee review | Monthly or at milestone gates | Executive Sponsor / Project Manager | Decisions, approvals, escalations |
| Charter review | At phase gates and whenever material change occurs | BCMS Project Manager | Updated charter or change record |
| Budget review | Monthly or when spend variance exceeds tolerance | Budget Owner | Budget status and change request if required |
| Closure review | At project completion | Executive Sponsor | Closure approval and BAU handover |

This Charter must be reviewed and, where necessary, updated if any of the following triggers occur:

- Change to Executive Sponsor, BCMS owner, project manager, or key governance roles.
- Significant change to organisational structure, operating model, products, services, or business priorities.
- Addition, removal, relocation, or closure of material sites or operating locations.
- Major technology transformation, cloud migration, data centre change, system replacement, or network change.
- New or changed legal, regulatory, contractual, customer, insurer, or stakeholder expectations.
- Acquisition, divestment, outsourcing, insourcing, or material supplier change.
- Material incident, near miss, crisis, disaster recovery activation, cyber event, or operational disruption.
- BIA results showing recovery requirements that materially differ from initial assumptions.
- Continuity risk assessment identifying unacceptable risk or significant capability gaps.
- Budget variance exceeding [Threshold %] or [Amount].
- Timeline variance exceeding [Number] weeks or threatening key external deadlines.
- Change in certification intent, certification body, or assessment timetable.
- Audit, review, or management findings requiring change to project direction.
- Exercise results showing significant weaknesses in plans, resources, or recovery capability.
- Leadership decision to expand, reduce, pause, or accelerate implementation.

Change control requirements:

| Change Type | Approval Required | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| Minor schedule adjustment within agreed tolerance | BCMS Project Manager | Updated project plan |
| Material milestone delay | Steering Committee | Change request and revised timeline |
| Scope expansion or reduction | Steering Committee | Updated scope statement and impact assessment |
| Budget increase | Executive Sponsor / Finance approval | Budget change request |
| Change to project objectives or success criteria | Executive Sponsor | Revised Charter |
| Risk acceptance for unresolved capability gap | Accountable Executive / Risk Committee | Residual risk acceptance record |
| Project suspension or cancellation | Executive Sponsor | Formal decision record and transition plan |

Version control must be maintained for this Charter. Superseded versions must be retained in accordance with [Organisation Name] document retention requirements. Updates must be communicated to all affected stakeholders, and any approved changes must be reflected in the project plan, budget, risk log, issue log, and relevant BCMS deliverables.

BCM-002.title: BCMS Scope Statement
BCM-002.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [BCMS-POL-001] | 1.0 | [Business Continuity Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO 22301:2019 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy defines the boundaries and applicability of the organisation’s Business Continuity Management System (BCMS). It establishes which business activities, locations, services, processes, people, information assets, technologies, suppliers and interested parties are included in the BCMS, and how any exclusions are controlled.

The purpose of the BCMS scope is to ensure that business continuity planning, risk treatment, continuity strategies, exercises, performance monitoring and continual improvement are applied consistently to the parts of the organisation that are essential to delivering products and services at agreed levels during and after disruptive incidents.

## Scope

The BCMS applies to the organisational activities, products, services, locations and supporting capabilities listed in this Policy. The scope shall be interpreted broadly to include internal and outsourced activities that materially affect the organisation’s ability to continue prioritised services following disruption.

### In-Scope Organisational Areas

The following organisational areas are included within the BCMS:

| Area | Inclusion Rationale |
|---|---|
| Executive leadership and crisis management | Provides strategic direction, decision-making authority, stakeholder engagement and escalation during disruptive events. |
| Business continuity management function | Owns the BCMS framework, programme coordination, business impact analysis, continuity planning, exercising and reporting. |
| Operations and service delivery teams | Deliver the organisation’s prioritised products and services to customers, users or beneficiaries. |
| Information technology and digital services | Supports systems, infrastructure, applications, networks, data, communications and recovery capabilities required for continuity. |
| Information security and cyber incident response | Supports protection, response and recovery where cyber events affect continuity of operations. |
| Facilities and workplace services | Supports site availability, physical access, utilities, workplace safety and alternate working arrangements. |
| Human resources | Supports workforce availability, welfare, succession, communications and people-related continuity arrangements. |
| Finance | Supports payroll, supplier payments, financial controls, insurance claims and liquidity-related continuity needs. |
| Procurement and supplier management | Supports continuity requirements for critical suppliers, service providers and outsourced processes. |
| Legal, compliance and governance | Supports legal obligations, regulatory communication, contract interpretation and governance oversight. |
| Communications, customer support and stakeholder engagement | Supports internal and external communications before, during and after disruption. |

### In-Scope Products and Services

The BCMS applies to the following products and services:

| Product / Service | Scope Treatment |
|---|---|
| [Priority Product or Service 1] | Fully in scope, including delivery processes, supporting systems, key staff, facilities, suppliers and customer communications. |
| [Priority Product or Service 2] | Fully in scope, including operational dependencies and recovery arrangements. |
| [Priority Product or Service 3] | In scope where disruption could materially affect customers, legal obligations, revenue, safety, reputation or contractual commitments. |
| Internal enabling services | In scope where required to support prioritised products, services or statutory obligations. |

Additional products and services shall be brought into scope where business impact analysis, risk assessment, contractual obligations, legal requirements or management direction identifies a material continuity need.

### In-Scope Locations

The BCMS applies to the following physical and virtual operating locations:

| Location Type | Scope Treatment |
|---|---|
| Primary offices and operational sites | In scope where they support prioritised activities, critical staff, records, systems or customer-facing services. |
| Data centres, server rooms and technology hosting locations | In scope where they host or support systems, data or infrastructure required for continuity. |
| Remote and hybrid working environments | In scope where personnel perform prioritised activities or access critical systems remotely. |
| Third-party hosted environments | In scope where outsourced platforms, cloud services or managed services support prioritised activities. |
| Alternate work locations and recovery sites | In scope where used as part of continuity or recovery strategies. |

The specific sites and environments currently included in the BCMS are:

| Site / Environment | Address or Description | Primary BCMS Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| [Head Office] | [Address] | Executive management, support functions, stakeholder communications. |
| [Operational Site] | [Address] | Delivery of prioritised services and operational processing. |
| [Technology Hosting Environment] | [Description] | Hosting of critical applications, infrastructure or data. |
| [Cloud Platform / Managed Service] | [Provider / Description] | Support of critical digital services and recovery capability. |
| [Remote Workforce] | [Applicable Regions / Teams] | Continuity of work during site unavailability or access disruption. |

### In-Scope Processes and Capabilities

The BCMS includes the following processes and capabilities where they support prioritised activities:

- Business impact analysis.
- Continuity risk assessment.
- Business continuity strategy and solution design.
- Business continuity plans and recovery procedures.
- Incident response, crisis management and emergency communications.
- Technology recovery planning and coordination.
- Supplier continuity and third-party dependency management.
- Workforce continuity and succession arrangements.
- Facilities and workplace continuity.
- Communications with employees, customers, regulators, suppliers and other interested parties.
- Continuity exercising, testing and lessons learned.
- BCMS performance monitoring, audit support and continual improvement.
- Documented information required to operate, maintain and evidence the BCMS.

### In-Scope Interested Parties

The BCMS shall consider the continuity needs and expectations of the following interested parties where relevant:

| Interested Party | Continuity Interest |
|---|---|
| Customers, clients, users or beneficiaries | Timely delivery of agreed products and services, communication during disruption and restoration of normal service. |
| Employees, contractors and temporary workers | Safety, welfare, clear instructions, access to work arrangements and role clarity during disruption. |
| Regulators and public authorities | Compliance with legal, regulatory, reporting and public interest obligations. |
| Suppliers and outsourced service providers | Defined continuity expectations, escalation paths and contractual service commitments. |
| Shareholders, owners or governing body | Protection of enterprise value, reputation, resilience and strategic objectives. |
| Insurers, auditors and assurance providers | Evidence of effective continuity governance, controls, testing and improvement. |
| Community and public stakeholders | Responsible management of incidents that may affect public welfare, safety or confidence. |

### Out-of-Scope Areas

The following areas are excluded from the BCMS unless management formally determines otherwise:

| Excluded Area | Reason for Exclusion | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| [Non-critical Business Unit / Activity] | Does not currently support prioritised products, services, legal obligations or material stakeholder commitments. | Exclusion shall be reassessed during scope review, business impact analysis updates or material organisational change. |
| [Decommissioned System / Legacy Service] | No longer supports active operations or customer commitments. | Exclusion applies only while the system or service remains inactive and is not relied upon for continuity. |
| [Low-impact Internal Activity] | Disruption would not materially affect continuity objectives, contractual obligations, legal requirements or reputation. | Exclusion shall not prevent necessary communication, safety or security arrangements. |

No exclusion shall be permitted where it would undermine the organisation’s ability to meet approved continuity objectives, protect people, satisfy legal or contractual obligations, or maintain prioritised products and services at agreed levels.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain a documented BCMS scope that clearly defines the boundaries and applicability of the business continuity management system.

2. The BCMS scope shall include all products, services, processes, locations, technologies, people and third-party dependencies required to maintain or recover prioritised activities within approved continuity objectives.

3. The BCMS scope shall be based on the organisation’s context, strategic objectives, interested party requirements, legal and regulatory obligations, contractual commitments, business impact analysis and continuity risk assessment.

4. The BCMS scope shall identify in-scope organisational units, functions, physical locations, remote working arrangements, information systems, data, suppliers and outsourced services that contribute to the delivery of prioritised products and services.

5. The BCMS scope shall include activities performed by third parties where those activities are necessary for the continuity of prioritised products, services or statutory obligations.

6. The organisation shall not exclude any activity, dependency, location, system, supplier or service from the BCMS if its disruption could create unacceptable impact to customers, legal compliance, safety, financial stability, reputation, contractual performance or strategic objectives.

7. Any exclusion from the BCMS scope shall be justified, documented, approved and periodically reassessed to confirm that it remains valid.

8. The BCMS scope shall be aligned with approved business continuity objectives, business impact analysis results, recovery priorities and continuity strategies.

9. The BCMS scope shall be communicated to relevant internal and external stakeholders who have responsibilities for business continuity, incident response, recovery, supplier management, audit, assurance or governance.

10. Business units within the BCMS scope shall participate in business impact analysis, continuity risk assessment, continuity plan development, exercising, training, incident response and continual improvement activities as directed by the BCMS owner.

11. Owners of in-scope products, services and processes shall ensure that supporting dependencies are identified and kept current, including people, facilities, systems, data, suppliers, equipment, records and communication channels.

12. Information technology and digital service dependencies within the BCMS scope shall be mapped to the business activities they support and shall have recovery arrangements consistent with approved business continuity requirements.

13. Critical suppliers and outsourced service providers within the BCMS scope shall be subject to continuity expectations, due diligence, contract requirements, performance monitoring and escalation arrangements proportionate to their importance.

14. The BCMS scope shall be reviewed whenever there is a material change to the organisation, including acquisitions, divestments, new products or services, major technology changes, site changes, outsourcing changes, regulatory changes or significant incidents.

15. The BCMS scope shall be maintained as controlled documented information and shall be available as evidence for internal review, management oversight, audit and assurance activities.

16. Changes to the BCMS scope shall be approved before implementation where they affect continuity obligations, recovery priorities, organisational responsibilities, resource requirements or assurance commitments.

17. The organisation shall ensure that the BCMS scope remains practical, accurate and representative of actual operating conditions.

18. The BCMS scope shall support a consistent and repeatable approach to planning, responding, recovering and improving across all in-scope areas.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Governing Body / Board | Provides oversight of organisational resilience and confirms that the BCMS scope supports the organisation’s strategic objectives and risk appetite. |
| Executive Management | Approves the BCMS scope, ensures adequate resources are available and resolves scope-related conflicts or prioritisation issues. |
| BCMS Owner / Business Continuity Manager | Maintains this Policy, coordinates scope definition, facilitates reviews, records exclusions, monitors scope alignment and reports scope-related issues to management. |
| Business Unit Owners | Identify in-scope products, services, processes, dependencies and impacts; maintain accurate continuity information; participate in BCMS activities. |
| Process Owners | Document process dependencies, recovery needs, critical resources and hand-offs that affect continuity. |
| IT / Technology Leadership | Identifies and maintains technology dependencies, recovery capabilities, system ownership, hosting arrangements and service restoration priorities. |
| Information Security Lead | Ensures cyber, data protection and information security dependencies affecting continuity are considered within the BCMS scope. |
| Facilities / Workplace Services Lead | Maintains information on site dependencies, utilities, workplace access, alternate locations and facility recovery arrangements. |
| Human Resources Lead | Supports workforce availability, role coverage, employee welfare, succession and communications requirements within the BCMS scope. |
| Procurement / Supplier Management Lead | Ensures critical suppliers and outsourced services are identified, assessed and managed in line with continuity requirements. |
| Legal / Compliance Lead | Advises on legal, regulatory and contractual requirements that affect the BCMS scope. |
| Internal Audit / Assurance Function | Provides independent assurance that the BCMS scope is appropriate, documented, maintained and consistently applied. |
| Employees and Contractors | Comply with applicable continuity requirements, participate in exercises and report changes or issues that may affect continuity. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all personnel and third parties with responsibilities affecting in-scope activities.

The BCMS Owner shall monitor compliance through routine governance activities, including:

| Monitoring Activity | Frequency | Responsible Role | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| BCMS scope review | At least annually | BCMS Owner | Approved scope record, review minutes, action log. |
| Business impact analysis validation | At least annually or after material change | Business Unit Owners | Updated impact analysis records and dependency maps. |
| Continuity risk assessment review | At least annually or after material change | BCMS Owner / Risk Function | Updated risk assessment and treatment actions. |
| Supplier continuity review | At least annually for critical suppliers | Procurement / Supplier Management Lead | Supplier assessments, continuity attestations, contract records. |
| Technology dependency review | At least annually or after major technology change | IT / Technology Leadership | Application inventory, recovery mapping, service ownership records. |
| Scope change assessment | Before implementation of material change | Change Owner / BCMS Owner | Change assessment, approval record, updated scope documentation. |
| Internal audit or assurance review | As scheduled | Internal Audit / Assurance Function | Audit plan, findings, corrective actions. |
| Management review reporting | At planned intervals | Executive Management / BCMS Owner | Management reports, decisions and action tracking. |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in one or more of the following actions:

- Requirement to update incomplete or inaccurate scope information.
- Escalation to the relevant business owner or executive sponsor.
- Formal corrective action with assigned owner and due date.
- Suspension or delay of organisational changes that create unmanaged continuity exposure.
- Additional assurance, testing or supplier review.
- Disciplinary action where non-compliance is deliberate, negligent or repeated.
- Contractual remedies where third-party obligations are not met.

The BCMS Owner shall maintain a record of significant non-compliance issues, corrective actions and management decisions related to the BCMS scope.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business justification and where the exception does not create unacceptable continuity exposure.

All exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Exception description | Clear statement of the activity, location, system, supplier, product or service to be excluded or treated differently. |
| Business justification | Explanation of why the exception is necessary or appropriate. |
| Impact assessment | Assessment of potential effects on customers, legal obligations, operations, safety, reputation, finance and contractual commitments. |
| Risk assessment | Identification of continuity risks introduced by the exception and any compensating controls. |
| Duration | Proposed start date, end date and review date. |
| Owner | Named accountable owner responsible for managing the exception. |
| Approvals | Required approvals based on risk and business impact. |
| Review requirements | Conditions that would trigger reassessment or withdrawal of the exception. |

Exception approval requirements are as follows:

| Exception Risk Level | Minimum Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Low | BCMS Owner and relevant Business Unit Owner. |
| Medium | BCMS Owner, relevant Business Unit Owner and Risk or Compliance representative. |
| High | Executive Management approval. |
| Critical or organisation-wide | Governing Body or delegated executive committee approval. |

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not be approved indefinitely. The BCMS Owner shall maintain an exception register and ensure exceptions are reviewed before expiry or when material changes occur.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant internal or external changes may affect the BCMS scope.

Review triggers shall include, but are not limited to:

- Launch or retirement of products or services.
- Changes to customer commitments, contractual obligations or service levels.
- Changes in legal, regulatory or industry expectations.
- Organisational restructuring, merger, acquisition, divestment or major outsourcing.
- Opening, closure or relocation of sites.
- Significant changes to technology platforms, hosting arrangements, data flows or recovery architecture.
- Identification of new critical suppliers or changes to supplier delivery models.
- Material findings from incidents, exercises, audits, assurance reviews or management reviews.
- Business impact analysis or risk assessment results that indicate scope changes are required.
- Changes in workforce model, including remote, hybrid or distributed working arrangements.

Policy maintenance shall follow the process below:

| Step | Activity | Responsible Role |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Identify need for scope or Policy review. | BCMS Owner, Business Unit Owner or Executive Management |
| 2 | Gather relevant information, including business impact, risk, dependency, supplier and legal considerations. | BCMS Owner with supporting functions |
| 3 | Assess proposed changes and determine implications for continuity objectives, resources and assurance. | BCMS Owner / Risk Function |
| 4 | Consult affected stakeholders. | BCMS Owner |
| 5 | Obtain required approvals. | Executive Management or delegated authority |
| 6 | Update this Policy and related BCMS documentation. | BCMS Owner |
| 7 | Communicate approved changes to relevant stakeholders. | BCMS Owner / Communications Lead |
| 8 | Track resulting actions to completion. | BCMS Owner |

The BCMS Owner shall ensure that superseded versions are retained in accordance with the organisation’s document retention requirements and that the current approved version is accessible to relevant stakeholders.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Interested Party ID | Enter a unique identifier for the stakeholder entry using a consistent format, e.g. IP-001, IP-002. |
| Interested Party Name | Enter the name of the interested party or stakeholder group, e.g. specific regulator, customer segment, supplier, employee group, shareholder, local authority. |
| Interested Party Type | Select the stakeholder category. Allowed values: Customer, Employee, Supplier, Regulator, Government/Public Authority, Shareholder/Investor, Community, Partner, Insurer, Emergency Service, Certification Body, Other. |
| Internal/External | State whether the interested party is within or outside the organisation. Allowed values: Internal, External. |
| Relationship to Organisation | Briefly describe the party’s relationship to the organisation, such as contractual customer, critical supplier, statutory regulator, workforce, parent company, community neighbour. |
| Relevant Products/Services/Activities | List the products, services, locations, activities, or business processes through which this party is relevant to the BCMS. |
| BCMS Relevance Rationale | Explain why this party is relevant to business continuity, including how they can affect, be affected by, or perceive themselves affected by disruption or recovery arrangements. |
| Continuity Needs and Expectations | Record the party’s continuity-related needs or expectations in plain language, such as service availability, recovery times, notification, access to information, regulatory reporting, safety, welfare, or supply continuity. |
| Specific BC Requirements | Enter measurable or explicit continuity requirements where known, such as RTO, RPO, maximum outage, minimum service level, notification deadline, reporting deadline, contractual recovery clause, or required alternative arrangements. |
| Requirement Source | Identify where the need, expectation, or requirement comes from. Allowed values: Contract, SLA, Law/Regulation, Licence/Permit, Policy, Customer Requirement, Supplier Agreement, Risk Assessment, BIA, Stakeholder Consultation, Management Decision, Other. |
| Legal/Regulatory/Contractual Obligation | State whether the requirement is a binding obligation. Allowed values: Legal, Regulatory, Contractual, Internal Commitment, Non-binding Expectation, To Be Determined. Include the obligation name or clause where applicable. |
| Priority/Criticality | Rate the importance of this interested party to the BCMS. Allowed values: Critical, High, Medium, Low. Base this on impact to continuity, compliance, safety, customer commitments, reputation, and recovery priorities. |
| Impacted Sites/Functions/Processes | List the organisational sites, departments, products, services, or processes affected by this party’s requirements; use official process or location names where available. |
| Expected Communication During Disruption | Describe what the interested party expects to receive during a disruption, such as incident notification, service status updates, recovery estimate, regulatory report, workaround instructions, or all-clear notice. |
| Communication Channel | Enter the approved communication method(s). Allowed examples: Email, Phone, SMS, Customer Portal, Supplier Portal, Regulator Portal, Website, Press Release, Teams/Slack, In-person Briefing, Other. |
| Communication Frequency/Timing | Enter required timing or frequency for disruption communications, e.g. within 1 hour of incident declaration, every 4 hours until resolved, daily by 10:00, as contractually required, upon material change. |
| Internal Relationship Owner | Enter the internal role or named position responsible for managing the relationship with this interested party, e.g. Head of Customer Operations, Procurement Manager, HR Director, Compliance Manager. |
| Requirement Owner | Enter the internal role accountable for ensuring the continuity requirement is addressed in the BCMS, such as BC Manager, Process Owner, IT Service Owner, Facilities Manager, Legal Counsel. |
| Mapped BCMS Process/Control/Document | Reference the BCMS document, process, plan, BIA, risk assessment, communication plan, recovery strategy, or procedure that addresses this party’s requirements. |
| Evidence/Source Reference | Provide the document, system record, contract ID, regulation reference, meeting minutes, stakeholder interview reference, or repository link that supports the entry. |
| Assessment Date | Enter the date the interested party and its requirements were assessed or confirmed, in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Next Review Date | Enter the planned review date in YYYY-MM-DD format; set according to BCMS review cycle or sooner for critical parties or changing obligations. |
| Status | Select the current status of the entry. Allowed values: Draft, Under Review, Approved, Action Required, Retired. |
| Change Notes | Record material changes since the last review, such as new requirement, changed SLA, new regulation, updated owner, removed stakeholder, or no change. |

### Maintenance

The BCMS Manager owns this register, with input from Compliance, Legal, Procurement, Sales/Account Management, HR, Operations, IT, and process owners. It should be reviewed at least annually and whenever contracts, regulations, services, suppliers, organisational context, BIAs, or stakeholder expectations change, drawing from the compliance obligations register, contract/SLA repository, supplier register, customer records, BIA outputs, risk assessments, and stakeholder consultation records.

BCM-004.title: Context of the Organisation (BCM)
BCM-004.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [BCM-POL-001] | 1.0 | Business Continuity Manager | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO 22301:2019 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy defines the mandatory requirements for identifying, assessing, maintaining and using the internal and external issues that may affect the organisation’s Business Continuity Management System (BCMS).

The purpose of this Policy is to ensure that business continuity planning is based on a current and practical understanding of the organisation’s operating environment, strategic direction, dependencies, threats, constraints and opportunities. This enables the organisation to design, implement and improve continuity arrangements that are relevant, proportionate and aligned with business needs.

## Scope

This Policy applies to all business units, functions, locations, personnel, contractors and third parties involved in the organisation’s BCMS.

It covers the identification and management of internal and external issues that may affect the organisation’s ability to:

- Achieve its business continuity objectives.
- Maintain critical products, services and activities.
- Meet obligations to customers, regulators, employees and other interested parties.
- Respond to and recover from disruptive incidents.
- Maintain an effective and continually improving BCMS.

The Policy applies to both routine operations and periods of organisational change, including changes to strategy, structure, technology, facilities, suppliers, markets, regulatory obligations, threat environment and risk profile.

This Policy does not replace the Business Impact Analysis, Risk Assessment, Crisis Management Plan, Incident Response Plan or Business Continuity Plans. It provides the mandatory context requirements that inform and support those documents.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall maintain a documented understanding of the internal and external issues that are relevant to the purpose, strategic direction and continuity objectives of the organisation.

2. The organisation shall ensure that business continuity planning considers both current and foreseeable issues that may affect the ability to continue or recover critical products, services, processes and activities.

3. The organisation shall identify internal issues that may affect business continuity, including as applicable:
 - Organisational strategy, objectives and priorities.
 - Governance structure and decision-making arrangements.
 - Products, services, processes and critical activities.
 - Workforce capability, availability, skills and succession risks.
 - Technology platforms, data, applications and infrastructure.
 - Facilities, premises, equipment and physical operating environment.
 - Financial position, funding constraints and investment priorities.
 - Organisational culture, risk appetite and resilience maturity.
 - Existing policies, standards, plans and operating procedures.
 - Dependencies between departments, systems, sites and functions.
 - Lessons learned from incidents, exercises, audits and reviews.
 - Planned organisational change, transformation or restructuring.

4. The organisation shall identify external issues that may affect business continuity, including as applicable:
 - Legal, regulatory and contractual obligations.
 - Customer, partner and market expectations.
 - Supplier, outsourcing and third-party dependencies.
 - Political, economic, social and environmental conditions.
 - Public health, civil emergency and community risks.
 - Natural hazards and climate-related threats.
 - Cyber, information security and technology threat landscape.
 - Utility, transport, telecommunications and infrastructure dependencies.
 - Industry trends, competitive pressures and sector-specific risks.
 - Geographic, cross-border and jurisdictional considerations.
 - Availability of emergency services and mutual aid.
 - Media, reputational and stakeholder perception risks.

5. The organisation shall document relevant internal and external issues in a controlled BCMS context record or equivalent approved repository.

6. The BCMS context record shall be sufficiently detailed to explain why each issue is relevant, how it may affect continuity, and what part of the organisation or BCMS it may influence.

7. The organisation shall assign ownership for monitoring each significant context issue or category of issues.

8. The organisation shall use the identified internal and external issues to inform:
 - BCMS scope and boundaries.
 - Business continuity objectives.
 - Business Impact Analysis criteria and assumptions.
 - Risk assessment and treatment priorities.
 - Continuity strategies and solutions.
 - Incident response and crisis management arrangements.
 - Supplier and third-party continuity requirements.
 - Exercise and testing priorities.
 - Training and awareness activities.
 - Management review and continual improvement.

9. The organisation shall assess context issues for their potential impact on the BCMS, including potential effects on critical activities, recovery priorities, resources, dependencies, compliance obligations and stakeholder expectations.

10. The organisation shall consider both negative and positive implications of context issues, including risks that may disrupt operations and opportunities to improve resilience.

11. The organisation shall maintain documented criteria for determining whether an issue is material to the BCMS. At a minimum, materiality shall consider:
 - Potential impact on critical products or services.
 - Potential effect on recovery time, recovery capacity or service continuity.
 - Legal, regulatory, contractual or customer significance.
 - Reputational, financial or operational consequences.
 - Effect on key dependencies, resources or suppliers.
 - Likelihood of change within the planning horizon.
 - Relevance to executive decision-making.

12. The organisation shall ensure that context information is obtained from credible and appropriate sources, which may include:
 - Strategic and business plans.
 - Risk registers and enterprise risk reports.
 - Internal audit and assurance reports.
 - Incident, near-miss and exercise reports.
 - Supplier and contract management records.
 - Regulatory updates and legal advice.
 - Customer requirements and service commitments.
 - Threat intelligence and security reports.
 - Facilities, technology and operational performance data.
 - Market, industry and environmental monitoring.
 - Interviews or workshops with business leaders and process owners.

13. The organisation shall review internal and external issues at planned intervals and whenever a significant change occurs that may affect business continuity arrangements.

14. The organisation shall require business units and process owners to notify the Business Continuity Manager of material changes that may affect the BCMS, including but not limited to:
 - Launch, withdrawal or major change to products or services.
 - Opening, closing or relocation of offices, warehouses, plants or service centres.
 - Significant workforce change, industrial action risk or loss of key skills.
 - Introduction, replacement or retirement of critical systems.
 - New outsourcing, supplier change or material contract amendment.
 - Merger, acquisition, divestment or restructuring.
 - New regulatory, contractual or customer continuity requirement.
 - Significant change in threat, hazard or geopolitical exposure.
 - Major incident, crisis, audit finding or exercise outcome.

15. The organisation shall ensure that changes in context are evaluated for their effect on existing business continuity strategies, plans, resources and assumptions.

16. The organisation shall update affected BCMS documents, plans and records when context changes make current arrangements inaccurate, insufficient or no longer appropriate.

17. The organisation shall ensure that business continuity objectives remain aligned with the organisation’s strategic direction and the identified context.

18. The organisation shall ensure that context analysis considers interested parties whose needs and expectations may affect continuity planning, including customers, employees, regulators, suppliers, shareholders, insurers, emergency services and community stakeholders.

19. The organisation shall maintain traceability between material context issues and resulting BCMS decisions where those issues influence scope, priorities, controls, resources or improvement actions.

20. The organisation shall ensure that context information is communicated to relevant personnel in a manner appropriate to their roles and responsibilities.

21. The organisation shall protect sensitive context information, including commercially sensitive, security-sensitive, legal, personnel and supplier information, in accordance with the organisation’s information classification and handling requirements.

22. The organisation shall not base business continuity plans solely on outdated assumptions, undocumented knowledge or informal understanding of the operating environment.

23. The organisation shall ensure that executive leadership considers significant context issues as part of BCMS governance and management review activities.

24. The organisation shall maintain evidence that internal and external issues have been identified, reviewed and considered in BCMS planning and improvement decisions.

25. The organisation shall ensure that identified context issues are incorporated into continual improvement activities where they reveal weaknesses, emerging threats, new dependencies or opportunities to strengthen resilience.

The following minimum information shall be maintained for each material context issue:

| Field | Mandatory Requirement |
|---|---|
| Issue ID | Unique identifier for tracking and reference |
| Issue Type | Internal or external |
| Issue Category | Strategy, legal, operational, technology, supplier, workforce, environmental, market, security or other relevant category |
| Description | Clear statement of the issue and its relevance to continuity |
| Source | Origin of the information, such as risk report, business plan, audit, incident review or regulatory update |
| Affected Area | Business unit, process, product, service, site, system, supplier or stakeholder affected |
| Continuity Implication | Explanation of how the issue may affect continuity, recovery or resilience |
| Materiality Rating | High, medium or low based on approved criteria |
| Owner | Role accountable for monitoring the issue |
| Required Action | Action needed, if any, such as review, update, treatment or escalation |
| Review Date | Date the issue was last reviewed |
| Status | Open, monitoring, action in progress, closed or superseded |

The following review triggers shall apply:

| Trigger | Required Action | Responsible Role | Target Timeframe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scheduled BCMS context review | Review and update the BCMS context record | Business Continuity Manager | At least annually |
| Significant organisational change | Assess continuity implications and update affected BCMS documents | Change Owner with Business Continuity Manager | Before change implementation where practicable |
| New or changed legal, regulatory or contractual obligation | Assess relevance to continuity arrangements | Legal/Compliance with Business Continuity Manager | Within 30 calendar days of identification |
| Major incident or crisis | Review assumptions and context issues revealed by the event | Incident Owner with Business Continuity Manager | Within 30 calendar days after closure of the incident review |
| Exercise or test identifies context weakness | Update context record and improvement actions | Exercise Lead with Business Continuity Manager | Within 20 business days |
| Material supplier or outsourcing change | Assess dependency and resilience implications | Procurement/Third-Party Owner with Business Continuity Manager | Before contract approval or renewal where practicable |
| New or emerging threat relevant to critical activities | Assess potential effect on continuity strategies and plans | Risk Owner with Business Continuity Manager | Within 30 calendar days of identification |
| Management review decision | Update context record and related BCMS actions | Business Continuity Manager | Within 20 business days after approval of minutes or actions |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Executive Management | Provide direction and support for understanding the organisation’s continuity context; ensure business continuity remains aligned with strategic priorities; review significant context issues and approve material changes affecting BCMS scope, objectives or resources. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Own and maintain the BCMS context process and context record; coordinate reviews; facilitate workshops or interviews; ensure context issues inform BCMS planning; escalate material issues; maintain evidence of review and action. |
| BCMS Steering Committee or Governance Forum | Review significant internal and external issues; confirm whether the BCMS remains appropriate to the organisation’s environment; monitor actions arising from context changes; resolve cross-functional issues. |
| Business Unit Leaders | Identify and communicate internal and external issues affecting their areas; validate context information; ensure business continuity plans reflect current operating realities; notify the Business Continuity Manager of material changes. |
| Process Owners | Identify dependencies, constraints, vulnerabilities and changes affecting critical activities; support Business Impact Analysis and risk assessment activities using current context information. |
| Risk Management Function | Provide relevant enterprise risk, operational risk and emerging risk information; support assessment of context issues; align BCMS context with broader risk management activities. |
| Legal and Compliance Function | Identify legal, regulatory and contractual obligations relevant to continuity; advise on changes that may affect BCMS requirements; support interpretation of compliance implications. |
| Procurement and Third-Party Management | Identify supplier, outsourcing and supply chain issues affecting continuity; ensure material third-party changes are communicated; support assessment of supplier dependencies and resilience expectations. |
| Information Technology and Information Security | Identify technology, cyber, data, infrastructure and service dependency issues; advise on technology resilience implications; ensure continuity assumptions align with technical recovery capabilities. |
| Facilities and Physical Security | Identify site, access, utility, safety, environmental and physical security issues affecting continuity; support assessment of location-specific dependencies and hazards. |
| Human Resources | Identify workforce, skills, labour relations, welfare and availability issues affecting continuity; support planning for people-related disruption scenarios. |
| Internal Audit or Assurance Function | Provide independent assurance over the effectiveness of context identification, documentation, review and use within the BCMS, where included in the audit plan. |
| All Personnel | Report material changes, emerging issues, incidents, dependencies or concerns that may affect business continuity through established reporting channels. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all in-scope personnel, functions and locations.

The Business Continuity Manager shall monitor compliance through routine BCMS governance activities, document reviews, management reporting, exercises, audits and follow-up of improvement actions.

At a minimum, monitoring shall include:

- Verification that a current BCMS context record exists and is controlled.
- Confirmation that internal and external issues are reviewed at planned intervals.
- Evidence that material changes are assessed for continuity impact.
- Traceability between material context issues and BCMS decisions, plans or actions.
- Review of whether business continuity objectives remain aligned with current organisational context.
- Confirmation that relevant business units have contributed to context identification and validation.
- Follow-up of overdue actions arising from context reviews.
- Review of audit, incident and exercise outputs for new or changed context issues.

The following compliance measures shall be used:

| Compliance Area | Evidence Expected | Monitoring Frequency | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context record maintained | Current approved BCMS context record or equivalent repository | At least annually | Business Continuity Manager |
| Scheduled review completed | Review minutes, approvals, updates and action log | At least annually | Business Continuity Manager |
| Change impacts assessed | Change records, impact assessments, updated BCMS documents | For material changes | Change Owner |
| Business unit input obtained | Workshop outputs, interview notes, sign-offs or validation records | At least annually or during major change | Business Unit Leaders |
| Context reflected in BCMS planning | Updated Business Impact Analysis, risk assessment, plans, strategies or objectives | During BCMS review cycle | Business Continuity Manager |
| Actions tracked to closure | BCMS action tracker with owners and due dates | Monthly or as agreed by governance forum | Business Continuity Manager |
| Significant issues escalated | Governance papers, risk reports, management review records or decision logs | As needed | Business Continuity Manager |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in:

- Required remediation actions.
- Escalation to the relevant manager or executive sponsor.
- Inclusion in BCMS management reporting.
- Internal audit findings or assurance actions.
- Suspension of approval for affected business continuity documents until context issues are addressed.
- Disciplinary action where non-compliance is deliberate, repeated or creates material organisational risk.

Managers shall ensure that personnel under their responsibility understand and comply with this Policy. Failure to identify, report or assess material context changes may result in ineffective continuity arrangements and shall be treated as a governance concern.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business justification and the exception does not create unacceptable risk to the organisation’s continuity capability.

All exception requests shall be submitted to the Business Continuity Manager and shall include:

- Description of the requirement for which an exception is requested.
- Business reason for the exception.
- Scope of the exception, including affected business units, sites, processes, systems or suppliers.
- Risk assessment and continuity impact.
- Compensating measures or alternative controls.
- Requested duration of the exception.
- Exception owner.
- Approval from the relevant executive or governance forum.

The Business Continuity Manager shall review each request and may require input from Risk Management, Legal, Compliance, Information Security, Procurement, Facilities or other relevant functions before approval.

Exceptions shall be time-bound and shall not be open-ended. Approved exceptions shall be recorded in the BCMS exception register and reviewed at least quarterly until closed.

| Exception Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Maximum Standard Duration | 12 months unless explicitly approved by executive management |
| Minimum Review Frequency | Quarterly |
| Approval Authority | Business Continuity Manager and relevant executive sponsor or governance forum |
| Required Evidence | Approved exception request, risk assessment, compensating measures and review record |
| Closure Requirement | Evidence that the exception is no longer needed or that the Policy requirement has been met |

Emergency deviations from this Policy during an incident or crisis may be authorised by the incident or crisis management lead where necessary to protect life, safety, legal obligations, critical services or organisational interests. Such deviations shall be documented and reviewed after the event.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant internal or external changes may affect the organisation’s business continuity arrangements.

The Business Continuity Manager is responsible for coordinating the review and ensuring the Policy remains accurate, practical and aligned with the organisation’s BCMS.

The review shall consider:

- Changes in organisational strategy, structure, products, services or operating model.
- Changes in legal, regulatory, contractual or customer requirements.
- Results from Business Impact Analysis and risk assessment activities.
- Findings from incidents, exercises, audits and management reviews.
- Changes in technology, suppliers, facilities or workforce arrangements.
- Emerging threats, hazards, dependencies or opportunities.
- Feedback from business units and interested parties.
- Changes to related policies, standards, plans and procedures.

Material changes to this Policy shall be approved by [Approval Authority]. Minor administrative updates, such as formatting, role title changes or document reference updates, may be approved by the Business Continuity Manager, provided they do not alter the intent or mandatory requirements of the Policy.

The following maintenance schedule shall apply:

| Activity | Frequency | Responsible Role | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Policy review | At least annually | Business Continuity Manager | Updated or reconfirmed Policy |
| Context record review | At least annually and after significant change | Business Continuity Manager | Updated BCMS context record |
| Governance review of material context issues | At least annually or as required | BCMS Steering Committee or equivalent forum | Decisions, actions and escalations |
| Business unit validation | At least annually or during major change | Business Unit Leaders | Confirmed or updated context inputs |
| Exception review | Quarterly until closure | Business Continuity Manager | Updated exception register |
| Action tracking | Monthly or as agreed | Business Continuity Manager | Updated BCMS action log |

Version history shall be maintained for this Policy.

| Version | Date | Summary of Change | Author | Approver |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Initial issue | Business Continuity Manager | [Approval Authority] |

BCM-005.title: BCMS Gap Analysis
BCM-005.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [BCMS-GAP-001] | 1.0 | [Business Continuity Manager] | [DD MMM YYYY] | ISO 22301:2019 | Internal Confidential |

## Purpose

This report presents the results of a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) gap analysis performed to assess the organisation’s current business continuity arrangements against the requirements and intent of ISO 22301:2019.

The objectives of this report are to:

- Establish a clear view of current BCMS maturity and readiness.
- Identify gaps between existing practices and the expected components of a conforming BCMS.
- Prioritise remediation actions based on business risk, implementation effort and dependency.
- Provide management with an evidence-based action plan to support implementation, certification readiness and continual improvement.
- Support informed decision-making regarding resources, ownership, timelines and governance for the BCMS programme.

This report is intended for management review, BCMS implementation planning, internal audit preparation and evidence of due diligence during certification readiness activities.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Assessment start date | [DD MMM YYYY] |
| Assessment end date | [DD MMM YYYY] |
| Report date | [DD MMM YYYY] |
| Assessment lead | [Name / Role] |
| Business continuity sponsor | [Name / Role] |
| Report prepared by | [Name / Role / Department] |

### Scope of Assessment

The assessment reviewed the current state of the organisation’s BCMS across governance, planning, operational resilience, business impact analysis, risk assessment, continuity strategies, incident response, exercising, performance evaluation and continual improvement.

The scope covered the following organisational areas, unless otherwise stated:

| Scope Area | Included |
|---|---|
| Legal entities | [Entity names / All operating entities] |
| Locations | [Head office, regional offices, data centres, warehouses, remote workforce locations] |
| Business functions | [Critical and supporting business functions] |
| Products and services | [Key products, services and customer-facing obligations] |
| Technology services | [Core platforms, networks, cloud services, end-user computing, telephony] |
| Third parties | [Critical suppliers, outsourced service providers, managed service providers] |
| People arrangements | [Employees, contractors, key role holders, response teams] |
| Documentation reviewed | [Policies, BIAs, risk assessments, plans, exercise records, incident logs, supplier records] |

### Out of Scope

The following areas were not assessed in detail and may require separate review:

- Detailed technical disaster recovery testing of individual infrastructure components, unless evidence was already available.
- Formal occupational health and safety compliance review.
- Physical security design assessment beyond business continuity implications.
- Financial audit of continuity-related budget and cost assumptions.
- Full third-party assurance review of supplier BCMS capabilities beyond available contractual and due diligence evidence.

### Assessment Rating Scale

The following rating scale was applied to each assessment area:

| Rating | Definition | Typical Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Conforming | Requirement is addressed, implemented, evidenced and operating effectively. | Suitable for audit evidence with minor improvement only. |
| Largely Conforming | Requirement is mostly addressed, with limited gaps in evidence, consistency or formalisation. | Low to moderate remediation required. |
| Partially Conforming | Some relevant activity exists but is incomplete, informal, inconsistently applied or not fully evidenced. | Moderate remediation required. |
| Non-Conforming | Requirement is not addressed or there is no reliable evidence of implementation. | Significant remediation required. |
| Not Assessed | Area was not reviewed due to scope limitation or unavailable evidence. | Requires follow-up assessment. |

### Risk Priority Scale

Findings were prioritised as follows:

| Priority | Meaning | Management Response Expected |
|---|---|---|
| High | Gap could materially affect continuity capability, customer commitments, regulatory obligations, safety, revenue or certification readiness. | Immediate action plan, named owner and tracked remediation. |
| Medium | Gap may reduce effectiveness, consistency or auditability of the BCMS but is unlikely to cause immediate material disruption alone. | Planned remediation within agreed implementation timeline. |
| Low | Improvement opportunity or documentation refinement with limited operational risk. | Address through continual improvement or routine document updates. |

## Executive Summary

The organisation has established several business continuity practices, including incident response arrangements, some departmental recovery procedures, technology recovery activities and informal management oversight. However, these practices are not yet integrated into a fully structured, consistently evidenced and formally governed BCMS aligned to ISO 22301:2019 expectations.

The gap analysis found that the strongest areas are operational awareness, practical knowledge of critical services, existing technology recovery capability and experienced personnel who understand key dependencies. The weakest areas are formal BCMS governance, documented scope and objectives, complete business impact analysis, consistent continuity risk assessment, approved continuity strategies, structured exercising, performance monitoring and management review evidence.

The organisation is considered to be at an implementation maturity level where certification readiness is achievable, provided that remediation is managed as a formal programme with executive sponsorship, accountable process owners, defined deliverables and evidence capture from the outset.

### Overall Assessment Result

| Overall Area | Current Status | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| BCMS governance and leadership | Partially Conforming | High |

### Key Themes

The analysis identified the following cross-cutting themes:

1. **BCMS responsibilities are understood informally but not formally assigned**
 - Key continuity activities are performed by capable individuals, but accountability is not consistently documented in role descriptions, governance forums or approved plans.

2. **Business continuity documentation exists but lacks integration**
 - Departments maintain local documents and recovery notes, but these are not consistently linked to a central policy, business impact analysis, continuity strategy or maintenance cycle.

3. **Business impact analysis needs to be completed and standardised**
 - Some functions have identified critical processes and recovery expectations, but there is no complete, approved and consistently applied method for determining maximum tolerable disruption, recovery priorities, dependencies and resource requirements.

4. **Continuity strategies are not consistently justified by analysis**
 - Recovery options exist in practice, particularly for technology, but they are not consistently mapped to business impact requirements, risk exposure, supplier constraints and resource assumptions.

5. **Exercises and tests are not yet sufficient for certification readiness**
 - The organisation has participated in incident handling and some technical testing, but there is no structured exercise programme covering business, technology, supplier and leadership response scenarios.

6. **Performance evaluation and management review are underdeveloped**
 - BCMS performance measures, internal audit planning, management review inputs and improvement tracking require formalisation.

### Certification Readiness View

Based on evidence reviewed, the organisation is not yet ready for external certification assessment. A realistic certification readiness target may be achievable within approximately **six to twelve months**, depending on resource availability, management commitment and the speed at which business impact analysis, continuity planning, exercising and internal audit activities can be completed.

## Methodology

### Assessment Approach

The gap analysis used a combination of document review, stakeholder interviews, process walkthroughs and evidence sampling. The assessment focused on whether required BCMS elements are:

- Defined in approved documentation.
- Implemented in day-to-day operations.
- Understood by relevant personnel.
- Supported by records and evidence.
- Measured, reviewed and improved.
- Consistent across in-scope functions and locations.

### Activities Performed

| Activity | Description |
|---|---|
| Kick-off meeting | Confirmed assessment objectives, scope, stakeholders, evidence requests and timelines. |
| Document review | Reviewed existing continuity, incident response, disaster recovery, risk, supplier, governance and training records. |
| Stakeholder interviews | Interviewed management, function owners, technology leads, facilities, HR, procurement and operational representatives. |
| Process walkthroughs | Walked through current practices for incident escalation, recovery planning, plan maintenance and technology recovery. |
| Evidence sampling | Sampled available plans, test records, incident records, supplier documents and management meeting outputs. |
| Gap rating | Rated each area using the assessment scale defined in this report. |
| Findings validation | Reviewed preliminary findings with key stakeholders to confirm accuracy and context. |
| Action planning | Developed recommended actions, ownership model and priority sequencing. |

### Stakeholders Consulted

| Role / Function | Purpose of Engagement |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | Confirmed leadership expectations, risk appetite and strategic priorities. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Reviewed BCMS governance, documentation and implementation approach. |
| Risk Management | Reviewed risk assessment alignment and enterprise risk integration. |
| Information Technology | Reviewed disaster recovery, infrastructure resilience, application recovery and service dependencies. |
| Information Security | Reviewed cyber incident continuity impacts and response integration. |
| Facilities / Physical Security | Reviewed site disruption, access, utilities and relocation arrangements. |
| Human Resources | Reviewed people availability, welfare, communications and succession considerations. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Reviewed critical supplier dependencies and contractual continuity obligations. |
| Business Function Owners | Reviewed critical activities, recovery requirements and operational workarounds. |
| Communications / Legal / Compliance | Reviewed internal and external communication, regulatory and contractual obligations. |

### Evidence Reviewed

The assessment considered available evidence including, but not limited to:

- Business continuity policy or equivalent governance documentation.
- Crisis management and incident response procedures.
- Departmental continuity plans and recovery instructions.
- Disaster recovery plans and technical recovery runbooks.
- Prior business impact analysis outputs, if available.
- Enterprise and operational risk registers.
- Supplier lists, contracts and service level agreements.
- Incident records and post-incident reviews.
- Exercise or test records.
- Training and awareness materials.
- Management meeting minutes and action logs.
- Internal audit schedules and findings, if available.

### Limitations

The findings are based on evidence made available during the assessment period. Where documentation was unavailable, incomplete or not formally approved, the assessment treated the area as not fully evidenced even where stakeholders described relevant practices. This approach reflects audit expectations that BCMS arrangements must be demonstrable, repeatable and maintained.

## Analysis

### Overall Maturity Assessment

The organisation’s BCMS maturity is assessed as **developing**. There is a clear foundation of operational knowledge and practical response capability, but the system is not yet sufficiently formalised, integrated or evidenced to demonstrate consistent conformity.

The current state is typical of an organisation transitioning from informal business continuity practices to a formal management system. The most important next step is to move from individual knowledge and isolated documents to an integrated BCMS that is governed, measured, tested and improved.

### Strengths Identified

The assessment identified the following strengths:

- Management recognises the importance of continuity and resilience.
- Operational teams understand key services and many practical dependencies.
- Technology recovery arrangements exist for some systems and platforms.
- Incident escalation routes are used in practice.
- Experienced personnel are available to support BCMS implementation.
- Remote working capability provides a useful continuity option for some functions.
- There is willingness across departments to participate in business impact analysis and planning.
- Existing risk, supplier, information security and incident management processes can be leveraged rather than duplicated.

### Principal Gaps Affecting Certification Readiness

The most significant gaps affecting certification readiness are:

1. **Lack of approved BCMS scope, policy and measurable objectives**
 - Without these elements, the BCMS lacks a formal baseline against which performance can be assessed.

2. **Incomplete business impact analysis**
 - Continuity strategies and plans cannot be reliably validated until critical activities, impacts, recovery requirements and dependencies are agreed by business owners.

3. **Insufficient continuity risk assessment**
 - Threats and disruption scenarios are not yet systematically assessed in relation to critical activities and recovery assumptions.

4. **Unvalidated continuity strategies**
 - Current recovery arrangements may be practical, but they are not consistently linked to business requirements or tested under realistic conditions.

5. **Inconsistent plan quality**
 - Plans vary by department and may not provide sufficient guidance during a disruption.

6. **Limited exercise and test evidence**
 - External assessment will expect evidence that plans and capabilities have been validated, lessons have been captured and improvements have been tracked.

7. **No formal BCMS performance evaluation cycle**
 - Internal audit, management review, corrective action tracking and metrics are essential to demonstrate that the BCMS is operating as a management system.

### Risk Implications

If the identified gaps remain unresolved, the organisation may face the following risks:

| Risk Area | Potential Impact |
|---|---|
| Operational disruption | Delayed recovery of critical processes due to unclear priorities, dependencies or responsibilities. |
| Customer commitments | Failure to meet service expectations or contractual recovery obligations. |
| Regulatory or legal exposure | Inability to demonstrate reasonable continuity planning and governance where required. |
| Financial loss | Increased downtime, manual workarounds, recovery costs or revenue interruption. |
| Reputation | Loss of stakeholder confidence following a poorly managed disruption. |
| People dependency | Excessive reliance on key individuals without sufficient deputies or documented procedures. |
| Supplier dependency | Failure of critical suppliers without viable alternatives or continuity assurance. |
| Certification readiness | Delays or unsuccessful external assessment due to insufficient evidence and incomplete system operation. |

### Root Cause Themes

The findings appear to be driven by the following root causes:

- Business continuity has been treated as a set of operational activities rather than a formal management system.
- Ownership is distributed but not clearly governed through an approved accountability model.
- Documentation has developed locally without a single BCMS architecture or template set.
- Business impact analysis has not been completed as a business-wide exercise.
- Exercise and testing activities have not been planned as a structured validation programme.
- Performance review mechanisms have not yet been established for the BCMS.
- Evidence management has not been embedded into day-to-day BCMS activities.

### Dependencies for Successful Remediation

The recommended remediation plan depends on:

- Executive sponsorship and active management participation.
- Appointment of accountable owners for each remediation action.
- Availability of business function owners for BIA workshops and plan development.
- Support from IT for application recovery mapping and disaster recovery evidence.
- Procurement support for supplier continuity assurance.
- Internal audit capability or external support for BCMS audit readiness.
- Timely approval of BCMS policy, scope, objectives and governance documents.
- A central repository for controlled BCMS documents and records.

| Phase 4 | Validation | Exercise programme, plan walkthroughs, technical recovery tests and improvement tracking. |

### Success Criteria

The remediation programme should be considered successful when:

- The BCMS scope, policy, objectives and governance are approved and communicated.
- All critical activities have completed and approved BIAs.
- Continuity risks are assessed, treated and tracked.
- Continuity strategies are approved and resourced.
- Business continuity, crisis management and disaster recovery plans are aligned and controlled.
- Staff with continuity responsibilities have completed role-based training.
- Exercises and tests have been completed with documented outcomes.
- Corrective actions are tracked and closed with evidence.
- BCMS metrics are reported to management.
- Internal audit has been completed and findings addressed.
- Management review has been performed and decisions documented.
- Certification readiness has been confirmed through evidence review or mock assessment.

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution

This report is intended for internal use by authorised personnel with responsibility for business continuity, risk management, governance, audit, compliance, technology resilience, supplier management and executive oversight.

| Recipient / Group | Purpose |

| [Executive Leadership Team] | Awareness of BCMS readiness, risks and required actions. |
| [Business Continuity Manager] | Implementation planning and remediation tracking. |
| [Risk Management Function] | Integration with risk assessment and treatment processes. |
| [Information Technology Leadership] | Alignment of disaster recovery and service continuity actions. |
| [Internal Audit] | Audit planning and assurance preparation. |
| [Function Owners] | Completion of BIA, planning, training and exercises. |
| [Procurement / Vendor Management] | Supplier continuity assurance and contract review. |
| [Compliance / Legal] | Review of continuity obligations and external commitments. |

Distribution outside the organisation requires approval from [Document Owner] and [Executive Sponsor], unless disclosure is already authorised under an approved customer, regulatory or assurance process.

### Confidentiality Requirements

This report is classified as **Internal Confidential** because it contains information about operational dependencies, continuity weaknesses, supplier reliance, recovery assumptions and management system readiness.

Recipients must:

- Store the report only in approved corporate repositories.
- Not forward the report to unauthorised parties.
- Avoid placing the report in public, shared or unmanaged locations.
- Redact sensitive operational details before external sharing, where appropriate.
- Use the report only for legitimate governance, assurance and implementation purposes.
- Protect supporting evidence in accordance with organisational information handling requirements.

### External Sharing

If this report is shared with auditors, customers, regulators or third parties, the following controls should be applied:

| External Party | Sharing Condition |

| Certification body | Permitted where approved by [Executive Sponsor] and limited to assessment purposes. |
| Customer | Only where contractually required or approved by Legal and the Executive Sponsor. |
| Regulator | Only through authorised regulatory communication channels. |
| Supplier | Only extracts relevant to supplier actions, with sensitive internal findings removed. |
| Consultant | Permitted under an active confidentiality agreement and approved engagement scope. |

### Record Retention

The approved version of this report, supporting evidence, action plans and management responses should be retained in the BCMS repository for a period consistent with the organisation’s records retention schedule and audit evidence requirements.
