BCM-008.title: BCM Strategy & Solutions Document
BCM-008.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| BCM-POL-003 | 1.0 | Business Continuity Manager | [Effective Date] | ISO 22301:2019 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy defines the mandatory requirements for establishing, approving, maintaining and exercising the organisation’s Business Continuity Management (BCM) strategy and selected continuity solutions.

The purpose of the BCM strategy is to ensure that the organisation can continue or recover its priority activities within approved timeframes following disruptive incidents. The strategy shall be based on business impact analysis, risk assessment, stakeholder needs, legal and contractual obligations, and the organisation’s risk appetite.

This Policy ensures that continuity solutions are practical, funded, assigned to accountable owners, tested, and capable of supporting the organisation’s approved recovery objectives.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All business units, functions, sites, subsidiaries and controlled operations within [Organisation Name].
- All priority activities identified through the Business Impact Analysis.
- Supporting people, processes, premises, technology, information, suppliers, logistics, facilities, records and communications required to deliver priority activities.
- Internal and third-party services that support continuity or recovery of priority activities.
- Strategic, tactical and operational continuity solutions, including workarounds, alternate resources, recovery arrangements and resilience measures.

This Policy applies to employees, contractors, temporary workers, service providers and other parties with responsibilities for planning, delivering, supporting or assuring business continuity capability.

This Policy does not replace incident response plans, crisis management plans, disaster recovery plans, emergency response procedures or departmental recovery procedures. Those documents shall align with the strategy and solutions mandated by this Policy.

## Policy Statements

1. **The organisation shall maintain an approved BCM strategy.** 
 The BCM strategy shall define how the organisation will protect, continue, restore or recover priority activities following a disruption. It shall be documented, approved by senior management and maintained as part of the Business Continuity Management System.

2. **The BCM strategy shall be based on approved business impact and risk information.** 
 The strategy shall be derived from current Business Impact Analysis and risk assessment outputs, including:
 - Priority activities and their dependencies.
 - Maximum tolerable periods of disruption.
 - Recovery time objectives.
 - Recovery point objectives, where information or technology recovery is required.
 - Minimum business continuity objectives and acceptable service levels.
 - Critical resources required to continue or recover operations.
 - Key threats, vulnerabilities and single points of failure.
 - Legal, regulatory, contractual and stakeholder obligations.

3. **Each priority activity shall have selected continuity solutions.** 
 Each activity designated as a priority activity shall have one or more approved continuity solutions capable of meeting its recovery objectives. Solutions shall be specific enough to be implemented and shall identify the people, resources, systems, information, facilities and third parties required.

4. **Continuity solutions shall be proportionate to business impact and risk.** 
 The level of investment, complexity and resilience required shall be proportionate to:
 - The impact of disruption.
 - The urgency of recovery.
 - The organisation’s risk appetite.
 - Customer, regulator and stakeholder expectations.
 - Health, safety, legal and financial exposure.
 - Reputational consequences.
 - Operational feasibility and cost.

5. **Continuity solutions shall be selected using defined evaluation criteria.** 
 Proposed continuity solutions shall be assessed before approval against the following criteria:

 | Evaluation Criterion | Mandatory Consideration |
 |---|---|
 | Recovery capability | Ability to meet approved recovery time and service level requirements |
 | Resource availability | Availability of people, facilities, technology, information, equipment and suppliers |
 | Practicality | Ability to implement the solution during realistic disruption conditions |
 | Resilience | Ability to withstand likely disruption scenarios and dependency failures |
 | Scalability | Ability to operate for the expected duration and volume of demand |
 | Security and privacy | Protection of information, systems and personal data during continuity operations |
 | Health and safety | Protection of employees, contractors, customers and other affected parties |
 | Legal and contractual compliance | Alignment with obligations and commitments |
 | Cost and value | Justifiable cost compared with impact reduction and recovery benefit |
 | Testability | Ability to validate the solution through exercises, tests or evidence-based assurance |
 | Dependency risk | Reliance on internal teams, technology, sites, suppliers or infrastructure |
 | Implementation timeframe | Time required to establish and operationalise the solution |

6. **The BCM strategy shall address key resource categories.** 
 The strategy and selected solutions shall address, as applicable:
 - People and workforce availability.
 - Premises, workplaces and alternate locations.
 - Technology infrastructure, applications, networks and endpoints.
 - Data, records and information access.
 - Equipment, materials, tools and specialist assets.
 - Suppliers, outsourced services and third-party dependencies.
 - Communications with employees, customers, regulators, suppliers and other interested parties.
 - Transportation, logistics and physical access.
 - Finance, procurement and emergency purchasing.
 - Manual workarounds and temporary operating methods.
 - Mutual aid, reciprocal arrangements or shared services where approved.

7. **The organisation shall maintain a strategy-to-activity mapping.** 
 The Business Continuity Manager shall maintain a documented mapping of priority activities to approved continuity solutions. The mapping shall be available to plan owners, incident leaders and relevant assurance stakeholders.

 | Priority Activity | Recovery Objective | Minimum Acceptable Service Level | Selected Solution | Primary Owner | Key Dependencies | Validation Method |
 |---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
 | [Priority Activity 1] | [e.g., 4 hours] | [e.g., 60% capacity] | [e.g., alternate team site and remote access] | [Role] | [Systems/Suppliers/People] | [Exercise/Test/Review] |
 | [Priority Activity 2] | [e.g., 24 hours] | [e.g., daily processing cycle] | [e.g., manual workaround and delayed batch processing] | [Role] | [Records/Application] | [Tabletop/Walkthrough] |
 | [Priority Activity 3] | [e.g., 72 hours] | [e.g., priority customers only] | [e.g., third-party surge support] | [Role] | [Supplier/Contract] | [Supplier assurance review] |

8. **The organisation shall consider strategic continuity options before selecting solutions.** 
 Business units shall evaluate relevant strategic options, which may include:
 - Accepting short-term disruption where impact is within approved tolerance.
 - Reducing the likelihood or impact of disruption through resilience measures.
 - Protecting critical assets, information, facilities or infrastructure.
 - Relocating work to alternate premises or remote working arrangements.
 - Reallocating work to another team, site, region or supplier.
 - Replicating resources, data, systems or equipment.
 - Substituting manual processes, alternate systems or simplified service models.
 - Prioritising critical customers, products, services or transactions.
 - Suspending non-priority activities to release resources.
 - Outsourcing, insourcing or invoking contracted recovery services.
 - Maintaining stock, spare capacity, alternate routes or emergency supplies.

9. **Selected solutions shall be documented in sufficient operational detail.** 
 Each selected solution shall include:
 - The priority activity or dependency it supports.
 - The disruption scenarios it is intended to address.
 - The recovery objective it is designed to meet.
 - Required resources and minimum capacity.
 - Trigger points for activation.
 - Decision authority for invocation.
 - Responsible owner and supporting roles.
 - Implementation steps or reference to the relevant plan.
 - Internal and external dependencies.
 - Communications requirements.
 - Known constraints, assumptions and residual risks.
 - Validation method and test frequency.
 - Funding, contract or procurement requirements, where applicable.

10. **Recovery objectives shall not be approved unless achievable solutions exist or improvement actions are formally tracked.** 
 Where a priority activity has a recovery objective that cannot currently be met, the gap shall be recorded, risk assessed and managed through an approved improvement plan or risk acceptance decision. Unfunded or aspirational recovery objectives shall not be represented as operational capability.

11. **Continuity solutions shall support approved incident response and recovery structures.** 
 Selected solutions shall align with the organisation’s crisis management, incident management, emergency response, disaster recovery and departmental recovery arrangements. Plans shall not contain conflicting priorities, decision rights, escalation paths or recovery assumptions.

12. **Continuity solutions shall include defined activation criteria.** 
 Each solution shall specify the conditions under which it may be activated, including:
 - Expected duration of disruption.
 - Loss or degradation of a critical resource.
 - Impact on customers, safety, legal obligations or revenue.
 - Failure to restore normal operations within defined thresholds.
 - Direction from the Crisis Management Team or authorised incident leader.

13. **People-related solutions shall be practical and sustainable.** 
 Workforce continuity solutions shall address:
 - Minimum staffing levels and critical skills.
 - Deputies and alternates for key roles.
 - Cross-training requirements.
 - Remote or hybrid working arrangements.
 - Staff welfare, fatigue management and shift patterns.
 - Access to contact details, instructions and collaboration tools.
 - Constraints affecting availability, including travel, illness, local incidents or caring responsibilities.

14. **Technology and information recovery solutions shall align with business recovery needs.** 
 Technology recovery capabilities shall be aligned with approved business recovery objectives. Application, infrastructure, data and access recovery priorities shall be agreed with business owners and reflected in disaster recovery plans, backup arrangements and restoration procedures.

15. **Data and records required for continuity shall be identified and protected.** 
 Business units shall identify the information, records and data required to continue or recover priority activities. Appropriate backup, replication, secure access, retention and recovery arrangements shall be implemented and tested.

16. **Premises and facilities solutions shall address loss of site or access.** 
 Where priority activities depend on physical locations, the strategy shall define suitable alternate arrangements, which may include alternate sites, remote working, relocation, shared facilities, reciprocal arrangements, mobile units, manual processing locations or temporary suspension of non-priority services.

17. **Supplier and third-party continuity solutions shall be subject to assurance.** 
 Where priority activities depend on third parties, the responsible business owner shall ensure that continuity expectations are defined, contractually supported where appropriate, and periodically assured. Supplier recovery commitments shall be consistent with the organisation’s own recovery objectives.

18. **Manual workaround solutions shall be controlled.** 
 Manual or temporary workarounds shall be documented, authorised and tested where they are relied upon to meet recovery objectives. They shall include controls for accuracy, approval, security, reconciliation, backlog management and return to normal operations.

19. **Communications solutions shall be included in continuity strategy.** 
 The organisation shall maintain reliable methods for communicating during disruptions with employees, contractors, customers, suppliers, regulators, media representatives and other relevant interested parties. Communications solutions shall include alternates where primary channels are unavailable.

20. **Financial and procurement arrangements shall support timely continuity response.** 
 The organisation shall define emergency procurement, delegated spending authority and supplier engagement arrangements needed to implement continuity solutions within required timeframes.

21. **Selected solutions shall be approved by accountable business owners and senior management.** 
 Business owners shall approve solutions for their priority activities. Senior management shall approve the overall BCM strategy, material investment decisions, residual risks and any acceptance of capability gaps.

22. **Continuity solutions shall be funded, resourced and implemented.** 
 Approved solutions shall have assigned owners, implementation dates, resource commitments and funding where required. Business units shall not rely on unimplemented solutions as evidence of continuity capability.

23. **Residual risks shall be recorded and managed.** 
 Any remaining risk after the selection or implementation of continuity solutions shall be documented, assigned an owner and treated through mitigation, transfer, avoidance or formal acceptance.

24. **Continuity solutions shall be validated through exercises and tests.** 
 Selected solutions shall be validated at planned intervals and after significant changes. Validation may include tabletop exercises, walkthroughs, simulations, technical recovery tests, call tree tests, supplier tests, live exercises or evidence-based reviews.

25. **Exercise outcomes shall inform strategy improvement.** 
 Lessons learned from exercises, incidents, near misses, audits and post-incident reviews shall be used to update the strategy, solutions, assumptions, recovery objectives and improvement actions.

26. **Changes affecting continuity capability shall trigger reassessment.** 
 Business units shall notify the Business Continuity Manager of changes that may affect the BCM strategy or selected solutions, including:
 - New or changed products, services or processes.
 - Organisational restructuring.
 - Site openings, closures or relocations.
 - Technology changes, migrations or outages.
 - Supplier changes or contract terminations.
 - Changes in customer, legal or regulatory obligations.
 - Significant changes to volumes, operating hours or service commitments.
 - New threats, vulnerabilities or material incidents.

27. **Continuity solutions shall protect information and maintain security controls.** 
 The use of alternate sites, remote access, manual processing, emergency communications, third-party services or temporary tools shall not remove the requirement to protect confidential information, personal data, intellectual property and critical systems.

28. **The BCM strategy shall include prioritisation rules for constrained conditions.** 
 Where resources are limited during a disruption, priority shall be given to:
 - Protection of life, health and safety.
 - Compliance with legal and regulatory obligations.
 - Activities with the shortest approved recovery timeframes.
 - Services with the highest customer, financial, operational or reputational impact.
 - Commitments to vulnerable customers or critical stakeholders.
 - Activities required to support recovery of other priority activities.

29. **The organisation shall maintain evidence of strategy and solution decisions.** 
 Records shall be retained to demonstrate how continuity strategies and solutions were selected, approved, implemented, validated and improved. Evidence shall include analysis outputs, decision records, approvals, exercise results, risk acceptances, supplier assurance records and improvement tracking.

30. **The BCM strategy shall be communicated to relevant personnel.** 
 Personnel with continuity responsibilities shall receive appropriate information, training or briefing on the strategy, selected solutions and their roles during disruption. Sensitive details shall be shared on a need-to-know basis.

31. **The strategy shall support return to normal operations.** 
 Selected solutions shall include arrangements for controlled transition from continuity operations back to normal operations, including backlog clearance, reconciliation, customer communication, data integrity checks and deactivation of temporary controls.

32. **The organisation shall maintain a BCM strategy lifecycle.** 
 The BCM strategy shall follow the lifecycle below:

 | Stage | Required Activity | Output | Accountable Role |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Analyse | Review business impact and risk information | Confirmed priority activities and dependencies | Business Continuity Manager |
 | Design | Identify feasible continuity options | Proposed strategy options | Business Owner |
 | Select | Evaluate and choose proportionate solutions | Selected continuity solutions | Business Owner |
 | Approve | Confirm funding, risk position and accountability | Approved BCM strategy | Senior Management |
 | Implement | Establish resources, contracts, plans and controls | Operational continuity capability | Solution Owner |
 | Validate | Exercise, test or otherwise confirm capability | Validation evidence and lessons learned | Business Continuity Manager |
 | Improve | Address gaps, changes and lessons learned | Updated strategy and improvement actions | Business Owner |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board or Governing Body | Provides oversight of BCM strategy, ensures continuity capability supports organisational resilience, and holds senior management accountable for implementation. |
| Chief Executive Officer or Executive Leadership Team | Approves the overall BCM strategy, ensures resources are available, accepts material residual risks and resolves cross-functional prioritisation conflicts. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Owns the BCM strategy process, maintains the strategy documentation, coordinates analysis and solution selection, monitors implementation, supports exercises and reports capability status. |
| Business Unit Heads | Identify priority activities, approve recovery requirements, select and implement suitable solutions, assign solution owners and ensure departmental plans align with the strategy. |
| Priority Activity Owners | Define operational requirements, maintain activity-level recovery arrangements, validate solutions and escalate capability gaps. |
| Crisis Management Team | Invokes strategic continuity decisions during major disruptions, prioritises resources, directs recovery actions and approves major deviations from normal operating priorities. |
| Incident Management Team | Implements relevant continuity solutions during incidents, coordinates tactical recovery activity and reports status to the Crisis Management Team. |
| IT Service Owner or Disaster Recovery Manager | Ensures technology recovery solutions support approved business recovery needs and that technical recovery plans, backups, access arrangements and restoration priorities remain aligned. |
| Information Security Manager | Ensures continuity solutions maintain appropriate security, privacy, access control and information protection requirements. |
| Facilities Manager | Maintains site resilience, alternate workplace arrangements, building recovery requirements and facilities-related continuity solutions. |
| Human Resources Manager | Supports workforce continuity, role cover, staff welfare, contact information, remote working arrangements and emergency communications to personnel. |
| Procurement or Supplier Management Lead | Ensures critical supplier continuity requirements are defined, assessed, contracted where appropriate and monitored. |
| Finance Lead | Supports emergency funding, payment continuity, delegated authority and financial controls during disruption. |
| Communications Lead | Maintains internal and external communication arrangements for continuity events, including stakeholder messaging and media coordination. |
| Legal and Compliance Lead | Advises on legal, regulatory and contractual obligations affecting continuity strategy and recovery priorities. |
| Internal Audit or Assurance Function | Provides independent assurance over design, implementation and effectiveness of BCM strategy and selected solutions. |
| All Employees and Contractors | Follow continuity instructions, participate in exercises where required, maintain awareness of their role and report issues that may affect continuity capability. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory.

The Business Continuity Manager shall monitor compliance through a combination of documentation reviews, business unit attestations, exercises, incident reviews, supplier assurance, management reporting and internal audits.

The following minimum monitoring activities shall be performed:

| Monitoring Activity | Minimum Frequency | Evidence Required | Responsible Role |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of priority activity strategy mapping | At least annually and after significant change | Updated strategy mapping and approval record | Business Continuity Manager |
| Review of solution implementation status | Quarterly | Action tracker and status report | Business Continuity Manager |
| Review of open capability gaps and residual risks | Quarterly | Risk register and treatment plans | Business Unit Heads |
| Validation of selected solutions | At planned intervals based on criticality | Exercise or test records | Solution Owners |
| Supplier continuity assurance for critical dependencies | At least annually or on contract renewal | Supplier assessment, test evidence or attestation | Procurement or Supplier Management Lead |
| Technology recovery alignment review | At least annually and after major technology change | Recovery alignment record | IT Service Owner |
| Management reporting on BCM strategy effectiveness | At least annually | BCM performance report | Business Continuity Manager |
| Independent assurance review | Based on audit plan | Audit report and management actions | Internal Audit or Assurance Function |

Non-compliance may include, but is not limited to:

- Failure to define continuity solutions for priority activities.
- Reliance on unapproved or untested recovery arrangements.
- Failure to implement agreed continuity solutions.
- Failure to report significant changes affecting recovery capability.
- Maintaining recovery objectives that cannot be met without documenting the gap.
- Failure to address known continuity risks or overdue improvement actions.
- Failure to ensure third-party recovery commitments align with business needs.
- Unauthorised deviation from approved strategy during a disruption.

Where non-compliance is identified, the responsible owner shall prepare and implement a corrective action plan. Material non-compliance shall be reported to senior management and may be escalated to the Board or governing body.

Failure to comply with this Policy may result in management action, contractual remedies, supplier escalation, withdrawal of approval for business changes, risk acceptance escalation, or disciplinary action in accordance with [Organisation Name] policies and applicable law.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a justified business need and the associated continuity risk is understood, documented and approved.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requestor | Name and role of person requesting the exception |
| Business area | Function, site, service or process affected |
| Policy requirement affected | Description of the requirement that cannot be met |
| Reason for exception | Business, technical, financial or operational justification |
| Priority activity affected | Activity or dependency impacted by the exception |
| Risk assessment | Potential operational, financial, legal, customer, safety and reputational impacts |
| Compensating controls | Temporary or alternative measures to reduce risk |
| Duration | Requested start date and expiry date |
| Action plan | Steps required to achieve compliance or reduce exposure |
| Approvals | Required business, risk and senior management approvals |

All exceptions shall be:

- Recorded in the BCM exceptions register.
- Risk assessed before approval.
- Approved by the relevant Business Unit Head and Business Continuity Manager.
- Approved by senior management where the exception affects a priority activity, approved recovery objective, legal obligation, customer commitment or critical supplier dependency.
- Time-bound and subject to review before expiry.
- Reassessed if the risk context changes.

Permanent exceptions shall not be permitted. Long-term inability to meet this Policy shall be treated as a formal risk requiring senior management decision and documented treatment.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect BCM strategy or selected continuity solutions.

A review shall also be triggered by:

- Completion of a Business Impact Analysis refresh.
- Completion of a major risk assessment refresh.
- A significant incident, disruption or near miss.
- Exercise or test results indicating strategy weakness.
- Major organisational, technology, supplier or site change.
- New or changed legal, regulatory or contractual obligations.
- Material change in customer expectations or service commitments.
- Internal audit findings or management review actions.
- Identification of a significant continuity capability gap.

The Business Continuity Manager is responsible for coordinating review and maintenance of this Policy. Business Unit Heads are responsible for confirming that strategy requirements and selected solutions remain accurate, feasible and aligned with business needs.

Updates to this Policy shall be approved by [Approving Authority]. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s document retention requirements.

Policy maintenance records shall include:

| Record | Minimum Content | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Review log | Review date, reviewer, changes required and approval status | Business Continuity Manager |
| Version history | Version number, change summary, author and approval date | Business Continuity Manager |
| Approval record | Approver name, role, decision and date | Business Continuity Manager |
| Distribution record | Audience, communication date and method | Business Continuity Manager |
| Improvement actions | Action owner, due date, status and closure evidence | Business Continuity Manager |

BCM-009.title: BCM Policy
BCM-009.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [BCM-POL-001] | 1.0 | [Business Continuity Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO 22301:2019 | Internal |

## Purpose

The purpose of this BCM Policy is to establish the organisation’s commitment to maintaining an effective Business Continuity Management System that protects people, sustains critical operations, safeguards stakeholder interests, and enables timely recovery from disruptive incidents.

This policy sets mandatory requirements for identifying business continuity risks, defining recovery priorities, maintaining business continuity plans, conducting exercises, responding to disruptions, and continually improving organisational resilience.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- All business units, functions, departments, sites, and subsidiaries within [Organisation Name].
- All employees, contractors, temporary workers, consultants, and third parties who perform work for or on behalf of [Organisation Name].
- All products, services, processes, systems, facilities, suppliers, and information assets that support the delivery of time-critical activities.
- All phases of business continuity management, including planning, implementation, operation, exercising, review, maintenance, incident response, recovery, and continual improvement.

The Business Continuity Management System shall cover the activities, locations, services, and dependencies defined in the approved BCM scope statement and supporting documentation.

Where business functions or services are outsourced, the accountable internal owner shall ensure that applicable business continuity requirements are defined, agreed, monitored, and evidenced through supplier governance arrangements.

## Policy Statements

1. [Organisation Name] shall establish, implement, maintain, and continually improve a Business Continuity Management System appropriate to its purpose, operating context, risk profile, stakeholder expectations, and strategic objectives.

2. Executive management shall demonstrate visible commitment to business continuity by approving this policy, assigning accountable roles, providing adequate resources, supporting exercises, reviewing performance, and promoting a resilience culture across the organisation.

3. Business continuity objectives shall be established, documented, measurable where practicable, aligned to organisational priorities, and reviewed at planned intervals.

4. The organisation shall identify internal and external issues that may affect its ability to achieve business continuity outcomes, including operational, financial, technological, legal, regulatory, contractual, geographic, environmental, supply chain, workforce, and reputational factors.

5. The organisation shall identify relevant interested parties and determine their business continuity needs and expectations, including customers, employees, regulators, suppliers, partners, shareholders, insurers, and community stakeholders where applicable.

6. The scope of the Business Continuity Management System shall be formally defined, approved, maintained, and communicated to relevant stakeholders.

7. The organisation shall conduct and maintain business impact analyses to identify time-critical activities, dependencies, impacts over time, recovery priorities, minimum operating requirements, and recovery time expectations.

8. The organisation shall conduct and maintain risk assessments for disruption scenarios that could affect time-critical activities, including loss or unavailability of people, premises, technology, data, suppliers, utilities, transport, communications, and key facilities.

9. Business impact analysis and risk assessment outputs shall be used to determine appropriate business continuity strategies and solutions.

10. Business continuity strategies shall be selected, approved, and implemented to meet agreed recovery priorities and continuity objectives.

11. Business continuity solutions shall address, as applicable, workforce arrangements, alternate work locations, technology recovery, data availability, manual workarounds, supplier continuity, stock and equipment requirements, communications, facilities, and critical records.

12. The organisation shall document and maintain business continuity plans that define how critical activities will be continued, recovered, or restored following a disruption.

13. Business continuity plans shall be practical, accessible, role-based, and sufficiently detailed to support timely decision-making and coordinated response under disruptive conditions.

14. Business continuity plans shall include, as appropriate:
 - Activation criteria.
 - Roles, responsibilities, and authorities.
 - Escalation and notification procedures.
 - Contact details for key personnel and external parties.
 - Immediate response actions.
 - Continuity and recovery actions.
 - Internal and external communication requirements.
 - Resource requirements.
 - Dependencies and interdependencies.
 - Manual workaround instructions.
 - Stand-down and return-to-normal guidance.

15. The organisation shall establish an incident response and crisis management structure capable of assessing disruptions, activating plans, making decisions, communicating with stakeholders, and coordinating recovery actions.

16. Business continuity and incident response roles shall have clearly defined responsibilities, authorities, alternates, and escalation paths.

17. The organisation shall maintain effective internal and external communication arrangements for disruptive incidents, including mechanisms for employee notification, management briefings, customer updates, supplier coordination, media handling, and regulator communication where required.

18. Business continuity plans, crisis communications materials, contact lists, recovery procedures, and critical records shall be controlled, protected, backed up where appropriate, and available during a disruption.

19. Personnel with assigned business continuity responsibilities shall receive appropriate awareness, training, and role-specific instruction.

20. All employees shall be made aware of their responsibility to follow business continuity arrangements, report disruptive incidents promptly, participate in exercises when required, and support recovery activities relevant to their roles.

21. The organisation shall conduct planned exercises and tests to validate business continuity plans, recovery arrangements, communications, decision-making, roles, and assumptions.

22. Exercises shall be proportionate to business risk and may include desktop exercises, call-tree tests, technical recovery tests, scenario simulations, supplier continuity tests, relocation tests, or full operational exercises.

23. Exercise outcomes shall be documented, reviewed, and used to identify corrective actions, lessons learned, and improvement opportunities.

24. Business continuity documentation shall be reviewed and updated following material organisational change, significant incidents, exercises, changes in critical suppliers, changes in technology or facilities, changes in legal or contractual obligations, or at planned intervals.

25. The organisation shall define and monitor business continuity performance measures to assess whether BCM arrangements are effective, current, and aligned to business needs.

26. Management shall review the performance and suitability of the Business Continuity Management System at planned intervals and ensure that decisions, actions, risks, resource needs, and improvement opportunities are recorded and followed through.

27. Business continuity risks, issues, corrective actions, and improvement actions shall be tracked to completion by accountable owners within agreed timeframes.

28. The organisation shall integrate business continuity requirements into relevant business change activities, including new products, new services, mergers and acquisitions, technology changes, facility changes, major supplier changes, and organisational restructuring.

29. Critical suppliers and outsourced service providers shall be assessed for their ability to support the organisation’s continuity requirements, and appropriate continuity obligations shall be included in contracts or service agreements where applicable.

30. The organisation shall protect the safety and welfare of personnel during disruptions and shall not prioritise business recovery actions over life safety.

31. The organisation shall comply with applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and customer business continuity obligations.

32. The organisation shall retain documented evidence of BCM activities, including business impact analyses, risk assessments, plans, exercises, training, incidents, reviews, approvals, exceptions, and corrective actions.

33. The organisation shall promote continual improvement of business continuity capability through lessons learned, audit results, management review, changing risk information, stakeholder feedback, and operational experience.

34. This policy shall be communicated to employees and relevant external parties as appropriate and shall be made available in a controlled manner.

35. Non-compliance with this policy shall be recorded, assessed, escalated, and remediated in accordance with the organisation’s governance and disciplinary processes.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors / Governing Body | Approves the organisation’s overall commitment to business continuity; provides oversight of significant continuity risks; ensures business continuity remains aligned with organisational strategy and risk appetite. |
| Chief Executive Officer / Executive Leadership Team | Sponsors the Business Continuity Management System; approves policy direction; ensures resources are available; holds senior leaders accountable for business continuity readiness. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Owns the BCM framework and methodology; coordinates business impact analysis, risk assessment, planning, exercising, reporting, and improvement activities; maintains BCM documentation standards; provides guidance to business units. |
| Business Unit Leaders | Own continuity arrangements for their areas; identify critical activities and dependencies; ensure plans are current; assign plan owners and alternates; ensure staff participate in training and exercises. |
| Plan Owners | Develop, maintain, and exercise assigned business continuity plans; ensure contact lists, recovery procedures, and resource requirements remain current; track plan-related corrective actions. |
| Crisis Management Team | Leads strategic and tactical response to significant disruptions; assesses incident impact; activates response structures; approves key communications; prioritises recovery activity; coordinates cross-functional decisions. |
| Incident Response Team Leaders | Manage operational response activities; implement approved recovery actions; report status, issues, and resource needs to the Crisis Management Team or designated escalation point. |
| Information Technology / Disaster Recovery Lead | Maintains technology recovery capabilities; aligns IT recovery arrangements with business continuity requirements; performs technical recovery testing; reports recovery risks and constraints. |
| Facilities / Workplace Services | Maintains premises continuity arrangements; supports alternate site, access, utilities, building safety, and workplace recovery requirements. |
| Human Resources | Supports employee communication, welfare, workforce availability planning, role coverage, and post-incident people-related support. |
| Communications / Public Relations | Prepares and coordinates internal and external communications during disruptions; supports media, customer, stakeholder, and public messaging as authorised. |
| Procurement / Supplier Management | Embeds continuity requirements into supplier selection, contracting, and performance monitoring; coordinates supplier continuity assurance for critical suppliers. |
| Risk, Compliance, and Internal Audit | Provides oversight, challenge, and assurance over BCM arrangements; supports monitoring of compliance obligations, risks, audit findings, and corrective actions. |
| Employees and Contractors | Understand applicable continuity arrangements; report incidents promptly; follow instructions during disruptions; participate in training, exercises, and recovery activities as required. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this policy is mandatory. The Business Continuity Manager, supported by business unit leaders and assurance functions, shall monitor compliance through planned and event-driven activities.

Minimum monitoring activities shall include:

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Accountable Owner | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Review of BCM scope and applicability | Annually or after significant change | Business Continuity Manager | Approved scope statement, review record |
| Business impact analysis review | Annually or after significant change | Business Unit Leaders | Approved BIA records |
| Continuity risk assessment review | Annually or after significant change | Business Continuity Manager / Risk Owner | Risk assessment records, risk treatment actions |
| Business continuity plan review | At least annually and after relevant change | Plan Owners | Updated plans, approval records |
| Contact list validation | At least quarterly | Plan Owners | Contact test results, updated contact lists |
| Crisis management exercise | At least annually | Business Continuity Manager | Exercise report, attendance, lessons learned |
| Business unit plan exercise | At least annually for critical functions | Business Unit Leaders | Exercise report, action log |
| Technology recovery testing | According to approved recovery test schedule | IT / Disaster Recovery Lead | Test results, recovery evidence |
| Critical supplier continuity review | At least annually for critical suppliers | Procurement / Supplier Management | Supplier assessment records, action plans |
| BCM training and awareness | At onboarding and periodically thereafter | Business Continuity Manager / HR | Training records, awareness communications |
| Corrective action tracking | Monthly until closed | Action Owners | Action register, closure evidence |
| Management review of BCM performance | At least annually | Executive Leadership Team | Meeting minutes, decisions, action records |

Performance indicators shall be defined and maintained to evaluate the effectiveness of BCM arrangements. Indicators may include:

- Percentage of critical business impact analyses reviewed within schedule.
- Percentage of business continuity plans reviewed and approved within schedule.
- Percentage of planned exercises completed.
- Percentage of corrective actions closed by due date.
- Exercise performance against recovery expectations.
- Currency of crisis and recovery contact details.
- Availability of critical recovery resources.
- Completion rates for BCM training and awareness.
- Number and severity of BCM audit findings.
- Number of continuity incidents and lessons learned.

Non-compliance shall be managed as follows:

| Severity | Examples | Required Action | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low | Minor plan formatting issue; contact detail update overdue by less than 30 days | Correct within agreed timeframe | Plan Owner |
| Medium | Business continuity plan overdue; exercise delayed; corrective action missed without approved reason | Formal remediation plan required | Business Unit Leader and Business Continuity Manager |
| High | Critical function without a current plan; repeated failure to exercise; unresolved dependency affecting recovery capability | Immediate management attention and risk acceptance or remediation required | Executive Leadership Team |
| Critical | Known inability to recover critical services within required timeframes; failure to activate response arrangements during major disruption; material breach of legal or contractual continuity obligation | Urgent executive escalation, corrective action, and formal risk treatment required | CEO / Board or delegated committee |

Failure to comply with this policy may result in management action, contractual remedies, supplier escalation, disciplinary action, or other corrective measures consistent with organisational policies and applicable law.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy are permitted only where compliance is not feasible, would introduce greater risk, or requires a phased implementation approach approved by authorised management.

All exceptions shall be documented, risk assessed, time-bound, and approved before being relied upon. Permanent exceptions are not permitted unless formally approved as part of a documented scope or risk decision by executive management.

Exception requests shall include:

| Required Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Requesting function | Business unit, department, or service requesting the exception |
| Policy requirement affected | Specific policy requirement that cannot be met |
| Business justification | Reason the exception is required |
| Risk assessment | Potential impact to people, operations, customers, legal obligations, reputation, and recovery capability |
| Compensating measures | Alternative controls or arrangements that reduce risk |
| Duration | Requested start and end date |
| Action plan | Steps to achieve compliance or reduce reliance on the exception |
| Owner | Accountable individual responsible for managing the exception |
| Approval | Required approval by the appropriate authority |

Exception approval authority shall be based on risk severity:

| Exception Risk Level | Approval Authority | Maximum Review Period |
|---|---|---:|
| Low | Business Continuity Manager | 12 months |
| Medium | Relevant Business Unit Leader and Business Continuity Manager | 6 months |
| High | Executive Leadership Team member accountable for the affected area | 3 months |
| Critical | CEO or delegated executive committee | 1 month |

Expired exceptions shall be treated as non-compliance unless renewed through the approved exception process before expiry.

## Review & Maintenance

This policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect business continuity requirements, including:

- Changes to organisational strategy, structure, products, or services.
- Significant changes to critical processes, systems, facilities, suppliers, or workforce arrangements.
- New or changed legal, regulatory, contractual, or customer requirements.
- Significant incidents, near misses, exercises, or lessons learned.
- Material changes to the organisation’s risk profile or operating environment.
- Audit findings or management review decisions requiring policy updates.

The Business Continuity Manager is responsible for coordinating policy review and proposing updates. Material changes shall be approved by [Approving Authority]. Minor administrative updates may be made by the policy owner where they do not alter policy intent or mandatory requirements.

The current approved version of this policy shall be stored in [Document Repository/System]. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.

Policy communication shall occur following approval and shall include relevant employees, contractors, and third parties where applicable. Training and awareness materials shall be updated as needed to reflect policy changes.

BCM-010.title: BCM Objectives
BCM-010.content:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [BCM-POL-Objectives] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | [Business Continuity Manager] |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | ISO 22301:2019 |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes the mandatory requirements for defining, approving, maintaining, monitoring, and improving measurable Business Continuity Management (BCM) objectives.

The purpose of BCM objectives is to ensure the organisation sets clear, measurable targets that support continuity of critical products, services, processes, systems, facilities, people, suppliers, and stakeholder obligations during and after disruptive incidents.

This Policy ensures BCM objectives are:

- aligned with organisational strategy, risk appetite, and continuity priorities;
- based on business impact analysis, risk assessment, and stakeholder requirements;
- measurable, monitored, and reported;
- assigned to accountable owners;
- maintained as circumstances change;
- used to drive continual improvement of the Business Continuity Management System.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- all business units, functions, departments, and locations within the scope of the organisation’s Business Continuity Management System;
- all personnel with responsibility for business continuity planning, incident response, crisis management, technology recovery, supplier continuity, facilities recovery, communications, or service restoration;
- outsourced processes, third-party services, suppliers, and partners that support critical activities;
- BCM objectives relating to continuity capability, preparedness, response, recovery, testing, training, awareness, performance, and improvement.

This Policy applies to BCM objectives at enterprise, function, process, site, service, and project levels where such objectives are required to support business continuity outcomes.

This Policy does not replace detailed business continuity plans, crisis management plans, disaster recovery plans, incident response procedures, or departmental operating procedures. Those documents shall support and align with the objectives established under this Policy.

## Policy Statements

1. The organisation shall establish measurable BCM objectives that support the continuity and timely recovery of priority activities, products, and services.

2. BCM objectives shall be aligned with the organisation’s business strategy, operating model, risk appetite, legal and contractual obligations, stakeholder expectations, and continuity policy commitments.

3. BCM objectives shall be based on current business impact analysis, continuity risk assessment, incident experience, lessons learned, exercise outcomes, and management priorities.

4. BCM objectives shall be documented in a controlled format and shall include, at minimum:
 - objective statement;
 - business rationale;
 - scope of application;
 - measurement method;
 - target or threshold;
 - accountable owner;
 - supporting actions or initiatives;
 - required resources;
 - review frequency;
 - status and evidence source.

5. BCM objectives shall be specific enough to enable objective evaluation of whether they have been achieved.

6. BCM objectives shall be measurable using defined metrics, evidence, or performance indicators. Vague objectives that cannot be measured shall not be approved.

7. BCM objectives shall be achievable within approved organisational resources, capabilities, and timeframes, unless formally recorded as stretch objectives approved by senior management.

8. BCM objectives shall be relevant to the organisation’s continuity priorities and shall contribute to improved resilience, preparedness, response, recovery, or assurance.

9. BCM objectives shall be time-bound and shall include target dates, reporting periods, or review cycles.

10. BCM objectives shall include appropriate targets for recovery capability, including recovery time, recovery point, minimum service levels, resource availability, communication timeliness, and plan effectiveness where relevant.

11. The organisation shall define BCM objectives at appropriate levels, including enterprise-level objectives and, where applicable, objectives for business units, sites, services, processes, technology platforms, suppliers, and specialist response teams.

12. BCM objectives shall be consistent with approved business continuity strategies and shall not conflict with crisis management, emergency response, information security, technology recovery, health and safety, legal, or communications requirements.

13. BCM objectives shall consider dependencies that may affect continuity performance, including personnel, facilities, technology, data, suppliers, equipment, utilities, logistics, records, and external services.

14. BCM objectives shall include requirements for maintaining readiness, including training, awareness, plan maintenance, exercising, supplier engagement, and incident response capability.

15. BCM objectives shall be reviewed for practicality before approval, including confirmation that responsible owners have authority, resources, and access to information needed to achieve the objective.

16. Each BCM objective shall have a single accountable owner responsible for delivery, tracking, evidence collection, issue escalation, and reporting.

17. Where delivery of a BCM objective depends on multiple teams, supporting owners shall be identified and their responsibilities shall be documented.

18. BCM objectives shall be approved by appropriate management based on their level, impact, cost, and organisational significance.

19. Enterprise-level BCM objectives shall be approved by [Executive Sponsor / Executive Committee].

20. Business unit, site, service, or process-level BCM objectives shall be approved by the relevant business owner and the [Business Continuity Manager] or delegated BCM authority.

21. The organisation shall maintain a central BCM Objectives Register or equivalent controlled record.

22. The BCM Objectives Register shall be kept current and shall be available for management review, internal audit, external audit, and relevant operational reviews.

23. The following minimum objective categories shall be considered when setting BCM objectives:

| Objective Category | Example Objective Area | Typical Measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Critical activity recovery | Ability to restore priority activities within approved recovery targets | Percentage of critical activities with validated recovery arrangements |
| Plan readiness | Completeness and currency of continuity plans | Percentage of plans reviewed and approved within schedule |
| Exercise and testing | Validation of response and recovery capability | Percentage of planned exercises completed and actions closed |
| Training and awareness | Preparedness of personnel with continuity responsibilities | Completion rate for required BCM training |
| Incident response | Timeliness and effectiveness of incident escalation and mobilisation | Time to notify, escalate, convene, and communicate |
| Technology recovery | Availability and recoverability of systems supporting critical activities | Successful recovery test rate and recovery target achievement |
| Supplier continuity | Assurance over critical third-party dependencies | Percentage of critical suppliers with reviewed continuity arrangements |
| Improvement actions | Closure of findings, gaps, and lessons learned | Percentage of corrective actions closed by due date |

24. BCM objectives shall include both outcome measures and activity measures where appropriate.

25. BCM objectives shall not be limited to completion of documentation. They shall also measure the effectiveness of preparedness, response, recovery, and improvement activities.

26. BCM objectives shall be supported by action plans where achievement requires specific projects, remediation, resource allocation, or capability development.

27. Action plans supporting BCM objectives shall define tasks, owners, due dates, dependencies, resource requirements, risks, and progress status.

28. BCM objectives shall be communicated to relevant personnel and stakeholders in a manner appropriate to their role and responsibilities.

29. Personnel assigned responsibilities for BCM objectives shall understand the objective, expected outcome, measurement method, reporting requirements, and consequences of non-achievement.

30. BCM objectives shall be monitored at defined intervals based on criticality, risk, and reporting needs.

31. At minimum, BCM objectives shall be reviewed quarterly by the [Business Continuity Manager] and reported to [Management Review Forum / Risk Committee / Executive Committee].

32. High-priority BCM objectives or objectives linked to significant continuity risks shall be monitored more frequently where required by management.

33. The following monitoring schedule shall apply unless a more stringent schedule is approved:

| Objective Type | Minimum Monitoring Frequency | Minimum Reporting Audience |
|---|---:|---|
| Enterprise BCM objectives | Quarterly | [Executive Committee / Risk Committee] |
| Critical service or process objectives | Monthly or quarterly based on risk | Business owner and [Business Continuity Manager] |
| Remediation or improvement objectives | Monthly until closure | Objective owner and BCM function |
| Exercise and test objectives | After each exercise or test | Exercise sponsor, BCM function, and relevant management |
| Supplier continuity objectives | At least annually, or more frequently for high-risk suppliers | Procurement, business owner, and BCM function |
| Training and awareness objectives | Quarterly | BCM function and relevant management |

34. Performance against BCM objectives shall be supported by evidence such as completed exercises, test results, training records, plan reviews, audit outputs, incident records, supplier assessments, management approvals, and corrective action closure records.

35. Objective owners shall provide status updates using agreed reporting formats and shall ensure reported information is accurate, timely, complete, and supported by evidence.

36. BCM objective performance shall be evaluated using clear status definitions.

| Status | Definition | Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| On Track | Objective is expected to be achieved by the target date and evidence supports progress | Continue monitoring |
| At Risk | Objective may not be achieved without management attention or corrective action | Define and track recovery actions |
| Off Track | Objective is unlikely to be achieved, target has been missed, or performance is below threshold | Escalate and implement corrective action |
| Achieved | Objective has met the defined target and evidence is retained | Record closure and consider whether ongoing monitoring is required |
| Deferred | Objective has been formally postponed with approved justification and revised date | Maintain approval record and reassess risk |
| Cancelled | Objective is no longer required and cancellation has been approved | Retain rationale and approval record |

37. Where a BCM objective is at risk, off track, deferred, or cancelled, the accountable owner shall document the reason, business impact, corrective action, revised timeline, and approval where required.

38. Failure to achieve a BCM objective shall be assessed for impact on continuity capability and shall be escalated where it could affect the organisation’s ability to maintain or recover critical activities.

39. Material issues affecting BCM objectives shall be reported to management without undue delay.

40. The organisation shall evaluate BCM objectives during management review and use the results to determine whether the Business Continuity Management System remains suitable, adequate, and effective.

41. BCM objectives shall be revised when there are significant changes to:
 - organisational strategy or priorities;
 - products, services, processes, or operating model;
 - locations, facilities, workforce arrangements, or supply chain;
 - technology platforms, data environments, or recovery architecture;
 - legal, regulatory, contractual, or stakeholder requirements;
 - business impact analysis or risk assessment results;
 - incident outcomes, exercise results, audit findings, or lessons learned;
 - resource availability or risk appetite.

42. New or changed business initiatives that materially affect continuity requirements shall consider whether new or revised BCM objectives are required.

43. BCM objectives shall be integrated into relevant planning and performance management activities where appropriate, including risk management, operational resilience planning, technology recovery planning, supplier management, project governance, and management review.

44. BCM objectives shall be realistic, but they shall not be reduced solely to match current weaknesses where those weaknesses expose the organisation to unacceptable continuity risk.

45. Where current capability does not meet required continuity outcomes, BCM objectives shall include improvement targets and planned actions to close the gap.

46. BCM objectives shall be retained as documented information in accordance with the organisation’s record retention requirements.

47. Records relating to BCM objectives shall be protected from unauthorised alteration, loss, or disclosure.

48. BCM objectives shall be version-controlled where changes affect targets, ownership, measurement methods, scope, or approval status.

49. Superseded BCM objectives and historical performance records shall be retained to demonstrate objective setting, monitoring, decision-making, and improvement over time.

50. The organisation shall ensure that outsourced activities and supplier dependencies supporting critical activities are reflected in BCM objectives where relevant.

51. Procurement, contract owners, and business owners shall ensure continuity objectives for critical suppliers are defined, monitored, and escalated where supplier performance or assurance is inadequate.

52. BCM objectives shall not require personnel to compromise life safety, legal obligations, ethical responsibilities, or health and safety requirements in order to meet continuity targets.

53. Where there is a conflict between BCM objectives and life safety, legal compliance, or emergency response requirements, life safety and legal compliance shall take precedence.

54. BCM objectives shall be reviewed after disruptive incidents to determine whether objectives were appropriate, achievable, and effective.

55. Lessons learned from incidents, exercises, audits, and reviews shall be used to update BCM objectives and improve continuity capability.

56. The organisation shall maintain enough resources, competence, information, tools, and management support to enable BCM objectives to be achieved.

57. BCM objectives shall be included in BCM awareness, training, or communications where personnel need to understand their role in achieving them.

58. BCM objectives shall be proportionate to business criticality and risk. More demanding objectives shall apply to activities, services, systems, and suppliers whose disruption would cause significant harm to the organisation or its stakeholders.

59. BCM objectives shall be traceable to the continuity needs they support, including impact tolerances, recovery priorities, stakeholder expectations, or approved risk treatment decisions.

60. No BCM objective shall be considered complete until the defined evidence has been reviewed and accepted by the accountable owner and, where required, the BCM function.

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board / Governing Body | Provides oversight of BCM direction, risk appetite, and significant continuity objectives; receives reporting on material BCM performance and unresolved risks. |
| Executive Sponsor | Approves enterprise-level BCM objectives; ensures objectives align with organisational strategy and priorities; removes barriers to achievement. |
| [Business Continuity Manager] | Owns this Policy; coordinates the BCM objective-setting process; maintains the BCM Objectives Register; reviews objective quality; monitors performance; reports progress; supports owners; escalates issues. |
| Senior Management | Ensures BCM objectives are established for areas under their control; assigns accountable owners; provides resources; reviews progress; resolves issues and approves corrective actions. |
| Business Process Owners | Define and deliver BCM objectives for critical activities, services, and processes; provide evidence of progress; ensure continuity arrangements meet approved recovery needs. |
| Site / Facility Managers | Establish and monitor site-level continuity objectives where facilities are required for critical operations; support recovery and exercise objectives. |
| Technology / IT Service Owners | Define and deliver technology recovery objectives for systems, infrastructure, applications, data, and services supporting critical activities. |
| Crisis Management and Incident Response Leads | Ensure response and mobilisation objectives are understood, exercised, measured, and improved following incidents and exercises. |
| Procurement / Supplier Management | Supports supplier-related BCM objectives; obtains continuity assurance from critical suppliers; escalates supplier continuity gaps. |
| Risk Management Function | Aligns BCM objectives with enterprise risk processes; supports risk assessment and escalation of continuity risks. |
| Internal Audit | Provides independent assurance over the design, implementation, monitoring, and effectiveness of BCM objectives as part of approved audit activity. |
| Human Resources / Learning and Development | Supports BCM training and awareness objectives; maintains training completion evidence where applicable. |
| All Personnel Assigned BCM Responsibilities | Understand and perform assigned duties; complete required training; support achievement of relevant BCM objectives; report issues that may affect continuity capability. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory for all personnel and organisational areas within scope.

The [Business Continuity Manager] shall monitor compliance with this Policy through:

- review of the BCM Objectives Register;
- quarterly status reporting;
- management review input;
- business continuity plan reviews;
- exercise and test results;
- corrective action tracking;
- supplier continuity assurance reviews;
- training completion records;
- internal audits;
- incident and lessons learned reviews.

The following compliance indicators shall be used, at minimum, to assess implementation of this Policy:

| Compliance Indicator | Expected Evidence | Minimum Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| BCM objectives are documented and approved | Approved BCM Objectives Register | Quarterly |
| Objectives include measurable targets and owners | Objective records with metrics, thresholds, owners, and dates | Quarterly |
| Performance is monitored and reported | Status reports, dashboards, meeting minutes | Quarterly |
| Off-track objectives are escalated | Issue logs, escalation records, corrective action plans | Monthly or as required |
| BCM objectives align with business impact analysis and risk assessment outputs | Traceability to impact analysis, recovery priorities, and risk treatment decisions | At least annually |
| Objectives are updated after significant change | Change records, revised objectives, approval evidence | As required |
| Evidence of achievement is retained | Exercise reports, test results, training records, plan approvals, supplier reviews | As required |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in:

- escalation to the accountable manager or executive sponsor;
- requirement to produce a corrective action plan;
- additional oversight, reporting, or assurance activity;
- reassessment of continuity risk exposure;
- suspension or rejection of incomplete BCM deliverables;
- supplier performance management action where non-compliance involves a third party;
- disciplinary action in accordance with organisational policies where non-compliance is deliberate, negligent, or repeated.

Where non-compliance creates a material risk to continuity of critical activities, the issue shall be escalated to [Risk Committee / Executive Committee] without undue delay.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a justified business reason and where the resulting continuity risk is understood, documented, approved, and subject to time-bound review.

Requests for exception shall include:

- the specific requirement for which exception is requested;
- reason for the exception;
- affected business unit, service, process, site, system, or supplier;
- risk assessment and potential continuity impact;
- compensating controls or interim arrangements;
- proposed duration of the exception;
- action plan to return to compliance, where applicable;
- accountable owner;
- required approvals.

Exceptions shall be approved by the [Business Continuity Manager] and the relevant senior business owner. Exceptions that may affect critical services, legal or contractual obligations, stakeholder commitments, or enterprise risk appetite shall also be approved by [Executive Sponsor / Risk Committee].

Exceptions shall not be open-ended. Each exception shall have an expiry date and shall be reviewed before expiry.

The [Business Continuity Manager] shall maintain an Exceptions Register and report active exceptions to management at agreed intervals.

| Exception Risk Level | Approval Required | Maximum Initial Duration | Review Frequency |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Low | [Business Continuity Manager] and business owner | 6 months | At expiry |
| Medium | Senior manager and [Business Continuity Manager] | 3 months | Monthly or quarterly |
| High | [Executive Sponsor / Risk Committee] | 1 month | Monthly |
| Critical | [Executive Committee / Board-delegated authority] | By specific approval only | As directed |

Exceptions shall be withdrawn or revised if the risk increases, compensating controls become ineffective, or the business justification is no longer valid.

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually by the [Business Continuity Manager] to ensure it remains suitable, adequate, and effective.

This Policy shall also be reviewed when any of the following occur:

- significant organisational change;
- material change to business continuity scope, strategy, or risk appetite;
- major incident or crisis affecting continuity capability;
- significant audit finding or management review decision;
- material change in legal, regulatory, contractual, or stakeholder expectations;
- substantial change to critical activities, suppliers, technology, facilities, or operating model;
- recurring failure to achieve BCM objectives;
- identification of unclear, obsolete, or ineffective policy requirements.

Policy changes shall be approved by [Approving Authority] before publication.

The [Business Continuity Manager] shall ensure the current approved version is available to relevant personnel and that obsolete versions are removed from routine use or clearly marked as superseded.

Records of review, approval, communication, and policy changes shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records management requirements.

BCM-012.title: Business Continuity Plan(s)
BCM-012.content:
