BCM-023.title: Exercise & Test Reports
BCM-023.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [BCMS-RPT-EXTEST-001] | 1.0 | Business Continuity Manager | [YYYY-MM-DD] | ISO 22301:2019 Business Continuity Management | Internal Confidential |

## Purpose

This report records the results of business continuity exercises and tests performed during the reporting period. It provides evidence that the organisation has evaluated its business continuity arrangements, identified strengths and weaknesses, captured lessons learned, and assigned corrective actions for improvement.

The report is intended to support management oversight of the Business Continuity Management System by documenting:

- Exercise and test scenarios conducted.
- Participating functions, sites, suppliers, systems, and stakeholders.
- Planned objectives and success criteria.
- Actual performance against expected recovery arrangements.
- Issues, gaps, dependencies, and improvement opportunities.
- Decisions, recommendations, corrective actions, and accountable owners.

This report is not a business continuity plan. It is an evidence record and management summary of exercise and test outcomes.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Reporting period covered | [YYYY-MM-DD] to [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Report prepared by | [Name / Role] |
| Report reviewed by | [Name / Role] |
| Report approved by | [Name / Role / Committee] |
| Date of report issue | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Next scheduled report | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

### Scope of Exercises and Tests Covered

This report covers business continuity exercises and tests completed within the reporting period for the following areas:

| Area | Included in Scope | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Crisis management arrangements | Yes | Activation, escalation, decision-making, communications |
| Incident response coordination | Yes | Interface between incident handling and continuity response |
| Business continuity plans | Yes | Departmental and process-level recovery procedures |
| Technology recovery arrangements | Yes | Application, infrastructure, data recovery, remote access |
| Workplace recovery arrangements | Yes | Alternative working locations and remote working capability |
| People availability arrangements | Yes | Role coverage, deputies, call trees, welfare considerations |
| Supplier and third-party dependencies | Yes | Critical supplier notification and workaround arrangements |
| Customer and stakeholder communications | Yes | Internal and external communication templates and approvals |
| Regulatory and contractual notification processes | Yes | Decision points, responsibilities, and evidence capture |
| Manual workarounds | Yes | Feasibility, capacity, data integrity, and approval controls |

### Exercises and Tests Included

| Ref | Exercise / Test Name | Date | Type | Scenario Theme | Business Area / Process | Overall Outcome |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| EX-001 | Crisis Management Tabletop | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Discussion-based exercise | Loss of primary office following building access denial | Executive, Facilities, HR, Communications | Partially achieved |
| EX-002 | Critical Application Recovery Test | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Technical recovery test | Unavailability of [Critical System] | IT, Operations, Customer Service | Achieved with observations |
| EX-003 | Call Tree and Notification Test | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Communications test | Out-of-hours emergency notification | All priority response teams | Partially achieved |
| EX-004 | Supplier Disruption Scenario Exercise | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Functional exercise | Failure of [Critical Supplier] service | Procurement, Legal, Operations | Achieved |
| EX-005 | Departmental Business Continuity Plan Walkthrough | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Plan validation exercise | Loss of key staff and system access | [Department / Function] | Not fully achieved |

### Out of Scope

The following were not assessed during this reporting period:

- Full live relocation to an alternate physical site.
- Extended multi-day crisis simulation.
- Complete end-to-end disaster recovery failover for all production systems.
- Customer-facing communications release to live public channels.
- Unannounced exercise of all business units simultaneously.

These exclusions should be considered when interpreting the overall assurance level provided by this report.

## Executive Summary

During the reporting period, the organisation completed five business continuity exercises and tests covering crisis management, critical system recovery, emergency communications, supplier disruption, and departmental plan validation. The programme demonstrated that the organisation has established practical continuity arrangements and that key response personnel understand their core responsibilities.

The strongest results were observed in supplier disruption handling and critical application recovery, where defined escalation routes, technical recovery steps, and decision-making structures were generally effective. The organisation was able to demonstrate recovery capability for [Critical System] within the agreed target timeframe, subject to improvement in evidence capture and post-recovery validation.

Several areas require management attention. Notification testing showed gaps in contact data accuracy and deputy coverage. The crisis management tabletop highlighted inconsistency in documenting strategic decisions and maintaining a clear action log during fast-moving situations. The departmental walkthrough found that some workarounds are not sufficiently detailed to support sustained operations without reliance on informal staff knowledge.

Overall, the business continuity capability is assessed as **moderately effective**, with a need for targeted improvement before the next full programme cycle. No critical failure was identified that would invalidate the business continuity approach; however, several important weaknesses should be corrected to improve confidence in actual incident performance.

### Overall Assessment

| Assessment Area | Rating | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| Exercise design and relevance | Effective | Scenarios were credible, aligned to priority activities, and appropriate for current organisational risks. |
| Participation and engagement | Mostly effective | Core teams participated actively; some deputy roles and third-party representatives were underrepresented. |
| Plan usability | Partially effective | Plans are available and structured but some recovery steps lack operational detail. |
| Response coordination | Mostly effective | Teams understood escalation paths, but decision and action logging needs improvement. |
| Communication arrangements | Partially effective | Templates and channels exist, but contact data and out-of-hours responsiveness require improvement. |
| Recovery capability | Mostly effective | Key technology recovery objectives were met for tested systems, with improvements needed for validation records. |
| Lessons learned process | Effective | Issues were captured and converted into actions with accountable owners. |

### Key Outcomes

- Business continuity arrangements are in place and testable.
- Critical roles are generally understood by primary role holders.
- Priority systems and processes have recovery approaches defined.
- Emergency communications capability requires further strengthening.
- Business continuity plans need more precise workaround instructions in selected areas.
- Evidence collection during tests should be improved to support auditability and management review.
- Corrective actions have been assigned and should be tracked through closure.

## Methodology

### Exercise and Test Approach

The exercises and tests were conducted using a structured business continuity validation approach. Each exercise or test included defined objectives, participants, scenario assumptions, expected outcomes, evaluation criteria, and evidence collection methods.

The programme used a combination of discussion-based, functional, communications, and technical testing methods to provide broader assurance across people, process, technology, facilities, and third-party dependencies.

### Exercise Types Used

| Exercise / Test Type | Purpose | Evidence Generated |
|---|---|---|
| Tabletop exercise | Validate understanding of roles, decisions, escalation, and coordination in a simulated disruption. | Scenario injects, participant notes, decision logs, facilitator observations. |
| Technical recovery test | Confirm that selected systems, infrastructure, data, or applications can be recovered within expected tolerances. | Recovery logs, timestamps, screenshots, system checks, issue records. |
| Communications test | Confirm that notification channels, call trees, and contact lists are accurate and effective. | Call records, response times, failed contact attempts, contact list updates. |
| Functional exercise | Validate practical execution of selected continuity procedures without a full live disruption. | Action logs, role performance observations, workaround results. |
| Plan walkthrough | Assess completeness, clarity, and usability of continuity plans with process owners and recovery teams. | Plan mark-ups, improvement notes, participant feedback, action tracker entries. |

### Evaluation Criteria

Each exercise and test was assessed against the following criteria:

| Evaluation Criterion | Description |
|---|---|
| Scenario relevance | Whether the scenario was realistic, risk-based, and appropriate to the business activity being tested. |
| Objective achievement | Whether stated exercise or test objectives were met. |
| Timeliness | Whether escalation, decision-making, communications, and recovery activities occurred within expected timeframes. |
| Role clarity | Whether participants understood responsibilities, authority levels, and handover arrangements. |
| Plan usability | Whether documented procedures were accessible, current, clear, and actionable. |
| Communication effectiveness | Whether internal and external communications were timely, accurate, and approved appropriately. |
| Recovery performance | Whether tested recovery arrangements met agreed business needs. |
| Evidence quality | Whether adequate records were created to demonstrate performance and support improvement. |
| Lessons learned | Whether issues and opportunities were identified, prioritised, and assigned for action. |

### Rating Definitions

| Rating | Definition |
|---|---|
| Achieved | Objectives were met with no significant weaknesses identified. Minor observations may exist. |
| Achieved with observations | Objectives were substantially met, but improvements are required to increase reliability or consistency. |
| Partially achieved | Some objectives were met, but material gaps were identified that could affect incident response or recovery. |
| Not fully achieved | Objectives were not met or significant weaknesses were identified that require prompt corrective action. |
| Not tested | The area was not assessed during the exercise or test. |

### Information Sources

The following sources were used in preparing this report:

- Approved exercise plans and test scripts.
- Facilitator notes and observer records.
- Participant feedback forms.
- Crisis management and business continuity plan documents.
- Technical recovery logs and system validation records.
- Communications test records and contact list results.
- Action logs and decision logs created during exercises.
- Post-exercise debrief notes.
- Interviews with exercise leads, business process owners, and recovery team members.
- Supporting records from IT, Facilities, HR, Procurement, Legal, Communications, and Operations.

### Participants

| Role / Function | Participation Level | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Executive crisis leadership | Participated | Primary decision-makers attended tabletop exercise. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Participated | Planned, facilitated, and coordinated reporting. |
| Incident response leads | Participated | Supported escalation and coordination scenarios. |
| IT recovery team | Participated | Completed technical recovery test activities. |
| Facilities management | Participated | Supported workplace access denial scenario. |
| HR | Participated | Covered people availability, welfare, and remote working considerations. |
| Corporate communications | Participated | Reviewed stakeholder messaging and approval flow. |
| Legal / Compliance | Participated | Advised on notification triggers and record keeping. |
| Procurement / Supplier management | Participated | Supported critical supplier disruption exercise. |
| Departmental process owners | Participated | Validated process-level plans and workarounds. |
| Deputies / alternates | Limited participation | Attendance inconsistent across functions. |
| Critical suppliers | Limited participation | Direct involvement limited to selected supplier scenario. |

## Detailed Findings / Results (with structure)

### EX-001 - Crisis Management Tabletop

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Exercise date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Exercise type | Tabletop exercise |
| Scenario | Primary office becomes inaccessible due to a building safety incident. Staff are unable to enter the site for at least five business days. Key meetings, customer commitments, and regulated activities must continue remotely or from alternate arrangements. |
| Scope | Crisis management team activation, workplace continuity, staff welfare, communications, decision-making, escalation, and business priority setting. |
| Participants | Executive crisis team, Facilities, HR, IT, Communications, Legal, Business Continuity Manager, selected business process owners. |
| Objectives | Validate crisis activation, assess leadership decision-making, confirm remote working assumptions, test internal communication approval process, identify workplace recovery gaps. |
| Overall outcome | Partially achieved |

#### Results

| Objective | Result | Evidence / Observation |
|---|---|---|
| Activate crisis management team using documented escalation route | Achieved with observations | Core team assembled within expected timeframe; two alternates were unclear on joining instructions. |
| Establish incident facts, assumptions, and immediate priorities | Achieved | Team identified safety, customer impact, staff access, and regulatory priorities. |
| Confirm remote working capability for impacted staff | Partially achieved | Remote working assumed for most roles, but some teams rely on site-based equipment and paper records. |
| Approve internal staff communication | Achieved with observations | Draft message was prepared quickly, but approval sequence was unclear between HR and Communications. |
| Maintain action and decision log | Partially achieved | Decisions were discussed and agreed but not consistently recorded with owner, rationale, and timestamp. |
| Identify business priorities for first 24 hours | Achieved | Priority processes and customer commitments were identified. |

#### Strengths

- Senior leadership engaged constructively and made timely decisions.
- Safety and staff welfare were prioritised appropriately.
- The business impact of site loss was well understood by Facilities and Operations.
- Existing remote working tools provide a credible continuity option for many staff.
- Communications team had suitable draft messaging templates available.

#### Issues and Gaps

| Issue ID | Issue | Impact | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| EX001-01 | Deputies were not consistently briefed on crisis team joining instructions. | Response may be delayed if primary role holders are unavailable. | Medium |
| EX001-02 | Decision log discipline was inconsistent. | Reduced ability to evidence decisions, communicate rationale, and support post-incident review. | Medium |
| EX001-03 | Some departmental dependencies on site-based materials were not fully documented. | Remote continuity may fail for activities requiring physical records, specialist equipment, or local access. | High |
| EX001-04 | Communications approval responsibilities were unclear between HR and Communications. | Delays or inconsistent messaging could occur during staff communications. | Medium |

#### Lessons Learned

- Crisis response effectiveness depends on clear administrative discipline, not only good discussion.
- Deputy role readiness should be tested as actively as primary role readiness.
- Workplace loss planning must include physical records, specialist equipment, printing needs, secure storage, and mail handling.
- Communication templates should include pre-agreed approval routes for different message types.

---

### EX-002 - Critical Application Recovery Test

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Test date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Test type | Technical recovery test |
| Scenario | [Critical System] becomes unavailable due to a severe infrastructure failure. Recovery is initiated using the approved recovery procedure and recent backup or replicated environment. |
| Scope | Recovery of [Critical System], supporting database, application services, authentication dependency, data validation, user access confirmation, and business acceptance testing. |
| Participants | IT infrastructure, application support, database administration, cyber incident response representative, business system owner, operations user representative. |
| Objectives | Recover system within target timeframe, validate data integrity, confirm user access, test escalation and communication to business stakeholders, record evidence. |
| Overall outcome | Achieved with observations |

#### Recovery Timeline

| Time | Activity | Owner | Result |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 09:00 | Test initiated and recovery bridge opened | IT Recovery Lead | Completed |
| 09:08 | Incident ticket and recovery log created | Service Desk Lead | Completed |
| 09:15 | Application outage confirmed and recovery procedure invoked | Application Support | Completed |
| 09:30 | Database restore / failover initiated | Database Administrator | Completed |
| 10:20 | Application services restored in recovery environment | Infrastructure Lead | Completed |
| 10:35 | Authentication and access checks completed | Identity Services Lead | Completed |
| 10:55 | Business validation testing commenced | Business System Owner | Completed |
| 11:25 | Data reconciliation completed | Database Administrator / Business User | Completed with observation |
| 11:40 | Recovery declared successful | IT Recovery Lead | Completed |
| 12:05 | Debrief completed and issues logged | Business Continuity Manager | Completed |

#### Results

| Objective | Target | Actual | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Recovery initiation after test start | 15 minutes | 15 minutes | Achieved |
| System technical recovery | [X hours] | [X hours / minutes] | Achieved |
| Business validation completed | [X hours] | [X hours / minutes] | Achieved |
| Data loss within acceptable tolerance | [Defined tolerance] | [Actual result] | Achieved |
| User access confirmed for business users | 100% of selected test users | [Percentage]% | Achieved with observations |
| Recovery evidence captured | Complete recovery log and validation evidence | Partial screenshots and logs retained | Achieved with observations |

#### Strengths

- Recovery procedure was available and broadly accurate.
- Technical teams understood recovery sequence and dependencies.
- Recovery bridge provided effective coordination.
- Business owner participated in acceptance testing and confirmed system usability.
- Recovery met the expected timeframe for the tested scenario.

#### Issues and Gaps

| Issue ID | Issue | Impact | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| EX002-01 | Some validation evidence was not captured at the time of testing. | Audit trail is weaker and may reduce confidence in recovery proof. | Medium |
| EX002-02 | Recovery procedure contains outdated screenshots for the database administration step. | Recovery may be delayed if less experienced staff use the procedure. | Low |
| EX002-03 | User access testing did not include all priority user groups. | Some access issues may remain undetected in a real recovery. | Medium |
| EX002-04 | Dependency on identity service was confirmed verbally but not formally documented in the recovery checklist. | Future tests may overlook a critical dependency. | Medium |

#### Lessons Learned

- Recovery success should be evidenced in real time using a standard evidence checklist.
- Business validation must include agreed priority user groups and key transactions.
- Technical recovery documentation should be maintained in step-by-step form suitable for use under pressure.
- Dependency mapping should be embedded directly into recovery procedures.

---

### EX-003 - Call Tree and Notification Test

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Test date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Test type | Communications test |
| Scenario | Out-of-hours notification to priority response team members following a simulated major disruption. |
| Scope | Emergency contact details, primary and deputy role holders, notification escalation, response tracking, and confirmation of availability. |
| Participants | Crisis management team, incident response leads, departmental continuity leads, deputies, Business Continuity Manager. |
| Objectives | Confirm contact details accuracy, measure response time, validate deputy escalation, test notification record keeping. |
| Overall outcome | Partially achieved |

#### Notification Results

| Metric | Target | Actual | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Total contacts tested | [Number] | [Number] | Completed |
| Successful first-attempt contacts | 95% | [Percentage]% | Partially achieved |
| Responses received within 15 minutes | 90% | [Percentage]% | Partially achieved |
| Responses received within 30 minutes | 100% | [Percentage]% | Partially achieved |
| Incorrect or outdated contact records | 0 | [Number] | Not achieved |
| Deputy escalation successful where primary unavailable | 100% | [Percentage]% | Partially achieved |

#### Results by Group

| Group | Contacts Tested | Successful Contact | Late Response | No Response | Incorrect Details |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Crisis management team | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] |
| Incident response leads | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] |
| Departmental continuity leads | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] |
| Deputies / alternates | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] |
| Specialist support roles | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] | [Number] |

#### Strengths

- The notification process was initiated promptly.
- Most primary role holders responded within the expected timeframe.
- Response tracking template was available and used.
- Participants understood that the test did not require mobilisation, only acknowledgement and availability status.

#### Issues and Gaps

| Issue ID | Issue | Impact | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| EX003-01 | Several contact records were outdated or incomplete. | Emergency notification may fail during an actual disruption. | High |
| EX003-02 | Some deputies were unaware they were listed as alternates. | Escalation may fail when primary role holders are unavailable. | High |
| EX003-03 | Response tracking did not capture all attempted contact methods consistently. | It may be difficult to prove escalation effort or identify failed channels. | Medium |
| EX003-04 | Some staff did not understand expected response format. | Availability status may be unclear during mobilisation. | Low |

#### Lessons Learned

- Contact data must be reviewed more frequently and validated by role owners.
- Deputies should receive explicit appointment, briefing, and testing.
- Notification tests should include multiple channels where appropriate, such as phone, SMS, email, and collaboration tools.
- Standard response wording should be included in notification messages.

---

### EX-004 - Supplier Disruption Scenario Exercise

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Exercise date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Exercise type | Functional exercise |
| Scenario | [Critical Supplier] suffers a prolonged service outage affecting delivery of [critical service / product]. Estimated restoration is unknown for the first 24 hours. |
| Scope | Supplier escalation, contractual review, operational workaround, customer impact assessment, procurement options, communications, and management reporting. |
| Participants | Procurement, Operations, Legal, Business Continuity Manager, Service Owner, Finance, Communications, supplier relationship owner. |
| Objectives | Validate supplier escalation route, assess workaround feasibility, identify contractual and customer impacts, confirm management reporting process. |
| Overall outcome | Achieved |

#### Results

| Objective | Result | Evidence / Observation |
|---|---|---|
| Identify supplier owner and escalation route | Achieved | Supplier owner and escalation path were confirmed from supplier management records. |
| Assess operational impact | Achieved | Impacted services, customers, and internal dependencies were identified. |
| Review contractual obligations | Achieved | Legal and Procurement confirmed service commitments, notice provisions, and evidence requirements. |
| Identify workaround | Achieved with observations | Workaround was feasible for short duration but capacity limits apply after [X] days. |
| Prepare management update | Achieved | Clear summary of impact, options, decisions required, and next steps was produced. |
| Determine customer communication need | Achieved | Communications decision route and draft holding message were confirmed. |

#### Strengths

- Supplier ownership was clearly assigned.
- Procurement and Legal involvement improved quality of decision-making.
- Operational workaround was realistic and understood by process owners.
- Management briefing was concise and decision-focused.
- Exercise demonstrated good collaboration between commercial and operational teams.

#### Issues and Gaps

| Issue ID | Issue | Impact | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| EX004-01 | Workaround capacity limit is not documented in the continuity plan. | Leadership may overestimate how long operations can continue without supplier service. | Medium |
| EX004-02 | Alternative supplier onboarding steps are not fully defined. | Substitution may be delayed during prolonged disruption. | Medium |
| EX004-03 | Supplier continuity evidence is held by Procurement but not linked to business continuity records. | Business continuity assessment may not reflect supplier resilience posture. | Low |

#### Lessons Learned

- Supplier disruption planning should include duration-based decision points.
- Workarounds need documented capacity, quality, cost, and compliance constraints.
- Critical supplier records should be integrated with business continuity dependency mapping.
- Alternative supplier strategies should be pre-assessed where recovery time is business-critical.

---

### EX-005 - Departmental Business Continuity Plan Walkthrough

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Exercise date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Exercise type | Plan walkthrough |
| Scenario | Combined loss of key staff and restricted access to [Department System / Shared Drive / Office Location] during a peak operational period. |
| Scope | Department-level continuity plan, priority activities, role coverage, manual workaround, records access, internal dependencies, and recovery sequencing. |
| Participants | [Department Head], departmental continuity lead, process supervisors, selected staff, IT representative, Business Continuity Manager. |
| Objectives | Confirm plan completeness, validate priority activity recovery steps, identify staff coverage issues, test workaround clarity, confirm dependencies. |
| Overall outcome | Not fully achieved |

#### Results

| Objective | Result | Evidence / Observation |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm priority activities and recovery sequence | Partially achieved | Priority activities were known but not all were reflected in the documented plan. |
| Validate key role coverage | Partially achieved | Deputies exist informally but are not consistently named or trained. |
| Confirm manual workaround steps | Not fully achieved | Workaround relies on experienced staff knowledge and lacks step-by-step instructions. |
| Confirm access to required records | Partially achieved | Some records are available electronically; others are stored locally or require specific permissions. |
| Identify technology dependencies | Achieved with observations | Main system dependencies identified; reporting and shared storage dependencies need clarification. |
| Confirm communication requirements | Achieved | Internal escalation contacts and stakeholder groups were identified. |

#### Strengths

- Departmental leadership understands priority activities and key operational risks.
- Staff demonstrated practical knowledge of how work could continue during disruption.
- Important dependencies were identified through discussion.
- The walkthrough identified improvement needs before a live incident occurs.

#### Issues and Gaps

| Issue ID | Issue | Impact | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| EX005-01 | Business continuity plan does not fully reflect current departmental processes. | Response may be based on outdated or incomplete instructions. | High |
| EX005-02 | Manual workaround lacks step-by-step procedure and approval controls. | Workaround may be inconsistent, inefficient, or create errors during disruption. | High |
| EX005-03 | Deputies are not formally documented for several priority roles. | Recovery may be delayed if key individuals are unavailable. | High |
| EX005-04 | Access permissions for shared records are not validated for deputies. | Deputies may be unable to perform assigned recovery tasks. | Medium |
| EX005-05 | Recovery sequence does not include dependencies on upstream and downstream teams. | Process recovery may be misaligned with dependent activities. | Medium |

#### Lessons Learned

- A departmental plan must be usable by trained deputies, not only by experienced primary staff.
- Manual workarounds should include triggers, steps, forms, approval points, reconciliation, and return-to-normal instructions.
- Access permissions should be tested for role coverage, not only for named individuals.
- Departmental continuity planning should be reviewed after process or system changes.

| F-004 | EX-002 | Recovery evidence capture is incomplete. | Medium | Technology recovery | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| F-005 | EX-002 | Recovery checklist does not fully document identity service dependency. | Medium | Technology dependency | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| F-006 | EX-003 | Emergency contact data contains outdated records. | High | Communications | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| F-007 | EX-003 | Deputy notification and awareness are inconsistent. | High | People resilience | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| F-008 | EX-004 | Supplier workaround capacity limits are not documented. | Medium | Supplier continuity | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| F-009 | EX-004 | Alternative supplier onboarding steps require definition. | Medium | Supplier continuity | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| F-010 | EX-005 | Departmental plan is not fully aligned to current processes. | High | Plan maintenance | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| F-011 | EX-005 | Manual workaround is insufficiently detailed. | High | Process recovery | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |
| F-012 | EX-005 | Deputies and access permissions are not consistently documented or tested. | High | Role coverage | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open |

## Analysis

### Overall Capability Assessment

The exercise and test programme provided meaningful assurance across several key business continuity capabilities. The organisation has established continuity plans, crisis arrangements, recovery procedures, communication channels, and supplier escalation routes. The exercises confirmed that these arrangements are not merely theoretical and can be used by key personnel during simulated disruptions.

However, the results also show that performance depends heavily on experienced individuals. This creates resilience risk where continuity arrangements are not sufficiently documented, delegated, or rehearsed by deputies. The most significant improvement need is to make continuity arrangements repeatable under pressure by ensuring plans are current, procedures are step-based, contact data is accurate, and evidence is captured consistently.

### Themes Identified

| Theme | Analysis | Risk if Not Addressed |
|---|---|---|
| Role coverage and deputies | Deputies are named inconsistently and are not always briefed or tested. | Recovery may fail or be delayed when primary role holders are unavailable. |
| Documentation usability | Some plans describe what should happen but not how to perform required steps. | Staff may rely on informal knowledge, leading to inconsistent response and increased errors. |
| Communications readiness | Notification process exists, but contact accuracy and response standards require improvement. | Delayed mobilisation, unclear availability, and inconsistent stakeholder messaging. |
| Evidence and record keeping | Technical recovery and crisis exercises did not always produce complete records. | Reduced auditability, weaker lessons learned, and difficulty demonstrating due care. |
| Technology dependency mapping | Key dependencies are understood by specialists but not always embedded in recovery documents. | Recovery procedures may fail when dependent services are overlooked. |
| Supplier continuity | Supplier disruption response is reasonably strong, but workaround limits and substitution steps need greater detail. | Extended supplier failure may exceed workaround capacity before alternatives are ready. |
| Departmental plan currency | Some departmental plans lag behind actual processes and system use. | Response instructions may be inaccurate during a disruption. |

### Severity Profile

| Severity | Number of Findings | Summary |
|---|---:|---|
| High | 6 | Contact data, deputy readiness, departmental plan currency, manual workarounds, role coverage, site-based dependencies. |
| Medium | 6 | Decision logging, recovery evidence, technology dependencies, supplier workaround limits, alternative supplier steps, permissions validation. |
| Low | 1 | Supplier continuity record linkage and minor documentation improvements. |

### Performance Against Exercise Objectives

| Exercise / Test | Objectives Achieved | Objectives Partially Achieved | Objectives Not Fully Achieved | Overall Interpretation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| EX-001 Crisis Management Tabletop | 2 | 4 | 0 | Leadership response is sound, but supporting discipline and workplace assumptions require improvement. |
| EX-002 Critical Application Recovery Test | 4 | 2 | 0 | Technical recovery is viable for the tested system, with evidence and dependency documentation improvements needed. |
| EX-003 Call Tree and Notification Test | 1 | 3 | 2 | Notification capability requires corrective action before it can be considered reliable. |
| EX-004 Supplier Disruption Scenario Exercise | 5 | 1 | 0 | Supplier disruption handling is effective for the tested scenario, subject to documenting limits and alternatives. |
| EX-005 Departmental Plan Walkthrough | 2 | 3 | 1 | Departmental plan needs material improvement before reliance in a significant disruption. |

### Business Continuity Risk Implications

The findings have the following implications for organisational resilience:

- **Time-sensitive response risk** - Outdated contact details and unclear deputy arrangements could delay mobilisation during the first critical hour of a disruption.
- **Operational continuity risk** - Manual workarounds and departmental recovery steps may not be sufficiently reliable for sustained disruption.
- **Decision governance risk** - Weak decision logging could impair accountability, legal defensibility, and post-incident review.
- **Technology recovery assurance risk** - Recovery may be technically successful, but incomplete evidence reduces the ability to demonstrate performance consistently.
- **Supplier dependency risk** - Workaround options exist but may be time-limited and not adequately governed for prolonged outage scenarios.
- **People resilience risk** - Continuity arrangements are vulnerable where knowledge is concentrated in primary individuals.

### Positive Assurance Points

The following positive assurance points should be recognised:

- Exercises were conducted using credible disruption scenarios.
- Senior management participated in continuity validation activities.
- Critical technology recovery can be achieved for the tested application within the expected timeframe.
- Supplier disruption response is supported by clear ownership and effective cross-functional coordination.
- Staff demonstrated strong practical understanding of business priorities.
- Lessons learned were identified and translated into action items.
- No evidence was found that the overall continuity framework is ineffective; weaknesses are correctable through focused improvement.

## Recommendations & Actions

### Priority Recommendations

1. **Strengthen emergency contact and notification arrangements**
 - Validate all crisis, incident response, departmental continuity, and deputy contact details.
 - Confirm preferred and alternate contact channels.
 - Define expected response wording and response time requirements.
 - Repeat notification testing after corrective updates.

2. **Formalise deputy roles and readiness**
 - Confirm deputies for all priority response and recovery roles.
 - Brief deputies on responsibilities, joining instructions, authority limits, and required tools.
 - Include deputies in future exercises and access testing.

3. **Improve crisis decision and action logging**
 - Introduce a standard crisis log template.
 - Assign a trained scribe for crisis management meetings.
 - Record decision owner, timestamp, rationale, action, due time, and status.
 - Include log maintenance in future tabletop and live exercises.

4. **Update departmental business continuity plans**
 - Align plans to current processes, systems, dependencies, and priority activities.
 - Add step-by-step workaround procedures.
 - Document manual controls, approval requirements, reconciliation, and return-to-normal steps.
 - Validate plans with staff who do not perform the process daily.

5. **Improve recovery evidence standards**
 - Use a recovery evidence checklist for technical tests.
 - Capture timestamps, screenshots, logs, validation records, user acceptance evidence, and issue notes.
 - Retain evidence in the approved business continuity evidence repository.

6. **Document supplier workaround limits and alternatives**
 - Add duration, volume, cost, quality, compliance, and staffing limits to supplier workaround plans.
 - Define trigger points for executive decisions.
 - Pre-assess alternative supplier onboarding requirements for critical services.

7. **Validate access permissions for recovery roles**
 - Test that deputies can access systems, records, shared folders, collaboration channels, and recovery documentation.
 - Remove reliance on named individuals where role-based access is more appropriate.
 - Document any privileged access requirements and approval routes.

### Corrective Action Plan

| Action ID | Related Finding | Corrective Action | Priority | Owner | Due Date | Success Measure | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| A-001 | F-006 | Complete full validation of emergency contact lists for crisis team, incident leads, continuity leads, deputies, and specialist support roles. | High | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | 100% of records confirmed by role owner; outdated entries corrected. | Open |
| A-002 | F-007, F-012 | Confirm and brief deputies for all critical response and recovery roles. | High | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Deputy register approved; briefing attendance recorded; joining instructions issued. | Open |
| A-003 | F-002 | Implement standard decision and action log template for crisis management and continuity response. | Medium | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Template approved, stored in response pack, and used in next exercise. | Open |
| A-004 | F-003 | Identify and document site-based records, equipment, specialist tools, printing, mail, and secure storage dependencies. | High | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Dependency register updated and reviewed by Facilities and process owners. | Open |
| A-005 | F-004 | Introduce technical recovery evidence checklist for all system recovery tests. | Medium | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Checklist completed for next recovery test with retained evidence. | Open |
| A-006 | F-005 | Update [Critical System] recovery procedure to include identity service, shared storage, monitoring, and reporting dependencies. | Medium | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Recovery procedure updated, reviewed, and approved by system owner. | Open |
| A-007 | F-008 | Add workaround capacity limits and duration-based decision points to supplier disruption plan. | Medium | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Plan includes time, volume, staffing, cost, and quality constraints. | Open |
| A-008 | F-009 | Define alternative supplier onboarding steps for [Critical Supplier / Service]. | Medium | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Onboarding checklist approved by Procurement, Legal, and Operations. | Open |
| A-009 | F-010 | Review and update [Department] business continuity plan to reflect current processes and priority activities. | High | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Updated plan approved by department head and Business Continuity Manager. | Open |
| A-010 | F-011 | Develop step-by-step manual workaround procedure for [Priority Activity]. | High | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Procedure tested by a deputy or alternate staff member with successful completion. | Open |
| A-011 | F-012 | Validate access permissions for deputies across required systems, shared records, and collaboration channels. | High | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | Access test completed with exceptions remediated or formally accepted. | Open |
| A-012 | F-001 | Update crisis team joining instructions and distribute to primary and deputy members. | Medium | [Role / Name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | All crisis team members confirm receipt and understanding. | Open |

### Management Decisions Required

| Decision ID | Decision Required | Recommended Option | Decision Owner | Required By |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| D-001 | Confirm acceptable investment for improving departmental manual workarounds. | Approve targeted process documentation and cross-training for priority activities. | [Executive Sponsor] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| D-002 | Determine whether notification testing should be unannounced in the next cycle. | Conduct one announced retest followed by one unannounced test. | [Crisis Management Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| D-003 | Confirm approach for alternate supplier readiness for [Critical Supplier]. | Complete pre-assessment and maintain standby onboarding pack. | [Procurement Lead] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| D-004 | Confirm central repository for exercise evidence and recovery records. | Use [Approved Repository] with restricted access and retention controls. | [Business Continuity Manager] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

### Follow-Up Testing Plan

| Follow-Up Activity | Purpose | Target Date | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Emergency contact retest | Confirm corrected contact details and deputy escalation. | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Role / Name] |
| Crisis logging mini-exercise | Confirm use of decision and action log template. | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Role / Name] |
| Departmental workaround validation | Test revised manual workaround using deputy staff. | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Role / Name] |
| [Critical System] recovery evidence retest | Confirm recovery evidence checklist and dependency updates. | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Role / Name] |
| Supplier disruption follow-up review | Validate workaround limits and alternative supplier onboarding steps. | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Role / Name] |
| Access permissions test | Confirm deputies can access required systems and records. | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Role / Name] |

### Action Tracking and Closure Criteria

Corrective actions from this report will be tracked by the Business Continuity Manager through the approved improvement tracking process. Actions may be closed only when:

- The agreed corrective action has been completed.
- Evidence of completion has been provided and retained.
- The action owner confirms the outcome is implemented.
- The Business Continuity Manager verifies that the action addresses the finding.
- Where appropriate, the improvement has been retested or validated.
- Any residual risk has been documented and accepted by the appropriate authority.

### Residual Risk Considerations

Where actions cannot be completed by the target date, the action owner must provide:

- Reason for delay.
- Interim risk mitigation.
- Revised completion date.
- Impact on business continuity readiness.
- Escalation requirement, if any.

High-severity findings that remain open beyond their due date must be escalated to [Management Committee / Executive Sponsor] for review.

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution

This report is distributed to the following roles and groups for awareness, action, oversight, and management review:

| Recipient / Group | Purpose of Distribution |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | Oversight and decision-making on resilience priorities. |
| Crisis Management Team | Awareness of exercise results and required improvements. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Ownership of report, action tracking, and programme improvement. |
| Department Heads | Implementation of function-specific corrective actions. |
| IT Leadership | Technology recovery improvement and evidence management. |
| Facilities Management | Workplace continuity and site dependency remediation. |
| HR | People availability, welfare, and contact data support. |
| Procurement / Supplier Management | Supplier continuity and alternative supplier action ownership. |
| Legal / Compliance | Notification, record keeping, and contractual considerations. |
| Communications Team | Stakeholder communication templates and approval routes. |
| Internal Audit / Assurance | Independent review and audit evidence, where applicable. |
| [Management Committee] | Review of overall continuity capability and action status. |

### Confidentiality Classification

This report is classified as **Internal Confidential** because it contains sensitive information about business continuity capabilities, recovery arrangements, operational dependencies, supplier reliance, technical recovery performance, and identified weaknesses.

The report must be handled in accordance with organisational information handling requirements. It must not be shared externally unless approved by [Authorised Role] and subject to appropriate confidentiality protections.

### Handling Requirements

| Requirement | Instruction |
|---|---|
| Storage | Store in [Approved Repository] with access limited to authorised personnel. |
| Access | Grant access based on business need and role responsibility. |
| External sharing | Prohibited unless approved by [Authorised Role]. |
| Redaction | Remove sensitive system, supplier, personnel, and weakness details before wider distribution. |
| Retention | Retain in accordance with the organisation’s records retention schedule for business continuity evidence. |
| Disposal | Dispose of securely using approved methods when retention period expires. |
| Version control | Maintain approved versions and preserve the final issued report as an evidence record. |
| Action evidence | Store action closure evidence with the report or in the linked improvement tracker. |

### Confidentiality Notice

This document is intended only for authorised internal recipients. It contains information that could increase operational, security, supplier, or reputational risk if disclosed inappropriately. Recipients must not copy, forward, publish, or discuss the contents outside the approved distribution group without prior authorisation.

### Approval

|---|---|---|---:|
| Report prepared by | [Name] | [Signature / Electronic Approval] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Reviewed by | [Name] | [Signature / Electronic Approval] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Approved by | [Name] | [Signature / Electronic Approval] | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Audit Programme ID | Enter the unique identifier for the annual or cycle-based internal BCMS audit programme, e.g. BCMS-AUD-PROG-2026. |
| Audit Year/Cycle | Enter the audit programme period covered, e.g. 2026, 2026-H1, or 2026-2027. |
| Audit Number | Enter a unique sequential audit reference within the programme, e.g. IA-BCMS-001. |
| Planned Audit Date | Enter the planned start date of the audit in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Planned Audit Duration | Enter the planned audit duration in hours or days, e.g. 4 hours or 2 days. |
| Audit Type | Select the type of internal audit: Scheduled, Follow-up, Special, Thematic, Process, Site, Remote, or Combined. |
| BCMS Process/Area to be Audited | Enter the BCMS process, activity, or area to be audited, e.g. Business Impact Analysis, Risk Assessment, Exercising and Testing, Incident Response, Management Review. |
| Site/Location | Enter the physical site, remote location, or virtual scope covered by the audit, e.g. London HQ, Data Centre A, Remote, or All Sites. |
| Organisational Unit/Function | Enter the business unit, department, or function responsible for the area being audited. |
| Audit Scope | Define the boundaries of the audit, including processes, teams, locations, systems, documents, and exclusions where applicable. |
| Audit Criteria | Enter the criteria against which the audit will be performed, such as ISO 22301:2019, internal BCMS policy, procedures, legal/regulatory requirements, contractual obligations, and prior corrective actions. |
| ISO 22301:2019 Clause(s) | Enter the applicable ISO 22301:2019 clause references, e.g. 4.1, 6.1, 8.2.2, 8.4, 8.5, 9.1, 9.2, 10.1. |
| Related BCMS Document(s)/Procedure(s) | Enter the controlled document titles or document IDs relevant to the audit, e.g. BIA Procedure, BCMS Policy, Exercise Plan Procedure. |
| Risk/Importance Rating | Enter the relative importance of the audited area based on business continuity risk and criticality using High, Medium, or Low. |
| Reason for Inclusion in Programme | State why this audit is included, considering process importance, BCMS risks, changes affecting the organisation, previous audit results, incidents, exercises, or regulatory needs. |
| Trigger/Event Link | Enter any related event or trigger reference, such as major organisational change, incident, failed exercise, new site, regulatory change, or leave blank if not applicable. |
| Previous Audit Result Considered | Summarise relevant prior audit performance, e.g. No prior audit, Previous minor nonconformities, Repeat finding risk, Satisfactory, or Not applicable. |
| Planned Lead Auditor | Enter the name or role of the assigned lead auditor who is competent and independent of the area being audited. |
| Planned Audit Team | Enter names or roles of additional auditors or technical experts, if any; enter N/A if none. |
| Independence/Objectivity Confirmed | Record whether auditor impartiality has been confirmed using Yes, No, or Pending; auditors must not audit their own work. |
| Auditee Process Owner | Enter the name or role of the manager responsible for the audited process or area. |
| Audit Method | Select the planned method: On-site, Remote, Hybrid, Document Review, Interview, Observation, Sampling, or Combined. |
| Planned Opening Meeting Date/Time | Enter the planned opening meeting date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format, including time zone if relevant. |
| Planned Closing Meeting Date/Time | Enter the planned closing meeting date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format, including time zone if relevant. |
| Evidence Sampling Focus | Describe the planned evidence sample focus, such as records, exercises, BIA outputs, risk assessments, continuity plans, competence records, incident logs, or corrective actions. |
| Audit Status | Select the current status: Planned, Scheduled, In Progress, Completed, Deferred, Cancelled, or Rescheduled. |
| Actual Audit Date | After completion, enter the actual audit start date in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until performed. |
| Audit Report Due Date | Enter the planned due date for issuing the audit report in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Audit Report Issued Date | After reporting, enter the actual issue date of the audit report in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until issued. |
| Report Recipient(s) | Enter the roles, committees, or individuals who will receive the audit results, including relevant management. |
| Follow-up Required | Enter Yes, No, or To be determined, depending on whether corrective action verification or follow-up audit is required. |
| Follow-up Due Date | Enter the planned follow-up or corrective action verification due date in YYYY-MM-DD format; enter N/A if no follow-up is required. |
| Programme Approval Status | Select the programme approval status: Draft, Under Review, Approved, Revised, or Retired. |
| Approved By | Enter the name and role of the person approving the audit programme, typically the BCMS Manager, Head of Risk/Compliance, or top management delegate. |
| Approval Date | Enter the date the audit programme or revision was approved in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Notes/Constraints | Enter any scheduling constraints, resource limitations, access requirements, confidentiality considerations, blackout periods, or dependencies. |

### Maintenance

The BCMS Manager owns this template and updates it at least annually, and whenever significant organisational, process, site, risk, incident, exercise, or audit-result changes affect the BCMS audit programme. Source inputs should be drawn from the BCMS scope, process inventory, risk assessment, BIA register, change records, prior audit reports, corrective action tracker, incident/exercise records, and document control system.

BCM-025.title: Internal BCMS Audit Reports
BCM-025.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [BCMS-AUD-REP-001] | 1.0 | Business Continuity Manager | [DD Month YYYY] | ISO 22301:2019 Business Continuity Management System | Confidential - Internal Use Only |

## Purpose

This report presents the results of the internal audit of the organisation’s Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) for the reporting period stated below. It records the audit scope, approach, evidence reviewed, results, findings, analysis, and agreed actions.

The report is intended to:

- Provide management with an objective assessment of whether the BCMS is implemented, maintained, and operating effectively.
- Identify areas of conformity, nonconformity, weakness, and improvement.
- Confirm whether business continuity arrangements are aligned with organisational objectives, risk exposure, business impact priorities, and stakeholder expectations.
- Support management review, corrective action planning, and continual improvement of the BCMS.
- Provide documented evidence that internal audit activities are being performed at planned intervals and are producing actionable results.

This report is not a certification assessment. It is an internal governance document designed to help the organisation improve resilience and ensure that business continuity arrangements remain suitable, adequate, and effective.

## Reporting Period & Scope

### Reporting Period

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Audit reporting period | [Start Date] to [End Date] |
| Audit fieldwork dates | [Audit Date(s)] |
| Report issue date | [DD Month YYYY] |
| Previous internal BCMS audit report | [Document ID / Date, if applicable] |
| Next planned internal BCMS audit | [Target Month / Year] |

### Audit Scope

The audit covered the design and operating effectiveness of the BCMS across the following areas:

- BCMS governance, leadership oversight, and assigned responsibilities.
- Business continuity policy, objectives, and supporting documentation.
- Business impact analysis and prioritisation of critical activities.
- Risk assessment and business continuity risk treatment.
- Business continuity strategies and solutions.
- Business continuity plans and incident response arrangements.
- Crisis management and communications arrangements.
- Exercise, test, and validation activities.
- Competence, awareness, and training.
- Document control and records management.
- Performance evaluation, monitoring, and management review inputs.
- Corrective action and continual improvement.

### Organisational Areas Included

| Area / Function | Included in Audit | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Executive Management | Yes | Governance, oversight, management review, strategic priorities |
| Business Continuity / Resilience Function | Yes | BCMS coordination, methodology, plans, exercises, reporting |
| Information Technology | Yes | Technology recovery arrangements, dependencies, continuity controls |
| Operations / Service Delivery | Yes | Critical activities, recovery priorities, manual workarounds |
| Facilities / Workplace Services | Yes | Site disruption, access, utilities, alternate working arrangements |
| Human Resources | Yes | Staff availability, welfare, contact information, role competence |
| Communications / Corporate Affairs | Yes | Internal and external communications during disruption |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Yes | Supplier dependencies and third-party continuity assurance |
| Finance | Yes | Critical finance activities and recovery dependencies |
| [Additional Function] | [Yes / No] | [Notes] |

### Locations, Systems, and Processes Reviewed

| Category | Items Reviewed |
|---|---|
| Locations | [Head Office], [Operations Site], [Data Centre / Cloud Environment], [Remote Working Arrangements] |
| Critical processes | [Customer Service], [Order Fulfilment], [Payment Processing], [Regulatory Reporting], [IT Service Operations] |
| Supporting systems | [ERP System], [CRM System], [Email Platform], [Collaboration Platform], [Core Application], [Backup Platform] |
| Third parties | [Managed Service Provider], [Cloud Provider], [Facilities Provider], [Logistics Provider] |
| Records sampled | Business impact analyses, risk assessments, continuity plans, exercise reports, action logs, training records, meeting minutes |

### Scope Exclusions

The following were not included in this audit:

| Exclusion | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Full technical disaster recovery test execution | Covered by a separate IT recovery test scheduled for [Month / Year] |
| Physical security audit | Reviewed only where relevant to continuity arrangements |
| Detailed supplier security assessment | Supplier continuity evidence was reviewed at a summary level |
| [Other Exclusion] | [Rationale] |

### Audit Criteria

The audit assessed whether the BCMS:

- Is supported by clear leadership commitment and assigned accountability.
- Addresses the organisation’s internal and external operating context.
- Considers the needs of relevant interested parties.
- Is supported by documented business continuity policy, objectives, and plans.
- Identifies critical activities, dependencies, and impact tolerances.
- Defines realistic recovery priorities and time-based recovery requirements.
- Uses risk assessment to inform continuity strategies and arrangements.
- Maintains documented plans that are usable during disruption.
- Provides training and awareness appropriate to assigned roles.
- Exercises and validates arrangements at planned intervals.
- Maintains records sufficient to demonstrate operation and improvement.
- Identifies nonconformities, implements corrective actions, and tracks completion.
- Provides management with meaningful performance information for decision-making.

## Executive Summary

The internal audit found that the organisation has established a functioning BCMS with several mature elements, including defined business continuity roles, documented plans for key services, regular exercise activity, and visible ownership by the Business Continuity Manager. The BCMS is generally aligned with the organisation’s critical service priorities and provides a practical basis for responding to disruptive incidents.

However, the audit identified several areas requiring improvement to ensure the BCMS remains complete, current, and consistently applied across the organisation. The most significant findings relate to incomplete linkage between business impact analysis outputs and recovery strategies, inconsistent evidence of plan review, limited assurance over key supplier continuity arrangements, and insufficient tracking of corrective actions from exercises and previous incidents.

No immediate evidence was identified indicating that the organisation is unable to respond to a major disruption. However, unresolved weaknesses could reduce confidence in recovery performance during a prolonged or multi-site incident, particularly where recovery depends on third-party services, key staff availability, or manual workarounds.

### Overall Audit Conclusion

| Rating Area | Assessment |
|---|---|
| BCMS design | Partially effective |
| BCMS implementation | Partially effective |
| BCMS operating effectiveness | Partially effective |
| Leadership and governance | Effective with minor improvement required |
| Business impact analysis and continuity strategy | Improvement required |
| Plans and response arrangements | Generally effective |
| Exercising and validation | Improvement required |
| Corrective action management | Improvement required |
| Overall audit result | Improvement required |

### Summary of Findings

| Finding Type | Count | Summary |
|---|---:|---|
| Major nonconformities | 1 | Corrective actions from exercises and incidents are not consistently tracked to closure. |
| Minor nonconformities | 3 | Gaps in plan review evidence, supplier continuity assurance, and alignment of recovery strategies to business impact analysis outputs. |
| Opportunities for improvement | 5 | Enhancements identified for metrics, training coverage, exercise realism, dependency mapping, and document usability. |
| Positive observations | 4 | Strong executive support, clear BCMS ownership, practical crisis communications arrangements, and active exercise programme. |

### Key Strengths

The audit noted the following areas of good practice:

- The Business Continuity Manager maintains a central BCMS document set and provides coordination across departments.
- Executive management receives regular updates on business continuity risks, exercise outcomes, and priority improvement activity.
- Crisis communications templates exist for staff, customers, suppliers, and media enquiries.
- Business continuity plans for core functions include practical response checklists, escalation contacts, and alternate working arrangements.
- Recent tabletop exercises involved cross-functional participation and realistic disruption scenarios.
- Staff interviewed demonstrated good general awareness of reporting routes during a disruptive event.

### Key Concerns

The audit identified the following concerns requiring management attention:

- Business impact analysis outputs are not consistently translated into tested recovery strategies.
- Some business continuity plans do not show evidence of review within the required review cycle.
- Corrective actions from exercises and incidents are not managed through a single controlled action register.
- Third-party continuity capabilities are not evidenced consistently for services supporting critical activities.
- Recovery assumptions rely on key individuals in several functions without documented alternates or cross-training.

## Methodology

### Audit Approach

The audit was conducted using a risk-based sampling approach. The audit team reviewed documented evidence, interviewed process owners, examined selected records, and tested whether BCMS activities were performed as planned.

The audit focused on whether controls and processes were not only documented, but also understood and used by relevant personnel. Where evidence was incomplete or inconsistent, the audit team sought corroborating information from interviews, action logs, meeting minutes, system records, and exercise reports.

### Audit Activities Performed

| Activity | Description |
|---|---|
| Document review | Reviewed BCMS policy, scope statement, objectives, plans, impact analyses, risk assessments, exercise reports, action logs, and management reporting. |
| Interviews | Conducted interviews with BCMS owner, executive sponsor, function leads, IT representatives, facilities, HR, procurement, and selected plan owners. |
| Evidence sampling | Sampled records for selected critical activities, sites, systems, suppliers, training completion, and plan review cycles. |
| Process walkthroughs | Walked through escalation, plan activation, crisis communications, recovery coordination, and post-incident review processes. |
| Trace testing | Compared business impact analysis outputs to continuity strategies, plans, exercises, and action tracking. |
| Follow-up review | Reviewed status of previously raised BCMS actions and evidence of closure. |

### Personnel Interviewed

| Role | Name / Identifier | Date | Topics Covered |
|---|---|---|---|

| Business Continuity Manager | [Name] | [Date] | BCMS operation, documentation, exercises, corrective actions |

| Procurement / Vendor Manager | [Name] | [Date] | Supplier continuity assurance and contract requirements |
| Communications Lead | [Name] | [Date] | Crisis communications and stakeholder messaging |
| [Other Role] | [Name] | [Date] | [Topics] |

### Evidence Reviewed

|---|---|
| Governance | BCMS policy, governance terms of reference, resilience committee minutes, management reports |
| Planning | BCMS scope, objectives, annual programme plan, audit schedule |
| Business impact analysis | Departmental impact analyses, critical activity register, recovery priority matrix |

| Monitoring and review | KPI reports, action registers, management review packs, corrective action records |
| Incidents | Incident logs, post-incident reviews, communications records, action follow-up evidence |

### Rating Definitions

Findings have been rated using the following definitions:

| Rating | Definition | Expected Management Response |
|---|---|---|
| Major nonconformity | A significant failure that affects the ability of the BCMS to achieve its intended outcome, or a repeated/systemic failure in a key BCMS process. | Immediate corrective action plan required, with senior management oversight. |
| Minor nonconformity | A specific gap or isolated failure that does not by itself indicate overall BCMS failure but requires correction. | Corrective action required within agreed timeframe. |
| Opportunity for improvement | A recommended enhancement that would improve maturity, efficiency, resilience, or evidence quality. | Management to assess and implement where proportionate. |
| Positive observation | Evidence of effective practice or notable strength. | Maintain and share where useful. |

### Limitations

The audit was conducted using sampling techniques and therefore does not provide absolute assurance that all issues have been identified. Conclusions are based on evidence available at the time of audit. Where records were not provided or were incomplete, the audit team assessed the impact based on available corroborating information.

### F-01 - Corrective Actions from Exercises and Incidents Are Not Consistently Tracked to Closure

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | F-01 |
| Finding type | Nonconformity |
| Severity | Major |
| Process area | Corrective action and continual improvement |
| Finding owner | Business Continuity Manager |
| Target completion date | [Date] |

#### Condition

The audit found that actions arising from business continuity exercises, incident reviews, and lessons learned activities are not consistently recorded, assigned, prioritised, tracked, or formally closed. Separate action lists are maintained in exercise reports, meeting minutes, email correspondence, and local department trackers. There is no single authoritative corrective action register for BCMS-related improvements.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- Tabletop exercise report dated [Date].
- Incident review for [Incident Name] dated [Date].
- Business continuity committee minutes from [Month] to [Month].
- Local action trackers maintained by [Department A] and [Department B].
- Interviews with the Business Continuity Manager and selected plan owners.

#### Examples Noted

| Source | Action Identified | Status Observed |
|---|---|---|
| Tabletop exercise [Exercise Name] | Update staff contact escalation list | No closure evidence provided |
| Incident review [Incident Name] | Define alternate approver for critical transaction process | Action recorded in minutes but not in central tracker |
| IT recovery test [Test Name] | Validate recovery sequence for [System Name] | Owner identified, but due date missing |
| Department plan review | Update manual workaround procedure | Department stated action was complete, but no evidence provided |

#### Risk / Impact

Without effective action tracking, known weaknesses may remain unresolved. This increases the likelihood that the same issues will recur during a real disruption and reduces management’s ability to monitor improvement. It also weakens the organisation’s evidence that lessons learned are being converted into measurable BCMS improvements.

#### Root Cause Assessment

The likely root causes are:

- No defined standard for recording and closing BCMS corrective actions.
- Exercise and incident outputs are not consistently transferred to a controlled action register.
- Action closure criteria are not documented.
- Senior management receives summary updates but not complete action ageing or overdue action analysis.

#### Required Correction

Establish a single controlled BCMS corrective action register covering exercises, incidents, audits, management reviews, plan reviews, and risk treatment actions. Define required fields, owners, due dates, priority, evidence requirements, closure approval, and escalation rules for overdue items.

#### Recommended Corrective Action

| Action | Owner | Due Date |
|---|---|---|
| Create a central BCMS corrective action register. | Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |
| Transfer all open actions from recent exercises, incidents, audits, and reviews. | Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |
| Define closure evidence requirements and approval criteria. | Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |
| Report overdue and high-priority actions to management monthly. | Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |
| Review register completeness at each resilience governance meeting. | Executive Sponsor / Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |

---

### F-02 - Recovery Strategies Are Not Consistently Traceable to Business Impact Analysis Outputs

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | F-02 |
| Finding type | Nonconformity |
| Severity | Minor |
| Process area | Business impact analysis and continuity strategy |
| Finding owner | Business Continuity Manager / Function Owners |
| Target completion date | [Date] |

#### Condition

The organisation has completed business impact analyses for major functions; however, the audit found inconsistent evidence that recovery strategies and plans are directly aligned with the recovery priorities, impact tolerances, dependencies, and resource requirements identified in those analyses.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- Business impact analysis records for [Department A], [Department B], and [Department C].
- Departmental business continuity plans.
- Critical activity register.
- Recovery priority matrix.
- Interviews with function plan owners.

#### Examples Noted

| Critical Activity | Business Impact Analysis Output | Plan / Strategy Evidence | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Critical Activity 1] | Recovery required within [Timeframe] | Plan identifies general workaround | No evidence workaround can meet the required timeframe |
| [Critical Activity 2] | Requires [System Name] and [Supplier Name] | Plan lists system but not supplier dependency | Supplier dependency not reflected in recovery approach |
| [Critical Activity 3] | Minimum staffing of [Number] trained personnel | Plan names one primary role holder | No alternate staffing arrangement documented |
| [Critical Activity 4] | Maximum tolerable disruption of [Timeframe] | No scenario test mapped to activity | Strategy not validated through exercise or test |

#### Risk / Impact

If recovery strategies are not traceable to business impact analysis outputs, the organisation may believe it can recover within required timeframes without sufficient evidence. This can result in unrealistic plans, incomplete resource allocation, and recovery failure during actual disruption.

#### Root Cause Assessment

The likely root causes are:

- Business impact analysis outputs and plan content are maintained as separate artefacts.
- Plan review checklists do not require traceability from impact analysis to recovery arrangements.
- Exercise reports do not consistently map scenarios to critical activity recovery requirements.

#### Required Correction

Update the BCMS documentation approach so that each critical activity has a clear trace from business impact analysis outputs to recovery strategy, plan content, resource requirements, dependencies, and validation activities.

#### Recommended Corrective Action

| Action | Owner | Due Date |
|---|---|---|
| Develop a traceability matrix linking critical activities to recovery requirements and strategies. | Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |
| Review all high-priority activities against documented recovery arrangements. | Function Owners | [Date] |
| Update plans where dependencies, staffing, suppliers, or workaround requirements are incomplete. | Function Plan Owners | [Date] |
| Include traceability checks in future plan reviews and exercises. | Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |

---

### F-03 - Business Continuity Plan Review Evidence Is Incomplete for Selected Functions

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | F-03 |
| Finding type | Nonconformity |
| Severity | Minor |
| Process area | Document maintenance and plan review |
| Finding owner | Function Plan Owners |
| Target completion date | [Date] |

#### Condition

Business continuity plans exist for the functions reviewed, but review evidence was incomplete for selected plans. Some plans showed outdated review dates, missing approver names, or changes made without clear version history.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- Business continuity plans for [Department A], [Department B], [Department C], and [Department D].
- Central BCMS document repository.
- Plan owner interview notes.
- Document control log.

#### Examples Noted

| Plan | Issue Identified |
|---|---|
| [Department A] Business Continuity Plan | Last review date older than required review cycle |
| [Department B] Business Continuity Plan | Updated contact list, but version history not amended |
| [Department C] Business Continuity Plan | Approver not recorded |
| [Department D] Business Continuity Plan | Recovery checklist references retired system name |

#### Risk / Impact

Outdated or uncontrolled plans may contain incorrect contacts, invalid escalation paths, retired systems, inaccurate dependencies, or obsolete procedures. During disruption, this can delay response and reduce confidence in plan use.

#### Root Cause Assessment

The likely root causes are:

- Plan owners are not consistently reminded of review deadlines.
- Document control expectations are understood by the BCMS owner but not consistently followed by all departments.
- The central repository does not currently provide automated review alerts.

#### Required Correction

Ensure all business continuity plans are reviewed, updated, approved, version-controlled, and stored in the authorised repository within the required review cycle.

#### Recommended Corrective Action

| Action | Owner | Due Date |
|---|---|---|
| Perform a full plan currency check across all functions. | Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |
| Update plans with missing review, approval, or version information. | Function Plan Owners | [Date] |
| Introduce a quarterly review status report for plan owners. | Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |
| Configure repository alerts or manual reminders for upcoming review dates. | Business Continuity Manager / IT | [Date] |
