### F-04 - Supplier Continuity Assurance Is Incomplete for Critical Third Parties

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | F-04 |
| Finding type | Nonconformity |
| Severity | Minor |
| Process area | Supplier and dependency management |
| Finding owner | Procurement / Vendor Management |
| Target completion date | [Date] |

#### Condition

The organisation has identified several suppliers that support critical activities; however, continuity assurance evidence was incomplete for a sample of critical third parties. Some supplier records did not include current continuity information, recovery commitments, recent test evidence, or escalation contacts.

#### Evidence Reviewed

- Critical supplier list.
- Supplier contracts and service schedules.
- Supplier due diligence questionnaires.
- Vendor management records.
- Interviews with procurement and business owners.

#### Examples Noted

| Supplier | Service Supported | Evidence Gap |
|---|---|---|
| [Supplier A] | [Critical Service] | No current continuity plan summary held |
| [Supplier B] | [System / Platform] | Recovery commitment not clearly documented |
| [Supplier C] | [Operational Service] | No recent exercise or test assurance evidence |
| [Supplier D] | [Facilities / Logistics Service] | Escalation contacts not validated within last review cycle |

#### Risk / Impact

Weak supplier continuity assurance may lead to unmanaged recovery dependencies. If a critical supplier cannot recover within the organisation’s required timeframe, the organisation’s own recovery plans may fail despite internal readiness.

#### Root Cause Assessment

The likely root causes are:

- Supplier continuity requirements are not consistently risk-tiered.
- Procurement records and BCMS dependency records are not fully integrated.
- Supplier review templates do not consistently request continuity and recovery evidence.

#### Required Correction

Define and apply a supplier continuity assurance process for third parties supporting critical activities, including documented recovery expectations, assurance evidence, escalation contacts, and periodic review.

#### Recommended Corrective Action

| Action | Owner | Due Date |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm the list of suppliers supporting critical activities. | Procurement / Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |
| Assign continuity criticality ratings to relevant suppliers. | Procurement / Business Owners | [Date] |
| Request current continuity assurance evidence from high-criticality suppliers. | Procurement | [Date] |
| Record supplier recovery commitments and escalation contacts. | Procurement / Business Owners | [Date] |
| Include supplier continuity status in BCMS management reporting. | Business Continuity Manager | [Date] |

### OFI-01 - BCMS Performance Metrics Could Better Support Decision-Making

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | OFI-01 |
| Finding type | Opportunity for improvement |
| Priority | Medium |
| Process area | Performance monitoring |
| Owner | Business Continuity Manager |

#### Observation

The organisation reports on business continuity activities, including exercise completion and plan status. However, metrics are primarily activity-based and do not fully show effectiveness, risk exposure, action ageing, or recovery confidence.

#### Suggested Improvements

Introduce a balanced BCMS performance dashboard including:

| Metric | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Percentage of critical activities with current business impact analysis | Shows completeness of impact assessment coverage |
| Percentage of critical activities with validated recovery strategy | Shows confidence in recoverability |
| Overdue corrective actions by age and severity | Shows improvement control and management attention needs |
| Plan review completion rate | Shows document currency |
| Exercise completion against annual programme | Shows validation progress |
| Exercise outcomes by pass / partial / fail | Shows effectiveness rather than only completion |
| Critical supplier continuity assurance status | Shows third-party dependency risk |
| Role-specific training completion rate | Shows preparedness of assigned personnel |

### OFI-02 - Exercise Programme Should Include More Severe and Compound Scenarios

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | OFI-02 |
| Finding type | Opportunity for improvement |
| Priority | Medium |
| Process area | Exercising and validation |
| Owner | Business Continuity Manager |

#### Observation

The exercise programme includes tabletop scenarios and selected IT recovery tests. Recent scenarios were useful but generally focused on single-event disruptions. There is an opportunity to strengthen resilience by testing more severe, concurrent, and extended disruptions.

#### Suggested Scenario Enhancements

| Scenario Type | Example |
|---|---|
| Compound disruption | Cyber incident combined with loss of key supplier support |
| Extended outage | Core system unavailable beyond expected recovery time |
| People availability | High absenteeism affecting critical process teams |
| Facilities disruption | Loss of primary site during severe weather event |
| Communications failure | Email and collaboration tools unavailable during crisis |
| Supplier failure | Critical third party unable to meet recovery commitment |
| Data integrity issue | Recovery required where latest backup may be incomplete or unreliable |

---

### OFI-03 - Role-Specific Training Coverage Should Be Improved and Evidenced

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | OFI-03 |
| Finding type | Opportunity for improvement |
| Priority | Medium |
| Process area | Competence and awareness |
| Owner | HR / Business Continuity Manager |

#### Observation

General business continuity awareness is included in staff communications and selected exercises. However, evidence of role-specific training for crisis team members, plan owners, communications leads, and recovery coordinators is inconsistent.

#### Suggested Improvements

- Define role-specific competence requirements for BCMS responsibilities.
- Maintain attendance records for training and briefings.
- Include new plan owners in structured onboarding.
- Provide annual refresher training for crisis management and recovery roles.
- Include deputies and alternates in training to reduce reliance on key individuals.

---

### OFI-04 - Dependency Mapping Should Be Expanded for People, Technology, Facilities, and Suppliers

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | OFI-04 |
| Finding type | Opportunity for improvement |
| Priority | Medium |
| Process area | Dependency management |
| Owner | Business Continuity Manager |

#### Observation

The organisation has identified major systems and suppliers supporting critical activities. Dependency mapping would be improved by documenting minimum people, skills, premises, technology, data, communications, equipment, and supplier dependencies in a consistent format.

#### Suggested Dependency Categories

| Dependency Type | Information to Capture |
|---|---|
| People | Minimum staffing levels, key skills, deputies, cross-training needs |
| Technology | Applications, infrastructure, cloud services, recovery sequence |
| Data | Critical data sets, backup requirements, integrity checks |
| Facilities | Sites, access requirements, utilities, specialist equipment |
| Suppliers | Services provided, recovery commitments, escalation contacts |
| Communications | Internal channels, external channels, alternate methods |
| Regulatory / stakeholder | Time-sensitive obligations and notification routes |

---

### OFI-05 - Continuity Plans Should Be Simplified for Emergency Use

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | OFI-05 |
| Finding type | Opportunity for improvement |
| Priority | Low |
| Process area | Plan usability |
| Owner | Function Plan Owners |

#### Observation

Several continuity plans contain useful information but are lengthy and not always optimised for use during high-pressure disruption. Plan users interviewed stated that shorter checklists and decision aids would improve usability.

#### Suggested Improvements

- Add one-page activation guides for each plan.
- Use clear role-based checklists.
- Include escalation decision trees.
- Place emergency contacts and immediate actions at the front of each plan.
- Remove obsolete background information from response sections.
- Provide offline copies of essential plan content where appropriate.

---

### PO-01 - Executive Support for Business Continuity Is Visible and Active

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | PO-01 |
| Finding type | Positive observation |
| Process area | Leadership and governance |

Executive management demonstrates visible support for business continuity through participation in resilience governance meetings, approval of the business continuity policy, support for exercises, and review of significant resilience risks.

---

### PO-02 - Crisis Communications Materials Are Practical and Accessible

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | PO-02 |
| Finding type | Positive observation |
| Process area | Crisis communications |

The organisation maintains practical crisis communication templates covering staff updates, customer notifications, supplier communications, media holding statements, and executive messaging. The materials are stored in the central repository and are known to the communications team.

---

### PO-03 - Cross-Functional Tabletop Exercises Are Being Performed

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | PO-03 |
| Finding type | Positive observation |
| Process area | Exercising and validation |

Recent exercises included representatives from business operations, IT, facilities, communications, HR, and management. This supports shared understanding of roles and improves cross-functional coordination during disruption.

---

### PO-04 - Central BCMS Document Repository Is Maintained

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Finding reference | PO-04 |
| Finding type | Positive observation |
| Process area | Documented information |

The Business Continuity Manager maintains a central repository for BCMS documents. This provides a strong foundation for document control, evidence retention, plan access, and audit readiness.

## Analysis

### Overall BCMS Maturity

The BCMS is operational and supported by a defined management structure. The organisation has made meaningful progress in documenting plans, identifying critical activities, conducting exercises, and establishing a central coordination role. The BCMS is no longer informal; it has repeatable components and visible management support.

The current maturity level is best described as developing to established. Core elements are in place, but consistency and evidence quality vary by function. The highest improvement priority is to strengthen the connection between analysis, strategy, validation, and corrective action.

### Key Themes Identified

#### 1. Governance Is Stronger Than Execution Evidence

Management support is visible, and BCMS responsibilities are broadly understood. However, execution evidence does not always demonstrate that actions are completed, reviewed, and closed in a controlled manner. This is most evident in corrective action tracking and plan review records.

#### 2. Business Impact Analysis Is Not Fully Driving Recovery Design

Business impact analyses have been performed, but they are not always used as the central reference point for recovery strategy design. Some plans describe general response arrangements but do not clearly prove that required recovery times, minimum resource needs, and dependencies can be met.

#### 3. Supplier Dependencies Require Greater Assurance

Critical services rely on suppliers, managed service providers, cloud platforms, facilities services, and specialist support. The organisation has identified many of these dependencies, but assurance evidence is inconsistent. Supplier continuity capability should be treated as part of the organisation’s own recovery confidence.

#### 4. Exercises Are Useful but Need Stronger Follow-Through

Exercises are being performed and are engaging the right stakeholders. The main weakness is not the absence of exercises, but the inconsistent conversion of exercise outcomes into tracked, verified improvements. Exercises should produce measurable evidence of capability and clear action closure.

#### 5. Documentation Exists but Usability Can Improve

Plans contain relevant information, but emergency users need concise, accessible, action-oriented content. A plan may be complete from a documentation perspective but still difficult to use under pressure. Short-form guides, checklists, and decision tools would strengthen practical response capability.

### Risk Assessment of Findings

| Risk Area | Current Exposure | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Inability to evidence continual improvement | High | Corrective actions are not centrally controlled or consistently closed. |
| Recovery time not achieved | Medium to High | Recovery strategies are not consistently traceable to impact analysis outputs. |
| Outdated plan information | Medium | Some plans lack current review or version evidence. |
| Supplier recovery failure | Medium to High | Critical supplier assurance is incomplete. |
| Confusion during incident response | Medium | Plan usability and role training can be improved. |
| Management decision-making gaps | Medium | Metrics do not yet provide a full view of effectiveness and residual exposure. |

### Repeat or Recurring Issues

The audit identified indicators that some findings may be recurring rather than isolated:

| Issue | Evidence of Recurrence |
|---|---|
| Action tracking inconsistency | Similar action tracking gaps noted in exercises, incident reviews, and meeting minutes |
| Plan review evidence gaps | Multiple functions affected |
| Supplier assurance gaps | More than one critical supplier lacked current continuity evidence |
| Dependency mapping limitations | Observed across several business impact analysis records |

These recurring patterns indicate a need for stronger central standards, clearer ownership, and regular management oversight.

### Positive Trend Analysis

The organisation has shown positive progress in the following areas:

- Business continuity is now discussed at management level rather than handled only as an operational task.
- More functions are participating in continuity planning and exercises.
- The central repository has improved evidence availability.
- Crisis communication content is more mature than in many comparable organisations.
- Business impact analysis coverage has improved across major functions.

### Residual Risk

If the findings in this report are addressed within the agreed timelines, residual BCMS risk is expected to reduce to an acceptable and manageable level. If actions are delayed, residual risk will remain elevated in the following areas:

- Ability to demonstrate that known continuity weaknesses have been corrected.
- Confidence that recovery arrangements meet required timeframes.
- Ability to recover services dependent on critical third parties.
- Plan reliability during a fast-moving incident.
- Evidence readiness for external review or certification activity.

## Recommendations & Actions

### Management Response Summary

Management should prioritise remediation in the following order:

1. Establish a controlled BCMS corrective action register and transfer all open actions into it.
2. Complete a traceability review between critical activities, impact analysis outputs, recovery strategies, and plans.
3. Update and approve all plans with incomplete review evidence.
4. Implement a supplier continuity assurance process for critical third parties.
5. Improve BCMS performance reporting to show effectiveness, overdue risk, and recovery confidence.
6. Expand the exercise programme to include compound and severe disruption scenarios.
7. Strengthen role-specific training and dependency mapping.

### Corrective Action Plan

| Ref | Action | Owner | Priority | Target Date | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-01-A1 | Create and approve a central BCMS corrective action register. | Business Continuity Manager | High | [Date] | Approved register template and published location |
| F-01-A2 | Transfer all open actions from exercises, incidents, audits, reviews, and risk treatments. | Business Continuity Manager | High | [Date] | Populated action register |
| F-01-A3 | Define action closure criteria, evidence requirements, and escalation rules. | Business Continuity Manager | High | [Date] | Approved corrective action guidance |
| F-01-A4 | Report overdue and high-priority actions to management monthly. | Business Continuity Manager | High | [Date] | Monthly management report |
| F-02-A1 | Create traceability matrix for critical activities and recovery strategies. | Business Continuity Manager | High | [Date] | Completed matrix |
| F-02-A2 | Review all high-priority critical activities for strategy alignment. | Function Owners | High | [Date] | Reviewed and signed-off traceability records |
| F-02-A3 | Update plans where recovery arrangements do not match required priorities. | Function Plan Owners | High | [Date] | Updated plans and approval records |
| F-03-A1 | Complete plan currency check for all business continuity plans. | Business Continuity Manager | Medium | [Date] | Plan review status report |
| F-03-A2 | Update plans missing review dates, approvals, or version history. | Function Plan Owners | Medium | [Date] | Updated controlled documents |
| F-03-A3 | Implement quarterly plan review status reporting. | Business Continuity Manager | Medium | [Date] | Quarterly report template and first report |
| F-04-A1 | Confirm list of critical suppliers supporting critical activities. | Procurement / Business Continuity Manager | High | [Date] | Approved critical supplier list |
| F-04-A2 | Obtain continuity assurance evidence for high-criticality suppliers. | Procurement | High | [Date] | Supplier assurance records |
| F-04-A3 | Record supplier recovery commitments and escalation contacts. | Procurement / Business Owners | Medium | [Date] | Updated supplier continuity register |
| OFI-01-A1 | Develop BCMS performance dashboard. | Business Continuity Manager | Medium | [Date] | Dashboard and reporting cadence |
| OFI-02-A1 | Update annual exercise programme to include severe and compound scenarios. | Business Continuity Manager | Medium | [Date] | Revised exercise schedule |
| OFI-03-A1 | Define role-specific BCMS training requirements. | HR / Business Continuity Manager | Medium | [Date] | Training matrix |
| OFI-04-A1 | Expand dependency mapping for critical activities. | Business Continuity Manager | Medium | [Date] | Updated dependency records |
| OFI-05-A1 | Add short-form activation guides to priority plans. | Function Plan Owners | Low | [Date] | Revised plan templates |

### Action Ownership and Escalation

Action owners are responsible for:

- Confirming acceptance of assigned actions within [Number] business days of report issue.
- Providing realistic target completion dates where placeholders are not final.
- Maintaining evidence of completion.
- Updating action status at the agreed reporting frequency.
- Escalating delays, resource constraints, or dependency issues to the Business Continuity Manager.

The Business Continuity Manager is responsible for:

- Maintaining the central action register.
- Monitoring overdue actions.
- Validating closure evidence.
- Reporting status to management.
- Coordinating follow-up audit activity where required.

Senior management is responsible for:

- Ensuring action owners have authority and resources to complete assigned actions.
- Reviewing overdue and high-risk actions.
- Resolving cross-functional barriers.
- Confirming acceptance of residual risk where actions are deferred or not implemented.

### Follow-Up Review Plan

| Follow-Up Activity | Timing | Responsible Party | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Action plan confirmation | Within [Number] business days of report issue | Business Continuity Manager | Confirmed action register |
| First progress review | [Date] | Business Continuity Manager | Status update to management |
| Evidence review for high-priority findings | [Date] | Internal Audit / Business Continuity Manager | Closure evidence assessment |
| Follow-up audit | [Date / Quarter] | Internal Audit | Follow-up audit report |
| Management review update | [Date] | Executive Sponsor | Management decision record |

### Closure Criteria

Findings should only be closed when:

- The agreed action has been completed.
- Evidence has been provided and reviewed.
- The underlying cause has been addressed, not only the immediate symptom.
- The updated process has been communicated to affected personnel.
- Any required documents, plans, registers, or reports have been updated.
- The Business Continuity Manager or designated reviewer confirms closure.
- For major findings, senior management has reviewed and accepted closure.

### Management Acceptance

| Role | Name | Acceptance Status | Date | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | [Name] | [Accepted / Accepted with Conditions / Not Accepted] | [Date] | [Comments] |

| [Function Owner] | [Name] | [Accepted / Accepted with Conditions / Not Accepted] | [Date] | [Comments] |

## Distribution & Confidentiality

### Distribution List

This report is distributed to the following roles for management action, oversight, and evidence retention:

| Recipient / Role | Purpose of Distribution |
|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | Oversight, resource allocation, and management decision-making |
| Business Continuity Manager | Action coordination and BCMS improvement |
| Internal Audit Lead | Audit record retention and follow-up |
| Risk Manager | Integration with organisational risk reporting |
| Information Security Manager | Coordination with technology and cyber resilience risks |
| IT Service Owner | Technology recovery and dependency actions |
| Procurement / Vendor Management Lead | Supplier continuity assurance actions |
| Function Plan Owners | Plan updates and department-level remediation |
| Communications Lead | Crisis communications improvement actions |
| HR Lead | Competence, awareness, and role coverage actions |
| [Other Recipient] | [Purpose] |

### Confidentiality Requirements

This report is classified as Confidential - Internal Use Only. It contains sensitive information about the organisation’s resilience arrangements, operational dependencies, recovery weaknesses, suppliers, systems, and management actions.

Recipients must:

- Use the report only for authorised governance, audit, risk, resilience, and improvement purposes.
- Not distribute the report outside the approved distribution list without permission from the report owner.
- Store the report only in approved repositories or secure document management locations.
- Avoid forwarding the report by unsecured email where secure collaboration options are available.
- Redact sensitive details before sharing extracts with third parties, unless approved by authorised management.
- Protect supplier, system, and incident details from unauthorised disclosure.
- Follow organisational records retention and information handling requirements.

### External Sharing

External sharing may be permitted only where there is a legitimate business need, such as certification audit preparation, customer assurance, regulatory engagement, insurance review, or supplier remediation. Any external version must be approved by the Business Continuity Manager and the Executive Sponsor, and must be reviewed for redaction of sensitive operational details.

### Column Guidance

| Column | What to enter |
|---|---|
| NC ID | Enter a unique sequential identifier for the nonconformity, e.g. NC-YYYY-###. |
| Date Identified | Enter the date the nonconformity was detected in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Identified By | Enter the name and role of the person or team that identified the nonconformity. |
| Source of Nonconformity | Select the source: Internal Audit, External Audit, Exercise/Test, Incident, Management Review, Monitoring/Measurement, Supplier Issue, Customer/Interested Party Feedback, Regulatory/Legal Review, Process Review, Other. |
| Source Reference | Enter the reference to the originating record, such as audit report ID, exercise report ID, incident ID, meeting minutes reference, ticket number, or assessment reference. |
| ISO 22301 Clause / BCMS Requirement | Enter the applicable ISO 22301:2019 clause number and/or internal BCMS requirement that was not met, e.g. 8.4.3, 9.2, 10.2, BCMS-POL-001 section 4. |
| Process / Site / Function Affected | Enter the business continuity process, location, department, service, product, or function affected by the nonconformity. |
| Nonconformity Description | Describe the actual failure to meet a specified requirement in factual terms; state what requirement was not met and what was observed. |
| Evidence / Objective Facts | Record the verifiable evidence supporting the nonconformity, such as sampled records, dates, document names, screenshots, interview notes, test results, or system logs. |
| NC Classification | Select severity: Major, Minor, Observation requiring correction, or Opportunity for Improvement if tracked in this register; classify Major where there is systemic failure, absence of required process, or significant BCMS impact. |
| Immediate Correction / Containment Taken | Describe the immediate action taken to control or correct the nonconformity and deal with consequences, or enter Not Required with justification. |
| Correction / Containment Owner | Enter the named person accountable for completing immediate correction or containment. |
| Correction / Containment Due Date | Enter the target date for completing immediate correction or containment in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Correction / Containment Completion Date | Enter the actual completion date for immediate correction or containment in YYYY-MM-DD format, or leave blank until completed. |
| Consequences / BCMS Impact | Describe actual or potential consequences for the BCMS, continuity capability, interested parties, legal/regulatory obligations, recovery objectives, exercises, incidents, or critical activities. |
| Root Cause Analysis Method | Enter the method used to determine cause, e.g. 5 Whys, Fishbone/Ishikawa, Fault Tree, Process Review, Interview Review, Data Analysis, or Not Applicable with justification. |
| Root Cause | Enter the confirmed underlying cause(s) of the nonconformity; do not restate symptoms or immediate errors only. |
| Similar NCs Exist or Could Occur Elsewhere? | Select Yes, No, or Unknown; based on review of whether similar nonconformities exist or could occur in other processes, sites, suppliers, services, or BCMS activities. |
| Similar NC Review Details | Summarise the review performed to determine whether similar nonconformities exist or could occur elsewhere, including scope checked and any related records found. |
| Corrective Action Required? | Select Yes or No; select Yes where action is needed to eliminate the cause so the nonconformity does not recur or occur elsewhere; if No, provide rationale in the corrective action plan field. |
| Corrective Action Plan | Describe the planned action(s) to eliminate the root cause, including what will change, deliverables, and acceptance criteria; if no action is required, record the justification. |
| Corrective Action Owner | Enter the named person accountable for implementing the corrective action. |
| Corrective Action Due Date | Enter the target date for completing corrective action in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Corrective Action Completion Date | Enter the actual date corrective action was completed in YYYY-MM-DD format, or leave blank until completed. |
| Action Status | Select one status: Open, Containment in Progress, Root Cause Analysis in Progress, Corrective Action in Progress, Awaiting Effectiveness Review, Closed, Overdue, Cancelled. |
| Effectiveness Review Method | Describe how effectiveness will be or was checked, e.g. re-audit, evidence review, exercise retest, KPI trend review, interview, sample testing, incident simulation, or management verification. |
| Effectiveness Review Date | Enter the date the effectiveness review was performed or is scheduled in YYYY-MM-DD format. |
| Effectiveness Review Result | Record the results of the effectiveness review, including evidence reviewed and whether the action eliminated the cause and prevented recurrence or occurrence elsewhere. |
| Effective? | Select Yes, No, Pending, or Not Applicable; select No if the corrective action did not eliminate the cause or evidence is insufficient. |
| Residual Issue / Further Action Required | Record any remaining issue, additional corrective action, new NC ID, or reason no further action is needed. |
| BCMS Risk / Opportunity Update Required? | Select Yes or No; select Yes if the nonconformity or corrective action requires updates to BCMS risks, opportunities, business continuity strategies, priorities, assumptions, or treatment plans. |
| Risk / Opportunity Register Reference | Enter the linked risk or opportunity ID if updated, or Not Applicable if no update is required. |
| BCMS Document / Process Change Required? | Select Yes or No; select Yes if policies, procedures, BIAs, risk assessments, plans, exercise arrangements, competence records, supplier controls, or other BCMS documents/processes must change. |
| Document / Process Change Reference | Enter the document control reference, change request ID, version number, procedure ID, plan ID, or Not Applicable. |
| Management Review Escalation Required? | Select Yes or No; select Yes where the NC, corrective action, trends, resource needs, ineffective action, or significant BCMS impact must be reported to management review. |
| Closure Approved By | Enter the name and role of the person authorised to close the nonconformity after verifying required actions and effectiveness. |
| Closure Date | Enter the date the nonconformity was formally closed in YYYY-MM-DD format; leave blank until closure approval is complete. |
| Retained Evidence Location | Enter the repository path, system link, ticket ID, SharePoint/Teams location, GRC record link, or document reference where supporting documented information is retained. |

### Maintenance

The Business Continuity Manager owns this register and updates it whenever a nonconformity is identified, action status changes, effectiveness is reviewed, or closure is approved, with formal review at least monthly and before management review. Source inputs are internal/external audits, exercises and tests, incidents, monitoring and measurement results, management review actions, supplier/customer feedback, legal or regulatory reviews, and the organisation's GRC/ticketing/document management systems.
