| Chief Information Officer / Technology Lead | Ensures secure operation of IT services, infrastructure, applications, cloud services and technology lifecycle processes; implements technical controls required by this Policy. |
| Risk Management Function | Maintains risk management methodology; supports risk assessment, risk register maintenance, risk acceptance governance and reporting. |
| Legal and Compliance | Advises on legal, regulatory and contractual cybersecurity obligations; supports external notification decisions; reviews supplier and customer security obligations. |
| Data Protection Officer / Privacy Lead | Advises on protection of personal data; supports privacy risk assessments, personal data breach assessment and privacy-by-design requirements. |
| Business Owners | Identify critical business processes and information needs; approve business risk decisions within authority; define recovery requirements; ensure security requirements are embedded in business activities. |
| System Owners | Ensure assigned systems are inventoried, risk assessed, access controlled, patched, backed up, monitored and maintained in line with this Policy. |
| Information Asset Owners | Classify information; approve access; define handling requirements; ensure information is retained and disposed of appropriately. |
| Procurement / Vendor Management | Ensures supplier security due diligence, contractual security requirements, supplier monitoring and exit planning are performed where required. |
| Human Resources | Supports personnel security processes, onboarding, role changes, termination, disciplinary processes and security awareness coordination. |
| Facilities / Physical Security | Manages physical access controls and environmental protections for facilities and areas housing information systems or sensitive information. |
| Incident Response Team | Coordinates security incident triage, containment, investigation, recovery, communication, evidence handling and lessons learned. |
| Employees, Contractors and Users | Follow this Policy and supporting procedures; complete required training; protect credentials and information; report security incidents, weaknesses and policy violations promptly. |
| Internal Audit or Independent Assurance Function | Provides independent assessment of cybersecurity governance, risk management, controls and compliance with this Policy. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory.

The organisation shall monitor compliance through a combination of management oversight, technical controls, operational checks, assurance activities and independent review. Monitoring activities shall be risk-based and proportionate to the criticality of systems, sensitivity of information and potential impact of non-compliance.

Minimum compliance monitoring activities shall include:

| Monitoring Activity | Responsible Role | Minimum Frequency | Evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Management review of cybersecurity risk and performance | Management Body / Executive Leadership | [Quarterly] | Meeting minutes, dashboards, action logs |
| Review of cybersecurity risk register | CISO / Risk Management | [Monthly] | Updated risk register, treatment plans |
| Access review for critical systems and privileged accounts | System Owners / IT Operations | [Quarterly] | Access review records, removal evidence |
| Vulnerability and patch compliance reporting | IT Operations / Security | [Monthly] | Scan reports, patch reports, remediation exceptions |
| Incident management review | CISO / Incident Response Team | After significant incidents and [Quarterly] | Incident records, lessons learned, action plans |
| Supplier security review for critical suppliers | Procurement / Vendor Management / Security | [Annually] or upon material change | Due diligence records, assurance reports |
| Security awareness completion review | HR / Security | [Quarterly] | Training completion reports |
| Backup and recovery testing review | IT Operations / Business Continuity Lead | [Annually] or as defined by criticality | Test reports, recovery evidence |
| Policy compliance assessment | CISO / Compliance / Internal Audit | [Annually] | Assessment reports, findings, remediation plans |

The organisation shall maintain evidence of compliance with this Policy and supporting documents.

Non-compliance shall be assessed based on severity, intent, impact, recurrence and risk. Corrective actions may include remediation plans, additional training, access restriction, supplier escalation, contractual remedies, disciplinary action or legal action where appropriate.

Personnel who knowingly violate this Policy may be subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract, in accordance with applicable law and organisational procedures.

Third parties who violate this Policy or related contractual security requirements may be subject to access suspension, remediation requirements, contract remedies or termination.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a documented business or technical justification and the associated risk is understood, approved and managed.

All exceptions shall:

- Be requested using the approved exception process.
- Identify the specific policy requirement that cannot be met.
- Describe the reason for the exception and affected systems, data, users, services or suppliers.
- Include a risk assessment and compensating controls.
- Have a defined owner and expiry date.
- Be approved by an authorised risk owner and the CISO or delegated security authority.
- Be reviewed before expiry and closed when no longer required.
- Be recorded in the exception register.

Permanent exceptions shall not be permitted unless approved by the management body as a formal risk acceptance and reviewed at planned intervals.

Emergency exceptions may be granted to protect safety, service continuity or security. Emergency exceptions shall be documented retrospectively within [5 business days] and reviewed for continued necessity.

Minimum exception record requirements are:

| Field | Required Content |
|---|---|
| Exception ID | Unique reference number |
| Requestor | Name, role and business unit |
| Policy Requirement | Specific requirement for which exception is requested |
| Business Justification | Reason compliance is not currently achievable |
| Affected Assets or Services | Systems, data, suppliers, processes or users in scope |
| Risk Assessment | Likelihood, impact, exposure and residual risk |
| Compensating Controls | Measures reducing risk during exception period |
| Exception Owner | Accountable person responsible for managing the exception |
| Approval | Authorised approver and approval date |
| Expiry Date | Date by which exception must be remediated or re-approved |
| Review Notes | Status updates and closure evidence |

## Review & Maintenance

This Policy shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant changes occur that may affect cybersecurity governance, risk, obligations or operating environment.

Triggers for review shall include:

- Significant cybersecurity incident or near miss.
- Material change to business operations, services or critical systems.
- Change in legal, regulatory, contractual or sector-specific cybersecurity obligations.
- Major technology change, cloud migration, outsourcing arrangement, acquisition or divestment.
- Significant audit finding, control failure or risk appetite change.
- New or materially changed threat affecting the organisation.
- Management body request.

The Policy Owner shall coordinate review, obtain input from relevant stakeholders and submit material changes for approval by the management body or delegated approving authority.

Supporting policies, standards, procedures and plans shall be reviewed and updated as necessary to remain aligned with this Policy.

The current approved version of this Policy shall be published in [Policy Repository / Intranet Location]. Superseded versions shall be retained in accordance with the organisation’s records retention requirements.

Revision history shall be maintained as follows:

| Version | Date | Description of Change | Author | Approved By |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | [Effective Date] | Initial approved version | [Author Name / Role] | [Approver Name / Role] |

NIS2-009.title: Incident Handling Policy & Procedure
NIS2-009.content:
| Metadata | Details |
|---|---|
| Document ID | [DOC-ID] |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Owner | Head of Information Security |
| Effective Date | [Effective Date] |
| Framework | NIS 2 |
| Classification | Internal |

## Purpose

This procedure defines how the organisation detects, triages, classifies, responds to, escalates, records, and closes cyber security incidents affecting its network and information systems.

It is intended to ensure that incidents are handled in a timely, consistent, evidence-based, and legally defensible manner, with appropriate attention to:

- Continuity of essential or important services.
- Protection of information assets, personal data, and business operations.
- Timely internal escalation and external notification where required.
- Preservation of evidence and accurate incident records.
- Coordination between technical, operational, legal, communications, and executive stakeholders.
- Post-incident learning and improvement.

This procedure supports the organisation’s wider cyber risk management, business continuity, crisis management, data protection, supplier management, and regulatory reporting arrangements.

## Scope

This procedure applies to all suspected and confirmed cyber security incidents involving:

- Corporate networks, cloud services, end-user devices, servers, applications, databases, operational technology, industrial control systems, telecommunications services, and managed service platforms.
- Information processed, stored, or transmitted by the organisation, including customer, employee, supplier, financial, operational, and regulated information.
- Systems and services operated by third parties on behalf of the organisation.
- Security events that may affect the confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, or resilience of network and information systems.
- Incidents that may disrupt the continuity or quality of essential or important services delivered by the organisation.

This procedure applies to:

- Employees, contractors, temporary workers, consultants, and privileged users.
- Internal technology, cyber security, operational, legal, compliance, communications, risk, and business continuity teams.
- Third-party service providers with incident reporting, monitoring, investigation, support, or recovery responsibilities.
- Business owners of affected systems, services, data, or processes.

Examples of incidents within scope include, but are not limited to:

- Malware, ransomware, spyware, or destructive code.
- Unauthorised access, account compromise, privilege escalation, or credential theft.
- Data exfiltration, leakage, alteration, or unauthorised disclosure.
- Denial-of-service attacks or service degradation caused by hostile activity.
- Exploitation of vulnerabilities in internet-facing, internal, or third-party systems.
- Compromise of cloud environments, software-as-a-service platforms, identity providers, or remote access services.
- Security incidents affecting operational technology, production systems, logistics systems, or safety-related environments.
- Supply chain compromise or notification of compromise by a supplier.
- Loss or theft of devices or media containing organisational information.
- Misconfiguration causing exposure of systems or information.
- Suspected insider misuse or unauthorised activity.
- Security incidents affecting service availability, resilience, or customer delivery obligations.

The following are outside the direct scope of this procedure, but may be linked to it:

- Physical security incidents with no cyber or information impact.
- Routine IT service requests and standard operational faults where no security concern exists.
- General complaints, fraud matters, or HR disciplinary cases unless there is a cyber security or information security component.
- Privacy incidents handled under separate data protection procedures, except where a cyber incident may involve personal data.

Where there is uncertainty, the event must be treated as a suspected cyber security incident until assessed by the Security Operations function or Incident Response Lead.

## Prerequisites & Inputs

The following prerequisites must be in place to support effective incident handling.

### Required Capabilities

| Capability | Minimum Requirement |
|---|---|
| Security monitoring | Logs and alerts from critical systems, identity platforms, endpoint protection, firewalls, email security, cloud services, vulnerability tools, and operational technology where applicable. |
| Incident reporting channels | Clearly advertised reporting routes, including [security mailbox], [service desk portal], [hotline], and emergency escalation contact details. |
| Incident response team | Named primary and alternate responders covering technical investigation, containment, communications, legal, compliance, data protection, business continuity, and executive escalation. |
| Asset and service inventory | Current list of critical systems, business services, owners, suppliers, locations, dependencies, and recovery priorities. |
| Contact lists | Up-to-date internal and external contacts, including executives, system owners, suppliers, regulators, law enforcement contacts, cyber insurers, legal counsel, and communications leads. |
| Evidence handling process | Defined approach for collecting, preserving, storing, and transferring evidence without compromising integrity. |
| Communication templates | Pre-approved templates for internal alerts, executive briefings, customer communications, supplier notifications, and authority notifications. |
| Recovery procedures | Documented backup, restoration, rebuild, failover, and service continuity procedures for critical systems. |
| Decision authority | Clear authority for declaring major incidents, invoking crisis management, isolating systems, shutting down services, and approving external notifications. |
| Training and exercises | Regular role-based incident response training and scenario exercises involving technical and business teams. |

### Required Inputs

This procedure may be triggered by any of the following inputs:

- Automated security alert from monitoring tools.
- Report from an employee, customer, supplier, partner, or external party.
- Notification from a managed service provider, cloud provider, software vendor, or threat intelligence source.
- Vulnerability disclosure or evidence of exploitation.
- Service outage or degradation with suspected malicious or unauthorised cause.
- Abnormal behaviour observed by IT operations, fraud, business teams, or operational staff.
- Notification from a competent authority, law enforcement body, sector body, information sharing group, or trusted external source.
- Discovery of exposed, altered, missing, encrypted, or deleted data.
- Detection of suspicious account activity, impossible travel, unusual authentication attempts, or unauthorised privilege changes.
- Evidence of command-and-control traffic, unauthorised remote access, persistence mechanisms, lateral movement, or data staging.

### Minimum Information to Capture at Intake

The person receiving or identifying the event must record the following information where available:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Date and time reported | When the event was reported or identified, including time zone. |
| Reporter details | Name, role, department, contact details, and organisation if external. |
| Detection source | Tool, user report, supplier notification, customer report, authority notice, or other source. |
| Affected systems | Hostnames, applications, cloud services, network segments, devices, suppliers, or business processes. |
| Description | What was observed, including error messages, alerts, suspicious behaviour, or user impact. |
| Initial impact | Known or suspected effect on confidentiality, integrity, availability, service continuity, safety, financial loss, or reputation. |
| Data involved | Types of information potentially affected, including personal data, customer data, credentials, regulated data, or commercially sensitive information. |
| Current status | Ongoing, contained, resolved, unknown, or escalating. |
| Immediate actions taken | Any containment, isolation, reboot, account lockout, or communication already performed. |
| Evidence available | Screenshots, logs, emails, files, alerts, tickets, supplier reports, or forensic images. |
| Urgency indicators | Ransom demand, active exfiltration, public exposure, customer impact, critical service disruption, or media attention. |

## Step-by-Step Procedure (numbered)

1. **Identify and report the suspected incident**

 Any employee, contractor, supplier, or system owner who identifies a suspected cyber security incident must report it immediately through one of the approved channels:

 - [Security mailbox]
 - [Service desk portal]
 - [Emergency incident hotline]
 - Direct contact with the Security Operations team or Incident Response Lead
 - Supplier incident reporting route defined in the relevant contract or service agreement

 The reporter must not attempt unauthorised investigation, delete files, power down systems, reimage devices, contact suspected attackers, or disclose the matter externally unless instructed by the Incident Response Lead.

 If the incident appears urgent or could affect critical services, the reporter must use the emergency channel and clearly state that immediate cyber security escalation is required.

2. **Create an incident record**

 The Service Desk, Security Operations team, or nominated incident coordinator must create an incident record in [incident management system] as soon as practicable.

 The incident record must include:

 - Unique incident reference number.
 - Date and time of detection and reporting.
 - Source of detection.
 - Initial description and affected assets.
 - Initial severity rating.
 - Assigned Incident Response Lead.
 - Current status.
 - Actions taken and decisions made.
 - Links to relevant alerts, tickets, logs, evidence, and communications.

 Security incidents must be tagged so they can be distinguished from ordinary IT incidents and service requests.

3. **Perform initial triage**

 The Security Operations team must review the available information to determine whether the event is:

 - A false positive.
 - A security event requiring monitoring.
 - A suspected cyber security incident requiring investigation.
 - A confirmed cyber security incident requiring response.
 - A major incident requiring escalation to crisis management.

 Initial triage should normally be completed within the target times below.

 | Initial Severity | Example Indicators | Triage Target |
 |---|---|---|
 | Critical | Ransomware, active data exfiltration, compromise of critical systems, widespread outage, operational technology impact, loss of essential service, public exposure of sensitive data | 15 minutes |
 | High | Privileged account compromise, exploitation of internet-facing system, confirmed malware on server, supplier compromise affecting services, significant data exposure risk | 30 minutes |
 | Medium | Malware on single endpoint, suspicious account activity, misconfiguration with limited exposure, attempted exploitation with partial evidence | 4 business hours |
 | Low | Blocked attack, policy violation with limited impact, suspicious email with no execution, unsuccessful login attempts without compromise | 1 business day |

 The triage assessment must consider:

 - Whether the incident is ongoing.
 - Whether the affected service supports essential or important business operations.
 - Whether personal data or sensitive business data may be affected.
 - Whether the incident is spreading or likely to spread.
 - Whether a third party is involved.
 - Whether the incident may trigger regulatory, contractual, customer, insurance, or public communication obligations.
 - Whether there is potential safety, operational, financial, or reputational harm.

4. **Classify the incident**

 The Incident Response Lead must assign or confirm the incident classification using the severity criteria below.

 | Severity | Description | Typical Response Level |
 |---|---|---|
 | Critical | Incident causing or likely to cause severe disruption to critical or regulated services, material operational impact, widespread compromise, significant data loss, active extortion, operational technology impact, or urgent regulatory concern. | Immediate executive escalation, crisis management consideration, continuous response, legal and communications involvement. |
 | High | Confirmed compromise or serious attempted compromise affecting important systems, privileged access, sensitive data, key suppliers, external-facing services, or multiple business units. | Formal incident response team activated, senior management notified, frequent updates. |
 | Medium | Limited compromise or credible threat affecting a small number of systems or users, with contained impact and no current evidence of major service disruption or significant data exposure. | Security-led response with business owner involvement. |
 | Low | Minor security incident, blocked attack, contained user-level issue, or event with minimal impact and limited likelihood of escalation. | Standard security handling and monitoring. |

 The classification must be reviewed throughout the incident. If new information changes the impact, likelihood, scale, or legal significance, the severity must be updated.

5. **Assign incident leadership and response team**

 For every confirmed incident, the Incident Response Lead must be assigned. For High and Critical incidents, the following roles must be appointed:

 - Incident Response Lead.
 - Technical Investigation Lead.
 - Business Impact Lead.
 - Communications Lead.
 - Legal and Compliance Lead.
 - Data Protection Lead where personal data may be involved.
 - Supplier Coordination Lead where third-party services are affected.
 - Executive Sponsor for Critical incidents or where material business impact is possible.

 The Incident Response Lead must establish the incident cadence, communication channels, meeting schedule, and decision log.

6. **Stabilise the situation and prevent avoidable harm**

 The Incident Response Lead must coordinate immediate actions to reduce harm while preserving evidence and avoiding unnecessary service disruption.

 Possible stabilisation actions include:

 - Disabling compromised accounts.
 - Revoking active sessions and tokens.
 - Blocking malicious indicators at email, endpoint, firewall, proxy, identity, or cloud controls.
 - Isolating affected endpoints, servers, containers, accounts, or network segments.
 - Suspending vulnerable services or exposed interfaces.
 - Applying temporary access restrictions.
 - Increasing logging and monitoring.
 - Preserving volatile evidence before shutdown where feasible.
 - Activating business continuity arrangements where services are disrupted.
 - Instructing users not to interact with suspicious systems, emails, links, or files.

 Any action that may materially affect business operations, customer services, safety, legal position, or evidence integrity must be approved by the Incident Response Lead and, where necessary, the Executive Sponsor.

7. **Preserve evidence**

 Evidence must be collected and handled in a manner that supports investigation, disciplinary action, insurance claims, contractual claims, regulatory enquiries, or legal proceedings.

 Evidence may include:

 - Security alerts and event logs.
 - Endpoint telemetry.
 - Firewall, proxy, DNS, VPN, and network logs.
 - Identity and access management logs.
 - Cloud audit logs.
 - Email headers and message content.
 - Malware samples.
 - Screenshots.
 - Disk images or memory captures.
 - Backup integrity records.
 - Supplier incident reports.
 - Communications with attackers, if any.
 - Decision logs and response actions.

 Evidence handling requirements:

 - Store evidence in [secure evidence repository].
 - Restrict access to authorised response personnel only.
 - Record who collected, accessed, transferred, or modified evidence.
 - Preserve timestamps and original file metadata where possible.
 - Use approved forensic tools for imaging or capture where practicable.
 - Do not alter affected systems unnecessarily before evidence is captured.
 - Keep copies of external communications and authority notifications.
 - Maintain a clear chain of custody for material evidence.

8. **Investigate the incident**

 The Technical Investigation Lead must determine, as far as reasonably possible:

 - What happened.
 - When it started.
 - How it was detected.
 - Which systems, accounts, services, networks, suppliers, or data were affected.
 - Whether the attacker still has access.
 - Whether data was accessed, altered, deleted, encrypted, staged, or exfiltrated.
 - What vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, credentials, processes, or third-party failures contributed to the incident.
 - Whether similar activity is present elsewhere in the environment.
 - Whether backups, recovery points, or failover services are intact.
 - Whether the incident may affect customers, service users, partners, or authorities.
 - What containment, eradication, and recovery actions are required.

 Investigation activities may include:

 - Log review and timeline reconstruction.
 - Endpoint and server analysis.
 - Malware analysis.
 - Account and privilege review.
 - Threat hunting across related systems.
 - Network traffic analysis.
 - Cloud configuration and access review.
 - Vulnerability validation.
 - Supplier evidence review.
 - User interviews.
 - Data exposure assessment.

 The investigation must be proportionate to the severity and potential impact of the incident.

9. **Assess business, legal, regulatory, and communications impact**

 The Incident Response Lead must ensure a multidisciplinary impact assessment is completed for Medium, High, and Critical incidents.

 The assessment must consider:

 - Impact on essential or important services.
 - Number and type of users, customers, sites, or business units affected.
 - Duration and geographical spread of disruption.
 - Actual or potential loss of confidentiality, integrity, availability, or authenticity.
 - Safety, operational, environmental, financial, contractual, or reputational consequences.
 - Personal data involvement and possible harm to individuals.
 - Cross-border implications.
 - Dependency on or impact to suppliers, partners, or customers.
 - Whether external notification is required.
 - Whether law enforcement, regulators, customers, insurers, or sector bodies should be informed.
 - Whether public statements or customer support guidance are needed.

 The impact assessment must be documented and updated as facts change.

10. **Escalate where severity or impact requires**

 Escalation must occur without delay where any of the following indicators are present:

 - Disruption or likely disruption to essential or important services.
 - Active ransomware, extortion, destructive malware, or data theft.
 - Confirmed or suspected compromise of privileged accounts.
 - Significant personal data or sensitive business data involvement.
 - Operational technology, safety, production, logistics, healthcare, transport, energy, financial, or telecommunications impact, where relevant to the organisation.
 - Material customer, user, or public impact.
 - Multi-site, multi-country, or supply chain involvement.
 - Media interest or risk of public disclosure.
 - Need to notify authorities, customers, suppliers, cyber insurer, or law enforcement.
 - Need for emergency expenditure, service shutdown, or exceptional operational decision.

 Escalation path:

 | Trigger | Escalate To | Target Time |
 |---|---|---|
 | Critical incident suspected | Incident Response Lead, CISO, CIO, Executive Sponsor | Immediately, no later than 15 minutes |
 | High incident confirmed | Incident Response Lead, CISO, affected business owner | Within 30 minutes |
 | Potential reportable incident | Legal and Compliance Lead, Data Protection Lead, CISO | Immediately after suspicion is identified |
 | Service continuity impact | Business Continuity Lead, Service Owner, Operations Lead | Within 30 minutes |
 | Supplier-caused or supplier-impacting incident | Supplier Coordination Lead, Contract Owner, Vendor Security Manager | Within 1 hour |
 | Public or customer communication risk | Communications Lead, Legal Lead, Executive Sponsor | Before any external statement |
 | Law enforcement or insurer involvement required | Legal Lead, Risk Lead, CISO | As soon as need is identified |

11. **Contain the incident**

 The Technical Investigation Lead must recommend containment actions for approval by the Incident Response Lead.

 Containment objectives are to:

 - Stop unauthorised access.
 - Prevent spread.
 - Protect critical services.
 - Preserve evidence.
 - Minimise operational disruption.
 - Prevent further data loss.
 - Maintain safe operations.

 Containment actions may include:

 - Account disablement, password resets, token revocation, or privilege reduction.
 - Host isolation or quarantine.
 - Network segmentation or blocking.
 - Blocking malicious domains, IP addresses, hashes, files, processes, or sender addresses.
 - Disabling vulnerable services, ports, protocols, APIs, integrations, or remote access.
 - Removing unauthorised access rules, forwarding rules, persistence mechanisms, or rogue accounts.
 - Temporarily suspending supplier connections.
 - Activating compensating controls.
 - Redirecting traffic, failing over services, or invoking manual workarounds.
 - Enforcing emergency access controls.
 - Applying emergency security configuration changes.

 Containment actions must be logged with:

 - Date and time.
 - Person authorising.
 - Person implementing.
 - System or service affected.
 - Reason for action.
 - Expected impact.
 - Actual result.
 - Rollback plan where applicable.

12. **Determine external notification requirements**

 The Legal and Compliance Lead, with input from the Incident Response Lead, Data Protection Lead, Communications Lead, and Executive Sponsor, must determine whether external notification is required.

 Potential external recipients include:

 - Relevant national or sector cyber authority.
 - Data protection authority where personal data is involved.
 - Customers or service users.
 - Business partners or suppliers.
 - Law enforcement.
 - Cyber insurer.
 - Contractual counterparties.
 - Sector information sharing bodies.
 - Public communications channels where appropriate.

 External notification decisions must consider:

 - Whether the incident has caused, or could cause, significant service disruption.
 - Whether the incident has caused, or could cause, material financial, operational, or reputational harm.
 - Whether customers, users, or other organisations may be affected.
 - Whether personal data has been compromised.
 - Whether there are contractual notification obligations.
 - Whether early warning to authorities is required even while facts are still developing.
 - Whether further detailed reporting will be needed after investigation.

 Notifications must be accurate, timely, approved, and based on verified facts where possible. If facts are incomplete, the notification must clearly distinguish known facts from assumptions and state that further updates will follow.

 No employee or supplier may notify an authority, customer, media outlet, or other external party about an incident unless authorised through this procedure.

13. **Prepare and issue required external notifications**

 Where notification is required, the responsible lead must prepare the notification using approved templates and obtain required approvals.

 Minimum content for an initial external notification should include, where known:

 | Information Element | Description |
 |---|---|
 | Organisation details | Legal entity, contact point, sector, and affected service. |
 | Incident summary | Concise description of what happened or is suspected. |
 | Detection date and time | When the incident was detected and when it likely began, if known. |
 | Affected services | Services, systems, locations, customers, or users affected. |
 | Current impact | Operational, service, data, safety, financial, or user impact. |
 | Suspected cause | Known or suspected cause, attack type, vulnerability, or third-party involvement. |
 | Actions taken | Containment, mitigation, investigation, and recovery steps completed or underway. |
 | Risk to others | Whether other organisations, customers, or users may need to act. |
 | Contact details | Named contact or function for follow-up. |
 | Next update | Expected timing or trigger for further information. |

 Required notifications must be tracked in the incident record, including:

 - Recipient.
 - Date and time sent.
 - Approved content.
 - Approver.
 - Delivery method.
 - Acknowledgement received.
 - Follow-up actions.

14. **Eradicate the cause**

 Once containment is in place and sufficient evidence has been preserved, the Technical Investigation Lead must coordinate eradication.

 Eradication may include:

 - Removing malware, unauthorised tools, persistence mechanisms, backdoors, rogue accounts, or unauthorised configuration changes.
 - Patching exploited vulnerabilities.
 - Correcting misconfigurations.
 - Rebuilding compromised systems from trusted images.
 - Rotating passwords, secrets, certificates, keys, and tokens.
 - Hardening affected systems.
 - Removing malicious inbox rules, OAuth grants, API tokens, or federation changes.
 - Reviewing and revoking unnecessary privileges.
 - Validating supplier remediation actions.
 - Closing exposed services or interfaces.
 - Applying detection rules for observed attacker behaviour.

 Eradication must not proceed in a way that destroys necessary evidence unless approved by the Incident Response Lead after consultation with Legal.

15. **Recover systems and services**

 Recovery must restore affected systems and services to a trusted, secure, and operational state.

 Recovery activities may include:

 - Restoring from known-good backups.
 - Rebuilding systems from trusted media.
 - Validating backup integrity before restoration.
 - Reconnecting systems in stages.
 - Re-enabling user access.
 - Verifying security controls and monitoring.
 - Conducting vulnerability scans or configuration reviews.
 - Performing functional business testing.
 - Confirming data integrity and completeness.
 - Applying additional monitoring for recurrence.
 - Communicating service restoration status to stakeholders.

 Before restoring a system to production, the Incident Response Lead must confirm that:

 - The cause has been addressed or an approved compensating control is in place.
 - The system is free from known malicious activity.
 - Required patches or configuration changes have been applied.
 - Credentials, secrets, and tokens have been rotated where necessary.
 - Logging and monitoring are enabled.
 - Business owner testing has been completed where appropriate.
 - Any residual risk has been accepted by an authorised risk owner.

16. **Maintain incident communications**

 The Incident Response Lead must ensure regular, controlled communication throughout the incident.

 Communication channels must be appropriate to the incident. If normal communication platforms may be compromised, alternate channels such as [out-of-band communication platform] or [emergency conference bridge] must be used.

 Communication principles:

 - Use factual, concise, need-to-know communication.
 - Avoid speculation.
 - Mark communications with appropriate confidentiality.
 - Do not share sensitive technical details broadly.
 - Do not use compromised systems for incident coordination.
 - Preserve copies of material communications.
 - Route media and customer communications through the Communications Lead.
 - Route legal, regulatory, and law enforcement communications through Legal and Compliance.

 Recommended update cadence:

 | Incident Severity | Internal Response Updates | Executive Updates | Business/User Updates |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Critical | Every 30-60 minutes or as agreed | At least every 2 hours during active response | As approved, based on impact |
 | High | Every 2-4 hours during active response | At least daily, or more often if impact changes | As needed |
 | Medium | Daily while active | As needed | As needed |
 | Low | At closure or by exception | Not normally required | Not normally required |

17. **Manage supplier involvement**

 If a supplier is involved or affected, the Supplier Coordination Lead must:

 - Notify the supplier through the approved incident contact route.
 - Request immediate confirmation of impact, containment actions, and expected service implications.
 - Request relevant logs, evidence, indicators of compromise, timelines, and remediation plans.
 - Confirm whether other customers or services are affected, where the supplier can disclose this.
 - Review contractual notification and cooperation obligations.
 - Coordinate technical response with the supplier’s incident team.
 - Ensure supplier communications are captured in the incident record.
 - Escalate supplier non-responsiveness or inadequate remediation to the Contract Owner and Executive Sponsor.

 The organisation must not rely solely on supplier statements where independent validation is feasible and proportionate.

18. **Monitor for recurrence or spread**

 Following containment and eradication, enhanced monitoring must be implemented for a defined period based on severity.

 | Severity | Minimum Enhanced Monitoring Period |
 |---|---|
 | Critical | 30 days or as approved by the Incident Response Lead |
 | High | 14 days |
 | Medium | 7 days |
 | Low | As determined by Security Operations |

 Monitoring may include:

 - Repeated searches for indicators of compromise.
 - Review of authentication anomalies.
 - Endpoint detection sweeps.
 - Network traffic monitoring.
 - Cloud audit log review.
 - Privileged access monitoring.
 - Email rule and forwarding checks.
 - Vulnerability rescans.
 - Supplier status updates.

 Recurrence must be treated as a continuation of the existing incident unless the Incident Response Lead determines it is a separate incident.

19. **Close the incident**

 The Incident Response Lead may close the incident only when all closure criteria are met.

 Closure criteria:

 - Incident has been contained, eradicated, and recovered, or residual risk has been formally accepted.
 - No evidence of ongoing unauthorised access remains.
 - Affected systems and services have been restored or decommissioned.
 - Required notifications have been completed or formally deemed not required.
 - Evidence and records have been preserved.
 - Root cause or most likely cause has been documented.
 - Corrective actions have been recorded and assigned.
 - Business owner has confirmed service restoration where applicable.
 - Legal, compliance, and data protection actions are complete or tracked.
 - Enhanced monitoring period has been completed or transferred to business-as-usual monitoring.
 - Post-incident review has been scheduled for Medium, High, and Critical incidents.

 Closure must be documented in [incident management system] and approved by the Incident Response Lead. High and Critical incident closures must also be approved by the CISO or delegated senior security authority.

20. **Conduct post-incident review**

 A post-incident review must be completed for all Medium, High, and Critical incidents, and for Low incidents where there is learning value.

 Target completion times:

 | Severity | Post-Incident Review Target |
 |---|---|
 | Critical | Within 10 business days of service stabilisation |
 | High | Within 15 business days of closure |
 | Medium | Within 20 business days of closure |
 | Low | At discretion of Security Operations |

 The review must cover:

 - Incident timeline.
 - Detection source and effectiveness.
 - Root cause or most likely cause.
 - Scope and impact.
 - Response decisions and effectiveness.
 - Communication effectiveness.
 - Evidence handling quality.
 - Supplier performance, where applicable.
 - Control failures or gaps.
 - What worked well.
 - What did not work well.
 - Required corrective and preventive actions.
 - Training, process, technology, or governance improvements.
 - Whether the incident classification and escalation were appropriate.
 - Whether reporting obligations were met in a timely and accurate manner.

 Corrective actions must be assigned an owner, due date, and priority, and tracked to completion.

21. **Update risk, control, and resilience records**

 Following closure and review, the relevant owners must update applicable records, including:

 - Risk register.
 - Asset and service inventory.
 - Business impact analysis.
 - Supplier risk assessments.
 - Vulnerability management records.
 - Security monitoring use cases.
 - Incident response playbooks.
 - Business continuity and disaster recovery plans.
 - Security awareness materials.
 - Technical standards and hardening baselines.
 - Lessons learned register.
 - Audit evidence repository.

 Where an incident reveals a material risk, control weakness, or resilience gap, the risk must be assessed and reported through the organisation’s risk governance process.

## Roles & RACI

### Role Descriptions

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board or Governing Body | Provides oversight of cyber resilience, receives reporting on significant incidents, ensures adequate resources and accountability. |
| Executive Sponsor | Makes senior business decisions during major incidents, approves material operational actions, supports external escalation and resource allocation. |
| CISO / Head of Information Security | Owns the incident handling capability, approves major response decisions, escalates material risks, ensures lessons are implemented. |
| Incident Response Lead | Directs the incident response, coordinates teams, maintains incident cadence, approves containment and recovery actions, ensures records are complete. |
| Security Operations Team | Performs monitoring, triage, investigation support, containment actions, threat hunting, and security tooling updates. |
| Technical Investigation Lead | Leads technical analysis, determines cause and scope, recommends containment, eradication, and recovery actions. |
| IT Operations Lead | Implements infrastructure, network, endpoint, identity, backup, and recovery actions. |
| Business Service Owner | Assesses business impact, confirms service criticality, supports recovery prioritisation, validates service restoration. |
| Business Continuity Lead | Coordinates continuity arrangements, manual workarounds, service recovery priorities, and operational resilience actions. |
| Legal and Compliance Lead | Assesses legal and regulatory implications, advises on notifications, evidence preservation, privilege, contractual duties, and law enforcement engagement. |
| Data Protection Lead | Assesses personal data involvement, harm to individuals, data protection notifications, and data subject communications. |
| Communications Lead | Prepares and controls internal, customer, media, and public communications in coordination with Legal and the Executive Sponsor. |
| Supplier Coordination Lead | Manages supplier engagement, evidence requests, contractual escalation, and supplier remediation tracking. |
| HR Lead | Supports incidents involving employees, insider activity, disciplinary matters, and workforce communications. |
| Risk Manager | Ensures material risks, issues, and treatment actions are reflected in risk governance records. |
| Service Desk | Receives reports, creates tickets, escalates suspected incidents, and supports user communications where authorised. |
| All Users | Promptly report suspected incidents and follow instructions issued by the incident response team. |

### RACI Matrix

| Activity | Board / Governing Body | Executive Sponsor | CISO | Incident Response Lead | Security Operations | IT Operations | Business Owner | Legal / Compliance | Data Protection | Communications | Supplier Lead |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Report suspected incident | I | I | I | C | R | C | R | C | C | I | C |
| Create incident record | I | I | A | R | R | C | C | I | I | I | I |
| Initial triage | I | I | A | R | R | C | C | C | C | I | C |
| Classify severity | I | C | A | R | C | C | C | C | C | I | C |
| Activate response team | I | C | A | R | C | C | C | C | C | C | C |
| Containment decision | I | C | A | R | C | R | C | C | C | I | C |
| Technical investigation | I | I | A | C | R | R | C | C | C | I | C |
| Business impact assessment | I | C | C | A | C | C | R | C | C | C | C |
| External notification decision | I | A | C | C | C | C | C | R | R | C | C |
| External communications | I | A | C | C | I | I | C | C | C | R | C |
| Supplier coordination | I | C | C | C | C | C | C | C | C | I | R |
| Service recovery | I | C | C | A | C | R | R | C | C | I | C |
| Incident closure | I | C | A | R | C | C | C | C | C | I | C |
| Post-incident review | I | C | A | R | R | R | C | C | C | C | C |
| Corrective action tracking | I | C | A | R | R | R | R | C | C | I | C |
| Significant incident oversight | A | R | R | C | I | I | I | C | C | C | I |

RACI key:

- **R** - Responsible for performing the activity.
- **A** - Accountable for the outcome and final decision.
- **C** - Consulted before or during the activity.
- **I** - Informed of progress or outcome.

## Records & Outputs

The following records must be created and retained for incidents handled under this procedure.

| Record / Output | Required For | Owner | Storage Location | Minimum Retention |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Incident record | All suspected and confirmed incidents | Incident Response Lead | [incident management system] | [retention period] |
| Initial triage notes | All suspected incidents | Security Operations | [incident management system] | [retention period] |
| Severity classification | All confirmed incidents | Incident Response Lead | [incident management system] | [retention period] |
| Decision log | Medium, High, Critical incidents | Incident Response Lead | [secure incident workspace] | [retention period] |
| Action log | All confirmed incidents | Incident Response Lead | [incident management system] | [retention period] |
| Evidence inventory | Medium, High, Critical incidents and any incident requiring evidence preservation | Technical Investigation Lead | [secure evidence repository] | [retention period] |
| Chain of custody record | Incidents involving forensic evidence | Technical Investigation Lead | [secure evidence repository] | [retention period] |
| Incident timeline | Medium, High, Critical incidents | Technical Investigation Lead | [incident management system] | [retention period] |
| Business impact assessment | Medium, High, Critical incidents | Business Service Owner | [incident management system] | [retention period] |
| Legal and notification assessment | Incidents with potential external notification obligations | Legal and Compliance Lead | [legal repository] | [retention period] |
| External notifications | Reportable or externally communicated incidents | Legal and Compliance Lead | [legal repository] | [retention period] |
| Customer or public communications | Incidents involving external communications | Communications Lead | [communications repository] | [retention period] |
| Supplier correspondence | Supplier-related incidents | Supplier Coordination Lead | [supplier management system] | [retention period] |
| Recovery validation record | Incidents requiring restoration or rebuild | IT Operations Lead | [change management system] | [retention period] |
| Post-incident review report | Medium, High, Critical incidents | Incident Response Lead | [GRC system] | [retention period] |
| Corrective action plan | Incidents with lessons or control gaps | Risk Manager / Action Owners | [GRC system] | Until completion plus [retention period] |
| Management summary | High and Critical incidents | CISO | [GRC system] | [retention period] |

### Incident Record Minimum Fields

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Incident reference | Unique identifier. |
| Title | Short description of incident. |
| Status | New, triage, active, contained, recovery, monitoring, closed. |
| Severity | Low, Medium, High, Critical. |
| Detection date and time | Time incident was detected. |
| Reporting date and time | Time incident was reported internally. |
| Incident start time | Known or estimated start time, if available. |
| Incident end time | Time incident was resolved or closed, if applicable. |
| Detection source | Tool, user, supplier, customer, authority, or other. |
| Incident type | Malware, ransomware, unauthorised access, data exposure, denial of service, supplier compromise, vulnerability exploitation, insider activity, or other. |
| Affected assets | Systems, applications, services, networks, devices, accounts, data stores, suppliers. |
| Service impact | Description of service disruption or degradation. |
| Data impact | Types and volumes of data affected or suspected. |
| Business impact | Operational, financial, customer, contractual, safety, reputational, or legal impact. |
| Root cause | Confirmed or most likely cause. |
| Response actions | Summary of containment, eradication, and recovery actions. |
| Notifications | Internal and external notifications completed or considered. |
| Evidence references | Links to evidence repository records. |
| Decisions | Key decisions and approvals. |
| Residual risk | Any remaining risk and acceptance decision. |
| Lessons learned | Summary of improvements identified. |
| Closure approval | Name, role, date, and approval record. |

### Incident Metrics

The CISO must ensure the following metrics are produced for management reporting:

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|
| Number of security incidents | Count by severity and type. |
| Mean time to detect | Average time from estimated start to detection. |
| Mean time to triage | Average time from report to triage completion. |
| Mean time to contain | Average time from confirmation to containment. |
| Mean time to recover | Average time from containment to service restoration. |
| Number of reportable incidents | Count of incidents requiring external authority notification. |
| Notification timeliness | Whether required notification timelines were met. |
| Recurring incident themes | Repeated root causes, affected systems, or control weaknesses. |
| Supplier-related incidents | Number and severity of incidents involving third parties. |
| Corrective action status | Open, overdue, and completed actions from incident reviews. |
| Exercise and training outcomes | Lessons from simulations and readiness testing. |

## Exceptions & Escalation

### Exceptions

Exceptions to this procedure are permitted only where:

- Following the procedure would create an immediate safety risk.
- Urgent containment is necessary to prevent significant harm and prior approval cannot be obtained.
- Legal counsel directs a different approach to preserve privilege, evidence, or legal position.
- A competent authority, law enforcement body, or court order requires a different approach.
- A supplier-managed incident requires temporary use of the supplier’s process, provided organisational records and oversight are maintained.
- Technical constraints make a required action impossible and an approved alternative is used.

All exceptions must be documented in the incident record, including:

- Nature of the exception.
- Reason for the exception.
- Person authorising or invoking the exception.
- Time and date.
- Risks created by the exception.
- Compensating actions taken.
- Whether further approval is required.

For High and Critical incidents, exceptions must be reviewed by the Incident Response Lead and CISO as soon as practicable.

### Escalation

Escalation must not be delayed because all facts are not yet known. Where there is credible suspicion of significant impact, the incident must be escalated on a precautionary basis.

The following escalation thresholds apply.

| Escalation Level | Criteria | Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| Security escalation | Any suspected cyber security incident. | Notify Security Operations and create incident record. |
| Incident leadership escalation | Confirmed Medium or higher incident. | Assign Incident Response Lead and response team. |
| Senior management escalation | High incident or material business concern. | Notify CISO, affected business owner, and relevant senior leaders. |
| Executive escalation | Critical incident, major service disruption, significant data impact, public exposure, extortion, or potential authority notification. | Notify Executive Sponsor and consider crisis management activation. |
| Governing body escalation | Incident with material strategic, financial, legal, operational, safety, or reputational impact. | Provide formal briefing through established governance route. |
| External escalation | Incident requiring authority, customer, supplier, insurer, law enforcement, or public notification. | Legal and Compliance Lead coordinates approved notification. |

### Crisis Management Activation

The CISO or Executive Sponsor must consider activating the crisis management process where:

- There is significant disruption to critical services.
- The incident affects multiple business units, countries, sites, or critical suppliers.
- There is active ransomware, extortion, or destructive activity.
- The organisation’s ability to communicate, operate, or recover is materially impaired.
- Media, customer, regulator, or public interest is likely.
- Safety, public welfare, or essential service delivery may be affected.
- Strategic decisions are required beyond the authority of the incident response team.

Where crisis management is activated, this procedure remains the technical and cyber response process, while the crisis management team manages enterprise-level decisions, stakeholder coordination, and strategic communications.

## Review

This procedure must be reviewed at least annually and after any of the following events:

- A Critical or High incident.
- A post-incident review identifies procedural weakness.
- A material change to the organisation’s services, systems, suppliers, operating model, or threat environment.
- A significant change in legal, regulatory, contractual, or sector expectations.
- Results from an incident response exercise indicate improvement is required.
- Audit, assurance, or management review identifies gaps.
- Changes to contact lists, escalation routes, monitoring capabilities, or notification arrangements.

The review must assess whether:

- Roles, responsibilities, and escalation paths remain accurate.
- Incident severity criteria remain appropriate.
- Reporting channels are accessible and understood.
- Detection, triage, containment, eradication, and recovery steps remain effective.
- Notification decision processes remain timely and reliable.
- Supplier incident coordination remains effective.
- Evidence handling remains legally and operationally sound.
- Records and metrics support auditability and management oversight.
- Lessons learned have been implemented.
- Training and exercise arrangements are adequate.

The document owner is responsible for coordinating the review, obtaining input from relevant stakeholders, updating the procedure, securing approval, and communicating material changes.

| Review Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Review frequency | At least annually and after significant incidents or material changes. |
| Review owner | Head of Information Security. |
| Review participants | Security Operations, IT Operations, Legal, Compliance, Data Protection, Business Continuity, Communications, Risk, Supplier Management, and representative business owners. |
| Approval authority | CISO or delegated senior security authority. |
| Evidence of review | Version history, review notes, approval record, and communication record retained in [document repository]. |

NIS2-010.title: Business Continuity & Crisis Management Policy
NIS2-010.content:
| Document ID | Version | Owner | Effective Date | Framework | Classification |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| [BC-CM-POL-001] | 1.0 | [Business Continuity Manager / CISO] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | NIS 2 | Internal |

## Purpose

This Policy establishes mandatory requirements for business continuity, backup management, disaster recovery and crisis management across [Organisation Name]. Its purpose is to ensure that essential services, critical business processes, information systems and supporting assets can withstand, respond to and recover from disruptive events in a controlled, timely and secure manner.

The Policy is intended to ensure that [Organisation Name]:

- Maintains continuity of essential and important services during disruption.
- Protects the availability, integrity and recoverability of information and systems.
- Establishes clear crisis decision-making, escalation and communication arrangements.
- Maintains effective backups and recovery capabilities proportionate to business impact.
- Tests, reviews and improves continuity, disaster recovery and crisis management arrangements.
- Meets applicable legal, regulatory, contractual and customer obligations relating to operational resilience and cybersecurity.

## Scope

This Policy applies to:

- All employees, officers, contractors, consultants, temporary staff and third parties acting on behalf of [Organisation Name].
- All business functions, operational sites, technology environments, networks, applications, data stores, cloud services, industrial or operational technology environments, and managed services used to deliver [Organisation Name] services.
- All information assets and systems that support essential, important or regulated services.
- All phases of continuity and crisis management, including preparedness, response, recovery, communications, restoration and post-incident improvement.
- All backup, restoration, disaster recovery, failover, high availability and data replication capabilities owned, operated or relied upon by [Organisation Name].

This Policy covers disruptive events including, but not limited to:

- Cyber incidents, ransomware, data corruption and destructive malware.
- Major technology outages or loss of critical applications, networks or infrastructure.
- Cloud service, telecommunications or managed service provider failures.
- Loss of workplace, data centre, operational site or other critical facility.
- Supply chain disruption affecting essential services.
- Power, environmental, health, safety, civil emergency or physical security events.
- Workforce unavailability or loss of key personnel.
- Any event requiring activation of crisis management, business continuity or disaster recovery arrangements.

## Policy Statements

1. **Business continuity governance shall be established and maintained.** 
 [Organisation Name] shall maintain a documented business continuity and crisis management capability with approved plans, defined ownership, sufficient resources and senior management oversight.

2. **Critical services and processes shall be identified.** 
 Business functions shall identify and document services, processes, systems, data, facilities, suppliers and personnel required to deliver essential and important services.

3. **Business impact analysis shall be performed and kept current.** 
 Each business function shall complete a business impact analysis to determine operational impact, recovery priorities, maximum tolerable disruption, minimum service levels and dependencies.

4. **Risk assessments shall inform continuity and recovery arrangements.** 
 Continuity, backup, disaster recovery and crisis management plans shall be based on credible disruption scenarios, cyber threat conditions, dependency risk and business impact.

5. **Recovery objectives shall be defined and approved.** 
 Recovery Time Objectives and Recovery Point Objectives shall be defined for critical processes, systems and data, approved by accountable business owners and reviewed at least annually or following material change.

6. **Recovery objectives shall be proportionate to business impact.** 
 Systems and services with higher operational, safety, legal, financial, customer or societal impact shall receive stronger resilience, backup, failover and recovery capabilities.

7. **Business continuity plans shall be documented.** 
 Each critical business function shall maintain a business continuity plan that defines activation criteria, roles, dependencies, manual workarounds, alternate operating arrangements, communication requirements and recovery steps.

8. **Disaster recovery plans shall be documented for critical technology services.** 
 Technology owners shall maintain disaster recovery plans for critical applications, infrastructure, networks, cloud services and data platforms, including technical recovery steps, dependencies, access requirements and validation activities.

9. **Crisis management arrangements shall be established.** 
 [Organisation Name] shall maintain a Crisis Management Team with authority to direct strategic response, make urgent decisions, allocate resources, approve communications and coordinate recovery during major disruption.

10. **Crisis activation criteria shall be defined.** 
 The Crisis Management Team shall be activated when an event causes or is likely to cause significant service disruption, legal or regulatory exposure, customer harm, public concern, safety impact, financial loss or reputational damage.

11. **Incident, continuity and crisis processes shall be aligned.** 
 Cyber incident response, IT service continuity, disaster recovery, emergency response, business continuity and crisis management processes shall be coordinated to avoid duplication, conflicting decisions or delayed escalation.

12. **Backups shall be performed for critical systems and data.** 
 Backup arrangements shall be implemented for systems, configurations, data, logs and documentation required to restore critical services and meet approved recovery objectives.

13. **Backup frequency shall reflect recovery requirements.** 
 Backup schedules shall be based on the approved Recovery Point Objective, data volatility, business impact and legal or contractual retention requirements.

14. **Backups shall be protected against compromise.** 
 Backup repositories shall be secured using appropriate access controls, encryption, segregation, immutability or offline storage where required to protect against ransomware, unauthorised modification, deletion or corruption.

15. **Backup access shall be restricted and monitored.** 
 Administrative access to backup platforms, recovery repositories and restoration functions shall be limited to authorised personnel, protected by strong authentication and monitored for suspicious activity.

16. **Backup integrity shall be verified.** 
 Backup jobs shall be monitored for completion and failure, and backup integrity shall be verified through automated checks and periodic restoration testing.

17. **Restoration capability shall be tested.** 
 [Organisation Name] shall test restoration of critical systems, data and configurations at planned intervals to confirm that backups are usable and recovery objectives can be met.

18. **Backup retention shall be defined and enforced.** 
 Backup retention periods shall be documented, approved and configured to meet operational, legal, regulatory, contractual and forensic requirements.

19. **Backup data shall be securely disposed of when no longer required.** 
 Expired backup media and stored backup data shall be disposed of securely in accordance with information classification, data protection and records retention requirements.

20. **Disaster recovery environments shall be protected.** 
 Recovery sites, standby environments, cloud recovery platforms and replicated systems shall be secured to a standard appropriate to production environments.

21. **Recovery dependencies shall be documented.** 
 Disaster recovery plans shall identify required personnel, credentials, infrastructure, network connectivity, third-party services, licences, certificates, secrets, hardware, cloud subscriptions and restoration media.

22. **Manual workarounds shall be established where feasible.** 
 Business functions shall define and maintain manual or alternate operating procedures for critical activities where technology recovery may not be immediate.

23. **Minimum operating capability shall be defined.** 
 For each critical service, business owners shall define the minimum resources, systems, data, staff and supplier support required to operate during disruption.

24. **Third-party continuity requirements shall be managed.** 
 Contracts and service arrangements for critical suppliers shall include appropriate requirements for continuity, backup, recovery, incident notification, testing, evidence provision and service restoration.

25. **Supplier recovery capabilities shall be assessed.** 
 [Organisation Name] shall assess the continuity and recovery capabilities of critical suppliers before engagement and periodically during the relationship.

26. **Continuity arrangements shall include cloud and managed services.** 
 Cloud, software-as-a-service, managed service and outsourced technology arrangements shall have documented recovery responsibilities, service restoration expectations and data recovery options.

27. **Emergency communications shall be maintained.** 
 [Organisation Name] shall maintain reliable communication channels for employees, executives, crisis team members, regulators, customers, suppliers, media and other interested parties during disruption.

28. **Contact information shall be current and accessible.** 
 Crisis contact lists, escalation paths and key supplier contacts shall be reviewed regularly and stored in a manner accessible during loss of primary systems.

29. **Crisis communications shall be controlled.** 
 External communications during crisis events shall be approved by authorised personnel and coordinated with legal, regulatory, customer, public relations and executive stakeholders as appropriate.

30. **Regulatory and stakeholder notification obligations shall be assessed promptly.** 
 During significant disruption or cyber-related crisis events, [Organisation Name] shall assess whether notification to competent authorities, customers, affected individuals, contractual partners or other stakeholders is required.

31. **Continuity and recovery plans shall consider information security.** 
 Recovery activities shall not bypass security controls unless formally authorised as an emergency exception and subject to compensating controls, monitoring and post-event review.

32. **Privileged access during recovery shall be controlled.** 
 Emergency privileged access granted during continuity or disaster recovery activities shall be time-bound, recorded, monitored and revoked when no longer required.

33. **Data integrity shall be validated before restoration to production.** 
 Restored systems and data shall be checked for integrity, malware, corruption and unauthorised modification before being returned to service where practicable.

34. **Recovery shall be prioritised based on business impact.** 
 In a multi-system or organisation-wide disruption, restoration activities shall follow approved service and system recovery priorities unless the Crisis Management Team directs otherwise.

35. **Continuity plans shall be tested.** 
 Business continuity plans, disaster recovery plans, backup restoration processes and crisis management arrangements shall be exercised at planned intervals and after significant organisational, technical or threat changes.

36. **Exercises shall include realistic scenarios.** 
 Testing shall include plausible scenarios such as ransomware, loss of cloud services, loss of key supplier, loss of site, loss of communications, data corruption and extended system outage.

37. **Exercise outcomes shall be documented.** 
 Results of tests and exercises shall be recorded, including scope, participants, scenario, outcomes, issues, recovery performance, lessons learned and agreed remediation actions.

38. **Deficiencies shall be remediated.** 
 Gaps identified through incidents, exercises, audits, supplier reviews or monitoring shall be tracked to completion with accountable owners and target dates.

39. **Plans shall be accessible during disruption.** 
 Current continuity, recovery and crisis management plans shall be available to authorised personnel through resilient access methods, including access when primary networks or identity services are unavailable.

40. **Staff shall be trained on continuity and crisis responsibilities.** 
 Personnel with assigned roles in business continuity, disaster recovery, backup management, communications or crisis management shall receive appropriate training and participate in exercises.

41. **Key personnel coverage shall be maintained.** 
 Critical continuity and recovery roles shall have nominated deputies or alternates to reduce dependency on single individuals.

42. **Continuity arrangements shall protect people first.** 
 During any disruptive event, the safety and wellbeing of employees, contractors, visitors and affected third parties shall take priority over asset protection and service restoration.

43. **Records shall be maintained.** 
 [Organisation Name] shall retain records of business impact analyses, recovery objectives, plans, backup schedules, test results, crisis decisions, communications, issues and remediation evidence.

44. **Post-incident reviews shall be performed.** 
 Following activation of crisis management, disaster recovery or significant continuity arrangements, [Organisation Name] shall conduct a post-incident review to identify root causes, effectiveness, lessons learned and required improvements.

45. **Continuous improvement shall be required.** 
 Business continuity, backup, disaster recovery and crisis management capabilities shall be improved based on test results, incidents, changes in threat landscape, business changes, regulatory expectations and audit findings.

The following minimum recovery classification model shall be used unless a formally approved alternative is documented:

| Recovery Tier | Example Services | Maximum Target Recovery Time | Maximum Target Data Loss | Minimum Expected Controls |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Tier 1 - Critical | Essential services, core customer platforms, identity services, security monitoring, critical operational technology | [0-4 hours] | [0-1 hour] | High availability or rapid failover, frequent backups or replication, tested recovery runbooks, priority support |
| Tier 2 - High | Important business applications, customer support systems, finance operations, key internal platforms | [4-24 hours] | [4-24 hours] | Scheduled backups, documented recovery plan, periodic restoration testing, supplier recovery commitments |
| Tier 3 - Moderate | Departmental systems, reporting platforms, non-critical collaboration tools | [1-5 business days] | [1-5 business days] | Standard backups, documented restoration process, periodic verification |
| Tier 4 - Low | Archive services, non-essential tools, low-impact reference systems | [More than 5 business days] | [As approved by business owner] | Retention-based backup or rebuild process, documented ownership |

The following minimum testing schedule shall apply:

| Activity | Minimum Frequency | Responsible Owner | Required Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Business impact analysis review | Annually and after material change | Business Process Owner | Approved business impact analysis and dependency record |
| Business continuity plan review | Annually and after material change | Business Continuity Plan Owner | Updated plan and approval record |
| Crisis management tabletop exercise | At least annually | Crisis Management Lead | Scenario, attendance, decisions, lessons learned and action plan |
| Disaster recovery exercise for Tier 1 services | At least annually | Technology Service Owner | Test report, recovery timings, validation results and issues log |
| Disaster recovery exercise for Tier 2 services | At least every [12-18 months] | Technology Service Owner | Test report and remediation actions |
| Backup restoration test for Tier 1 data | At least quarterly | Backup Service Owner | Restoration evidence and integrity validation |
| Backup restoration test for Tier 2 data | At least semi-annually | Backup Service Owner | Restoration evidence and integrity validation |
| Critical supplier continuity review | At least annually | Supplier Relationship Owner | Supplier assurance evidence and risk assessment |
| Crisis contact list verification | At least quarterly | Business Continuity Manager | Updated contact list and confirmation record |

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Board of Directors / Governing Body | Provides oversight of operational resilience, approves risk appetite, receives reporting on major continuity and crisis risks, and ensures appropriate resources are available. |
| Executive Management | Ensures this Policy is implemented across business functions, supports crisis decision-making and prioritises remediation of significant continuity or recovery gaps. |
| Crisis Management Team | Leads strategic response during major disruption, sets priorities, authorises emergency actions, coordinates internal and external communications, and oversees return to normal operations. |
| Crisis Management Lead | Maintains crisis management arrangements, coordinates exercises, manages activation processes and ensures crisis records are maintained. |
| Business Continuity Manager | Owns the business continuity management framework, supports business impact analysis, maintains continuity standards, coordinates testing and tracks improvement actions. |
| Chief Information Security Officer / Security Lead | Ensures continuity and recovery arrangements address cybersecurity risks, including ransomware resilience, secure restoration, incident coordination and protection of backups. |
| Chief Information Officer / Technology Lead | Ensures technology disaster recovery capabilities are implemented, maintained, tested and aligned with business recovery objectives. |
| Business Process Owners | Identify critical processes, approve business impact analysis outputs, define minimum operating capability, maintain continuity plans and participate in exercises. |
| Technology Service Owners | Maintain disaster recovery plans, define system dependencies, ensure recovery capabilities meet approved objectives and validate restored services. |
| Backup Service Owner | Maintains backup schedules, monitors backup completion, protects backup repositories, coordinates restoration testing and reports backup failures or risks. |
| Supplier Relationship Owners | Ensure critical suppliers meet continuity and recovery requirements, obtain assurance evidence and escalate supplier resilience risks. |
| Legal and Compliance | Advises on regulatory, contractual and notification obligations during crisis events and reviews external communications where required. |
| Communications / Public Relations | Coordinates approved stakeholder, customer, media and public communications during crisis events. |
| Human Resources | Supports workforce continuity, staff welfare, emergency contact processes and people-related communications during disruption. |
| Facilities / Physical Security | Maintains site continuity arrangements, access control, emergency response coordination and facility recovery planning. |
| Employees and Contractors | Follow continuity and crisis instructions, participate in training and exercises when required, and report disruptions, system failures or recovery concerns promptly. |
| Internal Audit / Assurance Function | Provides independent assessment of the effectiveness of continuity, backup, disaster recovery and crisis management controls. |

## Compliance, Monitoring & Enforcement

Compliance with this Policy is mandatory.

[Organisation Name] shall monitor compliance through a combination of management oversight, operational reporting, testing, audit, technical monitoring and supplier assurance. Monitoring activities shall include, where applicable:

- Review of completed business impact analyses and approved recovery objectives.
- Tracking of business continuity and disaster recovery plan completion and currency.
- Monitoring of backup job success, backup failures, restoration results and backup repository security.
- Review of disaster recovery exercise results against approved recovery objectives.
- Crisis management exercise participation and completion of action plans.
- Review of critical supplier continuity evidence and recovery commitments.
- Validation that critical recovery documentation is current and accessible.
- Security monitoring of backup platforms, privileged access and recovery environments.
- Management reporting on overdue remediation actions and accepted risks.

The following compliance indicators shall be reported to [Risk Committee / Executive Management] at a defined frequency:

| Metric | Target | Reporting Frequency |
|---|---:|---:|
| Critical business processes with current business impact analysis | [95-100%] | Quarterly |
| Tier 1 services with approved disaster recovery plans | [100%] | Quarterly |
| Successful backup completion rate for critical systems | [98-100%] | Monthly |
| Critical backup restoration tests completed on schedule | [95-100%] | Quarterly |
| Tier 1 disaster recovery exercises completed on schedule | [100%] | Quarterly |
| Open high-risk continuity or recovery findings past due | 0 | Monthly |
| Critical suppliers with current continuity assurance evidence | [95-100%] | Quarterly |
| Crisis contact list reviewed within required period | [100%] | Quarterly |

Non-compliance with this Policy may result in:

- Formal risk acceptance by an authorised risk owner.
- Mandatory remediation plans and management escalation.
- Restriction or suspension of affected services, systems or supplier arrangements.
- Disciplinary action for employees, up to and including termination of employment.
- Contractual remedies for third parties, up to and including termination of contract.
- Notification to regulators, customers or other stakeholders where required.

Deliberate failure to maintain, protect or test backups; unauthorised deletion or alteration of backup data; failure to escalate a major disruption; or unauthorised crisis communications shall be treated as serious policy breaches.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to this Policy shall be permitted only where there is a justified business, technical or operational reason and the associated risk has been assessed and approved.

All exception requests shall include:

- Description of the requirement that cannot be met.
- Business or technical justification.
- Affected services, systems, data, suppliers or locations.
- Risk assessment and potential impact.
